column4: Summary

Sources on 10 August reported clashes between security forces and insurgents along the Mocimboa da Praia / Palma Districts border in the Mpalanganha area.  Insurgent cells control some rural territory in this area north of MDP town, and are reportedly not allowing any seagoing vessels to use area water ways.

A group of around 15 military vehicles on the morning of 09 August were ambushed in the Awasse area by insurgents after having travelled from the large Mozambican army base in Mueda.  Insurgents on 09 August were reported to have taken control of Awasse, and have been continuously active in the Awasse area throughout 2020.  Sources later reported at least 15 soldiers killed in these clashes.  Reliable sources later reported that 55 soldiers were killed in this ambush, one of the deadliest of the insurgency.

Insurgents at around 0400hrs on 10 August attacked the port of Mocimboa da Praia town, clashing with security forces and South African Private Military Contractors in the area.  Sources later indicated that at least 55 soldiers were killed in fighting in the town with at least 90 others injured, while militant casaulties are currently unknown.  Other sources later claimed that up to 200 soldiers had been killed in these clashes, though this is unconfirmed. Mozambican forces in MDP had run out of ammunition before being resupplied by an ammo drop by South African Private Military Contractors.  PMC helicopters supporting Mozambican forces were limited in their ability to provide effective air support during the clashes as their limited fuel capacity forced them to return continually to Pemba to refuel. Insurgents began their assault on MDP on 05  August, and captured much of the town before launching a final assault on 10 August.  By the evening of 11 August, the town was reported to be under the full control of the insurgents.   Reliable sources later said at least 86 soldiers were killed in the MDP fighting.

142 new cases of COVID-19 were reported in Mozambique on 10 August - the single largest daily increase in cases since COVID was first detected in the country in March.  78 of the new cases are in the capital Maputo.  2,411 cases have been confirmed in the country so far, with 16 deaths.

Suspected RENAMO dissidents on 07 August opened fire on a bus in the Mutamira area near the N1 road just outside of Muxungue in Chibabava district, killing a child and injuring 3 other civilians at around 0600hrs.  The bus was travelling between Maputo and Nampula.  Other ambushes have occurred since August 2019 in the Mutindiri area; RENAMO dissidents continue to be active along the Manica-Sofala border.  These types of bus ambushes continue to be the dissident's primary method of attack.

Maputo City was declared Mozambique's third location with community trasmission of the COVID-19 outbreak after 5.1% of 837 tests run in the capital came back positive for the virus.  More than 75% of the cases in Maputo are in the Municipal District of Kampfumo, with 471 cases of the 611 positive cases in the city in this area.  Nampula and Pemba on 06 June and 22 June were also declared to be in the community transmission phase.

A police officer shot and injured a woman in Beira city on Saturday evening.  The officer was reportedly drunk and fired on the woman who was arguing with a relative of the police officer over a small debt owed to the woman.  The officer reportedly fled the scene after local residents attempted to lynch him, and he remains on the run.

ISCAP on 11 August released images displaying weapons, including at least 25 AK typle rifles, large quantities of ammunition, and several RPG launchers recently captured in clashes with security forces in Cabo Delgado.  Weapons on display likely were seized in an insurgent ambush of security forces in the Awasse area on 09 August.

Mozambican military forces were reported to have begun a withdrawal from Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) town on 10 August after clashes with insurgents in the area.  Insurgents by the evening of 11 August were believed to exercise semi-territorial control over the town and immediate surroundings.  Mozambican troops reportedly sustained significant losses in fighting with insurgents between 06-11 August before withdrawing from the town.  A large portion of the town's 30,000 people meanwhile are believed to have fled the area. This is the third occupation of MDP by insurgents in 2020. One source later reported as many as 1,000 insurgents had occupied the town.

Tanzania's military on 10 August announced it would launch a "manhunt" in forest along the Tanzania-Mozambican border in the Lindi, Mtwara, and Rovuma areas, saying it was targeting "criminals" hiding in the area.  Islamist insurgents operating in Cabo Delgado are widely believed to have a significant presence in Southern Tanzania and have long-standing links to the area, which are used as a pipeline and logistics corridor into insurgent areas of operation in Cabo Delgado.

Clashes between insurgents and the Mozambican military were reported on 10 August at the village of Chai along the N380 road when insurgents entered the village attempting to steal livestock.  4 soldiers were reportedly killed with others injured; no other casaulty information is currently available.
5 insurgents on 08 August attacked the village of Litamanda along the N380 road, killing 5 civilians and setting several huts on fire.  The insurgents reportedly wore Mozambican military uniforms.

A 4.9 magnitude earthquake was reported at approximately 0710hrs in the Mozambican Channel, 67 kms from Nacala port and 41 kms from Memba.  The earthquake was felt primarily in parts of Nampula province as slight tremors, and no casaulties or damage was reported in the aftermath of the incident.

Unconfirmed reports have indicated that insurgents in a 10 August assault on Mocimboa da Praia town destroyed a French made interceptor vessel recently purchased by the Mozambican government that had been docked at the town's pier.  Other reports indicated that a second patrol boat was damaged by RPG fire in the attack as well.

Speaking at a virtual Word Bank Event on 11 August, President Filipe Nyusi said that natural gas exploration projects in Cabo Delgado are not threatened by the ongoing insurgency in the province.  Nyusi also said that there were "signs of involvement" of foreigners in training and recruiting local youth into the insurgency.  LNG projects in Palma remain Mozambique's single most important economic asset and are projected to double the size of the Mozambican economy in the coming years.

200 additional Mozambican soldiers were deployed on 12 August from Pemba to the Afungi Penninsula / Palma area, soruces reported.  This came after Mocimboa da Praia town fell to a new insurgent assault earlier in the week.

Insurgents on 12 August were reported to be in control of large parts of the Palma - Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) road.  Insurgent control likely stretches from MDP town itself north towards the MDP-Palma District Border.  Insurgents are also reported to still be in control of Awasse village, west of MDP town along the N380 road.

A local police chief on 08 August attacked and badly injured a fellow officer in Chinde District of Zambezia, leaving the victim in critical condition.  The police chief after the attack reportedly went on the run and is currently being sought be authorities.

Mozambican security forces in Macomia District were reported to have recently stopped issuing "Guia de Marcha" passes to local residents which allow local residents to move freely from one area to another within areas impacted by the ongoing insurgency.  This stoppage in the issuance of these passes has in recent days prevented those attempting to flee the insurgency zone from doing so.  The reasons for this stoppage are not currently known.  Instances of these passes being sold illegally in Macomia have increased.  The goverment has consistently attempted to play down the significance of the insurgency, and stopping more refugees from moving south towards Pemba may be part of this strategy.

The Mozambican military on 12 August announced that it had killed 59 insurgents in fighting in Cabo Delgado in recent days, saying the the military had also destroyed six militant camps in recent operations.  No exact locations were specified for these clashes, and the statement was made a day after insurgents were confirmed to have captured Mocimboa da Praia town.  The military on Wednesday also said that it had repelled an insurgent assault on MDP town, though other sources widely agree the town has been occupied by militants.  Authorities also aknowldeged insurgent attacks in recent days on the villages of Anga, Buji, and Awasse, in addition to the MDP assault. Reliable sources later indicated that 73 insurgents had been killed in Mocimboa da Praia fighting.

An investigation by the Maputo Provincial Prosecutor Office into the case of 15 young female recruits at a police training facility who were allegedly impregnated by their instructors.  The 15 had been training at the Matalana Basic School, and the case case to light after recent routine medical exams.

The US's State Dpt on 07 August updated its travel warnings for Mozambique, advising against travel to "Ancuabe, Ibo, Macomia, Meluco, Metuge, Mocimboa da Praia, Mueda, Muidumbe, Nangade, Palma, and Quissanga Districts" due to the ongoing insurgency, while advising travelers to "reconsider travel" to Pemba.  The warning also advised that due to "violent attacks against vehicles", travel should be reconsidered along the N1 road between Chibabava and Gorongosa and along the N6 road beween Chimoio and Tica.

column4: Inhambane province on 11 August reported that all 50 COVID patients in the province had officially recovered, and that there were now no active cases in the province.  Inhambane is the first province to have no currently known active COVID cases.
A young man in the early morning hours of 13 August entered a residence in the T3 neighborhood of Maputo City, stealing a wallet and a mobile phone.  The man was later arrested by local police.
A young man in the early morning hours of 13 August entered a residence in the T3 neighborhood of Maputo City, stealing a wallet and a mobile phone.  The man was later arrested by local police.
A 26 year old man on 08 August beat his father to death with a blunt instrument during a domestic dispute in Autola da Matola in Maputo Province.  The man was later arrested by police.
A 26 year old man on 08 August beat his father to death with a blunt instrument during a domestic dispute in Autola da Matola in Maputo Province.  The man was later arrested by police.

Two people were killed and 18 others injured in a road traffic accident in the Nicoadala area of Zambezia on 11 August.  The accident took place along the N1 road when a bus driver hit a pedestrian and then lost control of his vehicle, flipping the bus.  3 of the 18 injured are in critical condition, while 15 suffered minor injuries.

RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo said on 09 August that he will "continue to defend" weapons held by his group until the government negotiates a new peace agreement with his faction.  Nhongo made this announcement from Tete, where he said the group maintains a number of bases.  Suspected RENAMO dissidents continue to carry out intermittent attacks along the Sofala-Manica border.

68 Malawian nationals on 10 August were detained at the Ressano Garcia border crossing after entering Mozambique illegally.  The group had been expelled from South Africa into Mozambique and were discovered in the Kumbeza area by authorities after a tip off from locals.

Mozambican customs officials were reported on 11 August to have seized 34,000 cell phones and 3,000 units of perfume that had been smuggled into the country.  The seizure occurred in central Beira, just after the trucks the smuggled goods left Beira port.
A young man was arrested in Nkobe District of Matola after he assaulted his mother during a domestic dispute.  The man has a past criminal history.

Local businessman Artur Magaia was kidnapped on 13 August from the Belo Horizonte area of Boane in Maputo Province.  Magaia was abducted while arriving back at his home by unidentified assailants.  The kidnappers followed Magaia to his home in one vehicle, while another vehicle waited for him at his home.  Security guards present at the scene reportedly did not attempt to stop the abduction.  The greater Maputo area has witnessed several high profile kidnappings so far in 2020.   Magaia is the owner of the Magaia Resort Bilene in Gaza province; his ID and other documents were found abandoned at the scene of the kidnapping.

Mozambican officials said on 13 August that Tanzanian authorities had arrested a group of suspected insurgents attempting to cross the Rovuma River into Cabo Delgado and who were destined for Mocimboa da Praia.  Officials also said that Maputo and Dodoma would improve coordination if fighting the ongoing Cabo Delgado insurgency.  This announcement comes after Tanzania said earlier this week that it would launch operations targeting "criminals" along the border.

Mozambique's Ministers of the Interior and Defense on 13 August announced that insurgents were not in control of Mocimboa da Praia or any other part of the country, but aknowledged members of the group were "present in parts of the town" and had carried out attacks, looting, and had destroyed part of the town.  The officials said insurgents in heavy fighting had sustained significant casaulties as well.  The ministers also said that insurgents are "no longer easy to identify" and camouflage themselves as civilians.  Neto went on to say that the insurgents had first infiltrated the town and attacked it "from the inside out" and had sabotaged attempts by security forces to launch martime rescues from the port.  The ministers also said that the situation remains tense in the town, and confirmed militants had fired on boats present at the port.  Jaime Neto, Minister of Defense said measures were being taken to assure the insurgency does not spread to "other regions", and said that Mozambique would not declare a "state of siege" in Cabo Delgado and did not need help from international partners to combat the insurgency.

79 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 13 August, along with 2 new deaths.  There have now been a total of 2638 cases in the country, along with 19 deaths.  933 cases have been diagnosed in Maputo City and Maputo Province, or about 35% of the total number of cases in the country.

Clashes are reportedly ongoing in the Mocimboa da Praia town area, where government officials claim their forces are attempting to regain the town.  Multiple sources indicated that insurgents after several days of fighting took control of MDP on 11 August, though on 13 August government officials denied that insurgents were in full control of MDP though aknowledged militants were present in the town.  No further details on these ongoing clashes is currently available.

A new outbreak of foot and mouth disease among hooved animals in Maputo province was reported on 12 August in Magude District.  Officials have banned any movement of hooved animals in and out of Maputo province for the foreseeable future.  The transportation of animals has not been banned but will require certificates showing veterinary inspections on animals have been carried out.

Insurgents armed with machetes and firearms at around 8pm on 09 August attacked Nambo village in the Mucojo AP post of Macomia District, beheading one person and shot another dead.  Four people were also abducted during the attack.  This village has been attacked multiple times by insurgents and lies in an area where insurgents maintain bush camps.

Insurgents on the evening 09 August attacked Nambo village in the Mucojo AP post of Macomia District, beheading one person and killing another.  Four people, three men and a woman, were abducted.  One of those abducted is reportedly a brother of an insurgent.

South Africa on 12 August repatriated 500 Mozambicans who had been illegally living in the country back to Mozambique.  This operation was part of ongoing anti-COVID measures taken by the South African government.  1,381 Mozambicans have been deported from South Africa since April, and this is the sixth batch of deportees sent back to Mozambique since that time.

Unconfirmed reports indicated that over 5,000 tons of an ammonium nitrate are being stored in two locations in Beira in Munhava-Vaz and Manga-Mascarenhas.  This report surfaced after a large amount of this chemical recently exploded in Beirut, Lebanon, killing 154 people; the ammonium nitrate in Beirut was also reportedly destined for Mozambique.

Sources indicated that insurgents in Cabo Delgado are likely operating out of 3 main cells.  One cell is likely based in Nangade District, close to the border with Tanzania.  A second central cell is likely based in the Narere / Mbau area of Mocimboa da Praia District, while a third cell is likely based in the Gagembe/Cagembe area, in northern Quissanga District.

A South Afircan MP and Deputy Shadow Minister, Dr Mimmy Gondwe, on 12 August published a press release calling on the South African government to provide "clarity" on Praetoria's plans to ensure the safety of South African investments in Mozambique from insurgents operating in Cabo Delgado.  This press release came as pressure has increased on the South African Development Community and South Africa specifically to provide more support to the Mozambican government's fight against Islamist insurgents in the north of the country.

A German media outlet reported on 13 August that Russia plans to install 6 military bases in Africa, including a base in Mozambique.  The base would most likely be located in either Cabo Delgado or perhaps more likely in Nampula province at Nacala port, where Russian private miltiary contractors have operated out of in the past.

On 11 August, military authorities imposed a new curfew in Mueda from 630pm to 6am. This comes as insurgents captured Mocimboa da Praia, and the threat of an insurgent attack on Mueda, site of a major military base, is increasing.

On the evening of 12 August, insurgents attacked Olumbi village south of Palma along the coast, briefly capturing the village before retreating.  No further information including regarding casaulties from this incident is currently available.

Mozambican military units over the night of 13-14 August repelled an insurgent attack on Macomia town.  Elements of the local population also fled into the woods during these clashes.  No details on casaulties are currently available.  Insurgents previously occupied Macomia, the capital of Macomia District, in late May after heavy fighting with Mozambican armed forces.

Mozambican military units over the night of 13-14 August were reported to have targeted insurgents just outside of Namacande/Muidumbe town, firing on insurgent positions to force insurgents to flee.  Local residents reportedly fled the area.  Insurgents in April occupied Muidumbe District capital Namacande as they raided several villages in the area.

President Nyusi on 14 August visited an IDP camp in Metuge, Cabo Delgado for those displaced by the ongoing insurgency.  This visit conincided with intensified clashes in the province as insurgents this week captured Mocimboa da Praia town.  Nyusi during the day said that the war in Cabo Delgado was the "fault of people who want to divide the country for its wealth".  Nyusi also reportedly visited Pemba where he spoke with both local officials and military personnel.  Camp residents meanwhile asked the president to restore security conditions to allow them to return to their homes.
Local media reported on 14 August that 3 Rapid Intervention Unit agents were arrested on charges of sexually assaulting a 22 year old girl in Maputo City in Mafalala District.
Local media reported on 14 August that 3 Rapid Intervention Unit agents were arrested on charges of sexually assaulting a 22 year old girl in Maputo City in Mafalala District.

1500 newly graduated riot police were reported on 14 August to have been deployed to Cabo Delgado.  This comes after the insurgents' recent victory at Cabo Delgado, and these reinforcements will likely be deployed in Pemba, Mueda, and Palma among other locations to help stem the insurgent advance.

Mozambican military units, including hundreds of troops recently deployed to Cabo Delgado on 16 August were reported to have surrounded Mocimboa da Praia town, which is still held by insurgents who captured the town last week.

70 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 14 August, with 34 new cases reported in Maputo City, 18 in Maputo province, 5 in Sofala, 4 in Nampula, 4 in Gaza, 3 in Cabo Delgado, 1 in Zambezia, and 1 in Manica.  This brings the nationwide total of cases to 2,708, with 19 deaths.

Egidio G. Vaz Raposo, an advisor to President Nyusi, on 17 August said in a Facebook post that Bishop Luiz Fernando Lisboa, the Bishop of Pemba, is a "logistician" for the Cabo Delgado insurgents, saying Lisboa provides food to the insurgency.  This came after Gustavo Mavie, a former director of the Mozambican Information Agency, wrote an article criticizing Lisboa for his critiques of the Maputo government.  Lisboa in recent years has continually raised awareness of the Cabo Delgado insurgency and its impact on Cabo Delgado, and has strongly criticized the government's failure to contain the insurgency.

Mozambican police on 15 August were reported to have launched an investigation into the kidnapping of Arthur Mabjaia, which occurred on 12 August in Boane.  Information on the kidnapping remains scarce though Mabjaia was reportedly kidnapped in the early morning hours by unidentified assailants in two vehicles that followed him to his home.

A fire broke out at the Chinese Road and Bridge Corporation camp in Maputo Province  in Catembe.  The blaze reportedly broke out at around 9am as part of a welding accident.  Some equipment was destroyed in the fire before firefighters at around 1pm put it out.

On the night of 15 August, Rajiv Nitin, the son of an Indian businessman, was kidnapped in Beira city from the Maquinino neighborhood.  Nitin was abducted at around 6:15pm by four unidentified individuals in a gray Toytoa truck along the Avenida Machado dos Santos.  Nitin's wife who was also at the scene of the incident was robbed of her purse. The four assailants were reported to be armed with "blunt instruments" as well as at least one firearm.  Police said they had immediately launched an investigation into the incident.

Clashes between insurgents and the Mozambican military were reported on 15 August in the MDP area.  No information on casaulties is currently available.  Insurgents continue to hold the town and much of the surrounding area.  Sources also reported that insurgents were being supplied via dhows after security forces surrounded the town.

83 new COVID cases in Mozambique were reported on 15 August, with 55 new cases in Maputo City, 12 in Maputo, 6 in Nampula, 1 in Manica, 4 in Inhambane, and 5 in Gaza.  This raised the nationwide total number of cases to 2,791, with 19 deaths.

64 new cases of COVID were reported in Mozambique on 16 August, raising the nationwide total to 2,855 cases with 19 deaths.  26 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 12 in Maputo, 9 in Sofala, 6 in Gaza, 4 in Tete, 4 in Manica, 2 in Nampula and 1 in Zambezia.

Mozambique on 17 August takes over the acting presidency of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) at the SADC's annual summit.  The ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado is widely anticipated to be among the topics to be discussed a the summit, though it remains unclear if Mozambique will take the oppurtunity to request for an SADC military intervention into Cabo Delgado to combat IS-linked militants in the province.  The SADC summit attendees later in the day issued a statement expressing "solidarity and commitment to support" Mozambique in combating the insurgency, though no tangible steps towards countering the insurgency via the SADC were publicly discussed or announced.

Clashes in Mocimboa da Praia between insurgents and Mozambican military units on 17 August were reproted to be ongoing.  Almost all residents of the town are reported to have fled the area, and communication links in the area remain cut.  Earlier reports indicated the town had been surrounded by Mozambican military units.  No information on casaulties is available at this time.

Mozambican authorities on 17 August announced that all foreign and national citizens wishing to enter or leave Mozambique would be required to obtain a "Guia de Marcha", a document allowing movements across Mozambican borders authroized by the Minster of the Interior.  These passes were previously used in Mozambique before the transition to democracy, and have been more recently used in insurgency impacted areas of Cabo Delgado.

5 girls on 17 August were reported to have escaped from an insurgent camp in the Mbau area and fled to the nearby village of Simbalongo.  This incident speaks to the continued presence relatively nearby of insurgent camps.
3 abducted girls on 17 August were reported to have escaped from an insurgent camp in the Quitereajo area.  Insurgents have consistenly been reported to maintain a presence in or around Quiterajo.
Mozambican police were reported to have seized 102 containers containing illegally logged wood from a ship in Pemba after a local tip off.

Sources reported on 17 August that Mozambican police arrested around 150 people recently on Inhaca island in Maputo for violations of the new 08 August State of Emergency.  Police officers however said only 11 of these individuals continue to be held, while the rest were released.

Many Nampula residents are reportedly disregarding anti-COVID measures such as social distancing, the wearing of face masks, and avoiding unneccesary travel, local officals said on 16 August.  Provincial authorities say not adhereing to anti-COVID measures in widespread across Nampula city and the wider province, and that only in "extreme" cases are police called to enforce anti-COVID measures.

Beira District Administrator Joao Oliveira on 14 August at a meeting with Beira police officials announced that anyone in the district not following anti-COVID measures of the State of Emergency including not wearing a mask would be arrested and would receive 3-15 days in prison or a fine.  This comes after 33 cases of COVID-19 have been diagnosed in Beira in recent weeks.
A military vehicle on 16 August was reported to have skidded off the road in Cuamba District, Niassa province.  One soldier was killed in the accident.

On the morning of 16 August, a man died after being set on fire in Rimbane, Cuamba District after he was caught by a group of local residents stealing items from a home.  Other gang members escaped the scene of the incident. Lynching incidents are relatively common in much of Mozambique, and this is the third such incident in Rimbane in the last 5 years.

Over 2,600 refugees from the Cabo Delgado insurgency are now present in the Santa Cruz area of Nampula city.  Many of these are recently arrived after insurgent attacks in recent months.  Local Catholic churchs are the primary shelter for these IDPs; IDPs continue to arrive in Nampula on a weekly basis fleeing from the ongoing insurgency.

59 new COVID-19 cases were reported in Mozambique on Monday, 17 August, bringing the countrywide total cases to 2,914 with 19 deaths.  25 cases were reported in Maputo City, 15 in Manica, 7 in Cabo Delgado, 5 in Nampula, 4 in Maputo, 2 in Sofala, and 1 in Gaza.
Unknown men set fire to three fishing inspection boats in Beira on two consecutive evenings on 15 and 16 August. No casualties were reported.
Unknown men set fire to three fishing inspection boats in Beira on two consecutive evenings on 15 and 16 August. No casualties were reported.

A group of 150 Illegal miners on 13 August were reported to have illegally entered a concession of a Montepuez mining company.  Two illegal miners drowned in a water reserve area in the conession, while a third miner was rescued after falling into the water.

Mozambique's Interior Ministry on 15 August issued a notice that the government will now charge 98 meticais per light vehicles, 247 meticais for trucks, and 48 meticais for motorcycles crossing all Mozambican borders.  For every hour a vehicle remains at the border, a fee of 824 meticais will reportedly be charged.  New entry fees will reportedly be charged for all "trains, aircraft, and ships".
Rapid Intervention Unit police on 15 August were reported to have detained a young man in Macomia town.  The man's body was discovered the next day in the nearby forest close to the N380 route.

Mozambican security forces on 16 August threatened to kill a Macomia man for unknown reasons.  This incident occurred one day after another Macomia man was abducted and reportedly killed by police in the town.

Mozambique on 18 August confirmed 77 new COVID cases, bringing the total number of cases in the country to 2991 while the death toll remains at 19.  49 cases were reported in Maputo City, 22 in Maputo, 3 in Niassa, 2 in Sofala, and 1 in Cabo Delgado.

Malaria is reported to have killed 365 people throughout Mozambique so far in 2020, with 35,136 people infected with the disease during the course of the year. Over the same period in 2019, 465 people had died of the disease.

Niassa officials say that late arrival at health facilities has led to a series of diarrhoea deaths in the province in 2020.  20 deaths have been reported in the province so far this year of diarrheal diseases, with 31,000 cases reported.

Mozambique's economy was reported by the National Statistics Institute to have contracted by 3.25% in the second quarter after growing 1.68% in the first quarter due primarily to the ongoing COVID pandemic.  The Mozambican Confederation of Economic Associations meanwhile said it had seen a 65% reduction in business activity countrywide in the first half of the year due to the pandemic, and said that total losses for all of 2020 could amount to abot $951 million, the equivalent of about 7% of GDP.  The organization also said up to 11% of the country's private workforce could lose their jobs by the end of the year.

South African MP and shadow Minister for Defense for the Democratic Alliance Party Kobus Marais called on 14 August for a "special fact finding envoy" to be deployed to Cabo Delgado to report back to the Southern African Development Community (SADC) on the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  Marais also said the SADC should consider the deployment of an intervention force to Cabo in order to protect South African interests and the interests of the SADC as a whole.

Mozambican airline LAM on 14 August announced that on 25 August it would resume commercial flights between Maputo and Lisbon with the Maputo-Lisbon leg offered on Tuesdays and the Lisbon-Maputo leg offered on Wednesdays.  The resumption of these flights has been postponed three times due to COVID.

Media sources in Maputo city have reported that the issuance of Identity Cards, Foreign Resident Identification Documents,and temporary documents was resumed on 17 August after having been halted due to the COVID pandemic.  The issuance of passports however remains suspended, though all recently expired passports have had their validity extended to 30 September.

Local media reported on 18 August that a fisherman led a group of 20 people in the Mocimboa da Praia area who had been captured by insurgents to escape from captivity.  The fisherman led the group in a nightime escape in recent days, swimming south from Mocimboa da Praia to areas held by Mozambican military forces.

Higher education classes as well as religious services are set to resume on 18 August across Mozambique as part of "Phase One" of the relaxation of anti-COVID measures.  Phase Two, the resumption of "medium-risk" activity, will begin on 01 September.

Mozambique's National Health Institute on 18 August indicated the pace of COVID cases in Mozambique is quickly accelerating.  The first case of the virus was diagnoses on 22 March in the country, and it took 81 days until 500 cases were diagnosed.  The next 500 cases took just 23 days, while the next 500 cases took just 14 days before nationwide cases stood at 1,500.  The rise of cases from 1,500 to 2,000 took another 14 days, but quickly acclerated from 2,000 to 2,500 in just 5 days.  92 districts, or 57% of the country's districts, now have confirmed cases, and community transmission is currently ongoing in Maputo City.  Despite this increase in numbers, 57% of cases diagnosed in the country are asymptomatic, and just 19 deaths have been recorded in the country.

The Southern Africa Social Communication Institute-Mozambique on 18 August demanded that journalists be permitted by the government to cover the Cabo Delgado insurgency safely, also calling on the Mozambican government to free Ibraimo Mbaruco, a Palma journalist who was reportedly taken into government custody on 07 April this year and remains missing.

Insurgents ambushed a minibus coming from Litandacau along Litandacau-Chai Road (Route N380) on the morning of 19 August. No casualties were reported. The vehicle managed to escape the ambush and arrive at Chai.

Hainan Airlines announced that a nonstop flight via Airbus A330-300 would be flying to Maputo International Airport (MPM) from Beijing Capital International Airport (PEK) and back starting on 22 August. The flight will leave Beijing reaching Maputo at 11:35. The plane will depart Maputo for Colombo (CMB) at 16:35. The aircraft will be grounded for 90 minutes during a technical stop in Colombo before flying into Nanchang, finally reaching China on 23 August. The flight was arranged to enable passengers intending to travel back to China.

Armed men dressed in Mozambican military uniforms were reported to have shot at two boats transporting civilians attempting to escape attacks from Nkomangano district on 13 August. At least 40 were reportedly killed during the attack and after the second boat sunk while travelling towards Palma.  The uniformed men in a motorized vessel approached the two boats and asked where they were travelling to.  Minutes later, the unidentifed men opened fire on the fleeing villagers.  The identity of the armed men remains unclear.  Those killed were reportedly displaced from other villages before fleeing to Nkomangano.

Mozambican security forces on 19 August announced the "maximazation" of patrol actions to fight and capture "terrorists" operating in Cabo Delgado.  This announcement did not include details of recent operations targeting insurgents in Cabo Delgado.

The Mozambican government said on 18 August that in 2019 it had suspended 289 "ghost" employees from public payrolls, saving approximately 16 million meticais or about $224,000 in the process.  The ghost workers were discovered after an audit.  26 government employees were also arrested for "irregularities" in 2019.

Approximately 60 Mozambican workers have been held in confinement at a cement factory in Salamanga, Matutuine, south of Maputo, since April.  The  group's foreign employer reportedly gave employees the option of living at the cement factory during the COVID pandemic or leaving their jobs.  Workers at the facotry are reportedly only allowed 2 days off per month, and the situation is casuing growing unrest among the families of the workers.

Mozambican authorities said on 19 August that they had closed down 225 "clandestine" bars and establishments throughout the country in inspections between 10-14 August.  Authorities said many establishments are not adhereing to state of emergency measures that stipulate they close at 2000hrs each night.

Authorities on 19 August were reported to have seized 1,025 bags of cement in Maputo City and Maputo province from a distributor and two retailers of cement.  Authorities said these businesses had "speculated" and attempted to take "advantage of the customer".

Sources reported on 18 August that clashes continued in Mocimboa da Praia, and that much of the city remains deserted, with large parts of the city reportedly in ruins.  Insurgents reprotedly still control much of the town.  Area residents continue to flee the area.

Refugees fleeing Mocimboa da Praia have indicated that insurgents have told them to leave the area "because they wanted to occupy" the area.  Insurgents have also reportedly warned refugees fleeing the area from going to Mueda.  Other reporting has indicated insurgents seek to make Mocimboa da Praia town their "capital".  Mueda meanwhile is a likely future target for insurgent operations.

Tanzanian forces on 18 August were again reported to be "in military maneuvers" along the Tanzania - Mozambique border in the Luagala area of Mbinga District in Rovuma Province.  Tanzanian forces are reportedly targeting insurgent supply lines and personnel in this area.  More Tanzanian operations are reportedly planned along other parts of the border.
Private mini-bus operatiors in Maputo city on the morning of 19 August were reproted to have stopped all activity, protesting over restrictions put in place as part of anti-COVID measures.

Police were tipped off by locals in Palma and discovered a vehicle containing five disassembled firearms and ammunition on 13 August.  These weapons were believed to belong to insurgents operating in the area.
Police in Macomia arrested 3 young men on 16 August at a local bar, accusing the three of being insurgents.  The identity however of these three persons has not been confirmed.

An interview with an anonymous Mozambican soldier serving in Cabo Delgado was featured on 18 August in local media.  In this interview, the soldier indicated that the insurgency is viewed by the miltiary as being "worst" in Mocimboa da Praia district, where the soldier says many insurgents have family and friends, and where the insurgents reportedly receive significant local support.  He also said that a number of soldiers have defected to the insurgents, and that many local unemployed people also "enlist" with the insurgency.  He also indicated that military logistics in Cabo Delgado are very poor, with basic supplies often diverted due to corruption in the army's officer corps.  The soldier went on to say that bodies of deceased soldiers are often not sent back to their families unless families exert pressure on the army, and that many of those killed in Cabo Delgado are buried in mass graves.

An independent media outlet conducted an extensive investigation into Mozambican military units equipped with Chinese armored fighting vehicles in Cabo Delgado.  The investigation revealed that these fighting vehicles, known as Tigers, were deployed to the province in September 2018, and that main bases for these vehicles are in Mueda, Ancuabe, and Mocimboa da Praia.  This deployment has largely been kept quiet.  Several of these Tiger vehicles have been captured by insurgents and the Tiger vehicles have proved to be a poor tool to counter the Cabo Delgado insurgents.

54 new COVID cases were registered in Mozambique on 20 August, increasing the total to 3,045 cases. The death toll remains at 19 deaths. The cases are distributed as follows: 32 in Maputo City, 10 in Maputo, 8 in Sofala, 3 in Zambézia, and 1 in Niassa.

Dozens of informal importers, known as Mukheristas, gathered at Kilometer 4 checkpoint of Ressano Garcia Border Crossing, northwest of Maputo after authorities seized their goods without specified reasons. The president of the Association of Mukheristas, Sudekar Novela, stated that the customs seized various goods including trucks used to transport the goods. The head of the border post left the area without interacting with the protesters.

Several higher education facilities and institutions reopened in Tete province for face-to-face classes while reportedly adhering to COVID safety precautions. Sanitizers, alcohol, and disinfectants which were placed the entrances of the institutions. While social distancing guidelines were placed on posters around the facilities.
Insurgents continued to exchange gunfire with security forces in Mocimboa da Praia on 7 August. Insurgents also renewed shelling attacks by firing several mortar shells during the armed exchange.
Insurgents continued to exchange gunfire with security forces in Mocimboa da Praia on 7 August. Insurgents also renewed shelling attacks by firing several mortar shells during the armed exchange.
Insurgents renewed gunfire exchanges with security forces at the dawn of 8 August. A sawmill was also destroyed by the insurgents during their advance.
Insurgents renewed gunfire exchanges with security forces at the dawn of 8 August. A sawmill was also destroyed by the insurgents during their advance.

Insurgents attacked Anga and Awasse villages while forcing locals to leave the areas near Mocimboa da Praia on 5 August. The insurgents reportedly burned several residences and kidnapped civilians in Anga Village.

Insurgents attacked Anga and Awasse villages while forcing locals to leave the areas near Mocimboa da Praia on 5 August. The insurgents reportedly burned several residences and kidnapped civilians in Anga Village.

Security forces exchanged gunfire with insurgents during the attempted advance to recapture Anga and Awasse villages on 6 August. The insurgents managed to security their positions in both villages. Unconfirmed reports stated that several of the insurgents withdrew under the cover insurgent mortar shell fire at security forces.

Security forces exchanged gunfire with insurgents during the attempted advance to recapture Anga and Awasse villages on 6 August. The insurgents managed to security their positions in both villages. Unconfirmed reports stated that several of the insurgents withdrew under the cover insurgent mortar shell fire at security forces.

Local media reported on 10 and 17 August, new batches of soldiers graduated from the Muxungue training facilities.  On 10 August, 500 of these soldiers were deployed north to Cabo Delgado.  An undisclosed number of newly graduated troops on 17 August were also deployed to Cabo Delgado.

Mozambican businesses reported losses of $453 million in the first half of 2020 due to the ongoing COVID pandemic, the Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique said.  The hotel and tourism industries have been the hardest hit industries in the country, seeing their economic activity shrink by more than 75%.

Montepuez Ruby Mining (MRM) on 19 August issued a statement sayng that small scale miners are being "exploited by illegal ruby smuggling unions, usually financed by foreign buyers".  The MRM also said that combating illegal miners in the Montepuez area is "beyond our cababilities" and called for greater government support to solve this problem.

Pope Francis recently called Pemba Bishop Luiz Fernando Lisboa, and expressed concern over the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  Lisboa briefed the Pope on the situation in Mocimboa da Praia, and also indicated that two women from a local congregation had been missing for at least a week.  The Bishop's office later made the details of this call public - likely a move to safeguard the bishop after an adviser to president Nyusi recently called Lisboa a "logistician" for the insurgency, prompting fears Lisboa could be targeted by the government or government supporters.

The Bishop of Pemba Luiz Fernando Lisboa said on 19 August that in the wake of the fall of Mocimboa da Praia to insurgents, thousands of refugees have fled the area to Mueda and to Palma.  Lisboa also said insurgents have taken over "almost the entire district" of Mocimboa da Praia.  He also said that more than 31,000 displaced people are in Mueda, 20,000 are in Chiurue, and over 50,000 are in Pemba.

column4: Police on an unclear date last week seized an AK-47 along with 24 bullets from a field in the Namapire area in Mandimba District in Niassa province.  "Unidentified individuals" abandoned the weapon in the field.

Three men were arrested last week on an unspecified date in the districts of Maua and Marrupa in Niassa Province in possession of an AK-47 and two semi-automatic pistols.  Police sources did not provide any further details on these operations.

Police on an unspecified date last week seized a 375 mm shotgun and four rounds of ammunition in Panjane, Magude District, Maputo Province.  No individuals were arrested in this operation.

On 20 August, 70 new cases of COVID were announced in Mozambique as well as one new death, bringing the total number of cases to 3,115 and the total number of deaths to 20.  36 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 17 in Maputo, 6 in Cabo Delgado, 6 in Manica, 3 in Nampula, and 2 in Gaza.
A 30 year old man was reported on 20 August to have been arrested in Intaka, Matola, Maputo Province for raping two young boys.
A 30 year old man was reported on 20 August to have been arrested in Intaka, Matola, Maputo Province for raping two young boys.

Zimbabwe's Foreign Affairs and International Trade Minister Sibusiso Moyo on 18 August said that the decisions of the Southern African Development Community regarding the insurgency in Cabo Delgado would form Zimbabwe's own decision on whether to intervene militarily in Mozambique or not.  While the SADC did discuss the insurgency at a recent summit, no clear actions to counter the insurgency were announced at this event.

Mozambican police on 09 August reportedly discovered 7 shotguns and 2 pistols in the Sommershield neighborhood of Maputo along with 52 combined rounds of ammunition.  The criminals in possession of these weapons reportedly abandoned them when they became aware of a police patrol in the area.
Mozambique on 18 August was reported to have signed the nuclear ban treaty, becoming the 83rd country to agree to "comprehensively ban" nuclear weapons.

Mozambique on 21 August reported 80 new COVID-19 cases, bringing the nationwide total number of cases to 3,195 and 20 deaths.  37 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 20 in Maputo province, 9 in Cabo Delgado, 9 in Nampula, and 3 in Gaza. 1 in Manica, and 1 in Tete.

The Mozambican Ministry of the Interior was reported on 20 August to have scrapped a new regulation that would require anyone travelling in or out of Mozambique by air to apply for authorization through the Ministry of the Interior.  The Ministry had said the move was an anti-COVID measure, but the move was widely criticized as unconstitutional.  The Ministry then on Thursday afternoon released a statement saying citizens would not need authorization to enter or leave Mozambique, and that foreigners, while still needing a valid entry visa or residence permit, would not require permission to exit the country.

Mozambican customs officials on 21 August were reported to have seized 650 boxes of skin lotion and 200 boxes of alcohol and gel in an operation in Pemba.  The cosmetics had not been properly declared, and were imported from Tanzania vis a truck that entered at the Negomano border.  No arrests have yet been reported in conjunction with this incident.

Mozambique on 20 August prohibited the importing of cattle, pigs, goats, and sheep for rearing and slaughtering from neighboring Malawi after an outbreak of foot and mouth disease in Chikwawa District, Malawi that was reported in early June

384 members of the RENAMO general staff were demobilized in the Serra da Gorongosa area on 20 August, local media reported.  Those demobilized were reportedly part of a "select group of officers" that had served directly under former RENAMO chief Afonso Dhlakama.  Since the resumption of the DDR process on 04 June, over 520 guerillas have been demobilized - or about 10% of the total 5,000 or so fighters the group still claims to have under arms.  RENAMO secretary General Andre Magibire counselled those being demobilized not to again take up arms, warning that any who do return to the bush would not be eligible for a blanket amnesty agree to in 2019 for all those demobilizing.
Construction on Xai Xai Airport has been delayed by at least 5 months as Chinese experts are currently unable to travel to the site, officials said on 21 August.

More than 300  internally displaced people from the conflict in Cabo Delgado were reported on 19 August to have recently arrived in Zambezia in the districts of Alto Molocue, Gurue, Namacurra, Milange, Mocuba, and Nicoadala.
column15: Alto Molocue, Gurue, Namacurra, Milange, Mocuba and Nicoadal Districts

column4: 9 government employees were reported on 20 August to have been arrested for smuggling wood in Pemba.  The smuggled timber was previously seized on 11 August, and had been destined for China.  Authorities said more arrests may be made in the coming days.

President Nyusi was reported on 21 August to have enacted the newly passed Disaster Management and Reduction Act, which gives the government special powers without the need to declare a state of emergency.

President Filipe Nyusi announced on 20 August that the government plans to introduce an electronic visa system to facilitate the entry of foreign nationals from any country into Mozambique. The electronic visa system aims to reduce the waiting time for visas, as well as increase the flow of tourists. This would also aid the country in recovering from the Coronavirus restrictive measures.

On 23 August, Mozambican health authorities announced 109 new Coronavirus cases across the country. These include 47 cases from Maputo city, 17 in Matola city, 9 in Namaacha district, 5 in Moamba, 3 in Boane, 2 in Marracuene, 2 in Matutuine,  1 in Manhica, 7 in Pemba, 6 in Nampula province, 2 in Beira, 1 from Niassa, and 1 in Massinga.  This brought the nationwide total number of cases to 3,304, with 20 deaths.

A report on 24 August indicated that the National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) had raided the home of Ivone Soares, a known parliamentary deputy for Renamo, on 9 July. The house search was conducted by at least 5 SERNIC officers using a search warrant issued by the Maputo City Court. 15 other SERNIC officers also surrounded the house. Soares was accused of conspiracy against state security and the officers were reported to be searching for documents and evidence which could be used against her. The raid led to the seizure of computers, mobile phones, cameras, notebooks, and Soares' 3 passports. Back in January, Soares was  questioned by one of the assistant attorney-generals, Amabelia Chuquela, about her reported financial support for the Renamo Military Junta, a dissident Renamo faction. It remains unknown as to who ordered the search, and the Attorney General's office had stated that it knew nothing about the operation.

Local media reported on 24 August that Total has signed a memorandum of agreement with the Mozambican government with regards to the security of the Mozambique LNG project in the Afungi site and its broader areas of operations. As part of the agreement, security measures around the LNG site will be bolstered in order to better protect the site from Cabo Delgado's growing insurgency.  Total will provide funding, logistical support, including land and air resources as well as technology to the Mozambican government, who will increase its security force presence in the area.  The agreement does expose Total and its partners to deeper entrenchment and involvement in local politics, and exposes the company to further scrutiny and possible reputational damage via security force execesses.

Unknown assailants set fire to the office of the Canal de Mozambique media outlet on the night of 23 August at around 8pm.  The arsonists allegedly broke into the journal's office, doused it in gasoline, and set it on fire.  Another source reported a molotov cocktail was used in the attack. No injuries were reported in this attack. This independent media outlet has often clashes with the government over the exposure of corruption.  Canal de Mozambique's executive editor after the incident said his outlet would "not bow down in the face of fire" and called the incident a "terrorist attack", also saying the paper would not stop its work.
Social media sources reported that local journalist Armando Nenane was arrested by police on 23 August.
Eight people were killed and two seriously injured on 23 August in a car accident in the Matola Rio area of Maputo city at around 5:30 am in an "illegal overtaking" incident.

91 new COVID cases were reported on 23 August in Mozambique, bringing the total number of cases to 3,395 countrywide along with 20 deaths.  Maputo City had 39 new cases, 31 were reported in Inhambane, 9 in Maputo province, 7 in Sofala, 2 in Manica, 2 in Nampula, and 2 in Zambezia.

Fitch Solutions on 23 August said that Mozambique was likely to experience a growth rate of 0.2% in 2020, and that the country would be the only nation in Southern Africa to avoid a recession this year.
IDPs continued to arrive in Mueda on 23 August, local media reported, fleeing from insurgents' recent takeover of Mocimboa da Praia.

Significant price increases have been reported for basic commodities such as rice, sugar, and wheat recently in Palma town, after insurgents recently captured Mocimboa da Praia.  Large numbers of refugees are also present in and around the town, having fled fighting further south.

A group of children on Sunday discovered at least 3 military uniforms and other military equipment in the Rovuma neighborhood of Mueda.  Local media reported this equipment was believed to have been left behind by soldiers who had deserted an army detachment in the town.

Five people, a grandmother and her 4 grand daughters, were killed in an arson attack in Diogo, Inhangoma District of Tete province on Sunday night.  Unidentified assailants at around 9pm reportedly locked the door of the house before setting it on fire for unknown reasons.

A British court has set a new hearing date for the "Hidden Debts" case for January 2021.  Former President Armando Guebuza is listed among the defendants, the first time the former president will be tried in relation to the case in any court.

RENAMO and other opposition political parties on 24 August called the arson attack on a media outlet in Maputo a "serious injury to democracy".  RENAMO chief Ossufo Momade called for the attack to "not go unpunished" like in other attacks on journalists in the country.

President Nyusi on 23 August condemned an attack by unidentified persons on the office of Canal de Mozambique, and said he had ordered an investigation into the attack in order to "bring the perpetrators" to justice.

240,000 people are now displaced across Cabo Delgado, Nampula, Niassa, and Zambezia due to the ongoing Cabo Delgado insurgency.  Over 227,000 people are displaced in Cabo Delgado itself, while over 7,500 are displaced into Nampula. Over 46,000 people are displaced in Pemba District alone.  The UN recently launched an appeal for $103 million, partially to support Cabo Delgado's displaced population.
Mozambican government officials said on 24 August that Mozambican income from tourism and cultural establishments had been reduced by 95% due to the ongoing COVID pandemic.

A suspected insurgent attack reportedly occurred in Quissanga District at around 12:30 on 25 August.  Insurgents reportedly raided 13 Outubro village along the N380 road.  This is the first reported insurgent attack in Cabo Delgado in several days after the recent fall of Mocimboa da Praia.

Polytechnic Institute of Maputo conducted a testing of all their students after 12 students tested positive for COVID on 24 August. 9 of those positive cases were reported in the professional internship program.
50 tons of relief goods were donated by the first lady of Mozambique to around 3,000 displaced persons in the 3 de Fevereiro CS of Metuge on 25 August.

Mozambique Airlines (LAM) announced the resumption of their weekly flights between Maputo and Lisbon on 25 August. LAM director-general, Po Jorge, stated that they later intend to resume flights to India, China and Brazil. The flights between Maputo and Lisbon will use leased Airbuses A330-300 from Hi-fly, a Portuguese company.

Poachers are believed to be active along the Zimbabwe-South Africa border.  Three lions were recently discovered poisoned with cyanide on the Zimbabwean side of Gonarezhou National Park.  5 men, reportedly Mozambican nationals, were later arrested in connection with the incident. A Zimbabwean official said that there is a "thriving lion bones and body parts market in Mozambique" driving poaching in the park.

column4: Zimbabwean security forces over the weekend were reported to have arrested 5 Mozambican nationals along the Zimbabwean - Mozambique border in Gonarezhou National Park on charges of poaching after 3 lions in the area were poisoned.

column4: The US Embassy and British High Commission on 24 August condemned the 23 August Canal de Mozambique arson attack, saying the incident "impacts the state of freedom of speech and freedom of the press in Mozambique".

Mozambique on 24 August reported 45 new cases of COVID-19 nationwide, along with 1 additional death.  This brings the total number of cases in the country to 3,440 with 21 deaths.  12 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 12 in Cabo Delgado, 8 in Maputo, 8 in Nampula, 4 in Tete, and 1 in Inhambane.

Two companies were reported on 24 August to be illegally mining gold in the Ntulo area of Niassa Province.  A local media outlet who sent reporters to investigate this operation said that despite these operations being illegal, Mozambican police were protecting the mining sites.  The local outlet reported that these mines did not have any of the prerequisite licenses to conduct mining, and that Chinese nationals were reportedly in charge of operations at these sites.

Insurgents reportedly remain in control of Mocimboa da Praia town, two weeks after initially capturing the town after several days of battle with Mozambican military units.  While the Mozambican military has been reported to have surrounded the town, no new fighting has been reported iin the area for several days as of 25 August.

Officials in Nampula report that despite the fact that 28 higher and technical institutions have been given permission to re-open in the province, very few students have returned to these schools, fearing COVID-19.
A bus was reported to have caught fire due to a short circuit in Ribaue District of Nampula on the afternoon of 25 August.  No injuries were reported.

Marine traffic continues to avoid Mocimboa da Praia port as of 25 August, another indication that insurgents continue to hold the town.  Marine traffic off the Cabo Delgado coast currently travels from Palma to Pemba and beyond but continues to stay outside of the Quirimbas Islands.

The National Migration service from 08-14 August refused entry to 25 foreign citizens who lacked entry visas.  Immigration officials also said that during this same period, 138 illegal immigrants were repatriated to their countries, of these 138, 132 were Malawian nationals.

UNICEF Mozambique said in Nampula it is currently supporting 14,400 Cabo Delgado residents displaced by the ongoing Cabo Delgado insurgency.  This is nearly twice the 7,500 Cabo Delgado IDPs recently reported to be present in Nampula.
3 people on 25 August were arrested in possession of dog meat in Canongola, Tete, local media reported.

68 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 26 August, bringing the nationwide total cases to 3,508 with 21 deaths.  41 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 9 in Gaza, 8 in Cabo Delgado, 3 in Tete, 3 in Manica, 3 in Maputo, and 1 in Zambezia.

Local media reported on 25 August that a local businessman in Lichinga on the night of 12 August had been abducted and murdered by unidentified assailants.  The man's body was reportedly later found in Majune District.  The businessman targeted in this abduction and murder was reportedly involved in the transport sector between Tanzania and Niassa.

The Directorate of Civil Identification on 25 August shut down all operations after a positive COVID case among the directorate's employees was reported.  The infected person was diagnosed on Monday, local media reported.

The Mozambican Ministry of Mineral Resources and Energy issued a warning to mining companies in Niassa that their production license may be revoked if the companies are not able to implement their production plans. The warning was issued during the visit of the Ministry General Inspector, Obede Matine, in Cuamba district in regard to restructuring small-scale mining. Matine stated that licensed companies are not complying with the plans they have presented to the government in obtaining their license, which causes illegal miners to conduct their operations.

Sources reported that veterans of the Mozambican military living in the Palma area are being armed as part of additional security measures to secure Palma and the Afungi Peninsula from the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

The Police of the Republic of Mozambique released a report on 26 August, stating that police arrested 201 individuals and seized 55 motorcycles, 14 bicycles, and four vehicles for violating the restrictions imposed during the state of emergency over the past week in the country.

The Ministry of Culture and Tourism announced on 26 August, the cancellation of the 2020 Maputo International Fair due to COVID pandemic. The Maputo International Fair was scheduled for October but has affected the tourism sector making it difficult to hold the fair.

Malawian police in the border town of Dedza on 26 August were reported to have arrested two members of a human trafficking ring and rescued 31 trafficked people who were being taken to Mozambique.  Those rescued included 17 children.  Traffickers were caught attempting to cross the border into Mozambique with their victims in the Dzalanyama forest area.  The victims reportedly were to be used for cheap Labour in Mozambique.

Malawian police in the border town of Dedza on 26 August were reported to have arrested two members of a human trafficking ring and rescued 31 trafficked people who were being taken to Mozambique.  Those rescued included 17 children.  Traffickers were caught attempting to cross the border into Mozambique with their victims in the Dzalanyama forest area.  The victims reportedly were to be used for cheap Labour in Mozambique.

A Mozambican explosives factory in Beira that was the final destination of a large order of ammonium nitrate that exploded in Beirut on 04 August is, according to a recent investigation, "part of a network of companies investigated in the past for illegal arms trafficking and supplying explosives to terrorists".  The factory is reportedly owned by the family of a Portuguese businessman previously investigated for allegedly supplying explosives used in the Madrid train bombings of 2004.  In 2005, the company's warehouses in Spain were raided and 785 kgs of explosives were seized from these locations.  The company also has links to President Nyusi's family.

ExxonMobil on 26 August announced that the company would provide a $50,000 grant to supporting displaced persons across Cabo Delgado.  The company said this money will primarily go to providing 20,000 meals a day for the displaced in the province, and will support programs designed to establish livelihood programs to promote income generation, to introduce self-sufficiency mechanisms, and to "implement a buffer zone" that will allow the displaced to return to their homes once security is restored throughout the province.

The bodies of a woman and her granddaughter were discovered on 21 August outside of Macomia town.  The two, who had been displaced from Mucojo AP, had gone out the day before to gather food.  The identity of their killers remains unknown.
7 soldiers on 15 August were reported to have raped a woman in Machova along the N380 road, just outside of Macomia.
Several Mozambican soldiers on 16 August assaulted a women in the Macomia neighborhood of Nanga A.

Macomia's District Administrator returned to the town on 20 August from Pemba after local residents pleaded with him to return to the town after several attacks by soldiers on civilians in the area were reported.  Upon his return, he called on local residents not to leave Macomia, saying the government would protect the town from the insurgency.

Farmers in Bilibiza have reportedly returned to their fields, with insurgents now seemingly no longer in control of the town.  Civilians are also reportedly returning to the towns of Cagembe, Tororo, Tapara, Bem vindo, and Ntessa, indicating insurgents are largely inactive in Quissanga District.  ADPP Junction was also reported to once again be largely secure - though an insurgent attack was reported in the area on 25 August.

The towns of Quissanga, Mahate, and Tandanhangue in Quissanga District remain largely deserted, with insurgents still reportedly within the vicinity of Quissanga town, media reports said on 26 August.
Insurgents on 25 August were reported to have attacked Ilha Mechanga off the Mocimboa da Praia coast, setting fire to several huts on the village  No further details are currently available.

Informal sellers are reported to be gradually re-occupying informal stalls in Maputo in the capital's downtown area.  This comes after operations earlier this year by police to clear out informal sellers from Maputo's streets and could trigger renewed police operations to clear the sellers once again.

South Africa's Hawks Directorate which investigates "priority crimes", is reportedly investigating a number of South African nationals' links to the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  At least one South African national, Mohammed Suliman, is believed to have died fighting for the insurgency.  The Directorate believes as many as 100 South African nationals could be in Mozambique fighting for the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

The continued outbreak of Foot-and-mouth disease has caused a continued suspension of the import of meat to Maputo, causing a meat supply shortage in the capital.  The suspension of import began last week as oxen, goats and pigs were restricted to the southern regions of the country. Magude was the epicenter of the outbreak and authorities have reported that it would take at least 3 weeks to resolve the outbreak.

The Ministry of Economy and Finance released a report stating that Mozambique has spent 95.5% of its yearly defense budget from January to June 2020. Defense was allocated 10.6 million Meticais and has spent 10.1 million, indicating that the defense sector has no funds to maintain their operations. A growth of 34.4% compared to the similar period last year.  Counter-insurgency operations are almost certainly the cause for this large increase in defense spending.

Mozambican Airports Company lost 22 million USD in profits due to the cancellation of flights and staff reduction caused by the COVID pandemic on 26 August. A local official stated that the government is preparing measures to gradually resume operations to make up for the lost profits.

Insurgents reportedly beheaded seven men on 21 August in an attack on Ilha Mionge/Nhonge and kidnapped 10 people in the attack.   Insurgents also looted the village, and loaded stolen goods onto 5 boats before sailing back to the mainland.

Insurgents reportedly beheaded seven men on 21 August in an attack on Ilha Mionge/Nhonge and kidnapped 10 people in the attack.  One source indicated as many as 20 people were abducted in this attack.

The Niassa Provincial Migration Services reopened border crossing points to Malawi and Tanzania on 27 August, as part of the issued Presidential Decree last week. Matchedje, Mandimba, and Entre-Lagos crossings were reopened as part of the first phase of the reopening. In addition, Provincial Migration Services Spokesman, Almeida Metenge, stated that the facility also continued to issue documents for foreigners residing in the country.

640 religious sites reopened and continued their services as part of the easing of COVID restrictions in Nampula province on 27 August. The religious sites are being inspected and monitored by the Health and National Inspection of Economic Activities personnel.

82 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 26 August, bringing the nationwide total cases to 3,590. The total deaths remain at 21. The new cases are distributed among Maputo 3, Nampula 1, Tete, 1, Sofala 15, Gaza 1, and Maputo City 61.  102 cases have been diagnosed in the past 48 hours in Maputo City.

The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and its partners announced on 27 August, that they will provide $6.6 million for projects assisting around 200,000 locals in Sofala and Manica provinces who were affected by the 2019 Cyclone Idai.

Police arrested a suspect in possession of an AK47, a Makarov pistol, and six magazines of ammunition after disembarking a bus at a terminal near Nagi Investment OS, west Nampula City. The suspect was coming from Cabo Delgado.

Locals gathered outside a police command post protesting against the police assault on a civilian for not wearing a mask in Lugela at around 18:00 on 26 August. Police reportedly fire warning shots after the locals vandalized the command post. A protesters was killed, and four others were injured.
Police reported on 27 August, that four individuals belonging to the same family were arrested after police found an air pressurized pistol inside their vehicle in Matola.

Police reported that three suspects were arrested for illegal weapons possession in Sao Damasso, Matola. Two of the suspects were found with a of a Walter type pistol while the other suspect was in possession of an air pressurized pistol.

A Mozambican military source on 27 August confirmed that insurgents continue to hold Mocimboa da Praia town, also saying that many military units had retreated from the MDP area after the town fell on the night of the 11th of August.  The source also said casualties were still unclear, but that the military had sustained significant losses.

A group of families who had been severely impacted by Cyclone Idai on 27 August held a protest outside the office and official residence of the Governor of Sofala, calling promised subsidies to be paid to them.  These families say that funds meant to be paid to them as part of Cyclone relief efforts have been withheld for some months.  Officials reportedly reacted quickly to these demonstrations and released 3 months worth of payments to beneficiaries of the Cyclone relief payments program.
A thief on 27 August was killed by a lynch mob in Erati District after the man was accused of breaking into a local residence.  A video posted online showed the man's corpse on fire.

Local sources reported that security forces on the night of 24 August in Mavuco, Moma District, Nampula entered the town with the intention of "extorting foreign citizens" who work as miners in the area.  One local resident was killed by these security force members in unclear circumstances, while they also seized one vehicle in the area.

The Islamic State in its al Naba magazine on 27 August published photos of insurgent fighters in Mocimboa da Praia (MDP), also saying that in capturing the town, insurgents had captured a large quantity of weapons, ammunition, and money while the property of "Christians" had been burned in the city.  The magazine also claimed that 130 government troops were killed in the attack on the port. The photos clearly also indicated the IS controlled all of the port town.   This was the first claim of the MDP attack by the Islamic State.  Exxon and Total's latest dealings with the Mozambican government were also mentioned in IS's magazine.

Sources on 27 August said that Mozambican security forces had killed as many as 100 civilians in operations in August in Cabo Delgado so far.  This included an incident on 13 August previously reported by Aldebaran that 40 civilians had been killed by men dressed in military uniforms off the Mocimboa da Praia coast, though these uniformed men were never conclusively identified.

Local sources indicated on 27 August that some Mozambican military units deployed to Cabo Delgado had not received extra pay they had been promised for serving in the area, as the government had promised them.  Soldiers in Cabo Delgado on multiple occasions have been reported to not be paid their salaries on time, or to have received extra stipends they were meant to receive as hazard pay.

Officials at Mozambican fisheries are on high alert after an outbreak in July in Malawi of the fish disease epizootic ulcerative syndrome (EUS) which can devastate fish populations.  The disease could easily spread into Mozambique via Malawian waterways.

The National Institute of Health on 28 August said that it expected COVID-19 to continue to impact Mozambique "throughout the year 2021", also saying Mozambicans should continue to take preventative measures to slow the spread of the virus.

Mozambican authorities on 27 August reported 61 new cases of COVID in the country.  33 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 12 in Maputo, 7 in Beira, 5 in Nampula, 2 in Chimoio, 1 in Gaza, and 1 in Zambezia.  The death toll stands at 21.  971 cases are currently active in Maputo City - or about 58% of the known total active cases in the country.

Former President Armando Guebuza on 27 August said in an interview that the country did not achieve independence "to burn newspapers", condemning the attack over the weekend on Canal de Mozambique's offices in Maputo.  Guebuza called the attack akin to taking Mozambique back to "a time when the country was not free".  Guebuza's strong criticism of the attack was notable as it can be viewed as a veiled rebuke of the FRELIMO government and its supporters, as pro-government elements are suspected of being behind the attack.  Guebuza has at times been at odds with the government of his successor President Nyusi, and is likely continue to openly criticize the government.

The Mocimboa da Praia - Palma road remains closed from the village of Quelimane south to MDP town as insurgents continue to control MDP and parts of the surrounding countryside.  The road will remain closed off by security forces until MDP is retaken from insurgent control.

The N380 road between Awasse and Mocimboa da Praia remains closed as insurgents continue to control MDP and parts of the surrounding countryside.  The road will remain closed off by security forces until MDP is retaken from insurgent control.
