column4: A media outlet in Maputo on 27 August reported that the majority of the capital's residents are not obeying anti-COVID measures.  Specifically, few people are wearing masks or practicing social distancing.  The announcement of the phased relaxing of restrictions reportedly led to most city residents disregarding these measures almost entirely.  Maputo has the largest number of COVID cases - 971 - of any of the country's provinces, a figure which represents nearly 60% of all confirmed cases in the country.

Local media in Nampula reported that the municipal council of Nampula city had made illicit payments to Abiba Aba, a RENAMO provincial delegate.  The mayor's office has denied these claims, saying that it had paid some funds to Aba as part of a legitimate transaction, while it was investigating other claims of illicit payments.

Two Mozambican officials on 28 August told a media outlet that conditions among displaced persons in reception centers in Cabo Delgado are very poor.  One official called conditions "deplorable" while another said that there is a serious lack of food and shelter at these centers.  More than 250,000 people have been displaced by the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado.
Insurgents on the night of 27 August reportedly attacked military positions in Awasse village.  No information on casualties is currently available.

Mozambican security forces in Pemba on 12 August at a bus stop in the city were reported to have detained a Mozambican national suspected of being a member of the Cabo Delgado insurgency in possession of 5 AK-47s as well as six military uniforms.  Authorities suspect the man may have been planning an attack in Pemba.  The man also carried "two strange folders".  The detained man denied he was a member of the Cabo Delgado insurgency and instead said the folders had belonged to his cousin, who he was to deliver them to in Pemba.  The man was presented to the press on Thursday, 27 August.

A crowd of hundreds of people was reported on 28 August to have gathered in front of the Sofala provincial government building, not adhering to social distancing measures in order to receive benefits for the victims of Cyclone Idai.  Sources later reported those gathered were protesting against the suspension of subsidy payments to Cyclone Idai victims.  Protests against these suspensions of payments were reported in Beira also on Wednesday and Thursday.

Mozambican Minister of the Interior Amade Miquidade said on 28 August that insurgents are mixed in with the population of Cabo Delgado, saying this fact meant the fight against the insurgents "must be done with great caution".  Notably, Miquidade also said that journalists were free to go to Cabo Delgado, saying there was stability in the province that the media should go and observe for themselves.  This quasi-invitation for journalists to report on Cabo Delgado is significant as for years the Mozambican government has actively stifled journalists attempting to report on the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

Mozambique's Minister for Mineral Resources and Energy Max Tonela said on 26 August that the country was in "no hurry" to launch a sixth oil and gas exploration licensing round.  The government had previously planned to launch this latest round in 2020 before the COVID pandemic began.  Mozambique's 5th licensing round was closed in June 2015, and the fifth round will likely be concluded before 2024.

Security forces in Pemba said on 28 August that they had recently shut down a gang of black market gem dealers which involved a number of Thai nationals.  Several individuals were arrested in this operation, while 15 kgs of precious stones, including large quantities of rubies, as well as over 300,000 meticais, computers, cell phones, and  other material used to smuggle precious stones.  Officers said that their is evidence that Pemba Airport employees had facilitated the group's activities in the past.

Security forces in Pemba said on 28 August that they had recently shut down a gang of black market gem dealers which involved a number of Thai nationals.  Several individuals were arrested in this operation, while 15 kgs of precious stones, including large quantities of rubies, as well as over 300,000 meticais, computers, cell phones, and  other material used to smuggle precious stones.  Officers said that their is evidence that Pemba Airport employees had facilitated the group's activities in the past.

Security forces in Pemba said on 28 August that they had recently shut down a gang of black market gem dealers which involved a number of Thai nationals.  Several individuals were arrested in this operation, while 15 kgs of precious stones, including large quantities of rubies, as well as over 300,000 meticais, computers, cell phones, and  other material used to smuggle precious stones.  Officers said that their is evidence that Pemba Airport employees had facilitated the group's activities in the past.   Sources later reported 3 Thai nationals were arrested in this operation.

Pemba Municipal Council announced that there are no land plots to allot for the requested temporary housing by displaced teachers on 28 August. The teachers previously fled their residences due insurgent attacks. Over 250,000 people have been displaced by the ongoing Cabo Delgado insurgency.

The president of the Mozambican Football Federation, Feizal Sidat, has tested for Covid-19, the organization has announced after receiving the results of his second test on 28 August. Sidat reportedly fell on 23 August upon his return from Maputo and conducted his first COVID-19 test, which tested negative. A follow-up test showed Sidat was positive for the virus.
Maputo Province Judicial Court sentenced a criminal charged with sexual assault with maximum imprisonment of 24 years on 28 August. The criminal previously sexually assaulted a child last 2019.

The National Institute of Land Transport recorded 392 deaths as a result of the road accidents in the 1st half of 2020. The number of fatalities was less compared to the previous year according to National Institute of Land Transport spokesman, Jorge Muiambo.
The President of the Republic, Filipe Nyusi, inaugurated the opening of the newly finished Nampula-Nametil Road  on the afternoon of 28 August, which is meant to de-congest Nampula city.

A magnitude 4.5 earthquake occurred in Caia, Sofala, around 06:06 on the morning of 30 August. No significant damage or casualties were reported as a result of this incident. The tremors were also felt in Chemba, Maringue, Cheringoma, Marromeu, Mutarara, Morrumbala, and Mopeia.
A 2-vehicle collision involving a heavy truck and a passenger vehicle killed 5 people and wounded 5 others in Kilometer 18, Tete, on the night of 28 August.

SERNIC agents arrested a security agent in Massinga on 28 August for faking his own death to evade arrest in relation to a theft which occurred on 3 August. According to local media, the suspect attempted to steal a TV set at a tourist complex, but was prevented by security guards which led to a violent confrontation between them. The suspect then attacked the security guard using a machete, injuring him. He then faked his own death by obtaining a death certificate which his wife presented to his employer and the police. The death certificate led to further investigations which led to the arrest of the suspect.

SERNIC agents arrested a security agent in Massinga on 28 August for faking his own death to evade arrest in relation to a theft which occurred on 3 August. According to local media, the suspect attempted to steal a TV set at a tourist complex, but was prevented by security guards which led to a violent confrontation between them. The suspect then attacked the security guard using a machete, injuring him. He then faked his own death by obtaining a death certificate which his wife presented to his employer and the police. The death certificate led to further investigations which led to the arrest of the suspect.

Mozambique recorded 61 new Coronavirus cases across the country on 30 August. These include 30 from Maputo city, 12 from Cabo Delgado, 9 from Maputo province, and 6 from Nampula.  One additional fatality was also reported.  3821 total cases have now been reported in the country, along with 23 deaths.

63 Coronavirus cases and 1 death were recorded in Mozambique on 29 August. 35 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 19 in Maputo, 4 in Cabo Delgado, 2 in Sofala, 1 in Gaza, 1 in Nampula, and 1 in Zambezia.  This raised the nationwide total number of cases to 3,760, with 22 deaths.

On the morning of 31 August, President Filipe Nyusi launched the Integrated Development Agency of the North (ADIN) in Pemba. ADIN is a public institution formed  in March which will provide employment opportunities in Northern Mozambique.  The agency will provide services, training, and technical assistance to create opportunities for employment, including self-employment, focusing on Cabo Delgado though also serving Niassa, Zambezia, and Nampula.  The new agency is part of the government's attempt to counter the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

Government security forces repelled an insurgent attack in Miangalewa area on 29 August. Local media reported that fighting took place between 0750 to 815 hrs after a military convoy of more than 300 troops (primarily members of the police force's Rapid Response Unit) entered the village, which was held by a force of around 100 insurgents.  After brief clashes, insurgents retreated from the area.  South African private military contractors also reportedly provided support to government forces in these clashes.  Casualties in these clashes are still not known.  Government forces were sent as reinforcements from Pemba to Mueda, and were able to proceed to Mueda after these clashes.
Recently graduated recruits arrived in Mueda from Pemba as reinforcements on 29 August. The troops also repelled an attack in the Miangalewa area while en route to Mueda.

Suspected RENAMO dissidents attacked a bus owned by the Correias de Mozambique postal service in the early morning hours between Save village and Muxungue, along the N1 road near the river crossing, on 30 August. The attack left the driver wounded.  This was the first attack along this section of the N1 road by suspected RENAMO dissidents since these attacks began in 2019, though attacks did occur in this area multiple times during the 2012-2016 RENAMO insurgency.
Counter-terrorism operations took place in the Quissanga area on 30 August. This comes as displaced individuals have arrived in the Paquitequete area of Pemba.

Mozambican military units on 30 August were reported to have begun a counter-offensive against insurgents in Mocimboa da Praia District, approaching Awasse village, where clashes with insurgents were reported.  No information on casualties is available at this time.

48 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 28 August.  This included 33 new cases in Maputo City, 8 in Maputo, 2 in Cabo Delgado, 1 in Nampula, 1 in Zambezia, and 1 in Inhambane.  This brought the nationwide total number of cases to 3,697, with 21 deaths.

Clashes were reported in Awasse between insurgents and Mozambican military units on 28 August between 0800 to 1400hrs.  No information regarding casualties were reported.  The village has reportedly been completely deserted by its civilian population.

President Nyusi on 31 August held a highly publicized meeting with Bishop of Pemba Luiz Fernando Lisboa where they reportedly discussed the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  The meeting came after government supporters recently accused Lisboa of being a "logistician" for the insurgency, and after Pope Francis publicly expressed support for Lisboa.
Unconfirmed reports on 31 August indicated that Mozambican military units retook the village of Awasse from insurgents after clashes.

A study released on 31 August indicated that about 3.79% of Maputo residents have COVID-19 antibodies.  The survey was carried out in 4717 random households throughout the city, and found that residents of Nlamanculo, Kamabukwana, and Katembe had the highest rates of antibodies, with at least 4.48% of people in these areas possessing them.  The survey also showed that 5.22% of market vendors had COVID antibodies, the highest rate of any progression.  If the study's findings are accurate, over 41,000 people in the capital would have had or have COVID-19 so far in the ongoing pandemic.

95 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 31 August, including 54 cases in Maputo, 30 cases in Maputo city, two cases in Gaza, two in Sofala, four in Nampula, one in Niassa, one in Cabo Delgado, and one in Inhambane.  This brought the overall number of cases to 3,916, with 23 deaths.

Mozambican security forces on 28 August  near Pemba intercepted at  two boats carrying 60 people towards Mocimboa da Praia town.  The group claimed they were travelling to fish in waters of MDP and had come from Nampula.  Security forces fired warning shots to stop the boats, and security forces believed the group were recruits for the Cabo Delgado insurgency travelling to join the insurgents.  It is unclear if the 2 boats were merely turned back from Mocimboa da Praia or if the group was detained.

Officials on 30 August in Pemba said they believe that an individual recently arrested on charges of smuggling weapons and other material into Pemba in order to launch insurgent attacks in the city was likely only one of several insurgents smuggling arms into the city.  Officials believe that other weapons "may have entered" the provincial capital and investigations into other possible insurgent activity in the city is ongoing.  Officials also said that the leadership of the insurgency are a mix of Mozambicans, Tanzanians, Somalis, Ugandans, and a small number of South Africans.

A 21-year-old man was  stabbed to death by 5 armed men at his backyard around 20:00 in Dondo, north of Beira, on 30 August. Local sources stated that the victim was attacked with blunt melee weapons and later stabbed to death.

Electricidade de Mozambique maintenance teams completely repaired and restored electrical services to around 50 neighborhoods in Matola on the afternoon of 30 August, after strong winds toppled down several power lines causing power blackouts around 50 neighborhoods in Matola on 29 August.

The president of the Tax Authority, Amélia Muendane, stated that smuggling takes 12.6% of its gross domestic product, and deprives the Tax Authority of over 40% of its budget. The most smuggled products are wood, seafood and precious stones.

Officials implemented the second phase of easing restrictions around Mozambique on 1 September. The second phase will allow the resumption of operations of classes, cinemas, theaters, casinos, gyms, driving schools, and motor sports.

Officials warned on 28 August that child marriages may increase for girls due to the closure of schools as a result of the COVID-19 in Mozambique. NGO officials stated that the girls are socially pressured to be no longer a burden to the family exposing them to a higher risk of untimely marriage.

The Mozambique government is using its 764 million USD from its partners to finance the activities of the Integrated Northern Development Agency (ADIN) on 31 August. ADIN will to provide social assistance to families in Cabo Delgado, Niassa and Nampula provinces and help to create employment opportunities in the north.  The World Bank will reportedly provide as much as $700 million of the total of this amount.
Police arrested a woman for killing a civilian due to a domestic dispute in Marracuence, north of Maputo City at around 01:00 on 1 September.
A car collided with a minibus near Shell area of Nacala Porto on the morning of 1 September. Several civilians were injured.
Police arrested a suspect for murdering a civilian and stealing his property in Tica on 1 September. The suspect claimed that the victim did not pay a debt of 300 Meticais leading to a dispute.
An unknown man assaulted and killed a civilian after the victim reportedly refused to pay a debt of 300 Meticais in Tica on 19 August .

Kenmare Resources suspended all mining operations at a titanium mineral mine in Moma on 31 August, due to the death of an employee who was killed during an accident at the wet concentrator plant during dry mining operations. The victim was reported to be a front-end loader operator.

Local pro-government militias on 27-28 August reportedly warned locals in the Chtunda and Xitaxi areas of Cabo Delgado that a major military operation was imminent in the area, and that they should move to safer areas, including Muidumbe/Namacande town.  This warning came just before a large military convoy on 29 August moved through Miangalewa town and clashed with a group of around 100 insurgents.

President Nyusi on 31 August said that reports that Cabo Delgado was "closed to journalists" were false, but also said the province is a "war zone and it is unpredictable".  Nyusi made this statement after one of his ministers also publicly invited journalists to come to Cabo Delgado to cover developments there.  For several years, the Mozambican government has cracked down on journalists covering the conflict in the province and this may be a sign of the government loosening some restrictions on journalists operating in the country.

President Nyusi on 31 August said that insurgents in Cabo Delgado were part of an "international terrorism network" and called for unity in the fight against the province's insurgents.  Nyusi also said the group had displaced about 250,000 in Cabo Delgado and that fighting the insurgents was an "unprecedented challenge".  The President and his government have more recently spoken increasingly openly regarding the conflict in Cabo Delgado, a marked change from the government's guarded stance earlier in the conflict.

Despite the recent re-opening of churches across Mozambique, restrictions remain in place prohibiting any person over the age of 65 from attending religious services.  Children under 18 are also not allowed to attend services, and no more than 50 people may attend an indoor service at one time.

123 new cases of COVID-19 were reported in Mozambique on 01 September.  These included 49 new cases in Maputo City, 29 in Niassa, 15 in Maputo, 6 in Nampula, 3 in Tete, 3 in Cabo Delgado, 2 in Gaza, and 1 in Inhambane.  There are now a total of 4039 cases in the country, along with 23 deaths.

A vehicle on 13 August carrying arms suspected to be intended for the Cabo Delgado insurgents was reportedly intercepted in the Pemba area.  No further details on this incident are currently available.
On 09 August, 3 suspected insurgents were arrested in the Pemba area, reportedly carrying small arms.  No further details on this incident is currently available.

President Cyril Ramaphosa of South Africa on 31 August said at a virtual press conference that within the Southern African Development Community the issue of the Cabo Delgado insurgency was being "discussed extensively based on briefings by the government of Mozambique".  The SADC at its recent conference expressed support for Mozambique as it faced the insurgency, though stopped short of committing to any kind of military intervention in the country, though this subject has reportedly been discussed behind closed doors.

Pro-government media on 01 September claimed that government troops from 26-29 August in a series of operations in the Mbau area of Mocimboa da Praia had destroyed 5 "terrorist" checkpoints in Cabo Delgado and destroyed 21 huts used by militants, also saying 9 insurgents were killed in these operations with no Mozambican military casualties suffered.  The report also said that a number of insurgents were captured in these operations.

Payments of subsidies to Cyclone Idai victims was reported on 01 September to have resumed after recent protests in Beira over a stoppage in these subsidy payments.  No demonstrations were reported in Beira during the day.

At around 9pm on 31 August, 2 Mozambican police agents were shot in Maputo City along Joaquim Chissano Avenue while parked at a fuel pump, killing one and injuring the other in the foot and hand.  The group of four unidentified assailants then fled the scene in a Toyota Auris. The two officers were approaching the vehicle after becoming suspicious of the occupants before the assailants opened fire.

Police officers in Nampula Province on 24 August were reported to have arrested a group of five banking and education sector employees of Rapale District on charges of theft of 18 million meticais via fraud.  The group reportedly opened more than 40 fake bank accounts to phantom employees.  Police officials say they believe more people were involved in this scheme and are being sought by the authorities.

69,000 needy families in Maputo Province are meant to begin receiving 1500 meticais a month (just over $20) to mitigate the impact of COVID-19.  The registration process for this stipend has reportedly caused some unrest in parts of Matola over arguments over who is and who is not included in the scheme.  No further details on this unrest is currently available.

Documents recently revealed that were sent to Mozambican authorities in May show that Credit Suisse intends to add President Nyusi as a witness in the Hidden Debts Case, calling on Nyusi to "account for his irregularities" in relation to accounts linked to the case.  The Mozambican government has reportedly not responded to this letter.  In this case before British courts, Mozambique is attempting to annul a debt of $622 million of a state-owned company to Credit Suisse.  Many of Mozambique's most powerful politicians, including Nyusi and former President Armando Guebuza, have been accused of corruption and linked to this case.

Sources reported 3 headless bodies were discovered on 31 August in the Nanjua area of Ancuabe District on 31 August.  If confirmed, this would be the first attack in this area by insurgents during the ongoing conflict in Cabo Delgado.  This attack is significantly outside of the usual insurgent zone of activity in central and north coastal Cabo Delgado.   Unverified conflicting reports later indicated that the Nanjua incident had been part of a criminal feud.

A Mozambican historian, Yusuf Adam, on 01 September said that at least 700 women have been kidnapped by insurgents and are used "as sex slaves and for agriculture" in Cabo Delgado.  Multiple instances of insurgents abducting women in the province have been reported since late 2017.

The US Embassy in Maputo stated that the US government guaranteed to give 42 million USD to assist the Integrated Northern Development Agency (ADIN)in providing social assistance to displaced families in Cabo Delgado, Niassa and Nampula provinces and enable economic opportunities in the northern region of the country.
Mozambican officials on 02 September announced an import ban of fish coming from Malawi in response to an outbreak of epizootic ulcerative syndrome in fishes in Malawi.

SAPO, a subsidiary company of the French Altice telecommunications announced its closure by the end of September in Mozambique and in several other countries on 2 September. The other countries included Angola, Cabo Verde, and East Timor. The closure of the local projects will lead to the continuation of its operations in Portugal.

NGO Ajuda de Desenvolvimento de Povo para Povo and the UNDP launched several agricultural projects to assist 15,000 victims of Cyclone Idai in recovering economically in Mozambique on 2 September.  The 29 million Meticais projects will operate under the Mozambique Recovery Mechanism programme. The NGO officials stated that the project was to promote gender equality, social inclusion, unity, and environmental growth.

Police announced on 2 September that 126 individuals were arrested during the past week as part of daily operations targeting violators of the restrictions placed on the country during the state of emergency in Mozambique. 52 vehicles and 63 motorcycles were seized during the operation.

Three cars, a truck, and two minivans crashed onto each other along the Bobole-Maputo road (Route 1) in Marracuene district, north of Maputo, on the morning of 2 September. 27 civilians were injured in this accident.

An explosive device was discovered in the Mulotane area of Maputo province on 02 September.  The military, who had previously used the area for training purposes, was believed to have left behind the device.

Customs seized 7,000 units of smuggled stereo devices and accessories coming from China at the Port of Beira on 1 September. Custom officials stated that only 1,000 units were reportedly declared for customs clearance.

Vice Minister of the Economy and Finance Carla Alexandra Louveira said on 02 September that subsides to the military for combat in Cabo Delgado, Sofala, and Manica as well as to frontline doctors combating COVID-19 promised by the government in June have yet to be paid.  It is not clear when these subsidies will be paid, though the government use donations from its international partners to make these payments in the coming months.  There have been reports in Cabo Delgado of some unrest among soldiers over the non-payment of these subsidies.

column4: 78 new cases of COVID were reported on 02 September in Mozambique, with 2 new deaths also reported due to the virus.  40 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 24 in Niassa, 7 in Cabo Delgado, 4 in Maputo, 1 in Nampula, 1 in Sofala, and 1 in Inhambane.  4,117 total cases have been reported in the country, along with 25 deaths.

Mozambican police were reported on 02 September to have arrested a South African national who had stolen 55 head of cattle and was attempting to return to South Africa.  The man was part of a gang who had stolen the cattle in Matutuine District.  Two other men involved in the theft escaped from police.

Mozambican police were reported on 02 September to have arrested a South African national who had stolen 55 head of cattle and was attempting to return to South Africa.  The man was part of a gang who had stolen the cattle in Matutuine District.  Two other men involved in the theft escaped from police.

RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo said on 01 September that his group refused to talk to RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade or other top RENAMO leaders, calling them "traitors", while also threatening to "beat FRELIMO".  Nhongo's group has called on the government to agree to a new peace deal with it before his group will disarm.

A police officer was shot and killed on Wednesday in Quelimane by a fellow officer.  The two officers were pursuing a suspect in the Sinacurra neighborhood of Quelimane when the incident occurred.  A police spokesman said the shooting was an accident.  The incident is currently being investigated.

Church officials in Pemba confirmed on 02 September that 2 nuns and 60 congregants present at the church of St. Joseph of Chambery in Mocimboa da Praia when the town was attacked in early August remain missing.  The two nuns are Brazilian nationals, while the 60 congregants are believed to all have been Mozambican nationals.  Church officials lost contact with the church during the battle for the city, and have had no word regarding the two nuns or the congregation since that time.

Police in Xipamanine, Maputo City, were reported on 02 September to have arrested two brothers on human trafficking charges after the two reportedly bought three children from their aunt from Chokwe district of Gaza province.

Large numbers of internally displaced persons, fleeing the ongoing insurgency, have fled to Pangane village in Macomia District in recent weeks.  As many as 5,000 people are now present in the town.  At least 14 passenger boats in recent days have brought refugees to the area.  Communities are fleeing from nearby villages as well as from parts of Mocimboa da Praia District, as well as from islands in the Quirimbas Archipelago where local residents fear insurgent attacks.

Insurgents on or around 17 August stopped a boat transporting refugees from Nhonge / Mionge island to Pemba.  The militants then towed the refugee's boat to shore with a motor boat, and killed the owner of the boat after he refused to allow militants to marry a girl from his family; militants also called the man an apostate.  It was unclear if the other occupants of the boat were allowed to go free after this incident.
A cement truck travelling in the Awasse area on 24 August was fired upon by insurgents.  No casualties were reported in this incident.

The Nampula government on 02 September said that it had submitted a plan to move villages inside the Mecuburi Forest to locations outside of the reserve area, due to illegal logging activities inside of the reserve.

An Ibo District official said on 31 August that there are over 13,000 displaced people due to the ongoing insurgency on Ibo Island, primarily from Quissanga and Macomia Districts.  The official said there are no proper accommodations for these refugees on the island, and that conditions continue to deteriorate on the island due to the downturns in tourism and fishing caused by the insurgency.

3 brothers over the course of 3 months have committed suicide in Mutauanha in Nampula city, sources said on 02 September as part of a property dispute.  The dispute apparently arose after the deaths of the 3 men's parents.  The unusual circumstances of the 3 deaths has drawn a significant amount of local community attention.

The Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWSN) in its projections for food security outcomes in September said that large parts of Gaza, Inhambane, Maputo, and some areas of Sofala, Manica, and Cabo Delgado will experience "crisis" levels of food insecurity.  The network also said that from October 2020 to January 2020, all of  these areas, as well as much of Tete and northern Manica would also experience "crisis" levels of food insecurity.  Much of the food insecurity experienced in the country is trigged by drought, while food insecurity in Cabo Delgado is primarily triggered by the ongoing insurgency.

South African Foreign Minister was reported on 02 September to have told a parliamentary committee that South Africa would provide intelligence support, naval patrols, or even defense forces to support the Mozambican government in the fight against the Cabo Delgado insurgency if Maputo requests this support.  This is perhaps the most public offer of direct military support made by the South African government to date to the Mozambican government.
Police rescued an eight-year-old and arrested a suspect for recruiting children for child labor in Govuro district of Inhambane on 2 September.

International Committee of the Red Cross announced the completion of the largest COVID treatment facility that could accommodate 200 patients in Pemba on 2 September. The facility was reported to be expandable to a 400-patient capacity. Planning Department head of the Cabo Delgado health department stated the healthcare facility was to in preparation for a possible response to the COVID cases.

Families displaced by RENAMO dissident attacks fled to Gondola, northwest of Beira. The families stated that they were forced to flee to the area and other safe places by the rebels without being able to take valuables or any goods. The families also mentioned the lack of essential goods including food and water in Gondola.  Over 3,000 people have reportedly been displaced recently due to RENAMO dissident attacks.

Mozambican Police Association created an inquiry commission and requested clarification on the deaths of the police officers in Maputo and Zambezia on 3 September. AMOPAIP President, Nazário Muenambane, stated that "It does not make sense that agents who guarantee order and public security are murdered in a strange and unclear manner."

90 new COVID cases were reported on 03 September in Mozambique, along with 1 new fatality, bringing the nationwide case total to 4,207 along with 26 deaths.  47 cases were reported in Maputo City, 22 in Niassa, 9 in Maputo, 6 in Nampula, 4 in Sofala, 1 in Tete, and 1 in Manica.  There are 2,800 active cases throughout the country.

Media reports on 03 September said that "busloads" of soldiers had been reported in recent days moving towards Mocimboa da Praia from Pemba, while military sources said it was the military's "priority" to retake the port from insurgents who have held it since 11 August.

Three individuals were missing after a boat transporting excessive cargo sunk due to bad weather in a lagoon in Gaza province on 3 September. The boat operator managed to survive and swim to the edge of the lagoon. A search operation was conducted by local authorities in response to the incident.
A minibus collided with a truck along N1 Road in Marracuene, north of Maputo, on the afternoon of 2 September. A civilian was killed and five others were injured.

Reports from local media on 03 September said that RENAMO commander Joao Muthandi had been killed by other RENAMO members in unclear circumstances in the Mangomonhe area.  One other source indicated that the killing may have been carried out by a FRELIMO death squad.

A young man on 01 September was arrested by security forces in Muambula on terrorism charges and is suspected to be a leading member of the Cabo Delgado insurgent.  The police arrested the man a tip off from locals, who said the man had arrived in the town the night before.

Mozambican Minister of the Interior Amade Miquidade on 02 September said for the second time in less than a week that journalists should cover the conflict in Cabo Delgado and to "continue to write and talk about the terrorist attacks", saying it was important that the full details of what was happening in the province were shared.  President Nyusi also in recent days made similar statements in an apparently coordinated effort to soften the government's stance towards the media in Cabo Delgado.

A survey released on 03 September of 7,692 people  in Quelimane, Zambezia between 24 May - 03 July indicated that some neighborhoods in the city have rates of 7% to 6.7% positive rates for COVID-19 anti-bodies.  Bicycle taxi operators have the highest rates of these anti-bodies at 9.4%.  About 2.5% of those surveyed in the city were positive for COVID-19 antibodies, about the same rate as in Pemba, which would suggest about 7,000 cases in the city to date.
The government was reported on 04 September to have set up a new website for applying for immigration documents.

Total representatives told the Financial Times on 02 September that the Joint Task Force it has set up with the Mozambican Government will be run by the Mozambican Ministries of Defense and Interior.  Total also said that it would train security forces at its sites in Cabo Delgado and would assure the protection of human rights as well as the brining of social and economic benefits for local communities.

Reports on 03 September indicated that community leaders in Mocimboa da Praia District are telling local civilians to leave their homes and journey into Palma District to avoid casualties in an expected government counter-offensive to retake Mocimboa da Praia town.

A train crash was reported in Meconta District on the morning of 04 September at 0430hrs.  Two trains reportedly collided in the area, though no casualties were reported. It will be two days until rail traffic can resume along the Nacala Corridor due to this accident.

A demonstration on 02 September was reported in Beira over the paying out of subsidies to Cyclone Idai victims.  Some of those collecting subsidies claimed others had fraudulently claimed their benefits, while authorities in some cases also reportedly withheld subsidies.

A demonstration on 02 September was reported in Dondo over the paying out of subsidies to Cyclone Idai victims.  Authorities in several case reportedly withheld subsidies from those who had registered for the payments last year, and only paid those who had registered for payments in 2020.
Police on 28 August seized two pistols in the Guava neighborhood of Marracuene District in Maputo; the weapons had been abandoned by unknown suspects.

Mozambique on 04 September reported 58 new COVID-19 cases.  31 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 15 in Maputo, 5 in Tete, 2 in Nampula, 4 in Niassa, and one in Cabo Delgado.  This brought the nationwide total number of cases to 4,265 with 26 deaths.

Six containers containing sand which were meant to contain copper arrived in China in recent days; two similar shipments last month also arrived inn China from Mozambique.  The owner of the containers believes that criminal elements at Nacala port stole the copper and filled the containers with sand before they were shipped.

Local media on 04 September reported tactics utilized by insurgents in Cabo Delgado.  The account says insurgents attacking a village usually arrive between 3-4am and surround a village to prevent any vehicles from fleeing and to prevent any villagers escaping to raise an alarm.   Insurgents then enter the village and divide families, generally then forcibly taking girls between 12-20 and boys between 10-25 with them.  In many cases insurgents then kill (often via decapitation) several adults in the village, including of parents of children and young adults the insurgents intend to abduct.  Insurgents also often kill husbands before abducting wives.  Lastly, insurgent loot and then set fire to the village they have attacked.  This account matches details provided in numerous village attacks in Cabo Delgado in recent years.

IDPS displaced from Cabo Delgado into Nampula province reportedly lack in many cases food and adequate shelter.  There is a significant lack also of reception centers in Nampula for the displaced, and many of those who have been in the province for several months say they are running out of money with no assistance provided by the government.  There are over 15,000 people displaced from Cabo Delgado currently in Nampula.

The Integrated Development Agency of the North was reported on 04 September to have made its first local donations, providing a batch of tractors and bulldozers for the "productive recovery of families affected by terrorist attacks".  The publicizing of this initial donation is part of a wider government outreach program to attempt to win back "hearts and minds" in Cabo Delgado.

Media reporting on 02 September indicated that the South African government does not have funds available to upgrade the current outdated equipment of the South African National Defense Force, and that budget cuts have largely crippled the military's capabilities.  The military is also currently judged to be under strength by the country's Secretary of Defense, while many South African politicians say a "complete overhaul" of the military is needed.  These reports surfaced as momentum has grown for a potential South African military intervention in support of the Mozambican government in Cabo Delgado.

At least 4 military helicopters were reported on the morning of 03 September to have flown from the Pemba area north towards areas impacted by the insurgency.  No further information on this development is currently available.
At around 5pm, a demobilized RENAMO member was reportedly shot dead by assailants in Chibabava District.  The motives behind the attack were not immediately clear.

Shop owners protested against the attempted demolition of their shops as part of a commercial establishment construction in Zona Verde, Maputo , on 5 September. The protesters stated that the construction is illegal and have called for the response of the municipality.

Mozambique recorded 76 Coronavirus cases and 68 recoveries nationwide on 5 Sept. These include 56 cases from Maputo city, 10 from Maputo province, 4 from Beira, 3 from Nampula, 1 from Niassa, 1 from Quelimane, and 1 from Montepuez, Cabo Delgado.

Mozambican Customs foiled the smuggling of 8,600 Kg of crabs at the Nampula Airport on 4 Sept. The crabs were on a plane bound fir Nairobi. Reports state that the owner of the goods did not submit the bank commitment statement.
Authorities foiled the smuggling of prohibited drug from Nairobi via the Nampula Airport on 4 September. The drugs were addressed to Nampula.
Authorities seized 21,000 pieces of smuggled capulanas at the Nampula Airport on 4 Sept. The shipper did not pay the necessary customs fees.

At least 140 RENAMO female members were demobilized and reintegrated at the military base in Vunduzi on 5 September. This demobilization is part of the ongoing DDR process between the Mozambican government and RENAMO, which now resulted in 1,075 guerillas being demobilized.  Up to 5,000 armed RENAMO members will be demobilized as part of this ongoing process.

A local report on 4 September stated that the Malawian police has arrested 2  "recruiters", including a Mozambican and a Malawian, before they crossed the Mancajira border with Mallawi and Mozambique. The suspects were transporting 14 civilians into Mozambique for unknown purposes. Reports state that these civilians were usually promised jobs upon arriving in Mozambique, though the exact nature of these jobs is unknown.  These kinds of "recruitment" schemes are often linked to the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

The Islamic State in Central Africa (ISCAP) claims to have killed and injured 20 Tanzanian soldiers in clashes in Mocimboa da Praia, Cabo Delgado, on 5 Sept. The militant group said fighting occurred at around 1200hrs on 05 September when militants repelled an attack by joint Tanzanian and Mozambican forces who were attempting to recapture the town.  IS also said that several Tanzanian/Mozambican army vehicles were set on fire, and weapons and ammunition captured by the militants.  ISCAP also posted the IDS of at least two Tanzanian nationals claimed to have been seized by the insurgents from the Tanzanian forces. No independent or official sources can verify these claims.  A second unconfirmed source reported that Tanzanian forces had in fact engaged a number of insurgents they had pursued from Tanzanian territory into Mozambique, along the southern banks of the Rovuma River, and that several Tanzanian soldiers were killed in this engagement.  Tanzanian military officials however on 07 September denied the report and said that their troops had not crossed into Mozambique.

On 6 September, Mozambique recorded 103 Coronavirus cases and 1 death. The death was recorded in Maputo city. Meanwhile the new infections include 4 from Cabo Delgado, 2 from Niassa, 1 from Nampula, 2 from Zambezia, 1 from Manica, 4 from Inhambane, 2 from Gaza, 2 from Maputo province, and 85 from Maputo city. 36 people also recovered from the virus.  The national case total now stands at 4,444 with 27 deaths.

Insurgents were reported to have attacked the island of Vamizi off the coast of Palma District in the early morning of 07 September, setting fire to village huts and kidnapping several women.  The attackers arrived just after midnight, and gathered island residents together after morning prayers, reportedly warning island residents to leave the island.  At least one person was also shot dead during the attack after reportedly recognizing one of the insurgents.  This is the first such reported attack on Vamizi, which lies less than 3 miles off the coast of Palma District, near Olumbi village, where insurgents have been previously active, and follows attacks in recent weeks on small islands off the Mocimboa da Praia Coast.

Insurgents were reported to have attacked the island of Vamizi off the coast of Palma District in the early morning of 07 September, setting fire to village huts and kidnapping several women.  The attackers arrived just after midnight, and gathered island residents together after morning prayers, reportedly warning island residents to leave the island.  At least one person was also shot dead during the attack.  This is the first such reported attack on Vamize, which lies less than 3 miles off the coast of Palma District, near Olumbi village, where insurgents have been previously active, and follows attacks in recent weeks on small islands off the Mocimboa da Praia Coast.  Sources later reported insurgents had looted tourist resorts on the island during the raid, and had stolen at least one boat in the attack.  Other sail boats belonging to local were also set on fire during the raid.

President Nyusi on 06 September announced the end of the State of Emergency in Mozambique, to be replaced by a "situation of public calamity" beginning on 07 September.  This is part of new powers given to the president in August to allow the government to put in place emergency measures to confront the COVID-19 pandemic, and the "situation of public calamity" will last indefinitely, unlike the state of emergency, which had to be renewed every 30 days.  Preventative measures in place under the state of emergency will remain in force, including on the wearing of masks and social distancing.  Bars will remain closed, while hours markets may remain open is restricted to 0600hrs to 1700hrs.  Anyone arriving in Mozambique is subject to a 14 day quarantine.  Other reopenings will continue, including of restaurants and of government offices issuing documents.  Passenger flights will resume, but only if other nations also allow flights originating in Mozambique to land in their countries.  University and higher education classes have already resumed, while 12th grade and lower grade schools will resume from 01 October, pending Ministry of Education approval.  The ban on visiting beaches will be lifted on 15 September.  Public and private workplaces are allowed to reopen, but must adhere to government mandates procedures and restrictions.

A document was circulated on 06 September reportedly from the office of the Bishop of Pemba Luiz Fernando Lisboa indicating that two nuns who were reported missing after the capture of Mocimboa da Praia by insurgents had been released by insurgents in unclear circumstances.   The Bishop later said that the two's release had been "secured" after 24 days of captivity, and that some of their 60 congregants had escaped from the area though others remaied in the area.

10 people have died of cholera in September in Montepuez District, local media reported.  Cholera cases have been reported among the local population as well as among IDPs fleeing the insurgency in other parts of the province.

A group of at least 17 young men from the village of Intutupue/Ntutupwe in Ancuabe District are reportedly members of the Cabo Delgado insurgency; some of these young men were released by authorities in Pemba in recent years after charges against them were dismissed due to a lack of evidence.  At least some of these young men returned to the village after being released and then shortly afterwards were reported by their families to have "disappeared" and are believed to have joined the insurgency; all 17 young men are reported to be "missing" from the area.  This report comes after 3 people were beheaded in the Nanjua village area of Ancuabe District in an apparent insurgent attack.  Intutupue is located less than 35 miles from provincial capital Pemba.

The Mozambique government lowered its growth forecast from 1.6% to 0.8% on 26 August, as a result of the COVID pandemic. During the press briefing, the government stated that it has considered approving a resolution for a three-year period medium-term fiscal scenario in which 3.8% growth rate was projected.

Cabo Delgado Insurgents on the night of 07 September attacked the village of Ruea, southwest of Mucojo town, setting fire to several village huts.  No information on casualties is currently available.  Ruea lies within the insurgent's zone of semi-territorial control within Macomia District's Mucojo Administrative Post, and has been targeted in the past by the militants.  One past incident in November 2019 saw one person was killed and part of the village set on fire.  The village in 2019 was also been be a source of recruits for the insurgency, and despite its small size more than 20 young men from Ruea have been reported to have joined the insurgency.

Insurgents on 06 September assaulted the village of Manica in Macomia, west of Mucojo town.  Insurgents in this attack stole chicken, goats, and cattle and set fire to several village huts.  Area residents fled into the nearby woods just before the attack.  Sources later said villagers were taken by surprise by the attack and that area residents had recently been returning to their homes.  Insurgents remained in the village until the morning of 07 September, and the group is likely also responsible for an attack later in the day of the nearby village of Ruea.  No casualties were reported.

113 new COVID-19 cases were reported on 07 September in Mozambique, including 61 in Maputo City, 29 in Maputo, 9 in Sofala, 5 in Cabo Delgado, 5 in Inhambane, 2 in Nampula, 1 in Manica, and 1 in Gaza, bringing the nationwide case total to 4557, with 27 deaths.

The World Food Program on 07 September said that of the 250,000 displaced people in Cabo Delgado, the organization is currently only able to reach 180,000, leaving 70,000 without aid.  Those not reached by aid are in the districts most impacted by the insurgency, where insurgents exercise varying degrees of territorial control.
Security forces arrested three suspects on theft charges after the group reportedly targeted tourists in Machubo of Marracuene on 7 September.
3 suspects were detained by security forces for stealing and selling 20 gas cylinders in Maputo on 8 September.

Officials announced the closure of the National Directorate of Civil Identification (DNIC) branch in Maputo on 8 September after one of its employees tested positive for COVID. The closure was to enable a disinfection team to sterilize the branch. The DNIC spokesman announced the resumption of work the following day.

President Nyusi said in a new speech that "intense fighting" had taken place between Cabo Delgado insurgents and the military on 05 September that resulted in a significant victory for government forces at Awasse, west of Mocimboa da Praia.  Other sources also reported on 08 September that Mozambican military units had retaken the important Awasse crossroads on Saturday. Casualties are currently unknown. Several skirmishes between the military and insurgents took place around Awasse from 27-31 August, though it was unclear in the aftermath of these clashes who controlled the area.  With the town in hand, the government now once again controls this important crossroads of the N380 - the only paved route to Mocimboa da Praia, and will likely attempt a move east towards the villages of Mumu, Ntotwe, and Manilha to fully secure the N380 before launching an assault on MDP itself.

A large number of people fled Vamizi Island in sail boats after it was attacked by insurgents on 07 September.  Several sail boats were reported to have been becalmed and were stranded in the waters just off of Vamizi while insurgents looted island homes.  These IDPs had reportedly intended to sail to Palma District to flee the attack.

Pemba's judicial court has acknowledged that since 2017, 130 defendants accused of links to the Cabo Delgado insurgency have been acquitted due to lack of evidence, compared to just 122 defendants tried and convicted.  Court officials say the reason for the large number of acquittals was due to the courts' inexperience in trying these kinds of cases before late 2017.  Several reports have indicated that at least some of those acquitted have made their way back to join the insurgency.

President Nyusi and RENAMO chief Ossufo Momade on 07 September in separate speeches called for RENAMO dissidents under Mariano Nhongo to join the DDR process and stop fighting.  Momade said that internal differences in the RENAMO party that caused the dissidents to take up arms could be settle peacefully.
A report released by the bank of Mozambique indicates that the Mozambican metical due to weak productivity due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic has depreciated 17.37% so far in 2020 vs the US dollar.

President Nyusi on 07 Sep warned that he would potentially re-impose restrictions in Mozambique if violations of anti-COVID measures continue, saying that he had reports of "unruly" consumption of alcohol as well as a lack of social distancing at beaches.  Nyusi said his government would "watch people for a while longer, and, if this prevails, we will roll back" the relaxation of anti-COVID measures.

A professor in Pemba was reported missing on the night of 07 September; he was later reported to have left behind a suicide note referencing his family's refusal to let him marry a woman.  The man remains missing as of the morning of 08 September.

A nanny was arrested in Maputo City on 08 September for kidnapping two children a week ago.  The women then brought the children to her family in Gaza Province, where they were then this week brought back from by police to their family.  There is some speculation that the children would ultimately have been trafficked into South Africa.
A nanny kidnapped two children at the home where she was employed and took them to relatives in Gaza Province.  The children were recovered a week later, and the nanny was arrested.
Police in Inhambane on 26 August arrested a group of three individuals for the forgery of documents.
Police on 28 August detained two individuals in Tete city on charges of the theft of 232 bags of fertilizer and 26 car tires from a local company.

90 new COVID-19 cases were reported in Mozambique on 08 September.  This included 54 cases in Zambezia, 23 in Cabo Delgado, 6 in Maputo City, 3 in Maputo, 2 in Tete, 1 in Manica, and 1 in Nampula, brining the total number of cases to 4,647 nationwide.  One new death was also registered, bringing the nationwide death toll to 28.

8 people were killed in an arson attack at the dawn of 08 September in Mualazi, Chifunde District of Tete when the homes of several artisanal gold miners were set on fire.  At least 5 other people were injured in the incident.  It was not immediately clear who was responsible for the attack.  Another source said that only 7 people had died in the incident.

A man on 08 September was reportedly killed in the Namanhumbyr area of Montepuez District, Cabo Delgado, in an apparent mob justice incident.  The man's body was left on a public road in the area.  It was not immediately clear why the man was killed.

The National Statistics Institute on 08 September reported that a study it had conducted of Mozambican enterprises indicated that business turnover in 2020 was down more than 50% due to the ongoing COVID pandemic.  The months of January - March saw an average of about a 25% decrease in turnover from the same period in 2019.  April saw a 60% drop, while declines of 47.5% and 51.9% were recorded in May and June respectively.
A well known dancer was arrested for stealing oranges in Maputo city on 06 September.  The man was also reportedly attacked by local civilians and injured after the theft.

An environmental NGO will go to court this week to challenge the British government's approval of $1 billion in funding for Mozambique's LNG projects.  The group brought the case saying that they were concerned taxpayer money was being used to "worsen the climate emergency" and said the decision approving the funding had been rushed throughout without proper oversight or due diligence.

A court on 08 September convicted 5 RENAMO members to 5 years in prison on charges of attempting to join RENAMO dissidents in Central Mozambique; charges of "conspiracy against the security of the state" were dropped.  The 5's sentence however was then commuted to a fine.  No evidence tying the 5 to the RENAMO Military Junta was actually presented in open court, though may have been presented at one closed session of court the judge of the case deemed "sensitive".  Charges against a sixth defendant were thrown out for lack of evidence.
A number of women were reportedly kidnapped on 08 September when insurgents attacked the village of Olumboa.

In a raid on the night of 08-09 September, insurgents set fire to several huts in Olumboa village, about 14 kms or 8 miles from Mucojo town.  This is the third attack in the area in three days after insurgent attacks on the nearby villages of Ruea and Manica on 07 and 06 September respectively.  1 villager was injured and a number of women kidnapped in this attack. most villagers had reportedly fled the village prior to the attack.  3 dhows were also stolen in this attack.

The Nacala Railway Line in Nampula has been reopened, local reports indicate on 8 September. The reopening allowed the resumption of the transportation of coal, general cargo, and passengers. This came after a closure caused by an accident in Meconta district when a train collided with wagons, resulting in a derailment.

Authorities detained the Macossa District Commander and 2 of his subordinates in Barue on 8 September due to bribery charges. The suspects were accused of releasing a race driver involved in a car accident in exchange for 45000 meticais, or about $633. Further investigations are underway in relation to the bribery charge.

The World Bank approved on 8 September a USD 104 million grant from the International Development Association (IDA) to support a skills development program for the youths of Mozambique. This project will invest in both Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) and Higher Education (HE) subsystems and support teacher training programs. This aims to improve education access, education curriculum quality, and skills development training and will focus on science, engineering, mathematics, and climate change.

At noon on 8 September, soldiers at a military base in Cuamba were reported to have fired on a drone flying near the base. No official statement from the military was released in relation to this incident.  Soldiers after the incident say that they believed the drone was flown by a local civilian attempting to spy on the military barracks, though the owner of the drone was not positively identified.

Amnesty International on 09 September said it had obtained a series of 5 videos and 3 pictures from sources in Cabo Delgado depicting torture and other abuses against suspected insurgents by security forces in the province.  Amnesty has called for an "independent and impartial investigation" into these alleged abuses. The organization said that "attempted beheading, torture, and other-ill treatment of prisoners, the dismemberment of alleged opposition fighters, possible extrajudicial executions, and the transport and discarding of large numbers of corpses into apparent mass graves" were seen in these videos.  The organization also confirmed that security forces seen in the videos wear the uniforms of the Mozambican Armed Defense Forces and the Mozambique Rapid Intervention Police.  The videos are believed to have been shot in the first half of 2020.

113 new COVID cases were reported on 09 September in Mozambique.  This included 42 new cases in Zambezia, 37 in Maputo City, 10 in Sofala, 8 in Maputo, 6 in Cabo Delgado, 6 in Tete, 5 in Niassa, 2 in Manica, and 1 in Gaza.  This brought the nationwide total number of cases to 4764 with 28 deaths.

Refugees from insurgent impacted areas, including from some of the Quirimba Islands, continue to arrive in Pangane, a source reported on 07 September.  At least 5,000 IDPs were recently reported to have gathered in this area.

Security forces in the early morning hours of 09 September reportedly drove insurgents out of Nambo village just northeast of Mucojo after clashes in the area.  Insurgents had earlier in the morning entered the village and killed two people.

Sources reported an insurgent attack on the village of Nambo, just northwest of Mucojo at around 0000hrs on 09 September, with several buildings in the village set on fire.  Sources later said two people were killed in this attack, with one person beheaded and while a woman was killed when her house was set on fire. The village was also attacked about a month ago by insurgents.  Insurgents also temporarily captured two local officials in the area, but the officials escaped insurgent custody during the course of the attack.

Total will pay for all food of military personnel guarding the Afungi LNG area during the "first phase" of the agreement it recently signed with the Mozambican government.  In the second phase, the company will also provide food for military personnel in Macomia, Mocimboa da Praia, and Mueda, local media reported.

Total was reported on 09 September to have won a tender to import liquid fuel for six months into Mozambique, beating out the current supplier, Sahara Petroleum, with a reportedly substantially cheaper bid.  Total as part of the bid will supply 680,000 tons of diesel, 275,000 tons of unleaded gasoline, and 60,000 tons of jet fuel.

The Mozambique Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) issued arrest warrants on 9 September for three individuals for embezzling and laundering money, forgery of documents, and electronic payment theft. This comes as two other individuals were being tried in Maputo in relation to the arrests. The suspects reportedly stole more than 1.8 million EUR.

The City Council announced the closure of several roads and restriction of traffic for 150 days as part of a city-wide road maintenance around Maputo starting on 10 September. The roads affected were the entire Avenida Mártires de Inhaminga and the road from Praça dos Trabalhadores until Praça 25 de Junho. While sidewalk repairs were being conducted in Zedequias Manganhela, Avenida Guerra Popular, and Avenida Alberto Lthuli.

column4: The Institute for Economics and Peace of Australia published a Register of Ecological Threats, warning that Mozambique is the second in the world with the highest risk of ecological shocks and may face five environmental threats by 2050. Mozambique is reportedly one of the “most fragile countries” due to their exposure to ecological threats and low or deteriorating “Positive Peace”.

RENAMO called for an investigation to determine and arrest the those responsible for the murder of a demobilized RENAMO member in Chibabava District on 9 September. RENAMO stated that Joao Muthandi was living in Panja locality of the district when he was killed by unknown assailants.

National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) suspended the operation of a cement factory in Matulo on 9 September, due to the lack of product quality and certification requirements. INAE spokesman stated that tests were conducted to determine the quality of the produced cement. As a result of inspections by INAE which started from 19 August.

Montepuez Ruby Mining (MRM) announced on 8 September, that 25 individuals were killed during illegal mining activities in northern Mozambique over the past six month. MRM stated that majority of the deaths were due to landslides during mining. MRM stated that in the most recent incident, a miner was found buried alive in their area and a miner was shot dead by Natural Resources and Environment Protection Unit in response to an attack by 30 armed men in the area last 30 August.

A policeman was attacked and injured by locals after being suspected of attempting to rob a motorcycle taxi driver in Chimoio on 6 September. This comes as police were accused of committing various criminal activities around Manica province.

National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) inspected 2,320 commercial establishments starting from 19 August until 5 September. INAE managed to seize 30,000 meticais worth of expired food items and reopened 87 gyms as part of the ease of restrictions around the country.

National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) inspected 2,320 commercial establishments starting from 19 August until 5 September. INAE managed to seize 30,000 meticais worth of expired food items and reopened 87 gyms as part of the ease of restrictions around the country.

Bank of Mozambique reported that the country’s public debt has reportedly increased to 120% during a fiscal risk statement. The 120% debt of the Gross Domestic Product directly impacts the resources used for the development of the country and lives of Mozambicans. This rapid increase in the country's debt is judged by many analysts to be unsustainable.

Tanzanian official Mtwara Regional Commissioner Gelasius Byakanwa denied reports that several Tanzanian soldiers were killed last week in Mozambique. Byakanwa stated that the border between Tanzania and Mozambique is secure even as attacks occur in Cabo Delgado. On 5 September, the Islamic State in Central Africa claimed to have killed and injured 20 Tanzanian soldiers in clashes in Mocimboa da Praia.  Byankanwa also called on residents of villages along the Rovuma River to provide authorities with information about "people entering the country illegally and people who endanger public security".
Customs seized 1,097 bottles of alcohol marked with forged import seals at a supermarket in Nampula on 9 September. Custom officials stated that the import seals were verified inauthentic.

Customs seized three packages of cocaine weighing one kilogram each inside a consignment of malaria medication in a refrigerated container at the Port of Beira on the evening of 06 September. Customs searched the container after its air-conditioning system failed. Customs stated that the container came from the port of Durban.

Municipality workers demolished several illegally placed night club and bar on the terrace and patio of a residence in Alto Mae, south Maputo City, on 9 September. Municipality officials previously warned the owner to revert her residence and remove the illegal facility.
Two suspects were detained by security forces for extortion and impersonating to inspectors of Electricidade de Mozambique in Mumemo area of Marracuene on 10 September.

Reports on 10 September stated that Unknown men stole several parts of an electrical transmission pole and caused power outages in Nkobe neighborhood, northwest of Maputo. Electricidade de Mozambique officials stated that around 30 families were left without electricity and that the accelerating cases of robbery stalled the planned expansion of electrical services in Matola.

South African Police in Richards Bay, South Africa seized 342.5 kg of heroin amounting to 4.4 million EUR and arrested a truck driver and two others coming from Mozambique on 9 September. Police stated that the drugs were inside a hidden metallic compartment of a truck.

Domestic flights in Zimbabwe on Thursday, 10 September while International flights would resume in October from the country, meaning flights between Mozambique and Zimbabwe will likely resume in October as well.  Travelers to the country will be required to have a PRC (polymerase chain reaction) COVID-19 clearance certificate issued from a certified facility 48 hours from departure.

Price increases of goods and services rose about 2.75% in August, with food, alcohol, tobacco, and non-alcoholic beverages the main goods that saw significant price rises.  Prices in Beira increased the most in the country at 3.65%, while prices in Maputo City rose in 2.16%.

On 01 September, insurgents were reported to have entered Quelimane village north of Mocimboa da Praia, firing weapons and causing people to flee.  No reports however of destruction, looting, or attacks on civilians in this attack were reported.

Insurgents during their 07 September attack on Vimizi island were reported to have warned locals that they would attack Palma town in the coming days; no such attack however over the past 5 days has yet materialized.

19 military vehicles carrying Mozambican soldiers on 31 August were reported to have moved from Nangade District to Palma and Mocimboa da Praia Districts.  Sources on 03 September reported "busloads" of soldiers being deployed to MDP.
column15: Mocimboa da Praia and Palma Districts

column4: Insurgents on 09 September were reported to have abducted at least one civilian in the village of Nacutouco after they were reported to have raided nearby Namba village.  Insurgents were later in the day reported to be in the vicinity of Nsano village.

A man on the night of 08 September murdered his grandmother in a physical assault in Manga, Beira, accusing her of practicing  witchcraft.  Killings of those accused of witchcraft are relatively common incidents, particular in rural Mozambique.

Mozambique's Ministry of Defense on 10 September issued a statement saying that images and videos released by Amnesty International allegedly depicting security forces torturing insurgents could be the work of "terrorists".  Officials said insurgents often masquerade as security force members and that the identity of those in uniform could not be confirmed.  Officials also accused Amnesty International of having been "silent" after different incidents in Cabo Delgado.

68 new Covid cases were confirmed on 10 September, with 50 cases reported in Maputo City, 11 in Zambezia, 4 in Niassa, 2 in Gaza, and 1 in Maputo.  4,832 cases have now been reported in the country, while 3 new deaths were also reported, brining the nationwide death toll to 31.

Cabo Delgado Insurgents attacked Maputo village located along the road between Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) and Palma, on the evening of 10 September; no information on casualties is currently available. The villagers reportedly fled to the village of Mute, 20km north of Maputo village. This comes after insurgents earlier this week attacked Vimizi Island, and last week entered Quelimane village, less than 20kms south of Maputo.

Around 800 displaced individuals from Cabo Delgado have arrived by boat to the coastal settlement of Msimbati in Mtwara region of Tanzania in recent weeks to seek refuge against the insurgency occurring in Cabo Delgado. Most of these Mozambican refugees came from islands off the Mocimboa da Praia/Palma coast, where insurgents have recently launched several attacks.
3 children were killed in an arson attack in Inhambane's Quissico area.  The arsonist had reportedly been targeting his ex-sister in law, who was also injured in the attack.
A man suspected of conducting an arson attack that killed 3 children in Quissico, Inhamabane, was arrested by police on 09 September.

Two police officers from the Rapid Intervention Unit (UIR) on Wednesday were injured in a suspected RENAMO dissident attack near Muxungue in Chibabava District, Sofala.  No other details regarding this attack are currently available.  The most recent RENAMO dissident attack reported in the area took place in late August in which dissidents near Save town fired upon a bus travelling through the area.

Henriques Dhlakama, the eldest son of late RENAMO leader Afonso Dhlakama, announced on 11 September that he intended to run for President in 2024.  Dhlakama will presumably attempt to run as the RENAMO candidate, and will have to unseat his father's successor, Ossufo Momade.  Momade in the wake of a heavy RENAMO defeat in the 2019 elections and amid an ongoing split from RENAMO by the RENAMO Military Junta is seen currently as politically vulnerable.

On 09 September, the US International Development Finance Corporation approved a $200 million loan to the Central Termica de Temane and agreed to provide up to $1.5 billion in political risk insurance to support LNG projects in the Rovuma Basin.  The $200 million loan will provide financing for the construction of a power plant and power lines in Mozambique,

Workers at the Bakhresa Grain Mill in Nacala on the morning of 11 September were reported to have gone on strike, causing a work stoppage at the mill.  The worker's union called for improvements in the workers' salaries, and for the company to provide assistance in providing workers with food and medical coverage.  The union also protested saying foreign employees receive 9 times the salary of a local worker, while foreign employees also receive substantial other benefits local employees do not enjoy.

al Naba, the Islamic State's weekly digital magazine, on 10 September featured two articles on Cabo Delgado.  In these articles, the group claimed that 70 government soldiers had been killed in recent clashes, including a large number of Tanzanian soldiers.  This came after the group claimed on 05 September to have killed 20+ Tanzanian soldiers in fighting on 05 September in Mocimboa da Praia.  These claims of clashes in MDP have not been confirmed.

Rajeev Kumar, India's High Commissioner in Mozambique, said on 09 September that trade between India and Mozambique had doubled between 2016 and 2020 but that the issue of kidnappings of Indian businessmen in Mozambique "has to be solved to encourage more people to enter the country".   Since the beginning of 2020, Mozambican authorities say there have been 9 prominent kidnappings targeting businessmen and their families.

86 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 11 September.  This included 38 new cases in Maputo City, 18 in Niassa, 13 in Maputo, 5 in Nampula, 4 in Sofala, 3 in Tete, and 2 in Zambezia.  This brings the nationwide total to 4,918, with 31 deaths.  There are currently 1,984 active confirmed cases in the country; 1120 of those are in Maputo City.

Unconfirmed reports that surfaced on 11 September reported that about 200 government troops had been ambushed in the Awasse area on 07 September by insurgents.  According to these reports, a group of Mozambican soldiers and Rapid Intervention Unit Police officers were blocked by two vehicles set on fire by insurgents.  Insurgents then attacked Mozambican military forces and forced them to retreat.  Local media reported "casualties on both sides" though no exact figures were reported.  Multiple reports previously indicated that government troops retook Awasse on 05 September.

Insurgents were reported to have attacked Mecungo (Quifuqui) Island on 07 September in small fishing boats, forcing people from their homes and setting fire to huts in the area.  Insurgents reportedly "gave orders to leave the islands" but did not attack island residents.

Security forces seized 10 Congo-bound trucks with South African license plates and trailers coming from Zimbabwe transporting sulfur for violating the SADC transportation regulation in Beira on the afternoon of 12 September. Officials stated that the vehicles should transfer the cargo onto vehicles licensed in Mozambique and transport the cargo towards Congo.
Insurgents on the afternoon of 11 September again attacked the island of Vamizi, arriving via a motorized dhow, reportedly setting fire to 30 homes as well as tourist lodges.

A group of insurgents was reported on 12 September to have attacked and destroyed two vehicles travelling from Palma to Mueda in the Pundanhar area at around 0500hrs, injuring an unknown number of people, while several people in the area were reported missing in the vicinity of the village.  At least 2 people were killed in the attack with 2 others confirmed to have been injured.   These include a man whose 2 children went missing after the attack and another man whose wife and 2 children were also missing. Further reports indicated that the vehicles were transporting people and goods from Palma to Mueda via a dirt track. According to those who survived, the militants wore uniforms similar to the Mozambique Army and ordered the vehicles stop. The first of 3 vehicles refused to stop; however, the 2 succeeding vehicles were attacked with small arms fire and were set ablaze. Insurgent activity in this area is very significant as militants are likely attempting to cut the last open road route between Palma and Southern Cabo Delgado.   Vehicles had been travelling along this route without military escorts as officials said that "we assumed that the route was safe".  Sources later indicated that at least 28 people died in this attack and a series of other attacks between 11-12 September.  At least 2 of the 28 killed were confirmed to have been killed in a separate incident from this attack.

The Ministry of Health on 13 September reported 229 new cases of COVID-19 across Mozambique, bringing the total number of cases to 5,269 with 35 deaths.   There are 2,270 active cases in the country.  170 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 32 in Maputo, 6 in Sofala, 6 in Gaza, 4 in Nampula, 4 in Tete, and 1 in Zambezia.  2,095 tests were carried out over the past 24 hours, meaning 10.9% of all tests conducted during this period were positive. This latest COVID case number is significant as it represents the highest number of confirmed cases in a single day during the outbreak by 61%.  The previous high was seen on 11 August when 142 cases were reported in a single day.  Maputo City, with more than half the country's active cases, continues to be the epicenter of confirmed cases in the country.  Spiking COVID cases could potentially lead the government to slow or even reverse some of the easing of COVID-19 preventative restrictions over the coming days and weeks; President Nyusi recently indicated if people did not take anti-COVID measures seriously the government would consider restoring some restrictions.

Mozambique recorded 122 Coronavirus cases on 12 Sept. 4 new deaths were also reported.  90 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 24 in Maputo, 4 in Beira, 2 in Nampula, 1 in Tete and 1 in Inhambane, bringing the nationwide total number of cases to 5040 with 35 deaths.

The World Food Program announced in a statement on 14 Sept that Norway has delivered support worth EUR 900,000 to Cabo Delgado. The aid will enable WFP to support at least 32,000 IDPs through 2 months worth of food assistance. The recent militant attacks in the province resulted in the displacement of more than 300,000 people as of September to throughout Northern Mozambique . At least two-thirds of these have been assisted by the WFP through food distribution, malnutrition treatment, and communication.

A graphic video was shared widely on 14 September depicting men in Mozambican military uniforms chasing, beating, and ultimately shooting dead a naked woman in Cabo Delgado.  The image was later geolocated as being in the Awasse area.  In the video, one of the men depicted tells the cameraman not to film as the group will be recognized, to which the cameraman responds "to not worry, I am filming from the back".  After the woman is shot dead, the men say they have killed "al Shabaab", the local name for the Cabo Delgado insurgents.  Initial analysis of the video has indicated that the uniformed men are likely members of the Mozambican military, though this has not been confirmed.  The faces of at least two uniformed men can be seen clearly in the video.

16 people were injured on Saturday afternoon in a road traffic accident involving the motorcade of RENAMO chief Ossufo Momade in the Malema area of Nampula Province.  One person was injured severely while the other 15 injured persons were released within hour of the accident.  The accident occurred after 5 vehicles of the motorcade collided with one another due to poor visibility along the EN13 road.

Insurgents on the night of 10 September were reported to have entered the village of Tete in Mocimboa da Praia, reportedly threatening village residents and expelling them from the village.  No other details regarding this incident are currently available.
