Insurgents on the night of 10 September entered the village of Mute in Palma District and threatened villagers, forcing local residents out of the village.  No further information on this incident is currently available.

Military officials in Palma over the weekend said that Palma District has been effectively surrounded after an attack over the weekend along the Palma - Nangade road.  Officials also said that that Palma was "surrounded and at this moment the defence and security forces have neither the conditions nor the capacity to reel the insurgents from Palma and recover Mocimboa da Praia".  At least one source reported that the road between Pundanhar and Palma has been "occupied" by insurgents and that the road has officially been closed, though the official closure of the road remains unconfirmed.

Mozambican military forces on 12 September were reported to have arrived at the scene of an insurgent attack along the Palma-Nangade road near Pundanahar, briefly clashing with militants and forcing them to flee the area. No casualty figures from this clash are available.

Mozambican officials said on 14 September that 500,000 people were likely to be impacted by flooding during the 2020-2021 rainy season, which is anticipated to last from October into March.  The Maputo, Incomati, and Umbeluzi basins will likely be the greatest impacted areas in the country by this flooding.

Two men were arrested on 09 September in Barue District of Manica on charges of fraud and on charges of practicing "false traditional medicine.  The two over a six month period charged patients over 235 thousand meticais, or about $3,270.

Mozambican health officials said on 14 September that a new outbreak of foot and mouth disease had been detected in Angonia District, Tete Province.  This comes after an outbreak of the disease was reported in Magude District of Maputo Province in mid-August.

Nampula Governor Manuel Rodrigues said that more than 20,000 IDPs from Cabo Delgado have been displaced into Nampula.  He also said there are IDPs in 15 different district of the province, but that these IDPs were concentrated in Meconta District and Nampula city.  The majority of the 250,000+ people displaced by the Cabo Delgado insurgency are still within Cabo Delgado itself.
700 new Mozambican military recruits graduated from training in Manhica on 14 September.  Local media said around 200 were likely to be deployed to Cabo Delgado in the near future.

The government's Emergency Operative Center on 14 September announced that there were more than 368,000 people displaced by conflict due to the Cabo Delgado insurgency and RENAMO dissident attacks in Central Mozambique.  This is the equivalent of 73,000 families, officials said.  The UN's Office of Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs meanwhile this week said that there are 345,000 IDPs throughout Mozambique, including 250,000 IDPs in Cabo Delgado.
Security forces detained two suspects for trafficking a pangolin inside a spare tire in Gorongosa on 2 September.

Security forces detained two suspects for trafficking a pangolin inside a spare tire along Highway N1 between Gorongosa and Nhamapadza on 2 September. The suspects worked for a telecommunications company. A follow-up operation was conducted.

Security forces detained three suspects involved in the smuggling of a pangolin in Gorongosa area during a follow-up operation on 12 September. Two of their accomplices were previously caught along the Highway N1 between Gorongosa and Nhamapadza.
Police arrested a smuggler for transporting Umbila wood in Panda of Inhambane on 8 September.
Several trucks transporting smuggled wood were travelling from Metarica towards Cuamba on 8 September. Local sources stated that the vehicles were destined towards Nacala Port to be shipped to China.

President Felipe Nyusi conducted a meeting the delegation of the Total led by the company’s Chairman and CEO Patrick Pouyanné in Maputo on 12 September. The meeting discussed the evolution of the liquefied natural gas project in Area 1 of the Rovuma Basin and positively received the progress made despite the challenges due to the COVID pandemic. The meeting also talked about the issue on replacing and maintaining routes, bridges, and roads affected by natural disasters. Another topic was the training and skills development of local workers and promotion of the LNG project to the locals.

A joint operation was conducted by the police and Natural Resources and Environment protection unit conducted an operation intending to minimize illegal charcoal production in Muanza on 3 September. 128 bags of charcoal were seized during the operation.

The Ministry of Health announced on 14 September that the increase in COVID cases could lead to the collapse of the healthcare system in the country. Health officials stated that there are limitations on the placed preventive measures and that the locals should change their behavior regarding the virus. Officials also stated that 44 new hospital admissions increasing the total admission to 122 which 26 were in isolation centers.  This announcement came after the country on 13 September announced over 220 cases in a single day, the highest daily number of confirmed cases during the ongoing pandemic.

A vehicle rolled over several times after it had a tire blowout along a road in Monapo, 90km east of Nampula, on the afternoon of 14 September. A civilian was killed, and several others were injured. The driver fled the scene of the accident.

The National Statistics Institute (INE) conducted a study which indicated that only 8,000 companies benefitted from the 500 million USD credit line for imports. INE stated that few companies would benefit from the credit line but this was not heeded by the Bank of Mozambique. INE also stated in their study that around 16,700 companies would benefit from the tax and contributory obligations, while 12,200 companies would benefit from loans and subsidized interest rates.

President Felipe Nyusi dismissed UN representative ambassador António Gumende on 14 September. No information was stated as to why Gumende was dismissed. Gumende was previously a journalist previously served as Mozambican high commissioner and wrote for the Mozambican Information Agency.

The Ministry of Health recorded 213 new COVID-19 cases in Mozambique on 14 September, increasing the total to 5,482. The active cases were reported to be 2,419. Out of the new cases 121 were reported to be from Maputo City, 50 in Zambezia, 35 in Maputo, 5 in Tete, and 2 in Cabo Delgado.   While 64 cases were reported to have recovered resulting to 3,024 total recoveries. The number of fatalities still remain at 35.
Beaches on 15 September were officially reopened to the public in Mozambique as part of the easing of anti-COVID-19 measures.

A military vehicle on 15 September carrying military personnel in the Mucojo area reportedly turned over, resulting in minor injuries of several soldiers.  No further details on this incident are currently available.

The Mozambican government on 14 September issued a statement denouncing a video posted online showing uniformed men believed to be in the Awasse area of Cabo Delgado, beating and ultimately executing a naked woman who they then identify as "al Shabaab", a local name for the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  The government statement said that the military does not agree "with any barbaric act that substantiates the violation of human rights".  The statement also said an investigation into the incident would be launched.

Mozambican Airline LAM said on 15 September that it would continue flights between Maputo and Lisbon which were restarted in August until January 2021.  Initially these flights were only meant to last through the end of September, but due to demand this flight schedule has been extended.  The airline has also restarted flights between Maputo and Johannesburg on Wednesdays.
A group of 108 IDPs from Mocimboa da Praia are currently camping on Paquitequete beach in Pemba, and have been present in the area for 3 weeks due to a lack of shelter.

Locals on 15 September said that two "cargo" boats travelling from Pemba to Palma which had left Pemba "days ago" had not yet reached Palma and that nothing was known about the whereabouts of these boats.  Some local have speculated that these boats could have potentially been seized by insurgents off the coast of Mocimboa da Praia District.

Classes were suspended at the Instituto Politecnico de Chigodole on 15 September in Manica after two students tested positive for COVID-19 at the school.  The two positive cases are both from Maputo.  The school had been re-opened on 01 September after being closed for 6 months due to the ongoing pandemic.

An anonymous military source on 15 September indicated that the Mozambican military had reportedly identified the uniformed men who executed a naked woman near Awasse in a video released on 14 September.  The source said the men were in fact military members and that the "case is already being dealt with internally".

Images published online on 15 September appeared to show the remains of tourist lodges in Vamizi Island destroyed in insurgent raids earlier in the month.  Insurgents in previous attacks warned island residents they should leave Vamizi; it remains unclear currently if insurgents are actively occupying the island.

An investigation into the leadership of the Cabo Delgado insurgency reported on 14 September that a man called Ibn Omar, born Bonomade Machude Omar and nicknamed "Rei da Floresta" or King of the Forest, is a native of Mocimboa da Praia town and is a top leader of the Cabo Delgado insurgency and may be the paramount leader of the group.  The investigation said that Omar was the mastermind behind most of the group's attacks.  Omar reportedly studied abroad in a number of Muslim countries, and reportedly built a significant network prior to the launching of the insurgency.  Omar now reportedly uses this network to provide the insurgency with regular information on military movements and operations in Cabo Delgado.  In previous reports, Omar had been identified as "Bonomar from Mocimboa da Praia" and was believed to be one of the group's top leaders though previous reports did not indicate he was potentially the top commander of the group.  The investigation also referenced two other insurgent leaders called "Mousse" or Mussa in Macomia District as well as Canimambo de Macomia; both of these men have been referenced in past reports as leaders of the insurgency.

231 confirmed COVID cases were reported on 15 September, a new high record high daily number of cases in the country.  2 new deaths due to the virus were also reported on Tuesday.  This brought the nationwide total number of cases to 5,713 with 37 deaths.  77 cases were reported in Maputo City, and 66 cases in Maputo.

A gang of 3 suspected thieves was arrested on 05 September in Matola.  The three had reportedly been behind several home break-ins in the area.  The three were arrested at dawn of the 5th after they were found preparing to break into a home in Matola.

An insurgent attack 18 residences were set on fire was reported on Quissengue / Quissenge on 14 September.  The village lies approximately 6 miles or just over 9 kms south of Olumbe. Three civilians were injured.
Insurgents on the afternoon of 13 September attacked Ningaia village, about 5.5 miles or 9 kms southwest of Mucojo.  Several homes were set on fire while militants also looted food and other items.

The Mozambican Bar Association (OAM) on 14 September said that Mozambican judges are "harassing lawyers", saying that this issue has been the most significant in Beira in Sofala.  In Beira, several lawyers have complained about judicial behavior, to which judges have retaliated by initiating criminal proceedings against the lawyers.  The OAM also condemned attacks against journalists in the country, citing the example of the arson attack on the offices of Canal de Mocambique in Maputo.

3 individuals were arrested by police in Beira between 09-12 September on charges of having fraud in relation to Cyclone Idai subsidies.  The three had charged small fees to customers seeking to be placed on roles to receive Cyclone Idai victim subsidies.  These roles however were false.

Mozambique's Interior Minister Amade Miquidade said on 15 September that the footage of uniformed men killing a woman in Cabo Delgado recently released on social media may have been filmed by insurgents attempting to discredit the government.  He also called the killing and other abuses seen in videos circulating of alleged security force abuses "acts of subversion" meant to sew division between the Mozambican security forces and regular citizens.  Miquidade went on to say that there was likely a "nucleus where these videos are prepared" and that the government would conduct an investigation to identify this "nucleus".

More than 300,000 people will be included in a cholera vaccination program in Cabo Delgado set to take place between 21-25 September, health officials said on 15 September..  The campaign is primarily aimed at the displaced population of the province but will also cover some individuals not targeted in last year's campaign. Over 1,500 cases of cholera and 26 deaths have been reported in Cabo Delgado over the 2019/2020 rainy season.

The Center for Democracy and Development (CDD) published a new report on 15 September saying that the Mozambican government has failed in protecting human rights and promoting democratic institutions.  The report said human rights violations have become increasingly common in the country over the first half of 2020, particularly by the police, saying the country has "institutionalized the police state and impunity".  The report cited police killings of civilians in Maputo and Beira,, as well as the disappearance of Palma journalist Ibrahimo Mbaruco in April as examples of this impunity.  The report also said hate speech targeting those critical of bad governance and defending human rights has increased, seemingly with government encouragement.

Gemfields company announced on 14 September it expected an interim net loss for the six months as the company had only been able to hold one sale due to the covid-19 pandemic.  The company is unable to project when it will next be able to hold auctions or generate new revenue from gemstone sales.

National Health Institute Survey Director, Sergio Chicumbe stated on 16 September that Mozambique has still not reached the peak of the COVID-19 infection. Chicumbe mentioned that over the past 48 hours the Ministry of Health recorded 442 cases of Covid-19, 291 of them (66%) in Maputo city and this reflected an increase in infections, not based on the increased number of tests conducted.
Police temporarily detained individuals without masks in Beira City and conducted an awareness-raising talks before giving people masks and letting them go in Beira City on 15 September.

Police arrested a smuggler and seized five slaughtered cattle inside a minivan at a checkpoint in Nhongonhane area of Marracuene on the afternoon of 15 September. The smuggler confessed that he the stolen goods were to be delivered to Chicumbane of Gaza province. Officials previously banned any movement of hooved animals in and out of Maputo province due to the outbreak of foot and mouth disease among live stock in Maputo province since August.

Police arrested a smuggler and seized five slaughtered cattle inside a minivan at a checkpoint in Nhongonhane area of Marracuene on the afternoon of 15 September. The smuggler confessed that he the stolen goods were to be delivered to Chicumbane of Gaza province. Officials previously banned any movement of hooved animals in and out of Maputo province due to the outbreak of foot and mouth disease among live stock in Maputo province since August.
Border guards seized 4 tons of smuggled poultry hidden under a fake floor panel inside unrefrigerated containers at Muloza border crossing, northwest of Maputo on 13 September.

RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo stated in a 15 September interview that he will not negotiate with RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade to resolve their relationship. Nhongo stated that the demobilization and reintegration is a failed process and Ossufo does not value the lives of those who died for democracy.  Specifically, Nhongo said the process had failed as demobilized veterans were provided with only very small amount of money and material in return for going back to civilian life. Nhongo also mentioned that the invitation for negotiations is “unreasonable” as Ossufo does not recognize Nhongo leadership.

President Filipe Nyusi dismissed Pedro Commissário Afonso from his position as the Deputy Minister for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation using a presidential order on 16 September. Afonso was initially appointed in February of this year.  It was not immediately clear why Afonso was removed from his position.

Amnesty International called for an "immediate and impartial investigation" into the extrajudicial killing of a naked woman in the Awasse area of Cabo Delgado in a video shared in recent days on social media.  The video was reportedly originally shared between several phones in Cabo Delgado on 07 September, around when clashes were reported in Awasse.  The organization said it had verified that the woman had been shot 36 times by 4 different shooters.  The woman was shot dead just west of Awasse town outside of an electrical substation along the R698 road.  Amnesty also said a Mozambican military source it had contacted had confirmed Mozambican troops were responsible for the killing, saying the woman had attempted to "cast a spell" on the soldiers and had refused to show them an insurgent hideout in the area.

Businessman Artur Magaia was reported to have been released by kidnappers on 15 September at an undisclosed time after a ransom was paid for his release.  This ransom was reportedly for over one million dollars, though this fact has not yet been confirmed.  The businessman was taken to a Maputo City hospital immediately after his release and was reported to be in poor health.  Magaia, who owns a customs brokerage service, was kidnapped on 11 August from his home in the Belo Horizonte area of Boane.  It is unclear if Boane was released in Boane or Maputo City; no further information on his kidnappers is currently available at this time.

281 cases of COVID-19 were reported in Mozambique on 16 September, along with 2 additional fatalities.  This brought the total number of countrywide cases to 5,994 along with 37 deaths.  77 cases were reported in Maputo City, 68 in Maputo, 44 in Tete, 24 in Zambezia, 17 in Niassa, and 1 in Cabo Delgado.  This was out of a batch of 1,441 test results reported over the past 24 hours.  There are currently 2,491 active cases in the country.  This represents a new high of COVID-19 cases reported in a single day in Mozambique.

Joao Abreu, the chairman of the board of directors of Mozambique's Civil Aviation Institute said on 16 September that Mozambique would resume flights with six countries on a reciprocal basis after interruptions due to COVID-19.  Flights with Portugal, Turkey, Qatar, Ethiopia, Kenya, and South Africa have been authorized at a frequency of two fighters per week.  Airlines from other countries meanwhile interested in resuming flights to Mozambique should apply through diplomatic channels, officials said. All passengers upon arrival into the country must present a negative COVID test from the past 72 hours and observe a quarantine of 10-14 days, depending on whether or not they take a new COVID-19 test upon arrival.

Mozambique's Defense Minister Jaime Neto said on 16 September that a video showing men in military uniforms who beat and shot dead a woman in Cabo Delgado was "fake" and that "malicious people" had doctored the footage, and that some of those responsible had been identified by the government. He denied that Mozambican soldiers had committed the killing, and said the culprits would be arrested, paraded before the public, and punished.

A journalist with DW Africa was abducted at around 1900 hrs from his home on the night of 13 September in Maxixe, Inhambane, by two masked assailants armed with knives who forced him into a vehicle without number plates.  The man was then taken to a nearby beach, where he was bound and then beaten unconscious by his captors, who also robbed him of two phones, ID documents, and a tape recorder.

A journalist with DW Africa was abducted at around 1900 hrs from his home on the night of 13 September in Maxixe, Inhambane, by two masked assailants armed with knives who forced him into a vehicle without number plates.  The man was then taken to a nearby beach, where he was bound and then beaten unconscious by his captors, who also robbed him of two phones, ID documents, and a tape recorder.

A reporter for TV Station TV Sucesso was attacked on Sunday night in Nampula City by three unidentified men who seized his camera.  The next day, he found his attackers had left the camera at a local police station, and had erased footage which reportedly showed FRELIMO party members who had infiltrated an opposition RENAMO party event held Sunday night.  The journalist's attackers had contacted him after the Sunday night attack at around 0400hrs on Monday morning, telling him to retrieve his camera from the police station and advising him to delete any images and footage he had of the FRELIMO members saying if he did not, he would "see what will happen".  The journalist at the police station was also advised by police to delete any footage of FRELIMO members in order to "avoid problems".
Insurgents attacked Manica village on the night of 13 September,  looting supplies and several chickens from the village.  Militants had attacked this village just 7 days before on 06 September.
Insurgents on 09 September attacked Pamuto village just northeast of Mucojo.  No details regarding this attack are currently available.

Clashes were reported on 10 September in the Tete/Namaringa villages area along the Mocimboa da Praia - Palama road between insurgents and Mozambican military forces.  Unknown casualties were reported in this fighting.

Insurgents attacked the town of Maganja on 12 September in Palma District, just outside of the LNG Gas  Camp, injuring 2 civilians.  This village had been attacked in the past by insurgents but had not been targeted by them for several months.

Security forces on 12 September clashed with insurgents an Manilha, 15kms west of Mocimboa da Praia town, as government forces moved towards MDP.  Heavy fighting was reported in this village, but no casualty information is available from this fighting.

Insurgents were reported by military sources on 12 September to still be in control of Mocimboa da Praia town - a full month after they initially captured the town on 11 August.  Insurgents since that time have successfully fended off probes by the Mozambican military to retake the town, and have consolidated their positions in wider MDP District.
Local sources in the Quiterajo area say the town is mostly deserted, and local residents of the area consider the town to be essentially under insurgent control.
Insurgents on 11 September attacked a village in the vicinity of Pundahar, looting items from the village.
Two vehicles were reportedly fired on in the vicinity of Pundahar town on 11 September by insurgents.
Insurgents in a roadside ambush on 12 September beheaded two Somali nationals around 30 kms west of Palma town in the 10 Congresso area.
Cabo Delgado insurgents on 09 September raided Metundo Island, setting several homes on fire, though no casualties were reported in this incident.

Municipality employees have begun demolishing around 600 stalls and makeshift establishments along Ave Herois de Liberdade and Ave 1 de Julho in Quelimane on the evening of 15 September. The demolition comes after a 90-day notice and voluntary removal of their stalls. The vendors were to be relocated at indicated markets by the Quelimane Municipal Council. Several of the stall owners were dissatisfied with the relocation due to the lack of adequate space for several of the owners.

An armed man stabbed his daughter to death for having albinism and to steal the victim’s organs in Pambara village in Cuamba district on 11 September.  Attacks on those with albinism is a regular occurrence in much of Southern Africa.

An unknown man sexually assaulted a 15-year-old in Nhongonhane area of Marracuene, north of Maputo City, on 16 September. The suspect managed to escape after the incident. Police conducted a search for the suspect after the victim’s parents were informed by the victim.

Police arrested a suspect wanted for sexual assault of a teenager in Malhampsene area of Matola, west of Maputo City, on 16 September. The suspect previously raped the victim in Nhongonhane area and fled.

The European Union intends to create a reinforce support strategy by the end of the year to Cabo Delgado due to the ongoing conflict. EU ambassador, Antonio Sanchez-Benedito Gaspar conducted a meeting with leaders of Integrated Development Agency of North Mozambique (ADIN) and The Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development. The meeting discussed the establishments of main lines of work and mapping the region to enable cooperation and promotion. Gaspar stated that they showed interest to work with the African Development Bank and World Bank to enable infrastructure and long-term development hubs in Cabo Delgado, Niassa, and Nampula.

Mozambique Defence Armed Forces (FADM) disguised as tribal elders entered an insurgent-held village near Pundahar vicinity pretending to attend a marriage and opened fire on a large group of insurgents on the afternoon of 16 September.  It was unclear how many insurgents were killed and wounded in this ambush, but militants afterwards reportedly fled from the area. Unconfirmed reports said 19 militants were killed in this clash.

At least 7 people were injured on the morning of 17 September in a suspected RENAMO dissident attack between Inchope and the bridge over the Pungue River in Gorongosa District while travelling along the N1 Road.  Three people were seriously injured in the incident.  The first attack occurred at around 0745 hrs, while a second attack occurred around 1000hrs.  All 7 people injured were injured in the first attack.  The Mozambican military later said the attacks had been committed by RENAMO dissidents under Mariano Nhongo.
Insurgents on 15 September were reported to have attacked the village of Namadoro outside of Pangane town, seizing fish catches from locals.  No casualties were reported in this attack.

Mozambican military units on 14 September intercepted a group of insurgents near Diaca village in Cabo Delgado as the militants travelled to attack an area village.  In the ensuing clashes, 6 militants were reportedly killed. Initially, soldiers fighting the militants had been forced to retreat but redoubled their attack after they were reinforced by troops from Nanenda village.

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa announced on 16 September that South Africa would reopen borders in October, restoring economic activity with its neighboring countries, including Mozambique. This comes as the country was moved to level 2 of the country's reopening process which saw most of South Africa's economy reopened.

Police arrested a traditional doctor for vandalizing a tomb for black magic in Vanduzi of Manica province on 13 September. The 66-year-old suspect was found guilty and was fined to pay compensation to the bereaved family. The suspect conducted the crime on 12 September as she destroyed the tomb to create an amulet.

A 66-year-old traditional doctor destroyed a tomb to create an amulet in Vanduzi of Manica province on 12 September. Police arrested the traditional doctor in response to vandalizing the tomb for black magic.

Municipal authorities demolished 34 stalls as a part of the operation to enable the construction of a police station in Polana Caniço A, east Maputo, on the 17 September. The demolition comes after several meetings with the stall owners and relocation to another market. Several stall owners protested that they were not informed of the demolition and claimed to have lost assets during the clearing operation.

Mozambique Liberation Front (FRELIMO) announced their unconditional support for the Security and Defense Forces (SDS) after calls of an investigation regarding the human rights violation. FRELIMO officials stated that they would continue with the SDS to work to unite Mozambicans and that Cabo Delgado should be treated like any other province in Mozambique which should be fought for.

Montepuez Ruby Mining (MRM) announced on 17 September the death of an illegal miner after an excavation site collapsed on the company’s concession. Unconfirmed sources stated that the miner reportedly died last 7 September and that victims body was exhumed and was buried at a cemetery by other miners.  1 other person was reported to have been injured in this incident.

The Mozambican Ministry of Land and Environment announced on 16 September a decrease of 70 percent in elephant poaching cases since 2014 due to the authority’s efforts with the protection of natural resources. Officials stated that the number of cases has gone to from 1,200 to 360 during the past 5 years.

The European Union has guaranteed 50 million EUR to Mozambique as a part of their support framework development in Cabo Delgado. Half of the funds will be used to assist around 300,000 IDPs due to the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delagado.

The European Parliament discussed the humanitarian situation in northern Mozambique on 17 September. The discussion focused on the support that the European Union would provide for the security situation in Cabo Delgado. The security situation in Cabo Delgado is  a concern for Portugal, and will be given greater attention as Portugal is to assume the presidency of the Council of the EU, Portuguese MEPs said. Additionally, Portuguese MEPs urged the EU not to ignore the security situation and stated that it should be addressed along with the ongoing pandemic.  The European Parliament passed a resolution expressing "deep concern" over the situation in Northern Mozambique and called for the EU to work closely with the Southern African Development Community to resolve the worsening humanitarian crisis in the Cabo Delgado.

The European Commission called for a transparent and effective investigation into the murder of woman who was caught on video by suspected security forces in Cabo Delgado.  European Parliament officials stated that the EU have has opened a political dialogue focused on humanitarian developments and security issues in Cabo Delgado and are ready to discuss options for assistance. Officials also mentioned that the report by Amnesty International is extremely shocking. All accusations leveled at the involved members of the security forces must be investigated with full respect for the legal rights of both the victims and the accused.

The Mozambican Foreign Ministry denied reports it had appointed a Brazilian drug smuggler as a consular attaché in Belo Horizonte city of Brazil. Sources stated that Brazilian prosecutors believed that the drug smuggler was hired as an attaché at the Mozambican honorary consulate, and local media reported the story. Previous local reports stated the government hired Brazilian, Marcos Roberto de Almeida, also known as "Tuta", who was wanted by the Federal Police in Brazil. Almeida was reported to be the partner of wanted drug trafficker Gilberto Aparecido dos Santos who was previously detained in Mozambique in April during a joint operation between the US DEA, Mozambican, and Brazilian police.
Mozambique on 17 September reported 167 new cases of COVID, bringing the total number of infections to 6,161 with 39 deaths.  73 new cases were reported in Maputo City and 43 new cases in Zambezia.

RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo claimed on 17 September in an interview with DW that one of his sons on Wednesday had been shot at five times by security forces and his motorcycle seized in the Chiadeia area of Nhamatanda.  Nhongo also threatened to launch attacks in Nhamatanda District saying he would "paralyze everything" in the district and that he would attack sugar producing parts of the district as well.  A Nhamatanda official meanwhile said he had no knowledge of the reported incident involving Nhongo's son.

A member of the RENAMO dissident group the RENAMO Military Junta said on 17 September that he had lost contact with his family in the Manica capital of Chimoio, and believes they have been abducted by Mozambican security forces.

Local media on 16 September identified one of the soldiers recently seen in a video in which uniformed men killed a naked woman near Awasse.  The soldier, Ramiro Moises Machatine, was then reported by at least two unverified sources to have been killed, with one source saying he had been killed on the orders of high ranking officers in an effort to cover up the incident.  This last piece of information remains unconfirmed as of 18 September.

A Total spokesman on 18 September confirmed that a meeting between Total CEO Patrick Pouyanne and President Nyusi on 12 September had focused primarily on security, and that the Maputo government had reiterated its commitment to "respect international humanitarian law".  A statement previously released on these talks had not mentioned talks regarding security.
103 new COVID cases were reported on 18 September in Mozambique.  57 new cases were reported in Maputo City with 18 in Zambezia.

Former President Armando Guebuza on 17 September said that he would answer questions on the "Hidden Debts" case but said that there were "more than enough" reasons to distrust the Mozambican Public Prosecutor's Office.  Guebuza said this questioning was an attempted "political assassination".  This incident further demonstrated the continued deterioration of relations between the Nyusi government and former President Guebuza.

Sources reported on 17 September that District Services Agents of Economic Activities had ordered the immediate closure of a fuel station in Angoche.  This came after the motorcade of RENAMO chief Ossufo Momade had stopped and fueled at the station earlier in the day.
A bus in Inharrime village travelling to Tete was reported on 18 September to have caught fire due to mechanical problems.  No injuries were reported as part of the incident.

Officials aid on 18 September that Mozambique loses as much as $60 million annually to illegal fishing activity.  Russian, Panamanian, and Seychelles flagged vessels most commonly carry out illegal fishing off the Mozambican coasts.  Corruption also often facilitates this illegal activity, and has most recently facilitated Chinese companies participating in illegal fishing.

A prominent lawyer in Zambezia was reported on 12 September to have committed suicide in Chinde District.  Unconfirmed reports said the man had recently poached animals in Chinde District and had been discovered, and that he had killed himself before he could be arrested.
A man was arrested and reportedly beaten by police on 18 September in the Boquisso area of Matola.  Local media said the man was arrested for "playing his trumpet".

The Center of Public Integrity (CIP) accused the National Election Commission (CNE) for the lack of accountability regarding the funds allocated to the electoral parties last year during elections. CIP stated that around 180 million meticais were handed over to the parties for the elections, but no accounts were created to show the expenses of the parties. CIP warned the risk of mishandling of the public funds and corruption during the electoral financing procedure.

Security forces seized a China-bound shipment containing several smuggled electrical and railway equipment being in Beira Port on 18 September. The railway equipment was reported to be from the Sena railway lines which links Beira Port and Moatize.

367 Mozambicans returned back from South Africa to Mozambique on 16 September. Among the returning individuals included illegal immigrants and prisoners. Officials said that the prisoners sent back were due to  prisons in South Africa. The returning individuals were tested for the COVID-19. Among the 251 illegal immigrants, 116 were previously detained for crimes, drug trafficking, poaching, forgery of documents and voluntary homicide.

Security forces detained 31 Malawian illegal immigrants while attempting to pass immigration in Tete on 15 September in attempts to go back to Malawi. 10 of the immigrants had passports but lacked the requirements to travel.

A fire was reported on the night of 18 September at Situ Island Resort, approximately 30kms north of Pemba.  Partial damage to some buildings at the resort was reported, with at least 3 cabins damaged by fire.  Initial reports suggested an insurgent attack at the location, though two different sources said the fire was not insurgency related.  Resort officials later said the buildings had been targeted in an arsonist attack, though it was still not believed to be insurgency related.

Suspected RENAMO dissidents attacked 5 passenger buses between Inchope and Gorongosa in the Pungue River crossing area along the N1 road on Sunday morning, 20 September. The attack left 2 civilians dead and 8 others wounded. The victims were brought to Gorongosa Health Center, while 2 of the victims, who were critically wounded, were transported to the Chimoio Provincial Hospital.  The attack was reported to have lasted approximately 30 seconds.  These five buses were escorted by police, who were unable to prevent the attack, were not reported to have engaged the attackers, and did not capture any assailants after the incident. Reports also indicated that the police escorts and buses did not stop during the attack and only finally stopped when they arrived in Gorongosa town.
Insurgents on the morning of 20 September attacked the village of Litamanda, beheading a young man.

Insurgents in the late morning of 20 September were reported to have fired on two men on a motorbike in the Litamanda area ; the two were able to escape though abandoned thee motorbike which was captured by insurgents.

Insurgents who had earlier in the day been active in the Litamanda area were reported to have abducted two young men in the Darumba area, and to have entered Darumba village later, where they ordered local residents to participate in prayers.   The two men who had been abducted were able to escape while the insurgent prayed.

Two men in the Darumba area of Macomia who escaped from insurgents after being abducted told a local media outlet that the insurgents had "lists" of government officials and were travelling to different villages and offering money for "reliable information".  The young men also said the insurgents travelled with multiple "hostages", including young women likely forced into marriages with the group's fighters.

24 people were buried in the past week after attacks on 11-12 September in the Pundahar Area.  Insurgents launched a series of attacks over this two-day period that were previously reported though casualties from these incidents remained unclear.  Many of those killed had been Palma residents travelling along this road.  The death toll was confirmed after several Palma residents travelled to the Pundahar area and discovered the bodies of their friends and relatives.  These attacks also forced the closure of the Palma - Pundahar Road, the last road route between Palma and the south.  Among the dead was a village chief from the Palma area and his wife.

273 New COVID Cases were reported in Mozambique by officials on 19 September, including 139 new cases in Maputo City and 65 new cases in Maputo Province.  There have now been 6537 cases reported countrywide. 1 new death was also reported, bringing the total number of deaths to 41 in the country.  This was the second highest number of COVID cases reported in a single day during the ongoing pandemic.

Mozambique recorded 234 new Coronavirus cases and 2 deaths on 20 September. The cases include 104 from Maputo city and 94 from Maputo province. Both deaths were recorded in Maputo city. The total cases now stands at 6,771.

On the morning of 21 September, reports indicate that the owner of Empatel, Artur Magala, has been discharged from the hospital and is currently recovering at his home in Maputo. Magala was kidnapped for ransom in Boane, Maputo province, and was released last 15 September. He was admitted to the ICU after falling ill in captivity.
In an attack over the night of 18-19 September, insurgents beheaded 4 local residents in the Chitachi village area after they were surprised while gathered around a camp fire.

Insurgents over the night of 20-21 September raided the village of Litamanda for the second time in 24 hours, carrying out looting.  Two civilians were found killed.  The day before, insurgents killed one person in the village.

A media source reported on 20 September that an alleged poisoning attempt of former President Guebuza's family is currently being investigated.  The alleged attempt was reported to have occurred between June and July 2019 via an "organic phosphoric pesticide" added to a desert being prepared for the family.  This report surfaced after Guebuza recently accused Mozambican officials of targeting him in a "political assassination" by calling on him to answer questions related to the hidden debts case.

Media sources reported that unidentified armed men believed to be RENAMO dissidents had carried out an attack on two cargo trucks travelling between Muxungue and Inchope on the afternoon of 20 September.  A source later indicated this attack occurred near the Guengere area near a bridge crossing the Guengere River.

Media sources reported on 21 September that as part of Total's deal with the Mozambican government, additional special forces, naval and police forces will be deployed to protect the Afungi Peninsula, LNG facilities, and workers living in neighboring communities.  Total also has the option of unilaterally terminating the contract if the government does not provide sufficient support and may then contract private military security in the area.  As previously reported, Total will provide equipment, vehicles, and pay increase to Mozambican military troops operating in the area.
Two men working in fields near Kiwiya/Quiwia village, about 20kms northeast of Palma town, were reportedly decapitated in an apparent insurgent attack on 17 September.

Attacks on 11-12 September that resulted in the deaths of at least 24 people in the Pundahar area have resulted in widespread fear in Palma town, where residents feel increasingly threatened by insurgent attacks despite a heavy security force presence.  No shipments of basic goods have reached Palma town for a week, and supply boats into the town from Pemba have also reportedly been at least temporarily stopped.  Foreign traders are also reportedly leaving the town as one Bangladeshi trader was killed in the Pundahar attack.  Many people in the Palma area are reportedly preparing to leave the area, while IDPs in the town and surrounding area receive little to no support.

Media sources said a "very early" curfew is currently being enforced in Palma town, one source said the curfew begins at about 1730hrs.  Local residents also said it is "very dangerous" to talk on the phone due to security force surveillance. This comes after the 11-12 Pundahar attacks which cut the last land route to Pemba, and other insurgent attacks in Palma in recent weeks.

A group of 90 soldiers were reported by local media to have been deployed to Vamizi island to prevent new attacks on the area after insurgent raids on 07 and 11 September.  Since 17 September, locals have not been allowed to leave the island by the security forces.

Two employees of the Urbanization Council and two Municipal Police were suspended for selling 11 cemetery plots in Gondola of Manica province on 20 September. The suspects reportedly sold each land plot for around 3,000-6,000 meticais.

Mozambican Minister of Culture and Tourism, Eldevina Materrula, stated that around 3,000 tourism sector employees return to work as part of the government’s efforts to resume economic activities in stages. Materrula also stated that around 11,000 employees are expected to return to work upon the later phases. The Minister mentioned that the COVID-19 previously affected 95% of the country’s tourism sector.

Organization of Mozambican Workers (OTM) trade union federation called for the resumption of talks regarding an increase in minimum wages. The discussion with the Labour Consultative Commission (CCT) was previously suspended due to COVID-19. OTM stated that the talks should be resumed after restrictive measures are being eased.

City Council officials announced the opening of a COVID-19 emergency center in Maputo on 21 September. Health and Social Action Municipality Councilor, Alice de Abreu, stated that the center will new center will have six sectors to tackle the Coronavirus. The sectors include which includes, diagnosis and surveillance, case management, community mobilization and communication, management of resources and logistics, water, sanitation, hygiene, mobility, and prevention.  The center opened as cases have spiked in the capital, with over half of the country's active cases located in the city.

Mozambique’s foreign trade saw drops in exports of 33.2% and imports of 23.1% respectively during the second quarter of 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The National Statistics Institute (INE) stated that a deficit in the trade balance of goods was around 660.8 million USD.

The Ministry of Health recorded 141 new COVID cases bringing the total cases to 6,912 in Mozambique on 21 September. The total death increased to 44 after a single death was reported.  The new cases included 94 new cases in Maputo City and 23 new cases in Maputo.

The Bank of Mozambique (BM) announced on 21 September that it would implement a unique bank identification number, which can identify fake identities and deter any possible financial crimes, including money laundering and financing of terrorism.

RENAMO dissidents denied on 21 September conducting attacks between Inchope and Gorongosa in the Pungue River crossing area along the N1 road on the morning of 20 September. RENAMO dissident leader, Mariano Nhongo, questioned the accusation and stated that the government should investigate the credibility of the accusations. The Police of the Republic of Mozambique in Sofala previously claimed that the armed attack was conducted by the RENAMO dissidents using AKM-type weapons.
column15: Road N1 between Gorongosa and Nhamatanda

column4: 50 cases of acute diarrhea due to suspected food poisoning were reported in Muthepo village near Memba on 21 September. Local farmers stated that the food poisoning may be due to the seafood bought from the local market. The farmers also stated that several fishermen in the area have subjected to use an illegal fishing method which infected the fish caught.
Unknown men sexually assaulted a 13-year-old child in Machava, west of Maputo, on 21 September.  Locals stated that the suspects were members of the National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC).

7 people were killed when anti-personnel mine exploded in a forest in the Namunaburi area of Pebane District of Zambezia on 14 September.  The group was reportedly poaching in the area and found the device.  The group then took the mine home and attempted to open it, causing it to explode.

The MASC Foundation proposed an initiative for locals to work with security forces by calling out any suspected individual linked with the insurgents in Cabo Delgado. MASC officials stated that the proposal would sensitize the local population and enable them to distance themselves from any suspected insurgent and report them to the authorities.
National Criminal Investigation Service agents detained 3 suspects and recovered four stolen vehicles and 20 forged vehicle registration booklets in Maputo on 20 September.

SERNIC agents detained two suspects for vehicle theft in Maputo on 21 September. The suspects were part of a chop shop and sold the car parts. Two vehicles and a set of forged keys were seized from the suspects.

Police seized a vehicle transporting 12 weapons after the driver and passengers fled upon spotting the police in Chibuto on the evening of 14 September. 22 cartridges, 9 12-gauge shotguns, and a bulletproof vest.
A vehicle collided with a motorcycle in Guro area of Manica province on 14 September. A civilian died and another was injured.
A civilian on a motorcycle ran over and killed a civilian along Matola-Gare Street, Matola, on 14 September.

Three men armed with AK-47s stole 50,000 meticais at a gas station in 3 De Fevereiro, Mocuba, on the morning of 12 September. The victim later filed a report to the police leading to the arrests of the suspects. Police seized three AK-47s and 21 ammunition rounds.

Three men armed with AK-47s stole 50,000 meticais at a gas station in 3 De Fevereiro, Mocuba, on the morning of 12 September. The victim later filed a report to the police leading to the arrests of the suspects. Police seized three AK-47s and 21 ammunition rounds.
Police arrested a suspect for impersonating a policeman in Xai-Xai on 12 September. The suspect attempted to demand 40,000 meticais from another officer leading to his arrest.

The World Food Program said on Tuesday that the insurgency in Cabo Delgado has now displaced over 310,000 people and created an "urgent humanitarian crisis".  The organization said it was "deeply concerned" regarding the situation.  The WFP also said many people have lost access to food and their livelihoods.  The WFP also said it needs $4.7 million a month in order to be able to deliver food in the province, and it hopes to reach 300,000 people with deliveries this month. The WFP also said it expects food insecurity to continue into early 2021 at least.

Mozambique's Ministry of Health on 22 September reported 202 new COVID cases in the country, with 57 cases in Maputo City, 38 in Maputo, 38 in Tete, 35 in Zambezia, 31 in Gaza, 2 in Inhambane, 1 in Cabo Delgado, and 1 in Niassa.  One additional fatality was also reported.  The total number of cases has now risen to 7,144 with 45 deaths.

Mozambique's Ministry of Health said on 21 September that there had been 2,996 COVID infections over the past 3 weeks, or about 43% of all cases reported in the country since the pandemic began.  Deputy National Director of Public Health Beninga Matsinhe said that Mozambique is failing in compliance with preventive measures and that without a change in behavior, the country would see significant pressure applied to the health system".  Matsinhe said that the city of Maputo meanwhile is at risk of exceeding its hospitalization capacity, with about half of its 113 beds prepared for COVID patients currently occupied.

Mozambican police on Tuesday warned that they would take "tough measures" against people violating anti-COVID measures across the country.  Countrywide reports indicate that there are ongoing and large scale violations of the "Situation of Public Calamity" including the not wearing of masks and no attempt at social distancing.  Police also said many businesses are clandestinely selling alcohol against anti-COVID restrictions.

Police officials said on 22 September that they are considering re-imposing a ban on visiting public beaches in Mozambique, saying that many people after the ban on visiting beaches was lifted on 15 September did not adhere to anti-COVID measures such as social distancing and the wearing of masks when visiting the beach.  Authorities say they will re-evaluate the policy over the coming weekend and decide whether or not they will allow public beaches to remain open.

The Mozambican government on 16 September submitted a letter to the EU, requesting support in training and logistics for counter-terrorism forces plus technical training of personnel and medical assistance in combat zones, it was reported on 22 September.  In addition to this military support, Mozambique also said it hoped to receive additional humanitarian support for victims of the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.
Insurgents on 18 September were reported to have abducted two fishermen from Pangane beach.  No other information on this incident is currently available.
Insurgents on 18 September reportedly beheaded 3 people and left their bodies in the middle of the road near Pundahar.  No further information on this attack is currently available.

A local media outlet reported on 22 September that anonymous military sources had confirmed that Mozambican soldiers were responsible for killing a naked women near Awasse, an incident seen in a recent graphic video posted to social media.  The source also said soldiers were acting on "higher orders".  The media source also said that a separate source indicated that the soldiers responsible for the killing had been detained since 15 September.

Mozambican troops have reportedly set up a series of 10 checkpoints along the N1 road between Inchope and Muxungue, and are forcing passing vehicles to pay small bribes.  The troops have been deployed in theory at least to provide security against RENAMO dissident attacks along this route.  An unconfirmed report meanwhile said that an ambulance which had not paid a fee at one of these checkpoints had been fired upon on Sunday afternoon along the N1 road in Sofala.

Mozambican Prime Minister Carlos Agostinho do Rosario announced on 22 September the  start of an anti-cholera vaccination campaign and called for the cooperation of the locals in Cabo Delgado. The PM warned locals to avoid possible disinformation and unconfirmed statements regarding the purpose of the campaign. Previous rumors stated that health workers were spreading the disease rather than preventing it.

Police arrested two suspects for armed robbery charges in Lichinga on 21 September. The suspects were in possession of 2 pistols, 14 ammunition, and several medication from the National Health System. The two arrested are suspected of the murder of a guard who was protecting medical supplies in Lichinga.

The National Penitentiary Service announced they had located fugitive Abdul Afonso Tembe also known as BO, in Manica Central Prison on 22 September. Tembe was caught under a false name of Lucio Antonio Ferreira. Tembe was previously charged with a 12-year sentence for theft and possession of illegal weapons and was in prison serving this sentence.  Tembe was being sought in connection with the slaying of Maputo prosecutor Marcelino Vilanculos in April 2016.
Four vehicles were involved in an RTA in Gorongosa on the afternoon of 21 September. Two civilians were killed and 10 were injured.
Police detained eight suspects for poaching in Panda, Inhambane province on 22 September. 9 various weapons were seized from the suspects during the arrest.

Police in Palma on Tuesday said that they had arrested a "considerable number" of insurgents, including several native to Palma District itself.  No exact number of insurgents was confirmed.  Unconfirmed reports had previously indicated Bonomade Machude Omar or "Ibn Omar", a man identified as one of the top leaders of the insurgency, was among those detained.  Police in Palma also confirmed that at least 28 people had been killed in insurgent attacks from 11-12 September in the Pundahar area, and that these attacks had been launched by a group of 65 insurgents.

Helicopters piloted by South African-based PMC Dyck Advisory Group were reported on 18 September to have fired shots between Licangano and Xinavane villages, southwest of Macomia town at suspected insurgent targets after a local source reported suspicious movements by unknown individuals in the area to authorities.  No details are available regarding any possible casualties. The woman then fled to Macomia town, where they reported these incidents to the authorities.

Insurgents on 22 September abducted a husband and wife in the Litamanda area, reportedly beheading the man in front of his wife before freeing her and telling her to go back to the village she had come from and tell people about the incident.  Insurgents were also alleged to have said they would not leave the Litamanda area.

Elsewhere near Namaluco, southeast of Macomia, insurgents beat a man, giving him 100 lashings before setting him free and telling him to spread the word of their presence to his village. The man in Namaluco  fled to Macomia town, where they reported these incidents to the authorities.

Locals sources stated that Northern Mozambique has experienced a decrease in COVID rates as an average of 12 cases per day was reported over the past 30 days. Officials stated that Cabo Delgado, Niassa and Nampula had also averaged 18 recoveries per day. Southern Mozambique has over that period seen an average of 58 recoveries per day but also an average of 67 new cases per day.

Deputy Justice Minister Filimão Suaze announced 23 September a projected economic growth rate of 2.1 percent for 2021. Suaze mentioned that a draft Economic and Social Plan, and the 2021 Budget have been submitted to the parliament for approval. The budget was planned with the expenditure of around 309 billion meticais and revenue of 266 billion meticais. Suaze also stated that the current inflation rate of the country throughout the year was around 5 percent.

The Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM) Party, accused FRELIMO of preventing MDM to allow it to conduct meetings in Inhambane on 23 September. MDM leader, Daviz Simango, stated that a booked venue at the last minute had said it would not allow MDM to hold a meeting on its premises in Inhambane on 20 September, saying that unknown men threatened the venue owners forcing them to cancel.

The Attorney General announced that 340 cases of corruption were being handled as of the first half of 2020. Central Office for Combating Corruption spokesman, Cristóvão Mondlane, stated that the rate of corruption cases has been increasing since 2015 as corruption cases for the year were reported to be around 437. While 2016 saw 493 cases, 2017 with 695 cases, 2018 with 761 cases, and 2019 recorded 764.

The Ministry of Health recorded 148 new COVID cases and 4 COVID related deaths on 23 September. Officials stated that the deaths were reported in Maputo City bringing the total number of deaths to 49 countrywide. While the number of total cases were reported at 7,262. 79 cases were reported in Maputo, 26 in Tete, 20 in Inhambane, 15 in Maputo province, 3 in Cabo Delgado, 2 in Niassa, 2 in Nampula, and 1 Zambezia.

Robbers broke into the laboratory of the Institute of Health and Sciences and stole around several pieces of lab equipment in Quelimane on 20 September. The stolen devices amounted to 2.6 million meticais. Police conducted a search operation leading to the detention of a suspect and recovered 11 microscopes in the area.

Police recovered 15 stolen microscopes during a search operation for wanted robbers in Namacurra on 20 September. An investigation was conducted to arrest the robbers who stole laboratory equipment from Institute of Health and Sciences in Quelimane.

Ncondezi Energy announced on 23 September that GE’s withdrawal from the new-build coal power 300-megawatt project will not affect the project. Ncondezi Energy also stated that in conjunction with China Machinery Engineering Corporation, a leading investor, that another company can be hired to take over role of GE as the technological partner of the project.

Health authorities conducted a COVID 12-day epidemiological survey of 6,000 locals to determine the spread of the virus in Beira on 22 September. The survey was to determine the percentage of locals infected with the virus and the risk rate of contracting the virus in the area.
A woman set fire to a residence which killed her son in Mossurize of Manica province on 22 September. Police responded and detained the suspect.
A woman set fire to a residence which killed her son in Mossurize of Manica province on 22 September. Police responded and detained the suspect.

Several locals gathered and protested outside a sports club in Maputo city demanding the dismissal of the current board officials for non-payment of the salaries of their employees and players. The protesters also called for the creation of a temporary board of directors due to resolve the issue.
Customs seized a truck transporting smuggled clothing and shoes which had been declared as "locks and insecticides" in Beira on 23 September.

Insurgents in an attack on 24 September reportedly abducted a large number of people, mostly women and children, in Bilibiza.  One unconfirmed report said as many as 200 people were abducted in the incident.

A large group of insurgents on the late afternoon / early evening of 24 September were reported by several sources to have launched a new attack in the village of Bilibiza, resulting in 8 civilians killed.   Sources report that these include 5 civilians who had been beheaded during the attack.  A single source later reported as many as 40 civilians may have been killed in the attack. The insurgents were also reported to have forced a meeting with locals,  and accused them of having raided a nearby abandoned insurgent base. A large number of people, including many children were alleged to have been abducted from the area during this attack.  Further looting and destruction of houses was also reported in the village, with nearly all remaining village inhabitants forced out of the area by the militants.  Insurgents were still reportedly present in the village on the morning of 25 September.  Note that President Nyusi claimed on 24 September that the Mozambican military had repelled an insurgent attack in the area.

Rumors in Palma town on 24 September spread that a group of insurgents had clandestinely entered the town and left threatening messages behind of a coming large-scale attack in the area. After these rumors were spread, security forces deployed into different points around Palma town.  This development occurred as an insurgent attack was reported at Bilibiza and as attack rumors were also reported in Nangade District.

The Ministry of Health recorded 137 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 24 September bringing the total to 7,399 cases. 2 new deaths were reported in Maputo bringing the total to 51 deaths nationwide.  96 of the new cases were recorded in Maputo City, 18 in Maputo Province, 10 in Tete, 6 in Gaza, 2 in Sofala, 1 in Nampula, 1 in Inhambane, and 1 in Zambezia.

The National Migration Service (SENAMI) announced that starting 1 October locals travelling to South Africa must have a PCR Certificate stating a negative test result for COVID which is valid up to 72 hours.

Four education officials were detained on embezzlement charges in Inhassunge of Zambezia province on the afternoon of 24 September. The suspects reportedly embezzled around 700,000 meticais by transferring money from the account of the District Directorate of Education, Youth, Science and Technology to the accounts of their families.

The National Health Institute (INS) announced the preliminary results from an epidemiological survey in Tete on 24 September in which 1,942 people were tested for COVID anti-bodies. INS stated that 0.7 percent have been exposed to COVID. The survey was to determine the prevalence of locals being exposed to the Coronavirus. 1.7 per cent prevalence was reported in the neighborhood of Matundo. 3 of the 10 neighborhoods tested had no positive results for COVID anti-bodies.  The 0.7 prevalence was significantly lower than rates seen in Nampula, Pemba, and Maputo in similar studies.  This would indicate about 2,135 people have had COVID in Tete city.
60,000 people were reported to have been displaced in Cabo Delgado since insurgents captured Mocimboa da Praia on 11 August.  Over 310,000 people have been displaced in the province since 2017.

Security force members were reported to have raped a young girl on the island of Ibo. This incident was reported on 24 September by local media, though it was unclear when this incident occurred. The soldiers were reportedly transferred to other areas of Cabo Delgado after the incident, and were not detained.

Media sources reported that military forces deployed to Ibo Island tightly control the island.  Everyone travelling to and from the island must present "Guias de Marcha" documents giving their name, place of origin, and destination.  Security forces have for the past two months imposed these controls to prevent insurgent attacks on the island.  IDPs arriving to the island are sometimes not forced to present an ID as many have lost these documents while fleeing insurgent impacted areas.  In some cases, security forces detain individuals for interrogation.
Power outages continue to be reported in parts of Meluco, Quissanga, Ibo, Macomia, Muidumbe, Mueda, Nangde, Mocimboa da Praia, and Palma, media sources reported on 24 September.

column4: President Nyusi said on 24 September that Mozambican security forces had "strongly repelled an attack" of insurgents in Bilibiza, Quissanga District, without providing further details.  This contrasts with other reports that insurgents had raided the town, destroyed much of it, killed several locals, and abducted a large number of women from the area.

The Episcopal Conference of Mozambique announced on 24 September that it cancelled the academic year for all its seminaries throughout Mozambique due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, saying that the "exponential" rise in cases in recent weeks had led to this decision.

Rumors of a planned insurgent attack were reported on 24 September in Nangade town.  Similar rumors were reported in Palma and Bilibiza towns; an insurgent attack did target Bilibiza but not Nangade or Palma towns on the evening of 24 September.

Clashes on the afternoon of 25 September were reported in the Bilibiza area, with South African Military Contractor helicopters attacking insurgent positions in the area while fighting was reported between insurgents and Mozambican troops.  Casualties are currently unclear.  Satellite images meanwhile of Bilibiza in the early morning hours of Friday showed village homes on fire.  These clashes came after militants attacked and occupied Bilibiza on the evening of 24 September.

Insurgents were reported to have raided the village of Mahate, Quissanga District on 24 September, setting several huts on fire in the area.  No other details on this incident are currently available.

Police Rapid Intervention Units on 24 September stationed along the N380 road in the Moja/Guenda area were reported to have erected an illegal checkpoint where they charge passing vehicles a fee to pass.  Some passersby are accused of being "insurgents" by the police and charged larger fees, a local resident who passed through the checkpoint reported.

NGO officials on 23 September indicated that over 1,000 refugees in recent weeks have fled from Cabo Delgado into Southern Tanzania.  Previous reports had indicated about 800 Mozambican nationals had fled into Tanzania due to the ongoing insurgency.

Former RENAMO deputy leader Raul Domingos said this week that the demobilization and disarmament campaign targeting armed RENAMO members was a "failure", saying the kinds of material being supplied to former guerillas such as zinc sheets, hoes, machetes, and seeds was not enough to construct a house or allow guerillas to establish a business for themselves.

The UN Sec. General's rep to Mozambique Mirko Manzon said on 24 September that the solution to the insurgency in Cabo Delgado involved dialogue, also saying the ongoing peace process between RENAMO and the government required "continuous dialogue", just as RENAMO dissidents should also be engaged in dialogue.  Manzon also said that about 985 RENAMO guerillas have been demobilized during the ongoing DDR process, with about 4,000 yet to be demobilized.  Manzon said that the DDR process could potentially go according to schedule and be completed by the end of 2021, depending on developments related to the ongoing COVID pandemic.

The Ministry of Sea, Inland Waters, and Fishery announced a 5-month ban on shrimp fishing in Mozambican waters starting 1 November. The ban was to enable the capture of seafood sustainable, according to the Director General of National Fisheries, Cassamo Junior. Cassamo Junior also stated that mangrove crabs fishing would also be banned from 15 October until 31 December.

The National Migration Service of Mozambique (SENAMI) announced on 24 September that 14 Mozambican Embassies worldwide will begin to collect data for issuing and renewing passports and national ID cards by the end of the year. The initial reopening will begin with embassies in Portugal and Ethiopia.

Locals in Matundo are forced to gather water in the Zambezi River due to the constrained water access in Tete. Locals stated that a 5km walk to the river has put civilians at risk with the wildlife in the area, as a civilian was reportedly killed. Fundo do Investimento e Património do Abastecimento de Água (FIPAG) began investigation of the restricted water access.

Eswatini representatives announced on 23 September, that they are willing to provide assistance to Mozambique’s fight against insurgency within Cabo Delgado during a meeting with President Filipe Nyusi.

President Filipe Nyusi conducted a meeting with the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) President, Peter Maurer, on 24 September.  The meeting discussed the impact of COVID and potentially increasing the cooperation and activity of the ICRC within Mozambique.
A car and a truck collided with each other along Route N4 in Matola, west of Maputo, at around 04:30 of 25 September. Three civilians were killed.

President Filipe Nyusi announced on 23 September, during the UN General Assembly that Mozambique is “open to international support to combat terrorism.” The president stated that he welcomed all initiatives and partnerships for assisting to limit the insurgency in Mozambique.

The Ministry of Health recorded 190 new COVID cases and two new COVID deaths in Mozambique on 25 September.  123 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 35 in Inhambane, 18 in Maputo, 10 in Zambezia, 2 in Nampula, 1 in Cabo Delgado and 1 in Tete. The new cases increased the total to 7,589 positive cases while deaths were reported at 53.

Insurgents exchanged gunfire with South African Private Military Contractor helicopters in the mangrove forests between Ilha Ibo and Ilha Quirimba in the early morning of 26 September in the Tandanhague area.  Insurgents reportedly opened fire on four helicopters in the area who returned fire.  No casaulty information is available.
column15: Ilha Ibo and Ilha Quirimba mangroves

column4: Mozambique recorded 226 Coronavirus cases and 4 deaths on 27 September. The cases include 108 in Zambezia and 40 in Maputo city. The deaths were recorded in Tete (1), Inhambane (1), and in Maputo city (2).

Mozambique Police presented 2 individuals accused of recruiting and serving as informants for terrorists in Cabo Delgado. The suspects carried out their actions in Pemba and Montepuez. One of the men is from Nampula and a Montepuez resident, and said his brother-in-law had asked him if he knew any "young people who want to join al Shabaab". The second man arrested is a trader working in Pemba and Mocimboa da Praia, who said insurgents had attempted to convince him to join their movement but that he had refused, though he did aknowldeged sharing military movements with a Tanzanian national who is believed to be a member of the insurgency, including on troop movements and positions. Security officials say the two confessed to having regular contact with terrorists, and in engaging in terror recruitment activities.

Mozambican Police raided a drug factory in Naamacha on 24 September. 7 suspects, including 2 Mozambican and 5 Mexican nationals were arrested. According to reports, drugs produced in the factory were packed in small plastic bags painted with animals, making them appear as bundles of meat. According to the Mexican suspects, they have no knowledge of the drug factory as they were only hired as cattle herders.

Mozambican Police raided a drug factory in Naamacha on 24 September. 7 suspects, including 2 Mozambican and 5 Mexican nationals were arrested. According to reports, drugs produced in the factory were packed in small plastic bags painted with animals, making them appear as bundles of meat. According to the Mexican suspects, they have no knowledge of the drug factory as they were only hired as cattle herders.
A 25-year-old man was arrested on 25 September for sexually assaulting his 5-year-old stepdaughter in Ponta do Ouro the day prior.
A 25-year-old man was arrested on 25 September for sexually assaulting his 5-year-old stepdaughter in Ponta do Ouro the day prior.

Suspected RENAMO dissidents initiated an armed attack on a convoy of three vehicles on the Dombe-Espungabere Road (Road 260), near the Muwawa site in Maquina, Dombe, on Sunday evening 27 September. According to a source on the ground, the suspects were fired on the vehicles after a convoy failed to stop after beinig ordered to do so by the assailants. The attack resulted in 2 people killed and at least 4 wounded.  Authorities later accused the RENAMO dissident group RENAMO Military Junta of having carried out the attack, though the group's leader, Mariano Nhongo, denied responsibility.

A source reported that unknown gunmen (suspected RENAMO dissidents) had fired live ammunition on a farm vehicle between Dombe and Maquina, north of Dombe, on 27 September. The driver escaped unharmed; however, the vehicle sustained some damage.

Reports stated on 27 September that the Mozambique Police in Pemba have detained a religious leader accused of training youths for terrorists gangs. These reports have not been confirmed nor denied by the Mozambican Police.

Three men disappeared on the afternoon of Thursday 24 September while travelling on a bicycle between their village of Segundo Congresso and Pundanhar along the river Rovuma river.  They were found killed on 25 September.

Three men disappeared on the afternoon of Thursday 24 September while travelling on a bicycle between their village of Segundo Congresso and Pundanhar along the river Rovuma river.  They were found killed on 25 September.

On 24 September, armed men attacked a vehicle transporting people and goods on the road between Nangade and Pundanhar. The vehicle and its cargo were set on fire. Another source later reported two people were killed in this attack.

The Ministry of Health on 26 September reported 168 new COVID cases with 1 new death.  82 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 36 in Maputo, 17 in Zambezia, 14 in Inhambane, 7 in Tete, 4 in Gaza, 3 in Sofala, 2 in Manica, 2 in Niassa, and 1 in Cabo Delgado.  This brought the nationwide total of cases to 7,757 with 58 deaths.

Police Commander Bernardino Rafael said on Saturday that insurgents do not control Mocimboa da Praia and other locations in Cabo Delgado, saying that while some villages had been abandoned due to ongoing fighting, that militants did not occupy these villages.  Rafael also said that while security forces were not present in MDP, they did "exercise greater control" than the insurgents in the town.  This statement came despite multiple reports over the past last month and half that the insurgency does in fact control the town.  Rafael also indicated that security forces had recovered the island of Vamizi, and had also "displaced" terrorists from the islands of Vumba, Quifungo, and Mitundo.
column15: MDP and other insurgent held areas

column4: Sporadic gunfire was reported on the morning of 28 September at around 0400hrs in Palma as troops deployed throughout the town.  One source reported that security forces were believed to have received information about insurgent operations in the town after capturing at least one insurgent, and had launched an operation to target militants.  No other information on this incident is currently available.

Mozambique on 28 September reported 305 new cases of COVID-19, a record number of cases, along with one new death.  165 new cases were reported in Maputo City, along with 76 cases in Maputo.  This brings the total number of cases to 7,993 in the country and total deaths to 59.

Local media reported that product prices in Palma have increased significantly with the cutting of the Palma-Pundanhar road.  Gasoline prices have increased to 300 meticais per liter vs. 64 meticais per liter before the road was closed.  There is also a growing possibility of a food shortage in the town.  Sources also say IDPs continue to arrive into Palma, both by land and by boat.  This includes nearly 35,000 people displaced into the district from neighboring Mocimboa da Praia.
Over 1,500 IDPs were reported to have fled the Bilibiza area into Metuge after insurgents entered the town on 24 September.

US Assistant Secretary for African Affairs Tibor Nagy was reported in the past week to have asked Zimbabwe Foreign Minister Sibusiso Moyo for Harare’s assistance to combat the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  Moyo countered by asking that the US first drop sanctions against Zimbabwean officials before any intervention in Cabo Delgado.

Officials announced the closure of a ticketing booth of the National Directorate of Civil Identification (DNIC) branch for 24 hours in Maputo on 29 September after one of its employees tested positive for COVID. The closure was to enable a sterilization team to conduct disinfection procedures. 14 other employees were placed under home quarantine after contact tracing.

The US Trade and Development Agency (USTDA) intends to expand Mozambique’s energy sector by funding two projects in Praia da Rocha. Ventos de Inhambane was to develop a wind power plant with energy storage near Delphos International which will undertake the study. The second project was by Globeleq Calanga Wind, which would develop a two-phase wind power project with energy storage in the Manhiça district. The study will be performed by DNV GL Energy USA.

The Mozambican Minister of Economy and Finance announced that the government would have to redirect resources to fund and support the war against insurgency in Cabo Delgado. Adriano Maleiane stated that the government is short of funds for the war effort and would have to "invent" to allocate more funds to the military.

An economy consultancy company stated that Mozambique in 2020 will likely see negative growth of 1.3 percent due to the COVID pandemic.  This would be the first negative growth year in the country in 30 years. Mozambique is expected to recover solidly with a predicted 2.9 percent growth rate by 2021. The growth rate is anticipated with the inflation rate of 3.2 percent during 2020 and 4.1 by 2021.

A credit rating agency announced that Mozambique will experience difficulties in reversing its growing debt, which is expected to surpass 100 percent GDP this year due to the development of the gas sector. The credit rating agency also stated that the country’s recovery will depend on its economic response and improvements along with the development of the gas sector of the country.
