RENAMO leader, Ossufo Momade, stated that his party members were targeted and harassed politically by FRELIMO. Momade stated that the political intolerance against his members threatened the coexistence between political parties. Momade also said RENAMO is complying with the DDR process and that they should not be politically targeted.

Military personnel expressed dissatisfaction against the mandatory deduction of a day of salary to support the local sports clubs in Maputo and Mocuba associated with the armed forces on 28 September. The military personnel also stated that the support should not be mandatory.  This deduction came as many soldiers, including even those deployed to active fighting zones in Cabo Delgado, are often reported not to receive their pay on time.
Police arrested a suspect after stabbing and injuring a civilian during a dispute over the scratch of the suspect’s vehicle in Fernao Veloso, north Nacala on the evening of 27 September.
Police arrested a suspect in possession of a shotgun suspected to be used with a previous murder in Naherenque, north Nacala on 27 September.

Insurgents were reported to have attacked the Cagembe area on 22 September, killing two people in a village raid and beating several others.  Unverified reports also said homes were destroyed in the area and that some people were kidnapped by insurgents.  Insurgents reportedly gathered civilians together in the village and accused them of having looted a nearby former insurgent base.

Insurgents on 24 September ambushed a state electricity team's vehicle between Mueda and Mocimboa da Praia near Awasse, destroying the vehicle.  One EDM worker was killed in the attack as he was working on an electricity line, while the other workers fled the scene.

268 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 29 September, increasing the total number of nationwide cases to 8,556 with 59 deaths.  199 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 31 cases in Maputo, 31 in Zambezia, 4 in Inhambane, 2 in Tete, and 1 in Nampula.

There are reportedly divisions between political and military leaders on how best to proceed to retake Mocimboa da Praia.  Some military leaders reportedly want the assault to be led by South African Military Contractor helicopters, aerially bombarding the insurgents before being followed by a ground assault.  Some officers have argued that the town has been effectively emptied of civilians and contains only insurgents, while political leaders are more cautious regarding potential civilian casualties in the town.

Residents of Mafambisse, Sofala Province on Monday held a demonstration in the town calling for an end to RENAMO dissident attacks and conflict between the opposition and government.  This came after RENAMO dissident attacks in Manica over the weekend.  RENAMO Military Junta chief Mariano Nhongo had previously threatened to launch attacks in Mafambisse to "paralyze" sugar production in the area after Nhogo's son was allegedly fired upon by security forces.

Insurgents were reported to have killed an unknown number of civilians and 2 Mozambican soldiers last week in a raid in the Naliendele village area, northwest of Palma town.  At least 3 people were injured in the clashes.  One other source said that 5 soldiers were killed in the fighting.

Minister of Economy and Finance, Adriano Maleiane, stated on 29 September that the Mozambican state will lose around 21 billion meticais or about 249 million euros in revenue due to the ongoing COVID pandemic.  He also indicated that the tourism sector has been the worst impacted in the country. Maleiane also mentioned that the drop in revenue will lead to the rearrangement of priorities, so that the larger and more important goals are not affected.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Verónica Macamo, stated on 29 September that the Mozambican government does not currently intend to request assistance from the United Nations to send a peacekeeping force to combat insurgents in Cabo Delgado. Macamo mentioned that the Defense and Security Forces are currently deployed to counter the insurgency are effective.

Deputy National Director of Public Health, Benigna Matsinhe, announced that locals must focus on following anti-COVID recommendations after the recent sudden increase in COVID cases in recent weeks. Matsinhe stated that over the last 7 days, 1,071 people tested positive and 14 deaths were reported across the country.  Maputo continues to be the epicenter of the outbreak in the country.

Insurgents attacked a border guard position near Nyica do Rovuma village, 7km from the Rovuma River, and about 29 kms / 18 miles northwest of Palma, on the afternoon of 28 September.  Insurgents killed at least one border guard in the attack and drove other guards away from the area.  The insurgents also set fire to the village after this attack.

Insurgents attacked a border guard position near Nyica do Rovuma village, 7km from the Rovuma River, and about 29 kms / 18 miles northwest of Palma, on the afternoon of 28 September.  Insurgents killed at least one border guard in the attack and drove other guards away from the area.  The insurgents also set fire to the village after this attack.

Insurgents abducted a couple and asked them which village they lived before infiltrating Nyica do Rovuma village, 7km from the Rovuma River, and about 29 kms / 18 miles northwest of Palma, on the afternoon of 28 September. The insurgents later then attacked a border guard positions and set the village on fire.  The husband later escaped insurgent custody; it is unclear if the woman escaped however.

A fire was reported at lumber storage areas in Diaca and N'nango village of Mocimboa da Praia district on the evening of 29 September. The fire was suspected to have been initiated by insurgent attacks in the areas.

A fire was reported at lumber storage areas in Diaca and N'nango village of Mocimboa da Praia district on the evening of 29 September. The fire was suspected to have been initiated by insurgent attacks in the areas.
Insurgents on 22 September beheaded 5 people near Novo Cabo Delgado village, killing the five as they were working in fields in the area.

Some Palma residents have reportedly been issued arms to protect the town and their communities from potential insurgent attacks, several sources reported in recent days.  It is suspected, though not confirmed, that these arms have  been provided by government agents.

Local sources reported that security forces on 30 September killed a suspected RENAMO dissident militant in Sofala.  An unconfirmed video appeared online showing a deceased man, allegedly the militant, bearing head wounds and sprawled on the ground near uniformed Mozambican military personnel.  These reports also stated that the militant had been captured and then executed by security forces.  The exact location of this incident within Sofala Province is currently unclear though is likely along the N1 road where RENAMO dissident attacks have occurred in the past.

An insurgent attack on 30 September was reported in the Pangane area, with insurgents reportedly setting several area homes on fire and spreading panic in the town. Insurgents in this attack destroyed the home of the village's mayor and detained civilians in a mosque.  Several people were reported missing following this attack.

The Ministry of Health issued a warning that all companies and institutions should prepare facilities and training employees for managing possible COVID cases within their workplaces. These facilities should include an "isolation room" for those suspected to have COVID.  The warning comes in response to the constant increase in COVID cases around the country.
The Mozambican Football Federation announced that four members of the national football team tested positive for COVID will remain in Mozambique after the team was to attend an event in Lisbon.

The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) suspended several commercial establishments due to the employees testing positive for COVID in Maputo city on 30 September. INAE spokesman Tomás Timba stated that the infrastructures did not comply with the safety preventive measures and exposed their workers to the virus. INAE also stated that there was a lack of safety equipment at these establishments which includes masks and disinfection equipment.

The President of the Republic, Filipe Nyusi, announced on 30 September that the government would intensify inspections and accountability as part of increase safety measures against the pandemic. Nyusi stated that the beaches would remain open as a show of his trust to the public to abide to the safety precautions.

The Ministry of Health (MISAU) recorded on 30 September 172 new COVID cases and two more deaths bringing the total number of cases to 8,728 and total deaths to 61. The highest number of daily cases were reported in Maputo City as 88 cases were reported. with 23 recorded in Zambezia. 22 in Maputo province, 14 in Sofala, 9 in Inhambane, 8 in Gaza, 4 in Niassa, two in Cabo Delgado, and one in Nampula.

Confederation of Economic Associations President and Businessman, Agostinho Vuma, who was attacked and injured by unidentified assailants in July, called for justice and increased attention by security forces on targeted attacks on businessmen and employees in Maputo on 30 September. Vuma stated that his attackers were still unidentified even three months after the attack and that security officials have not even contacted him regarding his case.

Locals sources stated on 30 September that two family members were killed after being beaten to death by another family due to a dispute over livestock in Magude. The Chongo family attempted to retrieve lost cattle which led to the dispute and attack on the family.

The Red Cross of Mozambique stated that it has been facing problems in assisting IDPs, armed attacks victims’ due areas where the victims took refuge. The organization worries that its volunteers may get caught in attacks as they travel to the refugee location in the central region of the country, where the insurgency is occurring.

President of the Republic, Filipe Nyusi, announced that Mozambique intends to have 20 percent of its energy coming from renewable sources by 2040 as part of the Renewable Energy Initiative. The project was to promote public and private investment as projections indicate 8% of average annual demand for electricity over the next 25 years. The project also aims to allow more than 10 million Mozambicans to have access to electricity by 2024.

Locals recovered the body of an elder local along the beach in Praia do Fernao Veloso, north Nacala, on 30 September. The victim was intending to fish in the beach. Police recovered a knife, an iron rod for spear fishing, and a plastic bag near the victim.

A fire broke out due to unknown origins north of Mocimboa da Praia in the Malinde village area on 29 September. It was not clear if the fire was related to insurgent activity.  Insurgents do remain in control of MDP town, though it is unclear if they control Malinde and nearby areas.

A fire broke out in Assane area the north of Palma near the Rovuma River border on 29 September. It was not clear if the fire was related to insurgent activity. Assane is just across the river from Tanzania.
Locals  warned that many attacks by suspected RENAMO dissidents in Central Mozambique are not being reported by the media.

President Nyusi said on 30 September that all intensive care beds in Maputo City had been occupied and that bed occupancy rates in the capital had tripled over the last 3 weeks.  Nyusi also said that new COVID cases would not be able to be referred to hospitals in Maputo or be given a ventilator.  Health officials previously said there were around 115 intensive care beds set aside for COVID patients in Maputo.  Nyusi also again said that Mozambicans are too relaxed in the fight against COVID and often do not adhere to anti-COVID measures, saying his government intends to "tighten up the inspection and accountability measures".

Around 168,800 12th grade students return to school as classes resume around the country on 1 October after having been closed down for months due to the ongoing pandemic.  The Minister of Education and Human Development stated that 222 schools out of 311 schools, or about 71% of schools are resuming classes after inspections.  Students will attend classes three times a week, for a maximum of 4 hours and 30 minutes a day.  Classes in grades without exams will resume on 19 October.  Grade 10 classes will resume on 19 October countrywide, while grade 7 classes will resume on 02 November.

The PRM Commander-in-Chief, Bernardino Rafael, stated that gold miners in Cabo Delgado were linked to terrorism. Rafael called on the locals to be vigilant and denounce any form of insurgency within communities. Rafael also stated that he intends to reinforce the police to provide order and security within Montepuez district.

Two vehicles and trailers were attacked on 30 September between Mucojo and Macomia.  The vehicles, which were owned by General Alberto Chipande, were transporting cattle out of the Pangane area after an insurgent attack.  Both vehicles were set on fire and destroyed, and the whereabouts of the drivers and the cattle are currently unknown.

Local media indicated insurgents had left behind threatening messages in Pangane after a raid in the town on 30 September of an attack on Macomia town to "commemorate" 3 years of insurgency, saying that militants would arrive into the Macomia area on the night of 04 October, just ahead of the anniversary of the 05 October 2017 attack on MDP that began the insurgency. The threat comes after two vehicles and trailers were attacked on 30 September between Mucojo and Macomia.

Local media on 29 September reported that one of the insurgency's top leaders is a man named Abdala Likonga, a native of Mocimboa da Praia.  Likonga reportedly studied Islam in Kenya and the DRC before returning to Mozambique.  He later faked his death before joining the insurgency, and participated in the 2017 attack on MDP.  Sources also alleged that Likonga received terror training in the DRC - a potential reference to alleged insurgent connections to the Islamic State-affiliated Allied Democratic Forces of the DRC.  Likonga is also sometimes known by the moniker "ghost of the jungle".  Likonga works closely with Bonomade Machude Omar, also known as Ibn Omar, believed to be another of the group's top leaders in MDP.

Unconfirmed media reports said that insurgents in an attack on 26 September killed 6 family members in Chai Administrative Post near the south bank of the Messalo River at Cabo Delgado Communal Village, decapitating all 6, which included two men, two women, and two children.  A similar beheading attack was reported on 22 September in the Novo Cabo Delgado village area.
column15: South Bank of Messalo River, Chai AP, Cabo Delgado Communcal Village area

column4: Media sources reported on 30 September that Portugal and France have both separately explored possibly providing military support to Mozambique in Cabo Delgado, but that President Nyusi has refused these offers of potential support and prefers to continue to use South African private military contractors as the only supplemental force to Mozambican troops in the province.

Reports said Mozambican troops in the Mucojo area had clashed with insurgents in the early morning hours of 30 September at around 0400hrs.  Security forces were later reported to have withdrawn from the area after realizing they were significantly outnumbered by the attacking insurgents.  Militants were believed to have attacked with more than 100 fighters.  Insurgents were later reported in this attack to have killed 10 soldiers in a barrakcs in the town.

Local sources reported insurgents over the weekend attacked the Nabubussi area of Mocimboa da Praia town, one of the few areas where local residents had remained after insurgents captured MDP on 11 August.  Militants set fire to multiple homes in the area, and villagers fled.  No other information on this attack is currently available.

Mozambique government issued a public tender for four renewable energy projects investments expected to be worth around 200 million EUR. The tender was to install three solar farms in Sofala, Tete, Niassa, and Inhambane provinces. Each of the energy projects would be able to produce 40 megawatts of electricity. The initiative aims to promote alternative sources of quality and low-cost energy.

An alleged Islamic State Central Africa Province (ISCAP) infographic claimed that the insurgent groups in Cabo Delgado conducted 118 attacks and have inflicted 909 casualties in Mozambique in 2020.  The infographic also claimed that the militant group operated in Tanzania and attacks were not publicized by the media. The group's info graphic also claimed group fighters had killed 23 people in the DRC and 9 people in Tanzania during the course of the year as well.

The Minister of Health announced that 442 deaths due to malaria occurred during January to August across Mozambique.  About 8.36 million cases of malaria have been reported across Mozambique.  Half of the cases were recorded in Nampula and Zambezia.

Government officials announced on 30 September the continuation of the alcohol sale and consumption ban around public places in Mozambique. Officials also reiterated that offenders will be fined or may be detained. The Minister of the Interior stated that beaches, parks, avenues, roads, sidewalks, bus stops, taxi ranks and markets are all covered by the ban. The municipal authorities would ensure compliance with measures aimed at minimizing the spread of COVID-19.

Health authorities announced 1 October that almost half of the recorded COVID cases in Mozambique occurred during September.  4,812 infections were reported during the month with 38 deaths. Authorities stated that the pandemic is accelerating in the country.

The Ressano Garcia border crossing between Mozambique and South Africa reopened after South Africa closed all of its borders due to the COVID-19 pandemic.  South African officials stated that 32 out of 56 border posts were operational due to the pandemic. South Africa's borders with Zimbabwe and Botswana remain closed for the time being as these two countries are attempting to prevent the spread of COVID into their countries. South Africa is also opening its ports and will allow the loading and off-loading of cargo.  South Africa also announced it would not allow tourist travelers from 60 countries with high COVID rates.

Thousands of Mozambicans were denied entry to South Africa due to inconsistencies with their COVID tests and test results on 2 October. Locals sources stated that some of the test results did not indicate if the traveler was negative for COVID. Others reportedly obtained the certificate required beyond the 48-hour requirement to travel out of Mozambique.
Police arrested a suspect for sexually assaulting his 15-year-old daughter in Maputo on 1 October. The suspect claimed he conducted the crime due to the victim being possessed.
Police arrested a suspect for sexually assaulting his 15-year-old daughter in Maputo on 1 October. The suspect claimed he conducted the crime due to the victim being possessed.

RENAMO drafted a resolution calling for an investigation on the suspected human rights violations in Cabo Delgado, Niassa, Sofala and Manica provinces on 01 October. RENAMO parliamentary bench rapporteur, Venâncio Mondlane, stated that the document was submitted for deliberation to the Permanent Commission of the Assembly of the Republic.
column15: Cabo Delgado, Niassa, Sofala and Manica

column4: Former President Joaquim Chissano stated that the government should identify an "interlocutor" among the insurgents of Cabo Delgado in order to open a potential dialogue with the militants to end fighting in the province. Chissano said the government should "dig for the reason for this war" in order to better understand its causes and identify potential solutions.
column15: Cabo Delgado, Niassa, Sofala and Manica

column4: The Ministry of Health recorded 160 new Coronavirus cases and 1 death in Mozambique on 1 October. Maputo city recorded 110 new case which was followed by 26 cases in Maputo province. The total number of cases have increased to 8,888 while a total of 62 deaths were reported.

Around 200 truck drivers conducted a protest along the N1 Highway in Bobole, north of Marracuene District on the afternoon of 1 October demanding improved working conditions. The protesters also condemned suspected illegal activities conducted by their managers. The truck drivers said they are paid low wages, their vehicles are poorly maintained, and that they are regularly targeted by police for minor infractions.  The demonstrations occurred along a 3km stretch of the road though truck drivers did not block the route.  The drivers said they would not leave the site until their demands were met.

A group of insurgents in the early morning hours of 30 September attacked Mucojo town, occupying it and setting fire to homes and government buildings.  Fires were reported in the town up to 04 October.

Total CEO Patrick Pouyanne on 01 October said during a press conference that a "Daesh enclave is settling within Mozambique" calling this a major problem for East African stability, and saying that it would be "good if the situation is brought back under control, not just for Total's project but for the stability of the region".

Sources in Palma reported there was no power in the town since 25 September, and that diesel supplies for generators had run out in much of the town.  The BIM bank was closed on 30 September indefinitely while BCI bank reportedly plans to close on 01 October, also for an unknown amount of time.  It was unclear if Standard Bank, also in the town, would remain open.  These latest reports came as insurgents have menaced sea lanes between Palma and Pemba as well as the Pundanhar road over the past month.  Fuel prices have become significant inflated in the town, as have prices for food and other supplies.
Mozambique Football Federation cancelled the 2020 season due to the pandemic on 2 October. The federation as forced to take action and interrupt the sports season due to the decision by FIFA.
The Mozambican Basketball Federation, Roque Vicente Sebastiao, tested positive for COVID after returning back to the country on 2 October.
Police arrested two Nigerians in possession of two kilograms of cocaine in Matola, west of Maputo city, on 23 September.

An 02 October analysis piece said that the Mozambican Navy possesses just 12 patrol and coastal combatant vessels to cover its coast of about 1,535 miles - or one vessel for every 127 miles.  2020 estimates meanwhile indicate that there are probably only about 200 active naval officers out of the combined 11,200 personnel of the Mozambican armed forces.  Mozambique in recent years did purchase 3 HSI 32 interceptor naval patrol vessels, and was given 10 speedboats and two other interceptor vessels by Portugal and India in 2018-2019.  Despite efforts to bolster this force, Mozambique's ability to control and enforce law and order within its own maritime territory remains limited.  This was demonstrated recently in August and September attacks by insurgents on islands off the Palma and MDP District coasts.  Mozambique at least in the short term does not have the capacity to curtail insurgent amphibious attacks via small dhows on islands close to the Cabo Delgado coast, and will either need to increase its number of vessels and personnel operating in these waters or call on allies to provide naval support in this area.

Security forces recovered the body of a 25-year-old woman who was sexually assaulted and murdered near the Machava Stadium, west of Maputo, on 2 October. The victim reportedly went missing on 30 September while traveling to her boyfriend's house from Maputo city.

The Ministry of Health recorded 91 new COVID cases bringing the total cases up to 8,979 in Mozambique on 2 October. Two additional deaths were reported increasing the total to 64. Majority of the COVID cases were reported in Maputo city as 73 cases were recorded. 7 cases were also Tete province which was the second highest daily cases.

Minister of the Interior, Amade Miquidade announced that police will enforce safety precautions in minimizing the COVID-19 pandemic in Mozambique. The Police will work in coordination with the Ministry of Health, the National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE), the National Land Transport Institute (INATTER), and local and municipal authorities in imposing the precautions.

A fire broke out in Mucojo at the dawn of 2 October. No information was stated as to what started the fire. Insurgents activity is existing within the areas of Mucojo as previous attacks have occurred in the area.

Insurgents conducted an attack by setting fire to residences and killing villagers in Naunde village in the administrative post of Mucojo in the early morning hours of 3 October. Locals sources stated that private military contractor helicopters were travelling towards the village. Insurgents also were alleged to have attacked the Kirimiza/Crimiza area, just north of Olumboa, which was also targeted by insurgents in recent weeks.
A fire broke out in west Diaca village area on the afternoon of 1 October; this may be a potential insurgent attack, though this is currently unconfirmed.

Officials stated that poaching activity in Niassa continued to increase as 400 poaching traps were seized during the month of August in reserve areas in the province. 500 traps for small animals were previously found during the first half of 2020.
Security forces detained an insurgent in Matemo Island on 3 October. The insurgent was later brought to Ibo Island.

Insurgents reportedly attacked and set fire to Crimiza/Krimisi, south of Mucojo, on 3 October.  Insurgents in this area also reportedly forcibly recruited several young men into the group in this area. Locals were reportedly fleeing to Pagane and Mucojo areas due to the attack. Casualty information was currently unavailable. Insurgent attacks were also reported in Naunde village.
Fires were reported again in Mucojo at the dawn of 3 October; it was unclear if fires in the area were set on the day or during a 30 September insurgent attack.

Fires broke out in Bangalla II, south Macomia on the morning of 3 October. No details as to what started the fires and if the incident was related to insurgents. Insurgent attacks in the area of Macomia have been increasing during past weeks.

Instituto Nacional de Petróleo (INP) president Carlos Zacarias stated that Mozambique LNG and Rovuma LNG projects will conduct major investments in local companies, with $2.5 billion to go to local companies. This is expected to create about 5,000 new jobs in Cabo Delgado during construction, with another 1,000 jobs to be created during operations.
Police arrested a young man in Matola, Maputo, for vandalizing surveillance cameras, as reported by a local media outlet on 4 October.

Fires were reported in Mucojo on 4 October, after insurgents were reported to have attacked the town on 30 September  It was unclear if fire was set on 30 Sep or if fires burning in the town were set during a new attack on 03 Oct.

Fires were reported in Mucojo and Diaca, near Mocimboa da Praia on 4 October. It remains unknown whether these fires are due to terrorist attacks; however, fires were reported in both areas over recent days.

Five armed men attacked a passenger transport vehicle after the bus driver attempted to remove a barricade placed by the gunmen in Subida dos Macuas, approx. 40 Km. away from Mavago in Niassa province, at around 03:00 on Friday morning, 2 October. The attack resulted in the death of the driver. The criminals were also reported to have seized more than 85,000 meticais and 6 mobile phones from the passengers. This incident has been confirmed by the Public Relations Department of the Mozambican Police in Niassa. A search is underway to track down the perpetrators.  Sources later indicated the incident was not likely linked to the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  One incident February attack incident reportedly involving insurgents did occur in Niassa's Mecula District, but this has been to date the only incident believed to be linked to the insurgency to have occurred in the province.

Sources reported on 2 October that helicopters were seen flying over Pemba beach areas to conduct patrols. Conflicting reports have indicated that the helicopters bombed the vicinity of the Londo lighthouse; however this has been denied by other sources.
Mozambique recorded 147 Coronavirus cases and 2 deaths on 4 October. 104 of these cases and 2 of the reported deaths were recorded in Maputo City, while 26 cases were recorded in Maputo province.

A report on 3 October has indicated that at least 839 Mozambicans who were previously displaced to Tanzania in the Kitaya area along the banks of the Rovuma River due to the Cabo Delgado insurgency have been forcibly returned to Mozambique. The civilians are now at the Negomano border in Mueda.  Many IDPs displaced in MDP and Palma District had recently fled into Tanzania after insurgents have either cut off or menaced alternative routes south away from conflict zones in Cabo Delgado.
Mozambique recorded 70 Coronavirus cases and 141 recoveries on 3 October.
Pro-government militia clashed on 30 September in the Magaia area north of Muidumbe with insurgents, leaving one militant dead.  Insurgents had attempted to attack the village.

A group of insurgents advancing on Muidumbe / Namacade town on the morning of 03 October was engaged by a pro-government militia group in the Magaia area, north of Muidumbe/Nacade.  The militia included "war veterans".  A group of at least 7 insurgents was allowed to enter the village, and then was attacked by the militia, who captured 5 militants, while two escaped.  The insurgents were driven back towards Miangalewa, a town the militants have been constantly active around.  No information on casualties is currently available. Sources also indicated a similar skirmish had taken place in the area on 30 September, with one person killed, though no other details are currently available regarding this previous clash.
A road accident killed 4 civilians and wounded several others at least 10 Km away from the Lingonha River in Zambezia on the morning of 5 October.

Reports on 3 October indicate that military personnel from one of the barracks in Mueda have complained about living in quarters for several months without any date for being demobilized The military personnel also threatened to speak out against their leaders and called for greater "freedom", stating "We are human and free, not in prison. We have biological needs!"  Mueda is the site of a large military base critical to the fight against the ongoing Cabo Delgado insurgency.

A woman stole a newborn baby from her friend in Polana Canico, Maputo, on 3 October. This came after the suspect pretended to be pregnant for months to avoid being kicked out of their home. SERNIC arrested the suspect, following a search.

A woman stole a newborn baby from her friend in Polana Canico, Maputo, on 3 October. This came after the suspect pretended to be pregnant for months to avoid being kicked out of their home. SERNIC arrested the suspect, following a search.

Road users complained of different toll prices on 3 toll gates on N6 in Dondo and Nhamatanda in Sofala, as well as in Vanduzi in Manica. The users stressed that different toll prices does not make sense as it is on the same road.
column15: N6 in Dondo, Nhamatanda, and Vanduzi

column4: Residents were reported to have fled from Pangane and Mucojo villages in Cabo Delgado from 30 September - 04 October following multiple insurgent attacks in the area.  Over 1,000 people fled to Macomia town in recent days.
Insurgents on 04 October were reported to have attacked the Guludo area, setting several homes on fire.  No other information on this attack is currently available.

Prices of basic goods were reported to have increased in Mueda as the area continues to be hit by electricity outages.  The cost of a bucket of water was reported to have increased by 5X from 10 to 50 meticais, for example.

A Pemba man was arrested by authorities in the port city in recent days on suspicion that he is connected to the ongoing insurgency.  The man was reported to have recently obtained a large amount of wealth by unclear means.

Insurgents on 04-05 October were reportedly gathering spoils captured from raids in the Mucojo area in recent days.  Insurgents reportedly had taken 4 vehicles along with 3 small motorboats, and were loading food and other supplies into the vehicles and boats for transport to Mocimboa da Praia.  Insurgents reportedly piloted these boats north of MDP on 04 October, and returned for more supplies to the beaches around Mucojo on 05 October.  These vessels reportedly travel by night to avoid being targeted by DAG helicopters.

Soldiers in the village of Nanga, just north of Macomia in Cabo Delgado on Monday night fired multiple small arms rounds for unknown reasons, though local sources later reported soldiers had not engaged insurgents.  Many local residents fled into the bush at the sound of gunfire

The Ministry of Health recorded 100 new COVID cases increasing the total to 9296 cases in Mozambique on 5 October. 9000 cases were reported to be local transmission while 296 were from outside the country. A majority of the cases were recorded in Maputo Province with 38 cases. Followed by Maputo city with 29, 16 in Sofala, 8 in Tete, 4 in Inhambane, 2 in Cabo Delgado, 2 in Zambezia, and one in Gaza.  The death toll remains at 66 countrywide.

Malawi Foreign Affairs Minister, Lucky Sikwese, visited Mozambique as part of a  trip strengthening diplomatic ties between the countries. Malawi Foreign Affairs Minister intends to conduct a meeting with President Filipe Nyusi in Songo. Sikwese will also visit the Cahora Basa hydro power Dam as part of the Malawi and Mozambique interconnection project to provide electrical supply to Malawi.

Port officials have begun testing ship crews from areas at risk to COVID upon entering and exiting the Port of Beira on 6 October. The testing comes as the port began receiving large cargo vessels and the resumed commercial activity.

False negative COVID test certificates were reported be sold to travelers intending to travel to South Africa near the Ressano Garcia border post on 6 October. Authorities stated that they have begun to identify the suspects and  to have an "even more controllable or verifiable document."

International Monetary Fund approved the issuance of emergency aid to 28 of the world's poorest countries, including Mozambique on 5 October. The measure was placed to assist the countries to cover their dept repayments with the IMF for the upcoming six months and enable the countries to provide medical and relief efforts to the locals during the pandemic.

Police detained two suspects and recovered two stolen vehicles in Maputo Special Reserve, southeast of Maputo, on the morning of 5 October. The vehicles were suspected to have been driven from Ponta do Ouro border crossing and to have come from South Africa.  One suspect confirmed that the "owner" of the vehicles was to take possession of them in the Salamanga area.

Insurgents clashed with security forces in two separate incidents on 30 September in Pangane.  A small force of under 50 security force members was driven out of the town, though no casualty figures were confirmed.  Insurgents in a separate incident set parts of the village on fire.  Sources later indicated 2 soldiers and 5 civilians were killed in this attack.

Helicopters manned by South African private military contractors on 30 September attacked insurgents in the Mucojo area as militants raided area villages.  The helicopters temporarily forced insurgents to halt these attacks, but after flying back to Pemba, insurgent attacks in the area resumed.  No information on casualties was received.

An insurgent attack was reported on 30 September on the village of Rueia southwest of Mucojo, burning down several structures in the village and carrying out looting.  Insurgents beheaded at least 3 people in this attack. Insurgents between 30 September and 02 October beheaded another 3 people in a separate incident.  3 others were killed in a nearby village as well.  This was part of a larger spree of attacks in the area during these days by insurgents, in which militants travelled by motorbike between villages.

An insurgent attack was reported between 30 September and 02 October on the village of Nambo northeast of Mucojo, burning down several structures in the village and carrying out looting.  This was part of a larger spree of attacks in the area during these days by insurgents.

An insurgent attack was reported between 30 September and 02 October on the village of Runho near Mucojo, burning down several structures in the village  and carrying out looting.  This was part of a larger spree of attacks in the area during these days by insurgents.

An insurgent attack on 01 October was reported on the village of Messano southeast of  Mucojo, burning down several structures in the village and carrying out looting.  This was part of a larger spree of attacks in the area during these days by insurgents.  Insurgents also threatened local villagers to leave the area and not return.

An insurgent attack was reported between 30 September and 02 October on the village of Manica west of  Mucojo along the road to Macomia, burning down several structures in the village, and carrying out looting.  This was part of a larger spree of attacks in the area during these days by insurgents.

An insurgent attack was reported between 30 September and 02 October on the village of Nambija near Mucojo, burning down several structures in the village and carrying out looting.  This was part of a larger spree of attacks in the area during these days by insurgents.

Authorities on Tuesday announced the emergency closure of the Ressano Garcia Border Crossing from 1200 - 1700hrs after a border guard officer at the Lebombo Crossing Point on the South Africa side tested positive for COVID-19.  This is Mozambique's busiest single border crossing and was only fully re-opened on 01 October after South Africa announced a gradual lifting of anti-COVID measures.

5 people were injured on the morning of 06 October along the Inchope-Muxungue section of the N1 road after gunmen suspected to be RENAMO dissident opened fire on a bus carrying passengers that was part of a convoy travelling north.  A police escort was present but did not engage the attackers.  The attack occurred on Tuesday at around 0800hrs, about 30 kms north from Muxungue.  The gunmen had fired from forest areas alongside the road.  One person was hit in the thigh with a bullet and was in stable condition; the other 4 received only minor injuries.  Police later said they believed RENAMO dissidents carried out the attack.
column15: N1 Road, 30 minutes' drive north of Muxungue

column4: President Filipe Nyusi stated during a speech on 4 October that the videos circulating regarding security force abuses in Cabo Delgado are "doctored" to promote fear among the population. Nyusi also mentioned that the videos were a strategy used by the insurgents to sew discord.

The Ministry of Health recorded 102 new COVID cases and 1 new death bring the total numbers to 9,368 cases and 67 deaths in Mozambique on 6 October. Maputo City recorded the highest number of cases with 58. While 27 cases were recorded in Maputo province.
Two trailer trucks collided with each other along the National Road 221 between Guija and Mabalane on 6 October. 5 civilians were killed and four were injured.
column15: National Road 221 between Guija and Mabalane

column4: Around 3,500 civilians have passed through the Ressano Garcia border since the partial reopening since 1 October. A majority of the civilians that have passed through were due to commercial activity in South Africa. The low number was due to effects of the pandemic and the constraints brought about by the requirement of the negative PRC COVID 19 test certificate.

Mozambican civil society organization launched a National Network of Human Rights Defenders in Maputo to protect activists in the country. Center Democracy and Development Director Adriano Nuvunga stated that the National Network of Human Rights Defenders was to bring the civil society organizations closer and improve protection and security among the groups.

Unknown men have made several bomb threats against Mozambican civil society leader and Director of the Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) Adriano Nuvunga residence since 3 October, saying a bomb had been placed in his home and would explode at any moment.  Nuvunga subsequently evacuated his family from the home. The messages are reportedly aimed at "scaring him into silence".  Nuvunga has recently been critical of the government's security operations in Cabo Delgado, and has called for an investigation into human rights violations by security forces in the province.  Amnesty International condemned the threats and called for a prompt investigation into them.

Elias Dhlakama, the younger brother of former RENAMO chief Afonso Dhlakama, said on 06 October that Ossufo Momade's tenure as head of RENAMO was proceeding "with many difficulties".  Elias also said he was considering a bid for the presidency of RENAMO in order to "save the party."  Elias also said he was "surprised" that his nephew Henriques Afonso Dhlakama (son of Afonso) was running for the presidency and said the younger Dhlakama "understands little about politics".  Elias previously placed second in the RENAMO leadership contest of January 2019, losing to Momade.

Authorities have launched a request for children street vendors to wear masks as part of the preventive measures against the COVID pandemic in Manica province on 7 October. Manica Governor, Francisca Tomas, stated that there is a high number of children without any mask or gloves in the public squares and bazaars in Chimoio.

Mozambique and Malawi agreed to reactivate the Joint Defense and Security Commission after 12 years of inactivity.  The commission was originally formed to tackle inter-country security matters, fight against organized crime, illegal immigration, terrorism, human and drug trafficking. This comes after President Filipe Nyusi conduct talks with Malawi President Lazarus Chakwera in Songo village on 6 October.
38 Malawians who entered the country illegal through the Ressano Garcia border crossing were repatriated back to their country through the Maputo International Airport on 6 October.

Pictures emerged this week, local media reported, of a large protective wall built around parts of the residential areas of the LNG camp on the Afungi Peninsula by Total. The wall was built over recent months to better secure the camp from potential insurgent attacks.

The President of the Nhamatanda Municipal Council was accused of falsifying his 12th Class literacy certificate which qualified him to be official and head of the municipal council in Nhamatanda. The Ministry of State Administration and Public Service, Attorney General, and Sofala State Secretariat stated that Antonio Charumar Jaoa also conducted illegal payments, land sale, misuse of public funds, and state assets. He is also accused of having allotted public work awards to companies owned by family members.

Health officials launched an investigation on 7 October regarding the fake COVID-19 certificates being sold for 7 USD to allow citizens to travel to South Africa at the Ressano Garcia border crossing.

Mozambique's airports reportedly experienced 24 million USD losses due to the COVID pandemic. Airport officials stated that within a month and half they would be able to gain an international health certification as a safe airport against the pandemic, in order to accept more flights. Currently, slow resumption of international flights, have already been approved in reciprocity with Mozambique. Among the countries are Ethiopia, South Africa, Portugal, Qatar and Turkey.

Insurgents on 28 September were reported to have ambushed an EDM (state electricity company) travelling near Chitunda to repair a powerline in the area cut during recent fighting.  One worker was shot and injured in the attack, while another was abducted by insurgents, though later released.

Insurgents on 28 September abducted an EDM worker during an ambush near Chitunda, later releasing the man and telling him to pass a message to his company that powerlines in the area should not be repaired.  Electricity in the area has been cut since late September in the area, which has resulted in power outages in parts of Muidumbe, Palma, Mueda, Macomia, and Mocimboa da Praia districts.
A man on 29 September was found dead in Malamba in Palma District, and was believed to have been killed by insurgents.  No further details regarding this incident are currently available.

Insurgents in a 24 September attack killed 7 people in Mucojo.  Those targeted reportedly were among residents who had previously fled the town before recently returning.  Insurgents also set fire to parts of the town.  Insurgents returned to attack the town on 30 September for a second time in a week.
Insurgents were reported to have abducted an unknown number of people from the town of Pangane on 30 September following a raid on the village and clashes with security forces.

Insurgents in an 01 October attack on Messano village gave several elderly civilians funds to travel out of the area, telling these villagers to flee and not return.  The militants also told the villagers they should not stay in Macomia town, as insurgents planned to soon attack the area again.

On 01 October, two boats loaded with IDPs travelled from Pangane to Matemo island to escape insurgent attacks.  One boat capsized, leaving an unknown number of people dead.  Local media reported bodies washed up along the shore on Matemo island.

IDPs displaced from Bilibiza denounced 4 suspected insurgents to authorities in Metuge, likely on or around 24 September. The insurgents had travelled among the IDPs after recent insurgent attacks on Bilibiza.  When the group reached IDP camps in the Metuge area, the suspected insurgents were handed over to authorities, who arrested the group.

The Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) called for the government to investigate the disappearance of journalist, Ibraimo Mbaruco, who went missing six months ago in Cabo Delgado. Mbaruco went missing at around 18:00 of 7 April in Palma after texting a friend that he was surrounded by soldiers. Juma Saíde Alide, Mbaruco’s colleague previously stated that Mbaruco was taken by armed men on a motorcycle.

Machipanda Border Crossing to Zimbabwe in Manica Province is not yet fully opened to all types of traffic due to limited operations. In addition, the limited operation was due to Zimbabwean authorities continually observing the COVID safety measures in Mozambique.

The Ministry of Health recorded 96 COVID cases bringing the total to 9,494 cases in Mozambique on 7 October. Maputo City recorded the highest cases number of 58, with 11 cases in Zambezia, 10 in Maputo, 7 in Tete, 4 in Gaza, 4 in Inhambane, 1 in Nampula, and 1 in Cabo Delgado.  One additional fatality was also reported, bringing the nationwide death toll due to COVID to 68.

RENAMO leader, Ossufo Momade, stated that he order the dismantling of the RENAMO bases in Maringue and Cheringoma of Sofala province on 7 October. Ossufo Momade stated that the priority was to demobilize RENAMO bases in Sofala province which will be followed by the other bases in different provinces.

RENAMO leader, Ossufo Momade, stated that he order the dismantling of the RENAMO bases in Maringue and Cheringoma of Sofala province on 7 October. Ossufo Momade stated that the priority was to demobilize RENAMO bases in Sofala province which will be followed by the other bases in different provinces.

Deputy Justice Minister Filimao Suaze announced that Mozambican courts are obliged to stop using prison terms in cases where offenders can be sentenced with alternatives starting January 2021. The announcement was to stop the overcrowding in Mozambican prisons and on reduce prison usage on criminals.

RENAMO leader, Ossufo Momade, stated that his party was being prevented from conducting meetings in Inhambane province. Momade also intends to call the President of the Republic, Filipe Nyusi, for clarifications regarding the issue. The incident comes as RENAMO members were forced to vacate a room for rent in the city of Maxixe.

RENAMO members intending to conduct a meeting were forced to vacate an event hall for rent in Maxixe city on 7 October. The event hall owner was reportedly instructed to not allow any party to conducting meetings. RENAMO leader, Ossufo Momade, stated that his party was being prevented from conducting meetings in Inhambane province. Momade also claimed that the ruling party, FRELIMO, not to allow this political meetings in their commercial establishments.

Magaia village and several other villages in Muidumbe, Cabo Delgado, have reportedly created defense militias to cooperate with security forces against the insurgents in Muidumbe district in recent months.  Some militiamen are reportedly "war veterans".  Pro-gov militia recently ambushed insurgents in the Magaia area.

The National Director of Public Health, Rosa Marlene stated on 8 October in response to the reports of false negative PCR COVID certificates being sold at the Ressano Garcia Border Crossing that the Ministry of Health would certify laboratories to conduct COVID PCR tests.  Marlene also said the Ministry of Health would issue international travel certificates which both would be required by travelers to leave the country. The National Migration Service (SENAMI) spokesman Celestino Matsinhe stated that four foreigners were refused entry due to the absence of a work visa along with the negative COVID certificate. SENAMI also announced that it has waved application fees and would refund the fees for those who made appointments before 30 September.
Police arrested a suspect for murdering his stepson due to a domestic dispute in Beira on 3 October.

Mozambique's security forces in a revised version of the 2020 state budget will receive a significant increase of 19.5% in spending, or about 5.6 billion meticais of extra funding.  The Mozambican military will receive an extra 2 billion meticais, increasing the military's total budget to 10.2 meticais.  The General Police Command will receive an extra 1.3 billion meticais, increasing their budget to 2 billion meticais overall.  State Information and Security Services will receive an extra 600 million meticais, for a total budget of 3.1 billion meticais; these were the three largest budget increases among security forces in the country.
A motorcycle taxi crashed into a ditch during a vehicle chase in Vaz, west Beira, on 8 October. Police arrested the driver for lacking official public driving documents and reckless driving.

Unidentified men suspected to be party members of AMUSI or possibly FRLEIMO members attacked Francisco Jamal Intata, a founding member of United Movement Action for Integral Salvation party (AMUSI) on 28 September. Intata initially claimed that the attack was ordered by the AMUSI President and Secretary General. In response, AMUSI President Mario Albino stated that the attack was initiated by FRELIMO. Albino stated that a group claiming to be AMUSI members were financed by FRELIMO to conduct attacks. FRELIMO denied the claims and stated that they do not know any AMUSI members for them to conduct such attacks.

South African Police detained a Mozambican human trafficker and rescued two children intended to be given to child laborers in Tshwane, South Africa. The police questioned the children leading to the arrest.  The man had recently crossed into Guateng from Mozambique, and was reportedly part of a larger child smuggling ring based in Mozambique.
The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) closed down a dumpling production facility in Maputo city on 8 October, due to unsanitary practices.

RENAMO National Political Commission member Alfredo Magumisse, stated on 1 October, that security forces have blamed RENAMO dissidents for the murder and kidnappings of around 10 RENAMO members from Metuchira and Macorococho villages in Nhamatanda district.

RENAMO delegates said on 07 October that they will boycott sending members to participate in a parliamentary visit to the insurgency-impacted provinces of Cabo Delgado, Manica, and Sofala.  RENAMO General Secretary Andre Majibire said on Wednesday that the delegation was "just a tourist trip to let people think that the Assembly is involved in solving the problem".  This boycott came after the FRELIMO-dominated parliament failed to setup a RENAMO-proposed commission to look into human rights abuses in Manica, Sofala, Niassa and Cabo Delgado.

RENAMO secretary-general, Andre Magibire, rejected a recent proposal by former president, Armando Guebuza, in sending former guerilla fighters to Cabo Delgado on 8 October. Guebuza previously called for fighters who fought for the liberation of Mozambique including the RENAMO fighters to join forces against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

Text messages on 8 October were reported to be circulating calling for civilians in Cabo Delgado to return to Mocimboa da Praia. The messages also stated that the conflict was over and tells others to return to the area. Unconfirmed reports stated that the messages were sent by security forces or insurgents, though no conclusive details were uncovered to identify the senders.

The Ministry of Health announced 145 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 8 October, increasing the total to 9,639 cases. 63 cases were recorded in Zambezia, followed by Maputo City with 38 cases, 24 cases in Maputo province, 10 in Sofala, 3 in Tete, 3 in Niassa, 1 in Nampula, 1 in Manica, 1 in Inhambane, and 1 in Gaza.

The Minister for Mineral Resources and Energy, Max Tonela, stated on 8 October during a speech in Macanga, that illegal miners should be re-organized into associations to stop illegal mining in the country. The strategy could be employed to boost the country's economy by promoting associations and cooperatives.

Poor living conditions were reported by refugees who arrived at Matemo village, as little to no food, water, sanitary conditions, and accommodations were left at the vacated island. Majority of residents previously fled from the island after attacks by the insurgents. A small population have remained on the island.

Four young men in the Torrone Velho neighborhood of Quelimane were arrested on 08 October by security forces on unknown charges. One local politician told media that the arrest was related to "Cabo Delgado".  Local residents meanwhile said the group had a large amount of money and had spent it on "alcohol and connections with women".  Other local residents said the men did not provide clear information about where they worked or who they worked for.  While the arrest of the men is confirmed, their association with the insurgency has not yet been verified.

Local media and other sources reported that DAG helicopters launched an attack on insurgents on an unspecified Quirimbas Archipelago island on 08 October after insurgents had occupied the island after previously expelling local residents.  Reports also indicated some insurgents had fled from this attack and landed in boats on the mainland of Palma District.  Insurgents were reportedly targeted after cell phone location data was used to locate insurgents; phones being used had been stolen from civilians in Bilibiza in a recent attack.  One source later reported the incident had taken place between Ibo and Quirimba Islands in mangrove forests in the area, and that helicopters were deployed to repel and insurgent attack.

Fires were reported in Pangane, northeast of Mucojo, on 8 October. It was unknown if the fires were related to insurgent activity in the area. Previous fires were reported in nearby Mucojo just a day before.  Insurgents have been active in the area since 30 September.

Fires were reported in Mucojo on 7 October. It was unclear if the fires were due to insurgent activity. Fires have been previously recurrent in Mucojo since 30 September when insurgent attacks in the area began.

Security forces destroyed 427 traps used to snare animals placed in Chamba and Milepa areas at Niassa Reserve last week, officials announced on 6 October. 207 traps were for large animals while 226 traps were setup for smaller ones.

Security forces destroyed 427 traps used to snare animals placed in Chamba and Milepa areas at Niassa Reserve last week, officials announced on 6 October. 207 traps were for large animals while 226 traps were setup for smaller ones.

The EU's Mozambican representative  Antonio Sanchez Gaspar announced on that Friday morning that the EU would assist Mozambique in its fight against the Cabo Delgado insurgency via development, humanitarian support, and security assistance, namely, logistics, training, and technical assistance provided to the Mozambican military.  No direct military support in the form of manpower or weapons of war, however, will be provided.  No other details on this assistance are yet available.

RENAMO secretary general requested the media to use the name 'Military Junta of Mariano Nhongo', rather than ‘RENAMO Military Junta' to disassociate Mariano Nhongo’s group from the political party. Nhongo and his group have been waging attacks in Central Mozambique since August of 2019, and reject Ossufo Momade's leadership of the opposition political party.

Local sources reported on 7 October arrest of Malawi Medical Society senior officer Andrew Ngomwa in Zobue of Tete province for sexual assault charges. Ngomwa was on the run and escaped from Malawi (where the assault had occurred) after her sister filed charges on 21 September.

Locals media stated on Friday that insurgents in Cabo Delgado continue to recruit demobilized soldiers who have in many cases received at least two years training before leaving the military. This report also stated that defectors from the security forces also continue to join the insurgency.  Many of those joining the group are demoralized do to corruption and poor pay.  In some situations, soldiers have defected to the insurgency after being surrounded or captured by the militants.

A report released on 08 October by the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime said that recent drug seizures in Mozambique strongly indicate that crystal methamphetamine produced in Afghanistan is being shipped with heroin and being transited through Mozambique for the South African meth market.  A dhow seized off the Pemba coast in December 2019 carried a mixed cargo of heroin and 299 kgs of meth, while authorities in May 2020 seized a truck carrying a mixed cargo of meth and heroin at the Komatipoort border post on the South African/Mozambican border.  The drugs most commonly enter Mozambique via dhow travelling from Pakistan which anchor between 30-50kms off the shores of ports in Cabo Delgado and Nampula, and offload cargo to smaller fishing boats which then transport the drugs to the shore.
column15: Nampula and Cabo Delgado coastal waters

column4: Reports  08 October indicated a number of people were detained in Palma after reports that several insurgents had fled into the area after being attacked by DAG helicopters on islands off the Palma coast.  Some of those detained were kept in custody while others were reportedly released.  Sources later indicated that some of those detained had not been released over a week later.

RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo on 09 October, speaking from the Gorongosa area in an interview said that his group would not negotiate with the government while they were being "hunted with weapons".  Nhongo also claimed that on 07 October, 5 RENAMO members had been kidnapped and murdered in Dombe in Manica.  He also said in recent days another RENAMO member was murdered in the Punge River area, close to where several reported RENAMO dissident attacks have occurred.  Nhongo also blamed recent escalations in the conflict on the government, saying it was pursuing a purely military solution and had ignored Nhongo's calls not to sign a deal with RENAMO leadership when Nhongo had called for new talks.

Fire were reported at Ibo Island on 9 October. The cause of the fire was not clear, and could be related to a possible insurgent attack. A significant military force has been present on the island for several months.

The Ministry of Health announced the 1 new COVID related death and 103 new cases in Mozambique on 9 October. A total of 9,742 cases and 69 deaths were reported around the country. 63 of the new cases were from Maputo City and 11 cases were from Tete province.C863

The Public Health Laboratories National Director, Sofia Viegas, stated that the country is not in any impending danger of running out of reagents for the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) tests used to spot COVID on individuals. Viegas clarified that around 160,000 PCR tests were to arrive by the end of November and that 60,000 are arriving within the next few days.

Trans African Concessions (TRAC) announced that roadworks along the Moamba and Matola Interchange (Route N4) would commence on 13 October. TRAC stated that traffic delays and congestion may be expected due to the maintenance.

United Nations Secretary-General for Mozambique, Mirko Manzoni, invited RENAMO dissident leader, Mariano Nhongo, to participate in a peace dialogue. Manzoni stated that any issues can be resolve through talks. President Filipe Nyusi in a Friday speech meanwhile also restated his readiness to conduct talks with RENAMO dissidents.
Local sources reported on 9 October that Unknown men abducted and murdered a community leader and RENAMO member in Inhambane province. This report is currently unverified.

Vale Mining Company announced that it would retain all its employees and maintain its workforce despite of the effects of the COVID pandemic. Vale stated that it had 3,456 workers in the country, in which 92% were Mozambicans. Minister for Mineral Resources, Max Tonela, stated that the mining company is gradually recovering from suspension of operations and returning to normal production process.

National Director of Public Health, Rosa Marlene, stated that the usage of international travel certificates at the border will depend on the Ministry of Health and Ministry of Interior as both ministries share the responsibility in issuing such certificates.  It remains unclear if these certificates are currently being used at the Ressano Garcia crossing.

The Ministry of Health stated on 9 October that false negative Covid-19 tests were being used to travel to South Africa. The Ministry also mentioned that the tests were being sold at the Mozambican border post of Ressano Garcia. The usage of the false negative Covid-19 tests comes as a 72-hour limit to obtain the results was imposed, just days after the reopening of the borders within the scope of the relaxation of restrictions imposed by the new coronavirus.

RENAMO dissident leader, Mariano Nhongo, stated on 9 October that five RENAMO members were abducted and murdered in Dombe. It was unclear if Nhongo was referring to members of his group or members of the mainstream RENAMO party. This claim is currently unverified.

RENAMO dissident leader, Mariano Nhongo, stated on 9 October that a member of RENAMO was murdered during an attack along a road in Pungwe district.  It was unclear if Nhongo was referring to a mainstream RENAMO party member or a member of his breakaway group.

The International Organization for Migration announced that 52 Malawian migrants were assisted to return back to their country after being held at a security holding facility in Ressano Garcia. The migrants were previously stopped at the checkpoint in the area for lack of documents of illegally crossing the border.

Three armed men kidnapped a businessman by forcing him inside his own vehicle in Beira on the evening of Friday, 9 October. The victim was heading to his vehicle after Friday prayers when he was abducted. No details were released as to identity of the businessman. Witnesses stated that victim called for help and leading to nearby locals to approach the scene but one of the armed kidnappers to fire random shots and escaped.

During a visit in Chimoio on 9 October, President Filipe Nyusi stressed his willingness to hold dialogues with RENAMO dissidents to maintain peace in the country. The president stated that armed attacks on National Road 6 make the economy unfeasible and there must be security, peace, and tranquility for the desired plans to be achieved. Manica province is among the Mozambique provinces which has been impacted by armed attacks by RENAMO dissidents. Nyusi called on the armed men to join the Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration program.

Mozambique recorded 157 Coronavirus cases and 1 death on 11 October. At least 112 of these cases were recorded in Maputo city, 28 in Maputo, 6 in Gaza, 5 in Tete, 4 in Inhambane, and two in Zambezia. The single death was also reported in Maputo city.  This brought nationwide cases to 10,001 with 71 deaths.  There are currently 2,585 active cases in the country.

Security forces arrested an alleged Cabo Delgado insurgent recruiter on 10 October . The suspect, identified as 39-year-old Joseph Adremane Kumocho, had been moving between areas impacted by the Cabo Delgado insurgency, and Nampula. He was also reported to have recruited 72 people in Macomia to join the terrorists. According to local media, the suspect owned a mosque in Macomia district.  Other sources later reported however that the man had been falsely linked to the insurgency and had been set free due to a lack of evidence.  This report is currently unconfirmed.

Bad weather killed 5 civilians in Chimoio and nearby areas on 10 October. Strong winds and rain caused the collapse of several walls and homes in the town, causing at least 5 deaths. 7 people were also injured in the storm.
On 10 October, Mozambique recorded 102 Coronavirus cases and 1 related death.
The smuggling of 17 tons of frozen chicken and 600 boxes of alcoholic drinks was foiled at the Ressano Garcia Border Crossing in Moamba on the night of 7 October by border guards.

A report by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) citing field studies from 20-22 September stated that at least 7,780 people (1,507 families) have been displaced in Central Mozambique by ongoing violence. This displacement was caused by RENAMO dissident attacks in the region, particularly in Gondola in Manica and Chibabava and Buzi in Sofala.

At least 15 elephants caused panic among residents in Magude, Maputo province, on 12 October. The animals were reported to be from the Kruger National Park in South Africa. The elephants destroyed crops in the area, local media reported.
European Union Foreign Ministers on 12 October held talks in Luxembourg on the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  Assistance from the EU to Mozambique was also discussed in this meeting.

12 individuals died in the past week due to exposure while fleeing from Mucojo Administrative Post to Macomia after a recent string of attacks in the area. Around 3000 displaced civilians reported to have fled from Macomia district.

Locals sources stated that residents are not adhering to the social distancing precautions set by the government inside public transporting in several areas of Mozambique. Several drivers reportedly follow the social distancing measures in areas where security patrols are present but neglect the precautions upon arriving in unpatrolled areas.

A study conducted by the MASC Foundation and Instituto de Social and Economic Studies indicated that there are "factors that favor the evolution of the conflict in the provinces of Niassa and Nampula".  According to the study, organized crime, smuggling, deteriorating humanitarian situations, and weak state control are serious issues in both provinces, as they were in Cabo Delgado before the insurgency began.  The study also said that insurgents in these two provinces have "efficient functioning structures, including recruitment networks" who carry out radicalization in these areas.

The Mozambican Ministry of Economy and Finance announced that it intended to restructure the pension system due to the suspected imbalance between the contributors and beneficiaries. The Public Employee Social Security System (SPSFP) stated that the number of civilian pensioners has risen by 8.3 per cent, and that of military pensioners by 8.5 per cent.  An increasing pension burden is putting growing pressure on state finances.
A civilian died after being attacked by a crocodile along the Monapo River at around 03:00 on 9 October. The victim was reportedly fishing with his relatives.

Two civilians died due to a cholera outbreak in Matemo Island on 12 October. Many civilians have fled to the island after recent insurgent attacks on nearby mainland areas including Mucojo and Pangane.

The Ministry of National Defense announced on 12 October that 2,701 new recruits were drafted for the mandatory military service to join the Armed Forces of Defense of Mozambique (FADM). The recruits were registered with the 2020 military census which will join the second group of the Normal Effective Service.

The Ministry of Health announced 87 new COVID infections and 1 related death in Mozambique on 12 October.  This brings the total number of cases to 10,088 and 72 fatalities. There are 2,462 active cases in the country, including 1,586 cases in Maputo City.

326 former RENAMO members will hand over their weapons as part of the Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration of RENAMO’s armed wing in Gorongosa area of Sofala province in the coming days, according to RENAMO officials. RENAMO secretary, Andre Magibire, announced that the DDR was at its fourth phase after the armed wing of the political group signed a peace agreement last August 2019.
A child died after a wall collapsed due to heavy rainfall in Amatongas, east of Chimoio, on 10 October. 4 other individuals reportedly died in Chimoio as a result of the storm

A couple stabbed and killed a civilian due to a financial dispute in Urbanizacao, south Maputo, according to sources on 13 October. The suspects were later arrested and one of the suspects claimed that he took the knife from the victim and stabbed him in self defense.

Around 188 residences and public infrastructures were destroyed while 629 were damaged due to the storm on 10 October. 1194 families were reportedly affected and 427 required food assistance. Three health posts, two schools and 10 religious gathering sites were also damaged in Chimoio and Gondola.

Mozambique on 12 October published a proposal for a sovereign wealth fund the country plans to set up, saying it anticipates $96 billion in revenue from natural gas projects in the country.  Lawmakers would regulate the fund while the Ministry of Economy and Finance would manage it.  The fund would be built up to contribute to fiscal stability when commodity prices fluctuate.  The plan would be set up before 2022, when oil production is expected to begin.  An independent company would audit the fund annually, with the Mozambican Central Bank providing quarterly updates on the fund.  The proposal states that over the first 20 years of LNG production, half of the state's revenue would go to the fund and half to the government's budget.  After 20 years, 80% of revenue from the projects would go to the fund.  The proposal also says that whenever gov revenues from natural resources are 10% less than what's budgeted for, the state can withdraw as much as 4% of the previous year's income.

A group of insurgents on 10 October entered Mucojo village and seized 25 goats.  Insurgents also demanded small numbers of civilians left in the area flee from the village.  Insurgents reportedly entered the village "peacefully".  Another source later said however that 2 civilians had been killed during this incident, and that insurgents had stolen fish and salt in this raid.
A community leader was detained after being accused of sexually assaulting his niece in Homoine on 13 October. The local community stated that the suspect had previous encounters with the victim.
The new Bank of Mozambique's roof in Chimoio branch was damaged due to the storm during the weekend.
A driver was injured after jumping out of a vehicle with faulty brakes along the Ferrovario-Costa do Sol in east Maputo on 11 October.

Local sources stated on 13 October that traffic police arrested eight drivers during an inspection of 1995 vehicles in Maputo during the weekend. 172 were fined for traffic violations. Traffic police also cleared out 21 vehicles for overcrowding.

Local sources stated on 13 October that traffic police arrested eight drivers during an inspection of 1995 vehicles in Maputo during the weekend. 172 were fined for traffic violations. Traffic police also cleared out 21 vehicles for overcrowding.

Security Forces released suspected insurgent recruiter 39-year-old Joseph Adremane Kumocho in Montepuez on 13 October. Kumocho was previously detained on 10 October, had been reportedly traveling between areas impacted by the Cabo Delgado insurgency, and Nampula.  His family members intervened and reportedly convinced authorities the man was innocent.
Security forces released three Marines were released after paying bond in Montepuez on 13 October. The marines were previously detained last April on Ibo island for abuses against civilians.

Police detained two suspects for selling forged false negative COVID test results at Ressano Garcia on 13 October. The suspects were in possession of a laptop and printer during the arrest. The suspects confessed to selling the test results for around 2500 - 3000 meticais and that a third person known as "Freeman" is the head of the group.

The Centre for Public Integrity (CIP) stated that Mozambique’s debt to China is not transparent and alarming due to the debt being around 2 billion USD. CIP also stated that the debt to China can affect the country’s resources for the social sectors, specifically in areas related with the current pandemic. CIP demanded the government explain how it would tackle the debt and the projects associated with it. CIP also said that the government does not publicly disclose how the debt is paid.

President Filipe Nyusi announced on 12 October the armed conflict in Manica province of central Mozambique carried out by the RENAMO dissidents has affected 131 teachers and 12 schools, 11 in Gondola and 1 in Machete. This comes as the president announced that a total of 1,800 teachers were affected by the ongoing violence in the north and central areas of Mozambique.

President Filipe Nyusi stated on Monday, 12 October, that 138 schools were affected by the ongoing insurgency since 2017. 45 schools were reportedly destroyed, impacting 60,000 students and 1,132 teachers. The president also said the worst affected areas in terms of school districts were as follows: Mocimboa da Praia with 452 teachers and 32,247 students impacted,, 359 teachers and 10,047 students in Quissanga, and 115 teachers and 7,698 pupils in Macomia.

Locals sources on 13 October stated that South African Forces and Mozambique security forces detained 302 illegal immigrants and smugglers along the borders of KwaZulu-Natal-Maputo since 1 October. Around 500,000 meticais worth of contraband were seized in KwaZulu-Natal-Maputo area.

Two civilians were killed and 17 others were injured during heavy rains and strong winds in Zambezia province on 10 October. Several residences, educational facilities, churches, health institutions, and power stations in Gurue area of the province were damaged.

The Mozambican Water Supply Investment and Assets Fund (FIPAG) announced that water restrictions would be put in place in Nampula due to the low water levels of the local dam. FIPAG Director, Inacio Nhazombe, stated that each residential area in Nampula is to have nine hours of water interruption every other day, reducing daily usage of 40,000 cubic meters to around 22,000 cubic meters.

The Ministry of Health announced 170 new COVID cases bringing the total 10,258 in Mozambique on 13 October. Another COVID related fatality was also reported from Maputo city increasing the number of deaths to 73. Maputo city recorded 68 cases, 57 cases from Sofala, 14 were from Maputo province, 11 were recorded in Zambezia, nine in Nampula, eight from Tete, two from Cabo Delgado, and one from Niassa.

The Mozambique Health Minister Armindo Tiago announced on 13 October that he tested positive with COVID but was asymptomatic. The minister stated that tests were carried out on individuals who were previously in contact with the minister.

RENAMO party announced that 173 armed members began the Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration process in Cheringoma on 12 October. The armed members stated that they would only handover their weapons by 14 October.

RENAMO announced on 13 October that Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration process of 43 armed members at a base in Chemba was set to finish on 24 October. This comes as other members in Cheringoma have been demobilized while Maringue was set to begin a day after.
The RENAMO party stated on 13 October that the DDR process of 145 armed members in Maringue was scheduled to start on 25 October.

Gunmen shot and killed a businessman identified as Amity Samigy in Maputo on the evening of 13 October.  Assailants opened fire on Samigy after he reportedly resisted a kidnap attempt; he was hit by 3 bullets.   The incident took place at the intersection of Alberto Lithuli and Josina Machel Avenues.

The Mozambique government has requested debt relief from China, according to the Minister of Economy and Finance, Adriano Maleiane on 13 October. Maleiane stated that the government has two types of loans from China, one from the government and another from a baking system which totaled to $1.3 billion.  Other sources say that Mozambique's debts to China could be close to $2 billion.  China has not yet answered Mozambique's request.

Airport security detained a customs treasurer who reportedly stole 21.9 million meticais at Maputo International Airport during the previous week, according to local sources on 14 October. The suspect was in coordination with a customs broker who issued forged receipts to allow the clearance of several goods in exchange for money.

Several sources reported that Insurgents between Friday and Monday were reported to have launched a new raid on the village of Nambo, killing 3 people.  Insurgents also set multiple homes on fire  and abducted at least 2 people from the village.

Several sources reported that Insurgents between Friday and Monday were reported to have launched a new raid on Pangane village, killing 2 soldiers and 5 civilians in this raid.  Militants also reportedly set two military vehicles on fire in this raid.  Insurgents also reportedly set fire to area homes, and abducted as many as 60 people in the attack.
