This report remains questionable at this time as sources also indicated 5 civilians and 2 soldiers had been killed in a previous attack on the village on 30 September.
Insurgents in an attack over the weekend were reported to have abducted 2 people from Nambo village.

Insurgents in an attack over the weekend were reported to have abducted 60 people from Pangane village.  Sources later indicated that in this attack, over 200 people had been intially detained by insurgents before an unspecified number of children were separated from their parents and taken towards Quiterajo.

Local authorities recovered 20 bodies of illegal miners after landslide along the Meluli River in the Namaita Administrative Post, south of Nampula, on 14 October. The community leader stated that search operations were ongoing as more victims were suspected and other people are missing.  A large group of illegal miners had set up a camp in the area, and had been advised to leave the area in late September by authorities.

Txivuno Txavanana Association of NGOs Director, Arteonesa Sambo, announced an increase of sexual assault and rape cases were reported during the COVID pandemic. Sambo stated that most of the victims do not call on authorities for the fear of reprisals.

The Mozambican Workers’ Organization (OTM-CS) stated that around 32,000 labor contracts were suspended since March due to the COVID pandemic. OTM-CS Secretary-General, Alexandre Munguambe, announced that 1,500 employees from 27 of its companies lost their jobs.

Five RENAMO members were reportedly abducted and murdered in Manica province on 7 October. The victims were reportedly shot and killed due to suspected political issues.  It was unclear if this claim referred to a previous claim made by RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo regarding 5 people killed in Dombe.

Airlink Airlines announced that it intends to resume weekly flights between Maputo and Johannesburg starting 28 October. Two flights will be conducted each week. These new flights follow the lifting of the travel ban due to the COVID pandemic.

Insurgents on the evening of 14 October at around 1700hrs attacked the village of Nacate, south of Macomia; this attack occurred as one group of insurgents clashed with military units in the area.  Insurgents burned houses in Nacate and carried out looting but were ultimately forced to withdraw from the town, as Mozambican soldiers reportedly significantly outnumbered insurgents.  At least one person was reportedly killed in one of the homes set on fire by the militants.

Clashes on the evening of 14 October were reported in the Nacate area, less than 12kms south of Macomia at around 1700hrs. A group of around 80 insurgents had reportedly moved through forests near the village and reportedly intended to attack Macomia overnight from the south after moving north along the N380 road, but were engaged by about 200 Mozambican soldiers in the area.  One group of insurgents engaged the soldiers, while two other groups carried out looting and set fire to several village houses.   One local media source indicated that military reinforcements had been called to the scene of the fighting.  Clashes lasted about 3 hours before insurgents withdrew from the area.

Two gunmen shot and killed a businessman identified as Amity Samigy in Maputo on the evening of 13 October.  Assailants opened fire on Samigy after he reportedly resisted an abduction attempt while closing his business; he was hit by 3 bullets after one of the gunmen came out of a light van.  The incident took place at the intersection of Alberto Lithuli and Josina Machel Avenues.

President of Zimbabwe, Emmerson Mnangagwa, announced that several experts were deployed to the border posts to determine if the country was ready to be reopened to neighboring countries.  Zimbabwe is reportedly preparing to re-open its borders, including those shared with Mozambique.

A group of around 200 Cabo Delgado insurgents attacked Kitaya village in Tanzania, just across the border from Mozambique on the night of 14 October at around 1900hrs, sources reported. 20 civilians and 3 soldiers were killed according to several sources an election candidate's home, a health facility, a cashew nut factory, a hospital, several shops, and at least 9 vehicles were destroyed in the attack.  After the attack, insurgents reportedly retreated back into Cabo Delgado, re-crossing the Rovuma River. ISCAP later claimed responsibility for this attack, publishing photos online purporting to show weapons, ammunition, and at least one military vehicle reportedly captured in the assault.  The attackers also reportedly threatened to return to the Kitaya area.

The Maputo City Judicial Court issued an order on 14 October for the dissolution of three public companies that created unauthorized loans and were part of the "hidden debts" debt case.  Prodindicus and Mozambique Asset Management (MAM) were initially issued orders for closure.  Ematum, the third company also linked to the hidden debts case was is still pending. The court issued that all assets should be liquidated.

ISCAP through its media channels on the evening of 15 October claimed responsibility for an attack on 14 October on Kitaya village in Tanzania's Mtwara Region, saying the group had attacked a Tanzanian military barracks of the "Tanzanian Crusader Army", killing and injuring several soldiers.  Photos were also later released online by the group allegedly showing a military vehicle, weapons, and equipment captured in the attack.  In a video posted online, insurgents can be seen in Kitaya, shouting Islamist slogans and firing small arms while a military vehicle can be seen in the background.  In this video, a militant also proclaims that the group is "al Shabaab from Mozambique" and the group had come to "remove Magufuli", Tanzania's President.

RENAMO General Secretary, Andre Magibire, stated that several of their members in the Gorongosa area were being forced to pay fees and to join FRELIMO. Magibire stated that 5,000 meticais was paid to be a  delegate and 500 meticais as a common member.

The European Union announced a de-radicalization program was being prepared to assist Mozambique against the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado. The program was to have a "three-link approach" which would discouraging recruitment and radicalization, and which aims to foster social cohesion.

The National Institute of Disaster Management (INGC) stated they installed six warning systems to indicate flooding due to the rainy season as it may affect 22,000 families living near the Save Basin in Govuro district of Inhambane province. INGC stated that the basin may overflow due to the rainfall expected during the end of 2020 to the start of 2021.

President Filipe Nyusi conducted talks with South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, discussing the security situation of Mozambique on 14 October. The talks focused of the insurgency ongoing in Cabo Delgado and the socio-economic impacts of COVID pandemic.

The Ministry of Health announced 145 new COVID cases bringing the total to 10,537 cases in Mozambique on 15 October. No fatalities were reported during the day. 8,214 total recoveries were recorded as 179 individuals recovered over the past 24 hours.  The death toll stands at 73.

Sekelekani Communication Studies and Research Centre stated 41 deaths due to domestic violence cases were reported so far in 2020 in Mozambique. Around 3,904 cases of physical violence, 1,259 of psychological violence, 796 of property violence and 478 of serious violence were reported since the beginning of 2020. The majority of the victims were reported to be women.

The Mozambican Health Ministry announced that 1889 cases out of 2280 active cases which is equivalent to 83 percent of confirmed COVID cases were in Maputo city as of 14 October. In addition, 53 of the 73 fatalities occurred in Maputo city, which accounts for 78 percent of the deaths.

Locals sources stated on 15 October that Security forces detained a Tanzanian national for illegal hunting in Mecula, Niassa. The suspect was in possession of an AK-47, 40 ammunition rounds, three bicycles, two mobile phones, and four pans. Seven other suspects reportedly managed to escape and are being sought by security forces.

11 prisoners escaped from a prison in Massangena on 9 October. Security forces conducted a search operation leading to the arrest of three fugitives in Chicualacuala. Three police officers were detained for the escape of 11 inmates.

11 prisoners escaped from a prison in Massangena on 9 October. Security forces conducted a search operation leading to the arrest of three fugitives in Chicualacuala. Three police officers were detained for the escape of 11 inmates.
Local sources on 15 October stated that three fugitives were detained by police in Chicualacuala. The fugitives were among the 11 prisoners who escaped from a prison in Massangena.

Officials announced that an 8km wall continues to be built along part of the border of Mozambique and South Africa. The wall would start from the boundary of Isimangaliso Wetlands Park moving to the western boundary of Tembe Elephant Park of South Africa in order prevent the smuggling of goods between the two. Additional security patrols were also deployed in the area.

Chambo ferry services resumed operations between Mozambique and Malawi through Lake Malawi/Lake Niassa on 16 October. The ferry services were previously stopped due to the enactment of the state of emergency in Mozambique.

The Ministry of Health announced that they are finalizing the creation of a barcode based COVID test result for real-time verification of the results authenticity. The barcode was a response to the previous reports of false negative test results that were being sold at border crossings in Mozambique to travel outside the country.

Police detained two smugglers and seized a truck transporting 185 kg of cocaine and 158 kg of heroin in Ribaue, west of Nampula, on the evening of 14 October. The drugs were hidden in a compartment under the floor of the truck bed. The smugglers were in possession of 119,420 meticais.

Police detained two smugglers and seized a truck transporting 185 kg of cocaine and 158 kg of heroin in Ribaue, west of Nampula, on the evening of 14 October. The drugs were hidden in a compartment under the floor of the truck bed. The smugglers were in possession of 119,420 meticais.  Sources later confirmed that the drugs had been transported through Cabo Delgado.  One of the smugglers was a Mozambican national, while the other was a naturalized Mozambican national originally from Tanzania.  This was the largest quantity of "heavy drugs" ever seized in the province, a police source said.
Police arrested a Nigerian suspect in possession of 530 g of cocaine hidden inside sewing materials in Maputo City on 15 October. The suspect confessed that the drugs were bound for China.

Tax Authority of Mozambique seized 60,000 bottles of smuggled alcohol during inspections of a warehouse around Tete on 15 October. Officials stated that tax evaded by the smuggled goods would have cost around 4 million meticais worth.
Insurgents on the afternoon of 16 October attacked the Olumbi area in Palma District, reportedly driving Mozambican marine units out of the village and inflicting unknown casualties.
Civilians travelling between Mucojo and Macomia on 09 October indicated that at least 10 roadblocks in the form of tree trucks and other debris had been placed by insurgents along this route.

Security forces on 05 October reportedly shot two young men who were talking on a phone after curfew in Palma town.  The two fled after being approached by soldiers, who then opened fire on the two.  At least one of the two was killed and the other injured; one source reported both were killed.

Insurgents on the night of 14 October were reported to have attacked Ndique village of Quissanga District, shooting dead two people.  This was one of the furthest south attacks in Cabo Delgado since insurgents attacked towards Metuge in April/May earlier this year.

Mozambican forces this week were reported to have seized arms caches in Palma town from several houses, though it was not clear how many guns were seized or the exact date of this incident.  This local media report came after security forces in Palma had recently been reported to have distributed arms to some local civilians after multiple attacks in Palma District.  It was unclear if those in possession with these weapons were affiliated with the insurgents, civilians armed by the authorities, or a criminal group.

A study by the National Health Institute on 15 October reported that about 5.2% of Beira's population has had COVID-19, according to a random sample of 8,297 individuals in the city. This positivity rate would indicate that over 30,000 people in Beira have either had or have COVID-19. Many market sellers are the most exposed to the virus, with 8.3% of market sellers carrying antibodies.  Truck drivers were also highly exposed with 10.3% of those tested carrying antibodies.

The government announced that it would hire 1,444 health professionals to provide assistance against the COVID pandemic. The increased health staff was as follows: 60 general practitioners, 300 nurses, 300 medical technicians, 120 lab technicians, 60 pharmacists, 60 administrative technicians, 60 ambulance drivers, 120 health facility and ambulance assistants.

The Ministry of Health announced that 19 out of 34 COVID inpatients throughout the country were in critical condition. Almost of the patients were admitted in health facilities within Maputo city, while one patient was in Tete province.
Police arrested six suspects for kidnapping cases in Beira on 16 October. The suspects reportedly targeted businessmen in the area.

Security forces seized 30 ammunition magazines, several military uniforms, and medication during a search operation near Cagembe on 14 October. The security forces reportedly captured the insurgent’s hideouts in the area.  No clashes were reported in the area.  Pictures of these patrols published online showed large numbers of troops at these bases.

A large fire was reported on 16-17 October in Olumbi, Palma District.  Sources later confirmed that insurgents had driven Mozambican marine units out of the town and had set fire to much of the village, also carrying out looting.

A significant portion of a settlement in Mahate, Quissanga, was reported to have caught on fire late on Saturday, 17 October. This occurred the same night a fire was reported in the coastal area of Olumbi, south of Palma. Both incidents are suspected to be insurgent attacks.

President Filipe Nyusi received the special envoy of the Botswana President, Lapologane Legoa, during a visit in Mozambique on 16 October. During the meeting, both officials discussed bilateral issues including peace, security and development.

On 16 October, the Manica provincial delegate of the National Disaster Management Institute, Augusto Alexandre, announced that the storm which impacted the province the week prior has resulted in the destruction of 23 schools in 3 districts. 90 classrooms were also destroyed, affecting 1,400 students. In addition, the death toll has increased to 8 while 7 others were injured. At least 204 houses were completely destroyed while some 1,066 houses incurred partial damage. Roads also became impassable while pylons were blown out, resulting in power disruption. Authorities are now trying to restore power by raising fallen pylons; authorities are also carrying out other repair operations. The government also provided food and building materials to residents in Gondola and Vanduzi.
On 17 October, Mozambique recorded 95 Coronavirus cases and 1 death. These include 54 cases in Maputo city and 37 from Maputo province. The new death was also from Maputo city.

On 16 October, Mozambique recorded 75 new Coronavirus cases. 60 of these were from Maputo city, 6 from Maputo province, 3 cases from Manica,  2 from Gaza, 1 from Nampula, 1 from Zambezia, 1 from Tete, and 1 from Inhambane.

Mozambique recorded 159 Coronavirus cases and 1 death on 18 October. The new fatality was recorded in Maputo city.  86 new cases were reported in Maputo city, 47 in Maputo, 12 in Sofala, 5 in Cabo Delgado, 5 in Zambezia, 2 in Gaza, 1 in Tete, and 1 in Manica.

In a 32-minute audio message released on Sunday evening, 18 October, Daash spokesman Abu Hamza al-Qurashi attacked a number of Arab leaders and militaries, while calling on its followers to attack foreigners in the countries where the militants are present. Al-Qurashi also praised the organization’s operations against the Egyptian Army in North Sinai, as well as its followers in Mali, Mozambique, Nigeria, Chad, and Somalia targeting foreign forces and local armies.

A group of at least 700 people arrived in Pemba in several boats on Saturday from several Quirimbas Islands and villages in insurgent impacted areas; this came after recent insurgent attacks drove these IDPs from their homes.  Many of those arriving to Pemba were reported to be in poor health and were in need of food, water, and shelter.  Sources reported aid to this large group of IDPs only arrived on Monday.

Two 5-year-old girls went missing for more than 5 days in the Khongolote neighborhood in Matola, their families reported on 19 October, fearing that they might be kidnapped. The children went out to buy sweets at their neighbor's house but never came back. Police have been alerted regarding the incident.

A man beat his father-in-law to death in Nacala Porto on the afternoon of 18 October. The suspect was reported to have warned the victim against visiting their home, but went on to visit during the day of the incident. Police had since arrested the suspect.

Elderly Residents in Mudizingadzi, Chimoio, protested on 17 October against community leaders who failed to provide the support money given by the government for the victims of Cyclone Idai. During the protests, the demonstrators attacked one community leader, who was later taken to the Chimoio Provincial Hospital for his injuries. The protest began after many local residents realized their names were not on a list to receive subsidies while many "strangers" names had been included.

During the protests, the demonstrators attacked one community leader, who was later taken to the Chimoio Provincial Hospital for his injuries. The protest began after many local residents realized their names were not on a list to receive subsidies while many "strangers" names had been included.

On 19 October, face-to-face classes for Grade 10 students resumed in Mozambique. This applies to more than 800 schools nationwide as part of the gradual resumption of physical classes amid the Covid pandemic. Sources indicated that over 90% of schools were fit to resume classes.  This reopening comes after 12th grade classes restarted on 19 October.

On 18 October, authorities announced the restoration of power supply in Palma and Mocimboa da Praia after 3 months of power outage. This came after government forces launched an operation along the road connecting Mueda to MDP in order to carry out repairs on the Awasse substation which provides electricity in the region. This substation was previously destroyed during fighting between insurgents and government forces in August. According to reports, the government forces, along with the electricity team, were met with insurgents controlling areas near MDP, during the restoration operation. However, the insurgents later retreated after brief clashes with security forces near Awasse.

This came after government forces launched an operation along the road connecting Mueda to MDP in order to carry out repairs on the Awasse substation which provides electricity in the region. This substation was previously destroyed during fighting between insurgents and government forces in August. According to reports, the government forces, along with the electricity team, were met with insurgents controlling areas near MDP, during the restoration operation. Several houses were set on fire by around 10 armed insurgents at around 1900hrs on 18 October in Ntapwala, Macomia District.  Insurgents also reportedly kidnapped two women from the village.  Militants retreated from the area after pro-government militia reportedly arrived in the area.  Sources later said insurgents beheaded 2 people in this attack. At least two people were also injured in this attack.

Several houses were set on fire in an insurgent attack at around 1900hrs on 18 October in Ntapwala, Macomia District.  Insurgents also reportedly kidnapped two women from the village.  Militants retreated from the area after pro-government militia reportedly arrived in the area.
Multiple helicopters on 17 October were reported to have flown over Pemba towards Quissanga, reportedly to engage insurgents.  No further details on this military action are currently available.

The Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) said on 19 October that between 30 September - 08 October, at least 20 people were killed in a series of raids in the Mucojo area, including at least 2 Mozambican soldiers who were killed in Pangane.  The CDD also said that militants had used five motorboats to transport looted goods from area villages to their stronghold of Mocimboa da Praia.  The CDD also said insurgents had launched attacks on nearby islands during this time.  The CDD also said about 20 boats over the weekend carrying IDPs had arrived in Pemba, and that the number of displaced persons in Pemba alone could reach 80,000 as the insurgency continues.

An NGO reported on 19 October that at least 10 people, mostly IDPs, have recently died on Matemo island due to deteriorating humanitarian conditions; this included 6 deaths due to diarrhea on the island on 15 October.  Many of those living on Matemo currently are IDPs displaced by the ongoing Cabo Delgado insurgency.

The European Union’s ambassador to Mozambique, Antonio Sanchez-Benedito, stated that the peace agreement with RENAMO cannot be renegotiated. The announcement comes as RENAMO dissident leader, Mariano Nhongo, called for the renegotiation of the 2019 agreement and demanded the resignation of RENAMO president, Ossufo Momade. Benedito stated that the Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration (DDR) of the RENAMO armed members was already underway as part of the agreement.

World Food Programme (WFP) announced that 53% of individuals were malnourished due to the growing insecurity and poor infrastructures and facilities in Cabo Delgado. The province was reported to have the second highest rate of chronic malnutrition in which more than half of were children below 5. WFP called for immediate assistance which would require $4.7 million in providing relief to the IDPs of the province.

Local sources reported on 19 October that police arrested three individuals for attempting to traffic a child for 7,000 meticais in Curromana area of Molumbo.  The suspects were related to one another.

Local sources reported on 19 October that police arrested three individuals for attempting to traffic a child for 7,000 meticais in Curromana area of Molumbo.  The suspects were related to one another.

10,000 IDPs arrived at the Metuge IDPs camps during the recent weeks from insurgent impacted areas of Cabo Delgado and have strained camp resources in the area. Cabo Delgado District Administrator Antonio Nandanga stated around 13,000 families or 56,000 IDPs were currently being supported in camps in Metuge and Pemba.

Tensions between Vale mining company and local residents in Cateme area of Moatize continued due to the disagreements over the maintenance provided by the mining company to the local residents. The mining company was giving out social projects to improve the livelihood of the residents but was declined after many locals preferred direct payments.
National Institute of Disaster Management (INGC) said that a total of 30,000 IDPs from Cabo Delgado are now present in different locations around Nampula.

The Ministry of Health recorded 214 new COVID cases bringing the total to 11,080 cases in Mozambique on 19 October. 125 of the new cases were recorded in Maputo city, 52 cases were recorded in Maputo province, 14 in Zambezia, 14 in Inhambane, six in Tete, and three in Niassa. While 323 daily recoveries were reported leading to a total of 8,836.

The Democratic Movement of Mozambique claimed that FRELIMO members have targeted MDM members and vandalized their party vehicle by destroying its windows and flattening the tires in Mabote early morning of 16 October. The members were conducting their work when they were attacked.

Mozambican Youth Organization (OJM), a FRELIMO group, was reported stoned and attacked an MDM Brigade in Macuacua on 19 October according to The Democratic Movement of Mozambique. FRELIMO members denied the accusations against its members.
Officials announced that Inhambane prisons are overcrowded as around 12,000 prisoners are held in a 600 capacity prison. The prisoners were reported to lack adequate living conditions.

11 companies have reportedly closed due to the COVID pandemic in Niassa province on 15 October. Around 150 jobs were removed, mostly within the hospitality and tourism and construction and services. Department of Labour and Social Security stated that nine other companies have suspended operations which affects another 160 employees.

Insurgents were reported by local outlets to have re-entered Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) on the evening of 19 October. The insurgents reportedly left the town during the early morning of 20 October.  While security forces have not retaken the town since it fell to insurgents in early August, insurgents have been reported at various times to have maintained a presence only in some neighborhoods.
Insurgents attacked Matemo Island on 20 October, kidnapping 5 youths from the island.

Insurgents attacked Matemo Island on 19-20 October.  Insurgents reportedly left messages behind after this attack threatening IDPs on the island to leave the area and not to return. Insurgents also carried out looting and destroyed homes in the attack, and kidnapped 5 people.  Insurgents intially arrived on the island on 19 October, but two boats they used to reach the island were destroyed by government helicopters.  insurgents then carried out raids on the island, before capturing a new boat on the night of 20 October, and sailing back to the mainland.  Sources later indicated at least one person was killed by insurgents during this attack.

Security forces engaged in heavy clashes with insurgents during operations from the 16 until the 18 October in the Awasse area.  Three sources have reported that as many as 270 insurgents were killed in these clashes.  Security forces reportedly "surrounded and slaughtered" militants in a coordinated effort in these clashes, and were allegedly supported by pro-government militia forces in the area which included "war veterans". It has been confirmed that at least some clashes did in fact occur in the area as Mozambican troops protected electricity company workers who were carrying out repairs on the Awasse Power Station, though this casualty count is unconfirmed.  Troops also reportedly seized military equipment and military vehicles in these clashes, carrying 7 truckloads of equipment captured in these clashes back to Mueda.  Sources later indicated that a local 80 year old veteran of the independence war called "old Naveta" had led pro-government militia forces in these clashes.

Clashes were reported on 18 October between Mozambican military units supported by pro-government militias against insurgents in the Chinda area, south of Awasse.  Clashes were also reported in the Awasse area, where pro-government sources claimed over 270 insurgents had been killed.

Insurgents over the weekend were reported to have attacked Churumba, south of Mahate in Quissanga.  No casualties were reported though insurgents reportedly inflicted material damage.  No other details on this incident are currently available.
Officials suspended two gold mining companies for polluting the Rovue river in Manica province on 20 October.  The companies had reportedly dumped waste into the river.
The Ministry of Health recorded 110 new COVID cases and three deaths in Mozambique on 20 October. 70 of the new cases were recorded in Maputo city and 31 cases were recorded in Maputo province.

A fire suspected to be related to an insurgent attack was reported on 19 October in Olumbi village in Palma.  Sources later confirmed insurgents carried out an attack on this day and carried out looting and destruction of property in the village.

The Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) NGO on Tuesday said that foreign companies operating in Mozambique had been "pressuring the government" not to proceed in passing a law that would require more goods and services to be sourced locally.  The CDD said that the Local Content Law was shelved by the government with no explanation in August 2019.

Mozambican authorities on 20 October issued arrest warrants for 3 former Credit Suisse bankers in connection with the "Hidden Debts" case.  Mozambique also issued an extradition request for the 3 on 16 October.

Dozens of boats carrying IDPs have arrived to Pemba in recent days.  Local media said at least 92 boats have arrived to the town over the past 5 days, including 25 boats on Saturday, 19 on Sunday, 17 on Monday, and at least 24 boats on Tuesday.  On Tuesday, over 1800 IDPs arrived to the port in a single day  Nearly 3,400 people have arrived to the city during this time, mostly coming from Matemo island and parts of Mucojo administrative post after recent insurgent attacks in these areas.  Many of those arriving had reportedly sold their own clothes in order to pay for boat rides fleeing the insurgent zone, sources reported.
An insurgent attack on 18 October was reported in Nanhoma, Quissanga District. No casualties were reported in the incident, though looting was carried out.
Insurgents on 19 October were reported to have attacked Koko village, south of Macomia along the N380 road, setting several homes on fire and kidnapping at least one person.

An insurgent attack was reported on 21 October in the Embada area of Meluco along the N380 road.  No further details regarding this incident were immediately available.

Insurgents on 19 October attacked the village of Iba, Meluco, setting fire to several homes and carrying out looting.  No casualties were reported in this attack.  This village is located roughly 10 miles or about 17 kms southwest of Macomia town in an area that has not recently experienced insurgent attacks. This was the first attack reported in Meluco for at least 2 months.

South African Airline Airlink has announced new flights to Beira, Pemba, and Vilanculos.  The new Pemba flights will begin on 28 October, while flights to Vilanculos and Beira will begin on 10 November.  Beira flights will be offered on Tuesdays and Thursdays, Pemba flights on Wednesday and Friday's, and Vilanculos flights on Tuesdays and Saturdays.

Mozambican troops north of Nacate on 14 October were reported to have repelled an attempt by militants to attack Macomia town.  This came after insurgents on the night of 14 October were driven back from the Nacate area after raiding this village.  No other details regarding this clash are currently available.

column4: Insurgents on 14 October attacked the village of Namalala along the N762 road between MDP and Palma in Palma district, setting fire to several homes and injuring several local residents.  Large numbers of local residents subsequently fled to Palma town.  No exact casualty figures are currently available.

DAG helicopters on the night of 16-17 October attacked insurgents in Olumbi village after militants drove Mozambican marines out of the area.  Insurgents, who had set fire to the village and carried out looting, were reported to have withdrawn in the face of these helicopter attacks.
A crocodile attacked and killed a 25-yr-old woman while fetching water from a river in Chemba, Sofala on 19 October. There are now seven deaths in the district this year caused by crocodile attack.

The Mozambique Police announced on 20 Oct that they have arrested a total of 408 criminal suspects during anti-criminal operations in Maputo province during the first half of 2020. 39 firearms, including 10 AKMs, 17 pistols, eight shotguns and 591 ammunition were seized by the police in these operations.

The Ministry of Health recorded 141 new COVID cases bringing the countrywide total to 11,331 cases in Mozambique on 21 October. One death was recorded in Maputo city in the last 24 hours, bringing the nationwide COVID death toll to 79. 110 of the new cases were recorded in Maputo city, 20 cases were recorded in Maputo province, one in Zambezia, one in Manica, three in Tete, and three in Cabo Delgado. While 158 daily recoveries were reported leading to a total of 9,165 recoveries.

A provisional release was granted on 21 October to six defendants who were accused of involvement in targeting businessmen in the city for kidnappings.  The reason for these provisional releases on bail was not immediately unclear.

Insurgents on 20 October attacked Koko village along the N380 road for the second time in 2 days, but were met by Mozambican troops who repelled the attack.  No casualties were reported in this incident.
Insurgents on 20 October raided the village of Nangololo/Nangororo near Embada along the N380 road, setting fire to homes and carrying out looting.  No casualties were reported in this attack.
Insurgents on 20 October raided the village of Roma along the N380 road, setting fire to homes and carrying out looting.  No casualties were reported in this attack.

A group of business leaders in Beira calling themselves "Beira Against Abductions" at a press conference on 22 October announced that they were beginning a work stoppage, effective Friday-Sunday, for three days in protest against ongoing kidnappings targeting business people.  There have been at least 9 such abductions in 2020 in the country.  The group is also calling for security forces to put an end to these kidnappings.  Stores, bakeries, pharmacies, goods warehouses, and other facilities across the city will be shuttered during this time.  The group says kidnappings are increasingly brazen and happen in broad daylight, and that police are often slow to respond to these cases.  The group also said it wants to put a stop to kidnappings across Mozambique, not just in Beira.

A member of RENAMO's Political Commission reportedly recently said that demobilized members of RENAMO had recently joined the RENAMO Military Junta because they felt insecure in their areas because they were allegedly being pursued by security forces.

President Nyusi and RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade on 21 October met in Maputo, discussing the DDR process.  The two  after this meeting said that around 25%, or around 1,300 of RENAMO's military force had been demobilized.  A document released after this meeting indicated that as of 21 October, RENAMO bases at Inhaminga, Cheringoma, and Maringue had been closed. The two also discussed reports of alleged persecution, kidnappings, and murders of RENAMO members by government supporters, and agreed to launch a joint investigation of these reports.

A survey released on 19 October showed that COVID anti-bodies are less prevalent in Lichinga, the Niassa capital, than in any other part of the country.  The survey of 3,783 random people showed that just 0.3 percent of people in the city had COVID antibodies.  This would indicate just 639 COVID cases in the city out of a population of roughly 213,000 people.

Tanzania's Inspector General of Police Simon Sirro on 21 October acknowledged the recent Cabo Delgado insurgent attack on Kitaya village, saying around 300 insurgents had participated in this attack, and had killed several people in the area.  Authorities said they had arrested several "locals and foreigners in connection with the terrorist incident" and were working with its regional neighbors to "flush out the terrorists".  No exact casualty numbers were provided by Tanzania.  Sirro also said that some of the insurgents involved in the 14 Oct attack were involved in a string of murders in the Kibiti area in 2017.

In a previously unreported incident on 07 October, insurgents killed two civilians and set several houses and buildings on fire in a raid on the island of Makalowe/Macaloe, just off the coastal town of Pangane.  This came after insurgents launched multiple raids in the Mucojo area in early October.

Insurgents in early October were reported to have contacted the mayor of Manica village by phone, threatening him with death.  Insurgents in the area were reported to have stolen cell phones from many local residents in the Mucojo area during a series of raids earlier this month.  This enables insurgents to be able to target individual community/political/security leadership in different areas, and cuts off communications between local communities.  In some cases however insurgents have been geolocated by the government using cell phone data and subsequently targeted.

Reliable sources reported this week that a pro-government militia has been formed in recent months and is operating in Licangano, west of Macomia.  Local police units have reportedly provided arms to this group.  Insurgents were reportedly active in the Licangano area in September, though no other reports of insurgent activity in this area has been recently reported.

Reliable sources reported this week that a pro-government militia has been formed in recent months and is operating in the Lyaula and Nangude areas of Muidumbe District.  These villages are located west of the N380 road, near areas heavily impacted by insurgent attacks.  These groups may have been involved in recent clashes with insurgents in the Magaia area.

Pro-government militias in the past week were reported to have carried out an operation in the Chitunda area, searching for insurgents, though none were found.  Militias from Lyaula and Nangude were involved in this operation.

The port of Maputo from January to August recorded a drop of 13% volume of cargo compared to the same period in 2019 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.  This included a drop from 8.1 million tonnes of transit cargo to 7 million tonnes; most of this transit trade is to and from South Africa.

228 COVID cases were reported on 22 October in Mozambique, along with 2 new deaths.  This raised the nationwide total number of cases to 11,559, with 81 deaths.  156 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 49 cases in Maputo, 12 cases in Cabo Delgado, 6 in Zambezia, 4 in Gaza, and 1 in Manica.  The 156 new cases in Maputo City represented a new daily case high for the city.

The WFP reported on 23 October that more than 3,000 IDPs had landed at Cabo Delgado beaches over the previous 3 days fleeing from violence in insurgent impacted areas of Cabo Delgado.  Sources earlier this week had reported 3,400 IDPs arriving to the city between 16-20 October.  Reports continue to indicate that many of those arriving are dehydrated and malnourished.

Mozambique's National Institute for Disaster Management said on 22 Oct that over 424,000 people have been displaced by the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado and RENAMO dissident attacks in Central Mozambique. The largest number of displaced people, around 300,000, are displaced across Cabo Delgado.  Other displaced persons are spread throughout Niassa, Nampula, Zambezia, Sofala, and Inhamabne.

Insurgents on 20 October were reported to have attacked Churumba/Chumbua village in Quissanga, carrying out looting and setting homes on fire.  Insurgents previously had been reported to have raided the village on 17 October.

At least 22 people have died in the first weeks of the 2020/2021 rainy season.  992 houses have been destroyed in Manica, Zambezia, Maputo, and Maputo city. It has been projected that the rainy season could potentially impact 1,684,000 people across the country.

Sources indicated that Cabo Delgado insurgents had skirmished with Tanzanian security forces at Kilambo on the evening of 21 Oct, with insurgents pushed back after brief clashes.  No casualties have been reported.  This town is located about 27 kms from Kitaya, which was attacked by insurgents on 14 October, and is located less than 5kms from the Rovuma River, the border between Tanzania and Mozambique.  This report is currently unconfirmed.

A leaked audio message from 21 October reportedly from Commander of the Police's Rapid Intervention Unit (UIR) Francisco Quisasse is reported to have strongly criticized UIR officers for cowardice, saying he would prefer "10 highly combative men" rather than "1000 cowards".  UIR officers are frequently utilized in fighting against insurgents across Cabo Delgado.

A leaked audio message from 21 October reportedly from Commander of the Police's Rapid Intervention Unit Francisco Quisasse indicated that armed "former combatants", likely referring to veterans of the country's civil war, had secured Diaca village and were moving into the Awasse area.  This was part of a longer message allegedly directed at Rapid Intervention Unit members in which he strongly criticized some officers for cowardice in Cabo Delgado.

Friday is the first day of a 3 day planned closure of commercial establishments in Beira as part of a protest against ongoing kidnappings and security force inaction to stop these kidnappings.  Business leaders who are part of the "Beria Anti-Abduction Movement" said on Thursday this work stoppage would last 3 days, and that "next steps" would be announced after this period.  At least 3 prominent businessmen have been kidnapped from Beira this year, and kidnappings targeting business leaders are also common in Maputo City.  Reports on Friday indicated that between 70-80% of commercial establishments across the city were closed, pariticpating in this strike.

It was announced on 21 October after talks between President Nyusi and RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade that 3 RENAMO bases had been closed in Central Mozambique, and that 1,300 RENAMO armed members have so far been demobilized of around 5,000 armed RENAMO members.  The RENAMO base at Inhaminga was one of the three bases reported to have been officially closed down.

It was announced on 21 October after talks between President Nyusi and RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade that 3 RENAMO bases had been closed in Central Mozambique, and that 1,300 RENAMO armed members have so far been demobilized of around 5,000 armed RENAMO members.  The RENAMO base at Cheringoma was one of the three bases reported to have been officially closed down.

The RENAMO base at Maringue was one of the three bases reported to have been officially closed down.

78 Mozambican citizens were repatriated by South Africa to Mozambique at the Ressano Garcia border post. South Africa was reported to have carried out this action without first notifying Mozambican authorities.  Among those repatriated were a number of people serving jail sentences in South Africa.

Allied Democratic Forces rebel fighters linked to the Islamic State's Central Africa Province (ISCAP) attacked a prison in Beni in the DRC, setting free 1,300 prisoners on 20 October.  This attack is believed to be linked the Islamic State's "BREAKING THE WALLS" global campaign in which the group has encouraged its various affiliates to conduct prison break attacks across the world.  This has raised concerns over a potential attack by Cabo Delgado insurgents, who are believed to be linked to ISCAP, on Cabo Delgado's Mieze prison which holds large numbers of suspected insurgents.

A survey released on 22 October indicates that 3.56% of the population of Matola carry COVID anti-bodies.  The survey took 8,536 random samples between 14 September to 19 October.  This positivity rate if applied to the city's entire population would indicate over 36,700 cases in Matola.  Only just over 11,000 cases have been confirmed countrywide as of 23 October.

Sources on 22 October reported that at least 11 schools in Gondola District in Manica are unable to resume classes as they are in areas impacted by RENAMO dissident attacks, impacting over 5,250 students.  Many students in the area say they will not return to school for fear of attacks.

Local media reported that a young man from Chiure, Cabo Delgado, had recently joined the insurgency.  The young man was reportedly offered large amounts of money prior to joining and told he would receive a large monthly salary for joining the group.  Before leaving Chiure, he allegedly received an undisclosed amount of money via a mobile money transfer to his phone.

The Center for Democracy and Development (CDD) said on Friday that as many as 1,000 IDPs are arriving to Pemba port in Cabo Delgado per day, displaced by ongoing insurgent attacks in different areas of Cabo Delgado.  Many of those arriving are in poor health and require humanitarian assistance, and humanitarian supplies are running out in Pemba, different sources have said.  The CDD also said that it had been expected that at a recent meeting of the government's Council of Ministers, the deteriorating situation in Cabo Delgado would be discussed and a delegation of ministers would travel to Pemba to observe the situation firsthand, but that this did not occur.

Kidnappers on 18 October were reported to have attempted to kidnap the son of a Beira businessman.  The young man was able to escape the attempt but received at least one gunshot wound in the incident.  No other details on this attack are currently available.

189 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 23 October, including 113 new cases in Maputo City, 25 cases in Maputo, and 25 cases in Sofala.  One new death was also reported.  The total number of countrywide cases is now 11,748, with 82 deaths.

The World Bank on 23 October approved a new $100 million grant for Mozambique to help to mitigate economic impacts of the COVID pandemic by supporting the COVID response in the country, and providing support to businesses.

The pandemic has caused a reduction of about 80% traffic across Mozambique's borders, officials said on Friday.  Between 10-16 October, 20,909 exits and entries across these borders were reported, vs 102,306 entries and exits last year during the same week.

DAG helicopters on 20 October attacked and destroyed two insurgent motor boats at Matemo island, killing an unknown number of insurgents and hostages taken by the group.  Pro-government sources claimed that at least 5 boats used by insurgents had been destroyed, as had at least one mosque insurgents were hiding in, and that 34 insurgents were killed with 69 injured, along with an unknown number of civilians.  An alternative report said that on 21 October, insurgents had sailed from Matemo to the island of Quilhaule, where they were again attacked by military helicopters, and that all insurgents and their captives on board these vessels were killed, resulting in around 30 deaths.  These two reports of at least 30 deaths are believed to refer to a single incident that occurred on waters off Matemo.
Local sources reported that by 20 October, another 5 deaths due to diarrhea had occurred on Matemo Island.  10 deaths had previously been reported on 19 October among IDPs.

Police sources stated they had recently arrested a man who had "rented" weapons to kidnappers in Maputo City and seized two weapons in his possession.  This incident was reported on 23 October, though the exact date this incident took place was not clear.

Police sources stated that they had recently tracked a kidnap gang to the Ponta do Ouro area, where the gang intended to carry out an abduction.  An unknown number of gang members were arrested in this incident and vehicles seized.  This incident was reported on 23 October, though the exact date this incident occurred was unclear.
On 21 Oct, Dr Antonio Mujovo died of COVID-19 in Maputo City, the first physician to die of the virus during the pandemic in Mozambique.

The  National Human Rights Commission announced on Friday, 23 October that it will investigate cases regarding the maltreatment of Mozambicans in South Africa after South Africa this week deported a large group of Mozambican nationals back into Mozambique without first notifying Mozambican authorities.

The International Monetary Fund African Department Director announced that discussions will likely soon be conducted regarding a Mozambique financing programme to correct the economic imbalances. Abebe Aemro Selassie stated that the programme should encourage strong and solid recovery in response to the imbalances created by the COVID pandemic.  Mozambique is also likely to benefit from around $54 million in debt relief from the IMF in the near future.

Local elders complained that the National Institute for Social Action (INAS) had withdrawn Cyclone Idai aid stipends in Chimoio recently to many needy locals but was providing subsidies to other people who reportedly "do not need" these funds. INAS officials have denied these claims.  These complaints come after recent demonstrations in Chimoio, and could result in new unrest in the city.

Local source stated on 22 October that Police seized a pistol from two individuals during an operation in Maputo as part of a 2-month operation against illegal weapons possession.  It was unclear on what exact date this seizure occurred.

Police recovered two pistols found along public roads during a patrol in Chokwe, according to local sources.  This incident was reported on 22 October, though the exact date of the seizure was unclear.
Police seized a shotgun from an individual in Chipopo town of Machaze district. This incident was reported on 22 October, though the exact date of the seizure was unclear.
Police seized a Kalashnikov and shotgun from an individual in Alto-Benfica in Zambezia during an operation against illegal weapons possession.

Police seized 70 various weapons during an operation conducted from the 19 August until 21 October against illegal weapons possession in Maputo, Gaza, Manica, and Zambezia. Most of the weapons Kalashnikovs, Short-Gun, STAR, Browing, and Makarov brands.

President Filipe Nyusi announced on Saturday, 24 October a week-long ceasefire between the Mozambique Defence Armed Forces (FDS) and RENAMO dissidents, beginning on 25 October. The ceasefire is meant to allow new talks with the dissidents in an attempt to stop attack in the center of the country. The President stated that the FDS were ordered not to pursue the RENAMO dissidents during this time but will "remain on alert".

A three-week old male infant died due to COVID-19 infection in Maputo city on 23 October. Reports claimed that the child was diagnosed on 19 October. Total death cases in Mozambique due to COVID-19 is now 82.

A total of 45 sexual abuse cases of children by suspects over 60-yrs-old were recorded by the Mozambican Police from January to October 2020 in Manica. The city of Chimoio in Manica has the highest record with 15 cases.  This represented a doubling of these incidents compared to the same period in 2019.
A 60-yr old man sexually abused an 18-month-old baby in a suburb in Chimoio city, according to a report on 26 Oct. The incident took place last week. The suspects was later arrested by the police.
Security forces arrested a 60-yr-old man in Chimoio for allegedly raping an 18-month-old baby, according to a report on 26 Oct. The incident allegedly took place last week.

Beira businessmen continued their strike 24 October, keeping shop closed in the city to protest against the kidnapping incidents targeting businessmen and security force inaction. Shops, bakeries and businesses remained closed for three days until 26 October.

Beira businessmen continued their strike 25 October, keeping shop closed in the city to protest against the kidnapping incidents targeting businessmen and security force inaction. Shops, bakeries and businesses remained closed for three days until 26 October.
Two individuals were arrested on 24 Oct in Matola for vehicular theft.  The two were attempting to sell the vehicle when they were arrested.

147 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 24 October, including 90 new cases in Maputo City, 30 in Maputo, 10 in Manica, 9 in Gaza, 4 in Cabo Delgado, 3 in Inhambane, and 1 from Niassa.  4 new deaths were reported as well, bringing the countrywide death toll to 85.  There have been a total of 11,895 cases countrywide.  2562 cases are currently active.

Health officials reported 91 new COVID cases on 25 October, including 56 new cases in Maputo City, 14 in Maputo, 14 in Cabo Delgado, 3 in Gaza, 2 in Nampula, 1 in Zambezia, and 1 in Niassa.  1 new death was also reported from the virus.  This brought the total number of cases to 11,986, along with 86 deaths.

President Nyusi, speaking from Pemba, said on 24 October that he would bolster Mozambican military forces in Cabo Delgado "starting next week" as the fight against the insurgency continues in the area.  Nyusi landed in Macomia town on Saturday and met with military officers, and also flew over parts of the province impacted by the insurgency, saying he had seen villages destroyed by insurgent attacks.  Notably, in talks with local residents in Macomia, many asked to be evacuated to safer areas.  Over 300,000 people are already displaced from insurgency impacted areas of Cabo Delgado.  Nyusi during this visit also flew to Ibo island, where thousands have been displaced.

At least 7,402 IDPS were reported to have arrived on 127 boats between 16-23 October to Pemba, the IOM said over the weekend.  The majority of those arriving landed on Paquiteqete beach.  A majority of these new arrivals are coming from Mucojo AP and parts of Quissanga and Ibo Districts, including Matemo Island.  Insurgents have attacked all these areas recently, with reports that militants warned local residents to flee these areas and not to return.  Other IDPs have also been arriving in Metuge and Pemba via land routes.

The CIP released a report on 25 October saying that from October 2017 to October 2020, there have been over 600 terrorist attacks in Northern and Central Mozambique which have caused at least 2,000 deaths and have led to a displacement of at least 424,000 people. This 424,000 people represents about 1.4% of the country's total population.  The more than 300,000 people displaced in Cabo Delgado represents about 13% of the province's population. This also represents an increase of more than 2700% displaced persons from between 2018 - 2020.  Only about 4.6% meanwhile of those displaced are currently housed in IDP reception centers.

Sources have indicated that youths in the Pundanhar area have recently received training, weapons and supplies from the Mozambican military to assist in combating insurgents active in the area.  Pro-gov militia activity in the Pundanhar area reportedly triggered an insurgent attack on the village on 26 October.

Local sources stated that insurgents raided the village of Pundanhar at approximately 1600 on the afternoon of Monday, 26 October, lighting a number of houses there on fire. A border guard sergeant and one other  person were killed in the attack. Insurgents reportedly left messages behind saying that the attack had been launched in revenge for local youths having participated in clashes against insurgents.  Militants also said they could return to the area for new attacks "at any moment".
President Filipe  Nyusi called for the unconditional removal of sanctions imposed on Zimbabwe by the international community during anti-sanctions day, 25 October.

Two organizations representing Mozambican doctors on 23 October said there is a lack of personal protective equipment in the fight against COVID-19. In the letter written on 23 October, medical professionals claimed that they needed urgent action to improve prevention and treatment management of the general population in relation to COVID 19.

Total said recently that it has invested $ 200 million into Mozambican companies for projects associated with the LNG projects on the Afungi Peninsula.  This is part of $850 million Total will invest in local companies associated with these projects.

On 26 October, community leaders in Nampula demanded an increase in allowances in recognition of their contribution to FRELIMO victories in the province in the 2019 elections.  Their demands were recognized by Governor Manuel Rodrigues, however immediate solution was not offered.

On 23 October, Standard & Poor’s (S&P) maintained the rating  of Mozambique's foreign currency debt at CCC+ or below investment recommendation. The country's rating is the third lowest on the scale of sovereign credit quality.  S&P said this relatively low rating is due to Mozambique's "low GDP per capital, fragile governance and institutions, large external and budget deficits, and huge debt burden", which will remain above 100% of GDP until at least 2023.

Security forces arrested a 29-yr-old Ethiopian at a checkpoint in Tete last week over alleged connection in facilitating smuggling of migrants. The suspect was accused of accompanying 37 Ethiopians being trafficked into Changara district.

An 18-yr-old girl died due to severe dehydration and illness while travelling to Pemba among other IDPs on 24 October. The woman was among a large group of IDPs who travelled from insurgent impacted areas and had virtually no food or water during their journey.
A civilian lost his life while travelling to Pemba on 25 October by boat among other IDPs.  The man was fleeing from Pangane when his condition deteriorated.

Sources reported that at least 10,000 IDPs have arrived in Pemba by boat since 16 October as of 26 October. These IDPs have primarily come from Quissanga, Macomia and Ibo districts which have been impacted by the insurgency. More than 300,000 people are now displaced as the humanitarian situation in Cabo Delgado province rapidly deteriorated for the last 10 months.

The Ministry of Health (MISAU) recorded 175 new COVID-19 cases on 26 October, with total number 12,161 cases.  Two more deaths were recorded bringing the total deaths to 88.  Maputo City has 2,014 active cases, Maputo has 482 cases, while less than 70 active cases have been confirmed in the rest of the country.

A large number of Rapid Intervention Unit ((UIR) officers on 21 October were reported to have deserted their posts in Pemba.  Officers in the city reportedly had low morale and criticized their commanders, saying the ongoing war in Cabo Delgado was benefitting certain powerful people in the country.  Local sources meanwhile said that some dissenting UIR officers had been imprisoned in the Mieze prison outside of Pemba.

Local media reported that the Tanzanian villages of Mihambwe, Chicongo, and Nanyamba along the Rovuma River had received threats from insurgents regarding potential attacks targeting these areas.  Insurgents on 14 October raided the village of Kitaya, just across the Rovuma River from Cabo Delgado, killing 23 people.

Bishop of Pemba Luiz Fernando Lisboa in a 23 October interview indicated that there could be as many as 80,000 IDPs in Pemba.  Another organization recently said that there could be as many as 80,000 IDPs in the city in the near future.  One other source reported that there are more than 100,000 IDPs in the Pemba area It is unclear if there are indeed that many IDPs in Pemba, though over 10,000 IDPs did arrive into the city between 16-26 October.

Two police officers on the morning of 25 October fired shots targeting three fishermen at the ADPP crossroads for unknown reasons.  Local residents then attacked the two officers for firing on the fishermen; the officers then fled the area.

Two police officers on the morning of 25 October fired shots targeting three fishermen at the ADPP crossroads for unknown reasons.  Local residents then attacked the two officers for firing on the fishermen; the officers then fled the area.

Sources reported that IDPs that have fled into Palma District are provided with almost no supplies except for water for handwashing.  This report comes as thousands of IDPs over the past two weeks have fled insurgent zones south towards Pemba; a smaller number of residents in past months have also fled parts of Palma and Mocimboa da Praia District to safer areas of Palma.

A report released on 26 October by the Center for Public Integrity (CIP) said that many IDPs in Cabo Delgado have been the victims of sexual abuse or attempted sexual abuse.  In many cases, local officials who have the power to put IDPs on official IDP lists for those who should receive aid withhold placing names on lists in exchange for sexual favors from vulnerable women and girls.  These kinds of incidents have been reported most commonly in Pemba, with a smaller number of incidents reported in Nampula.

RENAMO Military Junta leader Mariano Nhongo said on 26 October that he had not been contacted by the government on a potential dialogue; this came after President Nyusi declared a ceasefire with the dissident group for 1 week beginning on 25 October.  Nhongo said he would only hold talks with Nyusi and not with RENAMO chief Ossufo Momade.  Nhongo also said Momade must be removed from RENAMO leadership for any negotiation to be successful. Nhongo also said he doubted the government was sincere that it wanted negotiations, saying FRELIMO supporters recently kidnapped two people in Gorongosa.  He also warned his group would not enter into "false negotiations".

RENAMO dissident chief Mariano Nhongo said that two RENAMO dissidents had been "kidnapped" in the Gorongosa area on 25 October by FRELIMO, on the first day of the truce. This report is currently unverified.

112 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 27 October, including 29 cases in Maputo City, 29 in Sofala, 23 in Maputo, 12 in Cabo Delgado, 11 in Gaza, 4 in Zambezia, 3 in Tete, and 1 in Manica.  This brought the nationwide total number of cases to 12,273.  One new death was also reported in Maputo City, bringing the nationwide death toll to 89.

Mozambican officials said on 26 October that they anticipate that the bridge over the Montepuez River along the N380 road will be full repaired within 2 months.  This bridge was destroyed by flooding last December.

column4: Road traffic along the Palma-Pundanhar road was reported to have been halted on 26 October after an insurgent attack on Pundanhar, causing a significant rise in prices in Palma town.  It is unclear when traffic along this road will resume, with insurgents believed to still be in the vicinity of the road.
Prices of basic goods increased significantly in Palma on 26-27 October after road traffic into the town from the Pundanhar road was cut after an insurgent attack on Pundanhar on 26 October.
The UN said on Tuesday that Foreign Direct Investment to Mozambique had decreased by 27% in 2020 to $0.8 billion due to the ongoing global pandemic during the first half of 2020.
3 cholera cases were diagnosed amongst IDPs in Montepuez who recently fled from Macomia, sources reported on 26 October.
Around 150 cases of diarrhea and other illnesses have been reported among IDPs who have recently fled to Pemba from insurgency impacted areas of Cabo Delgado.

Nacala Airport is set to re-open to traffic in November, after 6 months of closure due to COVID-19. LAM will restart flights to and from the airport while cargo is expected to be transported between Nacala and Palma as well.  Ethiopian Airlines is also reportedly considering flights to and from Nacala.

EDM was reported on 27 October to have called for "intervention" at 12 electric substations across Maputo, Gaza, and Inhamabne to prevent overloading, saying that six high voltage transmission lines across the south have reached capacity.

The South African Navy is reportedly considering establishing a new permanent base at Richard's Bay on the KwaZulu-Natala north coast near the border with Mozambique in response to recent insurgent attacks off the coast of Cabo Delgado.

Mozambique has the lowest COVID-19 fatality rate among the countries of South African Development Community SADC. The fatality rate is only 0.7%, that is 88 deaths out of 12,161 cases.  It is widely believed based on anti-body testing that COVID rates have been much higher in Mozambique than official numbers, though death rates do appear to have remained low.

Police officers allegedly caught and filmed a couple having sexual intercourse in a vehicle and posted it on social media in Maputo over the weekend. The couple will be filing a criminal case for the 5 officers. The spokesman for the police stated that the officers violated the law and will be disciplined accordingly.

Around 150 municipal workers in Gorongosa have yet received their salaries for the past four months due to poor collection of revenue. Officials claimed that efforts are made to pay the workers' pending salary immediately.

Authorities in Pemba say that the city has effectively run out of space to hold IDPs arriving in the city.  This comes after over 10,000 IDPs arrived to Pemba from between 16-26 October.  Pemba's mayor, Florete Simba Motarua, said meanwhile that the port city had a population of around 204,000 according to the 2017 census, but currently has a population of over 300,000 with waves of IDPs arriving in the city in recent years, driven from their home areas by the ongoing insurgency.  Maotarua said the city has no land to build new reception centers for those arriving.

President Nyusi said on 28 October that the RENAMO Military Junta had carried out a new attack on a passenger bus in Sofala province on 26 October, after the government's unilaterally declared truce began on 25 October.  This attack reportedly took place between Zove and the Gorongodzi River, in Chibabava District when gunmen fired on a passenger bus at around 1800hrs.  No injuries were reported.  Nyusi indicated that the truce still was in effect, saying that news of the truce may not have reached RENAMO dissidents before this previously unreported incident occurred.

Police in Pemba on 27 October were reported to have be preventing the recording of videos or taking of pictures of displaced people arriving to Paquiteqete beach in Pemba.  This came after the arrival of as many as 12,000 IDPs between 16-27 October to the city, which has led to growing pressure on the Mozambican government to provide humanitarian support to these IDPs.

Local residents in the Koko area, south of Macomia along the N380 road are reported to be forming a pro-government militia in order to counter insurgent attacks in the area.  Insurgents had attacked the village on 19-20 October.

5 additional deaths from diarrhea on Matemo island have been reported in the past week among IDPs.  This is an increase from 15 deaths already reported, bringing the total number of diarrhea related deaths on the island in recent weeks among IDPs to 20.

Several Rapid Intervention Unit (UIR) officers were reported last week to have been arrested following reports that they had refused to conduct patrols in Pemba. Those officers arrested were reportedly sent to Mieze prison, west of Cabo Delgado.

Sources indicated on 27 October that between 16-27 October at least 12,000 IDPs had arrived to Pemba via 150 boats, displaced by the ongoing insurgency.  Previous reports from 26 October indicated 10,000 IDPs had arrived to the city since 16 October.

PRM Commander General Bernardo Rafael claimed on 29 October that security forces in clashes in the last 3 days had killed 108 insurgents near an insurgent base known as "Siria/Syria", which pro-government sources indicated was located along the Messalo River in the vicinity of Miangalewa, XItaxi, and Nguri.    Security sources also on Thursday said that they had destroyed 3 tones of food products recently looted from local communities by insurgents.  Security forces allegedly also destroyed 6 insurgent encampments, 15 vehicles, and 20 motorcycles in these operations.  Rafael said that on Thursday morning, 19 insurgents were killed in a single attack on this base while 89 more "terrorists" had been killed in the general vicinity of this base in the past 72 hours.  The 108 insurgents reportedly killed is regarded as questionable at this time.  Interior Minister Amade Miquidade later however said that just 22 insurgents had been killed by security forces in the past 3 days.  Government sources also indicated that insurgent "leaders of foreign nationality" had been targeted in these operations.  Unconfirmed pro-government claims previously indicated that Mozambican soldiers had clashed with insurgents in the Nguri and "Syria" areas on 25-26 October.

column4: Pro-government sources indicated that 89 Cabo Delgado insurgents were killed in clashes between 26-28 October in a government assault on the insurgent base of "Syria", believed to be located along the Messalo River between Miangalewa and the Mbau Forest in Mocimboa da Praia.  Insurgent camps and up to 35 insurgent vehicles and motorcycles were destroyed in these attacks, pro-government sources said.  Government sources also said that between 19-22 insurgents were killed in a government assault in this area on the morning of 29 Oct.  The report is currently unconfirmed.
column15: Messalo River between Mbau Forest and Miangalewa

column4: 142 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 28 October.  This brought the nationwide total number of cases to 12,415.  Two new death were also reported in Maputo City, bringing the nationwide death toll to 91.
An inspection campaign has been launched on 27 Oct for 10 days by Maputo City Council to crack down on unlicensed car wash stores.

The 2020 Global Hunger Index report showed that Mozambique was one of the 40 countries where hunger problem is classified as "serious". The GHI scoring is based on the values of four indicators- undernourishment, child wasting, child stunting and child mortality.

Illegal extraction of sand is reportedly  ongoing in the districts of Inhassunge and Chinde, Zambezia. Residents claimed that foreign vessels have docked in the area and load unspecified quantities of heavy sand at night. Source stated that the local authorities were aware of this yet no action has been taken against these smugglers.
