Residents claimed that foreign vessels have docked in the area and load unspecified quantities of heavy sand at night. Source stated that the local authorities were aware of this yet no action has been taken against these smugglers.
Zimbabwe announced it would re-open land borders on 01 December following the closure of borders to contain the spread of COVID-19.

The Mozambique Government approved on 27 Oct a bill that will make active journalists carry a state-issued media card.  This bill will next be debated in parliament, where the FRELIMO majority is likely to pass it.

Zimbabwe called on SADC to aid Mozambique in its fight against Islamist insurgency on 28 October. Ruling party ZANU-PF said on Wednesday that the country is ready to provide military assistance to Mozambique, however, the decision must be a collective SADC-AU initiative.  ZANU-PF called regional assistance to Mozambique "urgent", saying the "odds are stacked against the Mozambican military". Mozambique to date has not made an official appeal to the SADC for direct assistance in fighting the insurgency, but did recently request indirect support from the EU.

Daily numbers of displaced people arriving in Pemba have decreased this week, sources at the port have revealed. The number has fallen to about 500 daily arrivals since Monday, as opposed to an average of 1,000 new IDPs arriving daily last week.  On Tuesday, 374 people were reported to have arrived; at least 12 of these were described as "seriously ill" with diarrhea, vomiting, and malaria.  Current estimates indicate there are more than 1,000 IDPs currently in Pemba.

The Mozambique Government said on 28 October that it is concerned that much of the country's population is disregarding COVID-19 prevention measures. This is in relation to social distancing in public places and family events, frequent hand washing, and other measures.

Interior Minister Amade Miquidade on 28 October was reported to have "demanded" that RENAMO hand over all information it possessed regarding the RENAMO Military Junta group.  This caused a heated debate in parliament.  Miquidade said RENAMO dissidents are using bases and armed caches previously possessed by the mainstream RENAMO group and said the government wants information on these bases and arms. He demanded that RENAMO provide info in relation to the "bases, men, location, and hiding places".

President Nyusi said on 28 October that dialogue between the government and the RENAMO Military Junta had begun with a view towards ending attacks in the center of the country.  The dissidents however have not commented on these talks other than to say earlier this week that the government had not reached out to them.  Interior Minister Amade Miquidade meanwhile said on 28 October that the government had received information that a number of dissidents wanted to abandon armed attacks.

The Islamic State claimed credit for new clashes in Cabo Delgado with security forces on 28 October, saying multiple Mozambican soldiers were killed in these clashes and ammunition seized from the troops.  These clashes are believed to have occurred between Miangalewa and the Mbau Forest along the Messalo River, and came after the government claimed it had killed at least 22 insurgents in clashes in the area over the past 3 days.
column15: Messalo River between Mbau Forest and Miangalewa

column4: The National Institute of Communications of Mozambique (INCM) said on 28 October that it would block mobile phone sim cards that are not registered by 06 November.  The government has in the past issued similar threats, including in 2010, 2015, and 2016, and it is not clear if the INCM would actually follow through with this threat.

Interior Minister Amade Miquidade on 28 October admitted the Mozambican government was utilizing private security companies and private military contractors in Cabo Delgado, the first public admission by the government that it does use the private contractors in the conflict.  The government had previously denied these reports or refused to comment.  Miquidade said that "international companies require a type of protection that only private security companies can adequately provide".

Interior Minister Amade Miquidade said on 28 October that reports of 270 insurgents killed in the Awasse area in fighting with security forces between 16-18 October were "rumors".  Several pro-government sources reported this high death toll previously.

Exxon Mobil's managing director Jos Evens for Mozambique said Wednesday that no final investment decision had been made on Area 4 in the Mamba reserves area of the Rovuma Basin.  Evens also said that Area 4 partners would discuss the project next year.

Several images shared online by pro-government sources this week purportedly showed Mozambican armed forces carrying out operations against insurgents in Awasse, Matemo, and "Syria 1 and 2 Bases". Pictures from Matemo were geo-located and shown to be actually located in Mocimboa da Praia town.  Other locations seen in these pictures were unverified.

Unconfirmed reports by pro-government sources on 28 October indicated that the security forces in recent days carried out aerial patrols over Pangane, Mucojo, Quiterajo, Mocímboa da Praia, Ulumbe, Namoto, Nhica do Rovuma, Diaca, Awasse, Xitaxi, Mianguale and Primeiro de Maio across Cabo Delgado, saying all of these towns and villages were abandoned by both local residents and insurgents and were not under the direct control of insurgents.

MDM representatives in Nampula on 05 October closed their primary political offices in the city, protesting against Vasco Napaua, their local MDM representative.  This is one of several ongoing internal MDM disputes, and several MDM members in recent months have abandoned the party, the third largest in the country, and joined RENAMO, the main opposition party in the country.

The Mozambican Prime Minister, Carlos Agostinho do Rosario, told parliament on 28 October that the number of displaced people throughout Mozambique has risen to 435,000 people do to the Cabo Delgado insurgency and RENAMO dissident attacks in Central Mozambique.

Total said that between January and October it had transported 174 tons of food, 104 tons of educational material, 4.2 tons of medical supplies, and 1.5 million liters of fuel to Palma district.  Much of this was transported by road.  Total said that while it was pleased to have provided this support, this was also "not a viable, long-term solution" for the district, also noting that O&G projects on the Afungi Peninsula should bring very significant revenues into Palma District and the wider province of Cabo Delgado.

Confederation of Economic Associations (CTA) President, Agostinho Vuma, tested positive for COVID on 28 October. Vuma reportedly was asymptomatic and has conducted self-quarantine followed by the positive test result. CTA called on those who had contact with Vuma to be vigilant and take precautions.
STS Mozambique freed a trapped hippopotamus caught on a double cable snare after in Maputo Special Reserve on 29 October. The animal was reportedly seen dragging a log which was tied to cables.

The Fund for Investment and Assets of Water Supply (FIPAG) regional director announced that several chemical substances may affect water distribution in Tete and Moatize. Around 268,000 families were suspected to be affected by the deposit of nitrogen oxide and hydroxide. The chemical deposits may also reportedly reduce water pressure within several neighborhoods of the mentioned areas.

The Fund for Investment and Assets of Water Supply (FIPAG) regional director announced that several chemical substances may affect water distribution in Tete and Moatize. Around 268,000 families were suspected to be affected by the deposit of nitrogen oxide and hydroxide. The chemical deposits may also reportedly reduce water pressure within several neighborhoods of the mentioned areas.

RENAMO Spokesman, Jose Manteigas, stated that the opposition party had nothing to negotiate with RENAMO dissidents and called on the dissidents to join the peace agreement and start the Disarmament, Demobilization, and Reintegration process.  This came after government ministers called on RENAMO to negotiate with the dissidents after President Nyusi declared a one week ceasefire with the RENAMO Military Junta starting on 25 October.

President Felipe Nyusi announced that resumption of issuing tourist visas and the end of the requirement for quarantines for those who arrived with a negative PCR test result from the past 72 hours. The president also said that PCR test validity for multiple entries to the country has been set to 14 days since the date of the sample collection.  Children up to 11 years old are exempted from having to present a negative COVID test.  Nyusi also announced that from 15 November, all training of national sports teams may also resume.  7th grade classes meanwhile and adult literacy classes will resume on 02 November.

Local Pemba residents during a meeting with the city council demanded increased security due to robberies conducted in Natite and Cariaco neighborhoods in the city during the evenings. Locals also stated that corrupt policemen were stopping local residents and impounding vehicles if they refused to pay bribes around 50 to 100 meticais.

Local Pemba residents during a meeting with the city council demanded increased security due to robberies conducted in Natite and Cariaco neighborhoods in the city during the evenings. Locals also stated that corrupt policemen were stopping local residents and impounding vehicles if they refused to pay bribes around 50 to 100 meticais.

Mozambique on 29 October reported 110 new COVID cases and no new deaths.  This brought the total number of cases to 12,525 countrywide. This included 58 new cases in Maputo City, 22 in Maputo, 13 in Cabo Delgado, 9 in Tete, 3 in Zambezia, 2 in Gaza, 2 in Manica, and 1 in Inhambane. There are currently 1,860 active cases in Maputo City, 238 active cases in Maputo province, and less than 100 cases spread throughout the rest of the country.

The Muidumbe District government issued a circular on 23 October, saying that all state officials and agents who have left the district must return to their positions in the district by 01 November, saying that security has been restored in the district which will allow the beginning of reconstruction works and the resumption of public services.  Any government employee not reporting to their post will have their "absences marked and their salaries will be discounted".  Muidumbe District despite this circular is still threatened by insurgent attacks, though pro-government militia and security forces have repelled some recent attack attempts in the district.

Unexplained gunfire was reported in the vicinity of Nanga north of Macomia on 28 October.  Many local residents fled into the woods out of fear.  No further information on this incident is currently available.

Unexplained gunfire was reported in the vicinity of Nacate south of Macomia on 28 October.  Many local residents fled into the woods out of fear.  No further information on this incident is currently available.

Interior Minister Amade Miquidade on 29 October acknowledged that security force operations recently that have targeted insurgents in parts of Cabo Delgado have displaced local civilians, but said that the operations were necessary to re-establish security in the province.
column15: Messalo River between Mbau Forest and Miangalewa

column4: 252 people tested positive for COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, Mozambique's Ministry of Health reported.  173 new cases were reported in Maputo City, with 54 reported in Maputo Province, bringing the nationwide total number of cases to 12,777.  The death toll stands at 91.

Officials announced the completion of the restoration of the bridge connecting Monapo to Monapo Rio on 30 October. The rehabilitation cost around 5 million USD, which separated the railway, pedestrian walkway, and vehicle bridge.

Local sources stated that on 30 October illegal miners are active in parts of Manica, Tete, and Sofala.  Security forces only intermittently target these mining sites but often allow them to operate.   Many gold smugglers later sell illegally mined gold in Maputo City.

Mozambique National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) incinerated a large quantity of illegal drugs in Beira on 30 October.  The drug were intended to be smuggled on a ship bound for Kenya and had been seized in August.

Several sources reported insurgents on the morning of 31 October attacked Muidumbe/Namacade, the district capital of Muidumbe District.  Insurgents also attacked several nearby villages simultaneously. At least 9 people were killed in this series of attacks, including at least 5 people killed near the district capital. One report indicated that insurgents launched the Muidumbe attacks in retaliation for clashes between 16-18 October near Awasse where insurgents were reported to have suffered significant casualties.  Insurgents reportedly remained active in Muidumbe District into Sunday, 01 November.

The Islamic State's Central Africa Province (ISCAP) on 30 October claimed its fighters had attacked three "Christian villages" in Mtwara District of Tanzania near the "artificial border" between Tanzania and Mozambique, causing "material damage" in attacks on 28 Oct. The group also said its fighters had returned to "their positions safely" after the raids. Fires were reported in the Michenjele area, while attacks in Kitama and Nanyamba wards were also reported.  One source in Tandahimba District indicated 5 people had been killed in an attack in the area in an attack, though this information has not yet been confirmed  Note that the district where attacks reportedly did occur are in Newala District, and not in neighboring Mtwara as claimed by ISCAP.  All the attacked wards are within at most 13 miles / 21 kms of Cabo Delgado.

At least 7 people in the Mandimba village area of Nangade District approx 50 km southwest of Palma were injured by two separate rocket barrages fired believed to have been fired by the Tanzanian military, according to local sources on 29 and 30 October.  Other sources later also reported this incident.  Tanzanian military units were believed to have launched these rocket strikes targeting insurgents after insurgent incursions were reported into Tanzania between 28-30 October.  The village is located about 7kms from the Rovuma River, and about 19kms/12 miles from Pundanhar, where insurgents have recently been active. Those injured were all evacuated to intensive care at local medical facilities. The Mozambican authorities have yet to release official statement on the cross border fire.

At least 7 people in the Mandimba village area of Nangade District approx 50 km southwest of Palma were injured by two separate rocket barrages fired believed to have been fired by the Tanzanian military, according to local sources on 29 and 30 October.  Other sources later also reported this incident.  Tanzanian military units were believed to have launched these rocket strikes targeting insurgents after insurgent incursions were reported into Tanzania between 28-30 October.  The village is located about 7kms from the Rovuma River, and about 19kms/12 miles from Pundanhar, where insurgents have recently been active. Those injured were all evacuated to intensive care at local medical facilities. The Mozambican authorities have yet to release official statement on the cross border fire.

The Islamic State's Central Africa Province on 01 November published a claim saying the group had taken control of Muidumbe/Namacade town in Muidumbe District, also saying several Mozambican soldiers had been killed and captured when insurgent launched an attack on a barracks in the town.  The claim said that "IS fighters informed" the Islamic State's propaganda wing Amaq that they had captured the town after these clashes.  This claim is unconfirmed, and comes after insurgents on the night of 30-31 October launched attacks on several Muidumeb District villages.

Speaking on 31 October in an interview released on Sunday, RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo said that peace talks with the Maputo government, which reportedly took place through UN special envoy to Mozambique Mirko Manzoni, had failed.  Nhongo said he spoke with Manzoni on Friday.  Nhongo also said that the one-week ceasefire which ended on 31 October was used by the government as a tool to "harass" the RENAMO Military Junta.  Nhongo said that in order for there to be any new negotiations, the government must publish terms proposed by the RENAMO dissidents that were sent to the Maputo government in September of 2019. Both sides almost immediately accused one another of breaking the ceasefire after President Nyusi unilaterally declared a one-week cessation of hostilities starting on 25 October.  It is not clear if any direct talks actually ever took place between the government and the dissidents, or if all communication came through UN rep Manzoni
Insurgents on 31 October were reported to have kidnapped 5 people in an attack on Pundanhar during a raid on the village.

Insurgents over the night of 30-31 October attacked Pundanhar. This attack took place as many civilians were fleeing the area after insurgents also attacked the area 4 days prior.  Insurgents further south launched simultaneous attacks on several Muidumbe District villages.  Sources later indicated military troops ambushed militants in the area.

Insurgents on the morning of 31 October attacked Muatide, Muidumbe District, west of Muidumbe/Namacade town.  Insurgents also attacked several nearby villages simultaneously.  At least 3 people were killed in the Muatide attack; multiple houses were also set on fire in this raid.  One report indicated that insurgents launched the Muidumbe attacks in retaliation for clashes between 16-18 October near Awasse where insurgents were reported to have suffered significant casualties.

Several sources reported insurgents on the morning of 31 October attacked Miteda village, Muidumbe District, west of Muidumbe/Namacade town and southeast of Mueda town.  Sources said 3 civilians were killed by insurgents in this attack. Insurgents also attacked several nearby villages simultaneously. One report indicated that insurgents launched the Muidumbe attacks in retaliation for clashes between 16-18 October near Awasse where insurgents were reported to have suffered significant casualties.

Several sources reported insurgents over the morning of 31 October attacked Muambula town, Muidumbe District, just southwest of Muidumbe/Namacade town.  Insurgents also attacked several nearby villages simultaneously.  One report indicated that insurgents launched the Muidumbe attacks in retaliation for clashes between 16-18 October near Awasse where insurgents were reported to have suffered significant casualties.  Sources later said at least one family was killed in Muambula during this attack, with at least 3 people killed.

Several sources reported insurgents on the morning of 31 October attacked Nchinga village, Muidumbe District, just north of Muidumbe/Namacade town.  At least 5 civilians were beheaded in this attack. Insurgents also attacked several nearby villages simultaneously.  In this attack, insurgents kidnapped several children from the village.

Several sources reported insurgents on the morning of 31 October attacked Nchinga village, Muidumbe District, just north of Muidumbe/Namacade town.  Insurgents also attacked several nearby villages simultaneously. One report indicated that insurgents launched the Muidumbe attacks in retaliation for clashes between 16-18 October near Awasse where insurgents were reported to have suffered significant casualties.

Several sources reported insurgents on the morning of 31 October attacked 24 March village, Muidumbe District, west of Muidumbe/Namacade town and near Muatide village which was also raided.  Insurgents also attacked several nearby villages simultaneously.  At least one person was killed in this attack.  Insurgents in this raid also occupied and damaged a local church, and destroyed facilities of a local radio station.  Hundreds fled into the bush after this attack.

119 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 01 November, with 1 additional death also reported. 93 deaths have now been reported countrywide. 67 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 27 in  Cabo Delgado, 8 in Maputo, 7 in Zambezia, 6 in Tete, 2 in Niassa, and 2 in Inhambane.  There are currently 2,452 active cases in the country.

Insurgents on the morning of 31 October attacked Namacule village, Muidumbe District, just south of Muambula village, which was also attacked.  Insurgents also attacked several nearby villages simultaneously.  One report indicated that insurgents launched the Muidumbe attacks in retaliation for clashes between 16-18 October near Awasse where insurgents were reported to have suffered significant casualties.

Insurgents on the morning of 31 October attacked Namade village, Muidumbe District, just west of Muambula village, which was also attacked.  Insurgents also attacked several nearby villages simultaneously.  One report indicated that insurgents launched the Muidumbe attacks in retaliation for clashes between 16-18 October near Awasse where insurgents were reported to have suffered significant casualties.

Insurgents on the morning of 31 October attacked Nampanha village, Muidumbe District, south of Muambula village, which was also attacked.  Insurgents also attacked several nearby villages simultaneously.  One report indicated that insurgents launched the Muidumbe attacks in retaliation for clashes between 16-18 October near Awasse where insurgents were reported to have suffered significant casualties.

Insurgents on the morning of 31 October attacked Magaia village, Muidumbe District, northeast of Muidumbe/Namacade town.  Insurgents also attacked several nearby villages that morning.  One report indicated that insurgents launched the Muidumbe attacks in retaliation for clashes between 16-18 October near Awasse where insurgents were reported to have suffered significant casualties.  Magaia village had previously been the site of two previous clashes between pro-gov militias and insurgents.

A Rwandan citizen was arrested last week by police in Marracuene, Maputo province, for trafficking shark fins and endangered marine animals.  The man had reportedly procured poached animals in Vilankulo, Inhambane, and intended to sell them to a customer in Maputo city.

A Rwandan citizen was arrested last week by police in Marracuene, Maputo province, for trafficking shark fins and endangered marine animals.  The man had reportedly procured poached animals in Vilankulo, Inhambane, and intended to sell them to a customer in Maputo city.
Rains over the weekend caused some flooding and destruction of crops in Muecate, Nampula, and Monapo Districts of Nampula Province.

Tanzanian authorities were reported on 31 October to be blocking the exports of basic goods across the border into Mozambique as part of a strategy to attempt to "starve" the insurgency operating in Cabo Delgado.  This came after reports over the weekend of new raids on Tanzanian border villages launched by Cabo Delgado insurgents.

Palma town continues to be largely without electricity, sources reported on 02 November, except by generator.  This contradicts reports that EDM had recently restored power to the town.  Supply shortages and high prices also continue in Pemba.

Security forces in recent days are reported to have resumed house to house searches as part of anti-terror operations in Palma town.  These kinds of operations had recently been halted briefly in Palma.

About 532,000 7th grade students were set on 02 Nov to resume face to face classes across Mozambique in 8,000 public primary schools.  This came after President Nyusi announced the resumption of these classes last week.  Students will be required to wear masks, wash hands, socially distance, and observe other anti-COVID measures.  Only schools in some parts of the insurgency impacted zone of Cabo Delgado will not be able to open on Monday.

Clashes were reported on 31 October and 01 November in the Muidumbe/Namacade town area between insurgents and Mozambican military troops.  Troops were reportedly supported by DAG helicopters.  One unverified source said troops had retreated but clashes continued between pro-government militias and insurgents.

Clashes were reported on 31 October and 01 November in the Muidumbe/Namacade town area between insurgents and Mozambican military troops.  Troops were reportedly supported by DAG helicopters.  One unverified source said troops had retreated but clashes continued between pro-government militias and insurgents.

Mozambique said on 01 November that all expiring driving licenses can be renewed until 31 December, even if they expire before that date.  This is to ease demands on Mozambican authorities attempting to renew these drivers licenses while also dealing with anti-COVID restrictions.

Sources reported hundreds of people were displaced in Muidumbe over the weekend due to insurgent attacks.  Local populations fled into the bush in the area, with almost no basic supplies.  Insurgents as of 01 November still remained in the Muidumbe town area, and it was unclear when civilians could return to their homes.

Cabo Delgado provincial governor Valige Tauabo warned over the weekend that the 2020-2021 harvest in Cabo Delgado has likely been  impacted due to thousands of farmers displaced across the province due to the ongoing insurgency.  This impact however at least according to government statistics may be less significant than expected, with just 5,900 hectares of land not planted due to the insurgency, while over 569,000 hectares have been planted in the province.
A local rapper, Bander, and his two companions were arrested for theft in Maputo  He pleaded not guilty as they only stole a plasma TV in a house of an acquaintance.

On 02 November, 142 new cases of COVID were announced in Mozambique as well as one new death, bringing the total number of cases to 13,130  and the total number of deaths to 94.  74 new cases were reported in Maputo City, followed by Cabo Delgado with 41 mew cases.  15 new cases of hospitalizations due to COVID were reported in Maputo City in the last day meanwhile, brining the total number of hospitalizations countrywide to 60; 58 of these patients are in Mpauto City.

The Media Institute of Southern Africa's Mozambique chapter (MISA) accused the Maputo government on 02 Nov of failing to protect journalists against threats and violence, and said the government often uses state institutions to "intimidate journalists".  The group calls on the authorities to take steps and establish appropriate measures for the protection of journalists, especially those working in high risk areas.

28 fishing boats were seized for illegally fishing this year in the Bazaruto Archipelago National Park's protected waters, according to park's administrator, Armando Nguenha, on 02 Nov. 29 buoys were anchored along the perimeter of the protected waters, however, Inhambane Governor Daniel Chapo believed that these buoys are not enough to prevent illegal fishermen operating in the protected area. Chapo called on the society to cooperate in protecting and preserving the park and its wildlife.

206 police officers were expelled by the  Police of the Republic of Mozambique (PRM) from January to September 2020 due to unsatisfactory conduct, Commander-General Bernardino Rafael stated on 30 Oct. Expelled officers were allegedly involved in various disciplinary issues, including criminal cases.  This was out of a total of 326 officers prosecuted in 2020 between January and September for "disciplinary issues and even criminal acts".

Around 700 people from 137 families from the districts of Nhamatanda and Gorongosa have been displaced over the past three weeks due to the RENAMO dissident attacks in Central Mozambique. Instituto Nacional de Gestão de Calamidade (INGC) is providing food and clothes to the IDPs.   IDPs said that attacks had intensified in March of this year, and said in October, "attackers" had killed 3 people, raped three girls, carried out looting, and set several homes on fire in these districts

A boat carrying refugees capsized near the island of  Makalowe on 29 October at about 1900hrs.  54 people have drowned, including women and children; 20 people survived the accident. The victims were fleeing from the ongoing conflict in other parts of Cabo Delgado to Pemba City. The boat began its journey from Palma town, picking up a large number of passengers in the Namandingo area, sailing towards Makalowe.  When near Makalowe, the boat saw fires on the island from an ongoing insurgent attack, causing the boat to change course which led to the boat capsizing.

An insurgent attack was reported on the evening of 29 October on the island of Makalowe.  Insurgents set fire to homes on the island, causing local civilians to flee into the bush.  IDPs on a boat sailing to Makalowe saw the fires caused by this attack, causing them to change the course of the boat, which led to the boat capsizing and killing 54 people.

Suspected RENAMO dissidents on Tuesday morning at around 0600hrs fired on a bus in the Matenga area of Sofala, south of the Pungue River.  Passengers of the bus said that it was attacked in a "thinly wooded area, with shots coming from both sides of the road". A man and a woman were injured in this attack.  The woman was hit in the leg by a bullet while the man was injured by glass shattered by the gunfire.  The bus was travelling between Chimoio and Nampula.  RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo later denied responsibility for the attack.

The EU on Monday signed a new deal with the Mozambican Government to provide 100 million Euros or about $116 million of support to Maputo.  This kind of direct support from the EU had been suspended since the revelations of the "Hidden Debts" case in 2016.  This grant will be accompanied by "mechanisms for monitoring control, strengthening the transparency of the public management".  The EU is also reported to be "studying the type of support it can provide" to Mozambique in fighting the ongoing Cabo Delgado insurgency.

Local media reported South African private military contractor Dyk Advisory Group (DAG) in recent months have been training police in Cabo Delgado, but have been flying much fewer helicopter sorties to attack insurgents in insurgent impacted zones.  Local media also said that the Maputo government has recently contacted "other security companies" as it attempts to fight the insurgency.

Face to face Grade 7 calsses were reported on 03 November not to have been able to resume due to a lack of COVID protective materials and a "lack of hygiene conditions".  106 of 497 primary schools will reportedly open in the coming days though a majority of the province's 7th grade classes will remain closed.

Local media reported on 02 November that 20 people, including 15 children (aged 12-15), were beheaded in the village of 24 de Marco in Muidumbe District.  Many of the teenagers killed were reported to be in the village to participate in a traditional initiation ceremony.   All those killed were reportedly Makonde from Mueda District.  This came after insurgents launched district wide raids on multiple villages beginning on the morning of 31 October, including on Namacade/Muidumbe, the district capital.  At least 9 other people had been reportedly killed in the raids.  Insurgents were still reported to have been in control of several area villages on 01 November.

Local media reported on 03 November that large parts of Mocimboa da Praia, Nangade, Palma, and Mueda remain without power.  Sources had previously reported the restoration of power in much of the area after EDM workers, protected by security forces, carried out repairs at the Awasse Power Station.  Sources now indicate however that these repairs were unsuccessful, partially due to militant attacks.  in Palma town, generators continue to be the sole source of power, with increases in the cost of gas also reported.  Media reports also indicated that individuals are charged 100 meticais in Palma in order to charge their cell phones.
column15: Mocimboa da Praia, Nangade, Palma, and Mueda

column4: Rockets were reportedly fired on Mandimba village on 31 October in Nangade District by Tanzanian security forces believed to be targeting insurgents at around 1100hrs.  At least 5 people were injured in this incident.  Similar attacks were reported on 29-30 October on the village.  Many residents after three days of shelling fled the area.  Neither Tanzania nor Mozambique have officially commented on these attacks.

Sources reported that "large quantities" of aid provided to IDPs on Cremisse island in Quissanga District and other parts of the district are on sale at informal markets.  Sources also report poor conditions among IDPs across these islands, with cases of cholera and other diseases on the rise.

In a previously unreported incident on  29 October, insurgents were reported to have attacked Lissulo village in Nangade (reportedly near Nangade town), killing one person and injuring two others.  Insurgents also reportedly kidnapped several people in the village.

Insurgents reportedly kidnapped 8 people in an attack on Lissulo village in Nangade (reportedly near Nangade town) on 29 October, but then later released this group who were able to return to their village over the weekend.

Mozambique and Malawi signed a new MOU on Saturday on the construction of a railway line, beginning in 2021, between the two countries.  This will be a 44 km line between Mutarara in Tete to Lilongwe, the Malawi capital.
OPEC on 30 Oct approved a $50 million loan to Mozambique for the purpose of "promoting access to energy".

Nigerian citizens of Imo State were reported on 02 November to have petitioned the Ehime Mbano council to inquire into the disappearance of Theodore Chukwudi Malachi, a Nigerian citizen who was reportedly abducted by the Mozambican military in March of 2020 in Cabo Delgado and has not been heard from since.  Malachi was detained along with fellow Nigerian national Paul Obasi, who was released after being held for 3 weeks.  The petition said that it was believed Malachi was believed by Mozambican security forces to be a man called "Amiss Hassan", a Tanzanian national who is reportedly connected to the insurgency.

Insurgents on 31 October were reported to have attacked Lyautua village in Muidumbe District, carrying out looting and destruction of property.  Insurgents attacked over 10 other villages during a series of raids over the weekend in the district.

Insurgents on 31 October were reported to have attacked Matambalale village in Muidumbe District, carrying out looting and destruction of property.  Insurgents attacked over 10 other villages during a series of raids over the weekend in the district.

Insurgents on 31 October were reported to have attacked Lutete village in Muidumbe District, carrying out looting and destruction of property.  Insurgents attacked over 10 other villages during a series of raids over the weekend in the district.

Insurgents on 31 October were reported to have attacked Saba Saba village in Muidumbe District, carrying out looting and destruction of property.  Insurgents attacked over 10 other villages during a series of raids over the weekend in the district.

Insurgents on 31 October were reported to have attacked Nangunde village in Muidumbe District, carrying out looting and destruction of property.  Insurgents attacked over 10 other villages during a series of raids over the weekend in the district.

Insurgents on 31 October were reported to have attacked Litapata village in Muidumbe District, carrying out looting and destruction of property.  Insurgents attacked over 10 other villages during a series of raids over the weekend in the district.

Minibus drivers on 02 November were reported to have gone on strike in Maputo City after authorities declared minibuses were obliged to approached the Xipamnine terminal via the Avenida de Angola, a longer route than their preferred route through Rua do Mercado Vulcano.

RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo in an 03 November interview denied his group was responsible for an attack on Tuesday on a minibus in Sofala.   Nhongo also said that no truce had been observed in the past week despite its declaration by the Maputo government.  He said that Rapid Intervention Unit police officers on 30 October had "went to the homes of RENAMO members, took them, and killed them", and accused the government of "beheading" 20-30 RENAMO members.  No further details regarding these accusations are currently available.

More than 11,200 IDPs arrived in Pemba between 16-29 October, the UN's Office for Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs said on 02 Nov.  Other sources had previously reported over 12,000 IDPs arrived by boat to the provincial capital during this time, fleeing insurgent attacks in other parts of the province.

At least 40 people are believed to have died on Sunday, 01 November, when a vessel carrying IDPs sank between Ibo and Matemo.  32 people survived this accident.  The boat the group were travelling in was only meant to carry 30 people.  This was the second shipwreck incident reported off the Cabo Delgado coast in recent days, after 54 people reportedly drowned last week off another island just of the Mucojo area coast.

Insurgents on 01 November reportedly ambushed a security force patrol near Pundanhar.  Other sources said that security forces had instead ambushed insurgents in the area, a day after militants had attacked Pundanhar town.  Unverified reports said 33 people were killed in these clashes, with media reports saying all those killed were insurgents, and that some militants retreated from the area.

The Pundanhar - Palma Road was reported on 03 November was reportedly reopened to traffic after being temporarily closed by security forces due to two insurgent attacks in the Pundanhar area in less than a week between 24 -31 October.  Trucks carrying goods again on 05 November arrived into Palma via this road.

It was reported that a civilian militia captured, mutilated, and beheaded three suspected insurgents in Muidumbe District on 01 November, allgedly in Muatide village.  Pro-government militia brought the captured militants into the village in the district where they were then executed.  This incident occurred during mass insurgent raids across Muidumbe between 31 October - 01 November.

Only 29,000 out of  84,000 grade 7 students in Zambezia would resume classes this week as their schools meet sanitary conditions, officials announced on 03 November. Actions are underway to improve conditions and sanitation in primary schools.
410 harmful fishing gear was destroyed by Mozambican authorities after inspecting  7,134 fishing gear pieces throughout the second half of October.

72 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 03 November, with 38 new cases in Maputo City, 21 in Maputo, 6 in Nampula, 4 in Zambezia, 2 in Niassa, and 1 in Inhambane.  1 additional death was also reported.  There have now been a total of 13,202 COVID cases reported in Mozambique along with 95 deaths.

Sources reported insurgents on 04 November attacked Nampanha village at around 0730hrs, carrying out looting and setting homes on fire.  Almost all village residents were reported to have fled the area before this attack.

Cell phone communication in Muidumbe District since 31 October has reportedly been cut off, possibly due to insurgent attacks in the district.  No further detail regarding this development is currently available.
Insurgents on 04 November were reported to be in control of Muidumbe/Namacade town in Muidumbe and still present in the area.  This came after insurgents attacked the district capital on 31 Oct.

Local sources in Macomia town indicated the district capital had been mostly deserted by local residents after recent attacks by insurgents both in Macomia District and neighboring Muidumbe.  There is reported to be high tensions and fear in Macomia, which is still held by government forces.
On 04 Nov, security forces arrested a 30-yr-old man for allegedly killing a suspected thief in his house in Maxixe city. The victim's body, thrown into the Inhambane Bay, was recovered on 23 July.

Only 6,000 out of 24,000 grade 10 students in Inhambane will resume classes this week as their schools meet sanitary conditions, officials announced on 04 November.  About 42,000 7th grade students are still unable to go to school with sanitary conditions reportedly not met at around 800 schools in the province.  Parents also reportedly fear sending their children to school in many parts of the province.

Security forces arrested a 25-yr-old illegal recruiter in Vilankulo on 04 Nov. The suspect allegedly deceived more than 40 young people into paying 200 meticais on false promises that they would be given jobs in Brazil.

People in Manica are reported not to be obeying COVID-19 prevention measures, according the  country's secretary of state, Edson Macuacua, on 04 Nov. Locals were allegedly celebrating events at night to escape police detention.

The Mozambican Parliament passed an amended budget on 04 Nov, with an 8.5% increase. Prime Minister Carlos Agostinho do Rosario  stated that the increase in budget will be allocated for COVID-19 response team, humanitarian assistance for IDPs  and strengthen operational capacity of the defence and security forces who are fighting the ongoing Cabo Delgado insurgency.

Over 13,000 people have arrived in Pemba at Paquietequete beach on 274 vessels over the past 3 weeks, the IOM reported on 05 November.  Boats carrying people continue to arrive in Pemba on a daily basis with IDPs fleeing from insurgency impacted areas of Cabo Delgado.  Sources indicated that during that time, 236 people arrived suffering from different illnesses, including malaria and diarrhea.

RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo said that on 03 November, government security forces allegedly kidnapped and hung a party delegate in Gondola, Manica.  Nhongo also said that the government is insincere in saying it wants a dialogue with his group.  Nhongo also said he has lost faith in UN special envoy to Mozambique Mirko Manzoni, saying Manzoni "leans to one side" and did not treat his group fairly.  Nhongo also indicated he had reported attacks on RENAMO dissidents to Manzoni.

The Joint Command of the Ministries of the Interior and Defense on 05 November acknowledged that insurgents remain in control of Mocimboa da Praia and that the situation in Cabo Delgado is "serious".  This is significant as security forces have previously denied that insurgents controlled the town, saying they were merely active near it.  Security sources also acknowledged that the Awasse electricity sub-station remains out of commission leaving large parts of the insurgent zone without power.

Police Commander Bernardino Rafael said on Wednesday said that insurgents have killed up to 270 people throughout Cabo Delgado over the past 3 months.  Rafael also said that 50 security force members had been injured in recent clashes with insurgents in different areas of the province.

On 27 October, Dyck Advisory Group helicopters attacked insurgent positions near Pundanhar as part of an attempt to reopen the Palma-Pundanhar road.  Insurgents briefly retreated from the area over a space of four days but later returned to attack the town on the night of 31 October.
Dyck Advisory Group helicopters on 01 November attacked insurgents in the Pundanhar area.  No other details regarding this incident are currently available.
Sources on 03 November indicated that insurgents had been driven out of the Pundanhar area after clashes with security forces.  Militants had occupied the town and surrounding areas since 31 October.

The District of Nangade's government on 03 November issued a directive that all teachers in the district should return to their jobs by 06 November.  A similar directive was issued by the government of Muidumbe last week to its employees, just before insurgents launched attacks across the district.  In Nangade, at least one recent insurgent attack has been reported while 3 different shelling incidents were also reported in the last week after Tanzanian troops launched shells believed to be targeting insurgents into the district.
The Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) stated the economy of Mozambique will decline by 2.3% this year due to the COVID pandemic and would recover by 1.2% in 2021.

The Ministry of Health announced that 81 new cases were reported in Mozambique on 04 November, including 50 cases in Maputo City, 10 in Cabo Delgado, 8 in Tete, 7 in Gaza, 3 in Maputo, 2 in Zambezia, and 1 in Inhambane.  There are now a total of 13,283 countrywide cases along with 95 deaths.
Electricidade de Moçambique (EDM) closed off the power utilities of a pharmacy and a bar in Tete on 5 November, for electrical theft charges. Both owners of the establishments were detained.

Tanzania in recent days reportedly expelled around 1000 Mozambican refugees back across the border into Cabo Delgado into the Negomano border area in Mueda District.  The group had previously fled insurgent attacks in the province.  8 of those deported were reported to have tested positive for COVID.

108 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 05 November, including 51 cases in Maputo City, 30 in Maputo, 11 in Sofala, 7 in Zambezia, 4 in Cabo Delgado, 2 in Gaza, 2 in Manica, and 1 in Inhambane.  2 new fatalities were also reported.  There are now 13,391 cases in the country along with 97 deaths.

President Nyusi on Thursday said that RENAMO dissidents are "not cooperating in the dialogue" and said that the Mozambican state will no longer "assist and pander murders", saying the government if necessary would "defend Mozambique".  Nyusi also noted the dissidents had carried out attacks twice on 26 October and 03 November, showing they were not interested in the peace process.

Sources on 05 November reported insurgents beginning on 31 October had carried out a series of beheadings at Muatide at the Madjedje Football field in the area.  Insurgents who invaded Muidumbe on 31 October were reported to have captured local residents who fled into nearby countryside areas before bringing them to this field for execution, which has reportedly been ongoing throughout the week.  Local media indicated that 40 people in recent days had been beheaded in this area, and that this death toll could be significantly higher.  Mozambican troops based at Mueda were reportedly attempting to reach Muatide to drive militants from the area, but had been unable to do so in recent days as militants clashed with pro-government militia at Lutete, between Mueda and Muatide.  This report is currently unconfirmed.

Mozambican PM Carlos Agostinho do Rosario on 05 November met with Tanzanian President John Magufuli for talks in Dodoma, the Tanzanian capital, on the sidelines of Magufuli's inauguration where the two reportedly spoke on cooperation in the fighting against terrorism.  This discussion happened after three shelling attacks between 29-31 October in Nangade District that it is believed Tanzanian troops launched, reportedly targeting insurgents, after recent insurgent raids into Tanzania.

Mozambican police on 04 November destroyed over 500 kilos of illicit drugs in Nampula which had been seized in several different recent police operations.  The island of Mozambique, Mossuril, and Angoche remain the most "vulnerable channels" for drug trafficking in Nampula, authorities said.

The Mozambican military according to a parliamentary report believe that some RENAMO deputies and members "support the actions of the RENAMO Military Junta".  The reports also indicated that at least 11 people have died in RENAMO dissident attacks, and said these attacks began with ambushes of vehicles in Manica province but have evolved into attacks on construction sites and production units.

Clashes were reported in the Lutete area on 05 November between pro-government militia forces and security forces, resulting in the death of at least two militia members.  These clashes erupted after the militia mistook security force members for insurgents.  Soldiers later withdrew from the area to Mueda.

Mozambican media announced that Mozambique's sovereign wealth fund will be jointly managed by the country's Assembly, the Ministry of the Economy and Finance, and the Bank of Mozambique to ensure transparency.  This fund is meant to serve as an investment for the state of profits from oil and gas projects in the Rovuma Basin.

Mozambique has approved a new "Recovery of Assets" law which will allow the judicial system to seize and revert to the state all assets proven to have been acquired through illegal activities such as corruption, trafficking in drugs, people, or weapons, terrorism, tax evasion, tax fraud, loan sharking, and money laundering.
South Africa on 04 November began conducting rapid COVID-19 testing at the Lebombo Border Post just across from Ressano Garcia to ease the crossing of travelers into Mozambique.

The EU and Portugal on 05 November launched a new four year project in Cabo Delgado to train and employ young people in the natural gas field.  800 people are participating in the pilot program.  This kind of program as seen as an important way to counter the appeal of the province's ongoing insurgency.

A border official and two other people including one South African national were arrested on 04 November at the Ressano Garcia border crossing for involvement in a fraudulent stamp updating scheme for foreign nationals to be able to remain in Mozambican territory.

The Green Resources, a Norwegian forestry company, renounced on 6 November their rights over 54,000 hectares of land, in Sanga, Chimbonila, Ngaúma and Mandimba districts of Niassa. The renunciation of the lands was to avoid any possible conflict over the territory.

President Felipe Nyusi said on 05 November that the current justice system has had gaps that allowed several suspects involved with attacks in Cabo Delgado free. Nyusi indicated that a number of these suspects continue to be members of the insurgency at present.

The Famine Early Warning Systems Network that food relief being provided to Mozambique is predicted to assist less than half of the estimated needs from November until March 2021.  In Cabo Delgado, over 435,000 people have been displaced but food aid by the end of September only reached 274,000 people in the province.  By March, food aid is expected to reach about 367,000 people.

Heavy rainfall and strong winds damaged several residences, as well as public and private infrastructure in Marracuene District, north of Maputo City, on the afternoon of 5 November. Several trees and electricity poles were knocked down by the storm. No casualties were currently reported.

About 640 hectares of farmland were submerged due to after opening one out of eight floodgates of the Cahora Bassa Dam due to heavy rainfall in Mutarara district. The Cahora Bassa Dam reservoir level was already high due to the rain. Several islands along the Zambezi River were also submerged.
Electricidade de Moçambique (EDM) shut off power to the Super Mares supermarket in Tete for electrical theft charges on 3 November. This comes after a pharmacy and a bar were also closed down.
Electricidade de Moçambique (EDM) stated that Princess Cinderella School in Maputo City was charged for electrical theft due to their alarm usage.

The Ministry of Health announced 94 new COVID cases and two new deaths in Mozambique on 6 November, bringing the total to 13,485 cases and 99 deaths. 98 recoveries were also reported increasing the total recoveries to 11,275.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Veronica Macamo, called for the humanitarian support for the IDPs in Cabo Delgado on 6 November, calling on Europe and America for new support as over 435,000 are currently displaced in the province.

Insurgents launched an attack in Nanjaba village on 05 November at around 2200hrs, kidnapping 6 women.  2 people were also killed in this attack by beheading and homes in the village destroyed.  Insurgents when entering the village chanted "God is great".  No security force action in the area in response to this attack was reported.  Nearly the entire village was destroyed by fire.
Insurgents launched an attack in Napala village on 06 November in the early morning hours at around 0100hrs. Three people were killed and houses in the village were razed.

Unidentified assailants at around 0700hrs kidnapped the daughter of a businessman and restaurant owner in Matola on 09 November.  The 26-year-old Portugese national was abducted on the street, just after she had left her home.  Police were reported to have immediately begun an investigation into the abduction.  Notably, sources reported the woman's family were "middle income" and not wealthy like other kidnap victims.
Insurgents on the afternoon of 07 November kidnapped 2 women during an attack on Nambine/Nambini village along the Macomia-Mucojo road.

On 07 November, Mozambique reported 92 new COVID cases, including 46 new cases in Maputo City, 19 in Maputo province, 12 in Cabo Delgado, 3 in Nampula, 3 in Zambezia, 3 in Tete, 3 in Manica, 2 in Sofala, an 1 in Gaza. There have now been 13,577 COVID cases countrywide, along with 99 deaths.
Insurgents on the afternoon of 07 November beheaded 1 man and kidnapped 2 women from Nambine/Nambini village along the Macomia - Mucojo road.

OCHA reported on 09 November that nearly 1,000 people fleeing insurgent impacted areas had arrived in Pemba between 03-06 November, and that 13,730 people had fled to Pemba since 16 October, though daily IDP arrival in the city are down as compared to late October.  Other sources said that between 15-20 boats continue to arrive per day to Pemba.

Maputo's Attorney General has filed charges at a Maputo court against former Mozambique Finance Minister Manuel Chang as well as against three former central bank employees linked to the "Hidden Debts" case.  Chang remains in South African custody, with both the US and Mozambique seeking his extradition.  Chang had not been formally charged yet in this case.

Several sources indicated on 06 November that insurgents remained in control of large parts of Muidumbe District, including the Muatide area had carried out at least 10 more beheadings at a local football field by Friday.  40 beheadings were previously reported in this area during the week.  Insurgents reportedly remain present at the Madjedje field where they have brought local residents found hiding in the bush for execution.  There is some indication that these executions may have continued up to 08 November, when satellite imagery showed fires in the area.

Mozambican police officers on the afternoon of 08 November cleared the Costa do Sol beach in Maputo City at around 1500hrs after thousands of people on the beach refused to obey anti-COVID measures, not observing social distancing or wearing masks.  Temperatures of 41 degrees Celsius led to many going to this and other beaches.  Mozambique's public beaches were re-opened on 15 October after they were closed for several months due to the pandemic.

Police in Manica were reported on 05 November to have arrested an active duty soldier and a demobilized soldier, along with one other suspect on suspicion of being members of a kidnap ring that recently abducted a Bengali trader in Chimoio.  The active duty soldier was home on leave after heaving served on frontline areas in Cabo Delgado. The arrest occurred just after the gang robbed a local merchant in Vanduzi on Thursday.  Two other suspects escaped.  AN AK47 and ammunition were seized from the two.

A group of 5 criminals, armed with at least one firearm, robbed a local merchant on 05 November in Vanduzi, Manica.  3 of the 5 were arrested shortly after the incident.  The group is believed to have taken part in several kidnappings including one incident in Chimoio on 03 November.

Local media reported that on 03 November a kidnap gang abducted a Bengali businessman in Chimoio from the Bairro de Junho area.  The man's whereabouts remain unknown.  On 05 November, three members of this gang were arrested in Vanduzi.

Mozambique on 08 November reported 191 new COVID cases nationwide, bringing the nationwide total number of cases to 13,768, while there are still just 99 deaths.  There were 151 new cases reported in Maputo City, 17 in Maputo, 12 in Zambezia, 4 in Tete, 4 in Inhambane, 2 in Cabo Delgado, and 1 in Gaza.
The IOM reported on 06 November alone, 335 IDPs including 160 children had arrived to Paquitequete beach in Pemba

South Korea on 09 November was reported to have raised its travel warning for Mtwara District in Tanzania, which borders Mozambique's Cabo Delgado district, where an insurgency is ongoing.  South Korea raised the alert level to "red", the second highest level of its four tier system, saying its nationals should cancel trips to the area or if in the area should leave unless they have "essential reasons" to remain in the area.

Local media reported a group of 150 Rapid Intervention Police force members are due to be punished this week after they refused to go on patrols in parts of Cabo Delgado.  The group are expected to be demoted out of the Rapid Intervention Unit and to be transferred out of Cabo Delgado.  Their salaries are also expected to be reduced from a monthly wage of about 11,000 meticais (about $150) down to 8,000 meticais (about $109).

In a previously unreported attack, President Nyusi said that suspected RENAMO dissidents on 29 October attacked a bus carrying passengers between Chibabava and Muchanga Districts in Sofala, leaving one person seriously wounded.

President Nyusi over the weekend said that RENAMO dissidents in a previously unreported attack on 29 October had fired on a passenger bus in the Matenga area of Nhamatanda District, though no injuries were reported.

President Nyusi over the weekend said that RENAMO dissidents had fired on a truck owned by a construction company on 03 November as it travelled along the N1 road in the Gove area, saying there had been casualties in this attack without giving exact details.

Mozambican police over the weekend in Angonia District of Tete province were reported to have detained a Malawian national and seized over 1.5 tones of cannabis sativa the man had smuggled into Mozambique in a vehicle with a false bottom.  The man had travelled from Malawi and was transiting to Zimbabwe when he was discovered and arrested.

Mozambican police over the weekend in Angonia District of Tete province were reported to have detained a Malawian national and seized over 1.5 tones of cannabis sativa the man had smuggled into Mozambique in a vehicle with a false bottom.  The man had travelled from Malawi and was transiting to Zimbabwe when he was discovered and arrested.

Health officials in Manica expressed concern over the increase of malaria cases this year. Around 350,000 cases were reported in the first half of 2020, versus 400,000 total number of cases in 2018 and 500,000 total cases in 2019. Fundacao para o Desenvolvimento da Comunidade (FDC) aimed to reinforce preventive measures and spread awareness to the most remote areas about the disease.

Nampula Province Government recently opened Corrane Settlement in Meconta for the displaced families.  It hosts 338 people from Cabo Delgado in Namialo town, who fled from insurgent attacks. The settlement camp has four boreholes with safe drinking water and a medical center.  There are more than 34,700 IDPs from Cabo Delgado spread throughout Nampula province.

180 people fleeing from Cabo Delgado have received plots of land in Savane, Dondo District of Sofala province.  These are the first IDPs reported to have arrived in Sofala; most Cabo Delgado IDPs are displaced in parts of Cabo Delgado itself, while others are displaced into Niassa, Nampula, Zambezia, and into bordering district of Tanzania.

Two lions have been captured and moved to a hunting area in Marromeu district after threatening residents and animals in Magude and Moamba districts. Goats and cattle in the area were  devoured while crops were destroyed. Reports claimed that they escaped from a conservation area at the Mapulanguene, Magude.

78 imprisoned Mozambicans were repatriated from South Africa in October, as South Africa attempts to depopulate prisons to prevent the spread of COVID-19.  These people involved were serving prison sentences in South African for various crimes, particularly poaching, illegal possession of firearms and theft. A total of 2,213 Mozambicans were also repatriated from South Africa between January to September of this year.

Ministry of Health in Mozambique announced on 08 November that 55 new COVID cases were reported across the country.  There are now 13,823 cases in the country along with 99 deaths.  27 cases were reported in Maputo City, 14 in Maputo, 8 in Tete, 5 in Zambezia, and 1 in Nampula.

A communique published on the night of 09 November indicated that 9 journalists were forced to flee from their facilities at the Francisco de Assisi Community Radio Station at the Parish Church of the Sacred Heart of Jesus in Muidumbe in the 24 March village area when insurgents attacked on 31 October.  These journalists have since reportedly hidden in the nearby woods for 10 days, though the ultimate fate of the journalists remains unknown with the National Community Radio Forum unable to reach the group.  The statement also said that the radio's facilities had been destroyed, and at least one of the journalists lost at least one family member in the attacks.  Several hundred people remain hiding in bush areas in Muidumbe after these insurgent attacks. This report comes after insurgents were reported to have still held parts of the district on 06 November, a week after militants initially launched an assault that overwhelmed security forces in the area.  At least 79 people have been reported to have been killed in attacks in Muidumbe during these raids.

Cabo Delgado health officials confirmed the death of 60 people due to a cholera outbreak on Matemo island.  Officials said the outbreak was caused after insurgents in previous raids seized medical equipment from the island.

Yara, the second largest fertilizer company in the world, was reported on 04 November by local media to have abandoned plans to develop a fertilizer plant using natural gas in Cabo Delgado.  Yara had been preparing to set up a fertilizer production and distribution system at government set prices in exchange for Maputo providing gas at a low price to the company.  This larger scale plan fell through, but the government in 2016 then agreed to a Yara proposal to produce nitrogen fertilizer to export, but after four years of negotiations, no agreement on the price of natural gas to Yara could be agreed upon.  This development is seen as significant as the Yara plant would have provided significant local jobs and substantial support to Mozambican agriculture.
Six armed kidnappers assaulted a mother and later abducted the child with albinism from their residence in Molumbo in Zambezia early morning of Sunday, 8 November.
Six armed kidnappers assaulted a mother and later abducted a child with albinism from their residence in Molumbo early morning of Sunday, 8 November.

The Parliamentary Committee on Constitutional Affairs, Human Rights and Legality (1st Commission) recommended increased logistical and military capacity of the Defense and Security Forces (SDS) on 9 November. The 1st Commission noted that the logistical and military capacity of the SDS lacks the necessary essentials to perform their duties.

Minister of Justice Helena Kida said on 10 November that an insurgent attempt to take over the Mieze  prison occurred on an unknown date.  She also said attempts were made to take over prisons at Mocimboa da Praia and Macomia.  In two of these attempts (likely at Macomia and MDP) were repelled by security force agents.  The MDP prison was closed down before the town fell to insurgents, while the Macomia facility has been closed down because of the threat to the facility.  The Mieze facility is still in operation and hold a large number of suspected insurgents.

Insurgents reportedly set parts of central Chilundo village on fire, north of Muidumbe on the evening of 4 November. The casualties were currently unavailable.

Insurgents reportedly set several areas of Muambula town on fire on the evening of 6 November. Casualties were not reported. Insurgents in a series of attacks on Muambula between 31 Oct - 06 November reportedly ransacked most of the Nangololo Mission Church, which was also used by insurgents as a base of operations in early November.

Zimbabwe President Emmerson Mnangagwa stated on 10 November that Zimbabwe is ready to assist Mozambique against their fight with insurgency in Cabo Delgado on social media. The Zimbabwe President condemned the ongoing insurgency in the country in the wake of reports that 50 people were recently beheaded in Muatide in Muidumbe District.

The Ministry of Health announced 69 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 10 November, bringing the total to 13,892 cases. 45 cases were from Maputo city, 9 in Cabo Delgado, 8 Sofala, three in Maputo, two in Zambezia, one in Nampula, and one in Gaza provinces.
Security forces detained 29 Ethiopian nationals in Degue town, north of Tete, on 11 November. The Ethiopians were arrested for lacking residential documents after crossing the Zambezi River.

Maputo Airport security detained a Vietnamese woman attempting to smuggle five rhino horns and 160 lion teeth found inside her baggage at Maputo International Airport on 11 November.  The woman was detected by a police canine.

A Vietnamese woman attempted to smuggle five rhino horns and 160 lion teeth inside her baggage at Maputo International Airport.  The woman's baggage was discovered and she was taken into custody on 11 November.

Local sources reported that insurgent exchanged gunfire with pro-government militia forces and have captured Matambalane village in Muidumbe District on 11 November.  Matambalane is located within 14 miles / 23kms of Mueda town. A vehicle was burned in this incident.  Pro-gov militia forces retreated towards Mueda after these clashes.

Mozambique's Public Prosecutor Office on 11 November charged 12 Iranian citizens arrested in December 2019 in Mozambican territorial waters with terrorism.  Charges said that the 12 belonged to a terrorist organization and planned to supply insurgents with arms and ammunition in Cabo Delgado. The group reportedly had a number of AK47s and ammunition in their possession in addition to illegal drugs. These 12 had been transporting a large quantity of heroin to the Cabo Delgado coast when they were detained.  3 other Iranian nationals drowned attempting to escape security forces in this incident.  When the group was arrested, they were widely reported to be drug traffickers - it still remains unclear if the group was in fact supporting the insurgency.  No drug trafficking charges were levied against the group.

99 New COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 11 November, along with 5 deaths.  These 5 deaths were significant as they were the highest total of daily COVID deaths reported so far in the pandemic in Mozambique.  There have now been a total of 13,991 cases in the country with 104 deaths.  Maputo City has 1,314 active cases, Maputo has 247, while the rest of the country has less than 180 cases.

Insurgents were reported on 11 November to still be in control of most of Muidumbe District, including the district capital Namacade/Muidumbe and villages around the capital.  Insurgents have controlled these areas since 31 October.  Insurgents were also reported during this occupation to have destroyed the Namacade district HQ, which had been rebuilt in April after it was destroyed by an insurgent attack in that month.

UN Sec Gen Antonio Guterres on 11 November expressed shock over recent reports of mass beheadings in Muidumbe District, calling for an investigation into these incidents and for those responsible to be held accountable.  President Macron of France also issued a statement saying "Barbarians hijack a religion of peace to sow terror: Islamist terrorism is an international threat that calls for an international response."  Several other governments have also issued condemnations of the Muidumbe attacks.  Note that reports of 50 people being beheaded in the Muatide area have not yet been confirmed.

The National Institute of Meteorology (INAM) warned that heavy rainfall and strong winds would impact Manica and Sofala provinces from 11-12 November. INAM stated that Mussorize, Machaze, Sussundenga, Gondola, and Macate areas of Manica province would be the most affected, while Buzi, Chibabava and Nhamatanda areas will be affected in Sofala province.

The National Institute of Meteorology (INAM) warned that heavy rainfall and strong winds would impact Manica and Sofala provinces from 11-12 November. INAM stated that Mussorize, Machaze, Sussundenga, Gondola, and Macate areas of Manica province would be the most affected, while Buzi, Chibabava and Nhamatanda areas will be affected in Sofala province.

Insurgents on the night of 11 November were reported to be present in Miteda town, on the western border of Muidumbe District, and were reported to be advancing towards Mueda town.  This followed reports earlier in the day that militants exchanged gunfire with Mozambican forces and drove them out of the Matambalane area.  Thousands of IDPs are reported to be in and around Mueda town.

The National Statistics Institute announced that Beira was rated as the most expensive city since October. Beira was recorded with 0.63 percent inflation, which was followed by Maputo with 0.57 percent, and Nampula with 0.34 percent.

Officials warned that erosion caused by waters from the Indian Ocean and Zambezi River are threatening Chinde town. Around 500m of land has eroded over the past five years and families have evacuated due to the threat. Zambezia governor stated that retaining walls were needed to minimize the erosion.

Three former Mozambique Bank officials charged as part of the Hidden Debts Case have been identified.  The three are former Governor Ernesto Gouveia Gove, Administrators Waldemar de Sousa and Joana Matsombe.  Earlier this week, all three were charged as part of the "Hidden Debts" case along with former Finance Minister Manuel Chang though they were only identified as "three former Bank of Mozambique employees".  None of the three were reportedly notified of the charges, and it is unclear if any of the three have been arrested.

The National Assembly on 11 November approved an amended budget with 171 delegates in favor.  RENAMO and MDM delegates, who control just 38 total seats, voted against the new budget, calling it a "waste" of public resources.  The new budget allows for increased defense spending related to conflict in Central and Northern Mozambique, as well as increases in spending to counter the ongoing pandemic.  The new budget increases expenditure by 8.3% from about $ 4.73 billion to $5.12 billion

The Mozambican Ministry of the Sea, Inland Waters and Fisheries announced its officers had seized 112 items used for illegal fishing in Gaza province on 9 November. 70 mosquito nets and 42 trawl nets were seized as part of an inspection over the closed season on the mangrove areas.

Dozens of truck drivers complained that National Crime Investigation Service (SERNIC) agents extort money from deliverers along National Road 1 near Cemiterio de Lhanguene south Maputo City, with the most recent extortion incident reported on 02 November. The drivers stated that they were being questioned by SERNIC agents upon their return from South Africa before officers demand bribes from them.

Fire due to suspected insurgent activity was reported in Muatide on 8 November. The insurgents have previously occupied the village.
Fires were reported in Muambula village in Muidumbe District on 03 November, likely part of an insurgent attack.
Seven insurgents surrendered and reportedly handed over their weapons to the police in Homba village in southeast Muidumbe District on the morning of 11 November. The group were later taken to Mueda.

The National Institute for Disaster Management (INGC) requested assistance from cooperation partners for additional finances as part of a contingency plan due to the rainy season. INGC stated that it only had 800 million meticais to use for 1.7 million people that will likely be impacted by the rainy season.

RENAMO delegates reportedly refused to join a debate on the human rights situation in Cabo Delgado in the country's national assembly, and walked out of a parliamentary session.   RENAMO stated that FRELIMO intends to conduct minimal token working visits to the conflict zones. RENAMO also mentioned that their previous attempt to conduct working visits in response to the international committee were blocked by FRELIMO.  RENAMO delegates were also upset over a report produced by a FRELIMO exploratory committee that said that the Mozambican military had "nothing to do with" human rights abuses and had only committed "excesses" in a small number of instances.
Police arrested two suspects for impersonating and extorting locals along public roads in Maputo city on 9 November. One of the suspects was a former policeman.
RENAMO reportedly plans to close the Vunduzi Base in Sofala this month which houses 384 guerillas.  It is unclear when exactly this base will be closed.

The Zimbabwean Embassy in Maputo announced its resumption of consular operations in Mozambique after it suspended services past March due to the COVID pandemic. Similar services were also resumed in Eswatini. The operations included issuing birth, national identification documents, and passports. Four consular officers arrived at the embassy.

The Mozambican government denied the reports of mass beheadings in the villages in north Cabo Delgado. Cabo Delgado Governor Valige Tauabo stated that there were no recent killings and the last incident took place on 6 April at Xitaxi when insurgents  The dismissal comes as previous reports stated that 50 individuals were beheaded at a football field at Muatide area in Muidumbe district.

Attorney General's Office (PGR) announced on 12 November that they managed to recover just 9 million USD from 2 billion USD lost by the country in the "Hidden Debts" case.  The country has already paid off 350 million USD of illegal loans.

South African officials announced that it would allow travelers from all countries into the country after amending its Level 1 COVID restrictions, removing the red-list system subject to necessary health protocols and the presentation of a negative COVID certificate.  This could potentially also increase cross border traffic in and out of Mozambique via the South African borders.

Several sources reported that two security guards were killed in an attack by unidentified assailants on a farm owned by a Portuguese businessman outside of Beira.  6 assailants entered the farm in the early morning hours of 12 November, tied up two farm guards, and executed them.  The group attempted to enter the main house, causing damage to the residence, and were given about 40,000 meticais by the businessman to leave.  The group was reportedly armed with blunt objects and at least one firearm and injured two other farm workers in the attack.

The National Meteorological Institute (INAM) warned of heavy rainfall and strong winds in Cabo Delgado, Nampula, and Niassa provinces on 13 November. Namuno, Balama and Montepuez are likely to be the most affected districts in Cabo Delgado. In Nampula, the districts of Mecuburi, Lalaua, Ribeue, Rapale, Muecate, Nacarroa and Erati will be affected. While in Niassa, Mecula, Marrupa, Nipepe, Mavago, Majune, Muembe, Sanga, Chimbonila, Ngauma and Lichinga city are the affected areas.
