Police arrested a traffic policeman and a driver on bribery charges in Beira on 12 November. The policeman accepted 100 meticais from the driver for not inspecting his vehicle.  Anti-corruption officers then arrested the two.

The National Institute for Disaster Management (INGC) announced that there is a deficit of 6.4 billion meticais or about $87.1 million to help IDPs and those impacted by the country's ongoing rainy season. INGC previously stated that it only has 800 million meticais or about $23 million to use for providing assistance to the affected individuals.

The European Union (EU) discussed the ongoing issues of Mozambique on 11 November. MEP Paulo Rangel inquired on what actions had already been taken by the EU in ending the ongoing insurgency in the country, saying Mozambique had been "abandoned" to face "Islamic extremist violence" on its own.
103 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 12 November, bringing the total cases to 14,094. 71 new cases were reported in Maputo City, which is followed by Gaza province with 8 cases.

The Mozambican parliament, the Assembly of the Republic (AR), approved a resolution condemning the violence in northern and central parts of the country. The resolution also requests the government to strengthen the logistical and material capacity of the Defence and Security Forces (SDS). The resolution was approved by the parliament with the majority of the votes coming from the FRELIMO party.

A local businessman was shot dead by gunmen in Ndenganamade village of Nangade Sede on the night of 12 November. The victim was identified as Mussa Ayubo Nkamushino, a local businessman, who was previously detained in July by security forces on suspicion of supplying insurgents with food and other supplies; he was released after being held for one month, allegedly after paying a bribe.  There is some speculation that Nkamushino may have been targeted over his alleged ties to the insurgency.  Local residents later said the incident "was the work of soldiers".

Local sources and media reported on 12 November that many Mueda residents and IDPs in the area are attempting to leave the town after recent insurgent attacks in Muidumbe District, east of Mueda.  Demand for public transport has increased out of the area, leading to increases in public transport fares. There are between 20,000 to 30,000 IDPs in the Mueda area.  Other sources indicated that some Mueda residences had fled to nearby bush areas fearing advancing insurgents.

On 13 November, the US's Tanzanian embassy issued a new "Security Alert" for the Mtwara Region of Southern Tanzania saying "There have been reports of violence in Mtwara Region in southern Tanzania.  Increased activity by extremists along the southern border has led to attacks against both government and civilian targets."  The US embassy advised travel to the region be re-considered, or that travelers to the region exercise "extreme caution" and monitor local media for breaking events.

A Portuguese woman kidnapped on Monday in Matola was reported to have been released on Thursday night by her captives to her family, and was unharmed.  No further details on her release were available.  The woman was abducted Monday morning just after leaving her home in Matola; her family own a small restaurant in Matola.

The UN on Friday called for "urgent measures to protect civilians" in Cabo Delgado after recent militant attacks in the area.  The UN statement said that the situation in the province was "desperate" and that there was a risk that IDPs would be "killed, sexually abused, kidnapped, or forcibly recruited" by armed groups.

Several people were injured on 12 November when a vehicle carrying a large number of IDPs leaving the Mueda area crashed near Nairoto town on the Mueda - Montepuez road.  Several people were injured though no exact casualty details are available.

Sources continue to say that the beheading of 50 people in the Muatide area between 31 Oct - 08 November has not yet been confirmed, though sources do agree that insurgents did take over Muidumbe District during this time and did kill a large number of civilians.

Sources on 11 November said that a group of insurgents occupy the village of Mandela along the Messalo River in the south of Muidumbe District.  A group of seven militants surrendered this week to pro-government militias in the Homba area, west of Mandela.

Reports on 12 November that on 10 November, Mozambican military units and pro-government forces had mistook one another for insurgents and clashed in the Matambalale village area.  This came after reports in recent days of a similar security force on security force clash at Lutete.  At Matambalale, pro-gov militia believed uniformed men in the area were insurgents, while troops believed militia, who were without uniforms, were also insurgents, leading to clashes which resulted in an unknown number of casualties.   The military withdrew from the area, leaving pro-government militias in control of the town.

The Forum of Community Radios announced that seven out of nine journalist who fled from insurgent attacks in Muidumbe recently were safe. The remaining two journalists were reported to be still be missing.  This came after reports last week that the 9 had fled into the bush near Muidumbe following insurgent attacks.

National Mining Institute (INAMI) announced on 13 November that around 500 local employees in the mining industry have either lost or had their jobs suspended during the course of 2020 due to the pandemic.

Public Health Department Head Geraldino Avalinho dismissed five insecticide sprayers for illegally selling and distributing insecticides in Nampula. The suspects were part of spraying program by the government to prevent malaria cases in the area.
Contaminated water reportedly killed six civilians and hospitalized 37 others after having diarrhea in Namuno, southwest of Montepuez, sources reported on 13 November.

133 COVID cases and 6 related deaths were reported by the Ministry of Health for the daily tally in Mozambique. The deaths were 2 women and 4 men who were from Maputo City. 76 of the new COVID cases were from Maputo City, followed by Maputo province with 28 cases.

Government officials conducted talks with Malawi officials at Chiponde border crossing on 13 November. The meeting included talks over a border pass to easily identify civilians from each country. The meeting also included security measures in response to ongoing smuggling and human trafficking.

Mozambican Episcopal Church Officials stated that the current situation in Muidumbe is "critical" and  “very unstable.” The Bishop of Chimoio stated they were finding ways to assist the arriving IDPs. The Episcopal church over the weekend called on the government of Mozambique and international institutions to "properly resolve their serious problems" in Cabo Delgado.

The State Secretary for Youth and Employment announced on 13 November that 175,683 youth jobs were created in Mozambique from January - September.  Officials stated that 87,099 of the jobs were permanent, 70,063 were seasonal, and 14,476 as temporary jobs.

Swiss officials announced that it would deploy unarmed military personnel under the UN to assist in the peace process in Mozambique on 11 November. At least 2 members would assist with the disarming, demobilizing and re-integrating (DDR) of armed RENAMO members in Central Mozambique.

Three bank branches reportedly closed down due to the advance of insurgents towards Mueda on 14 November. The banks closed down were Banco Commercial de Mozambique (BCI), Millennium BIM, and ABSA. The closure of the banks caused frustration among locals.

Local sources stated that unknown men abducted a businessman at the intersection of Salvador Allende and 24 de Julho Avenues, south Maputo City, on the afternoon on Saturday, 14 November. The incident occurred at about 1100hrs when Ismael Harron, a businessman of the Uzeir Trade Center group based in Beira was targeted by four men exited a car and abducted Harron at gunpoint, also threatening Harron's driver.
