column4: Unconfirmed reports on 15 November stated that insurgents had issued warnings to Muidumbe and Mueda residents to leave their areas before 20 November.  Government sources in the area were also aware of this threat.  This rumor has spread fear in the town, with reports of large numbers of local residents attempting to flee south to Montepuez.

Unconfirmed reports on 15 November stated that insurgents had issued warnings to Muidumbe and Mueda residents to leave their areas before 20 November.  Government sources in the area were also aware of this threat.  This rumor has spread fear in the town, with reports of large numbers of local residents attempting to flee south to Montepuez.

Significant numbers of insurgents on the evening of 15 November were reported to have arrived into the Ntchinga area of Muidumbe District from the Chitunda area to the northeast.  Ntchinga village is located just northwest of Namacade/Muidumbe town.  This could indicate the beginning of new militant operations either in Muidumbe District, where insurgents have been present in several villages since 31 October, or potential militant operations towards either Mueda or Macomia in the near future.

Activities in Mueda has been disrupted following threats on insurgent attacks. On 16 November, Nagy bus services suspended its services to Mueda district over potential insurgent attacks in addition to the onset of the rainy season, local media reported.  Sources also indicated that FRELIMO party officials were fleeing Mueda ahead of a potential insurgent attack. This follows unconfirmed reports from over the weekend that insurgents had warned Mueda and Muidumbe residents to leave these areas by 20 November, and reports that large numbers of militants were present in the Ntchinga area, about 23 airline miles from Mueda.  Mueda is the site of a large Mozambican military base where significant numbers of troops are stationed.

Zimbabwean officials on 14 November said that the country could have intervened in Mozambique against the ongoing Cabo Delgado insurgency, but that international sanctions against the country were preventing it from doing so.  The Zimbabwean military in the 1980s did intervene in the Mozambican Civil War, deploying troops for a 14 year period to defend the Beira corridor from RENAMO attacks.  Zimbabwe also deployed troops into the DRC in the early 2000s to intervene in the 2nd Congo War.
On 15 November, health officials said there were 108 new COVID cases along with 3 new deaths in the country.  There have now been 14,448 cases in the country along with 113 deaths.

A Pakistani national living in Chalaua, Moma District of Nampula Province was found dead in his home on 15 November.  The man was reportedly found hanging in his home - one source reported he had been strangled.  Unconfirmed reports said the man may have been connected to illegal gold mining in the area.  No other details on this incident are currently available.
Local media reported that an Ancuabe merchant in Metoro received a threat to leave the area immediately.  It was unclear if this threat was related to terrorism or criminality.

An average of between 85 - 130 displaced persons arrived at Paquitequete beach in Pemba over the past week aboard boats fleeing from insurgent impacted areas of Cabo Delgado.  This is a significant decline from late October, when hundreds of IDPs were arriving per day to the city.

Nangade District's Administrator has been out of the district since the end of September, as have several other district officials, local media reported, and are working out of Pemba.  This is both because of the threat of insurgent attacks as well as due to the ongoing power outage across much of the province.

Hundreds of IDPs have arrived into Montepuez District in recent days fleeing from insurgent impacted zones.  Many more IDPs in recent days have also been reported to be fleeing the Mueda area for Montepuez ahead of a potential insurgent attack.
Local media reported that prices for basic good remain high in Palma as shortages in the town continue due to insurgents having largely cut the town off from land routes.
Over 350 families arrived in Meluco area on 17 Nov as they flee areas affected by the ongoing Cabo Delgado insurgency.  WFP sent food assistance to the displaced families.

66 COVID daily cases and 3 related deaths were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 16 November. 62 new cases were reported in Maputo City, with one case each reported in Maputo, Cabo Delgado, Zambezia, and Inhambane. These new cases brought the country's number of infections to 14,514. The deaths were 2 women and a man from Maputo City bringing the national death toll now at 116.

Beira Central Hospital is still on poor condition a year after it was reopened following Cyclone Idai.  A video recently posted to social media showed water gushing from the ceiling  of the operating room during heavy rains. A source claimed that this was due to blocked gutters that were yet to be cleared. Authorities have yet to comment on the video nor offered intervention for issues in the hospital premise.

Over  559 families in Mutarara have been affected by the rising waters of Zambezi river, which as brought by the announced discharges from the Cahora Bassa dam. Over 1,400 tons of various crops have been destroyed. Source claimed that a warning on the opening of Cahora Bassa Dam, however, it was not received by several locals in the area.

A truck crashed into tents in Hulene neighborhood Maputo city around 0200 on15 Nov, which injured the truck driver. Police later concluded that the accident was caused by the over speeding and fatigue of the driver.

Mozambique will invest 30 million USD in the rehabilitation of the Dona Ana-Vila Nova da Fronteira railroad spur, Tete, it was reported on 16 Nov. This aims to re-establish the rail connection with Malawi. The connection between the two countries  was interrupted in the 1980s by the Mozambican Civil War.

A study recently released by the UN's World Institute for Development Economics Research on Mozambique says that a small group of top FRELIMO politicians have created a "limited access" society whereby this group effectively controls the state and uses this monopoly on power to dominate business in the country as well.  These elites control the state and economic activity to such a degree that the study says there is "no effective separation between party and state and big business".  This reality has had many negative outcomes, including increasing poverty in much of northern Mozambique which is extremely remote from Maputo.

The IOM reported on 17 November that in the past week, 33,000 people had moved from areas impacted by the insurgency into safer areas of Cabo Delgado.  Large numbers of the displaced have arrived into Montepuez District in the past week fleeing from Mueda after reports that insurgents threatened local residents to leave Mueda by 20 November.  The IOM said that 355,000 people are displaced throughout Cabo Delgado at present - compared to just 88,000 in January 2020.
Local authorities announced that 47 civilians have died due to malaria in Sofala province over the past 9 months. A total of 746,000 cases were reported in the province alone.
The Minister for the Sea and Fisheries Augusta Maita stated that 12.5 million plastic waste is dumped by Mozambique into the sea yearly.

The Saudi Minister for African Affairs, Ahmed Bin Abdul Aziz Kattan, visited Mozambique as part of preparations for the Arab-African summit and cooperation between countries. The two-day visit also discussed potential trade and investment between two countries.

The Mozambican Minister of Health, Armindo Tiago, stated Mozambique has passed through the COVID peak and that majority of the cases are recorded within Maputo city and Maputo province. Over 60 percent of the cases were reported in these areas. Tiago stated that civilians throughout Mozambique continue to flout anti-COVID measures which could lead to new case spikes, particularly during the rainy season.

A commission from Mozambique's parliament that recently visited the country's borders said that there are "challenges" along the borders and recommended that the national police and border forces should carry out more patrols and checks along the country's borders.

52 new COVID cases and 2 new related deaths were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 17 November. 28 cases and 1 of the deaths were reported in Maputo city. The other death was recorded in Inhambane province.

WHO officials said that COVID pandemic in Mozambique is under control, with the country reporting a very low .08% mortality rate, also saying the government took precautions early in the pandemic to prevent the spread of the virus.
The IOM stated that no new boats transporting IDPs have arrived in Pemba since 11 November. Around 14,400 IDPs were reported to have previously arrived in the area.

A new FRELIMO "Center of News" site appeared online on 17 November.  The site is registered by "Defense MZ", which also operates a separate site, defesamoz.info, which regularly publishes pro-government reports and updates.

The US and members of the Global Coalition against the Islamic State in a recent meeting discussed the insurgency in Mozambique.  US officials said they were looking into partnerships with "South Africa, Tanzania, and other states" in the region to attempt to try to help Mozambique in its fight against the insurgency and to prevent militants from gaining a greater foothold in the province.

Local sources stated that prices for transportation between Mueda and Montepuez have doubled, costing between 1,000-1,500 meticais. The prices were around 700 meticais previously, which later increase due to the lack of transportation as thousands flee the Mueda area for Montepuez.

Locals stated that supplies have decreased for food and goods while their prices increase in Palma due to the increased demand for passenger transportation in Mueda. Locals are reportedly forced to obtain their food items from Tanzania.

Locals were reported to be fleeing from Nangade and Pundanhar areas due to previous insurgent attacks and the potential of renewed attacks in these areas. Much of the Nangade-Palma road is reportedly deserted due to insurgent attacks.

Insurgents entered Nturene village on 06 November, disrupting a funeral and firing guns in the air to frighten local villages.  No casaulties were reported, though insurgents stole clothes in this incident and abducted two women.
Insurgents abducted two women after randomly firing shots in Nturene, south of Olumbi in Palma District, on 6 November. The insurgents previously arrived at the village and disrupted a funeral.

Police officials announced the arrest of 34 suspects for various criminal charges during a countrywide operation in Mozambique on 16 November. Majority of the suspects were involved with murders and assaults.

Security forces destroyed seized illegal fishing items in Bazaruto Island on 10 November. 2,564 fishing lines, 380 fishing reels, 332 pairs of scuba fins, 287 nylon cable traps, 133 fishing masks, 112 respirators, 90 containers filled with fishing hooks, 47 harpoons, 25 wetsuits, 12 gillnets, and 2 longline nets were destroyed.

Around 1,000 IDPs recently deported from Tanzania into the Negomano area of Mueda District were reported to have settled in the area as it is relatively secure from insurgent attacks and do not want to leave the area.  IDPs in the area are from different areas of Cabo Delgado, primarily districts close to the Tanzanian border, who had previously fled into Tanzania after insurgent attacks in the area.

Media and NGO sources said on 17 November that there are now a total of over 515,000 IDPs displaced across Cabo Delgado, an increase from 480,000 IDPs reported by some organizations at the beginning of November.  The majority of those displaced are from the insurgency impacted areas of Mocimboa da Praia, Palma, Macomia, Quissanga, Ibo, Nangade, and Muidumbe.  The WFP said on Tuesday that the increasing number of refugees in reducing aid capacities with an urgent need for more resources.

UN rep to Mozambique Mirko Manzoni said in an interview on 17 November that "international jihadists from Somalia, Yemen, Libya Uganda and the DRC" were present in Cabo Delgado and possessed "very sophisticated weapons".  Manzoni also called for military assistance to be provided to the Mozambican military, rather than any direct military intervention in the province. Manzoni in this interview also said he was "optimistic" that attacks by RENAMO dissidents in Central Mozambique would be resolved soon which would allow Mozambican forces to concentrate on the fight against the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

Local sources reported that more than 80 people died of cholera in an outbreak on Matemo Island, which houses thousands of IDPs, in the month of October.  This caused many IDPs on Matemo to flee to nearby Ibo island, though many IDPs were turned back from Ibo for fear of the spread of cholera, and were sent instead to Quirimbas Island, which is now also reported to be crowded with IDPs.

Local sources reported that more than 80 people died of cholera in an outbreak on Matemo Island, which houses thousands of IDPs, in the month of October.  This caused many IDPs on Matemo to flee to nearby Ibo island, though many IDPs were turned back from Ibo for fear of the spread of cholera, and were sent instead to Quirimbas Island, which is now also reported to be crowded with IDPs.  There is now a significant risk of a similar outbreak on Quirimbas Island.

The Minister of Economy and Finance, Adriano Maleiane announced that the debt of Mozambique stands at 12.37 billion USD. Maleiane also said that 16% of the debt was owed to China, which is around 2.02 billion USD.
A bus crashed onto the side of the after losing control of its brakes along the Avenida de Mozambique, Maputo City, at around 09:00 on the morning of 18 November. No casualties were reported.

63 new COVID cases and a single related death were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 18 November, bringing the total number of cases in the country to 14,629 along with 119 deaths.  This included 43 cases in Maputo City, 8 in Zambezia, 4 in Manica, 2 in Nampula, 1 in Cabo Delgado, and 1 in Maputo province.

National Directorate of Civil Identification (DNIC) detained an employee for illegally issuing National ID cards in Maputo city on 17 November. The suspect was caught in the act after receiving 100 meticais from a civilian to issue and register the data for the ID card.
National Directorate of Civil Identification (DNIC) arrested an employee for illegally collecting registered data from the National ID cards database in Maputo city on 13 November.
The National Criminal Investigation Service (Sernic) announced that they obtained evidence (CCTV footage) to track and detain the suspects involved in the kidnapping of a businessman on 16 November.

Mozambican and Malawian representatives conducted a meeting starting on 18 - 21 November. The meeting was to discuss security and cooperation between the two countries. The security section of the meeting will cover illegal immigration, human trafficking, and smuggling of minerals and goods.

The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) warned that various human rights violations are occurring due to the conflict in Cabo Delgado on 18 November. UNHCR stated that some of the violations include sexual violence and increased teenage pregnancies, child recruitment, and increased risk factors in relation to the COVID pandemic.  The UNHCR also said more than 3,000 structures have been destroyed in the insurgency, and also said 90% of those displaced by the ongoing insurgency are living with relatives and friends, rather than in IDP camps.

The EU People's Party on 18 November has called on the EU parliament to hold a debate regarding insurgent attacks in northern Mozambique. The party says it wants pressure placed on the EU to "act urgently" in Mozambique.  The topics of issues to be discussed at the next plenary session of the EU parliament will be chosen on 19 November.

RENAMO officials called on RENAMO dissidents to stop their attacks on civilians in Sofala and Manica provinces on 17 November. RENAMO leader, Ossufo Momade, stated that RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo should discuss issues with Momade.  Nhongo has in the past refused to engage in talks with Momade, who he has repeatedly called a "traitor" and has said he would only hold peace talks with the government.

The Defense Minister, Jaime Neto, announced on 18 November that the Mozambican government is determined to target the leaders of the insurgent groups in Cabo Delgado.. Neto also stated that the government is conducting an offensive against insurgent bases, saying that the military is targeting militant supply lines and external funding "through international and regional cooperation based mainly on the exchange of information".

Mozambique President Filipe Nyusi announced that the country is open to "any kind of support" in counterinsurgency efforts in Cabo Delgado. Nyusi stated that insurgency cannot be combated unilaterally and that the country has been receiving assistance from other countries.  The EU in October did agree to provide some support to the Mozambican government and military, though this will not include any direct intervention or provision of weapons to the Mozambican military.

In a speech on Wednesday addressing military staff graduating from a training, President Nyusi said that RENAMO dissidents had carried out 2 new attacks on 17 November, in which 3 people were injured, including one person seriously.  No other details on these incidents were provided.  Nyusi also said that it was "evident that we have to take care of them at the level they need", referring to RENAMO dissidents, saying the group was uninterested in peace talks.

Sources on 15 November indicated that at least 6 Mozambican military armored vehicles along with other reinforcements had arrived in the Mueda area.  Helicopters manned by South African Private Military Contractors were also reported in the area at this time.  A mixed group of 70 Mozambican military officers and DAG personnel were reported to have arrived in the town as part of this group.
A RENAMO dissident attack was reported to have been carried out in the Dombe area on 17 November, leaving three people injured.   No further information on this incident is currently available.

A RENAMO dissident attack was reported to have been carried out in the Chamboca area, but resulted only in material damage, according to a speech given by President Nyusi.  No further information on this incident is currently available.
Reports indicated that Mozambican military forces clashes with insurgents in Miangalewa town on 19 November, and re-established control over the town.  No casualty information is currently available.

Sources reported on 19 November said that a large force of at least 1,000 Mozambican military units, including Rapid Response police officers and regular army units had attacked insurgent positions at Muidumbe/Namacande, allegedly killing a number of insurgents and retaking the town.  One other source reported a large pro-government militia contingent was also involved in this operation while a separate group of pro-gov militia fighters remained behind in Mueda to protect the town  Operations to rescue civilians from the nearby bush were also reportedly ongoing.  Pictures of this  operation were also posted online, showing troops patrolling a mostly deserted Namacande town.  One source reported at least 16 insurgents killed in this operation.  Note that one photo posted online also purportedly depicted operations in Miangalewa town, east of Muidumbe/Namacande, where insurgents have long maintained camps.  A separate source reported that this operation had taken place, but that insurgents had deserted these towns before the Mozambican military entered them, and that no clashes had taken place.  Casualties and the clashes referred to in this report remain unverified, though it is confirmed that Namacande and other villages were retaken by the government.  Government troops during this operation also destroyed insurgent stocks of rice and "more than 350 kilos of dried fish", with officials saying that militants were "in trouble and have nothing to eat".

Sources on 18 November reported that Mueda residents continued to flee the town ahead of a potential attack by insurgents in the area.  FRELIMO politician and general Alberto Chipande meanwhile was reported to have evacuated his entire family from the town, which caused panic.  Reports from the town also indicated there was a rumor widely spread saying starting on 19 November, no one would be allowed to enter or leave Mueda.

The Mozambican Bar Association accused Mozambican police of conducting excessive inspections for COVID precaution measures. The association stated that they will create a way to protect human rights. The statement comes after reports stated that the police were conducting inspections that were with clear signs of violence and militarization.

Minister of Justice, Constitutional, and Religious Affairs, Helena Kida, announced on 18 November that two police instructors accused of having sexual relations with female police candidates at the Matalane training center in Maputo had been expelled from their positions.

The Provincial Office for Combating Corruption launched an investigation after accusations of corruption were made against the mayor of Nampula, Paulo Vahanle.  An audit was conducted municipality's accounts to start of the investigation.  Vahanle is a member of the opposition RENAMO party, and as mayor of the country's third largest city, is one of only a handful of RENAMO politicians in a position of significant power.

Mozambique Health Minister Armindo Tiago announced on 18 November that there is a shortage of protective equipment for medical staff working against the pandemic in Mozambique. Tiago stated that the shortage was due to some companies that won a tender in June that have yet to provide protective equipment.  The government is currently working to alleviate this shortage.

RENAMO officials clarified that their armed members do not have hidden or undeclared weapons and all armaments have or are being handed over to the authorities as part of the disarmament, demobilization and reintegration (DDR) process. RENAMO also said that 60 million Euros meant to be distributed as part of the DDR process has not been released.

Minister of Justice, Constitutional and Religious Affairs, Helena Kida, said that the government has recorded 13 kidnapping cases during January to October Across Mozambique, but has detained just four suspects as part of these cases. Kida stated that the government intends to increase police capacity in the areas which were prone for kidnapping.

Tanzanian authorities said on 19 November that Tanzanian police had arrested an unspecified number of people who "want to join" the Cabo Delgado insurgency in Mtwara District.  Those arrested according to authorities came from Kigoma, Mtwara, and other parts of the Tanzania and were described as "many Tanzanians, many young people".  Several of those arrested were also reported to be residents of villages along the Rovuma River, just across from Cabo Delgado, and had aided insurgents in providing on the ground intelligence before the 14 October attack on the Tanzanian village of Kitaya.  One official also warned that the group was believed to be carrying out recruiting activities in villages along the Tanzanian border with Mozambique.

Police chief Bernadino Rafael was reported to be in Mueda on 17 November, with military units in the town holding a public parade to welcome the police commander.  This came as tensions were high in the area over a possible assault by insurgents on Mueda.

94 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 19 November, including 67 new cases in Maputo city, 19 cases in Maputo, 3 cases in Cabo Delgado, 2 in Zambezia, 2 in Nampula, and 1 in Tete.  1 new death was also reported during this period.  This brought nationwide cases to 14,723, with 120 deaths.

A crowd gathered on 19 November in front of a local leader in the Manga Mascarenhas neighborhood of Beira, protesting after local authorities recently failed to distribute mosquito nets.  Demonstrators chanted "we want mosquito nets" and accused local leaders of negligence; no violence was reported as part of this demonstration.
Security forces reportedly captured a number of insurgents in retaking Namacande/Muidumbe town, and has transported those captured to Montepuez, local sources reported.

Mueda's Rural Hospital was reported this week to have shut down over fears of a potential insurgent attack on the town and to have dis-charged in-patients.  A group of around 100 doctors, nurses, and other staff reportedly left the town after the hospital was closed down, leaving behind a group of just 7 health care workers behind to receive medical emergencies.
Local media reported that Nangade's local court has been closed for several months and that the local district presiding judge left the area after insurgent attacks on Nangade district villages.

Satellite imagery from the afternoon of 19 November showed fires in parts of Nameneco village in Macomia district, south of Quiterajo in what is suspected to be an insurgent attack on the town.  No further information on this incident is currently available.

Government troops on 19 November were reported to be back in control of Muatide village as part of a wider offensive against insurgents to retake Muidumbe District.  It was unclear if any clashes occurred in the village. Muatide in early November was reported to be the site of multiple beheadings carried out by the insurgents targeting local villagers.

Government troops on 19 November were reported to be back in control of Muambula town as part of a wider offensive against insurgents to retake Muidumbe District.  It was unclear if any clashes occurred in the town. Muambula is the site of a large Catholic church and insurgents over the past two weeks had reportedly used the town and church as one of their main bases during their occupation.

Pro-government sources reported that on or around 19 November, the Mozambican Air Force, likely referring to DAG helicopters, destroyed 6 insurgent canoes and insurgent food stockpiles in the Lago Inguri area.

Government forces on or before 19 November conducted patrols between Macomia and Litamanda, reportedly clashing with insurgents and clearing them from the area.  This operation took place reportedly as security forces also retook Muidumbe/Namacade town and other villages in Muidumbe District from insurgents.

Insurgents in early November carried out killings in the Miangalewa area after civilians fled parts of Muidumbe District follow an insurgent offensive into the area that began on 31 October.  Insurgents pursued civilians into the area where they carried out these killings.  It is unclear how many civilians were killed near Miangalewa though the area has long been the site of an insurgent camp.
RENAMO dissidents reportedly carried out an attack on a vehicle in the Bunga area in Manica on 17 November, causing damage to the vehicle though no casualties were reported.

An NGO warned that the levels of sexual violence against women have been increasing as a result of being displaced due to the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado. Child marriages are also increasingly significantly in IDP camps. Mozambique already has very high rates of child marriage, and a 2011 study indicated that 48% of women aged 20-24 were married before the age of 18, with 14% married before the age of 15.

Mozambican Police Bernardno Rafael conducted a meeting with the Tanzanian Police Chief Simon Sirro in preparation to conduct joint operations along the Tanzania-Mozambique border in Mtwara, Tanzania. Both police chiefs signed a memorandum to share information and deploy additional patrols along the Cabo Delgado - Tanzania border in order to combat insurgents, which Tanzanian officials referred to as a "criminal gang".

Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM) and the Mozambican National Resistance (RENAMO) accused government authorities of having excluded their members and their families from receiving financial aid  during the pandemic in Inhambane.  Opposition party members say these stipends have been politicized, and that only FRELIMO supporters are receiving this aid.

Journalists who recently fled insurgent attacks in Muidumbe said that civilians had fled into the woods, and that many unaccompanied children were in these bush areas, also saying that they had come across many dead bodies during their escape.  The journalists also said that insurgents had used a church in the Muambula area as their base of operations, and said that insurgents had abducted "countless women" during the Muidumbe attacks, which began on 31 October.

Rains in Cabo Delgado are expected to begin in the coming weeks and will likely last until April, with forecasts indicating rains may be heavier than normal.  Many roads in the province will be made unusable during these rains, and humanitarian access to remote areas will likely be slowed or cut off during this time.

Police began investigations regarding a poisoning case of a family in Molumbo on 20 November. Two children reportedly died while five were in a critical condition due to an unidentified substance found on the ingested cornmeal eaten by the family.

The WHO delivered additional equipment to increase the Ministry of Health’s capabilities to conduct COVID testing in Mozambique on 19 November. WHO stated that the Ministry of Health is able to test 2,000 samples daily after this delivery as compared to the previous 1,600 test conducted per day.
Police arrested a suspect for forging COVID test results, marking them negative and selling them in Maputo on 18 November.

Government officials announced that 74,149 students were displaced due to the insurgency in Cabo Delgado while six teachers have been killed in the province. The minister for education and human development, Carmelita Namashulua stated that 1,125 teachers were also displaced by the insurgency.
Only 500 classrooms have been repaired/rebuilt in Sofala province, out of 2,700 destroyed/damaged by Cyclone Idai in March/April 2019.  Another 190 classrooms are currently being rehabilitated.

Mozambican officials on 20 November after meetings with Tanzanian security officials said that Tanzanian security forces had arrested "562 terrorists or terrorist collaborators" in the aftermath of the 14 October Kitaya attacks.  This came after Tanzanian officials reported on 19 November that they had arrested an unspecified number of people who wanted to join the Cabo Delgado insurgency, including a large number of Tanzanian nationals.  Tanzanian authorities said those arrested were from Kigoma, Mwanza, and other parts of the country.  A large number of those arrested were reportedly from Mtwara District, and had provided local intelligence to insurgents to support the 14 October attack on the Tanzanian village of Kitaya.
Additional patrol vessels were given to the Coast Guard to conduct maritime patrols in the waterways of Zambezia on 17 November, officials announced.
Coast Guards detained illegal fishermen and seized 35kgs of illegally caught shrimp in Xai Xai on 14 November.

As part of a new security agreement with Tanzania, 516 insurgency suspects will be extradited to Mozambique to face terrorism charges.  Most of those detained had reportedly fled into Tanzania fleeing Mozambican security forces, local media reported.  Among those detained are Mozambicans, Tanzanians, Somalis, Ugandans, Congolese, Rwandans, and Burundians, according to Mozambican security officials.

56 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique along with 1 new death on 22 November, bringing the nationwide case total to 14,981 with 124 deaths.  35 new cases were reported in Maputo City, along with 11 cases in Zambezia, 3 in Maputo province, 3 in Cabo Delgado, 3 in Nampula, and 1 in Tete.

Illegal mining activity in Manica according to local authorities in polluting the Pungue River, and harming the city of Beira in Sofala's water supply.  Beira residents are being advised to decant their water before consuming it, though saying the water quality is still within the standards set by the WHO to be deemed consumable.

A large number of displaced people fleeing from Muidumbe and Mueda have recently arrived in Nairoto AP in Montepuez District; local authorities describe the situation as "worrying" and that humanitarian aid is being provided to the displaced in the area.

Security forces on 22 November seized two boats transporting 500kgs of crab illegally caught on a beach near Beira.  Two suspects transporting the crab fled when their vessel was approached by security officials.

4 people were killed and 27 injured on the night of 21 November when a truck lost control and rolled off the N1 road in the Malova area of Massinga District, Inhambane.  The incident occurred when the truck, which was carrying more than 30 people, was speeding in reduced visibility along the highway.

Zimbabwe's Minister of Defense and War Veterans Affairs Oppah Muchinguri on 23 November in a speech at Zimbabwe's Staff College said that the SADC was "under threat" from acts of terrorism in Mozambique which required a collective effort to overcome.  She also said the Harare government was "deeply concerned" about the security situation in Mozambique, saying Mozambique is Zimbabwe's "gateway to the sea" which must be secured.
Two people died on Saturday in a canoe accident on the Zambezi River in Chinde District.  4 other people survived the accident, which was occurred due to the canoe being overloaded.

The EU on 19 November signed an agreement with The Wildlife Conservation Society on a new project which will work to disrupt illegal wildlife smuggling/poaching supply chains out of Niassa's Special Reserve.  The project will also look to combat illegal logging in the area.  The project will seek to reduce community-based threats to wildlife and other natural resources, and support local communities' livelihoods and reinforce their involvement and management of the Niassa reserve.  The project will also coordinate actions to combat poaching and other illegal activities.

A crowd of RENAMO members on 23 November demonstrated in Tete city, calling for the ouster of Ossufo Momade, the president of RENAMO.  The group were led by Hernani da Silva, a member of Tete's Municipal Assembly and a RENAMO member.  In a statement, da Silva said that the group believed that the "safest and fastest way to strengthen the internal union of the RENAMO party" would be the resignation of Momade.  The demonstration ended with clashes between da Silva's group and a group led by RENAMO's Tete provincial political delegate Evaristo Tatamo, a supporter of Momade.  People on both sides were injured in this brawl.  It is unclear if police intervened in this incident.

A crowd of RENAMO members on 23 November demonstrated in Tete city, calling for the ouster of Ossufo Momade, the president of RENAMO.  The group were led by Hernani da Silva, a member of Tete's Municipal Assembly and a RENAMO member.  In a statement, da Silva said that the group believed that the "safest and fastest way to strengthen the internal union of the RENAMO party" would be the resignation of Momade.  The demonstration ended with clashes between da Silva's group and a group led by RENAMO's Tete provincial political delegate Evaristo Tatamo, a supporter of Momade.  People on both sides were injured in this brawl, with at least 2 seriously injured.  It is unclear if police intervened in this incident.

The High Commissioner of Botswana to Mozambique High Commissioner Mr Pitso conducted talks with Zimbabwean Ambassador to Mozambique Douglas Nyikayaramba discussing the Disarmament Demobilization and Reintegration (DDR) and ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

Dozens of insurgents on boats reportedly abducted two civilians after intercepting a civilian vessel near Quifuqui Island on the evening of Monday, 23 November. The insurgents forced around 20 people to hand over their valuables including their mobile phones. The captives were taken to Mocimboa da Praia, where one of the two reportedly managed to escape.
RENAMO member and Tete's Municipal Assembly member, Hernani da Silva, stated that he was receiving death threats related to his calls for the ouster of RENAMO chief Ossufo Momade.

Four thieves were caught by the locals and burned to death for stealing livestock in the Uachavane area of Moamba district, northwest of Maputo City, on 22 November. The suspects were reportedly unidentifiable due to the decomposition of the suspects’ bodies.

A grenade exploded in Zimpinga 1 in Gondola on 17 November. Two children were killed and three others were injured.  The grenade was likely left over from the country's Independence War and Civil War periods.

The Ministry of Health announced two more COVID deaths and 72 positive cases in Mozambique on 23 November bringing the total to 15,109. 31 cases were recorded in Maputo city , 20 cases were reported in Maputo province, 11 in Gaza, 5in Zambezia, 4 in Tete province, and one in Niassa.

A man in Mueda on an unspecified date in early November was arrested and assaulted by security forces in the town after it was discovered that he had an identity card saying he was born in Mocimboa da Praia, and security forces suspected him of being an insurgent.  The man was released after other local police intervened.

Military personnel in the Ancuabe area on an unspecified date in early November detained two priests who were travelling with local residents in the area.  Both priests were reportedly beaten by security forces for unknown reasons, but were later released after the Catholic church officials learned of their arrests and intervened.

Insurgents reportedly continue to receive intelligence regarding security force movements, positions, and personnel, partially by paying security force members for information.  In an insurgent attack on security force positions in Quissanga earlier this year, insurgents were reported to be aware of the presence of an officer who many of the insurgents knew personally, and attempted to capture him in the clashes.  In July, insurgents were also aware of a government operation to attack an insurgent camp in Mocimboa da Praia, partially through videos and pictures posted by Mozambican soldiers online, which allowed insurgents to set an ambush in which a significant number of troops were killed.

Police on 24 November at checkpoints in parts of Pemba District in Cabo Delgado were reported to be searching for 12 specific people, questioning travelers and demanding ID documents.  The 12 individuals are reportedly all male, though it is unclear if those being sought are criminals or terror suspects.

A document purportedly sent to the Mozambican government by the RENAMO Military Junta in September 2019 was recently made publicly available.  In the document, the dissidents called for military officers to have a base salary of 15,000 meticais, and called for all demobilized RENAMO men to be given a pension, including backdated pay for "years of service".  The document also called for the reintegration of RENAMO military personnel into the military and parity of RENAMO commands in all sectors of the country's military.  The document also calls for the ouster of RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade, and for new negotiations to take place between the government and new RENAMO leadership.

Insurgents wearing military uniforms on the night of 21 November were reported to have landed on Quifuqui Island off the Palma Coast.  Three civilians were killed during the attack on the island, and insurgents reportedly abducted two people in the attack as well.

Insurgents wearing military uniforms on the night of 21 November were reported to have landed on Quifuqui Island off the Palma Coast.  Insurgents abducted two people in this attack, though one source indicated more captives taken.

Security forces in Nangade on an unspecified date in November detained a group of Catholic priests and nuns, reportedly harassing them and searching them roughly, saying the group were "dressed like insurgents".  Catholic church authorities learned of the situation and intervened, and the group were released.

Soldiers and police stationed in and around Palma and the Afungi Peninsula continue to receive extra subsidies on top of their regular pay for protecting these areas.  A source recently reported this is causing growing unrest among other soldiers and police stationed across Cabo Delgado who also want subsidized pay for serving in this active conflict zone.

Residents of the Mapulanguene in Magude District of Maputo Province who were displaced from their land 13 years ago to create game farms, safari lodges, and other tourist attractions who are meant to be receiving 20% of government revenue from these projects say they have never been paid by the government. The government has also not fulfilled local employment quotas at these projects.

Sources on 24 November reported that the Mozambican military had recently obtained a number of Armored Personnel Carrier (APC) from a South African-based company.  At least five of these Marauder vehilces are currently being used by the Mozambican military in Cabo Delgado.  These vehicles are equipped with explosive-resistant reinforced armor, and considered to be of superior quality to Chinese-made APCs previously used by the Mozambican military and police in fighting the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

Tensions have risen in Mecanhelas District of Niassa Province over local "community leaders" who have been officially recognized by the government.  150 new community leaders in the past 3 years have been recognized by authorities, adding to 600 community leaders already recognized by the government.  This rise in "community leaders" could cause conflict as different local leaders pursue different objectives in the district.

Sources indicate that security forces in Cabo Delgado in clashes with insurgents regularly carry out extra-judicial killings when insurgents are captured.  Those executed have also included female insurgents, who are often sexually assaulted before being killed - as was the case in a September incident when a woman suspected of supporting the insurgency was shot dead near Awasse - an incident that was filmed and later released online.

Unconfirmed reports from two sources on the afternoon of 24 November indicated that insurgent had launched a new attack on Namacade/Muidumbe, the capital of Muidumbe District, recapturing the town.  There were also indications insurgents had again carried out looting and destruction of property, and of attacks on civilians. This comes just 5 days after security forces retook the town in an operation in which government officials said 16 insurgents were killed.  Troops also were reported to have entered several other Muidumbe villages, though there were indications insurgents had withdrawn from towns and villages in the district rather than directly engage the military.  After the army's recapture of Namacade, it was unclear if any garrison was left behind in the town.  Other sources reported clashes in the Muidumbe area, though it was unclear who controlled the town.

Security forces detained three senior officials of the Mozambican Tax Authority at Beira Central Prison in Sofala. The officials were accused of forging documents and abuse of power. The officials were the Head of Inspection of the Provincial Forest Services, and two Regional Heads of Investigation and Intelligence. The suspects forged documents for a company exporting wood items.

The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) detained four wanted suspects in Nampula on 24 November. The group's leader was a previously wanted fugitive who escaped Maputo Central Prison last 2014. One of the other members was wanted for absentia in Inhambane province while another suspect was previously pardoned by in Monapoeja district.  The group had committed several robberies using a firearm.
1,500 IDPs from Cabo Delgado arrived in Montepuez in recent days and have received distributed farming and agricultural tools for rebuilding their livelihood.

The National Statistics Institute (INE) announced that the gross domestic product of Mozambique fell 1.09 percent during the 3rd quarter of 2020 in comparison to the previous year. INE also stated that the country’s economy has recovered compared to the second quarter of 2020.

World Food Programme stated that insufficient funding was preventing the organization from fully assisting around 400,000 displaced civilians in Cabo Delgado. WFP stated that it managed to assist only 152,000 IDPs last month when it was able to aid 234,000 in September.  The WFP says it only has about $98.7 million to support IDPs in Mozambique over the next 6 months, about 35% of the funds it considers necessary.

Armed men murdered a family of four with melee weapons at a school in Tchumene, west of Maputo, on the evening of 21 November. The father of the family reportedly worked as a guard for the school and lived their with his family.

Sofala provincial attorney’s office, Joaquim Tomo, stated that senior state officials have failed to declare their assets according to the Law on Public Probity of 2012. Tomo stated that 1,530 individuals have failed to declare their assets. Around 25 of the said individuals could be fined for undeclaring their possessions.

122 new COVID cases and 1 related death were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 24 November. A total of 127 deaths and 15,231 cases were recorded. 179 recoveries were reported bringing the total to 13,401.
National Institute for Disaster Management (INGC) stated that around 70 IDPs from Cabo Delgado recently arrived in Nampula to the Corrane reception area of Meconta District.

815 Cabo Delgado IDPs arrived in several cities of Zambezia province recently, local media reported on 24 November. The IDPs reportedly arrived in Quelimane, Alto-Molocue, Mocuba, Nicoadala, Namacurra, Chinde, Morrumbala and Milange. Local authorities stated that land distribution for the IDPs has slowed down due to the availability of materials for building their shelters.

Insurgents on the night of 13 November attacked the island of Mecungo (Quifuqui) off the MDP coast, carrying out looting of food and other items.  An unknown number of people were also abducted.  No casualties were reported.
Insurgents on the night of 13 November abducted an unknown number of people in a raid on the island of Mecungo (Quifuqui).

Pro-government militia members on 17 November registered a formal complaint that Mozambican soldiers had carried out "looting" in Palma town.  No further details on this incident are currently available.

Two reporters on 24 November were attacked by residents of Muatala, Nampula City after the two attempted to collect statements and images of people being evicted from their home.  The journalists' equipment was seized, and the incident was reported to the police.

DAG helicopter positions in Pemba are reportedly operating out of a base along the Av. Da Marginal from a helipad base constructed in recent months.  This remains DAG's primary base in Cabo Delgado, and the group does not maintain bases in government towns such as Macomia or Mueda due to security concerns.

Maritime traffic between Pemba and Palma remains low along the Cabo Delgado coast due to the threat of insurgent attacks between the two locations.  Satellite tracking of marine traffic in recent days shows that vessels remain clustered in the Pemba area as well as in waters outside of Palma.  Journalists in Pemba also report that there are only a small number of smaller local vessels are willing to make this journey for fear of militant attacks.

The Minister of National Defense, Jaime Neto stated that the security situation in Cabo Delgado is under control of the security forces.  Neto also mentioned that joint operations with Tanzania were also being conducted along the borders to strengthen security presence.

President Filipe Nyusi in a speech criticized media for spreading "disinformation" to the public which has aided insurgents in Cabo Delgado. The president stated that security forces should be vigilant against such disinformation which aligned with the strategy of the insurgents.  He also called on the military to "safeguard" human rights.  Nyusi did not name any specific media outlets in the speech.

Portuguese Foreign Minister stated that Portugal will contribute to aiding with the training and education of the military forces of Mozambique against insurgency. The Foreign Minister also offered support through the EU and bilateral support. This comes as Portugal’s Prime Minister offered their country’s support to fight the terrorism in Cabo Delgado during a call between the PM and President Filipe.

Portugal Secretary of State for EU Affairs Ana Paula Zacarias stated that Mozambique needs to authorize EU in conducting their expert mission in the country. Zacarias mentioned that the authorization should have already taken place. The expert mission was to determine the required amount of deployed support to Mozambique. The EU was previously requested to provide training and other support to the country’s military against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

The World Food Program (WFP) announced that it would decrease its food aid to the IDPs starting next Tuesday, 1 December, due to the lack of funding. WFP previously stated that it hoped to reach about 750,000 IDPs and host communities in the coming months.  The WFP said that it needs $96 million to support IDPs over the next 12 months, but that only about $11.7 million of that has so far been secured.

The SADC intends to conduct a meeting to discuss the ongoing security issues in Mozambique during the The Extraordinary Organ Troika Summit on 26-27 November (Thursday-Friday). The summit will be attended by the Force Intervention Brigade, Troop Contributing Countries, Democratic Republic of Congo, and Republic of Mozambique.

The Secretary of State in Nampula stated that locals are preventing IDPs from resettling by stopping them from occupying their issued land plots in Corrane Settlement. The Nampula Secretary of Statesta6ted that careful screening has been made on the IDPs to prevent focus of terrorism in the area. Nampula province is about to resettle 37,000 IDPs, in which only 2,000 have only been resettled.

World Vision Charity stated that one child is sexually assaulted every six hours in Mozambique during January to September of 2020. Almost all the victims are female, according to police sources. Maputo, Gaza, and Nampula provinces were reported to have the highest cases of rape. An increase was also reported during the start of the COVID pandemic.

World Vision Charity stated that one child is sexually assaulted every six hours in Mozambique during January to September of 2020. Almost all the victims are female, according to police sources. Maputo, Gaza, and Nampula provinces were reported to have the highest cases of rape. An increase was also reported during the start of the COVID pandemic.

World Vision Charity stated that one child is sexually assaulted every six hours in Mozambique during January to September of 2020. Almost all the victims are female, according to police sources. Maputo, Gaza, and Nampula provinces were reported to have the highest cases of rape. An increase was also reported during the start of the COVID pandemic.

The Institute of Economics and Peace released an issue of the Global Terrorism Index indicating that Mozambique went up by 8 ranks in the index. The index stated that Mozambique is significantly impacted by its growing terrorism threat.

Mozambique reportedly lost an expected 2 billion USD economic gain due to the delay of some Oil and Gas projects in the country. Sources stated that due to the pandemic, natural gas has devalued which led to the delay of the projects. Mozambican Hydrocarbon Company's reports and accounts stated that the loss would negatively affect the country's economy. The revenue of the delayed final investment decision was expected to come by early 2022, being inline with the estimations of Oslo-based research group.

Rising sea waters destroyed several residences near Barra Beach in the north of Inhambane on 25 November. Around 80 meters of beach line was reduced by the high sea waters and broke through placed sand barriers setup by homeowners to prevent the increasing sea level.

Major Oil and Gas companies and the Mozambique government were reported to be conducting negotiations over the LNG projects in Mozambique. The talks were to figure out how to extract additional gas from the shared oil fields while cutting costs due to the COVID pandemic and worsening security situation in northern Mozambique.

Local sources stated that international journalists have not been granted permits to travel Cabo Delgado and cover the ongoing insurgency. A small number of local journalists were granted permits to protect them from the military. Photography was also reported to be banned during the coverage of the insurgency.

71 new COVID cases and 1 related death were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 25 November increasing the total cases to 15,302 and 128 deaths. 38 cases were recorded in Maputo city, 15 in the Maputo province, 7 in Nampula province, 4 in Zambezia province, two in the Manica province, and one in Tete province.

Suspected RENAMO dissidents attacked a vehicle in the Seventine village next to the N260 raod in Dombe Administrative Post of Sussundenga district, south of Chimoio, on the afternoon of 25 November at around 1400hrs.  Three civilians working on an AIDS relief project connected to USAID were injured.
Locals found a remnant IED and called security forces to dispose of the explosive at the backyard of a residence in Matola, west of Maputo City, on the evening of 26 November.

Environmentalists and Johannesburg officials stated that Mozambique may be fined for not complying with international standards against poaching. Officials stated that Mozambique may lose its commercial agreements due to not conforming with the international standard on anti-poaching.

165 daily COVID cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 26 November. 119 were reported to be in Maputo city, 14 in Maputo province, 13 in Sofala province, 9 in Cabo Delgado, 4 in Nampula, 3 in Zambezia, and 3 in Gaza. A total of 15,467 cases were reported since the first infection.

297 Mozambique nationals were reported to have been deported by South African officials due to illegal residency in South Africa on 26 November. Several of the deportees were also charged with various criminal activities.

A local leader was reportedly beaten to death for being accused of spreading cholera inside an IDP center in Nangua, Metuge, on 25 November. The suspects threatened to destroy the IDP center due to the outbreak of cholera.

Seven civilians were killed after being struck by lightning during heavy rainfall and strong winds in Manica province on the evening of 25 November. Several public infrastructures and residences were destroyed.

Thousands of people on the afternoon of 25 November fled Nangua camp in Metuge after a riot in which a local leader was killed.  This came after an outbreak of diarrhea in the camp that left 5 people dead.  Residents rioted after accusing the local leader of spreading the disease, attacking him, and beating him to death.  Security forces arrived at the camp to break up the riot, firing live ammunition and arresting several people involved in the attack on the local leader.  Much of the camp was deserted by the morning of 26 November.

Thousands of people on the afternoon of 25 November fled Nangua camp in Metuge after a riot in which a local leader was killed.  This came after an outbreak of diarrhea in the camp that left 5 people dead.  After clashes with security forces, many IDPs later fled the camp.

Local sources stated that security forces exchanged gunfire with insurgents between Namacande and Muatide on 26 November. Insurgents were later reported to be back in control of both areas. Insurgents as previously reported had remained in control of some areas of the Muidumbe countryside even after being pushed out of Namacande and other Muidumbe District towns in the government's 19 November counteroffensive.

Local sources stated that security forces exchanged gunfire with insurgents between Namacande and Muatide on 26 November. Insurgents took control of both areas. Insurgents as previously reported had remained in control of some areas of the Muidumbe countryside even after being pushed out of Namacande and other Muidumbe District towns in the government's 19 November counteroffensive.
Unconfirmed reports stated that insurgents conducted an attack on Nangade, north of Muidumbe, on 26 November.

Gunmen shot and killed the former RENAMO deputy, Rosa Chukwa, and another woman who were travelling inside a vehicle in Lichinga on the evening of 26 November. The suspects fled from the area after firing around 20 shots on the vehicle.  Police sources later said the women were intercepted by a group of gunmen who opened fire on them, and said that the killers had been "hired by someone" to conduct the attack though reasons for the assassination were unclear.  Chukwa was a RENAMO member of Mozambique's parliament from 2000-2005, but later left the party to join the MDM opposition party; it was unclear at the time of her death which party she was affiliated with, though her son reportedly accused RENAMO of being behind the killing.

Police arrested two suspects for theft charges in Matola, west of Maputo city on 27 November. The suspects previously broke into a supermarket and stole several goods. Police recovered food items and other goods.

President Filipe conducted talks with Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Costa regarding the acquisition of COVID vaccines when they become available. The talks also discussed the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado, and potential Portuguese/EU support for Mozambique in combating the insurgency.

Local authorities announced that will screen IDPs arriving from Cabo Delgado in Nampula before resettling them. Officials stated that the screening was to prevent Cabo Delgado insurgents from infiltrating other parts of the country.

A mortar exploded in a residential area of Palma on 27 November. Three civilians were injured. Sources later reported the explosion was the result of an accidental discharge by a military unit stationed nearby.

SADC Presidents after a meeting on 27 November in Gaborone said there was an "urgent" need for the region to support Mozambique in combating the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  The Presidents of Botswana, South Africa, Zimbabwe, the DRC, and Malawi attended the conference, while Moz Minister of Defense Jaime Neto represented the Mozambican government, while Tanzania's VP represented the Dodoma government.  SADC members also agreed on a "comprehensive regional response", which will reportedly include a "Regional Center to Comat Terrorism" which will be operational by 2021.  This center will "facilitate effective surveillance and timely interventions by the Region".  A communique released after the summit also said the group accepted a UN proposal to re-align the Force Intervention Brigade (FIB), which is deployed in the DRC, in order to create two Quick Reaction Forces.  One source said these QRFs could be deployed into Mozambique - though this is unconfirmed and the FIB's current mandate is limited to deployments in the DRC.

Reports on 29 Nov indicated that clashes occurred between GSF and insurgents in Ntushi, approximately 12 km east of Mueda and just south of President Nyusi's home village of Namaua. No other details on this incident are currently available. Sources later indicated as many as 18 government soldiers were killed in this clash, though this casualty information is unverified.

A deep water port in Macuse will begin in 2021, disclosed on 30 Nov by Orlando Marques, chairperson of Thai Mozambique Logistics. The building of the port will be complete in 2023 and will be fully operational on 2024. The Macuse concession covers the construction and operation of Macuse port and of a new, 620 kilometer long railway linking Macuse to Chitima in the Moatize coal basin in Tete province. The government granted the concession to the Thai company Italthai Engineering, which holds 60% of Thai Mozambique Logistics.

39 new COVID cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 27 November. 17 were reported to be in Maputo city, 8 in Maputo province, one each for Cabo Delgado, Nampula, Manica and Gaza. A total of 15,506 cases were reported since the first infection. COVID-19 death toll in the country remains 128 as there were no new death cases reported.

27 COVID cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 29 November. 17 were reported to be in Maputo city, 4 in Maputo province, 2 in Niassa, 2 in Manica and one each for Cabo Delgado and Gaza. A total of 15,613 cases were reported since the first infection. COVID-19 death toll in the country is now 130 as there two new death cases were recorded for the last 24 hours.

Several false reports on 30 November indicated that the town of Mueda had been captured by insurgents.  Sources in and around Mueda town however denied the town had fallen and said Mueda was still held by government security forces, though acknowledged insurgents do remain present in parts of the adjacent district of Muidumbe.

Mozambican authorities said on 30 November that they had seized 1,100 kgs of crab in Central Mozambique in operations in less than a week, including the seizure of 600 kgs of crab outside of Beira on 28 November in the Maria River mangroves.  A week before, 500 kgs of illegally harvested crab was seized in the same area.

The EU in recent talks with the Mozambican government said that 15 million euros had been given to Maputo for the fight against terrorism in Cabo Delgado, but that no direct military aid would be provided to the country.  The EU is instead focused on supporting IDPs displaced in Cabo Delgado, and to help improve the political/economic/ social situation in Cabo Delgado which triggered the insurgency.

Insurgents were reported on 30 November to be in control of Muidumbe/Namacande town.  This came after reports last week of clashes in the area between security forces and insurgents, though it was unclear who was in control of the town.  Insurgents also remain in control of several other towns in Muidumbe District, and are able to threaten Mueda town from these areas.

The IOM said on 27 November that between 28 October - 25 November that more that 45,000 people fled Muidumbe due to insurgent attacks, and that over 37,000 of the displaced had travelled to Mueda while about 5,000 had moved south into Montepuez and 3,000 had traveled to Pemba.  Around half of the displaced from Muidumbe are children.  Some of these IDPs were displaced for the first time, while others were displaced for the 2nd or 3rd time, the organization said.  The IOM also said that over 144,0000 people are displaced in hard to reach areas due to insecurity.

Cabo Delgado's government said on 29 November that "virtually all economic activity" has been suspended in most of the province due to insurgent attacks, including mining in the Montepuez area, despite this area still being under government control.  Montepuez Ruby Mining auctions have not been held since December 2019, while insurgent attacks have also disrupted harvests of cashew nuts, one of the province's main exports, an industry that employs over 265,000 people.
Police in Maputo on 27 November detained 28 people in the Beluluane area on different charges, including for failing to comply with anti-COVID measures, alcohol consumption and prostitution.

The Center for Democracy and Development (CDD) reported on 27 November the opening of a "Youth Hub" in Montepuez to help "empower and engage youth in the search for solutions to their challenges".  The Montepuez facility is meant to prevent young people in the area from becoming involved in the illegal drugs trade, and to prevent local youths from joining the insurgency.

A FRELIMO deputy of the Beira Municipal Assembly was attacked on 27 November in the Assembly Chamber by an MDM member.  MDM later said FRELIMO was exaggerating in their reports of the incident, and that their delegate was merely attempting to make the FRELIMO deputy give up the floor after he had exceeded his speaking time. FRELIMO later filed a police report over the incident.

Mozambique over the past 5 years has lost over 2.6 billion (just over $35 million) to corruption, the country's Minister of Justice Helena Kida said on 28 Nov.  340 cases of corruption have been reported in the country in the first half of 2020; 764 cases were reported in 2019, 761 in 2018, 695 in 2017, and 493 in 2016.

Media sources said that Mozambican officials who on 27 November attended an SADC summit in Botswana in which the Cabo Delgado insurgency was discussed requested a "shopping list" of military equipment to fight the insurgency.  SADC leaders had reportedly expected a detailed plan on the fight against the insurgency.   Mozambican Defense Minister Jaime Neto meanwhile was reported to have left the room while the SADC discussed the Cabo Delgado insurgency, and an unnamed official said SADC countries speculated Mozambique had no serious interest in an actual SADC intervention in Cabo Delgado.

At a meeting of UN agencies in Maputo on 27 November, Minister of Foreign Affairs Veronica Macamo said that there was a risk that the Cabo Delgado insurgency could spread throughout the region and to "other regions" if the government and its partners did not stop the insurgency in the near future, calling for renewed international support.

Maputo Central Hospital on 27 November was reported to be under significant pressure treating COVID patients, and is in need of more medical professionals to support critical patients at the hospital.  There have been 220 COVID cases and 1 death among the hospital's staff during the pandemic.
Police in Mogincual District of Nampula seized 30 firearms at a farm in the area.  No ammunition was reportedly found in the area however.  No other details on this seizure are currently available.

After insurgents recently kidnapped at least two people sailing to Pemba from Palma, local authorities in Palma were reported to have banned local vessels from travelling the Palma - Pemba route until further notice.
Unconfirmed reports on 28 November indicated that there had been a COVID outbreak among military personnel in the Montepuez area, and that a significant number of soldiers were under quarantine.

Unconfirmed reports on 28 November said that there had been an outbreak of cholera in Montepuez District.  This comes after IDPs in recent weeks have been arriving into the district, fleeing from Mueda and Muidumbe districts.

The National Petroleum Institute of Mozambique was allegedly not notified on the talks between two major O&G companies, reports stated on 27 November. The two companies were in talks to increase the amount of gas they can extract from a shared field that straddles their two liquefied natural gas (LNG) developments, worth a combined $50 billion. It is important to note that any changes to resource-sharing agreement on the amount of gas each can extract has to be approved by the government.

RENAMO is engaged in the DDR process for its former fighters in Zambezia, a RENAMO political delegate disclosed on 26 November. Several former fighters in the province were still waiting to be tapped by DDR. RENAMO officials also say that while the DDR process is ongoing in other parts of the country, it is moving "not as fast as would be desirable", particularly in Sofala and Manica Provinces.

On 30 November, Collaboration on International ICT Policy for East and Southern Africa (CIPESA) are calling the Mozambican government to enhance media freedom, digital rights and freedom of expression ahead of the Universal Peer Review process in April 2021. The UPR offers all UN member states the opportunity to declare what actions they have taken to improve the human rights situation in their countries and to fulfil their obligations.

88 COVID cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 30 November. 40 were reported to be in Maputo city, 24 in Zambezia, 24 in Gaza and seven in Maputo province. A total of 15,701 cases were reported since the first infection. COVID-19 death toll in the country is now 131 as there was one new death case recorded for the last 24 hours.

Over 170 former RENAMO fighters were demobilized on 30 November as part of the demilitarization, disarmament and reintegration (DDR) process in Mabote, Inhambane. The demobilization process started on 27 November at this base.

Mozambique saw the fourth most malaria infections in the African region, according to a report released this Monday. 95% of malaria cases worldwide were in the WHO African region. Nigeria (27%), the Democratic Republic of Congo (12%), Uganda (5%), Mozambique (4%) and Niger (3%) accounted for around 51% of all cases worldwide.

November broke the record of deaths caused by COVID-19 with a total of 39 deaths versus 31 on October and 38 in September, Analise Epidemiologica disclosed on 30 Nov. November also saw rising rates of hospitalizations.

Heavy rains dropping 50-75mm in 24 hours with thunderstorms and strong winds are expected to hit the provinces of Sofala, Manica, and Inhambane starting 02 December, Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia announced on 01 December. Meanwhile, districts in the provinces of Maputo and Gaza may experience light to moderate rains with thunderstorms and strong winds in the evening.

Executive Secretary of Conselho Nacional do Combate on HIV/AIDS disclosed on 01 December that the disease infects 356 people per day in Mozambique. Amid the ongoing anti-HIV effort by the government, 130 thousand new HIV / AIDS infections were registered for 2019. By September 2020, 1.3 million people were on antiretroviral treatment, with the 30% rate of treatment abandonment in 2019.

Security forces arrested on 01 Dec three men over alleged connections to the killing of four family members in Maputo province. Investigations are still underway to apprehend other suspects. The murders took place in the premises of a school in Tchumene, outskirts of Maputo on 21 November.
Government officials on 01 December issued a warning to the residents of Beira and Dondo cities of 'moderate flooding' over the next 48 hours.

Government officials on 01 December issued a warning to the residents of Beira and Dondo cities of 'moderate flooding' over the next 48 hours.  There was also a reported flood risk in areas of the Buzi and Pungue River Basins.
A Mozambican security force member was killed in an road accident in Maputo city on the early morning of 29 Nov. No other details on this incident are currently available.

On 01 December the Mozambican government approved a 'Visa for Humanitarian Assistance' decree that will be granted to foreign nationals who come to the country to provide non-profit humanitarian work under state of emergency and publice calamity.

On 30 November, Cabo Delgado Secretary of State Armindo Ngunga announced that the Mozambican government are discussing the building of 100 new villages for the displace citizens by the Cabo Delgado insurgency. He added that the basic model community will include houses, schools, leisure spaces and hospitals. However, the budget and deadline for the construction of the new villages are still uncertain.  Some of the villages will be built in Ancuabe District, and others in other more secure areas of southern Cabo Delgado.

A lack of rain has negatively impacted the water supply in Maputo, according to the director of Nacional de Gestao de Recursos Hídricos on 01 December. The low levels of rain resulted in the low water levels at Pequenos Libombos reservoir which supplies the province. The aforementioned dam has only 19% of storage, versus the expected level of 30%. This is the same case with Corumana dam with 23% and Nampula with 30%.

69 COVID cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 01 December. 41 were reported to be in Maputo city, 13 in Sofala, seven in Gaza, four in Niassa, three in Zambezia, and one in Tete. A total of 15,770 cases were reported since the first infection. COVID-19 death toll in the country is now 131 as there was no new deaths recorded for the last 24 hours.  The 13 new cases in Sofala were notable and could signal the beginning of a new outbreak in the province.
RENAMO armed members on 30 November demobilized at a base in Funhalouro District in Inhambane.  The demobilization of armed members in Mabote District was previously reported.
RENAMO armed members on 30 November demobilized at a base in Vilanculo District in Inhambane.  The demobilization of armed members in Mabote District was previously reported.

US Coordinator for Counterterrorism Ambassador, Nathan A. Sales travelled to Maputo, Mozambique 02-03 December to discuss ongoing efforts to combat terrorism in the region. The discussion will also include how the US can assist these Mozambique during the operations. Sales will also travel on 04 Dec to South Africa for talks with the Pretoria government on security cooperation.

Unconfirmed reports on 02 Dec stated that unidentified men looted 10 houses and vandalized the Viaka Sabine secondary school in Muambula.  It was unclear if the town had been attacked again by insurgents or looted by security forces after military units briefly held the town in late November.

30 Ak-47 rifles and 15 Batak weapons were recovered  in Metacusse, Malema, Nampula, a source disclosed on 02 December. Investigation into the origin of the weapons is still ongoing.  This was the second reported weapons seizure in Nampula in a week.  Weapons seized in the 02 Dec incident were in very poor condition and believed to have been buried in the area after or during the civil war period.

Three armed men abducted a 54-yr-old Indian-Mozambican businessman in Zimpeto, Maputo on the afternoon of 27 Nov at around 1700hrs. The victim, who was on his way home, was forced to enter the suspects' vehicle.   His kidnappers reportedly fired shots in the air to force the victim into their vehicle. The suspects have yet to contact the family of the victims. The police stated that investigations on the incident are underway.  This was the second time the man was abducted; during his first abduction,  kidnappers demanded a ransom.  The family did not publicize the case after their experience in the previous kidnapping.
Video was released on 02 December by local media showing an alleged insurgent captured by security forces in an unspecified beachside area of Cabo Delgado.

At least 4 people were killed in lightning strikes on 30 November in Changara District of Tete, sources reported.  One other person was seriously injured in these strikes and a home set on fire as well.
A heavy rainstorm flooded large parts of Maputo on 01 Dec, while strong winds knocked down trees, damaged vehicles, and destroyed public light posts in some parts of the city.

Unconfirmed reports on 02 December said that as many as 10 Rapid Response Unit officers had died of a mysterious illness in Xinavane B village, just south of Macomia town in Macomia District.  The majority of those who died complained of pain and swelling in the abdomen before death.

Insurgents in a previously unreported incident in the first half of November attacked Matemo Island, raiding a maternity hospital in order to loot medical supplies. Insurgents scrawled "al Shabaab" and "Mujahido" on the walls of the hospital. Acting on intelligence, security forces reportedly ambushed the insurgents at the hospital, and shot seven militants dead in the ensuing clashes.  Security forces recovered a motorbike and weaponry in the wake of this clash.

Several NGOs are considering pulling out of operations in Central Mozambique over rising insecurity linked to RENAMO dissident attacks.  The most affected areas are Gondola, Sussungdenga, Machaze, and Mossurize in Manica.  Police sources meanwhile say they are working to improve security in these areas, and that checkpoints and police postings have been increased to identify and "neutralize" those responsible for attacks.

Insurgents and government security forces clashed with one another on 27 November in the vicinity of Namacande.  No casualty information was available.  Insurgent previously attacked security force positions in the area on 26 November.

Insurance companies working with companies in Cabo Delgado are increasingly reluctant according to sources to insure vehicles travelling by road from Pemba to Palma.  This is due to the fact that insurgents are present along parts of the main road route between the two locations, and also menace the alternative Pundanhar road to Palma as well.

120,000 lost their jobs in Mozambique due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Paulo Correa, World Bank's chief economist in Mozambique said on 01 Dec. The greater job loss incidence is evident in the northern part of the country.

On 02 December, Portugal reiterated its support to Mozambique in the fight against terrorism as well as for humanitarian assistance in Cabo Delgado province. The Cabo Delgado insurgency is now on the agenda of the European parliament, Portuguese ambassador to Mozambique, Maria Amelia Paiva,  disclosed following a meeting with the Secretary of State for Nampula, Mety Gondola.

Truck drivers staged a peaceful demonstration in Nampula to demand a wage increase to 25,000 meticais with medical assistance, professional recognition, employment contracts and payment of social security system contributions, on 02 December. The protest was disrupted upon the arrival of Mozambican police, who detained 19 truck drivers. Demos also took place in Beira and Maputo.  Despite this, the group vowed to continue the protest in order to improve their working conditions.

Security forces arrested 19 truck drivers protesting in Nampula on 02 December. The arrest follows an attempt of the police to stop the demonstration's protesters were demanding a wage increase to 25,000 meticais with medical assistance, professional recognition, employment contracts and payment of social security system contributions.

Truck drivers staged a peaceful demonstration in Beira to demand a wage increase to 25,000 meticais with medical assistance, professional recognition, employment contracts and payment of social security system contributions, on 02 December. Despite this, the group vowed to continue the protest in order to improve their working conditions.
