The arrest follows an attempt of the police to stop the demonstration's protesters were demanding a wage increase to 25,000 meticais with medical assistance, professional recognition, employment contracts and payment of social security system contributions.

The Institute of Social and Economic Studies reported this week that Foreign Direct Investment in Mozambique over the past 10 years is not having the expected impact on Mozambique's economic development.  Instead, the report says, investment has created conflicts between companies and communities near project sites.  Particularly in the case of the extractive industry, the Mozambican state fails to collect revenues and reinvest profits back into communities.

Insurgents ambushed Mozambican troops twice in Matambalale village of Muidumbe District on 29 November; sources previously reported this incident as having occurred on 01 December. The attacks, which took place during military patrols in the area, left 25 Mozambican troops dead and at least 15 others injured.  Media sources said that a colonel and a major were among those killed.  Initial reports indicated 28 soldiers killed. Soldiers, and not Rapid Intervention Unit police officers, who often have served as frontline fighters in Cabo Delgado, were attacked in this incident.

96 COVID cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 03 December. 55 were reported to be in Maputo city, 18 in Cabo Delgado, 14 in Maputo, 6 in Zambezia, two in tete and 1 in Niassa. A total of 15,866 cases were reported since the first infection. COVID-19 death toll in the country is now 132 as there was one new death recorded for the last 24 hours.

The Global Terrorism Index said  that Mozambique saw the second highest increase in the number of deaths from 2018 to 2019 in Sub-Saharan Africa.  Mozambique recorded a total of insurgent-related 319 deaths, in 2019, against 133 registered in 2018, which represents a 140% increase.  Deaths caused in terror related attacks in 2020 will likely vault Mozambique to the top of this list, with hundreds killed in Cabo Delgado this year alone.

A road accident involving a minibus and a truck killed 13 people and injured five others in Inhamizua area of Beira city at around 0450 on 03 December. Injured and deceased victims were taken to Beira Central Hospital. Authorities stated that the cause of the accident was the truck's failure to give priority to the bus as well as poor visibility due to heavy rains.

Unconfirmed reports indicated that around 01 December, a group of Mozambican soldiers was attacked by pro-government militia in an ambush, with both sides mistaking the other for insurgents.  This incident reportedly occurred in Macomia District.  Several sources reported that as many as 119 people were killed in this clash, and that bodies from these clashes had been shipped to Nampula, with dozens more also injured in the incident.

Insurgents last week on an unknown date (estimated as 26 Nov) attacked Ingundi village in Muidumbe District, setting homes on fire.  In attacks on this village and 3 other nearby villages, an unknown number of people were also killed.

Insurgents last week on an unknown date (estimated as 26 Nov) attacked Nanhoka village in Muidumbe District, setting homes on fire.  In attacks on this village and 3 other nearby villages, an unknown number of people were also killed.

Insurgents last week on an unknown date (estimated as 26 Nov) attacked 24 of March village in Muidumbe District, setting homes on fire.  In attacks on this village and 3 other nearby villages, an unknown number of people were also killed.

Insurgents last week on an unknown date (estimated as 26 Nov) attacked Muambula village in Muidumbe District, setting homes on fire.  In attacks on this village and 3 other nearby villages, an unknown number of people were also killed.

Insurgents in the first half of November landed on Matemo Island and raided a hospital on the island, carrying out looting and vandalism of the facility.  Insurgents scrawled "al Shabaab" and "Mujahido" on the walls.  Insurgents were later ambushed by security forces at the hospital, leaving 7 militants dead, while other insurgents were able to flee the attack.

US Ambassador Nathan A Sales in meetings with President Nyusi and other top Mozambican officials from 02-03 December discussed America's commitment to support counter terrorism in Mozambique, including deepening US support for the fight against the insurgency.  The US will also give $42 million to assist humanitarian and socio-economic development projects in Cabo Delgado to assist Mozambique's Agency for Integrated Development in the North.

4 Poachers were brought to the Massinger Health Unit on 03 December after being shot and wounded by South African rangers in Kruger Park.  The group was attempting to poach rhinos in the park.  After receiving medical treatment, the group were arrested by police.  At least one shotgun was also seized from the group.

In a previously unreported incident in October, insurgents in Mocimboa da Praia town went to the house of a local man and forced the man to call three of his relatives to come to his home.  The insurgents then set the man's home on fire and took his brothers into the forest.  Three days later, the dismembered remains of his brothers were found.  The man then fled the MDP town.
Insurgents on an unknown date in October abducted three men in MDP town, took them into a nearby forest, and executed the three.

Elias Dhlakama, RENAMO delegate to the National Assembly and brother of the late RENAMO leader Afonso Dhlakama, this week was reported to have said in the assembly that the war in Cabo Delgado would be led by the country's military, rather than by the police.  Dhlakama also said that the money allocated for defense is not being used in support of the military but rather for the police.  Mozambique's Rapid Intervention Unit police forces often serve as frontline forces in Cabo Delgado.

The Central Office for the Fight Against Corruption this week said that Mozambique had lost about 1.2 billion meticais or $16.4 million due to corruption over the first half of 2020.  This is in contrast to 2019, in which an estimated 500 million meticais were lost during the course of the year - less than half of the amount lost in the first half of 2020.

Sources on 03 December indicated that armored convoys were able to travel between Pemba and Palma via the Montepuez - Mueda - Nangade - Pundanhar route.  Insurgents were last active along this route in the Pundanhar area between 01-03 November, and there is still a significant threat of insurgent attacks in the Pundanhar area of Palma.

Sources on 02 December indicated over recent weeks over 50,000 IDPs have arrived into Montepuez District, fleeing primarily from Muidumbe and Mueda districts.  Many of these IDPs were already displaced in Mueda, and fled the threat of new insurgent attacks in that district.

Local reporting indicates the government's Northern Integrated Development Agency which was set up to provide employment opportunities and in general stimulate development in Cabo Delgado is largely inactive and is not actively participating in supporting the around 500,000 IDPs in the province.  The agency was officially "launched" in late August and is meant to be supported by hundreds of millions of dollars by both the Mozambican government and international donors, but these resources have not yet been mobilized with no clear indication of when this agency will be functional.

Members of the EU Parliament on 03 December called for a "more active and urgent" role for the EU in Mozambique to combat the ongoing humanitarian crisis with over 500,000 people displaced in Cabo Delgado.  MEPs also expressed concerns over challenges the rainy season could pose in addition to the IDP crisis.

The Mozambican National Assembly on 03 December approved the Economic and Social Plan and State Budget for 2021.  FRELIMO assembly members voted for the budget while RENAMO and MDM voted against it.  The budget deficit is estimated to be about 102 billion meticais, or about 9.1% of GDP.  Mozambique also anticipates a GDP growth of about 2.1% during the coming year.

INAM on 04 December predicted strong wins and rain in Southern and Central Mozambique on 04 and 05 December.  This will impact large parts of Tete, Zambezia, Sofala, Inhambane, Gaza, and Maputo Province/Maputo City.

Malawian media reported on 04 December that President Lazarus Chakwera in the SADC Gaborone meeting last week said that the Malawi Defense Force would send troops to Mozambique to help defeat the Cabo Delgado insurgency, and that these troops could be dispatched as early as 15 December.
On 4 December, a ship was reported to have crashed and damaged a dock at the port of Pemba. It was unclear to what extent the damage could potentially disrupt future activity at the port.

Lightning struck a house in Morrumbala, Zambezia, on 3 December, killing a family of 4 people. This occurred amid a storm which also impacted the districts of Mocuba, Ile, Gurue, and some Quelimane City districts. In Mocuba, electricity supply was cut off in multiple neighborhoods due to the storm.

Due to this, the National Directorate of Water Resources Management (DNGRH) warned of worsening urban floods in Dondo and Beira in the next 48 hours. The DNGRH called on citizens to observe precautionary measures.

Personal Envoy of the UN Secretary-General to Mozambique, Mirko Manzoni, announced on 4 December that all combatants in Renamo's military base in Mabote, Inhambane, have completed the demobilization process and will be returning to their communities. As a result, the base has been closed, which is a first base outside Sofala province to be closed down.
On 4 December, Mozambique recorded 120 Coronavirus cases in 24 hours, bringing the total number to 16,038. A Coronavirus related death was also recorded in Maputo.

At least 3 irrigation systems in Mopeia, Zambezia, need USD 200 million to bring their operations to standard. The subpar operations of these irrigation systems have compromised rice production, according to district director of Economic Activities, Gilton José.

Some schools in Quelimane city remain closed due to poor sanitary conditions, press sources reported. This is despite the government disbursement of money to improve hygiene and cleaning conditions in schools throughout Mozambique.  These schools were originally closed down due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

A report prepared by Standard Bank Mozambique indicates that private sector companies in the country have continued to recover from the Coronavirus-related crisis in November. Due to this gradual recovery, companies started to raise workforce numbers last month, which marks as the strongest since February. Businesses also reported increased workloads, shop openings, and marketing efforts. However, efforts to expand inventory levels in businesses were constrained by the lack of purchasing power.

The European Investment Bank will lend a 20-year soft loan of EUR 100 to Mozambique. This loan aims to aid in the repair of drinking water supply systems and water infrastructure in regions affected by strong cyclones last year. The loan was signed in a ceremony in Maputo on 3 December.

According to Cabo Delgado provincial secretary of state Armindo Ngunga on 3 December, The government will not sent any humanitarian aid to people who remain in areas regularly attacked by militants. He added that the government does not want insurgents to steal aid, and that aid will only be sent to locations where people have moved as refugees.  This is expected to cause further displacement of civilians still living in insurgent impacted areas.
Security forces arrested a man in Maputo City on 05 December for stealing MZN 1,000,500 from his father. No other details on this incident are currently available.

Egypt and Qatar expressed their support to the Mozambican government on 03 Dec over humanitarian crisis led by insurgency in Cabo Delgado. President of Egypt Abdel Fattah Al Sisi added that combating terrorism in Africa will require involvement of the international community and Egypt is committed to work with the affected countries.

Security forces recovered a stolen Ford Ranger hidden inside a truck covered with traditional brooms in Mpumalanga, South Africa on the afternoon of 05 Dec. The truck was allegedly bound to Mozambique via Lebombo border post. The driver of the parked vehicle was nowhere to be found.

In addition to 5 Marauder vehicles reported on 24 November to have been purchased from a South African company by the Mozambican military, sources report at least two tanks from South Africa have also been obtained by the Mozambican military for action in Cabo Delgado.  The specifications of these tanks are currently not known.

Health Minister Armindo Tiago announced on 03 December the plans to build 49 new district hospitals which can benefit an estimated total population of 7.62 million people. The project will provide 4,000 new hospital beds and greater access to emergency surgical care.

On 04 December, Mozambican Defence Minister Jaime Neto urged the ministry officials to draw up plans to combat terrorism in Cabo Delgado and against  Renamo Military Junta in Manica and Sofala over the next 12 months. The statement was made during a meeting with the ministry's coordinating council. The Mozambican forces reassured to defend the country in its fight against insurgents.

Pope Francis donated about 100,000 euros (121,000 US dollars) to support the victims from terrorist attacks in the province of Cabo Delgado, sources reported on 06 December. The donation will be allocated for the building of two health posts, one in Chiure, the most populous district of Cabo Delgado, and the other in Montepuez.

95 COVID cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 05 December. 71 were reported to be in Maputo city, 10 in Maputo province, seven in Gaza, four from Inhambane and three from Zambezia. A total of 16,133 cases were reported since the first infection. COVID-19 death toll in the country is now 133 as there was one new death recorded for the last 24 hours.

The alleged second-in-command of the Renamo Military Junta, Joao Machava, defected from the group and joined the demobilization of the Renamo militia at their base in Ribye, Mabote district on 04 December. Machava was the spokesperson for the Junta, and its leader Mariano Nhongo from June 2019, and joined Nhongo in denouncing the leader of Renamo, Ossufo Momade.

111 COVID cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 06 December. A total of 16,244 cases were reported since the first infection. COVID-19 death toll in the country is now 133 as there was no new death recorded for the last 24 hours. 64 cases were from Maputo city, 22 were from Gaza, 9 from Manica, 7 from Zambezia, 5 from Maputo province, two from Nampula, one from Inhambane and one from Cabo Delgado.

14 people were injured in a road accident involving two passenger buses around the National Stadium of Zimpeto, Maputo city on the morning of 07 December. Rescue teams responded immediately at the scene.
column15: National Stadium of Zimpeto, Maputo city

column4: Police Commander Bernardino Rafael on 04 December said during a visit to Quissanga District that residents could return to the area, which had previously been overrun by insurgents.  Other government sources said that Quissanga District has been retaken by government forces and secured from insurgent attacks.  Around 45,000 people fled Quissanga District in March when insurgents captured much of the area.  Many residents returned to the district before renewed insurgent attacks in September and October, though no militant attacks were reported in Quissanga in November.

Malawi's Ministry of Foreign Affairs on 07 December released a statement denying reports that the country would deploy troops to Cabo Delgado, as was reported by Malawian media outlets last week.  The statement said that during a recent SADC Troika Secretariat meeting, Malawi and other countries did not discuss sending troops to Mozambique, though "peace and security matters" in the DRC and Mozambique were discussed, which included a "comprehensive regional response".  The statement then reiterates that no members of the SADC committed to send troops to Mozambique and this option "is yet to be considered".

The SADC's Parliamentary Forum held on 04-05 December passed a motion condemning terror attacks in Mozambique while some MPs called for "immediate collective action by the SADC in line with the SADC Mutual Defense Pact".

Unconfirmed reports have indicated that the Mozambican military has obtained at least 5 military helicopters ( Mil Mi-24 and Mil Mi-8s) from South Africa, or a South African company, and that these aircraft had been seen in Nacala, being outfitted for combat operations in Cabo Delgado.  This came after confirmed reports in recent weeks that the Mozambican military had obtained several armored personnel carriers (APCs) of superior quality to Chinese made vehicles the military had previously utilized in Cabo Delgado.

Sources have indicated that Mozambican military units positioned in Ibo District have recently intercepted vessels travelling towards Pemba and seized goods from these vessels unlawfully.  Security forces are deployed in this area to protect Ibo Island and other nearby islands from militant attacks, and to prevent insurgents from infiltrating Pemba via sea lanes.

The UN estimates that humanitarian organizations will require $254.4 million to assist 1.1 million people in need of humanitarian assistance in Cabo Delgado and neighboring provinces who are either displaced or in need of assistance due to the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  Note that just $35.5 million as judged to be needed for this same task in May of 2020.

Journalist Ibrimo Mbaruco as of 07 December has been missing for 8 months in Cabo Delgado.  Mbaruco worked at a local radio station in Palma town, and last was heard from when he told a colleague in an SMS that he was surrounded by security force members.  Authorities meanwhile on multiple occasions have denied  detaining Mbaruco and say they are investigating the case.

A group of at least 30 insurgents on the afternoon of 07 December attacked the village of Mute, Palma District, setting fire to several huts in the raid. One source said the attack began at 1600hrs, and that militants infiltrated the village mingling with the population before launching the attack. Insurgents occupied the village overnight, and fires were reported in the village in the early hours of 08 December as well.  This village is located about 27 kms south of Palma town, and lies just north of the Olumbe crossroads.

Electricidade de Mozambique dismantled a network at a public health center in Cariaco, Pemba on 07 December which had been illegally using electricity.   The illegal consumption generated a loss worth 2 million meticais according to EDM Director of Cabo Delgado, Gildo Marques. He added that an inspection will be launched in almost all public institutions to check each electricity networks and usage.

At least six boats carrying 320 internally displaced people from insurgency impacted areas were reported on 07 December to have arrived in arrived in Pemba.  Captains of the ships bringing the refugees to Pemba reportedly lied to authorities saying that the passengers were not IDPs.

The Mozambique Government repatriated 89 people over illegal immigration and illegal stays in the country,  media reported on 07 Dec.  The group included 58 Ethiopians, 12 Malawians, five Ghanaians, four Somalis, four Zimbabweans, three Bengalis, three Tanzanians and three Nigerians who were detained in different operations in Niassa, Nampula, and Maputo City.

Security forces arrested a woman, her husband and brother-in-law in Chamanculo, Maputo City on 30 Nov over alleged consumption and selling of prohibited drugs such as cannabis sativa. A 10,000 meticais worth of cannabis sativa was recovered from the suspects.

Annual meetings will resume between the governors Cabo Delgado and Niassa in Mozambique, and those of Mtwara, and Songueia of Tanzania, authorities announced on 04 Dec. This regular meeting, which was suspended for four years, will assess border concerns as well as reinforce cooperation in the social, economic and political areas.  The resumption of these meetings, which last took place in December of 2016, is likely a result of a recent Mozambique - Tanzania agreement to coordinate security responses along their common border as Mozambique continues to grapple with the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

The Portuguese parliament will discuss support for Mozambique and insurgent attacks in Cabo Delgado on 09 December, media sources reported on 04 December. Two of the three parties that submitted the request will be heard during the hearing in the parliament.  The Aga Khan Development Network will also address the Portuguese parliament on the situation in Cabo Delgado.

Portugal's Defense Minister, Joao Gomes Cravinho, will meet with his counterpart Jaime Bessa Neto, in Maputo city from 09 December until 11 December. The meeting will address the Cooperation in the Field of Defense (CDD) between the two countries as well as Portuguese Presidency of the Council of the European Union (PPUE) on January 2021.

Insurgents on 08 December reportedly retreated from the Nkonga village area after clashing with pro-government militia fighters.  Insurgents had earlier raided Nkonga before the arrival of local militia. Insurgents after this attack moved towards Lijungo village.  No information on casualties is currently available.

An insurgent attack on Nkonga Village, Nangade District, was reported in the early hours of 08 December by a group of at least 30 insurgents.  Insurgents reportedly set fire to homes in the village; another insurgent attack in the Pundanhar area of Palma was later also reported.  Sources later said insurgents two weeks before had left threatening messages in the area warning of an attack after local residents reportedly found a motorcycle that had been in the possession of insurgents. in the nearby forest that was brought into the village.  Insurgents fired gunshots in this attack and local resident fled the area.
Journalist Omar Rajua of Carta de Mozambique was reported on 08 December to be receiving threats on Facebook by pro-government accounts labelling him a "terrorist".

An illegal toll facility has been operating and charging 250 meticais per trip for each vehicle along a road in Moamba, Maputo, a source disclosed on 06 December. The toll fees were collected for the Association of Transporters of Inerts and Areeiros da Moamba which led to conflicts on other associations. Fees were supposed to be allocated for road repairs, though no repairs have ever been undertaken.

Tanzanian police arrested a suspected recruiter for the Cabo Delgado insurgents in recent days. The suspect was arrested last week after crossing the border of Lago district of Niassa province into Tanzania with a group of 15 people reportedly travelling to join the Cabo Delgado insurgents. A source suggest that the suspect was a trader in an undisclosed district of the province.

The business manager of deceased businessman, Aly Majolela, has gone missing in Niassa province, a source reported on 08 December. It was not determined if the manager was abducted or recruited by insurgents. Businessman Majolela was murdered with his wife last August in Majune district.

82 COVID cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 06 December. 29 were reported to be in Maputo city, 33 in Maputo province, 14 in Zambezia, four in Gaza, one each for Niassa and Manica. A total of 16,326 cases were reported since the first infection. COVID-19 death toll in the country is now 136 as there were three new deaths recorded for the last 24 hours.

Insurgents on the afternoon of 08 December were reported to have ambushed a convoy of four vehicles travelling between Nangade and Palma near Mandimba in Nangade, just west of Pundanhar.  The vehicles were stopped, passengers were robbed of their belongings, and the 4 vehicles set on fire.  At least one person was killed and three injured in these attacks.  Note some sources reported only two vehicles were attacked in this incident, and said passengers fled the vehicles after observing "strange activity" in the area, and returning to the vehicles, found they had been destroyed.
Hundreds of IDPs fled the Mute village area and from nearby villages on 07-08 December after insurgents attacked Mute.  At least 400 civilians reportedly fled into the bush and towards Palma town.

Insurgents clashed with security forces in Mute village area, driving troops from the village on 07 December.  At least 3 soldiers were injured in these clashes.  Sources later reported one soldier killed in the clashes; security forces also claimed insurgents utilized mortars and rocket-propelled grenades in these clashes though this is unconfirmed.

Troops from Palma, supported by South African Military Contractor attack helicopters, attacked insurgent positions on 08 December in the Mute area.  No information on casualties is currently available.

Insurgents on 08 December attacked Ngueo village, just 2kms north of Mute village, in the early morning hours.  Homes in the village were reportedly set on fire; no information on casualties is currently available.  Insurgents the previous day attacked and occupied Mute village.

The Office for Combating Corruption announced that 108 corruption cases were being investigated in Maputo province. Various security and management units were conducting the investigations. Around 2 million meticais were embezzled in these cases.
A vessel with 6 naval interceptors can be seen in satellite imagers of waters just off Pemba port.  This vessel has reportedly been present in the area since July of 2017.

Company officials announced on 5 December that 700 employees fear the loss of work due to the kidnapping of business owner Ismail Harun. Harun was kidnapped on 14 November.  Officials stated that the employees were not paid November salaries as finances were suspended as they required the signature of the kidnapped businessman.  No updates on Harun's case meanwhile are currently available.

Local media stated that vehicles stolen in South Africa are regularly smuggled into Mozambique and then to Sango Border Crossing in Gaza Province and then into Zimbabwe. This porous border post has increasingly become a major smuggling point for vehicles, clothing, drugs, and illicit alcohol into Zimbabwe from Mozambique.

A new Malawian media outlet said that despite Malawian government denials that Malawi had offered to deploy troops into Cabo Delgado, this offer was indeed discussed at the recent SADC summit.  This offer was however then "stopped as unlawful" as the Mozambican government did not consent to the deployment.  This report is unconfirmed.

Around 100 new Navy recruits graduated after completing their training in the port of Pemba City on 7 December. The new soldiers would be deployed in the coastal areas of the province to counter the ongoing insurgency.

Defence Minister Jaime Neto announced on 6 December that Mozambique’s borders are porous which have allowed the smuggling of illegal weapons to the country. Neto stated that the smuggling of weapons has allowed violence and destruction in communities, feeding the insurgency in Cabo Delgado in particular.  The Mozambican-Tanzanian border is where the majority of these weapons have been smuggled through.
Security forces arrested seven suspects for selling poached animal goods in Muanza District, Sofala Province over the weekend.  The suspects were selling two elephant tusks and leopard skin.
A train derailed due to weakened train tracks caused by heavy rainfall in Doa area of Sofala Province on 7 December. No casualties were reported.

US Coordinator for Counterterrorism Nathan Sales stated that the US intends to be a “preferred partner” of Mozambique to fight against Cabo Delgado insurgents in a statement on 08 December.  Sales said the US was working on an agreement with Mozambique on boosting counter-insurgency capabilities and clarified that no US troops would be provided.  No deadline for this agreement has been set.  The diplomat went on to say that the US wants to help Mozambique secure its borders as part of the effort to defeat the insurgency.  Sales also said that the US viewed militants in Cabo Delgado as "insurgents aligning themselves with the Islamic State".
Officials are transferring IDPs from Pemba to several “resettlement villages” which included villages in Ancuabe district. The IDPs were given shelter kits, housing land plots, and farming land.

The National Health Institute conducted surveys of the COVID exposure rate in two cities of Gaza Province. The total population of Xai-Xai and Chokwe were 132,884 and 67,954. Xai-Xai city had a 3.7 percent exposure rate which is equivalent to 4917 individuals being exposed to the virus, while Chowke had a 5.2 percent exposure rate comparable to 3533 locals being exposed to the virus. The total sample size used in Xai-xai was 6,270, and in Chokwe it was 3,412.

Mozambique police commander Bernadino Rafael stated that insurgents are “dying everyday” in Cabo Delgado, partially because according to Rafael security forces had cut off insurgent supply lines.  Rafael stated that without the security forces efforts, insurgents would have reached other provinces and expanded their territory.  Rafael also said that it was unclear how many insurgents were present in the province, though they were known to be continuing recruitment efforts.  He said some insurgents do defect from the group and return to their communities.  Rafael also said that insurgents do not use the port or airport of Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) "because we are there", also saying security forces are in full control of the coasts of Cabo Delgado.  Rafael also said that many IDPs fleeing insurgent impacted zones were women and children, and that security forces were trying to "find out from the wives where their husbands are".  Insurgents have controlled MDP and parts of the coast for several months - despite Rafael's claims.

Secretary of State Armindo Ngunga stated on 8 December that 75% of the population of Pemba are now IDPs and have congested initial reception centers. New relocation centers were opened in Metuge, Chiure, Acuabe, and Montepuez in attempts to ease the overcrowding in Pemba. The government is attempting to move IDPs out of Pemba to other "new villages" it is attempting to establish in more secure areas in the south of the province.

The Portuguese Defense Minister arrived in Maputo as part of the three-day visit. Gomes Cravinho conducted a meeting with Mozambican Defense Minister Jaime Neto. The meeting will discuss the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

Police stated that gunmen shot and killed a Somali trader and injured another trader while the two merchants were attempting to buy corn in the Sanga area of Niassa around 06 December.  The two were reportedly attacked by youths for unknown reasons after the traders contracted the youths about purchasing corn.  The suspects threw the bodies at a nearby stream and escaped.

A group of 8 insurgents conducted a 15-minute attack and stole from commercial establishments in Chai Village along the N380 road in Macomia District at the dawn of 9 December. The insurgents reportedly stole the food items from shops in the town, and fired several shots to frighten away village residents, who fled into the nearby bush.  No casualties were reported and insurgents reportedly told locals they were only attempting to resupply themselves.  Insurgents retreated towards Miangalewa.

Large numbers of contractors working at the LNG site in Palma on Tuesday and Wednesday were advised to remain at home after insurgents on 07-08 December attacked the villages of Mute and Ngueo in Southern Palma District.  Only a small number of buses transporting workers from Palma to Afungi were reported to be operating on Tuesday-Wednesday, with military escorts.  Other operations and meetings at the LNG Project sites were reported to have ben postponed due to the attacks.

A suspected insurgent attack was reported in the early morning hours of 09 December on the village of M'Tamba/Mandimba in Nangade District, with several homes in the village set on fire by militants.  No further details on this attack are currently available.

Security force members on 04 December were reported to have opened fire on a civilian vehicle in the Muambula area of Muidumbe District after the vehicle's driver refused to provide details regarding the value of goods being carried in the vehicle.  The soldiers then reportedly demanded money, before firing on the vehicle and injuring the driver.  The driver was able to drive to Miteda, where he lost consciousness.  At Miteda, other passengers of the vehicle said they were again harassed by security force members who demanded to know the value of the vehicle's cargo.

The OFAC-sanctioned Iran cargo ship GOLSAN made a U-turn at 130 nautical miles away from Palma coast and resumed travel towards Mozambique at around s of 13:07 on 7 December. No details were mentioned for the route diversion.  The vessel was on course to potentially enter waters in which Cabo Delgado insurgents have been active in recent months.  The vessel's ultimate destination was Venezuela.

Defence Minister Jaime Neto restated his request for international support against insurgency in Cabo Delgado to the Portuguese Defense Minister Cravinho.  This request, specifically for training and other indirect support to the Mozambican government and security forces, was previously made to the EU as well. The call for the request comes as a meeting between Defense Ministers was conducted during Cravinho’s three-day visit in Mozambique.
Port security arrested several Iranian nationals suspected to be involved in accident that damaged port facilities in Pemba recently.  The suspects were set to be on trial on 11 December.

The Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP) is considering providein1g humanitarian aid to Mozambique due to the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado. CPLP also said that its support does not exclude possible military support.

Mozambican Prime Minister Carlos Agostinho do Rosario stated that IDPs in Cabo Delgado have increased by 20 percent since the end of October, bringing the total number of IDPs to 560,000 currently.  There are also estimated to be around 10,000 people displaced by RENAMO dissident attacks in Central Mozambique.

Insurgents reportedly blocked the road in the Mandimba area before conducting attacks on vehicles in the area on 8 December. Traffic congestion was reported in the area, forcing several drivers to leave their vehicles and flee. The road closure and traffic have disrupted travel towards Palma through the route via Pundanhar.

Police arrested two suspects for extortion charges in Manica on 9 December. The suspects extorted around 50,000 to 100,000 meticais from a civilian by faking a kidnapping. Another suspect was later arrested for providing details of the victim to the suspects.

2 COVID related deaths and 67 new cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 9 December. 48 new cases were reported in Maputo, 8 in Niassa, 5 in Maputo, 3 in Nampula, and 3 in Zambezia. The fatalities were recorded in Maputo City.  There have now been 16,440 cases in the country with 138 deaths.
The Ministry of Health announced 47 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 8 December. 33 were recorded in Maputo City, 10 in Sofala, 3 in Maputo, and one in Cabo Delgado.

Flash floods were reported in Sofala province after a 10-hour heavy rainfall on 3 December. The flooding reportedly closed off roads. A civilian was killed during this flooding incident. Two civilians were missing after their boat was wrecked along the coast of Beira

Flash floods were reported in Sofala province after a 10-hour heavy rainfall on 3 December. The flooding reportedly closed off roads. A civilian was killed during the incident. Two civilians were missing after their boat was wrecked along the coast of Beira

The Mozambican government has never directly asked military support to assist in fighting the insurgency in Cabo Delgado, Council of Ministers spokesman Filimao Suazi said on 09 December.  Suazi said Mozambique  has asked for support from its international partners to support the Maputo government in the fight against Cabo Delgado.

Police announced on 10 December the arrest of two armed robbers during an operation in Montepuez.  The two had reportedly targeted foreign nationals in robbery incidents in the area. The robbers were in possession of two pistols, a Kalashnikov, two license plates and several ammunition.

All Mozambican police have had leave suspended during the holiday season in order to "guarantee public order" during this time. All police officers were summoned for the outlined security plan during Christmas and New Years.

Local officials have recently begun assembling solar panels to provide an alternative source of electricity in Mueda and Nangade. Large parts of Cabo Delgado province lacked electrical supply since August due to insurgent attacks on the Awasse substation. The solar panels were to power the local health center, district buildings, police stations, and educational facilities.

Large parts of Cabo Delgado province lacked electrical supply since August due to insurgent attacks on the Awasse substation. The solar panels were to power the local health center, district buildings, police stations, and educational facilities.

The Cuban government called for investigation into funding for the insurgency in Cabo Delgado on 9 December. Ambassador of Cuba to Mozambique Pavel Diaz Hernandez stated shutting down the finances of the insurgents would assist in reducing the issue in the province. Hernandez also mentioned that international support coming from neighboring countries would assist greatly against the insurgency.

Security forces detained three individuals in Nangade district since the past two weeks. The detainees were suspected to have links with insurgents, though at least one of the three detained suspects was released in unclear circumstances.
Security forces detained a young man in Xinavane area, Macomia district in the recent weeks. This comes as security forces detained individuals suspected to be involved with insurgents.
Two people were detained for suspected links with insurgents by security forces in Changane, west Macomia on 27 November.
Security forces arrested a man accused of speaking on phone with insurgents in Monjane village of Afungi district on 7 December.

Spain announced that they are prepared to support Mozambique in its fight against insurgency in Cabo Delgado on 9 December. Spanish ambassador Alberto Cerezo stated they are waiting for the Mozambican government as to what support they require.

Council of Ministers Spokesman Swazi stated that 33 individuals have been killed during the 2020/2021 rainy season in Mozambique. Swazi said that the government is currently assisting around 23,827 people, 5,281 affected families, and 36 wounded.

Mozambique Minister of Health stated that COVID vaccinations campaign would likely be conducted in the country in mid-2021. The Minister of Health said that prequalification for the campaign will be conducted by the WHO based on the global Covax initiative, which offers equitable access to vaccines in low and middle income countries.

Sources this week reported the Mozambican government agreed to a new deal with a South African defense contractor.  The company initially provided five Marauder security vehicles, with another seven currently being delivered. Four Gazelle-type helicopters are also set to be delivered on February of 2021. The company will also provide training for 15 Mozambican combat pilots, provided by former South African Defense Force members.

A South African private military contracting company renewed their contract in assisting the Mozambican government to provide air support in Cabo Delgado recently, several sources reported.  The support was also to assist the Mozambican military, which they have been doing since April 2020 with attack helicopters providing air support to Mozambican military forces primarily.

The Association of War Veterans called on the government to provide better support for pro-gov militias in Cabo Delgado, saying militias of war veterans are currently active in Nangade, Macomia, Palma, Mocimboa da Praia, and Muidumbe districts.

Sources stated that insurgents are still present in Nchinga area of Muidumbe District as of 10 December. This comes as insurgents have been predominantly active in the district during November.  Note that one other source denied this claim.
Locals sources reported that insurgents beheaded a civilian in Muambula village, Muidumbe District, on 6 December.

IDPs in Ngalane, Metuge called for Prime Minister Carlos Agostinho on 9 December to provide weapons and arm locals against insurgents operating in the province. Agostinho rejected the idea of arming locals though stated that all Mozambicans are part of the fight against terrorism. The request comes after locals stated that they were tired of recurring insurgent attacks without adequate security response.

IDPs in Nanjua, Ancuabe called for Prime Minister Carlos Agostinho on 9 December to provide weapons and arm locals against insurgents operating in the province. Agostinho rejected the idea of arming locals though stated that all Mozambicans are part of the fight against terrorism. The request comes after locals stated that they were tired of recurring insurgent attacks without adequate security response.

A major oil company stated that it was closely monitoring security situation in Cabo Delgado after reports of an attack near an oil project. Transportation between Palma town and the LNG projects on the Afungi Peninsula was limited this week due to these attacks and some operations at the LNG sites temporarily suspended.  The attack was conducted in Mute less that 25km from the natural gas processing industrial zone in Area 1 of the Rovuma basin.

SERNIC agents are reportedly undergoing counter-terrorism training to deal with the terrorism related matters in Cabo Delgado. The training was to help SERNIC agents understand how the insurgents operate in the province and to improve intelligence services in Cabo Delgado.

Police arrested 3 civil servants on charges of falsifying documents in Beira. The suspects previously issued 538 forged employment certificates to foreigners over the past two years, and had been issuing these false certificates for at least 3 years.

The Ministry of Health announced that 1 COVID death and 81 new cases were recorded in Mozambique on 10 December. The death was recorded in Inhambane province.  There have now been a total of 16,208 cases throughout the country.

A buildup of  trucks  was reported in Nangade after attacks in the Pundanhar area earlier this week cut the Palma-Nangade road.  A small number of trucks on 10 December reportedly attempted to drive from Nangade to Palma, though it was unclear if they were able to make it through.
Security forces detained a suspect for rape charges in Nampula on 07 December. The suspect was involved in sexually assaulting two children.

Insurgents on 10 December were reported to still be present near Mandimba and Pundanhar, two days after insurgents attacked, looted, and set on fire vehicles travelling through the area and cutting off traffic at least temporarily to Palma.  It is unclear if militants actually are actively blocking the road, though local sources indicated insurgents were still within proximity of the mostly abandoned village of Pundanhar.
Sources also reported that insurgents conducted a new attack on Nkonga village in Nangade District on 10 December though no further details on this attack are currently available.

A group at least 20 Insurgents on motorcycles on 10 December conducted a new attack on Machava village, about 30 kms from Nangade town.  Militants reportedly carried out looting in the village and residents fled from the area.  Rumors that this group was coming to attack Nangade town itself spread fear in the town though no such attack materialized.

Rumors that a group of militants were coming to attack Nangade town on 10 December spread fear in the town though no such attack materialized.  Rumors spread after an insurgent attack in a village about 30kms from Nangade.

In waters just off Mucojo meanwhile, a group of 6 insurgents were reported on Thursday to have briefly abducted several fishermen.  The fishermen were later released, though their catches and fishing equipment were stolen by the militants.

Insurgents on 11 December were reported to have attacked Litingina town on Friday afternoon/early evening, killing 1 person and setting fire to two vehicles.  There had been concern in the town the day before regarding a potential militant attack after insurgents raided Machava village, east of Litingina.  A group of around 20 insurgents was responsible for the attack, mounted on 6 motorcycles.  During the course of the insurgency, the town has been attacked several times by militants though had not been targeted in recent months.  Litingina is located about 14 kms south of Nangade town, the capital of the district.  Sources later indicated at least 14 people were killed in attacks on Litingina and other nearby villages.

Mozambique's parliament on 11 December was reported to have approved an extension for pre-trial detentions to 12 months.  This was reportedly done in order to be able to keep several "Hidden Debt" suspects in custody without trial, though could be used to extend other detentions without trial.

Local media reported on 11 December that Quissanga District residents who fled the area after insurgent attacks fear returning to the district despite recent statements from Mozambican Police Commander Bernardino Rafael saying the district was safe.  IDPs from Quissanga in Metuge IDP camps say they have received no official information about a return to the district.  More than 40,000 people during the course of the year have fled the district, representing as much as 75% of its population.  No recent insurgent attacks have been reported in Quissanga though insurgents remain active just north in Macomia District.
Insurgents reportedly remain active in the Darumba area of Macomia District.  No attacks have been reported in this village recently though insurgents did attack the village of Chai on 09 December.
Insurgents were reported on 06 December to be active in Mucojo AP of Macomia District.

RENAMO Dissident Leader Mariano Nhongo on 11 December claimed that security forces had abducted two of his sons, three grandchildren, and a daughter in law in Inchope AP in Gondola District in Manica.  Security forces denied any reports regarding such a kidnapping.  Note that Nhongo has threatened targeted attacks in the past after accusing the security forces of targeting his family.

Portugal's Defense Minister said on 09 December that Portugal would in January 2021 dispatch a team of Portuguese military personnel to design with Mozambican military officials a logistical organization and military training program that will be provided by the Portuguese military to their Mozambican counterparts.  The training will be carried out in Mozambique and will involve "rapid intervention forces, special forces, marines and military personnel in the area of ​​tactical air control".  Special areas of interest to be covered are cyber defense, cartography, hydrography, and industrial defense cooperation.

Government sources on 10 December said that Mozambican troops had retaken the village of Mute from insurgents who took over the village on 07 December.  Clashes had been reported in the area again on 08 December as government troops supported by South African military contractor attack helicopters launched a counteroffensive in the area.  No information on casualties is currently available.

Portuguese Foreign Minister Augusto Santos Silva on Friday a possible UN intervention against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. Silva said currently Mozambique is pursuing bilateral cooperation with Portugal and the EU though a UN intervention could also be a possibility though would likely take longer to materialize.
Local sources stated on 11 December that four bodies of soldiers killed in Cabo Delgado were transported back to Tete.  It was unclear what incident the 4 had been killed in.

Khindlimuka Association stated that Mozambique is the fourth country affected by HIV and lack of funds is hampering the fight against the virus in Mozambique.  Khindlimuka stated that before their funding was decreased, the association had around 10 projects in minimizing HIV in the country. In response, MPs have called for increase funding to fight in Mozambique.

The World Bank approved a 100 million USD grant to Maputo Urban Transformation as part of the International Development Association. The grant was to finance critical urban infrastructure investments and support the implementation of municipal improvements.

The trial of the former Maputo mayor David Simango was delayed upon the request of his lawyer. Simango was scheduled to be tried on 11 December. Simango was charged with abuse of office and power during his term.

Security forces detained a suspected insurgent during a vehicle search in Mueda. The detainee was in possession of several bladed weapons, firearms, and a military uniform. The driver of the vehicle was later release upon investigation.

Mozambique Police conducted a meeting outlining the security plan during the holiday season in the country. The meeting was also attended by the National Migration Service, National Ground Transportation, and National Tax and Customs Authority. Police officials announced intended security checkpoints, vehicle searches, inspections on travelers, enforcement of COVID precautions, and COVID certificates across the country.

Police arrested a woman on the night of 11 December who was carrying 3 dismantled AKM assault rifles in a basket.  She confessed that the rifles belonged to her son and his friends and that they would be coming to her home that night.  Plain clothes police deployed to the area and on the morning of 12 December arrested the 5 suspected insurgents who were also in possession of ammunition and cash.  The woman also remains in police custody.

On the early morning of 12 December, 5 suspected militants were arrested by police in Pemba in the Bairo de Alto Gingone area near the Pemba airport.  The arrest occurred after police arrested a woman on the night of 11 December who was carrying 3 dismantled AKM assault rifles in a basket.  She confessed that the rifles belonged to her son and his friends and that they would be coming to her home that night.  Plain clothes police deployed to the area, capturing 5 militants, who were also in possession of ammunition and cash.  The woman also remains in police custody.
A source reported on 12 Dec that some entrepreneurs in Beira city are using the services of private armed guards in fear of being kidnapped. No other details on this incident are currently available.

Security force deployments were reported on 12 December in areas of Nangade after insurgent attacks targeted several villages in the district.  No clashes however were reported between the military and insurgents.

Insurgents on 13 December attacked Samora Machel village, south of Nangade in the early morning hours.  Sources later indicated as manhyh as 276 homes in the village were set on fire by insurgents in this attack.

Insurgents on 13 December attacked Namuembe Chini village, south of Nangade in the early morning hours.  No information on casualties were reported.   The nearby village of Samora Machel was also attacked.

Insurgents on the evening of 11 December attacked Chianga village, setting fire to several homes.  In this attack and attacks on several other nearby villages, 14 people were killed and several vehicles also set on fire.  Insurgents were armed with firearms and machetes in this attack.

Insurgents on the evening of 11 December attacked Namiune village, setting fire to several homes.  In this attack and attacks on several other nearby villages, 14 people were killed and several vehicles also set on fire.  Insurgents were armed with firearms and machetes in this attack.

Insurgents on the evening of 11 December attacked Naleke village, setting fire to several homes.  In this attack and attacks on several other nearby villages, 14 people were killed and several vehicles also set on fire.  Insurgents were armed with firearms and machetes in this attack.

Insurgents on the evening of 11 December attacked Lucuamba village, setting fire to several homes.  In this attack and attacks on several other nearby villages, 14 people were killed and several vehicles also set on fire.  Insurgents were armed with firearms and machetes in this attack.

Insurgents on the evening of 11 December attacked Chicuaia-Nova village, setting fire to several homes.  In this attack and attacks on several other nearby villages, 14 people were killed and several vehicles also set on fire.  Insurgents were armed with firearms and machetes in this attack.

Insurgents on the evening of 11 December attacked 25 de Setembro village, setting fire to several homes.  In this attack and attacks on several other nearby villages, 14 people were killed and several vehicles also set on fire.  Insurgents were armed with firearms and machetes in this attack.

Zimbabwean media reported that the country's military was to deploy soldiers to combat insurgency in Mozambique, according to a 13 December report.  A Zimbabwean Defense official reportedly said that "we are most likely to intervene in the war", and said that Harare was concerned other SADC countries were unwilling to send troops to Mozambique.  This intervention will reportedly occur "with the framework of the SADC Brigade" which has been operated in the DRC.  Note that there is no current indication that Mozambique has yet requested the SADC's direct intervention.

Heavy rainfall and strong wind damaged in six resettlement sites which houses 500 families across Buzi and Chibavava districts of Sofala province from 25 – 28 November, a source stated on 14 December. A total of two upgraded shelters, 102 emergency shelters, and 45 tents were completely destroyed.

One COVID related death and 132 new cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 12 December. 67 cases were from Maputo city and 10 from Maputo province. There were also 16 cases from Niassa, 15 from Cabo Delgado, 11 from Zambezia, six from Sofala, three from Gaza, two from Nampula, one from Tete and one from Inhambane.  There have now been 16,812 cases in the country with 140 deaths.

Three COVID related deaths and 142 new cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 13 December. 82 cases out of 142 new cases were from Maputo city.  There have now been 16,954 cases in the country with 142 deaths.

President Mnangagwa arrived in Maputo on 14 Dec to discuss the Islamist insurgency in Mozambique. He will join other SADC leaders, Botswana, South Africa and Tanzania, for a new meeting of the SADC Troika, a continuation of the Gaborone 27 November summit.

On 14 Dec, Mozambican government announced that they will launch a new electronic system called Sistema Electronico de Selagem e Rastreio de Carga em Transito SEERC next week. The new system will aid in eliminating the smuggling and embezzlement of goods. During the first phase of the launch, the system will operate in the three main national freight transit corridors, Maputo Corridor, Beira Corridor and Nacala Corridor.

The UNHCR indicated on 14 December that over 424,000 people have fled insurgent attacks in Cabo Delgado.  Mozambican authorities meanwhile indicate that over 570,000 have fled the insurgency into different parts of Cabo Delgado, Niassa, and Nampula.
Road travel between Mueda and Nangade was reported on 11 December to have ceased after several insurgent attacks were reported between the two towns.

A new insurgent attack was reported in Chai village along the N380 road on 11 December, resulting in at least four people killed.  Insurgents also carried out looting and set several homes on fire; local residents fled south to Macomia town.  Sources later indicated that at least 12 people were killed in this attack or in the hours after it when several residents who had fled into nearby bush areas were tracked down by insurgents and beheaded.

Several sources reported that Suffering Matequenha, a former RENAMO deputy, was taken away from his home by a group of 10 men in police uniforms on the night of 13 December in Nhamaonha, Chimoio.  The men reportedly rammed the gate of his compound and jumped over walls into his property, ordered him to come with them, blindfolded him, and took him away to a "black vehicle with tinted windows" according to his wife.  The group reportedly would not answer questions from Matequenha's wife, who demanded the group identify themselves.  Authorities in Manica meanwhile deny that they have detained Matequenha and said his family should file a complaint with the police over the incident.
The SADC will hold an extraordinary summit in January to discuss the security situation in Cabo Delgado.  This announcement came after the SADC Troika held a meeting in Maputo on 14 December.

The SADC agreed to hold a secondary SADC summit in South Africa to discuss the regional strategy in distributing the COVID-19 vaccines. No specific date has been set for the COVID vaccine distribution summit.

An SADC meeting held in Maputo on 14 December reportedly discussed the regional economic cooperation which included the renewal of the Mozambican railway operation along the ports of Nacala, Beira and Maputo. The meeting also included the infrastructure project to build a deep-water mineral port in Techobanine.

Border officials briefly closed down Ressano Garcia Border Crossing  around 07:00 after an employee tested positive for COVID and reopened the crossing at around 10:00 on the morning of 14 December. The temporary closure caused traffic congestion to travelers passing through the border.

Border officials briefly closed down Ressano Garcia Border Crossing  around 07:00 after an employee tested positive for COVID and reopened the crossing at around 10:00 on the morning of 14 December. The temporary closure caused traffic congestion to travelers passing through the border.

The Assembly of the Republic revised the Penal Procedure Code and adjusted the pre-trial detention to a minimum of 4 months which can be extended up to 16 months. The extension is based on the case if it is related to terrorism, violence, organized crime, or complex criminal cases.

The Tax Authority announced that In-Transit Electronic Sealing and Cargo Tracking System (SEERC) will be launched to stop goods from being criminally diverted in transit to domestic market. The Tax Authority stated that around 67 million meticais of goods are being stolen while in transit, this also includes theft, smuggling, and black-market sales. The SEERC will ensure tracking of all cargo in transit and provides electronic sealing of goods to prevent theft.

Zimbabwe President’s Spokesman George Charamba stated that SADC "is fast moving towards a subregional response against Islamic insurgency", saying that Zimbabwe would contribute troops and equipment to the SADC brigade once the SADC sanctions intervention in Mozambique.  Zimbabwean officials have been arguably the most hawkish regarding a potential intervention in Mozambique.

Police Deputy Commander Bernardo has ordered policemen to reduce roadblocks during the holiday season. The reduction of roadblocks was to prevent any inconvenience to long-distance travelers. Bernardo stated that an operation “Prevent COVID-19” was conducted to coordinate with locals during the holiday season and minimize future COVID cases.
Government officials was reported to have revoked the press credentials of a journalist on 09 December after he recently covered incidents related to insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) arrested four suspects for hijacking a truck and stole 3 million meticais worth of products being transported to a warehouse in Matola on 12 December. The suspects also attempted to sell the vehicle for 1.5 million meticais.

The Municipal Council of Nampula collected just 82% of expected revenues during the months of October and November. A total of 98,395,110 meticais out of the planned 119,825,326 meticais. The low revenue was due to the lack of donations from local NGOs and unimplemented projects for 2020.

More than 140,000 IDPs were reported to be “stranded” in areas of Cabo Delgado according to the International Organization of Migration. IOM stated that most IDPs are located along the coastal districts of the province. Obstacles like access to transportation and finance are common issues for the IDPs to be unable to travel away from the province.
Locals sources stated that several soldiers were reported to be intoxicated during their shift outside a church in Pemba on 11 December.

Pemba Mayor Florete Simba stated IDPs are putting pressure on water, health centers, sanitation, and other services in Pemba. Over 130,000 IDPs are believed to be present in and around the city after being driven out of insurgent impacted areas.

Sources indicate in Pemba that police receiving incoming IDPs often "receive money" before allowing IDPs to go free.  Police also reportedly track all IDPs arriving into the city and conduct searches of all arriving IDPs attempting to discover potentially concealed terrorists.

Pemba Mayor Florete Simba warned that Pemba has recently seen a surge in criminality, particularly in small scale thefts, after recent large increases of IDPs in the city.  The local government has created a security committee to attempt to confront this new crime surge.

The Assembly of the Republic approved on 13 December to amend the Penal Code on the crime against human freedom which now included human trafficking. The current part of the article on the crime determines that the victim's consent does not exclude or mitigate the criminal liability of the agents.

The Ministry of Health announced the 1 new COVID related death and 48 new cases in Mozambique on 14 December. A total of 16,689 cases and 143 deaths were reported around the country.  47 of the new cases are Mozambican nationals.

Security forces arrested three driver and 46 illegal Ethiopian immigrants who were inside three long-haul trucks in Tete province near the border of Malawi on 15 December. 1 million MWK were seized from the immigrants.

Security forces arrested three driver and 46 illegal Ethiopian immigrants who were inside three long-haul trucks in Tete province near the border of Malawi on 15 December. 1 million MWK were seized from the immigrants.  Three trucks and containers, along with some Malawian currency was also seized.

Helicopters likely piloted by South African military contractors was reported to have conducted patrols over parts of Quissanga, Ibo, Macomia, and Palma in recent days, tasked with destroying "any sailing vessel" found along the coasts of these districts.  This directive was meant to target insurgents using vessels to conduct attacks on islands and other vessels sailing just off the Cabo Delgado coast.  An unspecified number of small sailing vessels seized by insurgents have reportedly been destroyed in these sorties.

Pro-government militia in early December based out of Litingina were reported to have launched an operation in forests near the village, reportedly killing and dismembering at least one insurgent.  Body parts of the insurgent were later brought back into the village.  This incident reportedly triggered insurgent raids on multiple Nangade villages between 11-13 December that left 14 people dead.

Local media reported that large numbers of people, including local residents and insurgents, continue to inhabit Mocimboa da Praia.  This includes people captured by insurgents who are held in an old car park.  Insurgent leaders meanwhile live in abandoned hotels in the area, with several of them living in the Milamba area near the Mocimboa Airport.  Insurgents meanwhile reportedly have stockpiled food in the town, raided from villages across insurgent impacted areas in the province.  Many civilians, particularly those with useful professions, are allowed by insurgents to continue living in the town.  Electricity meanwhile in the town is being provided principally by solar panels.

A battalion of security forces exchanged gunfire with insurgents during a military reconnaissance mission in Awasse area, north of Muidumbe, at around 0900hrs on 15 December, with clashes lasting until around 1600hrs.  Insurgents hiding in the bush and in abandoned homes in and around the village ambushed this patrol. 6 soldiers were killed and 16 others were injured.  Sources later indicated that as many as 24 insurgents were killed in these clashes, according to a local media outlet.  The insurgent death toll was later reported as 31. Security forces reportedly abandoned their vehicles in the area and withdrew to Mueda.
Sources announced that several open box vehicles were deployed to Cabo Delgado this week and received by security forces on 15 December in order to enhance the fight against Cabo Delgado insurgents.

Security forces detained an insurgent identified as Ehatche in Matemo Island. Ehatche is the  brother-in-law of an insurgent named Momade Nsuco, and Ehatche was suspected of having served as a guide for insurgents in attacks in October on the island.  Ehatche had reportedly intended to leave Matemo to attack Nambo village along with other insurgents prior to his arrest.  Meanwhile Nsuco's wife and children reportedly in recent weeks travelled to join the insurgents in the Nacutuco and Illala areas.

President Nyusi on 16 December in his address to the nation said that over 570,000 people have fled insurgent impacted areas of Cabo Delgado.  Nyusi also said Maputo had received offers "from all corners of the world" to help in the fight against the insurgency, saying Mozambique would "keep training our military to fight".  Nyusi also said Mozambique would need to manage these offers to avoid a "mix of interventions", and said the country would "develop our capabilities internally" and would be the "first line of defense" of the country.  Nyusi went on to say that the state had contained the insurgents from 2012-2017 before the group escalated its activities, and that the group had bases in Mocimboa da Praia, Nangade, Palma, and Quissanga Districts.  He also said that foreign nationals from Tanzania, the DRC, Somalia, Uganda, and Kenya were members of the group.

President Filipe Nyusi announced on Wednesday that Mozambique would form an anti-kidnapping unit to prevent and minimize the increasing kidnapping cases. Nyusi requested the assistance of the international community in the project.

Police detained two suspects for stealing food stamps intended for IDPs in Pemba on 15 December. The suspects was volunteer with an NGO who stole the foods stamps worth 3,000 meticais for each family. The suspects would sell the stamps to other families in different markets in the city.

RENAMO members in Inhambane supporting Elias Dhlakama claimed that they are being discriminated against and undermined by Momade Ossufo supporters. Those supporting of Elias Dhlakama also stated that they lost their leadership positions due to the internal dispute.

The Ministry of Health announced 40 new COVID cases and 1 related death in Mozambique on 15 December. The death was recorded in Maputo City. There have been 17,042 cases in the country along with 144 deaths.

The Portuguese Foreign Minister, Augusto Santos Silva will travel as an envoy in Cabo Delgado, upon the request of the EU Foreign Minister Josep Borrell Fontelles. The Portuguese FM will discuss the situation of Cabo Delgado with Mozambican officials to allow the EU security mission the country. Fontelles also remarked that every issue ongoing in the north is related to the insurgents and at some extent such incidents are due to poverty and inequality.

The National Institute of Meteorology announced that 30 to 50mm of rainfall is expected within in Maputo and Gaza provinces starting on the afternoon of 16 December. Flooding is expected to occur due to heavy rains. INAM also mentioned that waves may reach 3 meters in height.

The National Institute of Meteorology announced that 30 to 50mm of rainfall is expected within in Maputo and Gaza provinces starting on the afternoon of 16 December. Flooding is expected to occur due to heavy rains. INAM also mentioned that waves may reach 3 meters in height.

The UN Human Development Report stated that Mozambique is the worst-off Portuguese-speaking country in Africa. The average life expectancy at birth was 60.9 years. 8 percent of rural populations have access to electricity. Only 0.8 doctors are available for every 10,000 locals. Around 62.9 percent live below the poverty line.

RENAMO stated that their members are being targeted in Manica province on 15 December, particularly in Barue, Gondola, Chimoio, Mossurize, and Machaze. RENAMO Provincial Assembly of Manica Head Celestino Manuel Jo stated that one member was killed while others were reportedly tortured earlier this year. This comes after the kidnapping of a former RENAMO national assembly member was reported earlier this week.

The company Electricidade de Moçambique (EDM) disassembled an illegal underground power connection without an electrical meter inside a bakery shop in Maputo on 14 December. EDM initially turned off the electrical supply in the area after the shop owners refused to allow inspectors inside the shop.

The US updated its travel advisory for Mozambique on 14 December, saying that travelers are advised not to travel to Pemba due to threat of terrorism. The advisory also says US nationals should not travel to parts of Cabo Delgado due to the threat of insurgent attacks. Travelers are also requested to reconsider their travel to Manica and Sofala due to the high criminal activity in these areas - referring to ongoing RENAMO dissident attacks.

The advisory also says US nationals should not travel to parts of Cabo Delgado due to the threat of insurgent attacks. Travelers are also requested to reconsider their travel to Manica and Sofala due to the high criminal activity in these areas - referring to ongoing RENAMO dissident attacks.

The Centre for Public Integrity (CIP) said the Mozambican government has not been transparent during the hiring of PMCs in Cabo Delgado.

Police Commander Gen. Bernardino Rafael apologized for “errors and crimes” committed by police agents in a speech on 15 December. Rafael stated that the apologies were on behalf of policemen who have abused their power and promised that there will be changes in police conduct. This comes as multiple accusations of abuses by police across the country, including several incidents in Cabo Delgado.

The Minister of Health Beninga Matsinhe requested on Monday, 14 December, for Mozambicans to stay home during the holidays and avoid traveling. The minister stated that heavy traffic, public gatherings and movement between cities may increase the risk of the spread of COVID-19.

The Government spokesman Filimao Swazi denied that insurgents held several districts in Cabo Delgado in a speech given on Tuesday. Swazi stated that all districts in the province are still under government control.  This is despite the fact that multiple government officials have admitted that insurgents do openly control some territory in Cabo Delgado, including the port of Mocimboa da Praia.

UNICEF provided 275,000 USD to assist IDPs in obtaining personal identification documents in Metuge on 15 December. The campaign was to restore the registration records burned by the insurgents during recent attacks. The IDPs were from Muidumbe, Macomia, Mocimboa da Praia and Quissanga. The campaign is being conducted in coordination with the Ministry of Justice, Constitutional and Religious Affairs.
Locals sources stated that residents of villages around Mueda have recently requested weapons from the security forces to combat insurgents.

Locals protested against the price increase on bus fare to Montepuez from Mueda on 16 December. The protesters demanded the intervention of the government to resolve the issue. The price reportedly increased to 700 meticais to 1000 meticais; this is increase is due to many IDPs and residents of the Mueda area fleeing to Montepuez after recent insurgent incursions near Mueda.

Japan was reported on 11 December to be donating around $1.9 million to fund the purchases of boats and lifejackets for Mozambique's coastguard in order to enable to coastguard to rescue people from coastal areas of Cabo Delgado impacted by the insurgency.
Insurgents in the Mandimba area of Nangade on 08 December reportedly kidnapped two women after attacking vehicles in the area.

The government has recently advised fishermen and traders not to sail into the northern waters of Ibo District or beyond, as security forces are conducting operations to locate and destroy insurgent vessels along the Ibo/Macomia/Mocimboa da Praia/Palma coast, and that any vessels sailing in these waters may be attacked.
