column4: Insurgents on 07 December were reported to have shot and injured a man in Muambula in Muidumbe District.  The previous day, insurgents beheaded a man in the village.

President Nyusi in a state of the nation speech on 16 December said that Mozambique had "no other option" but to launch operations against the RENAMO Military Junta which operates in Central Mozambique.  Nyusi said the government had attempted to engage the group in a dialogue, but that the group continued attacks.  The President said that Mozambique would now "unleash rigorous operations against the enemy and that is what is happening now".

The Ministry of Health announced that a COVID related death and 101 new cases in Mozambique on 16 December. The death was recorded in Maputo city. A total of 17,143 cases have been recorded since the first infection, while 15,421 have recovered.  Maputo City has 1,421 active cases, while Maputo has another 102 active cases.

President Nyusi stated during his State of the Nation address on 16 December that a third of RENAMO military members, or 1,490 out of 5,221 armed RENAMO members have been demobilized and re-integrated to society. 6 RENAMO bases have also been closed down across several provinces as part of the ongoing DDR process.

The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) stated that food shortages and price increase were reported in 5 provinces of Mozambique starting on 8 December. INAE continued to monitor the price fluctuations in Inhambane, Niassa, Manica, Tete and Zambezia until 14 December. In Inhambane and Manica specifically, shortages of staple products such as fish, eggs, and potatoes have been reported.  The price of the food items increases from around 30 to 120 meticais depending on the product. INAE spokesman Timba stated that the government would contact main supplies and importers to resolve the shortage of food products and increase inspections during the holidays.
column15: Inhambane, Niassa, Manica, Tete and Zambezia

column4: Local authorities were accused of facilitating illegal Chinese logging and of corruption by licensed forestry operators in Manica on 15 December. Forestry operators stated that allowing the purchase by the Chinese has led to the low price of products in the market. The operators also stated that the Chinese are do not have the right to purchase goods unlike licensed operators, who must comply to rules and regulations.  Chinese operators also allegedly do not pay taxes on their illegally logged timber.

Mozambique Ministry of Defense denied reports that Mozambique received military equipment from South Africa. This came after reports recently indicated a South African defense contractor had provided military vehicles and helicopters to the Mozambican government.

RENAMO called on police to clarify security force involvement in the 13 December abduction of a former RENAMO deputy in Manica. RENAMO spokesman Eduardo Leite stated that Suffering Matequenha was abducted by armed men wearing police uniforms in Nhamaonha, Chimoio, on 13 December.  Police have denied involvement in the incident, while some sources indicate that RENAMO dissidents may have been behind the abduction, though Matequenha's family who were present during the incident accused the police of kidnapping the former deputy.

RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade called on local youths to not get involved with the armed attacks conducted by dissidents in Zambezia on 15 December. Momade denounced the dissident attacks stating that it is unjustifiable to target defenseless civilians.  The mainstream RENAMO party denies as connections with the RENAMO Military Junta.

Security forces arrested 20 illegal residents made up of Congolese and Burundian nationals during an operation in Nampula. The detainees confessed of staying in a residence in Namutequeliwa neighborhood.  There is some speculation that the group could be connected to the insurgency in Cabo Delgado, though this is currently unconfirmed.

South Africa National Prosecuting Authority has reportedly launched an investigation to prosecute Dyck Advisory Group (DAG) activities and those of another associated company based in South Africa. DAG reportedly violated the South Africa anti-mercenary law by aiding another foreign power without the approval of Pretoria Department of International Relations and Cooperation. The involvement of DAG in the Mozambican conflict has been considered controversial as the company did not have permission from the South African government to operate in Mozambique.

The President of the Republic, Filipe Nyusi, issued on the afternoon of 16 December a pardon to release elderly/seriously ill inmates. The pardon was to be implemented by the end of December. The pardon also included prisoners who have served half of their sentences or were marked for good behavior.  This pardon was made official on 28 December, with 1,182 inmates pardoned.

Security forces detained 32 illegal immigrants intercepted last week at Pemba airport. 30 of the detainees were Somalis and two Ethiopians. This comes as 35 illegal immigrants were detained the previous week. All 67 immigrants were questioned upon arrival in the country. Security officials stated that the detainees claimed to be tourist but did not possess visas or the financial means to support themselves in the country.

President Nyusi stated during his 16 December address to the nation that the insurgency in Cabo Delgado was initially promoted by a Tanzanian national identified as Abdul Shakulo, who preached a radical form of Islam beginning in 2012. Most of the other leaders of the group according to Nyusi were Tanzanians nationals who have since been killed in the conflict, including Sheik Ibrahimo, Sheik Hassan Zuzure, Abdul Azize, Sheik Aji Ulathule, and Faragi Nancalaua.  Nyusi also said insurgents had been recruited from Tanzania, Congo, Somalia, Uganda, and Kenya, in addition to Mozambique. Nyusi also claimed that the Mozambican government had been aware of the insurgency since 2012, and that the Mozambican government had "managed to contain their expansion until 2017".

The Nangade - Palma road as of 14 December was reported to be in use again with food supplies again arriving in Palma after the route was closed due to insurgent attacks along the road on 08 December.  One source reported the route was initially reported to be clear of insurgents on 11 December, though insurgents are believed to remain in the vicinity of the road, particularly in the Pundanhar and Mandimba areas, and remain a threat to traffic along the route.

Pro-government militias based out of Mueda between 14-16 December carried out counter-insurgency operations in parts of Muidumbe District between Muatide and Muidumbe, allegedly killing several insurgents in these operations, though no specific casualty numbers are currently available.  These militias are now reported to be wearing uniforms assigned to them after mistakenly clashing with troops in recent months in at least 2 incidents in Muidumbe.

RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo on 17 December was reported to have said that on 21 December, he would nominate representatives for talks with the Mozambican government, but called on the National Assembly to approve an amendment to protect the group's representatives; Nhongo said he wanted to "ensure that my men will not be kidnapped".  This came after Nhongo this week accused the government of having kidnapped three of his children and three grandchildren from Gondola District.

President Nyusi in his 16 December Address to the Nation said that Mozambique would "soften" state of emergency measures meant to counter the COVID-19 pandemic.  These measures, which are meant to take effect on 19 December, will include: All passengers still are required to submit negative COVID tests upon arrival to the country; these tests however can now be conducted 96 hours prior to arrival, rather than the 72 hours prior to arrival previously required. The issuance of visas for tourism "at the border" will be resumed. The Ponta de Ouro Crossing with South Africa will be reopened to alleviate pressure on the Ressano Garcia and Namaacha border posts. Private event capacities allowed are adjusted up to 50 people per gathering up from 40.  Outdoor gatherings can include up to 150 people. Markets will be allowed to remain open to 6pm, adjusted from 5pm. Bars, tents, and kiosks can open from 9am - 4pm from Sunday to Friday, and from 9am to 7pm on Fridays and Saturdays
Security forces arrested 3 men for exhuming the bones of a murder victim in Zambezia on 17 December. The exhumed victim was murdered on 2016 in Mopeia district.
A truck overturned while crossing a bridge along the Mueda-Montepuez road. No casualties were reported.
A truck overturned a fell into a ditch along the Mueda-Montepuez road near the entrance to Mueda. No casualties were reported.
A civilian was killed after he hit by a train in Trevo area of Matola, west of Maputo city, on 17 December.

The National Health Institute conducted a study of COVID exposure rates in Inhamabane, finding high COVID exposure rates in the towns of Maxixe and Massinga. Maxixe which has a population of 123,868 had a 5.5 percent exposure rate, or indicating that about 6,812 likely COVID cases in the city during the pandemic. With a population of 184,531, Massinga recorded a 7.4 percent exposure rate, or equal to about 13,655 cases. The total sample size in Maxixe was 3,974, and in Massinga it was 1,577.

UNFPA on 17 December declared a level two emergency in Cabo Delgado due to the ongoing IDP crisis in Cabo Delgado.  This emergency level will allow regional humanitarian assets and procedures to be mobilized and deployed to Cabo Delgado to improve humanitarian responses in the province.

The Ministry of Health announced that 113 new COVID cases were recorded in Mozambique on 17 December bringing the total to 17,256. Maputo city recorded 57 cases, followed by Maputo province with 24 new cases.  There were 7 cases in Sofala, 6 in Nampula, 6 in Zambezia, 4 in Cabo Delgado, 3 in Tete, 2 in Gaza, and 1 in Manica.

The Portuguese Parliament discussed during an assembly session the insurgency ongoing in Cabo Delgado on 18 December. The meeting would also discuss the role of Portugal in assisting Mozambique. The parties,  CDS-PP and PAN stated that the duty is not only of the UN but of the EU in supporting Mozambique to minimize the humanitarian crisis and combat terrorism.

A man who was recently released by insurgents after being abducted in the Mucojo area said militants had told him they intended to attack Macomia town and the provincial capital of Pemba, though no date for this attack was specified.  Insurgents reportedly spared him specifically so he could spread this message.

Security forces ambushed insurgents on motorcycles travelling from Litingina village at an intersection in Nangade District on 11 December, just after insurgents attacked Litingina.  Six insurgents were killed, sources reported.  Media reports later indicated as many as 16 insurgents were killed in an ambush near Litingina, with 4 insurgents escaping from this clash, though all 4 were reportedly wounded.

American Senator Robert Menendez on 17 December called on the US government and its partners to provide assistance to Mozambique against its fight on insurgency in Cabo Delgado. Menendez stated that the security situation in country was dire and has not garnered proper attention from other lawmakers and leaders. Menendez said that counter-terrorism training and humanitarian assistance is not enough to defeat the insurgency in Mozambique.  Menedez also said that Mozambique and its partners must work to address the "social and economic inequalities" that have enabled the insurgency.
Insurgents were reported to have attacked Magundula Island, about 4kms off the Mucojo coast.  The exact date of this attack, and other details regarding this incident, are currently unavailable.
Insurgents were reported to have fired on a convoy of 5 vehicles and to have set them on fire in an ambush between Nangade and Mueda on 16 December.  No casualties were reported in this attack.

South Africa's Minister of International Relations and Cooperation announced that the South African government would provide support to "a sovereign state" against any terror threat, referring to a potential request from the Mozambican government for assistance in combating the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

A UN official stated that the situation on Cabo Delgado is "really dire" and requires a greater international intervention amid the ongoing crisis. The UNHCR stated that the insurgency could develop into a long-term conflict resembling the ongoing insurgency in Nigeria.

The EU has approved a 30 million EUR grant to assist 700,000 homes in Zambezia and Nampula in the provision of electricity. The grant is part of the EU’s PROMOVE and PROLER assistance programs to develop rural areas and provide energy generation in Mozambique.

The EU has approved a 30 million EUR grant to assist 700,000 homes in Zambezia and Nampula in the provision of electricity. The grant is part of the EU’s PROMOVE and PROLER assistance programs to develop rural areas and provide energy generation in Mozambique.

Heavy traffic congestion due to the slow processing of documents at the Machipanda Border Crossing along Mozambique-Zimbabwe border was reported on 18 December. The majority of the long waiting time was due to long-distance truck drivers crossing the border. Truck drivers stated that traffic is expected to worsen during the holidays.
Police arrested two suspects for forging driving licenses in Ponta Gea, south Beira, on 14 December. The suspects were working inside a small print shop.

Police detained three suspects for forging documents and national ID cards in Matola, west of Maputo, on 18 December. Several vehicle registration booklets and debit cards were seized in this operation.

UN and partners called have launched an appeal for 2021 funds of $254 million in assisting up to 1.1 million people in Cabo Delgado on 18 December. UN stated that in 2020, the needs of IDPs have been rapidly increasing and require more urgent funding. The UN also said that other factors such as the upcoming rainy season will worsen this crisis.

Antonio Juliao, Permanent Secretary of Nacala District, was arrested over charges of embezzlement of state assets, a source reported on 20 Dec. Among the alleged embezzled assets were electrotechnical equipment that were purchased several times but were not visible in the district.

Former RENAMO Guerillas based in Catine, Homoine claimed to have been "forgotten by the government" after being excluded from the Disarmament, Demobilization and Social Reintegration (DDR) process in Inhambane province, a source disclosed on 20 Dec. The group claimed that upon leaving the Makauleza base they received a promise from Afonso Dhlakama, late leader of FRELIMO that they should wait for the demobilization process. Former guerillas in this area have not officially been accepted into the DDR process, and are thus not yet able to officially demobilize.

Following  insurgent attacks on villages in Nangade last week, several private and public institutions have been closed. Among the affected institutions were the Civil Registry Office, the District Court and the District Attorney's Office while several villages have also been abandoned.. Transportation has been affected as well, as passenger transport fees increased from 200 to 500 Meticais. Some people have even fled towards Palma from Nangade district, despite insecurity along this route.

The Ministry of Health announced that 91 new COVID cases were recorded in Mozambique on 20 December bringing the total to 17,568. Another death was also recorded in the last 24 hours with the national death toll now at 148. Maputo city recorded 44 cases, followed by Sofala province with 14 new cases.  There were 8 cases in Zambezia, 7 in Gaza, 6 in Tete,  6 in Maputo, 5 in Cabo Delgado, and 1 in Inhambane.

UN envoy to Mozambique Mirko Manzoni confirmed on 21 December that Mariano Nhongo, leader of the RENAMO Military Junta group, recently expressed willingness through contacts to participate in a dialogue with the Mozambican government.    Manzoni recently spoke directly to Nhongo to confirm this.  Nhongo has reportedly agreed to suspend dissident attacks in order to engage in talks.

South African officials announced over the weekend that a new strain of COVID is driving a resurgence of the virus in that country.  This mutation of the original COVID virus is reportedly more contagious than previous strains, and is similar to a strain of the virus currently impacting the UK.

A new tropical storm system named Chalane was reported over the weekend to be developing off the northeast coast of Madagascar.  The storm is expected to impact Madagascar by 26 December, and could move towards northern Mozambique in the following days.

In a recent interview, retired Zimbabwean military officer and owner of Dyck Advisory Group (DAG) Lionel Dyck said that DAG's "strike capabilities" in Cabo Delgado are "almost entirely airborne", saying his force attacks insurgent camps from the air and also attacks insurgent supply lines on land and sea.  Dyck also indicated that he believed his company and the Mozambican military had slowed the insurgent advance though more effective ground support was needed.  Dyck also said "we also intend to move our base of operations closer to Mocimboa da Praia"

A truck transporting bricks collided with a vehicle along Avenida Marginal in Maputo on the morning of 22 December. Several bricks fell off the truck and blocked half of the avenue. Casualty information is currently unknown.

Aga Khan Development Network Rep. Nazim Ahmad to Portugal told media on 21 December that there is risk of insurgency related violence spreading across Mozambique. Ahmad stated that the risk of the ongoing conflict in Cabo Delgado must be taken to account across the country. Ahmad stated that the religious issue is only one factor and "does not account for what is happening."  Ahmad also said that there must be "external armed intervention to protect the population", though he also acknowledged the Mozambican government was hesitant to sanction such an intervention.

The government donated 15 boats to fishing associations in Metuge on 18 December. The boats were to enable fishing associations to provide adequate supplies of marine goods and ensure the security of food supply in the region. The provision of these boats was part of the government's soft power approach to attempt to undermine the appeal of the insurgency by providing tangible economic benefits to the population of Cabo Delgado.

The Government announced that it expects a decrease in border crossings during holiday season due to the pandemic. Around 57 percent of people are expected to cross the border in comparison to 2019‘s figure of 837,000. Official also stated that the Ressano Garcia Border Crossing is to operate from 06:00 until 12:00 due to allow locals to enter Mozambique, while civilians entering South Africa have until 22:00 to pass through during the holidays.

The National Institute for Disaster Management stated that 45,000 displaced families displaced from Cabo Delgado have been relocated to new districts.  The majority of the displaced were relocated in Montepuez, Chiure, and Balama districts of the same province. Other locations where families have been relocated to include Nampula and Niassa provinces.

Former RENAMO dissident spokesman Joao Machava called RENAMO dissident leader Nhongo to stop attacks on civilians, saying these attacks violated the original objectives of the RENAMO dissidents, which was to find a peaceful solution to differences among RENAMO members which arose after the RENAMO Congress of January 2019.  Machava also said that significant disinformation regarding the DDR process was circulating, preventing many RENAMO military members from joining the process.  Machava left the dissident group earlier this month to join in the DDR process.  Machava also stated that Ossufo Momade has deviated from the original plans of the former RENAMO leader, Afonso Dhlakama.  This call for peace comes as Nhongo recently publicly said he would participate in a dialogue with the government.

The Ministry of Health announced the death of one COVID patient and 129 new cases in Mozambique on 21 December. 52 of the new cases were recorded in Maputo city, 10 in Maputo province, 21 in Gaza, 16 in Inhambane, 11 in Zambezia, and 17 in Nampula.

The National Road Administration announced that new toll rates will be implemented starting 02 January in different provinces. The provinces included Gaza, Inhambane, Manica, Sofala, Zambézia, Tete, Nampula, Cabo Delgado and Niassa. Eight toll bridges were affected of the new toll rates
RENAMO dissidents on 11 December attacked a vehicle carrying National Statistics Institute employees in the Mossurize area, though no casualties were reported.

Three RENAMO dissidents, including a man described as an aid to RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo, were captured by security forces on or around 11 December in the Mossurize area, after dissidents attacked a vehicle in the district.  No other details regarding this incident are currently available.

An oil and gas company revitalized health center just outside an LNG project area in Afungi on 21 December. The company supported the restoration of Maganja Health Clinic. Maganja has been targeted in the past by insurgent attacks.

South Africa announced that a curfew would be implemented from 23:00 to 04:00 and allow the border to be  open to travelers from 06:00 to 22:00 as part of the agreement on both the Ressano and Lebombo Border Crossing for the upcoming holidays.

An NGO stated that around 1.3 million people will need assistance in Cabo Delgado in 2021. The ongoing insurgency has affected 36 percent of health centers in the province, which are either destroyed or damaged. The NGO also mentioned that 176,000 individuals have no access to water and hygiene sources, while 900,000 locals are experiencing food insecurity due to the disruption of markets.

Bishop of Pemba Luiz Lisboa said that direct external military intervention would be most helpful solution for Mozambique. The bishop also said better intelligence gathering was necessary to compliment the military response. Lisboa also stated that talks with insurgents are not doable as there is no one leader of the group.

Mozambique's neighbor Malawi on 22 December closed its borders for 14 days and restricted public gatherings to 100 people after a new surge of COVID cases.  No new cases had been reported in Malawi for two months before the country reported 46 new cases on 22 December.  There have been a total of 6,248 COVID cases along with 187 deaths in Malawi.  Malawi re-opened its borders and airports in October after positive cases fell.  This move by Malawi comes amid a new spike of cases in South Africa driven by a new, more contagious strain of COVID.

Local media on 22 December in an unconfirmed report citing an anonymous military source said that Police Commander Bernardino Rafael was planning to launch a Christmas offensive to retake Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) town from insurgents by the end of the year.

South Africa closed all beaches in Kwazulu Natal Province, bordering Mozambique during the holidays to minimize the spread of new COVID infections and possible spread of the new strain. There is a significant threat of the spread of this new strain into Mozambique.  Multiple flights in recent days have been cancelled to South Africa amid the ongoing spread of this new strain.

The Minister of Health Armindo Tiago said that 641 health professionals left their jobs due to insurgent attacks in Cabo Delgado during 2020.  41 hospitals have also been closed down in Cabo Delgado, including 27 which were destroyed by insurgents.
Local sources reported a new COVID outbreak with several new cases reported in the Palma/Afungi area.  This report is currently unconfirmed.

Several NGOs Regional Directors conducted a solidarity visit to Cabo Delgado and affected areas of Mozambique on 18 December. The NGOs included FAO, IFAD, IOM, UNFPA, UNHCR, WFP, and UNDP. This trip included a visit resettlement areas of the IDPs in Cabo Delgado. The UN Regional Directors stated that the province is experiencing  simultaneous humanitarian, development and human rights crisis.  This joint visit comes amid an  escalating IDP crisis and amid increased attention to the area from humanitarian organizations.

The Ministry of Health announced that another COVID related death and 72 cases in Mozambique on 22 December. T37 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 10 in Manica, 8 in Sofala, 5 in Niassa, 5 in Maputo, 3 in Gaza, 2 in Nampula and 2 in Inhambane.

The family members of a former RENAMO provincial delegate Suffering Matequenha claimed that they were receiving kidnapping and death threats in Manica from unknown persons..  This comes after Matequenha was recently abducted by unidentified uniformed persons near Chimoio.  Police say they are investigating the incident.
Unknown men destroyed equipment and two statues inside a church in Morrumbene, north of Inhambane, at around 12:00 of 21 December. No casualties were reported.
Security forces are reportedly forcing IDPs in camps in Metuge to remain in their tents for up to 18 hours a day.  This comes amid reports of IDPs being mistreated in different areas of Cabo Delgado
Security forces reportedly arrested 3 family members on 20 December in the 25 de Junho area of Metuge.

Local sources stated that SDS Forces questioned and assaulted an elderly IDP in the 25 de Junho area at around 0900hrs.  The officers reportedly questioned why the man had come from the Ancuabe area when a travel document he was carrying said he was coming from Bilibiza in Quissanga, and also questioned why the man had a significant amount of money.  The victim was attempting to sell fish in the area.

Security forces in Ibo have recently been reported to have committed abuses against IDPs on the island.  Security forces operating on the island effectively operate outside the jurisdiction of local authorities.

The National Institute of Meteorology announced  heavy rainfall in Maputo, Gaza, and Inhambane province may start on the afternoon of 23 December. The rainfall was expected to be accompanied by strong winds and are to last till the evening of 24 December. Flooding was expected on rivers and several roads.

Farmers protested against the lack of security in Sidwava area of Matola on 22 December. The protesters accused the local government of taking some of their crops and selling them. The protesters demanded that the government should clarify who was invading their fields and taking their crops. The farmers stated that they were losing crops during the harvest.

Farmers protested against the lack of security in Sidwava area of Matola on 22 December. The protesters accused the local government of taking some of their crops and selling them. The protesters demanded that the government should clarify who was invading their fields and taking their crops. The farmers stated that they were losing crops during the harvest.
A minibus overturned and crashed after a tire blowout along the Nhamatanda-Chimoio route in Sofala province on the evening of 20 December. 3 civilians were killed and 16 were injured.

Police on 21 December were reported to have seized and destroyed the nets of several fishermen in Moma, Nampula, saying the fishermen's nets were illegally modified.  Security forces in clashes with the fishermen fired shots to disperse the crowd.

Fishermen attacked ministry of fisheries inspectors for attempting to seize and destroy nets in Moma, south of Nampula, on 21 December. The inspectors were deployed with policemen who were conducted an inspection if the fishermen were following the issued closed season for mangrove crabs and shrimps. Inspectors found fine woven nets which illegal and were used to obtain smaller catch.

UNICEF announced that 250,000 children have been displaced in Cabo Delgado, and are at higher risk for disease in Cabo Delgado on 22 December. UNICEF said that the lack of safe water, sanitation and hygiene services are increasing the risks of a disease outbreak and further spread COVID among children in the province.  UNICEF is appealing for $52.8 million to meet humanitarian needs in Mozambique in 2021.

Government officials called for people to remain vigilant even with the relaxation of anti-COVID measures on 20 December. Public Health Director Benigna Matsinhe stated that the government is trying to maintain a balance between following the restrictions and appreciating the ease of safety measures. This comes as President Nyusi has warned locals that the relaxation of anti-COVID measures may be reversed if the COVID situation worsens.

Several countries as of 22 December had banned flights to South Africa, including Israel, Turkey, Germany, Suadi Arabia, and Switzerland amid the spread of a new more contagious strain of COVID-19 in the country.

PRM launched a new operation by the police called the Accident Prevention Plan. Police from the traffic unit, National Salvation Service Public Administration, National Roads Authority, Directorate for Transport and Maputo City Communication, and Municipal Police, were among the units included. The accident prevention plan was to minimize road traffic accidents during the holiday season.

Long lines of trucks for clearance and other processes have been causing traffic at the Forbes Border Post on 23 December. Truck drivers clarified that they have complete documents, but the issuing of clearance have been slow during the holiday season. Border officials responded that there were no problems with the issuance of visas though the processing has slowed down.

President Nyusi said on 22 December that a "great cyclone" could potentially form in the Mozambique channel in the coming days.  National Meteorological officials have said a tropical storm currently forming northeast of Madagascar could potentially dissipate over that country, but could also proceed into the Mozambique channel and impact the center and north of the country.  Nyusi also said officials had told him that the dissipation of the storm over Madagascar was the most likely scenario, but that Mozambican should still take precautions in the event that the storm turns into a Cyclone and impacts Mozambique.  Cyclones Kenneth and Idai struck the country in 2019.

RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo on 23 December declared a unilateral ceasefire with the government, saying that there had been no attacks by his group for a week, and that his group would not launch any new attacks.  Nhongo also said he had appointed a 5 member committee to engage in talks with the government, which he would dispatch for talks on 28 December.  Nhongo went on to say that he was "calling on the government and the embassies to end the war and enter into negotiations".

Studies indicate that parts of Inhamabane has been the province with the highest exposure to COVID-19 after antibody tests in Maxixe and Massinga showed 5.2% and 7.4% exposure to the virus in these cities.  There is significant concern in the province that COVID could be further spread in the province from South Africans travelling into Mozambique over the holiday season.  A new more contagious strain of the virus has recently been identified in South Africa and is driving a new spike of cases in the country.

Sweden donated 3 million EUR to assist IDPs in Cabo Delgado. The funds were expected to provide relief for 95,300 IDPs. The funds were to aid the UN Humanitarian Air Service, which requires 117 million USD to continue its work in Mozambique.

RENAMO dissident Mariano Nhongo stated that the Mozambican military are still conducting operations searching for dissidents in Nhamatanda in the Boza area. Nhongo previously announced his openness to talks and this week declared a unilateral ceasefire with the government.

President Nyusi on 22 December called for RENAMO dissidents to join the DDR Process. The president also called for RENAMO dissident leader Nhongo to conduct talks to resolve the ongoing disputes with the political party RENAMO and to stop attacks in Manica and Sofala.

Chicualacuala officials announced that 1,200 families are cut off road access due to rising river levels brought about by heavy rainfall in Gaza province. Officials stated that if heavy rainfall continues the area would be lack access to food and medications.
The Ministry of Health announced that three COVID deaths and 189 new cases were reported on 23 December. 130 of the cases were from Maputo city which is followed by Niassa with 28 new cases.

Insurgents on the night of 23-24 December attacked Mute village in southern Palma District, carrying out looting and setting several homes on fire.  Unconfirmed reports said Mozambican troops had clashed with insurgents in the area.

Two sources reported that insurgents in recent days retreated from the Awasse area after recent clashes in the area with security forces.  State-linked sources reported insurgents lost 31 fighters in this clash (which took place on 15 December), though this in not confirmed.  Note previous reporting said 24 insurgents had been killed in clashes in the area, along with six soldiers.  It is not clear if government troops have advanced into the Awasse area.

Tropical Depression Chalane which has been forming in recent days east of Madagascar is now anticipated to strengthen into a Tropical Storm as it moves west and make landfall in Madagascar on 26 December.  The storm could potentially regain strength after clearing Madagascar and entering the Mozambican Channel early next week.  If the storm does impact Mozambique, it would likely make landfall on 29 or 30 December, and would likely most significantly impact Nampula, Sofala, and Zambezia, though Manica, Tete, and even northern parts of Inhamabane and Gaza could also be affected by the storm.

State-linked sources reported that Mozambican troops on the evening of 23 December had clashed with insurgents in the Mute village area, killing 4 insurgents and capturing 6 firearms from the group.  Note that other sources reported that insurgents had successfully attacked Mute and carried out looting in the village.  Some sources later indicated 6 insurgents were killed in the clashes.  Images of 4 insurgents killed in the clashes as well as equipment and weaponry were later shared on social media networks.

State-linked sources reported that Mozambican troops on the evening of 23 December clashed with insurgents in the Mapalanganha area, located in the far south of Palma District just north of the border with Mocimboa da Praia District.  Insurgents meanwhile overnight attacked the village of Mute, further to the north.

President Nyusi in late December announced that Mozambican troops since 25 November had launched operations targeting the RENAMO Military Junta in areas along the Pungue River, including in the Cundze area of Gorongosa, and the Chimibe and Ndombe areas along the river, as well as the Pinhananga base, a primary HQ for the group.

column4: President Nyusi on 22 December said that Mozambican forces were pursuing RENAMO dissidents in the Chimaniamani Park area in Manica, though no other details regarding this operation were provided.
President Nyusi on 22 December said that Mozambican troops were "hunting down" RENAMO dissidents in the Manguerre and Galinha AP areas of Muanza, Sofala though provided no further details.
A van collided with a truck along the National Road 1 (N1) in Manhica, north of Maputo city, on 23 December. 5 civilians died and another civilian was injured.

The Mozambican Tax Authority announced that they have collected more tax revenue this year leading to 110.3 percent of the set target. The Tax Authority stated that the tax revenue was due to the changes made with the measures during the pandemic. Tax Authority officials stated that Value Added Tax contributed with the revenue increase along with Corporate Income Tax, Personal Income Tax, and taxes from companies.

Hospital Central De Nampula announced that external consolations and surgeries would be suspended until 5 January. The suspension was to allow the employees to celebrate the holidays. The Central Bank of Nampula’s Aid Team organized a team to work in shifts during the suspension to prevent any lack of medical care.

An international mining company announced it intends to install 11.2 Megawatt hybrid power system in Balama, west Montepuez, on 25 December. The solar energy plant was also to install a battery-based electricity storage system.

Three armed robbers shot and injured a business trader after he refused to hand over his money in Beira at around 07:00 on 24 December. The suspects fled from the area after forcibly stealing the cash.

Servico Nacional de Investigacao Criminal SERNIC detained a 22 year old citizen in Morrumbene on 24 Dec over alleged involvement in destroying statues inside a Catholic church. The suspect allegedly destroyed musical instruments and threw the crowns of child Jesus and saints in the altar on 21 Dec.

President Nyusi on 27 December said people should leave flood-prone areas in Central Mozambique ahead of the possible landfall of Tropical Cyclone Chalane in the coming days.  The storm is currently over Madagascar, and is expected to enter the Mozambique Channel on 28 December.  Current forecasts indicate that if the cyclone continues to strengthen, it would likely make landfall in Mozambique on 30 December, and most heavily impact Sofala and Zambezia.  Other provinces likely to be impacted though to a lesser extent include Manica, Nampula, and Tete. As many as 4 million people could be affected by the storm, Nyusi said.

The Joint Typhoon Warning Center late on 27 December said that the system was expected to intensify with wind speeds increasing from 30 to 40 knots over the next 24 hours.  This forecast would see the eye of the tropical cyclone making landfall south of Beira on 30 December, with wind speeds of between 55-65 knots.  Note that Chalane could still dissipate over Madagascar/ the Mozambique Channel over the coming days though this appears increasingly unlikely according to forecasts.

The body of Sofrimento Matequenha, a former RENAMO deputy to the National Assembly and provincial delegate to the Manica Assembly, was discovered in the Mpnaganga / Pundanganga Forest area of Gondola on Friday.  The body bore signs of a physical assault, and was only conclusively identified on Saturday.  Matequenha had been kidnapped from his home in the Chimoio area on 13 December by unidentified uniformed men.

105 families have resettled in the new village built by Montepuez Ruby Mining MRM in Namanhumbir, a source disclosed on 28 Dec. The village was built by the mining company to relocate families residing within the MRM concession in Nthoro. The new 2400-hectare village has water and electricity infrastructure, a primary school, market, church, mosque, police station, cemetery and a landfill.

The Ministry of Health announced that three COVID deaths and 54 new cases were reported on 26 December. The total COVID-19 death toll in Mozambique is 159. 23 of the new cases were from Maputo city, 23 from Maputo province and eight from Cabo Delgado.

The United Nations warns the humanitarian situation in Cabo Delgado province as 'extremely critical', UN resident coordinator in Mozambique, Myrta Kaulard disclosed on 28 Dec.  Kaulard noted that 2020 began with about 90,000 displaced in Cabo Delgado, and is ending with over 500,000 displaced. Thousands of children are allegedly malnourished with lack of proper shelter, adequate food and clean water.  A total of 254 million USD was appealed by UN as part of the UN assistance plan, with a budget of 136 million dollars (111 million euros) for food security and 28 million dollars (23 million euros) for shelter.

A  225-meter steel bridge over Montepuez river in Bilibiza, Quissanga was inaugurated by President Nyusi on 28 December. The bridge facilitates transportation between southern Cabo Delgado to the districts of Macomia, Muidumbe, Mueda, Nangade, Mocímboa da Praia and Palma . This is the replacement of the old bridge after it collapsed on 2019 December due to heavy rains and overflow of water from the river.
column15: Montepuez River Crossing along N380 road

column4: Cyclone Chalane on 28 December entered the Mozambique Channel, moving west towards Sofala Province.  The cyclone is now expected to make landfall in Mozambique between Muanza and Machanga on the morning of 30 December, with winds of up to 90kms with gusts of up to 110 kms.  Sofala, Zambezia, Manica, Gaza, and Inhamabane are all expected to be impacted by the storm.  The Cyclone is expected by 31 December to impact parts of Eastern Zimbabwe.  The Cyclone/Tropical Storm will bring a threat of flash flooding and mudslides in many areas.  The storm has weakened to a degree moving across Mozambique but is expected to regain some strength in the Mozambique Channel.
Three cases of domestic violence were reported in the neighborhoods of Mafalala, Alto Mae and Aeroport on 25 Dec. No other details on this incident are currently available.

Three sexual abuse cases were reported in the in the neighborhoods of Bagamoio, Aeroporto and Triunfo on 25 Dec. Victims are under the age of two, three and 18.  No other details on this incident are currently available.
A 22-yr-old man was killed after he was ran over by a car in Maputo city on 25 Dec. No other details on this incident are currently available.

The Ministry of Health announced that two COVID deaths and 103 new cases were reported on 27 December. The total COVID-19 death toll in Mozambique is 161. Breakdown of cases per province has yet to be disclosed by the source.

Mozambique's Meteorolgy Institute (INAM) has warned of heavy rains (100 millimeters in 24 hours) in Beira, all of Southern Sofala, and in Manica, including Chimoio, and rains of over 50 millimeters in 24 hours in Northern Sofala and Manica as well as in most of Zambezia and northern areas of Inhamabane due to the approaching Cyclone Chalane.  The Cyclone is expected to make landfall on 30 December near Beira.  Rains will likely begin on the night of 29 December.  Note that Cyclone Chalane is currently anticipated to drop less than half of the amount of rain brought by Cyclone Idai in 2019.
Some businesses in Beira on 27 December began boarding up storefronts and making other preparations ahead of the expected landfall of Cyclone Chalane over the coming days.

Police Commander General Bernardino Rafael said on 25 December that insurgents had threatened to attack Macomia on Christmas, calling for residents to remain vigilant in the area.  No such attack materialized on Christmas day or in the days immediately following.

Macomia residents in a meeting with Police Commander General Bernardno Rafael on 25 December called for weapons to be provided to them to fight insurgents.  This request came amid a proliferation in recent months of pro-government militias forming across parts of Cabo Delgado to protect communities from insurgent attacks.

Police Commander Bernardino Rafael on 25 December said that Mozambican military units in the week before Christmas had carried out operations in Macomia District that resulted in 37 insurgents killed, 21 weapons seized, 3 terrorist vehicles, 10 motorcycles, 9 bicycles, and 17 boats destroyed.  It was unclear where these operations discussed by Rafael reportedly took place in Macomia District, though if boats were destroyed the operation likely took place at least partially in Mucojo District on the Macomia coast.  Rafael also said that if insurgent attempted to attack the town again, they would find "a ready answer".

Local sources reported that an insurgent named Omary Khamis, a Tanzanian national, was captured in late October of 2020 in Pemba by security forces near Praia do Wimbi in a rented house. Khamis had reportedly posted multiple times on social media regarding insurgent attacks in Cabo Delgado.  He had also reportedly passed information to the insurgents about flights in and out of Pemba to and from other parts of Cabo Delgado. Khamis previously had worked in Tanzania, Kenya, and Mozambique.

Mozambican troops on 22 December advanced to Awasse town, which was found to have been abandoned by insurgents. Troops at Awasse found multiple dead insurgents, believed to have been killed in clashes with the military on 15 December.  Insurgents reportedly left a note behind in the area questioning the nationality of the soldiers who had attacked them the week before. The military now is reportedly setting up a new base in the Awasse area in order to hold this town, its important crossroads, and a nearby electrical sub-station.  It is unclear if insurgents abandoned Awasse just before the military's arrival, or if they left the area the week prior.

The Mozambique Red Cross has activated its "Early Action Protocol to prepare for Cyclone Chalane, which is expected to make landfall in Mozambique over the coming days.  These actions include supporting communities to reinforce school buildings and houses, and ensuring access to clean water in flood prone areas.  The Mozambique Red Cross says that it expects the most severe impact of the storm to be in the areas of Buzi, Dondo, Muanza, and Beira in Sofala.  Of these districts, Buzi is considered particularly vulnerable.
