Over 1 million COVID-19 cases have been reported in Mozambique's neighbor South Africa, with many of the new cases belonging to new COVID variant 501.V2, which is considered more contagious.  South Africa has also recorded 26,735 COVID deaths.  The 501.V2 variant is known to be present in large numbers in KwaZulu-Natal, bordering Mozambique.  South Africa's seven-day rolling average over the past two weeks has nearly doubled from 10.24 new cases per 100,000 to 19.86 new cases per 100,000 as of 26 December.

Insurgents in the early morning hours of 27 December were reported to have killed 5 civilians in a village raid on Saba Saba in Muidumbe District, north of Namacande town and west of Chitunda.  No further details regarding this incident are currently available.

Public bus transportation doubled prices for bus rides during holiday season at Junta Bus Terminal in Maputo. Local sources stated that prices to Xai-xai, Gaza was around 600 meticais and can go up to 1500 meticais instead of 300 meticais. While travel to Xipamanine was for 300 meticais.

Police exchanged gunfire with civilians after refusing the judicial court’s decision to move from a plot of land in Metengobalame of Tsangano District on 26 December. Six civilians were killed, and six others were injured. The dispute over the plot of land came after the Malawian owner filed an eviction for the illegal land tenants.

Local sources on 25 December stated that a large buildup of trash has been neglected in Montepuez.  Locals stated that the waste accumulation was due to the lack of fuel for vehicles that can collect the waste.
A power outage was reported due to a short circuit cutting off electrical supply to 25 residences in Nacala on 25 December.

Mozambique Electricity (EDM) dismantled four illegal power connections stealing electricity in Magoanine A, north Maputo City, on 28 December. The suspects stated that they do not remember their last payment to EDM. EDM responded with a 30-day grace period that allowed to pay off their debt.

President Nyusi announced that the security forces are advancing their ground against insurgents in Cabo Delgado. Nyusi also stated that security forces should be maintain "maximum readiness" and said that insurgents have been "silent" recently.

NKC African Economics stated that the inflation rate in Mozambique would remain moderate and may increase due to the increasing prices. 2021 would include the weakening of the currency and rise in good and energy prices.  12 month average inflation in Mozambique stands at about 3.14%.

Tropical Storm Chalane moved towards the coast of Sofala on the morning of 29 December. The storm was expected to reach winds of 90km/h and gusts of 130km/h. The National Meteorological Institute stated that the storm is currently very weak but may intensify before landfall.

Insurgents at around 0500hrs on 29 December attacked Olumbi town in southern Palma.  This attack occurred at the same time as another insurgent attack at Monjane, less than 10kms from the LNG camp.  A number of people were reportedly abducted during this attack.  Sources have indicated at least 5 people were killed in this attack.  Note other sources reported insurgents had launched their attack initially earlier on 28 December and remained in the village overnight.
Insurgents reportedly kidnapped several people in an attack on Monjane village in the early morning hours of 29 December.
Insurgents reportedly kidnapped several people in an attack on Olumbi village in the early morning hours of 29 December.

Insurgents on 29 December were reported to have ambushed soldiers between Monjane and Patacua in Cabo Delgado, killing 2 soldiers while 1 insurgent was also killed.  This came after insurgents raided Monjane village, with security forces responding to this attack.

Insurgents in an attack at around 0500hrs on 29 December attacked Monjane village, less than 5 kms from the southern end of the LNG camp on the Afungi Peninsula, setting several homes on fire.  Sources later indicated 1 person was killed in this raid and 40 homes set on fire.  Residents meanwhile fled towards Senga village.

Five civilians were killed as a result of an insurgent attack at around 05:00 of 29 December less than 10kms south of the Afungi LNG Camp.   Workers at the camp were instructed to remain in their residences and a majority of road traffic between Palma and the LNG camp ceased. International companies operating in the area said they were in continual contact with the government over these attacks.

Tropical Storm Chalane in the late-night hours of 29 December was reported to have intensified by the National Institute of Meteorology (INAM), which announced the storm's winds had increased from 90 to 110 km per hour to 90 to 130 per hour, with gusts of wind of 150km per hour.  The Directorate of Water Resources Management meanwhile warns of floods in Beira, Dondo, and as far north as Quelimane.  Waves of up to 6 meters should be expected from approximately 0445hrs to 1656 on 30 December.  Satellite Imagery as of 0200hrs Maputo time showed Chalane close to making landfall north of Beira in Dondo and Muanza Districts.  Based on its current trajectory, the eye of the storm will pass over Central Sofala before passing over districts of Manica south of Chimoio before entering Eastern Zimbabwe at around 1400hrs.

Tropical Storm Chalane is expected to make landfall around 0500hrs with winds of between 90 to 100 kms per hour south of Beira and will impact Muanza, Buzi, Dondo, and the Beira areas initially.  Rains of 100 millimeters in much of Sofala on 30 December are also expected.  Chalane is expected to strengthen into a category 1 cyclone before striking Central Mozambique.  Chalane is also expected to generate waves of over 6 meters on Wednesday. The storm in a worst-case scenario the National Institute for Disaster Management (INAM) said on Tuesday could affect over 71,000 people, including 23,230 people in Beira.  The INAM has issued a red alert over the approaching storm.  Other sources however indicate that as many as 1.5 million people may be affected by the cyclone.  Authorities in Beira on Tuesday ordered the mandatory evacuation of several coastal areas. Zambezia and Manica are also expected to be impacted by the cyclone later in the day.  The Cyclone by Wednesday afternoon is expected to impact Zimbabwe.

Local sources stated that the murder suspects involved with the death of Former RENAMO deputy reportedly used a security force vehicle. Meanwhile, police officials stated that the murder was conducted by RENAMO dissidents.

RENAMO called for an inquiry into murder of former RENAMO deputy on 29 December. RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade stated that his party is still waiting for an answers regarding the murder from security forces.  Momade stated that the victim’s family stated that the victim was kidnapped by men wearing police uniforms.

Security officials announced that the former RENAMO deputy’s body was to be exhumed as part of investigations on 28 December. No specific date was stated when the exhumation would be conducted. The victim’s family requested police protection during the exhumation and a proper burial for the former RENAMO deputy.  It remains unclear who murdered the former deputy after his abduction earlier this month by uniformed men from his home in Chimoio.

National Health Institute (INS) warns of a possible second wave of COVID cases in Mozambique, with positivity rates rising slightly in late December to 6.9% of those tested. INS Director Gudo stated that the safety measures should be strengthened as the rise in cases has been noted in South Africa and nearby countries. Officials stated that the worst hit country in SADC is Africa with 18,423.6 cases per 1 million individuals in the country are infected.

The Ministry of Health announced another COVID related death and 62 new cases in Mozambique on 29 December. The death was recorded in a hospital in Maputo City. Maputo City still has the highest number of active cases with a total of 1,318 cases.  48 cases were reported in Maputo, 12 in Nampula, and 2 in Cabo Delgado.

NGOs delivered relief foods to around 4050 families in 79 communities of Maputo Province on 29 December. The aid was to ensure food security for the upcoming year starting from November 2020 to March 2021.

Chimoio residents are preparing for the arrival of Cyclone Chalane. Several locals stated that they could not leave the area due to not having any other area to live. Locals have reinforced their residences to ensure that the heavy gusts will not damage their residences. Roads were also repaired to improve access to the area.

The Municipal Council of Beira encouraged residents to store medical aid, food, and water for next few days in preparation for the possible impacts of Tropical Storm Chalane. The officials also requested civilians to stay at home and avoid “places of risk” as cyclone approaches. The call for preparation comes as Tropical Storm Chalane is expected to become severe as it passes through the Mozambique canal towards the country.

Beira Municipal Council issued on Tuesday, 29 December an order for the mandatory removal of locals from high-risk locations in preparation for the arrival of Cyclone Chalane. Officials stated that coastal areas of Dama, Rio Lolio, Praia Njalane, Casa Partida and Praia Nova must be evacuated. In addition, maritime travel has been suspended along the Sofala coast while businesses were closed in the city ahead of the approach of the cyclone.
Officials evacuated IDPs displaced by Cyclone Idai from Nyamatanda camp in Chimanimani.  The evacuation was in preparation of Cyclone Chalane.

Mozambique Airlines (LAM) announced the cancellation of flights due to the Cyclone Chalane approaching Mozambique on Tuesday, 29 December. LAM stated that flights from Maputo to Tete, Quelimane, Beira and Nampula have been cancelled and will be rescheduled after the storm passes. The following flights are as follows: For 29 December: TM 136/137 Maputo-Tete-Maputo, TM 1104 Maputo-Quelimane-Beira-Maputo, TM 1156 Maputo-Beira-Nampula-Maputo, TM 190/191 Nampula-Lichinga-Nampula. For 30 December: TM 1130 Maputo-Nampula-Tete-Maputo, TM 100/101 Maputo-Beira-Maputo, TM 110/111 Maputo-Chimoio-Maputo, TM 136/137 Maputo-Tete-Maputo, TM 144/145 Maputo-Quelimane-Maputo.

Security forces detained a suspect for burying his child alive in Mavoco of Boane on 26 December. Security forces recovered the body of the child during an investigation on the residence of the suspect.

Security forces detained a suspect for burying his child alive in Mavoco of Boane on 26 December. Security forces recovered the body of the child during an investigation on the residence of the suspect.
Police arrested several suspects and seized 780kg of tourmaline stones in Mirrote, north of Nampula, on the 30 December. The suspects lacked adequate papers to transport and sell the stones.

Tropical Storm Chalane made landfall in Beira of Sofala Province in the early morning of 30 December. Chalane was reported to have sustained winds of 85km/h with gusts exceeding 120km/h, and was officially classified as a "Severe Tropical Storm". Locals reported to have walked from Manga district to downtown due to the lack of transportation. Damages were reported in Praia Nova area, though the city's municipal council issued a statement saying the storm "did not cause much damage". Several powerlines and trees were toppled. 5 people were later reported to have been injured as the storm passed over Beira, though no fatalities have yet been reported.  Flooding due to heavy rains continues to be a threat in rural areas of Central Sofala and Manica as the storm moves west towards Zimbabwe.

The Central Hospital of Beira issued a warning of possible increase in diarrheal diseases brought about the Tropical Storm Chalane on the morning of 29 December. Hospital officials stated that no casualties have been reported during the storm.

The National Institute of Disaster Management (INGC) said on 30 December that as many as 1.2 million people in Mozambique could be impacted by Tropical Storm Chalane due to high winds and rains, and that the impact of the storm would be assessed in the coming days, initial assessments indicated that around 1,500 schools, 220 health units and several of the major roads in Sofala were affected by the storm.

South African officials said on 29 December that 34 border posts between South African and Mozambique will remain closed, except for the Kosibay Border Post to Ponta da Ouro into Mozambique, which be  reopened on 01 January.

Media reports on 30 December indicated that while several businesses were closed and few people moving about the city, there was only minimal damage caused by Tropical Storm Chalane in the city, after the storm passed over Beira on the morning of 30 December.

Mozambican officials on 29 December said that Mozambique had not imported any cases of a new more contagious strain of COVID-19 from neighboring South Africa.  Note that other sources said more than 100,000 South Africans crossed into Mozambique during the holidays.
The Ministry of Health announced two COVID related deaths and 113 new cases in Mozambique on 30 December. Both deaths were reported in Maputo city. 150 new recoveries were also reported for the day.
RENAMO leader Momade called for end of RENAMO dissident attacks in Central Mozambique. Momade stated that RENAMO dissidents are an insult to the Mozambican state.

The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) inspections were reported to be beyond the planned goal. A total of 31,072 inspections were carried out. The inspections were mostly products and commercial establishments. The Inspector General stated that the inspections were redoubled due to the pandemic.

Tropical Storm Chalane continued to head westward over Chimoio on the afternoon of 30 December. Chalane is generating 83km/h winds and that roofs were blown off after passing through Beira. A civilian was killed after he was electrocuted during the storm. Currently 240 individuals were homeless, 48 residences were destroyed, and 30 schools and health centers were heavily damaged.
Officials stated that no major damages were reported after Tropical Storm Chalane passed through Zambezia on 30 December. The storm reportedly knockdown trees, poles, and roofs.

Interprovincial bus transportation has improved after the ceasefire announced made by RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo. Drivers stated that the truce has allowed them to travel to RENAMO dissident prominent areas without fearing attacks and passengers have increase due to the ceasefire.

Mozambique's electricty company announced that several electrical transmission lines have been knocked down by Tropical Storm Chalane in Sofala on 30 December. Several interruptions were reported but no exact details were mentioned regarding the damages caused by the storm.

Local sources stated that forged negative COVID test results were being sold at black markets around 3,000-3,500 meticais along border crossings on 30 December. The results were being reportedly sold by employees working for the testing centers.

Daewoo Engineering & Construction won an LNG plant construction in Mozambique on 31 December. The estimated 455 million USD project involved the construction of two liquefaction trains and facilities in Afungi.

The National Road Administration (ANE)announced that the new toll fees would be imposed on 2 January. The new toll fees were part of the Self-Sustained Road Maintenance Program. The program was to cover eight toll bridges in Cabo Delgado, Nampula, Zambezia, Manica, Inhambane and Gaza.

Total on 01 January evacuated several of their employees from its LNG project in Cabo Delgado due to possible threats of an insurgent attack. The minimized workforce was in response to increasing insecurity near the LNG camp. Total continues to monitor the situation and is in contact with the government over insurgent attacks in the area.
The Ministry of Health announced another COVID related death and 57 new cases in Mozambique on 1 January. 17 new daily recoveries were also reported.
Security forces destroyed several seized fishing nets and illegal fishing materials in Thipani village near Larde on 31 December.

Security forces detained a suspected insurgent after arriving with IDPs in Paquitequete beach, north Pemba, on 1 January. The suspect was arrested after not being able to show national IDs and documents, and was reported to have arrived from Kiziwi Island.

Mozambican security forces at around 2200hrs on 01 January were reported to have targeted a house in Quitupo village after receiving information of insurgency activity in the area.  2 insurgents were found hiding in the house, and killed after a brief exchange of fire.    Security sources on 04 January largely confirmed the report regarding targeting insurgents in Quitupo, saying insurgents in the home opened fire on police and injured one officer, also saying that at least one insurgent was killed in the incident.  Security forces also said that there were insurgents "in three residences" in the area.  Some sources later disputed security force and media accounts of this incident, saying it had never occurred.
Insurgents in late December were reported to have left behind notes threatening a new attack in the vicinity of the LNG camp on 05 January.

Evacuations to Palma, Pemba, and other locations from the Afungi LNG Camp continued on Saturday after recent insurgent attacks on villages and towns close to the camp.  These evacuations took place after several recent insurgent attacks south of the LNG Camp, while insurgents also were active just outside of the camp on 01 January as evacuations began.

Mozambique's Ministry of Health recorded 341 Coronavirus cases on 3 January, marking the highest number of daily cases announced since infections were recorded in the country. One related death was also reported in Maputo city. This brings the total cases to 19,309. Maputo city currently has the highest number of active cases, recording 244. Maputo province recorded 50 cases, Gaza with 11 cases, Zambezia with 10 cases, 9 cases in Nampula, 7 in Sofala, 6 in Tete, 3 in Manica, and 1 in Inhambane.
A dead body of a 33-yr-old civilian was recovered on Costa do Sol bridge in Maputo on 01 January. The victim was presumed to have drowned. No other details on this incident are currently available.

A 12-yr-old girl was allegedly assaulted by a 34-yr old man in Ferroviario neighborhood, Maputo city, according to a report on 01 January by the City Police Command. The suspect was later arrested by the police.

A nine-yr-old girl was allegedly assaulted by a 27-yr-old man in Ferroviario neighborhood, Maputo city, according to a report on 01 January by the City Police Command. The suspect was later arrested by the police.

Security forces arrested two suspects over alleged involvement for sexually assaulting young girls in two separate incidents in Ferroviario neighborhood, Maputo city, according to a report on 01 January by the City Police Command. No other details on this incident are currently available.

The Ponta de Ouro border post, between South Africa and Mozambique, was reopened on 01 Jan after being closed for 9 months.  The post was closed since March 2020 as ordered by South African authorities in a bid to curb the spread of COVID-19 infections. Mozambican authorities reassured that the joint force of the immigration authorities and the Frontier Police is ready, and all the border services are in place for the re-opening of this border post.  All those crossing the border must display a valid negative COVID-19 test; the re-opening of the border is meant to ease pressure on the Ressano Garcia post into South Africa.

The Ministry of Health (MISAU) recorded on 02 January 174 new COVID cases and one more death bringing the total number of cases to 19,309 and total deaths to 169. The highest number of daily cases were reported in Maputo City as 108 cases were reported, with 38 in Maputo province, 11 recorded in Gaza, 10 recorded in Zambezia, six from Tete and one from Manica.

Due to the heavy rains and strong winds on 28 Dec, at least 1,085 people are in dire need of humanitarian assistance in Namirroa, Erati, according to the Administrator of Erati, Araujo Momade, on 31 Dec. Several houses and other properties were destroyed. National Disaster Management Institute (INGC) assured that aid and goods were on their way to the community.

On 02 January, the government of Zimbabwe imposed a 30-day national lockdown and closed its international borders in a bid to curb the spread of COVID-19 infection. No travel in or out of Zimbabwe would be allowed until the end of January.  The country has seen about 6,000 new COVID cases since the beginning of November, after recording just 8,374 cases up to the end of October.  Zimbabwe, along with Mozambique's other neighbors South Africa and Malawi, have all recently went into various forms of lockdown after recent COVID spikes.

A civilian was injured after being beaten by unidentified suspects in an area between the avenues of Eduardo Mondlane and Olof Palm Avenues in Maputo city, a source disclosed on 02 January. The attackers allegedly attempted to cut his genitals during the attack. The motive of the attack was still unknown.

Mozambique Minister of Health, Armindo Tiago,  announced that the government plans to start COVID vaccinations campaign around July of 2021, and could begin as early as May.  The vaccine will be received via the Covax vaccination program of the WHO, which plans to distribute 2 billion doses of the vaccine worldwide to 91 developing countries by the end of 2021. The campaign will start following the arrival of the vaccine between May and June. Around six million doses will be received, which will cover 20% of the country's population. Priority groups have been identified, however, details were not disclosed.  Neighboring South Africa meanwhile has said it will begin vaccinations in February.

Local media reported that Total had suspended all construction work at the Afungi LNG Camp in Cabo Delgado after recent insurgent attacks.  The company also released a statement over the weekend saying that it had reduced personnel at the Afungi site due to the "evolving security situation". The company and the Maputo government are now reportedly in consultations regarding the security situation outside of the camp. Total over the weekend was reported to have evacuated large numbers of personnel from the site, starting on 01 January; insurgents also clashed with troops just outside the perimeter fence of the camp at Quitunda village on the night of 01-02 January.  Several insurgent attacks elsewhere, south of Palma and the Afungi Peninsula, were reported in late December.

Insurgents on the night of 01-02 January were reported to have attacked the town of Olumbi in southern Palma District.  Militants set fire to several homes in the area and were still present in the town in the early morning hours of 02 January; no information on casualties is currently available.  Insurgents also attacked the town also on 29 December, reportedly abducting several people.  Olumbi is located less than 20 kms from the Afungi LNG Camp.

The UN's Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS) said on 31 December that it had officially begun operations in Cabo Delgado to provide humanitarian assistance to hard to reach areas of the province.  Over 500,000 people are currently displaced in Cabo Delgado.

Maputo City's Judicial Court on 31 December ordered the seizure of assets of a bookshop in Maputo's business district.   The bookshop reportedly owed one million meticais to a supplier, which led to this order.
3 children were reportedly sexually assaulted on 01 January in Nampula city, police officials reported.  No further details on this incident were immediately available.
Mozambique will avoid a recession in 2020, with a growth rate of 0.2%.  The country by some economists had been predicted to fall into recession in 2020 due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.
SERNIC agents in late December arrested several people in an undercover operation in Rapale, Nampula, after a man attempted to sell a woman to a group of people in the area.
3 members of a 10 man gang were arrested in late December by SERNIC agents on charges of having robbed an Islamic Association building of several items earlier in the month.

Sources reported that some recent successes against insurgents in Mozambique have been driven by the recent mobilization of elements of the Makonde ethnic group in Cabo Delgado, manifesting in the formation of local pro-government militias led by "former combatants".  The mobilization of these groups is reportedly due to efforts of Makone political leadership.

At least 12 boats are currently in Pemba harbor, loaded with food, equipment and other supplies, but are unable to travel between Pemba and Palma after recent bans on maritime travel between the two, local media reported on 02 January.

Major General Eugenio Musso in an address of Mozambican troops in Mueda on 03 January called 2021 a "decisive year to resolve the problem we have.  We have to annihilate the invaders", referring to Cabo Delgado insurgents.  Musso also criticized disinformation he said that was spread via social media regarding the Cabo Delgado conflict.

Police on 31 December - 01 January arrested a number of youths in possession of fireworks in Pemba.  The use of fireworks in the city had been banned for celebrations over the holidays this year, likely due to fears over potential insurgent attacks in the city.

Flooding caused by Tropical Storm Chalane over the course of 28 December was reported to have killed 7 people in Central Mozambique.  Three people drowned in flooding in Chimoio, the capital of Manica, one other person drowned elsewhere in Manica, while 2 drowning deaths were reported in Zambezia and 1 in Sofala.  10 people were injured in Sofala, Manica, and Zambezia by the storm while 36,000 people were impacted, while 15,000 were homeless. 12,000 houses were destroyed and 18,000 were partially damanged during the storm. Locals have called on the government on how to repair their residence if they do not have finances.

Ressano Garcia border crossing was briefly closed on 01 January after three immigration staff on the South Africa side tested positive for COVID.  Facilities on the South African side of the border were closed, disinfected, and later re-opened.

Police on 29 December arrested two people, a man and a woman, in Chiure, Cabo Delgado, after the two arrived from Macomia District.  The man reportedly had a bullet wound in his arm he was attempting to conceal, and police said the two were posing as a couple and were not in fact together.  It is unclear at this time police suspected the two of being involved in the insurgency.

Police detained an individual transporting firework on a vehicle for questioning in Pemba on the afternoon 30 December. The arrest comes after security officials imposed a ban on fireworks during the holidays.

Locals were reported on 31 December to returning to areas of central Macomia, particularly to villages near Macomia town itself, according to local sources on 31 December after insurgent attacks impacted much of the district during 2020. Macomia residents were assisted by security forces to reach their farmlands and residences in the area.
Local health officials announced that a cholera outbreak was reported in Memba on 31 December. Around 10 villagers were reported to be currently ill.

Local media reports indicate that a "network" of security and health officials are believed to be participating in a scheme to sell false negative COVID tests currently circulating in Mozambique.  Several of these tests have been found at the Ressano Garcia Border, and are sold from between 3,000 to 3,500 meticais.

Eletricidade de Mozambique (EDM) estimated around 10 million meticais or about 110 thousand Euros of losses due to the Tropical Storm Chalane. EDM officials stated that most of the losses were due to the damage to electrical transmission poles. Around 250 transmission poles of medium and low voltages were damaged in Manica and Sofala provinces.

Police arrested two suspects for killing their son in Vanduzi district of Manica on 4 January. The suspects confessed that they conducted the crime as a form of "black magic." They also stated that the victim was possessed by an evil spirit.

Police arrested two suspects for killing their son in Vanduzi district of Manica on 4 January. The suspects confessed that they conducted the crime as a form of "black magic." They also stated that the victim was possessed by an evil spirit.

South African police detained 23 Mozambicans for attempting to illegally enter South Africa and failing to produce negative COVID tests at the Ponta do Ouro Border Crossing and were transferred to Mozambique security forces.  The group said they could not afford COVID tests in Mozambique.

Traffic congestion was reported as a long line of cargo trucks were reported after a delayed opening of the Ressano Garcia Border Crossing on the morning of 3 January. The border crossing reportedly closed two and half hours before on Saturday, 2 January.

Armed individuals stabbed and injured a civilian before robbing him in Missao Roque in Maputo city at around 23:00 of 23 December. The victim was reportedly returning from work and was carrying a bag of squid.
Men armed with machetes attacked and injured a civilian in Maputo City on the evening of 25 December.

USAID in Mozambique announced on 04 January that the agency would work with Mozambique on the management of natural resources and fire in Niassa Special Reserve. The project will run through 2023 and has a budget of $900,000.

Security forces recovered the body of a soldier who was shot dead after not responding to the given passcode in the Muagamula area of Macomia District (just north of Macomia town) on the evening of 4 January. The drunk soldier had forgotten the passcode and attempted to enter the barracks, and was subsequently shot dead by fellow soldiers.  Another source later reported the man who was killed was a civilian; this is unconfirmed.
Travelers heading to Maputo were struck due to heavy traffic congestion along the National Road 4 (N4) towards Maputo on the morning of 4 January.

The National Petroleum Institute announced the resumption of drilling on Coral South LNG project in the coming days after an 8-month suspension due to the pandemic.  Drilling will likely resume in the coming days, with a drilling vessel present in Pemba on 05 January. INP stated that oil extraction is expected to begin in 2022.

6,000 people were reported to be stranded after flooding due to rains submerged a vital road in Changanine of Chibuto District on 5 January. Locals have called the government to repair the road. Other contractors stated that locals were assisted in taking alternative roads.

The Ministry of Health announced that 154 new COVID cases and two deaths in Mozambique on 04 January. 68 cases were recorded in Maputo city, 23 in Maputo province, 31 in Niassa, 15 in Zambezia, 12 in Gaza, 4 in Cabo Delgado, and one from Inhambane.

National Health Institute (INS) announced that Mozambique is acquiring new equipment to attempt to detect a new strain of COVID prevalent in South Africa.  No cases of this new strain have yet been detected in Mozambique.
An illegal miner died after the collapse of illegal mine in Namanhumbir at around 05:00 on 31 December. Officials stated that the victim's body was recovered during the rescue operation.

National Institute of Meteorology warned of intense heat reaching temperatures of 36 to 42 degrees Celsius in Maputo, Gaza, and Inhambane on 6 January. INAM stated that the weather is expected to change as heavy to moderate rainfall by the end of the same day.
Police officials announced that 326 police officers were expelled from force in 2020. The officers expelled were involved with criminal activity.

Military registration across Mozambique for citizens aged 18 and above was launched on 04 January and will continue until 28 February.  Military officials hope to register more than 200,000 young Mozambicans for military service.  This registration is mandatory, though many still do not register for military service; there are expected to be 651,000 Mozambicans who will reach the age of 18 this year.

Military sources stated that two insurgents had infiltrated the Quitunda area just outside of the Afungi LNG Camp on or before 01 January, hiding among refugees who had fled the Mute area after previous insurgent attacks in that village.  An investigation was conducted in response to the report of the insurgent presence in the area, with at least one insurgent shot dead.  One other source reported this infiltration occurred after insurgents attacked the village of Monjane/Mondlane on 29 December, with several insurgents infiltrating among refugees fleeing from the village.

Total was reported to have evacuated 500 employees to Pemba on 01-02 January. Around 3,000 employees were currently staying at the Afungi LNG Camp.  Other personnel were reported to have been withdrawn into Palma town.

Heavy traffic congestion continued at Ressano Garcia border crossing on the afternoon of 5 January. The delay was due to the verification of the required negative COVID test result. A 15km line was reported along National Road 4 (N4). Around 5 rows of vehicles were reported on both sides of the road allowing only one lane for both sides to travel on. Locals stated that no food or water were available at the border crossing and the border guards have turned locals away from crossing to South Africa.

Security forces deployed to Namandingo village near Maganja village, southeast of Palma, on 2 January, after insurgents had infiltrated a village just outside of the LNG camp the day before.  The villagers reportedly fled due to the deployment but then later returned to the area.

Niassa police commander Arnaldo Chefo on 05 January warned that insurgents could potentially infiltrate Niassa from Cabo Delgado. The PRM commander stated that police have been deployed in Niassa against the possible infiltration of insurgents into the province. There has been at least one clash in Niassa suspected to have been related to the insurgency in early 2020.
A minibus overturned in Nampula city on the morning of 5 January. 18 civilians were injured.  Two of those injured were hospitalized while the rest were discharged.

Cabo Delgado declared a cholera outbreak on 06 January in Montepuez after one death from the disease and 11 infections were reported in the area.  Cholera outbreaks in Cabo Delgado in 2020 occurred in Metuge, MDP, Macomia, Ibo, Pemba, and Montepuez Districts.  2,125 cholera cases were reported in Cabo Delgado in 2020.  The spread of the virus in Montepuez is concerning due to a large number of IDPs in the area.

The WFP on 06 January said that food assistance in Cabo Delgado could be reduced or even halted in March due to a lack of funding.  The organization said it requires $10.5 million a month to provide food assistance to 750,000 people, including 500,000 IDPs and 250,000 people in host communities impacted by the ongoing insurgency.  The WFP needs $132.4 million for 2021, but has only secured $24.4 million in funding for the year so far.

Sources on 05 January reported large numbers of Mozambicans crowded along the Ponta do Ouro Border post attempting to cross into South Africa.  Long queues were reported due to requirements that those entering South Africa having to provide a negative COVID test obtained within the past 72 hours.  A lack of food, water, and facilities and poor conditions have been reported at the border.

A single source on 05 January reported that a "foreigner" attempting to infiltrate government forces had been captured in an unspecified location in Cabo Delgado.  The captured man was reportedly attempting to scout army positions.  The nationality of the man was not revealed.

Portuguese Defense Minister Joao Gomes Cravinho on 06 January said that there would be a "very significant reinforcement" of military cooperation with Mozambique in terms of military training in the first half of 2021.  The minister said Portugal was working on an "exact definition" of what this deployment would entail.  No specific date for this deployment has been specified.

The Mozambican Navy has reportedly increased surveillance of Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) port, Mozambican Defence Minister Jaime Neto said on 06 January. He also acknowledged the continued presence of insurgents in the area district, though denied that insurgents still control MDP itself.  Neto also said operations were underway to "annihilate the enemy".  Despite this claim, there are no indications that the government has retaken MDP.

The Ministry of Health announced that 79 new COVID-19 cases were in Mozambique on 05 January. All of the 79 cases were in home isolation. 23 of the cases were from Maputo city, 20 from Niassa, 13 from Sofala, nine from Manica, seven from Gaza, four from Cabo Delgado, two from Tete and one from Maputo province. No Covid-19 deaths were reported and the death toll currently stands at 171.

The Ministry of Health announced that 125 new COVID-19 cases and one COVID-related death were recorded in Mozambique on 06 January. The total number of confirmed cases in the country increased to 19,667, while discharged cases were 17,141 and deaths 172.  40 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 37 in Manica, 9 in Sofala, 6 in Cabo Delgado, 6 in Tete, 4 in Gaza, and 1 in Niassa.

More than half of 700 Zambezia contractors have reportedly declared bankruptcy due to the COVID-19 pandemic and insurgency in northern and central Mozambique. In addition to these uncontrollable factors, contractors were also competing with Maputo contractors. Zambezia Provincial Contractors Association claimed that local works were awarded to other contractors instead of prioritizing local companies.  Contractors have appealed to local government for assistance.

National Civil Identification Service have begun to issue identification cards to more than 500,000 internally displaced people in Cabo Delgado, media reported on 06 December. Technicians of the agency have begun working in the accommodation centers in Metuge and Pemba districts. The three-month documentation campaign period, funded by the United Nation Children's Fund, came after an assessment revealed that IDPs who lost their valuables would need identification to access government services which include land licenses.

1,591kg of live mangrove crabs were seized by Fisheries Inspection authorities from fishermen along the coastline of Beira City over illegal fishing during 'closed season'. In addition, two vessels used to ferry the illegally caught crustaceans were also seized while two individuals were released after being detained over alleged connection with the illegal fishing. The closed season ran from 15 October until 31 December.

Nampula city is facing a water crisis, following a significant demand among residents.  Reports suggest that a water drum currently costs 10 to 15 meticais vs previous amount of two meticais.  Residents were worried that if the crisis continues, outbreaks of diarrhea associated with cholera may soon occur.

Officials at the Lebombo border post in South Africa denied entry to citizens of Mozambique who have taken a rapid COVID-19 test at the Ressano Garcia border post in Mozambique. Several travelers were stranded as a result of the incident. One of the affected travelers claimed that when they arrived in Mozambique, after being denied in South Africa, with no officials was there to assist them. As of midday in Mozambique, the queue of vehicles at the Ressano border crossing has increased in length from 15 to 17 KM.

Mozambican Police (PRM) with National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) seized and recovered three AK-47s, five pistols and two SKS, in Maputo City, Manica and Niassa on 06 January. No other details on these operations are currently available.

Mozambican Police (PRM) with National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) seized and recovered three AK-47s, five pistols and two SKS, in Maputo City, Manica and Niassa on 06 January. No other details on these operations are currently available.

On 30 December, security forces seized seven firearms, four pistols and two shotguns in Maputo City and Maputo Province.
Mozambican Police announced on 23 Dec that two pistols and two shotguns were seized during operations in Cabo Delgado and Maputo Provinces.
Mozambican Police announced on 23 Dec that two pistols and two shotguns were seized during operations in Cabo Delgado and Maputo Provinces.
Mozambican Police announced on 16 Dec four AK-47 type of firearms, two pistols, two SKS and two shotguns were seized during operations in Niassa and Cabo Delgado.
Mozambican Police announced on 16 Dec four AK-47 type of firearms, two pistols, two SKS and two shotguns were seized during operations in Niassa and Cabo Delgado.
Mozambican Police announced on 09 Dec that five firearms were seized during operations in Maputo City and Gaza. Three of the weapons were pistols, another one was a shotgun and a short-gun.
Mozambican Police announced on 09 Dec that five firearms were seized during operations in Maputo City and Gaza. Three of the weapons were pistols, another one was a shotgun and a short-gun.

Mozambican authorities on Thursday morning announced they would no longer accept rapid COVID-19 test results from South Africa at the two countries' mutual borders.  This came after South African authorities in recent days had refused to accept COVID-19 rapid test results carried out in Mozambique, creating massive lines at the Ressano Garcia Border Post as Mozambicans attempted to enter South Africa.  Mozambican officials say they will only allow PCR rests carried out by certified laboratories.
column15: Ressano Garcia and Ponta do Ouro Border Posts

column4: The Ministry of Health announced four COVID deaths and 294 new cases were reported in Mozambique on 7 January. The deaths were reported in Maputo city and Nampula. The cases were recorded as follows: 158 in Maputo city, 45 in Sofala province, 44 in Inhambane province, 27 in Cabo Delgado, 8 in Zambezia, 6 in Manica province, 3 in Maputo province and 3 in Tete province.

HIV/AIDs reportedly killed 582 people in Niassa province as of 2020. COVID restrictions have decreased programs to prevent HIV by 50%, which could trigger an increase in new cases and deaths in Niassa and elsewhere.

The National Operative Center announced that 63 individuals have died during the rainy season in Mozambique to date. 80 were injured and 112,464 were affected starting October 2020.  This included 7 people killed in Tropical Storm Chalane. The rainy season has destroyed 14,938 residence and partially damaged 23,116 homes. The rain has also affected the  classes of 124,700 students as 1,115 classrooms were destroyed.

Officials stated that a water shortage may occur due to the lack of rain in Maputo province. Officials stated that the dams that provide the city's water are at 18 percent capacity and that possible restriction on water usage may be taken if the lack of water continues.

More than 21,000 COVID cases were reported in South Africa, a record number of cases for the country.  South Africa also on 06 January reported 844 new COVID deaths, a dramatic rise in deaths in the country.  The new spike in COVID cases in South Africa is due to a new COVID strain that is more contagious; no cases of this new strain have yet been detected in Mozambique.

A Chinese national died after suffocating caused by a fire that broke out inside a cabin of a ship in Quelimane Fishing Port at around 01:30 on 7 January. An investigation was conducted to determine the cause of the fire.

Suspected FDS members forcibly abducted two civilians after raiding a residence in Sembezeia of Sussundenga district at around 20:00 of 29 December. The man's family says on 30 December local police officials said security forces were not involved in the abduction of the man.  One other sources reported two people were abducted in this incident.  The case bears some similarities to the case of former RENAMO deputy Sofrimento Matequenha, who was detained by "uniformed" men in December and later found dead in Gondola District.  Security forces also denied arresting Matequenha.  Sources later reported the two were detained on charges of being connected to the RENAMO Military Junta, but were released by 08 January.

The Mozambique government conducted talks with the South African government to resolve the increasing traffic congestion at the border crossing brought about by the earlier closing times of the crossing in the South Africa. The border crossing was scheduled to close at 21:00 and reopen at 06:00 which is considered to the most busiest border crossing between the countries.

UN envoy to Mozambique Mirko Manzoni stated that there is “favorable environment for dialogue” between the Mozambique government and RENAMO Military Junta. The announced unilateral truce by the RENAMO dissidents demonstrates that the group is expressing their attempt to end the conflict in Central Mozambique.  There have been no reports in recent weeks to indicate that these talks have been initiated.

Local sources stated that Turkey set up a spy network on 2016-2017 in Mozambique. The network was to monitor Turkish dissidents. The network reportedly had a list of individuals to monitor and was deployed in preparation for a large scale of activities which included to monitor the Turkish embassy.  Members of Turkey's Gullenist Movement were targeted in particular, and the Turkish government at the time made effort to pressure the Mozambican government to shut down businesses owned by Gullenists in Mozambique, though this effort was unsuccessful.

The Ministry of Health announced that  19 COVID cases were admitted into hospitals while six individuals were discharged during the past 24 hours. The admission were as follows: 15 in Maputo, two in Zambezia, one in Gaza and one in Sofala. Officials stated that the wards are currently experiencing the highest number of COVID admissions of the entire pandemic. Currently 71 patients are admitted in Maputo, six in Nampula, five in Zambezia, five in Tete, two in Manica, 1 in Sofala, and 1 in Gaza.
Insurgents on 05 January killed four people in an attack on Quirimba Island after militants landed on the island from the mainland.  Insurgents also stole a boat on the island.

Insurgents on 05 January attacked Olumboa and Darumba villages in Mucojo AP, forcing civilians to flee the area.  This came after reports that insurgents had also attacked nearby Quirimba Island on the same day.  No other details about the Olumboa and Darumba attacks are currently available.
Insurgents on the night of 06 January were reported to have landed and been present on Matemo island, though no attacks were immediately reported.

Insurgents on 05 January attacked Olumboa and Darumba villages in Mucojo AP, forcing civilians to flee the area.  This came after reports that insurgents had also attacked nearby Quirimba Island on the same day.  No other details about the Olumboa and Darumba attacks are currently available.

The United Kingdom on the evening of 07 January imposed a ban on passengers coming from Mozambique and other countries as a safety measure against a new strain of COVID-19 from South Africa, starting on 9 January. The passenger ban is expected to last at least two weeks.  The only exceptions to these rules will be British and Irish citizens, holders of long-term visas, and permanent residents, who must isolate for 10 days on arrival.  Flights to the following countries have also been temporarily halted: Angola, Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Namibia , Zambia, Zimbabwe, Seychelles, and Mauritius. This follows UK’s previous ban on flights with South Africa and those who had been in South Africa in the past 10 days which was announced on 24 December.  Note that the South African COVID strain has not yet been detected in Mozambique.

An investigation by local media reported on 08 January that Mozambican frontier police units are participating in a scheme in which illegal Mozambican migrants are smuggled into South Africa.  This scheme involves Mozambican nationals who lack documents being transported from Namaacha in private transport vehicles to the South African border at Macuacua, where there is no official border post.  Frontier police in the area are aware of these arrivals, but are paid to allow migrants to then cross the border.  The entire trip for one migrant costs approximately $20 USD.

Mozambican officials on 08 January announced 521 new COVID cases along with 5 new deaths.  30 new hospitalizations were also reported.  The case breakdown by province is currently unavailable.  This is the highest daily COVID total by a significant margin.  On 03 January, the previous high daily case total was reported with 341 cases.  This is a 52% increase in the highest daily case total.

Officials announced on 8 January, that Mozambique is one of the countries that will likely receive doses of the COVID vaccine from the Indian government.  The High Commissioner of India to Mozambique Kumar said two vaccines have been approved that will soon be distributed to some countries, of which Mozambique is considered a priority country.

The Ministry of Industry and Trade announced that the delays at Ressano Garcia border crossing could impact the trade between Mozambique and South Africa. Minister Mesquita stated that the curfew and COVID testing placed by South Africa have caused large queues and delays at the border crossing. South Africa previously imposed a curfew from 21:00 until 06:00 on their country’s side of the border crossing. South Africa Minerals Council Chief Economist stated that the delays have impacted chrome exports. Around a 25 to 32 percent decline was reported due to the pandemic; new restrictions along the border could further disrupt trade.

74 transporters in Maputo were fined for carrying excessive numbers of passengers in Maputo city as of 07 January. Police officials announced the imposed fines were part of the Operative Plan Festas since 15 December. A fine of 500 meticais per additional passenger was imposed.

Locals sources stated that the delays at Mozambique and South Africa border crossings continued on  08 January. Rapid COVID tests conducted in both countries were not being accepted by both countries.  Reports of tensions between countries was brought about the rapid testing from each country. Negotiations were conducted at the Ressano Garcia border crossing as the Ministry of Health officials, National Service of Migration (SENAMI), and Police conducted talks with South African counterparts.

Mozambique on 09 January reported 879 new COVID cases, a new record for daily cases in the country, along with 6 deaths, also a new deaths record reported in a single day in Mozambique.  This came after 521 cases were reported in the country on Friday, which was also a record number of cases at the time of reporting.  Previous to these new daily highs in cases, Mozambique had not previously seen a daily case load of more than 341.  Of the new cases, 547 were reported in Maputo City, 53 in Maputo, 83 in Inhambane, 45 in Zambezia, 38 in Manica, 36 in Tete, 28 in Cabo Delgado, 21 in Sofala, 15 in Nampula, and 13 in Gaza.

South Africa and Mozambique on 09 January were reported to have agreed on measures to ease long queues at the Lebombo Border, following a meeting between South Africa’s Home Affairs Minister Aaron Motsoaled and his counterpart in Mozambique, Naledi Pandor on the afternoon of 08 January. Among the measures agreed upon by the ministers as well as the ministers of health are as follows, truck drivers and co-drivers exempted from taking a COVID-19 antigen test, however, their employers will be responsible for testing the drivers every month. For trucks drivers who are carrying passengers, they will be tested together with their passengers.

Mozambique on 10 January reported 578 new COVID cases along with 5 new deaths, bringing the nationwide total number of COVID cases to 21,939 with 192 deaths.  Though down from Saturday's record of 879 new cases, the Sunday total is the second highest number of cases confirmed in a single day during the pandemic in Mozambique.  This is the third consecutive day in which Mozambique has reported over 520+ cases, after not having reported more than 341 cases on a single day previously.  293 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 69 in Nampula, 54 in Gaza, 51 in Maputo, 43 in Sofala, 35 in Tete, 13 in Zambezia, 11 in Inhamabane, and 9 in Cabo Delgado.  As of 10 January, there are 2,497 active cases in Maputo City, 390 cases in Maputo, 251 in Sofala, 214 in Nampula, 166 in Cabo Delgado, 143 in Inhambane, 125 in Manica, 113 in Tete, 112 in Zambezia, 103 in Niassa, and 94 in Gaza.

Two service counters of National Directorate of Civil Identification DNIC in Maputo City were closed on 11 January for disinfection after two cases of COVID-19 infection were recorded on 08 January. Services of the affected counters will be reopened on 12 January. Civil Identification Services will be available at 24 de Julho, KaMavote, KaMubukuane, KaTembe, KaMaxaquene and Magoanine service points.

Infantario de Matola, a local nursery in Matola in Maputo Province has run out of capacity due to the increase number of abandoned children sent to the institution. Most of the children have diseases that require special care as some were abandoned at the institution's gate by unknown people.

A group of 10 insurgents raided Matemo Island and abducted at least four people, a woman and three children, on 07 January.  Some sources later reported as many as 30 insurgents took part in this raid, and that as many as 21 people were kidnapped.  Some looting was also carried out by militants in the area.  The insurgents were reportedly guided to Matemo by fishermen they had kidnapped in the Olumboa area. The incident came a day after sources claimed that presence of insurgents were seen in the area.

Insurgents reportedly beheaded 8 fishermen in the area of Olumboa on 07 January. A second source reported 6 people killed in this incident. Insurgents had abducted a group of 19 fishermen in Olumboa and forced them to serve as guides for a raid on Matemo Island. The victims were fishing for crab and shrimp to sell at Matemo Island.  A military helicopter reportedly flew over the area during these beheadings, forcing insurgents to flee and halting these attacks.

On 08 January, Mozambican Frontier Police dismissed claims on their alleged involvement in the illegal immigration of Mozambicans into South Africa. The statement came after independent television station STV broadcasted a  detailed report on the aforementioned activities in the Macuacua area of the border.

President Nyusi on 11 January travelled to Tanzania for a two day visit for talks with the country's president, John Magufuli.  Mozambique's new top commander for the northern theatre, Major-General Eugenio Mussa, also accompanied Nyusi on this trip.  The two will discuss a joint response to terrorism along the border, as the Cabo Delgado insurgency, which has also spilled over into areas of Tanzania, continues.  Other issues such as economic and diplomatic ties will also be discussed.

Anthony Tata, the US's Acting Under Secretary of Defense for policy, met on 08 January with Mozambican Minister of Defence Jamime Neto and Minister of the Interior Amade Miquidade.  Tata reportedly discussed potential Department of Defense support for training to the Mozambican military to improve its capability to defeat insurgents in Cabo Delgado. Both sides reportedly agreed to "the importance of identifying needs in the areas of equipment and services including in strategic planning to counter this threat".

General Eugenio Mussa was recently promoted as the new commander of military forces in Cabo Delgado.  The exact date of this promotion is currently unclear.  Mussa previously had campaigned against RENAMO in Central Mozambique.  Mussa has now reportedly based himself out of Mueda, and appears to be assuming increasing control of operations in Cabo Delgado, after the counter-insurgency effort in the province had been largely directed by the police's Rapid Intervention Force.  Mussa on 11 January was reported to be in Tanzania, meeting with Tanzanian officials alongside President Nyusi.

The British High Commission on 10 January released a statement noting the record number of 879 COVID cases reported on 09 January, saying that this very large increase in COVID cases was likely due to the "abandonment of preventive measures against COVID-19 during the festive season", a statement also made by Mozambique's National Health Institute on Saturday.  The BHC in Maputo also recommended that all meetings, celebrations or "other activities which imply bringing large numbers of people together should be postponed".

395 new COVID cases on 11 January were reported in Mozambique, with 214 new cases reported in Maputo City, and 42 new cases reported in Niassa.  29 new hospitalizations were also reported in the country over the past 24 hours.

Security forces, reportedly acting on a tip from local sources, attacked insurgents on 08 January who had landed on Matemo island on Wednesday night.  Security forces were reported to have targeted a group of 10 insurgents, some of whom had sheltered in local homes and schools.  Police Commander Bernardino Rafael said that security forces were "sure that the terrorists had left" after this operation. 4 insurgents were reportedly killed, while at least 5 militants escaped the island in a stolen motorboat.  One other source later reported that a military helicopter had fired upon the insurgents, killing 4; this final detail remains unconfirmed.

A group of at least 10 insurgents on 07 January abducted at least 19 fishermen in the Olumboa area, killed at least 7 of them, and then forced a small number of them to serve as guides for an insurgent raid on Matemo Island.

Two people who had been detained in Sembezeia, Sussundenga, Manica Province, were released late on 08 January shortly after a story regarding their arrest on 29 December was reported.  Police reportedly initially denied they were involved in arresting the two people.  After the story was published, it was reported that the two were detained at Munhinga Police Post in Sussundenga, and they were released without charges.

Mozambique was reported on 11 January to have sent several samples of from COVID-positive cases in the country to the UK for analysis to determine whether or not a new strain of COVID prevalent in South Africa is spreading in Mozambique.  This comes after the country in recent days saw record numbers of new cases.

New security force operations in recent days have reportedly been launched targeting RENAMO dissidents in parts of Central Mozambique, according to security force sources.  A military spokesman on Saturday said that the armed forces had "already restored peace in the central region".

Eswatini on 08 January was reported to have tightened a lockdown in the country amid an ongoing spike in COVID cases.  The kingdom said international travel would only be allowed for medical attention, schooling, work, and business.  Social gatherings have been banned, and only funeral gatherings can not include more than 50 people.  These restrictions will be reviewed after 2 weeks.  Eswatini, South Africa, Malawi, and Zimbabwe of Mozambique's neighbors have all within the past 1 month tightened COVID lockdowns and restrictions as COVID cases have spiked across the region.

Nampula in 3 days registered 136 new COVID cases from 08 - 10 January, after reporting almost no cases in December and the first week of January.  The flouting of COVID restrictions over the Christmas period is believed to have triggered this spike in new cases.

Between 03-10 January, more than 130 people were hospitalized with severe COVID-19 cases, with over 2,000 positive cases reported and 15 new fatalities.  A majority of this new spike in cases, deaths, and hospitalizations occurred between 08-10 January; this represents the most significant COVID spike during the course of the pandemic in Mozambique, which began in March 2020.

South Africa on 11 January announced the closure of all land borders until 15 February except for transportation for fuel, cargo, raw materials, medical emergencies, diplomats, and citizens returning to the country.  This closure comes in response to what President Cyril Ramaphosa called a "massive increase" in COVID-19 infections in recent weeks. This closure includes the Lebombo Border Post across from Mozambique's Ressano Garcia.  All other restrictions including the ban on public gatherings of more than 50 people, night curfews, and a ban on alcohol sales and the closure of all beaches remain in place.  Air transportation in and out of South Africa will also remain open.

Tanzanian government representatives on 11 January told President Nyusi in talks that they will cooperate with Mozambique to fight against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  Coordinated efforts to combat the insurgents was the main topic of discussion between the two leaders, according to media reports.  The two sides also reiterated an agreement originally made in November to resume a joint commission on defense and security along the border.

A fire broke out due to a short circuit inside the IT section of the Central Office for Combating Corruption (GCCC) in Maputo on 11 January. An investigation to determine the cause of the fire was conducted. Center for Democracy and Development (CDD), Adriano Nuvunga, stated that the fire may be premeditated as several of the files containing cases involved government officials were present in the area where the fire occurred.  GCCC’s director stated that all of the files were backed up and none were lost. Nuvunga mentioned that security personnel were also possibly involved with the suspected fire and may not treat the case seriously.
