column4: Police arrested a 37-year-old for murdering his aunt in Inhassorro, north of Inhambane, on 9 January. The suspect used blunt weapons to murder the victim.
Police arrested a 37-year-old for murdering his aunt in Inhassorro, north of Inhambane, on 9 January. The suspect used blunt weapons to murder the victim.

Police arrested three siblings for murdering their mother in Zambezia on 9 January. The suspects initially filed a missing report to the police in late December, after killing her claiming she was using witchcraft.

Officials stated that around 900 displaced families are being resettled in Ancuabe District in Mesa AP. 950 land plots were given to the IDPs as part of the resettlement in Nanzua area of Ancuabe. Officials stated that the resettlement project would also include basic social infrastructure such as schools, health facilities, churches, and a police station.

The son of former President of Samora Machel, Samora Machel Jr. said that he had tested positive for COVID. Machel tested positive after suffering from a high fever. Machel also said that the general laxity of the public has brought the increase in cases.

The South African border of the Ressano Border Crossing reportedly opened at 9:30 on Sunday, 10 January. The late reopening of the border has continued to delay entries to both countries, even with the new improvements imposed. This comes as the South African side of border opened at 11:00 on Saturday, 9 January. Officials stated that 43 individuals have tested positive at the border crossing.

Officials stated that a traveler was denied entry to South Africa after having his test result returned but was able to cross on 9 January. The traveler initially attempted to enter on Friday, 8 January.

South Africa on 11 January announced the closure of all land borders until 15 February except for transportation for fuel, cargo, raw materials, medical emergencies, diplomats, and citizens returning to the country.  This closure comes in response to what President Cyril Ramaphosa called a "massive increase" in COVID-19 infections in recent weeks. This closure includes the Lebombo Border Post across from Mozambique's Ressano Garcia.  All other restrictions including the ban on public gatherings of more than 50 people, night curfews, and a ban on alcohol sales and the closure of all beaches remain in place.  Air transportation in and out of South Africa will also remain open. The border crossing would only be open to the following: Transportation of fuel, cargo, and goods. Emergency medical attention for a life-threatening conditions. The return of South African nationals, permanent residents, or persons with other valid visas. Travelling diplomats. The departure of foreign nationals. Daily commuters from neighboring countries who attend school in South Africa.

Border officials stated that around 75 positive COVID cases were confirmed at the Ressano Border Crossing towards South Africa on Saturday.  Subsequently, government officials deployed 20 additional health officials to screen travelers in response to minimize the positive cases entering the border crossing.

The Ministry of Health announced 157 active COVID cases were reported in Manica province during the first week of January, representing 33.9% of those tested for COVID recently in the province. National Institute of Health (INS), stated that the rate of COVID positivity was the highest compared to Nampula and Maputo province, which had positivity results of 29.4% and 29.1% respectively.  INS said that most of the new infections are aged between 30-39 years.
A child was killed during a hit-and-run near a gas station in Pemba at around 21:00 of 9 January.

Insurgents on Sunday were reported to have attacked the Quenhachimbuko/Quinhandoa area, killing an unknown number of people, close to Ingoane village.  This came after insurgents on Friday were reported to have been active in the Olumboa and Matemo Island areas, within about 30kms of this new attack.  Some local fishermen had reportedly recently returned to parts of Mucojo AP after fleeing the area in late 2020, triggering these new attacks.

A South African private military contracting company that recently signed deals with the Mozambican government to provide military equipment and training to the Mozambican military is reported to be setting up a new division to offer advanced training.  This training has an emphasis on asymmetric conflict, special forces operations support, as well as pilot and vehicle operator training and medical training.  It is significant that the company is now reported to be offering these new specialized training in the wake of reports of the company's agreement with Mozambique, though no further reports have yet indicated that the company will provide additional training or supplies to the Mozambican military.

Media sources reported on 07 January that "difficult talks" between Total and the Maputo government are scheduled for the near future.  Total will reportedly raise with the Maputo government several Cabo Delgado related issues, including the government's failure to honor security guarantees promised in October, the government's lack of offered political solutions, and the failure of military operations in Cabo Delgado to defeat the insurgency.  These sources also reported that South African private military contractors operating helicopters in Cabo Delgado have been of "limited effectiveness".

Media sources indicated that the French external security intelligence agency (DGSE) recently opened an office in Maputo.  There has been widespread speculation that France may look to offer Mozambique increased military support in 2021 to help combat the Cabo Delgado insurgency; particularly as French company Total continues to operate in the Afungi LNG Area.
A man murdered his wife in Aeroporto, west Quelimane, on the night of Monday, 11 January. Police managed to arrest the suspect the following day.
Police arrested a suspect wanted for the murder of his wife in Quelimane on 12 January.

Mozambique Airlines (LAM) announced the end of weekly flights between Lisbon and Maputo on 12 January. The cancellation of the scheduled flights was due to the COVID pandemic in Europe. The flights were initially scheduled to end officially on 15 January. These had been the first Mozambican airline flights to Europe in nearly 10 years.

The Ministry of Health announced on 12 January that initial COVID samples sent abroad for testing for the new South African COVID strain had tested negative. The samples were randomly collected.  There remains however significant fear that the new strain of COVID has spread into Mozambique from South Africa.  Mozambique will continue to test new COVID cases for the new strain over the coming days and weeks.

Long queues of travelers were reported at Lebombo Border Crossing towards Mozambique on 12 January. The long lines were possible reasons for spreading COVID. South African President Ramaphosa announced during his national address that 20 land borders in South Africa would be closed due to the increasing COVID cases.

South African Deputy Minister of Home Affairs conducted an inspection of security forces along the Lebombo and Ressano Border Crossing. The inspection comes after reports of illegal crossing of locals from Mozambique to South Africa. The inspection also comes as reports of long lines were reported at border crossings.

President Nyusi suggested that local youths in Cabo Delgado recruited by insurgents could be pardoned if they surrender. Nyusi said that the youths have been manipulated by the insurgents into being involved with the ongoing conflict. Nyusi also stated that some of the youth insurgents who recently participated in an attack on Matemo Island were “allowed to leave peacefully because the FDS knew that they were innocent.”

Locals sources on 11 January reported Nampula residents have continued to neglect anti - COVID measures in the city as cases continue to increase. Most of the city residents stated that COVID does not exist or they are immune to the virus. Health officials announced that 69 new cases were recorded in the city; there are now 214 active cases in Nampula.  As of 10 January, 932 individuals during the pandemic had tested positive for COVID-19 in Nampula, with 8 deaths and 711 recoveries were recorded.

Police arrested an insurgent in Matemo on 8 January. The insurgent was a 19-year-old local youth who denied the charges. The arrest comes after gunfire exchanges were reported after insurgents arrived on the island with at least 4 insurgents reportedly killed.

A fire broke out inside a health facility in Alto Molocue, southwest of Gurue, on the night of 12 January. The fire reportedly destroyed a large amount of medication. The medical storage stored materials for 17 hospital units. Only a small portion of medications were recovered.

Officials issued a flood alert for Mambone village due to the rise in water levels of the Save river. Officials stated that the river was at 4.62 meters, just one meter away from the flood alert level. The water levels on 11 January were at 3.38m and rose the following day.

South Africa’s Home Affairs Deputy announced that 300 undocumented Mozambicans were returned back to Mozambique through the Ressano Garcia Border Crossing on 12 January. This announcement came after South Africa announced the re-closure of its borders due to a new spike in COVID cases in the country.

The Ministry of Health announced that 4 new COVID deaths and 662 new cases in Mozambique on 12 January. The cases were recorded as follows: 204 cases in Maputo city, 198 in Manica province, 86 in Maputo province, 52 in Gaza, 21 in Cabo Delgado, 21 in Nampula, 17 in Inhambane, 12 in Tete, 8 in Sofala, four in Zambezia, and three in Niassa.

730 New COVID-19 Cases were reported on 13 January, including 311 cases in Maputo City and 185 cases in Maputo Province.  73 cases were reported in Inhambane, 46 in Gaza, 39 in Manica, 31 in Cabo Delgado, 29 in Sofala, 8 in Tete, 7 in Zambezia, and 1 in Nampula. 4 new deaths were also reported. There have now been 23,726 cases nationwide along with 205 deaths. 21 new hospitalizations were also reported. This is now the second highest total number of COVID cases reported in a single day during the course of the pandemic.

The SADC summit that was set to include the presidents of several countries from around the region as well as President Nyusi that was meant to be held in Maputo from 17-20 January to discuss the insurgency in Cabo Delgado was on 13 January postponed indefinitely due to increasing numbers of COVID-19 cases in Mozambique.  There are some reports as well that the Mozambican government was not prepared for this summit, though that has not been confirmed.

Mozambique's National Meteorological Institute announced on 13 January that a tropical storm was forming in the Indian Ocean, and could impact Madagascar by 19 January.  The storm could then enter the Mozambican Channel by 20-21 January, and then shortly thereafter potentially impact the Mozambican Coast.  It is unclear at this time the precise areas of the country the tropical storm would potentially impact.

Mozambican police officials on 13 January said that 21 people who had been abducted by insurgents in a recent raid on Matemo island had been rescued by police forces.  Police Commander General Bernardino Rafael said that police had tracked insurgents by "aerial means" and had been able to separate hostages from the insurgents.  15 women and 6 children were rescued, after having been transported from Matemo to "another region of the province" close to Olumboa village in Mucojo AP, close to Matemo island.  Some of the hostages later said a group of 30 militants had initally kidnapped the group, and had intended to take them to the de-facto insurgent capital of Mocimboa da Praia to "study in a madrassa" before a government helicopter arrived in the area to rescue the group. Sources later reported that at least 6 insurgents were captured in this incident.

Two Malawian government ministers, Lingison Belekanyama, Minister of Local Government and Muhammad Sidik Mia, Minister of Transport, died on 12 January from COVID-19.  There have been 50 COVID deaths in Malawi since 01 January, and Malawi is likely to announce a new more stringent lockdown due to the ongoing COVID-19 case spike in the coming days.

Beira Mayor Daviz Simango announced on 12 January that authorities in Beira would "reinforce" the enforcement of administrative measures put in place by the State of Public Calamity.  This includes cracking down on the operation of street vendors and preventing the "excessive consumption" of alcohol to prevent the spread of COVID-19.  All street vendors have been ordered to conduct business out of markets rather than the streets.  There are currently more than 200 active cases in Beira city, a majority of which have been detected since 01 January.

Health officials on 13 January said Maputo City was in danger of running out of intensive care beds for COVID-19 patients.  About 90% of beds at the Polana-Canico Health Centre are currently full; this is the primary COVID-19 isolation ward in Maputo City.  Another 200 beds can be added at Polana Canico and at Maputo Military Hospital, but after recent COVID case increases even these capacities could soon be exceeded.  116 COVID patients are currently hospitalized in Maputo City - out of 135 people hospitalized due to COVID in the country.

President Nyusi on 13 January in an address to the nation announced new restrictive measures to combat the ongoing COVID-19 spike in the country.  All new measures will take effect from 0000hrs 15 January and will remain in place for 21 days. The measures include: Closure of casinos, bars, "barracas", nightclubs, beaches, gymnasiums, cinemas, theatres, museums, and galleries.  Mozambican public beaches are also now closed. Closure of all commercial establishments by 1800hrs. Weddings and other private events must take place before 2000hrs. Religious services, conferences, and meetings cannot exceed 50 participants. Funeral ceremonies cannot exceed 20 participants; funerals of COVID victims cannot exceed 10 participants. Restaurants hours will be restricted from Monday to Friday to 0600hrs to 2000hrs, and 0600hrs to 1500hrs on Saturday to Sunday. Bottle Stores hours will be restricted from 0800hrs to 1300hrs, and will be closed on Sundays. All travelers must present COVID-19 tests upon entry/exit into/out of Mozambique obtained within 72 hours of departure. Expired documents will now be valid until 30 May, 2021. People with flu-like symptoms should not come to work.

Officials announced on 13 January that water reservoir levels are at almost 30 percent capacity due to the little rain in Nampula during the weekend. Officials stated that the threat of water shortage is constant and that FIPAG has deployed trucks transporting potable water to the city. Officials also said that eight water intakes and 31 additional fountains were being built in Namiteca, Muhala-Expansao, Namicopo and Muatala neighborhoods.

Mozambique's Minister of Transportation Janfar Abdulai announced that South Africa’s partial closure of borders threatens Mozambican economy due to the pandemic. Minister Abdulai stated that closure of the borders have reduced traffic and have paralyzed cargo transportation and tax collection. The border closures have reduced the incoming cargo load towards the ports in Mozambique.

The Portugal Parliamentary Committee on Foreign Affairs adopted a resolution to prioritize the Mozambican crises among the issues to be addressed during Portugal’s presidency of Council of EU. The resolution would also allow the Portuguese government to interceded with the international community to ensure efforts are being conducted in Mozambique.
At least 6 insurgents were captured on 13 January in an operation in the Olumboa area by security forces who also rescued at least 21 hostages taken by the group, local sources indicated.

UNICEF stated that 250,000 children have been displaced by insurgents in Cabo Delgado. The displaced children were also at risk from different water borne diseases due to the rainy season. The organization also mentioned that services for water, hygiene and sanitation are insufficient as displaced individuals have been increasing causing an overcrowding at displacement centers.

Health officials have announced the sudden increase of COVID case numbers in Inhambane on 13 January. Officials stated that the disregard for the anti-COVID measures have brought the increase in the province. Security officials have announced a strict reinforcement of precautionary measures against the pandemic. Overcrowding in public areas was reported as locals not wearing masks and lack of handwashing areas were the main cause for the increased cases in the province. At least 220 positive COVID cases have been reported in the province since the beginning of the year - after very low numbers of cases in the province in recent months.

The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) warned that cement prices had increased significantly in Maputo on 13 January. Prices have increased to around 445-465 Meticais, a 255 Meticais difference for a 50kg cement sack. INAE stated that they have conducted a survey to determine what the cause of the price increase was.

Health officials announced that Malaria deaths have decreased in Nampula last 2020. 64 deaths were recorded during 2020, a 78 decrease in comparison with 2019 which recorded 142 deaths. A total of 2.4 million were diagnosed with Malaria during 2020. The reduction of cases was due to the increasing preventive measures by health professionals and organizations.

The IOM is appealing for $2 million to support of Tropical Storm Chalane victims on 12 January. The $2 million was to assist 24,000 IDPs at resettlement centers and 61,000 locals who were affected. The call for support comes as the National Institute for Disaster Management and Risk Reduction stated that around 73,000 individuals were affected by the tropical storm. IOM’s assessment stated that 5,000 families in 52 resettlement sites in Manica and Sofala provinces were destroyed or damaged, along with five health centers and two schools.

Human Rights Watch (HRW) warned that the ongoing conflict in Cabo Delgado has deteriorated human rights in Mozambique. The “serious abuses” by security forces which have reportedly targeted journalists and locals in the province. The abuses were in relation with the worsening humanitarian situation in Cabo Delgado due to the insecurity and violence. The abuses by security forces included arbitrary arrests, abductions, torture, excessive force against unarmed civilians, intimidation, and extrajudicial killings, according to HRW.

HRW stated that abuses were also recorded in Central Mozambique due to the attacks cause by RENAMO dissidents. The organization also denounced attacks by RENAMO dissidents. The dissidents have continued to attack private and public vehicles in Manica and Sofala provinces, near Gorongosa. Around 24 individuals have been killed since August 2019 and at least six journalists were attacked during 2020, according to the local media reports.

Acrow Bridge Engineering and Supply Company announced on 13 January that it would provide the National Road Administration 26 modular steel bridges. The bridges will be installed in rural areas damaged by the 2019 Cyclone Idai in the country. The bridges were to enable the recovery of isolated regions and provide strengthened vital roads which are frequently impacted by disasters.

Police arrested seven suspects for embezzling 15 million meticais from the Education sector in Beira. Officials stated that 20 individuals were involved with the crime in secondary school of Matadouro and Josina Machel areas. The suspects requested the salaries and bonuses through the State Financial Administration System (SISTAFE) which enabled them to receive the monthly wages from 350,000 to 1 million meticais for each registered employee. The other 13 suspects are currently being pursued.

Mozambique government officials intends to fast track the restart of the 20 billion USD LNG project by an oil and gas company in Cabo Delgado. The Minister Energy Max Tonela stated that there has been no change to the schedule for the beginning oil extraction from the Rovuma Basin, and that the government is working with Total to resume activities at the Afungi LNG Camp.  Operations at the camp could potentially restart as early as February or March - though there is some potential that talks between Total and the government could delay the restart of operations at the camp for a longer period.

Mozambican military units on 09 January reportedly exchanged fire with a group of pro-government militia in Muidumbe District; it is unclear exactly where in the district the incident occurred.  There were reportedly a number of casualties in this incident though no further information is currently available.

Civilians attempted to recover their property in Muidumbe District after insurgents largely took over most of the district in November have reportedly not been able to do so, with soldiers preventing local residents from returning to their homes, according to local reports.  Soldiers have recently been reported to have blocked local residents from returning into the Matambalae area to retrieve property.

President Nyusi via a Presidential Order on 14 January officially appointed Eugenio Ussene Mussa to the rank of General of the Army, and to the post of Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Defense of Mozambique. Mussa previously held the position of Commander of the Civic Service of Mozambique, and he replaces Lazaro Henriques Menete, who had led the army since 2017.  Mussa had recently been reported to have been put in charge of directing the Mozambican military's operations against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

The National Director of Medical Assistance stated that 68 percent of COVID patients being hospitalized in Mozambique require at least 10 days of care. There have been significant rises in COVID-related hospitalizations and deaths in recent days, with 19% of all deaths due to COVID in Mozambique occurring since 01 January.

The Ministry of Health announced a reduction in cataract surgeries in Mozambique due to the COVID pandemic. Around 5,000 cataract surgeries were performed in 2020, half of what was conducted last 2019.

Mozambique health officials announced on 14 January that the Maputo Military Hospital is being prepared to receive COVID patients. The announcement comes as hospitalizations are increasing in the country. The military is able to accommodate 100 beds. Officials stated with short notice, the Maputo Military Hospital and the Polana Canico Hospital can make 200 more beds available to COVID patients.

Security forces conducted arrested around 80 suspects for attempting to cross the Mozambique-South Africa towards South Africa on 14 January. The arrest comes as South Africa announced the closure of its borders as a precaution to slow the infection of the pandemic. African National Congress stated that around 300 Mozambicans were detained during the past two days along the border attempting to illegally enter South Africa.

Locals stated that increase in prices on potatoes have made it so expensive that the public has avoided in purchasing them in Nampula. Vendors stated that the potatoes have expired due to the decrease in sales.

President Nyusi confirmed that the Mozambique government has applied to receive COVID vaccines from the WHO. The vaccines would cover at least 20% of Mozambican population. The application was conducted as Mozambique qualifies for the subsidized vaccines under the COVAX facility.
Mozambique Tax Authority announced that the country loses 12.9% of GDP due to illegal exports. Tax Authority Muendane announced that the country’s GDP is around 14.9 billion USD as of April 2020.
6,000 displaced individuals are sheltering in Namanhumbir AP in Montepuez District on 14 January. Around 500,000 IDPs were reported to not have shelter and food across Cabo Delgado.

The construction of a floating LNG platform continues to progress in the waters of the Rovuma Basin.  The platform is expected to be completed in early 2022, in time for the arrival of a module to allow the exploration of LNG resources in the area.  Another vessel that will drill offshore oil wells is also expected within the next one month.

On 12 January, Florence Parly, France's Minister of the Armed Forces, said that France found the situation in  Cabo Delgado "very worrying" and that France was "seeing how we can support" via training, also saying France would "Like to be able to  it with our European partners" with French military units stationed at Reunion Island and in Mayotte.  French troops stationed in the area are the 2nd Marine Infantry Parachute Regiment along with French Foreign Legion Units stationed at Mayotte.  Several French naval vessels are also based out of these territories.  There has been speculation in recent months that France could potentially provide naval support to Mozambique along the Cabo Delgado coast to crack down on insurgent maritime activities in the area.

An investigation by local media reported that poachers in Zimbabwe in recent years have colluded with police officers to transport ivory across the Zimbabwean border into Mozambique to Mozambican ports, and then to Chinese fishing boats operating in Mozambican waters.  These boats often gather ivory for up to six months before shipping ivory back to China.

The closure of Lebombo border crossing in South Africa has reduced the crossing of civilians from Mozambique by 1,900. National Migration Service stated that around 3,500 civilians usually cross the border. The closure comes as South African officials conducted safety measures against the increase number of COVID cases.

The Ministry of Health announced 6 new COVID deaths and 543 cases in Mozambique on 24 January. 178 cases were recorded in Maputo City and 161 were recorded in Maputo Province.  45 people have now died of COVID-19 in the first two weeks of January, the highest number of deaths from COVID since the beginning of the pandemic in the country.  178 new cases were reported in Maputo City, and 161 in Maputo Province.  27 new hospitalizations were also reported during this period.

On the evening of 14 January, at least two cases of a new, more contagious strain of COVID-19 originating in South Africa were detected in the Nantes region of France from among a group who had recently returned from Mozambique.  One patient has been hospitalized in Paris in critical condition, and had spent 10 days in December in Mozambique as part of a religious group's trip to the country.  It was not immediately clear where the group had travelled within Mozambique when they were in the country.

On 15 January, 735 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique, including 243 new cases in Maputo City, 273 in Maputo Province, 98 in Zambezia, 53 in Sofala, 48 in Manica, 23 in Cabo Delgado, 20 in Tete, 8 in Niassa, and 5 in Nampula. 5 new deaths were also reported during this time.  There have now been 25,004 COVID cases in the country, along with 216 deaths.  There are currently over 5,000 actives cases in the country, including 3,227 active cases in Maputo City.

A military helicopter on 08 January flew over Olumboa in Mucojo AP while insurgents were beheading a group of fishermen, sources reported, forcing insurgents to flee from the area and reportedly stopping these killings.  8 people had been killed in this attack, though 11 were able to escape.

Sources reported that security forces had carried out "bombings" of insurgent positions on the morning of 14 January in the Mucojo and Olumboa areas of Macomia.  It was unclear if these were airstrikes, strafing, or artillery fire targeting insurgents in these areas.  No further information on these incidents is currently available.

Sources reported that security forces had carried out "bombings" of insurgent positions on the morning of 14 January in the Mucojo and Olumboa areas of Macomia.  It was unclear if these were airstrikes, strafing, or artillery fire targeting insurgents in these areas.  No further information on these incidents is currently available.

Medical professionals are not observing anti-COVID measures while assisting locals at health centers in Maputo. Local sources stated that most individuals entering the health centers are wearing mask while medical staff were not well-equipped. Locals stated that there were no temperature checks outside the hospitals, lack of handwashing, and disinfection procedures.

A patient claimed that he was “beaten” by two medical staff at Hospital Psiquiatrico Do Infulene in north Maputo city on 15 January. The patient stated that he was assaulted after refusing to take his medication.
