column4: South African border security detained 90 individuals who attempted to cross border towards Lebombo from Ressano Garcia on Thursday, 14 January.  South African media stated as much as 200 illegal immigrants were detained on 13 January. The Immigration Affairs stated that the humanitarian situation at border crossings was concerning due to the lack of anti-COVID measures.

South African border security detained 90 individuals who attempted to cross border towards Lebombo from Ressano Garcia on Thursday, 14 January.  South African media stated as much as 200 illegal immigrants were detained on 13 January. The Immigration Affairs stated that the humanitarian situation at border crossings was concerning due to the lack of anti-COVID measures.

Zimbabwean Minister of Provincial Affairs died of COVID on Friday, 15 January. Minister Ellen Gwaradzimba was previously suffered from COVID related complications.  This comes amid a region-wide COVID spike across Southern Africa; two Malawian Ministers also died of the virus in recent days.

Police arrested four poachers and recovered seven ivory tusks in Cuamba district, south Niassa province on 15 January. The suspects were transporting the poached goods to the buyers when they were arrested.

National Migration Service (SENAMI) stated that there were 728 deportations from South Africa and Eswatini between 14 December 2020 to 15 January. SENAMI spokesman stated that 665 were returned through Ressano Garcia, 65 from Ponta D’Ouro, and 114 from Namaacha.  630 were deported due to illegal immigration, and 98 due to an "illegal stay”.

858 new COVID cases were reported on Saturday in Mozambique, bringing the nationwide total number of cases to 25,862.  298 cases were reported in Maputo City, 208 in Maputo, 117 in Manica, 113 in Gaza, 54 in Niassa, 28 in Sofala, 24 in Cabo Delgado, 14 in Nampula, and 2 in Zambezia. 18 new deaths, including 17 in Maputo City were also reported.  This was the highest number of deaths due to COVID-19 in a single day, and brought the total COVID death toll in Mozambique to 234.

Mozambican Police arrested four individuals in four different cases of forgery of identification cards in Maputo Province, Alberto Sumbane, spokesman of National Directorate of Civil Identification (DNIC) disclosed on 16 Jan. The arrests, whose details were not disclosed, were reported by a bank agency to DNIC following an increase in cases of forgery of ID cards used to open bank accounts and embezzle banks. Sumbane urged the citizens to report to police authorities  and DINIC in cases of lost ID.

Illegal fishing declined in Bazaruto Archipelago National Park (PNAB) of the Inhambane coast to 85 recorded cases in 2020 against 162 in 2019, Tomas Chibale, head of PNAB Protection and Inspection, stated on 16 Jan. He added that strict inspections were implemented this year as 25 vessels used for illegal fishing were seized in 2020 while in 2019 the authorities confiscated four.

Sources reported on 17 January to Mozambican Police (PRM) has suspended the district commander of Morrumbala, Afonso Dias, accused of having a relationship with a 16-yr-old child. The Zambezia Provincial Prosecutor's Office demanded his suspension while the investigation is still ongoing.  A source claimed that while in position, Dias were threatening witnesses to refrain to speak against him.

Another tropical cyclone, Eloise, is likely to enter the Mozambique Channel on 21 January after passing over Madagascar. Based on its present course, Cyclone Eloise will make landfall in Madagascar on 20 January with winds of over 90KM/hour. The tropical storm will slow down upon passing through the lands of Madagascar, however, it is expected to grow stronger once it reaches the Mozambican Channel. Joint Typhoon Warning Centre (JTWC) stated that the likely wind speed of Cyclone Eloise is 70KM/hour once it enters the Mozambique Channel.  The storm could then potentially impact Central Mozambique next weekend.

Security forces arrested five individuals in Chihango neighborhood of Maputo city, authorities announced on 17 January, over their alleged involvement in drug trafficking and illegal possession of firearms. Two pistols and 21 ammunition were recovered from the suspects.  One of the suspects was a Nigerian national, while another was a South African national.

Insurgents on the afternoon of 16 January ambushed three vehicles of a six vehicle convoy, some of which were carrying a football team from Mueda, travelling near Pundanhar, Palma from Nangade. The attack killed 6 people while others were allegedly missing. The targeted vehicles were destroyed while other items were looted by the insurgents.

No traffic was reported along the Nangade-Palma road on 17 January after insurgents attacked a convoy of vehicles and killed at least 5 people along this route on 16 January.  This route for months has been intermittently attacked by insurgents, and is usually closed down for a short time after these attacks.

Chimoio Mayor, Joao Ferreira, tested positive for COVID-19 and is currently in home isolation. Mayor Ferreira stressed the importance of the adherence of the preventive measures as the disease was serious especially with symptoms.

689 new COVID cases were reported on 17 January in Mozambique, bringing the nationwide total number of cases to 26,551.  290 cases were reported in Maputo City, 138 in Inhambane, 52 in Gaza, 52- Sofala, 33 in Maputo, 25 in  Nampula, 21 in Zambezia, 19 in Niassa , 16 in Tete and 14 cases in Manica. Seven new deaths, including five in Maputo City were also reported which brought the total COVID death toll in Mozambique to 234.

President Nyusi on 14 January promoted Bertolino Capitine to the position of Deputy Chief of Staff of the FADM, replacing Raul Dique.  In keeping with Mozambican military tradition since 1994, the deputy chief of staff is drawn from the ranks of RENAMO. As previously announced, Nyusi also promoted Eugenio Mussa to the role of Chief of Staff of the military.

895 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 18 January - the highest COVID total in a single day during the course of the pandemic.  There have now been 27,446 total cases in the country.  8 new deaths were also reported, the second highest daily death toll of the pandemic.  315 cases were reported in Maputo City, 182 in Maputo, 126 in Zambezia, 119 in Inhambane, 81 in Niassa, 52 in Sofala, 11 in Gaza, 8 in Manica, and 1 in Tete. 43 new hospitalizations were also reported countrywide over the last day - there are now 219 people hospitalized across the country, of whom 173 are in Maputo City.  There are 8,313 active cases in Mozambique, including 5,276 in Maputo City.

Local media reported that some corrupt military officers in the Mozambican army in Nampula will accept a bribe of 3,000 meticais (or about $40) from new recruits which will allow them to more quickly advance through the ranks of the military.

Sources on Monday reported that security forces had deployed towards Mucojo, according to residents of Macomia town, after recent insurgent activity in that area.  No further details on this deployment are currently known.

Agaia Mario, the government of Cabo Delgado's Provincial Director of Economic Activities, said on 14 January that insurgent attacks had forced 80,000 households in the province to abandon agriculture since 2017, endangering food security in the province.

A local media station reported that a "racket" in which border police are bribed to allow Mozambican nationals to illegally cross the border into South Africa in the Macuacua area is still ongoing - despite police claims to the contrary.  Local media initially reported on this illegal operation earlier in the month.

The Integrated Classification of Food Security Report was released on Monday, 18 January for Mozambique, and indicates that an estimated 2.9 million people in Mozambique will face "severe food insecurity" between January and March.  This will include 2.1 million rural residents and 800,000 urban residents.  About 20% of those facing food insecurity are in Cabo Delgado province, primarily due to the impact of the insurgency.  The situation is expected to improve between April - September.

Nampula Province said on 18 January that there are currently 41 active COVID cases among health workers in the province; there have been 133 total confirmed cases among health workers in Nampula during the pandemic, though no deaths.

The EU's representative for foreign policy Josep Borrell said on 15 January that the EU mission to Mozambique is set to begin on Tuesday, and that "all procedures will prepared" , and only a final Mozambican government authorization was necessary for the mission to begin.  The mission will be led by Portuguese Foreign Minister Augusto Santos Silva, and is meant to travel to Cabo Delgado, pending security conditions allowing this.  Borrell indicated that coastal surveillance missions along the Cabo Delgado coast were being considered as a possible intervention to be offered to the Mozambican government.

President Nyusi on 16 January called on RENAMO Military Junta leader Mariano Nhongo to surrender before "it is too late", and join the DDR process, saying Nhongo could do this "through the contact channel at his disposal" and that the same was true of the "followers of Matsangaissa junior".  Nyusi also said in this speech that RENAMO's "demands" had been met in previous talks.  This comes after RENAMO dissident leader Nhongo recently called for new talks with the government.

Angola and Mozambique held a bilateral defense and security summit on 12-13 January, with Mozambican Defense Minister Jaime Neto meeting with Angolan Minister of Defense Joao Ernesto dos Santos.  It was unclear if the two discussed potential Angolan military assistance to Mozambique in the context of the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  There have been rumors in recent months that Angola would deploy forces to Cabo Delgado, though this has never been confirmed.

A group of 11 Bangladeshi nationals and 24 Somali nationals were detained on arrival in Pemba airport on 12 January, local media reported after arriving on a flight from Tanzania. All those detained reportedly had "false visas".  Media reports said the group reportedly travelled to Cabo Delgado to participate in artisanal ruby mining in the Montepuez area, but may have been detained on suspicion of connections to the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

Two men were detained on 16 January in Mueda and their vehicle seized after security forces found they were carrying unspecified "war material" according to local media.  The two had travelled from Nampula into Cabo Delgado through Montepuez before being stopped in Mueda.  It has not been confirmed if the two were members of the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

A large number of civilians have remained at borders crossing with South Africa in Ressano Garcia on 18 January. Officials stated that several of the civilians have attempted to illegally cross the border. Local sources stated that there are “agents” who assist with the illegal border crossing to South Africa.

Officials have continued to warn civilians to evacuate the lower grounds along the Buzi River due to the rising water levels and flooding on 16 January. The rising flood waters are endangering a group of 140 families.

Two civilians were killed after their vehicle was swept by floods along the Buzi River in Mossurize District on Sunday, 17 January. Authorities have conducted a search operation for the third missing civilian.

Local sources stated on 14 January that police abuses have increased after recent anti-COVID measures were imposed. Locals stated that police have seized products from shop owners and sellers, while illegal arrests, and even sexual assault were being conducted by police. The police have reportedly in many cases threatened locals for violating the anti-COVID measures.

China announced that a case of COVID was reported after a Chinese national coming from Mozambique tested positive. The patient reportedly travelled from Mozambique to Malawi before departing to Guangzhou.

Unconfirmed reports on 16 January said that last week Mozambique Defense Minister Jaime Neto had travelled to Harare for talks with Zimbabwean officials to request assistance against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. This report is currently unconfirmed.
The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) closed a restaurant due to several unsanitary violations in Maputo on 16 January.

National Electoral Commission (CNE) elected Bishop Carlos Matsinhe as the president on 15 January by an 11-6 vote.  RENAMO members voted against Matsinhe, saying that a cleric should not serve in the role.

Security forces arrested four people for producing fake National Identity cards in Maputo. The suspects reportedly attempted to open bank accounts with forged documents which were spotted by bank officials leading to the arrest.
Chokwe Mayor Lidia Frederico reportedly died of unknown illness on 16 January. The former mayor was under the FRELIMO party. Lidia was the former Municipal Assembly Secretary in Chowke.
40 students test positive for COVID after the holidays in Maputo province. The students were home quarantined and isolated.

Police detained five suspects (including 3 Nigerian nationals) for drug trafficking in Albasine, north Maputo City, on 16 January. The suspects were arrested after attempting to threaten a Nigerian national who they suspected received 8kg of cocaine. The suspects were hired by a another individual who stated that they would be paid 50,000 meticais after recovering the drugs.

The Portuguese State and Foreign Affairs Minister will arrive in Maputo on 19 January as a part of a three-day visit. Minister Augusto Santos Silva is representing the Vice-President of the European Commission, along with Josep Borrell, to conduct meetings with local officials regarding the security situation in Cabo Delgado.

Health officials announced that isolation wards are now at 243 admissions for COVID patients. 192 were in hospitals in Maputo, 11 in Tete province, 10 in Nampula, 7 in Zambezia, 6 in Matola, 5 in Manica, 5 in Gaza, 3 in Sofala, 2 in Cabo Delgado, 2 in Inhambane. This comes as the National Director of Medical Assistance previously announced that the country’s private hospitals are at a 100 percent capacity on COVID patients. Director Ussene Isse also mentioned that public hospitals are at an 80 percent of the maximum capacity. Tents have been set up outside the Central Hospital of Maputo just to accommodate extra COVID patients.

A group of children and teenagers was reported on 19 January to have recently escaped insurgent captivity in Nangade and were in government custody in the Ntamba area in the district.  The children told authorities the insurgents had had little food, and had given little to no food to their captives.  They also said insurgents were relying on raids to obtain food.  The group had been abducted from different villages in Nangade, Mueda, Mocimboa da Praia, and Muidumbe.

Local sources stated that insurgents in parts of Cabo Delgado, specifically Nangade, MDP, Muidumbe, and other parts of the north and central insurgent zones of the province are running low on supplies.  This has reportedly often led to insurgents not providing food to people they take prisoner.

Members of the same family brawled with each other due to a dispute over narcotics in Bloco 1, central Nacala, on the evening of 16 January. A civilian was killed after being stabbed several times. Police managed to arrest two of suspects while another managed to escape after stealing a parked vehicle.

Members of the same family brawled with each other due to a dispute over narcotics in Bloco 1, central Nacala, on the evening of 16 January. A civilian was killed after being stabbed several times. Police managed to arrest two of suspects while another managed to escape after stealing a parked vehicle.

Local sources stated that a health center in Albazine, north Maputo city, has been operation in unsanitary conditions. No anti-COVID measures such as disinfecting hands have been noted in the health center perimeter. Hospital wastes were reported outside the health center.

Tropical Storm Eloise on 19 January was reclassified from a "moderate" to a "severe" storm, and Mozambique's meteorological office, the INAM, projected it would impact Mozambique on 24 January.  The storm's current trajectory would have it impact parts of Sofala, Inhambane, and Gaza.  Metro France's projection of the trajectory of Eloise (based on current trajectory and strength) would see the storm's epicenter impact areas of Central Inhambane during landfall.   UNOCHA stated that the storm is to weaken after making landfall in Madagascar and will strengthen while crossing the Mozambique Channel. 2.6 million were exposed to the high windspeeds.

A new security agreement between the Mozambican government and Total was reported on 18 January, with the two sides agreeing to a "reinforcement of security" around the Afungi LNG Camp in Cabo Delgado.  The two sides see oil exploration still going ahead on schedule by 2024.  No details regarding this reinforcement of security are currently available.  This came after a meeting between top Total officials and President Nyusi as well as Minister of the Interior, Amade Miquidade, Minister of Defense Jaime Neto, and Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy, Max Tonela.

Military helicopters (likely DAG group) on 16 January were reported to have "bombed" Ntuleni/Nturene village in the south of Palma District, killing an unknown number of insurgents.  This was likely a strafing incident.  Sources later reported that insurgents had used civilians as human shield in this incident, and that there may have been civilian casualties.

Security forces in an operation over the weekend in Olumbi village reportedly killed an unknown number of insurgents who had hidden in a mosque.  No further details on this incident are currently available.

Government forces in recent days carried out "bombings" via helicopter targeting insurgents in Nkonga village, Nangade, reportedly destroying several homes.  This was likely a strafing incident.  No information on casualties is currently available.

Several sources reported that Minister for Agricultural and Rural Development, Celso Correia, has kept an increasingly low profile while the Integrated Development Agency of the North (ADIN), which Correia heads, has not made any tangible progress in developing.  Correia in recent years had been considered the most powerful minister within the government.  The ADIN when conceived in 2020 was meant to be the Mozambican government's primary soft power approach to countering the insurgency in Cabo Delgado, providing aid and jobs to the population of Cabo Delgado and other neighboring provinces.  However, the ADIN months after it was officially "launched" is effectively non-existent, with no programs to its name or notable activity reported.  Correia previously had indicated that he had as much as $500 million of support from the World Bank, with more support promised, allegedly, from the EU, and USA; it is unclear if this support was actually provided or not.  The lack of activity from the ADIN and Correia is increasingly conspicuous as hundreds of thousands of people remain displaced across Cabo Delgado in need of immediate humanitarian assistance.  Sources report Correia's public absence may indicate some loss of influence in the Nyusi government, though this remains unconfirmed.

Insurgents retreating from close to the Afungi LNG Camp on 02 January reportedly raided Monjane village after having attacked the village days before on 29 December.  Several homes were reportedly set on fire in this attack.

Insurgents on 01 January were reported to have clashed with police units at Quitunda, a resettlement village just outside of the Afungi LNG Camp perimeter.  No casualties were confirmed in this incident.  Clashes reportedly lasted from late on the night of 01 January into the early morning hours of 02 January before insurgents retreated from the area.
A minivan collided into a tree after its tire burst in Beira on morning of 18 January. 6 civilians died and 9 others were injured. The driver managed to escape from the area.

An NGO stated that more than 1 million children are involved in child labor in Mozambique. The NGO stated that the children are forced to work in prostitution rings, tobacco, sugar cane production, pesticide handling, fishing nets trawling, illegal mining, weaving, illegal alcohol drinks, construction, human trafficking and smuggling, exposure to radiation, and illegal trade.

Manica officials announced that they were on high alert and are tightening anti-COVID measures in the province. Provincial Health Director Isidoro stated that additional measures were put in place to fight against the pandemic.
The Ministry of health announced 4 new COVID deaths and 824 new cases in Mozambique on 19 January. 411 of the new cases were recorded in Maputo while 104 were recorded in Maputo province.

The National Directorate for Civil Identification (DNIC) opened 11 proceedings against employees for “illegal acts” against the DNIC. Four lawsuits were filed for employees in Manica and one in Maputo. 12 individuals were detained in relation to the cases.  Several of these cases were related to the falsification of documents.

Local sources stated that roads were being affected by the ongoing soil erosion in Morrumbala District on 20 January. The road repair reportedly cost 20 million meticais annually. The area is used by around 100 trucks transporting food items daily. The local Infrastructure and Planning Director stated that 195km out of 695km road network were impassable due to ongoing emergency repairs.

The Foreign Affairs Minister Sibusiso Moyo of Zimbabwe passed away due to COVID on the morning 20 January. Minister Moyo was at a local hospital when he succumbed to the illness.  Moyo's death comes after the recent deaths of two Malawian government ministers from COVID-19 amid a spike in virus cases throughout Southern Africa.

Weather Services announced on that Tropical Storm Eloise is expected to intensify into a tropical cyclone after by the night of Saturday, 23 January.  Eloise is predicted to have wind speeds of over 200km/h after crossing the warm waters of the Mozambique Channel. Based on its current trajectory, Eloise is to make landfall in Vilankulos of Inhambane. INAM stated that rainfall is expected to occur in Sofala, Southern Gaza, Inhambane, Maputo City, and Maputo province.  The storm is forecast to cause “significant damage” to villages and towns along its route. Storm surges are also expected upon the arrival of Eloise in the coastal areas of Mozambique. Mozambique National Meteorology Institute previously classified Tropical Storm Eloise as a "moderate" to a "severe" storm.
column15: Sofala, Southern Gaza, Inhambane, and Maputo

column4: Mozambique President Nyusi appointed a new Tanzanian high commissioner on 11 January, though this was not publicly reported until 20 January. Ricardo Sampaio Mtumbuida is regarded as close to President Nyusi and previously served as a Mozambican intelligence official.  Sources later reported that Mtumbuida has been tasked with attempting to convince Tanzania to provide additional security and intelligence support to Mozambique's fight against the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

1,126 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 20 January, along with 18 new deaths.  This is a new high in daily case totals, up from 895 cases which were reported on 18 January.  The 18 deaths matches the highest one day reported death toll due to COVID in the country.  421 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 222 in Maputo, 205 in Manica, 80 in Inhambane, 36 in Tete, 36 in Niassa, 32 in Nampula, 29 in Zambezia, 28 in Cabo Delgado, 26 in Gaza, and 11 in Sofala. There are currently 9,637 active cases in the country, along with 218 hospitalizations.

Unconfirmed reports circulated on 19 January indicating that RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo had been captured during the course of an afternoon in an undisclosed location in Sofala Province, and had been wounded in this operation.  These reports as of 20 January remain unconfirmed, with no substantive details regarding this incident currently available, and with growing indications that this is a false report.  Defense Minister Jaime Neto on 20 January commented on these rumors when questioned by journalists, denying them and saying that when Nhongo had been arrested, the media would be immediately informed by the government.

Unspecified security force operations targeting RENAMO dissidents were reported in parts of Sofala Province on 19 January; no further details on this operation are currently available.  Note on 20 January, Def Min. Jaime Neto said that Nhongo had refused a recent offer by President Nyusi to participate in the DDR process, and was being "hunted down".

Insurgents looted a vehicle on 15 January in the Pundanhar area after two civilians abandoned the vehicle after seeing suspicious activity along the road.  The two civilians later returned to the vehicle and returned to Nangade town.

A joint statement was issued on 20 January be the United Nations Regional Directors of East and Southern Africa (FAO, IFAD, IOM, UNFPA, UNHCR, WFP and UNDP Resilience Hub) regarding the situation in Cabo Delgado.  The organizations said they were very concerned over the worsening humanitarian crisis and violence in the province, which has forced 565,000 people to flee their homes. A majority of these people are dependent on aid, and in some cases are in hard to reach areas. The organizations said there was an "urgent need" to expand programs to support these IDPs, many of whom still do not live in formal camps.  The organizations also said development initiatives were needed to combat the appeal of the insurgency, and that the government of Mozambique and international community should band together to "end all forms of violence in the country".  Also on Wednesday, UN officials said that tens of thousands of people could die in Cabo Delgado if more assistance was not provided to the hundreds of thousands of IDPs in the area.  The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic has also made the situation more complex. Other UN officials also noted there is an ongoing cholera epidemic in Cabo Delgado that has not yet been contained, adding to the crises facing the province.

Speaking at the swearing in ceremony in Maputo of new Mozambican military chief Eugenio Mussa, President Nyusi on 20 January called on Mussa and new army leadership to "re-establish peace" in Cabo Delgado, and to coordinate action with other security forces to "restore order" in the central region.  He also said the military should design "sustainable training programs which attach priority to the special units", and said the military should "defend aggressively every infrastructure and economic project underway or those to be developed across the country, but paying special attention to the ones in the Afungi Peninsula".
Locals reported that unexplained gunfire and heavy weaponry north of Montepuez towards Nairoto on 19 January.
A cholera outbreak was reported in December in Liukwe in Macomia District, killing between 6-10 people, according to several sources.

Insurgents attacked the village of Litingina and 4 other villages in Nangade District on 16 December. 10 civilians were killed in Litingina during the attack. Insurgents had also attacked Litingina just days earlier.

Insurgents attacked Nkonga and four other villages in Nangade District on 16 December. 10 civilians were killed in Litingina during the attack. Litingina and other area villages were also attacked just days earlier.

Insurgents attacked Machava and four other villages in Nangade District on 16 December. 10 civilians were killed in Litingina during the attack. Litingina and other area villages were also attacked just days earlier.

Insurgents attacked Samora Machel and four other villages in Nangade District on 16 December. 10 civilians were killed in Litingina during the attack. Litingina and other area villages were also attacked just days earlier.

Insurgents attacked Nkonga and four other villages in Namiune District on 16 December. 10 civilians were killed in Litingina during the attack. Litingina and other area villages were also attacked just days earlier.

Officials were reported to have recently increased security measures in Matemo Island in response an early January insurgent raid. The additional security was to prevent insurgents from returning to the island. Officials have called on the locals to support the soldiers.

Health Minister Armindo Tiago announced that the Cabo Delgado government will build "health porches" in resettlement villages in Cabo Delgado to facilitate quick medical care for the sick. The health units were to allow mobile medical staff to conduct consultation visits and reduce costs among the IDPs.

South Africa's Minister for International Relations and Cooperation, Naledi Pandor on 20 January expressed concern that southern African countries had not yet found a joint solution to the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  Pandor also said that the SADC had been unable to agree on joint support for Mozambique, also saying that South Africa had "made every possible effort with the government of Mozambique" to find a way to provide support, but that these efforts had been unsuccessful.  Pandor went on to say that South Africa was "very concerned" about the ongoing deterioration of the humanitarian situation in Cabo Delgado.

The EU donated 7.6 million EUR through the WFP to support IDPs in Mozambique on 20 January. The donation comes as WFP stated that they would provide “uninterrupted assistance” to the affected families. The donation was to provide assistance to 323,000 families in the country.

Officials stated that around 1000 Mozambicans have illegally attempted to cross the border towards South Africa since 12 January, when South Africa again closed its borders in an attempt to stop the spike of COVID-19 in that country. South African authorities stated that dozens of illegal immigrants are deported every 20 minutes.

Officials stated that several border guards have colluded with traffickers to allow them to use clandestine crossings in Lebombo area. The crossings allowed several immigrants to travel to Johannesburg.

Continued flooding has destroyed 8 villages in Buzi District on since 18 January. 3 civilians were killed and 3, 1256 families affected. The flooding has been ongoing since Monday, 18 January. Two villages were initially affected as 1,650 hectares of plantation were submerged by the floods.

WFP stated that 2,100 IDPs were at risk for hunger due to food shortages at Corrane resettlement center among Cabo Delgado IDPs in Nampula. The lack of rain has affected agricultural production in the area.

South Africa reportedly secured 50 million vaccines for three months between April and June. The African Union announced that an estimated 270 million doses would be given to the African countries from April to June 2021.  Mozambique has yet to receive large quantities of the vaccine.

Eight bodies were recovered by three fishermen in Nambo village on 7 January; those killed were believed to have been killed on 06 January.  The fishermen stated that the bodies were found after they fled Magundula Island; those killed may have been brought back from Matemo Island, though this is not confirmed.

Metropolitan Transportation Agency stated 100 buses will be allocated to various routes in Maputo from July to August. The additional buses were to minimize the lack of transportation in the province.

Health officials announced the increasing demand for ventilators due to the rising COVID cases in Maputo City on 20 January. Polana Canico Hospital stated that out of 120 capacity for COVID patients, 83 patients are admitted. Only 78 of the beds have ventilators.

Portuguese Foreign Affairs Minister Augusto Santos Silva and President Nyusi conducted talks in Maputo which concluded on 20 January regarding the EU supporting Mozambique against insurgency. Nyusi welcomed the support in the areas of logistics, health, and military training. Silva for his part said that the talks had focused on EU support for Mozambique in military training, support for humanitarian action, and for support to the Agency for Development of Northern Mozambique.

The Mozambique Bar Association stated that police seizure of alcohol during the weekend was illegal. Lawyers stated that the police specifically targeted alcohol vendors and placed the liquor for sale on a vehicle where the owners could not identify their own products. Police previously seized large amounts of alcohol from vendors in Maputo and stated that the vendors were violating anti-COVID measures.

The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) announced on 20 January that the alcohol seized by the police will be returned to the vendors. INAE stated that police have failed and focused on alcohol when they were ordered to collect other products during the operation. A recovery team was reported to be in the process of giving the seized alcohol back to the vendors.
Several social media images showed policemen seizing large amounts of alcohol at a market in Maputo on 15 January. Police stated that the vendors violated anti-COVID measures.

The National Health Institute stated that January has already experienced a third of the total COVID deaths in Mozambique. Health officials stated that the current month has seen 83 deaths out of a total of 249 deaths. The rise of COVID deaths doubled just in the month of January. COVID cases also was reported to have had a weekly positive rate of 30 percent more.

The Port of Beira on 21 January issued a notice of closure of some operations of the port terminals and closure of export and import gates due to the approach of Tropical Storm Eloise. The port announced its current operations as follows: 21 January - Closure of export entrance gates for trucks and cargo is scheduled at 23:59. 22 January - Closure of import entrance gates for trucks and cargo is scheduled at 07:00. 22 January - Closure of import exit gates for trucks and cargo is scheduled at 15:00. 22 January – Suspension of terminal operations is scheduled at 15:00. 24 January – Reopening of import and export gates and resumption of operations is scheduled at 07:00.

Tropical Storm Eloise entered the Mozambique Channel at the dawn of 21 January after passing over Madagascar.  Eloise is predicted to cause 100km/h winds and 150km/h gusts, with rainfall of 100-200mm.  The Cyclone is anticipated to make landfall between Beira in Sofala Province and Vilankulos in Inhamabane.  The storm will likely impact as far south as Maputo province.  Eloise is expected to intensify into a Category 3 Tropical Cyclone with 150km/h winds and 170km/h gusts once its epicenter has reached Mozambique, which is now anticipated to be in the early hours of 23 January/ late night hours of 22 January.  There is a risk of flash floods, mudslides, storm surge flooding, power outages, and storm surges due to this storm. Previously, weather Services stated that Tropical Storm Eloise is forecast to cause “significant damage” to villages and towns along its route.

A report from Africa Confidential (AC) released this week indicated that President Nyusi has lost significant popularity in the FRELIMO party over his handling of the Hidden Debts Scandal, relations with RENAMO, and most importantly over his handling of the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  The escalation of the insurgency has now forced Nyusi to take a direct role in combating the insurgency, and his political future is likely to be significantly impacted by whether or not security forces over the coming year can retake Mocimboa da Praia and secure the Afungi LNG Camp.  There is also increasing opposition to President Nyusi in FRELIMO circles forming around former Presidents Chissano and Guebuza; Nyusi also is alleged to have significantly enriched himself and his family in recent years and hopes to defend this wealth.  Note that Presidents Guebuza and Chissano are also accused of being deeply involved in corruption during their respective administrations.

Insurgents on Tuesday were reported to have attacked a vehicle carrying passengers and goods in the Pundanhar area along the Nangade - Palma road, resulting in 3 deaths.  The vehicle the three were travelling in was set on fire by insurgents, while an unknown number of other passengers fled the scene.  This came after insurgents over the weekend had attacked a convoy of vehicles, killing at least 5 people and setting 3 vehicles on fire.  Travel along this road was reported to have ceased after the Tuesday attack, but could resume over the coming days.
Traffic has halted between Nangade-Palma road due to the recent attack on a vehicle by insurgents on 19 January. The vehicle was torched and three civilians were killed.

Eswatini extended its partial COVID lockdown for another four weeks. The lockdown was due to the increasing cases of the new COVID variant; the country has recorded more than 2,000 cases over the past two weeks despite an ongoing lockdown.

Mining Company Vale announced that the company has begun to close down its coal mining operation in Mozambique. Vale signed an agreement with Mitsui to acquire Mitsui’s interest in the Moatize coal mine and Nacala Logistics Corridor. Vale stated that after consolidating the interest then it would begin divesting its Mozambican assets.

Elephants trampled and destroyed crops in Matutuine and Magude districts of Maputo. Around 5 hectares were destroyed by the pachyderms. Forestry officials stated that they were still waiting for Conservation Areas Administration to drive the elephants to another location.

Elephants trampled and destroyed crops in Matutuine and Magude districts of Maputo. Around 5 hectares were destroyed by the pachyderms. Forestry officials stated that they were still waiting for Conservation Areas Administration to drive the elephants to another location.

Officials announced that the amount of cargo handled by Maputo Port has declined by 13 percent in 2020.  18.3 million tons of cargo was handled during 2020, compared to 21 million tons during 2019. Maputo Port Development Company (MPDC) stated that the decline was due to COVID and closure of borders.

Criminal Investigation Service(SERNIC) announced that a suspect wanted for sexually assault was arrested in Maputo. The suspect was wanted since November 2018. The suspect reportedly befriended the victims family before conducting the assault.

The Attorney General's Office announced that 8 were detained after being prosecuted for embezzling 11 million meticais from the Maputo Cargo Terminal. Three of the suspects were Tax Authority employees and five were customs agents.  Another 4 suspects are likely to be detained related to this case in the coming days.

A cement factory closed in Dugongo of  Matutuine District after 16 of their employees tested positive for COVID, according to sources on 21 January. Factory officials stated that the positive employees were to remain at the factory for monitoring.
The Ministry of Health announced that 12 COVID deaths and 829 new cases were reported on 21 January. Maputo city recorded 249 cases and Gaza province recorded 169 cases.

Around 400 families stranded by flooding were being rescued as operations were ongoing in Buzi area since the morning of 20 January. The operations initially began clearing families from Mandie-1 and 2, Martinoti, Companhia do Buzi, and Muchenessa areas. The rescue operation was conducted after vital roads were cut off by rising water levels. Sources on 22 January indicated that as many as 3,000 people had been evacuated from the Buzi area ahead of the arrival of Cyclone Eloise.

The National Directorate of Civil Identification (DNIC) announced that several ID facilities were closed in Maputo City due to COVID infections among their employees. The closure of the ID facilities would last for 10 days for disinfection. Seven DNIC employees tested positive.

The National Institute for Disaster Management and Risk Reduction (INGD) estimated that around 600,000 people at risk due to Tropical Cyclone Eloise. The INGD announced that response teams were placed in preparation to the arrival of the tropical cyclone.
Police arrested a Nigerian citizen for possession of 1.7kg of heroin in Maputo City on 20 January. The drugs were found hidden inside a box of clothing.
Montepuez Ruby Mining (MRM) announced on 22 January the death of an illegal miner on the evening of 17 January. The victim was unidentifiable and was mining for gold.
Montepuez Ruby Mining (MRM) announced the death of an illegal miner on 20 January. The victim was a 20-year-old from Namanhumbir, Montepuez.
The UK government announced the travel ban to Tanzania and DRC as a precaution to stop COVID. The travel ban exempted British, Irish nationals and third country nationals with residents rights.

Police arrested a suspect for murder charges in Namicopo, Nampula City of Nampula on 19 January. The suspect previously murdered his relative with two other suspects during a dispute over narcotics in Nacala. The other suspects were detained just right after the incident.

The Mozambique National Institute of Meteorology (INAM) announced that Tropical Storm Eloise’s epicenter has picked up winds speed of 140km/h and gust up to 160km/h. INAM warned that 200mm of rainfall is expected during the next 24 hours in all of Sofala, and parts of Manica and Inhambane.  The trajectory of the storm has now shifted north towards Sofala, rather than initial predictions that said the storm would impact as far south as Maputo City. 100 mm of rainfall is expected in Gaza, Zambezia, and parts of Manica and Inhambane. INAM stated that the cyclone is now expected to make landfall on the coast of Dondo and Buzi Districts of Sofala Province while generating waves up to 14m in height.
Security forces detained a Chinese national in possession of 8.4kg of dried seahorse in Bazaruto Island intended to be smuggled out of the country.
Security forces detained a Chinese national in possession of 8.4kg of dried seahorse in Bazaruto Island intended to be smuggled out of the country.

Tropical Storm Eloise on 22 January was reported to have officially become a category 3 Cyclone, and as of the evening of 22 January is  currently making landfall or near making landfall north of Beira between in Dondo and Muanza Districts.  All of Sofala, along with the districts of Machaze, Macate, Sussundenga and Mossurize in Manica as well as the districts of Govuro, Inhassoro, Vilankulo, and the Bazaruto area of Inhambane will be impacted by the cyclone.  Other areas of Manica, Zambezia, Inhambane, and Gaza are also at risk of being impacted by the cyclone.  Winds of over 100km per hour are expected along the coastal zone, along with winds of 150-200 kms per hour near the epicenter of the storm.  Rainfall of up to 500mm over a 48 hour period are expected, with the highest amount of rain likely north of Beria along the Zambezi Basin.  There is a significant risk of flooding throughout parts of Sofala and Inhambane, particularly along the Save, Pungue, and Buzi Rivers, where water levels were already reported to be at alert levels prior to the arrival of Cyclone Eloise.

Palma government officials were ordered by a government directive issued on 21 January to return to the district by 02 February.  This directive has been issued despite the fact that Palma remains largely cut off from the rest of the country, due to the control of Mocimboa da Praia by insurgents, and insurgents also menacing the Nangade-Palma road.

Beira Mayor Daviz Simango on 22 January called on city residents to remain calm and seek shelter is safe areas as Cyclone Eloise approached the city, and is expected to make landfall in the early morning hours of 23 January.  Reports from the city during the afternoon of 22 January said shops had been closed and streets emptied of people.  Some stockpiles of food and other emergency supplies are present in Beira, other sources reported.  At least 900 IDPs are already present in Beira due to the impact of Tropical Storm Chalane and other heavy rains particularly in Buzi district in recent weeks.

Heavy rains over the past 24 hours from 22 January were reported in Inhambane Province in Massangena, Maxixe, Jangamo, and Vila Franca do Save.  Water levels have risen in these areas close to flood levels, including in the Save River, and flooding appears likely in these areas as well as in parts of Inhambane and Sofala as Cyclone Eloise approaches.

The Buzi and Pungue Rivers are already reported to be two meters above alert levels in Sofala Province, before the arrival of Cyclone Eloise. Increased flooding in areas adjacent to both of these rivers is very likely over the next 48 hours as the cyclone is expected to arrive near Beira early on 23 January.
LAM on 22 January cancelled flights between Maputo and Beira, Nampula, and Quelimane due to the approach of Cyclone Eloise.

Insurgents launched an attack on border police positions and the village of Mandimba along the Nangade-Palma road in Nangade District of Cabo Delgado, within 5 kms of the Tanzanian border, on the night of 22-23 January, with several homes set on fire.  Police in the area reportedly fled as insurgents approached the area.  Sources later reported that the insurgents had in begun the attack 1 day earlier on 21 January, and killed one civilian and two border police members.  Note that reports later indicated as many as 7 people may have been killed in this attack.  Insurgents also reportedly physically assaulted several villagers accused of collaborating with government forces.  Local civilians also said the militants had spoken in Swahili and Somali. Insurgents also carried out some looting in the village before withdrawing from the area aboard motorcycles.

National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) announced the seizure of 220 tons of cement being sold illegally in Mozambique between 13 to 21 January. The operation was conducted after reports of increasing prices of cement bags in the country. INAE stated that the cement bags being sold were in poor storage or condition.

The Ministry of Health announced that 623 new COVID cases and 7 related deaths in Mozambique on 22 January. A total of 348 recoveries were reported. The cases were recorded as follows: 375 in Maputo City, 106 in Gaza, 56 in Maputo Province, 35 in Manica, 21 in Sofala, 15 in Niassa, 8 in Zambezia, 6 in Nampula, and 1 in Cabo Delgado.

A fire burned down six residences after starting due to an electrical short circuit in Barrio Military, south Maputo City, on 21 January. Firefighters responded but were not able to douse the flames.  At least 30 people were made homeless by this fire.

Health officials announced that there are increasing numbers of COVID infected health professionals in Maputo Central Hospital. The hospital director stated that currently 100 staff were infected and 250 have recovered. The director stated that if the high number of infections continue among health professionals health services in the capital could suffer.
Nhamatanda Districts Near Beira was one of the most heavily impacted by flooding caused by Cyclone Eloise on 23 January, with hundreds displaced in the district due to flooding.

Buzi District Near Beira was one of the most heavily impacted areas by flooding caused by Cyclone Eloise on 23 January.  A total of 6,800 people were displaced by flooding; a large number of these were reportedly in Buzi.

11 people were killed and 12 injured across Central Mozambique as Cyclone Eloise hit Beira City and other areas in the middle of the country with wind speeds of up to 140km/h and gusts of 160km/h on 23 January.  At least 4 of these deaths were reported in Beira itself, while one fatality was confirmed in Zambezia.  As many as 29,310 homes, primarily in Sofala but also in neighboring provinces were destroyed by the Cyclone. Authorities stated that most of the victims died due to trees felled by the cyclone.  Eloise left Beira without power and flooding was reported in some areas of the city as well.  Authorities were attempting to restore power and communications on Sunday, as they assess the level of the damage in the affected areas. Some significant damage was reported at the Ponta Gea Health Center and some other areas of the city while Praia Nova and other flood prone areas of the city were evacuated.  Initial assessments indicate the storm did not impact Beira as substantially as had first been feared it would, though damage assessments are ongoing.  Severe flooding was also reported in the districts of Buzi and Nhamatanda, also in Sofala province.  As many as 314,000 people were affected with a majority in Sofala, Manica, Zambezia, and Inhambane have been impacted by the storm - including a large majority in Sofala, where 162,305 people were impacted by the cyclone. 20,012 people are still currently displaced.

An early morning report on 23 Jan disclosed that small tributaries draining into the two catchment areas of the Buzi and Save rivers were overflowing as a result of the rain from Tropical Cyclone Eloise. As a result, flooding was reported on some nearby roads. Specifically, sections of the EN1 were very close to flooding as a result of the heavy rains on Saturday. In total, approx 3000 people from Buzi district have been forced to evacuate as a result of the rains and flooding. Rains have continued in central and south of Mozambique as Tropical Cyclone Elouise crossed the border into Zimbabwe Saturday evening.

Mozambique's National Institute of Meteorology (INAM) forecasts on 24 January strong rains with thunderstorms in Maputo and Gaza Provinces until Monday, 25 January. Residents are advised to take precautionary measures during this time of calamity. Risk areas in Gaza are as follows- Chicualacuala, Chigubo, Mabalane, Chibuto, Massingir, Limpopo, Chonguene, Massangena, Mapai, Guija, Mandlakazi and Bilene, and  Chokwe and Xai-Xai cities. Meanwhile, for Maputo province, the risk areas are Matutuíne, Boane, Namaacha, Moamba, Marracuene, Magude and Manhica districts, and Maputo and Matolacities.

Mozambique's National Institute of Meteorology (INAM) forecasts on 24 January strong rains with thunderstorms in Maputo and Gaza Provinces until Monday, 25 January. Residents are advised to take precautionary measures during this time of calamity. Risk areas in Gaza are as follows- Chicualacuala, Chigubo, Mabalane, Chibuto, Massingir, Limpopo, Chonguene, Massangena, Mapai, Guija, Mandlakazi and Bilene, and  Chokwe and Xai-Xai cities. Meanwhile, for Maputo province, the risk areas are Matutuíne, Boane, Namaacha, Moamba, Marracuene, Magude and Manhica districts, and Maputo and Matolacities.

14 Cuban health professionals, including 5 doctors and 9 nurses, arrived in Mozambique on 24 January as part of Cuba's support for Mozambique in combating the ongoing pandemic. Their activities will commence on 27 January provided that their PCR tests were negative.  31 more Cuban health professionals are set to arrive in Mozambique on 03 February.

Services are closed starting 24 January at the Igreja Santo Antonio da Polana in Maputo City after some priests tested positive for COVID-19 infection. Affected priests were well and currently on quarantine.

790 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 24 January, along with eight new deaths. 273 of the new cases were from Maputo city and 60 were from Maputo province, 71 cases from Gaza, 36 from Tete, 258 from Inhambane, 18 from Sofala, one from Manica, 61 from Zambezia, and 12 from Niassa. The new cases brought the country's number of infections to 32,418 with the national death toll now at 305.

Authorities disclosed on 22 January that security forces re-arrested eight of the 15 prisoners who escaped from Penitentiary Establishment in Ile district on May 2020. The eight prisoners were arrested in the province of Zambezia however, the exact location was not disclosed. Efforts are ongoing to capture the seven other escapees.

Helicopters flew over the Mandimba area on 23 January after an insurgent attack on the village the night before.  Insurgents however had fled the area and the helicopters did not conduct any combat operations near the village.

UN's Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha) stated on 25 January that around 6,800 people have been displaced and 5,000 houses were damaged or destroyed as Cyclone Eloise made a landfall in Beira City and the adjacent Buzi district and caused heavy flooding over the weekend. As much as 142,000 hectares or 350,000 acres was flooded by the Cyclone, with thousands in need of food aid in Central Mozambique.

On 22 January, security forces detained a customs broker over alleged connection to the robbery of 11 million Meticais from the safety deposit boxes at the Cargo Terminal of Maputo International Airport. The exact location of the suspect's arrest was not disclosed. The customs broker was the ninth suspect who was arrested over alleged involvement to the crime, three other suspects were still at large. Among the group were officials from Customs and Tax Authority of Mozambique.

On 21 January, insurgents launched an attack in Namiune village, Nangade. A village leader was allegedly beheaded after he was beaten by the insurgents. Four male children, aged between 10-12-yrs-old, were abducted. Sources later reported at least 3 people were killed in this attack.  The village, located 30 KM from Nangade HQ, was previously attacked by insurgents  between 10-12 December 2020.

On 21 January, insurgents launched an attack in Namiune village, Nangade. A village leader was allegedly beheaded after he was beaten by the insurgents. Four male children, aged between 10-12-yrs-old, were abducted. The village, located 30 KM from Nangade HQ, was previously attacked by insurgents between 10-12 December 2020.

EDM on 24 January was reported to have restored power to most areas impacted by Cyclone Eloise, including Vilankulo, Inhassoro, Beira, Dondo, Nhamatanda, Gorogosa, Inchope, Inhassunge, and Luabo.  Power was disrupted in many areas in Central Mozambique throughout Saturday.  Some power outages continued in some isolated areas of Inhambane, Sofala, Manica, and Zambezia on Sunday.  Vodacom's network was also temporarily interrupted in parts of Sofala, the company reported.
Significant flooding and damage to structures was reported in the Quelimane area on 23 January due to Cyclone Eloise.

Insurgents set up a road blockade in the 5th Congresso village area of Macomia to attempt to block security forces based in Macomia town from using this route to travel north towards Muidumbe.  Local residents observed this road barrier and reported it to security forces.  Pro-government militia then pursued insurgents into the Litamanda area.

Clashes were reported on 21 January in woods near Chai and Nova Zambezia between pro-government militia and insurgents.  Fighting was reported in the early morning hours when militia from these villages entered bush areas near Litamanda, looking for insurgents after militants set up road barriers near 5th Congresso village.  Clashes left 6 militants dead and 2 militia fighters injured.  The remaining insurgents were reported to have retreated back towards Miangalewa.

Local media reported that South African Private Military Contractor Dyck Advisory Group currently has only one helicopter operational in Cabo Delgado, despite being contracted to keep 4 helicopters in operation in the province.  This report is currently unconfirmed.

Vehicles on Sunday were reportedly unable to travel to Palma from Nangade for fear of insurgent attacks.  This came after insurgent raids on 21 and 22 January along the Nangade-Palma road, and after two attacks the week previously along this route.  A large number of vehicles on Sunday were reported to be waiting in Nangade to travel to Palma, and had been unable to move along this road for at least 5 days.

At least one child was killed in Zambezia due to Cyclone Eloise on 23 January, sources reported in a drowning incident in the Mutchessane region in Munhonha District.  Chinde, Luabo, Mopeia, and Maganja da Costa were the most significantly impacted areas in Zambezia by the Cyclone.

Manica's districts of Mossurize, Machaze, Sussundenga, and Macate were the most impacted by Cyclone Eloise on 23 January, with over 200 families in Mossurize displaced by flooding.  Multiple area roads in Manica were also flooded and made impassable due to the Cyclone.
Dondo District in Sofala was significantly impacted by Cyclone Eloise over the weekend, with hundreds displaced in the district due to flooding.

Road and traffic officials closed off an alterative bridge due to the collapse of one its support pillars over Save River due to heavy rainfall starting 22 January. Officials stated that a maintenance and repair team will be deployed once the rain stops. Vehicles transporting goods are limited to 35 tons once the bridge reopens. The National Road Administration stated that the a contingency plan was in effect to work on the bridge after the passage of Tropical Depression Eloise.

Health officials announced that a transit ward was turned into a COVID treatment center at Central Maputo Hospital. The ward was to treat patients transiting to General Hospital of Polana-Canico.  A 24-hour team was set on standby and that the transit ward was to allow additional bed capacity outside the General Hospital of Polana-Canico, which houses a 100-bed capacity for COVID patients. 65 beds were currently occupied at Polana-Canico.

Global Climate Risk Index stated that Mozambique is ranked as the number 1 country vulnerable to climate change after impact of Cyclones idai and Kenneth in 2019.  This index was compiled without taking into consideration Tropical Storm Chalane which impacted Mozambique in late December and Cyclone Eloise, which impacted the country on 23 January.

The Ministry of Health announced 14 COVID deaths and 363 new cases in Mozambique on 25 January. 118 of the new cases are in Maputo province, and 99 are in Maputo city. 19 new hospitalizations were also reported increasing the total to 225 admitted COVID patients.

The National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD) stated that evacuations continued out of Buzi District on 24 January. The evacuation operations have continued since 21 January with elderly, women and young children in front of the queue as the district flooded even before Cyclone Eloise hit the area on 23 January.

The health minister announced the addition of 320 new beds for COVID patients within this week in Mavalane General Hospital in Maputo. Three buildings and a tent would be built in response to the increasing COVID cases.  The minister also stated that PPEs will be distributed to health care workers as the number of positive cases within the medical professionals have also increased.

Portugal Foreign Minister Silva announced that he hoped an agreement on a “framework of enhanced cooperation” would be achieved over the coming weeks in talks between the EU and Mozambique. Silva said that Mozambique expressed a clear desire for support in security, humanitarian action, and envelopment.  The EU will work with the Mozambican government to achieve a framework to fight the insurgency as well as support humanitarian efforts in Cabo Delgado.

Local sources stated that a sex worker claimed that she received death threats from police in Chimoio on 24 January after sleeping with her.  An officer reportedly refused to pay her and threatened her with a firearm.

The National Institute for Risk Management and Natural Disaster Management called on locals to leave high risk areas for flooding along the Incomati River in Moamba District on 25 January. Officials stated that the rainfall recorded was around 200mm within the past 24 hours including rainfall in the neighboring countries of South Africa and Eswatini. The high amount of rain may cause rivers to overflow.

Security forces in Pemba arrested a Chinese national in connection with the illegal export of 82 containers of unprocessed logs on 25 January.  The ship carrying these containers left the port of Pemba and is en route to China.  This shipment of timber had previously been seized by authorities, and the man arrested had been meant to this timber secure, after the company he worked for was awarded control of the assets.  The case may also have involved officials from customs, the tax authority, the forestry department, customs brokers, and members of the military and an investigation into the case is ongoing.

An intelligence report released recently indicated that Total is seeking to relocate some of its operations on the Afungi Peninsula to the French territory of Mayotte after recent insurgent attacks near the Afungi LNG Camp.  Moving operations to Mayotte would ensure the security of Total personnel and operations as the insurgency continues to be a significant threat in Cabo Delgado.  Under a proposed plan, Mayotte would serve as a logistics platform and would be used for some equipment storage.  There are no immediate plans to base large numbers of expat workers on Mayotte due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and various logistical obstacles.  Total has reportedly asked some subcontractors to assess the costs of shifting some operations to Mayotte, though no final decision on this potential move has been made.

A French frigate, Nivôse, was reported on 24 January to have detected a dhow sailing in the Mozambique Channel sailing without a flag.  The frigate interdicted the dhow by deploying a helicopter, and forced the unflagged vessel to stop for an inspection.  Upon boarding the vessel, security personnel conducted a search in which they discovered 417 kgs of methamphetamines and 27 kgs of heroin, worth 40 million euros.  The Nivôse continued patrols in the Mozambique Channel after this seizure.

A French frigate, Nivôse, was reported on 24 January to have detected a dhow sailing in the Mozambique Channel off Pemba Bay, sailing without a flag.  The frigate interdicted the dhow by deploying a helicopter, and forced the unflagged vessel to stop for an inspection.  Upon boarding the vessel, security personnel conducted a search in which they discovered 417 kgs of methamphetamines and 27 kgs of heroin, worth 40 million euros.  The Nivôse continued patrols in the Mozambique Channel after this seizure.  The seized drugs were trasnported to Reunion Island; other sources later said that the crew of the boat were Iranian nationals.

A UN official on 26 January said that 441,686 people had been impacted by Cyclone Eloise, and that a total of 43,327 people had been displaced in the country by the storm.  This includes over 90,000 children. Another source reported as many as 288,000 people impacted by the cyclone.  At least 7 deaths occurred in Sofala, 1 in Manica, and 1 in Zambezia.  Initial reports had indicated that 170,000 people had been impacted by the cyclone with just over 8,000 people displaced.  56,364 residences were partially or totally destroyed. Initial reports stated that 9,806 houses were partially destroyed by the cyclone, 4,154 completely destroyed, and another 3,007 homes flooded.  74 health facilities were also destroyed, along with 322 classrooms partially destroyed and 89 classrooms were completely destroyed.  Parts of Sofala Province, including the city of Beira, Dondo, Nhamatanda, and Buzi Districts were the areas most impacted by the cyclone.  Some areas of Zambezia, Manica, and Inhambane also experienced flooding and the displacement of local communities.

1,274 new COVID-19 cases were reported in Mozambique on 26 January - a new record in daily cases.  This was out of 2,980 test results received back in the past 24 hours. 10 new deaths were also reported.  There are now 12,379 active cases in the country.  481 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 243 cases in Maputo, 170 in Niassa, 103 in Zambezia, 77 in Gaza, 71 in Inhambane, 57 in Tete, 29 in Sofala, 21 in Nampula, 19 in Manica, and 3 in Cabo Delgado.  There have now been 34,055 cases in Mozambique along with 329 deaths due to the virus.  6,015 active cases are currently in Maputo City, along with 2,184 cases in Maputo.

Mozambican Prime Minister Rosario called on residents living in flood-prone areas in Gaura Guara, Buzi, to resettle in more secure areas as parts of Buzi District flood every year. Rosario stated that most of Buzi town is submerged due to flooding and was worsened by Cyclone Eloise. Most of  the town residents were relocated to Guara-Guara.

The overflooding of Save River reportedly submerged 130 residences and closed down Machanga health center. The locals transferred to the local registry office which was situated on a higher ground. Around 800 families were displaced by the flooding in the area.
Heavy rainfall has increased water levels just 30cm below the flood alert level in the Ressano Garcia area on 25 January, increasing the threat of flooding in the area.

The UNCHR issued a report that security conditions in Cabo Delgado remain unstable. Even with the ongoing military operations in several parts of the province, the security situation remains volatile due to the presence of insurgents. The report, which covered the period from 15 December - 15 January, noted escalations in attacks by insurgents in Palma, Nangade, and Macomia, including attacks in the Afungi Peninsula.  Quissanga, Macomia, Meluco, Mocimboa da Praia, Muidumbe, and Nangade have been the worst impacted by insurgent attacks.  The report also noted that as many as 100,000 people have been displaced since 2020.

The Health Minister announced that COVID vaccinations could start as soon as February or March after the country will receive 70,000 doses of COVID vaccines. The minister said that health workers would be the first to be prioritized as around 70,000 health workers are working in the Mozambican health service. The minister also mentioned that vaccines are not the only solution and that personal protective equipment supply is also adequate in relation to the requests made by the health units.  Vaccines for the wider populace in Mozambique will likely not be available until later this year.

DP World announced it would train Angolan workers in exchanges with Mozambique. The announcement comes after DP World signed a concession contract to operate in the port of Luanda. The training of the Angolan workers was to take place in Maputo.

Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy announced that at least 12,000 people were made homeless in Zambezia due to Cyclone Eloise. The announcement comes after assessing the damage caused by Cyclone Eloise. 33,000 were affected by electrical outages and Chinde District is still experiencing an electrical blackout.

The African Union announced that the organization would deploy a mission to Mozambique in “the next few days” to assess the country's needs for support in fight against terrorism in Mozambique. The AU stated that they are coordinating with SADC and Mozambique in assessing the support required.

Mozambican authorities are making efforts to intercept a Chinese-owned ship transporting illegally logged timber after it departed from the Port of Pemba. The operation comes after a Chinese national was detained for smuggling the illegal timber to the ship. The ship was previous held at the port five months after the illegally logged timber was flagged.

An investigative report by local media said on 26 January that a criminal scheme has been in operation for some time at the Maputo and Pemba airports in which illegal immigrants are provided with illegal documents and fake visas to enter Mozambique for a fee of $1500.  A number of migration officials are believed to be behind this scheme.  A number of Pakistani, Somali, and Bangladeshi nationals have entered Mozambique via this scheme.  An investigation into this network is ongoing.

Locals protested by blocking roads with burning tires against the new precautionary measures against COVID in Manhica, north of Maputo City, on 14 January. The protesters rejected  the security measures and stated that their livelihood was affected and preferred to die with COVID rather that die from hunger. The protest was dispersed by security forces.

Aid workers warned of the potential spread of COVID in IDP camps who were affected by Cyclone Eloise in Sofala. The lack of access to hygiene and sanitation services and over crowding may increase the risk of spreading COVID. NGO officials stated that the pandemic is a concern, but the initial response was to move locals to safer areas.  At least 18,000 people were displaced by the Cyclone on 23 January.

Police Chief Bernardino Rafael on 27 January removed the entire command of the first regiment of the Frontier Police stationed in the Namaacha area near the border with Eswatini and not far from the border with South Africa.  He also announced all members of the frontier police stationed in the Macuacua area were facing disciplinary proceedings  This was later reported to have impacted 63 officers.  This comes after investigations by a local media outlet revealed police in the area were allowing Mozambicans to cross into South Africa illegally for a bribe of 200 South African rand, or about $13.  The police conducted their own investigation, and determined accusations against the border police to be true.

Health Minister Armindo Tiago on the afternoon of 27 January said that the COVID-19 strain circulating in South Africa that has driven a large increase of cases in that country has been present in Mozambique since November 2020.  He said that this strain has led to an increase of cases in Mozambique, also saying this increase in cases has been driven by a lack of compliance with preventive measures.  Tiago indicated that the country had recently received samples back from December COVID cases that were 70% positive for the new COVID variant.
Curfews in Palma town remain in place, media sources report, starting at 1800hrs each night. Palma residents say only soldiers can be seen on the town's streets in the evening.

Residents of Palma say staple product price fluctuation continues on a week by week basis, primarily because the Nangade road is now routinely cut off by insurgents, limiting the arrival of supplies by road into the town.

Insurgents on 24 January attacked security forces in Olumbe village in southern Palma District.  Heavy fighting was reported in the area though no information on casualties is available.  Security forces retreated from the area after this attack.

Media reporting indicated that Tanzania largely views the Cabo Delgado insurgency as an internal matter for Mozambique to address, and that clearing areas near the Afungi LNG area is the primary task the Mozambican government should be focused on, rather than any more significant political or societal issues related to the insurgency.

Road and transport officials announced that three roads in Gaza are impassable in the wake of Cyclone Eloise and overflowing of the Limpopo River. The Mapai-Pafuri road ( Route N222) was submerged at the Km 16-17 Section. While the Dindiza-Zinhane road (Route R441) is submerged for 2 km between Km 108 and 110. Lastly, the Chicualacuala-Pafuri road (Route R455) has 20 Km of its extension submerged between Km 35 and 55. Officials stated that the Dindiza-Zinhane road is open as an alternative route.

Road and transport officials announced that five roads in Sofala remain impassable in the wake of Cyclone Eloise. Among the impassable roads are the Guara Guara-Buzi road (N281) as 14km remain submerged. The Casa Banana-Inhaminga road (R1001) was closed due to erosion of an aqueduct. While the 38km extension of N282 near Maciamboza river due to the rise in water levels of the at the Km 19 mark. 14km of Gorongosa-Piro road (R564) are also impassable due to the rising flows of the Vanduzi and Nhadue rivers and the Nhamatanda-Metuchira road (R1000), after a bridge collapsed over the Metuchira river. Furthermore, four roads were conditionally opened depending on the water level. The Tica-Buzi road (N280), Guara Guara-Nova Sofala road (N281), Maringue-Chemba road (R565) and Marínguè-Chauaua road (R1005) were conditionally reopened depending on the road status which were still at risk for flooding and road erosion.

Road and transport officials announced in the wake of Cyclone Eloise that three roads are impassable and four were conditional alternatives in Manica province. The Dombe road (R520) is reportedly flooded at the Km 18 mark due to the overflowing of the river. While the Rotunda junction (R969) and the Chicamba crossing (N6),were submerged and their aqueducts were damaged along the entire route. The four alternative roads with restricted access were, the Chimoio-Espungabera road (N260), Mossurize-Chitobe road (R441), Sussundenga-Padeado road and Catandica-Cagore road. The alternative roads were being monitored due to the rising flows of the Buzi, Mossurize, Mucessa, and Inhazonha rivers.
