The National Migration Service (SENAMI) announced a foreign journalist working for a news media outlet must leave Mozambique by 30 January. The deportation of the journalist comes after a complaint made GABINFO and issued a statement that the journalist could not prove that his news company was accredited in the UK - despite the fact that the journalist was not required to be accredited in the UK.  This move is thought to be tied to his organization's coverage of the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  Similar reports regarding this journalist had been previously reported though the journalist had been able to avoid deportation previously.  This case has generated significant outcry amongst civil society groups in Mozambique, who accused the government of a "lack of transparency and professionalism" in this case.

The Nangade-Palma road as of 28 January was reported to still be inaccessible after recent insurgent attacks along this route, with multiple trucks loaded with supplies waiting in Nangade town.  Some trucks also returned to Mueda in recent days.  Sources in Palma also report no vehicles have entered the town from the Nangade road this week.  This has created shortages of basic products in Palma, and increases in prices in the town. Sources reported seeing insurgents in the Mandimba area as recently as 26 January, and militants may still be in the area.

Health officials said on 24 January that 270 diarrhea cases were reported in Metuge. The cases were recorded during the first week of January. Awareness programs were being intensified to assist the population in preventing a cholera outbreak.

Police commander general Bernardino Rafael on 26 January said that the police force in Mozambique was in need of reform "urgently", saying many police officers have not been able to advance in their careers or have not received pay raises for many years, also saying corruption among the police force is a major issue.  This corruption problem is partially due to the low salaries police receive, Rafael said.  Rafael this week was also strongly critical of border police who had allowed illegal crossings of the Mozambique border into South Africa and Eswatini for bribes.

Local sources stated that 7th grade students unable to take exams in parts of Sofala due to Cyclone Eloise. Most schools were flooded or are used as relocation centers for displaced individuals. The Sofala Education director stated that most schools are flooded in Buzi District and there was no way to travel to other areas after the cyclone.

January has seen a record number COVID fatalities and infections. 14,139 cases have been reported so far in January; prior to this month, September with 4,812 had seen the highest number of cases in a single month.  587 new hospitalizations have also been reported this month; previously October had seen the largest number of hospitalizations with 194.  139 deaths up to 25 January were reported during the month - in contrast to 39 deaths in November, the previous month with the highest death toll.

Mozambique significantly raised interest rates by 300 basis points on 27 January to try and stop significant inflation. The Central Bank of Mozambique increased its interbank rate to 13.25% from 10.25%. The increase in interest rate was an upward revision of the inflation outlook indicating a continued decline in value of the metical, and is an attempt to prevent significant inflation.

Heavy rainfall has reportedly flooded 692 residences, 120 classrooms, and affected 3,150 in Maputo province on 25 January. Six health units, 516 agricultural lands, and 32 roads were also flooded. Students were transferred to nearby schools to take their examinations.  Around 1,62 tons of crops were destroyed by the heavy rain.

World Bank regional director Taufila Nyamadzabo warned against the sanitation problems in outlying Maputo neighborhoods on Wednesday. Director Nyamadzabo stated that much work is still required to reduce the flooding issues in the neighborhoods of Maputo City. The director is expecting that within 2 years that the issue may be resolved. This comes as Mozambique received 100 million USD from the World Bank on December 2020 to restructure Maputo City.  Flooding due to heavy rains was reported in recent days in the capital.

Around 250 families called on city municipality of Maputo demanding a resolution to provide support to families whose residences were destroyed by a landslide in Hulene on 26 January. The Maputo government has stopped paying for rented houses of this group, who say they are now facing threats of eviction.

A civilian who claimed to have escape from the insurgents in Manilha, Cabo Delgado reportedly told local media that insurgents' logistics and supplies lines are deteriorating.  According to this civilian, insurgents in Manhila recently met with a Tanzanian national described as a top leader of the group who reportedly told insurgents that there was "no money" left to fund the groups' activities.  This leader allegedly told insurgents they should return to their home villages, while insurgents rejected this, saying they feared for their lives if they returned to their home areas.  Insurgents are also increasingly unable to loot food supplies from villages as they have driven large numbers of civilians out of areas they are active in, leaving abandoned villages with no lootable supplies.  This is one of several recent unconfirmed reports that insurgents are experiencing some shortages, including of food supplies, in areas they control.

The Ministry of Health announced that 871 new COVID cases and 7 deaths in Mozambique on 27 January. The infections were reported in Maputo city were 504, 67 in Maputo province, Gaza recorded 83 cases, 7 in Inhambane, 7 in Sofala, 44 in Manica, 13 in Tete, 67 in Zambezia , 74 in Nampula, and 5 in Niassa.

A fire burned down 50 tents at the central market in Quelimane on the late evening of Wednesday, 27 January. No casualties were reported. Firefighters responded to the incident but had difficulties in dousing the blaze. Firefighters stated that a malfunction had led to the empty tanks in their fire trucks. No details were mentioned as to what started the fire.

Total on 28 January denied reports that it would transfer majority of its operations to Mayotte. The oil and gas company said that it will continue to run offshore operations from Pemba alongside its major subcontractors, though some logistical operations may move offshore “to optimize part of the logistical chain.” The company also acknowledged it had early in January reduced the number of staff at the Afungi LNG Camp due to the ongoing security situation.

South African officials announced on 28 January that 1210 Mozambicans were deported from the country between 16 - 22 of this month. A majority of the deportees were attempting to cross the border illegally. 16 Mozambicans were also deported from Eswatini. 936 cases were due to illegal immigration and 290 were due to illegal residency.

Health Researchers in South Africa reported this week that a new more contagious strain of COVID spreading throughout the region is 20 – 200% more contagious than original COVID strain. Another finding was that antibodies are less effective in neutralizing the South African variant.  Mozambican officials announced earlier this week that the South African strain had been present in the country since November.

The Economist Intelligence Unit stated that most African countries won’t be able to conduct mass immunizations against COVID-19 until 2023; the poorest countries on the continent, which includes Mozambique, may not see mass vaccination campaigns until 2024.  The forecast comes as vaccinations were based on the level of economy and that middle-income countries would fall by late 2022 and early 2023. Most low and middle income countries in Africa are relying on the COVAX initiative which aims to ensure 6 billion vaccinations for the poorest countries.

11 new COVID deaths and 907 new cases were recorded by the Ministry of Health on 28 January. The fatalities included eight men and three women. Maputo city recorded 326 new cases, 126 cases were recorded in Maputo province.  There were 12,732 active COVID cases in the country as of Thursday.

The Tete Provincial Court issued that Vale Mining Company should compensate 158,000 EUR to farmers for closing off a large quantity of farmland by fencing their mine in central Mozambique. The court ruled in favor of 48 farmers in Moatize District, demanding 300,000 meticais each. This came after the company recently announced it planned to exit its Mozambican operations, which have been loss making for years.

The Ministry of Public Works, Water Resources and Housing issued a warning for the possible flooding of along the Zambezi River due to the increase water discharge coming from Cahora Bassa dam. The reservoir is increasing significantly, from 1,740 to 3,000 cubic meters per second. Doa and Mutarara districts in Tete province would be directly affected, he said, as will Tambara, in Manica province; Chemba, Caia and Marromeu, in Sofala; and Mopeia and Chinde, in the province of Zambézia.

Officials stated the Incomati River is 0.3 meters above the alert level at Ressano Garcia. The movement of the water is expected to reach Magude and Manhica areas. All residents in the areas were advised to avoid flood prone locations.

UN announced that 530,000 people have been displaced by the Cabo Delgado conflict, which is five times more in comparison to the numbers registered since March 2020. Around 90 percent are sheltered by communities. UN stated that they required 254 million USD to provide adequate assistance to 1.1 million IDPs till 2021. The main needs and challenges faced by displaced communities continue to be related to lack of shelter facilities, access to basic services and fear of being persecuted in the areas they are relocating to.

A UNHCR stated that insurgents have caused disruption in accessing Quissanga, Macomia, Meluco, Mocimboa da Praia, Muidumbe, and Nangade Districts in Cabo Delgado over the past year and have made access to these districts difficult.

Police Commander in Chief Bernardino Rafael announced this week that the security situation is improving in Quissanga, Macomia, Ibo, and Meluco, allowing for the return of civilians to these district.  The chief stated that though there is security improvement in Nangade, there are "points of instability" still in parts of the district.

Police Chief Bernardino Rafael stated that RENAMO dissidents have not yet accepted the offer by government to join DDR Process. The chief also stated that the dissidents have shown previous disinterest in conducting talks.

Transparency International’s (TI) regional adviser stated that Mozambique dropped 3 positions from 146 to 149 on the Corruption Perception Index for 2020. The TI adviser stated that the country is at risk for a continuous “downward spiral” due to the poor governance and corruption.

Portuguese Defense Minister Joao Cravinho on 29 January stated that EU is in dialogue with Mozambique regarding setting up a military training mission to the country to support Mozambique in its fight against the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  Cravinho said this mission would likely be "similar to the EU Training Mission in Mali".

Security forces arrested a man in possession of 61 kg of heroin and 5kg of crystal meth while unloading the narcotics on a Nacala beach on Saturday, 23 January. Five Tanzanian nationals associated with the man escaped the scene and are being sought by authorities.  The drugs were suspected to have been shipped from Tanzania.

Security forces arrested a man in possession of 61 kg of heroin and 5kg of crystal meth while unloading the narcotics on a Nacala beach on Saturday, 23 January. Five Tanzanian nationals associated with the man escaped the scene and are being sought by authorities.  One other source reported that two Mozambican nationals had also escaped police.  The drugs were suspected to have been shipped from Tanzania.
A suspected insurgent attack was reported just east of Nguri lake in the vicinity of Iangua village in Muidumbe District on 27 January, with a large fire reported in the area.
A suspected insurgent attack was reported on 27 January on Congo island, with a large fire reported on the island.  This report is currently unconfirmed.
SENAMI repatriated 105 illegal immigrants back to their respective countries. 100 Malawians, 4 Guinean, and a South African were all sent back.
Security forces detained three members of a five-man gang for stealing a vehicle in Maputo on 7 January. Several license plates were recovered from the suspects.
Security forces detained five suspects wanted for stealing a bus in Catembe District, south Maputo, on 27 January.

Officials reported on 29 January that a group of 5,500 families affected by Cyclone Eloise remained cut off in the Save area, Machaze District, in Manica Province.  The families were cut off due to flooding in the area and lack all basic necessities, sources reported, and are in need of immediate aid.  One official said food supplies are available to transport to the families, though there is a lack of transportation to evacuate them from the area.

A warehouse in Inhassunge on 25 January was reportedly robbed of humanitarian supplies meant for Cyclone Eloise victims in Inhassunge, Zambezia.  The warehouse had held large stocks of rice, beans, and oil, and was stocked in December ahead of Tropical Storm Chalane.  When officials arrived on Monday to begin food distribution to families impacted by the cyclone, they discovered the warehouse was empty.  An investigation into the incident is ongoing; one arrest was made after it was initially reported though the individual in question was later released.

Local sources stated food prices have increased in Palma as the road to Nangade as of 29 January remained cut off due to the presence of insurgents.  Sources stated that a kg of rice is 220 meticais while 25kg is 4,000 meticais. A liter of gas is 500 meticais, 1kg sugar is 150 meticais, 25kg of flour is 2,500 meticais, 1kg of potato is 150 meticais, and 1kg of cassava is 100 meticais.

South African employed Mozambican agricultural workers who returned to Mozambique for the holidays have prohibited from travel to South Africa until 15 February.  The suspension traveling across the border comes was to contain the second wave of COVID in South Africa.  Even Mozambican workers with 12 month work visas were refused access to South Africa in recent weeks.

30 Portuguese civil society organizations issued a public manifesto addressed to the EU and Portuguese Government regarding their concerns for the IDPs in Cabo Delgado on 29 January. The organizations called for more support to the over 500,000 people displaced in Cabo Delgado.

Sofala Health Director Massalambane stated that the healthcare system in the province has been strained due to the increasing number COVID tests in  the province. Director Massalambane said that around 600 samples daily are being sent for testing and only two laboratories in the province can handle up to 500 test per day.  Since the start of the year, over 1,213 cases have been diagnosed in Sofala, with 6 deaths.

The Beira Municipal Council stated that it will take 30 days to clean up all waste caused by Cyclone Eloise. 20 trucks would be used to clear out the waste along the streets in Beira. The city council has set up teams in all 26 neighborhoods of the city.

Nampula Lurio University suspended classes due to COVID cases and disinfection of the campus on 29 January. Three positive cases were recorded at the Faculty of Health Services. The positive cases were employees of the university and no students have tested positive for the virus.
A crocodile killed a teenager on the Mzimhlophe River near Motaze on 29 January. The victim was grazing his cattle when the attack occurred.

The WFP stated that 53% of children are malnourished in Cabo Delgado due to food insecurity in the province.  The WFP and other organizations are currently in the midst of scaling up programs to assist IDPS, including children, in the province.

President Filipe Nyusi gave an address to the SADC, saying that COVID pandemic is worsening in the region. The president said that the first of January 2021 accounted for 22 percent of the 346, 010 total number of cases since the beginning of the pandemic in the region. This had been largely due to a new COVID strain which has been reported in SADC countries. 50% of all new daily COVID infections at present on African continent are reported in the SADC region.   Nyusi called for continued cooperation and collaboration between SADC states to stop the spread of COVID-19. Nyusi also said in this speech that SADC members should pool their resources in order to procure and distribute COVID vaccines.

Seven new COVID deaths and 597 new cases were recorded by the Ministry of Health on 30 January. The fatalities were all men aged between 49 and 75. Maputo city registered 158 new cases, followed by the province of Gaza with 79 cases. There were 13,393  active COVID cases in the country as of Saturday.

UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres stated on 28 January during his 2021 priorities speech to the UN General Assembly that Chad, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Mozambique are a source of great concern due to it increasing challenges on terrorism as well as causes of economic, climate and social roots issues. He added that African peace implementation forces, including future multinational collaborations, deserve predictable funding and a mandate in the UN Security Council under Chapter Seven of the UN Charter. He wanted the international community to recognize aforementioned missions and said they should be supported with a mandate from the Security Council and should have access to all necessary resources and equipment.

The Ministry of Health warned on 29 January against self medication in COVI-19 cases, saying as it may aggravate the clinical condition and may hinder the recovery process for COVID-19. People were advised to take precautions on what they believe on social media regarding treatment of the virus. Pharmacists were urged to be more vigilant and all professionals were called to disseminate factual information on how to deal with COVID-19 and other diseases.

Mozambican Police arrested four suspected robbers in Beluluane, Maputo on 30 Jan over alleged robbery and assault accusations along the road. The suspects were allegedly responsible for robbing a female civilian of her possessions at the Beluluane Market. An operational vehicle was recovered from the suspects.

A source reported on 30 Jan a group of four suspects robbed a female charcoal seller of her possession at Beluluane Market. Reports suggest that two of the suspects distracted her while two others took advantage and stole her valuables. The suspects were later arrested by the police.

The World Bank committed on 27 January $12 billion support for COVID-19 vaccinations to African countries. According to David Malpass, president of the World Bank, the money will be in the form of grants or on 'highly concessional terms'. The project will target 21 countries in Africa, including the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Niger, Mozambique, Tunisia, Eswatini and Cabo Verde among others. As per Africa Centres for Disease Control, the estimated cost of vaccinating 60% of Africa’s 1.3 billion people would be between $10 billion and $15 billion.

Privinvest founder Iskander Safa in newly filed documents in the Hidden Debts case was reported on 31 January alleged that President Nyusi and other top Mozambican officials accepted large payments deemed "campaign donations", denying these payments were illegal or that they were bribes.  President Nyusi at the time (2014) was running for the presidency and was the Minister of Defense.  A FRELIMO spokesman meanwhile on 29 January said that President Nyusi and the FRELIMO party had "nothing to do" with the Hidden Debts, and that Nyusi at the time was allowed to receive political donations.  The documents allege that President Nyusi received $1 million, as well as was given a Toyota Land Cruiser.  Nyusi also allegedly had requested these additional "campaign contributions" after Privinest had already paid $10 million to FRELIMO, and $7 million to then Finance Minister Manuel Chang.  Note that Former President Guebuza had previously also been named as having been involved in the Hidden Debts case and to have reportedly received bribes in connection to it.

New reports suggest that Cyclone Eloise left three people dead, more than 10,000 displaced and 2,200 houses destroyed in the province of Manica alone.  The Cyclone struck the province on 23 January, with flooding in the following days.  Locals were urged to be cautious as the risk of flooding increases as rivers reached alert levels.

Four new COVID deaths and 949 new cases were recorded by the Ministry of Health on 31 January. Three of the fatalities were in Maputo city while one in Cabo Delgado province. As of Sunday, there were 14,328  active COVID cases in the country. Maputo city recorded 417, 211 in Maputo province, 38 in Gaza, 24 in Inhambana, 7 in Manica, 36 in Tete, 59 in Zambézia, 27 in Nampula, 99 in Niassa, and 31 in Cabo Delgado.

Zitamar's founder and editor, Tom Bowker, was set to be deported from Mozambique on 30 January, as had been threatened by Mozambican authorities earlier in the week.  Authorities are believed to have deported Bowker for his outlet's reporting both on the Hidden Debts Scandal as well as for the outlet's coverage of the insurgency in Cabo Delgado, which included coverage of security force abuses and the government's poor handling of the insurgency. A source claimed that Bowker was called into the Migration Services with his lawyer on 25 January and told him verbally that he had to leave by Saturday, based on a complaint from Gabinfo, the government information office.  Authorities had previously threatened Bowker with deportation, though had not followed through on these threats.  It was unclear as of 02 February if Bowker remained in Mozambique, though his legal team was challenging the authorities fuling.

Authorities announced on 30 Jan that the next heads of state summit of the African Union will be held on a virtual format due to the rapid spread of the COVID-19 on the continent. The summit, which was initially set to take place in Maputo on 06-07 February, is due to elect the chairperson, deputy chairperson and other members of the AU Commission. Among other issues, the fight against COVID-19 pandemic will be discussed.

Strong winds with gusts up to 70 kilometres per hour, with moderate to heavy rain (30 to 50 millimeters in 24 hours) and severe thunderstorms are forecasted from the afternoon of 01 February until 02 February in the provinces of Maputo, Gaza and Inhambane, according to the National Meteorological Institute (INAM) .These may affect the following areas in Maputo -Matutuine, Boane, Namaacha, Marracuene, Moamba, Magude and Manhica districts, and the cities of Maputo and Matola. The districts of Chicualacuala, Chigubo, Mabalane, Chibuto, Massingir, Limpopo, Chongoene, Massangena, Mapai, Guijá, Mandlakazi, Bilene, and in Chokwé and Xai-Xai cities of Gaza Province were also warned of rains and winds. The districts of Zavala, Inharrime and Panda of Inhambane were also affected. INAM advises residents to take safety measures.

Nigeria's Deputy Foreign Minister on 30 January after talks with Mozambican officials in Maputo said Nigeria was willing to provide support to Mozambique in the fight against Cabo Delgado insurgents, saying Nigeria would cooperate with Mozambique in any way Maputo saw fit.

Defense Minister Jaime Neto on 29 January said that the insurgency in Cabo Delgado has been increasingly weakened by security force operations in the province, saying that security forces had prevented insurgent from taking over Palma District, as insurgents had threatened in late December, also saying that the government wanted civilians to return to their "areas of origin" in the province to resume "day to day activities".

Defense Minister Jaime Neto on 29 January said that RENAMO dissident attacks had decreased significantly in Central Mozambique along the N1 and N6 roads and that security forces were "permanently in pursuit of the enemy".  Neto also said that RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo had rejected an offer of dialogue from the government and that the only alternative was to pursue the RENAMO dissident leader.

1,275 new COVID cases were reported on 29 January in Mozambique, the largest number of cases reported in a single day in the country.  9 new deaths were also reported, along with 28 new hospitalizations.  262 hospitalizations were reported nationwide.  590 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 145 in Maputo, 137 in Inhambane, 90 in Sofala, 74 in Zambezia, 66 in Gaza, 58 in Manica, 57 in Niassa, 32 in Nampula, 25 in Tete, and 1 in Cabo Delgado.  13,239 active cases were reported countrywide.

As of 01 February, Palma was reported to still be isolated with no supplies reaching the town by road in recent days after recent insurgent attacks along the Nangade-Palma Road.  This has caused significant rises in price of basic goods in Palma town as shortages of food and other products worsen.  No recent supplies have reach the town via sea or by the Tanzanian border either, local sources indicated.

Reports on 30 January reported that insurgents attacked Nkonga village in Nangade District at around 0900hrs. Insurgents carried out looting and set huts on fire in this attack.  Most local residents had fled the village prior to this incident after attacks in December.  Insurgents also reportedly abducted several women in the area.

Police arrested four individuals for stealing 41 TV sets from a warehouse in Machava, west Maputo, on 1 February. Police have conducted an investigation regarding the involvement of a warehouse employee.

The Center for Public Integrity stated an increased risk for COVID infections were expected at morgues in Maputo. The risk was due to the lack of measures to dispose the bodies of COVID victims, and several morgues are reportedly overcrowded.

An investigative report on 31 January said that a deposit of 500,000 meticais or over $66,000 is required as a deposit before hospitalization for COVID-19 at the Heart Institute.  At Maputo Private Hospital, a deposit of 390,000 meticais for patients in need of oxygen and a deposit of 650,000 meticais for those requiring ventilators was required.  At the Central Hospital of Maputo, a deposit of 250,000 meticais was required for those needing "resuscitation"; these amounts are beyond the means of nearly all Mozambicans.

Mozambique Airlines (LAM) delayed payment of January salaries due to the decreased revenues; company officials recently said that the airline is in a difficult situation. LAM director Jorge stated that the some of the contracts have been suspended and there has been a reduction in cash flow due to the pandemic.

Local business council officials stated that increases in COVID infections in Inhambane have led to rising prices and deteriorating healthcare in Inhambane. Residents stated that the prices of food items are varying and expensive.  Hospitals are reportedly running low on basic supplies as COVID cases increase in the province.

A conflict monitor said that Insurgent violence has escalated by 129% in 2020 compared to 2019.  This violence has surpassed the ongoing insurgency in Egypt. Two-thirds of the targets during these incidents were civilians wherein 1,600 deaths have been reported showing a 169% increase in fatalities.

The SADC has recently increased operations to combat the sudden rise in smuggling across the region. This includes a crackdown in smuggling in Mozambique, where smuggling across the country's porous borders is common.

Several locals have continued to erect illegal electrical networks on EDM power lines in Nacala. The illegal electrical networks were noted in Macone, Ontupaia, Maiaia, and Triangulo neighborhoods. Several thieves have also targeted the electrical power boxes in the area.

France and Portugal recently were reported to have conducted several meetings to discuss a potential counterinsurgency strategy in Cabo Delgado without input from Mozambique, which has been reluctant to request outside assistance to combat the insurgency.  These meetings were meant to clarify how the EU could contribute to counter the insurgency in Cabo Delgado; the EU has offered military training and humanitarian assistance to Mozambique to achieve this.

The Ministry of Health announced that January has been the worst month so far in Mozambique during the COVID pandemic. 201 deaths were recorded, accounting for 54.7% of the total deaths along with 20,012 infections which is 51.7% of the total infections. Hospitalizations have also increased as 801 were recorded for the whole of 2020 while 887 were recorded in January.
Security forces arrested a trader transporting food items at Tanzania-Mozambique border in Namoto on 19 January. No details were mentioned as to what charges were.

Tanzania is currently not allowing transportation of food items across the Namoto border crossing into Tanzania. Local traders stated that no details were mentioned regarding the suspension of food item trading.

Security forces recovered the bodies of three individuals and buried them in Pundanhar area on 19 January. The funerals were reportedly conducted in Nacala. The victims were previously ambushed by insurgents with their vehicle set on fire leaving their bodies along a road in Pundanhar.

The Ministry of Health announced 806 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 1 February, along with 19 deaths. 50 patients were also hospitalized for COVID. 406 of the cases were from Maputo city, 195 from Maputo province, 134 were from Inhambane, 37 in Nampula, 15 in Zambezia, 13 in Niassa, three in Tete and three in Sofala.

Rainfall renewed flooding was reported in neighborhoods of Maputo City on the afternoon of 1 February. The flooding has also affected several parts of Matola. This came after warnings of heavy rains and winds in Southern Mozambique.

South Africa's government on 01 February said it would donate an unspecified quantity of COVID vaccine does to Mozambique and other neighboring countries after receiving a donation of 7 million doses of the vaccine provided by telecoms company MTN.  In South Africa itself, the government hopes to achieve group immunity by vaccinating 40 million people, or about 67%.

Large numbers of IDPs have reportedly returned to their respective areas in Cabo Delgado as of 01 February. A majority of those who have returned were agricultural workers. Sources stated that the areas remain prone for water-borne illnesses. The areas include Metuge, Ibo, Quissanga, Meluco, and Macomia.

Sources stated that the areas remain prone for water-borne illnesses. The areas include Metuge, Ibo, Quissanga, Meluco, and Macomia.

Sources stated that the areas remain prone for water-borne illnesses. The areas include Metuge, Ibo, Quissanga, Meluco, and Macomia.

A new study published by researchers in Cabo Delgado determined that government forces "lack the military capacity" to end insurgent attacks in the province, and that better training and/or outside military support is likely necessary to defeat the insurgency.  The study, which interviewed IDPs from insurgent impacted zones, also said the government ignored signs of the budding insurgency that began to emerge in 2010.  The study also said the militant group is composed of "jihadists" of several different ethnicities and nationalities, and said many joined the group due to promises of employment, of scholarships to koranic schools, and for direct payments.

Hundreds of civil servants who have fled over the past year from insurgent attacks in Cabo Delgado are reported to be refusing calls by district governments to return to the districts where they work.  Muidumbe, Ibo, Palma, and Nangade have all issued these summons in recent months, with Palma ordering its civil servants to return to the district by early February, despite the fact that the district is isolated due to insurgent presences in the south and west of the district.  Government employees from these districts sheltering in Pemba say that insurgents continue to operate in these districts and that security has not been restored in these areas.  On 23 October, Muidumbe District issued a statement requiring civil servants to return to their posts in the district - this was just over a week before insurgents in a series of attacks beginning on 31 October virtually overran all of Muidumbe District, killing dozens of people, including in the Muatide area beheadings in November.

A convoy of 14 vehicles carrying passengers and supplies, including food, departed from Nangade for Palma on 02 February, accompanied by a military escort, (including military and pro-government militia personnel) and was confirmed to have arrived in Palma later in the day. No vehicles carrying supplies have been able to reach Palma since mid-January, after several insurgent attacks along this route, including in the Mandimba and Pundanhar areas.  The last such attack was reported on 22 January.

Health officials launched an anti-malaria campaign starting in Metuge and Ibo of Cabo Delgado province on 2 February. The campaign administered drugs against malaria which aims to reduce 80 percent of the malaria cases in the province. The campaign will include three phases wherein a 30-day spacing would be given per phase.  738,000 cases of malaria were reported in Cabo Delgado in 2020, which was a decrease by 22% compared to 2019.

Health officials distributed mosquito nets due to the increase in malaria cases in Zambezia province on 27 January. The nets were to prevent a further increase in cases. Health officials also stated that spraying would be conducted in populated areas.

Security officials stated that around 50 human trafficking victims were identified during 2018 and 2019 in Mozambique. 29 of the victims were identified last 2018 and 22 in 2019. 29 were local male and 18 were local women. Among the trafficked individuals was a Rwandan female.

The Ministry of Health announced the construction of warehouses for vaccine storage and distribution in the country. The warehouses were placed strategically to respond from one location to another within 48 hours. Three warehouses already were built in Zambezia, and another in Inhambane.
Mozambican Airlines (LAM) suspended all flights from Maputo-Inhambane and Maputo-Vilankulo until March due to impact of the pandemic. LAM stated that the suspension was temporary.
3 naval ships were stuck in Beira Port due to the low tide brought about by Cyclone Eloise. An operation was launched to reposition the ships to higher water levels.

10 civilians have died due to lighting strikes during heavy rainfall in Tete in recent thunderstorms in the province.  No specific details regarding where these lightning strikes occurred were immediately available.  The National Institute for Disaster Management (INGD), stated that the 3,300 families were affected by the heavy rainfall.
A 4.3 magnitude earthquake was felt in parts of Manica province on the night of 1 February. The epicenter of the quake was reported in Chipinge, Zimbabwe. No casualties were reported.

The Ministry of Health announced 17 COVID deaths and 800 new cases in Mozambique on 2 February. 432 of the new cases were recorded in Maputo City, 82 in Manica, 50 in Niassa, 49 in Gaza, 46 in Tete, 42 in Inahmbane, 31 in Zambezia, 28 in Cabo Delgado, 22 in Maputo, and 18 in Nampula.  No cases were reported in Sofala.  307 people are currently hospitalized across Mozambique, including 210 in Maputo City.    There are 14,843 active cases in the country.

The Regional Administration issued a warning that 30,000 people may be danger due to flooding of Limpopo River in five districts of Gaza province.  The areas of Pafuri, Combomune, Chokwe, Guija, Sicacatee and Xai-Xai were at risk due  to the potential flooding of the Limpopo from the Nwanetsi and Chingwedzi branches. The Massingire dam on the Rio dos Elefantes also is at 40% capacity and is not discharging water.
