Mozambican health authorities on 02 February said that they were awaiting official communication from the South African government related to potential donations of COVID-19 vaccines to Mozambique.  This came after SA President Cyril Ramaphosa said that the country would donate an unspecified number of COVID vaccine doses to Mozambique and other neighboring countries.

President Nyusi in a speech on 03 February said that youths who are members of the Cabo Delgado insurgency will "not be harmed" if they surrender to the government.  Nyusi said many insurgents want to return to their families and communities but fear retaliation.  He also said the security forces have instructions to "guarantee their safety and their reinsertion to society".  In the speech, delivered on Heroes' Day, also said that "challenges and constraints" continue to face the country, including fighting the RENAMO military Junta in Central Mozambique as well as fighting the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

In a speech delivered on 03 February, President Nyusi said Mozambique was in a "serious situation" due to the increase of COVID cases in the country in recent weeks, saying more restrictive measures to halt the spread of the virus could be imposed.  Nyusi said he would address the nation on 04 February regarding the state of calamity  measures and the state of COVID -19 in the country.
Insurgents on 31 January attacked the Nkonga village area for the second time in two days, setting fire to homes and carrying out looting before withdrawing from the area.
Pro-government militias mobilized to the Nkonga area after two insurgent attacks in the area on 30-31 January.  No clashes in the area have been reported in recent days.

Clashes occurred last week on an unknown date in the Panjele area of Mocimboa da Praia between pro-government militias and insurgents, close to the Nangade-MDP districts border.  The militia reported 27 insurgents killed in these clashes along with 3 militia members, with another two militia members injured.  The militia also reported capturing weapons, including RPGs and assault rifles from the insurgents.  This casualty count has not been confirmed and is likely inflated.  It was unclear if the militia or insurgents initiated this fighting.
Insurgents on or before 31 January erected a roadblock along the Pundanhar - Palma road.  Civilians in the area discovered the roadblock on Sunday.

The Maputo Mayor, Eneas Comiche, announced that the city would cancel titles of people living in mangrove forest areas of the city on 3 February. The mangroves are part of the Mozambique Land Law which are partially protected zones and cannot be acquired. Comiche stated that the locals have been living in the area even before 2020.

The Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) stated that Mozambique fell two places in Economist's democracy index for 2020 from 120 to 122. The country was classified as an "authoritarian" government.  Angola and Guinea Bissau, other Portuguese speaking African countries, had similarly poor scores in this index.

Doctors Without Borders (MSF) has appealed for vaccines for Southern Africa amid region wide COVID outbreak. MSF  stated that healthcare workers in other countries have started vaccination over the past two months and African countries have still to receive a large supply of vaccinations.  The organization also said it would be "indefensible" if lower risk citizens in other countries were vaccinated before health care workers in Southern Africa.

Local authorities stated that 7 civilians have died due to the diarrhea outbreak at the 25 September Center in Metuge as of 29 January.  Several casualties of the outbreak were reported in the Ntacota and Taratara.
Officials stated that an unidentified number of deaths due to a diarrhea outbreak have been reported in Ntacota and Taratara areas on 29 January.
Officials stated that an unidentified number of deaths due to a diarrhea outbreak have been reported in Ntacota and Taratara areas on 29 January.
Local sources showed videos of the markets running out of food supplies on 1 February. The lack of food items has also increased prices as a sack of rice cost 6,000 meticais.

Health centers were reported to have run low on medical supplies in Palma on 2 February. Pharmacies saw high demand from by locals who were attempting to obtain their prescriptions.  This came amid a general supply shortage in the town due to insurgent attacks along the Nangade-Palma road which had forced a halt to supply convoys to Mozambique.

The Ministry of Health announced 17 COVID deaths and 1173 new cases in Mozambique on 3 February. The cases are distributed as follows: 316 in Maputo City , 122 in Maputo province, 148 in Gaza, 121 in Inhambane, 195 in Sofala, 34 in Manica, 34 in Tete, 21 in Zambezia, 41 in Nampula, 70 in Niassa, and 71 in Cabo Delgado.

The National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD), stated that 57,000 hectares of agricultural crops were destroyed during the landfall of Cyclone Eloise in Mozambique. The two-day heavy rainfall affected 41,193 farmers.

President Nyusi in an address to the nation on 04 February announced new measures and restrictions taken by the government, effective from 05 February for 30 days (to 07 March), to stop the spread of COVID-19.  These restrictions will include: A mandatory curfew for the Greater Maputo Area, including Maputo City, Boane, Marracuene, and Matola, from 9pm to 4am daily. The postponement of the resumption of face-to-face classes of all levels of education. Places of worship, conferences, and religious celebrations will close for this period. Commercial establishments will be from 9am-7pm from Monday to Saturday, and from 9am to 4pm on Sunday.   Restaurants will be allowed to open from 7am to 8pm during the week.  Public event capacity is limited to 20 people. State events capacity is limited to 50 people. All recreational sport matches are banned.  The curfew is the first implemented in Mozambique since the Mozambican Civil War's end in 1992.

Defense Minister Jaime Neto on 03 February said that the country's security forces were "doing everything to neutralize Mariano Nhongo, whether by capture or other means".  Neto said no deadline had been set for RENAMO dissident leader Nhongo's surrender, and that security forces were currently "on the man's trail" in Central Mozambique.
Police arrested a motorcycle thief in Nampula on 3 February. The suspect impersonated a rider hailing motorcycle taxis and would bring to secluded areas before stealing the motorcycles.

National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) arrested a Congolese national in possession of counterfeit cash in Nampula on 31 January.  The arrest came after a tip was received regarding a group of people printing counterfeit money in the Mutauanha neighborhood.
Mozambique Airlines (LAM) announced that they have paid their staff salaries on 2 February. This comes as LAM previously announced a delay in salaries due to the lack of revenue.

Border police detained 736 border violators during a week-long operation from 23-29 January in Mozambique. 502 Mozambicans were detained, followed by 142 Malawians, 40 Zimbabweans, 28 Zambians, and 24 Tanzanians.
Police detained four suspects for stealing TV sets from a warehouse in Machava, west of Maputo city, on 1 February. A fifth suspect managed to escape.

A bus crashed into a drainage after attempting to overtake on a road in Junta, south Maputo City, at around 21:00 of 3 February. 6 passengers and the driver were injured. The driver claimed that the brakes failed but passengers stated that he was driving too fast and missed the roundabout.
SENAMI repatriated 81 foreign nationals to South Africa and Eswatini on 29 January. 46 Malawians, 12 Tanzanians, 12 Pakistanis, and 4 Zimbabweans were deported.

Police arrested a businessman identified as Minoj Hassam, in possession of 180kg of ephedrine in Pemba on 3 February. Ephedrine is used in the manufacturing of narcotics.  The seizure reportedly took place in the Cariaco neighborhood at a filling station. Police had reportedly monitored Hassam for some time in relation to "drug trafficking, money laundering, smuggling, and other crimes".  Hassam previously worked for the Aga Khan Foundation and was also previously a councilor for the Pemba City Council.

Portugal donated 90,000 EUR to support the fight against transnational crime by United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) in Mozambique. The UNODC aims to combat drug trafficking, money laundering and transnational organized crime. The financial support would allow appropriate training and the Global Maritime Crime Programme.

Observatório do Cidadão para Saúde (OCS) stated in a research that Mozambique has a shortage of COVID tests at public hospitals. Locals stated that public hospitals have not any provided test to voluntary individuals suspected with COVID. OCS also stated in their research that private hospitals reportedly been conducting tests even with long lines. The testing reportedly cost around 1,000 to 5,000 meticais.

Mozambique Deputy Director of Health announced that the country has COVID tests available for next 6 months. Health Deputy Director Matsinhe stated that the individuals with the “usual symptoms” are the only ones given the test while the rest are being denied, which officials say has created a feeling of a “lack of tests”. Matsinhe also mentioned that the delay in giving out the results may give an impression of the lack of equipment to conduct the tests.

Standard Bank Analysis stated that business activity has declined in Mozambique during January. The country’s business activity index fell from 49.3 points in December 2020 to 47.5 as of January. A solid deterioration in business conditions and the fastest seen in four months, the largest decline was since April 2020.  The fall in January represented the largest drop in business conditions since April 2020.

Bank of Mozambique intends to conduct calls checking “proof of life” to retired employees starting 8 February. This process would last until 26 February, to attempt to discover ghost accounts. The checking will be conducted by the Pension Fund of the Bank of Mozambique.

Mozambique will receive 2.4 million COVID vaccine doses by end of February as part of a joint program between the WHO and Global Alliance for Vaccines.  This will cover roughly 7 percent of the Mozambican population, including the country's frontline healthcare workers.

The Ministry of Health was reported on 04 February to not have enough PPE to protect health officials in Mozambique. The government previously received 100 million USD to provide prevention and treatment for COVID. Several health workers have complained about the increased risk due to the lack of PPE.  This has contributed to over 1,500 Mozambican healthcare workers testing positive for COVID-19 during the course of the pandemic.
Police arrested 16 Malawian illegal immigrants arrested in Tete, on Tuesday, 2 February. The immigrants were hiding inside a residence. The immigrants intended to travel to South Africa.
Police arrested 3 Malawian illegal immigrants inside a residence arrested in Chingodzi, central Tete, on 29 January.
Local sources stated that bus company, Greyhound will be shutting down by 14 February. The company based out of South Africa had previously offered routes to Maputo.

Local sources stated that oil and gas companies recently refused requests to import supplies to Palma. This came after recent shortages reported in the district after insurgent attacks along the Nangade-Palma road disrupted supply flows to the town.
Local sources stated that around 30,000 meticais were recently paid to the military to escort food and goods convoys travelling to Palma from Nangade.

Sources in Palma reported on 04 February that supplies that arrived in the town via an escorted convoy on 02 February had already run out, and that prices in the town for basic goods remained high.  A 25kg bag of rice was priced at 2,000 meticais (over $26), while a 25 kg bag of flour was priced at 1,800 meticais (just under $24).  Food supplies in the town remain low.

692 COVID cases were reported on 05 February in Mozambique, along with 9 new COVID deaths.  This brought the total deaths in the country to 436 along with 43,184 total COVID cases.  358 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 132 in Sofala, 60 in Maputo, 42 in Cabo Delgado, 36 in Manica, 34 in Tete, 20 in Nampula, 11 in Inhambane, 10 in Zambezia, and 3 in Gaza.  There are currently 16,532 active cases in the country, with 342 people hospitalized with the virus, including 255 in Maputo City.

Unconfirmed reports on 05 February reported that new army chief Eugenio Mussa was ill with either malaria or COVID-19 and had been hospitalized in Maputo City.  Other unverified reports said that the general had passed away.

Media sources reported on 05 February that Total will utilize Pemba for almost all of its logistics requirements in Area 1 of the Rovuma Basin.  This will be carried out from the Muxara area.  Mayotte is being investigated as a potential "support base", the company said, but most logistics related activities will be based out of Pemba.

Mozambique from 01-04 February reported a total of 50 COVID deaths, representing 11% of all COVID deaths in the country to date.  Mozambique since 08 January has seen a major spike in COVID cases, with over 20,000 cases reported in January.

On 04 February, 1,055 new COVID cases along with 12 new deaths were reported in Mozambique.  This included 476 new cases in Maputo city, 176 in Gaza, 127 in Maputo, 124 in Sofala, 81 in Inhambane, 27 in Nampula, 21 in Zambezia, 13 in Tete, 7 in Manica, and 3 in Niassa.  No new cases were reported in Cabo Delgado.

Police detained a woman in Machava in Matola on 05 February for allegedly violating the "public calamity" measures.  The woman just hours later was found dead in Machava by local residents with signs of trauma on her body, with police suspected in her death.

Police detained a woman in Machava in Matola on 05 February for allegedly violating the "public calamity" measures.  The woman just hours later was found dead in Machava by local residents with signs of trauma on her body, with police suspected in her death.

Insurgents on 30 January in an attack on Nkonga village forced a local girl to lead the insurgents to a group of women and girls who had hidden in the bush during the attack.  2 of these 6 girls were abducted by the insurgents, who withdrew from the village after carrying out looting and setting homes on fire.

Insurgents on 01 February attacked Lijungo village, about 50kms south of Nangade.  Insurgents set several homes on fire and carried out looting.  The village had already been mostly abandoned by local civilians before the raid.

The City Council announced that it would open a morgue for COVID fatalities in Maputo City on 4 February. This move was made to de-congest other morgues which had been receiving COVID fatalities. Council officials stated that the new morgue can take in 60 bodies which is aimed to reduce potential spread of COVID at morgues which are taking in new virus fatalities since a spike in deaths in January.

Unconfirmed reports stated that there were 38 new COVID cases among American diplomatic staff in Maputo. The outbreak of COVID among the diplomatic mission was reported to be disrupting diplomatic activities at the embassy.

Officials stated that the health system is stressed in Manica province due to the COVID pandemic. Provincial Health Services Director, Xavier Alcides Isidoro, stated that 140 medical professionals were infected with COVID. The province has currently 933 active cases and 5 deaths.

The Japanese government donated $4.2 million to support IDPs in Cabo Delgado on 5 February.  Japanese Ambassador to Mozambique, Hajime Kimura, stated that the Japanese government has also intends to provide assistance to install water supply systems in Monapo, Nampula province.

The Japanese government donated $4.2 million to support IDPs in Cabo Delgado on 5 February.  Japanese Ambassador to Mozambique, Hajime Kimura, stated that the Japanese government has also intends to provide assistance to install water supply systems in Monapo, Nampula province.

The Order of Doctors of Mozambique Chairperson Dr Gilberto Manhica stated that the Mozambican health system has been “weak” for a long time and the COVID pandemic has caused a further deterioration in the health system.  He also said shortages in protective equipment had led to large numbers of health workers being infected with COVID-19.

Local sources released a video showing police assaulting a civilian after President Nyusi implemented a curfew from 21:00 to 04:00 on the night of 5 February. The curfew was implemented Maputo City, Matola, Boane village, and Marracuene district.

928 COVID cases were reported on 06 February in Mozambique, along with 15 new COVID deaths.  This brought the total deaths in the country to 451 along with 44,112 total COVID cases. There were 276 cases in Sofala, 263 cases from Maputo city, 66 from Maputo province, 76 cases from Tete, 60 from Gaza, 52 from Cabo Delgado, 47 from Zambezia, 44 from Manica, 25 from Nampula and 19 from Niassa. There are currently 317 people hospitalized with the virus and 78% of these patients were in Maputo City.

On 06 February, a local clinic was shut down during a joint operation by district and village police officers in 3 de Fevereiro, KaMavota, Maputo City. The clinic allegedly served as a guest house at night. Two people were arrested during this operation.
On 06 February, Two people were arrested for illegally operating a clinic/guest house by police officers in 3 de Fevereiro, KaMavota, Maputo City.

488 COVID cases were reported on 07 February in Mozambique, along with 9 new COVID deaths. This brought the total deaths in the country to 460 along with 44,600 total COVID cases.  203 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 40 in Maputo Province, 51 in Gaza, 30 in Manica, 100 in Cabo Delgado, 35 in Niassa, 12 in Nampula, 12 in Zambezia and five cases in Tete.  There are currently 316 people hospitalized with the virus.

A restaurant owner pushed a cameraman of STV, Sebastia Ngomane, and damaged his camera in a bid to prevent him from filming at Rayan Pastelaria e Restaurante, Maputo City on 05 February. The incident was triggered as the STV journalist, Anfonso Chavo, attempted to interview a female employee of the restaurant after another young employee declined a scheduled interview  regarding the curfew in Greater Maputo region. Media Institute of Southern Africa MISA-Mozambique condemned the incident and stated that that no one should resort to violence or other means to obstruct the journalists' work material.
column15: Rayan Pastelaria e Restaurante, Maputo City

column4: The United Nations' Office for Drugs and Organized Crime (UNODC) representative, César Guedes, commended Mozambique's fight against drug trafficking, a source reported on 08 February.  This comes after several recent high profile drug seizures in Mozambique and in Mozambican coastal waters.

President Filipe Nyusi stated on 06 Feb, during the opening session of the virtual 34th summit of the African Union, that he hopes to see a "firm intent" from the African Union in the fight against insurgency in Cabo Delgado Province. Nyusi added that the Mozambique for solidarity from the AU in the fight against the Cabo Delgado insurgency, but also said the AU has not provided "concrete support" to Mozambique in the fight against the insurgents.

Smuggling of essential items across the Malawian-Mozambican border has recently been reported at the Tsangano and Ntcheu border areas.  Items commonly smuggled include wheat flour, cooking oil, beer, and soft drinks.  Police are not deployed in these areas, making smuggling in these locations easier for smuggling gangs.

There is a significant risk of flooding along the Limpopo River in Gaza Province as water levels continue to increase. The current water levels in the river area caused by large volumes of water flowing from the Beit Bridge station in Zimbabwe. The increasing flow may result in the destruction of the dikes at Chokwe.  River levels were already relatively high due to the ongoing rainy season, which included large volumes of rain brought by Cyclone Eloise last month.  Flooding along the Limpopo, particularly in places like Chokwe and Xai Xai, could potentially displace thousands of people.

On the evening of 31 January, a motorcycle mechanic was killed in a road accident at the intersection of Marrere, Nampula City. The deceased, who was under the influence of alcohol, was driving at a high speed when he collided with a commercial motorcycle bound to a fuel station. A local claimed that the intersection was a accident prone area.

On 26 January, a road accident was reported involving  a car and a motorcycle at the intersection of Marrere, Nampula City. Two occupants of the motorcycle sustained injuries in the accident. No other details on this incident are currently available.

Mozambique's Ministry of Defense on 08 February released a brief statement saying that Eugenio Mussa, the recently appointed Chief of Staff of the Mozambican Defense Armed Forces, had passed away after a brief illness.  Mussa had been promoted to lead the Mozambican Defense Armed Forces on 14 January.  Sources later indicated Mussa had died of COVID-19.

It was reported on 08 February that it was difficult for locals to move between areas in Pafuri, Chicualacuala due to recent heavy rains in the area which had caused flooding.  Some food shortages in the area were reported as well.

Several sources have reported ongoing security force operations targeting insurgents in Cabo Delgado between 04-08 February.  One such source reported military helicopters carried out operations on the night of 05-06 February targeting militants in Mocimboa da Praia; fires were also reported in the town over the weekend.  Military helicopters reportedly carried out out strafing attacks on militants in several locations in Macomia ( including areas north of Macomia town along the N380 Road) and Mocimboa da Praia as well, also saying these operations were ongoing.  Some sources have also referred to ground force operations in parts of Macomia and Muidumbe Districts, though no other details regarding these operations are currently available.

Several sources have reported ongoing security force operations targeting insurgents in Cabo Delgado between 04-08 February.  One source reported that helicopters between 04-06 February had targeted insurgents in strafing attacks in Macomia and Muidumbe, allegedly killing a number of militants including reportedly 8 insurgent leaders, including one Tanzanian national and two men described as "Arabs".  This report indicated these operations were carried out after insurgent communications were intercepted regarding militants gathering in these two districts.  Another source indicated that military helicopters were carrying out strafing attacks on militants in several locations in Macomia ( including areas north of Macomia town along the N380 Road) and Mocimboa da Praia as well, also saying these operations were ongoing.  Some sources have also referred to ground force operations in parts of Macomia and Muidumbe Districts, though no other details regarding these operations are currently available.

Several sources have reported ongoing security force operations targeting insurgents in Cabo Delgado between 04-08 February.  One source reported that helicopters between 04-06 February had targeted insurgents in strafing attacks in Macomia and Muidumbe, allegedly killing a number of militants including reportedly 8 insurgent leaders , including one Tanzanian national and two men described as "Arabs".  This report indicated these operations were carried out after insurgent communications were intercepted regarding militants gathering in these two districts.   Another source indicated military helicopters had carried out "bombings" in Muidumbe over a five day period, and that these operations were ongoing.  Some sources have also referred to ground force operations in parts of Macomia and Muidumbe Districts, though no other details regarding these operations are currently available.
column15: Insurgent held areas of Muidumbe District

column4: 34 more trucks carrying supplies escorted by soldiers and pro-government militia on Saturday travelled from Nangade to Palma.  Helicopters also reportedly escorted the convoy along at least some of the route to protect against insurgent attacks.  This came after food shortages and significant food price inflation had been reported in Palma due to this route being cut off by insurgents during the second half on January.

South Africa on 07 February announced that it would pause the roll-out of COVID-19 vaccinations after a trial showed the AstraZeneca vaccine was less effective in preventing the new South African COVID vaccine.  Tests conducted by South Africa recently revealed only a 22% lower risk of developing mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in those who received this vaccine versus those given a placebo. This same variant is currently the dominant strain in Mozambique, and some of the vaccines recently received by South Africa had been meant to be donated to Mozambique.  This will mean at least a partial postponement of a vaccination campaign in Mozambique.

Former RENAMO dissident spokesman Joao Machava said in a recent interview that RENAMO dissident leader had reportedly been deserted by most of the men of the RENAMO base in Mabote District of Gaza, which had been Nhongo's main source of support previously.  According to Machava, around 170 armed men had previously joined Nhongo from this base; it is unclear how many still are under the command of Nhongo.  Only one dissident attack has been reported in Central Mozambique so far this year.

A government issued study advises against the restoration of Beira “Palace of Weddings” which was damaged by cyclones due to large amount of money required.  The study instead said authorities should focus on strengthening coastal protection works to shield the city from the impact of extreme weather events such as Cyclone Eloise, which hit the city on 23 February.

UNODC announced that an office based in Maputo would be set up to coordinate joint maritime security efforts  between Mozambique, South Africa, and Tanzania. This office will focus on information gathering and exchanges between the three navies of the countries, and is intended to help strengthen patrol and security along the countries' collective coasts.

Security forces arrested a Portuguese suspect for breeding and illegally selling endangered turtles from his residence in Nampula on 8 February. 79 radiated tortoises were seized from the suspect.  The man had bread the tortoises for 16 years, reportedly selling them, according to authorities.  Note the suspect himself said he had been attempting to register a business in order to legally sell the turtles, and said he had intended to eventually sell the animals - though also said he had not yet actually sold any of them.
Thieves stole a 100Kw power transformer in Catembe, south of Maputo City, on 8 February, cutting off electricity to the area and leaving 150 local families without power.
Around 150 families lost electricity when thieves stole an electrical power transformer in Catembe, south of Maputo City on 8 February.

Mozambique intends to apply for a non-permanent seat on the UN Security Council, sources reported on 08 February.  The AU is supporting Mozambique's bid.  President Nyusi in an 08 February speech said that "the importance that we dedicate to national, continental, and international peace and security has impelled us to apply, on behalf of the continent, for a non-permanent member seat of the UN Security Council".

Local media on 08 February reported that COVID measures are not being followed in much of Maputo City at commercial establishments.  Many stores reportedly lack adequate required prevention measures against COVID, including handwashing areas, the enforcement of social distancing, limiting store capacities, and a lack of temperature monitoring devices.  The city has recorded more than half of the COVID-19 cases in the country, and is currently under a curfew to prevent the further spread of the virus

312 new COVID cases were recorded in Mozambique by the Ministry of Health for Monday, 8 February. 5 new deaths were also recorded increasing the total to 465.  128 of the new cases were recorded in Maputo City and 57 in Cabo Delgado.  There are currently 17,005 active cases in the country.

The Ministry of Health stated that the first week of February was the most fatal week of the pandemic in Mozambique so far, with a high COVID mortality rate of 9.7 a day with a total of 68 deaths. In comparison, there were 201 COVID deaths in January 2021, having an average mortality rate of 6.5 day. A total of 460 COVID victims have died since 25 May 2020. As of December last year 166 individuals had died due to the pandemic.

Zimbabwean Ambassador to Mozambique, former General Douglas Nyikayaramba, passed away due to the Coronavirus. Nyikayaramba also served a the chief of staff administration for the Zimbabwe National Army, and played an important role in the coup that ousted Robert Mugabe in 2017.

Local sources stated that an inmate tested positive for COVID inside the Maputo Province Prison Pavilion 4 in recent days, and was placed in isolation on 08 February. The incident has reportedly caused panic among the other 100+ inmates of the facility. This comes as five prison personnel tested positive for COVID.

Amnesty International stated that gender violence against women has increased in Mozambique due to the pandemic. People spending more time in their homes has amplified structural problems such as poverty, inequity, high unemployment, and failures of the criminal justice system.  This is part of a wider region-wide trend tracked by the organization.

A low pressure system was reported on 09 February to be forming over the Mozambique Channel, and is likely to become a Tropical Depression by 12 February.  This storm could potentially further intensify and then impact the Mozambican coast on 13 February, likely hitting Zambezia, Sofala, and Inhambane.

Police arrested 94 people in Maputo City and another 140 in Maputo province for violating curfews during the weekend. The curfew was previously instituted on 05 February from 21:00 to 04:00 as part of new anti-COVID precautions.

Police arrested 94 people in Maputo City and another 140 in Maputo province for violating curfews during the weekend. The curfew was previously instituted on 05 February from 21:00 to 04:00 as part of new anti-COVID precautions.

Police arrested a suspect in a murder case in Manhica on 06 February. A crowd of locals on Saturday night attacked a police station at the 3rd February AP post, attempting to lynch the man.  The crowd destroyed several vehicles in the police compound before being dispersed by police.

Police arrested a suspect in a murder case in Manhica on 06 February. A crowd of locals on Saturday night attacked a police station at the 3rd February AP post, attempting to lynch the man.  The crowd destroyed several vehicles in the police compound before being dispersed by police.
Police arrested three suspects and seized 100kg of cannabis at undisclosed location in Zambezia on 8 February. The drugs were transported from Beira. The suspects were the smuggler and two buyers.

The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) stated that bars are trying to bypass COVID rules by declaring themselves "bottle stores", as bars have been closed down under the current anti-COVID restrictions while bottle stores may remain open until 1300hrs daily.

Mozambican President Filipe Nyusi on Friday in a speech stated that police should enforce COVID measures and the curfew but not abuse civilians. Nyusi said “I did come here to tell you to ensure compliance with the government decree on the State of Public Calamity”. Nyusi previously imposed a curfew from 21:00 to 04:00 starting 5 February; there have subsequently been some reports of police abusing their authority targeting civilians who have violated the curfew.

Locals sources stated that Zimbabwean forces had recently trained two companies of Mozambican troops in Manica province.  The newly trained soldiers were to be deployed to combat the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  No other details regarding this training are currently available.

President of Cabo Delgado's Business Council Julio Sethy voiced concern regarding recent statements that O&G major Total was considering Mayotte as a logistics base for some of its activities as this could potentially take business away from Pemba and Cabo Delgado as a whole. Sethy said that if the resources were in Mozambique, it made no sense that French territory would be used as a logistics base.  Total recently did indicate it could move some logistics support activity to Mayotte, but that Pemba would serve as the primary logistics hub for the company's activities in Cabo Delgado.  This comes after insurgent attacks near the Afungi Peninsula caused Total to evacuate a large number of its personnel from the area in early January, and to consider moving some of its activities out of Palma District due to insecurity.

A  lawyer for a detained businessman in Pemba stated that his client is not guilty of drug smuggling charges he was arrested on over the weekend in Pemba.  The businessman in question, Minoj Hassam, was arrested in possession of 180kgs of ephedrine; Hassam's lawyer says police initially claimed Hassam was caught with a large quantity of cocaine, before later claiming he had been caught with ephedrine.

Police arrested a pastor and his gang for stealing from a residence in Memo area of Marracuene, north of Maputo City, on 8 February. Police stated that the pastor dropped his mobile at the scene of the crime which led to the arrest.

A fire as part of a suspected insurgent attack in Mtmaba village in Nangade District on the night of 2 February and into the early morning hours of 3 February.  No further details regarding this attack are currently available.
SERNIC detained two Somali nationals for drug smuggling at Nampula Airport on 5 February. The suspects had arrived from Kenya and were in possession of 168kg of miraa (khat).
SERNIC detained two Somali nationals for drug smuggling at Nampula Airport on 5 February. The suspects had arrived from Kenya and were in possession of 168kg of miraa (khat).

Cashew manufacturing company, Olam, announced it was shutting down operations in Mozambique after 22 years of work in the country.  This came after the company reported a lack of raw materials to produce its product as well as global trends in world wide cashew nut markets.  Cashew nut prices fell significantly in 2020. The company had employed around 3,000 workers in Mozambique.

Police in Pemba said in recent days that three insurgent youths had fled from insurgent-controlled forest areas and surrendered to authorities in Pemba. The youths were in possession of around 3 million meticais, which they are believed to have stolen in various insurgent raids.  The three are believed to surrendered to take advantage of a recent amnesty offered by President Nyusi to insurgents in Cabo Delgado.

In a press conference on 09 February, Total CEO Patrick Pouyanne indicated that the Mozambican government in recent talks agreed to extend the security cordon around the Afungi LNG Camp to 25kms.  Pouyanne also said the security situation in Palma District was "problematic", as insurgents had come within less than 10 kms of the camp in late December and early January.  He went on to say that "if on the ground, the armed forces and the police are able to re-control the area that we agreed together" that operations could re-start at the Afungi LNG Camp by the end of the first quarter.  Despite this terror threat, Pouyanne also indicated that the LNG project was still slated to start production in 2024.

Portuguese Defense Minister João Cravinho stated that training for Mozambican security forces by the EU may start in early April.  Cravinho also said that there would be "logistical support in terms of equipment".  Training support will be designed to help the military fight against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

The Ministry of Health stated that 15 individuals have died due to COVID and 873 new cases in Mozambique on 9 February. The cases were recorded as follows: 348 in Maputo city, 183 in Inhambane, 116 in Tete, 104 in Sofala, 85 in Gaza, 77 in Maputo province, 41 in Cabo Delgado, 13 in Zambézia, and 6 in Nampula. There have been 480 deaths and 45,785 total COVID cases.

Girl Child Rights, a local NGO, announced that 26 girls were saved from early marriages out of the 109 cases in Manica in 2020. During the last quarter of 2020 206 cases of violations of children were reported in various districts of Manica province. Half of the reported cases were linked to early marriages.  Local populations are able to report cases of early marriage through a special Child Speech Line.

133 cases of cholera have been reported in Namialo, Meconta in Nampula Province, along with 52 hospitalizations, though no deaths have been reported, officials said on Monday. Officials conducted a meeting at the Emergency Operational Centre stating that the situation is concerning and that several individuals might bring the disease to Nampula city and Monapo district.

The National Inspection of Economic Activities of Mozambique (INAE) accused cement suppliers of manipulating the price for cement bags in Maputo on 9 February. INAE stated that cement supplies were being sold for 700 meticais per 50kg bag due to high demand.  Market prices for cement are reported to be 455-465 meticais per 50kg bag.

The Mozambican government on 09 February indicated that the face to face SADC meetings in Maputo set to occur in March would not take place due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs officials, Alfredo Nuvunga, said that a virtual meeting may take place on scheduled by 20-21 March.  An SADC Summit had been set to take place in January in Maputo in which regional leaders had been meant to discuss potential regional support for Mozambique in fighting the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

Johnson and Johnson (J&J) stated that the delivery of their new COVID vaccine has been fast tracked to South Africa after the AstraZeneca vaccine proved less effective against the South African strain of COVID. South African health officials stated that the J&J vaccine can be stored in refrigerators in comparison to other vaccines that require sub-zero temperature storage.  South Africa had initially indicated it would provide large quantities of the AstraZeneca vaccine to its neighbors, including Mozambique; it is unclear if the country still plans to donate these vaccine doses to Mozambique after it receives new J&J vaccine supplies.

The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said this week that 90% of health centers in insurgent impacted areas in Cabo Delgado have been attacked by insurgents during the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. The health facilities have been deliberately targeted in these attacks, the organization said.

Police arrested a suspect involved with the sexual assault and death of a woman near Machava, north Matola, on 6 February. The victim's body was found just a few meters from her residence.  Note that security forces were initially suspected in this incident as the woman had been detained shortly before being discovered dead.

A supply ship reportedly left Pemba traveling to Palma, indicating the possible reopening of a maritime supply routes to Palma, which recently had been cut off from road supply routes due to insurgent attacks. Authorities in recent months had banned local vessels from sailing between Palma and Pemba after a number of insurgent attacks on islands in the Quirimbas Archipelago and piracy style attacks on local vessels.

EDM announced that the state electricity company had suffered a loss of 9 million meticais in 2020 in the Mabalane and Mapai areas of Gaza. These losses were due to the theft of electrical equipment and clandestine connections. A majority of these clandestine electricity theft incident were noted in Mabalane and Mapai areas in Gaza province. Company officials stated that they have been in coordination with the police to detain the suspects in these cases.

EDM announced that the state electricity company had suffered a loss of 9 million meticais in 2020 in the Mabalane and Mapai areas of Gaza. These losses were due to the theft of electrical equipment and clandestine connections. A majority of these clandestine electricity theft incident were noted in Mabalane and Mapai areas in Gaza province. Company officials stated that they have been in coordination with the police to detain the suspects in these cases.

Mozambique's state revenue reportedly dropped by 14.8% in 2020. A total revenue of 236.3 billion meticais was reported during 2020 in comparison to 276.7 billion meticais in 2019. Expenditure has also reportedly increased by 60.5 billion meticais in the last year for a total of 374 billion meticais in spending.

43,000 families were impacted across Gaza due to flooding brought about by Cyclone Eloise and rains in the aftermath of the cyclone.  No deaths were reported. The National Institute for Disaster Risk Management stated that water levels around Limpopo river remain high, though are dropping back down to normal levels. 32,000 hectares of agricultural products were affected by the high-water levels.

Around 100 doctors who work as administrators for the Ministry of Health will be integrated into frontline medical staff treating COVID-19 cases.  Ministry of Health announced that the  doctors would be placed in hospital units to minimize the further transmission of COVID. Among the doctors deployed will be Minister of Health, Armindo Daniel Tiago.

Three doctors were hospitalized due to COVID at the isolation center in Quelimane of Zambezia Province. 50 health workers in the province have been infected with COVID-19 since the start of the pandemic.

Mozambique has registered a high rate of COVID-19 cases of the South African strain in recent months.  The National Health Institute (INS) stated that 20% of all COVID cases in Mozambique are of the new South African strain. This positivity rate is as high as 30% in Maputo City, Maputo Province, and Sofala.
Local sources stated that the Director of District Health Services for Mocimboa da Praia has died due to an illness at Pemba Provincial Hospital on the evening of 9 February.

The National Institute for Disaster Management (INGD) stated on 10 February that 16 civilians have died due to flooding in recent days along the banks of the Meluli River in Nampula province.  A majority of the deaths were reported in the Rapale area. Around 9,000 individuals were affected by the flooding in the province.  170 classrooms were also affected by the flooding, suspending the studies of around 14,482 students.

Pro-government militia forces on 05 February clashed with insurgents in the Ntchinga area of Muidumbe, reportedly attacking an insurgent bush camp.  No details on casualties are available.  Insurgents had been previously reported to have been based in this area.

A large group of government troops, supported by 8 helicopters, advanced to the Awasse area on 05 February.  This force may have been bound for Mocimboa da Praia, though it is unclear if the force advanced past Awasse; insurgents previously have controlled all of the N380 road between Awasse and MDP.

A medical charity in the first week of February returned to Macomia district, providing medical services in the Muagamula area outside of Macomia town, providing treatment to as many as 100 people per day.  The charity had previously withdrawn from Macomia in June 2020 after insurgent attacks in the district, leaving a lack of medical services in the area over the last 8 months.  Security conditions have improved in recent months around Macomia town itself, which appears to no longer be under direct threat of militant attack.  Insurgents do however remain active in the district north of Macomia around Chai, and in Mucojo AP on the coast.

Mozambique's meteorological institute said on 10 February that a low pressure system currently forming in the Mozambican Channel could still develop into a tropical depression and could impact maritime traffic in Central Mozambique.  The system could bring heavy rains, strong winds, and thunderstorms on 13 February into Maputo and Gaza.

A group of insurgents are reported to be present in the Nkonga area of Nangade District, and have carried out abductions in this area in recent days.  Insurgents had previously been reported in early February to have raided Nkonga and other nearby areas.  Large numbers of IDPs in recent days have fled the Nkonga area, arriving in Nangade town which is about 50kms away, saying that insurgents in the area are carrying out kidnappings and attacks on civilians in the area.

A group of insurgents are reported to be present in the Nkonga area of Nangade District, and have carried out abductions in this area in recent days.  Insurgents had previously been reported in early February to have raided Nkonga and other nearby areas.  Large numbers of IDPs in recent days have fled the Nkonga area, arriving in Nangade town which is about 50kms away, saying that insurgents in the area are carrying out kidnappings and attacks on civilians in the area.

Security force sources this week in Cabo Delgado said that operations had been carried out in Muidumbe and Macomia which had resulted in the deaths of 8 insurgent leaders, including one Tanzanian national and two "Arab" individuals, including one man reported to be one of the group's top commanders.  Military sources however have not provided specific details about the forces involved or specific areas where these operations in these districts took place  Sources also said insurgents were losing ground and had only a small number of supply bases left, and that security forces controlled "logistical channels" in the province, cutting insurgents off from food and other supplies.  The source also reported that insurgents were deserting the group in increasing numbers.
Sources on 08 February that military helicopters carried out attacks on insurgnet positions in the Xitaxi area.  No further information on this incident is currently available.

The Mozambican Military after a 22 January attack at Mandimba were reported to have deployed reinforcements to the area.  The exact number of these reinforcements is unclear.  50 border guards had been deployed to the town when insurgents attacked Mandimba in late January, killing at least one border guard and driving the rest of this contingent temporarily out of the area.

An insurgent attack was reported on Nkonga village in Nangade on 02 February, in which insurgent carried out looting and reportedly killed an unknown number of civilians.  This report is currently unverified.

The Ministry of Health announced six more COVID deaths and 951 new cases in Mozambique on 10 February. The new cases brings the total deaths to 486 and total cases to 46,736. The current new cases are as follows: 269 in Sofala, 251 in Maputo city, 158 in Maputo province, 69 in Manica, 59 in Cabo Delgado, 54 in Gaza, 53 in Niassa, 37 in Nampula, and 1 in Zambezia.

Local health officials reported outbreaks of acute diarrhea in Moma, Memba, and Erati, in Nampula on 8 February. Local officials say they are monitoring these outbreaks; a cholera outbreak is also ongoing in the province.

Local health officials reported outbreaks of acute diarrhea in Moma, Memba, and Erati, in Nampula on 8 February. Local officials say they are monitoring these outbreaks; a cholera outbreak is also ongoing in the province.

Police detained a suspect for transporting 1,400L of stolen petrol in the port of Pemba on 4 February. Security forces stated other suspects managed to escape. The fuel was stored in various drums which were being loaded on two rowing boats at the port.

Police detained a suspect for transporting 1,400L of stolen petrol in the port of Pemba on 4 February. Security forces stated other suspects managed to escape. The fuel was stored in various drums which were being loaded on two rowing boats at the port.

Local sources stated that Mavalane General Hospital lack of X-ray films to print out X-rays for patients. Patients reportedly are currently forced to use their cell phone to take copies to show to doctors and those who do not have a mobile phone cannot be diagnosed.  If the patient does not have a phone with a camera, a copy of the X-ray was sent to the patient via Bluetooth to assure the legibility of the X-ray.

The National Directorate of Public Health called on the public to continue to wear masks outside their residences. The National Directorate of Public Health stated that the use of masks is mandatory in all public places, gatherings, where people are crowded, public spaces, markets, public transport and semi-collective passenger and common areas.

Local sources stated that some health workers were found illegally selling COVID diagnostic tests for 1,000-1,500 meticais at Maputo Central Hospital (HCM).  Many people at public hospitals have recently reported they are not able to obtain a COVID test, but the tests reportedly can be obtained for an illegal payment.  Since a rise in cases in Mozambique in early January, there has been a lack of COVID tests in the country, and some people seeking tests at public hospitals are turned away.

The Manhica Health Research Centre (CISM) announced that the facility would begin conducting clinical trials of BCG, a tuberculosis drug, in the treatment of COVID-19.. Around 520 health professionals may be recruited to take part in this trial.  Some similar tests in South Africa, the Netherlands, and Australia have yielded results that seem to indicate the drug does not prevent COVID-19 infections but can prevent severe cases of the virus.

Since 2015, 46 civil construction companies have closed down due to a lack of public and private contracts in Manica.  A construction company association spokesman said only 3 such firms are still operating in the province, and that the awarding of public tenders to companies with connections to the state had taken away business from companies that were forced to shut down.

The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) announced that 43 tents/stalls were closed down due for violating measures issued during the State of Public Calamity in Nampula in operations between Sunday and Tuesday. The stalls had allegedly sold alcoholic beverages, and were not allowed to do so under the current anti-COVID restrictions.

The Bank of Mozambique (BM) announced on 9 February that it had reinforced additional precautionary measures against COVID. Sanitizing stations were placed in each of branch and ATMs. Social distancing of 2 meters and checking of temperatures was also implemented at branches.

Total's Chief Executive Patrick Pouyanné in remarks on 09 February said that despite security issues, the company planned to have LNG projects in Cabo Delgado up and running by 2024.  He also said in terms of onshore operations, the company intended to restart work by the end of the first quarter of the year, as long as the security situation around the Afungi LNG site had improved.

A report on 11 February indicated that the Islamic State's core organization had recently "recognized" the success of the Islamic State's Central Africa Province (ISCAP) and had "sent funding and a reinforcement of trainers and strategists through a preexisting network of regional facilitators and logisticians".  No other details on this development were immediately available.

The Vatican announced on 11 February that the Bishop of Pemba, D. Luiz Fernando Lisboa, was being transferred to a Brazilian diocese.  Lisboa had been the Bishop of Pemba since June 2013, and had led significant church efforts to support IDPs in Cabo Delgado since the beginning of the insurgency in October 2017.  Lisboa was also unique in that he regularly criticized the government and military's conduct in the war against the insurgents publicly; his independent position and backing of the Catholic Church, evidenced by public messages of support for Lisboa from Pope Francis, meant he arguably was the only high-profile public figure on the ground in Cabo Delgado who could speak critically of the government and military without substantial repercussions.  In an interview, Lisboa later indicated that threats he had received may have been part of the reason he was transferred, also saying such threats were normal for journalists, human rights activists, and members of the church in Cabo Delgado.  Lisboa also said he had never asked to leave Pemba, and there is some speculation that the Pope and Catholic Church may have been under some pressure from the Maputo government to transfer Lisboa out of the country.

Mozambique's meteorological institute said on 11 February that a low-pressure system continued to form in the Mozambique Channel, and could potentially become a tropical depression on 12 February.  The storm could begin to impact Southern Mozambique on Friday, before making landfall on Saturday, and then likely dissipating on Sunday.  The storm will likely make landfall in Inhambane, and would also impact Gaza and Maputo.  The storm could bring winds up to 70kms per hour, with rains between 50 to 100 millimeters. This could affected maritime activities as possible high waves and strong winds become evident along coastal areas in Southern Mozambique.

Two Hedge Fund groups have filed lawsuits against the Mozambique government related to Hidden Debts Scandal. The two funds are owed about $30 million in loans, which were part of $2 billion loaned to the Mozambican government for a coastal patrol force and a tuna fishing fleet in a deal in which high ranking government officials received large kickbacks.  Mozambique's government has said the deal was brokered by corrupt officials and not by the government itself, and has refused to pay back these loans, and is seeking judgements in court to nullify any government responsibility to pay this money back.

Local sources stated that food insecurity has worsened in recent months in Monapo, Nampula.  Irregular rainfall in the area has led to a poor planting and harvest season, while prices for food staples have also increased in the area.

571 Mozambicans were reportedly deported back to Mozambique through Ressano Garcia between 30 January-5 February. 21 more were deported through Ponta Border Crossing.  This comes as the borders between South Africa and Mozambique were partially closed until 15 February leading to an increase in illegal border crossings. During 16-22 January around 1,210 Mozambicans were deported from South Africa, in which a majority of the deportees were illegal immigrants.

The National Penitentiary Services (SERNAP) states their concern regarding new convicted individuals during the pandemic and the potential spread of the virus in prisons. SERNAP stated that prisons have seen an increase of convicted individuals during the pandemic. During the first two days of 2nd week of February 90 individuals were admitted to Machava Penitentiary, in which 35 of  those convicted were charged for disobedience.

15 COVID deaths and 1,054 new cases were reported in Mozambique on 11 February. The new cases increases the total deaths to 501 and new cases to 47,790.  This included 458 new cases in Maputo City, 428 cases in Gaza, 289 in Maputo, 233 in Niassa, 186 in Cabo Delgado, 103 in Manica, and 32 in Zambezia.  There are now 17,161 active cases in the country, including 9,655 active cases in Maputo City.

Flooding due to rains have submerged several roads along the N13 between Malema and Ribaue on 12 February. This flooding cut the road between Nampula and Cuamba, halting traffic between the two cities. Public works officials stated that they would determine if they are able to conduct maintenance on the road by 07:30.

Police arrested a suspect in possession of a semi-automatic weapon in Mapai on 6 February. The suspect attempted to bribe the police with 20,000 meticais during the arrest.  The man was reported to be a poacher and had used the weapon in poaching activities in several national parks.

Local sources stated that eight tank cars of a train derailed and overturned, spilling diesel into the Umbeluzi River near Goba on the morning of 12 February. Officials stated that the spilled diesel will not affect water consumption in region due to the closure of the discharge points of the Libombos Dam. Authorities reportedly stated that teams were sent clean up the derailment and spillage.

The South African Weather Service stated that disruptive rainfall is expected initially affect Inhambane on of the afternoon of Friday, 12 February. The rain may continue until as late as 16 February as the storm travels towards Gaza and Maputo provinces. INAM Meteorologist Tembe stated that at least 3-days of rain is expected to fall on Gaza and Maputo.  The National Directorate of Water Resources Management issued warnings that some neighborhoods in the Maputo and Matola cities may experience flooding.  Some areas of Gaza along the Limpopo River are also in danger of new flooding.

A local journalist working in Cabo Delgado stated that most new coverage of the insurgency in Cabo Delgado is currently limited to government provided information.  The journalist also described reporting on the insurgency in the province as "difficult", and that some journalists have been disappeared by government forces.

A local journalist working in Cabo Delgado reported that insurgents in the province had previously published updates regarding their attacks and other activities, but more recently do not communicate on these networks.  Updates on the insurgency in Cabo Delgado are now primarily provided by government sources, the journalist indicated.

The Central Office for Combating Corruption (GCCC) report says corruption cost Mozambique 14.2 million euros in 2020. The economic loss was most evident during the pandemic. The GCCC also said these losses to corruption have become more evident during the pandemic.

As many as 5,000 families are still cut off in Machaze District in Manica in the wake of Cyclone Eloise.  Flooding in the district has cut off roads in the area and prevented basic food supplies from being provided to the area.  An air bridge has been supplying families in the district with essential products.

Local media reporting indicates that large segments of general public are not adhering to anti-COVID measures in Maputo City. Locals stated that they were only adhering to the COVID precautions once they are inside establishments or public transportation. Very few people are wearing masks, washing their hands, or maintaining social distancing in much of the capital.  This is despite the fact that the city has seen a major spike in COVID cases over the past month, with more than 9,000 active cases of the virus reported in the capital.

Maputo Municipality on 10 February banned passenger transport in open box vehicles, also known as "my loves". Public transportation routes were also readjusted to have the last daily route at 20:10 so that all vehicles have stopped operations by 21:00. The ban and adjustment comes as the government attempts to stop the spread of COVID in the capital.  The council also adjusted operating hours for commercial markets and restaurants in the capital.  The Zimpeto market will now operate from 0600hrs to 1700hrs Monday to Saturday, and from 0600hrs to 0000hrs on Sundays.  Restaurants will be allowed to operate from between 0800hrs to 2100hrs.  Mozambique's mayor also said police have been instructed to expel informal traders from the Baixa area.

Sources in Palma on 12 February reported that costs of basic food staples remain high, despite the arrival last week of at least two convoys loaded with food supplies into the town.  It is unclear if any further convoys since 06 February have reached Palma.

South Africa's International Relations and Cooperation Minister Nalendi Pandor in an interview on 12 February said that South Africa had been "engaging" with Portugal on providing assistance to Mozambique to fight the Cabo Delgado insurgency, though said she could "not say much".  The minister also said Portugal already had "soldiers, feet on the ground".  She also said that Mozambique had not yet "concretely" indicated what the country needed in terms of military assistance.

Unconfirmed reports on 12 February indicated that a human rights violation investigation had been opened against a South African private military contractor operating in Cabo Delgado.  No further details on this investigation are currently available.

Unconfirmed reports on 12 February said that a South African private military contractor contracted by the Mozambican government was operating 5 drones to support Mozambican military operations in Cabo Delgado.  It was unclear if these drones possess attack capabilities or not.

Unconfirmed reports on 12 February indicated a South African private military contractor was operating a small number of patrol ships off the Cabo Delgado coast to help cut insurgent maritime supply lines and to prevent insurgent attacks on islands in the Quirimbas Archipelago.

The Mozambican military with support from South African private security military contractors has reportedly recently blocked cell phone and internet signals in some parts of Cabo Delgado in order to disrupt insurgent communications, a closed source reported on 12 February.

Paulo Filipe Nguirangue, a member of the RENAMO Military Junta, surrendered to authorities in Beira on 12 February.  Nguirangue claims to be a "general" and one of dissident leader Mariano Nhongo's main deputies.  Nguirangue also surrendered an assault rifle to security forces, and said that he wanted to join the DDR Process. He said he had only joined the dissidents after Nhongo himself had threatened to kill him if he did not join.  The dissident commander also alleged that the dissidents had received support from Sandura Amborsio, a former RENAMO deputy, who has previously denied any contact with the Military Junta.  A police source later said Guirande had surrendered earlier in the week after he and a group of dissidents had been closely pursued by a group of security forces.

RENAMO spokesman Ivan Mazanga on 11 February said that the ongoing curfew in the Greater Maputo City Area was "unconstitutional", saying it illegally limited the movement of people.  Mazanga also said police regularly committed "excessive and illegal actions".
Police arrested several civilians for violating COVID precautions by not wearing masks in Beira on the afternoon of 12 February.

The local municipal council in Chimoio announced the city will erect a new morgue designated for COVID-19 fatalities.  The municipality stated that the COVID morgue was to reduce the risk of spreading COVID. This  comes amid rising COVID cases and fatalities in Manica and Mozambique as a whole.

Beira hospitals on 11 February were reported to have begun mass COVID testing for patients with symptoms. Both Beira Central Hospital (HCB) and the Hospital da Mulher 24 de Julho are now conducting mass tests and are able to receive results of tests in 30 minutes.  Rapid testing will also be made available in the near future at Ponta Gea, Munhava, and Chingussura.  These measures were meant to take pressure off two labs in the city that had been conducting 350-400 tests per day in recent weeks.

Mozambique police announced that crime has reduced by 16 percent nationwide during the period of 30 January to 5 February of 2021, in comparison to the same period 2020. 96 criminal cases nationwide were recorded during this period in comparison to 114 crimes during the same period last year. Police performance was currently recorded at 81% in comparison to 83% operability last year.

Police arrested RENAMO dissident Chief of Staff, Paulo Filipe Nguirande in Gorongosa area on or before 11 February.  Police seized an AK machine gun and 5 rounds from the militant.  Nguirande later held a press conference saying he had surrendered to government forces and wanted to join the DDR process.

Flooding due to rains have submerged the Canicado-Chinhacanine Road in Guija District, sources indicated on 12 February. Local sources stated that civilians have been crossing the submerged portion of the route via boat in recent days.

The National Directorate of Water Resources Management (INGD) warned of flooding brought by overflowing of the Maputo, Incomati, and Umbeluzi rivers in Maputo province due to expected heavy rains over the weekend. Officials stated that water levels are already high in these rivers before this weekend's rains. INGD stated that some roads have remained impassable, thought there is no need to provide for accommodation centers. In Manhica district, around 8,500 people were reported to have fled Calanga and travelled to Manhica town, while the Mulelemane area was reported to be cut off from the rest of the district due to flooding.

The National Directorate of Water Resources Management (INGD) warned of flooding due to the overflowing of the Mutamba and Inhanombe in Inhambane, which could be caused by heavy rains over the weekend.

Mozambican officials announced on Friday that an extraordinary SADC summit meant to be held in Mozambique on the insurgency in Cabo Delgado would be postponed to either May or June 2021.  The postponement was due to an ongoing spike of COVID-19 throughout Southern Africa; the summit had been meant to be held in Maputo in January before being initially postponed.  There has been some speculation that the Mozambican government also wanted to delay the summit as it seeks to avoid a direct military intervention in Cabo Delgado by the regional bloc.

The National Statistics Institute (INE) stated that inflation has sharply increased in Mozambique as prices had increased by 4.09% over the course of 1 year. From December 2020 to January 2021 alone, prices increased 1.18%.  Food prices have been most significantly impacted by these inflation rates, and basic food staples over the past year have increased by an average of 10%. The Bank of Mozambique warned that the cost of living could worsen due to the decline of the metical due to the COVID-19 pandemic, insurgency in Cabo Delgado, and natural disasters.

Deputy Director of Health Benigna Matsinhe stated that COVID-19 vaccines could arrive at “any time” and cold storage facilities for vaccines are prepared. Matsinhe clarified that the vaccines are set to arrive based on the quota of the COVAX mechanism, in which Mozambique is entitled to have enough vaccines to inoculate 20 percent of the population.  The exact date for the arrival of this portion of vaccine doses is currently not known, and Matsinhe said this could occur any time between late February to May.

The Ministry of Health announced 13 new COVID deaths and 798 new cases in Mozambique on 12 February. The new cases were recorded as follows: 231 were recorded in Maputo city, 122 in Gaza, 103 in Inhambane, 92 in Tete, 71 in Niassa, 59 in Manica, 52 in Maputo province, 37 in Cabo Delgado, 25 in Sofala, 5 in Nampula, and 1 in Zambezia.

South Africa announced on 13 February that they will reopen 20 land border crossings on 15 February including borders with Zimbabwe, Mozambique, and Botswana.  The border posts to be reopened with Mozambique will be the Lebombo and Kosibay (Ressano Garcia and Ponto do Ouro) posts.  The borders posts were closed on 11 January as South Africa locked down to attempt to prevent the spread of COVID-19.  The reopening these posts will include an operation on fake COVID-19 test certificates. Those with fake certificates will be denied entry and barred from visiting South Africa for at least five years.

The reopening these posts will include an operation on fake COVID-19 test certificates. Those with fake certificates will be denied entry and barred from visiting South Africa for at least five years.

A project for the rehabilitation of the water supply system in Pemba was launched on 12 February, to aid in minimizing the pressure on the system brought by the recent increase in the city's population due to large influxes of IDPs into the city due to the ongoing Cabo Delgado insurgency. 20 new water holes will be opened to help expand the network distribution from 250 to 383 kilometers.
Three armed Pakistani nationals reportedly invaded a store and abducted its owner in Xipapanine, Maputo City on the morning of 13 February. No other details on this incident are currently available.

The Ministry of Health announced 11 new COVID deaths and 863 new cases in Mozambique on 13 February.  247 new cases reported in Maputo city, and 119 in Maputo province, 129 cases from Inhambane, 82 from Sofala, 69 from Cabo Delgado, 66 from Gaza, 64 from Tete, 55 from Zambezia, 16 from Nampula, 13 from Manica and three from Niassa. These new cases brought the country's number of infections to 49,451 and the national death toll is now at 525.  51 new patients were hospitalized while 21 were already discharged from the hospital.

Media reports on 13 February said large numbers of civilians are not observing social distancing in Maputo City, thus the increasing the risk of acquiring the coronavirus. Among the places listed where social distancing was not being observed and COVID-19 was likely being spread were markets, bank queues, schools, public transport, transport stops and terminals, government offices, and family gatherings.

Around 2100hrs on 13 February, Daviz Simango, Mayor of Beira City and head of the MDM party, was transferred to South Africa from Beira City due to an undisclosed illness. Daviz's brother, Lutero Simango, confirmed the report and assured that Simango's condition is under control. A source claimed that Simango's wife tested positive with COVID-19 last week while the result of Simango's test was not revealed. Some sources did later report Simango is believed to be ill with COVID-19. Simango has been mayor of Beira since 2003, and head of the country's third largest party since its founding in 2009.

According to the Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia INAM, heavy rains and strong winds will impact the provinces of Maputo, Gaza and Inhambane until 16 February. Starting 15 February, rains between 50 and 100mm with winds of up to 70 kilometers per hour and severe thunderstorms are expected to affect several district in these provinces. These strong winds may generate waves up to five meters high south of the parallel 24 degrees south. Affected districts in Maputo will likely be Matutuíne, Boane, Namaacha, Marracuene, Moamba, Magude, Manhiça, Maputo and Matola cities. In the province of Gaza, the impacted areas will be Chicualacuala, Chigubo, Mabalane, Chibuto, Massingir, Limpopo, Chonguene, Massangena, Mapai, Guija, Mandlakazi, Bilene and the cities of Chokwe and Xai-Xai. Meanwhile in Inhambane, the bad weather could affect districts of Zavala, Inharrime, Panda, Jangamo, Homoine, Morrumbene, Funhalouro, Massinga, Vilanculos, Mabote, Inhassoro, Govuro and the Maxixe and Inhambane cities.
