Angola announced on 14 February that the country would send oxygen tanks to Mozambique to help the Maputo government treat patients hospitalized with COVID-19. The tanks were sent to the country on 15 February. This came after President Nyusi and President Lourenco of Angola spoke on the phone on 14 February.  The two during this conversation also discussed the security situation in Cabo Delgado.

The Ministry of Health announced 10 new COVID deaths and 814 new cases in Mozambique on 14 February. This included 210 cases in Maputo Province, 159 cases in Maputo City, 107 in Zambezia, 88 in Inhambane, 60 in Sofala, 59 in Cabo Delgado, 56 in Gaza, 48 in Tete, 19 in Niassa, 7 in Manica, and 1 in Nampula.  There are currently 18,031 active cases in the country. These new cases brought the country's number of infections to 50,265 and the national death toll to 535. 294 patients were hospitalized, 79% of which are in Maputo City.

A dead body of a 30-yr-old man was recovered in a puddle of water in the neighborhood of Ricathla, Marracuene district on 13 Feb. Witnesses claimed that the victim, whose hands and feet were tied, was allegedly beaten to death.  The man is thought to have been killed in another area and then transported to Ricathla. Residents call for security reinforcements to crack down on criminality in the area.

International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) chief Peter Maurer on 14 February urged humanitarian aid organizations to look into providing more support for the  humanitarian crisis in Cabo Delgado, saying Mozambique faced a "triple humanitarian crisis" of climate change, COVID-19, and armed conflict.  Maurer also announced that ICRC will scale up its 2021 programs with a focus on assistance, health and training programs on the promotion of International Humanitarian Law for weapons bearers.  Included in these programs will be the rehabilitation of 9 health centers serving over 175,000 people in Pemba; hospitals in the Montepuez area will also receive assistance from the organization.  Maurer also said that it was likely "very early" for IDPs to begin returning to their homes, saying the security situation was "not yet" stable.  Maurer visited Cabo Delgado on Sunday, before meeting with President Nyusi and other officials in Maputo on Monday.

Two men were arrested by police in Maputo City on the night of 12 February just after 2100hrs after one of the men was seen on a widely shared video on social media networks in which he insulted President Nyusi.  The other man arrested had filmed the video, which the two said was meant to show that the curfew was not being adhered to in parts of the capital.  The men on 15 February were reported to have been freed after the intercession of the Mozambican Bar Association, and after considerable outrage over the well publicized case.  Nyusi later received the two men on 16 February for a conversation in which the two men apologized for the video.

Speaking on 15 February from Macomia District, Deputy Chief of Staff of the Mozambican Armed Forces, Bertolino Capitine, said that the military would not be victorious "if the population is hostile to the Mozambican State", also saying that the "time has come for us to destroy" the insurgency, saying conditions were favorable for the army to achieve this goal.  He also said this would be a way to honor Eugenio Mussa, former head of the military, who died in early February of COVID less than a month after being promoted to the role.

Health Minister Armindo Tiago on 12 February began working at Maputo Central Hospital, after health authorities shifted 100 doctors working for the Health Ministry in administrative roles to part time work in hospitals amid a spike in COVID cases across the country.

150 inmates were evacuated from Guija penitentiary to Macia, sources reported on Monday, though the evacuation took place last week.  This came amid flooding in Gaza due to a rise in water levels in the Limpopo River amid heavy rains in Southern Mozambique.

Pope Francis appoints supplementary bishop of the Maputo diocese, Dom Antonio Juliasse Sandramo, as “apostolic administrator” of Pemba to replace departing bishop, Luiz Fernando Lisboa.   Bishop Sandramo stated that he will continue to assist IDPs displaced by the ongoing insurgency in the province.

The Quelimane municipal council stated that Mayor Manuel de Araujo did not show up to a trial against him for allegedly defaming FRELIMO and MDM members on 15 February, reportedly due to an "official trip. De Araujo and his supporters say the cases against him are of a "political nature"; the mayor as the top elected official of the capital of Zambezia is one of the most significant elected political officials in the country for RENAMO.

South African technicians conducted a cleanup removing the fuel spilled along Umbeluzi River in Boane District on 14 February. Deputy Minister of Public Works, Housing and Water Resources, Cecilia Chamutota, stated that the first phase would last for a week; officials also said that the drinking water supply to residents in the Greater Maputo area would not be disrupted by these cleanup operations. Local maintenance teams are assisting the South African technicians in checking the water quality levels.

Zimbabwe has received its first shipment of COVID vaccines from China on 15 February. 200,000 doses of vaccine were reported to have arrived in Zimbabwe with another 600,000 expected to arrive in a second batch. Mozambique in the near future could also explore attaining vaccine doses from China, or could possibly attain quantities of this vaccine from Zimbabwe or South Africa.

The Brazilian government on 11 February expressed its readiness to assist Mozambique in the fight against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado and against the Military Junta in Central Mozambique. The Brazilian government called on Mozambique to define the support it requires.

Zimbabwe announced that it would extend its anti-COVID lockdown for two more weeks.  Zimbabwe saw a major spike of cases in December and January though has seen a gradual fall in case numbers in early February, consistent with broader trends across Southern Africa.

DRC Foreign Affairs Minister conducted a meeting with President Nyusi on 12 February in Maputo.  After these talks, Nzeza said the two countries faced the same problems in combating insurgencies, and that the two would continue to exchange information in the fight against "terrorism".  The Islamic State's Central Africa Province (ISCAP) has claimed attacks in both Mozambique and the DRC.

The Ministry of Health announced 12 COVID deaths and 426 new infections in Mozambique on 15 February. Eight men and four women died of the virus during treatment. The new cases are as follows: 144 in Inhambane, 99 in Maputo city, 61 in Maputo province, 38 in Nampula, 34 in Gaza, 22 in Niassa, 17 in Sofala, 6 in Cabo Delgado, 4 in Zambezia, and 1 in Tete.

Mozambican researchers are creating a climate risk map that would show the which cities in the country are more vulnerable to severe weather conditions. The risk map would simulate the effects of natural disasters in each area.  Beira and Maputo will be focusi of this risk map; Beira in particular is considered vulnerable to climate change natural disasters as the city lies below sea level and has been struck by two cyclones in recent years.

Mozambique Electricity (EDM) stated only 500 Mw of electrical supply is allocated to Mozambique from the  Cahora Bassa Hydroelectric Dam which has a 2,075Mw capacity; 1,500Mw is allocated to South Africa ESKOM. The 500Mw was divided into 300Mw and 200Mw between firm and non-firm energy. EDM stated that the country still does not have enough electrical generation capabilities to supply both national and regional demands.

RENAMO may file accusing security forces of illegal and excessive actions in imposing the curfew against locals with the Constitutional Council in Maputo City on 15 February. The accusation comes as police reportedly have used illegal use of force to impose the curfew. RENAMO also stated that the curfew has also affected public transportation, and has limited civilians' fundamental rights of free movement.

Local media reports indicated on 16 February that a group of five teenage girls on an unspecified date last week arrived in Macomia town after they were released by insurgents two weeks ago from an insurgent bush camp located along the Messalo River.  The girls, 4 of whom were from parts of Mucojo AP in Macomia and 1 who was from Mocimboa da Praia district, had been abducted in 2018 in insurgent raids.  The group told authorities that the insurgents had told them they were free to return to their villages due to food shortages in the insurgent camps.  They also said that recently their had been significant "hunger" amid the insurgents and their captives. During their captivity, the girls said they had been responsible for cooking meals for the insurgents and for shifting insurgent mobile camps to different locations.  The group also said that insurgents had recently begun covering the tops of their camp huts with leaves and grass so as not to be identified and targeted by military helicopters patrolling over insurgent zones.

Journalist Tom Bowker confirmed in a tweet on 16 February that he had been deported from Mozambique, and "banned for 10 years", also saying that it was a "politically motivated move, without legal foundation".  Bowker had previously been reported to have been ordered out of the country by 30 January.  Bowker was reportedly deported on a flight out of Maputo City.  The journalist had worked for an outlet covering the conflict in Cabo Delgado, as well as aspects of the ongoing "Hidden Debts" case, both of which are politically sensitive subjects in the country.  Sources later said this was the first expulsion of a foreign journalist from the country in more than 20 years.

TVM media an interview of a girl claiming to have been released by insurgents in Cabo Delgado after insurgents reportedly experienced food shortages. The girl stated that she had been abducted a year ago in Naquitengue, Mocimboa da Praia.

Local sources stated a small trader, Armazens Anita was paid around 8.5 million USD between 2018-2019 for supplies for the military in Cabo Delgado.  This was despite the fact that these supplies could have been purchased from larger suppliers in Pemba.  Anita then reportedly transferred these payment to personal bank accounts, and may have not provided some of the supplies to the Mozambican military.  Transactions made by Anita subsequently have been flagged and reported them to banking authorities.

Local sources stated that Mozambique agreed to repay 224 million USD of loans to Brazil after the country agreed to support Mozambique in a campaign for one the non-permanent seats on the UN Security Council on 2022. The dealt was reportedly made by the Mozambique Foreign Minister Veronica Macamo and Brazilian FM Araujo. Mozambique will repay the money and the debt will be restructured to have a longer repayment time and no extra interest. Some of these loans are connected to the "Hidden Debts" Case.

Sources have indicated that no new supply convoys have reached Palma after two convoys arrived in the town in early February.  This is partially due to the security threat of insurgent attacks along the Nangade-Palma road, but also is due to heavy rains which have made travel difficult to impossible along stretches of this route.  This lack of convoys means that the town's food shortage crisis continues.

Palma continues to face food shortages and high food prices as only two supply convoys have reached the town over the past month. This is due to the risk of insurgent attacks along the Nangade-Palma road and due to poor road conditions due to rains on this route.  Officials in Palma on 17 February were reported to have appealed to local merchants to decrease high prices.

Security forces reportedly deployed every 4-5km along the road between Mueda to Palma to escort convoys to Palma in early February, sources indicated.  It is unclear if these deployments remained in place after the week of 07-13 February.

Approximately 27,000 individuals are isolated due to the submerging of two bridges brought about by flooding which began last week.  Water and food sources in the area are limited as rains continue in Southern Mozambique.

Two bridges to Boane District have been submerged by the overflowing Umbeluzi River due to heavy rainfall. Fishing boats were reportedly used as means of commute to cross the overflowing river, costing 15 meticais per trip. The boats were reportedly filled and no COVID precautions are being observed.  Flooding in the area has also damaged water pipes and as of Monday limited supplies of water to the area.

South Africa intends to create a special border security force to deal with illegal immigration coming from Mozambique. South African officials said that illegal immigration was not only due to the pandemic and that most individuals do not have the adequate requirements to cross the border crossings. The Border Management Authority will be a full-time force to monitor the South African border for the illegal activity.

The Ministry of Health announced that higher hospitalization rates have occurred in February compared to January. The Ministry of Health stated that over the first half of February, an average of 36.1 patients have been hospitalized by COVID. in Mozambique, compared to January, which averaged 28.6 patients hospitalized per day.  As of 15 February, 542 patients have been admitted.  During 2020, the highest average number of hospital admissions was 6.2 patients during the month of October.

Minister of Health Armindo Tiago stated on 15 February that authorities have “promised” to begin vaccinations of Mozambicans for COVID-19 between February and March. Tiago also said the country is in the midst of selecting what vaccine or vaccines should be used in the country, saying a variety of vaccines could be eventually used.

South Africa intends to give out its million doses of the AstraZeneca vaccine to other African countries through the African Union. The vaccine was initially attempted to be returned to India due to its inefficacy against the South Africa COVID variant. The donation comes as South Africa received the Johnson & Johnson vaccine.  Some of these donated doses could eventually be provided to Mozambique.

South Africa was reported on 17 February to have secured the first batch of the Johnson & Johnson Covid-19 vaccines.  The vaccines are to replace large stocks of the AstraZeneca vaccine held by the South African government; the AstraZeneca vaccine in recent studies appeared to be less effective against a new strain of COVID in South Africa.  It was not immediately clear how many doses of the J&J vaccine were received by South Africa.  The J&J vaccine also has the advantage of being administered in a single shot; some doses of this vaccine could eventually be provided by SA to Mozambique.

A tropical depression that this week has brought significant rain to much of Southern Mozambique has moved into the Mozambique Channel, and strengthened into a Tropical Storm, named Guambe.  Guambe could potentially strengthen in the coming hours into a cyclone, but is not presently anticipated to make landfall again.  The storm in anticipated to move south/southeast before dissipating south of Madagascar.  The strengthening system over at least the coming day will continue however to bring rains across parts of Southern Mozambique, including most significantly in Inhambane, Sofala, Gaza, and Maputo City/ Maputo Province. The Southern Mozambican Coast between Beira in Sofala and Xai-Xai in Gaza will be the most heavily impacted areas by this storm.  Strong winds, rain, and a storm surge along the coast can be expected, and the storm could continue to affect Mozambique as late as Saturday.

1,109 COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 16 February, along with 4 new deaths, bringing the total number of deaths to 551.  364 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 177 in Gaza, 150 in Sofala, 106 in Maputo, 103 in Tete, 101 in Inhambane, 36 in Nampula, 29 in Cabo Delgado, 18 in Niassa, 14 in Zambezia, and 11 in Manica.  There are 18,983 active cases in the country, and 291 hospitalizations.

A bridge was reported on 15 February to have collapsed due to flooding in the Catuane AP area of Maputo Province, isolating around nearly 6,000 people in the area living in 9 villages.   This came after rains continued in the area for more than a week.

Portugal indicated on 17 February that its Defense Ministry would likely send 60 Portuguese military personnel to Mozambique in April to conduct trainings for Mozambique's marines and other military units.  This training force will then be split between Southern and Central Mozambique to conduct different trainings.

The UK 15 February extended a flight ban on individuals travelling from Mozambique to prevent the spread of the South African variant of COVID-19.  The ban was originally imposed in January.  The UK has banned people travelling from 33 countries from entering UK territory to prevent the spread of this variant.

Government officials on 16 February said that a low pressure system that began to affect Mozambique on 12 February has so far impacted 11,411 people across Southern Mozambique, damaging 2,330 homes as well as at least 15 roads.

A large group of insurgents on 16 February were reported to have ambushed a military unit in the Nanili area, along the Mueda-Mocimboa da Praia border; the day prior, clashes were reported at Roma a village along the R698 road west of Diaca.  This military convoy was travelling to Nanili to reinforce pro-government militia who were under attack by insurgents. This attack reportedly started at around 0400hrs, with clashes lasting until around 1200hrs.  A seond source reported clashed ended around 1500hrs.  Militants also fired an RPG at one vehicle, though this projectile failed to detonate.  Other sources later indicated that a second vehicle had sustained heavy close range fire from militants (from a distance of 3-5 meters) and was badly damaged.  Soldiers stationed in the Namaua area reportedly reinforced the ambushed patrol to allow it to withdraw from the area safely.  Some military equipment was abandoned during this incident and seized by insurgents.   Troops after this engagement withdrew towards Namaua, leaving the area in the hands of the insurgents.  Video emerged after this incident showing an armored vehicle with visible damage from small arms fire and at least one RPG on four of the vehicle's windows.

Insurgents on 16 February attacked Mozambican soldiers at a post in the Xitaxi area in Muidumbe District, forcing soldiers to retreat.  Insurgents reportedly seized some military equipment in the wake of this retreat.  1 soldier was reportedly injured in these clashes.  Insurgents also were reported to have looted food items in this attack.

A large number of vehicles loaded with supplies is reportedly waiting in Nangade for military clearance to travel to Palma, but have not been given the go-ahead.  This convoy is waiting for a military escort, but no such escort in recent days has materialized, despite reassurances from the military that an escort will be provided.  This comes amid a supply shortage in Palma, which has received only two supply convoys' worth of goods since mid-January.

The Ministry of Health announced 10 new COVID deaths and 829 new COVID cases in Mozambique as of 17 February. The new cases were as follows: 357 in Maputo city, 116 in Gaza, 104 in Maputo province, 100 in Sofala, 40 in Inhambane, 47 in Cabo Delgado, 22 in Tete, 20 in Manica, 15 in Niassa, and 8 in Zambezia. The total active cases have increased to 19,207

Several neighborhoods in Maputo City experienced flooding on 17 February amid ongoing rains. Several neighborhoods included Belo Horizonte were reported to have flooded in Matola municipality. Locals stated that the flooding has been ongoing since 13 February. A lack of drainage in many neighborhoods is also exacerbating this problem.

The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) stated they are investigating businesses that have started to sell alcohol online. The INAE stated that digital sales are illegal as they does not promote any economic activity and the deliveries conducted are not adhering to COVID restriction measures.

The Civil Society Learning and Training Center (CESC) conducted a study which revealed that local communities in Niassa and Nampula cooperate in the illegal logging conducted by Chinese companies. CESC stated that the communities prefer to work with the illegal operators who promptly pay local communities in comparison to the  government and licensed operators not providing required licensing fee allotments to these communities.

The Department of Medical Assistance stated that 170 health professionals have been infected with COVID in Zambezia province. Officials stated that 15 remain infected and 155 have recovered. Six of those infected are under hospital care while the other nine were home quarantined.

Zimbabwe will begin COVID vaccinations on voluntary frontline workers on Thursday, 18 February. Around 200,000 Sinopharm vaccines were donated from China. The initial target of the vaccines included healthcare staff, immigration officials and funeral employees.  Zimbabwe could eventually donate some vaccine doses to Mozambique.

Local sources stated that police stations are a potential site for spreading COVID as police unprepared to take counter measures at the stations. Police reportedly keep COVID precaution violators at stations in close proximity to one another, creating situations in which the virus can more easily spread. Police officials responded and claimed that the allegations against the police stations are false and that there are no detainees in subunits and the police are not to detain violators but pass them to referred institutions.

RENAMO says that The National Reconciliation and Peace Fund created by the Nampula government is bankrupt and is not conducting programs to benefit former RENAMO guerillas, as the fund was designed to do. The Nampula government has refuted the claims and stated that 90 projects were created by the program. The program was created to assist the financial income generation of demobilized RENAMO combatants.  RENAMO members say this $10 million fund, which was created in 2014, has never benefited any demobilized RENAMO members in the province.
Police arrested four pastors for violating COVID precautions in Manica province on 17 February. The suspects were holding a religious gathering of more than 50 people in attendance.

Russian made helicopters were reported in Pemba being flown by Mozambican pilots between 08-11 February, indicating that these pilots have now been trained by South African Private Security Company, and indicating that the Mozambican military is no longer solely reliant on Dyck Advisory Group helicopters to provide air support for operations targeting insurgents in Cabo Delgado.
Insurgents on 07 February abducted two women near Lago Chai, assaulted the two, and then released them.  Insurgents remain active in this area and maintain bush camps along the nearby Messalo River.

Helicopters, piloted either by South African military contractors or Mozambican military personnel, attacked insurgent positions in the Mbau area of Mocimboa da Praia on 10 February.  One source reported several casualties though no exact numbers were available.
Military helicopters on 09 February were reported to have targeted insurgent positions in the Mbau area.  No information on casualties was available.
Military helicopters on 09 February were reported to have targeted insurgent positions in the Chinda area of Mocimboa da Praia.  No information on casualties was available.
Military helicopters on 09 February conducted an attack on the Miangalewa area in Muidumbe District, where insurgents have long maintained positions.  No information on casualties was available.
Military helicopters on 11 February were reported to have carried out strikes between Mbau and Chitunda, along the MDP-Muidumbe border.  No information on casualties were available.

column4: Sources on 18 February reported that the primary reason supply convoys cannot currently travel between Nangade and Palma is due to a lack of availability of helicopter escorts for these convoys.  In early February, helicopters escorted the convoys during two convoy runs.  These helicopters in recent weeks however have been involved in operations targeting insurgents, and the military has either not given the go ahead for these convoys to proceed without air support, or are unwilling to travel along this road without air support, as multiple insurgent attacks have taken place along this route in recent months.

898 new COVID cases and 10 related deaths were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 18 February. The new cases were recorded as follows: 337 in Maputo city, 103 in Tete, 103 in Sofala, 96 in Cabo Delgado, 82 in Inhambane, 66 in Maputo province, 54 in Gaza, 45 in Manica, 6 in Zambezia, 4 in Niassa, and 2 in Nampula. The total active cases are at 19,148. While 947 daily recoveries were reported. Mozambique has current 19148

Hospital officials state that hospitalizations continue to increase due to COVID in Mozambique. 35 patients were admitted to different medical centers during the 16-17 February. 279 people were hospitalized as of 18 February, a large majority in facilities in Maputo.

Local sources stated that a former insurgent was reported missing in Angoche, Nampula. The former insurgent was a PE teacher who joined the insurgency in 2020 and but returned to his native Angoche in January to take advantage of an amnesty announced by the president. Police sources later confirmed they had arrested the man and taken him back to Cabo Delgado to interrogate him for information regarding the insurgency.

COVID-19  vaccinations began in South Africa on 17 February after the South African President Cyril Ramaphosa was vaccinated at a clinic in Cape Town.  The vaccinations were started after 80,000 Johnson & Johnson vaccines arrived in South Africa to replace doses of the AstraZeneca vaccine.  South Africa expects to receive 420,000 more doses of the J&J vaccine in the coming weeks; SA could eventually provide some doses of the vaccine to Mozambique.

Beira Health Chief Ileshi Jani stated on 17 February that COVID infections and deaths were increasing significantly in the city. Jani stated that the city's health system in nearing the collapse, and Sofala is the second most affected province currently by the pandemic. Jani warned the local public not to relax and adhere to the safety measures.

State-owned airports revenues fell by half during 2020 as 1.4 million MZN of income was reported during the year. This  54.2% decrease was caused by the impact of the pandemic. Only a million passengers were recording during 2020 while 2.2 million passengers were recorded in 2019. Domestic passengers decreased from 1.4m to 825,900 and hauled cargo declined from 17.2m tonnes to 8.8m tonnes.

Tropical Storm Guambe could turn into a cyclone and continues to bring in torrential rain in south and central Mozambique as of Thursday. Guambe was generating winds up to 90km/h. Guambe is expected to travel along the coast of Gaza and Maputo provinces but is unlikely to make landfall in the country, and will travel south and then southeast over the coming days.

Local sources stated that the government military recruiting efforts have slowed down due to the rainy season in Cabo Delgado. Around 6,294 local youths were recruited from Cabo Delgado during the month of January and into February - this recruitment will last until the end of February.  The military's goal was to recruit 14,952 soldiers in the province by the end of February - a target the military will clearly not reach.

The Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM) Party stated that it was not clear when the Beira mayor and President of MDM Daviz Simango will return to Mozambique. Simango is still hospitalized in Netcare Milpark Hospital, outside Johannesburg, South Africa. Simango was transported to the hospital on 13 February and has since been under observation.

Media sources reported on 16 February that road traffic in Massangena district has been interrupted due to intense rains in the region. Food supply trucks have been stranded for in the area for days, worsening food security in the area. Massangena Administrator announced that 22,000 civilians in the district are being affected due to the lack of food.

Two soldiers were reported missing after their boat sank while monitoring water levels on the Incomati River near Manhica on 17 February. Two government officials who were also in the boat were rescued on Wednesday and received medical treatment.

The Mozambican Workers Organization (OTM) is calling for employers to release workers in Maputo and Matola by 19:00 to adhere to the imposed curfew. OTM also stated that because of the lack of transport created about by the COVID precautionary measures, employees are unable to get home by 21:00.

22 police officers have died due to the COVID pandemic to date in Mozambique, police officials said this week.  Police Commander Rafael stated that precautionary measures must be followed by policemen.

The National Migration Service stated that daily traffic between South African and Mozambique has decreased from 3,500 to 1,150 citizens crossing since 15 February. The National Migration Service stated that the decrease has been brought about by the pandemic and the new requirements to travel between countries. Travelers are required a negative PCR test, for which South Africa has increased its price for testing from 170 rand to 200-300 rand (870 MZN to 1000-1500 MZN).

Tropical Storm Guambe on 19 February was reported to have intensified into a Tropical Cyclone, and continues to move south through the Mozambique Channel, with winds between 100 to 150 kms.  The storm continues to impact southern coastal areas, primarily in Inhambane. Gaza, Maputo, Sofala, and Manica will all also likely be impacted by the storm. Guambe is still not projected to make landfall in the country, though will still bring heavy rains and strong winds to much of Southern Mozambique into Saturday.

Police commander Bernardino Rafael on 18 February said that police officers have made “mistakes” in enforcing anti-COVID measures during the state of calamity imposed by the president. Commander Rafael stated that the “mistakes” were related to excess force in used in enforcing anti-COVID measures.

Two bus depots were closed in Nampula as part of court seizure order due to unpaid compensation for an accident in which two people were injured Nampula.  The bus company had failed to pay a large court ordered fee to the victims, who were injured by a company bus in a March 2019 accident.

Strong winds caused by storms destroyed several residences in the Maganja da Costa district of Zambezia province from 16 February. 13 schools were also destroyed during the incident. 15 civilians were injured by the gales. The storms also caused electrical blackouts after 14 transmission lines were toppled down.

Insurgents on 16 February after driving off security forces in the Nanili area reportedly carried out looting in the village, which was one of the few still inhabited villages in Mocimboa da Praia district, and had been under government control.  Large numbers of civilians fled the village before this raid, and the village was later reported to be "abandoned".

Total on 18 February was reported to be recruiting a liaison officer based in Cabo Delgado to liaise with the Mozambican military.  This indicates the company's strengthening its relationship with the military, which is increasingly taking charge of the counter-insurgency effort in the province.

A gang of six men stole a motorbike and other goods, and also sexually assaulted a woman and her daughter in an incident in Medeiros, just outside of Lichinga.  Police were able to arrest two of the gang members though the other four are still being sought.

Two people were killed and 17 injured due to strong winds and rain in Cuamba, Niassa, on 17 February.   284 homes, 17 classrooms, and 3 health units were also destroyed by storms, local media reported.

Insurgents on the night of 19 February reportedly set much of Quionga town on fire, and carried out looting, after clashing with local militia units.  Insurgents were reported to have remained in the vicinity of Quionga until at least the next morning.  Sources later indicated that a church mission project run which is operated by a South African church had been targeted by insurgents during this raid, and a building owned by the mission had been set on fire.

RENAMO Dissident leader Mariano Nhongo in an interview released on 19 February confirmed that he was uninjured and had not been captured, as had been rumored in recent weeks.  Nhongo also said that his group "is not shaken" despite the recent high-profile defections of Joao Machava and Paulo Filipe Nguriande.  The dissident leader also said that he still had "energy", and that his group was waiting for the government to open new talks with them.  He also said that the RENAMO dissidents are "not organizing to make war" though said that the "Government is continuing with the fight".

The Ministry Health stated that 12 new COVID deaths and 677 new cases were reported in Mozambique on 19 February. The cases were reported as follows: 275 in Maputo city, 122 in Maputo province, 106 in Cabo Delgado, 52 in Niassa, 50 in Inhambane, 45 in Tete, 15 in Manica, 9 in Zambezia, 2 in Sofala, and 1 in Gaza. 585 daily recoveries were also reported. Active cases remained at 19,228.

Agricultural minister Celso Correia on 17 February stated that the cashew industry will not collapse despite the exit of OLAM from the country. Minister Correia stated that the pandemic is the reason for the decline in sales of cashews. OLAM recently announced it would withdraw from Mozambique ending its support for small scale cashew producers.  10 cashew processing plants across Mozambique employ several thousand people, and there has been speculation that these jobs could be in danger with OLAM's exiting Mozambique.

The Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) stated that food prices had increased in Nampula on 19 February. INAE monitored 12 essential goods in the province, rice, corn flour, cooking oil, wheat, potatoes, onions and beans. INAE stated that these inflation rates are genuine and not the result of price speculation.

NKC Africa Economics stated that Mozambique’s economy will continue to decline, after falling by 2.4% in the last quarter of 2020, part of a 1.2% decline for the year of 2020. The economy due to the impact of COVID-19 is expected to lead to further economic decline in the country for at least the first quarter of 2021.

Mozambique Foreign Affairs and Cooperation Minister, Veronica Macamo conducted talks with her German counterpart, stating Mozambique's need for more support to combat terrorism. Macamo stated that the country and international partners should mobilize more support to fight against insurgency. The meeting also called for the extension of support for RENAMO's disarmament, demobilization and reintegration (DDR) process.
Police rescued a civilian who attempted to commit suicide by throwing himself into  Maputo bay on 14 February.

Amnesty International said that there is little to no government support for IDPs in areas where they are being resettled in Cabo Delgado.  It is also unclear if the government intends to permanently or temporarily resettle IDPs in areas where they have been resettled.

Police arrested a lab technician at a private clinic for falsifying COVID results in Nampula City on 19 February.  A Nigerian suspect was also detained for attempting to obtain a fake COVID result. The suspect was in possession of several documents which contained forged test negative COVID results.

Police conducted an operation targeting open box vehicles, also known as "my loves", for transporting passengers in Maputo city on 19 February. 11 open box vehicle drivers were fined for illegally operating during the ban. The open box vehicles were previously banned in the city to prevent the spread of COVID-19.

A new storm front was reported to be moving into Southern Mozambique by 21 February, likely bringing strong winds and heavy rains.  This comes as Cyclone Guambe affected the southern coastal areas of the country last week.

The Ministry of National Defence stated all of the youths that have not registered for the compulsory military draft can now do so until 30 March and have the possibility to be “regularize” their status if they register. Authorities have previously registered 51% out of 200,000 individuals targeted for compulsory military service enlistment. Officials said they had expected to have enlisted more young people in the draft, and blamed insurgent attacks in Cabo Delgado and dissident attacks in Central Mozambique for "impairing" the process, along with the COVID-19 pandemic and the ongoing rainy season. The draft period was meant to have concluded on 28 February.

Railway officials announced works had resumed to repair and maintain works parts of the Beira-Zimbabwe railway. These works currently are focused on the line from Beira to Machipanda, which costs 200 million USD. The railway was to support 45kg/ m for better support and productivity. Repairs was currently at 30% completion. Officials stated that the repair was previously scheduled to resume earlier, but was delayed by the pandemic.

Locals stated that flooding issues have continued in Catuane AP, isolating four villages and 2,500 people. The flooding was due to the increased water in the Maputo River after the opening of dam floodgates from Eswatini.  People in the area are forced to take boats to come and go from these villages, and food is reportedly scarce in the area.
Emergency repair teams repaired a bridge to Catuane AP allowing travel back to some parts of the area, though at least 2,500 people remain isolated in 4 villages in the AP due to ongoing flooding.

The African Union announced that it expects that distribution of 1 million AstraZeneca vaccine doses will start next week. Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention officials stated that the vaccines will hopefully be delivered to the member countries by 26 February. Among the members, is Mozambique which is likely to receive an unspecified number of vaccine doses.

Mozambique Airlines (LAM) saw a 44% decline in passengers in January in comparison to the previous year.  LAM officials stated that 29,923 passengers were recorded in January 2021 while 53,249 passengers were recorded in the same month during 2020.

Security forces arrested seven civil servants for embezzlements charges in Doa, Tete.  The suspects were wanted for embezzling 6 million MZN during 2018 to 2020. This comes as three other embezzlement suspects were detained in Mutarara.

Police arrested three civil servants for embezzling 3 million MZN in Mutarara, Tete.  These crimes were committed between September to November of 2020. The suspects were identified by the Provincial Services of Economy and Finance.

The Portuguese ambassador to Mozambique Maria Amelia Paiva called on Friday for “concrete responses” regarding cooperation in the fight against insurgency in Cabo Delgado. Portuguese ambassador to Mozambique Paiva also said technical issues regarding future cooperation between Portugal, the European Union (EU), and Mozambique were still being resolved. Portugal recently said that 60 soldiers would be sent to Mozambique to train Mozambique security forces to combat insurgency, but this was still being discussed by Mozambican authorities.

A group of 20 civil society groups issued a statement on Friday, saying they are concerned over growing repression in the country and the targeting of journalists, activists, and human rights defenders by figures "close to the central government" after the departure of the Pemba bishop Luiz Fernando Lisboa in Mozambique on 19 February.  The organizations say that Lisboa was transferred out of Mozambique due to pressure from the Maputo government.

Central Hospital Beira's ophthalmology block will be accepting COVID-19 patients once bed capacity at the Hospital 24 de Julho has exhausted,  the Ministry of Health said on 20 February.  This comes amid rising COVID cases in Beira, which has seen the second most cases of COVID in the country of any one location.  In Beira, the rate of positive cases reached 40%, meaning out of all people who were tested, 40% were positive with the virus.

National Penitentiary Service (SERBAP) stated that the situation in penitentiary facilities is already critical as the system has 19,000 inmates and just an 8,000 bed capacity.  Prison officials also say the risk of spreading COVID-19 in the over populated facilities is very high. The recent surge of prisoners has been driven by the arrest of violators of the Maputo curfew. For 2021, almost 3,000 inmates were admitted to these establishments.

The Ministry Health stated that four new COVID-related deaths and 764 new cases were reported in Mozambique on 20 February. The cases were reported as follows: 195 in Maputo city, Sofala with 147 cases, 116 from Gaza, 100 from Maputo Province, 67 from Manica, 64 from Nampula, 60 from Cabo Delgado, eight from Niassa, three from Zambezia, two from Tete and two from Inhambane. 532 people have fully recovered from the virus, which brings the total number of recoveries to 34,921.

Sources indicated that on the night of 19 February, a group of 30 insurgents attacked pro-government militia in the Quionga area.  Clashes reportedly began around 1600hrs. Four people were reportedly killed during the attack. Helicopters operated by private military contractors provided air support to the militia for a limited time during these clashes, but the militia was eventually forced to withdraw from the area after running out of ammunition and when reinforcements from Palma failed to arrive. Insurgents then reportedly set much of Quionga on fire, and carried out looting.  Some sources reported that militants by the morning of 20 February had withdrawn from the area, withdrawing north of the town, and that militia units had re-occupied the town, though this is currently unconfirmed.  Intermittent small arms fire was reported in the Quionga area over the night of 20-21 February, though no new clashes were confirmed in the area.

Former Health Minister, Helder Martins, has resigned from the government’s Technical and Scientific Commission, a source disclosed on 20 February. Martins wrote a letter to President Filipe Nyusi on 16 February which was published in the media saying that the commission, whose goal is to give advice on how to handle the COVID-19 pandemic, should not be headed by a politician. He added that current Health Minister, Armindo Tiago, is a brilliant doctor but lacks experience in dealing with the pandemic. He also stated that the commission is not efficient in communicating with the public and  no attempt had been made to mobilize NGOs to combat the coronavirus.

70 COVID-19 cases were reported among inmates and prison staff between 1 January and 18 February, according to the National Prison Service (SERNAP) National Director for Health Care, Cemilde Anli, on 19 February. Eight people are currently infected with the virus, five are in the Provincial Penitentiary Establishment of Maputo (EPPM), two at the Machava Maximum Security Establishment (aka BO) and one at the Inhambane Provincial Prison Establishment. Obligatory quarantine or isolation on any new entries into the prison has been imposed to curb the spread of the virus. Anli's statement contradicted the announcement of government spokesperson, Deputy Justice Minister Filimao Suaze, on 4 February, that there was no contamination in the country’s prison facilities.

Mozambique has been added to a 33 countries by Kuwait as COVID-19 'high-risk' countries, a source disclosed on 21 February. A total of 68 countries were now part of the high-risk list in the country. Kuwait also extended a ban on the entry of non-nationals into the country until further notice.

The Ministry Health stated reported eight new COVID-related deaths and 675 new cases were reported in Mozambique on 21 February. 152 of the new cases were from Maputo city, and 114 from Maputo province. 129 new cases were reported from Cabo Delgado, 95 from Sofala, 75 from Niassa, 44 from Inhambane, 42 from Tete, 16 from Gaza, seven from Zambezia and one from Manica. The total number of confirmed cases in the country increased to 55,643 while the national death toll is now at 595.

The intensity of tropical cyclone Guambe has decreased and is currently outside the Mozambique Channel, according to National Meteorological Institute (INAM) on 21 February. Guambe is now a severe tropical storm. INAM advised that heavy rains will be experienced today to tomorrow especially the provinces of Niassa, Tete, Manica and Gaza as part of new storm systems.

The dead body of one of the two missing soldiers was recovered on the morning of 20 February. A boat conveying four occupants sank while monitoring water levels on the Incomati River near Manhica on 17 February. The second missing body was recovered on Sunday afternoon. Authorities claimed that the victims were found in exact same place where their vessel sank.  Two government officials who were also in the boat were rescued on Wednesday and received medical treatment.

The body of the second missing soldier was recovered on the afternoon of 21 February. A boat conveying four occupants sank while monitoring water levels on the Incomati River near Manhica on 17 February.  The first missing body was recovered on Saturday morning. Authorities claimed that the victims were found in exact same place where their vessel sank. Two government officials who were also in the boat were rescued on Wednesday and received medical treatment.

The Mayor of Beira city and President of the Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM), Daviz Simango, died on 22 February of COVID-19 while receiving medical treatment in South Africa. A press conference will take place in Beira this afternoon by MDM to provide an official statement on the incident. Simango was transferred to a health facility in South Africa from Beira City on 13 February.

Unconfirmed reports on the night of 20 February indicated that insurgents skirmished with security forces in the Quionga area; no casualties were reported.  This came after militants the night before clashed with militia forces in the area and carried out looting in Quionga.

Security forces from Palma, including pro-government militia units, were reported to have been sent as reinforcements to the Quionga area on 20 February after militants attacked the town the previous day, driving away pro-government militia units and carrying out looting in the area.

Small arms fire was reported near Quiwiwa on 21 February.  This came after insurgents attacked Quionga twice on 19 and 20 February.  No further information on these shots is currently available.  The most likely explanation is random gunfire by security forces.

2 gang members were killed, and another was injured when police on 20 February exchanged fire with a criminal gang who had just committed a robbery in Lumbiza in Macaloge AP of Sanga District, Niassa. The injured gang member later died at the hospital.  2 other gang members were subsequently arrested.

A 5 man gang robbed the home of a merchant on 20 February in Lumbiza in Sanga District, Niassa, taking 55,000,000 meticais along with 36 mobile phones.  Police responded to the scene and engaged the group in a gun battle in which 3 criminals were shot dead.

A mining company announced on 22 February announced the restart of the Balama Graphite Operation in Cabo Delgado within the next three months. The company will commence rehiring staff in the near future. The mine was closed in March 2020 due to the COVID-19 impacts such as travel restrictions, limited workforce mobility, and weak end user demands due to the worldwide pandemic among other issues.

Poor living conditions were reported by the people residing at an IDP camp in Guara Guara, Buzi. Residents could not abide authorities' recommendation on social distancing to prevent spread of COVID-19 as up to 10 people sleep in one tent. Food shortages are another issue for the residents who have special needs as only beans and pasta are provided. A total of 710 families resettled in Guara-Guara resettlement center due to severe weather events.

Sources reported that there are rumors circulating in the Angolan military that the country could potentially send troops to Mozambique to help fight the insurgency, with the approval of the SADC, the African Union (AU) and with UN financial support. Despite these rumors, other sources say Mozambique has not directly asked for Angolan or any other African country for direct intervention in the country, which would be required for an intervention.

Nampula province authorities reportedly launched an operation to remove informal street sellers in a bid to curb spread of the COVID-19 virus. Sellers have been removed from streets in Nacala Port, Tchumbo Market and Waresta wholesale market among others. Strict COVID-19 protocols have been enforced to help minimize a surge of new cases and deaths in the province. A total of 13 coronavirus-related deaths have been reported in the province.

The Africa Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) of the African Union said it recently received an offer for 300 million doses of Russia’s Sputnik V vaccine to be provided Africa Vaccine Acquisition Task Team (AVATT). Some of these doses may be donated to Mozambique. The AVATT team was set up by the African Union and aims at immunizing 60% of the continental population.  The AVATT says it has already secured over 270 million doses of AstraZeneca, Pfizer, and Johnson & Johnson vaccines in the first allocation phase.

Due to the heavy rains, 11,000 people from three communities in Mavago, Niassa, have been isolated, media reports said on 22 February. Some portions of the roads leading to other districts have submerged while some bridges have reportedly collapsed following recent heavy rains.

On the afternoon of 22 February, the non-executive director of Hidroelectrica de Cahora Bassa, Francisco Itai Meque, passed away due to an undisclosed illness. He previously served as Deputy Minister of Education and Governor of Inhambane Province and of Zambezia Province. Further information regarding his death is not available at this time.

On 22 February, Former Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Oldemiro Baloi, was transported to a health facility in South Africa for medical treatment. Further information regarding his illness is not available at this time.

The Ministry Health stated that four new COVID-related deaths and 517 new cases were reported in Mozambique on 22 February. 196 of the new cases were from Maputo city, and 75 from Maputo province. 82 new cases were reported from Zambezia, 54 in Inhambane, 51 in Sofala, 37 in Nampula, 14 in Gaza, 14 in Niassa, three in Tete and one in Manica. The total number of confirmed cases in the country increased to 56,160 while the national death toll is now at 599.

After being heavily impacted by insurgency, the districts of Macomia, Quissanga and Mocimboa da Praia are reportedly not hiring teachers this academic year. A directive defending this policy was signed by Cabo Delgado Governor Valige Tawabo on 11 February.
column15: Macomia, Quissanga and Mocimboa da Praia

column4: According to the Ministry of Mineral Resources and Energy on 19 February, a South African oil company will invest $ 760 million in developing additional natural gas reservoirs around the fields of Inhassoro and Temane. The investment will allow the production of 23 million giga joules of natural gas per year and the generation of 450 megawatts (MW) of electricity at the Temane Combined Cycle Thermal Power Plant.

The first batch of COVID-19 vaccines is expected to arrive in Mozambique by the end of the month, health officials said on Monday.  Officials indicated that an undisclosed quantity of Chinese vaccine doses will arrive in the country, and that Mozambique is still negotiating with other providers for more doses. It will be administered first to healthcare professionals who are most exposed to the virus. Order of priority of the administration of the vaccine will be based on the citizens' level of exposure until everyone will be gradually reached.

The Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said there are 668,000 internally displaced persons (IDPs) that have been displaced by the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  This included 570,000 newly displaced persons in 2020. Significantly, there were over 430,000 IDPs displaced from July to December in the province.  Nearly 610,000 of these IDPs are displaced in Cabo Delgado itself; notably, this includes 144,000 IDPs in Pemba District, 114,000 in Metuge, 57,000 in Ancuabe, 66,000 in Mueda, and 54,000 in Montepuez.

The Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) stated that over 50,000 Cabo Delgado IDPs are present in Nampula Province, including 19,000 in Nampula District and 18,000 in Meconta.  This comes amid reports that 668,000 internally displaced persons (IDPs) have been displaced by the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

A recent OCHA report indicated that 36% of health facilities in Cabo Delgado had been destroyed by the ongoing conflict, and that there are currently no functional health clinics in Mocimboa da Praia, Macomia, Muidumbe, or Quissanga District.

7 individuals died due to COVID and 435 new COVID cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 23 February. The new cases were noted as follows: 111 in Sofala, 71 in Maputo city, 65 in Cabo Delgado, 52 in Niassa, 48 in Inhambane, 39 in Zambezia, Tete with 25 cases, 15 in Maputo province, and 9 in Manica province.

A fire linked to a suspected insurgent attack was reported just before 0100hrs on the morning of 22 February in Quionga town.  This came after insurgents attacked the town on both 19 and 20 February.  Other sources said insurgents had raided businesses in the area, and that no casaulties were reported.

The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) stated that locals have turned residences into makeshift bars and liquor stores in Nampula. This violates COVID restrictions, which had mandated the closing down of bars under current restrictions. INAE officials called on locals to take the COVID precautions strictly.

Health authorities stated that cholera cases are declining in Nampula on 23 February. Medical officials stated that an average of 10 cholera patients were reported during past few days in comparison to a 30-patient average in more recent weeks. Currently, 211 cases were reported in Namialo, including 12 hospitalized patients.  Officials stated that the decrease in cases was due to the improvement of individual and collective hygiene in the area.

The National Administration of Conservation Areas (ANAC) stated that 86 dolphins were found dead and washed up on the beach of Bazaruto Island on 23 February. This comes after local authorities found 25 dolphins on 21 February.  Local sources stated that the incident may be related due to the climate phenomena in Inhambane province and the previous Tropical Storm Guambe. ANAC stated that 7 other dolphins were rescued. ANAC announced that an investigation is being conducted to determine the cause of death of the dolphins.

Health authorities stated that cholera cases are increasing in Cabo Delgado province.  Since the beginning of 2021, sources have reported 4,916 cases and 55 deaths were reported, with Metuge District reported the highest number of cases.  There have been more than 400 new cases of the disease reported in recent weeks.  Cholera surveillance and response meanwhile has been disrupted in the districts of Mocimboa da Praia and Macomia, and there is no reliable information on current cholera cases in those districts.

A minibus overturned along the National Road 7 between Changara and Tete city near Makhonje village on the afternoon of 22 February. Civilian fatalities and injuries were reported. No specific numbers were mentioned.

Medical officials announced that families, relatives, of/and COVID patients themselves were identified to be at risk for developing mental problems due to fear and restrictions. 15 COVID patients were suffering from psychosis, depression, and anxiety after recovering from the virus, media sources reported.

The Portuguese Ambassador to Mozambique Maria Amelia Paiva stated that Portugal is open in assisting Mozambique in the "operationalization" of COVID vaccination plans for the country. Paiva also said that Portugal would provide protective equipment to Mozambique against COVID-19.

An independent media outlet announced the death of journalist Juma Aiuba inside his residence in Nampula. Aiuba was a well-known independent journalist in the country. Aiuba also worked with NGOs in promoting democracy in the country.

Around 20% of Mozambique's population will be vaccinated as part of the COVAX. The first phase will cover 3% of the population, which includes healthcare workers and elderly with ages above 70. The second phase was to vaccinate 17% of the population, citizens with chronic diseases, individuals aged 15 to 69, and aged 50 to 69, “essential” workers from outside the health sector, informal employees, and transport workers.  Doses of the vaccine provided by the COVAX program may not arrive in Mozambique until May.

Police arrested a Zimbabwean suspect smuggling of a ton of cannabis on a road near the Machipanda-Tete provincial border on 23 February. The cannabis was hidden inside 28 pieces of 50kg-bales of used clothes.

Police arrested a Zimbabwean suspect smuggling of a ton of cannabis on a road near the Machipanda-Tete provincial border on 23 February. The cannabis was hidden inside 28 pieces of 50kg-bales of used clothes.

Police arrested a suspect wanted for the murder of a high ranking police officer in Mogovolas, south of Nampula, at dawn of 21 February. The suspect was attempting to break into a residence when he was arrested. The suspect was member of gang.

The Centre for Public Integrity (CIP) has called the government to increase monitoring of megaproject to avoid tax losses.  The CIP said that between 2010-2019, Mozambique granted tax benefits of 172 billion meticais to companies in Mozambique engaged in megaprojects in the country, but only collected 100 billion meticais in taxes.

The Ponta de Ouro border post reported of heavy traffic due to the large number of individuals crossing to return to Mozambique on 21 February. Around 130 travelers both national and foreigners reportedly crossed during the first day of the post's reopening.  Border officials stated that the crossing is open from 06:00 to 20:00 during the Easter season, in contrast to the common schedule of 08:00 to 17:00. Joint operations are preparing for the large influx of crossings on 24 Wednesday.
column15: Ponta de Ouro border post, Matutuine

column4: Security forces in Nangade town on 19 February detained four suspects for collaborating with insurgents.  The suspects allegedly had passed information to insurgents operating in the district, including information on convoys that travelled between Nangade and Palma in early February.    Two of those arrested were Tanzanian nationals, while the other two were Mozambican nationals; all four worked as local traders.

On the afternoon of 24 February, a plane carrying 200,000 doses of the Chinese-made VeroCell COVID-19 vaccine landed in Maputo.  At least one study has indicated this vaccine is 86% effective against the predominant strains of COVID-19, though it is currently unclear how effective this vaccine is against the South African variant, which is believed to have driven Mozambique's recent COVID case spike.  These vaccine doses have been donated by China, and are not part of the COVAX program which will provide Mozambique with large quantities of the vaccine later this year.
Mozambique's government on 23 February authorized the emergency recruitment without public tender of new health professionals due to the ongoing COVID-19 spike in the country.

The UN's Office for Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs said in a recent report that 1.3 million people throughout Northern Mozambique are dependent on humanitarian assistance, primarily due to the impacts of the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  This includes 950,000 people impacted by "severe food insecurity".  Over 668,000 people have been displaced to date by this conflict.

MDM Leader and Beira Mayor Daviz Simango will receive a state funeral, Mozambique's government decreed on 23 February.  Simango died on 22 February in South Africa while hospitalized with COVID-19.  The funeral is scheduled for Friday in Beira.

Mozambican health officials were reported on 24 February to be concerned that COVID-19 was being spread into Mozambique from Tanzania.  Some districts bordering Tanzania have seen significant spikes in COVID cases in recent weeks, despite cases nationwide trending downwards.  Tanzania in June of 2020 said that the country was free of COVID-19, and President Magufuli had discouraged the wearing of masks and social distancing.  Tanzanian health officials recently have begun to take the virus more seriously, though by now the virus is thought to have spread thoroughly throughout the country.

The UN's Population Fund on 24 February reported that it had delivered reproductive health kits to support 150,000 vulnerable women and girls in Palma District.  This came amid an ongoing food and other supply shortage across Palma District.
Amid an ongoing food shortage in Palma, 1kg of rice currently costs about 400 meticais, or about $5.33, compared to a price of 45 meticais or about $.60 in Pemba for 1 kg of rice.

Significant numbers of IDPs in recent weeks and days have reportedly returned to parts of Macomia, sources reported.  This comes amid a drop in insurgent attacks in the district so far in 2021.  Many IDPs say they do want to return to their home areas, and do not want to stay in IDP camps in Southern Cabo Delgado where they receive minimal to no government support.

India's ambassador to Mozambique Shri Ankan Banerjee said on 24 February that New Delhi was ready to donate 100,000 doses of a COVID-19 vaccine.  It was unclear if Mozambique had yet accepted this offer of vaccines.
Two young men were recently released by insurgents and arrived in Ibo District in recent days.  The two were reportedly released due to food shortages among the insurgents.

Insurgents on the morning of 15 February reportedly attacked Mozambican military positions (and pro-gov militia) in the Roma area along the Mocimboa da Praia - Mueda border.  This resulted in an unknown number of casualties.  The next day, insurgents also attacked Nanili/Namili, just south of Roma, forcing government troops to withdraw from the area.  Sources conflicted as to whether a "large" group of insurgents were involved in this attack, or if a smaller group of 10 militants were responsible for the incident.

The Department of Health on 24 February announced that cholera cases have spread across Nampula, Erati, Monapo, and Memba districts. A total of 593 cases were reported in the past 24 hours. Health Director Geraldinho Avalinho said that outbreak started in the Corrane area of Meconta district before spreading to the mentioned districts just after the rainy season. Surveillance teams are monitoring the situation in these districts.
