Surveillance teams are monitoring the situation in these districts.

A vehicle collided with another vehicle and overturned along Route N1 in Namaita Administrative Port in southwest Nampula on the morning of 23 February.  2 civilians were killed and 12 were injured in the accident.

The US Embassy in Maputo announced on 23 February that the US government will support Mozambique by providing 3.7 million USD to  support the logistics of the COVID-19 vaccination campaign in the country. The support would also include medical treatment for COVID patients and oxygen supply. The assistance was to be coordinated with the WHO's COVAX program. The support comes as a part of the aid plan to strengthen the healthcare system of the country during the pandemic. The US previously donated 50 fans to the Ministry of Health and invested more than US $ 20.4 million to train, provide supplies and equipment against the pandemic.

Malawi traders stated that cooking oil is being smuggled from Mozambique into Malawi. Demand for cooking oil is in Malawi and the price of local cooking oil has risen, leading many to buy smuggled Mozambican oil.  Local traders says there are "no serious patrols" along the borders with Mozambique and that traders "order" products and receive the smuggled goods in the Mloza and Nkando areas.
Police detained five public school employees of Matadouro and Josina Machel schools in Beira on 18 February. The suspects were charged for embezzling almost 15 million MZN, or about $200,000.

Local sources stated that around 40 teachers working for the Institute of Health Sciences of Nampula are still waiting for unpaid salaries for the years 2015 and 2016. The teachers stated that they have contacted the Provincial Health Directorate of Nampula and were told that the issue has been acknowledged and that officials were waiting for financial availability to pay these arrears.

Customs detained a suspect in possession of 4kg of heroin and 2kg of cocaine in Nacala Port in Nampula province in recent days.  Hours after this seizure, the drugs "disappeared", and it is unclear currently what happened to these narcotics.

Customs detained a suspect in possession of 4kg of heroin and 2kg of cocaine in Nacala Port in Nampula province in recent days.  Hours after this seizure, the drugs "disappeared", and it is unclear currently what happened to these narcotics.

MDM officials stated that MDM Leader and Beira Mayor Daviz Simango's body arrived in Beira on 25 February. Simango is scheduled to be buried on 26 February during a state-held funeral. Simango died on 22 February in South Africa while hospitalized with COVID-19.  The funeral is scheduled for Friday in Beira.

A new proposed law on broadcasting and the media will come before the Mozambican National Assembly in the coming days.  This law has been called "anti-democratic" by civil society, who say the law muzzles independent press.  This proposed law is widely expected to be passed however and become a law.

Insurgents on the morning of 24 February attacked a group of 3 civilians gathering firewood near the abandoned village of Nandimba, around 6kms northwest of Palma town, targeting the group with small arms fire.  One person was abducted by the militants, while the other two escaped.

Insurgents on the morning of 24 February attacked a group of 3 civilians gathering firewood near the abandoned village of Nandimba, around 6kms northwest of Palma town, targeting the group with small arms fire.  One person was abducted by the militants, while the other two escaped.

Macomia officials were reported to have recently travelled to Pemba to attempt to convince traders to return to Macomia town and district, guaranteeing security and saying the insurgency has been largely driven out of the district.  This comes amid reports that some IDPs displaced from Macomia have recently returned to the district as insurgent attacks have decreased in the area.  Some services, including electricity, have been restored in Macomia.

Sources indicate the insurgents remain present in the Mucojo and Quiterajo areas, despite security force operations targeting militants in these areas in recent weeks.  Fishermen who recently attempted to return to their home villages in these areas reported a continued insurgent presence in these coastal APs.

Sources indicate the insurgents remain present in the Mucojo and Quiterajo areas, despite security force operations targeting militants in these areas in recent weeks.  Fishermen who recently attempted to return to their home villages in these areas reported a continued insurgent presence in these coastal APs.

Concerns have recently been raised that insurgents may be attempting to establish a presence on Saufo Island in the Rovuma Estuary.  An insurgent base on this island would allow the group to potentially tax or exercise other forms of control over smuggling routes between Tanzania and Cabo Delgado.  These concerns have been raised after militants in recent days attacked Quionga, in Northern Palma, and later reportedly retreated north towards the Tanzanian border.

Insurgents in the early morning hours of 16 February attacked pro-government militia positions in Nanili village on the western border of MDP District, south of Roma, which insurgents had attacked the previous day.  Clashes began around 0400hrs and ended by 1300hrs.  Militia units reportedly ran out of ammunition, and after a military convoy was ambushed while en route to reinforce militia positions at Nanili, militia withdrew from the area.  At least 2 people were killed in these clashes, including 1 person who was beheaded.

The Ministry of Health announced that 5 new COVID deaths and 677 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 25 February. The new cases are distributed as follows: 141 in Maputo province, 136 in Maputo city, 94 in Tete, 81 in Sofala, 74 in Cabo Delgado, 70 in Zambezia, 56 in Nampula, 19 in Manica, 13 in Niassa, 5 in Inhambane, 1 in Gaza.  There are currently 18,304 active cases in the country.  The new cases increases the total to 57,597 and 613 total deaths.

The Ministry of Health announced 2 new COVID deaths and 325 new cases in Mozambique on 24 February. A majority of the new cases were recorded in Maputo province with 105 cases. 90 were recorded in Maputo city, 69 in Sofala, 52 in Niassa, 20 in Zambezia, 19 in Manica, 13 in Nampula, and 9 in Inhambane. The active cases were at 18,438.

Mozambique will receive an undisclosed number of COVID-19 doses from Portugal, who announced on 24 February that it would provide 1 million vaccine doses to Portuguese speaking countries (PALOP) and East Timor. These doses will be delivered "over the next six months".  This distribution represents 5% of the total 20 million doses Portugal has purchased.
Police arrested a pastor for sexual assault charges in Chihango, north Maputo city, on 24 February. The suspect reportedly recruited minors in his congregation and assaulted them.

Police arrested a suspect in Majune district in possession of a semi-automatic firearm on 18 February.  The man confessed to being a member of a larger criminal gang, who were targeted by police on 20 February.

Police arrested 2 gang members in Lumbiza in Sanga District of Niassa on 20 February after a gun battle in which 3 other gang members were killed.  Police clashed with the group just after they had robbed a local merchant.  The captured gang members also provided information about other members of the gang who are being pursued by police.

A police officer refused a bribe of 1,300 USD and detained a Zimbabwean drug dealer in Vanduzi area of Manica province on 18 February. 28 packs of cannabis were seized during the arrest. The suspect was travelling to Zimbabwe.

A police officer refused a bribe of 1,300 USD and detained a Zimbabwean drug dealer in Vanduzi area of Manica province on 18 February. 28 packs of cannabis were seized during the arrest. The suspect was travelling to Zimbabwe.

The Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA) said on 25 February that the economic conditions in Mozambique are expected to deteriorate over the coming months due to restrictions imposed to stem the spread of COVID in the country.  CTA Chairman Vuma stated the economy declined significantly in December and January and is expected over the near term future to continue to decline.  Mozambique saw 40,000 jobs lost last year and 1,075 companies closed down as a result of the pandemic.

FRELIMO MPs speaking in the National Assembly on 25 Feb said there was "encouraging news" from the ongoing fight against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado, saying troops had killed significant numbers of insurgents in recent weeks, though did not provide specific details on any military operations.

RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo in a 25 February interview said that he is still waiting for Maputo to reach out to initiate talks with his group. Nhongo stated that he will not violate the ceasefire which was declared last December. A team of five members of his group are ready to begin a dialogue with the government.  Nhongo also accused the government of "bombing" dissident camps five times in Gorongosa; it was unclear when these "bombings" occurred.  Only one dissident attack, which took place in early January, has been reported in Central Mozambique in 2021.

The National Assembly returned to session on 25 February.  RENAMO called on President Nyusi to answer for allegations he had received 1 million USD as part of the "Hidden Debts" scandal.  The opposition also demanded the government present information regarding how funds meant to help fight COVID-19 have been spent in the country.  RENAMO also said the government has delayed aspects of the DDR process.

Local officials stated that two communities, Paia and Cuvir, were cut off from Maua district HQ in Niassa province due to the heavy rains which recently destroyed area roads. Maúa district administrator Ilda Macome stated that even alternative roads were inaccessible to the areas.
Security forces seized 1,624 illegal fishing gear during an ongoing 3-month operation in the mangrove areas of Mozambique. The operation began on 15 December and would conclude on 31 March.
Security forces arrested two suspects in possession of Ivory tips in Chimoio on 26 February. The suspects were  identified as teachers who intended to look for buyers for the ivory.

Security forces on the afternoon of 24 February shut down the road between Nangade and Mueda after receiving information regarding the movements of suspected insurgents near Litingina, south of Nangade along the R763 road.

Security forces on the afternoon of 24 February shut down the road between Nangade and Mueda after receiving information of regarding the movements of suspected insurgents near Litingina, south of Nangade along the R763 road.

Local sources reported suspected insurgent movement between Ngangolo and Quibaoni, along the Mueda-Nangade Road after 1200hrs on 24 February. Insurgent movements were also reported near Litingina, leading to the road being closed down by security forces.

On Thursday morning (25 February), a group of 20 insurgents then attacked Luneke village, about 10kms from Nangade town, and forcing civilians to flee to the district capital.  At least 4 people were killed in this attack and two were injured, sources later indicated.  Insurgent movements in the area and this latest attack have also led to a further postponement of supply convoys being dispatched from Nangade to Palma. FDS troops responded to the area and later reported killing 6 insurgents in clashes.
A LAM Boeing 737 landed at Quelimane Airport on the afternoon of Friday, and skidded off the runway during this landing.  No injuries were reported during this incident.

Deputy National Director of Public Health Benigna Matshinhe said on 26 February that Mozambique should be able to vaccinate 20% of Mozambicans by the end of the year, also saying that 6 million vaccine doses are likely to arrive in the country as part of the COVAX program in May.  The country's 90,000 health officials will be the first priority of the vaccination drive.  After these workers, people 70 and older and people with chronic health conditions will next be vaccinated.  A second phase will include people with HIV/AIDs and tuberculosis, as well as people between 50-69, and "key workers" outside of the health sector including teachers, security force members, childcare workers, and emergency response personnel.  This news comes after Mozambique this week received its first 200,000 doses of COVID vaccine, donated by China.  100,000 more doses are expected in the near future also from India.
Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said on Thursday that the districts of Mocimboa da Praia, Muidumbe, Macomia, and Quissanga are "impossible" to access for the provision of humanitarian aid.
column15: Mocimboa da Praia, Muidumbe, Macomia, and Quissanga

column4: Medical charity MSF said on 25 February that aid being provided to people displaced by the Cabo Delgado insurgency in resettlement centers in Cabo Delgado, Nampula, and Niassa is "insufficient because support has not been channeled to match the needs", saying in most of these centers which are primarily located in Southern Cabo Delgado, there is a lack of food, water, health care, hygiene, shelter, and income generating activities.  Over 668,000 people have been displaced by the ongoing insurgency in the province.

Insurgents on 23 February kidnapped a group of 6 civilians (3 men and 3 women) in the Mitope area of Mocimboa da Praia who were returning from nearby fields, and was reported to have later beheaded at least 2 of the men.  A second source said all 3 men were beheaded.

Insurgents on 23 February kidnapped a group of 6 civilians (3 men and 3 women) in the Mitope area of Mocimboa da Praia who were returning from nearby fields, and was reported to have later beheaded at least 2 of the men.  A second source said all 3 men were beheaded.

Security forces have postponed a new supply convoy to Palma from Nangade after insurgents were active in areas south of Nangade along the road to Mueda on 24-25 February.  Because of this insecurity, a convoy that had been assembling in Nangade was sent back to Mueda.

The Ministry of Health announced 7 new COVID deaths and 621 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 26 February. The new cases are as follows: 130 in Cabo Delgado, 115 in Maputo city, 108 in Nampula, 95 in Zambezia, 40 in Tete, 32 in Niassa, 26 in Gaza, 20 in Maputo province, 11 in Sofala, 5 in Inhambane, and 4 in Manica.

Civil society organizations have expressed concern over the draft press and broadcasting laws debated at the Mozambican Parliament session on 26 February. The laws were initially drafted 10 years before during the Presidency of Armando Guebuza. The laws, civil society organizations say, would "hamper the work of journalists"

UN Secretary-General Spokesman Stephane Dujarric stated that the food insecurity, severe climate, and ongoing conflict have caused the humanitarian situation to continually worsen in Cabo Delgado. Dujarric stated that the Humanitarian Response Plan requires 254 million USD to assist 1,100,000 individuals affected by these issues in Cabo Delgado.

The National Migration Service (SENAMI) said on 25 February that they had refused entry to Mozambique to 14 foreigners who did not meet the necessary requirements to enter the country. 10 of the foreigners lacked a work visa, while three others were unsure as to where they were staying, and another had a forged work visa.  These individuals include 7 Nigerians, one Angolan, one Rwandan, one Ghanaian, one Indian, one Togolese,  one Beninese and one Somali.

Local sources stated that Total has invested around 250 million USD for natural gas exploration in Mozambican companies. The oil and gas company reportedly stated that the investment is part of a 1 billion USD the company says it has spent with companies registered in Mozambique.

Secretary Gen. of MDM Jose Domingos has taken over as interim president of MDM after the death of President Daviz Simango. The interim period will continue until an MDM president is elected.  A meeting will be held in early April to discuss holding a congress to pick the next leader of the party.

FRELIMO MPs have reportedly indicated they intend to endorse a new controversial law for media and broadcasting.  This law will allow the government to exercise a greater degree of control over the media, and has been roundly criticized by civil society groups.  FRELIMO, which has a large majority in the National Assembly, can pass this bill without any support needed from RENAMO or MDM MPs.

Officials announced the suspension of boat travel between Manhica and AP of Calanga due to the death of two soldiers last week. Around 8,500 individuals are unable to reach the district HQ of Manhica due to the suspension of boats. Calanga Administrative Official Juvenal Armando stated that the suspension was put to place until conditions are safe for boat transportation.
A ship sank due to overcrowding on Zambezi River in Caia District, Sofala province on the evening of Monday, 22 February. Four individuals died.

Authorities announced that the trial of a group of Iranian nationals for terror charges was delayed due to the lack of translators. The hearing was reportedly to be conducted in Portuguese. The suspects were previously detained for on a ship loaded with weapons in Pemba Bay in late 2019.

A Nampula delegate for a veterans association, Eugenio de Fatima said on 27 February that members of the group are willing to deploy to Cabo Delgado to reinforce the Mozambican military if called upon.  De Fatima also said that the organization would need to be officially asked by the government to deploy to Cabo Delgado and could not do so as "volunteers".

Hospital Geral Polana Canico personnel say that there has been an increase of young COVID patients in the hospital, with 4 patients between 20-30 with no pre-existing conditions recently hospitalized with the virus.
column15: Hospital Geral Polana Canico, Maputo City

column4: Two insurgents were captured and beaten by locals in the area of Quirindi, a source disclosed on 25 Feb. Their weapons were also seized during the incident, and locals also beat the two militants before later handing them over to the military authorities.

The Ministry of Health announced 10 new COVID deaths and 554 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 27 February. This brings the total number of COVID-19 cases diagnosed in the country to 58,772, while the coronavirus total death toll reached 630. The new cases are as follows: 129 cases from Maputo province, 108 from Maputo city, 98 cases from Zambezia, 75 from Inhambane, 68 from Cabo Delgado, 38 from Nampula, 29 from Gaza, six from Tete, five from Niassa and three from Manica.

On the night of Friday 26 February, at around 1800hrs, militants attacked the village of Quirinde, on the coast approximately 20km north of Palma.  In addition to carrying out killings, looting, and setting part of the village on fire, several villagers were also reportedly abducted in this attack.

On the night of Friday 26 February, at around 1800hrs, militants attacked the village of Quirinde, on the coast approximately 20km north of Palma, and 6 kms east of Quionga, which was attacked one week previously.  Insurgents reportedly attacked the village by land and by sea, landing a small number of fighters on a beach outside the town.  Militants were armed with small arms and machetes. Three people were reportedly killed in this raid while others sustained injuries during the incident.  A second source reported 7 people killed in the attack, while houses were set on fire and looting carried out.  The following day, militants attacked the Namoto border post near the Rovuma river on the Mozambique – Tanzania border.  In response to these attacks Mozambique security forces deployed helicopters and ground troops to the area in an attempt to pursue the attackers.  Large numbers of people fled the area after these attacks.
Insurgents on the evening of 27 February were reported to have raided Namoto border post along the Cabo Delgado - Tanzania border.  No further details regarding this attack are currently available.

On 27 February, Health Minister Armindo Tiago stated that Ministry of Health needs a further ten days to complete its preparations for vaccinating health professionals against the COVID-19 virus, which includes sending the vaccines from Maputo to the provincial capitals, and training all the vaccination staff in administering the vaccine. The vaccination plan will be announced in the next ten days as well.  The country received 200,000 doses of the vaccine last week.

Mayor of Quelimane, Manuel de Araujo, said on 01 March that the city is facing challenges related the spreading of COVID-19 on public transport in the city. 16-seater van called 'chapa 100' are used for public transport in the city and are often overcrowded.

Police officers detained a 60-yr-old corn farmer in Manica on 27 Feb for allegedly owning a plantation with more than 300 cannabis sativa plants. Investigations is ongoing to apprehend other suspects who were involved with the crime.

On 28 Feb, the Iranian Government imposed travel bans on passengers from 32 high-risk countries, including Mozambique, to help curb spread of COVID-19 and its new strains. Other countries included are UK, Angola, South Africa, Argentina, Bolivia, Botswana, Brazil, Burundi, Cape Verde, Chile, Colombia, Democratic Republic of Congo, Ecuador, Eswatini, French Guinea, Lesotho, Guyana, Malawi, Mauritania, Namibia, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Rwanda, Seychelles, Suriname, Tanzania, Uruguay, Venezuela, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Travelers who have been in the aforementioned countries for more than four hours will be denied entry into Iran. Meanwhile, all passengers, including Iranian citizens, above the age of eight-yr-old  coming from abroad must present a valid negative COVID‑19 test certificate at the port of entry.

9,330 teachers will be hired in Mozambique to respond to the demand in the National Education System a Ministry of Education and Human Development (MINEDH) spokesperson, Gina Guibunda said on 01 March. Nampula province, with the largest number of student population, will receive around 2,685 teachers, followed by Zambezia with 1,938 teachers. The government aims to fulfill the needs of the students before the academic year 2021 commence on 22 March.

Sources on 01 March reported long lines at shops, shortages, and high prices in Palma as no supply convoys have reached the town in nearly one month.  The N380 road continues to be blocked by insurgents in Mocimboa da Praia district, while convoys have not travelled the Nangade-Palma road since early February.  Local media reported that Palma in recent days did receive some supplies by sea, but that these supplies were inadequate to relieve the food insecurity situation in the town.

Helicopters and two battalions of the police's Rapid Intervention Unit were reported to have been dispatched to the Quirinde area on 26 February after an insurgent attack on the village.  No clashes however were confirmed to have occurred in the area.

Cabo Delgado governor Valigue Tauabo on 01 March said that he wanted to "acknowledge" cooperation and collaboration between "Defense and Security Forces and Former Combatants who are doing a very excellent job in the district of Muidumbe".  Pro-government militias consisting of former combatants have been operating in Muidumbe and other districts of Cabo Delgado and have become increasingly active over the past 6 months.
Unconfirmed reports on 28 February indicated a continued insurgent presence in the Quirinde area, after militants attacked the village on 26 February.

At least 3 people died due to malnutrition and starvation in Palma over the past week, local media reported on 27 February.  This comes as the town continued to receive little to no supplies due to insurgents controlling the main road to Palma, while insurgent attacks south of Nangade also disrupted a potential new convoy travelling from Nangade to Palma.

Andre Matsangaissa Junior, one of the top leaders of the dissident RENAMO Military Junta, was announced to have defected from the group on 01 March, and met with President Nyusi in Maputo.  Matsangaissa is the nephew of Andre Matsangaissa, who had been a soldier and FRELIMO member before becoming the first leader of RENAMO, died in a raid targeting FRELIMO in 1979.  President Nyusi meanwhile called on all RENAMO Military Junta members in Manica, Sofala, Tete, and Niassa to join the DDR process.

On 02 March, Amnesty International published a report accusing South African private military firm Dyck Advisory Group (DAG) of having killed large numbers of civilians in indiscriminate helicopter attacks in Cabo Delgado. According to Amnesty's report, DAG helicopters in many cases fired machine guns and dropped bombs "indiscriminately" into crowds of people, and had on many occasions illegally fired on civilian infrastructure, including on hospitals, schools, and homes. These accounts were based on multiple interviews with civilians present during attacks by DAG helicopters.  This report also detailed significant violations by government security forces and by insurgents.

The Ministry of Health announced 11 new COVID deaths and 578 new cases in Mozambique on 28 February.  These new cases brought the country's number of infections to 59,350 and the national death toll is now at 641.  217 patients are currently hospitalized, 152 of it were in Maputo city.

The Ministry of Health announced 12 new COVID deaths and 257 new cases in Mozambique on 01 March. 137 of the new cases were recorded in Maputo province, followed by 64 cases in Inhambane, 23 in Maputo city, 15 in Nampula, 10 in Zambezia, 5 in Gaza, 2 in Sofala, and 1 in Tete. These new cases brought the country's number of infections to 59,607 and the national death toll is now at 653.

On 01 March, Maputo city received 13,920 doses of Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccines intended for more than 9,000 health care professionals in the city.  Training of technicians to administer the vaccine began on 01 March.  60% of the 200,000 vaccines received from China last week will be used to treat Mozambican health workers.

The National Council of the Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM) said on 27 February that MDM congress will be held in April 2020 to elect a new Party President. The decision was made hours after the funeral of former party president Daviz Simango. MDM Secretary-General, Jose Domingos, will serve as interim head of the party until a new president is elected.

216 Mozambicans were deported from South Africa via the Ressano Garcia border crossing on 26 Feb. One of the deported citizens was accused of murder, another of selling narcotics, and 22 allegedly involved in robberies. A total of 5,491 Mozambicans were deported from South Africa between 01 January and 26 February.

Security forces arrested a 30-yr-old missionary of the African Evangelical Church of Christ over alleged abduction and sexual abuse of a 14-yr-old civilian at his house in Bairro 6 of Inhamissa, Xai-Xai, authorities disclosed on 02 March.

Researchers of University of Lurio and other European Universities in a recent report on 28 February said that sea levels along the Cabo Delgado Province could rise by 22 meters in 2050.  This could lead to 86km of the coastline disappearing while 69km of coastline would be significantly impacted by erosion. 35-40% of coastal communities as a result would likely fall into poverty as fishing livelihoods would be substantially negatively impacted.

The criminal case filed against the  executive editor of the weekly Canal de Mozambique, Matias Guente, has been shelved, media sources reported on 01 March. A case was filed in 2020 against Guente over alleged violation of state secrecy after he published an article about a contract between the Mozambican government and the US multinational Anadarko for the security of natural gas projects in Cabo Delgado.  Canal de Mozambique's offices meanwhile were attacked in a firebombing incident in 2020 in Maputo.

37 new COVID-19 cases were detected in Cabo Delgado on 27 February. 20 of the new cases in the province were found in Mueda District, two cases of Chiure, one in Balama, one in the District of Montepuez, one in the District of Ancuabe and 1 in the District of Namuno.

Due to heavy rainfall, transportation of goods on the road between Zumbo and Maravia districts has been interrupted with large trucks carrying goods unable to travel along the road; only light vehicles are currently able to travel on this route.
Analysts said on 01 March that Mozambique's meticais will continue to depreciate for the rest 2021, hitting 77.7 meticais per dollar, against rates of 69.5 meticais per dollar in 2020.

Mozambican Police arrested three suspects in Machava on 26 Feb over the alleged theft of 31 gas cylinders. Reports suggests that suspects were responsible for stealing  gas cylinders in homes and commercial establishments and selling them on the black market.

Albano Cariz, the councilor for Beira's Construction and Urbanization, will replace Daviz Simango as the Mayor of Beira. Cariz previously came in third place during 2018 municipal elections. He is due to be sworn on 05 March.
A 42-yr-old woman was sexually abused and murdered by a 73-yr-old man in Maluana, Manhica on the morning of 25 February. The suspect was later arrested by the police.
Security forces arrested a man for raping and killing a 42-yr-old woman in Maluana, Manhica on 25 Feb. He is detained at the Manhica District Command.
Two men from Zimbabwe were arrested for allegedly smuggling a corpse into the country from Mozambique on 21 February. The dead body they had smuggled belonged to the wife of one of the suspects.

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa stated on 28 February that South Africa had signed an agreement with Johnson & Johnson to secure 11 million COVID-19 vaccines. Ramaphosa added that 20 million doses of Pfizer’s vaccine had also been secured while 12 million vaccines would come from the World Health Organization’s COVAX scheme. The government is still finalizing an allocation of vaccines from the African Union. Some of this vaccine supply could eventually be donated to Mozambique.

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa stated on 28 February that they will ease restrictions rom alert level 3 to 1 due to a decline in new COVID cases. The country's curfew will be from midnight to 0400hrs, gatherings will be allowed and alcohol sales would return to normal license provisions.  South Africa has had the worst COVID outbreak in Africa.

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa stated on 28 February that the South African military was continuously monitoring the developments in northern Mozambique to ensure there is no threat to surrounding countries, including South Africa. Ramaphosa also said Mozambican Government reportedly briefs the Southern African Development Community (SADC) region on the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

A ship loaded with supplies have docked arrived Palma on 26 Feb, local sources reported.  This was the first shipment of supplies to arrive in the town since early February.  Regular supply shipments by sea are reportedly set to resume to Palma as the town has been largely unreachable by road in recent months due to insurgents controlling parts of the N380 road and threatening the Nangade-Palma road.

Authorities stated on 01 March that 180 tons of various essential products and another 45,000 L of fuel will be transported weekly from Pemba to Palma via supply ship.   Regular supply shipments by sea are reportedly set to resume to Palma as the town has been largely unreachable by road in recent months due to insurgents controlling parts of the N380 road and threatening the Nangade-Palma road.  Significant food insecurity, shortages, and large price increases on basic products have been reported in recent weeks in the town.

On 23 February, two private security companies, Advanced Training and Support Division of Paramount Group, and Dubai-based Burnham Global  announced the recent signing of a multimillion dollar contract with an African government to provide a range of military training and advisory services. Reports suggest that a pilot project has been operating in the undisclosed country since mid-2020, and due to its success , the government decided to commission the expanded programme.  The unnamed country is believed to be Mozambique, where both companies were confirmed to be operating in mid-2020.

Media reported on 27 Feb that the Paris Club Creditor Countries representatives have agreed to an extension of Mozambique's debt moratorium until June, allowing Mozambique to defer $250 million in payments.

3,467 people who had sought shelter in Nampula province were believed to have returned from their homes in Cabo Delgado. Emergency Operational Centre (COE), Alberto Armando stated that these people are no longer in the areas where they were initially mapped, and are believed to have returned to their home districts in Cabo Delgado.   Over 40,000 IDPs from Cabo Delgado are currently living in Nampula.

Mining company Gemfields announced that they would restart product at their Montepuez mine in March after suspending its operations for a year. The operation will be restarted in phases until the entire mine is fully operational.

Dyck Advisory Group said on 02 March that the company had hired lawyers to conduct an independent investigation into its own activities in Mozambique. The investigation has been launched in response to a report by Amnesty International saying the South African private military company was responsible for human rights violations and reckless targeting of insurgents that have reportedly caused civilian casualties in Cabo Delgado.

A study published on 27 February said that the Mozambican government has not given adequate revenues to communities where natural resources are being exploited in Niassa, Nampula, and Zambezia provinces. The study said that many communities are only given between 30,000 - 300,000 meticais per year by the government (between $400 to $4000), and in many cases have not received any revenue from  the government.  Communities near mining resources are meant to receive 2.75% of all revenue generated by these resources.

A video was recently posted online showing Dyk Advisory Group personnel active in Cabo Delgado.  The video shows clips of armed private contractors, weapons, and various aircraft in Cabo Delgado.  The video also included footage of DAG helicopters flying over forest and coast terrain in Cabo Delgado.  This video emerged shortly before a Amnesty International Report was published accusing DAG of human rights abuses, including the killing of civilians, in Cabo Delgado.

The Ministry of Health announced 12 new COVID deaths and 307 cases in Mozambique on 2 March. Sofala province recorded 58 cases, 55 cases in Niassa, 41 in Maputo city, 31 in Zambezia, 35 in Cabo Delgado, 24 in Maputo province, 23 in Nampula, 21 in Inhambane, 10 in Tete, 7 in Gaza, and 2 in Manica. 59,598 total cases in the country have been reported to date.

The UN Population Fund announced 2 March that it would require 12 million USD to support women and girls affected by violence in Cabo Delgado. Women and girl IDPs living in camps are prone to sexual violence and more prone to be impacted by disease in the province as well.

Palma residents stated that they are experiencing food shortages due to the lack of local harvests brought about by drought and insurgent attacks in the district Locals stated that they depend on supply shipments which also have been hindered by the insecurity of the Nangade-Palma road as vehicles have been attacked by insurgents along this route.

Local sources stated that wealthy and high-income Mozambicans with COVID-19 in recent months have travelled to Johannesburg and Europe for treatment.  Mozambique's own health system has struggled in February and January amid an ongoing COVID-19 case spike.

Police detained six individuals for spreading disinformation related to cholera in Namutequeliua, Nampula, on 2 March. The suspects initially broke into the district secretary’s residence, causing significant material damage, and saying the secretary was spreading cholera.  The date of the initial crime was not immediately clear.

Police detained six individuals for spreading disinformation related to cholera in Namutequeliua, Nampula, on 2 March. The suspects initially broke into the district secretary’s residence, causing significant material damage, and saying the secretary was spreading cholera.

Mozambique saw a decline in fishery exports in 2020 by 56% compared to 2019 due to the reduction of catches by the industrial and semi-industrial fleets due to the ongoing pandemic. The Minister of Fisheries Augusta Maita stated that the current fishing season meanwhile has had a "difficult" beginning due to Cyclone Eloise and Tropical Storm Chalane.

The Deputy National Director of Public Health Benigna Matsinhe stated that during February a 3.4% increase in COVID-19 cases was reported 20,696 new COVID cases were diagnosed, compared with 20,012 in January. Deaths have increased by 36% as 274 were recorded during February, in comparison with 201 in January. Hospitalization has also increased by 13% as 887 were recorded in January while 1,002 were recorded by February.  Despite a drop in cases towards the end of the month, February was so far the worst month of the pandemic in Mozambique to date.

Amnesty International stated in a report released on 02 March that insurgents in Cabo Delgado are guilty of war crimes, and have deliberately burned villages and killed civilians. Insurgents also regularly carry out beheadings, and other mutilations with machetes.  Insurgents also regularly target women for abduction, detention, rape, and forced marriage.

Amnesty International in an 02 March report said that Mozambican troops are guilty of war crimes, and have carried attacks on civilians suspected to be involved with the insurgents in Cabo Delgado. In many cases, civilians suspected of cooperating with insurgents were reportedly executed or tortured.  Soldiers have also raped local women, and regularly disappear local civilians as well.  Government forces have also tortured and carried out summary executions of suspected /confirmed insurgents.

Police arrested a suspect for sexually assaulting her niece in Chiango, north Maputo City, on 1 March. The suspect reportedly lured the victim with gifts before conducting the crime. The suspect was released four days later.

Police arrested a suspect for sexually assaulting her niece in Chiango, north Maputo City, on 2 March. The suspect reportedly lured the victim with gifts before conducting the crime. The suspect was released four days later.

Reports from Pemba indicate that South African military contractors operating in Cabo Delgado are and have been utilizing modified propane tanks as "homemade bombs" which are used to target insurgents in the province.  These bombs have no aiming mechanisms and are "low tech", and are a considerable risk of causing civilian casualties.

The Order of Doctors organization stated that the Ministry of Health should be concerned with the country's lack of a vaccination plan. The organization stated that the vaccination campaign cannot be done in a disorderly manner and without any criteria, saying that after doses from China arrived last week, the government had no plan on how to distribute the vaccine and to who.

The National Institute of Health Deputy Director-General stated that the negative test certificate for individuals who recovered from COVID is a serious violation of the health protocol, saying for those who recovered from COVID that the test should not be necessary.

Mozambique fell by 16 points on the scale on Freedom in the World Report 2021 compared to last year's report. A total of 49 countries were analyzed. Mozambique was the 16th out of 27th of the "partially free" category. Mozambique has fallen the furthest on this yearly report since the beginning of the 2010's than any other country analyzed.

Security forces responded to an insurgents attack at Luneke near Nangade and clashed with militants, killing 6 of the group's members on 25 February.  Insurgents reportedly later returned to Luneke and again attacked the village.

Insurgents on the evening of 25 February returned to the village of Luneke after an earlier raid on the village and clash with security forces, setting residences on fire and looted valuables. Insurgents launched this second attack on the village after security forces killed 6 insurgents after the initial attack.

The insurgents reportedly blocked off a part of the Mueda-Nangade road preventing vehicles' passage on 1 March after insurgents were reported to be active near Litingina. Local sources stated that the blockade isolated Nangade town.

Insurgents were reported to have placed barricades on a road in the Muiha area, northwest of Nangade town, on the morning 2 March. This comes a day after they reportedly blocked part of Mueda-Nangade road.

Insurgents chased several farmers away from the farmlands near Namatil in Mueda District, near the border with Nangade and close to the Rovuma River, on the morning of 2 March. The insurgents also blocked off a road in  Muiha Area on the same day.
Local sources stated that insurgents were spotted near Litingina area on 1 March. The insurgents also reportedly killed two civilians in nearby Eduardo Mondlane village.
Insurgents killed two civilians coming from a farm in Eduardo Mondlane village near Litingina area on 1 March. No further details regarding this incident are currently available.

Military helicopters were reported to have been deployed to Nangade District south of Nangade town after insurgents killed two people in the area on Monday.  No further details on this operation are currently available.
Insurgents on 22 February beheaded two people in the Ngalonga area of Nangade District, near the border with Mocimboa da Praia
Unconfirmed reports on the morning of 03 March said militants had attacked Ntamba in Southern Nangade, setting fire to several homes.  No further details on this attack are currently available.

The German government issued a press release stating that it would provide 2,064,000 doses of the Astrazeneca / Oxford vaccine to Mozambique to fight the COVID pandemic. The vaccine donation comes as part of the COVAX initiative. The donation was in coordination with the EU to provide fair and accessible vaccines worldwide.  This batch of vaccines is expected to arrive in Mozambique within the next 3 months.

Insurgents on the night of 02 March at around 2000hrs were reported to have attacked the Namoto area for a second time in 72 hours, setting a border post in the area on fire.  No details on casualties were available.  Insurgents were believed to have returned for this second raid after discovering the border post's defenses were weak in an initial raid on the night of 27 February.  Ahead of this attack, border police reportedly evacuated the area via helicopters.

The Spanish government has issued the extension of the quarantine period for travelers coming from Mozambique upon arrival in Spain. The mandatory quarantine has been set for between 7-10 days for passengers without stopovers arriving at any Spanish airport. Travelers are able to access limited essential areas such as food groceries, pharmaceuticals, and attendance at health centers.

The World Food Program (WFP) intends to expand assistance to over 500,000 IDPs in Cabo Delgado. The WFP is already providing assistance to 400,000 IDPs as of February 2021. More than 650,000 people have been displaced in Cabo Delgado due to the ongoing insurgency.

The Ministry of Health recorded 481 new COVID cases and 3 deaths in Mozambique on 3 March. The breakdown of the new cases are as follows: 162 in Maputo city, 82 in Maputo province, 67 in Cabo Delgado, 65 in Sofala, 55 in Inhambane, 19 in Nampula, 13 in Zambezia, 9 in Manica, 8 in Tete, and 1 in Gaza. The total number of cases has increased to 60,395 while deaths have increased to 668.  There are currently 15,721 active cases in the country.

Police arrested a murder suspect for killing domestic worker in the Juba area of Boane, southwest of Maputo city on 3 March. A guard and a child were also injured during the attack. The suspect was also wanted for three other murders and two other robbery charges.

Police arrested a murder suspect for killing domestic worker in Juba area of Boane, southwest of Maputo city on 3 March in a home invasion incident. A guard and a child were also injured during the attack. The suspect was also wanted for three other murders and two other robbery charges. The suspect also confessed to an attack in Tchumene 2 neighborhood.  The suspect began this murder and robbery spree on 25 December.
An armed man murdered a maid and injured three residents in Maputo province on 25 February in a home invasion incident.
An armed man murdered a father after breaking into a residence in Matola, west of Maputo city on 25 December in a home invasion incident.
Two dead bodies were discovered on 27 February in the Nhica de Rovuma area.  The two were likely killed in an insurgent attack while gathering wood in the area.

The Ministry of Health announced that 121,530 vaccines have been distributed throughout the provinces of Mozambique on 02 March. The remaining 78,470 doses have not yet been distributed and are held by the Ministry of Health. The distributed doses will be used to vaccinate 60,765 health professionals across the country.

The French government has reportedly donated 2 million EUR to Mozambique for relief for cyclones and climate disasters. The funds were also to support projects of the Foundation for Biodiversity Conservation (Biofund).

The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities ordered the closure of Limpopo Supermarket in west Xai-Xai on 3 March. The closure of the supermarket was due to the non-compliance of the supermarket with COVID precautions.

The Human Rights Commission of the Mozambican Bar Association (OAM) on 03 March called for police to stop detaining people who violate curfew in Maputo. OAM stated that the detention of the violators puts them at risk for COVID as detention cells were over populated with violators. The curfew is currently in place from 21:00 to 04:00 and has been in effect since 5 February.  OAM said that violators are being exposed to a higher risk of getting COVID by being detained.

Eight armed gang members shot and injured a civilian in Muaruaneque area of Cuamba at around 21:00 on Monday,  01 March. The gang reportedly targeted a civilian vehicle and stole mobile phones and cash from the travelers.
Eight armed gang members along the Cuamba-Nampula road on the night of 01 March ambushed a vehicle, stealing mobile phones and cash from the travelers.
Police thwarted an attempt recently by kidnappers in Cuamba to kidnap a child with albinism.
Police thwarted an attempt recently by kidnappers in Cuamba to kidnap a child with albinism.

The Cabo Delgado governor Valige Tawabo recently visited Miteda village in Muidumbe District, but was forced to use using an indirect route to reach the village due to the presence of insurgents in the district. The governor also couldn't visit Namacande due to "security reasons", local media reported.  Insurgents since late October 2020 have maintained a significant presence in the district.

The Mozambique government is waiting on the EU to present a “political document” that is required to allow the training mission by the EU in the country. Portuguese Minister of State and Foreign Affairs stated the document is being prepared; Portugal indicated earlier this year it would send at least 60 soldiers to train Mozambican security forces for operations against insurgents in Cabo Delgado.

Palma's hospital has recently reported seeing large numbers of patients ill due to malnutrition in the area due to supply shortages.  Amid this supply shortage, other sources report many residents want to leave Palma, selling their possessions and attempting to leave the district.

Six new COVID deaths and 775 new cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 4 March. The cases were recorded as follows: 431 in Maputo city, 129 in Zambezia, 88 in Sofala, 72 in Maputo province, 18 in Inhambane, 15 in Nampula, 8 in Tete, 8 in Gaza, 3 in Cabo Delgado, and 3 in Manica. 17 patients were hospitalized while 14 were discharged leaving 181 individuals admitted at COVID hospitals.

President Nyusi in an address to the country on 04 March said that the government would allow the resumption of face to face classes at all schools and universities beginning on 08 March.  The training for national sports teams has also been allowed to resume.  All other "State of Public Calamity" measures however are to remain in place, including the Maputo curfew, for another 30 days from 07 March as the country attempts to stem a second wave of COVID-19 cases.

4 railway workers disappeared on Monday, 1 March, between Inhaminga and Marromeu as they were carrying out a technical survey during a train breakdown in the area. The group on 04 March were found about 2kms from where they had disappeared.  The group became lost while attempting to get a phone signal in the area.  Security forces discovered the group.  There had been some concern that the four had been abducted by RENAMO dissidents after a suspected dissident attack was reported in a nearby area on 04 March.

National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE)  personnel stopped 16 weddings in February for violating COVID restrictions. The weddings were previously banned as a part of measures designed to minimize the effects of the pandemic. These clandestine weddings were held primarily in Maputo City and Sofala.

The World Bank was reported on 04 March to be preparing emergency financing to help Mozambique and 29 other African countries access COVID-19 vaccines.  This financing is expected to help Mozambique attain additional vaccines on top of doses which will be donated to the country through the COVAX program.

Officials stated that vaccinations in Maputo City of health care workers will begin on Monday, 8 March and ending on 12 March. Officials stated that vaccinations will target health personnel who are at least 18 years of age or older, and who have no Covid-19 symptoms or active disease.  10,229 vaccinations are expected to be carried out.

Mozambique recently requested to postpone financial assistance talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) due to pandemic. IMF Africa Director Abebe Aemro Selassie stated that the country was having difficulty in conducting the necessary work to prepare for a new IMF assistance program due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Security forces arrested a suspected insurgent in the Quionga village area in recent days. The suspect was reportedly involved with the attacks in Quionga and Quirinde villages.

Exxon on 04 March was reported to have delayed its final investment decision for the third time on an LNG project in the Rovuma Basin.  The company had been expected to invest up to $30 billion in this project.  There is no current forecast of when the final investment decision on the project will be made.  The final decision is reportedly based on lowering costs, the security situation, and a potential resource sharing agreement with Total, as well as if the project is at the time of the decision deemed a high priority for the company.
Local sources stated that insurgents attacked along Pundanhar Road on 4 March. Two individuals were found killed. This report is currently unconfirmed.

The National Institute of Health (INS) issued a warning of the risk of a “third wave” of COVID cases in Mozambique.  Health personnel said that while cases in the country have stabilized and began to decline, there is still a 20% positivity rate in tests currently being conducted.  Health officials also say there should not yet be any relaxation of preventative measures, which could trigger the third wave.  One well known epidemiologist also said that curfews should be extended to Nampula, Beira, and Quelimane to prevent major outbreaks in those large cities.

The Prime Minister Carlos Agostinho do Rosario stated that a national vaccination plan will be launched at 15:00 on Friday, 5 March. The plan will provide guidelines in implementing vaccinations against COVID in an efficient and safe manner.

Two Gazelle helicopters were reported to have been recently delivered to the Mozambican military by a South African private military contractor.  The two helicopters were first seen in February in Nacala.  This comes after reports in recent months that the company trained at least 15 Mozambican pilots to operate these aircraft (4 Gazelle helicopters in total) along with 12 Marauder armored vehicles.

Militants on 03 March were reported to have ambushed a military vehicle in the Litingina area, killing three soldiers, including a lieutenant colonel, local media reported.  The other two soldiers killed were a sergeant and a corporal.  The vehicle was reportedly travelling south towards Mueda when it was attacked in Litingina by the insurgents, who were hiding in bushes near the road.  The vehicle did not stop, though troops did reportedly fire an RPG at insurgents in the area.   A civilian vehicle behind the military vehicle saw the attack and turned around, driving back towards Nangade.

On Wednesday, militants attacked N'gangolo village, south of Litingina, and killed two people from the same family. Insurgents were also reportedly present in Samora Machel village on Wednesday night, though no attacks in the area were reported.
Insurgents were reportedly present in Samora Machel village southeast of Nangade and just east of Litingina on Wednesday night (03 March), though no attacks in the area were reported.
A group of at least five insurgents in the Litingina area on 03 March were seen to have placed logs in the R763 road, blocking the route off, just after ambushing a military vehicle in the area.

Pro-government militia active in Nangade District are reportedly unable to advance to fight insurgents who are currently active on the R763 road to Nangade as they are awaiting approval to conduct an operation from the Mueda military command.  Insurgents in recent days have carried out several attacks south of Nangade, effectively cutting the Mueda-Nangade road.

Reports on 05 March indicated that Nangade town is effectively cut off after recent insurgent attacks south and southwest of the town which began in late February.  Poor weather conditions also have made local roads difficult to travel on.  Insurgents in early March were also reported to have been active at Muhia, northwest of Nangade, and Namatil, west of the town.  Insurgents have long been active in the Mandimba area, east of Nangade along the road to Palma, and there is growing apprehension that Nangade could potentially be directly attacked by militants in the near future.

Mozambique intends to vaccinate 16 million people by the beginning of 2022, the government said on Friday. The government said it also hopes by the end of 2022 to vaccinate the entire population of the country.

57 UN specialists are still awaiting visas to enter the country to conduct a mission to Cabo Delgado. UN officials stated that the visas were delayed due to the holiday and the ongoing pandemic. The group are waiting for new humanitarian visas, a new class of visa which were only created by the Mozambican government in December.  The UN also said that health and other aid has taken almost 3 months to be released by customs.
Police arrested 17 illegal Malawian immigrants in Mutarara of Tete province on 03 March. The immigrants were crossing the Dona Ana Railway Bridge when they were detained.

RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade on 05 March called on RENAMO dissidents to join the DDR process. Momade stated that dissidents should follow Andre Matsangaissa Junior, who joined the DDR recently, defecting from the RENAMO dissident group.

UN resident coordinator on 04 March stated that humanitarian organizations continue to have difficulty entering parts of Cabo Delgado due to weather and security issues. Several of the districts with restricted access were Mocimboa da Praia, Muidumbe, Palma, Macomia, and Quissanga. Efforts were reportedly being made to secure humanitarian teams to enter the districts, but the ongoing issues were “complex”. The UN local coordinator also mentioned that the lack of assistance to the areas has increased the risk of disease outbreaks like malaria and cholera.

Police recovered the body of a civilian who was murdered by his son after he refused to participate in a traditional ceremony to attempt to resolve the family's money problems in Manjacaze District of Gaza on 4 March.

The Judicial Court in Maputo sentenced two defendants in a kidnapping case on 05 March. The suspect were identified as Adolfo Jaime and Ana Priscila, while a third defendant was acquitted for the lack of evidence regarding his involvement with the kidnapping.
The Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs stated on 6 March that they were working on repatriating stranded Filipino seafarers in Beira whose fishing vessel was sunk during Cyclone Eloise.

Authorities are planning to construct a 7.5 billion meticais worth of sanitary landfill in Maputo City to improve solid waste management for the next five years. The opening of the landfill will lead to the closure of the health-hazard Hulene Dump. The Hulene dump, which received 1200 to 1400 tons of solid waste daily, has affected the health of people living near the site in recent years.

Six new COVID deaths and 602 new cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 06 March. 174 of the new cases were from Maputo city and 109 from Maputo province. 105 new cases from Cabo Delgado, 96 from Sofala, 46 from Nampula, 25 from Zambezia, 20 from Inhambane, 14 from Niassa, 10 from Tete and two from Manica. 33 patients were hospitalized while 37 were discharged leaving 171 individuals admitted at COVID hospitals. These new cases brought the country's number of infections to 62,131 while the national COVID-related death toll now at 686.

Mozambique's vaccination campaign began on 08 March, with second doses scheduled to be administered on 05-09 April 2021. Because of the country's limited supply of vaccine doses, only health care workers for the immediate future will receive vaccinations.  Health Minister Tiago received the first shot at Maputo Central Hospital at 0800hrs.

Jangamo District Hospital is still not open to the general public due to a lack of medical equipment and health care professionals, a source disclosed on 07 March.  Construction of the hospital was completed in 2019.  Officials say they will open the hospital in April.

Difficulty of traveling along bush roads in Pemba were reported on 06 March due to large holes present on the roads caused by erosion following a rainstorm.  Motorists in medium to heavy vehicles were advised to take precaution while driving on the damaged roads.

A man in the Pemba area said on social media his vehicle had slipped off a Pemba road into a hole caused by erosion due to these rains on the night of 06 March; images of this accident were later posted online. No injuries were reported in this incident.

Another 485,000 doses of the vaccine against COVID-19 arrived at the Maputo International Airport on the morning of 08 March. 385,000 of the vaccines came via the Vaccines Global Access (COVAX) while 100,000 doses arrived from by India. The additional vaccines arrived on the same day the National Vaccination Campaign against coronavirus commenced in the country. 65,000 health care professionals  are expected to be immunized during the first phase of the aforementioned campaign. The first phase of vaccinations is scheduled to end on 12 March and the second dose will be given after 21 days.

The deputy head of the Mozambique Armed Defence Forces, Bertolino Kapetine, dismissed on 07 March the allegations from a recent Amnesty International report accusing government forces and a private security firm supporting the government of killing hundreds of civilians in Cabo Delgado. Kapetine stated that security forces' mission is defend the territory and not harm the locals. He also added that the report was written by people who have not been to Cabo Delgado.

42 floating fish farming pens were vandalized by unidentified people at the Chipembe dam in Balama, sources reported on 08 March. Several 100 liter tanks used to float the cages were stolen, likely for domestic use by locals living nearby.

About 270 families residing within the vicinity of Inhambane Airport will be relocated to restore security and visibility conditions necessary for the airport's operations. Affected families will be resettled in the neighborhoods Muele III, Marambone and Malembwane.

A dead body of a 25-yr-old man was recovered in Maxaquene C neighborhood of Maputo City on the morning of 06 March. A rope was allegedly tied around his neck, which showed signs of aggression. Residents suspect that he was a thief and was lynched by unidentified people on the night of 05 March.

Reports on 08 March indicated that N380 route north of Macomia was unpassable as at least two bridges in the area were damaged due to bad weather conditions.  Insurgents in some areas have also reportedly blocked the road with makeshift barricades.

Insurgents in some areas north of Macomia town along the N380 road have reportedly blocked parts of the route with makeshift barricades, including using vehicles to block part of the road, trees and other debris in other areas, and at some points have dug trenches near the road.  The exact location of these barricades is currently unclear, though militants have historically been based around Miangalewa and active in the Chai. and Litamanda areas, as well as in areas further south.

Sources reported on 08 March that the Montepuez-Mueda road was reported to be in poor condition due to the heavy rains and due to mud slides along several sections of the road.  Conditions were reported to be especially poor near Mueda, with the road impassable to most vehicles, including heavy trucks.

The Mueda-Nangade-Palma road  continues to be in poor condition due to the rains and is largely unusable.  For several weeks, the military due to the threat of insurgent attacks has closed this road (including most recently between Mueda and Nangade).
column15: Mueda - Nangade - Pundanhar to Palma road

column4: A dead body of a 40-yr-old man was recovered inside the trunk of a vehicle parked on the Maputo ring road, in Marracuene around 1500hrs on 06 March. Reports suggest that the vehicle arrived in the early hours of Saturday morning and remained unattended in the afternoon. Initial investigation stated that the victim may have died of asphyxiation

Security forces in operations in recent days reportedly attacked insurgent positions in the Nkonga area, southeast of Nangade town, supported by at least 5 attack helicopters and elements of pro-government militia.  In combined air and ground operations, security forces were reported to have killed an unknown number of insurgents, and to have freed an unknown number of people recently abducted by insurgents in other areas of Nangade.

A launch ceremony to begin the DDR process in Manica Province was held on 08 March in Chiuala in Barue, with government and RENAMO officials in attendance. 782 armed RENAMO members are expected to be demobilized in the DDR exercises carried out in this area.

On Sunday, 7 new COVID deaths were reported, along with 378 new cases.  This included 121 new cases in Maputo Province, 98 in Maputo City, 74 in Zambezia, 26 in Cabo Delgado, 24 in Niassa, 20 in Nampula, 13 in Inhambane, 8 in Sofala, 3 in Gaza, 1 in Manica, and 1 in Tete.  There are currently 15,402 active cases in Mozambique, including 9,726 cases in the capital.
Police arrested a suspect for attempting to poison his family in Bairro das Mahotas, north of Maputo city, on 7 March. The suspect had placed insecticides in the potable water.

The World Bank announced that the Mozambique economy is expected to decline by 0.8% in 2021 due to the recession. The country is expected to slightly recover in 2022, with growth of  1.3% expected.  Mozambique experienced its first economic decline in nearly 30 years in 2020 due to the ongoing pandemic.

The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) shut down a large wedding celebration being held in Costa do Sol, Maputo on Sunday, 7 March. Around 200 were attending the wedding.  The organizers of the wedding said that anti-COVID measures were adhered to and the party should not have been shut down.

Local sources stated that food insecurity has worsened in Monapo of Nampula province on 8 March, with many in the area forced to eat grass.  This situation was caused due to a lack of agricultural production.

Sources reported in early February that Portugal and other EU countries are reportedly "reluctant" to provide aid to Mozambique via the Northern Integrated Development Agency (ADIN).  The ADIN was set up last year and was meant to be used to further development in Cabo Delgado and other areas of Northern Mozambique to attempt to counter the insurgency, but has largely been dormant as of March 2021.

The Ministry of Health announced 5 new COVID deaths and 183 cases in Mozambique on 8 March. 51 cases were reported in Maputo city, 68 in Maputo provinces, 5 in Gaza, 3 in Inhambane, 32 in Sofala, 4 in Zambezia, 15 in Nampula, 3 in Niassa, and 2 in Cabo Delgado.

Locals claimed that police aggressively assaulted a trader before arresting him at Mercado Waresta, west Nampula, on the afternoon of 7 March.  The man was allegedly beaten by police, and his right leg was "seriously injured" in the incident. The suspect was detained for violating COVID precautions.  Police after the incident reportedly threatened locals, warning them not to talk about the incident.

Mozambican coal mines reportedly lost a third of their production and more that half of their revenue during 2020. Mining Company Vale stated that only 5.9 million tons of coal were produced during the pandemic in comparison to 8.8 million tons on 2019. The financial revenue fell by 54% from 1 billion USD to 473 million USD.
A train on the Sena line briefly de-railed on 08 March, before railway technicians on 09 March restored the line.  No injuries or major damage were caused in the incident.
column15: Sena Line between Mazamba and Cundue

column4: Matola Provincial Hospital was reopened after being refurbished with additional inpatient and treatment wards for COVID patients on 8 March. The new section will have 50 beds and a channeled oxygen system. This adds extra bed capacity to the greater Maputo City health network, which has been strained since the beginning of a nationwide spike in COVID cases that began in early January.

A group of insurgents on Sunday morning reportedly targeted the village of Chacamba in Nangade District.  Chacamba is located about 13 airline kms northeast of Nangade town.  Insurgents on the same morning also raided Namuembe village, south of Nangade. Many residents of these villages fled to Nangade town, where they reported the attacks.  No details on casualties are currently available from these raids.

Insurgents on Sunday morning reportedly targeted the village of Namuembe in Nangade District.  Namuembe is located about 27 airline kms southeast of Nangade town.  In the village, insurgents set fire to homes and carried out looting, and were believed to have remained present in the area into the early morning hours of 08 March.  This attack occurred the same morning as a raid on Chacamba village, northeast of Nangade town. Many residents of these villages fled to Nangade town, where they reported these attacks.  No details on casualties are currently available from these raids.

Nine RENAMO dissidents joined the disarmament, demobilization and reintegration (DDR) process in Chiuala, Manica on 8 March, sources reported.  They joined over 700 RENAMO armed members in the area who joined the DDR process on Monday.

The Agency for the Integrated Development of the North (ADIN) could begin operating in June, media sources reported.  The ADIN is meant to function as a vehicle to facilitate development in Cabo Delgado and other areas of Northern Mozambique, but despite receiving millions of dollars of funding from international partners

35 people were reported to have died in recent days in the Muecate area of Nampula province on 9 March. An investigation was conducted to determine the cause of death of the civilians.  25 of the fatalities were from the same family. Food insecurity in the area has been reported, and these deaths may be due to locals consuming wild fruits and grass.

The Association of Commerce, Industry and Services (ACIS) called on 8 March for the government to change the Maputo curfew as it was “impracticable” for the business sector. ACIS director Chichongue proposed that the curfew should start at 23:30 instead of the current time of 21:00. Chichongue stated that the in the past month, businesspeople and their employees have been constrained by the current schedule of the curfew.  The union has not threatened demonstrations or strikes at this time over this measure.

Security forces seized 95kg of narcotics hidden inside a Toyota Hiace minivan in Murrupula of Nampula province on or before 07 March. 50 packs of crystal meth and 39 packs of heroin were hidden inside coffee and sweets containers packages were seized. Security forces managed to detained one of the suspects who was a local while the other suspect managed to escape.

Security forces managed to detained one of the suspects who was a local while the other suspect managed to escape.

The African Development Bank announced that the organization had purchased 26 modular steel bridges to replace destroyed bridges in several provinces of Mozambique. The modular bridges will be temporarily put in place in affected areas of Manica, Sofala, Nampula, and Cabo Delgado. Around 500,000 individuals are expected to use the bridges. The bridges are funded under the Post Cyclone Idai and Kenneth Emergency Recovery and Resilience Program.
