column4: Andre Matsangaissa Jr, a former top leader of the RENAMO Military Junta, called for truce in Central Mozambique on 9 March. Matsangaissa Jr called for an amnesty for the RENAMO dissidents and stated the amnesty would also protect the local civilians. He also demanded the withdrawal of the security forces from the provinces of Manica and Sofala which are currently targeting the dissidents and claims that the dissidents want to have a dialogue to also participate in the DDR.

Armed Forces of Defense of Mozambique General Staff Chief Bertolino Capetine in an 08 March statement said that civilians will soon be able to return to their home areas in Mocimboa da Praia District, also saying the media would be invited to "witness this great act".  Capetine said that Mocimboa da Praia is not under the control of insurgents, though said some infrastructure in the town was destroyed by the militants last year.  This statement was made despite substantial evidence that insurgents do in fact still hold MDP.

The Institute of Socio-Economic Studies in an 09 March reported stated that the insurgency in Cabo Delgado could expand towards Nampula and Niassa. The report said that religious cells that eventually turned into insurgent cells in Cabo Delgado have also been present in recent years in these two provinces.  Similar socio-economic conditions in these areas has also made the threat of the expansion of the insurgency into these areas possible.

The Ministry of Health announced that 2 civilians died of COVID and 179 new cases were reported. The cases were recorded as follows: 38 in Maputo city, 9 in Maputo province, 17 in Inhambane, 3 in Sofala, 3 in Manica, 67 in Zambezia, 12 in Nampula, 22 in Niassa, 2 in Tete, and 6 in Cabo Delgado.

The Minister of Health Armindo Tiago said that more than 15,800 health professionals have been vaccinated against COVID as of 10 March.  65,000 health care workers nationwide area slated to be vaccinated during the first phase of the vaccination plan.

Insurgents attacked 3 de Fevereiro village, 9km east of Nangade on 4 March. The insurgents burned down several residences in the village. Most civilians fled to Nangade town before the incident. The insurgents then withdrew to Samora Machel after the attack.

Insurgents sent threatening messages to civilians in Palma town, saying they would attack Palma on 5 March. Security forces were deployed to the area in response to these threats.  No such attack materialized.

Insurgents sent threatening messages to civilians in Palma town, saying they would attack Palma on 5 March. Security forces were deployed to the area in response to these threats.  No such attack materialized.
Border police on the night of 02 March evacuated from the village of Namoto near the border with Tanzania ahead of an insurgent attack later that evening.

Insurgents in an 06/07 March raid targeting Chacamba village in Nangade were reported to have abducted 5 people, including a mother, her two sons, and two civilians who were detained by the group allegedly for having consumed homemade alcoholic beverages.

In an insurgent raid targeting civilians near Nkonga, 3 people were reportedly killed and 3 others abducted on 06 March.  This incident reportedly took place shortly after a military operation targeting militants in the Nkonga area.

In an insurgent raid targeting civilians near Nkonga, 3 people were reportedly killed and 3 others abducted on 06 March.  This incident reportedly took place shortly after a military operation targeting militants in the Nkonga area.

Insurgents on 07 March attacked the Nonje area, west of Mandimba along the road to Palma.  A group of 60 border guards reportedly fled the area during the attack; several of these officers received unspecified minor injuries they were treated for in Nangade.  20 of these guards later arrived in Nangade, though the other 40 guards were reportedly missing after the attack.

Government helicopters on 07 March were reportedly active over Nkonga and along the Palma-Nangade road after insurgent attacks in these area.  No further details on these military operations are currently available.

Macomia District administrator Tomas Badae said on 10 March that virtually all public infrastructure, including his own residence in Macomia were destroyed in an insurgent attack in May of 2020, and that only health services in the town are currently operational; health services in the town are provided by military forces deployed in the area.  A medical charity also recently re-started operations in the area.  Badae also said that only about 2,300 people have returned to the town, out of 16,425 inhabitants before the late May 2020 insurgent attack.

The Ministry of Health announced 7 new COVID deaths and 292 new cases in Mozambique on 10 March. 134 of the new cases were recorded in Maputo city, 46 in Nampula, 28 in Zambezia, 26 in Niassa, 23 in Maputo province, 13 in Sofala, 13 in Inhambane, 5 in Cabo Delgado, 2 in Manica, 1 in Tete, and 1 in Gaza.

The Ministry of Health stated that COVID cases are decreasing in Mozambique in recent days.  Just 2 new deaths were reported on 09 March, the lowest death toll in the country since early January.  The positivity rate of recent test batches has dropped down to between 13.5% to 14.6%, after positivity rates of daily test totals were well above 20 to 30% during the major case spike in January and February.

The National Statistics Institute (INE) stated that the February inflation rate was 1.34%, and that the inflation rate over the year so far has been 2.54%.  From 01 March 2020 to 28 February 2021, the country saw an inflation rate of 5.1%. This current annual inflation rate is the highest since 2017. Maputo, Nampula, and Beira have seen the highest rates of inflation so far this year.

Mozambique Airlines (LAM) signed a new deal with Total to provide flights along the Maputo-Pemba-Afungi route.  The company will dedicate a Bombardier Q400 aircraft to provide these flights for three years as part of this contract.

Mozambican Prime Minister Rosario acknowledged on 10 March that the country's GDP had decreased by -1.3% in 2020 compared to growth of 2.2% in 2019.  This decline was due to the ongoing pandemic.  Predictions this week have indicated that the Mozambican economy is likely to shrink again this year before likely seeing modest growth in 2022.

Kenmare Resources reported an increase in COVID cases among the company’s employees during the first quarter in Moma of Nampula province at a project in the Moma area.  177 company employees have so far tested positive in Nampula for the virus, and are in isolation, though the company also said the majority of these cases were asymptomatic.  The company in December had reported just 25 cases among its work force.

UNOCHA stated that 55 deaths and around 5,000 cholera cases were reported in Northern Mozambique as of 24 February.  Metuge saw a majority of these cases, where most of IDP camps are located. Doctors without borders stated that only 10% of IDPs are living in the camps, often in inhumane conditions; even this 10% has overwhelmed available facilities with diseases common in these camps.

Prime Minister of Mozambique Rosario stated on 10 March that stability is “gradually” returning to Cabo Delgado, though also said that terrorism continues to impact parts of the province.  He also said the government will continue to "strengthen the operational capacity" of the military in the province.

The Former Combatants of the Liberation Struggle Association (ACLLIN) issued a statement on 10 March rejecting Amnesty International report accusing the security forces of human rights violations in Cabo Delgado. ACLLIN stated that the report by Amnesty International is “an empty document” and that security forces are focused on engaging insurgents who have been committing the inhumane acts in Cabo Delgado. This rejection of the report was significant, as the ACLLIN represents an important constituency within FRELIMO.

The Water Supply Investment and Assets Fund (FIPAG) reported on 8 March that the Monapo River dam has reached 100% maximum capacity.  Despite the increased capacity, officials that manage the reservoir say water shortage issues in Nampula city will continue as demand continues to outstrip increases in supply.

A civilian who claimed to have survived from the attack in Bilibiza in 2020 stated that several of the insurgents were from Tanzania and spoke Swahili. The civilian also stated that among the insurgents were a number of Arabs and “white people”, indicating a foreign national presence in the ranks of the terror group.
Local sources reported that an insurgent presence has been recently reported in the coastal areas of Mucojo and Pangane on 10 March.
Local sources reported that an insurgent presence has been recently reported in the coastal areas of Mucojo and Pangane on 10 March.

Palma Economic Activities District Director Antonio Khanlawia stated on 10 March that 40 tonnes of supplies arrived via ship this weekend in Palma on 07 March.  Khanlawia stated that another 160 more tons of goods on two ships to arrive to Palma later week. Local sources stated that Total has allowed three trucks on board supply ships to transport a total of 105 tons of food to be shipped to Palma. Total has reportedly also imposed price controls on the food being transported to the area, to prevent significant price increases when the goods reach the market in the town.  This resumption of regular supply shipments to the town, if continued, will likely alleviate the food and other supply shortages seen in Palma since mid-January, after insurgent attacks along the Nangade-Palma road effectively stopped supply convoys from reaching the town by road.

The Dyck Advisory Group (DAG) issued a letter on 10 March in response to the human rights violations stated by Amnesty International (AI) regarding the issues in Cabo Delgado. The letter stated that DAG supports the ten principles of the UN on human rights, labor, environment, and anti-corruption.  The company also said it would investigate the abuses reported in the recent AI report, and would report within one year on the company's progress in implementing the UN's 10 principles on human rights.

The United States' Treasury Department on 10 March designated Cabo Delgado's insurgent group, sometimes identified as Ahlu Sunnah Wa Jama (ASWJ), as a foreign terrorist organization over its reported association with the Islamic State (IS), also sanctioning Abu Yasir Hassan, who the US identified as the group's leader, as a "specially designated global terrorist".  The US government also said the links between IS and the Cabo Delgado militants were "incontrovertible".  These sanctions will freeze all assets the group has in any US jurisdictions and bars any Americans from doing business with group members.  In this designation, the US identified the Cabo Delgado insurgency as "ISIS-Mozambique", saying that though IS groups its Mozambique and DRC franchises together in its "Central Africa Province" or ISCAP, the Mozambique and DRC groups were distinct from one another.   The Treasury Department also sanctioned the DRC based Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), which has been linked to IS as a foreign terrorist organization, calling it "ISIS-DRC", and sanctioning ADF leader Seka Musa Baluku. No insurgent attacks so far in 2021 in Cabo Delgado have been claimed by ISCAP.
column15: Insurgent Impacted Areas of Cabo Delgado

column4: Traffic was able to resume on 07 March between Mueda and Nangade after this road link was recently disrupted by insurgent attacks along the road.  Militants had also placed road barriers in the Litingina area, which were cleared by security forces.

The Mozambique Supreme Court on 11 March ordered the release of 11 of 18 people detained in relation to the "Hidden Debts Case".  Among the released were Zulficar Ahmad, Fabiao Mabunda, Manuel Matusse, Maria Moiane, Sergio Namburete, Khessaujee Pulchand, Mbanda Henning, Simione Mahumane, Crimildo Manjate, Naimo Quimbine, and Sidonio Sitoe.  Ndambi Guebuza (son of former president Armando Guebuza), Bruno Langa, Angela Leao, Gregorio Leao, Cipriano Mutota, Teofilo Nhangumele, and Antonio do Rosario remain in custody.  20 people were arrested in relation to the case in February 2019.

The general secretaries of FRELIMO and RENAMO met in Maputo on 11 March for talks and announced their commitment to "peace, national reconciliation, and the preservation of democracy".  At these talks, RENAMO called on FRELIMO to stop "persecuting" its members.  The two parties also agreed to hold future talks.

The Ministry of Health announced that 4 new COVID deaths and 471 cases were reported in Mozambique on 11 March. The new cases are as follows: 238 in Maputo city, 73 in Maputo province, 59 in Zambezia, 36 in Nampula, 25 in Sofala, 14 in Niassa, 13 in Inhambane, 9 in Gaza, and 2 in Cabo Delgado.

President Filipe Nyusi announced the dismissal of Army Commander Ezequiel Isac Muiianga, Airforce Commander Messias Andre Niposso, Marechal Samora Machel Military Academy Commander Chume, Deputy-Commander Samora Machel Military Nampele, and Deputy-Commander of the Lt. Gen. of Armando Emílio Guebuza Higher Institute of Defence Studies Mataruca.
Police arrested three suspects for murdering a civilian in Nampula city on 8 March. The suspects disposed of the body after the incident.
Police arrested three suspects for stealing a vehicle in Chowke on 9 March. The suspects stole the vehicle from Chihango, north Maputo City.

The US government Interim Coordinator for Counterterrorism John Godfrey criticized with the presence of a private military contractors (PMC) in Cabo Delgado. Godfrey said that the PMC complicates the ongoing conflict rather than address the issue of terrorism, saying the US is concerned over the presence of PMCs in the province.
Heavy rainfall and flooding were reported on 11 March in Metuge district of Cabo Delgado. These rains impacted the tens of thousands of IDPs in the district, including at the large 25 of June site.

Total is reported to have told "key staff" to be ready to return to the Afungi LNG Camp in the near future.  Total evacuated hundreds of people from the site in January after insurgent attacks close to the LNG Camp in late December/early January.
Police arrested a suspect for sexually assaulting a 7-year-old girl in Macate district on 11 March.

Local media reported that around 42,000 families are experiencing a food crisis in Maputo province after crops were destroyed by heavy floods in the first months of 2021. Most of the impacted families are in Magude, Manhiça, Marracuene, Matutuine, and Boane districts. Government agencies are working with communities to supply them with replacement seeds to replant in these areas.

IDPs in Corrane, Nampula have complained that the relief food being delivered is not enough to meet the needs of around 600 families (about 3,000 people) in Corrane. The President of the Nampula Provincial Assembly, Amisse Mahando, stated the local government recognizes the IDP's poor conditions and will seek to provide more support to IDPs in the area.

Minister of Defense Jaime Neto in an 11 March statement said the Maputo government is willing to collaborate with any organization on the promotion of human rights in Cabo Delgado. Neto said the government wants to work with civil society organizations to prevent youths from joining the insurgency, and that NGOs will be able to contribute to the development effort in Cabo Delgado through the Integrated Northern Development Agency.

The Minister of Health Armindo Tiago announced that Mozambique is set to receive 1.7 million more doses of COVID vaccines by May. This will allow the country to continue to vaccinate priority groups in the coming months.

President Nyusi on 12 March appointed Maj. Gen. Cristovao Chume as the Commander of the Army, a day after removing Ezequiel Isac Muianga from the position.  Brig. Gen. Candido Jose Tirano has appointed the Commander of the Air Force.  Nyusi has not yet filled the chief of the general staff of the FADM, after General Eugenio Mussa died in February just weeks after being appointed to this position.

Local media released a video filmed on 11 March filmed by a man riding a bicycle through the streets of Mocimboa da Praia.  In the video, widespread destruction can be seen across the town, with destroyed, burned buildings seen throughout the video.  The town also appears deserted with no other people seen in the video besides the man filming.  Insurgents captured the town in an assault in August of 2020, and have remained in possession of the town ever since.  Reports in recent months have indicated that the town is largely deserted, though militants reportedly move in and out of the area and that a small number of militants do live in the town.

PM Agostinho do Rosario said on 10 March that 1,490 RENAMO members had so far been demobilized during the DDR process, accounting for 29% of all 5,221 armed RENAMO members.  This number excludes over 700 RENAMO members currently being demobilized in Manica, which will bring this number over 33%. do Rosario also called on RENAMO dissident members to also join the DDR process.

In an interview on 12 March, RENAMO Military Junta leader Mariano Nhongo said that he and fighters in his group would not join the DDR process until the government agrees to new talks with the dissidents.  Nhongo also said his group had submitted a document with the dissidents' demands in October of 2020, and was waiting for the government's response to this document.  The dissident leader went on to deny that his group was involved in a recent attack on a train in Sofala, and also said attacks would come to an end if negotiations with the government go ahead.  He also dismissed calls for RENAMO Military Junta members to join the DDR process by former RENAMO dissident commander Andre Matsangaissa Jr, saying Matsangaissa Jr was being used by the government as "bait" to lure dissidents out into the open.

Pro-government local militiamen exchanged gunfire with insurgents during a search operation in Nangade District on Wednesday, 10 March. Eight insurgents were killed during the clash, though the exact site of this gun battle was not immediately clear. The insurgents had recent been involved in murder of an abducted man, and later released a woman who warned that the insurgents planned to attack Ntamba and Liche in the district.  Militiamen from Ntamba, Liche, Ngalonga and Nambeda villages and from Nangade town deployed in response to these threats, pursued the militants, and eventually engaged them in clashes.  Five firearms and several machetes were recovered in the aftermath of the incident.

Insurgents during the week of 07 March abducted a couple in an unspecified area of Nangade, killing the man and releasing the woman, who was told to warn local civilians that the insurgents intended to attack the villages of Ntamba and Liche in the near term future.

Insurgents on or before 10 March told a woman they had abducted and then released that they intended to attack the villages of Ntamba and Liche in Nangade District.  This led to a mobilization of local militias who attacked insurgents on 10 March, killing 8 of the militants.  Insurgents may seek to target these villages in the future.

Insurgents on or before 10 March told a woman they had abducted and then released that they intended to attack the villages of Ntamba and Liche in Nangade District.  This led to a mobilization of local militias who attacked insurgents on 10 March, killing 8 of the militants.  Insurgents may seek to target these villages in the future.

A suspected insurgent attack was reported in the early morning hours of 11 March in Pangane in Macomia District.  Insurgents reportedly set buildings on fire in the town.  No further details are currently available.

8 new COVID deaths and 359 new cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 12 March. The new cases were recorded as follows: 95 in Maputo city, 59 in Nampula, 53 in Maputo province, 47 in Zambezia, 43 in Sofala, 25 in Tete, 15 in Cabo Delgado, 12 in Niassa, 9 in Inhambane, and 1 in Manica.
A minivan collided with a cyclist along National Road EN10  of Quelimane to Nicuadala at around 05:00 on the morning. A civilian was killed and 9 were injured as a result of the accident.

President Nyusi on the evening of 12 March announced the promotion of Joaquim Rivas Mangrasse to the position of Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Defense of Mozambique.  Mangrasse was also promoted to admiral by Nyusi.  He previously served as the "Chief of the Military House", and previously as the Deputy Commander of the Navy.  His appointment comes a day after Nyusi removed the country's Army and Airforce commanders.

An Appeals Court in the UK ruled on 12 March that the Hidden Debts case will not be judged by an English court. The case will instead go forward to trial in an arbitration forum in Switzerland, as requested by Prvinvest, a Lebanese firm involved in the case.

A trial of Dondo Mayor Manuel Chaparica and Dondo District Frelimo Party first secretary, Felisberto Cheiro began on 10 March.  The mayor is charged with corruption, and is accused of making and receiving illegal payments as part of a kickback scheme in which he hired an "adviser" who funneled money back to the mayor.  The scheme took place in 2019.

The Municipal Police of Maputo announced that demolitions will continue to clear out illegal residences and infrastructure in the mangrove area of Mapulene in Maputo city on 12 March. Mayor Eneas Comiche previously stated that the mangroves are a part of a special reserve containment.

The Hospital General De Mavalane announced that it had increased its COVID Inpatient Centre inpatient capacity by 250 beds in Maputo on 12 March. The beds were a donation from three companies operating in the country.

The Mozambique Supreme Court added the charge of influence peddling to charges against Ndambi Guebuza, son of former President Armando Guebuza as part of the "Hidden Debts" case. The supreme court stated that the previous charge of passive corruption for an unlawful act was dropped against eight of the case's defendants.

The US State Department's spokesman Ned Price on 12 March on 11 March said that the US was calling on the Mozambican government to investigate recent allegations of abuses of human rights.  This comes after  the recent Amnesty International Report which indicated that Mozambican security forces and private military contractors had committed abuses in Cabo Delgado.

Locals media indicated that African foreign nationals in Nampula have recently complained regarding police abuses in Nampula. Local authorities denied the allegations and stated that recently detained individuals were illegal immigrants. African Foreigners Union of Nampula President Marcelo Amusre stated that six foreign nationals have been detained for six months and 10 others were held under questionable charges.
Vendors have left their stalls at the market in Nampula due to unaddressed poor conditions. Vendors stated that sanitary conditions in the market were unacceptable.
A boat transporting five civilians sank along the Zambezi River near Chemba District. Three children were reported missing by local authorities. Two civilians who were with the children were rescued.

US Acting Coordinator for Counterterrorism and Acting Special Envoy for the Global Coalition to Defeat ISIS John Godfrey on 11 March said that the US would provide support to the Mozambican government in countering terror finance in the country.  He also said the US was considering counter-narcotics assistance and assistance to help the Mozambican government to better secure its borders.  He also said the US was considering other forms of assistance to Mozambique including helping to build capacity to "interdict terrorist attacks and do crisis response in an effective way".

The Macomia District Government on 11 March issued a statement calling for all government employees to return to several towns of the district, saying these areas had been secured from the insurgency. The villages and towns covered in this directive area Macomia town, Licangano, Muagamula, Machova, Bangala 1 and 2, Ntapuala, Koko, Nacate, Paz, Nova Vida, Nova Zambezia, Nguida, Liukwe, Nkoe e 5 Congresso. The directive calls for district employees to return to these areas within two days, and said that school in these areas will restart on 19 March.

Three new COVID deaths and 292 new cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 13 March. These new cases brought the country's number of infections to 64,296 while the national death toll now at 722. A total of 49,814 have been declared recovered.

Recent Analysis by the Institute for Social and Economic Studies (IESE) has indicated that Nampula and Niassa are "recruiting camps" for the insurgents in Cabo Delgado.  The group according to the research has extensive recruitment networks that operate in both provinces, tapping into "radical religious cells" in some districts.  HIgh wages for figters and the potential to send money back to their families are used as some of the insurgents' most potent tools to recruit new members. The districts in Nampula were Angoche, Mossuril, Nacala-a-Porto, Nacala-a-Velha, and Memba. The districts in Niassa are Lago, Sanga, and Mecula.

The group according to the research has extensive recruitment networks that operate in both provinces, tapping into "radical religious cells" in some districts.  HIgh wages for figters and the potential to send money back to their families are used as some of the insurgents' most potent tools to recruit new members. The districts in Nampula were Angoche, Mossuril, Nacala-a-Porto, Nacala-a-Velha, and Memba. The districts in Niassa are Lago, Sanga, and Mecula.

RENAMO on 11 March strongly criticized the ongoing curfew in Maputo City, saying it violates the country's Constitution. The curfew was initially imposed on February and extended for another 30 days this month to curb surge of COVID-19 pandemic. Prime Minister, Carlos Agostinho do Rosario, dismissed the accusations.

The COVID-19 vaccination of Health Professionals in Beira city is scheduled to end on 15 March. The program was supposed to end on 12 March, but was extended to cover some members of the Defence and Security Forces who have yet been immunized. Out of all who were vaccinated in the city, only two experienced mild side effects such as pain, weakness and dizziness.

Floods brought by adverse weather conditions in the low lands of Mozambique affected production of essential food items, including tomatoes. At the Zimpeto Wholesale Market in Maputo City, a box of tomatoes is currently sold for 1300 meticais versus its price for the last few weeks at 800 meticais, meanwhile, bag of pepper has increased from 200 to 400 meticais.
column15: Zimpeto Wholesale Market in Maputo City

column4: Three new COVID deaths and 220 new cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 14 March. These new cases brought the country's number of infections to 64,516 while the national death toll now at 725. A total of 50,380 have been declared recovered.

A total of  1,075 companies in Mozambique declared bankruptcy in 2020, mostly due to being severely affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, deputy president of the Confederation of Economic Activities of Mozambique (CTA), Maria Assuncao Abdula, disclosed on 11 Mar.

Sources reported on 15 Mar that RENAMO precented to the National Government a list of names of 300 guerillas to be integrated into the Mozambican Police force.  36 of those in the list will be assigned to the Unit for the Protection of High Individuals (UPAI). The list was forwarded last week.  The 300 have been covered by the DDR process.

The US Embassy in 15 March announcement said that the US and Mozambican governments on Monday launched a "two month Joint Combined Exchange Training (JCET) training program".  In this program, US Special Forces will provide Mozambican marines with counter-insurgency training, to better equip the marines in the fight against the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  An opening ceremony attended by US and Mozambican military officials was held on Monday as well.  The US as part of this program will provide "medical and communications equipment".

Tanzania's Inspector General of Police Simon Sirro on 12 March said that Tanzanian police were investigating a Tanzanian national, Abu Yasir Hassan, who was recently identified by the US as the leader of the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  Sirro also said it was difficult to "immediately establish" the identity of Hassan, saying someone by that name with a criminal record in Tanzania is listed as deceased.  The US Treasury Department recently said that Hassan is between 38 and 40, and is from the Pwani area of Tanzania.  Hassan is also allegedly known as "Abu Qim", and according to at least one source led the coordinated assault on Mocimboa da Praia in August 2020 which led to the port being captured by militants.

Local media reported on 13 March that a large operation is being prepared in Cabo Delgado in the near future against the insurgency, and will focus on targeting militants in Palma, Mocimboa da Praia, and Nangade.  This report is currently unconfirmed.
column15: Palma, Mocimboa da Praia, and Nangade

column4: Instances of nighttime thefts of crops are increasing in Palma District due to food shortages in the region after land supply routes to the district were cut off in January and February. This has led to some farmers spending the nights in their fields to protect their crops.

As many as 4,000 IDPs, likely displaced from Southern Palma by insurgent attacks, are reported to be present in the village of Maganja, near the Afungi LNG Camp.  Only 3,000 people originally lived in this area, with the population in recent months growing to 7,000.
UN Secretary-General Guterres called for $254 million in donations to assist Mozambique to meet the challenges of "Violence, climate crises, and the COVID-19 pandemic".

President Filipe Nyusi on 15 March promoted to the rank of Brigadier to Carlos Rafael Mandongue, Rui Jorge Mandofa, Tome Jose Tome and Chongo Vidigal.  The President also promoted Zefanias Natal Alberto Mambirisse and Sidonia Eda Zacarias Fiosse Massangaie to the rank of Commodore, in separate presidential orders. Fernando Francisco Tsucana was also promoted to the First Deputy Commissioner of the Police.
The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) closed down a hidden nightclub in Maputo on the night of 15 March.  The nightclub had been operating clandestinely for the last year.

Seven health workers reportedly had mild adverse reactions to the COVID vaccine in Maputo province on 15 March. Provincial Health Services Representative Tchamo stated that the small group of health workers experienced mild headaches and discomfort. Tchamo said that out of the 4,440 health workers in Maputo, 3,873 are vaccinated and the remainder will be vaccinated in the coming days.

Local sources stated that several health workers refused to be vaccinated in Nampula on the morning of 15 March. Only 79 percent of the health workers reportedly took the vaccine in the province. Officials stated that the vaccination was voluntary and called on those vaccinated to encourage those not vaccinated to get the shot.

30 armed RENAMO dissidents based in the provinces of Sofala and Manica joined the Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration (DDR) process on 15 March.  RENAMO Secretary general Andre Majibire said the dissidents had been based out of various camps in Sofala and Manica.
A residence collapsed due to intense rainfall in Milange district of Zambezi province on 14 March.  4 civilians were killed.
A group of drunk men beaten a civilian to death during a dispute in Alto Molocue of Zambezia province on 14 March.

The Ministry of Health announced that “everything is in order” for the start of the face-to-face classes to start in Mozambique from 22 March. Deputy National Director of Public Health, Benigna Matsinhe reassured locals that safe conditions have been put in place to resume classes.  Classes had initially been meant to resume on 08 March.

Security forces returned three abducted girls to their families in Macomia and Palma districts on 16 March. The girls were found in the woods in Macomia district on 11 February after having escaped from an insurgent base in the area.

Security forces returned three abducted girls to their families in Macomia and Palma districts on 16 March. The girls were found in the woods in Macomia district on 11 February after having escaped from an insurgent base in the district.

An aid agency working in Cabo Delgado reported on 16 March that insurgents in some cases have beheaded children, including one incident in which a mother told the agency she had watched her 12 year old son be beheaded.

President Nyusi called on military to “eliminate all types of threats to sovereignty” at swearing-in of new FADM chief in Maputo on 16 March. The president stated that the Mozambique government won’t tolerate "the group of Mariano Nhongo".
A suspected terror attack was reported on 15 March near Ntamba in Nangade District.  No further details on this incident are currently available.

Local sources stated that food shortages continued in Palma of Cabo Delgado as of 16 March. Local officials said that prices of goods have increased even with the incoming shipments of goods via maritime routes.  There have been supply shortages and high prices in Palma since mid January, when insurgents cut the last road route to the district via the Pundanhar road.

The UNHCR this week said that as many as 90,000 IDPs continue to live in poor conditions in Sofala Province.  Many of these people were initially displaced by Cyclone Idai in 2019, while some were displaced by Chalane and Eloise more recently.

The Mozambique government on 16 March approved several documents regarding changes to the administration of Area 1 project for natural gas exploration in Rovuma. These adjustments include "aspects of development, ownership, construction, financing, operation and maintenance of the project".  This comes after Total and the government met earlier this year for talks on security arrangements around the LNG Camp.

An NGO working in Cabo Delgado on 16 March warned that the needs of displaced children in Cabo Delgado "far outweigh resources available to support them", also saying children have often been targeted in violence in the province.  This comes after reports earlier this week that children as young as 11 have reportedly been beheaded in insurgent attacks in the province.

Mining Company Syrah Resources stated that they resumed operations as of 16 March at Balama, southwest of Montepuez after suspending operations due to the pandemic. The mining company stated that they would progressively increase plant operations.  The mine employs around 650 people, nearly all of whom are Mozambican nationals.

District Economic Activities Service Director stated  that around 6,000 locals are on the verge of experiencing a severe food crisis in Tambara district of Manica province on 16 March.  This crisis has been caused by heavy rains in farmland areas which have destroyed crops in parts of the district.

Custom officials on 17 March denied previous reports that insurgents had attacked and injured border guards at Nonje village on 07 March. The Delegate of the Tax Authority of Mozambique clarified that the border guards were safe during the time of the insurgent attack in Nonje. The officials also clarified that the Negomano border crossing is the only functioning border post due to the pandemic. The three other border posts in Cabo Delgado were closed, and the agents reportedly were not at the site of the attack when it occurred.

The Ministry of Health announced 3 new COVID deaths and 287 new cases in Mozambique on 16 March. The new cases were reported as 130 cases in  Zambezia, 60 in Maputo city, Maputo province with 19, 7 in Inhambane, 9 in Manica, 2 in Tete, 11 in Nampula, 37 in Niassa ,and 12 in Cabo Delgado.
A driver killed a traffic policeman during a hit-and-run incident in Chongoene, east of Xai-Xai District on 13 March. The suspect was later detained in response to the incident.
A driver killed a traffic policeman during a hit-and-run incident in Chongoene, east of Xai-Xai District on 13 March. The suspect was later detained in response to the incident.

The World Bank announced that around 850,000 people in Mozambique fell into poverty in 2020 as a result of the COVID pandemic which created job and revenue losses.  About 63.7% of the population of Mozambique live below the poverty line.

Officials announced that 15 more Cuban healthcare professionals arrived in Mozambique on Tuesday, 16 March. A total of 39 Cuban healthcare professionals were expected to arrive in the country The medical group included doctors and nurses, who were deployed to augment COVID patient care in the country. 15 other healthcare workers are expected to arrive on 24 March. The Cuban healthcare workers will be dispersed to 15 COVID centers in the country and work on a three-shift basis. The current group joins a previous team of 14 Cuban doctors and nurses who arrived in January.

The State Administration and Civil Service stated on 16 March that 8,000 government workers have been infected with COVID during pandemic, along with 80 deaths, out of a total work force of 340,000. The security forces have been most infected with 1,383 COVID cases. 773 active cases and 610 recovered among the armed forces, with 13 deaths also reported. Currently, 912 police and security administrative employees are quarantined. The government health sector is the second highest with 1,306 COVID cases. 734 active cases were reported along with 6 deaths. Maputo City remained the highest with the COVID cases for civil servants with 3,106 cases.

Licungo Basin Management Division Director Luis Migeia warned on 16 March that water levels have continued to rise in Licungo River and the continued flooding could destroy crops. The water is currently above 6 meters and the districts of Gurue, Namarroi and Lugela are all at risk of experiencing new flooding.

The Public Health Deputy National Director Benigna Matsinhe announced that 46,439 health professionals were vaccinated in Mozambique during the 8-13 March. Matsinhe stated that 61,017 health workers should be vaccinated according to the target and only 76% of the target has been achieved. The first phase of the vaccination campaign targeting healthcare workers has been extended due to the target not being yet reached.

Local sources stated that despite the US designation as terrorist for Abu Yasir Hassan as the insurgent leader in the ongoing conflict in Cabo Delgado, Hassan's background and other details regarding his life remain unclear. Hassan allegedly is a Tanzanian national born in the Pwani Region between 1981-1983.  Hassan was known as one of the top leaders of the group before the start of the insurgency, and reportedly has links to "radical groups in Congo", and had reportedly lived in the DRC as well.  However, Tanzanian police officials this week said that their records showed Hassan was deceased.

An anonymous US State Department official said in recent days that training to be provided by US Special Forces to Mozambican Marines will focus on "basic soldiering skills", and could lead to more assistance to the Mozambican military in the near term future which would include combat casualty care, planning, and logistics.  The US is also reportedly looking into providing enhanced intelligence provision assistance to Mozambique.

Unconfirmed reports stated that the Mozambique government will not renew Dyck Advisory Group (DAG)'s contract at the end of March. This report comes after DAG was accused of committing crimes against civilians in a recent Amnesty International Report.  DAG also was initially contracted by the Ministry of the Interior, while the Ministry of Defense is now leading the counter-insurgency campaign in the province.  The Mozambican air force has also recently trained several pilots to fly helicopters purchased by the government, which would likely take over DAG's role of providing air support to the Mozambican Military.

An NGO released a report stating the IDP tally per district in Pemba City on 16 March. Paquitequete has 9,879 IDPs, Ingonane with 14,411, 6,224 in Natite, 5,645 in Cimento, 20, 538 in Cariaco, 19,672 in Josina Machel, 19,672 in Alto Gingone, 16,620 in Eduardo Mondiane, 4,074 in Maringanha, 7,089 in Chuiba, Mahate with 11,280, 3,301 Muchara, and 6,331 in Metula.  Thousands of IDPs also remain in areas outside of the city, displaced by the ongoing Cabo Delgado insurgency.

Local sources stated that police have deployed every 200 meters along the Save River near Save on 16 March. The deployed policemen reportedly have demanded water from residents driving in the area from residents.

Mozambique Police Commander-in-Chief Bernardino Rafael announced on 16 March that Mozambique Armed Defense Forces (FADM) have created two new Defense and Security Forces Operational Theatres.  These theatres are a new Southern Operational Theatre and a "Special Operational Theatre" which will cover the Afungi area of Cabo Delgado.  Rafael said the special theatre had been set up to guarantee security for the Afungi Area's natural gas resources.  These two new theaters are in addition to the two existing Central and Northern Operational Theaters.

17 RENAMO dissidents have joined the DDR process in Sofala province on 12 March. The dissidents said they had a "bad time" serving in the group which led to their defection.  No further information on this incident is currently available.

30 RENAMO dissidents reportedly joined the demilitarization, disarmament and reintegration (DDR) process in Tete province on 14 March, RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade announced.  Momade also called for RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo to also join the DDR process.  No further details on this defection are currently available.

ENI and the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS) signed an agreement to identify “collaboration opportunities” in Mozambique on 17 March. The agreement will to prioritize Cabo Delgado province and provide prospects in technical education and training, food safety and nutrition, health, access to energy and economic broadening in relation to agriculture to the local population.
RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade called for creation of a new reconciliation commission on 15 March, saying the Mozambican people are "tired of war".

Mozambique National Directorate of Civil Identification (DNIC) expanded their ID card services into four new countries: Zimbabwe, Malawi, Tanzania, and Eswatini.  The country already provides ID card issuing services to its nationals in China, Germany, Ethiopia, Kenya, the US, and South Africa.

A suspected thief died after being electrocuted in Bairro Nauaia of Nacala area on the morning of 16 March. The victim was found with a pair of cutting pliers and several severed cables. Mozambique Electric arrived and cleared the body from the area. The victim reportedly intended to steal electrical cables.

Police Commander-In-Chief Bernardino Rafael on 17 March said that security forces are continuously conducting operations to restore peace and order in Central Mozambique. Specifically, current operations are focusing on targeting RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo.

The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) stated that violations of COVID restrictions continue in Mozambique. This included a recent incident in which an illegal night club was shut down in downtown Maputo.  The INAE recently inspected 799 establishments, many of which were "found to be operating illegally."

The Ministry of Health announced 268 new COVID cases and a single death in Mozambique on 17 March. The cases were recorded as follows: 118 in Maputo city, 56 in Maputo province, 33 in Zambezia, 20 in Nampula, 19 in Cabo Delgado, 9 in Sofala, 7 in Inhambane, 4 in Gaza, and 2 in Tete.

Tanzania President John Magufuli was confirmed on 17 March to have passed away. Tanzanian Vice President Samia Suluhu Hassan stated that former President died of a heart disease, though several sources said Magufuli had died due to complications brought on by COVID-19.

The Mozambican Liberation Front (FRELIMO) postponed the meeting of the party's Central Committee due to COVID restrictions.  The meeting was set for later this month; no date for a new meeting has been set.

Mozambique Airlines (LAM) announced on 17 March that they would temporarily suspend flights between Mozambique and Kenya due to "operational reasons" starting 29 March (Monday) until further notice. The airlines apologized for the inconvenienced caused for passengers, travel agents, and public.

Local sources stated that three civilians were killed and four were injured in recent crocodiles attacks along Zambezi River in Chueza and Malingapansi villages in Marromeu District. The victims were gathering water when they were attacked.

Air France on 18 March announced it would operate two flights per week from Paris-South Africa-Mozambique and back starting 20 June. The flights were set to be scheduled on Mondays and Fridays. The flights from South Africa to Mozambique were set to from morning while flights to Mozambique to South Africa were scheduled for the afternoon.

Insurgents on 21 January kidnapped 2 young girls from Mucojo.  The two were able to escape from the insurgents in mid-February, were discovered by security forces in an undisclosed area of Macomia district, and by mid March were returned to their families.
A cement truck turned over and landed on a smaller vehicle around 0900hrs on 18 March along Avenida Eduardo Mondlane in Machava, west of Maputo city.  A civilian was injured during the accident.

The Minister of Public Works Machatine announced that work road maintenance would be conducted to the regional road between Milange and Mulumbo. Several traders and transportation operations have requested the government to repair the road, which is reported to have been badly impacted by heavy rains during the ongoing rainy season.

column4: Mozambique Electricity (EDM) stated that 11 cases of recent theft have occurred around Maputo city of transformer posts and other electrical infrastructure parts, which has recently led to power cuts in the city. Areas affected included Alto Mae, Coop, Central, and Sommerschield.  Around 4 million MZN worth of equipment have been stolen.

Mozmabique Electricity (EDM) stated that 11 cases of recent theft have occurred around Maputo city of transformer posts and other electrical infrastructure parts, which has recently led to power cuts in the city. Areas affected included Alto Mae, Coop, Central, and Sommerschield.  Around 4 million MZN worth of equipment have been stolen.

Exxon is likely to delay its Rovuma LNG financial investment decision until 2023, media reports said on 18 March.  Exxon had previously delayed a final investment decision in Mozambique which was initially set to be made in 2020. Exxon delayed the decision initially as the company looked to cut capital expenditure across its business amid low oil prices; insecurity in Cabo Delgado may have also factored into this decision.

Around 8 million students from the 1st to 12th grade restarted classes in Mozambique on 15 March. The Minister of Education stated that classrooms will have only a maximum of 25 students to allow a 1.5m distancing per student.  Students will also spend a maximum of 5 hours per day at school.

The Ministry of Health announced that there have been significant decreases in hospitalizations and deaths due to COVID-19 in Mozambique in the month of March so far.  A 55.2 percent decrease was seen during the first 15 days of March as 5,418 cases were recorded in comparison with the first 15 days of February which saw 12,087 new cases. An average of 361.2 infections have been recorded daily in March, against a daily average of 802.4 cases in February.

The National Migration Service (SENAMI) stated 214 Mozambicans were deported from South Africa and one from Eswatini from 06 to 12 March. SENAMI stated that this indicates a 100 percent increase as no records of deportation occurred during the same month of the previous year.

The National Human Rights Commission said on 18 March that 114 people with albinism have disappeared in Mozambique since 2014.  In 55 of these instances, there are pending criminal cases, though many of these disappearances are unexplained.  People with albinism are often targeted and stigmatized in Mozambique, and are sometimes also targeted in ritualistic killings.

Minister of Mineral Resources Tonela stated that works at Afungi LNG Camp will restart in the near future, saying this restart had been discussed with Total and would soon be announced publicly.  Tonela also said Total and the government continue to discuss security and how to resolve "the entire issue" of terrorism in Cabo Delgado.

Interior Minister Amade Miquidade announced on 18 March that Antonio Bachir has been promoted as new deputy commander of special operations zone at Afungi.  President Nyusi on 15 March had announced the promotion of Bachir to the rank of Deputy Commissioner of the Police.  This announcement is notable as it indicates the police continue to be in charge of security operations in this critical area, even while the military are meant to be taking a lead in combating the insurgency.

Security forces fired warning shots to disperse locals after a dispute occurred during a food distribution event in Palma on 17 March in an incident that lasted from about 0900hrs to 1300hrs. Several civilians were reportedly injured during the shooting.  Confusion at the event began when rumors were spread that food distributors were prioritizing their families with food packages rather distributing food to the general public.  Food distribution after the event was reportedly suspended.

RENAMO President Ossufo Momade stated that around 1400 RENAMO armed members were waiting to be demobilized as part of the DDR process in Zambezia province on 18 March. Momade previously arrived at Quelimane Airport to take part for the DDR process in the province. Momade said that those participating in the DDR process should encourage RENAMO dissidents also to join the demobilization.

Cahora Bassa Hydroelectric Plant (HCB) officials warned locals of possible flooding as discharged water was increased from 3,100 to 3,700 cubic meters of water per second from the HCB dam. The officials stated that by April they would increase this flow to 4,100 cubic meters of water per second. The increase in discharged water was to secure the structural integrity of the dam after considering the moderate to heavy rainfall in the Upper Zambezi region. The current increase in discharge water may cause low to moderate flooding in Cahora Bassa, Marara, Tete, Motize, Doa and Mutarara areas of Tete province; Tambara district could be affected in Manica province. In Sofala province, Chemba, Caia and Marromeu districts are expected to be affected by the water discharge, while Luabo, Mopeia and Chinde districts could possibly be affected in Zambezia.

The Mozambican Government on 19 March declared five days of national mourning due to the death of Tanzania's President John Magufuli.  The government said the decision was made due to the "strong ties" between Tanzania and Mozambique.  The days of national mourning will be observed from 20-25 March.

On 19 March, Health Ministry officials announced 347 new COVID cases along with 3 new deaths, brining the nationwide total of cases to 65,799 and 740 deaths.  123 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 55 in Maputo, 44 in Nampula, 32 in Niassa, 26 in Zambezia, 21 in Sofala, 19 in Tete, 14 in Inhambane, 6 in Gaza, 4 in Manica, and 3 in Cabo Delgado.  There are currently 12,644 active cases in the country, and 146 people hospitalized with severe COVID cases.

Two insurgents were found hanged after being lynch by suspected vigilantes in a Lijungo village in Nangade District on 18 March. The insurgents had previously conducted attacks in the villages of the district. Two other insurgents were found in Ngangolo.

Two insurgents were found hanged after being lynch by suspected vigilantes in a Ngangolo village in Nangade District on 18 March. The insurgents had previously conducted attacks in the villages of the district. Two other insurgents were found in Lijungo.

A group of locals in Palma protested at a food distribution event on 15 March in Palma. Locals claimed that food distributors were prioritizing their own families and not fairly distributing food aid in the town, saying but families and relatives of the officials jumped queue and other individuals paid bribes to be prioritized at the food distribution event.

Residents at a food distribution event rioted on 17 March at around 0900hrs in Palma town, saying local food distributors were prioritizing their own families.  Locals claimed that the ticket holders in a food distribution line were being ignored but families and relatives of the officials jumped queue and other individuals paid bribes to be prioritized for the food distribution event.  Security forces fired warning shots to disperse locals after a dispute occurred. Several civilians were reportedly injured during the shooting.  This series of incidents ended at around 1300hrs.  Confusion at the event began when rumors were spread that food distributors were prioritizing their families with food packages rather distributing food to the general public.  Food distribution after the event was reportedly suspended.

The Ministry of Health announced four new COVID deaths and 255 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 18 March. The case breakdown were as follows: 81 of the positive cases were from Maputo city, 13 from Maputo province, 45 cases from Zambezia, 37 from Nampula, 36 from Manica, 23 from Cabo Delgado, nine from Sofala, eight from Inhambane, and three from Tete.

The Mozambique government on 19 March was announced to have set up a Special Unit for Airport Cargo Control to strengthen security measures against smuggling drugs and illegal products through the entry posts.

UNHCR stated that there are now nearly 700,000 IDPs displaced by the Cabo Delgado insurgency, with about 630,000 of those people displaced in the last 1 year.  Only 39% of a UNHCR appeal for support has been funded in Cabo Delgado. UNHCR stated that they still required 11 million USD to provide assistance to the IDPs.

China on 19 March was announced to have forgiven 2% of Mozambique's debt to Beijing, equivalent to 32 million EUR of Mozambique’s debt.  China also said it would provide a further 19 million EUR to support social and economic projects in the country. The Mozambican Minister of Economy and Finance stated that the debt with China of 1.6 billion EUR, which represents around 16% of the country's total public debt.

UN officials stated that the lack of essentials and poor conditions in refugee camps of Cabo Delgado could make local IDPs vulnerable to radicalization.  There are now nearly 700,000 IDPs displaced by the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado, a large majority of whom have been displaced within the province.  Some IDPs have also fled into Niassa and Nampula.

RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade says he excepts more of the RENAMO dissidents to defect and join the DDR process in the near future. Momade stated that other members of the dissident group are expected to follow the example of the group members who have recently joined the process.
Police arrested a drunk suspect for sexually assaulting her niece in Malhazine, central Maputo city,  on 18 March.
Police arrested a drunk suspect for sexually assaulting her niece in Malhazine, central Maputo city,  on 18 March.

Cabo Delgado's Secretary of State said on 19 March that the Mozambican army is “target of defamation”.   Armindo Ngunga stated that several organizations are sharing contradictory and baseless information against the security forces.  This likely refers to a recent Amnesty International report which accused government soldiers of having committed numerous human rights abuses during the counter-insurgency campaign in the province.

National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) officers on 18 March seized 440 kilos of heroin, along with 180 kilos of cannabis and 5.5 kilos of morphine in a raid in the Sampene neighborhood of Quelimane.   An unspecified quantity of cocaine was also reportedly seized.  The drugs were valued at  least 11 million euros.  Authorities say they suspect an extensive drug smuggling network uses Quelimane as a waypoint along a drug smuggling routes.  A large quantity of the drugs were believed to have come from Tanzania.  Police also expressed surprise at the size of the bust.

Security forces arrested four suspects in possession of a large quantity drugs worth more than 30,000 meticais  in Marara, Tete on 20 March. The drugs recovered were Azethromycin, Amoxicillin, Chrlorophyllamine and anti-Malaria drugs owned by National Heath System.  The criminals were reportedly selling the drugs at an informal network in Tete City. This is the third time the suspects have vandalized pharmacies in the province to steal drugs.

Japanese Embassy in Maputo announced on 18 March that Japan has donated five water treatment trucks with an estimated value at  $4.7 million has donated equipment to purify water consumed by people displaced in Cabo Delgado. The Japanese government has earlier donated around $1.9 million to fund the purchases of boats and lifejackets for the coastguard in order to enable to officers to rescue people from coastal areas of Cabo Delgado impacted by the insurgency.

On 19 March, Minister of Defense Jaime Neto challenged the newly appointed Director of the Department of Military Information in the Mozambique Armed Forces General (FADM), Rui Jorge, to enhance the information collection system of the country for better forecasts of the movements of criminals and insurgents.  Neto said "we want us to surprise the enemy and not the other way around".

The floating platform for the natural gas production in the Rovuma basin will arrive in Mozambique in the first quarter of 2022, Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy, Max Tonela, disclosed on 22 March. He stressed that the project is on track for the operation to start in July 2022. The project is expected to produce 3.4 million tons per annum of natural gas from the gas reserves.

The Ministry of Health announced three new COVID deaths and 347 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 19 March. The case breakdown were as follows: 123 of the positive cases were from Maputo city, 55 from Maputo province, 44 cases from Nampula, 32 from Niassa, 26 from Zambezia, 21 from Sofala, 19 from Tete, 14 from Inhambane, six from Gaza, four from Manica, and three from Cabo Delgado. All recoveries reported today, a total of 28, were from Zambezia Province.

Mozambican Police arrested three suspects allegedly part of an international firearms trafficking gang in Chicualacuala in recent days. The weapons were sold to poachers who operate in the Greater Limpopo Transfrontier Park, which includes the areas of Mozambique, Zimbabwe and South Africa. Security forces recovered firearms and more than 1 billion meticais cash inside the house of one of the suspects.  Those arrested included a bank manager, a money changer, and a local businessman. The fourth gang member is still at large.
Two people were killed while seven others were injured in a road accident involving three vehicles along Maputo Ring road in Muhalaze around 1740hrs on 20 March.
An 8-yr-old boy died after he fell into a water reservoir in Matola-Rio, Boane around 1100hrs on 20 March. The victim allegedly fell into the water while passing along the area with other children.

Face to face classes have resumed in all public and private primary and secondary schools in Mozambique today, a year after classes were suspended to contain the spread of the COVID-19 infection. More than 8 million students are expected to attend school on alternate days in a bid to reduce number of students per class and prevent the spread of the virus. Break time will also be reduced and constant handwashing will be enforced.

An 18-yr-old worker died and another person was injured after a gold mine collapsed in Manica district on 15 March. Authorities warned the workers to refrain from going to mines during rainy season and to legalize their activity.

Heavy vehicles will not be able to use the Limpopo bridge, at the entrance of Xai-Xai city from 24 March for a 14 period as repairs on the bridge are carried out. Vehicles weighing more than 3.5 tons will be required to use alternative routes, such as Chissano-Chibuto-Chongoene, for the duration of the works.

Police in the Sampene area of Quelimane arrested a Tanzanian and two Mozambicans on 18 March while also seizing over half a ton of narcotics at a residence in the city.   This is one of the largest recent drug busts in the country. The drugs included 440kg of heroin, 180kg of cannabis, and 5.5 kg of morphine.
President Nyusi on 22 March travelled to Dar es Salaam for the funeral of the late Tanzanian President John Magufuli, who passed away after an illness last week.
Water levels in the Messalo River fell in recent days, allowing easier movement across the River into Mueda, Nangade, and Muidumbe Districts.

Some of the population of Olumbe village has reportedly been able to return to the area amid growing local confidence that military units deployed in the area are able to provide security.  The Olumbe area has been repeatedly attacked by insurgents in recent years.

There are reportedly visible and significant security force deployments in the Olumbe area, local media reported on 20 March.  This has allowed the return of some of the local population to the area, after Olumbe in recent years was targeted multiple times by insurgents.

Mozambique's Minister of Combatants, Carlos Silia, on 19 March called on veterans to continue to support the Mozambican military in its fight against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  He also said former combatants should "promote vigilance" in communities and IDP reception centers to prevent their infiltration by insurgents.  Silia said some veterans were "together with the FDS" in fighting against the insurgents, alluding to pro-government militias operating in Cabo Delgado.

Local sources reported IDPs in Montepuez over the weekend complained food meant to be distributed by local NGOs was being diverted to family and friends of officials in the area, rather than to needy IDPs.  Similar reports in Palma last week led to riots over this perceived aid diversion, and to police forces firing shots to disperse a crowd, resulting in several injuries.  Complaints over this issue have also recently been reported in Pemba.

Sources reported that food aid provided to IDPs in Pemba is in some cases being sold at marked up prices in parts of the city.
A thief was arrested for stealing electrical pylons and transformers in Beira and was later arrested by the police on 20 March.
A thief was arrested for stealing electrical pylons and transformers in Beira and was later arrested by the police on 20 March.
A fire broke out and burned down two grocery stores at Mercado de Fajardo, south Maputo City, on the night of 22 March. No casualties were reported. The fire was due to an electrical short circuit.

The Swedish government announced that it would provide 689,000 EUR to assist IDPs in Cabo Delgado on 22 March. The UNHCR stated that the Swedish government also provided 69 million EUR to assist the UN with in implementation of UNHCR activities in Mozambique.

The Ministry of Health released statistics showing that COVID rates on 21 March fell to a 12.3 percent positivity rate in Mozambique. This is the lowest positivity rate for COVID testing in the country since 05 January.
Police arrested a suspect for killing an infant in Xipamanine, south Maputo City, on 22 March. The suspect reportedly committed the murder in Chamanculo area on 20 March.
Police arrested a suspect for killing an infant in Xipamanine, south Maputo City, on 22 March. The suspect reportedly committed the murder in Chamanculo area on 20 March.

Officials announced the teaching activities were to resume only at three village due to the current insecurity in Muidumbe District in Cabo Delgado on 22 March. The limited resumption of teaching was due to the previous insurgent attacks.

Local sources on 22 March stated that around 7,000 locals are at risk of hunger after crops were destroyed by flooding earlier this year in Tambara District of Manica.  Out of the 37,000 hectares of corn and bean crops affected, 500 were in severe condition. District Services for Economic Activities spokesman Kingston stated that even with the lack of the essential crops, sesame crops would be used to provide cash and allow farmers to obtain money.

The Spanish Agency for International Cooperation initiated a program to combat corruption in Mozambique on 22 March. The program will provide more stringent measures to combat deep-seated corruption in the country. This comes as 2019 data from the Central Office for Combating Corruption stated that corruption during the past 10 years had lead to the loss of 528 million EUR.

The National Economic Activities Inspectorate (INAE) shut down a club not adhering to COVID restrictions during a raid on the night of Saturday, 20 March. A restaurant was also shut down which had 80 customers, a majority of which were not following the imposed precautions by the government against COVID.

Mozambique Airlines (LAM) stated that passenger numbers have dropped by 30 percent from January to February 2021.  The carrier had 29,923 passengers in January, and just 20,936 passengers in February.

Officials announced the need for 7,000 tents to be provided for students to hold classes in Sofala in Beira, Nhamatanda, Buzi, Cheringoma, and Muanza.   The tents are meant to serve in the place of schools in the province damaged/destroyed in recent years by cyclones in the country.
The Deputy Director of Public Health announced that 88% or around 57,000 healthcare workers across Mozambique were vaccinated as part of the first phase of vaccinations in Mozambique.

The Ministry of Health announced 94 new COVID infections and a single death were reported in Mozambique on 22 March. 30 new cases were in Maputo City, 32 in Nampula, 15 in Gaza, 6 in Sofala, 4 in Maputo province, and 1 in Inhambane.  This is the lowest single day total number of cases in the country in 2021.

The Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy Tonela announced on Monday, 22 March that 20 companies were interested in acquiring Vale mining company and logistical operations at Moatize in Tete province. There had been concern that Vale's exit from Mozambique could mean the end of the coal sector in the country and the loss of thousands of jobs.
Police arrested two suspects for stealing 70 cattle and transporting them in Catandica of Manica Province on 23 March. The suspects stole the livestock at Serra Choa area.
Police arrested two suspects for stealing 70 cattle and transporting them in Catandica of Manica Province on 23 March. The suspects stole the livestock at Serra Choa area.

Police arrested a suspect for sexual assault charges in Maputo City on 22 March. The suspect reportedly assaulted two children who were forced to drink alcohol by the suspect. The victims were taken to a shipyard after they were intoxicated.

The Mozambican Tax Authority announced on 22 March that it would launch 150 mobile collection points in Beira on 22 March. These collection points are meant to encourage the payment of taxes and reduce travel costs to tax payers. The Mozambican government stated that it expects the mobile collection points would cover around 240,000 taxpayers. The vehicles comes as 15 initial mobile collection vehicles were deployed to begin the operation.

Several sources on 23 March indicated that Total will restart operations at the Afungi LNG Camp in Palma District in April,  after the recent implementation of new security measures to protect the site.  Several reports in recent weeks had indicated the company was looking to restart operations.  This  comes after Mozambique on 16 March announced the creation of a "Special Operational Theatre" around the Afungi area.

An illegal mine collapsed at the Montepuez Ruby Mining Concession (MRM) in Namanhumbir, Montepuez district around 1600hrs on 18 March 18, 2021. A 25-yr-old illegal miner was killed while two others were rescued alive and taken to the hospital; 1 of the 2 later died of his injures. The collapse was believed to have been caused by the recent weather conditions.

Mozambican Police seized two boxes of suspected to contain Miraa at the Nampula International Airport, authorities disclosed on 23 March. The drug reportedly came from Kenya. Security authorities expressed concerns on the recurring seizure of Mira in the city.

Several sources reported that several dozen schools are unable to reopen in insurgent impacted areas of Cabo Delgado.  This report came as schools across the country that had been shut down due to the COVID-19 pandemic restarted classes this week.  In Muidumbe, only schools in Lutete, Miteda, and Namande villages along the western border of the district are able to reopen.  None of the 27 schools in Mocimboa da Praia are able to reopen, while 6 schools in Macomia and 5 in Quissanga will remain closed.  No details were available regarding schools that would remain closed in other areas of the province, though it is almost certain that a number of schools in Palma and Nangade Districts will also not be able to re-open.

Dyck Advisory Group (DAG), a South African private military contractor (PMC) providing air support to the Mozambican security forces in Cabo Delgado, will officially end its involvement in the conflict on 06 April.  DAG stated that negotiations are ongoing with the Mozambican government. Mozambican crews flying four recently purchased Gazelle helicopters will take over from DAG in providing air support to Mozambican ground forces.  Another Dubai-based PMC will reportedly employ Ukrainian crews to fly two Russian made helicopters used as troop transports in Cabo Delgado.  The Mozambican personnel flying the Gazelles were recently trained by a PMC in South Africa; there is some evidence these crews have already seen action against the insurgents in Cabo Delgado.  This new fleet of helicopters along with armored personnel carriers acquired recently by the Mozambican military will be based in Mueda, rather than in Pemba, where DAG helicopters had flown out of.  Unconfirmed reports that DAG's contract had not been renewed and that the company's operation in Mozambique was coming to an end first surfaced last week.  Other unconfirmed reports meanwhile said that the Dubai-based PMC's contract in Cabo Delgado will begin on 06 April.  This contract is reportedly with the Ministry of Defense, rather than Ministry of the Interior, who had contracted DAG, and this transition is a further sign of the shift of leadership in the counter-insurgency campaign in Cabo Delgado from the police to the military.
