The Ministry of Health announced 148 new COVID infections and three deaths were reported in Mozambique on 21 March. 67 new cases were in Maputo City, 27 in Maputo province, 19 cases from Gaza, 14 from Nampula, 10 from Inhambane, eight from Niassa, two from Tete and one from Cabo Delgado.

According to the United Nations researchers in Somalia, a member of al-Shabaab who defected to the Islamic State in Somalia, Mohamed Ahmed "Qahiye" fled Somalia in 2018 for Ethiopia amid inter-IS conflict in Somalia.  Qahiye in early 2020 the was reported to have travelled from Ethiopia to Mozambique to join the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. Qahiye in 2017 masterminded a major attack on a hotel in Bosaso, Somalia.

On 22 March, officials at the UNHCR warned that the number of internally displaced people (IDPs) in Cabo Delgado is expected to reach 1million by June 2021. The forecast was due to the ongoing insurgency which continues to attack civilian areas across the province.  There are currently around 700,000 IDPs in the province.

An NGO on 23 March disclosed that the Mahate Health Center can no longer treat the increasing numbers of incoming patients. A tent was installed in the center to serve as an intermediary solution. The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) is planning to rehabilitate nine primary health facilities, including Mahate.

On 21 March, the Pakistani Government imposed a complete ban on travel from 12 countries, including  Mozambique, effective from 23 March to 05 April in an effort to prevent the spread of COVID-19 in the country. The decision is part of an effort to stop the spread of the South African and Brazilian COVID strains into Pakistan.

The Ministry of Health announced 190 new COVID infections and three deaths in Mozambique on 23 March. Two deaths occurred in Maputo City and one in Maputo Province. 59 of the new cases were from Nampula, 58 from Maputo city, 18 from Niassa, 14 from Gaza, 13 from Manica, seven from Maputo province, seven from Inhambane, five from Sofala, five from Cabo Delgado, and four from Tete. A total of 306 people have recovered from the virus on the same day while 10 more people were hospitalized.

On 24 March, Total and the Mozambican government announced the progressive resumption of construction activities at the Afungi LNG Camp after the establishment of a 25km security permitter around the site.  The statement issued by the two said that the Mozambican security forces were in charge of security in the zone, while Total was in charge of security in the camp itself, also clarifying the company does not use any armed private security providers.

Mozambique is among one of the 37 critical countries in the world with a water crisis, according to the data released by UNCIEF on 22 March. The organization disclosed that about 1.4 billion people do not have access to water worldwide and that the children are the biggest victims.

A group of insurgents estimated to number at least 150 at around 1500hrs on 24 March attacked Palma town, with militants reportedly launching the assault from the north, north-west, and south-west of the town, and engaging soldiers in these areas.  Militants engaged soldiers on the road to Man'Guna, effectively cutting the road to the Afungi LNG Camp, and gunfire was also reported near the Exito station on the southwestern outskirts of Palma. One group of militants approached via the Nhica do Rovuma Road.  The Insurgent reportedly arrived with trucks intending to steal the food and good supplies arriving via boats.  Militants asked civilians in the town where security forces were during the attack saying "where are the pigs?". Sources later indicated the attack began at Man'Guna, before insurgents also attacked the areas of Quibuite and Quilaua in Palma, with a police station targeted early in the attack.  Militants reportedly utilized heavy weapons in these clashes.  Fighting was also reported near the Amarula Hotel as well as at the Palma airstrip on the northern side of the town; militants also fired at a civilian plane that was then forced to abort a landing into Palma.  Other sources said militants had targeted Standard Bank, BMI bank, and the Afrimax Complex during the attack; conflicting reports said these locations had been set on fire or robbed.  Unconfirmed reports indicated an unspecified number of security forces were killed in the fighting inside Palma.  Many local residents during the attack fled into the woods, while several people close to the beach were able to board boats in the area to escape; unconfirmed reports said some security force elements also fled to the boats.  A number of people were reported to be missing in the aftermath of the attack.  Several sources also reported Vodacom services were down in the Palma and Afungi areas after being cut around 1630hrs; it was unclear if militants or security forces were responsible for this.  By 1820hrs local time, military sources said the insurgent attack had been repulsed, saying insurgents had infiltrated the town and hidden in local residences.  However, at around 1900hrs other sources indicated gunfire continued in the town; gunfire in and around the town was again reported at 2020hrs. By 2200hrs, gunfire in the town had ceased, though it was unclear if insurgents remained in parts of the town. No confirmed information on casualties is currently available.  One unverified report meanwhile said that some of the militant leaders who led attacks in Muidumbe in October-November 2020 were involved in the assault.  A single source also claimed that Islamic State-linked media had claimed responsibility for the attack, though this has also not been verified.  ISCAP on 29 March officially claimed the attack. The insurgents were later reported to have intended to capture public officials to be used as bargaining chips to implement the sharia law in the area.

Two sources said insurgents had attacked the village of Assumane/Mapalanganha area, south of Mute along the R762 road at the same time as the Palma assault on the evening of 24 March; this reportedly triggered an evacuation of local sub-contractor personnel from the area.  Other sources however reported this attack did not occur, while others refered to an incident a day earlier in the Namalala area.

Several sources also reported Vodacom and other cell services were down in the Palma and Afungi areas during an insurgent attack on the area on the evening of 24 March.  The military later aknowledged this outage, but did not say whether or not the military or insurgents had cut comms in the area.

A plane attempting to land in Palma was unable to do so on the evening of 24 March as insurgents targeted the town in an assault.  Several sources indicated the plane was fired on by insurgents in and around Palma with "heavy weapons".
Militants at around 1500hrs 24 March assaulted the village of Man'Guna in Palma District, pushing security forces in the area back into Palma, before attacking Palma itself.

Manica Provincial Governor Francisca Tomas said on 24 March that 426 RENAMO armed members had officially been demobilized in the province in ongoing DDR efforts.  This reportedly included an unspecified number of RENAMO dissident members.  782 armed RENAMO members were reported in early March to be ready to join the DDR process in the province.  The DDR process is ongoing in Sofala and Manica, but has not officially begun in Inhambane, Tete, and Zambezia, where hundreds of other RENAMO armed members will reportedly also join the demobilization process.

Evacuations by air on the night of 24 March from Palma were reported not to be possible after an insurgent attack on the town that began earlier in the day, lasting for around 7 hours.  As of just before 0000hrs on 25 March, it was unclear if the town's airstrip was secure.  Clashes around the airstrip were reported earlier in the day, with insurgents also reportedly firing on a civilian plane that attempted to land in the town during this fighting.

A single credible source indicated in the early morning hours of 25 March that as many as 100 insurgents had participated in the 24 March assault on Palma, and that at least a portion of this insurgent force remained in the Palma vicinity as of 0300hrs local time.  Some insurgents were reported to likely be sheltering in homes in Palma.  Note that similarly, security force sources on 24 March reported that insurgents had infiltrated parts of the town and were hiding in civilian residences

A source indicated that some elements of the security forces, including Police Rapid Intervention Force officers remained in Palma, and had been ordered to hold their positions.  Other reinforcements were reportedly being deployed to the town, and were allegedly expected to arrive at around 0400hrs into the area.  Some of these reinforcements were reported to be taking up positions along the R763 road, so as to cut off an insurgent retreat towards Pundanhar.  Another source later indicated that 100 UIR officers on 25 March were deployed to Palma to reinforce forces already in the town.

Ongoing sporadic gunfire was reported near Amarula Hotel, Palma at about 06:00 morning of Thursday, 25 March. The gunfight in the area was initially reported at about 02:00. Earlier reports claimed that mortar fires were heard, however, it has yet been verified. Casualties were reported, but the exact number is still unknown. The Amarula Hotel was reportedly housing around 100 expatriates and civilians while there were reports of other expats in the town has yet been determined. There were concerns that the hotel, which was housing some local government officials as well as expats would be directly targeted, though this did not come to pass, though the hotel's outer perimeter was hit by a small number of assault rifle rounds. This development came after an unconfirmed report stated that a portion of the insurgents who attacked on 24 March remained in the town while other security reinforcements were reportedly being deployed.

The Ministry of Health announced 153 new COVID infections and two deaths in Mozambique on 24 March.  The new cases were recorded in Maputo city with 76 cases and in the provinces of Nampula -25, Maputo-24, Sofala-12, Tete-seven, Zambezia-six, Inhambane-two, and Cabo Delgado-one. A total of 615 people have recovered from the virus on the same day while 10 more people were hospitalized.

Unidentified gunmen abducted a trader in Paquitequete, Pemba city on the evening of 21 March. Reports suggest that the assailants used pickup similar to military vehicles in the city. The victim was suspected to be part of a terrorist group in the province. His brother was allegedly part of the militant group since 2017.

Security forces seized 356kg of heroin and crystal methamphetamine hidden on the truck bed of a Ford pickup in Nacala Port's Naherenque area in the early hours of 24 March.  The drugs were seized from several boats docked in the area. Suspects managed to escape as they became aware of the police presence in the area. Patrols are currently being carried out by the police in the area to apprehend the suspects.

Cahora Bassa Dam will open the floodgates to ensure structural safety of the dam. The water level in the dam has been rising continuously due to the rainy season. The Cahora Bassa Hydroelectric Power Plant will increase discharges gradually from 3,100 to 4,400 cubic meters and from 3,700 to 5,000 cubic meters of flow per second by the next 30 days. This may cause low to moderate floods in the Zambezi valley in the provinces of Tete, Manica, Sofala and Zambezia.

Reports on 24 March state that Mozambique is gathering support for securing a seat reserved for non-permanent members of the United Nations Security Council. Eight countries, namely Turkey, Portugal, Senegal, Niger, Serbia, Colombia, Czech Republic and the Republic of Jamaica, expressed their support for Mozambique in this goal.

A water shortage was reported in 24 March on the neighborhood of Albazine, Maputo City for more than 15 days. Other residents had to go to other areas of the city to fetch water. The reason behind the shortage of water was not disclosed.

Deputy National Director of Public Health, Beninga Matsinhe, stated that teachers and other staff of the Education Department in Mozambique will be included in the COVID-19 vaccination program to reduce the risk spreading the coronavirus in the schools. However, their inclusion is still subject to the availability of the vaccines.

On 01 April, the price of bread in Mozambique is expected to increase as a result of the rise in operating costs for bread makers. The basic raw ingredients for bread making has increased 24 percent from October 2020 until present. The price of the wheat flour, for example, rose from 1,650 to 2,100 Meticais per 50 kg sack. The exact amount of increase was not disclosed since it will vary per region.

147 out of 952 schools in Manica Province remain closed due to poor conditions. Reports suggest that affected schools have overgrown grass, damaged desks in the classrooms,  lack running water, and broken toilets.

The President of that RENAMO party, Ossufo Momade, claimed that the Demobilization, Disarmament and Reintegration (DDR) process of Renamo fighters has no definite end deadline currently.  He added that it's more important for the repentant guerillas to be fulfilled with the process' objective.  The process, which was restarted in July 2019, was initially meant to finish within 210 days.

A 32-yr-old woman succumbed to her wounds after being severely beaten by her husband with an iron rod in Manga District, Beira City on the early hours of 19 March. The attack came after the suspect has an argument with his wife an another man. The suspect was later arrested as he attempted to flee into Maputo.

On the evening of 22 March, security forces arrested a man at the entrance of Beira City for killing her wife with an iron rod. The suspects claimed that he went back to Beira to surrender to the police after he fled for a day to Maputo.

97 people were killed and 66 were injured in attacks by wild animals in 2020 a report by the National Administration of Conservation Areas (ANAC) reveals. Most of the deaths were attributed to the crocodiles.  71% of these deaths occurred in Tete and Zambezia. Increased risk is heightened during rainy season which may result to agricultural and residential areas to be flooded.

During the first quarter of 2021 in Maputo, four people have died of Malaria. The number of casualty have declined versus last year with nine deaths in the city. The data also shows that there was a decline with the new cases reported over the last two weeks compared to the same period last year, with 550 reported in 2021 and 575 reported in 2020.

Damaged roads were reported between Zimpeto and Komgolete neighborhoods due to heavy rains. Reports suggest that the water from Mabor,  Zimpeto Wholesale Market and other parts, including the Mozambique Avenue towards the and Mulawuze River created the craters on the roads in the area. Motorists are warned to take extra precaution when traveling in the area.

column4: Gunfire was reported in the early hours of 25 March in Palma, ending before 1000hrs.  Fighting at this time was reported in northern parts of the town, including near the Amarula Hotel, though the hotel itself was not directly targeted during the fighting, contrary to other circulating reports.  A small number of assault rifle rounds were however reported to have struck the outer wall of the hotel.

Insurgents were suspected to still be present in parts of Palma town in the late morning/early afternoon, hiding likely in civilian residences, as well as in mangrove areas as well as in forested areas close to the beach.

The Mozambican Government statement released on Thursday that security forces in Palma were "pursuing the enemy to establish security and order quickly". Some clashes during the day of 25 March were reported in Palma, though sources differed as to how many troops were actually deployed to Palma.

Several security force elements on 25 March remained in Palma, holding positions after clashing with insurgents in the town on 24 March.  Other troops have also reported to have been deployed in and around the town, with the military attempting to cut off a potential insurgent withdrawal along the Pundanhar road.

Insurgent activity in Palma was expected to increase at nightfall on 25 March, when insurgents were likely to emerge from their hiding places and would not be vulnerable to fire from military helicopters currently deployed over the town.  Militants may renew their attacks on some targets in the town; note yesterday insurgents' primary targets included two banks and a business complex as well as a police station.  Insurgents may also attempt to withdraw from Palma, particularly as they likely realize they will not be able to hold ground as additional reinforcements reach the town.

Local residents were reported on 25 March to have accused former governor Vriglilo Ferrao of a land grab in the Moatize area of Tete province. The former governor reportedly stole 50 hectares of land from a group of 100 farmers.
1 military transport helicopter were reported to be flying out of Pemba and suspected to be traveling to Palma on the afternoon of 25 March. This report came amid ongoing evacuations out of Palma.

The UN announced 2.9 million people may experience food insecurity in Mozambique over the coming months. The current expected number is 17 percent above the five-year average. UN stated that the economic challenges, brought about by the COVID pandemic and natural disasters as well as impacts from the Cabo Delgado insurgency have worsened the situation.

The Maputo City Education Directorate stated that around 12,709 students have held back registering for the school year in Maputo city for fear of COVID. The Education Directorate stated that 55,942 were currently enrolled out of the 68,644 students in the city.

The Ministry of Defence announced on 25 March officially confirmed the ongoing insurgent attack in Palma. The MOD spokesman Saranga stated that the government was working to “restore security and order” after stating that they were “pursuing the insurgent’s movements”.

The National Health Service announced that the government will proceed to administer the AstraZeneca COVID vaccine. The continued administration of the vaccine was due to its effectiveness based on the international technical organizations. The Minister of Health clarified that the CDC Africa, WHO, and European Medicines Society stated that the vaccine is effective and can be used in any country.

Airlink, a South African airline, intends to add a flight to Maputo starting 01 April.  The flights would be from Johannesburg to Maputo. Airlink CEO announced that the new flights were to promote trade and improve passenger traffic with the new routes.

The Ministry of Health announced a single new COVID death and 113 new cases in Mozambique on 25 March. This brings the total cases to 66,762 cases and 115 hospitalized. The cases were recorded as follows 41 in Maputo, 28 in Maputo province, 11 in Sofala, 5 in Tete, 1 in Zambézia, 11 in Nampula, 9 in and Cabo Delgado.

Police announced that they will conduct "Operation Easter 2021" in which additional security would be placed at Mozambican borders. Officials expect 150,263 visitors to travel to the country during the holiday period. The previous number of visitors was 225,296 in 2020.  The smaller number of expected visitors was due to the ongoing pandemic.

Most communications to Palma remained down throughout the attack on 25 March, though some people in the town were able to communicate via satellite links.  Comms remained down in the town as well on 26 March.
Cell communication networks were reportedly disrupted in Pemba during the initial attack in Palma on 24 March, but was restored later during the morning of 25 March.

UN said on 25 March that it was closely monitoring the deterioration of the humanitarian situation in Cabo Delgado. The announcement comes after insurgents launched an assault on Palma.  The UN also said it was communicating with "all relevant contacts to ensure that workers can leave the area".
Three insurgent youths reportedly surrendered to the security forces stationed in Nangade district on 12 March. The insurgents were taken to a police station following the surrender.

Local sources stated that several South African PMC helicopters deployed over Palma on 25 March. Local sources stated that the helicopters were having difficulty determining the insurgents from the civilians on the ground.  Some sources reported helicopters had engaged militants on 25 March in the town, though this was unconfirmed.
Local sources that large numbers of locals and some foreign nationals had fled into the bush around Palma during the insurgent attack on the afternoon of 24 March.

The Citizen's Observatory for Health (OCS) called the government to release a tally of daily vaccinations given in order to increase transparency.  OCS stated that the Ministry of Health must publish the tally as the National Vaccination Plan does not have concrete and expected dates for the availability of the information.

Police arrested two suspects for forging documents to withdraw money from bank accounts in Maputo city on 25 March. The suspects would search for accounts of deceased individuals and would claim the necessary profile and documents.
Local sources stated that 200 Rapid Intervention Units were based at Zambia village, south of Palma on 24 March prior to the assault on Palma by insurgents earlier in the day.
Joint Task Force military units were reported on 24 March to be deployed just outside of Palma, prior to an assault launched on the town by insurgents later that day.

Local sources stated on 26 March that the Two LNG employed Portuguese nationals were safe during the attack by insurgents in Palma. Around 200 individuals took refuge at the Amarula Hotel during the insurgent attack.
International media sources on 25 March reported bodies in the streets of Palma, saying some people had been beheaded in the ongoing insurgent attack on the town.  This report has not been confirmed.

Several sources on the evening of 26 March reported that insurgents had attacked a 17 vehicle convoy attempting to evacuate locals and expats from the Amarula Hotel.  The convoy was reported to have been travelling north towards Quionga when attacked; sources later confirmed the convoy was attacked initially just outside of the Amarula gates before being attacked again north of Palma.  Only 7 of the 17 vehicles in the convoy made it through these ambushes. 7 people were reportedly killed in these attacks, and other injured; at least some expatriates were believed to have been among the dead. The fate of the 10 vehicles and their occupants in the aftermath of the ambush was unclear.  Pro-Islamic State online chatter on Friday afternoon also reported this incident and said militants had inflicted multiple casualties in an ambush, though ISCAP has not officially claimed the attack.

Several sources on the evening of 26 March reported that insurgents had attacked a 17 vehicle convoy attempting to evacuate locals and expats from the Amarula Hotel.  The convoy was reported to have been travelling north towards Quionga when attacked; sources later confirmed the convoy was attacked initially just outside of the Amarula gates before being attacked again north of Palma.  Only 7 of the 17 vehicles in the convoy made it through these ambushes. Note that this second ambush occurred at least 6.5 kms north of the Amarula, and completely outside of Palma town, indicating a significant insurgent presence on the outskirts of the town as well as within. 7 people were reportedly killed in these attacks, and other injured; at least some expatriates were believed to have been among the dead. The fate of the 10 vehicles and their occupants in the aftermath of the ambush was unclear.  Pro-Islamic State online chatter on Friday afternoon also reported this incident and said militants had inflicted multiple casualties in an ambush, though ISCAP has not officially claimed the attack.

The third day of the Assault on Palma came to an end with as many as 180 people, including a significant number of expats still stranded at the Amarula Hotel in Northern Palma town.  Evacuation operations earlier in the day had reportedly allowed between 20-40 people to leave the area, but evacuation attempts were halted later in the day as gunfire was reported closer to the hotel.  Insurgents previously were reported to intend to attack the hotel due to the presence of a local administrator, though no direct assault on the hotel had been reported. One unverified report on 25 March indicated that one evacuation convoy had been turned back while travelling towards Afungi due to small arms fire; not further details on this incident are currently available.  Sources also confirmed the Amarula Hotel had not been directly attacked over the past day.
GSM services out of Palma remained down on 26 March with those still in the town relying on satellite communications.

Sources also reported intermittent skirmishes/ unexplained gunfire over the night of 25 March and into the morning of 26 March, though this was according to witnesses less intense then gunfire on 24 March.  At around 1340hrs, sources reported clashes between security forces and insurgents had intensified, with fighting reportedly audible from the Amarula hotel.
Insurgents were confirmed to still be present in Palma on 26 March; this came after one high profile report that insurgents had withdrawn from the town.
Unconfirmed reports on 26 March indicated that insurgents attacked the Palma Business Park with small arms fire.  No further information on this incident is currently available.

The National Human Rights Commission on 26 March called publicly for support to rescue 600 civil servants from Palma town, saying the group had fled the attack on Palma and were in an "intermediate zone and waiting for help".
The UN on Thursday saying it was trying to contact several agencies' workers in the Palma area to ensure their safety amid the ongoing attack on Palma by insurgents.
The US released a statement on 26 March condemning the ongoing insurgent attack on Palma, saying the US expressed solidarity with Palma and security forces attempting to end the attack.

Thousands of civilians in Palma were reported to have fled on Wednesday and Thursday towards Afungi and the Quitunda area, seeking shelter as the ongoing insurgent attack on Palma which began on 24 March continued.
Insurgents reportedly damaged a helicopter that was attempting to evacuate civilians from Palma on 25 March.  The aircraft was hit by at least one assault rifle round during this incident.

The South African Department of International Relations and Cooperation (Dirco) stated that several South African nationals were trapped in a hotel during the insurgent attack in Palma. Dirco spokesman Ngqengelele stated that they were working to assist the trapped individuals.
The Ministry of Health announced that 117 new COVID cases and 5 related deaths in Mozambique on 26 March. Among the new cases 16 were reported to be hospitalized.

Insurgents on the evening of 26 March were reported to have seized two vessels just off of Palma, and to have fired on a third vessel.  Several ships near Palma were reported to have moved away from the town in response to this incident.  This came as insurgents continued to move around Palma town and clash with security forces for a third day on Friday, after an initial assault that began on 24 March.

Evacuation operations in the morning of 26 March reportedly allowed 23 people to be evacuated from the Amarula Hotel, but evacuation attempts were halted later in the day as gunfire was reported closer to the hotel.  Insurgents previously were reported to intend to attack the hotel due to the presence of a local administrator, though no direct assault on the hotel has been reported.

Evacuation operations in the morning of 26 March reportedly allowed 23 people to be evacuated from the Amarula Hotel, but evacuation attempts were halted later in the day as gunfire was reported closer to the hotel.  Insurgents previously were reported to intend to attack the hotel due to the presence of a local administrator, though no direct assault on the hotel has been reported.    Among those evacuated on 26 March by helicopter were the district administrator and other local officials.

Clashes between UIR units and militants were reported to be ongoing during the day in Palma's outskirts as militants were able to effectively move throughout most of the town.  Insurgents retained this freedom of movement as of the early hours of Saturday.

Reports on 25 March indicated that DAG helicopters had  engaged militants in parts of the town, and allegedly also dropped improvised bombs on the insurgents, preventing a militant advance on the Amarula, though these helicopters on the night of 25 March withdrew from the area, running low on fuel.

Reports stated from civilians who had fled Palma on Wednesday and Thursday, with many saying they saw dead bodies of both adults and children in Palma's streets before fleeing, including several people who had been beheaded.  Other sources reported significant numbers of dead bodies, including of allegedly of expatriates, on the town's beach.  Reliable local media reported "dozens" of civilians killed in the assault along with at least "twenty-one soldiers also killed".  Current casualty estimates when taking into account the 7 reportedly killed in the convoy ambush indicate at least 40 dead in the Palma clashes so far, though this is likely a conservative estimate.

Human Rights Watch (HRW) stated that the insurgents have attacked civilians inside residences and on streets when they attempted to flee Palma between 24-26 March. HRW has called on the government to respond swiftly to protect civilians. This comes as social media and local sources stated that executed and beheaded civilians were seen along the streets of Palma as locals fled the town.

Insurgents had reportedly set fire to around two-third of the buildings in Palma as fighting for the town continued on Friday.  Fires were likely initially set before Friday. Unconfirmed reports said the insurgents used explosives to target three bank branches and a healthcare facility in the town. In addition, Palma’s military barracks and government infrastructures were also reported to have been destroyed by the insurgents.

Total on the evening of 27 March released a statement saying that no victims of the attack were "among the staff employed on the site of the project in Afungi".  The company also said it would reduce its workforce at the Afungi LNG site to a "strict minimum level", and that it was suspending a re-start of operations at the camp that had been set for April.  This is likely an indefinite suspension.  The company also said that it "trusts the Government of Mozambique whose public security forces are currently working to take back control of the area".

In Palma on 27 March, two different sources described ongoing security force operations.  One source said troops were conducting "house by house" searches for insurgents, and clashing with small bands of militants.  A second source said fighting was ongoing in the town, and that the military had pulled back from some neighborhoods, though had "mostly" encircled the town, though "not completely".  This source said security forces intended to surround insurgents, prevent their escape, and ultimately kill or capture those remaining in the town.  Regardless, the sources agreed that fighting was ongoing in Palma and the town appears to be contested, with neither side in control.  Additional government troops, according to a third source, had arrived into the area on Saturday.

Sources previously reported that insurgents in the assault on Palma had used "heavy weapons" in the initial attack on the town; specifically these weapons have been identified as high caliber machine guns, mortars, and RPGs.  Estimates of the number of militants involved in the attack have now increased from 100 to as many as 150.  Reporting from Saturday also indicated that potentially days before the assault began on Wednesday, some groups of insurgents had infiltrated the town and stayed with local supporters.  Other militants later arrived and began the attacks on the peripheries of the town while infiltrators attacked locations in Central Palma.

Media reports indicated that "nobody died in Amarula" referring to the Amarula hotel which was reportedly attacked on Friday night by insurgents.  Details regarding an alleged assault on the hotel are still unconfirmed, and many of those who had been sheltering at the hotel remain unaccounted for.

Sources on 27 March reported that a group of "19 workers and four guests" were rescued from a hotel on the outskirts of Palma "under heavy fire".  Other reports during the day indicated that unknown numbers of people were rescued from area beaches and from the bush outside the town.

Sources on 27 March reported that a group of "19 workers and four guests" were rescued from a hotel on the outskirts of Palma "under heavy fire".  Other reports during the day indicated that unknown numbers of people were rescued from area beaches and from the bush outside the town.

South African media said on Saturday that the South African government was "considering sending special forces" to Palma to evacuate South African nationals still believed to be trapped in the town.  At least one South African national was confirmed to have been killed when an evac convoy from the Amarula Hotel was ambushed by insurgents.  Note that previous unconfirmed information said French Foreign Legion forces were being deployed from Mayotte to help protect the Afungi LNG Camp.  Other unconfirmed sources said the UK and US were also considering sending special forces to help evacuate Palma.

An additional 1,000 people were expected to arrive into Pemba via boats fleeing from Palma on 29 March.  This came after as many as 2,000 people fleeing fighting in Palma arrived in the provincial capital on Sunday.

Sources also confirmed that ships that arrived to Pemba at midday on Sunday were carrying at least 1,400 people fleeing from Palma; other sources indicated by the end of the day at least 2,000 people fleeing from the attack had arrived by boat in Pemba.  Those that arrived on Sunday were initially not allowed to disembark; sources later confirmed the Sunday arrivals will be "released" from this temporary quarantine on Monday.  At least 1,000 more people will likely arrive in the port city over night or on Sunday morning.  One source said that many of the people that arrived into Pemba on ships on Sunday were members of the Friday night Amarula evacuation convoy who made it through an ambush laid by insurgents north of Palma

A civilian was struck in the foot after insurgents attacked an area near a military barracks in Quionga, local sources reported on 28 March. It was unclear if this attack took place on Sunday or before. Both civilians and soldiers fled during this attack. The driver was working with one of the companies supplying materials for the construction of the gas exploration platform in Afungi. Another witness claimed many other people remained in the forests after they escape the city, and many civilians in the area remain missing.

On 26 March, Maputo City Government expelled several informal street traders at Xipamanine Market, Maputo City. Affected traders complain on the lack of new stalls in the market. In addition, a recently built market has yet to be occupied by traders as they reportedly don't have customers in the area.

Police and military forces deployed to Pemba port and initiated a strict policy of no access in or out of the port as ships arrived carrying over 1,300 people fleeing Palma on 28 March. Media were removed from the area and filming prohibited.  Officially this is meant to limit the spread of Covid-19 into Pemba and evacuees were not allowed to leave without have a negative Covid-19 test.  This does not appear to be a Mozambique Government policy, but rather an action by local officials. This has resulted in a high level of frustration among the evacuees resulting in high tensions and creating a risk of unrest.  This risk will only grow as further ships transporting evacuees arrive at the port.

Intermittent clashes were reported to have continued in Palma on 28 March. Some northern parts of the town were allegedly cleared by security forces in house to house searches, though this is yet to be confirmed.  One source reported that troops deployed around the town want to prevent militants from escaping the area.  Other sources later confirmed that security forces on 28 March launched offensive operations into Palma to begin retaking the town.

Several sources reported that a large number of expats and civilians - as many as 60 people, remained missing after an evacuation convoy that north of Palma from the Amarula hotel on Friday night was ambushed by insurgents.  Only 7 of 17 vehicles made it through the ambush; 7 people were killed however in these 7 vehicles.  The fate of the 10 vehicles remain unclear.  New reports that those in the vehicles (up to 60 people) may have been killed surfaced after an audio recording circulated on 28 March in which a man in the area described the convoy's attempted escape and said that it was believed all of the group in the 10 vehicles had likely been killed.  Note that this recording was almost certainly made on 26 March, before conflicting reports said that many who had turned back from the convoy had made it back to the hotel, and later were evacuated.  As of Sunday, reports of dozens of expatriates killed in the convoy ambush are unconfirmed.

On 28 March, incomplete lists of missing people in the aftermath of the Palma attack were circulated; one of these lists seen by Aldebaran indicated hundreds of people remain unaccounted for.  A large majority of those reported missing are Mozambican nationals, though at minimum dozens of foreign nationals remain missing as well.  Efforts by the British, South African, and other government are ongoing to locate their nationals. Note that a large number of those missing are likely to be officially "located" on Monday after the identities of the hundreds of people, including large numbers of expats, who arrived via ship to Pemba on Sunday are verified.

Evacuations from the Palma area also remain ongoing, with more boat rescues reportedly being carried out 28 March morning from area beaches.  Local companies and service providers continue to use a variety of different sized craft to carry out these rescues.  Dyck Advisory Group owner Lionel Dyck said Sunday that DAG helicopters had rescued 120 people in operations on Saturday and Sunday with a number dead bodies also evacuated from the area to Afungi.  DAG helicopters also escorted a number of people to safety, according to Dyck.

Sources on 28 March also indicated as many as 6,000 to 10,000 people were waiting to be evacuated from the Palma area.  Large numbers of these people who had fled Palma were sheltering just outside of the Afungi LNG Camp, but had not been allowed to enter the camp itself; it was unclear how many people were sheltering in this area or if those refused entry were later allowed into the camp.

Pemba Provincial Hospital on 28 March  acknowledged that 35 patients so far had been admitted with injuries sustained in the Palma assault. At least one Portuguese national was reported to be receiving treatment at the hospital after being wounded in the Palma assault.

Mozambican FADM spokesman Omar Saranga meanwhile on 28 March gave an official update on the situation in Palma, the first provided by the government since 25 March  Saranga said that "dozens" of civilians had been killed by insurgents in the town, also saying that at least 7 people were killed in the convoy ambush that took place on Friday night.  Saranga also said that hundreds of people, including locals and foreigners, had been rescued from Palma; he also said that rescue operations were ongoing in and around the town.  Saranga also said that security forces have "strengthened their operational strategy on the ground" and called on civilians to report terrorist movements to the security forces.

No deployments of foreign troops to support rescue efforts have been confirmed as of 28 March.  Reports regarding potential deployments of US, UK, French, and South African troops have all circulated in recent days, with the most credible reports indicating that French Foreign Legionnaires were being deployed to help protect the Afungi LNG Camp.  SA President Cyril Ramaphosa on Saturday held an emergency meeting allegedly on the subject, but no deployment of South African forces has yet materialized.

The administration of the second dose of COVID-19 vaccine starts today, 29 March, across the country. The vaccinations covers all health professionals initially vaccinated from 08-12 March. The second dose will be administered 21 days from the first dose in compliance with the protocol to attain effectivity of the vaccine.

The Ministry of Health announced that 132 new COVID cases and four related deaths in Mozambique on 27 March. There were 57 new cases diagnosed in Maputo city and 26 in Maputo province. There were also 13 new cases in Nampula, 12 in Niassa, 10 in Sofala, six in Tete, four in Cabo Delgado, two in Zambezia, one in Manica, and one in Inhambane. A total of 93 have recovered from the virus.

Department of Foreign Affairs announced on 28 March that all Irish nationals in Palma were confirmed safe during the assault on the city.  Only a small number of Irish nationals were present in the area, the Irish government said.

Reports on 29 March claimed that workers from the Total gas project who escaped Palma following the insurgent assault be transported from Pemba to Maputo via an air bridge. A group of Portuguese workers boarded the first plane that took off from Pemba to Maputo on 28 March. According to Total, workers will have better connections to their home towns or countries in Maputo City.

The dead body of a man was recovered in Intaka, Matola city on 27 March. It was believed he was murdered since signs of an assault were visible on his body. The body was moved by the National Criminal Investigation Services officers for further examination.

Clashes Monday were reported to be ongoing in Palma.  Security forces on Monday reportedly made some progress against the insurgents, with one source reporting that a local radio station had begun broadcasting for the first time since Wednesday.  Security forces reportedly launched a renewed operation to retake the town on 28 March which was supported by DAG helicopters.  A media source alleged that militants in recent hours had received "reinforcements" and that fighting was ongoing.  One source also indicated insurgents had begun retreating from the town, having run low on ammunition and food, and were fleeing towards the Tanzanian border, though this is unverified.  It is confirmed that neither side remains in full control of the town as of Monday afternoon.

Military registration across Mozambique for citizens aged 18 and above will end on 30 March. The registration was launched on 04 January and scheduled to end 28 February, however, it was extended for another month due to under enrollments which authorities blamed on adverse weather and COVID-19 safety protocols.

Information surfaced also regarding the fate of some of the expatriates ambushed in a convoy on the night of 26 March.  One British-South African national caught up in the ambush obtained a firearm and shot dead two insurgents; this occured outside of Palma on the road to Quionga.  The man and a group of other survivors of the attack fled into the bush, and were reportedly evacuated out of the area sometime Sunday.

On 29 March, the Islamic State's Central Africa Province (ISCAP) officially claimed responsibility for the assault on Palma, the group's first claimed attack in Cabo Delgado since October.  ISCAP claimed 55 "Christians" killed in the assault, including soldiers and others from "crusader states" (read: expatriates), and also claiming to have seized and sacked the town.  The group also released a picture showing dozens of militants gathered together, dated 29 March.  It is unclear exactly where or when the picture was taken, though it is likely to have been taken in the Palma area.  A signpost for Mocimboa da Praia (held by militants since August 2020) can be seen in the background.

DAG founder Lionel Dyck on 29 March said that during the ongoing battle for Palma, Total had "done nothing" and had not provided fuel to DAG helicopters as they were running low while attempting to protect and rescue civilians in Palma.  Dyck also said he believed the company's policy was "they don't support any form of armed security outside their camp".  Dyck on Sunday said DAG helicopters between Saturday and Sunday had managed to rescue 120 more people from the Palma area, also saying a number of dead bodies had also been evacuated.  Notably, Dyck also indicated that the Mozambican military had not taken part in fighting in Palma until 28 March.   Sources over recent days had indicated that security forces had engaged insurgents, though these clashes had mostly occurred on the periphery of the town, with militants retaining control of most of the town proper.  Dyck went on to say that his company expected a new surge in insurgent attacks as the "fighting season" begins in Cabo Delgado as the rainy season ends.

Thousands of people are still reported to be sheltering in and around the Afungi LNG Camp as of Monday, though evacuations from the area via small boats continued overnight Sunday and in Monday.  Once source said between 6,000-10,000 people are waiting for a rescue, though it is unclear if all of this group is gathered around the Afungi area.  Large numbers of people are believed to be hiding in bush areas around Palma, while others are trapped in the town itself.

Other reports indicate a group of at least 400 had fled on foot from Palma towards Nangade, and said they encountered several burned-out vehicles from previous insurgent attacks, as well as roadblocks set up by insurgents.

Other reports indicate a group of at least 400 had fled on foot from Palma towards Nangade, and said they encountered several burned-out vehicles from previous insurgent attacks, as well as roadblocks set up by insurgents.

A large group of between 200-500 people, believed to be mostly Mozambican nationals, arrived on Sunday in the Namoto area after walking for three days from Palma, fleeing the insurgent attack.  The group said that during this three-day trek, they were targeted at least once by insurgents, who abducted an unknown number of people.  The group hoped to cross over to Tanzania, and said more people were likely to arrive in the area over the coming days, fleeing the Palma assault.  Some children reportedly died in the wilderness on the trek north.

GSM communications remained down in Palma throughout the weekend as fighting continued in the area.  Insurgents are believed to have cut communications in the area during the beginning of the assault on Palma on 24 March.

DAG helicopters withdrew on Thursday night from over Palma after running low on fuel.  DAG helicopters had been engaging insurgents in Palma; this withdrawal later contributed to the decision by expats and locals sheltering at the Amarula Hotel to attempt to escape in an evacuation convoy that was later ambushed by insurgents.
Insurgents between Palma and Namoto reportedly targeted a large group of IDPs fleeing Palma between 24-28 March, kidnapping an unknown number of people.

Kenyan authorities on 27 March confirmed that two Kenyan youths wanted in connection with al Shabaab recently fled to Mozambique to join the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  This is a likely indication of the increased draw of the Cabo Delgado insurgency to foreign fighters.

column4: Several sources reported that the Amarula Hotel was abandoned on the evening of 26 March by a large number of locals and expatriates sheltering at the facility.  Earlier in the evening, insurgents attacked a compound near the hotel, while DAG helicopters had also withdrawn from the area.  At this time, a large convoy of 17 vehicles from the Amarula attempted to evacuate a large number of people, fleeing north towards Quionga.  Only 7 vehicles were able to escape, while insurgents fired on the remaining 10 vehicles, killing at least 7 people.  One source also said 3 of these vehicles were destroyed in the ambush.  At least some of these vehicles then returned to the hotel.  Details regarding those remaining at the Amarula after the convoy attack are currently unconfirmed.  Media sources on Saturday afternoon indicated that those remaining in the hotel after this incident were able to make their way to a military barracks on Palma's beachfront, and were evacuated by boat from the area.  Conflicting reports had previously indicated that the hotel had been assaulted and breached by insurgents after the convoy ambush, forcing those remaining in the Amarula to flee into the bush.  A large number of people remain unaccounted for.

Reports on 27 March indicated that militants may have initially planned concurrent attacks on Nangade and Mueda, but eventually opted for a concerted assault on Palma.  Notably, pro-Islamic State chatter on closed social media groups on 27 March said that the "city of Nanjadi" would be the next target of the insurgency

Closed sources said on 26 March that over a 24 hour period, soldiers had arrived into Palma from Mueda, Pemba, and even Maputo, but these troops have been unable to push insurgents out of the town; significant numbers of troops remain deployed around the Afungi LNG Camp also.  Closed sources have reported several times that security forces hope to surround the large insurgent group in Palma by cutting off escape routes into the bush before eliminating the group, though insurgents as of day 3 still have the upper hand in the town.

The Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP) Council of Ministers approved a proposal for free movement of peoples between the Lusophone countries during a meeting on 26 March. The CPLP stated that each country would have to discuss a format and agreement on how the member states would complete the formalities regarding the free movement.

The UN's Jan Egeland said on 27 March that Norwegian Refugee Council teams meant to provide humanitarian assistance in Cabo Delgado were still "waiting for visas” to enter Mozambique.  Many of those waiting first applied for visas in December.

Portugal Foreign Affairs Minister Santos Silva said on Monday that his country in April planned to deploy a team of 60 military officials to provide Mozambican military forces with counter-insurgency training. This was reiterated in the wake of the Palma assault but had been previously agreed to months previously.

US Department of State Acting Special Envoy John Godfrey issued a statement saying the attack on Palma represented the "brazenness" of ISCAP in Mozambique, also saying one American on the ground in Palma had been successfully evacuated.

Supply ships transporting food items arrived at Palma on the morning of 24 March as part of a series of supply shipments to the town which had been experiencing food shortages throughout February and March.  Insurgents launched the assault on Pemba later that same day.

The South African Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) stated that they had deployed more staff to assist Mozambique to help for the search of the remaining South African citizens during the weekend.

2 new COVID deaths and 186 new cases were reported by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 28 March. This brings the total fatalities to 764 and cases to 67,197. 108 new recoveries were also reported.  54 of the new cases were from Nampula, and 50 from Maputo city, 26 cases from Zambezia, 19 from Niassa, 16 from Sofala, 12 from Maputo province, four from Gaza, four from Inhambane and one from Tete.
The Ministry of Health announced that 5 new deaths and 95 new cases in Mozambique on 29 March. This comes as 96 individuals recovered from the virus.

Health officials announced that anti-COVID measures will continue to remain in place past the Easter holiday. The National Immigration Service (Senami) previously said that around 150,000 are expected to cross the borders to Mozambique. Senami stated that most of the civilians crossing to the country are expected to be coming from South Africa.

Health officials announced on 27 March that the COVID daily positivity rate in Mozambique had fallen to 5.4 percent, the lowest positivity rate during this month of March. The previous positivity rate last Friday, 26 March was 7.9%.

Local sources stated that 12 South African citizens are suspected to be involved in the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  This information had previously been reported but was reiterated by SA authorities during the assault on Palma.

The Mozambican Health officials announced that they would implement enhanced COVID screenings at the country’s borders with South Africa and Eswatini during the Easter holiday. The stricter COVD screenings comes as part of the Operation Easter 2021 from 26 March to 7 April. The operation was to strengthen both security and healthcare operations at the borders as 150,263 individuals were expected to come into the country during the holiday.

column4: Local sources stated that 8 vehicles that were part of an evacuation convoy out of Palma on 26 March and around 50 people were unaccounted for after the convoy was attacked by insurgents twice in Palma and north of the town on 26 March.

Local sources stated that information regarding a potential attack on Palma was received by security forces in and around the town on 21 March.  It is unclear exactly what information security forces received at this time.

DAG on Monday dispatched two helicopters to meet a group of between 30-50 people hiding in the bush about 20kms from Palma; the exact location of this area and identity of those hiding in the area is unclear at this time.

Local sources stated that people fleeing from the insurgent attacks from villages around Palma were beginning to arrive in Mueda. A large number of the IDPs who fled in this direction were left alongside the road, unable to continue due to exhaustion.

Large varying commercial and civilian boats continued to arrive in Pemba on Monday.  New arrivals, according to one local media outlet, included 13 employees from the Amarula Hotel, and 14 Moz investment employees; at least 120 new arrivals were reported during the course of the day.  The individuals were transferred to Muxarra neighborhood. Other sources late on Monday reported ships and boats continue to evacuate people from the Palma and Afungi area with several ships en route to Pemba while others travelled north back to Palma to rescue more people.

Locals sources stated late on Monday that ships and boats continue to evacuate people from the Palma and Afungi area with several ships en route to Pemba while others travelled north back to Palma to rescue more people.

Local sources stated that several thousand peoples were still waiting to be evacuated from Afungi on 29 March. Between 6,000 - 10,000 people were previously reported in this area waiting to be evacuated after fleeing the insurgent assault on Palma.

The South African High Commission in Maputo announced that 43 South Africans caught up in the assault on Pemba had been located and were safe. The High Commission stated that the South African nationals were mostly in Afungi. Two SA nationals had fled into the bush near Palma and been rescued while one man had been found and rescued by helicopters.  One SA national has also been confirmed killed.  At least 10 other SA nationals however remain unaccounted for.

A South Africa military aircraft was deployed to pick up the body of a deceased South African national at Pemba on 29 March.  43 other SA nationals caught up in the assault on Pemba have also been located and are safe.  At least 10 other SA nationals as of 29 March remain unaccounted for.
A vehicle accident occurred along a road in Maputo City on the morning of 30 March, killing 3 civilians.
The Ministry of Health on 29 March announced that the COVID vaccine was made available to the public as part of the COVAX initiative in the "next few days".

Fighting continued in Palma throughout Monday, with security forces saying the militants controlled "about half" of the town.  Security forces also said Palma was "almost deserted" after nearly the entire population had fled the fighting.  Security sources also denied that they had ever fully withdrawn from Palma as had been the case in Mocimboa da Praia during the insurgent assault on the town in August of 2020, saying a "good part" of the town had always remained under government control.  Security forces supported by DAG helicopters during the day attacked several small pockets of insurgents and "one quite large group" according to DAG founder Lionel Dyck. Earlier reports that insurgents were "fleeing" from the town were proved false; other reports that insurgents had received reinforcements in the town remain unverified, though militants still according to all accounts do hold parts of Palma.  As noted previously, some progress by security forces appeared to have been made on Monday after a local radio station began broadcasting for the first time since Wednesday.

Security forces also said Palma was "almost deserted" after nearly the entire population had fled the fighting.  Security sources also denied that they had ever fully withdrawn from Palma as had been the case in Mocimboa da Praia during the insurgent assault on the town in August of 2020, saying a "good part" of the town had always remained under government control.  Security forces supported by DAG helicopters during the day attacked several small pockets of insurgents and "one quite large group" according to DAG founder Lionel Dyck.

Rescue operations also continued during the day on Monday, with DAG helicopters rescuing a small number of wounded policemen.  DAG since Saturday said it had rescued 220 people from the Palma area.  Others continue to be rescued from bush areas around the town, while several thousand people are waiting for an evacuation from around the Afungi Peninsula.
Local media on Monday afternoon flew over some areas of Palma, showing destruction and smoke rising throughout the town, saying during the report that fighting was still ongoing.

Note that an image previously reported to be of insurgents gathered together in the Palma area was later on Monday confirmed to be a still image taken from a video released by ISCAP later on 29 March.  The video appears to have been shot on a road close to the Mocimboa da Praia airport, and to have been taken relatively recently, potentially as recently as within 1 week.  MDP has been held by militants since August of 2020.  The video shows a large group of militants, as many as over 100, gathered together with a roll call being taken.  Other clips from the video show the militants armed with heavy caliber machine guns and RPGs.  One militant at the end of the video says "we are going to kill everybody", seemingly alluding to the upcoming Palma assault.

On 27 March, several sources reported that tug boats, small vessels, and at least one large ferry coordinated rescues from Palma and Afungi as insurgents continued to attack the town.  Much of this makeshift fleet sailed into Pemba on 28 March, having rescued at least 1,300 people from the area.  Rescue operations from the Palma area are ongoing.

UN agencies on 30 March were reported to have covered only 10% of a $254.4 million appeal made in December to help support humanitarian needs in Cabo Delgado.  These needs and the number of displaced are expected to increase significantly in the wake of the Palma assault.

The US government said on 30 March that it was "determined" to assist Mozambique against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  Pentagon spokesman John Kirby stated that the US will cooperate with the government of Mozambique in counterterrorism support and countering violent extremism.

Kenmare Resources stated that the company does not expect any disruption in its operations due to the ongoing battle for Palma.  Kenmare's operations are based in Moma, Nampula, far from the fighting in Cabo Delgado.
The South African government stated that 10 to 15 South African citizens are still unaccounted for as of 30 March in the wake of the Palma assault. 43 SA nationals have been accounted for.
Local schools have set up additional tents to prevent delays and allow additional groups of students to conduct classes in Beira on Monday.

Around 1000 reported employees working at the Afungi were evacuated via Zan Fast Ferries - Sea Star 1, a ferry boat from Afungi to Pemba at around 10:00 on 28 March. The evacuation comes as part of the second conducted plan after initial air evacuations were conducted earlier to rescue other employees.

UNOCHA stated that around 110,000 civilians resided in Palma district before the assault on the town began on 24 March.  This includes 67,000 residents and 43,600 IDPs. Several strategic points were setup to receive fleeing individuals who require humanitarian aid. The current situation in Palma has further aggravated the humanitarian situation in Cabo Delgado as previously 1.3 million require assistance and protection in the province. This comes amid reports funding for humanitarian efforts in northern province have only achieved 10% funding.

A British national was reported to be still missing as of 30 March, and has been unaccounted since joining the evacuation convoy out Palma on the afternoon of Friday, 26 March. 7 other local employees of the same company have been accounted for.

RENAMO officials announced that RENAMO Military Junta dissidents who have completed the DDR process can rejoin the political party. RENAMO General Secretary Andre Majibire stated that the dissidents would be welcomed and called on the public to respect the former RENAMO Junta members. Several senior dissident leaders have recently defected from the armed group.

Mozambican health workers on 29 March began receiving the second dose of the vircell vaccine which was donated by China in February.  88% of the country's health workers in early March received first doses of the vaccine.

The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) stated that the increase in the price of bread has been stopped after bakers were found to be intending to increase the prices without official approval. INAE assured that they would determine if the production prices have increased as claimed by the bakers.

Local media reported that on 24 March, concurrently with the assault on Pemba, militants had launched amphibious attacks on Mucojo and Quiterajo in Macomia District, killing an unknown number of people in both areas and kidnapping several people.  Insurgents were later also reported to be present in the Manica area, near Mucojo.  Local sources stated that insurgents arrived by boats to both areas.

Local media reported that on 24 March, concurrently with the assault on Pemba, militants had launched amphibious attacks on Mucojo and Quiterajo in Macomia District, killing an unknown number of people in both areas and kidnapping several people.  Insurgents were later also reported to be present in the Manica area, near Mucojo.  Local sources stated that insurgents arrived by boats to both areas.

Insurgents on 24 March reportedly launched an amphibious raid in the Quiterajo area of Macomia district, arriving by boat and killing an unknown number of villagers and local fishermen and abducting others.  This attack was carried out as insurgents also launched an assault on Palma town.

Insurgents on 24 March reportedly launched an amphibious raid in the Quiterajo area of Macomia district, arriving by boat and killing an unknown number of villagers and local fishermen and abducting others.  This attack was carried out as insurgents also launched an assault on Palma town.

On the afternoon of 30 March, the Mozambican military announced that Palma had been fully recaptured by security forces from insurgents, after militants launched an assault on the town that began on 24 March. The security forces also said it would "soon" be safe for the population to return to the town. This claim that the town has been fully recaptured is currently unconfirmed.

Around 40 insurgents on 25 March launched an attack in Manica, Macomia district, after attacking the Quiterajo and Mucojo areas the day before.  Five insurgents shot sporadically inside the village while others fired on people who attempted to escape to Macomia-Sede. At least 17 people were reportedly beheaded in the attack.
Former President of the National Elections Commission Abdul Carimo died due to an illness after being admitted at a hospital in Maputo on the morning of 31 March.

UN rep to Mozambique Mirko Manzoni said on 30 March that the DDR process had been completed in Manica, with 817 former RENAMO fighters disarmed and demobilized.  This process included the decommissioning of RENAMO bases in Tambara, Barue, and Mossurize.  Manzoni also said 43 RENAMO dissident members had joined the process in Manica in recent months.  More than half of RENAMO military bases have now been closed down, with 2,307 RENAMO fighters demobilized, which is equal to about 44% of the group's entire armed membership.   The DDR process is yet to begin in Tete, Inhambane, Zambezia, and Nampula where more than 2,500 combined RENAMO armed members are expected to be demobilized.

Local sources reported on 30 March that Portuguese construction company Mota-Engil has stopped using Pemba and Mocimboa da Praia ports as part of its logistics and shifted it to the ports in Tanzania. Note that Mocimboa da Praia has not been useable as a port since August of 2020, when it was captured by insurgents.  The company's personnel reportedly left the Palma area on 24 March; it was unclear if these personnel had left the port just ahead of the attack or were evacuated during the attack.

Hours after security force sources reported questionable claims that Palma had been fully recaptured by the Mozambican military and police forces, a group of journalists with a military escort travelled into the town on the afternoon of 30 March, and came under insurgent small arms fire.  The ambush occurred in central Palma near a church.  The group were able to withdraw from the area and returned to Afungi, with no injuries reported.  One journalist said the group had "suffered an ambush".  Reports that the town had been recaptured, which were questionable at best, were unsubstantiated.

DAG owner Lionel Dyck said on Tuesday that "Palma is lost" saying rescue efforts continue in bush areas around the town and that his helicopters continue to engage insurgents, also saying militants are moving house to house throughout the town.  Other sources have indicated the town remains contested between security forces and insurgents.

Security forces positioned on the Palma outskirts on Sunday launched a renewed offensive to retake the town, and security forces on Monday were reported to hold at least parts of the area, though the town at best remains contested.  Thousands of people are still believed to be stranded in bush areas around the town. Rescue efforts as of 30 March were ongoing, with DAG helicopters rescuing small groups of people (4-6 due to small seating capacity) at a time who are then being dropped at Afungi before the helicopters return to the bush to rescue more people.

The Water Supply Investment and Assets Fund (FIPAG) stated on 27 March that several clandestine water connections had damaged the main water lines in Nampula. The damages of around 1 million meticais were brought about by warehouse constructions. The main pipe was illegally extended and added with connections. Around 30,000 cubic meters of water were recently stolen.

Local sources stated that the Mozambican government conducted a cabinet meeting on 30 March, issuing minutes after the meeting.  There was no indication that the ongoing battle for Palma was discussed.

Local sources stated that some security force elements from Palma were deployed to Montepuez on 23 March during the visit of President Nyusi.  This may have weakened Palma's defenses, just a day before insurgents launched their assault on the town.  It was unclear why troops were not deployed from Mueda, the site of a large military base, which is significantly closer to Montepuez.

On 29 March, South Africa's government was reported to be in talks with the South African Development Community to create solutions in ending the violence in Mozambique as clashes in Palma were ongoing.. South Africa and Zimbabwe have previously pushed for a potential military intervention in Cabo Delgado, though this has been resisted by Mozambique.

International Organization of Migration officials stated that they had recorded 672 families or 3,361 individuals who had been displaced by the assault on Palma who had travelled to Mueda, Montepuez, and Pemba. The families traveled by foot, bus, boat, and/ or plane. Other sources reported large numbers of people had fled to Nangade, Meluco, and Ancuabe; a few hundred people also fled into Nampula Province.  Thousands more remain unaccounted for and potentially tens of thousands more in the coming weeks could be tracked to have been displaced from the Palma assault.
