Insurgents on 24 March attacked trucks carrying food north of Palma; this attack reportedly occurred just before the general assault on Pemba began.  At least three truck drivers were reportedly beheaded in this incident.
NGO sources reported on 30 March that at least 3 humanitarian workers who had been in the Palma area at the beginning of the insurgent assault remained unaccounted for as of Tuesday.

Clashes continued in Palma on 30 March, with intermittent gunfire reported during the morning.  The Mozambican military described "pockets of resistance" in several parts of the town, despite other security force elements earlier in the day saying the town had been fully recaptured. Other sources reported fighting in the hills along Palma's southern outskirts, where DAG helicopters reportedly inflicted significant casualties on insurgents who were believed to be attempting to position themselves to potentially attack towards the Afungi LNG Camp, where thousands of people are still awaiting rescue.

DAG helicopters in action on the afternoon of 30 March reportedly inflicted significant casualties on insurgents who were believed to be attempting to position themselves to potentially attack towards the Afungi LNG Camp, where thousands of people are still awaiting rescue. Other unverified reports said insurgents in Palma had utilized some captured vehicles and had fired on a DAG helicopter.

Sources on 30 March said insurgents in Palma were reported to be armed with an unknown quantity of RGPs - this echoes accounts form the first days of the clashes.  RPGs could also be seen in a video released by ISCAP on 29 March in which insurgents appeared to be marshalling their forces in Mocimboa da Praia earlier this month before launching the assault on Pemba.

Sources on 30 March indicated that an average of 80 military/police officer reinforcements continue to arrive daily to the Palma area by plane, though a significant number of soldiers have also been wounded in fighting in recent days as well.  One source indicated that as many as 40 soldiers with lower extremity injuries were being flown out of the Palma area on a daily basis.

Sources on 30 March continued to indicate casualties in Palma are significant as clashes in the town continue between insurgents and security forces.  Multiple sources have described bodies seen in streets across the town, and multiple people who have fled Palma have recounted stories from the first days of the assault on Palma in which insurgents killed large numbers of civilians.  One source reported insurgents during the initial phases of the attack moved through the town methodically, targeting individuals known to them, rather than killing indiscriminately; this is consistent with other insurgent attacks in which militants have targeted local officials, security force members, community leaders, and others they perceive to be working with the government or security forces. Insurgents were later reported to have attacked virtually anyone they encountered in the town.  Confirmed casualty figures are unavailable at this time, though reports from the town are now consistently indicating over 100 killed as a conservative estimate.

Insurgents reportedly fired at evacuation boats attempting to rescue people from the Palma's beaches on 27 March  A evacuee stated that his colleague died after being fatally shot on board a boat during this incident.

The insurgents executed several individuals in specifically targeted attacks that included an undetermined number of beheadings in Palma on 24 March as the militant assault on the town began. This follows similar past insurgent attack patterns in which militants target local community leaders, security force officials, and other individuals they regard as collaborating with the government and/or security forces.

Large groups IDPs have arrived in Nangade after fleeing more than 100kms from Palma amid the ongoing assault on the town by insurgents.  At least 14 unaccompanied children are among the groups that have recently reached Nangade. These IDPs said the insurgents during the assault had told local civilians they wanted to seize public officials as hostages to oblige the Mozambican government to implement sharia law; the militants reportedly directly blamed local officials for sharia law not being implemented in Cabo Delgado.  Insurgents reportedly also told locals that they wanted to capture the Palma District Administrator and other public officials, who were known to be sheltering at the Amarula hotel.

The Brazilian government issued a statement on 30 March offering the Mozambique assistance in fighting insurgency in Cabo Delgado. The Brazilian government was ready to cooperate with the Mozambican government and provide support.

An NGO released a statement on 30 March saying at least 3,100 people had fled Palma to the sea or bush, with an unknown number of people already in Pemba.  The NGO said some unaccompanied minors are among those fleeing, and that many more are expected to be recorded fleeing to other areas of Cabo Delgado.

The Ministry of Health announced that 70,000 teachers will be vaccinated as part of the second phase of the vaccination campaign in Mozambique. This comes as 3,604 diabetics, 3,224 elderly people, including retired people, and 400 workers for the funeral services have been vaccinated.

Former dissident leader Andre Matsangaissa has completed the DDR process and is again returned to life as a civilian, sources reported on 30 March.  Matsangaissa also called Mariano Nhongo and on other dissidents to join the DDR and stated that not every dispute can be resolved with guns.

A ship transporting 1,000 displaced people from Palma excepted to land in Pemba on Wednesday, 31 March.  This was the second large batch of people expected to arrive into Pemba after around 2,000 people arrived to the city on Sunday after being evacuated from the Palma area amid ongoing fighting.

Local sources stated that Total on 30 March had distributed 15 tons of food among thousands of displaced people currently stranded in Afungi area. The aid was in coordination with Doctors Without Borders.

A South African opposition party, the Democratic Alliance said that South Africa should send special forces to assist in evacuation efforts in Pemba, and that South Africa should reach out to Mozambique via the SADC as the battle for Palma continues.

18 Civil Society groups issued an open letter on 30 March calling on President Nyusi to request the SADC, AU, and other international partners to help the country counter insurgents in Cabo Delgado.  The letter also said the government should make efforts to remove children, girls, and women from "unsafe places" in the conflict zone.  The letter also said the government should issue regular information regarding the ongoing assault in Palma.

The Ministry of Health called on individuals to avoid crowds during the Easter holiday as part of the safety precautions against COVID.  Minister Matsinhe stated that Easter is important for Christians but churches and gathering areas remain closed as part of the stricter measures against the pandemic. Matsinhe also clarified that Mozambique has seen a decrease in COVID cases thanks in part to anti-COVID measures.

Local media stated that several bank employees in Maputo City have recently been found to be forging documents to steal large amounts of money from account owners. Police managed to recover a vehicle bought using the stolen money and stated that the gang was a large network as the criminals were working with bank employees. The criminals would target individuals who died due to COVID.  The bank in question was not named in this report.

The Ministry of Health announced 3 new COVID deaths and 174 new cases in Mozambique on 30 March. The case breakdown is as follows: 65 in Zambezia, 46 in Maputo city, 16 in Nampula, 16 in Niassa, 16 in Sofala, 5 in Maputo province, 5 in Tete, 3 in Cabo Delgado, 1 in Gaza, and 1 in Manica.

Large numbers of IDPs are arriving from Palma to Pemba via boats and special flights on 30 March. A total of at least 360 new IDPs arrived, 200 at Pemba Airport and 160 from boats. This follows the arrival of thousands of employees at the gas projects on Sunday.
A survivor stated that several locals drowned attempting to swim between Qiwia to Maganja, to escape to boats during Palma assault.

Survivors of the assault on Palma said that insurgents on Sunday had caught a group of people attempting to escape the area, and beheaded them.  No accurate casualty figures from this incident were available.  Insurgents retreated into the bush after the killings as DAG helicopters approached the area.

The Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) stated that six more South African citizens were evacuated from Mozambique on 30 March.  43 South African nationals were previously located and evacuated from the country in recent days.

Local sources stated that thousands of civilians are still displaced outside of Palma as of 30 March but are currently “trapped” due to the insurgent presence in the bush areas around the Palma.  Thousands also are still sheltering around the Afungi LNG Camp, awaiting evacuation.

Fighting between security forces, backed by DAG helicopters and insurgents continued for an 8th day in Palma on 31 March.  Local media reported military and police forces were gaining ground in the town, though did not provide specific detail.  Other sources reported clashes continued in parts of Central Palma, with militants utilizing urban guerilla tactics.  Security sources on 30 March had declared the town recaptured; renewed clashes however were later reported, with significant fighting taking place along the town's southern outskirts on Tuesday afternoon.

Fighting between security forces, backed by DAG helicopters and insurgents continued for an 8th day in Palma on 31 March.  Local media reported military and police forces were gaining ground in the town, though did not provide specific detail.  Other sources reported clashes continued in parts of Central Palma, with militants utilizing urban guerilla tactics.  Security sources on 30 March had declared the town recaptured; renewed clashes however were later reported, with significant fighting taking place along the town's southern outskirts on Tuesday afternoon.

Sources on 31 March continued to describe mass casualties in Palma.  Unverified video seen by Aldebaran showed dozens of people dismembered in an unspecified area of the town.  Reports consistently since 24 March have indicated there are large numbers of civilian casualties in Palma, while other sources have reported substantial military casualties as well.  No specified numbers are yet available, though conservative estimates indicate over 100 killed in the town.

Several sources in the past 24 hours have also reported at least three British special forces members were deployed on Monday night to help search for a British national still missing in the aftermath of the attack.  Unverified reports have said this man was killed in Friday's convoy ambush.  Other reports over the last week had indicated the US, France, and South Africa were all looking at deploying special forces to the Palma area for rescue missions.  French Foreign Legion forces reportedly were to be deployed additionally to help protect the Afungi LNG Camp, though this has not yet been confirmed.

Security forces continued to clash with insurgents in Palma during the afternoon of 31 March, with security forces conducting house to house searches, supported by DAG helicopters. Military sources said they were searching people left in the town to determine whether they were residents or insurgents.  The military on Wednesday acknowledged that "small groups" of militants remained in the town and had in some cases attempted to blend in with the local population, though also saying "there is no longer a large group of terrorists in Palma".  One unconfirmed source said insurgents had ambushed some security forces carrying out house to house searches. Other emerging reports referred to a new militant attack "between Palma and Afungi" though no other information on this possible incident is currently available.
Reports on Tuesday indicated insurgents in technical vehicles in Palma had fired on a DAG helicopter.  No further details regarding this incident are currently available.

Sources on 31 March reported that many as 10,000 IDPs fleeing the Palma assault were gathered together in the Quitunda area, just outside of the Afungi LNG Camp.  Some instances of locals banging on the camp walls have been reported.

President Nyusi on 31 March gave his first public remarks on the ongoing battle for Palma, saying the assault was "not greater than so many others we had".  Nyusi also said "let us not lose focus, let us not be disturbed".

In Pemba, Cabo Delgado Secretary of State Armindo Ngunga on 31 March warned that insurgents could attempt to infiltrate the provincial capital among IDPs fleeing from Palma, saying all new arrivals must be vetted and searched.

Local volunteers stated as of 31 March, at least 800 individuals were still missing since the start of the Palma attack. The volunteer have assisted in locating families who have been caught in the violence.  These 800 have been specifically reported as missing, though thousands more are likely unaccounted for, displaced into bush areas around Palma.
45 IDPs fleeing the Palma assault crossed the Rovuma River and arrived at Kilambo Village in Tanzania on the afternoon 29 March. The refugees were sheltered and been given food.

A wounder soldier stated during an interview on 31 March that there were "hundreds" of insurgents who attacked from various positions in Palma on 24 March, attacking a military post of 35 men stationed in one area of the city.  The soldier said he and his colleagues fled in the face of this attack.

DAG owner Lionel Dyck stated on Wednesday, 31 March that insurgents could potentially attack Afungi from "a distance" using mortars as the militants in Palma were confirmed over the past week to possess these weapons.

19 illegal Pakistani immigrants were arrested by migration officials in Munhonha area of Nicoadala District on 30 March. The illegal immigrants were caught riding a bus towards Maputo. The bus driver denied knowledge that the suspects were of illegal residency.

Large numbers of displaced individuals were reported on 30 March to have sought refuge at the Quitunda Resettlement Village, just outside of the Afungi LNG area. IDPs in the area were reported to be experiencing a worsening food and water situation as reports that the water supply had run out in the area. Total has distributed food relief to the refugees in attempts alleviate the current situation.

Portuguese company Construcoes Gabriel Couto stated that all their employees are safe and out of Palma area on 30 March. The 20 employees, 17 locals, and 3 foreigners were evacuated by boat from the area in the aftermath of the attack on Palma. The 20 employees were preparing for return of the works in Afungi, ahead of the now cancelled arrival of another 250 colleagues.

The World Food Program said on 30 March that it had successfully evacuated around 280 individuals, mostly women and children, from Palma in recent days. The evacuations have been ongoing since 24 March.

IDPs arriving in Pemba stated that food insecurity has been growing as IDPs continue to arrive to the city.  Potentially thousands of IDPs fleeing from Palma could arrive into the city over the coming days and weeks, likely further exacerbating the problem.

Several survivors from the Palma attack interviewed by local media said on 31 March stated that thousands are still stranded in the bush areas around Palma. The stranded survivors lack of food and water, according to the IDPs.

New Democracy, a small political party, strongly criticized President Nyusi for not publicly speaking on the ongoing battle for Palma, saying the President should be keeping the country informed on the situation.  The party also said there is a void of information with no updates provided by the government as to the situation.  RENAMO meanwhile has largely been silent on the ongoing situation in Palma.

RBR, an Australian company stated that they are conducting a search to account for some of a sub contractor team who were at an accommodation near Palma when the insurgent assault on Palma began on 24 March.  The company said that "as far as it is aware" its personnel are safe, though one report indicated one company member was killed on 26 March by insurgents in the town.

Local Community of Sant'Egidio groups in Cabo Delgado said on 30 March that 9 of the group's members have been killed in insurgent attacks over the past 6 months in Cabo Delgado.  The group regularly provide humanitarian assistance to communities impacted by the insurgency.

The Defense and Security forces on 31 March acknowledged that Palma has not been fully secured. Operational Theater spokesman Chongo Vidigal also stated that deaths are “relatively low” due to residents fleeing from Palma during the day of the attack. Vidigal also said security forces were working "on the ground in pursuit of the evil-doers".

The Pemba Diocese Antonio Juliasse stated there concerns that around 200 to 500 IDPs fleeing into Tanzania after receiving reports that they were “not being properly received”. Antonio Juliasse clarified that once these IDPs have crossed into Tanzania they are refugees and has called on the UN High Commissioner for Refugees for assistance.

The Dyck Advisory Group (DAG) has reportedly agreed to closer cooperation with Garda World to conduct operations in the Palma area.  The details of this deal were not immediately clear, particularly as DAG's contract in Mozambique is reported to be set to expire on 06 April.

The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) destroyed 625.5kg of seized drugs outside of a residence in Quelimane on 31 March. The burning of the narcotics was to discourage drug smugglers and dealers.  At least two people were previously arrested in connection to the case.

The Cabo Delgado Provincial Court sentenced a detainee held on poaching charges to 16 years in prison in Pemba. Andre Mariano Baridi was found guilty after being found coming from a poacher’s camp with several hunting tools and traps for large animals at Niassa Special Reserve.

Two ships transporting over 1,200 IDPs coming from Palma currently docked in Pemba on the morning of 1 April after arriving off Pemba on the night of 31 March. The ships were delayed due to bad weather. Initial reports stated that ship has yet to disembark the IDPs due to screening procedures. Other reports stated that the late docking was due to unsafe docking during evening.

The FRELIMO party issued a statement that the attacks in Palma are an attack on Mozambique’s sovereignty and development. FRELIMO said that the country should be united against the such incidents and denied reports that the government neglected the threat and activities of the armed group since 2017.

Security measures were put in place in Mueda on 24 March after the insurgent attack began in Palma to prevent an attack on the town.  Entry and exits to Mueda were sealed off as part of these measures.

The International Organization for Migration stated that 5360 IDPs displaced from Palma have arrived in Nangade, Mueda, Montepuez, and Pemba as of 30 March. IOM stated that recorded displacements are increasing quickly.

The Mozambican National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) announced that 600 civil servants remain in Palma as of 26 March. CNDH official Bitone stated that they have been talking with other organizations to assist in evacuating the remaining civil servants in the Palma area. CNDH also clarified that there have been no death reports and the civil servants were guaranteed that they are at a slightly safe location, waiting for evacuation.  Insurgents in many instances have singled out civil servants for targeted attacks.
The Ministry of Health announced 113 new COVID cases and 3 new deaths in Mozambique on 31 March. 758 recoveries were reported during the past 24 hours.

Unconfirmed reports on 31 March indicated that RENAMO dissidents attacked a public transport vehicle along the N1 road along the western edge of Gorongosa National Park.  Several civilians were injured but no specific numbers were stated. The civilians managed to escape from the area. This incident is currently unconfirmed.

Party for Peace, Democracy and Development leader Raul Manuel Domingos was appointed as a member of the State Council on the afternoon of 31 March. Domingos replaced Daviz Mbepo Simango, the former Democratic Movement of Mozambique, who passed away on 22 February.

Gemfields mining company which operates mines in Montepuez announced that it was monitoring the current situation in Palma, saying there could be an increased risk of illegal mining brought about by mass displacements.  As many as 60,000 IDPs displaced by the ongoing insurgents have fled to the Montepuez area, which has seen multiple illegal mining incidents in recent years.

Sources on 31 March reported that DAG's contract is still set to expire on 06 April, despite the fact that DAG has been the most active security force actor in the battle for Palma.  Sources indicate the last DAG sorties will take place on 01 or 02 April.  Unconfirmed reports on the afternoon of 31 March had indicated that DAG's contract could be renewed for another 3 months.  The withdrawal of DAG from Palma could embolden the insurgents, who for example have not been able to strike towards the Afungi LNG Camp before Wednesday largely thanks to DAG sorties.  Other sources on Tuesday night reported that negotiations between the government and DAG were "ongoing".

Police arrested a suspect wanted for kidnapping a baby in Quelimane on 1 April. The suspect stole the baby from Costa do Sol area during the previous week. The suspect was previously the caretaker of the baby.

The Ministry of Health announced 150 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 1 April. The breakdown of the cases are as follows: 42 in Zambezia, 35 in Maputo city, 24 in Sofala, 14 in Maputo province, 13 in Niassa, 12 in Cabo Delgado, 5 in Nampula, 3 in Tete, and 2 in Inhambane. No  COVID deaths were reported during the past 24 hours. 31 of the new cases were hospitalized while 32 recoveries were reported.

Security forces continued house to house searches in Palma as of 01 April, though no new clashes have been confirmed in the town in recent hours.  Security forces are reported to be in control of large parts of the town, though cannot at this time claim full control of Palma.

Multiple sources meanwhile reported that the body of a British national missing since 26 March had been recovered.  The man's company also issued a statement saying he appeared to have been killed while trying to escape the insurgent siege of the Amarula hotel.  The man was part of a convoy of vehicles that was ambushed by insurgents on Friday as it attempted to escape the town. This comes as 6 local employees remain missing.

Local sources stated that a Mozambican military helicopter mistakenly conducted an attack targeting a truck transporting civilians away from Palma; this incident reportedly either occurred on 24 or 25 March. Six civilians were killed and several others were injured.

In the initial hours of the assault on Palma on 24 March, insurgent robbed three banks and stole 90 tonnes of food from a WFP warehouse in Palma.  Large quantities of munitions  and 80 vehicles, including two fuel truck tanks, were also seized by the insurgents at this time.  Unconfirmed reports indicated that some insurgents may have been able to flee Palma with this loot back into insurgent held areas.
Military forces in Palma on 31 March said they were searching people left in the town to determine whether they were residents or insurgents.

Unconfirmed sources on 01 April indicated insurgents had threatened a new attack on Pemba over the weekend.  Note that insurgents in the past have threatened several attacks on the provincial capital, though none have yet materialized.

Sources stated that employees of at least one NGO were evacuated from the Afungi area on 1 April. The evacuation was due to the lack of adequate dependable evacuation methods in the area.  Sources later confirmed Total had also begun pulling out its remaining staff in the area during the day as well.

Galp Energy Company denies reports that it will sell its gas exploration stake on 1 April. Previous reports during the day had stated that the energy company would sell its stakes for the gas exploration in Mozambique due to the ongoing violence and insurgency in the northern province.
UNICEF stated on 1 April stated that more than 350,0000 children are displaced across Cabo Delgado. This includes 17,000 children believed to have been displaced in the attack on Palma.
An unidentified explosion occurred at a mill in Ilha de Mozambique on 31 March. 2 civilians were killed and 4 were injured.

The Ministry of Health announced that COVID hospitalizations in Mozambique are declining as only 92 COVID cases are currently hospitalized in the country as of 1 April. Of the 92 inpatients, 57 were in Maputo City and 12 in Zambezia, 8 in Nampula, 6 in Maputo province, 7 in Sofala, and 2 in Tete.

The African Union (AU) on 02 April called for “urgent” action in Mozambique in response to the Palma assault by insurgents.  AU Chairman Moussa Faki Mahamat condemned the attack and called for a coordinated and urgent regional and international action against the ongoing insurgency.
A vehicle collided with a truck on the Ring Road in Maputo City at around 11:00 1 April. A civilian died during the accident.

Southern African Development Community (SADC) members on 01 April stated that they would take action against the insurgency behind the scenes in aftermath of Palma attack. This comes as Zimbabwe President and outgoing SADC chairman Mnangagwa and his Botswanan counterpart Mokgweetsi Masisi conducted a meeting regarding Mozambique on 31 March.  Mnangagwa stated that the SADC would respond in a helpful manner to ensure the integrity and sovereignty of Mozambique after being attacked by insurgents.  The SADC is reportedly drafting a response to attempt to assist Mozambique in the ongoing battle against the insurgents.

UN warned of a “prolonged” humanitarian crisis in Mozambique as people are continuously displaced in the country. An increase in IDPs is expected in the following days and weeks, with potentially tens of thousands displaced by the attack.  The UN has also said before the Palma attack, it only had about one third of $254 million needed to provide humanitarian assistance in Cabo Delgado; these needs are likely to significantly increase in the wake of the Palma attack.

Municipal Residents say that there is a resurgence of crimes in Muatala, south of Nampula, during the evenings recently . Locals stated that the 25 de Setembro is the most common area for criminal activity. Even with the police in the area, crimes have taken place at the market of the residential unit.

Three deaths and a total of 413 cholera cases were recorded during the month of March in Nampula. Officials stated that individuals affected by the disease take a long time to get checked up at the hospital causing the disease to worsen before being treated.

Sources stated that insurgents on a boat boarded and hijacked a Palau-flagged cargo vessel identified as ALFAJIMBO docked at Palma on 24 March. Crew members escaped the attack and were able to board another vessel to safety.  Unconfirmed reports indicated two other vessels attacked at this time.

Sources on 02 April reported the ongoing evacuations of remaining Total and subcontractor personnel from the Afungi Peninsula.  Sources later indicated Total's evacuation had begun on 01 April.  By late morning, most of these evacuations had been completed, though one small group of workers still on site was set to be the last group to be evacuated. Some organizations had evacuated staff from the area on 01 April, and at least 5 vessels on Friday were reported to be just off Afungi to assist in these evacuations. Total had initially said last weekend it would maintain a minimal crew to continue operations at Afungi but appears to be withdrawing even these personnel at this time as well. No official statement from the company has been released. Ongoing evacuations have likely been triggered by reports that DAG, which in the battle for Palma has been the most effective element of the security forces, is set to withdraw as its contract with the Ministry of the Interior expires. Large numbers of IDPs have also fled to areas just outside the Afungi LNG Camp.  Palma meanwhile is not yet confirmed to have been fully secured from the insurgents.

Reports indicated that insurgents on 02 April had hijacked two vessels, a small landing craft and a 9m motorboat, off the Palma coast.  Other sources later reported virtually all vessels off of Palma had left the area, though some vessels were reported off Afungi, carrying out evacuations from the LNG Camp.

Reports on the night of 01 April indicated insurgents had attacked and overrun two security force positions near Quitunda, outside of the Afungi LNG Camp. Unverified reports on 02 April meanwhile indicated insurgents had infiltrated among IDPs in the Quitunda area.  Another source reported the incident had taken place "south of Palma".

Media reports on Friday said that South Africa had dispatched South Africa National Defense Force troops to Cabo Delgado to assist in the evacuation of its citizens.  Reports earlier this week indicated that between 10-15 South African nationals were still missing who had been in the Palma area as the assault began. SA President Cyril Ramaphosa said the SANDF was working to secure the safety of South Africans still stranded in Mozambique.

Mozambican military spokesman Chongo Vidigal on 02 April said that the Afungi LNG Camp was "far from danger" and that the camp was "beyond the reach" of insurgents who had attacked nearby Palma.  He also said that "at no time was its integrity at stake."  Other sources reported that outskirts of the camp were being patrolled constantly.  This announcement was made shortly before Total was reported to be pulling all remaining personnel out of the Afungi LNG Camp.

Local media reports on 02 April indicated that Tanzania had deported an unknown number of IDPs in Negomane, Mueda District who had fled the Palma attack and crossed the Rovuma River into Tanzanian territory. The IDPs were reportedly fed and investigated in Tanzania prior to deportation.

Insurgents on the night of 31 March attacked a command post of Mozambican troops between Afungi and Palma, but later withdrew.  No information on casualties is available from this clash, and it is unclear if insurgents attacked the area out of positions in Palma or outside the town.

Clashes in Palma were reported on 02 April, though exact details regarding the fighting remain vague.  Security forces in recent days have been conducting house to house searches attempting to locate insurgents remaining in the town.  Other reports over the past 48 hours indicated insurgents had hijacked two boats just off Palma, a small landing craft and a 9m motorboat, before launching at least two attacks on security forces south of Palma.  Militants may be receiving reinforcements from other areas, and as of Friday maintain at least some offensive initiative.  Palma remains contested, with fires also reported in the town over the past day.
DAG helicopters destroyed two boats hijacked by insurgents just off Palma on 2 April. A small landing craft and a 9m motorboat had been seized by militants the day before  being destroyed by DAG.

Several sources on the evening of 02 April said insurgents were reported to have attacked civilians and security forces near the Afungi LNG Camp.  Thousands of IDPs reportedly fled this attack.  This report is currently unconfirmed.  Sources later said no attack had targeted the Afungi Camp itself, though other sources reported an attack on the Quitunda area with unspecified casualties.

Also on the night of 02 April, the WFP announced it was suspending evacuation flights from Palma due to a "deterioration in security", saying the organization was concerned with increasing levels of violence in the area.
Sources stated that 2 Somali nationals as 2 April were missing in Palma after the insurgent assault on the area which began on 24 March.

The Swiss government made 1 million USD available for humanitarian assistance for IDPs in Cabo Delgado on 2 April. The aid is meant to improve healthcare and drinking water access at displacement resettlement villages.

UNOCHA said as of 02 April there are currently 9,150 IDPs in Nangade, Mueda, Montepuez, and Pemba. 2944 IDPs were in Nangade, 4,202 in Mueda, 1683 in Montepuez, and 1775 IDPs in Pemba.  309 IDPs were also in Nampula.  As many as 24,000 had sheltered outside the Afungi LNG camp, while hundreds more were reported to be present along the Cabo Delgado - Tanzania border.

As many as 24,000 had sheltered outside the Afungi LNG camp, while hundreds more were reported to be present along the Cabo Delgado - Tanzania border.

World Food Program announced on 2 April that the organization expects to provide support to 50,000 IDPs affected by the Palma attacks with humanitarian assistance.  This comes as 1000 IDPs arrived in Pemba during the past 24 hours between 01-02 April.

ISIS released an infographic and several images related to the attack on Palma on 1 April. The images showed militant wearing red bandanas gathered at a junction and the infographic claiming that they killed 55 security forces.  The Palma attack was also covered in an issue of the group's al Naba magazine.

The Southern Africa Development Community (SADC) announced the regional block would conduct a meeting in the coming days to discuss the ongoing conflict in Cabo Delgado. The meeting was called in the aftermath of the assault on Palma. Sources later reported this meeting was delayed until at least 08 April.

The Turkish government announced that Ankara was ready to provide assistance against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado on 2 April. Turkey's envoy to Maputo stated that there are external actors who do not want Mozambique's empowerment and development.

Tourism operators stated that a majority of tourist have cancelled their Easter reservations due to the COVID pandemic in Inhambane. Authorities stated that the recent attacks in Cabo Delgado also affected the reservations.

Officials stated that 75 percent of roads around Beira are worn out and should be repaired. Locals stated that the damaged roads have caused difficulty in travel recently in and around the city as potholes cause damages to personal vehicles.

The Ministry of Health announced that 194 COVID cases and 3 related deaths were registered in Mozambique on 02 April. 54 of the new cases were from Sofala, 46 from Maputo city, 35 from Zambezia, 17 from Tete, 14 from Nampula, 14 from Maputo province, eight from Inhambane, three from Gaza, three from Manica, and one from Niassa. 13 coronavirus patients have been discharged while for new cases were admitted.

Sources on 03 April indicated an unknown number of insurgents had infiltrated among large crowds of refugees gathered in the Quitunda village area.  Some sources later reported an attack in this area, just west of the Afungi LNG Camp, with unspecified casualties.  No further details on this incident are currently available.

The Mozambican Military on 04 April announced that it was in full control of Palma after clashes in the town began with a major insurgent assault on 24 March.  A military spokesman said troops had "completed" operations to retake the town on Sunday morning, saying areas around the Palma airstrip had been the last "sensitive area", but that this too had now been secured.  The military also said the next step would be "the creation of conditions for a safe return of the population".  Other sources reported the military had taken control of the airstrip on Saturday evening.  A handful of media outlets, including one international media outlet reported for the first time in days on the situation in Palma (though most reported from Pemba) , with one outlet showing footage from the area indicating that security conditions in the town had improved.   Other sources however reported that insurgents still possibly held positions on the outskirts of Palma, or were present just outside the town.  Security forces appear to currently have the upper hand in the town, though security forces' complete control of Palma cannot yet be confirmed.  Military sources also indicated that a "significant number" of insurgents were killed in operations in recent days in the town.

The Ministry of Health announced that 114 new COVID-19 cases and no related death were registered in Mozambique on 04 April. Of the 114 new cases, 56 cases were recorded from Nampula, 29 cases in Sofala and 29 are recorded in other provinces. Two more people were hospitalized due to the coronavirus while 14 were discharged.  A total of 159 people have recovered from the virus on the same day.

The Ministry of Health announced that 82 new COVID-19 cases and three related deaths were registered in Mozambique on 03 April.  49 of the new cases were from Maputo city, seven cases from Maputo province, 18 cases from Nampula, five from Inhambane, and one each from Cabo Delgado, Niassa and Tete. Eight more people were hospitalized due to the coronavirus while four were discharged.

On 03 April, small scale evacuations from the Afungi area by plane were carried out during the day by private contractors.  This came just a day after Total completed evacuations of its remaining personnel from the Afungi LNG Camp.

DAG's contract was confirmed to be expiring on 06 April, despite rumors last week that the company's contract would be extended for three months. DAG helicopters were reported to have flown their final sorties in the Palma area on 02 April.
Total reportedly made the decision to withdraw from Afungi after drone surveillance of areas near the Afungi LNG Camp indicated insurgents had moved closer to the area as fighting in Palma continued.
Insurgents were reported to be present either on the Palma outskirts or just outside of the town on 04 April.

Clashes between security forces and insurgents were reported on 03 April south of Palma and west of the Afungi camp.  Some sources had indicated this incident took place at Quitunda, while others reported the incident occurred further west of the LNG Camp.

Intermittent clashes were reported to have continued in Palma on 04 April near the Palma airstrip, with military sources saying the area had been cleared by the end of the morning.  According to the Mozambican military, this was the last area remaining in Palma to be held by insurgents, and the town was completely under security forces control
Security forces continued clearing operations around Palma on 03 April in a bid to secure the town.
Around 24,000 IDPs were reported to be sheltering outside of the Afungi LNG Camp as of 02 April, having fled over the past week from Palma town amid the ongoing insurgent assault on the area.

Sh2.4 billion contract has been signed by the Tanzania and Mozambique Governments to extend the Tanzania's National ICT Broadband Backbone into Mozambique. The construction of the fiber optic layout, power and transmission equipment, the mechanical building, the guard booth and the fireplace will be part of the project which will be funded by the Tanzania Government. The transmission systems will be installed at Mtambaswala and Masasi stations to facilitate communication services in Mtambaswala and across to Mozambique. Once the infrastructure is in place, Mozambique will start paying for the service.

More than 50 South African nationals who were reported missing through the South African High Commission in Maputo have been accounted for as of 03 April.  The deceased body of one South African national killed along with his family members were repatriated on 30 March. The South African National Defence Force continues to provide logistical support to the South African High Commission in Maputo including repatriation. This is the extent of the engagement of South African Military in Mozambique.
Several IDPs were reportedly killed by crocodiles or perished in deep mud on 24 March as they fled the Palma area as insurgents attacked the town.

A woman who escaped from Palma said that she had seen militants in the town with "uniforms with red scarves" also saying insurgents had carried "bazookas".  A video that previously surfaced showed insurgents in Mocimboa da Praia allegedly preparing for the Palma attack with red sashes tied around their heads.

The Zimbabwe Government denied on 03 April that it has deployed troops to Mozambique. Authorities said they were willing to provide military assistance, but only as part of a Southern African Development Committee (SADC) force.

Sources on 02 April reported that 9,900 people displaced from Palma have arrived in Nangade, Mueda, Montepuez, and Pemba. 45% of these IDPs are children and were displaced from the district due to the insurgent attacks on Palma which started on 24 March.

Sources on 02 April reported that 9,900 people displaced from Palma have arrived in Nangade, Mueda, Montepuez, and Pemba. 45% of these IDPs are children and were displaced from the district due to the insurgent attacks on Palma which started on 24 March.

Sources on 02 April reported that 9,900 people displaced from Palma have arrived in Nangade, Mueda, Montepuez, and Pemba. 45% of these IDPs are children and were displaced from the district due to the insurgent attacks on Palma which started on 24 March.

Mozambican military units clashed with insurgents at the Palma Catholic Church on 02 April. Soldiers managed to control the church later that day, according to military sources. Sporadic shooting was reported meanwhile in the nearby areas.

On 03 April, Mozambique's daily COVID-19 positivity rate fell to below five percent. Over the past 24 hours, 1,753 people were tested for the coronavirus that causes Covid-19, and 82 were positive which gives a rate of 4.7 percent. This marks the lowest positivity rate this year.

Tanzania authorities stated that they have no information about Mozambique refugees fleeing into the country.  In addition,  they said that the Tanzanian security forces are "ready to face and control any kind of threat", following the attack in Palma, Mozambique on 24 March. The UNHCR meanwhile said that around 600 Mozambican asylum seekers had been deported back to Mozambique in recent days. In response Tanzania denies any report that they sent back the asylum seekers.

No terror attack targeted the Afungi LNG site over the weekend, though insurgents were relatively close to the camp between 01-03 April.  Note that some sources over the weekend had reported insurgents had effectively surrounded the LNG camp, though this was later reported to be false.

A person was killed while three others were injured in a road accident involving one vehicle in Malanga, Maputo on the afternoon of 02 April. The vehicle reportedly crashed between the barriers of the bridge.

The Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM) has not been able to hold a conference due to the COVID-19 restrictions. The election of the new party president will take place during the said conference, following the death of their leader and Beira City Mayor Daviz Simango last February.
An insurgent was arrested in the town of Ancuabe on 02 April. Three other insurgents in parts of Acuabe and Metuge were arrested on the same day.
A suspected insurgent with machetes from his possession was arrested in Sunate, Ancuabe on 02 April.
Two insurgents were arrested in Metuge District on 02 April. No further details related to this arrest are currently available.

Militants on speedboats launched an attack on Nagulue, north of Mucojo and Pangane on 03 April. A person was kidnapped while food and fuel were stolen. Reports stated that a person was killed in the attack.

Militants on speedboats launched an attack on Nagulue, north of Mucojo and Pangane on 03 April. A person was kidnapped while food and fuel were stolen. Reports stated that a person was killed in the attack.

Air France announced on 05 April that it would begin operating a new twice a week flight between Paris and Maputo.  Flights from Paris to Maputo will be offered on Sunday and Thursday, while flights from Maputo to Paris will be offered Monday and Friday.  These flights will begin from 20 June.

Family members of missing individuals throughout the week continued to wait at Pemba Airport , and requested help in locating survivors from Palma. Several survivors who arrived at Pemba on 3 April stated that there are still more individuals stranded in Palma.  More than 24,000 people have reportedly massed outside of the Afungi LNG Camp.

Border officials announced the reduction of people crossing at the Ressano Garcia border on 5 April. Many travelers stated that the high cost of COVID testing is the reason for this downturn in border crossings.  Just under 27,000 people crossed the Ressano Garcia border in and out of Mozambique during the Easter period.

Sources reported on 05 April that 11,000 people were displaced outside of Palma District due to the battle for Palma. 20 percent of these IDPs were in Pemba, while others were in Montepuez, Nangade, and Mueda areas of Cabo Delgado.
The Mozambique military reiterated that soldiers were in control of Palma as of Monday.  DAG founder Lionel Dyck however also on Monday said it was "unlikely" soldiers had fully retaken Palma.

Local sources stated that a large number of insurgents reportedly “disappeared” or withdrew from Palma on 4 April, according to military sources.  Some insurgents are believed to have been killed, though a significant number of the group that attacked Palma remain at large.

Local sources stated that Pemba is “full” and at 90% of new arrivals are taken in by family or relatives living in the city. Other displaced individuals were reported to be living at schools, hotels, makeshift tented camps, and stadium in the area. UNCHR stated that around 690,000 IDPs have been displaced since 2017 and Pemba is reported to be hosting over 200,000 IDPs.

A local group stated that Palma is “destroyed” and cannot be returned to normalcy even if the security forces have secured the town. Locals are being transported to Pemba as security forces declared Palma safe.

The Macossa District PRM commander was accused of corruption during a trial at a judicial court in Barue on 5 April. PRM commander Matimbe was previously tried for the same charges in past years. Matimbe was previously detained for the suspected illegal release of poachers.

The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) stated that several commercial establishments were involved in a scam of selling sewage water claiming it to be cooking oil in Nampula. INAE stated that there was no evidence from the stores where the products were bought.

Security forces are reportedly gathering and transporting IDPs in bush areas around Palma to Quitunda near Afungi, on 4 April. Two locals stated that both the Quitunda and the Total precinct were safe. Helicopters were also reported to have been deployed to search and transport IDPs hiding in the bush areas.

Around 3591 IDPs were reportedly have been received by the National Institute for Disaster Management (INGD) as of 05 April. 43 flights and four ship journeys were used to transport the IDPs since the Palma attack began on 24 March. The IDPs were currently sheltered at five centers in the city and among the homes of friends and relatives. Among the IDPs were 669 are children and 529 are women.
Around 50,000 total displaced individuals were reported in Montepuez on 2 April; this includes 400 new arrivals.

The Ministry of Health announced 108 new COVID cases and no deaths in Mozambique on 5 April. This is the second consecutive day without deaths in the country. Total cases have increased to 68,227 while recoveries have increased to 57,234 after 110 new recoveries were reported.

Security forces announced on 05 April that locals are slowly returning to Palma. Security forces are conducting a screening process as to prevent the entry of insurgents hiding with civilians. The screening was also to allow the return of civilians in the district HQ.
Local sources stated that several local residents were suspected to have collaborated with the insurgents during the attack in Palma.

The Executive Board of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) announced on 5 April that Mozambique would be given a debt relief extension. The extension was to free up any financial resources to assist the country.

The Japanese government announced that it would provide 92 million meticais as a form of debt relief to Mozambique on 5 April. This comes as Japan has suspended the payment by Mozambique of clearing out their debt of 1.3 million USD.
Displaced people from Cabo Delgado are experiencing hunger brought about by the drought in Mutchessane, Zambezia. Officials stated that the daily support is not enough for everyone.

Cabo Delgado Governor Valige Tauabo arrived in Palma on Monday, 05 April. Tauabo stated that the government is hoping that locals can return to their homes within three days. The military announced the town was cleared of insurgents the day before.

Locals stated that sporadic gunfire occurred during the visit of the Cabo Delgado governor in Palma on 5 April. A media crew covering the aftermath of the attack is Palma were "hurried" out of Palma along with Governor Tauabo shortly after this incident.

The National Operational Emergency Center announced that it required 41 million meticais for funding to assist terror victims displaced by the Palma assault. The money was to assist 30,000 IDPs affected by the insurgency conflict. The financial assistance would reportedly provide food, medication, hygiene materials for a months’ worth of supplies.

Two policemen were detained for being part of several crimes in Matutuine District, south of Maputo city, on the morning of 6 April.  The two men were in possession of two firearms allegedly used in robberies by a gang of criminals.

Media reports said that 100 former British SAS soldiers were currently in Nacala to conduct training of the Mozambican military. Local sources stated that Burnham Global has obtained a contract to train the Mozambican army. This comes as previous reports stated that armored vehicles and aircrafts were purchased from Paramount group, a South African company.
Local sources stated on 6 April that a Zimbabwean national identified as Celestino Joaquim Taluza was still missing in the aftermath of the Palma attack.

Regional Leaders of the SADC are set to conduct a meeting this Thursday, 8 April in Maputo, to discuss the insurgency in Cabo Delgado and support for the Mozambican government. The meeting will also be a double summit between the SADC presidents and security members. The meeting is expected to lead to a double troika summit with a possibility of holding another meeting in Mozambique.

The National Institute of Health (INS) officials announced that 78% of COVID deaths in Mozambique occurred over a short period in 2021. INS stated that in 95 days the pandemic killed 616 individuals. The pandemic remains fatal for individuals over the age of 60 years old with 4.2 percent fatality rate. While 50-59 were noted with a 1.3 percent fatality rate.  Covid cases and fatalities declined in late March and into April.
Media reports on 06 April said an insurgent presence was reported near Namacande/Muidumbe.  A journalist, Fernando Lima, said in an interview that insurgents controlled the area.

Armed suspects at around 1000hrs in Chimoio robbed two Bengali nationals of 1.940 million meticais just after the two men exited a local bank.  The suspects approached the victims, fired a shot in the air from an AK-47, stole the money, and then fled the scene in a waiting vehicle.  Police were reportedly patrolling nearby areas but failed to stop the robbery.
Local sources stated that 1,000 displaced individuals from Palma have fled to Tanzania seeking asylum but were not allowed to enter the country.

Four co-defendants of the hidden debts case were released after being bailed out for a total of 11,136,000 meticais. The defendants were Manuel Renato Matusse, Maria Moiane, Sergio Namburete, and Zulficar Ali Esmail Ahmad. While Fabiao Mabunda, still remains in jail.
NGOs stated that Pemba can’t cope with additional displaced people. The increase in IDPs may expose Pemba to increased crime and exposure to COVID.
Local recovered the body of a newborn at a garbage dump in Novo area of Quelimane.  The baby was reportedly asphyxiated before being dumped in the area.

An intelligence analysis company issued a report this week that forecasts that insurgents would conduct an attack targeting Pemba in the next 6 months if the current security situation does not improve. The report also stated that the attack in Palma is the largest carried attack by the insurgents. This analysis also said Mtwara in Tanzania could also be targeted in the near future.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) announced that Mozambique is waiving a financial support program. Before the pandemic, Maputo had expressed interest for a support program, but did not seek this support during recent sessions with the IMF.

RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade said in a speech on 06 April that President Nyusi was minimizing the insurgent attack in Palma. Momade stated President Felipe Nyusi is more concerned with the natural gas projects than the humanitarian welfare of the displaced individuals in Palma. RENAMO condemned the actions of the government and demanded that the government should activate all its mechanisms to assist the IDPs and locals of Palma. Momade has also called on the government to request for international support to combat the ongoing insurgency.

Local sources stated that the Mozambique currency is still performing well after the metical increased by 14 percent against the USD since the start of February. Mining activity gained traction as excess dollar liquidity was reported in the market.  Mozambique's currency is the best performing in the world since the beginning of February.

Police arrested a suspected illegal miner in possession of two 10kg bags filled garnet stones who was stopped while traveling along National Road Number 1 near Nampula on 4 April. The suspect confessed that the stones were only suspected to be worth 120 meticais per kg.  He had reportedly gotten the stones in Nangade district in an illegal mining operation.

Police arrested a suspected illegal miner in possession of two 10kg bags filled garnet stones who was stopped while traveling along National Road Number 1 near Nampula on 4 April. The suspect confessed that the stones were only suspected to be worth 120 meticais per kg.  He had reportedly gotten the stones in Nangade district in an illegal mining operation.

Several IDPs stated this week that they don’t feel safe even in Mueda because it’s too close to insurgent controlled areas. The IDPs stated that travelling to Montepuez is more safe due to the distance from the conflict.
Insurgent attacked three villages near Muidumbe on or around 24 March, as the attack on Palma began.  Other details regarding these incidents are currently unavailable.
Insurgents are reported to have recently re-occupied the "Syria Camp", a mobile camp along the Messalo River which has long served as one of the group's primary bases.
Local sources reported that an insurgent training camps were reported to be operating near Diaca and Ntchinga on 7 April.  Insurgents reportedly used these camps to train for the assault on Palma.
Local sources reported that an insurgent training camps were reported to be operating near Diaca and Ntchinga on 7 April.  Insurgents reportedly used these camps to train for the assault on Palma.
Local source stated that 42 South Africans and 2 British nationals were being flown to Maputo from Pemba.  This group was reported to have been caught up in the assault on Pemba.

A survivor of the Palma attack stated that children suspected to be between ages 9-12 were used in attack by disguising them as security forces. The man also said insurgents had worn Rapid Intervention Force Uniforms, and wore red sashes on their heads to differentiate themselves from security forces.
The Rapid Intervention Unit on 05 April was reported to be conducting operations clearing the route towards Afungi. The road towards Afungi could be “re-opened at any time”, local media reported.

In a speech delivered on 07 April, President Nyusi said that Mozambican forces had retaken Palma, but also said "we do not intend to proclaim victory".  Nyusi also said his government had told the international community the "needs" to fight against terrorism, saying Maputo and its partners were assessing the country's "shortcomings" though the fight should still be led by Mozambique to preserve its "sense of sovereignty".  He also said his government would modernize, equip, and train security forces to defeat the insurgency, and announced the convening of the National Defense Council for a discussion on the insurgency.  Nyusi also said the war would not be won by "military means" saying employment must be provided for young people who were joining the insurgency.  This speech came just ahead of an SADC summit on the insurgency set to be held in Maputo on Thursday.

President Nyusi in an address to the nation on the night of 05 April announced that Mozambique would extend the curfew to all provincial capitals in the country, and that the curfew would be maintained in the Greater Maputo Area.  The curfew hours have been adjusted from 2100hrs  - 0400hrs daily to 2200hrs - 0400hrs daily.  This new measure will take effect from 06 April.  All other anti-COVID measures will remain in place for a further 21 days.

Telecommunications company Vodacom was reported to be conducting operations to restore communications in Palma area on 06 April. This comes as local sources reported that it has been four days since the last insurgent attack in the area and the road between Palma and Afungi is being cleared.
Mozambican special forces detained three suspected insurgents while clearing abandoned residences in Palma on 7 April. One of the insurgents were wearing civilian clothing to infiltrate the town.
DAG's contract with the government reportedly ended as of 6 April. The end of their was confirmed as their last flight missions were conducted on Friday, 2 April.

Local sources stated that around 23,000 IDPS are reported to have no access to water and food in Quitunda as of 7 April. No details were specified how the government intends to resolve the lack of supplies in the area. Local sources said that there was no evidence that the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction is providing supplies to the locals in the area. A campaign was conducted in Pemba to gather funds and provide food for the large groups of IDPs in this area.

President Nyusi called for a meeting of defense and security council on 7 April.  Nyusi ordered the SDS to analyze the current situation in Cabo Delgado. He stated that the combat must be led by the Mozambicans and that the international community should respect the country's sovereignty.

CRISIS in Zimbabwe Coalition (CiZC) called on the SADC to intervene in the ongoing insurgency in Mozambique. The CiZC demanded that the SADC troika devise a strategy to take on the insurgency in Mozambique.

Local sources stated that 500 of 3,000 classrooms damaged/destroyed by cyclones in Sofala since 2019 have been rehabilitated. More than 300,000 students reportedly are without classrooms since 2019. Several classrooms still remained without roofs and students are dismissed by noon due to the intense heat.

Local sources stated that a number of military leaders in Cabo Delgado are discontented due to the diversion of supplies to elite civilians in Pemba from their troops. Unconfirmed reports meanwhile stated that several military officials have sold information regarding security positions in Cabo Delgado.

The Ministry of Health announced 3 new COVID deaths and 65 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 6 April. The total cases have increased to 68,292. Daily recoveries were recorded at 692. 26 of the new cases were from Maputo city, 19 from Zambezia, 9 from Nampula, three from Cabo Delgado, two from Manica, one for Sofala, one for Gaza, and one for Inhambane.
The UN agencies stated on 7 April that they do not have access to the Palma area or to areas along the border with Tanzania where at least 1,000 refugees fled from the Palma attack.
The UNHCR stated that 1 million IDPs could be displaced in Cabo Delgado by June.  UNHCR spokesman Babar Baloch stated that around 700,000 IDPs were reported in the Cabo Delgado province to date.
Tanzanians are reportedly calling for the Tanzanian government to retrieve their family members in Palma area who were displaced after the insurgent assault on the town.

The Democratic Alliance (DA) called on the SADC to deploy military forces in Cabo Delgado to combat the insurgency. DA claimed that only military intervention is way to stop the violence in the province and restore security. The South African opposition party previously said on 30 March that South Africa should send special forces to assist in evacuation efforts in Pemba.

The Ministry of Health announced that 139 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 7 April. No new deaths were reported. Three hospitalizations were recorded while 9,579 active cases still remain. 137 daily recoveries were also recorded.

President Nyusi announced that an investigation regarding the human rights violations by army has been launched. If the investigation was to find the soldiers guilty, they would be punished, according to the president. Nyusi said that human rights violations would not be tolerated.
Road traffic was allowed to pass through the fully reopened bridge over Limpopo River in Xai-Xai on 6 April. Trucks weighing 3.5 tonnes can now travel along this route.

The UN warned Tanzania not to turn away refugees after reports of TZ authorities had recently turned back 1000 Mozambican asylum who seekers attempted to cross the Mozambique-Tanzania border fleeing the assault on Palma.
Local sources stated that children had participated in the assault on Palma between 24 March - 04 April.  Some of the children carried weapons and wore red scarves around their heads.

Diocese of Pemba Latifo Fonseca stated that insurgents have been recruiting children to conduct attacks in northern Mozambique. Fonseca said that several individuals who were kidnapped claimed that children were present at the insurgent camps. Fonseca raised concerns that the children were being trained with extremism and violence.

column4: The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) burned  700kg of narcotics in Nampula on 6 April. The narcotics were previously seized during operations from January to April. Officials stated that majority of the narcotics were cannabis, hashish, and heroin.

Teachers working in the villages of Miteda, Lutete and Namande of Muidumbe District spend their nights in Mueda due to insecurity in the area.  Government officials in the area also currently sleep in Mueda.  Militants are believed to hold Namacande and other villages in the district.

RENAMO military Junta leader, Mariano Nhongo in an interview on 08 April threatened to disrupt governance in central and northern Mozambique if the government refuses to negotiate. Nhongo also said that if the government continued to listen to "traitors", likely referring to mainstream RENAMO, it would be "burning time.   Nhongo also reiterated previous statements that a document which includes the requirements for the reintegration for him and his men were sent to the government on 2 October, 2020 and that he was still waiting for a response.  Nhongo also said a "time will come" when the group would "start our actions", saying his group was not currently launching attacks as it was waiting for a government response.
Local sources stated that the road between Cuamba to Malema remains in poor condition and in nearly unusable 8 April. Locals are still waiting for provincial officials to respond and repair the road.
Civil servants were reported on 05 April to be fleeing the Nangade area in the wake of the Palma attack.
Local sources stated 7 April that a journalist abducted in Palma one year ago remains missing. Ibraimo Mbaruco went missing after being surrounded by soldiers.

Mozambique's Volunteer Anonymous Solidarity Movement have assisted in locating people displaced by Palma attack. The organization has created a list of more than 4,000 IDPs and a communication system used by both the volunteers and IDPs to locate families. No specific details are currently available as to how many IDPs have been reunited with their families, though efforts to locate missing individuals continues as of 08 April

Reliable sources reported that a number of insurgents were present near Bilibiza, Mahate, and Quissanga town on 8 April. A local source reported that the insurgents have occupied these towns for several weeks; this occupation is not confirmed though at least a small insurgent group is believed to be currently present in the district.

Reliable sources reported that a number of insurgents were present near Bilibiza, Mahate, and Quissanga town on 8 April. A local source reported that the insurgents have occupied these towns for several weeks; this occupation is not confirmed though at least a small insurgent group is believed to be currently present in the district.

Reliable sources reported that a number of insurgents were present near Bilibiza, Mahate, and Quissanga town on 8 April. A local source reported that the insurgents have occupied these towns for several weeks; this occupation is not confirmed though at least a small insurgent group is believed to be currently present in the district.

Clashes between security forces and militants were reported near Tanganhane village, near Quissanga, on or around 24 March as the assault on Palma began. No further information on this incident is currently available.

Security forces stated on 8 April that a forensic team should be mobilized to identify corpses in Palma. Those waiting to be identified include 12 people killed outside of the Amarula hotel who are suspected to have been expats. 1

The SADC concluded a meeting in Maputo on Thursday, calling for a "collective response" against insurgent attacks in Cabo Delgado, calling these attacks a "threat to the entire southern African region".  The SADC Troika Summit said it would deploy a "technical team" immediately to Cabo Delgado to assess the "gaps" of the Mozambican security forces and assess the situation in the province as a while.  The technical team is likely to include some military elements, and the SADC appears to be strongly considering a military intervention of some form in Mozambique.

Kenmare announced on 08 April that they would resettle 3,000 people in June in Moma district of Nampula province. The resettlement was part of the social responsibility program of the company. The project was expected to cost 4 million USD and last for five years.

An NGO on 08 April reported stated that there are now 772,000 IDPs across Cabo Delgado, displaced by the ongoing insurgents. A majority of the IDPs are living at temporary centers with poor conditions.

President Nyusi stated that he had ordered security forces to continue operations and to fully Palma. Nyusi stated that the government has already requested assistance from the international community to support Mozambique. The continuation of security operations in Palma will allow the total restoration of order, security, and peace in the province.

Security forces were reported on 08 April to be escorting to and from Mueda to the Muidumbe district villages along the western Muidumbe district border as insurgents reportedly still control most of the district.
Local sources stated that Ibo island has reportedly been locked down since the Palma attack, with security forces stationed on the island preventing boats carrying IDPs from landing in the area.

Maputo authorities issued an order for firewood and charcoal vendors near the Limpopo railway in Mavalane to vacate or be forced to be vacated. Officials stated that the vendors have been in the area for a while and have posed a risk due to the traveling trains along the railway.
The UN announced that the IDPs in Palma have increased by 12,800 individuals, of which 43% were children.
Security forces have prevented any national private media to conduct media coverage of the Palma attack, local media stations reported on 08 April.

President Mnangagwa of Zimbabwe on 08 April said after the SADC summit that the summit had "agreed that the SADC Force should be resuscitated and capacitated immediately so that it can intervene".  This language was not included in the Summit's official communications, but does indicate SADC leaders are united in supporting some form of military intervention in Cabo Delgado.

Militants who attacked and occupied Pangane on 03 April were reported by locals to have either threatened to occupy the village until the end of Ramadan, or to occupy Macomia by the end of Ramadan, on 12 May.

Militants who attacked and occupied Pangane on 03 April were reported by locals to have either threatened to occupy the village until the end of Ramadan, or to occupy Macomia by the end of Ramadan, on 12 May.
A shooting  was reported in Expansao area of Pemba on 1 April. No casualties were reported. Locals fled from the area of the incident. No further detail on this incident is currently available.

A 40 man police unit trained under the DAG were deployed to Palma on 27 March. This force was reported to have engaged insurgents with some success on the western outskirts of the town during the battle for Palma.

Mozambican Health officials announced that 25 health professionals have died due to COVID as of 9 April. Ministry of Health officials stated that 3,270 health professionals were infected by the virus, 440 of which were doctors.

The African Union announced that it suspended plans to acquire AstraZeneca vaccines due to the global shortages of the vaccine. The vaccine was the cheapest of all global vaccines offered at $3 a shot.

Local sources stated that thousands of civilians are still displaced outside of Palma as of 30 March but are currently “trapped” due to the insurgent presence in the bush areas around the Palma.  Around 23,000 IDPs also are still sheltering around the Afungi LNG Camp, awaiting evacuation.

Local militias thwarted an attack launched by around eight insurgents in Novo Cabo Delgado village, Administrative Post of Chai, Macomia on 08 April. Insurgents already looted food and other goods before the militias engaged them in a gun battle. Three of the insurgents were killed and their weapons were seized during the battle. A local militia was also killed. Reports suggest that two of the isnurgents were from Miangalewavillage in Muidumbe district.

Unexplained gunfire was reported in Mecufi on the afternoon of 09 April.  Rumors spread the incident was related to the insurgency, though reports later indicated it this was a criminal incident.
Sources reported on 09 April that there was a suspected insurgent activity in Metoro of Ancuabe District. This report has yet been confirmed.
Unconfirmed reported on 09 April stated that insurgents were arrested in the Silva Macua area of Ancuabe District.

A 35-yr-old man strangled his disabled nine-yr-old son to death in Rio das Pedras, Massinga on 05 April. The victim's body was recovered on 07 April after his grandfather reported him missing. The suspect was arrested on 08 April.

On 08 April, security forces arrested a 35-yr-old man for killing his son in Rio das Pedras, Massinga. The crime happened on 05 April. The suspect claimed that he killed the victim because he was possessed by evil spirits.

Niassa Province launched an animal vaccination campaign on 10 April against various diseases. The nationwide campaign, which covers 1,376,831  dogs, cats, cattle and chickens, is expected to run until December 2021.

The Ministry of Health announced 72 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 10 April. The total cases have increased to 68,578. No COVID-19 related death reported, for the fourth time this week. 47 people have recovered while 54 were hospitalized due to the disease.

A possible insurgent attack may take place in Quitunda in the next few weeks, recent analysis produced on 11 April warned. In addition, the insurgents will attempt to seek control again of Palma to extend their area of control according to this analysis. Pemba will also be exposed to possible militant attacks as soon as the security forces leaves Pemba.

Pemba will also be exposed to possible militant attacks as soon as the security forces leaves Pemba.

Sources reported on 11 April that an armed attack was carried out by unidentified gunmen at a police station in Caprizange, Moatize district, in Tete. RENAMO dissidents were likely responsible for this attack.

Reports indicated that two gunmen shot at a vehicle on a road between Pemba and Chiuba on 11 April.  One vehicle was initially reported to be a UNICEF vehicle though was later reported to have been a civilian car.  Police are investigating the incident, which is believed to be related to criminality, rather than the insurgency.  Other reports indicated soldiers in the area were responsible for this incident, having fired on a car that drove near a military shooting range.

Vodacom voice and data connections in Alfungi remains intermittent as of 11 April. The telecommunications company reported on 06 April that operations were conducted to restore communications in Palma.
Vodacom voice connections in Quionga are working as of 11 April. The telecommunications company reported on 06 April that operations were conducted to restore communications in the area of Palma.

Vodacom voice and data connections in Palma were still not working as of 11 April. The incident came five days after the telecommunications company reported that operations were conducted to restore communications in Palma.

Authorities announced on 11 April that a sanitation fee will be included in the water bill in Tete City starting June 2021. The decision was made to improve the sanitation and drainage in the municipality.
The French Embassy in Mozambique classified Pemba as a 'red zone' since 01 April, after insurgents attacked Palma on 24 March.

Montepuez Ruby Mining (MRM) announced the death of two illegal miners following the collapse of an illegally dug mine around the MRM concession area on the morning of 05 April. One of the victims from Nangade and the other from Mocimboa da Praia district.

Montepuez Ruby Mining (MRM) announced the death of an illegal miner following the collapse of an illegally dug mine around the MRM concession area on 02 April. The victim was a 24-year-old from Namialo, Nampula. Another man managed to escape without any injury.

Security forces arrested a 48-yr-old suspected buyer of illegal rubies within the MRM concession area in Namanhumbir, Montepuez on 31 March. The suspect, a Guinean national, was arrested while supervising illegal mining operations.

Price increases of goods and services rose about 5.76 percent in March versus March 2020. This marked as the biggest rise in prices nationwide since 2019.  Prices in Beira increased the most in the country at 6.96 percent, followed by the city of Nampula with about 6.05 percent and the city of Maputo with 5.19 percent.

Sources on 09 April reported that over one million dollars were stolen in safes and ATMs at the branches of Millennium Bim, Standard Banking and Banco Commercial e de Investimentos in Palma during the 24 March attack. The robbery was allegedly carried out during the first three days of the attack, 24 until 26 March. The recent robbery can serve as was of funding the terrorist group for future attacks.

Mozambican Police and Army were accused of looting several facilities in Palma after the insurgents retreated.  This looting likely occured on or around 04 April as insurgents withdrew from the area.  A contractor claimed that the Amarula Hotel was undamaged and not attacked however, the restaurant and rooms were looted. Stolen mattresses were found stacked outside a police station. Authorities is yet to comment on the accusations.

Authorities on 09 April ordered Chinese mining company, DingSheng against destroying the dunes off the coast of Chongoene. The company had started to open a road connecting N1road to the coast and was removing dunes in order to build a warehouse as they intend to transport minerals from Chibuto to the coast. However, the company's action was not authorized and considered as illegal.

The United States warned Mozambique of risk of contamination of explosives after Mozambique declared the country was free of anti-personnel mines on 2015. The local government should have a sustainable cleaning capacity in place to assess and identify parameters of the minefields. The extensive contamination will hinder the return of IDPs to their hometowns and also obstruct economic development. From 1992 to 2015, US provided Mozambique 56 million dollars assistance as they support demining activities in the country.

A new study by the Observatorio do Mundo Rural says that insurgents in Cabo Delgado may be trafficking women and girls abroad, saying the group abdducted "hundreds of women" when it captured Mocimboa da Praia.  Women who recently escaped insurgent camps say that children and adolescents were trained "doing military training and fighting machetes".  The study also says women who escaped the insurgent camps describe the insurgents as well organized, with foreign fighters, a "traveled Mozambican middle class" and youthes from Cabo Delgado angry at the state.
