column4: Banco de Mozambique announced on 11 April that SIE Xmoney Mozambique Lda is not authorized to conduct fundraising operations following an investigation which showed that the latter has been practicing financial pyramid shemes and has been making false promises on a certain interest or profit to be gained by investing with them. Authorities warned the public to refrain from engaging in illegal and fraudulent contracts.

The Ministry of Health announced 40 new COVID cases and one COVID-related death in Mozambique on 09 April. The total number cases have increased to 68,506 while the death toll is at 789. The country has a total of 9,577 active cases and 58 people are hospitalized.

The Ministry of Health announced 180 new COVID cases and two COVID-related deaths in Mozambique on 11 April. Most of the new cases were registered in the provinces of Nampula with 76 new cases and Zambezia with 59. The total cases in the country have increased  to 68,758 while the death toll is at 791.

According to the International Organization for Migration’s (IOM) there were 14,576 people displaced from Palma have arrived in Nangade, Mueda, Montepuez, and Pemba as of 09 April. 44% of these IDPs are children and were displaced from Palma following the 24 March insurgent attacks in the disrict. Continuous assistance across the province by both humanitarian agencies and local government  werer reported.

A man was found beheaded on Sunday in Palma, police sources said.  The man had fled Palma during the assault on the town but returned after the end of the battle.  He reportedly discovered large caches of rice, flour, and cooking oil had been stored in his home during his absence.  He reported the incident to security forces, who then seized these supplies.  The man was later discovered to have been murdered.  Insurgents clandestinely still active in the town are suspected to be behind the incident.

President Nyusi called for “stronger border cooperation” in response to the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. President Nyusi stated during the double troika summit that the strengthening of the borders should be part of the means to resolve the ongoing insurgency.

A professor at King's college said recently that there is "formal covert communications" between ISIS's core group and the Cabo Delgado insurgents, also saying there had been "strategic silence" over the past 5 months in order not to attract attention to the group as it planned the attack on Palma.

Sources stated that there is "clear evidence" that Mozambican fighters have been given military training from other Islamist insurgents operating in the eastern Congo. This comes as reports of the shelling attacks have successfully targeted areas in Palma.

Police arrested a suspect in possession of two bags of garnet stones at a security checkpoint in Anchilo, east of Nampula, on 8 April. The suspect was coming from Ancuabe District to meet with a Chinese buyer.

Police arrested a suspect in possession of two bags of garnet stones at a security checkpoint in Anchilo, east of Nampula, on 8 April. The suspect was coming from Ancuabe District to meet with a Chinese buyer.
Local sources stated that two illegal miners died after an illegal mine collapsed in Montepuez on 5 April.

The National Migration Service (SENAMI) refused entry to 38 foreigners due to the lack of accommodation during operations between 27 March and 2 April. SENAMI stated that two lacked a working visa, three lacked a specific job description, three for the lack of subsistence and another with a forged passport.
Sources stated that the Spanish Embassy advised their employees in Pemba to relocate to Maputo in the aftermath of the Pemba attack.
The Ministry of Health announced 66 new COVID cases and 3 related deaths in Mozambique on 8 April. The total number of cases have risen to 68,466, while deaths have increased to 788.
Unidentified suspects raided a supply warehouse in Namiuta near Bilibiza on 6 March.
Additional security measures were reported to have been put in place on 13 April around supply warehouses in Namiuta.  This follows an incident in which a warehouse was looted in March.

The European Union will donated 7.9 million EUR as a humanitarian aid in response to the humanitarian crisis brought about by the insurgency in northern Mozambique. The financial aid was part of thee 24.5 million assistance for the Africa and Indian region.

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) announced on 8 April that around 14,000 IDPs have been displaced to Nangade, Mueda, Montepuez and Pemba. The organization has provided mental health and psychosocial support and protection assistance to more than 1,000 new IDPs as they were received at transit centers.  IDP numbers are increasing by the day, and thousands are still displaced in the Quitunda area, just outside of the Afungi LNG Camp.
The Ministry of Health announced one COVID death and 40 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 9 April.  Maputo city recorded 15 cases and 6 cases for Maputo province.

Several sources on 07 and 08 April reported that insurgents beheaded a group of 12 people just opposite the Amarula Hotel during the assault on Palma.  This incident reportedly occurred on 28 March.  A man believed to be a member of the security forces in an interview said that those killed had been "white" and were all foreigners, also saying he had "directed" the burial of the group, who are reportedly buried just outside of the hotel near the spot where they were killed.  The group's hands were allegedly bound before insurgents beheaded them.  One of the bodies was identified as a Zimbabwean man, Nyasha Mugwagwa. Mugwagwa worked for the hotel and a catering company.  Other sources have subsequently indicated that the other 11 people killed in the attack were Mozambican nationals.

The National Defense and Security Council (CDNS) conducted a meeting to discuss the situation in Cabo Delgado on the morning of 9 April. The meeting discussed potential  security measures against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  The meeting headed by President Nyusi discussed that the collaboration with the CDNS must continue to create a condition to "eliminate the threats to national security on all fronts."

Security forces detained a suspect acting as a SERNIC agent in Maxaquene, south of Maputo City, on 7 April. The suspect charged 40,000 meticais to individuals wanting to enter the police academy in Matalane. He also confessed to working with another suspect, one of whom was reportedly a police officer.

Police arrested a suspect wanted for kidnapping a baby in Zambezia on the night of 8 April. The kidnapper abducted the child from Costa do Sol neighborhood of Maputo. The suspect was claimed to be a family friend.

Police arrested a suspect wanted for kidnapping a baby in Zambezia on the night of 8 April. The kidnapper abducted the child from Costa do Sol neighborhood of Maputo. The suspect was claimed to be a family friend.

Local sources stated that there were at least 87 dead in Palma, which included 7 expats who were identified as “whites” and 80 local Mozambicans. In addition 12 bodies were still to be identified near the Amarula Hotel. The source stated “no embassies have reported any of their citizens missing”.

The Aga Khan Foundation raised concerns regarding the situation in Cabo Delgado. The foundation officials stated that their presence in the province depends on the government ultimately taking the steps to confront the insurgency and secure the province.

The Center of Public Integrity (CIP) stated that the government has failed to support the victims of the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. CIP called the government to increase their budget to provide support for the IDPs. CIP stated that based on their research that IDPs outside the permanent reception areas in Cabo Delgado and Nampula were not receiving aid for the past two months.

Other telecommunication operators, Tmcel and Movitel, are still not operational in Palma. This comes as Vodacom has reportedly managed to restore telecommunication operations though these area still reportedly unstable in Palma itself.
The Ministry of Health announced that two new COVID deaths and 180 COVID cases in Mozambique on 11 April. The deaths were recorded in Maputo City and Nampula.

President Nyusi stated in a 12 April speech that journalists should not create media and disseminate incorrect and altered information. Nyusi claimed that the wrong information discourages the public and affects the development of the country.

Officials announced that around 2 million livestock would be vaccinated for diseases around Mozambique. This was to prevent disease outbreaks such as the foot-and-mouth disease, anthrax, brucellosis, lumpy skin disease, Newcastle fever, and rabies. The campaign was to start from Guija District in Gaza.
The WFP stated that 1 million people were facing severe hunger in northern Mozambique on 13 April.  The organization is appealing for $82 million to confront this hunger crisis.
Two vehicles collided with each other after one of the vehicles cut off a vehicle along the Circular Estrada in Maputo City at around 08:45 on 12 April. Around 40 civilians were injured.

On Tuesday 13 April, the Portuguese wife of a Mozambican businessman was reported kidnapped on Avenida Mao Tse Tung, outside the Consulate of Portugal, in Maputo at 1100hrs.  The victim’s husband is the owner of a hotel in the city.  According to witness testimony reported to the press, a black car circled the consulate 3 times, stopped after the victim exited the Consulate, then 2 men forced her into the car at gun point using a Kalashnikov type rifle.

The victim's wife and daughter were injured after the assailants shot her while she attempted to help her husband. Other sources claimed that the victim’s family were beaten and injured. Video filmed of the alleged incident from a nearby residence showed a group of people forcing an individual into a waiting car just outside another residence before driving away.

column4: Police have remained “on trail” of kidnappers and are searching for Indian-Mozambican businessman, Arvin Kumar in Maputo City on 13 April. The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) stated that the they have the vehicle make and the suspects' descriptions.

IDP evacuations from Palma to Pemba continued on the morning of 9 April. 15 IDPs arrived at around 10:40. The IDPs stated that the current state of Palma remains terrible. The IDPs stated that people are still going hungry and are still not safe in the area.

The Mozambican government announced that 7 billion meticais is needed to manage the displaced people from Cabo Delgado. The Institute for Disaster Management (INGD) announced that the financial aid was to provided better food, shelter and education conditions. The funding as well was to re-launch the private sector and encourage small activities to generate income for displaced populations.

Former Pemba Bishop Luiz Fernando Lisboa stated that during an interview that he was indirectly threatened by the Mozambican government for speaking out about situation in Cabo Delgado. Bishop Lisboa stated that the government threatened to expel him from the country, and government supporters issued death threats against him.

Total reportedly closed the Air Traffic Control Tower at Afungi preventing air evacuations in Afungi during the evening of 12 April. The closure prevented the activation of lights of the airstrip. 8 journalists were stranded due to the “exclusion” environment due to travel organizers and the closure of the Air Traffic Control Tower.  This move was reportedly made due to insecurity in the area.

A group of four armed men armed with guns stole 80,000 meticais from a gas station in Nhamatanda on the night of 12 April. The suspects stole the gun from a guard and assault him before stealing the money.

Security forces recovered the body of a woman who was beaten to death and arrested her husband inside their residence in Dondo on 13 April. The suspect was reportedly a policeman who have disputes with the victim during the past few days. Security forces stated that the suspect killed the victim on 8 April.

Security forces recovered the body of a woman who was beaten to death and arrested her husband inside their residence in Dondo on 13 April. The suspect was reportedly a policeman who have disputes with the victim during the past few days. Security forces stated that the suspect killed the victim on 8 April.
Police officials refuted reports of a possible insurgent attacks in Pemba. The police stated that the reports were issued to create fear and terror to the municipalities in Pemba.

The Mozambican military says large portion of Palma's population “kidnapped” during battle of Palma and that death toll from attack still being determined. Security forces stated that the people were abducted during their escape from Palma. Brigadier Vidigal also recently stated that 35 insurgents have been killed during the battle for Palma.
Local sources stated that a soldier randomly fired shots in Metuge District on the evening of 12 April. No casualties were reported. The soldier was arrested following the incident.
Local sources stated that a soldier randomly fired shots in Metuge District on the evening of 12 April. No casualties were reported. The soldier was arrested following the incident.
Insurgents were reported to set fire to the hotel facilities after stealing valuables and ransacking the Hotel Palma on 25 March.

Road officials announced new construction works on National Road Number 1 (EN1) in Inhambane on 13 April. The construction will build three toll gates along the Highway. The National Road Administration stated that roads will be properly maintained with the toll payment of drivers.
The Ministry of Health announced that three new COVID deaths and 79 new cases in Mozambique on 12 April. 500 new recoveries were also reported within the past 24 hours.

Local sources stated that Palma has been nearly abandoned and those who have stayed stated that they have “nowhere to go.” This comes as many IDPs have been barred from entering the Afungi Camp for evacuation as part of strict security protocols.
Locals have reported a “wave of thefts” in Palma after the security situation recovered. The crimes were suspected to have been conducted by members of the community and security forces.

Security forces continue to be deployed around Palma area, along Palma-Afungi road, and Quitunda area, local media who visited the area reported this week. Security forces were also escorting vehicles travelling between the resettlement area and Palma.
Public transport vehicles was reported to be operating regularly between Palma and Afungi on 13 April. The transports were escorted by security forces.

The Rural Observatory (OMR) released a study stating that women and children were used as part of the strategy during the attack in Palma. OMT also stated that the women recruited in the attacks are victims of sexual violence and were forced to become wives of the insurgents. The women were tasked to perform logistical functions for the insurgents. While the children selected were around their pre-teens who were trained with machetes.

Police arrested two suspects who were involved with the armed attack on 11 April at a police station in Caprizange, Moatize district, in Tete. Police said the attackers were not "terrorists" but "oppurtunists".
Security forces arrested four suspects for forging COVID test results in Maputo City on 14 April. The suspects would sell the results for 3000 to 5000 meticais.
The Ministry of Health announced that 57 new COVID cases and no new deaths in Mozambique on 14 April. 71 daily recoveries were reported. Maputo recorded 17 new cases and Zambezia with 14.

The Mozambican police Commander-in-Chief Bernardino Rafael announced on 14 April that security forces should continue operations to search for RENAMO dissidents in central Mozambique. The operations were to allow the dissidents to join the DDR process. These operations are meant to pressure dissidents to join the DDR process.  He also said security forces were allowing free movement in the Muchungue, Inchope, and Caia areas of the N1 Road.
The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) closed 60 gyms for violating safety precautions against COVID on 11 April. The gyms were reported to grounds for cultivating COVID-19.

A part of the National Road N12 between Nacala-Porto and Nampula 3km near the Nacala Police Security post in Matibane district collapsed causing a trailer truck to be stranded on the afternoon of 14 April. The National Road Administration (ANE), stated that that intense rainfall has caused the road collapse. Drivers are advised to use the Matibane-Mussoril-Naguema-Monapo route

column4: Several sources reported that from 1200hrs into the night, communications were down in the Mueda area.   Several unconfirmed reports said insurgents had then attacked Mueda at around 2130hrs.  Sources later reportede that no attack had occurred in Mueda and the area was quiet , while a journalist who had initially reported the Meuda attack said that district officials did not confirm the incident, and that Movitel had issued a statement saying a fiber optic tower was down in the area.  The journalist also said there were unverified reports of an insurgent attack at the village of Cheba, 10-20 kms from Mueda.  Other sources reported unconfirmed insurgent activity in the Gananga area, west of Mocimboa da Praia port.

Four armed men abducted the Michal Nathoobai, son of a prominent businessman at around 1900hrs on the terrace of the Quinta do Nico restaurant  in Quelimane on 15 April, local sources reported.  The Michel was reportedly dragged from a restaurant into a car by the kidnappers.  Witnesses claimed that the attackers also stole mobile phones from several of the clients, and immediately fled with the victim.

Several sources on the evening of 15 April reported that insurgents had attacked a former combatants' barracks approximately 10kms outside of Palma on the road to Pundanhar.  The attack reportedly began at around 1800hrs on Thursday night.  No further details on the attack are currently available.

President Nyusi announced that hee would be travel to Nampula to inaugurate the the first industrial unit of the SUSTENTA program. The program was to finance several production of agricultural products, specifcally corn flour. The travel will also include the vist to the Small Commercial and Emergent Farmer (PACE) program.

Displaced people continue to arrive at the Quintunda village near Afungi Camp waiting for evacuation on the evening of Wednesday, 14 March. IDPs at Pemba stated that locals are stranded due to the lack of money to pay for the transport to Pemba.

The Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA) President Vuma stated that the kidnappings of businessmen and their relatives are hindering the investment sector of the country. The kidnappings is giving Mozambique an image instability due to the crime and terror causing the lack of investments. Vuma stated that foreign investors are giving up due to the fear of kidnapping and insecurity.

The Ministry of Health announced that around 216,771 would be innoculated as part of the second phase of the vaccination starting 19 April. The second phase of the vaccination campaign will include health training students on undergradaute courses, remaining diabetic patients from the first phase, immunosuppressant therapy patients , patients with chronic kidney failure and/ or undergoing haemodialysis.

The US Department of State issued a health travel advisory level 4 calling for individuals not to travel to Mozambique due to COVID-19. US citizens were advised to take caution due to the present health issues, terrorism, and crime. The Embassy in Maputo stated that warned US citizens not to travel to Cabo Delgado province due to terrorism. The Embassy also stated to reconsider travel to Pemba, along roads of EN1 and EN6 in Sofala and Manica provinces due to insecurity.

The Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM) announced that they were waiting for a response from the Ministry of Justice to elect a new party leader. The party has submitted the request for the gathering of their national council to host 150 individuals.

The Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA) President Vuma stated that Mozambique has lost 209 million USD and closure of 1,110 companies due to the attacks in northern Mozambique. Vuma stated that the loses amount as follows: 100 million USD was from the agricultural production, 95 million USD from the physical capital, and 14 million USD from the cash flow from value chains.

Defense Minister Jaime Neto stated that the insurgent attacks would not jeopardize the implementation of the national gas exploration projects in Cabo Delgado. Jaime Neto was at the Operational Theater preparing for conditions to enable the recovery of Palma and resumption of working operations by businesses.

RENAMO Antonio Muchanga accused SDS forces are also afraid of the insurgents that they fled during the attack on Palma. The RENAMO Deputy stated that security forces were not prepared to fight against the insurgents

Local sources stated that 32 employees working for a contractual company were quarantined in Eduardo Mondlane District of Pemba. The employees were transported to the area just hours before the insurgent attack in Palma. Four of the individuals were released and returned to their families in Nampula. The 32 employees were later asked to return to Cabo Delgado following the attack. Local sources stated  that the company they were under did not guarantee their safety and only one employee was given accomodation in Palma.
Local sources stated that reports of unexplained gunfire were heard near the town of Palma on the evening of 15 April.  No further info on this currently available.

The Ministry of Health announced 75 new COVID cases and no COVID deaths in Mozambique on 15 April. The cases were reported as follows: 34 in Maputo City, 13 in Maputo province, 3 in Gaza, 1 in Sofala, 1 in Manica, 1 in Tete, 7 in Zambezia, 10 in Nampula, and 5 in Niassa.
Sources stated that a Somali national identified as Abshii Nur was reported missing in Cabo Delgado since the Palma attack.

A National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) agent was sentenced for eight years in prison after a court hearing. The suspect was detained la\st September for the sexual assault of a 13-year old.

Police fired warning shots during a riot as protesters stoned a residence in Alto Molocue in Zambezia province on 15 April. Three civilians were killed and 11 were injured during the incident. Police stated that the riot started due to fake reports of children being kidnapped and held at the residence.

Police stated that the riot started due to fake reports of children being kidnapped and held at the residence.
The Ministry of Health announced that 3 new COVID deaths and 65 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 16 April. The total cases has increased to 69,067 and total deaths to 797.
Local sources stated that the road between Mecufi and Chiure were damaged due to heavy rainfall. The road damage has interrupted traffic in the area.

The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MADER), imposed an import ban on poultry coming from South Africa. The ban was due to the presence of avian influenza reported in Gauteng province of South Africa.

The National Statistics Institute (INE) stated that the annual inflation rose from 5.10 percent to 5.76 percent in March. This is the highest inflation rate in the country in the past three years. Moreover, the monthly inflation in March is 0.86 percent versus February with 1.34%, with emphasis on the price increase in the category of 'Food and non-alcoholic beverages'.

A source reported on 17 April that Zimbabwe discreetly deployed special forces troops to combat insurgents in Cabo Delgado. The special forces were allegedly sent to the country a week after the Palma attack.  This report remains unconfirmed.
The foreign ministers of the European Union (EU) were scheduled to meet on 19 April to discuss the situation in Cabo Delgado province.

The Ministry of Health announced one new COVID deaths and 67 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 17 April. The total COVID cases increased to 69,137 and total deaths to 798. A total of 19 people have recovered from the illness on the same day, which brought the country's number of recovery to 61,207.
On 17 April, Strong Live TV's Instagram account was reported to have been hacked.  No further details are available at this time.

The Ministry of Health announced 69 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 18 April. The total COVID cases have increased to 69,203 and total deaths remained at 798. 34 of the new cases were recorded in Maputo while 22 were recorded in Niassa province.

Mozambican Police Association (AMOPAIP) called on 17 April for officers intensify efforts in capturing members of Defense and Security Forces (SDS) allegedly collaborating with the Cabo Delgado terrorists. The statement came after security analysts revealed possible collaboration between the militants and security force elements, pointing out the accuracy and timing of the attacks which took place in Palma last month. An evidence of this alleged cooperation was the usage of government forces uniforms by the insurgents.

On 14 April, Minister of Works, Housing and Water Resources, Joao Machatine, announced that the construction of a bridge over the Limpopo River is expected to start this year. The bridge will connect the main village in the Mapai district to the Salane community, in Phafuri, Gaza province.

On 14 April, Total was reported to have terminated most of its agreements with its contractors for the Afungi LNG project. One of the affected contracts is for the "Afungi Camp Expansion", which relates to the building of the construction camp for 9500 workers.

A peacekeeping operation may not be the most effective response in dealing with insurgency in Mozambique, Hanna Tetteh, special representative of the UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres to the African Union (AU) and the head of the UN Office to the AU said. Teteh claimed the country can still try to use political processes to address some of the conflict's root causes.
A casino owner and coal mine employee were abducted in Benga near Moatize on 11 April. No other details are on this incident are currently available.

On 06 April, security forces arrested three people over their alleged connection to a weapons cache recovered in Palma. Four AKM rifles, four PKM machine guns, two 60mm mortar tubes, 20 rocket-propelled grenades, ammunition for AGS-17 grenade launcher and medical supplies were recovered.

As of 15 April, an estimated 11,104 individuals are being hosted at EPC de Quintuda in Quintuda, Palma. IDPs are still in need of urgent humanitarian assistance amid some assistance provided by the government.

Reports on 18 April stated that the number of children involved in child labor has grown significantly in Inhambane province. 29.5% of children from 7 to 9 years of age, 47.2% of 10 to 14 years of age and 23.2% of 15 to 17 years of age have experienced child labor. Inhambane ranks below the provinces of Zambezia, Tete and Nampula with the highest number of children involved in child labor.

A total of 20,497 people are expected to be immunized in Maputo City on 19 April as the second phase of COVID-19 immunization commenced. 216,771 people will be vaccinated nationwide.  Citizens who are over 60 years old with underlying health issues like diabetes and those who were immuno suppressed of the same age will also be part of the program. 38 teams composed of 152 technicians will immunize the target groups in all municipal districts of the city.

Authorities disclosed on 15 April that a total of 104 schools in Cabo Delgado Province have been destroyed by insurgent attacks. 168,639 pupils and 1,623 teachers were displaced from the province. Meanwhile,  194 schools in the province  have not been able to start the 2021 school year, due the lack of security in their area. Most affected by the attacks were Mocimboa da Praia, Palma, Quissanga and Muidumbe while Pemba, and Chiure and Montepuez districts were considered safest.

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) stated that 20,558 registered IDPs were recorded after the  attack on Palma as of 16 April. Significant increases in IDPs are continuously witnessed in Nangade, Mueda, Montepuez and Pemba districts. 43 percent of the registered IDPs were children. While 75% of the registered IDPs were living with foster families.

A fire razed a house along Marien Ngouibi Avenue of Maputo city on 19 April. Further information regarding the incident is not available at this time.

€250,000 worth of support will be provided by Portugal to fund non-governmental development organizations (NGDOs) projects in Cabo Delgado, authorities disclosed on 16 April. The support, coordinated by Camoes – Institute for Cooperation and Language, will be on top of the other support provided by Portuguese Government to Cabo Delgado.

Sources on 19 April reported that the Airports of Mozambique is on the edge of bankruptcy. The company suffered from many losses which was brought by previous large investments that have not been profitable. The managers of the company disclosed that they have no solution to reverse the current critical financial situation, however, they were closely working with specialists to work on the possible solutions.
The Ministry of Health announced 2 new COVID deaths and 25 new cases in Mozambique on 19 April. 1022 recoveries were also reported. 22 new cases were reported in Maputo City and 3 in Manica province.

RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade called the involvement of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) in fighting against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. Momade stated that the SADC "cannot remain indifferent to what is happening right now in Mozambique." Momade also mentioned that the announcement made by President Nyusi regarding sovereignty does not make sense due to the previous conflict with the RENAMO dissidents involved foreign soldiers.

The National Road Administration (ANE) announced that the bridges over Nacala and Muendaze rivers in Memba District were to be replaced in the next two months. The announcement comes as the ANE Director General conducted a visit in Nampula.

Mozambique Airports officials stated that 30 million USD is needed to repair the damages of Beira International Airport caused by 2019 Cyclone Idai. The repairs would also include the modernization of the airport.

Mozambique Airports Officials stated that they do not have a solution to resolve the financial crisis affecting the company. The Financial Director stated that they may recapitalize or lease the company to diversify the  business.

The Centre for Public Integrity (CIP) announced that the Ministry of Health has been promoting “impunity” by allowing medical materials to expire. The CIP stated the Health Minister Deputy ordered outdated materials to be removed and incinerated to gain more warehouse space. CIP said that the materials destroyed were estimated to be around 13.2 million meticais.

The National Road Administration (ANE) announced the resumption of road repairs between Monapo and Nacala-Porto after it was suspended by heavy rainfall. The road was damaged due to heavy rainfall and after a truck with heavy cargo attempted to pass through.

column4: President of the Northern Integrated Development Agency (ADIN) announced that 21 resettlement villages were to be created for the IDPs in Cabo Delgado. Officials stated that the creation of the villages is part of the Displaced Persons Management Plan.
The second COVID vaccination campaign started to accommodate the elderly in Sofala on 19 April. The vaccination was expected to cover 9,000 individuals.

The Ports and Railways of Mozambique Company announced that operations have increased by 270% leading to 4.7 billion meticais in revenue compared to the 1.3 billion meticais on 2019. Officials stated that they would rehabilitation and expand the Machipanda railroad with a customs terminal and improvements to the Ressano Garcia line and Pemba Port.

Locals have raised concerns of fears of a possible attack in Pemba. Locals stated that the advancement of the current insurgent situation in Cabo Delgado province as more IDPs arrive in the city and news of the attack has affected foster families.

The Public Health Deputy National Director Matsinhe stated that 2.6 million COVID doses were expected to arrivee by May. The plan was to initially cover 20 percent of the total population and later reach by 16 million.

A techical commission of the SADC has been assessing the current situation in Cabo Delgado since 15 April. The Commission was expected to report and present to the Ministerial Committee of the Organ and the  Extraordinary Organ Troika Summit by 28 and 29 April. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation (MINEC), stated that the commission was determining the following steps.

The Minister of Culture and Tourism, Eldevina Materula stated that the National Reserve of Pomene was to be considered as an investment project for tourism. The project was to foresee the development of resorts, construction of luxury villas and community lodges, which was expected to boost tourism.
Local sources stated that HIV/Aids-related disease kills three teachers in an average per month in Lichinga. The situation was aggrevated due to the lack of teachers in district.
Austria donated 1 million EUR to the UNFPA to support the needs of women and girls in Cabo Deglado.  The funds were expected to benefit 41,250 women in Cabo Delgado.

The Ministers of Transport and Communications of both Mozambique and Zambia were reportedly coordinating to improve logistics between countries. Zambia Minister Mutotwe Kafwaya visited Beira port for the next three days to discuss imports and exports. Both ministers were to provide port service providers and managers that would be involved with the transportation of goods.

A fire burned down a residence and ignited gas cylinder along Avenida Marien N'Gouabi in Mafalala, Maputo City on the afternoon of 18 April. Only material damages were due to the residence being used as a partial warehouse for goods.

The South African bank Standard Bank stated that the Mozambican currency has appreciated by 35 percent since January. The gain may be reversed due to the reported suspension of several foreign currency conversions and importers returned to the market benefiting from the recent gains.

A truck collided with another vehicle along Avenida Eduardo Mondlane in Nampula on the morning of 20 April. A civilian was killed. Police arrested the truck driver after witnesses stated that the he was driving recklessly.
Security forces detained a suspect for murdering a civilian in Morrumbene of Inhambane province on 14 April. The suspect murdered his girlfriend with a farming hoe.

The Center for Public Integrity (CIP) called on the government to prepare contract renegotiations with other companies. CIP warned that the government has been focused on Total and the current events in northern Mozambique, which has delayed the scheduled the liquefied natural gas exploration project in the Rovuma basin. CIP stated that the government must be prepared for the renegotiation with the other companies brought about by the attacks. This comes as other companies were resuming activities after the suspension.

Mozambican Health Officials stated that COVID cases have seen a decrease within a 24 hour period on 19 April. 520 COVID test were conducted where only 25 tested positive while 495 were negative results. A positivity rate of 4.8 percent was noted.

The Mozambican government stated that 723,000 IDPs have been displaced due to the violence from north and central Mozambique on 18 April. Government spokesman Filimao Suaze stated that 714,136 individuals were affected in northern mozambique while 8,726 individuals were affected in central Mozambique.

The Ministry of Health announced two new COVID deaths and 81 new cases in Mozambique on 20 April. Six new hospitalizations and 8 recoveries were reported. The cases were reported as follows: 17 from Nampula, 17 from Zambezia, 20 from Tete and 18 from Sofala, 6 from Maputo City, 1 from Maputo province, 1 from Gaza, and 1 from Manica.
Police arrested a suspect for 30 rape cases 7 de Abril, Chimoio in Manica province on 14 April. The suspect targeted children and women.

The Mitsui Company reached an agreement with Vale mining company to exit the joint venture in Mozambique. The agreement has led to the transfer of interests after Vale intended to sell their coal project. The transaction between companies was expected to be completed after the approval of the regulation authorities.

The Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA) stated that 410 companies and 56,000 jobs were affected by the attacks in Cabo Delgado. CTA stated that Mocimboa Da Praia was the most affected area, with 40% of the companies and 23% jobs lost.

Former Defense Minister Athanasio Mtumuke filed defamation charges against journalist Armando Nenane and BCI after previous reports of misappropriation of funds of 8 million meticais. The funds were reportedly to be used for the salaries of the military.

Ressano Garcia Customs announced the operation of a new terminal project budgeted at 3.5 million USD. The project will halve the passing trucks on National Road EN4 towards Maputo Port. The terminal was stated to start operating this coming May.

FRELIMO General Secretary Silva has rejected the idea of having foreign troops to support the security forces for ground operations and clarified that the would only be conducting training in Northern Mozambique. Silva stated that Mozambican forces ended the war with the RENAMO dissidents even with Zimbabwean and Tanzanian forces present.
Police detained a drug smuggler in possession of 19.5kg of heroin at Ressano Garcia border crossing on 19 April. The suspect's vehicle was seized during the arrest.
Police detained a drug smuggler in possession of 19.5kg of heroin at Ressano Garcia border crossing on 19 April. The suspect's vehicle was seized during the arrest.

30 Internacional Facility Service (IFS) employees subcontracted by CCS JV for the the construction of the Natural Gas Liquefaction Plant have returned to Palma on 18 April. Four of the employees were residing at the transitional center while 18 were staying at a hotel in the town. The company stated that the deployment was requested by the employees.

The Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA) called on Total and other companies to resume their activities after being suspended due to the insurgent attacks in Palma. CTA stated that a greater partnership and solutions against the insurgency should be formed to enable the development and industrialization of the area.
Security forces arrested a human trafficking suspect in Inhambane province. The suspect would take in individuals coming from Manica province and would traffic them to Mpumalanga, South Africa.

Total suspended two contracts with construction companies which were indirectly related to the gas project in Northern Mozambique. The contracts were related to the accommodation for displaced residents and new airport in the Palma area. The oil and gas company previously stated that the Mozambique Project LNG was suspended for security reasons.
The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) destroyed 86kg of narcotics during an operation in Sofala. 86kgs cannabis, 143g of heroin, 30g of cocaine, and four tablets were destroyed.

RENAMO and MDM called for the cancellation of the election for the Marromeu City Council President. Both parties issued a letter stating that the voting for Angelina Donquene's as the replacement of former Governor Diniz Djedje was tainted by fraud.

Inhagoia B residents protested on the morning of 20 April against the exclusion of their neighborhood from the COVID subsidies payment over the past year. The protesters stated that since the beginning of the pandemic, they were considered ineligible for the grant. Locals stated that they heard about the subsidies from residents living in other neighborhoods.

President Nyusi stated that the floating platform for the natural gas production in the Rovuma basin which was expected to arrive in Mozambique in the first quarter of 2022 will now arrive by December of 2021.  The platform could potentially start production in 2022, Nyusi also said, with a capacity of 3.4 million tons of LNG per year.
Local officials announced that the road paving has begun along the Marracuene-Macaneta administrative post Road, north of Maputo City. The 10km of road was to be completed within five months.

Security forces arrested five Malawians with "rented" national ID cards in Cuamba of Niassa province on 21 April. The suspects were on a bus to Ngauma which was stopped during an inspection. Three ID cards, two personal identification documents were seized. The suspects confessed to the rental of the ID cards for 13,000 meticais.

The Minister of Health Armindo Tiago stated that 31 health units have been destroyed by RENAMO dissidents during attacks in Manica and Sofala provinces. Tiago also said natural disasters in recent years have also destroyed several health facilities in these provinces.

Locals recovered three bodies suspected to be killed by security forces in Palma on the morning of 19 April.  It is unclear if the three were killed on Monday or previously. The victims were reportedly suspected insurgents. Security forces have been accused by the locals of abuses in the aftermath of the Palma battle.

The Ministry of Health announced 128 new COVID cases and three deaths in Mozambique on 21 April. 78 of the cases were reported in Maputo City, 16 in Maputo province, 12 in Tete, 10 in Niassa, 4 in Inhambane,  1 in Sofala, and 1 in Gaza.

Officials announced the closure of a fish market for one day in Maputo City as part of the sterilization of the market on the morning of 22 April. The closure was part of the safety precautions against COVID.

Severe Tropical Storm Jobo as of the morning of 22 April is estimated to slowly lose strength over the coming days as it approaches the Southern Coast of Tanzania, before turning northward and potentially making landfall near Dar es Salaam.  The storm could still bring heavy rains to areas as far south as the Mucojo area to the border with Tanzania.

Niassa governor Elina Judite Massengele stated that malaria deaths and infections have continued to decrease from 54 to 37 deaths between January to April. While cases also decreased from 292,692 cases to 126,578 cases. Niassa registered a 6.7 percent increase in diarrhea cases during the first two weeks of April, bringing cases to 19,876 and 5 deaths.

Maputo City municipal police increased inspections of school vehicles to assess their compliance with COVID preventive measures. The school vehicles were being checked for disinfecting alcohol, yellow paint to identify the vehicles, and the companions to ensure the social distancing inside the vehicles.

The WFP on 22 April said that more than 950,000 people across Mozambique are in need of food aid, including around 50,000 people affected by the assault on Palma.  The WFP currently plans to support IDPs with food aid across Cabo Delgado, Nampula, Niassa, and Zambezia, but needs $82 million to respond to the ongoing humanitarian crisis in Cabo Delgado and the wider north of Mozambique.

The Maputo City Council announced that it would repair the roads around the city start before October 2021 or the beginning of the next rainy season. Many roads were previously damaged due to the previous rainy season. The city council stated that they would conduct the repairs in a different way compared to the previous covering of pot holes.
Police detained a woman for illegally selling items on a street in Maputo City on 22 April.

Catholic bishops on 22 April expressed their concern to President Nyusi over the vulnerability of young people to recruitment by insurgent groups in Cabo Delgado, saying "marginalization" could lead to the spread of the insurgency into other areas of the country.

A consultancy projected on Thursday that ExxonMobil is likely to delay its Final Investment Decision in its Rovuma LNG project until 2023 due to insurgent activity and "uncertainty regarding project financing".  Exxon has already delayed its FID in this project several times.

The Nampula archbishop announced that construction of 200 houses were to be given to the IDPs in the Accommodation Center in Corane of Meconta District. The residences were donated by the Episcopal Conference of Mozambique, where the organization also intends to create 300 more residences for the IDPs.

The Ministry of Health announced that 85 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 22 April. 52 daily recoveries and 8 hospitalizations were noted. Maputo City recorded 58 cases and Tete province with 11.

DAG owner, Lionel Dyck stated that a security vacuum was created upon the departure of his company after DAG's contract ended with the government on 6 April.  Dyck also said insurgents could "dominate the whole area" if this security vacuum is allowed to continue.  Dyck also said the Mozambican military had given DAG inadequate support, and that many soldiers were ill equipped and poor trained.

The IOM on 23 April said that nearly 4,000 more people have fled Palma District in the past week, and that nearly 25,000 have now been displaced out of the district since the attack on the town.  6,970 of these IDPs are displaced in Mueda, along with 6,733 displaced in Nangade.  Another 5,000 have been displaced to Pemba, while 3,795 have been displaced to Montepuez.

The Pedagogical University of Maputo stated that its revenues fell from 12 million to 2.5 million meticais due to the COVID pandemic. The university stated that higher education officials conducted a meeting to discuss the impacts of the pandemic. Officials stated that they have prepared for the school opening next year.

The Cahora Bassa Hydroelectric Plant (HCB) stated that they produced 3,671.91GWh which is 6.1% above of  the planned electricity for the period. HCB officials stated that the modernization of the equipment has enable this better production.

The Nampula Mayor Vahanle was sentenced to 18 months in prison after being found guilty of various criminal charges. The mayor was charged for using public funds to make a payment of 36,000 meticais to the RENAMO party's delegate, Abiba Aba. Vahanle was also charged with abuse of office, embezzlement, misuse of application, deviations from application, fraud, breach of the rules of execution of the plan and budget and payment of undue remuneration. He was also allowed to pay 350,000 meticais for bail.
The Ministry of Health reported 74 new COVID cases and a single death in Mozambique on 23 April. The total has increased to 69,597 positive cases and 41 daily recoveries were recorded.

SADC will prepare a report after assessing the security situation in Cabo Delgado for the upcoming Troika Summit to be held in Maputo during the 28 and 29 April. The report was to give framework to the type of support needed in the country.  There had been early momentum behind a potential SADC intervention force, though it Mozambique will actually accept any direct intervention in Cabo Delgado.

The Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy of Mozambique Max Tonela announced Thursday that the oil and gas company Total would maintain their "main contracts" linked to the gas exploration project in Cabo Delgado. Tonela said that some sub-contractor's contracts were being cancelled but were "easy to re-mobilize" when the project restarts.  He also said everything was being done to restore security in the Palma area.
The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) detained two suspects for stealing vehicles in Maputo city on 24 April. The suspects previously stole a vehicle on 22 March.

The Ministry of Health announced that 46 new COVID cases and one related death were reported in Mozambique on 24 April. For the new cases Maputo City recorded 31 cases and Niassa province with six.  44 daily recoveries and three hospitalizations were noted.

Ossufo Momade, leader of RENAMO, stated on 23 April at Curane displaced center in Meconta that Mozambique must unite with its international partners to combat terrorism. He added that the ruling party, FRELIMO, is only focused about its refusal to seek assistance from foreign countries but is willing to hire 'mercenaries' without the public's knowledge.

Sources on 24 April stated that several roads are easily flooded in Maputo City when any amount of rainfall hits the city. Affected areas are Avenida Marcelino dos Santos, which divides Chamanculo C and D, Avenida Nelson Mandela in Magoanine C, Avenida Vladimir Lenine in Polana Canico and Avenida Coronel-General Sebastiao Marcos Mabote in CMC, among others. Locals urged the local government to find a suitable solution to the ongoing problems of pedestrians and motorists.

Ossuf Momade, leader of RENAMO, proposed on 24 April for former RENAMO guerillas to join Defense and Security System of the country to combat insurgents in Cabo Delgado. He stated that 362 RENAMO 'rangers' were waiting to be re integrated following the end of the ongoing Demilitarization, Disarmament and Reintegration process.

Armed assailants at around 1900hrs on Saturday kidnapped an Indian-Mozambican businessman identified as Depesh Ramesh in Chimoio.  The man was abducted along Ave. Mussorize after parking his car near his residence.  The assailants also fired two shots in the air to deter anyone from attempting to stop the kidnapping and forced the businessman into a waiting car.  The incident took place close to a Mozambican police station.  The victim is the son of a well-known local entrepreneur.

President Nyusi announced on 25 April that the curfew from 2200hrs to 0400hrs will remain in place in Maputo and Provincial Capitals, and will also be put in place in Manhica, in Maputo Province; the city of Chokwe, in Gaza; Maxixe and Villa de Massinga, in Inhambane; Villa de Gondola, in Manica; city ​​of Moatize, in Tete; city ​​of Mocuba, in Zambezia; city ​​of Nacala, in Nampula; and Montepuez in Cabo Delgado. Shopping centers are allowed to operate from 0900-1800hrs on Sundays, holidays and time-off days while bakeries and convenience stores can operate from 0500-2000hrs. These measures are part of the safety protocols to curb spread of the coronavirus.  Church services can resume with 30% capacity (or 100 people, whichever comes first) while other gatherings in closed spaces can resume with up to 50 people.  Casinos, cinemas, theaters, museums, auditoriums, galleries, and other similar facilities can also reopen at 40% capacity.

The Ministry of Health announced that 22 new COVID cases and no related deaths were reported in Mozambique on 25 April. For the new cases Maputo City and Province recorded 13 cases, Inhambane with four cases, Sofala with four cases and Manica with one.  49 daily recoveries and four hospitalizations were noted.

Sources on 25 April reported that the number of malaria cases in Mozambique increased by more than 426,000 from 2019 to 2020. However, the number of malaria-related dates during the same time period have decreased. Later this year Nampula Government will launch a provincial sanitation campaign to reduce mosquito breeding spots in all of its 23 districts. It is recalled that Nampula periodically conducted indoor spraying anti-mosquito campaigns since 2013. Nampula is one of the five provinces with the highest incidence of the disease.

The Country's Council of State on 22 April expressed concerns on security situation in Cabo Delgado province. The committee encouraged the security forces to intensify counterterror operations to provide better protection for the people as well as properties.

South African politicians on 25 April stated that despite efforts from security forces,  South Africa-Mozambique border remains a gateway for vehicle theft. At least 24 vehicles were reported stolen within a week in March and the recovery rate was very low.  South African National Defence Force spokesperson Brigadier General Mafi Mgobhozi said that additional officers were deployed in areas where there was a high demand for enforcement however, allegations were raised by the community about police working with syndicates.

Total on 26 April announced force majeure on the Afungi LNG project. The company also confirms the withdrawal of all project personnel from the site due to the security situation in the province. Total's move to declare Force Majeure absolves or at least is intended to absolve the company of any remaining liabilities or obligations in relation to its operations at the Afungi LNG Camp.  In the wake of the Battle for Palma, the company evacuated all personnel from the area, canceled most of the contracts with sub-contractors linked to the project, and has not given any indication of when the project could re-start.  There is widespread speculation that the company will not look to restart operations in Afungi for a minimum of one year, though this is unconfirmed.  Total is expected to require the government to provide significant security assurances in order to return which among other conditions will likely require a fortified Afungi LNG Camp and insurgents being cleared from Palma District.

National Heath Institute on 23 April announced the end of the COVID-19 second wave in the country. The announcement came after a downward trend in the number of new coronavirus cases was observed in the country since early March. There are now less than 40 hospitalizations countrywide, and the country has seen several days in recent weeks with no deaths.  There are currently 6,380 active cases in the country, including 4,372 in Maputo City.

Cabo Delgado Governor Valige Tauabo announced on 26 April the commitment to move teams of doctors to Palma, to provide primary health care to the locals. The mobilization will commence once the processes for the resumption of the services are in progress in the town. Authorities stated that 180 public health workers were displaced and another five are missing following the insurgent attack on 24 March.

Around 2000hrs on 25 April, unexplained gunfire was heard in north of Palma town which lasted for an hour. A source claimed that several houses in the town were razed by insurgents, though this detail is not confirmed.  Two generally reliable sources stated that security forces engaged in a gun battle with insurgents north of the Amarula Hotel area.  Further details regarding this clash are unconfirmed.

Unconfirmed reports indicated that 4 people were beheaded by insurgents on the night of 23 April in Palma town near the Palma Business Park.  Other sources later reported 5 bodies found in the area.  Sources also indicated an unknown number of homes had been set on fire in the raid.  No clashes with security forces stationed in the town were reported.  Other unverified reports on the night of 23 April indicated two beheaded bodies were found near the Palma airstrip - it is unclear if these two reports refer to the same incident.
Sources in Pemba on the night of 23 April reported significant numbers of police deployed and patrolling on foot in the city.

At least 11,000 remain displaced at Quitunda as of 23 April. Efforts as of 23 April were ongoing to provide food supplies to these IDPs primarily through private donors who are attempting to ship supplies to the area.  Other food deliveries to these IDPs have reportedly stopped over disagreements between the security forces and aid agencies.

Criminal Investigation Services (SERNIC) officers seized 25kgs of cocaine and arrested 3 Mozambicans in the Maringanha beach area.  The three arrested men said they were not connected to the drugs but had transported them unknowingly on behalf of a Tanzanian national.  SERNIC also said it had seized a motorbike and the engine of a vessel used to transport the drugs.

A boat transporting cargo reportedly sank due to the Tropical Storm Jobo while traveling from Pemba to Ibo Island on 20 April. The boat was identified as the Lurio era de Sirisa. No casualties were reported.

The National Petroleum Institute (INP) stated that Total has claimed Force Majeure to mitigate the negative effects of the suspension from the contracts that would cost goods and services. INP stated that during the suspension, the oil and gas company will not be able to comply with the their obligations and would be forced to suspend or terminate more contracts.

Portuguese ambassador in Maputo Antonio Costa Moura met with the Portuguese community during a three-day visit in Pemba. The Portuguese residing raised concerns due to the increasing IDPs and insecurity of the province. Moura stated that the oil and gas company's withdrawal does not involve the Portuguese State and that the "security is a horizontal issue that concerns us all."

The Mozambican government donated 171 million meticais to several institutions to fight against malaria in the country. Officials stated that Mozambique is the third country with the highest malaria cases as around 10 million malaria cases are reported annually globally.

The Ministry of Health announced that two deaths and 50 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 26 April. This brings the total number of COVID cases to 69,399, while the deaths have increased to 809. 6 new hospitalizations and 2 were discharged during the time of reporting.

The Beira municipal council announced that a wall was to be built along the sea to protect coastal infrastructures. The Beira mayor stated that only 80 million USD was available for the project which was budgeted at 92 million USD. A study was being conduct to determine the type of work needed along the 10km coast of Beira.
Police have requested the assistance of any witnesses and the public regarding the kidnapping of the bakery owner's son in Chimoio of Manica province.

President Filipe Nyusi has removed Cabo Delgado Province Secretary of State, Armindo Saul Atelela Ngunga under the 2nd Paragraph of Article 259 of the Constitution of the Republic. Armindo Saul Atelela Ngunga was reportedly appointed as Board of Directors President for the Integrated Development Agency of the North (ADIN). Ngunga was to replaced former ADIN Board of Directors President, Armando Alexandre Panguene.

The SADC technical committee issued a proposal calling for 2916 personnel to be deployed as part of the intervention against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. The report was regarding the Mozambique security situation assessment in Cabo Delgado, which was initially ordered during the start of the initial Double Troika Summit on 8 April. The technical committee conducted the assessment between the 15 to 21 April. The proposal included the following resources for the SADC support in Mozambique: Maritime: 2 Surface Patrol Ships with 180 personnel, which would include a helicopter patrol, 2 boats, and 2 optional drones. A submarine with 45 personnel and a Maritime Surveillance Aircraft under the operation of 10 personnel. Air: 2 UAVs operated by 4 personnel, 6 Helicopters (2x Utility, 2x Attack, 2x Armed) manned by 12 personnel, 4 Transport Aircrafts (2x Light Aircraft, 1x Medium Aircraft, 1x Heavy Aircraft) operated by 8 personnel, 12 Air Command and Control personnel. 42 Air Technicians, 3 Metrological Officers, and 4 Air Intelligence Officers. Ground Forces: 90 Light infantry Brigade HQ personnel, 3 battalions with 620 soldiers per battalion, 2 Special Forces Squadron with 70 personnel per squadron, an Engineer Squadron with 100 personnel, and a Signal Squadron of 120 personnel. Logistics: A Logistics Company made of 100 personnel with one Level 2 Field Hospital, a Field Recovery station, a Field Workshop, and a Field Mobility Storage. The proposal stated was to support both short- and medium-term operations. The technical committee stated that the air and seaports can provide operations for both heavy and transport aircrafts. The committee also recommended that a three-action course should be conducted which involves the deployment of security forces, training of the Mozambican military, and military support. The assessment and proposal by the technical committee was a response by the SADC after the insurgent attack in Palma area of Cabo Delgado on 24 March. The SADC stated on 8 April that they called for a "collective response" against insurgent attacks in Cabo Delgado, stating that the insurgent attacks in Palma are a "threat to the entire southern African region".

Local sources stated that there is a no transportation traveling to and from Palma of Cabo Delgado. The previous transportation to the area were reassigned to other areas. Sail boats previously traveling to the area were banned by the Lacustrine Police, and would only be allowed if they were traveling for important purposes.

The Center for Democracy and Development (CDD) stated that the proposal of the SADC to assist the Mozambican military by sending 2916 personnel was too "militaristic". CDD claimed that the SADC technical team made a poor analysis and inappropriate recommendations.
Local sources reported that there is a lack of water supply and sanitation in public areas in Quitunda. The area was prone to a possible disease outbreak due as it hosts a population of 20,000.
The Ministry of Health announced 47 new COVID cases and five deaths in Mozambique on 27 April. 35 of the cases were recorded in Greater Maputo. While five others were noted in Sofala.

President Nyusio stated that the challenge of the country against the insurgency is a only a scale of the "international terrorism". The president also stated that Mozambique is still "enjoying stability" regardless of the violence. The statement comes as the president was conducting a speech during the conference of the Portuguese-speaking African countries (PALOP).

The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) detained a suspect for running a network of illegal miners at the Montepuez Ruby Mining (MRM) area. The Tanzanian woman accused of leading the ring was residing in Nanhupo village of Namanhumbir AP. The suspect was part of the illegal ruby trade in the area.

Road construction workers have been advancing as they construct the rainwater basin for the Maxaquene C in Maputo City. The basin was part of the project to minimize the flooded portions of the city. The construction was part of the preparation for the upcoming rainy season on October.

Four armed robbers in a vehicle shot twice at the vehicle of a company employee and stole 1.4 million meticais near a bank branch along Rua Dos Irmaos Roby in Xipamanine, south Maputo City, at around 11:00 of 27 April. No casualties were reported. The suspects intercepted the victim and stole the suitcases filled with money before using another vehicle to escape. No injuries were reported.

The Attorney General of the Republic (PGR) will issue her annual report regarding the legality of the country and actions of the justice administration system. The PGR would discuss the control of legality, human rights, crime, prevention, and fight against corruption, asset recovery, procedural performance, international and local legal and judicial cooperation.

SADC and Botswana President has conducted a self-quarantine after his staff member tested positive for COVID, causing him to miss the Troika Summit to be held in Mozambique on 28 and 29 April. The meeting would be chaired by Vice President Tsogwane during the summit.

President Nyusi signed on Wednesday the approval of the emergency project agreement. The agreement was with the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development and UN to coordinate projects and implement activities in Pemba, Cabo Delgado. The projects were also tied to the the North Integrated Development Agency (ADIN) and National Sustainable Development Fund (FNDS). The project was to build health facilities, schools, among other infrastructures and services in a province affected by a serious humanitarian crisis.

On 27 April unidentified gunmen were reported to have attacked the residence of a local official in the Samoa area of Moatize District, near Zobue in Tete with small arms fire.  The official was not at his residence during the attack; policemen meant to be at their posts at the residence were also absent during the attack as well.  No casualties were reported.  The RENAMO Military Junta is suspected in this incident as a four-page letter was dropped by the suspects following the attack. The letter contested the leadership of Ossufo Momade, head Renamo party and claimed that they do not recognize the peace agreement signed on 2019..

Several sources have reported that fires were noted on the town in Palma on the night of 26 April.  local sources accused security forces of setting homes of locals on fire due to the possibility of the locals suspected of supporting the insurgents.

The local Mission Aviation Fellowship (MAF) has been transporting volunteers authorized to provide humanitarian aid and evacuation between Palma and Pemba. 335 refugees were previously evacuated on 41 flights.  1,546 kg of food aid was already donated to the IDPs.

The Center for Democracy and Development (CDD) stated that the cases of the hidden debts by the previous government officials has been transferred from Judge Evandra Uamusse to Judge Efigenio Baptista. CDD stated that the Baptista has been previously tried and convicted with a previous crime, leaving doubts of the transfer of the case. CDD stated that the hidden debts case is one of the biggest cases for Mozambique and senior judges are expected to take over the case.
The 14th Ordinary Session of the Council of Ministers announced that the first quarter of the 2021 has registered a nominal growth of 9.6% and a positive expenditure of 4.3%.

The US Embassy in Mozambique will provide 6 million USD as part of the funding of a five-year program to strengthen the capacity of radio stations and ability to inform the public around the country. The USAID Community Radio Assistance for Greater Empowerment of Mozambican Institutions program was to support 60 Mozambican community radio stations in Zambezia, Nampula, Niassa, and Cabo Delgado.

President Nyusi on 28 April announced that Cabo Delgado will receive USD 100 million in humanitarian loans approved by World Bank from the International Development Association (IDA). The support aims to build 800 classrooms, 200 teachers' houses, 10 hospitals, 43 water supply networks, 130 community infrastructures, 20,000 improved latrines and 40 public bathrooms, in the next few months.

The Southern African Development Community (SADC) postponed the Troika Summit scheduled today due to the unavailability of some heads of states. SADC and Botswana President has conducted a self-quarantine after his staff member tested positive for COVID, while incoming chairperson, President Cyril Ramaphosa, is appearing at the Zondo commission of inquiry. The scheduled 29 April Troika Summit aims to discuss the report of the Technical Assessment Team deployed in Mozambique. The officials have yet to provide a new date to resume the Summit.  Some reports believed that Southern African ministers have agreed to deploy a regional force in Mozambique and that the summit was postponed because of disagreement at the ministerial council of the SADC security

On 28 April, Italian company, Saipem, stated that they were working closely with Total to allegedly preserve the value of the LNG project after Total declared force majeure. Saipem did not provide information how long the force majeure was likely to stay in effect.

The Ministry of Health announced 42 new COVID-19 cases and zero deaths in Mozambique on 28 April. 10 of the new cases were recorded in  Maputo City, another 10 cases in Maputo province , while eight others were noted in Niassa, seven in Manica, four in Nampula, two in Inhambane and one case in Sofala. 93 people have recovered from the virus in the last 24 hours.

On 28 April, French Embassy in Maputo announced 3 million Euros will be provided to support a project to empower girls in Mozambique. The project led by the Association for the Economic Empowerment of Girls aims to create economic opportunities in disadvantaged urban areas. The project will be conducted in Pemba City.
Unidentified individuals - either insurgents or security force members, fired small arms sporadically on the night of 27 April, before setting several homes on fire in Palma.

Several houses in Malamba, Palma were destroyed by fires on the evening of 27 April. The cause of the fire is still unknown however, there is speculation the fires were caused by government forces stationed in the town. Mozambican Military on 29 April announced that the fires started by two alleged insurgents and stated that Palma is completely under government-control. Another source added that the incident was caused by insurgents who who from Pundanhar forest in search for food in Palma.
Sources on 28 April claimed that non-government organizations are not allowed access to enter Palma.

Several people, mostly women, staged a protest next to Dlhavela headquarters, Matola on the morning of 26 April to demand an explanation for alleged discrimination in the allocation of subsidies. The protest became violent as the protesters smashed windows and forcibly pulled on the door of the premises. Authorities claimed that the residents' issues are a result of lack of information about the eligibility of the grants.
Sources on 29 April reported that security forces arrested two people connected to the seizure of a Dhow containing drugs near Cauri, Wimbe beach.
On 29 April security forces conducted a raid in a mosque near Raphael's Hotel in Pemba following a tip-off over alleged presence of suspicious looking people entering the area

On 29 April Mozambican Police opened fire on two individuals aboard a vehicle after they refused to stop at a checkpoint in Avani. One of the target was shot dead while the other one sustained wounds.

Department of Safety and Security on 29 April reported that an offensive in Pemba city is unlikely to take place due to the significant presence of government forces and support of locals to the authorities.

More than 70 displaced people arrived in Nangade following burning of houses in Palma. Meanwhile an undetermined number of people arrived from the lowlands of Nangade lake. The influx of displaced people arriving in the town ignited panic among locals who eventually moved towards highly-secure town of Mueda. Displaced people in the town allegedly experienced severe hunger due to a lack of humanitarian assistance.

Several people arrived in Quitunda on the morning of 27 April following burning of houses in Palma. Displaced people in the town allegedly experienced severe hunger following the lack of humanitarian assistance.

Mozambique will hold a virtual meeting  for the  SADC Ministers of Employment and Labour and Social Partners on 30 April from 0900 to 1300 hours. Implementation of COVID-19 measure will be the main objective of the said meeting.

Authorities stated on 28 April that a total of 58 people were charged by Mozambican prosecutors with crimes of terrorism in 2020. These people were included in 13 separate cases, nine are still at the stage of preparatory investigation. Attorney General of the Republic of Mozambique Beatriz Buchili added that 36 criminal cases related to the armed attacks attributed to the self-proclaimed Renamo Military Junta were instituted on the same year. Out of these cases, 32 were recorded in Sofala and four in Manica.

On 29 April, Chongo Vidigal, spokesman for the Mozambican Armed Defense Forces, stated that Palma is completely under the control of government forces. He added that the houses burnt on the evening of 27 April were perpetrated by two alleged insurgents as a reprisal attack. He claimed that the assailants attacked the houses of the people they thought to have collaborated with government forces.

Authorities announced on 28 April that all athletes affiliated with Mozambican Sports Federation will be have COVID-19 immunization starting 03 May. The decision was made to allegedly reduce fears and optimize their performance 2020 Summer Olympics in Tokyo.

Local sources reported that police have been intimidating employees working on evening shifts pass curfew hours in Xai-Xai District on 29 April. Employees report that some police understand their situation regarding their work but others just detain them at police stations.

President Nyusi announced on Wednesday, 28 April that the security forces have a detailed plan to tackle the ongoing security situation against the insurgents in Cabo Delgado. Nyusi stated that the plan included the modernizing and building the capacity of the Mozambican security forces. Nyusi also clarified that Mozambique has never refused external support.

The Ministry of Health announced that they intend to conduct a study on November that would cover 11,058 households regarding the impact of HIV/ AIDs in Gaza province. The study would interview 23,877 people and 19,006 citizens aged at least 15 will be tested for HIV.
Police arrested a suspect in possession of two ivory tips in Maputo City on 29 April. The 28kg ivory tips were spotted being transported on a vehicle leading to the arrest.
Police arrested a suspect in possession of two ivory tips in Maputo City on 29 April. The 28kg ivory tips were spotted being transported on a vehicle leading to the arrest.
79 Mozambicans were deported through the Negomano border crossing from Tanzania between 17-23 April. Those deported had fled the Palma attack into Tanzania.

The Ministry of Health announced that 60 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 29 April. The breakdown of the cases are as follows: 29 in Maputo City, 6 in Maputo province, 2 in Gaza, 1 in Inhambane, 5 in Sofala, 1 in Manica, 11 in Zambezia, 2 in Nampula, and 3 in Cabo Delgado. Recoveries have reportedly reached 93% as daily recoveries were recorded at 995.

The Mozambican government and Operation Water signed a public-private partnership to develop the water  infrastructure around the country. The investment of 23 million USD was to benefit 300,000 individuals and provide access to water as eight projects were planned.

The Mozambican government has launched a web portal which is intended to combat fake news. Named Credivel, the website is a platform intended to verify the authenticity of content conveyed by the media or social networks that would raise uncertainty on the part of the reader. The website also includes a section where official government announcements are posted.

In a report cited by local media on 30 April, the UN Refugee Agency stated that the number of displaced civilians as a result of the armed attacks in Palma has reached around 30,500. Majority of these people have fled to Pemba, while the same report stated that dozens of other civilians were killed by militants during the attack on Palma which began on 24 March. The UN agency added that thousands of the displaced escaped Palma by foot, by road and by sea, often in bad health conditions, with injuries, or severe malnourishment. Moreover, there are still many more civilians believed to be stuck inside Palma.  The agency stressed that government troops are on the ground inside Palma, though it remains unknown to what extent they have secured the area. UNCHR aid workers are also unable to work in the region because of the risks.

On 1 May, police in Nangade received dozens of state employees who were previously captured by militants in Cabo Delgado.  The victims held for approximately 30 days, during which they were adequately fed and housed; however, they were released without supplies. The circumstances of this release remain unclear.  Family members previously believed that they had been kidnapped and killed. Nonetheless, many of these individuals have incurred malaria, hypothermia, and swollen feet.

Teachers in Inhambane province on 01 May complained about non-payment of overtime and Saturday duty. There are schools in the province who have yet to take Mathematics, Chemistry and Physics classes due to lack of teachers. Teachers warned the government that the students were at risk as their learning will be threatened if non-payment of overtime and Saturday subsidies will continue.

Mozambique Workers' Organization on 01 May demanded readjustment of minimum wage in 2021 following non-adjustment on 2020 during the celebration of the International Workers' Day in Nampula City. The group claimed that their demand reflects a right which must be respected by the National Government. However,  the Minister of Labor did  not promise any increase will take place, and will just leave everything to the negotiations that will begin this month.

Jean-Pierre Sbraire, Total's Chief Financial Officer, stated on 29 April that the Mozambique's LNG project will be delayed by at least a year due to the security situation in the area. The company trusts that the Mozambican Government and other partners will be able to restore security and stabilize the situation in the Cabo Delgado Province. Total also expressed confidence in the long-term viablility of the project.

The Ministry of Health announced that 48 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 01 May. The breakdown of the cases are as follows: 25 from Maputo city and 11 from Maputo province, three cases from Nampula, three from Sofala, two from Manica, two from Inhambane, one from Niassa and one case from Tete. Daily recoveries were recorded at 970 while no death was recorded over the last 24 hours.

Mozambican Government on 30 April vowed to restore security in Cabo Delgado to allow the Total's LNG project to resume. The commitment of the national government was discussed during the meeting attended by the Ministers of Mineral Resources and Energy of Mozambique, Max Tonela, and of Defense, Jaime Neto, and the president for Research and Production at Total, Arnaud Breuillac. The meeting took place four days after Total announced "force majeure" of the 20 billion Euros project following the 24 March attack in Palma.

Moderate to heavy rains and strong winds are expected to hit 24 districts of Maputo, Gaza and Inhambane from 30 April until 01 May. Affected districts  in the province of Maputo are Matutuine, Namaacha, Boane, Moamba, Magude, Manhica, Marracuene. Meanwhile, the cities of Maputo and Matola may experience by bad weather. In Gaza, affected districts are Chokwe, Bilene, Chongoene, Chibuto, Guija, Mandlakazi, Limpopo and the city of Xai-Xai. In the province of Inhambane, the alert is for the districts of Zavala, Inharrime, Panda, Homoine, Jangamo and the cities of Maxixe and Inhambane.
