Governor of Niassa, Elina Massengele, on 01 May stated that number of deaths caused by Malaria in the province rose from 157 in 2019 to 174 in 2020. Districts with most registered deaths were Lichinga, Mandimba, Mecanhelas and Mavago. The number of cases in the province increased 6 percent, from 743,884 cases last year, compared to 696,589 in 2019.

Banco de Mozambique announced that a total of US 60 million will be injected into the Interbank Foreign Exchange Market over the next 14 days. This is six times higher than the expected amount to be injected in the market. On 03 May USD 15 million will be made available; on 05 May, the foreign exchange market will receive another USD 10 million; and on the 07 May, USD 10 million will be injected. On the 10 May, another 10 million will be placed o; on  12 May, another USD 7.5 million will be injected; and the same amount will also be injected on 14 May.

The Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP) Council of Ministers decided to send a delegation to Mozambique to assess the military and humanitarian assistance that can be provided by the council. The exact date when the delegates will visit, however, has yet been finalized. Mozambican Government stated that the CPLP proposal is still under evaluation.

Insurgents allegedly entered Chai, north of Macomia on Saturday, 1 May. No shootings or attacks were heard in the area. However, an unconfirmed report stated that a potential attack may occur in the North and East of Macomia. Insurgents from Chai could potentially attack from the north area and from the northeast along the Macomia-Mucojo road.

Unconfirmed report on 01 May stated that a potential attack may occur in the North and East of Macomia. Insurgents from Chai could potentially attack from the north area and from the northeast along the Macomia-Mucojo road.

According to a UNCHR report on 30 April, several people in Quitunda suffer from physical assaults as they attempt to flee to safer areas using a boat. People are still fleeing Palma due to the violence which started on 24 March.

UNCHR on 30 April expressed concern on the rising of Internally Displaced People (IDP) who escaped the violence in Palma. Over 30,000 left the town and arrived on their destination without any belongings, often with health issues including injuries and severe malnutrition. Another concern is the people who cannot leave the area as few evacuation routes remain open.

Sources on 30 April claimed that about 23 houses were razed by insurgents in a neighborhoods in the south of Palma from 29-30 April. Some houses were allegedly set on fire while occupants engaged government forces in an exchange of gunfire.

Sources on 30 April claimed that exchange of gunfire has occurred in Palma several times last week. Intense confrontation between insurgents and government forces were reported from 25-29 April. Some houses were set on fire by insurgents during the clashes.

On 01 May, International Organization for Migration (IOM) recorded 1,895 IDPs were registered in Nangade, Mueda, Montepuez, and Pemba bringing the total number of IDPs to 33,283 people who have been displaced from Palma due to insurgency. Displaced people are still arriving to Nangade on foot and while some travel from Nangade to Mueda, Montepuez, and Pemba by bus.

A local militiaman opened fire on an unspecified number of insurgents who attacked Chai, Macomia District on 01 May. Insurgents responded to the fire leaving the militiaman injured. He was later rescued and taken to a hospital for treatment.
Three people were abducted by insurgents in Mucojo on 30 April. No other details are on this incident are currently available.

02 May Mozambique government sources issued a report stating that the country has overcome the second wave of coronavirus pandemic. In February, during the peak of the second wave, the country recorded more than 18 thousand active cases versus 02 May records that dropped to 2,234  total active infections. The number of people recovered from the disease rose to 66,931 across the country.

The Ministry of Health announced that 19 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 02 May. The breakdown of the cases are as follows: 15 from General Maputo area, two cases from Nampula, one from Inhambane and one case from Zambezia. Daily recoveries were recorded at 48 while one death was recorded over the last 24 hours.

President of RENAMO, Ossufo Momade, on 02 May appealed to Mariano Nhongo, Military Junta leader, to join the country's ongoing DDR process. The statement follows alleged attacks by RENAMO dissidents on civilians as a way of contesting the party's leadership.

Reports on 02 May stated that 12 out of the 15 neighborhoods in  Xai-Xai City have been threatened by erosion. Several houses in affected neighborhood were flooded following intense rains. City officials expressed intention to end the erosion problems in the metropolis but claimed that they do not have the budget address the issue.
Around 500 displaced people from Palma have arrived at Paquitequete beach, Pemba over the weekend. They were displaced from Palma due to the security situation in the town.

Sources on 27 April reported that the Joint War Committee Circular (JWLA-026 and 027) by Lloyd’s and the International Underwriting Association (IUA) designated Mozambique's coastline as a 'listed area' which means that shipowners will be required to notify their underwriters of voyages in this area. This comprises waters within 50 miles of Mozambique and Tanzania, to the north at Mnazi bay and to the south at Bai’a do Lu’rio. Relatively, it is expected that the insurance cost for vessels passing these areas due to the security situation in the province of Cabo Delgado. The zone will affect Area 1 (Total) and Area 4 (Exxon) and also ENI's LNG Coral South floating platform, which is 50 km from the coast. The announcement will seriously affect the normal traffic at the port of Pemba and all shipments related to the gas fields. Both insurgents and Mozambican Navy do not have a significant presence in the country's channel which was currently patrolled by French, South African, and Indian Navies. Reports suggest that Total and France may demand the French navy take control of the coastal waters of Cabo Delgado to fight terrorism.

Attorney General of the Republic of Mozambique, Beatriz Buchili, on 29 April suggested that Parliament to impose legal limit on the amount of cash that can be used in any transaction. Restrictions were needed to avoid payment of enormous ransoms in cash demanded by kidnappers in the country.

Reports on 30 April shows that Mozambican IDPs who crossed the Rovuma river into Tanzania border from Negomano, Mueda, were only screened, and sent back immediately across the border, often on board large trucks and trailers. In addition, affected IDPs were taken to the border at Negomano, in Mueda district were not provided transport from the border to their destination. The IDPs were expected to go on their own safely.

Aggrieved chapeiros or mini bus drivers commenced a strike on the morning of 03 May, blocking Machava Road.  The striking drivers threw stones at commercial vehicles who were not participating in the strike. The drivers condemned an order to accommodate only six passengers per ride as part of the COVID-19 protocols in addition to police collecting fines. They urged the government to review the restrictions as COVID-19 cases have dropped over the past weeks.

Police arrested five suspects in possession of 11 ivory tips during an operation in Tete and Vila de Chitima on 3 May. The suspects were also in possession of dandelions, leopard skin and a pangolin skeleton during the arrest.

Police arrested five suspects in possession of 11 ivory tips during an operation in Tete and Vila de Chitima on 3 May. The suspects were also in possession of dandelions, leopard skin and a pangolin skeleton during the arrest.

The National Penitentiary Service (SERNAP) transferred Anibal Antonio dos Santos Junior, also known as Anibalzinho from the Maximum Security Penitentiary Establishment to the Maputo Preventive Penitentiary Establishment.  The transfer was reportedly made because Anibalzinho's life was in danger at the first establishment. Anibalzinho was involved in the murder of a journalist on 20 November 2000 and has escaped three times from prison.

Local sources stated that insurgents who were positioned near Ilha de Macaloe attacked two civilian boats on the afternoon of 3 May. 7 civilians died and several others were injured. Insurgents reportedly abducted several of the escapng civilians. Sources stated that only six bodies were floating after the attack. Other civilians jumped overboard and swam towards the shores of Macomia District. Rescue boats later responded and retrieved the injured.
A vehicle overturned after a tire burst along a highway in Manjacaze, north of Xai-xai district, at around 19:00 on 3 May. Four civilians were killed, and several others were injured.

The RENAMO party accused the government of not being able to defend the residents of Cabo Delgado province. Party delegate Abiba Abba stated that " insurgents have attacked a defenseless population without mercy, plundering goods, and burning the infrastructures without the public knowing the amount of damage caused". Abba also mentioned that the government has not acknowledge its inability to defend the public in Cabo Delgado and has not accepted the military intervention of security forces from neighboring countries to assist in controlling the insurgency.

Local sources stated that 10 suspected insurgents wearing security uniforms near a water pumping station in Metuge District were sighted on the morning of 4 May. The Mozambique Defence Armed Forces deployed and conducted a search operation in response to presence of the armed men. This comes as sources earlier stated that insurgents intend to conduct an attack in the district.  Sources later indicated the armed men were likely other security force elements, and that this was a false alarm.

Local sources stated that 10 suspected insurgents wearing security uniforms near a water pumping station in Metuge District were sighted on the morning of Tuesday, 4 May. The Mozambique Defence Armed Forces deployed and conducted a search operation in response to presence of the armed men. This comes as sources earlier speculated that insurgents may intend to conduct an attack in the district.  Sources later indicated that the armed men were other security force elements, and that this was a false alarm.

Local sources stated that the distribution of the foods to the IDPs have been regulated by the district government and religious local leaders in Nacala-Porto. At least some of distribution is reportedly being directed to individuals who were local and were not displaced due to the previous attacks or natural disasters.

The Ministry of Health launched a HIV/AIDs "We are Equal" awareness campaign. The objective of the campaign was to minimize the stigma and discrimination brought about misinformation regarding HIV/ AIDs.  Around 160,000 males did not adhere to the antiretroviral medication and that the male groups between 15 to 29 year old are the most likely to obtain or spread the virus.

The Minister of Labor and Social Security Margarida Talapa stated the Mozambique employment situation has worsened due to the natural disasters, the COVID pandemic, and the Cabo Delgado insurgency. Around 3 million jobs were required to reduce the number of unemployed youth. Talapa stated that the government intends to create jobs as part of the Five Year Program. The program was officially dedicated to the employment of local unemployed youth.

The Mozambican government reportedly told Total at recent meetings that it was working on restoring security around Palma to enable the resumption of work on the gas exploration and liquefaction plants in Afungi.  Total on 26 April declared force majeure in its contracts with suppliers for the project, allowing it to violate the terms of these contracts.  Both the Mozambican government and Total have since insisted that Total has not abandoned the project, though it is likely to be a year or more before the project can be re-started due to insecurity.

The Electoral Institute for Sustainable Democracy in Africa (EISA) announced that the Mozambican political parties should disclose their funding sources. EISA stated that the disclosure was a form of transparency and to show who are the benefactors of the funding.

Police detained 21 individuals in Nampula who claimed that they were traveling to Cabo Delgado after reportedly being provided employment on 28 April. Police spokesman stated that false employment in the province was a recruiting method by insurgents. The police stated that suspects claimed that they had work IDs and job descriptions, but they did not have any details regarding their employer.

The Sofala Judicial Court has sentenced Mozambique Defense Forces officer Jeremias Felizardo Joao for threatening and robbery charges in Beira on 30 April. Joao stole 90,000 meticais and livestock in Gorongosa area in August 2020 as a member of the RENAMO Military Junta.

Police arrested a woman wanted for murdering her daughter by poisoning in Manica province on 3 May. The suspect forced her daughter to drink the poison to force an abortion after the mother consented to the victims sexual exploitation.

Many public transport drivers continued their strike as protest against the in Boane and Matola on the afternoon of 04 May.  The drivers previously condemned an order to accommodate only six passengers per ride as part of the COVID-19 protocols in addition to police collecting fines. The Mozambican Federation of Associations of Road Transporters (FEMATRO) was negotiating the current conditions with government.

DAG owner, Lionel Dyck reportedly has personnel on standby in Beira and in Mozambican National Parks, and could potentially remobilize to Cabo Delgado in short order if DAG was to strike a new deal with the government.

Ethiopian Airlines announced that they would suspend their services providing domestic flights within Mozambique as of Thursday, 6 May. The airlines stated that the suspension of operation was due to the market conditions brought about by the COVID pandemic. The airlines also mentioned that there was a drastic drop in demand in the local market, driving this suspension of flights.

Central Trade Union General Secretary Alexandre Munguambe stated that 2,500 workers have died due to the insurgent attacks in Cabo Delgado province. Munguambe stated that 714,000 employees were displaced by the ongoing conflict.

Local sources stated that the districts of Muidumbe, Mueda, Nangade, Palma and Mocuimboa da Praia have remained without electrical supply since September 2020. The lack of electricity was due to insurgent attacks. Around 25,000 locals are affected by a lack of electricity. Electricidade de Mozambique Director Marques stated power lines are out and that the Awasse Power Station remains disabled. Marquese clarified that electrical services will resume once the areas are secured.

EU Ambassador to Mozambique Gaspar stasted that the EU is committed to support Mozambique in their fight with insurgency. Gaspar stated that EU would support in assisting the displaced and improving security forces capabilities. The EU also said it would provide suppport base on the guidelines issued by the Mozambican government officials.

The Ministry of Health announced two COVID deaths and 31 new COVID cases in Mozmabique on 4 May. Officials stated that the current active cases were at 2.7% in relation to the total number of cases as a total of 1,867 people remain infected with COVID.

The National Directorate of Civil Identification (DNIC) announced that decrease in demand for the national ID cards between January to April of 2021 compared to the same period during the previous year. DNIC officials stated that even with the decrease in ID card production, they have surpassed their goal of producing 225,000 ID cards. DNIC stated that they would surpass their goal of 900,000 cards.

The New Democracy Movement (ND) group called on the government to accept the SADC's proposal against the insurgents in Cabo Delgado on the morning of 5 May. The New Democracy members stated the SADC can gradually withdraw their forces after training national security forces. ND members stated that the government's "irresponsible pride" was only limiting the potential support to logistical and tactical aid.

Public transport vehicles drivers in Maputo are reported to be protesting against the implementation of a new automated ticketing system. The drivers claimed that they would be charged with unknown amounts by this system. This comes as the government intends to implement an automated ticketing system where a 13 meticais fare is implemented and 1.5 meticais goes to the Maputo Metropolitan Transport Agency.

Local sources stated that poachers have returned to Magude after four suspects were detained during an operation in the first quarter of the year. Five court cases were ongoing related to the the illegal slaughter of wild animals in the area. Authorities stated that several of the firearms seized used to poach were being smuggled back out and being sold to poachers.  Poachers may be collaborating with security force elements in the area.

Employees creating masks under the Maputo City Council in Magoanine C, Maputo City claimed that they have not been paid their salaries. The Maputo City Council partnered with the Turkish Cooperation and Coordination Agency for Africa (TIKA) to produce masks locally with each employee to be paid 3,750 meticais per month.

The local government of Zambezia announced that they have collected 8 tons of relief goods to provide support to the IDPs in Cabo Delgado. The gathering of food is part of the the “Zambezia in arms with Cabo Delgado” movement which started on 20 April.

Oil and Gas Industry analysts say the delay in LNG projects in Mozambique will likely mean a start of production in 2026, and that the Rovuma LNG project could be delayed to 2029.  This could lead to a world wide deficit of 5.6 mpta in 2029.  Shortages in 2024 and 2025 could also be on the horizon.

FRELIMO officials announced that the Central Committee of their party will conduct a meeting between 22 and 23 May. The meeting was to discuss the 2021 Party Program and prepare the General, Legislative and Provincial Assemblies Elections.

Boat operators transporting displaced individuals between Palma and Pemba stated that the route was "difficult". Sailors stated that due to the high seas and wind, wooden boats were not safe, while other boats were targeted by insurgents. The passengers also are suffering as several IDPs are affected by bad weather, hunger, and sea sickness.

US Secretary of State and South Africa Minister of International Relations agreed to cooperate in combating insurgents in Cabo Delgado on 5 May. It is not immediately clear what this cooperation will entail.

The International Organization for Migrants (IOM) stated that IDPs displaced from Palma have increased to 36,000 during the week. The IDPs had previously totaled at 30,000 from the area. IOM stated that the influx of IDPs is constant and contradicts the government's statement that "the situation is under control".

Health officials stated that the vaccination campaign intended to inoculate 700 journalists working for 63 media outlets in Mozambique starting this Wednesday, 5 May. The Ministry intends to vaccinate a total of 1241 journalists both foreign and local across the country.

US troops in Mozambique on 06 May were reported to have completed a 2 month training of a batch of Mozambican marines in "tactical capabilities, wounded care, shooting, and execution of a mission while avoiding damage to civilians and property".  US forces will provide Mozambican marines with a second training in July.

The President of Equatorial Guinea Teodoro Obiang called on Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP) to be more involved in combating the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. The President of Equatorial Guinea stated that the insurgents were well funded and trained outside of the country and were able to aggressively conduct terror in the province by destroying personal and public property.

The Mozambican government announced that 280 million USD has been mobilized to implement the "Energy for All" program. The program was to allow 400,000 households to be part of the electrical grid and services. The program was to go parallel with the Five Year Program, which was to increase availability of electricity in homes from 34% to 64% countrywide.

The National Hydrocarbon Company (ENH) cancelled a dozens of public tenders ranging from the construction of infrastructures to the provision of services. The tenders were to be conducted in Maputo, Vilankulo and Pemba areas. The cancellation comes after the suspension of Total's LNG project.

The Zambezia Court has acquitted the Quelimane Mayor for libel charges against two MDM members. This comes as MDM members, Jose Lobo and Domingos Albuquerque claimed that the mayor planned to assassinate them after becoming mayor on 2019.

The UN stated that around 3 million people are expected to be affected by the ongoing food crisis in Mozambique. The UN previously issued a document saying that around 2.4 million people are already affected by the food crisis in the country. An estimate by the Global Network Against Food  Crises (GNAFC) that around 250,000 more people are likely to be affected by the crisis, while 310,000 individuals were deemed as in a state of "food emergency".

The EU is considering deploying a civilian training mission to Mozambique in support against insurgency. EU Foreign Policy Chief Josep Borrell stated that the country is requesting for assistance and that the EU will "try to send a training mission".

Sources claimed that insurgents are currently active south of Mocimboa de Praia. The insurgents were using trucks to bring supplies to their old bases near Messalo River and Mbau. The supplies were suspected to be transported via boats from Mocimboa de Praia or the looted goods from Palma.

Sources claimed that insurgents are currently active south of Mocimboa de Praia. The insurgents were using trucks to bring supplies to their old bases near Messalo River and Mbau. The supplies were suspected to be transported via boats from Mocimboa de Praia or the looted goods from Palma.

Sources stated that an insurgent presence were noted near Chai, south of Mocimboa de Praia. The insurgents were using trucks to transport their supplies to their old bases near the Messalo River and Mbau. The insurgent may intend advance towards Macomia or southern areas after the insurgents were reportedly supplying old bush bases previously used by the group.
Insurgents on or before 30 April killed at least 4 people near Matemo island, local sources reported, saying the four bodies were found floating in the area.
A group of 10 insurgents on or before 30 April were reported to have robbed a group of IDPS fleeing the Palma area of food and two speedboats.
Insurgents were reported by IDPs fleeing the Palma area to be beheading 3-4 people per day in the Palma area and setting houses on fire.

The US Agency for International Development (USAID) announced that it would provide support in Cabo Delgado, saying it would provide $700,000 in humanitarian assistance in partnership with the UNHCR for as many as 28,000 people displaced by the recent Palma attacks.

The Ministry of Health announced one COVID death and 56 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 6 May. 352 individuals recovered during the reporting period. 41 of the cases were recorded in Maputo while the remaining 15 were in Sofala and Nampula. Three new hospital admissions were reported. While 36 were still hospitalized.

The Ministry of Health recorded a single death and 21 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 5 May. The cases breakdown are as follows: 15 in Maputo City, 2 in Nampula, 1 in Maputo province, and 1 in Inhambane, 1 in Tete, and 1 in Zambezia.

The Mozambican government announced the cancellation of registration of Mozambican citizens living in Malawi.  The group of 1,056 Mozambicans had irregularities with their registrations, leading to this cancellation.

Municipal officers expelled dozens of informal vendors from the Malhampsene Transportation Terminal in Matola at around 06:00 of 6 May. The vendors complained to the officials that they do not have an official location to place their stalls.

RENAMO Parliament Member Herminio Morais accused FRELIMO officials of sabotaging DDR. Morais stated that FRELIMO has created an environment that would not allow DDR to conclude, saying authorities in many cases are "pursuing" RENAMO members who seek to join the DDR process.  As of 21 April, 2600 former armed RENAMO members have joined the DDR process.
Security forces arrested a Tanzanian national for trying to renew fake ID card at a National Directorate of Civil Identification (DNIC) in Maputo.
Fires were reported in the south of Palma due to a suspected insurgent attack on 05 May.  No further details regarding this incident are currently available.
Insurgents abducted four civilians during an attack in Chai village of Macomia District on 30 April.
Insurgents abducted several civilians during a raid on Pangane, northeast of Macomia, on 30 April. 5 civilians were beheaded by the insurgents during this attack.
Insurgents abducted several civilians during a raid on Pangane, northeast of Macomia, on 30 April. 5 civilians were beheaded by the insurgents during this attack.
Security forces arrested two suspected insurgents in Macomia on 2 May.  The two suspects had been moving "suspiciously" in the area at the time of their arrest.

South African ambassador to Angola, Oupa Monareng stated on 4 May, that a group of South African “technicians”, possibly military members, were in Cabo Delgado. The “technicians” were to assess what support South Africa should provide to Mozambique. The assessment by South Africa comes after the SADC technical team conducted an assessment in Cabo Delgado and recommended a 3,000 man force to support the Mozambican military in the province against the ongoing insurgency.

SERNIC seized around 72kg of illegal drugs inside a consignment of chess board boxes from Netherlands at the warehouse of the Mozambican Post Office, Maputo on 27 April. Two people were detained over alleged involvement with the recovered drugs. Authorities on 30 April destroyed the said illicit drugs including  2.14 kilos of cocaine, 12.25 kilos of heroin, two kilos of methamphetamine, 39.4 kilos of cathinone (also known as benzoylethanamine), 15.15 kilos of cannabis, 1.04 kilos of ecstasy and a large quantity of syringes.

Security forces detained a human trafficker and 50 illegal Ethiopian immigrants in Zumbo town of Tete province on 2 May. The immigrants were found inside an open box vehicle. The immigrants reportedly crossed from Zimbabwe to Mozambique intending to reach South Africa. The immigrants were detained at a local police station for questioning.

Suspected RENAMO dissidents attacked the residence of the head of the post for the Capirizanje AP in Moatize district at around 23:45 of 3 May with small arms fire. No casualties were reported.  The attackers left a letter behind after the shooting contesting the leadership of Ossufo Momade as head of RENAMO.  This followed a similar attack on 10 April also at Capirizanje.

Hundreds residents of Primeiro de Maio protested by blocking access to the Vale mine in Moatize at around 16:45 on 6 May. The protest was against a lack of access to Moatize River disrupting local livelihoods. The locals accused Vale Mining Company’s expansion of causing a blockade of river access. The mining company stated that they did not owe the locals any compensation after they signed a Memorandum of Understanding for their expansion. The locals stated that meetings were conducted with the mining company but no resolution was reached regarding the company’s strategy to compensate them for a loss of livelihoods.

A fire burned down four transit buses parked Camionagem de Mocambique in Inhagoia, south Maputo city, on the night of 6 May. No casualties were reported. No details were specified regarding what started the fire.

column4: Gems mined in Msawise Village of Niassa are reportedly being smuggled to Malawi. The unlicensed gems were then marked and claimed that they were mined in Malawi.  Wildlife smuggling from this area of Niassa also is transited into Malawi.

Sources stated has been a recent increase in illegal immigrants traveling from Nairobi to Pemba via Mozambique Airlines (LAM). The immigrants were given a free seat that is unregistered with LAM. Upon arrival to Pemba the illegal immigrants were asked to stay behind and are allowed entry by immigration officers who are part of this smuggling ring, according to a report on organized crime.
Human traffickers reportedly have established a smuggling route from Malawi to Tete province, circumventing Cabo Delgado, which had been a primary people smuggling route prior to the insurgency.

A recent report indicated that heroin smugglers have shifted their smuggling routes from Cabo Delgado to Niassa. The heroin is usually smuggled along with food items were previously transported to Mueda via the Unity Bridge along Rovuma River. The current route now has shifted to Lichinga along dirt roads of Niassa province, avoiding insurgent controlled areas and security forces deployed in these areas.
Insurgents are reportedly actively recruiting local youths from Zanzibar who travel to Mtwara in Southern Tanzania before then travelling into Cabo Delgado to join the insurgency.
Insurgents according to a new report are transporting supplies and new recruits via boats to Mocimboa da Praia from Mtwara in Tanzania. Dhows travel at night to avoid detection from Mtwara to MDP.

Insurgents have reportedly established a temporary smuggling base in an island along Rovuma River. The supplies at the smuggling base are transported from Tanzania south into insurgent territory.  Previous reports have also alluded to this base.

Drug smugglers have shifted to different drug smuggling routes in Mozambique, bringing heroin and methamphetamine into Mozambique via Pemba, Nacala, and Angoche, circumventing Mocimboa da Praia and Quissanga. The drug trafficking routes were changed due to the new areas being “safer” as areas impacted by the insurgency are more heavily surveilled.

Local sources stated that insurgents who were positioned near Ilha de Macaloe attacked two civilian boats on the afternoon of 3 May. 7 civilians died and several others were injured. Insurgents reportedly abducted several of the escaping civilians. A group of 40 individuals kidnapped in this incident later managed to escape from insurgent custody in the Pangane area and fled to Macomia by walking. The individuals were used as slave labor after being detained and were originally kidnapped near Macaloe island on 03 May while fleeing from Palma after the assault on the town.

Security forces deployed to disperse the protesters blocking access to the Vale mines in Moatize on the afternoon of 6 May. The protesters previously demanded compensation from the mining company for disrupting their access to the nearby river.  Several people were arrested in this operation.

South African Regional Airlines, Airlink will begin providing flights to Maputo to Kenyan Airlines passengers. The airlines signed a new agreement to diversify its services and operations.

The Ministry of Health announced one new COVID deaths and 30 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 7 May.  Maputo recorded a total of 13 cases, while Niassa had four cases. Cases have increased to 70,138 positive cases registered. 36 were still currently hospitalized.

Minister of Health Armindo Tiago stated on 7 May that no Indian COVID variant cases has been detected among the COVID patients in Mozambique. Tiago called on the public to adhere to the safety precautions as the Indian variant is more infectious and fatal.

Insurgents were reported on 06 May to be in the vicinity of Ngalonga village in Nangade District; many civilians fled the area and were reported to be sleeping in the nearby bush due to this development.

Villagers detained an individual after he was heard chanting "Allah Akbar" and suspected of being an insurgent in Nangade on the night of 6 May. The suspect was later handed over to security forces. Security forces later confirmed the suspect's links with the insurgents.
Police detained 24 illegal Malawian immigrants being transported by a bus in Inhambane on 7 May. The immigrants confessed that they intended to travel to South Africa.

Portugal and Mozambique Defense Ministers were set to sign a new agreement on Monday, 10 May on military cooperation. The agreement, Defense Cooperation Framework 2021-2026, is reported to be a "multifaceted response" that would provide for the training of Mozambican special forces, marines and commandos, and supply of ground-to-air equipment, and information sharing.

Locals raised concerns of regarding not receiving COVID subsidies while waiting in lines at Malanga, south Maputo City, on 7 May. The National Institute of Social Action (INAS) attended to only 38 individuals on their list. INAS spokesperson Cristiano Inguane stated that the subsidy was initially “discredited” causing the confusion. Inguane adds that the subsidy was not taken seriously by the public last year and now large amounts of individuals are flocking at payment posts.  This situation could eventually trigger unrest.
A subsea installation ENI vessel docked at Maputo is travelling to waters off Cabo Delgado, after Cabo Delgado's waters were declared a risk zone.
Local media stated that no specific date was scheduled for new the SADC Troika meeting on the Cabo Delgado insurgency. The meeting was previously postponed after having been scheduled for 29 April.

International Organization for Migration (IOM) stated 40,003 IDPs have fled Palma district as of May. 913 IDPs were newly registered in recent days.  IOM stated that the expected displaced is still higher and many individuals are still not registered.

The EU for Foreign Policy and Common Security, Josep Borrell stated on 6 May that military trainers and soldiers to train Mozambican forces should be deployed before the end of the year, saying Portugal has already offered to provide 60 soldiers as part of a training force, but also said the EU should provide additional troops as well.

Sources stated that on 07 May that 20,000 IDPs are still stranded in Quitunda over a month after the assault on Palma. The IDPs are still outside the Afungi site unable to travel to other areas due to the closure of the site.

Dozens of IDPs are still stranded on border with Tanzania, specifically in Qurinde area of Quionga Administrative Post, waiting to cross into Tanzania.  Those who fled from the area fled from Palma and other nearby areas.
Police arrested a couple after they threw scalding water on a woman due to the dispute involving their children in Nacala.

Local sources stated that more displaced people were expected to arrive in Pemba over coming days. Cabo Delgado Governor Tauabo stated that many IDPs were known to still be in transit to Pemba.

20 elephants on 07 May were reported to be posing a threat to locals in Massale village of Matutiune district. The elephants were transferred to Zinave National Park. The elephants previously resided in Maputo Special Reserve of the district.
The Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA) stated that business losses have reached 148.11 million USD due to terrorism in Cabo Delgado.

South African President Ramaphosa on 07 May stated that South African reserve forces were ready to provide assistance to intervene in Cabo Delgado if the SADC calls for a reserve force. Ramaphosa said that the withdrawal of investors from Mozambique is a great concern for SADC and Southern Africa Countries.

The Bishop of Pemba D. Antonio Juliasse in a 27 April interview strongly criticized the Mozambique government for not discussing the insurgency in Cabo Delgado frequently. The bishop stated that the government was not fighting against corruption which has reached higher levels. The bishop also said that there were no clear indications on how to resolve the conflict in province.

Locals have stated that wild animals have also been attacking and killing people as a civilian was killed by a buffalo attack and another civilian was killed during a crocodile attack in Moatize recent. Elephants were reported to trample on agricultural fields in Mahel and Mapulanguene AP.

According to the Director of the National Administration of Conservation Areas, Mateus Mutemba on 08 May, around 20 people were arrested between January-April 2020 over alleged involvement in poaching across the country. Elephants, rhinos, and lions were targeted by the criminals. Mutemba added that due to awareness programs led by the government, crime rates against wildlife have decreased.

The Ministry of Health announced one new COVID deaths and 43 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 08 May.  Greater Maputo recorded a total of 16 cases, while Niassa had five cases. Over the last 24 hours, three people were hospitalized and five were discharged.

Electricidade de Mocambique (EDM) stated on 06 May that they will set a fixed exchange rate of 75 meticais per USD to be applied for the conversion of the dollar components of remunerations and pensions of their workers. This is a 17 meticais difference from the previous conversion of 58 meticais per USD.

Maputo Province raised eight tons of food products to be donated for the families affected by the insecurity in Cabo Delgado Province. The products raised include flour, rice, cooking oil, sugar, mineral water, pasta and other non-perishables. The project was initiated by a group of women, Marinheiras de Moz, and supported by the local government to provide support for more than 700,000 displaced people.

Security forces arrested six illegal Pakistani immigrants who attempted to cross Ressano Garcia border, according to sources on 09 May. The suspects were in the company of a Mozambican national who acted as their 'guide' who was also arrested by the police. Upon interrogation, the suspects confessed that they entered the country from the border of Calomue border, district of Angonia on 03 May, and were bound to South Africa allegedly looking for better living conditions.

The Ministry of Health announced one new COVID deaths and 28 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 09 May. The breakdown of new cases are as follows-  12 cases recorded from Maputo city, four from Maputo province, five cases from Niassa, four from Sofala, and one each from Cabo Delgado, Zambezia and Tete. Over the last 24 hours, 43 people have recovered from the virus– 28 in Nampula, eight in Niassa and seven in Inhambane.

According to the Minister of Economy and Finance Adriano Maleiane on 04 May, the controversial bill on the statute for parliamentary officials and agents will entail additional costs of 104 million meticais. The draft bill has been approved the following day unanimously by all three parliamentary benches (Frelimo, Renamo, and MDM). The debate and vote on the bill will be held on 12 May.

The World Bank announced on 07 May that an additional USD 20 million support will be awarded for small, medium and micro enterprises affected by Idai and Kenneth Cyclones in Beira City. The announcement came a day after World Bank provided a USD 200 million support for the post cyclone recovery invested in projects related to water supply, reconstruction of public infrastructure, disease prevention, food security, social protection and weather early warning systems.

President Nyusi visited Zambia today, 10 May, following an invitation by counterpart President Edgar Chagwa Lungu. Nyusi is set to participate in the regional inauguration ceremony of the Kazungula Bridge and the facilities of the Single Border Post, linking Zambia and Botswana. The inauguration will also be attended by other SADC Heads of State and Government.

According to the 07 May analysis of the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), around 900,000 people are anticipated to face severe hunger in the provinces of Cabo Delgado, Nampula, and Niassa from April to September. In addition, food insecurity is expected to increase in the province of Cabo Delgado due to disruption of livelihood and markets caused by repeated displacement of the people. Meanwhile, harvests in the coastal and intermediate zone are expected to be below average in Cabo Delgado and Nampula due to below average rainfall.  769,000 of the 900,000 who will face severe hunger are in Cabo Delgado.

On 06 May, the Chinese Government handed over more than seven million meticais worth of food products and supplements for the victims of insurgency in Cabo Delgado. The donation reflects the good relationship between China and Mozambique.
Insurgents attacked Ngalonga village in Nangade District, looting food and burning houses on 07 May.  Pro-government militia later responded and drove the insurgents out of the village.

Pro-government local militiamen repelled an attack launched by insurgents in the village of Ngalonga, Nangade on the morning of 7 May. At least three insurgents were killed during the confrontation. Several houses were set ablaze while food items were looted during the attack. The incident came two days after an individual suspected to be linked with the insurgency in Cabo Delgado was detained after he was seen traveling around Ngalonga village.

The Minister of Defense, Jaime Neto, and his Portuguese counterpart, Joao Gomes Cravinho, will meet today 10 May to sign a cooperation agreement between the two countries until 2026. The signing will be held in Oeiras, Portugal where Neto will carry out an official four-day meeting.
On the evening of 09 May, armed criminals allegedly looted Shaquila Lodge in Nacala District. No other details are on this incident are currently available.

The abducted son of a prominent businessman, Michal Nathoobai, regained his freedom on 06 May. He was abducted by four suspects around 1900hrs on the terrace of the Quinta do Nico restaurant in Quelimane on 15 April. Zambezia Police confirmed his release, however, the details of his release are still unclear, and police were reportedly not involved in his release.

Former dissident leader Andre Matsangaissa stated that RENAMO dissident leader, Mariano Nhongo will surrender soon. Matsangaissa said that Nhongo will surrender to achieve peace and  other high level dissident leaders he cannot give anymore details regarding the departure of Nhongo from the dissident positions.  Nhongo himself in public statements has remained defiant towards the government.

Reports indicated that there have been 3,400 cholera cases and 16 deaths in Cabo Delgado between January and April 2021. During the entirety of 2020, there were 2,690 cholera cases and 38 deaths reported in Cabo Delgado. An increasing number IDPs in Chiure, Montepuez, Pemba, Metuge, and Ancuabe districts are impacted by the disease. Possible cholera cases were reported in Mecufi District due to the presence of cases of acute water diarrhea.

The Mozambican government announced that 4 out of 10 girls in the country get married before the age of 18.  21% of girls are married between 13-17.  Mozambique has some of the highest rates in the world of child marriages.

20 armed men attacked and killed a South African national in Nacala Porto on 9 May.  The man was reportedly the manager of an area hotel.  The Lodge was also reportedly looted and vandalized during the attack. Other local sources stated that the South African died of a heart attack.

The Portuguese government announced that it would deploy an additional 60 troops to Mozambique as part of new cooperation agreement. The agreement will remain in place until 2026. A total of 80 Portuguese troops will be deployed to Mozambique for this training, which will involve counter-insurgency tactics, intelligence training, and drone surveillance training as well.
Mozambique Minister Defence Net stated that Mozambique Marine training began on 10 May in Maputo City. The training was part of the five-year training from 2021 to 2026.

The EU is considering sending 200-300 soldiers as part of training mission in Mozambique. EU for Foreign Policy and Common Security, Josep Borrell stated that the negotiation with Mozambique has gone slowly. Borrell previously stated that the EU would send soldiers within the year as part of the EU's response to the Mozambican government’s call for assistance in combating the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

The Portuguese and Mozambican governments on 10 May signed a new agreement regarding the training of the Mozambican military on 10 May. Mozambique Minister of Defence Neto stated that the training was to be accompanied by other means of assistance which should enable the military to more effectively fight against the insurgents.

95 N1 level teachers were suspended from service after being hired “irregularly” in Niassa during 2020. Government officials announced that the teachers were hired during a time when hiring was suspended. Officials clarified that the suspension on the teachers was due to the teachers receiving salaries without having official contracts.

Local sources stated that there recently has been “irregular” distribution of food donated by the World Food Program in Chiure  in Cabo Delgado. Locals stated that several IDPs claimed that they have not received food support for the past three months, with no explanation as to why no food has been distributed.

A group of 40 individuals managed recently to escape from insurgent custody in the Pangane area and fled to Macomia by walking. The individuals were used as slave labor after being detained and were originally kidnapped near Macaloe island on an unknown date, likely in early April, while fleeing from Palma after the assault on the town.

Police announced that they would set up an anti-kidnapping brigade. The Brigade would be 200 units of trained police from Nhamatanda in Sofala province. The brigade would focus on the speedy resolution of kidnapping cases. This comes after multiple recent kidnappings in April and early May across the country.

The Association of Small Importers of Alcoholic Drinks (APIBA) called the government to extend hours of sale for alcohol. APIBA stated that alcohol trading was currently between 09:00 and 13:00 during Mondays to Saturdays. APIBA stated that this small window had negative impact on the businesses.

Students protested by gathering and marching towards the Republic Assembly building on the morning of 11 May. The protesters were against the approval of new benefits for parliamentary officials and agents. Security forces deployed and detained a protester while preventing the protesters from gathering outside the Republic Assembly building. The protesters were dispersed and later gathered at the Seventh Police Precinct demanding the release of another student who was prevented from protesting.

Around 40 protested by gathering and marching towards the Independence Square, in front of the City Hall on the morning of 11 May. The protesters were against the approval of new benefits for parliamentary officials and agents. Security forces deployed and detained a protester while preventing the protesters from gathering outside the Republic Assembly building. The protesters were dispersed and later gathered at the Seventh Police Precinct demanding the release of another student who was prevented from protesting.

Security forces deployed and detained a protester, Valdo Nhamuneque, while preventing student protesters from gathering outside the Independence Square on 11 May. A source claimed that the students sat in front of the station where Valdo was held. The students previously protested by gathering and travelling towards the square on the morning of 11 May. The protests were against the approval of new benefits for parliamentary officials and agents.

VISA sets up an independent exchange rate for the Mozambique metical. The new artificial exchange rate was fixed to 75 meticais per USD compared to the real current rate of 58 meticais per USD. The metical has been the strongest performing currency in the world in 2021, and made significant gains against the dollar; Visa may consider the current exchange rate as unstable and not reflective of the current economic situation in the country, according to economists.

Sources reported on 10 and 11 May that's that oil services company are pulling personnel out of Cabo Delgado, and relocating them to Maputo. The withdrawal comes after Total’s announcement of a general withdrawal from the region.  Other sources however have called these reports "fake news" and said some oil service companies had already pulled personnel out of the area in the aftermath of the Palma attack.

Bishop Alberto Arejula stated that the Mozambican government's action has focused on defending "the profits" from the well-being for a small handful of wealthy people. Bishop Alberto Arejula stated that the issue in Cabo Delgado has several facets and the government has focused at the oil and gas projects while neglecting local people.  The Bishop of Pemba also recently strongly and openly criticized the government over its handling of the Cabo Delgado insurgency.
Local sources stated that a woman was killed after being run over by a municipal police vehicle at a intersection along 24 de Julho Avenues in Maputo City at around 16:45 on 5 May.

Insurgents in recent days have been reported to be assembling in significant numbers in the Mocimboa da Praia area, and could potentially launch a new offensive after Ramadan, which ends on 12 May.  Insurgents' most likely targets are Palma, Mueda, Nangade, or Macomia towns, if a new significant offensive is launched.

On the afternoon of 11 May, former Minister of Labour, former Governor of Sofala province  and former ambassador to Angola, Helena Taipo, was released from pre-trial detention over alleged involvement in receiving bribes worth 113 million meticais at the National Social Security Institute (INSS). She was detained for two years  at the Preventive Establishment of the City of Maputo and currently is awaiting trial.

The Ministry of Health announced one new COVID death and 29 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 11 May. 12 of the new cases were recorded from Maputo city and Maputo province, and 10 cases in Zambezia. Over the last 24 hours, 85 people have recovered from the virus while 24 people are still hospitalized.

The Mozambican state electricity company (EDM) announced on 10 May the elimination of the payment of salaries for its employees in dollars. The decision was made after EDM received complaints following their initial statement to an exchange rate (75 meticais per dollar) which was higher than the country's current real exchange rate.

At least two UH-1H helicopters were seen flying around the coastal districts of Nampula on 11 May. Some of the locals believed that it was a trial flight from the military base in Nacala while others claimed it was conducted to intimidate locals who allegedly support the insurgency.

US travel advisory for Mozambique was updated on 10 May, and warns against travel to Pemba due to terrorism threats. Authorities also warned travelers to reconsider going to some parts of Sofala and Manica provinces due to crime.

According to the International Organization for Migration (IOM) data on 11 May, an additional 1,093 displaced persons from Palma were registered across Cabo Delgado, bringing the total number to 46,748 displaced persons from Palma in the aftermath of the insurgent assault on the town.

Security forces released a protester who was detained after a demonstration outside the Republic Assembly building on 11 May. The students previously protested by gathering and marching towards the Republic Assembly building on the morning of 11 May. The protests were against the approval of new benefits for parliamentary officials and agents.

The Mozambican Health Ministry stated on 10 May that new COVID variant cases found in India and Brazil have not been detected among the COVID patients in the country.  Authorities urged the public to adhere to the safety precautions as the new variants are more infectious and fatal.

The National Statistics Institute (INE) stated that the annual inflation has deflated from 5.76 percent in March to 5.19 percent in April. An average 0.03 percent fall in prices this month was seen in the consumer price indices from the cities of Maputo, Nampula, and Beira. Most significant price fall were for  tomatoes with 5.8 percent, fresh prawns with 12.3 percent, dried fish with 3.3 percent, cabbage with 8.9 percent, lettuce with 5.1 percent, and coconuts with 3.2 percent decrease.

A South African firm has allegedly hired to go and remove equipment left behind in Palma/Afungi by oil company subcontractors. The operations will allegedly commence on 18 May.   Several other sources however denied reports of this equipment recovery operation.

Sources this week accused the Mozambican military at Quitunda of holding up to 20,000 people in the Quitunda area outside of Afungi "hostage" and as a shield against potential insurgent attacks in the Palma and Afungi areas.  Thousands remain in the area and have not been allowed to flee the area by the Mozambican military.

Insurgents could potentially launch an attack on Quitunda village after the end of Ramadan on 12 May.  Insurgents have previously threatened attacks on Palma and the Quitunda area since the assault on the Palma area.

Sources on 11 May stated that the military troops in the Quitunda area continue to not allow the distribution of food and aid. Local volunteers from Vamoz were allowed to distribute the last of 30 tons of food sent last week.
Insurgents on 11 May were reportedly in recent days moved at least 4 large trucks captured in Palma towards Mocimboa de Praia, potentially to fortify insurgent positions in the district.
Sources on 11 May reported air force activity near the main road between Mocimboa to Mueda, reportedly to target any potential insurgent move along the road towards Mueda.

A source on 11 May disclosed that South Africa and Mozambique had had a discussion regarding Operation Copper. The discussion of the anti-piracy operation, which was launched 10 years ago, could be about its expansion into Cabo Delgado waters. Details about the discussion have yet been ascertained.

MDM on 11 May suspended Manuel Tocova and other party members in Nampula over the alleged intention of the officials to destabilize the provincial delegation of the party. Other affected party members include Maria Luísa Marrovica, Sismo Eduardo, Trinta Vicente, Calaveta, Isildo, Zito, and Luciano Tarieque.

The President of the Independent Party of Mozambique (PIMO), Yaqub Sibindy, stated on 10 May that the government should consider training guerillas to fight the Cabo Delgado insurgents as the latter also use guerilla tactics. He added that the 'government guerillas' should also train young fighters in tactics similar to the insurgent's strategy.

Only nine people infected with COVID-19 remained hospitalized at Polana Canico General Hospital, Maputo City on 11 May, out of 31 admitted across the country. It is recalled that the hospital reached its maximum capacity following the surge of COVID-19 cases last January and February 2021.

Secretary of State for the province of Niassa, Dinis Vilanculos, stated on 12 May that Niassa residents are being targeted for recruitment by the Cabo Delgado insurgents. Evidence suggests that young people from the districts of Ngauma, Muembe and Nipepe were recruited as the insurgents took advantage of the poor living conditions in these districts.

President Nyusi called on the media to show “respect for human dignity” while conducting their coverage of Cabo Delgado. The president stated that media should respect the rules in taking news and images about the insurgency in the province. This comes as 11 new members were sworn in to the Superior Council for Social Communication.

Sources clarified that a previous article regarding dismantling of project site in Afungi are “entirely untrue”. The previous report stated that oil and gas companies have hired a company to remove infrastructure and equipment around Afungi in response to the insurgent attack in Palma. An oil and gas spokesman stated that one of the companies stated in the article does not have equipment in Afungi and that the usage of the word “dismantling” was misleading.

Local police sources on 12 May said that crimes rates have declined in Sofala province. Police commander Joaquim Sive stated that there was an indirect reduction in crime. Police say they are still facing waves of vehicle theft, drug smuggling, illegal weapon usage, and robberies.
Various Indian and UK COVID variant strains this week have been detected in South Africa. The virus could spread to Mozambique as vaccinations in South Africa have slowed down.
The Ministry of Health announced 20 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 12 May. 13 cases were reported in Maputo province, five in Tete, and two in Nampula. No COVID deaths were reported.

The Catholic Charity Caritas suspended food deliveries in Pemba of Cabo Delgado after running out of funds on 5 May. The director of Caritas stated that their stocks in the warehouse emptied and they are currently negotiating for additional funds to purchase food.

Insurgents reportedly captured four transportation boats and six fishing vessels, abducting traveling displaced individuals near Makolowe Island on 29 April. The insurgents forced the individuals to land near Pangane.

Insurgents reportedly captured four transportation boats and six fishing vessels, abducting traveling displaced individuals near Makolowe Island on 29 April. The insurgents forced the individuals to land near Pangane.

Local sources stated that a woman claimed to have falsely reported the presence of insurgents in Nanjua of Metuge on 2 May. The report caused panic among locals causing displacements to resettlement centers.

Pro-government local militiamen ambushed insurgents retreating to Mocimboa da Praia near Ngalonga village on 7 May. Two insurgents were killed during the ambush. Pro-government militia had previously clashed with insurgents at Ngalonga earlier in the day.
Unknown men, likely insurgents, abducted three civilians in Napulubo and Nanga B, Macomia after traveling to gather water on 7 May.

Suspicious individuals, likely insurgents, reportedly pursued five girls who were attempting to gather water in Macomia on 8 May, though the girls escaped. This comes after a day as three girls were suspected to be abducted after attempting to gather water.
Unknown men, likely insurgents, abducted six girls who went to a watering well to gather water near Macomia on 25 April.
Security forces detained an individual working as a security guard for the Amarula Palma Hotel on 28 March. The detainee was reported fleeing during the attack on Palma leading to his arrest.

Security forces reportedly tortured a detained security guard working for the Amarula Palma Hotel during interrogations. The security forces were attempting to force him to confess he was a member of the insurgents. He was later released in early May in Pemba.

Security forces released a detained security guard on or before 06 May previously worked for the Amarula Hotel in Palma. The guard had been arrested after the assault on Palma, and was reportedly tortured and accused of being a member of the insurgency prior to his release.

The World Bank approved a 100 million USD grant for the International Development Association (IDA) to support the Mozambique government's Economic Linkages for Diversification Project. The project was to support businesses to foster economic growth.

President Nyusi was set on 13 May to travel to Paris to conduct a meeting with the French and Angola President, along with the Portuguese Prime Minister to discuss the development of African economies.

Civil society organizations accused a police of shooting and injuring two civilians during a dispute at a payment claim from the compensation of Vale Mining Company in Moatize on 7 May. The police was trying to clear a group of locals when the incident occurred.
An IDP claimed 6 May that insurgents have collected several stolen cars and motorbikes and may be creating their own dirt roads between Palma from Mocimboa da Praia.
column15: Between Palma and Mocimboa da Praia

column4: Reports recently have indicated that insurgents are posting lookouts off the Mocimboa da Praia coast to ambush boats transporting IDPs near Pangane coast.
Reports recently have indicated that insurgents are posting lookouts off the Mocimboa da Praia coast to ambush boats transporting IDPs near Pangane coast.

Around 0700hrs on 09 January, gunmen attacked a column of trucks in Zove/ Gooda area, Chibabava, Sofala, which led to the death of one person who was struck by two bullets. The attack, which resulted to major material damages, was attributed to the self-proclaimed Renamo Military Junta.

Unidentified gunmen opened fire on a train on the Sena Line travelling between Mazamba and Cundue in Cheringoma district at around 0610hrs on Thursday.  The driver of the train was hit in the shoulder in the attack and was taken to a local hospital.  Railway officials said that the attackers fired "several shots" at the train but were not seen during the attack.  During the 2014-2017 "proto war" RENAMO dissidents carried out attacks along this railway line, though the line has not been previously targeted during the ongoing RENAMO dissident insurgency.
column15: Sena Line between Mazamba and Cundue in Cheringoma district

column4: President Nyusi stated that Mozambique is receiving support from partner countries against insurgency in Cabo Delgado, though did not provide any more detail. Nyusi said that steps were being taken to restore tranquility to the country.

Amnesty International interviewed several survivors of the Palma attack who said that during the evacuation of white contractors was prioritized over black locals in Cabo Delgado.  Other sources however have indicated that DAG rescued a few hundred black locals and foreign nationals during the battle of Palma, and that there was no discrimination in terms of who was evacuated.  DAG later issued a statement saying it had rescued 240 people during the course of the battle for Palma, including 228 black Mozambican and other foreign nationals, 12 white foreign nationals, which included 2 dead bodies.

Minister of Health Tiago warned against a third wave of COVID in Mozambique if the public does not adhere to the strict preventive measures. Tiago stated that the warning was due to the increasing cases in South Africa, and the fact that at least a million Mozambicans were currently working in the country, which may possible lead to the virus strains crossing the border.

Municipal authorities are upgrading the coastal protection barrier off the Aevindada Marginal. The barrier was expected to be completed within four months’ time. The barrier was put in place in 2014 and noticeable damages were seen by 2019.

Doctors Without Borders (MSF) in a statement on 12 May said that the bureaucratic obstacles are slowing aid to Cabo Delgado. MSF stated that there were restrictions imposed by the government that limiting import of aid and issuance of visas for additional aid workers. MSF officials stated that the scale of the humanitarian response does not correspond to the required needs by the IDPs.

Local sources stated on 14 May that insurgents are demanding ransom money for the release of some of those they capture, and in some cases have allegedly demanded as much as 200 million metical, though this amount has not been verified.
The French Government has approved the funding of several million euro to support the IDPs affected by the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

The National Migration Service (SENAMI) announced that they have revoked fees for assistance and inspection of heavy vehicles at border crossings in Mozambique. SENAMI also increased rates of issuance of biometric documents. This includes the border facility card from 10 meticais to 50, residence declaration for foreigners from 296 meticais to 500, and exit statement document from 126 meticais to 250.

Rumors spread on the afternoon of 13 May in Mueda of an impending insurgent attack, spreading fear amid some areas of the town.  Some residents fled areas of the Rovuma neighborhood, where the attack would allegedly target first.   No attack on the town materialized however, though fighting between insurgents and pro-gov militia had been reported on 11-12 May near Diaca, about 45kms east of Mueda. This comes after previous false reports of an attack on Mueda in late April.

Pro-government militia clashed with insurgents near Diaca of Mueda district on 11-12 May. Several insurgents were detained in these clashes, with an unspecified number of insurgents killed. Other insurgents managed to escape. The insurgents were reportedly advancing towards Mueda to steal cattle and poultry.

Pro-government militia clashed with insurgents near Diaca of Mueda district on 11-12 May. Several insurgents were detained in these clashes, with an unspecified number of insurgents killed. Other insurgents managed to escape. The insurgents were reportedly advancing towards Mueda to steal cattle and poultry.

Local media sources on 13 May said that insurgents after the assault on Palma received wage increases from 100 thousand meticais to 120 thousand meticais.  Wounded insurgents are given 240 thousand meticais.  It was unclear if this is a monthly or yearly salary.  Insurgents were reported to have stolen over $1 million (and possibly significantly more) in the attack on Palma.
column15: Insurgent Impacted Areas of Cabo Delgado

column4: Some civilians who were kidnapped and either escaped or were released by insurgents in Cabo Delgado say that insurgents have abducted large numbers of children aged 11 and up who are being trained as fighters by the group.  This is one of several reports since the Palma attack that have indicated insurgents are increasingly using child soldiers.
column15: Insurgent Impacted Areas of Cabo Delgado

column4: Police said in a recent report that nationwide crime has decreased by 20 percent from the 1 to 7 May period this year compared to the same time last year. 96 crimes were recorded in comparison to the previous year of 120 crimes.

Cabo Delgado governor Valige Tauabo stated that all of Cabo Delgado province is in an "emergency" due to the Cabo Delgado insurgency. Governor Tauabo stated that the displaced were expected to remain displaced until the situation in the province has been resolved. The governor called on the local youth to avoid being recruited by the insurgents.

Zambezia Secretary of State Judite Mussacula called for “surveillance” at Zambezia IDP reception centers to detect insurgents on 11 May. The “surveillance” was to monitor insurgents who could possibly infiltrate reception centers.

The Maputo Poultry Association (ADAM) president stated the price of chicken feed, corn, soybeans, and concentrate have all risen significantly due to sellers speculating price increases. ADAM stated that the price increase were coming at an "inappropriate time" as businesses are still unprofitable due to COVID.

Visa issued a statement that exchange rates they recently established in Mozambique for electronic transactions were based on a range of rates available in currency markets or based on rates from the Mozambican government's regulatory body.

Rwandan President Paul Kagame reportedly recently sent a military team to Cabo Delgado determine the potential for the Rwandan military to provide some form of support for the Mozambican government against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  This team by 13 May was reported to be on the ground in the province.

Around one million  Mozambican citizens currently living and/or working in South Africa are currently at risk of exposure to a new "third wave" of COVID-19 in South Africa.  South Africa has recently said some new more contagious variants are currently present in the country.  Mozambicans living in SA could eventually spread these new variants into Mozambique if they return home in the coming months.

The Ministry of Health announced 28 new COVID cases were reported on the day also, with 7 in Maputo, 2 in Inhambane, 2 in Sofala, 3 in Manica, 3 in Tete, and 4 in Zambezia.  No deaths were reported. Officials stated that the recovery rate has increased to 97 percent after 267 cases recovered in Mozambique on 13 May.

President Nyusi stated on 13 May that Mozambique won’t be able to defeat terrorism alone. The president stated that terrorism does not respect borders, and saying also that Mozambique appreciates the "interest in supporting us in this struggle".  He also said claims Mozambique had refused offers of support against the insurgency "unjust" and said cooperation with several countries in regarding combating the insurgency was ongoing.

Officials donated equipment for self-employment and construction materials to 59 former RENAMO guerillas in Machaze district of Manica province on 12 May. District Administrator Joana Guinda stated that the materials were to help reintegrate the former RENAMO guerillas into society.

RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade announced on 03 May that the DDR process would be completed on schedule. Momade stated that the party is satisfied with the process and that the remaining 2621 RENAMO military members would join the process by the end of June 2021.

South African border patrol stated that stolen vehicles have been recovered during the Operation Corona along the KwaZulu-Natal - Maputo border crossing. Two vehicles, cannabis, packs of mandrax, and cocaine were seized.

South African border patrol stated that stolen vehicles have been recovered during the Operation Corona along the KwaZulu-Natal - Maputo border crossing. Two vehicles, cannabis, packs of mandrax, and cocaine were seized.

A recent report was issued indicating that some of earliest insurgent recruits to the insurgency were from the illegal miners community in Montepuez.  Many of those in this community had very poor relations with local government and security forces, and were vulnerable to recruitment by the insurgents.

President Filipe Nyusi stated that Mozambique’s economic growth is expected to be around 1.5% for 2021 and 2.8% in 2022. An International Monetary Fund (IMF) representative stated that recent projections however do not consider the economic effects of the Palma assault.

RENAMO MP Viana Magalhaes during a speech in parliament accused the FRELIMO government of “denying international support” for the fight against the  insurgency in Cabo Delgado. Magalhaes questioned the FRELIMO government's calls for sovereignty, saying this was being used as an excuse to keep foreign forces out of Mozambique. He also said the government's inaction has led to the current situation in Cabo Delgado.

Health authorities strengthened health surveillance at borders around Mozambique after reports that South Africa has confirmed recent COVID cases that were of the “Indian variant”. Health Services Director Santos stated that citizens arriving from South Africa where the variant was recorded were being registered.

Air France announced their postponement of Maputo-Paris flight from 30 June until 31 October. The reasons for the postponement were unclear. The airlines stated that passengers who have purchased their tickets could reschedule their flights.

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) on Friday called for the European Union to take a “more decisive role” in resolving the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado. IOM appealed to Portugal to provide an intervention to support Mozambican forces.

FRELIMO Party leader Sergio Pantie in parliament on Friday called for a “general mobilization” against terrorism in Cabo Delgado on 14 May. Pantie also urged the authorities to equip and modernize the defense and security forces (FDS) to confidently confront  terrorism.

On 13 May, President Nyusi stated that he is open to receive international support to fight insecurity but does not want "middlemen" or "errand boys". He added that the government is working closely with the Southern African Development Community (SADC) to mobilize support from the member countries.

A map released by the UN Office for Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs and the WFP recently lists Palma, Mocimboa da Praia, Macomia, Quissanga, and Muidumbe as areas with a “highly volatile security situation”. Insurgents are active in these districts and in most of them exercise semi-territorial control over some areas.

The exchange rate between Metical and USD significantly rose in the past week, from USD 1 = MT 65.5 from 06 April to USD 1 = MT 56.8 on 14 April. Reasons behind its sudden increase are still unknown however, experts believed hat the current economic circumstances could not explain the sudden appreciation.

On 15 May, President Nyusi urged the police forces and the Defense and Security Forces to coordinate with one another in the fight against armed violence in the country to attain better results. Nyusi highlighted importance of these coordination in dealing with Cabo Delgado insurgents in Northern Mozambique and RENAMO Military Junta in Central part of the country.

The Ministry of Health announced 49 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 15 May. 29 new cases were recorded from Maputo city, four from Maputo province, seven cases from Sofala, four from Manica, three from Inhambane and one each from Nampula and Zambezia. For the past 24 hours, 223 people have recovered from the infection. No death recorded related to the coronavirus for the past four consecutive days with the national death toll still at 826.

A suspected insurgent was arrested and severely beaten by locals of Macomia district on 13 May. Security forces arrived and rescued him from being killed. The suspect was currently being treated at a local health facility.
