Several traders have recently insisted on staying at the Zimpeto Wholesale Market despite efforts by the municipality to remove them in the area. Authorities planned to reorganize the market, thus the need of the traders to withdraw from the area. One of the traders stated that they were sent to Matendene market but there were no customers in the area.
column15: Zimpeto Wholesale Market in Maputo City

column4: The Ministry of Health announced 32 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 16 May. 10 news cases were reported each for Maputo and Manica, seven cases for Niassa and five cases for Inhambane. For the past 24 hours, 15 people have recovered from the infection. No death recorded related to the coronavirus for the past five consecutive days with the national death toll remains at 826.

Deputy Coordinator for Emergency Operations Centers of Inhambane province, Candido Mapute, stated that displaced people from Cabo Delgado that were seeking refuge in Inhambane, are receiving monthly food assistance and emergency shelter. About 61 IDPs from Cabo Delgado were reported in Massinga, Inharrime and Inhambane City.

Mozambican authorities on 17 May filed an application in the Johannesburg High Court for an order to extradite former Mozambican finance minister Manuel Chang immediately. Chang has been detained in SA for more than 28 months in relation to fraud and corruption charges as part of the "Hidden Debts Case" in Mozambique.

Ireland's Minister of State for Overseas Development Aid, Colm Brophy TD, announced on 12 May a grant of 2.6 million Euros in Irish Aid Support for Mozambique including delivery of emergency humanitarian supplies for Cabo Delgado.

President Nyusi arrived in France on 16 May to participate in a summit on Financing of African Economies to be held on 18 May. Bilateral relations between Mozambique and France and the situation of insurgency in Cabo Delgado, which led to the Total's announcement of force majeure on its activities in the province, will also reportedly be discussed.

Sources on 13 May disclosed that Total commenced the demobilization of their million-dollars worth of equipment from Afungi LNG camp.  Other sources recently however have denied this and similar reports.

The abducted son of a prominent businessman, Depesh Ramesh, was released from captivity on the morning of 17 May. He was abducted around 1930hrs on the terrace of the Quinta do Nico restaurant in Chimoio City on 25 April. Manica Police confirmed his release, however, the details of his release are not provided as the police were reportedly not involved in his release. The negotiation for the release of the victim was only between his family and the abductors.  The release of Ramesh was similar to that of the arrest of the son of a businessman in Quelimane recently, which did not involve the police and may have involved the payment of a ransom.

On 16 May, 66 out of 76 containers of logs illegally exported to China were returned to Pemba Port. A Chinese employee of the company Cheufang named Kelly, was detained after illegal logged timber left the port on August 2020. Efforts are ongoing to return the remaining containers in the country.

Cattle breeders in Magude have called for an investigation into a "strange disease" which led to the death of several cattle recently in Maputo province. More than 600 cattle have died in 2020. 75 percent of the breeders lost several animals due to lack prompt intervention by the authorities such as vaccination.

Galp Mozambique donated 45,000 visors to the Ministry of Health on 14 May to serve as protection against spread of COVID-19. Authorities claimed that the visors will aid in strengthening safety measures in a bid to prevent emergence of the coronavirus third wave.

Nacala-Porto Police arrested three individuals on 14 May over alleged involvement in the death of a South African national in Naherenque beach neighborhood four days ago. The suspects allegedly used machetes and blunt instruments to kill the victim, who was an employee of one of the companies that provides services to the Port of Nacala.
Local militia and insurgents clashed between Miteda and Muambula villages on 13 May.  No information regarding casualties were available.

Total CEO Patrick Pouyanne on 17 May said that the company its projects in Cabo Delgado, and is not pulling out of gas projects in Mozambique despite recent insurgent attacks. The company claimed that they have the confidence that the Mozambican Government will be able to restore peace in the province.  President Nyusi later said after talks with Total officials that the company "may demand that there is tranquility and peace" before restarting operations, and said Total would resume operations when the situation is "calm".

The Ministry of Health announced 21 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 17 May. The breakdown of new cases are as follows - Maputo City-4, Maputo Province-2, Inhambane-1, Sofala-2, Tete-1, Zambezia-12, and Nampula-1. Two deaths related to the coronavirus were reported after five days of no casualties. For the past 24 hours, six people have recovered from the infection while another six were hospitalized.

President Nyusi on 16 May stated that the Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration Process will not be completed until August due to financial limitations brought by the economic impact of COVID-19. 44% percent of the RENAMO's former guerillas have already joined the process, but more than 2,500 still need to be demobilized.

Several residents of Sabie administrative post in Moamba reported destruction of crops by hippos and elephants who recently escaped from surrounding conservation areas. More than 30 hectares of crops were destroyed by hippos in Malengane while elephants destroyed machambas in Mucacaza 1 community.

Reports on 17 May indicated that security forces are manipulating the distribution of food and other aid at Quitunda, near Palma, where between 11,000 - 20,000 people remain displaced in the wake of the assault on Palma.

A civilian sustained bullet wounds after an agent of the National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) shot sporadically in Beira City on 15 May. The victim was allegedly talking with his drunk friend, a border guard, when they were approached by the suspect. Reports suggest that they were having a discussion when the suspect started to shoot after an disagreement. The suspect was only detained for a few hours on the same day which prompted the victim's family to demand justice at the police station.

Agents of the National Criminal Investigation Service assigned to the Department of Investigation and Investigation of Criminal Proceedings have expressed disatisfaction over a lack of career progression and not receiving a 50 percent special bonus. The special bonus along with other perks should have reportedly been provided for agents with higher educational degrees in accordance with the law.

The Mozambican Bar Association (OAM), through its Human Rights Commission (CDHOAM) and the Provincial Councils (CPs)  announced on 18 May that they will provide legal assistance and sponsorship for people who were illegally detained or arrested though application of Habeas Corpus. The announcement was made to ensure compliance of rules involving people denied of their freedom.

Minister of Public Works, Housing and Water Resources, Joao Osvaldo Machatine, guaranteed on 17 May that 80% of the population will have access to drinking water by 2024. The goal of the project will be completed with to the inclusion of private sector.

Around 300 people in Inhambane province scheduled to receive the COVID-19 vaccine failed to come to the vaccination posts due to lack of time and/or coordination. The second dose of the vaccine will be administered in July 2021.

On 18 May, Portugal Prime Minister Antonio Costa stated that Portugal is willing to integrate military forces into any mission sent to Mozambique, and to provide any other means of support as part of an EU mission to Mozambique.  The type of support to be provided will be decided within the European Union. The statement came after Costa's meeting with Mozambican President Nyusi at the Summit on the Future of African Economies, hosted in Paris.

Surveillance at border control posts in Tete and Niassa have been heightened due to large numbers of illegal immigrants in recent months attempting to cross into Mozambique.  Local authorities in Tete said they have increased surveillance to prevent the replication of a similar situation in Tete to that of Cabo Delgado.  Illegal immigrants often cross into Mozambique with the facilitation of Mozambican criminal networks.  10 people in Tete have been arrested this year as part of these networks.  4,566 "border violators" have been arrested in Tete this year.

They also urged authorities to ensure that separated family members are traced and reunited as soon as possible. UNCHR's statement follows reports of IDPs were being forcibly returned to Negomano in Mueda after crossing into Tanzania.

On 18 April UNCHR appealed to Mozambican and Tanzanian governments to allow free movement of people fleeing violence and conflict in Cabo Delgado, in search of international protection, safety, and assistance, as well as the right to cross international borders to seek asylum. They also urged authorities to ensure that separated family members are traced and reunited as soon as possible. UNCHR's statement follows reports of IDPs were being forcibly returned to Negomano in Mueda after crossing into Tanzania.
The Ministry of Education and Human Development (MINEDH) on 17 May announced a deficit of 25,800 additional classrooms to accommodate 4,800 classes that are forced to study outside.

Sources stated that SADC leader disagree in regards to the the scale and scope of an intervention in Mozambique. Zimbabwe President Mnangagwa favored a more aggressive approach with a larger force deployed to Cabo Delgado; South Africa and Bostwana prefer a more conservative intervention and were against the idea of ZImbabwe leading such a force.  President Nyusi meanwhile has allegedly remained reluctant to support an intervention.

Local sources stated that several French companies expressed confidence in resuming investments in Mozambique. This comes after President Nyusi attended a 3-day talks in Paris. Technip, a main contractor for offshore operations in Rovuma Basin, stated that the Mozambique government has guaranteed that security is being restored which would enable projects to be developed more quickly. Executive Chairman of the African Energy Chamber Ayuk stated that during a meeting between President Nyusi and Total Chairman Patrick Pouyanne, Total had assured Nyusi that it would not abandon its Mozambique projects.

The FRELIMO central committee announced that it will meet during 22-23 May in Matola to evaluate the work of their party’s Political Commission, Verification Committee and the Central Office. The evaluation was in preparation for the political party’s elections.

The Ministry of Health announced 21 new COVID cases and 2 related deaths in Mozambique on 18 May. The new cases were recorded as follows: 12 in Zambezia, 4 in Maputo City, 2 in Maputo province, 1 in Inhambane, 1 in Tete, and 1 in Nampula.
The Denis Hurley Peace Institute released images showing 100 militants allegedly crossing from the Namoto area into Tanzania in early May.
A Catholic charity says there is “mounting speculation” that Tanzania is failing to respond against the insurgents or that the Tanzanian authorities are supporting the insurgency in Mozambique.

Bazaruto Archipelago National Park officials stated that revenue has dropped in revenue by more than 50% in Bazaruto Archipelago due to COVID. The Island previously received 26,000 tourists on 2019 and 10,000 during 2020. 31 million meticais were collected during 2019, which fell to 12 million meticais on 2020.

The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) announced that 100 commercial establishments were recently suspended, and 19 establishments were closed for selling alcohol in violation of COVID-19 measures. This comes as INAE inspected 146 stalls and 116 restaurants on 16 May.

UN stated that over 1,500 displaced people have been deported by Tanzania back to Mozambique in the aftermath of Palma attack. The IDPs were mostly children and women who had walked from Palma to Mozambique-Tanzania border.

An EU technical team that will provide training Mozambican security forces was set to arrive this week in Mozambique. The training was to enable Mozambican security forces to better conduct operations against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Costa stated that the European Union is also able to provide other forces and other support necessary.

The World Bank stated that on18 May that “we will not abandon” Mozambique by providing complementary support.  World Bank Director of Operations Axel van Trotsenburg stated that they would accompany Mozambique even if the challenge is difficult.

Rwanda President Kagame attended talks with Nyusi in Paris. Reports stated that Rwanda could potentially provide troops to Mozambique to fight against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado with French backing.

The US's Permanent Representative to the United Nations stated that the US government hopes for “swift and satisfactory conclusion” to conflict and insecurity in Mozambique. The US government is currently working with the Mozambican government to assist in protecting civilians, prevent possible attacks, and provide humanitarian relief.

The Ministry of Health announced 22 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 19 May. The cases were recorded as follows: 7 in Maputo city, 5 in Maputo, 4 in Tete, 4 in Nampula, 1 in Cabo Delgado, and 1 in Inhambane.

Insurgents attacked and killed a fisherman in Ilha Quifula, south of Pangane, on 15 May. Locals stated that the victim arrived in the island with his colleague and was fishing in the area when insurgents attacked and killed the man; his colleague escaped the attack.

An NGO issued a report stating concerns for around 350,000 displaced children who were affected by the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado. Most of the displaced children lacked identification documents, missing parents, and schooling. Many of the displaced children stated that they could not access public services.

Rickshaw taxi drivers assaulted policemen who attempted to seize their vehicles during an operation in Zimpinga on 10 May. The operation was to prevent rickshaws from operating in the area. A civilian was killed and 3 were injured in the incident.
Rickshaw taxi drivers assaulted policemen who attempted to seize their vehicles during an operation in Pemba 19 May.
Rickshaw taxi drivers assaulted policemen who attempted to seize their vehicles during an operation in Pemba 19 May.
Local sources stated that security forces have recently set security roadblocks to demand payments from passing vehicles in Pemba.

Saudi Arabia on 19 May announced it would provide support for the training of the Mozambican military. The Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia announced that the SADC is working with Saudi Arabia to assist security forces in Mozambique. This comes as the Crown Prince stated that 100 million EUR would be used to finance investments in the African countries.

A civil society organization launched a program to prevent conflict and exploitation in the mining and natural resources sectors on 19 May. The "For an Inclusive and Peaceful Society in Mozambique" is to last to for three years that allow civil societies to prevent and respond to crises or emergence of disputes between communities, institutions and the private sector.

Total on 19 May that it would continue the payment of "outstanding amounts" to small and medium-sized companies connected to the Golfinho/Atum project.  The company also said it remained committed to natural gas projects in Cabo Delgado, despite recent insurgent attacks.

The Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction announced on 19 May that Inhambane province requires 300 million meticais to recover from Cyclone damage suffered by the province in recent years. The funds were also to help rehabilitate the agriculture, health, education, and transportation sectors.

Ncondezi Energy stated that they are still waiting for the response of Electricidade de Mozambique regarding their studies based on the 300Mw coal powered electricity and coal mine in Tete on 19 May.  The studies were previously submitted to the government this past December.

The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) suspended Juga's Water branch in Avenida das Industrias, Machava, on 10 May. The branch was suspended due to poor work hygienic conditions of their collection, treatment , and sale of "purified" water. Other branches in Maputo were open.
Locals recovered the body of a civilian found on a truck bed in Maputo on the morning of 19 May. No details were available as to the cause of death.

The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Mozambique announced that interest rates would remain the same after a meeting in Xai-xai on 19 May. The committee stated that the Interbank Money Market Rate, which is used by the central bank for monetary interventions was at 13.25%. The interest rate paid by commercial banks to the central bank for money borrowed is at 16.25%. While the central bank deposit rate to commercial banks is at 10.25%.

The National Institute of the Sea conducts an investigation regarding the collision between two ships at Beira Port on 19 May. Two ships reportedly collided with each other during heavy fog at the port earlier in the day.

Two ships collided with each other at Beira Port due to the lack of visibility caused by a heavy fog early morning of 19 May. Both ships were docked after the incident. Port officials stated that an investigation to provide more details regarding the collision.

Frelimo Secretary-General Roque Silva called on the party's youth not to join any criminal group or the Cabo Delgado insurgency. Silva stated the insurgents were only recruiting youths with "empty promises".

A fire broke out burning down 200 stalls at the Chuaula Market, south Lichinga, at around 04:30 on 19 May. The fire was reportedly caused by a short circuit at one of the stalls. Firefighters responded and doused the flames four hours after responding.

Police Commander-in-Chief Rafael stated that additional resources would be provided to provincial police stations with resources to tackle organized crime in their respective provinces. The police were gradually deploying assets to district command for control and force missions.

Engineering students gathered and protested at the Faculty of Engineering in Eduardo Mondlane University, south Maputo City, early evening of 19 May. The protesters demanded a reduction of their 25,000 meticais tuition fees to 5,000 meticais for the second semester. The protesters claimed that they studied for only four weeks and have previously attempted to discuss the issue with the university board.

column4: South African jurist Andre Thomashausen stated that the prolonged detention of Manuel Chang was due to the inability of South Africa and Mozambique to decide on the extradition process. Manuel Chang was detained in South Africa on 2018 for diverting load funds and was involved with the "Hidden Debts" case in Mozambique. Thomashausen stated that South Africa is not responsible for resolving competing extradition requests from Mozambique and the US. This comes after the Mozambican government on 14 May again requested the extradition of Chang.

Local residents of Inhassoro marched in protest on 20 May, protesting against an oil company operating in the area, calling for the company to provide more jobs to locals in the area.  Protesters said the oil company was only providing jobs to people from Maputo, and said they would continue demonstrations until the company "comply with everything".  Other local residents said they had been charged up to 5000 metical to secure a job with the company, while others said the company had neglected the local community.

A truck smuggling cooking oil coming from Mozambique was involved in a vehicle accident near Milange on 14 May. The truck was transporting several 20L containers filled with cooking oil. Malawi security forces responded and began an investigation.

A truck smuggling cooking oil coming from Mozambique was involved in a vehicle accident near Milange on 14 May. The truck was transporting several 20L containers filled with cooking oil. Malawi security forces responded and began an investigation.

Locals recovered the body of a mother and three children of the same family inside their residence in Nhamaonha, east Chimoio, on the night of 20 May. The victims were suspected to be murdered by mother of the boyfriend of the deceased mother.

South African officials recently stated that they are still waiting for the Mozambican government to issue an “invitation” for them to intervene against the insurgency in Mozambique. The Mozambican government has previously stated that they are willing to request assistance.

Security forces detained two men suspected to be insurgents in Metangula, Lago District of Niassa province on 20 May.  The two reportedly spoke Kiswahili; it was unclear how they were identified as terrror suspects. The suspects were transported to Lichinga for interrogation. The two men allegedly were recruiting in different parts of the province.

An NGO stated that IDPs in some areas in Cabo Delgado are allegedly registering more than once as IDPs in different locations to receive additional relief goods. This is reportedly part of a wider corruption scheme in which the additional aid is reportedly sold on black market.

President Nyusi stated that talks in France with President Macron, Total, and others was a success, and assured that peace and security will be restored in areas impacted by terrorists. Nyusi assured Total security forces would create a secure environment for oil and gas companies to resume operations in Cabo Delgado. France also stated that they will support Mozambique against terrorism, though not specific form was stated.

An association for sexual minority rights stated that a study indicates that two out of three gay people are being discriminated in Mozambique. The study stated that most incidents occur in school where bullying is one of the common forms of discrimination; teachers often also initiate discrimination incidents.

The UK donated funds of 200,000 GBP for “safe trade” at the Mozambique-Malawi/Mozambique-South Africa border. The funding was used to purchase Covid Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for customs and border officials in maintaining a safe working environment at the border crossings. The fund is part of the Safe Trade Programme, which was implemented to enhance trade and business in East Africa.

The Mozambican government announced that it would build 250 houses for veterans of war of independence and civil war by 2023. President Nyusi also stated that the houses would be built in all provinces by the end of a five-year period.

The National Institute of Communications of Mozambique (INCM) stated that 3 million mobile phone SIM cards have been deactivated due to improper registrations since 2020. INCM stated that there are currently 16 million mobile phone SIM card subscribers in Mozambique. A majority of the improper registrations have included forged identification documents. Another irregularity was due to the sale of pre-registered SIM cards.

Dozens of semi-collective public transport employees went on strike at the intersection of Avenidas Eduardo Mondlane and Av. Karl Marx, Maputo City on Thursday, 20 May. The protesting drivers stated that police were limiting passenger capacities and said police demand excessive bribes and fees.  The protesters also accused police of unfair treatment compared to larger buses.

column4: Civilians who recently escaped from the custody of insurgents stated that the insurgents were selecting abducted individuals by profession. One of the selected individuals was a medical staff for the Hospital of Palma who was forced to give medical assistance to the insurgents. The insurgents also sought mechanics and drivers as militants lacked the ability to drive and maintain some vehicles they had captured.  Cellular phone technicians and fishermen were also sought by the group.
The Ministry of Health announced 18 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 20 May. Maputo City recorded 7 cases and Nampula province with four cases. 68 daily recoveries were recorded.

A boat transporting civilians capsized after entering rough waters between Pemba and of Ibo Island on the morning of 20 May. The boat was travelling from Pemba towards Ibo.  Security forces and other boats reportedly responded and rescued the civilians, though other civilians were reported to be missing during the rescue. Officials have responded and investigating the incident.

Security forces and other boats reportedly responded and rescued the civilians, though other civilians were reported to be missing during the rescue. Officials have responded and investigating the incident.

The Extended Vaccination Program officials stated that 240,000 people across Mozambique have received two COVID shots of 20 May.  The Extended Vaccination Program head stated that the number of vaccinated will increased further as the next phase would cover larger groups and reinforce the vaccination through education and communication campaigns.

Three RENAMO dissident members were reported on 21 May to have defected from the group in Pinanganganga in Gondola District of Manica.  The three included Bento Bonifacio Raice, who had reportedly been in regular contact with dissident leader Mariano Nhongo.  The three claimed that there have been "mass defections" from the group, and that only seven dissidents remained in bush areas of the Gorongosa area in Sofala.
Rumors spread that wives of insurgents living in Pemba were advised to move from the city to Nampula due to a possible insurgent attack which could occur between 20-25 May.

Sources stated that police in Pemba were conducting a campaign among motor taxi drivers and other public transportation employees in Wimbe, east Pemba, on 21 May to assure drivers are not susceptible to recruiting efforts by insurgents.
A source reported that security force checkpoints between Montepuez and Mueda often demand bribes and that "anyone" could likely successfully bribe their way through these checkpoints.

A Portuguese NGO has provided 2.6 tons of food aid to be given to IDPs in Cabo Delgado on 21 May. The NGO would also provide 560 school items and basic necessities such as hygiene, shelter and protection. The NGO stated that around 950,000 are affected by severe hunger.

The Ministry of Health announced that 323,349 Mozambique citizens have received the first dose of the COVID vaccine. This comes as the first phase inoculated 82,384 while the second phase vaccinated 240,965.

South Africa President Ramaphosa and President Nyusi will conduct a meeting before end of May to discuss a potential SADC military intervention in Mozambique.   President Nyusi is believed by many to only want military aid, rather than a military intervention, in Cabo Delgado.

South Africa Minister for International Relations and Cooperation stated that South Africa will push for “urgent military action” through the SADC to fight against insurgents in Cabo Delgado. Pandor said the SADC has never utilized its defense pact to intervene in an SADC country, but that the situation in Mozambique represented a threat to the region that must be dealt with.

A London court ruling will allow a shipbuilding company to “try to hold” President Nyusi responsible for damages in Hidden Debts case if Nyusi is found to have accepted bribes. This comes as Privinvest stated previously that they made campaign donations to Nyusi and other senior officials on 2014 after negotiating contracts for government maritime projects. The company denied the remittances were bribes.

The WHO warned that more than 1.2 million people were in need of medical aid in Cabo Delgado. WHO Regional Director for Africa Moeti stated that thousands of families were affected by the insurgency and had been deprive them of health services. Moeti said that the families should be ensured full access to mental health and social services. A plan was being reviewed by the WHO to provide additional human resources to establish the required mechanisms in improving essential health access.

The Ministry of Health announced 24 new COVID cases and 3 related deaths in Mozambique on 21 May. This comes as no deaths have been recorded in the past several days. This brings the total cases to 70,551 and 831 total deaths.

The Nampula Assembly called for vigilance among local communities to prevent terrorism from Cabo Delgado from spreading into the province. Assembly member Mahando stated that Nampula is currently sheltering around 70,000 IDPs and the communities should be attentive for possible insurgent infiltration among these population.

Mozambique is the 24th ranked in world for risk of mass killings in 2020-2021. The risk factors in Mozambique include the ongoing conflict between insurgents and security forces. The report stated that the governments intending to assist Mozambique should conduct a risk assessment on the killings and immediately create a resolution on how to assist the Mozambican government through the military and private sector investments.

Police detained a total of 30 suspects linked with in relation to Nacala lodge attack on 21 May. This comes as the first three detained suspects confessed and gave out information regarding the attack which occurred in early May.

Sources stated that tour operators and local population complained about destruction of marine ecosystem by an oil company in northern Inhambane. The tourism operators stated that dolphins have died and called on authorities to disprove the projects of the company.

Semi-collective drivers ended strike over limited passenger capacities on Friday, though tensions with security forces remain high. Police also denied reports of extorting the drivers due to the COVID precaution violations.

FRELIMO's Central Committee 2-day meeting will include discussion of national security, Cabo Delgado insurgency, and RENAMO dissident attacks, the 2021 political party program, and political party’s elections. The succession plan for the party after President Nyusi however will reportedly not be discussed.

The International Energy Agency (IEA) stated that the Mozambique gas fields cannot be developed if global warming was to be kept to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. IEA stated that carbon dioxide emissions should be reduced to zero by 2050.

The Muidumbe District Administrator stated on 14 May that civil workers should return to the district, despite sporadic fighting in the area and the presence of insurgents in the district. Health workers for the district have been told they should travel to Mueda, closer to Muidumbe.  Civil servants fear insurgent attacks in the district and are reluctant to return.

The IOM on 19 May said that there are currently over 54,000 people displaced after the Palma attack.  This includes 15,651 people in Mueda, 14,067 in Nangade, 11,741 in Pemba, 6,448 in Montepuez, 1,687 in Ibo, and 23,000 people at Quitunda, just outside of Palma.

President Nyusi on 22 May said that security forces repelled insurgents on 21 May who attempted to attack Olumbe village in Palma District.  5 insurgents were killed during while attempting to withdraw from the area.

President Nyusi announced on the morning of 22 May that he called an extraordinary summit of the “Double Troika” of SADC for the coming week. The summit aims to discuss insurgency in the province of Cabo Delgado. The summit scheduled last April was postponed due to  lack of quorum.

The Ministry of Health announced 17 new COVID cases on 22 May. No deaths have been recorded in the past 24 hours. This brings the total cases to 70,568 and 831 total deaths. The breakdown for the new cases were as follows- 11 cases in Maputo City, three in Maputo province, one case each for Gaza and Inhambane.

On 22 May, President Nyusi announced his rejection of "preconditions" set by the Renamo Military Junta to adhere with the Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration (DDR) process, saying the Military Junta must join the DDR process without preconditions.

Fighting between security forces and insurgents in the Diaca area of Cabo Delgado, approximately 45 km east of Mueda, was reported on 22 May. Further information regarding the clash is not available at this time.  Other sources later reported security forces had first engaged insurgents in the area on 21 May.

Minister of Public works, Joao Machatine, stated on 20 May that the country needs 800 million US dollars per year for the maintenance and paving of the national road network. He added that through the construction of toll gates, the government will avoid to resort to seeking international support or to the state funds.

About 1,375 IDPs were registered to have arrived by foot in Nangade and by bus from Nangade to Mueda, Montepuez, and Pemba on 19 May. These people were displaced from Palma following insurgent attacks last March.

Frelimo Central Committee announced on 23 May that 12th Congress will take place on 23-28 September 2022 at Escola Da Frelimo in Matola.

Sources on 23 May disclosed that people displaced from Cabo Delgado were allegedly forced to purchase land in the open displacement resettlement centers in the Montepuez district, to avoid conflicts with the locals. Locals of the district demanded 500 meticais payment for the land and another 200 meticais from the IDPs in exchange for a pass to receive humanitarian aid. Montepuez is one of the districts with the most displaced people following the 24 March Palma attack.

On 22 May, Mozambican State Councilor Raul Domingos warned that foreign military intervention in Cabo Delgado may potentially intensify the conflict. He pointed out the several failure of the foreign military aid during the course of the 16-year civil war. He added that creating better job opportunities could yield better results for young people who were enticed to join the insurgent group.

The Ministry of Health announced 22 new COVID cases on 23 May. No deaths have been recorded in the past 24 hours. This brings the total cases to 70,590 and 831 total deaths. The breakdown for the new cases were as follows- seven cases in Maputo City, six in Tete, four cases each for Niassa, and Maputo province, one case for Nampula. Six more people were reported to have recovered today.

A canoe carrying six people capsized in Ruvuma River around 0600hrs on 23 May while attempting to cross the river to their farms. The victims have yet been found. Ruvuma region’s head of the Tanzania Fire and Rescue Force, Chesco Mbata confirmed the incident and stated that the canoe was hit by strong waves that caused it to lose direction and subsequently capsized. A rescue operation has been launched.

On 21 May, the National Government announced the launch of international tenders next month for entities who will conduct a environmental, market, hydrological, geotechnical and financial impact studies for the construction of the Mpanda Nkuwa hydroelectric dam. The dam, budgeted at USD 4.5 to 5 billion, will be the second-largest hydroelectric dam in the country.

Analysts predicted that the Mozambican economy will only grow 1.2% in 2021. The prediction is taken into account the indefinite suspension of construction of LNG project in Cabo Delgado, new COVID-19 variants, and slow distribution of the COVID-19 vaccines.

The Ministry of Gender, Child and Social Action (MGCAS) stated on 23 May that the re-opening of schools are still delayed due to the creation of compliance checklist for institutions to ensure safe resumption of classes. More than 695 schools have been closed since 2020 to curb the spread of the COVID-19. Institution with international curriculum are allowed to re-open as long as they have sanitary conditions created.

A large group of people gathered for the 'walk for humanity' demonstration at a hotel on Av. Marginal in Maputo City around 0930hrs on 23 May, to renounce the insurgency in Cabo Delgado and call for support and solidarity with Palestinian people. The walk was organized by the Association of Friendship and Solidarity with Palestine. Mozambican police attempted to stop the protest by blocking the door at the hotel and stated that the walk was not authorized. After an hour, the police allowed the protest to take place as long as the group maintained social distance and did not raise flags or placards.

Center for Democracy and Development (CDD) on 24 May reported that Mozambican Police allegedly tortured a detainee to get a confession for a crime in Manica. The incident took place two weeks ago.

On 20 May, Faculty of Engineering of the Eduardo Mondlane University (UEM) stated that their students had had four weeks of classes face-to-face, and the rest of their classes online. The statement came after the students staged a protest against the full charge of 25,000 meticais fees for the five months of the last semester and claimed that they only had lectures for four weeks, and should pay no more than 5,000 meticais. The faculty added that in order to enroll for the following semester, the students must settle their remaining balance.

A study conducted by International Monetary Fund (IMF) revealed that Mozambique is the most indebted country in the Southern African Development Community (SADC) with a debt corresponds to 125.3% of the country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

National Migration Service (SENAMI) released a report on 24 May indicating that a total of 1,988 Mozambican nationals were repatriated back to the country from 08 and 23 May 2021. 1,980 out of 1,988 were illegal immigrants while eight committed various crimes. The breakdown of the deported citizens are as follows.-1,620  were deported from Tanzania, 242 from South Africa, 109 from Malawi, 11 from the Kingdom of eSwatini and six from Zimbabwe.

62 RENAMO dissidents have joined the demilitarization, disarmament and reintegration (DDR) process in the country, President Nyusi announced on 22 May during the opening of the IV Ordinary Session of the Frelimo Central Committee.  Nyusi called for the other dissident fighters to also join the DDR process.  Meanwhile 2,307 former armed RENAMO members have joined the DDR process, while 10 RENAMO bases have been dismantled.

As of 22 May, a total of 57,089 people were displaced from Palma since the insurgent attack on 24 March. 1,850 of which were elder people and 716 were children who were unaccompanied or separated from other family members.  Pemba, Nangade, and Mueda each are hosting more than 12,000 of these IDPs a piece.

President Nyusi reiterated on 23 May the Frelimo's commitment in the fight against corruption in Mozambique. He also expressed his dedication to restore peace in the northern and central part of the country amid armed attacks.

Mozambican security forces on Sunday reportedly retook Namacande, the capital of Muidumbe District after brief clashes between security forces and insurgents, according to several sources.  Gazelle and Mi-8 helicopters supported ground troop movements into the town.  Other reports indicated security forces had successfully also recaptured Diaca on the road to Mocimboa da Praia on 21 May, backed by Gazelle assault helicopters.  Clashes had been reported in this area over the weekend.

Security forces backed by Gazzelle Helicopters and pro-government militia clashes breifly with insurgents at Namacande before insurgents retreated.   Government troops reclaimed the district captial for the first time since December 2020.
Local sources stated that many civilians displaced from Palma continue to high in areas along the Palma-Nangade border area; many are still fleeing towards Nangade.
Dozens of fish and poultry vendors protested condemning the delay in building a market for them at Costa de Sol, west Maputo City on 24 May.
Hundreds of residents reportedly continue to flee each day from Palma. Sources stated that the fleeing of the residents was due to insecurity in the area.

The Ministry of Health announced that the Expanded Vaccination Program in its second phase will target 251,905 individuals. The first vaccination dose has reached 240,965 which corresponds to 96% of the intended coverage.

FRELIMO spokesman Caifadine Massane emphasized “sovereignty” during talks on combating terrorism at FRELIMO Central committee Meeting on 23 May. Massane stated that training of the Mozambican army should be at the forefront of any counter-insurgency effort.  President Nyusi stated that national sovereignty is threatened by the continued insurgency. Nyusi also stated that no country has been considered immune to the insurgency and has combatted it alone.  Nyusi also said Mozambique wants support against the insurgency but that "we do not want to depart from the situation".

IDPs complain of poor conditions at the 25 Junho Resettlement Camp in Metuge. The camp is home to 30,000 IDPs, who state that food supplies provided are not enough for the IDPs, while residences were dangerous due to the lack of construction supplies. IDPs stated that several residences were made from reed, straw, and canvas.

The Ministry of Health announced that no new COVID deaths were reported as of 23 and 24 May. This comes as authorities announced 17 total deaths since the beginning of May. A 47% percent  decrease in deaths has been 32 total deaths were recorded during the past month. A similar decline was also noted in COVID cases as 689 new cases were noted for the month of May while 2,070 were recorded for April. Hospitalizations were recorded at 84 patients as of May, while 159 during past April.

Local sources stated that 950 bodies have not been claimed by relatives from hospitals in Maputo. Hospital officials stated that unclaimed bodies were to be buried collectively. Many of these deaths were reportedly due to COVID, and have been left at the morgue due to a "lack of conditions to carry out funeral ceremonies".
RENAMO President Momade will address the Senior Staff Party Meeting in Maputo City on 25 May.

President Nyusi according to local media favors the deployment of an intervention force from Rwanda, rather than from the SADC.  This report comes after Nyusi recently was in Kigali for talks with Rwandan President Paul Kagame, and in Paris for talks with French President Emmanuel Macron.

The African Commission on Human Rights has requested neighboring countries of Mozambique to allow asylum seekers to flee from Cabo Delgado. This comes as reports of Tanzania denying entry and deporting displaced Mozambicans back to Cabo Delgado.

The Foreign Minister Macamo stated that the country is still going to determine what external support it will accept to help combat the Cabo Delgado insurgency. Macamo stated that in "due course" the government would specify what type of support is needed from the international community.

Public Health Laboratories National Director Sofia Viegas stated that 400 "suspicious" samples have been sent to South Africa to confirm if the Indian variant of COVID was present in Mozambique. Viegas also stated that Mozambique was in the process of creating a laboratory that would be able to test for the Indian COVID variant.

Criminal activity has increased in Mulauzi district near Khongolote, Matola. Locals stated that crimes were notable as the criminals would use the sewage channels and entrances as means to conduct their targeted thefts and attacks and escape using these canals as well.

The SADC's new Extraordinary Troika Summit will be held on 27 May in Maputo City.  The summit is expected to focus on combating the insurgency in Cabo Delgado, and different interventions the SADC can offer the Mozambican government.
The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) seized and destroyed gambling machines during a raid at several tents and residences used as gambling dens.
Minister of Agriculture Celso Correia blamed the existence of “wings” of FRELIMO on foreign influences, also saying the party would be able to "renew itself" in time for the next elections.
Armed locals reportedly stopped IDPs from claiming lands reportedly allocated by the government for their relocation in Malica, north of Lichinga, on 17 May.
Locals recently refused to hand over lands being allocated to IDPs and were preventing them from building their residences in Montepuez on 23 May.
Local sources reported that the closure of the Olam cashew processing pant in Nampula has left thousands unemployed, including many who have received no compensation for their work.
270 IDPs have reportedly built their homes in Mecufi, south of Pemba. The residences were constructed on 13 hectares of land to create the 3 de Fevereiro locality.

The Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM) announced that they would hold their National Council meeting in Maputo between 29 to 30 May. The meeting was to determine the dates for the congress that will elect the new MDM president after the recent death of Daviz Simango.
Several open box vehicles “my loves” continue to transport people around Maputo despite a ban on them operating.  Tensions between My Love operators and tensions remain high.
RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade stated that RENAMO expects the government to approve an SADC intervention against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado in the near future.
Police have continued to inspect arriving IDPs and their belongings in Pemba to ensure no insurgents are infiltrating the provincial capital.
Police arrested three wanted murderers in Chimoio on 21 May. The suspects are believed to have killed a woman and three of her children in Nhamaonha, Chimoio.

The Ministry of Health announced 2 new COVID deaths and 30 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 25 May. Maputo City was recorded with 17 cases, Tete with 8 cases, 1 in Inhambane, 1 in Sofala, 1 in Manica, 1 in Niassa, and 1 in Nampula.

Park officials stated that no cases of commercial poaching were reported at Limpopo National Park of Gaza Province over the past year. Park Administrator Pariela stated that only six poaching incidents for subsistence were recorded during this time.

Pro-government militiamen reportedly detained several security force members for setting homes on fire in Palma on 26 April. A militiaman stated that the soldiers were referred to their superiors and the incident was investigated.

Unconfirmed report stated that the Mozambique government is willing to accept an intervention force in Cabo Delgado, but only wants this force to be deployed around the Afungi Peninsula to protect the Afungi LNG Camp, while Mozambican forces carry out all other counter-insurgency operations.

President Nyusi intends to conduct a state of the nation address regarding COVID in Mozambique scheduled at 19:00 on 26 May. This comes as COVID deaths and cases have seen a decline during the month of May. Total deaths have reached 19 for the month while recoveries have increased to 97% of 70,636 COVID cases.

Hydroelectric de Cahora Bassa (HCB) have seen an increase in its dividends by 73.6% from 0.064 Meticais to 0.111 Meticais per share paid in 2020. HCB is expected to pay around 150 million meticais to their series B shareholders in response to their public sale during 2019.

Responding policemen shot dead a 19-year old who was the victim of a mugging in Changara of Tete province on 17 May. The victim was killed while the police opened fire at the thieves who were later detained.

Responding policemen shot dead a 19-year old who was the victim of a mugging in Changara of Tete province on 17 May. The victim was killed while the police opened fire at the thieves who were later detained.

Businessmen donated and handed over 1 million meticais worth of goods to the Maputo governor in Maputo Province on 26 May. The relief goods were to assist individuals affected by the insurgent attacks in Cabo Delgado.

The Rapid Intervention Units of the police still operating in Cabo Delgado reportedly continue to have close links with DAG, and receive training, supplies and equipment from the company, according to recent reports.

The National Institute of Health (INS) announced that a third wave of COVID is "unavoidable" in Mozambique. INS Deputy Director Gudo stated that the third wave will likely be triggered by possibly more transmissible strains and precaution measures can only delay the next outbreak.

Police assaulted and injured a vendor while being detaining on a street in Aeroporto B, Maputo City at around 11:00 of 28 May. The police were ordered to clear the streets of illegal vendors. A video showed that the police kept assaulting the vendor while being placed in a police vehicle.
Police assaulted and injured a civilian while detaining him on a street in Maputo City on 28 May.

The Botswana President Makgwetsi Masisi expressed support for collective intervention of the SADC against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado on 27 May. President Masisi stated that now is the time to act collectively against the insurgents in the region during the SADC Troika Summit.

Cabo Delgado Governor Tauabo said on 27 May that unemployment is the main cause for youths to join the insurgency.  Tauabo stated that that the insurgents were destroying the government's economic and social projects that create jobs.

The Ministry of Health announced 22 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 27 May. Majority of the cases were in Maputo City as 10 cases were recorded while Niassa is the second highest with 6 cases. This comes as 34 daily recoveries were reported.

Tanzanian Minister for Foreign Affairs Liberata Mulamula on 27 May was reported to have said Tanzania would not deploy troops into Mozambique to combat the ongoing Cabo Delgado insurgency, saying instead there should be talks to promote "peace and tranquility in Mozambique".  Other officials said that they "don't know whom to fight with" in Mozambique.  Other sources however reported that Tanzania would participate in the "formation of joint special forces".

The Maputo Municipal Council announced that they would license drivers of human-powered vehicles/carts  also known as "Txova". The licensing will allow the drivers of the Txova to follow the highway code and limit travel between 04:00 to 18:00.

The Electricidade de Mozambique (EDM) stated that two power distribution conductors ruptured caused an electrical transmission line interruption in Chinde in Zambezia province on 27 May. EDM stated that technical teams were already conducting repairs and may take a few days due to the damage.

The National Statistics Institute (INE) stated that Mozambique per capita 2020 GDP decreased compared to the previous year 2019. The per capita GPD on 2020 was at 467 USD, a decline of 55 USD compared to the per capita GDP of 522 USD in 2019.

Officials announced the presence of unidentified particles inside collected air samples to assess air toxicity in Tchumene, north Matola, on the 23 May. The particles reportedly caused panic among local residents, though no spike in illnesses was reported.

The National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD) announced a response plan to the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado. INGD General Director Meque stated that their focus would be creating shelter, sanitation, food and health care for the IDPs. Meque stated that 21 out of 28 resettlement centers which the institute have constructed are in Cabo Delgado.

Canadian Minister for International Cooperation Karina Gould announced that 186 million CAD would be provided to the Mozambique government to assist new and ongoing projects. The funding was to support the government's response to the pandemic and health system.

European Defense Ministers met discuss the ongoing insurgency in Mozambique on 27 May. Portuguese Defense Minister Cravinho stated that the EU technical team in Cabo Delgado was gaining momentum and has produced "results". This technical team has been on the ground since 19 May. This comes as Portugal is expecting that the EU training mission to be approved by June. Portugal was to provide 50% of troops for the mission.

Maputo Police Commander Zualo condemned the actions of the four policemen who attacked a vendor after detaining him on a street in Aeroporto B, Maputo City, on the morning of 28 May. Zualo stated that involved policemen were suspended and are awaiting disciplinary action.
The Muslim Movement of Mozambique (MMM) delivered 450 relief kits to IDPs in Cabo Delgado on 27 May.

Sources report poor conditions in Maganja in recent days after the arrival of large numbers of IDPs from Olumbe, who fled a recent insurgent attack.  Locals in the area report food shortages and no security presence, making the area vulnerable to insurgent attacks.
Insurgents on or around 21 May threatened locals in the Olumbe area, telling them that militants intended to occupy the town.  Locals fled the area in response towards Maganja.

Locals and IDPs were reported to have Olumbe AP in response to the 21 May attack.  Over 1,000 people fled the area due to this attack; insurgents reportedly threatened locals, saying militants meant to occupy the area and local residents should leave town.  Locals are reported to have fled to Maganja.

Former employees of a construction company accused their employer of “mistreatment”, saying they were dismissed without explanation. The company is currently involved in the construction of National Road 280 between Tica and Buzi of Sofala province.

column4: The Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM) will hold its Ordinary Session of the party's National Council in Beira during the 29-30 May. The meeting was initially set on 10 May but was suspended due to the pandemic restrictions and precautions.

China, Japan, and South Korea granted Mozambique suspension of its foreign debt as part of the initiative to mitigate the impact of COVID on developing countries. This postpones the payment 22 million USD. This comes as Portugal intends to conduct the similar suspension of debts for Mozambique.

French President Emmanuel Macron on 28 May announced that France is ready to provide assistance to Mozambique in fighting against insurgency. President Macron stated that it would only aid the Mozambican government upon their request, and it should be part of the SADC intervention.  He said if called upon, France has naval assets based at Mayotte and Reunion that could participate "immediately" in any intervention.

Kidnappers released an abducted Portuguese national who is the spouse of the businessman in Nampula on Friday, 28 May. The victim was previously abducted outside the General Consulate of Portugal, Avenida Mao Tse Tung, Maputo City on 13 April. No details were released regarding the release of the victim.

The Southern African Development Community (SADC) Troika summit was concluded without a formal position regarding the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. Analyst stated that the lack of a position was due to the Mozambican government's indecisiveness regarding the support it requires.

The SADC announced during the Double Troika Summit that another meeting would be conducted on 20 June in Maputo. This comes as no formal position was stated regarding a potential SADC intervention in Cabo Delgado.
The Ministry of Health announced 24 new COVID cases and one related death in Mozambique on 28 May. Majority of the cases were in Niassa with 8 cases while Maputo city was recorded with 6.

The reconstruction of the 44.6KM railway linking Tete province to Malawi was launched on 29 May. The construction was interrupted in 1986 by the civil war. The opening of the railway to Malawi will help boost the economy of the central region especially in trade.

The Ministry of Health announced 27 new COVID cases and one related death in Mozambique on 29 May. 14 of the new cases are from Maputo city and province, six are from Manica, four from Inhambane, and one each from Cabo Delgado, Nampula and Gaza provinces.  Over the last 24 hours, 267 has recovered and one was hospitalized due to the COVID-19 infection.

37-yr-old Rwandan journalist, Ntamuhanga Cassien, went missing after alleged officers of Mozambican police arrested him on 23 May in Inhaca, Maputo. One source reported 8 individuals who identified themselves as police officers detained Cassien; this included one Rwandan citizen.  However, a SERNIC spokesman said no arrest of a Rwandan citizen had been carried out by security forces.  Cassien was living in exile on the island after he escaped from Rwandan prison in 2017. He was imprisoned on terrorism and murder charges which were contested by human rights organizations.

MDM announced on 29 May that their extraordinary congress will be held on 03, 04, 05 December in Beira City under the supervision of the Secretary-General and interim head, Jose Domingos Manuel. The main agenda of the congress will be the election of the party's new president, following the death of Daviz Simango.

The European Defense Ministers on 29 May expressed their interest on the possible deployment of a Common Security and Defense Policy (CSDP) military training mission in Mozambique. The EU training mission is set to commence in three months time. Portugal will provide 50% of troops for the mission. Portuguese Defense Minister Cravinho earlier stated that the EU technical team in Cabo Delgado was gaining momentum and has produced "results".

The Ministry of Health announced 56 new COVID cases and no death recorded in Mozambique on 30 May. Over the last 24 hours, five people were hospitalized due to the COVID-19 infection while no hospital discharges were reported.
Sources on 25 May stated that up to 40 families arrive each day on foot in Mueda and Nangade from Palma following insurgent attacks in March.
Sources on 25 May stated that up to 40 families arrive each day on foot in Mueda and Nangade from Palma following insurgent attacks targeting Palma in March.

Sisters of various religious orders in Nampula called on the Mozambican authorities to take note of sexual harassment in schools in the town. They urged the government to enforce the existing laws to punish the perpetrators. Several students especially female students from low-income families were most vulnerable to such assaults.

Officials of National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) seized 10,000 liters of illegally sold contraband fuel in Garagua, Mossurize on 24 May following a tip-off. The suspects managed to escape as the security operatives arrived. An operation has been launched to capture the fleeing suspects.

Regional Intelligence officials were reported on 27 May to be increasingly concerned about the possibility of the insurgency in Cabo Delgado spreading north into Tanzania and south towards Malawi if the Mozambican Government failed to act on it soon. South Africa is also concerned about a potential expansion of attacks within its borders1.

The National Institute of Meteorology (INAM) on 31 May anticipates moderate to heavy rains (30 to 50 millimeters in 24 hours) with thunderstorms and strong winds in Maputo, Gaza, and Inhambane provinces from the afternoon of 01 June until 02 June. Affected districts in Maputo will be Matutuine, Boane, Namaacha, Marracuene, Moamba, Magude, Manhica, cities of Maputo and Matola. The districts of Massingir, Limpopo, Chonguene, Massangena, Guija, Mandlakazi, Bilene, and the cities of Chokwe and Xai-Xai will be affected in Gaza province while the districts of Zavala and Inharrime in Inhambane province. Civilians residing in the aforementioned areas are advised to adhere to precautionary and safety measures.

President Nyusi on 31 May stated that he expects more than 10 million of the country's inhabitants will have access to energy by 2024 following the launch of the Temane Gas and Energy projects in Maputo. He added that the project will create 3,000 jobs during the implementation phase and 200 vacancies during its operations.

Mozambican Association of Banks (AMB) announced on 31 May that the country's benchmark interest rate will remain at 18.9% for June. The percentage is based on a single index of 13.3 % (calculated by the Bank of Mozambique) and a cost premium of 5.6 percent (calculated by AMB).

The Hunger Early Warning Network in late May predicted a decline in food assistance to 714,000 IDPs in Cabo Delgado in August due to a lack of resources among NGOs providing humanitarian assistance in the province.  This includes to more than 60,000 people displaced by the March assault on Palma.

Insurgents attacked Palma on the night of 22 May, setting 14 houses on fire in the Quelimane area and destroying a mosque in the Quilaua area. Security forces clashed with insurgents, who retreated north towards Quionga after the exchange.  9 people were reportedly killed, including 4 civilians and 5 insurgents.  A second source reported 9 civilians killed and an unknown number of insurgents killed.  No security force casualties were reported.

In an address to the country on the night of 26 May, President Nyusi announced that the pandemic was "still far from over" and said all state of emergency measures would remain in place, except for the following exclusions.  These exceptions include: The re-opening of beaches, public swimming pools, and pre-school classes. Curfews in place across the country in cities will now be adjusted to 2300hrs to 0400hrs. Bottle stores selling alcohol may now operate from 0900hrs to 1700hrs from Monday to Saturday and will remain closed on Sundays. Restaurants may now stay open one hour longer to 2100hrs nightly. The government also allowed the resumption of business and work visas. Funeral attendance capacity has now been increased from 20 to 30 people. A Mwirti Lda mining company is set to start a new gold mining operation at Nairoto in Cabo Delgado. The mining is expected to yield tradable quantities by the end of 2021, according to company officials.

South African FM Naledi Pandor said on 26 May that the SADC's Organ on Politics, Peace, and Security was "deliberating" on insurgent attacks in Mozambique and had developed proposals to support Mozambique against the insurgency.

Security forces arrested three Tanzanian football players who were found attempting to forge National ID cards in Cabo Delgado on 25 May. The suspects were reportedly in possession of forged birth certificates.
Security forces arrested a suspect for attempting to obtain a counterfeit National ID cards in Nampula on 18 May.

Combomune farmers stated that a herd of elephants on the loose have been trampling on corn crops at agricultural areas on 26 May. Farmers called for the completion of the fence of the Limpopo Natural Park.

Locals reportedly paid bribes of 5000 meticais to pass through roadblocks manned by security forces from Palma in the aftermath of the assault on Palma. The locals stated that they initially charged men and women while exempting pregnant women, sick, and children.
The trial for Former Pemba Mayor Tagir Carimo resumes on 26 May. The former mayor was accused of misusing public funds, using counterfeit documents, and undue inducement payments.

The Mozambican government announced the closure of the public postal services due to a decline in business. The Institute for the Management of State Holdings Executive Director Matula stated that postal service was not able to reinvent itself and is not considered a “strategic company”.

The Ministry of Health announced 15 new COVID cases and a single related death in Mozambique on 26 May.  This brings the total cases to 70,651. While 76 daily recoveries were reported increasing the total recoveries to 69,193. Hospitalizations were at 17 inpatients.

Police announced the rescue of a Chinese businessman and arrest of two kidnappers in Ceramica area, north of Beira City, on the night of Thursday, 27 May. The kidnappers previously demanded for a ransom of 25 million meticais for the victim’s release after abducting him on 24 May. The victim was found with several abrasions. Police stated that two other suspects in the kidnapping are still on the run. The victim was abducted from Maquinino area and forced into a vehicle during the kidnapping which took place on Monday, 24 May.

The kidnappers previously demanded for a ransom of 25 million meticais for the victim’s release after abducting him on 24 May. The victim was found with several abrasions. Police stated that two other suspects in the kidnapping are still on the run. The victim was abducted from Maquinino area and forced into a vehicle during the kidnapping which took place on Monday, 24 May.
A 14-year old girl fled her residence due to an attempted forced marriage in Mutuali, west of Nampula on 27 May. The victim stated that the was forced to marry a nurse due to her mother's illness.

Former Minister of Transport Paulo Zucula was released from prison by an apeals court after being charged with money laundering, membership in a criminal association, and illicit business participation.

A two-seater training plane FAM 255 of the Mozambican Air Force crashed and damaged the outer walls of Hulene B Primary Complete School in Hulene B area, northeast of Maputo International Airport on the afternoon of 28 May. One of the passengers was injured along with two children.  No details were available as to what caused the crash. Police responded and a clearing team was deployed in response to the plane crash.

column4: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) stated on 28 May that more than 60,000 people have been displaced by the March 24 Palma attack.  This includes those who have fled out of the district and those who fled the town to the Afungi area.  From 19-27 May, 8,500 new IDPs were registered, with actual numbers of IDPs believed to be higher with many still unregistered.

Insurgents on the night of 28 May attacked and set fire to homes in the village of Quiwiya, about 15 airline kms from Palma.  The village had been mostly abandoned and damaged in previous insurgent attacks, and locals said insurgents had set fire to most of the remain structures in the town.  No casualties have been reported in this attack.  Video filmed from Palma showed a large fire several kms away in Quiwiya.  Note that one other source initially reported this incident had taken place on 28 May.

Locals reported unknown gunfire suspected to be warning shots by police for individuals violating the curfew near Pemba International Airport early morning of 27 May, though this explanation has not been confirmed.

Around 60 IDPs attempted to chase a vehicle believed by locals to be transporting food supplies in Metuge district.. The locals reportedly were seen falling off after grab hold onto the trailer while looking for food supplies.

A new report indicated that the Hidden Debts scandal has cost the Mozambique government 11 billion dollars USD. The scandal has also forced 2 million individuals into poverty. The Centre for Public Integrity (CIP) stated that the direct cost of the loans in payment of interest and capital so far as of 2019, is at 674.2 million USD. If Mozambique is obliged to service debts triggered by the scandal, there will be an additional 3.93 billion dollars to pay up to 2031.  The country is also estimated to have lost $10.7 billion in GDP between 2015 to 2019.

President Nyusi stated during the SADC Double Troika summit that the presidents agreed on border security, elimination of terrorist financing sources, and reconstruction of infrastructures.  The SADC has not committed however to any intervention in Cabo Delgado.

The Mozambique government is ending a cotton subsidy to suppliers this year because of a good performance by cotton sector. The government previously invested 240 million meticais to maintain the price of cotton to 25 meticais per kilo. Minister of Agriculture Correia stated that the subsidy is not needed as cotton supply has increase from 30,000 to 52,000 tons, which guaranteed 150,000 farmers salaries.

Security forces arrested two drug traffickers and seized a smuggling of marijuana hidden inside the animal pulled cart in Nyampanda Border Post at around 19:00 of 26 May. The five bags reportedly weighed at 100kg, and 100,000 USD were seized from the suspects.

Security forces arrested two drug traffickers and seized a smuggling of marijuana hidden inside the animal pulled cart in Nyampanda Border Post at around 19:00 of 26 May. The five bags reportedly weighed at 100kg, and 100,000 USD were seized from the suspects.

Portugal Defense Minister Cravinho stated that the EU training mission will likely be formally approved in June. Cravinho stated that the troops can then be expected to be deployed within 3 months, so likely in September. An EU technical mission is currently on the ground in Cabo Delgado to identify the parameters of a potential EU mission.

The Maputo Mayor Eneas Comiche on 31 May stated that security measures will be taken against police who were caught on camera attacking informal vendor on a street in Aeroporto B, Maputo City over the weekend.

Sources stated that Macomia residents have returned to the town a year after insurgent capture of the town. Macomia residents stated that the town is still in ruins with poor or complete lack of most public services. Doctors without borders are the only health providers and no banks were currently operating in the area. The town is also on perpetual alert for new terror attacks, and areas north and east of Macomia are regarded as effectively insurgent territory.

National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD) president called on IDPs to provide accurate data and cooperate with local authorities. The cooperation will allow authorities to direct IDPS to the humanitarian services they require.

The Electronic Sealing and Cargo Tracking System (SEERC) announced that its cargo tracking system in past year has prevented the smuggling of 6,000 different goods to neighboring countries of Mozambique. From January until May, 6,209 tracking alerts were registered, in 649 cases this prompted the intervention of customs rapid response teams to intercept and inspect vehicles transporting the goods in transit.

United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) stated 130 girls are subjected to early marriage in Mozambique daily. Five girls each hour are being wed prematurely even two years after a law was passed against premature marriage. The weak implementation of the law has allowed the prevalence of the high number of premature marriages, according to Social Affairs, Gender, Technology and Communication Chairwoman Mafuiane.

Universities are reportedly experiencing increased rates of dropouts due to COVID pandemic in Mozambique. Students were reportedly having difficulties in adapting with the new teaching methods. The Pedagogical University of Maputo stated that their dropout rate in 2019 was at 13.15%. In 2020, the number increased to 17.11%.
The Ministry of Health announced 15 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 31 May. 18 recoveries were also reported during the past 24 hours. 10 cases were recorded in Manica and Maputo with 2 cases.

The Mozambique government announced signing of an agreement for a $1 billion power plant in Inhambane, with construction to begin in the second half of 2021. The gas power plant and transmission lines will  boost energy supply in the province. The power plant is part of a countrywide project to provide electricity throughout Mozambique by 2024.

RENAMO Military Junta "Spiritual Leader" Today Tequezi has defected from the group on 28 May over a disagreement over the direction of the group.  No further information on this incident is currently available.

Local officials stated roads in Zambezia province are currently in poor condition. Sources stated that around 40% of the roads in the province are paved and the remaining are in poor condition. Around 300km of the National Road between Mocuba districts to Mulumbo is affected by these poor road conditions.

Sources stated that several soldiers have recently defected from the Mozambican army in Cabo Delgado. The defection of the soldiers was due to several factors including the lack of military equipment to fight against the insurgents, hunger, and the lack of payments to the troops.

Insurgents according to a report on 31 May are receiving significant numbers of new recruits, with many arriving by sea to Mocimboa da Praia.  New recruits are arriving "from various parts of Mozambique and even from outside the country".  This report is unconfirmed.

column4: Sources this week reported that a potential insurgent attack could target Mueda in the near to medium term future.  This alert is unconfirmed.
Immigration authorities deported 57 Malawian national for illegal immigration and COVID safety violations on 30 May. The illegal immigrants were abandoned by a smuggler near Mameme in Tete province.
A policeman was killed after being ran over by a vehicle along National Road 1 in Marracuene District, north of Maputo City, on the afternoon of 1 June.
Gunmen in a black vehicle shot dead a civilian and stole an undisclosed amount of money near the Predio Branco Building in west Nampula at around 13:00 on 1 June. The suspects managed to escape.

Local sources stated that IDPs continue to enter Montepuez District and are causing tensions with locals in Montepuez. The IDPs in the district are concentrated between Balama and Montepuez.

Health Minister Armindo Tiago stated that Mozambique has the fourth highest number of AIDS/HIV. Tiago stated that the Health Ministry records an average of 364 new AIDS/HIV cases daily.
The World Food Program announced that they have transported 900 humanitarian staff since December of 2020, along with 9.7 metric tons of humanitarian aid across Mozambique.

Cahora Bassa Hydroelectric (HCB) has donated 5 million meticais to the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD) for the victims in Cabo Delgado. INGD stated that the donation shows solidarity with the Mozambicans and the victims of insurgency in the northern province.
Special military units attacked insurgent positions in Nangunde and Ntchinga on 22 May.  Several militants who were local recruits from nearby villages were captured in these clashes.

Military units on or around 22 May attacked a 30 man insurgent camp in the Pundanhar area.  No information on casualties were available.  Militants fled the area after this clash.
8 insurgents were killed on or around 20 May May off Mitacata near Quiterajo when militants attacked a boat carrying IDPs; IDPs charged the insurgent boat and killed all 8 of the insurgents.
SADC leaders were reportedly disappointed regarding President Nyusi’s decision to request assistance from Rwanda, France, and other European companies at the recent SADC summit.

Security forces in Quitunda recently indicated they continue to stop IDPs from leaving the area over concerns that insurgents have infiltrated the 11,000+ IDPs in the area and that insurgents would leave the area with evacuees.
Insurgents reportedly attacked and sabotaged Awasse electrical station again on 5 May.  Insurgents have controlled this area for several months.
Security forces seized nine tons of garnet minerals from a Tanzanian smuggler in Chimoio on 28 May. The smuggled items were worth 350,000 meticais and were placed in 185 bags.

On 22 May, local militia in Chachamba captured 5 insurgents fleeing from Pundanhar after security forces overran insurgent positions in the area.  These 5 insurgent were later killed by vigilantes.

A security force member stabbed a suspected insurgent to death on 22 May in Chacamba in Nangade after a group of insurgents fled to the area from Pundanhar, where an insurgent base had been overrun by security forces.
Insurgents stole fish and money from six fishermen at Ntoni village near Pangane on 23 May. The fishermen reportedly fled to Pangane after the incident.
