Reports on 31 May indicated that insurgents were recently paid a ransom of $33,000 for two Indian nationals captured during the assault on Palma.  It is unclear exactly when this payment took place.

Insurgents on 31 May were reported to still be holding at least two Zimbabweans and one Somali national, demanding an unknown ransom for the three.  The group were captured by the insurgents during the assault on Palma in late March.

Sources stated that pro-gov militia pensions were not paid on time in Nangade district. The pro-government militiamen veterans reportedly stated that they have not received their pensions since January. Militia members recently travelled to Mueda to receive back pensions, but were only paid for February, and not from March onwards.

Police officials recently complained to the Cabo Delgado Governor Valige Tauabo that police in the province lacked the resources to fight insurgency. In response, Cabo Delgado Tauabo stated that the police were delaying economic development in the province by not defeating the insurgency.

Sources stated that Rwandan Police Chief Dan Munzuya recently met with the Tanzanian Police Chief in Tanzania.  The two discussed the movement of Rwandan and Tanzanian nationals across the TZ border into Cabo Delgado, and agreed to cooperate on this issue.

Security officials stated on 27 May that they are in firm control of Muidumbe and Palma, and have called on Muidumbe District residents to begin to return to the area.  Security forces recently reclaimed Namacande town in Muidumbe.

The Mozambique government met with National Institute of Social Security (INSS)discussing the scope of the debt forgiveness that would be allowed for companies. Around 17,000 companies were expected to benefit from the debt forgiveness.

The Association of Rwandan Refugees in Mozambique stated that local police in Inhaca Island knew where detained Rwandan journalist Cassien was, saying police detained him recently and then transported him to Maputo.  Authorities have denied that they detained Cassien.

Mozambican Association for Victims of Road Insecurity (AMVIRO) stated that poor road safety especially for children is evident across Mozambique. AMVIRO stated that that in 2020, there were 8550 deaths due to road accidents, and 100 of those deaths were children 13 and under.
RENAMO’s Chief of the General Staff Timosse Maquinze had a stroke and was reported to be in a Beira hospital on 27 May.
Immigration agents reportedly seized passports of the Environmental Management and Conservation Trust (EMCT) (anti-poaching division of DAG) in Limpopo National Park on 16 May.

Health officials on 01 June said about 323,000 people have been vaccinated in Mozambique out of a targeted 16 million for vaccinations.  This is only about 2% of the vaccination target.  This low vaccination rate is partially because Mozambique to date has only received about 1 million COVID vaccine doses.  A spike in cases in India has led to a slow down in the provision of doses from that country, and it is unclear when Mozambique will receive more doses, slowing the vaccination campaign in the country.

The Ministry of Health announced 55 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 1 June. Maputo registered with 31 cases and Zambezia with 11 cases. 22 daily recoveries were recorded. While 4 new hospitalizations bringing the total to 13 hospitalizations.

A parliamentary commission reported on an increase of land conflicts due to resettling of IDPs in Cabo Delgado as numbers of IDPs continue to increase.  More than 730,000 people have been displaced by the ongoing insurgency in the province.

The Ministry of Economy and Finance stated that the Mozambique public debt is "unsustainable". The Ministry of Economy and Finance released a report showing a decline in sustainability as of 2020. The country's ratio on debt exports was at 225.6% as of 2020, wherein the limit was only at 150%.
The Ministry of Health announced that around a million individuals in Mozambique infected HIV in Mozambique have not access to treatment.
The National Directorate of Healthcare issued an order that prohibits health professionals from restricting or preventing individuals from receiving treatment based on their clothing.

A court on 01 June sentenced a group of 11 Pakistani nationals to 10 - 20 years in prison for smuggling 430kg of narcotics on a boat in Pemba. The suspects were part of a 13-man international smuggling group.

Vehicle traffic was restricted by heavy rains and hail around Maputo City on the evening of 1 June. Power outages were also reported in various neighborhoods, which included Zimpeto, Magoanice C, Machava and Zona Verde.

Nhangau administrative post head stated that around 30km of road towards Nhangau are in a terrible condition due to the previous cyclones. Nhangau AP head Arriaga stated that they have contacted National Road Administration (ANE) for repairs and maintenance of the road.

Government troops and pro-gov local militia exchanged gunfire with insurgents in Ntchinga, northeast of Muidumbe, during a three day operation from 28-30 May. Security forces withdrew after their resupply requests were turned down.  Several weapons were seized during the offensive by government forces.

Security forces and pro-gov militia withdrew towards Mueda after running out of supplies in the Ntchinga area after clashes with insurgents in the area.

Insurgents reportedly returned to Quiwiya and burned several residences on 29 May. No specific details were mentioned as to how many residences were burned down.  They had launched a similar attack the day before.

Security forces reportedly withdrew from the Namacande area of Muidumbe district on 28 May after having recaptured the town on 22 May.  It was unclear if insurgents re-occupied the town, but the district capital is no longer garrisoned.
Robbers stole a machine used to replace ID cards in Chiure on the evening of 23 May. Security forces responded and conducted a search for the suspect.

Sources report that at least 10 security checkpoints are in place along the road between Mueda and Nangade.  Goods and people are able to travel between Nangade and Mueda, though there remains a high threat of insurgent attacks along this route.

Local media reported on 03 June that troops in Palma have continued to carry out looting and thefts in Palma town, robbing homes and private businesses.  Among locations targeted have been warehouses, containers, and private camps.  Thefts began during the battle of Palma and have effectively never ended.
Local media reported that Mozambican military units in late May staged an insurgent attack in Palma and carried out robberies of Standard and BCI banks, using explosives to break into the facilities.

Several soldiers in late May involved with a reported bank robbery Palma attempted to flee to Pemba. They were reportedly detained by other military forces. Senior officials were reported to have seized the stolen money.

Several soldiers in late May involved with a reported bank robbery Palma attempted to flee to Pemba. They were reportedly detained by other military forces. Senior officials were reported to have seized the stolen money.

Security forces recovered the body of a deceased woman who was suspected to be killed during a sexual assault incident in Ibo Island on or before 28 May. Local sources stated that the victim was suspected to have been attacked by soldiers due to her body being found near a military barracks.

The Ministry of Health announced that 72 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique over the past 24 hours. Maputo province recorded 39 of the new cases, which is 53.4% of the daily total cases. 8 daily recoveries were also reported.

Security forces reportedly handed over a detained Rwandan journalist to the Rwandan Embassy in Mozambique on 01 June. The journalist, Cassien was critical of Rwanda President Kagame. Cassien is likely to be extradited to Rwanda following his transfer.

Security forces detained three more suspects wanted for kidnapping a Chinese businessman in Beira on 2 June. One of the suspects was Chinese national who conducted the logistics of the suspects.  The man was originally kidnapped on 23 May in Beira before being rescued days later.

The National Institute of Meteorology (INAM) stated that 30 to 50mm or rainfall is expected to hit the provinces of Gaza, Inhambane, Sofala and Zambezia on 2 June. The rain was accompanied by thunderstorms, hail and strong winds. Limpopo, Chongoene, Mandlakazi and Xai-Xai city were expected to be affected in Gaza. While in Inhambane will be the districts of Zavala, Inharrime, Jangamo, Homoine, Morrumbene, Massinga, Vilankulo, Inhassoro, Guvuro and Maxixe and Inhambane cities. Machanga, Buzi, Dondo, Muanza, Cheringoma, Marromeu and Beira city in Sofala province. Zambezia is expected to be affected in the districts of Luabo, Chinde, Inhassunge, Mopeia, Nicoadala, Namacurra, Maganja da Costa, Mocubela, Mulevala and Quelimane city.

Local activists and jurists accused police of using brutal tactics against demonstrators in Mozambique. This comes as officials conducted a debate regarding the right for demonstrations in the country. An official stated that police responding to demonstrations are excessively using force.

Security forces seized a truck transporting 1,400kg of marijuana in Dondo of Sofala province on 2 June. The truck reportedly came from Malawi. The marijuana was packed into 79 20kg bags each marked as fertilizer. The suspects reportedly fled from the area during the seizure.  This is the largest drug seizure in Sofala in the past 10 years.

The Mozambique government requested additional support from the diplomatic missions and international organizations to provide support for displaced people in Cabo Delgado. Minister of Foreign Affairs Macamo warned that the IDPs are constantly increasing in the province. The province is in need of humanitarian relief, specifically food items.

The Mozambican government announced that water prices will be altered to both private and public supplies. The change in water prices was agreed upon during the meeting of the Council of Ministers to ensure the availability of water.

A mineshaft reportedly collapsed, killing an illegal miner at the Montepuez Ruby Mining Camp in Namanhumbir at around 19:00 on 29 May. Police managed to recover the body and stated that the collapse was not due to the weather.  8 illegal miners have been killed in 2021 in the Montepuez area in various accidents.

SADC members reportedly rejected President Nyusi’s request for Rwanda to be involved in the intervention in Cabo Delgado on 27 May. The SADC members told Nyusi that Rwanda could participate through the SADC to fight against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

Sources stated that as of 31 May, 64,099 displaced people have fled from Palma since end of March. This includes 17,213 IDPs in Nangade, 17,324 in Mueda, 14,598 in Pemba, 6,849 in Montepuez districts.

Security forces arrested a suspect for vandalizing several graves at São Francisco Xavier and Lhanguene cemetery in Maputo on 2 June. The suspect was in possession of 15kg of lead.

President Nyusi appointed Vicente Joaquim as Secretary of State for Maputo City on 2 June. Joaquim was the director in Eduardo Mondlane University. He served as a professor for Economics and Construction Management and Graphical Representation Techniques in Architecture and Urbanism.

On 03 June, Defense Minister Jaime Neto said that Mozambique on Thursday received 60,000 doses of COVID vaccine from China, specifically intended for the country's Defense and Security Forces.  Specifically, troops deployed in Cabo Delgado will be prioritized for vaccinations, though it is likely that troops in other provinces will also be vaccinated. This is the first batch of vaccines received by Mozambique in several weeks, and the country just recently reported that a slow-down in the acquiring of vaccines was in turn stalling the nationwide vaccination campaign.  Only about 2% of Mozambique's target goal of 16 million people have been vaccinated so far, and Mozambique in total has received only about 1 million COVID vaccine doses in total.

The Minister of Health Armindo Tiago stated that even with the decline in COVID cases in Mozambique, the pandemic is not over. Minister Tiago stated neighboring countries were experiencing a “third wave” which is a reason for concern and could spread to Mozambique.

The lawyer for the detained Rwandan journalist Ntamuhanga Cassien stated that he was unable to contact Cassien after reports that he was handed over the Rwanda Embassy for extradition. The lawyer stated that his client has the right to defense.

The Mozambique Defense Minister Jaime Neto and other Mozambican officials on 03 June met with their Tanzanian counterparts in Tanzania, discussing security cooperation and the fight against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.
The Mozambican National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) stated there are still many displaced people who have fled from Palma who are still hiding in the woods in Cabo Delgado in poor conditions.

Sources reports significant security force deployments in Macomia town during the recent celebration of the 56th anniversary of the town. Insurgents are known to be present in parts of the district, including areas north and east of Macomia town itself.
The Ministry of Health announced 42 new COVID cases and a single death in Mozambique on 3 June. Tete recorded 26 of the new cases, Maputo province with 7 and Maputo City with 6 cases.

The French Embassy Economic Service head reaffirmed that France would maintain support for Mozambique and that French companies will continue to operate in the country, saying 65 different French companies are currently operating in Mozambique.
Security forces claim they repelled an insurgent attack on Quiwiya on 29 May. Insurgents were previously reported to have set fire to homes in the village on 28 and 29 May.
Heavy rain and strong winds damage several areas in Tchumene of Matola in Maputo province on 1 June. Several residence roofs collapsed and trees were knocked over. No casualties were reported.

The Ministry of Health stated that there was significant decline in vaccinations for different diseases in Cabo Delgado in 2020. The decline was noted during the Expanded Vaccination Program in which only 59% of those targeted for vaccinations were reached in 2020 compared to 100 % in 2019.  Insurgent attacks and the large scale displacement of people were the main cause of this disruption.
Local sources reported that robbers attempted to steal a tanker in Fernao Veloso Bay on 03 June. No further information on this incident is currently available.

President Filipe Nyusi appointed Antonio Njanje Taimo Supeia as Cabo Delgado's Secretary of State on 03 June. Supeia replaces Armindo Ngunga, who will now head the Northern Integrated Development Agency.  The role of Secretary of State is effectively the most powerful local official in Cabo Delgado, including over the provincial governor.

Local sources stated that there is a lack of cooking gas in Maputo city due to the shortage from GALP for almost a month. Sources stated that refilling stations also lacked fuel to refill the gas cylinders. The cause of the shortage is unclear.
The 6th Criminal Section of the Judicial Court released a Portuguese national who was detained for possessing 79 endangered sea turtles in Nampula.

IDPs have called on the governor for financial assistance to start small businesses in Mecufi on 3 June. The IDPs stated that income-generating activities were needed to encourage trade and develop the region.
16 police instructors have been reported to have been transferred to other police divisions in the wake of reports of sexual abuse of cadets in Escola Pratica Da Policia Matalane, north Maputo City.

President Nyusi stated that a new water treatment plant in Moamba District would allow the production of 60,000 cubic meters of water per day and double by September. This water treatment plant will ease water restrictions in the Greater Maputo Area.

The Judicial court of Cabo Delgado issued an arrest warrant for Manica Economy and Finance Director Maria Nhalivilo for six criminal charges. Director Nhalivilo was charged for economic participation in business, embezzlement and the use of false documents when she was administrator of Mueda District from 2017-2019.
Beluluane Industrial Park (BIP) intends to invest 100 million USD in Boane district, southwest of Maputo City to create 20,000 jobs. BIP already employs about 7,000 local workers.

Tanzania intends to begin construction of its own LNG project in 2023. The delayed project was started after talks with Equinor, a Norwegian energy company. This construction is expected to take 5 years. The project was previously delayed by the former President John Magufuli. Tanzania has significant gas deposits offshore, just across the border from Cabo Delgado.

The International Organization for Migration released a report on 4 June indicating that a total of 67,848 IDPs have fled from Palma since March 24. 18,202 IDPs fled to Nangade, 18,061 to Mueda, 15,905 to Pemba, and 6,849 to Montepuez

Standard Bank Mozambique stated that the Mozambique economy has improved following a decline since March. The Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) was used to calculate this improvement. The PMI for April was at 51.3, and 51.2 in May.

The World Bank approved a grant to Mozambique with $115 million to expand the country's COVID vaccination campaign. 100 million USD from the International Development Association (IDA) and a 15 million USD from the Global Financing Facility (GFF). The funds will help fund the acquisition of more COVID vaccine doses and other supplies related to the delivery of vaccines, as well as support logistics related to the vaccination process.
The Electricity of Mozambique announced power interruptions in Maputo and Zambezia provinces will from 05:00 to 10:00 on 5 June.
The Electricity of Mozambique announced power interruptions from 06:00 to 16:00 Maputo City, Sofala province, Manica province, Zambezia province, Niassa province, and Nampula on 6 June.
The Ministry of Health announced 54 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 4 June. Maputo city recorded 25 of the new cases, while Tete province has the second most cases with 15 cases.

RENAMO President Momade stated that the DDR process will not be finished on time due to the pandemic and other factors.  Momade also said it is important that former guerillas are incorporated into the police, and said that the names of 362 RENAMO officers have been submitted to the government.
The EU ambassador Antonio Sanchez Benedetto Gaspar expects that the DDR process will be completed by end of 2022 at the latest, with all of RENAMO's 5,000 armed members disarmed by that time.

The Ministry of Health announced that 53 Mozambicans have positive for COVID who were repatriated from South Africa between Jan to May. The Ministry of Health stated that the cases were sent through the Ressano Garcia border crossing. The cases were located as follows: 10 in Maputo province, 4 in Maputo city, 5 in Gaza province, 16 in Inhambane, 4 in  Manica, 13 in Sofala, and 1 in Zambezia.

Mozambican government officials stated during talks in Tanzania that both Mozambique and Tanzania need to coordinate and exchange information to improve their response against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  Tanzanian security officials have reportedly viewed the Cabo Delgado insurgency as a primarily internal Mozambican problem, rather a cross border issue.

Tanzania refused to let 3,800 Mozambicans asylum seekers to enter the country from Cabo Delgado during May, returning these IDPs to the Negomano border post.  Thousands of Mozambicans from Palma have attempted to flee into Tanzania since the attack on Palma in March.

Locals sources stated that displaced people at IDP centers in Ancuabe are considering fleeing the centers due to the presence of security forces. The IDPs stated that they fled from their home areas originally due to security force abuses. This comes as security forces accused locals as insurgents even when they are innocent.

IDPs at Nanju IDP Camp in Ancuabe claimed that security forces at IDP camps often accuse IDPs of belonging to the insurgency.  Security forces reportedly camp outside of the IDP camps, and often accost IDPs with these accusations, particularly when they are carrying something of value.
Sources stated that security forces recently threatened a construction company employee who was attempting to deliver food and medication to IDPs near Quitunda.
On 02 June, President Nyusi appointed Vicente Joaquim as secretary of state in Maputo City. Joachim replaced Sheila Santana Afonso who was dismissed from the position last 01 June.

President Filipe Nyusi and President Emmerson Mnangagwa have agreed on 05 June to revive the Joint Permanent Commission (JPC), which had been inactive for about eight years between the two countries. They also talked about the current situation in Cabo Delgado following the Palma attack last March. President Mnangagwa previously expressed his willingness to provide assistance to Mozambique to deal with the militants but emphasized that it has to be the decision of SADC.

International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) announced on 02 June that they will begin to establish a presence in Mozambique over the coming months. The statement came after INSO conducted an assessment in the country and concluded that there is a significant need for their support.

On 04 June, President Nyusi announced the resumption of  the Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration (DDR) process this month in Tete Province. He reiterated his commitment to bring the process to completion amid setbacks including the coronavirus pandemic. He urged Mariano Nhongo, head of the self-proclaimed Renamo Military Junta, and his followers to surrender and join the process.

Sources on 06 June stated that the second phase construction of road connecting Major General Candido Mondlane road and Combatant's Square in Maputo City will commence this year following several postponements. Road users have complained over slow progress in the construction of this road. The construction of the road have been postponed several times without explanation leaving unfinished drainage ditches.

Sources on 07 June said that the voting for which African country will hold one of the non-permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council 2022 will take place on Friday, 11 June. Candidates are Ghana, Gabon & Congo-DRC while Mozambique is reportedly a pre-candidate for 2023-24.

The Ministry of Health announced 63 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 05 June. 21 of the news cases reported were from Maputo city and 16 were from Maputo province. 17 cases were reported from Tete, eight from Inhambane and one from Manica. No deaths related to the virus was recorded for the second consecutive day. Over the last 24 hours, three new patients were admitted to treatment centers while no patients were discharged.
A total of 26 deaths were recorded from 25 road accidents in Inhambane for the first quarter of 2021, against the 21 accidents in the same period of 2020 with the same number of deaths.
Construction of 48 houses is ongoing in the Malica Resettlement District, Lichinga intended for 48 families displaced from districts affected by insurgency in Cabo Delgado Province.

There is a heightened erosion risk in the coastal districts of Inhambane Province after more than a thousand hectares of forest in the province is currently being lost per year. The province is reportedly under pressure to produce wood to supply the high demand for firewood and charcoal in Maputo City. Gaza province previously supplies the capital with wood, however, much of Gaza has already been deforested.

The Ministry of Health announced 32 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 06 June. No deaths related to the virus was recorded for the third consecutive day. Over the last 24 hours, four new patients were admitted to treatment centers while three patients were discharged.

The number of birth rate recorded in Mavalane General Hospital has increased amid the coronavirus pandemic. Between March 2020 and March 2021, 7,264 deliveries were recorded, compared to 7,253 deliveries on same period of 2019 and 2020. Health authorities advised women in reproductive age to seek professional health care during pregnancy and comply to safety protocols to ensure protection for COVID-19.

On 03 June, the United States Government announced that it will donate 80 million US vaccine doses worldwide. COVAX will receive 75 percent of these doses. Reports suggest that the vaccines allocated for Africa will be selected in coordination with the African Union. Mozambique may benefit from these donations and has already received significant numbers of doses through the COVAX program.

UN Health Agency on 03 June warned that critical health facilities across Africa are at risk of being overwhelmed by increasing COVID-19 infections. The entire continent recorded a 20 percent increase in cases over the last two weeks while its struggle with the shortage of vaccines. Dr. Matshidiso Moeti, WHO Regional Director for Africa, stated that the third wave threat is rising that's why its vital to quickly administer the vaccines to high-risk individuals.

Maputo City Government committed to begin the rehabilitation works of roads with potholes in the city. The Julius Nyerere Avenue between Praca da Juventude and Praca Dos Combatentes will be prioritized as several motorists lament on the situation of the route which caused damage to vehicles.

On 07 June, truck drivers urged the authorities to open Machipanda border post, between Mozambique and Zimbabwe,  24hrs a day instead of its usual operating hours between 0600hrs until 2200hrs. The requested hours of operation will fast-track the handling of commodities and alleviate the concerns of the drivers.  The border is currently open between 0600hrs and 2200hrs.

Insurgents on the night of 28 May attacked and set fire to homes in the village of Quiwiya, about 15 airline kms from Palma. 10 people were killed, five of them were shot dead and the other five were decapitated after residents fled the village and were caught by insurgents a short time later just outside of Quiwiya. The village had been mostly abandoned and damaged in previous insurgent attacks, and locals said insurgents had set fire to most of the remaining structures in the town. Video filmed from Palma showed a large fire several kms away in Quiwiya.

Thousands of displaced people repatriated from Tanzania remained in Negomano Border Control due to the lack of financial capability to continue their travel to Mueda district. Affected families, who are staying in small huts in Negomano, received food aid from World Food Program.

Displaced people continue to arrive in Paquitequete beach, Pemba City. Some of them have stayed at the beach while attempting to relocate their family members. Reports suggest that these people were receiving humanitarian support from the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and the International Committee of the Red Cross.
Former Ministry of Health, Helder Martins, said lenient border control may be the reason behind the surge of new COVID-19 cases in the provinces of Maputo and Niassa.

Local media reported police on 07 June were on "high alert" after messages circulated on social media platforms in recent days threatening an insurgent attack in Maputo.  Threats received said that all embassy staff in Maputo should leave the city in 30 days or insurgents would target diplomatic staff with kidnappings, explosives, and beheading attacks.  The threat also referenced Abu Yasir Hassan, the supposed leader of the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  This comes after similar threatening letters were received in mid and early May by at least 3 embassies in Maputo; one similar threatening letter was also delivered to the private residence of a Mozambican national.  Additional police forces were deployed in different areas of the city after this threat was received to terminals, squares, and markets to prevent any potential attack.

Additional police forces were deployed in different areas of the city on 07 June after the threat was received to terminals, squares, and markets to prevent any potential attack.  Threats received said that all embassy staff in Maputo should leave the city in 30 days or insurgents would target diplomatic staff with kidnappings, explosives, and beheading attacks.  The threat also referenced Abu Yasir Hassan, the supposed leader of the Cabo Delgado insurgency. The potential targets of these threats, the distance from Cabo Delgado, and the manner in which the threat was conveyed are all significant departures from how the Cabo Delgado insurgents have operated in the past, making these threats highly suspect.

The United States Government announced on 07 June that training on battlefield rescue tactics for 40 Mozambican soldiers and doctors have been completed. 26 health care professionals were trained to provide emergency care during conflict situations while 14 soldiers learned how to provide emergency medical assistance to comrades during attacks. The announcement came a month after US accomplished training provided to Mozambican marines. These programs were funded by US including USD730,000 training equipment that will allow instructors to repeat the training program across Mozambique.

Heavy gunfire were heard around Quiterajo, Macomia on 01 June in the Criimize and Chilongo areas as security forces engaged suspected insurgents in the area during anti-terror operations. Several insurgents were allegedly killed in these clashes.  The incident came a few days after residents in Macomia district were warned not to move to the Quiterajo due to possible military operations.
On 31 May, residents of Chai AP were warned not to go to Quiterajo area due to the ongoing anti-terror operations launched by security forces.

Several insurgents were killed in a gun battle with security forces at a farm in the Marijilane area, near Pangane on 04 June. The insurgents were allegedly caught resting at the farm believed to be owned by FRELIMO senior member and general Alberto Chipande.

Sources on 07 June reported a security force operation targeting militants in the Tibamawe area near Nambo, Nacutoco, and Nfunzi villages in Macomia District.  No other information regarding this operation is currently available.

M-pesa was reported to have blocked approximately 2500 numbers associated with fraud schemes every month. The executive head of marketing at Vodafone M-Pesa, Daisy Madeira, stated that they have not yet blocked numbers from other telco operators but those suspected of fraud cannot make calls to Vodacoms.

Elephants roaming around Macossa district are reportedly factors of the severe famine in the district. The elephants are destroying and preventing harvesting of crops. Locals in the area have called on the local government to resolve the issue.
Police arrested 15 members of two groups for drug dealing in Nampula on 7 June. One of the groups reportedly were also wanted on robbery charges.

A Cabo Delgado Provincial Court sentenced former Mueda administrator Maria Nhalivilo and permanent secretary Guilherme dos Santos to five years in prison. Nhalivilo was tried in absentia after being charged for corruption. Dos Santos was charged for embezzlement, illicit participation in business and making false statements.

Security forces arrested four civil servants in Zambezia province on 1 June. This comes as 25 suspects were listed by the Attorney General's Office for corruption, abuse of office, fraud and forgery of documents charges.

South African State Security Minister Amanda Dlodlo on 07 June expressed support for an SADC intervention in Cabo Delgado, saying South Africa is already prepared to provide both military and political support in Cabo Delgado if invited.

President Nyusi conducted a virtual meeting with European Council President Charles Michel on 07 June regarding bilateral cooperation on Cabo Delgado. European officials said the EU will provide "concrete support" including security, development, and humanitarian support.

The Ministry of Health announced 31 new COVID cases during the past 24 hours in Mozambique on 7 June. 24 cases were recorded in Maputo city, Maputo province with 5 cases, one in Gaza province, and one in Tete province.

Local sources stated that fires were reported near Afungi on 07 June. No specific details were available as to what caused the fires. Previous similar incidents near Palma were reportedly due to the insurgents attacks.

UNICEF on 07 June announced that the organization would increase support from 51 million to 90 million USD for children affected by the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. UNICEF stated that they were going to reinforce their appeal due to the current situation of the province.
A ship was wrecked due to strong winds in Moma on 2 June. Two individuals were reported missing after the incident.
A soldier shot and killed himself in Macomia town on the evening of 04 June. The incident was reportedly due to the infidelity of the his wife.

Macomia's local administrator, Tomas Bedae, was reported in recent days to be encouraging local residents to return to the town and other parts of the district, and to fight against the ongoing insurgency.

The Budget Monitoring Forum (FMO) called on President Nyusi to respond to the judicial summons of Privinvest regarding the "Hidden Debts" cases. FMO stated that the president is disrespecting the general Mozambicans public by not responding to the summons.

The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Action has approved 128 schools to resume their activities in Mozambique.  Out of 1,574 pre-schools only 128 were allowed to operate while following COVID safety measures.

A remnant grenade detonated in a forest near Chimoio on 5 June. A child was injured during the blast. The victim was looking for firewood during the incident.  Four other children received minor injuries.  The explosive was likely left over from the Mozambican Civil War.

The Mozambican Health Ministry on 08 June announced that it would obtain 500,000 more doses of COVID-19 vaccine through a joint effort with 350 private companies who will fund this purchase.  120,000 of these doses will be allotted to the government and will be publicly distributed, while the other 380,000 doses will be privately distributed through the companies.  The Ministry also said it expects to receive six million COVID vaccine doses, primarily through the COVAX program.
National Director of Tourism Langa stated that there was a 53% reduction of tourists entering Mozambique in 2020 compared to 2019 because of the pandemic.
The Switzerland government donated 10 million USD for development projects in Nampula and Niassa of Northern Mozambique on 8 June.

A company providing bottled gas to Mozambique announced that the cooking gas shortage in Maputo was expected to end by 9 June. This came after talks between the government and the company after a rise in demand for cooking gas led to a shortage in the capital area.
There is weak demand for bus transport in Central Mozambique, primarily due to the COVID pandemic.

The UK government reportedly could withdraw 1 billion USD in financing to assist the Mozambique LNG gas project. The possible withdrawal of the support could come as an NGO is currently mounting a legal challenge to this funding due to the project's potential impact on climate change.
Sources stated that businesses in Cabo Delgado are at risk for bankruptcy in Cabo Delgado province due to the impact of the Palma attacks.

Three kidnappers abducted a Zimbabwean self-proclaimed “prophet” in Zimbabwe and brought him to Chikwidzire village, where the kidnappers demanded 10,000 rand from his wife.  Community leaders helped to negotiate his release.
Research recently released on the Cabo Delgado insurgency indicates that in some cases women have assumed combat roles in the insurgency, and in a few select cases, have served as combat commanders.

Mozambique's Oil and Gas Chamber has said it will boycott the Africa Energy Week due to the relocation of the event from South Africa to Dubai. The President of the Chamber of Oil and Gas of Mozambique, Florival Mucave stated that the relocation was an excuse and that the decision were unacceptable as the relocation takes away business opportunities from Africa.

The Ministry of Health announced that 20 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 8 June. This brings the total to 71,165. Two of the new cases were hospitalized. Eight of the new cases were from Maputo City, 6 from Tete province, 3 in Sofala, 1 in Nampula, and 2 in Maputo.

Tancoal Energy Limited mining company is reportedly relocating to Mozambique after difficulties experienced in Tanzania. The company was reportedly struggling in selling coal locally and nearby markets.
An armed man murdered his girlfriend inside their residence in Inhagoia B, south Maputo City, on the evening of 2 June. The man was later arrested by police.
An armed man murdered his girlfriend inside their residence in Inhagoia B, south Maputo City, on the evening of 2 June. The victim was reportedly killed after meeting with her friends.

The Ministry of Health admitted on 07 June that vaccination campaign has been disrupted by availability of COVID vaccines. The country hopes to obtain more vaccines in the near future in partnership with private companies.

Nacala Port officials announced on 7 June that coal exports were 28% less during the first quarter of 2021. Coal shipments have reached 1.1 million tons wherein 1.5 million tons was expected to be exported.

Local media reported on 8 June officials at 9 border posts will start charging taxes on light vehicles with foreign registration entering Mozambique. 10 USD charges were applicable to the Mandimba, Milange, Zobue, Cuchamano, Cassacatiza, Calomue, and Machipanda border crossings. 3 USD charges will be applied to vehicles crossing at Namaacha and Goba into Maputo province.

Sources stated that several neighborhood “chiefs” in Pemba were creating lists of people to receive food aid.  These "chiefs" were suspected of diverting food aid through these lists, and NGOs have called for these local leaders to stop presenting them with these lists.
An NGO stated that at least 51 children were kidnapped by insurgents in Cabo Delgado in the past year.  This is very likely a significant underestimate of child kidnappings in Cabo Delgado.

Unconfirmed media reports on 08 June said that President Nyusi wanted a third term to "guarantee political stability". Local sources stated that the third term would to enable Nyusi maintain immunity and avoid a summons in the "Hidden Debts" case.  Nyusi would need to change the constitution in order to run for a third term.

Maputo Governor Parque assured that the remaining former RENAMO armed wing members would be reintegrated in Maputo province. Parque stated that those former members who finished the DDR process would be supported in this reintegration.

The Red Cross in Mozambique's Andre Nhantabe on 09 June denied reports in the Mozambican press that the organization had suspended aid distribution to IDPs living in the homes of their relatives.  Nhantabe said he would correct the journalists who originally reported the suspension, and that he had instead said in response to a question from a journalist that the Red Cross would only stop aid deliveries to private homes of anyone specifically identified as connected to the insurgency.  He also said the Red Cross was calling for neighborhood leaders to stop presenting the Red Cross with lists of aid beneficiaries, as the Red Cross itself directly identifies beneficiaries.

The Mozambican Economic Climate Indicator reported recovery of the business in May compared to April. The index rose from 87.2 to 87.7 points after three months of decline during the first quarter of 2021. The rise in the index indicates an increase in employment and demand for employment.

Vale Mining Company has confirmed it will pay an outstanding balance of 2.5 billion USD to finance the Nacala logistics corridor serving the Moatize coal mine. The settlement of the balance would allow Mitsui to complete their purchase of the mine and corridor, this will allow Vale to fast track their exit from the coal mining in the country. The payment was scheduled on 22 June.

The United Nations General Assembly voted to allow Mozambique to be one of several countries to assume the vice-presidency of the UN General Assembly. The election was held at the seventh session of the United Nations General Assembly.

Sources reported on 09 June that demobilized RENAMO guerillas in Sofala, Manica, and Inhambane have received no subsidies for the past three months.  The government recently has told RENAMO it will resolve the problem in the near future.

Former Maputo mayor David Simango was sentenced to 18 months in prison for crimes of Acceptance of Offer or Promise and Abuse of Position and Function. Simango was also fined for 15 months of daily rate minimum wage. His apartment which was reportedly worth 457,000 USD was seized after the trial.

A former Mozambican police officer on the night of 08 June was abducted from his home in Beira by a group of individuals who identified themselves as police officers at around 2100hrs.  The group at first attempted to convince the man to come out of his home, saying they needed assistance in rescuing a person nearby who was being attacked by criminals.  The group then surrounded the man's home and broke into the residence, pointing a gun at the victim and forcing him outside  The man was forced into a waiting vehicle that then left the scene.  The police have not yet confirmed if their officers arrested the man.  The victim previously had previously served in Muanza District, and was dismissed from the service over "misconduct", and had previously been held in police custody for 3 months.

Mozambique Airlines (LAM) flight TM 315's front cockpit window detached about 40 minutes after departure from Pemba Airport at around 13:47 on 9 June. The plane flew back and landed safely at around 15:02. No casualties / injuries were reported, and the passengers and crew disembarked the aircraft without any issues. The flight was rescheduled while the plane was repaired and travelled for Maputo International Airport – it’s unclear if this flight back to Maputo included passengers. The plane then reportedly flew a passenger flight to Johannesburg Airport (JNB) in the its next flight following the initial flight to Maputo International Airport.
The Ministry of Health announced 74 new COVID cases in Mozambique on the 9 June. The highest were Tete province recording 31 cases and Maputo city with 16 cases.

The Mozambican government announced it is still waiting for the complete results of the 400 samples for the COVID India/ Delta variant sent to South Africa. Minister of Health official Tiago stated that the testing is slow and only around 20 to 40 samples are being analyzed per day.

The Montepuez district court sentenced seven people for illegal ruby mining for 18 months in prison on 9 June. One of the individuals was tried in absentia. The six detainees were charged with fines of 300 meticais a day leading to a total of 164,100 meticais. Montepuez Ruby Mining (MRM) was also issued to pay 300,000 meticais as compensation. Among the convicted were three policemen, two Garda World employees, and an MRM employee. Another Garda World employee was not present during the trial.
The Ministry of Health announced a single COVID death in Mozambique on 8 June. This brings the total death to 839. The victim who was a 43-year old woman was in Maputo city.

A fire broke out at Supermercado 1 De Maio, central Tete City, at around of 9 June. No casualties were reported. Firefighters reportedly had difficulty dousing the fire reportedly which burned down many stalls. Around 400 vendors operated in the market.

Mozambique Electricity (EDM) on 10 June announced that over 400 customers will be taken to court over electrical theft in Chowke. EDM stated that around 8 million worth of electrical supply have been stolen by these customers.

Local media reported on 09 June that SERNIC officers of the Criminal Investigation Service often demand a fee before beginning any action or investigation from civilians who report crimes to them.  SERNIC officers reportedly demand between 500 to 3000 meticais to open a case.

Sources stated that IDPs at Negomano border crossing are allowed to cross to Tanzania to shop at the local market. NGOs were currently also providing relief kits to the IDPs in the area, most of whom were displaced from Palma, fled to Tanzania, and then deported to Negomano.

Security helicopters conducted strafing attacks targeting insurgents who attempted to infiltrate Namacande on 4 June. No casualties were reported.  Security forces withdrew from Namacande on 28 May, though have continued air patrols over the district capital.

Sources stated that many locals believe that the ongoing conflict is a conspiracy to displace locals and seized their land without providing adequate compensation. Locals stated that the government was mishandling the ongoing insurgency to force people to leave and grab the evacuated lands in the province.  There is no evidence proving this theory, but its widespread belief is indicative of much of Cabo Delgado's population's view of the government and security forces.

Security forces recently have been deployed to the Chai area, quartering in civilian residences. The security forces have told locals they intend to use the village as a staging area for an offensive against insurgents bases along the Messalo River, north of Chai.

EU Representative Macamo stated that military support from the EU and KSA are being held up by bureaucratic processes, though also saying these delays are "normal". Macamo stated that Mozambique has expressed its willingness to receive support but the expected diplomatic terms were taking time and are something that cannot be done overnight.

Local media on 10 June reported that the Mozambican military had begun planting anti-vehicle mines along routes used by insurgents in Cabo Delgado, and had planted a mine recently that had detonated between Namacande and Chitunda, destroying a vehicle driven by the insurgents.  Other sources indicated this incident had occurred on 30 May.  The usage of these mines has not yet been fully confirmed, though several sources have reported this incident.

Local media on 10 June reported that the Mozambican military had begun planting anti-vehicle mines along routes used by insurgents in Cabo Delgado, and had planted a mine recently that had detonated between Namacande and Chitunda, destroying a vehicle driven by the insurgents.  Other sources indicated this incident had occurred on 30 May.  The usage of these mines has not yet been fully confirmed, though several sources have reported this incident.
The Ministry of Health announced 40 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 10 June. 31 daily recoveries were also reported. 16 cases were recorded in Maputo city, while 8 cases were in Nampula.
Former President Joaquim Chissano stated that the government should conduct talks with RENAMO dissident leader Nhongo and convince him to join the DDR process.
Sources have indicated that SADC extraordinary summit meant to be held on 20 June has been rescheduled to 23 June.  President Cyril Ramaphosa recently commented on this schedule change.
President Nyusi announced that he will not travel to the Olympics as originally planned due to the ongoing conflict in Cabo Delgado.

The National Institute of Communicable Diseases stated that a surge in COVID cases was reported in South Africa which could impact Mozambique. 8,881 COVID cases were reported in South Africa on 9 June, the highest number of cases in the country within the past five months.  There is a significant threat that this third wave could spread into Mozambique from over the border.

The Mozambican government after recent talks with France and Portugal reportedly is optimistic that the two countries will provide Mozambique with military vehicles in the fight against the Cabo Delgado insurgents and will provide other military support to the Mozambican military.  In recent talks, President Nyusi reportedly requested ground vehicles and transport helicopters from European countries.  France is also reportedly considering participating in the European training mission to Mozambique, though is allegedly reluctant to deploy and military personnel to the country.

The SADC according to recent reports remains divided and uncertain of what aid it can provide Mozambique in the fight against the insurgency; it is unclear if any direct military aid or an intervention force will be offered by the SADC at talks later this month in Maputo.

Security forces have arrested two civil servants on corruption charges in Nampula. The suspects reportedly embezzled 4 million meticais by setting up a network for charging fees to healthcare employee candidates in the Central Hospital of Nampula.
A group of 23 IDPs escaped from insurgent camps along Messalo River and traveled to Macomia on 08 June. The IDPs stated that they were treated as slaves during their detention at insurgent camps.

The National Institute of Statistics (INE) stated that between June and November 2020 as much as 76% of urban families were worried about not having enough food, and 37% said they had experienced at least one recent day without any food.

Unconfirmed reports stated that insurgents retook Namacande in late May, likely around 29-30 May after troops withdrew from the town on 28 May. Other sources said military helicopters fired on insurgents attempting to approach the town on 04 June; in either case, control over the town remains contested.

Former Maputo Mayor Simango will appeal his conviction of corruption charges. Simango's lawyer claimed that the evidence was contradictory to the sentence. Simango was previously sentenced by the court of 18 months in prison and 15 months of fines.
The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) arrested two smugglers and seized 11 ivory tips in Zona Verde, Matola, on 08 June.
The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) arrested two smugglers and seized 11 ivory tips in Zona Verde, Matola, on 08 June.

The National Migration Service (SENAMI) announced on 10 June that 100 illegal immigrants were deported from Mozambique between 29 May and 04 June, including Malawian, Burundian, and Chinese nationals. 46 others were still waiting to be repatriated. This comes as 151 immigrants were questioned regarding their immigration status. 146 were questioned in Tete province, 2 in Maputo, 2 in Sofala, and 1 in Niassa.

The Mozambique government acknowledged the disappearance of a Rwandan journalist Ntamuhanga Cassien. Officials stated that police were investigating the incident.  Several sources however have reported that state security forces arrested Cassien, and turned him over to the Rwandan embassy in Maputo.

National Director of Tourism Langa stated that 12,000 people remain unemployed in the tourism sector due to the COVID pandemic. Around 18,000 were without regular salaries. Langa stated that only 6,000 were reinstated by the government.

Mozambique government announced that Tanzania will not create a refugee camp for Mozambican refugees near the Tanzanian-Mozambique border for "security reasons". Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation Muchave stated that the IDPs were to be protected and transported at Negomano on the Mozambican side of the border, based on an agreement between the two countries.  The UN meanwhile has recently called on Tanzania not to turn away refugees fleeing into Tanzania from insurgent attacks.
Local gas cylinder vendors stated that gas cylinder supplies were being delivered in Maputo as of 10 June. This is slowly alleviating a gas shortage experienced this week in Maputo City.

The National Roads Administration stated that traffic will be suspended on the bridge along R448 in Macarretane, north of Chowke from 10 June to 15 June. The suspension was due to scheduled maintenance by reconnecting the bridge decks. The National Roads Administration announced a detour via Macarretane-Chókwe-Guijá-Caniçado-Chinhacanine road for light vehicles; semi-trailers were prohibited from travelling through the detour.

President Nyusi and Qatari Emir al-Thani spoke on the phone on 10 June discussing bilateral relations and possible support from Qatar. This comes as the emir also talked about possible joint interests.

The Mozambique government stated that SADC has been given the necessary information to determine what support the bloc can provide to Mozambique against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  This came after the recent completion of a visit to Cabo Delgado by an SADC technical mission.

Mozambique's Ministry of Defense on 11 June issued a statement denying that security forces in Cabo Delgado had used landmines targeting insurgents recently as was reported earlier this week by several sources.  A Defense Ministry spokesman said if these devices are used, this will only be done by the insurgents.  The spokesman also said Mozambique is a signatory to several anti-mine usage agreements.
The UN announced on 11 June 70,000 people have fled Palma district since the attack on Palma town, and that the total number of IDPs in Cabo Delgado is now around 800,000.

South Africa President Cyril Ramaphosa stated that South Africa are monitoring the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado to prevent it from0 spilling over into South Africa. He also said SA must work together with other SADC members to solve the problem of the insurgency.

The World Bank approved a $150 million USD grant to improve incomes and resilience in rural areas as part of the first phase of Mozambique’s Sustainable Rural Economy Program.  The 10-year program is meant to tackle the small agriculture producers and fishers and Small and Medium Enterprises.
The Ministry of Health announced that 76 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 11 June. Maputo City recorded 23 cases, 23 cases were also recorded in Tete, while 15 were recorded in Maputo province.

A Pemba official recently indicated that there has been a significant increase in street children in Pemba on 11 June. As many 67,000 displaced children are in the city. 157,000 IDPs are present in Pemba.

A Catholic NGO stated that about 100 displaced people are arriving daily to Paquitequete Beach, Pemba by sailboat. This comes as IDPs continue to flee the Palma area. The NGO stated that there are displaced individuals who have been stranded at the beach for more than 3 months.

The UN on 11 June said that about 10,000 Mozambican refugees have been forcibly removed from Tanzania back to Mozambique this year. UN stated that Tanzanian authorities either refused entry or transferred the refugees to another border crossing back to Mozambique.  Almost all of these refugees will have been deported in the aftermath of the assault on Palma.

The UNHCR on Friday stated that it is “seriously concerned” about safety of civilians and continued displacement of people in Cabo Delgado, saying the districts of Nangade, Mueda, Montepuez, Ancuabe, Metuge, Balama, Namuno, Chiure, Mecufi, Ibo and Pemba continue to receive new IDPs very day, while many other IDPs flee to Tanzania, only to be deported back into Cabo Delgado.

The Ministry of Health announced that the second phase of vaccinations against COVID was to start on Monday, 14 June. The ministry intends to vaccinate around 23,000 more people among groups now eligible for vaccinations, and will also administer second shots to those who received first doses in the first phase of the campaign.  Health officials say that about 350,000 people have received at least one shot.

Media reports on 11 June indicated that Total had officially reduced much of its Mozambique workforce, with reports that many company employees in Mozambique receiving their last month's salaries in June. This follows the company's declaration of force majeure in April following the assault on Palma.

The Ministry of Health announced that 106 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 12 June. Maputo City recorded 26 cases, Tete Province recorded 42 cases, while 19 cases were recorded in Maputo province. No deaths in patients infected by COVID-19 as the total number of deaths remains at 840. Over the last 24 hours, five people were hospitalized while no recoveries were reported.

The World Food Programme and National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction in Mozambique launched on 12 June a UAV/drone project to support search and rescue operations and emergency preparedness mapping.

Media sources on 13 June reported an ongoing transportation crisis in parts of Maputo, where there are no alternatives to "my loves", open box vehicles that have been officially banned during the pandemic by the government, though many still are in operation in the city.  This reduction in public transport has forced many locals to walk long distances across the capital.

National Institute of Statistics announced on 12 June a general price decline from April to May in Mozambique. The price drop is greatly influenced by falls in price in food and alcoholic beverages with a negative 0.34percent.  For May, Beira registered a drop of about 0.79percent; in Maputo, price declined by 0.20percent; while in Nampula there was a reduction of 0.16percent.

Sources on 14 June reported that Inhambane Government reshuffled its district administrators. The changes include, Azarias Xavier will be transferred from Jangamo to Homoine; Massinga Administrator Jose Jeremiah will be transferred to Jangamo district; Laurina Titosse, leaves Panda to run Massinga district and Elsa Tomo, from Inhambane municipalized district, will be moved to Inharrime.

National Institute of Health (INS) received on 11 June three Polymerase Chain Reaction machines Real-time (PCR), five reagents and 6500 RT-PCR reaction kits for Covid-19 testing, from World Health Organization. The three machines, worth approximately USD150,000,  will help increase the laboratory testing capacity by around 1500 samples a day. The total number of PCR machines donated by WHO to INS is now five.

On 13 June RENAMO leader, Ossufo Momade, accused the Mozambican government for not complying with the agreed process to manage the Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration (DDR) process for former RENAMO guerillas. Momade said that part of the agreement is to train demobilized fighters to be integrated into the police. He urged the international community to put pressure on President Nyusi to follow the agreement.

The Ministry of Health announced that 77 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 13 June. Maputo City recorded 17 cases, Tete Province recorded 35 cases, while 13 cases were recorded in Inhambane province. One patient infected by COVID-19 died as the total number of deaths increased to 841. Over the last 24 hours, three patients have recovered from the virus.

Mozambique will host the SADC Business Forum and Expo on 22-23 June at the AFECC Gloria Hotel and the Joaquim Chissano Conference Centre. The forum, an initiative of both SADC and Mozambican Government, is the largest entrepreneurship, opportunity and investment events in the entire southern African region.

95% of the companies who were closed during the coronavirus pandemic have resumed work, according to the Mozambican government. 52,000 employees have started working again following the re-opening of the companies. Meanwhile, Tete and Cabo Delgado Provinces have the highest number of companies that have yet to restart operations.  In Cabo Delgado, these closures have been related to insecurity, rather than the pandemic.

Sources on 14 June disclosed that Mozambican police arrested two brothers in Mossurize, Manica for beating their 96-yr-old father to death. The suspects confessed to their crime and accused their father of being a witch.

Sources on 14 June disclosed a 96-yr-old man was beaten to death by his two sons in Mossurize, Manica. Security forces arrested the suspects as they attempt to escape after the disposed the victim's body. The suspects confessed to the their crime and accused their father of being a witch.
Mozambican police arrested a young man in possession of a pistol-type firearm in Mossurize, Manica. The suspect allegedly used the weapon to terrorize civilians in the area.

Two Defense and Security Forces (FDS) operatives were killed in a road accident involving two vehicles in Macomia district in the afternoon of 12 June. The victims on a motorbike collided with another vehicle from opposite direction. Witnesses claimed that the accident was caused by a barrier in place along the narrow road.

Locals in Macomia district complained on 14 June over incidents of alleged extortion and abuse by Defense and Security Forces (FDS) members. FDS allegedly targeted people who were returning to the district with extensive questioning and some reported incidents of bribes being demanded.

Maputo Province Governor Julio Parruque warned local youths on 12 June not to be persuaded by insurgent groups and to immediately report to authorities any cases of recruitment or suspicious movement of individuals. Parruque also called for consistent surveillance to forestall insurgent or any illegal activities in the province, despite its distance from Cabo Delgado.

A 40-yr old man attacked his 17-yr-old pregnant wife with a machete  in Mossurize district, Manica, on 08 June. The victim was in critical condition and later transferred the intensive care unit at Chimoio Provincial Hospital. The suspect became violent after the victim received a school uniform and learning material from the government and claimed that the materials came from her lover. The suspect was later arrested by the security forces.
Security forces arrested a 40-yr old man for attacking his 17-yr-old pregnant wife with a machete  in Mossurize district, Manica, on 08 June.

A cashew processing factory in Chiure District on 14 June was reported to have laid off 400 of its 800 employees as cashew supplies to the factory have decreased significantly due to the impact of the insurgency.  The factory had been partially reliant on cashew supplies from Central and Northern Cabo Delgado, and these supplies have been cut off by the insurgency, who in the past have destroyed vehicles carrying the nuts and attacked local warehouses where the cashews are stored.  The factory had previously been supplied with 12-15 tons of nuts per day for processing, and currently only receives between 3-7 tons of nuts per day.  Most of the nuts now supplying the factory come from Chiure District and from Nampula.  Local officials just last week called on the company that owns the factory to keep its workers employed, but the company this week said it could no longer justify these costs.

Portuguese oil and gas company Galp on 14 June told a media outlet that it would not invest in onshore projects in Cabo Delgado until the Maputo government can guarantee "security and social stability".  Galp holds a 10% stake in an Exxon-led consortium in the Rovuma LNG project.  The company's CEO said that it was "very hard" for the company to predict when it could invest in the project due to the security situation, and said it maintains contact with the Mozambican government.  The company also said the government "needs to work with the local population to create the right kind of stability and social cohesion, as well as security, on the ground", also saying "that may take a while".

National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) officers in Nacala District of Nampula on 14 June announced the arrest of a 45 year old man who had been driving a vehicle along the road to Nampula bound for Maputo, transporting 55 kgs of crystal meth.  The arrest took place on Monday just after 0000hrs. The suspect said the drugs were planted in the vehicle and that he was merely transporting furniture.  Police said since January, 561 kgs of drugs have been seized in Nampula, and that drug seizures have been most common in the Nacala area and in the Aiube area of Angoche District.  Police said the drugs were believed to have come from Tanzania, and to have been trafficked by boat to the Nacala area before being loaded onto the truck.

The arrest took place on Monday just after 0000hrs. The suspect said the drugs were planted in the vehicle and that he was merely transporting furniture. Police said the drugs were believed to have come from Tanzania, and to have been trafficked by boat to the Nacala area before being loaded onto the truck.
