The newly appointed Cabo Delgado Secretary of State Supeia stated terrorism will be a main challenge for his administration. Supeia said that his administration will work closely with the North Operational Theater to confront the ongoing insurgency.  Supeia is the single most powerful political figure in Cabo Delgado, and takes over from Armindo Ngunga, who will now head the Northern Integrated Development Agency.
A man was reportedly found murdered and suspected to have had his organs harvested in Maputo City on 13 June. The victim was from Inchope who was looking for a job in Maputo.
The National Human Rights Commission stated that 114 people with albinism have disappeared in Mozambique in past 7 years.  Many are abducted and killed, and are targeted for organ harvesting.

The United Nations called on 11 June on Tanzania authorities once again to stop forced deportations of refugees back into Mozambique. UNHCR spokesman Babar Baloch stated that 9,600 displaced people attempting to seek a refuge in Tanzania have been deported this year so far from TZ back into Mozambique.
LAM Mozambique Airlines plans to sell its Embraer aircraft in a bid to minimize operation costs and standardize its fleet.

First Lady of Mozambique Isaura Nyusi on 12 June stated that there are now more than 1 million children in Mozambique involved in child labour.. Factors that contribute to this figure include natural disasters, the insurgency in Cabo Delgado, other armed attacks and the coronavirus pandemic. Nyusi added that concrete actions will be implemented to lessen the burden experienced by the young workers.

On 11 June, DP World Maputo launched the first container train service connecting Maputo and Harare, Zimbabwe. The new service will give people a faster option in delivery of goods to and from Zimbabwe and will help generate new business opportunities for customers in the two countries.

On 14 June, National Blood Service reported a 23% decrease in the number of blood donors in the first quarter of 2021 against same period in 2020. The decline in numbers was brought by the donors' fear of acquiring COVID-19 infection. Health authorities stated that the equipment used in the blood donation process does not pose a risk of getting the coronavirus.

On 14 June, MISA condemned recent statements from public entities linked to defense forces, saying they were effectively “veiled threats” against journalists. The group claimed that the statements aimed to limit the work of independent media in covering the conflict in several areas, especially in Cabo Delgado, which violates the principle of press freedom.

The Ministry of Health announced that 30 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 14 June.  No patient infected by COVID-19 died with the total number of deaths remains at 841. Over the last 24 hours, eight patients have recovered from the virus while six infected individuals were hospitalized.

Maputo City will immunize over 8,000 people in the second phase of COVID-19 vaccination which started on 14 June. For this second group, the people who will receive the first dose of the vaccine include kindergarten teachers, technical and professional education teachers, higher education and the diplomatic corps. Authorities stated that individuals who will be immunized on 14 June will have their second dose on 05 July.

A sharp increase of COVID-19 new cases were recorded in Mozambique over the weekend. 77 new cases were recorded on 13 June while 106 new cases on 12 June. Data on 12 June was the first time since April 11 that the number of new cases recorded was more than 100 in a 24-hour period. Only one person infected with the virus died during the weekend.

The Ministry of Health is 'on alert' after a 42.8% increase of COVID-19 cases in the country in recent weeks. From 01 to 14 June, 773 new cases of the coronavirus were recorded against 442 cases recorded in the second half of May. Officials stated that the rapid increase of cases suggests that people failed to comply on the safety measures and protocols imposed to prevent spread of the virus.

Internally displaced persons (IDP) stated that Palma district is partially under control of insurgents. Insurgents are able to enter most villages in the district and attack people, carry out kidnappings, and burn peoples houses down. The attacks allegedly have not stopped since the 24 March offensive.

Internally displaced persons (IDP) from Palma stated that thousands of people are still waiting for an opportunity to leave the district and Palma town itself as insurgents control large parts of the district and have effective freedom of movement in much of the district.

Globeleq, Source Energia and Electricidade de Mozambique (EDM) announced on 14 June the start of  the construction on the first IPP in Mozambique to integrate utility-scale energy storage with a solar PV plant in Tetereane, Cuamba City. The 19MWp (15MWac) solar PV plant and 2MW (7MWh) energy storage system, valued at USD 32 million, will provide clean power to over 18,000 households and create job opportunities in Niassa province.

World Food Program on 15 June said it was committed to increase humanitarian assistance to more people in Cabo Delgado Province. The increased level of assistance will be announced following the completion of the assessment visit scheduled to commence today, 15 June, by Executive Director of the World Food Program, David Baesley.  The WFP currently provides assistance to nearly 2 million people across Mozambique, including to around 700,000 displaced by the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

The construction of a commercial building near Beira International Airport has sparked conflict between the  Airports of Mozambique and Beira Government. Airports of Mozambique reportedly approved the said construction without the approval of the local government. According to the deputy minister of Transport and Communications, Manuela Ribeiro, the location of the building interferes the communication for air navigation at the Beira International Airport. The government has reportedly said it will demolish the building as it poses as a danger for air navigation.

World Bank stated that the economy of Mozambique may recover in 2021. However, risk of recession may still occur as the country face several challenges, including terrorist attacks and coronavirus pandemic.

Today, 15 June, Vodacom announced the interruption of its interconnection with TMCel, which is owned by the Mozambican state, due to the latter's outstanding debt to Vodacom.  The interruption will take effect on 0000hrs on 17 June. This development will prevent TMCel users from making calls to Vodacom, however, Vodacom users can continue to make calls to TMCel without interruption. Text messages between the two networks will not be interrupted.  TMCel according to a statement released by Vodacom owes it over 600 meticais or about $10 million.

A report on 15 June revealed that prison guards sexually exploit inmates in the Ndlavela Women's Prison, renting female inmates out to "clients".  Inmates disclosed that they receive cash payment ranging from around 3 to 30 thousand meticais per client. Those who refused to be exploited were allegedly assaulted. Authorities have yet to comment on the report.
Fires were detected around Palma town during the late night hours of 13-14 June.  Two sources reported security forces were allegedly behind this incident, though this is unconfirmed.
LAM flights from Maputo International Airport were delayed on 15 June due to fog. Authorities waited for improved weather before allowing flights to take off.

On the evening of 15 June, sources reported that Vodacom would not go forward with a halting of its interconnection with state-owned TMCel on 17 June after negotiations between the two companies mediated by the National Communications Institute of Mozambique.  Vodacom earlier in the day had announced that it would halt its interconnection with TMCel on Thursday due to 600 million meticais debt owned by TMCel to Vodacom.
RENAMO President Momade called on RENAMO dissident leader Nhongo to join the DDR process in Mocuba on 14 June. Momade has repeatedly appealed to Nhongo to demobilize with his remaining militants.

The Deputy Minister of Justice stated that the Mozambican government would investigate allegations of sexual abuse of female inmates at a jail in Maputo. This comes as the Minister of Justice Kida visited the jail on 16 June. The investigation comes after an NGO reported security guards at the jail were effectively forcing female inmates into prostitution.

The Mozambican National Institute of Social Action (INAS) will start paying another round of subsidies to Idai Cyclone victims in Beira this week. Around 32,000 families will receive these funds. INAS officials said subsidy recipient lists have been posted in neighborhoods with names and instructions on how to claim the subsidies. During August 2020, the first installment of the subsidies was suspended due to the non-compliance of the public, leading to demonstrations in Beira.

Sources stated on 14 June that state oil company ENH's debt has increased by 10 billion meticais ($159 million) during the 2nd quarter of 2020. ENH’s debt reportedly was at 65 billion as of June 2020 and increased to 75 billion upon review of their loans.

Sources stated that the policemen who assaulted a vendor during his arrest recently in Maputo City remain unpunished. A video of this abuse was posted online 2 weeks ago; officials say that a "process" to punish the officer is currently underway.

The Ministry of Health announced 83 new COVID cases and a single related death in the past 24 hours in Mozambique on 14 June. The cases were noted as follows; 35 cases in Tete province, 24 in Maputo City, 10 in Inhambane, 5 in Maputo province, 5 in Nampula, 1 in Gaza, 1 in Niassa, 1 in Zambezia, and 1 in Manica.

The local government reportedly distributed aid in Quissanga District on 12 June, providing 7 tons of aid to 721 displaced people in the Tandanhangue area. Cabo Delgado governor Valige Tauabo, who was at the aid distribution, called on IDPs to stay vigilant and "denounce strange movements" of potential insurgents in the area.

Security forces in coordination with pro-gov militia are conducting operations around Cabo Delgado and are fully in control of Palma town, security forces said on 15 June, also saying they are targeting insurgents in forest areas, though no specific new operations were detailed.

Municipal Passenger Transport Company employees conducted a strike against the limited income generation and unpaid salaries in Inhambane on 14 June. The employees stated that only two buses of the company were currently operating, and 20 employees haver not been paid for five months.

UNOCHA stated that during the month of May, IDPs fleeing from Palma doubled from 31,400 to around 64,000. This comes as most displaced have fled through road and by sea. UN also stated that the even with the ongoing expected harvest the insurgency has affected livelihoods which has caused food insecurity in the province.

UN announced that malaria cases have increased during the first five months of 2021 across Cabo Delgado. Around 343,000 cases and 30 deaths from malaria occurred during January to May of this year, in comparison to the same period last year which saw only 205,000 cases and 15 deaths.
Sources stated that police are targeting prostitutes for bribes in Chimoio province on 15 June.

Speaking from Nampula, the first secretary of FRELIMO in the province stated on 15 June that their party members and supporters were being targeted by insurgents in Cabo Delgado.  First Secretary Luciano de Castro stated that the insurgents beheaded individuals if they say they are members of the FRELIMO party or with the government. He also stated that if they do not know how to speak Arabic they are also killed. There are no reliable numbers as to how many FRELIMO members have been directly targeted in Cabo Delgado for their party membership.

Vodacom has reportedly presented an ultimatum to TMCel to pay a third of their debt (200 million meticais) in cash to avoid an interruption of service by 18 June. TMCel owes 600 million meticais to Vodacom, who initially threatened to stop their service due to the non-payment of their debt.  It is unclear if TMCel has agreed to pay this amount of money by Friday.

Around 10-12 gunmen attacked a pick-up truck transporting an INGO vendor near the Nangororo village, Meluco District, Cabo Delgado in March The vendor was injured, and his driver managed to escape during the attack. The vehicle was reportedly damaged.

Sources stated that cartels smuggling clothing goods are increasingly active along the Zimbabwe – Mozambique border near Mutare area. The smuggling cartels are reportedly bribing security forces and even repair gravel roads to maintain their operation.

Sources stated that smugglers are passing through Magaka area via Burma Valley to Manica province and were reportedly paying off security forces. The smugglers also work in close connection with the locals in both the areas near the Zimbabwe – Mozambique border.

The bishop of Pemba Sandramo stated that families hosting IDPs in Cabo Delgado should be included in aid distribution in talks with the ADIN.  He also said that there should be an "allocation of infrastructure" between IDPs and local residents.

Human Rights Watch (HRW) called on the Mozambican authorities acknowledge that they are holding Rwandan journalist Ntamuhanga Cassien and said that his repatriation would lead to the violation of his rights. HRW also stated that Cassien should have the right to a lawyer and a fair trial.  Cassien was abducted from his home by suspected security officers weeks ago, though Mozambican police deny they are holding him.
Local found a remnant grenade near Casa Branca area in Matola, west of Maputo City on 14 June. The grenade was later covered a tire after its discovery.

Five suspected insurgents were arrested in Machova, just southeast of Macomia town in early June.  The five suspects told locals they were travelling to Pemba and had come from Mucojo, where they had fled from an insurgent camp.  Locals were suspicious of the group, who asked for information regarding the best way to get to Pemba, which is a well-known route.  Locals reportedly seized the group and turned them into a local police station.

Police deployed to the White House area of Matola on the afternoon of 16 June and detonated a grenade in the area.  Locals reported the grenade, which was discovered along an area road, on Monday, but security forces did respond to the incident until Wednesday.
Insurgents in attacks on Litamanda and Chai villages north of Macomia town on the night of 15 June reportedly beheaded 6 people.  No further details on this attack are currently available.
Insurgents in attacks on Litamanda and Chai villages north of Macomia town on the night of 15 June reportedly beheaded 6 people.  No further details on this attack are currently available.

South African Airline Airlink will begin new flights between Kruger airport and Vilanculos Airport in Mozambique starting 2 July. The flights will operate on Mondays and Fridays, with additional options for tourism activities, such as safari and beach holidays.

South Africa has recorded 13,246 COVID cases in the past 24 hours authorities said on 16 June. This is the highest number of daily cases in SA since January, and raises the threat of the spread of a third wave into Mozambique.

Luxembourg officials on 10 June expressed willingness to deploy Luxembourgish troops to Mozambique as part of an EU training mission to the country.  The move is opposed by leftist parties in the country.

Local sources stated that the contractor set to work on the water supply system in Mocubela district of Zambezia “abandoned” the project without explanation. The construction was scheduled 7 January, 2019 with the deadline set for January 6, 2020. The work reportedly stopped halfway and the district director stated that the contractor already has received 50% of the funds.

Local residents recently have complained of poor road conditions in different areas of Cabo Delgado, with "huge" potholes worsened by the recent rainy season.  The road from Pemba to Montepuez is one of the roads most significantly affected.

Local residents recently have complained of poor road conditions in different areas of Cabo Delgado, with "huge" potholes worsened by the recent rainy season.  The road from Pemba to Chiure is one of the roads most significantly affected.

A new UN report issued on 16 June indicated that there is no direct connection between the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) and ISIS in Congo.  The report indicated that the ADF has benefited from a media relationship with ISIS, but that ISIS is not controlling/commanding the ADF in Congo and is not providing other direct support to the group.  The ADF is sometimes identified as the Islamic State Central Africa Province (ISCAP), the same franchise of the group which claims attacks in Cabo Delgado linked with the insurgency.

Mozambican Defense Minister Jaime Neto stated that the instability caused by the insurgency in Cabo Delgado is “under control”, particularly in Palma. Neto also indicated that the US, Portugal, and other SADC countries are providing support for the Mozambican military in its fight against the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

Municipal Passenger Transport Company bus drivers continued their strike in Inhambane on 16 June over unpaid salaries.  Many local civilians say they are "suffering" due to a lack of transport because of the strike in the city.

The Ministry of Health announced 113 new COVID cases and two deaths during the past 24 hours in Mozambique on 16 June. 66 cases were recorded in Tete province, 30 in Maputo City, 10 in Cabo Delgado, 3 in Maputo province, 2 in Inhambane, 1 in Gaza, and 1 in Sofala.

Security sources reportedly remain concerned regarding insurgents attempting to infiltrate among IDPs in different areas of Cabo Delgado, and security forces continue to heavily vet IDPs arriving into Pemba and other areas.

The Mozambican government will conduct an investigation of all prison facilities across Mozambique after reports of sexual exploitation scheme at Ndlavela prison. Minister of Justice Helena Kida previously conducted a visit to the prison after a report indicating that prison guards were sexually abusing inmates.

Health Minister Armindo Tiago on 16 June stated that Mozambique should be prepped for a “worst case scenario” of a third wave of COVID in the country. Tiago stated that the general public should continue to adhere to the prevention measures which are still the most effective tool against the pandemic.

Insurgents reportedly beheaded four displaced individuals during an ambush outside of Quitunda after a group of 15 individuals left from the Quitunda Resettlement Village on the afternoon of 13 June. The group was made up of armed men (with machetes, spears, and blunt weapons), mostly farmers and fishermen, to look for food.  Militants reportedly fired shots in the air, causing the group to disperse, after which insurgents captured 4 people who were then beheaded. Locals in the area claimed that insurgents set up an HQ near the former Anadarko Camp, between Palma and Quionga Administrative Post.
Locals fleeing from the Palma area reported in mid-June that insurgents have set up a camp near a former Anadarko camp north of Palma along the road to Quionga.

165 new COVID cases were reported on 17 June in Mozambique, including 49 cases in Maputo City, 45 in Tete, 28 in Maputo, 22 in Niassa, 9 in Sofala, 5 in Manica, 3 in Cabo Delgado, 3 in Inhambane, and 1 in Nampula.  There are currently 1,053 active cases in the country, including 515 active cases in Maputo City.  This is the highest number of cases in a single day in Mozambique since 11 April, when 180 cases were reported.

The Attorney General's Office (PGR) accused traditional healers of human and organ trafficking around Mozambique on 17 June. PGR officials stated that traditional healers often use body parts in their practices and that trafficking is a profitable illegal business. PGR stated that during 2020 six cases were registered, including two of which were human trafficking, one for labor and another for sex trafficking.

Gaza Infrastructure Services Director Alberto Matusse stated that 18 million meticais is required to compensate families who were displaced by the construction Chongoene airport. The families in the area were reportedly farmers and livestock owners prior to the construction of the airport.
Police deployed to prevent the presentation of a petition against the placed toll gates in Maputo on 17 June. Civil activists stated that illegal toll gates were placed along the ring road in Maputo.

The Minister of Justice Helena Kida issued a directive suspending all prison management at Ndhlavela prison on 17 June. This follows the minister’s visit to the prison to investigate the allegations of the prison management abusing female inmates.
Motorcycle taxis drivers have recently complained regarding the lack of police protection in Nampula. The drivers stated that they are being targeted by criminals on a daily basis in the province.

The National Migration Service (SENAMI) announced that mobile migration services will be able to issue passports at border posts in Maputo province. National citizens are required an national ID card or photocopy, a previous passport, and 2,400 meticais for processing.

Subcontractors remain unable to pay workers who were employed at Afungi LNG Camp due to the delay in payments by Total and other subcontractors. The Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA) stated that an oil and gas company has outstanding fee of 18 million USD. CTA also mentioned that out of the 28 contracts under the oil and gas company, 15 are directly contracted and 13 are subcontractors which have confirmed late payments.

The National Institute of Statistics (INE) and the World Bank warned that the quality of education has been badly affected by COVID in Mozambique. A COVID impact survey was conducted to determine the effects of the pandemic. The survey stated that only at least 50% of the students were able to engage in distant learning activities.
Suspected gunfire exchanges were reported between security forces and insurgents in Palma on 15 June. Fires near the beach area of the town were also reported.  This report is currently unverified.
A fire reportedly broke out north of Palma town on the evening of 14 June. No further details were mentioned regarding the incident, though it may be related to insurgent activity in the town.

The Minister of Justice Kida stated that there have been no previous complaints about sexual exploitation of inmates at prison before the current scandal.. Kida stated that no previous cases have been filed from the accused or the convicted.

The National Health Institute (INS) Deputy Director announced that increased “urban mobility” could possibly trigger an increase in COVID cases across Mozambique. Deputy Director Gudo stated that the more people are spending less time at home recently, and that this could increase possible COVID cases in the country. Gudo also said that this creates the conditions for the third COVID wave.

Sources reported of fires breaking out near Qurinde on night of 16 June. This comes as another fire was reported in the south of Palma.  These could be related to potential insurgent activity, though this is unconfirmed.

Sources reported of fires breaking out near Qurinde on night of 16 June. This comes as another fire was reported in the south of Palma.  These could be related to potential insurgent activity, though this is unconfirmed.

Border officials announced that operating timings at Ressano Garcia Border Post would be adjusted starting 16 June from 06:00 to 21:00. The adjustments were due to the new COVID restrictions in South Africa. South Africa has adjusted its curfew from 22:00 to 04:00. The timing changes are only limited to civilians. Cargos and shipments will continue from 06:00 to 23:00.

Health officials announced that more young people are getting infected with COVID in recent weeks.  Hospital officials stated that individuals most ages between Health officials say there has been a rise since late April in severe COVID cases of individuals aged 30 to 45 years.

Suspected armed men attacked a vehicle belonging to international football player Reinildo Mandava along N1 Road near Nicuadala, north of Quelimane, on the evening of 17 June. No casualties were reported. Police stated that ballistic teams were still determining if Mandava’s vehicle was struck with bullets or stones as the area is known for armed robbers targeting vehicles, though several sources indicated   The assailants reportedly began following Mandava in Caia in Sofala as he passed through the area.  Sources stated that Mandava was travelling to Nampula city to attend a wedding when the attack occurred. Mandava reportedly traveled to Locality de Zero police station for assistance.

Fires reported on the night of 15 June in Namau, east of Imbunho, north of Nido, and north of Quintoazi on the evening of 15 June. Insurgents are known to be present in these areas, and these fires may indicate insurgent activity, though this is unconfirmed.

Fires reported on the night of 15 June in Namau, east of Imbunho, north of Nido, and north of Quintoazi on the evening of 15 June. Insurgents are known to be present in these areas, and these fires may indicate insurgent activity, though this is unconfirmed.

The German government is donating 63 million EUR to Mozambique for development projects. 33 million EUR will go towards the funding of the education, technical and vocational sector. 15 million EUR each is to be allocated for the rehabilitation of the municipal structures in Sofala and the energy sector.
Sources on 17 June reported that insurgents currently maintain a significant camp near between Mucojo and Pangane along coastal Macomia district.
Sources on 17 June reported that insurgents currently maintain a significant camp near Quiterajo, along the Messalo River.

Three SERNIC agents and two Indian-Mozambican nationals who were members of a kidnap gang were reportedly arrested on Thursday in Maputo City in the Bairro das Mahotas area.  Security forces also rescued an Indian businessman who had reportedly been kidnapped Monday by the group.  Unconfirmed reports said police attempted to suppress reports of the incident because of the involvement of three security force members in this kidnapping.  Note this kidnapping was not previously reported.

A kidnap gang on 14 June was reported to have abducted an Indian businessman in Maputo City.  3 SERNIC agents were part of this 5 man gang.  The gang were arrested and the businessman freed on 17 June in Maputo City.  The 5 demanded a $600,000 dollar ransom for the victim.

194 new COVID cases were reported on 18 June in Mozambique, including 65 new cases in Maputo City and 59 new cases in Tete.  There are currently 40 people hospitalized in the country, and 1,245 active cases in the country.  No new deaths were reported in the country.

Armed criminals were reported to have begun following football player Reinildo Mandava in Caia of Sofala province after passing through the area; they would later attack Mandava's vehicle in Zambezia.

ENI started that they were on track regarding the Coral South offshore project in Mozambique for 2022 regardless of ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado. The project is expected to produce 3.4 million mt per year once completed.

The Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA) announced that no minimum wage increase is expected for foreseeable future. CTA spokesman stated that companies were having difficulties and negotiating a wage increase is unlikely. Trade unions meanwhile have been calling for an increase in the minimum wage.  Disputes over the minimum wage could eventually lead to civil unrest in Maputo and other cities.

The President of the Municipal Council of Nampula stated that the Nampula government not received the Municipal Initiative Investment funds for 6 months. President Vahanle stated that the non-transfer of the funds has negatively affected the financing of activities and proposed projects in the city.  The Maputo government is meant to distribute these funds.

RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade on 18 June renewed accusations against the government for not complying with DDR agreement. Momade also said that the current conditions are poor in Morrumbala. Momade previously raised the issue saying RENAMO militia members had not been integrated with the government security forces.

Cement companies on 18 June called on government to increase the price of cement claiming that the current prices are too low to turn a profit. A Chinese owned company is reportedly able to sell cement at low prices, while local companies say they are unable to do so.

Oil and gas company Total reduced staff on 11 June by 200 in Mozambique, leaving about 400 employees for the company in the country.  This reduction in staff is an indicator that the company will look to continue to operate with a minimal work force for an extended period of time, and the resumption of work at the LNG Afungi site before the end of the year is increasingly unlikely.

The World Health Organization (WHO) stated on 18 June that a third wave of COVID-19 cases is being experienced across Africa. WHO also called for the need of additional vaccine doses as seven African countries have run out of supply.

Security forces are currently conducting a search for importers of “al Shabaab” razors in Maputo City and Manica.  It is unclear who is importing these razors, though they have drawn concern as they bear the same name as the Cabo Delgado insurgents.  Arrests of some of those selling the razors was made in Maputo City on 16 June.

Security forces are currently conducting a search for importers of “al Shabaab” razors in Maputo City and Manica.  It is unclear who is importing these razors, though they have drawn concern as they bear the same name as the Cabo Delgado insurgents.  Arrests of those selling the razors were made in early June in Manica.

International Organization for Migration issued a report on 8 June saying IDPs continue to arrive in Matemo island, displaced from Palma district and other parts of Cabo Delgado.  There are currently over 31,000 displaced persons in Ibo District.
Authorities stated that there has been a notable increase in child marriage incidents in Quirambo Island as IDPs continue to arrive in the area.

Health authorities declared the end of the cholera outbreak in Cabo Delgado on 18 June. Officials have called on locals to observe proper hygiene to prevent new cases. Around 6,000 individuals were infected and 54 deaths were reported since February 2020 as part of this cholera outbreak.   Macomia and Ibo were worst effected by the cholera outbreak.

The administrator of Mossurize district is charged with corruption by local media. District administrator Fernando Samuel has been accused of charging 500 to 1000 meticais individuals claiming that it was for the rehabilitation of the local FRELIMO HQ.
The Mozambique government issued 6 days of national mourning for former Zambia President Kenneth Kaunda on 18 June.

Unconfirmed reports stated that President Nyusi asked for military support from Zimbabwe during an early June visit to the country.  Nyusi was allegedly encouraged to speak with the Zimbabwean government by France.  This reportedly was a request for bilateral support, rather than through the SADC.  This comes after other recent reports that France had attempted to support an initiative in which Rwanda would provide on the ground troop support to Mozambique in Cabo Delgado.

Sources stated that Vodacom has given TMCel to pay the 200 million meticais, a third of TMCel's debt to Vodacom.  TMCel had offered to pay this sum within 90 days. This comes after Vodacom Mozambique last week threatened to halt interconnections with TMCel over this unpaid debt.  It is unclear at this time if TMCel agreed to the 10 day payment period.
The Catholic University of Mozambique issued a report on 18 June that police are reportedly extorting IDPs for money due to their lack of identification documents in Pemba and Metuge.

UN Resident Coordinator Kaulard stated that the humanitarian crisis in Cabo Delgado will not end quickly, and said that there is an urgent need for increased support for the UN and its partners in Cabo Delgado.

The Ministry of Health extended the second phase of vaccination by one day against COVID-19 in some areas of Maputo City on 19 June. Authorities earlier scheduled 18 June as the last day for the second phase of vaccination against COVID-19 in the country. In 1 Junho Health Center, only 17 people showed up in the morning while over 30 people had been vaccinated in the morning at Mavalane General Hospital.

Air France commenced flights to Maputo on 20 June. The route will be an extension of the flight between Johannesburg and Paris as announced mid-April. It is operated with Boeing 777-300ER aircraft with remodeled cabins.

On 20 June, the Ministry of Health announced the administration of the second dose of the Covishield vaccine from 21 June to 2 July. The vaccination will cover 240,913 people across the country who received the first dose of the vaccine from 19 April to 15 May.

Two suspects assaulted a 16-yrold female student with a machete while on her way to school Mossurize, Manica on 08 June. Doctors claimed that the victim needs more specialized care and psychosocial support after the attack. Security forces arrested the suspects on 20 June.
Security forces arrested two suspects in Mossurize, Manica on 20 June in connection with the assault of a 16-yr old female student. The assault happened on 08 June.

On 21 June, Mozambique started the second phase of its National Vaccination Campaign, which aims to vaccinate about 250,000 individuals with the Oxford/AstraZeneca vaccine. This second phase, which ends on 2 July, targets final-year students in Health training course, patients with diabetes mellitus, those with respiratory and heart failure, people aged 51 years old and above living in accommodation centers, inmates and prison officers, agents of the Police of the Republic of Mozambique aged 51 years old and above, primary school teachers aged 51 years old and above, and journalists.

The Southern African Development Community (SADC) will hold an Extraordinary Summit of Heads of State and Government in Maputo, Mozambique's capital, on 23 June. The purpose of the meeting is to discuss the issues of cooperation and development in the region, efforts to support Mozambique in combating terrorism, food security in the region, gender and development, and the progress on the efforts to manage HIV and AIDS cases and the Covid-19 pandemic situation in the region. The meeting will also review the progress of the initiatives implemented under the 40th SADC theme: 40 Years Building Peace and Security and Promoting Development in the Face of Global Challenges.  The most pressing of these issues and the primary reason for the meeting is to discuss potential SADC support for Mozambique in the Cabo Delgado insurgency.
One person was killed and 4 others injured after their vehicle crashed on a protection barrier of the lampposts on the ring road in Albazine area of Maputo city on the afternoon of 20 June.

The Minister of Health, Armindo Tiago, confirmed on the morning of 21 June that the Delta/Indian variant of Covid-19 has been detected in Tete province. The minister emphasized the variant's high level of transmissibility and called for intensified prevention measures in the province.  Tete for the past week has seen higher numbers of cases of COVID-19 than in any other part of the country.
The Provincial Commander of the PRM in Manica, Francisco Simoes, was killed after his vehicle collided with a truck in Gondola District on the evening of 20 June.

Pro-government sources claimed that soldiers ambushed a group of insurgents in Novo Cabo Delgado village on 19 June, north of Macomia, killing 5 insurgents and injuring three others, who escaped after the clash.  Six weapons were also recovered from the dead insurgents after the clash. Pro-government militia were also reportedly involved in the fighting.  Conflicting reports indicated that 8 bodies had been discovered in Novo Cabo Delgado on 18 June.

A RENAMO dissident, Celestino Mathumba, who identified himself as a "general" within the group, on 20 June was reported to have defected from the RENAMO Military Junta and joined the DDR Process. Mathumba had been based in the Mavate area and said he was "tired of suffering" in the bush and called on other dissidents to leave the group and join the DDR Process. Mathumba also said the population in Manica "doesn't want us anymore" which had factored into why he defected from the group.

RENAMO on 21 June announced a halt to the DDR process in Tete over the failure by the government and police force/military to integrate RENAMO militia members into the security forces.  The DDR process was next set to go forward in Tete in the coming weeks, with hundreds more RENAMO militia members to be demobilized. This comes after RENAMO's leader Ossufo Momade had complained publicly on several occasions that the government was not allocating enough funding to the DDR Process, and also said that RENAMO militia members selected by the party were not being integrated into the police as agreed in the new 2019 peace deal.  Throughout the DDR process, RENAMO party officials and individual RENAMO members have said the process was not be fully adhered to by the FRELIMO-led government.  This suspension of the DDR process in Tete is the most significant set back in the demobilization process which was restarted in 2019, and could lead to another indefinite delay in the wider project of demobilizing all RENAMO armed members, which had been meant to conclude in 2021.

An NGO, Observatorio do Meio Rural (OMR), says that insurgents are kidnapping large numbers of children and pre-teenagers, from age 12-yrs-old and up, in Cabo Delgado to serve insurgency.   This matches other reports post Palma assault that have indicated insurgents are increasingly targeting children for forced recruitment.  The most recent mass kidnapping incidents occurred during and after the assault on Palma, as insurgents have continually targeted IDPs fleeing the attack.

Around 0100hrs on 20 June, a Mozambican Police officer was shot by a colleague three times in the vicinity of Provincial Civil Identification Services, Inhambane. Reports suggest that the injured officer was not identified by his colleague as he was wearing civilian clothes in an area with no electricity. An investigation into the incident has been launched.

140 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 20 June, with one new death also reported.  35 of the new cases were from Maputo city, 31 from Maputo province, 23 from Sofala and 21 from Tete, 11 cases were reported from Inhambane, nine from Manica, eight from Nampula and two from Niassa. Over the last 24 hours, eight people, all from Inhambane, were declared as fully recovered from the coronavirus.
The strike of municipal transport company workers continues in Inhambane City for an 8th day on 21 June. The company's workers are on strike due to late payment of wages for five months.

70 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 21 June, while no deaths related to the virus was recorded. 31 of the new cases were from Maputo city, 13 from Maputo province, 11 from Manica, 5 in Inhambane, 5 in Nampula, 3 in Gaza, 1 each in Tete and Sofala. Over the last 24 hours, 192 patients, including three foreign nationals, have recovered from the virus.

The Judicial Court of Quelimane found Quelimane Mayor Manuel de Araujo innocent for libel and defamation charges on 21 June. The charges were filed in 2019 by two members of the Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM) who Araujo claimed to be responsible if he will be murdered.

SADC Humanitarian and Emergency Operations Centre in Nacala was officially opened on 21 June to coordinate support for disaster preparedness, response & recovery efforts in the SADC Member States. Mozambican President and Acting President of the SADC, Filipe Nyusi, and the President of Botswana and Acting President of the SADC Organ for Cooperation in the Areas of Politics, Defence and Security, Mokgweetsi Masisi, attended the event.   The opening of this center comes after Mozambique since 2019 has been impacted by 3 cyclones.

Mozambique hosts about 27,000 refugees and asylum seekers who mostly from the Democratic Republic of Congo, Burundi, Rwanda and Somalia. These people were forces to flee from their countries due to conflicts, violence, persecution and human rights violations in their countries.

A National Service of Criminal Investigation (SERNIC) vehicle was involved in an accident in Malhangalene, Maputo City in the morning of 19 June. The driver fled the scene of the accident, leaving alcoholic beverages inside the vehicle.

On 21 June, was reported to have Total declared force majeure on more contracts of its LNG project in Cabo Delgado following the March 24 Palma insurgent attack. Details on these affected contracts were not disclosed, but this corresponds with reports that Total had let go of more local staff early in June in Mozambique and almost certainly does not plan to restart operations at the Afungi LNG Camp this year.

United States announced that it has granted USD30 million to the UN World Food Programme (WFP) to address food insecurity in communities affected by insurgency in Cabo Delgado and those affected by natural calamities and RENAMO dissident attacks in the central provinces of Sofala and Manica.

The support is part of more than $91 million donated by the US government for countries in Africa to combat the pandemic.

Sources claimed that FDS started shooting in the area and seized mobile phones and other goods believed to be owned by insurgents.

Mphanda Nkuwa hydropower dam director Carlos Yum stated on 15 June that Mozambique aims to sell a majority stake of the planned $2.4 billion hydropower project. The dam, which will be the largest across southern Africa, has the capacity to generate 2,075 megawatts of power mostly sold to South Africa. Authorities will  take up to four months to select the stakeholder and another six weeks to negotiate the joint development agreement.

The United Arab Emirates and Mozambique virtually discussed ways to ramp up cooperation and exchange information related to operations targeting transnational organized crime on 22 June. Best practices and projects were presented to enhance ways for effective crime prevention.

Deputy director of the National Health Institute (INS), Eduardo Samo Gudo, warned on 20 June citizens of Tete Province that COVID-cases may continue to increase over the next two weeks if they continue to disregard safety protocols. On 19 June, 116 out of 244 new cases were from Tete, while on 20 June, 20 out of the 140 new cases were from the aforementioned province.  The new Delta variant of COVID-19 has also recently been detected in Tete.

A consulting firm said on 18 June that it anticipates that Mozambique's inflation could rise to 5.3 percent this year versus 3.1 in 2020 due to the effect of coronavirus pandemic and a fuel price increase.

WHO on 21 June was reported to be setting up a hub in South Africa to provide companies from poor and middle-income countries the training and licenses to produce COVID-19 vaccines. The hub will likely to directly benefit Mozambique. Two companies had signed up to participate and are currently in talks with Pfizer and Moderna.

The rise of the pandemic is attributed to the non-compliance of the safety protocols imposed by the authorities.  There have been 1,463 new COVID cases in Mozambique in the past two weeks, compared to just 524 COVID cases in the two weeks prior.

Tanzania President Samia Suluhu Hassan, Zimbabwe President Emmerson Mnangagwa, and South Africa President Cyril Ramaphosa in Maputo, Mozambique on 23 June for a two-day State visit. An interruption of the Mozambican Social Security Information System, managed by the INSS, is scheduled to start around 1900hrs on 25 June until 27 June for maintenance work. The planned interruption aims to improve its technological systems as well as improvement of services provided to system users.

Mozambican Customs officials in Nacala Port on 22 June thwarted an attempt to illegally export four containers of illegally logged unprocessed logs to China. Reports suggest that the wood came from trees in Zambezia province and owned by an exporter named Bajone.

Cross border importers in Mozambique have expressed concerns in recent days as there was a reduction in the supply of essential products in South Africa due to the latter's tightening of COVID-19 restrictions.

South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa attended the summit in Maputo city on 23 June amid questions regarding the viability of SA's ability to launch an intervention in Cabo Delgado after the Minister of Defence and Military Veterans Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula announced that her department, the South African National Defence Force (SANDF), is having its budget cut by 15-billion Rand.

Mozambican Government will acquire a tracking technology that will allow security forces to track kidnappers and kidnapping victims. The said technology will arrive in the country within the next few days. The system will notify an operations center, through radio frequency, about the existence of any signal blocker called 'jammer' frequently used by certain criminals to make it difficult to track their vehicles which are often used in kidnap cases.

Experts warn that global warming threatens coastal cities, including the cities of Mozambique, across the world. Rising sea levels may contaminate agricultural soils with salt water and engulf strategic infrastructure such as ports or airports. In addition, floods and heat waves are becoming more frequent and intense, and warming increases ocean acidity.

President Nyusi stated on 23 June that the Southern African Development Community (SADC) should be the country's main partner in counter-insurgency operations in Cabo Delgado. The statement was made during the Extraordinary Summit of SADC Heads of State and Government in Maputo City. He added that the insurgency is a regional threat and it would require unity and solidarity between countries.  President Nyusi also expressed concerns with climate change that lead to water scarcity, extinction of forms of life, food shortages, displacement of families due to droughts and floods, tropical cyclones, and other phenomena.

Tanzania President Samia Suluhu Hassan arrived to participate in the SADC Summit today. Hassan's attendance in person was notable as Tanzania at other recent summits had sent ministers in the president's place, and could indicate a new willingness from Dodoma to coordinate a counter-insurgency response with Mozambique. Tanzania's cooperation in fighting insurgency is vital for Mozambique as the country shares a border with Cabo Delgado. However,  Tanzania previously has viewed the insurgency in Cabo Delgado as an internal Mozambican problem, despite the insurgency's known links to cells in Tanzania and attacks late last year on several Tanzanian border towns.  The UN on 11 June said that about 10,000 Mozambican refugees have been forcibly removed from Tanzania back to Mozambique this year.

On 23 June, the SADC's Extraordinary Summit of Heads of State issued a communique saying the summit had "endorsed the recommendations of the Chairperson of the Organ on Politics, Defense, and Security Cooperation and approved the Mandate for the SADC Standby Force Mission to the Republic of Mozambique, to be deployed under the SADC Standby Force in support of Mozambique to combat of terrorism and acts of violent extremism in Cabo Delgado".  The communique did not provide further details regarding this force.  The report referred to by the SADC communique had recommended the deployment of a 3,000 man force to Cabo Delgado to combat the ongoing insurgency.

Sources on 23 June reported that a Mi18 helicopter had been shot down or damaged between Palma and Afungi area, though this report is currently unconfirmed; one report said the helicopter had been forced to land in the area due to a technical difficulty.  Sources later indicated the helicopter was not shot down but had experiences a technical failure, though other sources continued to say that insurgents had hit the helicopter with small arms fire.  Sources later agreed the helicopter was not shot down, though was reportedly targeted by insurgents.

Clashes were reported between security forces and insurgents in Olumbe on 21-23 June. No other details on this incident are currently available.  Other sources later indicated insurgents had attacked the area on 24 June, and set fire to homes in the town.
Clashes were reported between security forces and insurgents in Olumbe on 21-23 June. Other sources reported security forces had attacked insurgent positions outside of Olumbe on 22 June.

Around 500 new displaced people from Palma arrived in Paquitequete beach over a 48 hour period between 21-23 June. IDPs fled from the area due to continuing insurgent attacks.
An IDP claimed that his family members were abducted by armed men in Palma on recently. Among the victims were his five children.  The man then fled Palma.

IDPs recently arrived to Pemba who fled from Palma said there are still thousands of displaced people in the Quitunda area, and cannot leave the area as they cannot afford to pay for boat fare to escape.

IDPs recently arrived to Pemba who fled from Palma said militants in Palma district carry out regular beheadings and shootings, as well as kidnappings across much of the district, forcing many district villages to be abandoned.
On 16 June insurgents reportedly entered southern part of Palma and spoke with the locals, telling locals that the militants care about civilians more than President Nyusi.

A source in Manica on 23 June disclosed that many retired Mozambican soldiers have not received allowances after serving the military for 11 years, and  may be open to support the RENAMO dissidents if given a significant salary.
Two unexplained fire incidents were reported on 20 June in Mocímboa da Praia. The cause of the fires is still unknown but could be linked to clashes in the area or a terror-related incident.

The Mozambican government on 23 June said that O&G major Total will assume responsibilities to companies contracted to the suspended Afungi LNG project in terms of outstanding payments owed. However, the process may take some time as the there are hundred of contractors involved in the said project.  Over $18 million are still owed to these companies.

Portugal’s foreign minister Augusto Santos Silva said on 23 June that the EU military training mission to Mozambique could be approved during the next meeting of EU foreign ministers scheduled for July 12. Portugal has already sent 60 soldiers to Mozambique to train soldiers.  Other European powers are expected to contribute to a potential military training mission to Mozambique.

Mozambican Workers Organization (OTM) on 23 June accused employers of avoiding discussion about wage increases. The union group stated that the companies are using the pandemic as an excuse to dismiss discussions on a wage increase which began 18 March last year. It is recalled that the Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA) announced last week that no minimum wage increase is expected for foreseeable future. CTA spokesman stated that companies were having difficulties and negotiating a wage increase is unlikely.  This disagreement could eventually trigger protests.

Vodacom on 23 June indicated it would continue to press TMCel for its 600 million meticais debt, also saying that TMCel originally owned 900 million meticais before Vodacom agreed to reduce this amount by 1/3rd. The company added that it will “do its best” not to impact customers as this dispute continues; connections to TMCel will not be interrupted however, some other services could be interrupted in the near future if a payment agreement cannot be reached.

A meeting on the DDR process between RENAMO Leader Momade and President Nyusi was held on 22 June. Both sides agreed to start integration of RENAMO combatants into police force however it was not clear if DDR in Tete will go forward as scheduled.  On 21 June, RENAMO had announced a halt to the DDR process in Tete over the failure by the government to integrate RENAMO militia members into the security forces.

On 23 June, South Korea announced an additional donation of USD 7 million to the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), to help improve the quality of education in the provinces of Zambezia and Nampula. The fund will be used to improve the skills of 1,400 teachers and school heads, provide access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services to over 17,500 pupils.

The US on 23 June announced a USD 19.35 million five-year program, USAID Local Governance Strengthening (USAID LOGOS) to strengthen local governments in  Cabo Delgado, Nampula, and Zambezia. The program will provide technical assistance, training, and support to strengthen economic governance and improve local capacity to deliver primary health, education, and water and sanitation services.

On 23 June, the Bank of Mozambique suspended Standard Bank from the Interbank Foreign Exchange Market (MCI) effective immediately. A source from Standard Bank confirmed the suspension but did not disclose further details regarding this development.  One source said this may indicate the bank faces liquidity problems, though this is unconfirmed.

TMCel Chairman Mohamed Rafique Jussob stated on 24 June that they will settle 200 million meticais out of the 600 million meticais debt to Vodacom within the next three months. After the said period, Jussob said that they will pay the current and accumulated debt, on an average of 12 million meticais monthly starting in June.

RENAMO Ossufo Momade on 24 June publicly questioned the silence of President Nyusi regarding his alleged involvement in the country's hidden debts case. Momade claimed that the president and its party, FRELIMO had received USD 1 million and USD 10 million respectively as part of this scandal.

Mozambican Police arrested two individuals in Albazine, Maputo City on 24 June over alleged falsification of identity cards, driving licenses, booklets, among others. Operational equipment including four desktop computers, a printer and a photocopier were recovered.

President Nyusi in an address to the nation on 24 June announced that Mozambique was in the midst of a third wave of COVID cases, and that the government would extend all anti-COVID measures for another 30 days, while some measures were modified  All measures will come into effect at 0000hrs on 26 June. These measures include: The extension of the curfew from 2200hrs to 0400hrs nightly; the curfew had been running from 2300hrs to 0400hrs.The curfew has been maintained in all cities and towns it was previously in place in, and has been extended to Gurue Town. The issuance of documents from public institutions will now be done by appointment only. The closure of all beaches for "leisure activities”. Religious events, conferences, and meetings should only be held at 40% capacity; open space events can include up to 80 people. Restaurants may operate from 0600hrs to 2000hrs.Bottle stores may operate from 0900hrs to 1500hrs Monday-Saturday, while remaining closed on Sundays. Theatres, cultural centers, and auditoriums must close down or remain closed unless granted special permission from the government. Shopping centers may operate Monday - Saturday from 0900hrs - 1800hrs, and on Sunday from 0900hrs - 1500hrs. This announcement comes amid a significant COVID spike in the country, which has seen two 400+ case days in the past 48 hours, after no such days for over 3 months.

Rwandan Defense Force spokesman Ronald Rwivanga said on 24 June in a media interview that Rwanda had "plans to deploy" forces to Mozambique though these plans have not yet been finalized.  A deployment of Rwandan forces would reportedly assist Mozambican forces in Cabo Delgado in combating the insurgency.  No details regarding what this deployment could entail are currently available. This interview came a day after the Southern African Development Community (SADC) approved a proposal to deploy its Standby Force to Cabo Delgado.  President Nyusi had previously visited Rwanda for talks with the country's President, Paul Kagame, in April.  The SADC meanwhile said it had not been informed by Mozambique of any Rwandan intervention in Mozambique.

441 new COVID cases were recorded in Mozambique on 24 June, with 5 new COVID deaths.  This includes 161 new cases in Maputo City, 130 in Tete, 98 in Maputo, 37 in Sofala, 7 in Manica, 4 in Gaza, 3 in Nampula, and 1 in Cabo Delgado.  There are now 2,433 actives cases in the country.  This is the highest number of cases recorded in Tete during the ongoing third COVID case wave.

Maputo residents are reportedly not following COVID restrictions in parts of the capital. Locals have also argued against the precautions recently announced by the Mozambique president; the ignoring of these restrictions is likely contributing to the current new wave of COVID cases in the country.

A police directive issued on 22 June directed police to seize “al Shabab” razors that have recently circulated in parts of the country. The razors were considered to be a means of propaganda by the insurgent group.

RENAMO President Momade issued an “address to the nation” on 24 June, stated that RENAMO supporters are still faced with a “climate of intimidation and threat” despite peace agreements between FRELIMO and RENAMO.  Momade accused FRELIMO of manipulating electoral results and leading the country by with poor policies, corruption, bias within the government, political intolerance against opposition, self-protection, social exclusion, and systematic attack on the collective reconciliation efforts.

Police shot and injured a civilian with small arms fire during the arrest of several suspects for drug crimes in Mafalala, south Maputo City, early morning of 24 June. The victim was reportedly not a resident in the area and was on a truck during the incident.  The woman wounded in the incident was struck in the abdomen, and is reportedly in critical condition.

Police shot and injured a civilian with small arms fire during the arrest of several suspects for drug crimes in Mafalala, south Maputo City, early morning of 24 June. The victim was reportedly not a resident in the area and was on a truck during the incident.

Security forces stated that insurgents attacked Palma town on 21 and 22 June, clashing with security forces.  On 22 June, sources reported clashes near Quitunda between insurgents and security forces, forcing many to flee the area.
Security forces stated that insurgents attacked Palma town on 21 and 22 June, clashing with security forces.  No further information on these incidents are currently available.

The Mozambican government announced that the  National Institute of Land Transport (INATTER) and the National Institute of Road Transport (INATRO) were being phased out due to their inability to regulate the rail and road sector.

Eduardo Mondlane University released a study stating that 74 percent of graduates students do not have jobs or have uncertain positions. 26 percent were unemployed while 48 had "precarious" jobs. Only 9 percent reportedly landed good jobs.

The President and Board Chair of Mozambique Ports and Railways announced the investment in the rehabilitation of the Beira-Mutare and the Maputo-Harare railway lines for 260 million USD. Four trains were to be imported as part of the project.

534 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 25 June, with 176 new cases in Maputo City, 147 in Tete, and 147 in Maputo province.  2 new deaths were also reported, along with 18 new hospitalizations, bringing the total number of hospitalizations in the country to 117.  There are now 2,746 active cases in the country.  This is the highest number of cases on a single day since early March.
Police arrested a 17-year-old for attempting to sell his 4-year-old nephew for 500,000 meticais in Tete on 20 June.
Mozambique's Police Command said that crimes have decreased compared to last year over the 12-18 June period; 106 criminal cases were reported, compared to 127 cases during the previous year.

President Nyusi announced that security forces will “intensify” operations against insurgents during a speech on Independence Day. Nyusi said the security forces will not sacrifice Mozambique’s sovereignty, and reiterated that the government has never refused support and the training from other countries.
Sources stated indicated that smuggling occurs regularly along Zimbabwe-Mozambique as Chipinge farmers in Zimbabwe smuggle sesame seeds to Manica province.

UNICEF renewed its appeal for funding for humanitarian support in Cabo Delgado,  saying $96.5 million is needed. The organization has previously appealed for $52 million. The support was to provide for those affected by the conflict and the natural disasters.  The organization has only received $16.3 million as part of this appeal, needing a further $80 million to achieve this goal.

President Nyusi in a 25 June speech called on RENAMO dissident leader Nhongo to join the DDR process during his address on Independence Day. He also called on the members of RENAMO dissidents to reconcile with mainstream RENAMO.

The National Migration Service (SENAMI) shut down the border crossing in Ponta do Ouro, south Maputo, early morning of 26 June. The interruption was due to the absence of the healthcare employees to validate the COVID test results. Border Port officials called on travelers to use alternative routes.

Fires occurred at village of Ncumbi, around 10km southwest of Palma Town on the late evening of 25 June and into the morning of 26 June. The fires were reported in at least two locations in the town. The incident may indicate possible insurgent activity, though this is unconfirmed.
Botswana President Dr Mokgweetsi Masisi stated that the SADC standby forces are not going to war in Cabo Delgado but going to “restore peace and normalcy” to Cabo Delgado.
Police conducted an operation raiding house and seizing an unspecified amount of drugs in Mafalala, south Maputo city on 24 June.

The National Institute for Disaster Management and Risk Reduction (INGD) stated that 83,832 individuals have been displaced from Palma as of 23 June.  These thousands of people have fled from the district over the past 3 months in the wake of the assault on the town.  Nangade, Mueda, Montepuez, and Pemba continue to be the most common destinations for these IDPs.

On 24 June, insurgents raided the town of Monjane, south of Palma.  Helicopters in response targeted militants south of Palma on 25 and 26 June. A civilian was also reportedly injured due to shrapnel from the helicopter attacks.

Mozambican Military helicopters on 25-26 June strafed insurgent positions south of the Afungi LNG Camp in response to an insurgent assault on Monjane.  No casualty figures are currently available.  President Nyusi in a speech on 25 June also mentioned these clashes, saying security forces were "hitting the enemy hard on the ground".

Reports on 26 June indicate that two fishermen were kidnapped by the militants in the Monjane area.  This came just after insurgents attacked the Monjane area on 24 June.

518 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 26 June, with 227 new cases in Maputo City and 130 in Maputo province.  Two new deaths were also reported, along with 22 new hospitalizations, bringing the total number of hospitalizations in the country to 127.  There are now 3,234 active cases in the country.

Silverio Ronguane, the deputy of the Assembly of the Republic and member of the Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM), will run for the party's presidency position, at the party's next congress scheduled in 3-5 December in Sofala. Ronguane is currently regarded as the favorite to replace the late Daviz Simango.

IGAS, a subsidiary of SA's Central Energy Fund, and Companhia Mocambicana de Gasoduto (CMG), a subsidiary of Mozambique's Empresa Nacional de Hidrocarbonetos, announced on 23 June that they will buy a 30% stake in the ROMPCO natural gas pipeline sold by Sasol. This development will increase their stakes to 40% each from their current 25%, meanwhile, Sasol, will reduce its shareholding from 50% to 20%. Sasol has yet to respond on this announcement.
Four people were killed and 12 were injured in a road accident in Chibuto district around 0630hrs on 27 June. Reports indicate that a Maputo City-bound bus collided head-on with a truck.

The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) shut down three clubs in Pemba for violating COVID-19 safety protocols.  Other leisure establishments in the town were also closed after operating beyond the permitted hours, the INAE announced.

RENAMO Mayors of Nampula and Island of Mozambique on 27 June said they believe the FRELIMO government is intentionally withholding municipal compensation funds for their cities because they are governed by the opposition.  Officials also stated that it has been three months since they got the FIA for the payment of employees' salaries.

The African Development Bank invested 60 million meticais to purchase chicken production kits for 290 new breeders in Zambezia and Niassa provinces. The investment will help reduce import and improve trade balance in the two provinces.

Reports on 27 June indicate the alleged presence of a Rwandan military contingent in Pemba. The report came three days after Rwanda announced plans to send  troops to support anti-insurgency operations in Cabo Delgado, but is currently unconfirmed.

On 24 June, Comoros said it would provide intelligence services support to Mozambique in Cabo Delgado in the fight against the insurgency.  This offer of support came in a meeting between Comoros Minister Dhoihir Dhoulkamal and Mozambican Minister of Foreign Affairs Veronica Macamo.

Reports on 28 June indicated that a businessman from Mocimboa da Praia, identified as Juma Wazir, was abducted in Balama district. The victim's family said they had not heard from him in the last two weeks. A source claimed that three days before the victim disappeared, he collected an undisclosed amount of money Pemba City. It was not yet confirmed if the incident was perpetrated by insurgents, security forces, or criminal elements.

Minister of Health Armindo Tiago announced on 28 June that Mozambique will start testing new variants of COVID-19 from August.  Currently testing of new variants are done in international laboratories, including South Africa and Germany.

434 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 27 June.  One new deaths was also reported, along with 21 new hospitalizations, bringing the total number of hospitalizations in the country to 143.  There are now 3,185 active cases in the country.

Around 200 new displaced people from Palma arrived in Paquitequete beach between 24-25 June. IDPs fled from Palma area due to continuing insurgent attacks. Some IDPs allegedly spent more than two night in the beach without basic needs as they do not have a family to accommodate them in Pemba.
The Ponta do Ouro border crossing remained closed down on 27 June over lack of health officials at the post to validate COVID-19 tests. Travelers were advised to use alternative routes.

The  Deputy Commander for Civil-Military Engagement of US Africa Command, Ambassador Andrew Young, stated on 22 June that US is committed in providing support including socioeconomic development, community resistance programs, and security assistance to Mozambique. The support will aid in combating the rise of insurgency in Cabo Delgado province..

Bank services in Nangade and Mueda districts have been shut down for more than a month for "undisclosed reasons"; this shut down of service is likely due to the threat of the insurgency in both districts. Commercial and Investment Bank (BCI) in Nangade shut down operations without notice, while BCI, Millennium BIM and Absa Bank in Mueda then also closed down indefinitely.  Insurgents in past raids in Mocimboa da Praia, Palma, and Macomia have targeted bank branches; security forces in some towns targeted by militants have also been accused of robbing banks in the aftermath of insurgent attacks.

On 27 June, Mozambique Airlines cancelled the evening Tete-bound TM 137 Flight from Maputo due to an aircraft anomaly warning. The aircraft reportedly issued a warning during take-off which prompted the pilots to return and comply on the safety protocols to assess the situation. Passengers were guaranteed to board another aircraft today, 28 June.
Authorities reopened on 28 June the Ponta do Ouro border crossing after it was closed down for two days due to the lack of health personnel to validate COVID-19 tests.

Hospitalizations due to the use of illegal substances increased by 7.9% in Mozambique in 2020. 9,788 hospital admissions related to drug use were recorded on 2020 versus 9,666 on 2019.  49.8% of the 2020 data was recorded in Maputo city followed by the province of Manica with 11.7%, and Sofala with 11%.
Reports on 28 June indicate that two people were murdered in Boane and Marracuene districts of Maputo Province over the weekend. Details of the both incidents were not disclosed.

Security forces detained 584 people in Maputo Province for violating COVID-19 safety protocols during the weekend. Detainees were later released.
Police reportedly covered up and allowed illegal parties around markets around Inhagoia area of Maputo City on the evening of 28 June.

Health authorities announced that 1,486 individuals were infected with COVID during the past weekend. This brings the total COVID cases to 75,138 cases. The Ministry of Health announced that the positivity rate is currently 12.73%. 61 COVID admissions were reported bringing the hospitalizations to 143 inpatients. 91 of the hospitalizations were in Maputo City. 34 deaths have also been recorded for the month of June. While 729 recoveries were recorded during the weekend increasing the percentage to 94.6%.

The Inhambane attorney’s office warned people it would be revoking their land titles for houses that were built near the vicinity of Inhambane airport within the airport's designated zone. The attorney’s office stated the municipal council illegally provided land titles on airport land. Around 900 residences were expected to be moved from the area and have their titles revoked as a security measure.

Sources stated that the lack of water infrastructure maintenance and reservoir cleaning has caused a poor water supply in outer neighborhoods of Maputo and Matola. Broken pipes and water leaks were caused by vandalism and weight of passing vehicle traffic, and have caused a growing public health threat in these areas.

Security forces are reported to be present in Tandanhangue village in Quissanga as of 28 June. The village was previously attacked by insurgents. Security forces are encouraging the local population to return to the area, though there is a continued fear of potential attacks by insurgents in the area.

The Mozambique government participated as an observer during an anti-ISIS coalition meeting in Rome on 28 June.  US Sec. of State Anthony Blinken said that there had been various discussions between coalition partners on the "ISIS threat in northern Mozambique". The meeting also discussed the possible steps to be taken by the coalition in Mozambique after several informal meetings regarding the ISIS threat in the country.

The NKC African Economics consultancy stated that the SADC deployment would likely take months and the number of forces deployed would less than the 3,000 troops expected to be deployed. The consultancy also stated that Mozambique still must finalize this deployment with the SADC.

The Bank of Mozambique started proceedings against the local branch of Standard Bank on 28 June. The local branch of the South African Bank was suspected from the Mozambique Interbank Foreign Exchange Market. Some sources have reported the suspension of Standard Bank's foreign exchange market activity may be due to Bank of Mozambique accusations that the bank has improperly used offshore accounts to maintain its position in the foreign exchange market amid recent flucutations in the value of the metical.

Media reports stated that demand for taxi cabs around Maputo has decreased significantly due to COVID. Taxi drivers stated that the current situation is worsening due to the lack of tourism and shut down of entertainment venues around Maputo. Even with the ease in COVID restrictions, there was no reported increase in demand for travel.
The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) stated that clubs and bars continue to operate in Pemba despite curfew. Three clubs were closed down after violating the curfew recently.

The International Transport Workers Federation and the Norwegian Maritime Unions (NMU) have advised ship owners to avoid changing crew members in Cabo Delgado due to the current threat from the insurgency, specifically the rising threat of kidnap for ransom in the province.  These unions advise that crew changes can still be conducted in Nampula and other parts of Mozambique outside of Cabo Delgado.

The Ministry of Health called on the public to adhere to preventive measures to stop the spread of COVID-19. Officials stated that the month of June has seen a notable increase in both cases and deaths related to the pandemic. Officials also said that the recent increase in restrictions was to prevent the third pandemic wave in the country.

284 new COVID infections and a single COVID death was reported by the ministry of health in Mozambique on 28 June. Majority of the cases were recorded in Maputo with 47 cases and 19 cases in Inhambane province. 33 new hospitalizations were reported bringing the total to 159 COVID inpatients.

A new projection of Mozambique's economic performance this year stated that the delay in the natural gas investments in northern Mozambique is expected to slow growth to 2.8%. The economy contracted by 1.3% in 2020.
Police arrested a 19-year-old girl for attempted murder in Quelimane on the evening of 23 June. The suspect used rat poison in attempting to murder her ex-boyfriend and his girlfriend.

International Organization for Migration (IOM) said 13,000 IDPs were on the move in Cabo Delgado between 3 to 16 June.  Around 85% of the IDPs were reportedly from Palma. Other locations of origin for the IDPs were from Macomia, Muidumbe, Nangade and Mocimboa da Praia. The main points of influx were noted in Pemba, Mueda, and Montepuez.

The SADC said on 28 June that $ 12 million will be allocated to the initial deployment of the SADC Stand-By force to Cabo Delgado.  These funds will come from the SADC’s “own resources”.  The Angolan Foreign Affairs Minister Antonio stated that the financing would come from contingency funding with contributions from involved member states. The participating members states in the standby force were also to provide “extra contribution” for the initial budget. Tete Antonio mentioned that the Council of Ministers will also to conduct a meeting in the future regarding sustainability funding to continue their peace-keeping operations in the region.
Sources stated that Rwandan security forces could deployed in Cabo Delgado as early as July, and could launch operations against the insurgency in August.  This report is currently unconfirmed.

Mozambican police in Xipamanine Market arrested a Nigerian citizen selling "al Shabab" branded razors.  The origin of these razors is still unclear, and it is uncertain if these razors are somehow linked to the Cabo Delgado insurgents.

Police sources said in a bulletin on 22 June that police stations in parts of Nampula and Tete had been attacked by "small groups of people" pretending to be IDPs in Tete and Nampula; these attackers reportedly were attempting to gain access to the stations, potentially to obtain weapons.  Police note these attacks are similar to attacks launched by insurgents in Cabo Delgado in the early days of the insurgency, though these attacks have not been confirmed to be linked to the CD militants.

2,720 were vaccinated during the first week of the ongoing vaccination campaign in Beira as of 27 June. District health director Joel stated that the vaccinated were members of priority groups covered health training course final year students, diabetic patients, journalists, athletes, police officers over the age of 50, primary school teachers over 60 years of age, cardiac ill patients, inmates, and prison staff.
The Japanese Company, Mitsui, donated 156 tons of rice to the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD) on 28 June.
