The National Inspection of Economic Activities (INAE) suspended the celebration of the 46th years of national independence in Maputo City and province during the 24 to 27 June. INAE inspected 245 establishments (173 restaurants, 13 event hall and 59 general commercial establishments).

Local sources stated that a newly built healthcare facility in Maringanha area of Pemba remains closed after it was built on 2020. Locals were forced to travel to access medical services at least 10km away. Locals stated that the healthcare facility is still not operational and the infrastructure is starting to age.

Mozambique on 30 June received 500,000 VeroCell COVID-19 vaccine doses at Maputo International Airport.  These doses have been procured through the UNIVAX program, a collaboration between private businesses and the Maputo government.

Sources stated that suspected 35 Rwandan military personnel were conducting a reconnaissance mission in Afungi.  Other sources said the group had arrived on 22 June to Pemba for a two week mission.  Rwandan military personnel previously visited Cabo Delgado between 07-09 May in preparation for an alleged Rwandan deployment of forces to Cabo Delgado.  Other sources reported as many as 200 Rwandan soldiers already in Cabo Delgado.
Police officials announced that over the long weekend that 88 were arrested for violating COVID precautions in Maputo city.

Limpopo National Park officials stated that no poaching has occurred for the past three years in the park of Gaza province. Park Administrator Francisco Pariela also announced the increase in investments on vehicles and light aircraft for patrols around the park.

Officials stated that COVID samples are now being sent to Germany and Sweden after South Africa has not returned results recently sent to be tested for the Delta variant of COVID to Mozambique.   South Africa itself is in the midst of a major spike in COVID cases.

The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) closed two establishments and suspended eight others for COVID-19 restriction violations in Maputo City. The closure of the establishments comes after 328 were inspected.

The Director of Surveys at the National Health Institute Chicumbe stated a new testing procedure was being conducted in Tete province; this includes a mixture of PCR testing and rapid blood tests to identify COVID cases.  This comes after a recent spike of COVID cases in Tete, where the Delta variant of the virus has been detected.
The Ministry of Health announced 406 new COVID cases and 3 COVID deaths were reported for Tuesday, 29 June. Maputo city reported 196 cases and Tete province reported 129.

The Diocese of Pemba Bishop Antonio Sandramo said on 29 June humanitarian aid and financial support for the IDPs in Cabo Delgado is being diverted, saying much of this aid ends up in the "structure of professionals", though did not name any specific individual or group diverting aid.  Locals meanwhile have accused local community leaders as well as local authorities of diverting aid.

The Center for Democracy and Development on 28 June accused police of conducting illegal searches and seizures in Maputo. Police reportedly raided several residences during an anti-narcotic operation in Mafalala, Maputo on 24 June. The raid resulted in several damaged property and injury of a woman who was accidentally shot.

Local media reported that there is a shortage of blood packs for critically ill patients in Hospital Central De Nampula on the afternoon of 28 June. Only 50 blood packs were remaining, the hospital requires 200 blood packs on an average for patient use.
Security forces arrested 9 suspects for violating the curfew and COVID restrictions in Moatize at around 23:00 on 28 June.

Officials announced that the Ressano Garcia Border Crossing will operate on new timings from 0600hrs to 2000hrs starting 29 June for those entering South Africa.  This is an adjustment according to new South African restrictions meant to curb the ongoing spike of COVID-19 in SA.

The President of the Association of Rwandan Refugees in Mozambique Cleophas Habiyareme said on 29 June that his organization has received no clear info as to the location of Ntamuhanga Cassien, a Rwandan journalist abducted in May outside of Maputo.  Habiyareme said his organization is "fearing that the worst has happened".   Some information indicates Maputo may have agreed to detain Cassien in exchange for Rwandan military support in Cabo Delgado.

Media reports indicate that conditions are very poor at the sites of "mega projects" in Chongoene, Chibuto, and Massingir in Gaza while the government also has failed to compensate thousands of families displaced by various projects.  At the Chongoene Airport site, the government reportedly exhumed bodies in the area with little to no organization, resulting in the destruction of human remains buried there.

At the Chongoene Airport site, the government reportedly exhumed bodies in the area with little to no organization, resulting in the destruction of human remains buried there.

A transit bus lost control after a brake failure and crashed into a tree on Avenida 24 de Julho in Maputo City on the evening 29 June. Two civilians were injured.

Suspected locals shot at and vandalized two vehicles used at a sugar factory in Xinavane area of Maputo province.  This incident was believed to have occurred as part of an ongoing dispute between the local community and the sugar factor over local farmland.

Sources stated that hospitalizations were rising in Tete due to the COVID pandemic. 21 hospitalizations have been reported in the province recently. The province reportedly has a 70-bed capacity for COVID inpatients.
Mozambique's Council of Ministers Spokesman Ludovia Bernardo stated that the council did not discuss the SADC deployment in Cabo Delgado during the weekly meeting which took place on 29 June.

Sources stated that 250 employees of the Ilha de Moçambique Municipal Assembly in Nampula have not been paid since April. Officials stated that the non-payment of salaries was due to the delay in paying the Municipal Compensation Fund.

The Disarmament, Demobilization, and Reintegration (DDR) process restarted in Moatize in Tete on 30 June. The DDR process in the area included 368 former RENAMO guerillas and 22 RENAMO dissident members in the area, and will be ongoing to 14 July. To date, 2,307 RENAMO militia members out of 5,221 have joined the DDR process, including 62 former RENAMO Military Junta members. The process is expected to conclude within 15 days in Moatize as the process involves the mobilization of both public and private partners and service providers.

A military spokesman on 30 June on state radio announced that security forces had killed 150 insurgents and captured 39 other militants in fighting between 21-23 June.  The military said insurgents had attacked Monjane and Palma, but had been repelled in these attacks, suffering significant casualties.  Militants reportedly attacked lower Palma town in this raid.

A military spokesman on 30 June on state radio announced that security forces had killed 150 insurgents and captured 39 other militants in fighting between 21-23 June.  The military said insurgents had attacked Monjane and Palma, but had been repelled in these attacks, suffering significant casualties.  No information was provided regarding military casualties.  Other sources had reported insurgents raided Monjane on 24 June; clashes appear to have happened at Monjane between 23-24 June.

The military said insurgents had attacked Monjane and Palma, but had been repelled in these attacks, suffering significant casualties.  No information was provided regarding military casualties.

The military said insurgents had attacked Monjane and Palma, but had been repelled in these attacks, suffering significant casualties.  No information was provided regarding military casualties.

576 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 30 June, along with 6 new deaths.  This included 196 cases in Maputo City and 175 in Tete.  33 new hospitalizations were reported as well.  There are now 4,317 active cases in the country.
Unknown men wearing uniforms and carrying weapons were reported between Meza and Nanjua on the evening of 28 June. Sources stated that the men were suspected military or militants.

The Bank of Mozambique and the French Embassy signed a memorandum of understanding whereby France will provide 500,000 Euros to Mozambique for the fight against financial crimes and money laundering in the country. The funding was also to strengthen the banking system to prevent and combat illicit activities.

An investigative report released on 23 June on $670 million of relief funds for COVID emergency relief donated to Mozambique. These funds were donated by the International Monetary Fund, World Bank, and EU. A part of the funds was reportedly used on COVID training workshops, which were claimed to be held in Pemba, though it was unclear if any money was actually spent on these workshops or any other COVID relief in Cabo Delgado; much of this funding appears to be missing and has not been clearly traced.

An investigative report released on 23 June on $670 million of relief funds for COVID emergency relief donated to Mozambique. These funds were donated by the International Monetary Fund, World Bank, and EU. Large amounts of this funding was reportedly spent on "lodgings and food" and "meals for officials", while no direct COVID relief funds have been traced to relief efforts outside of Maputo.  Large portions of this funding appears to be missing, and may have been diverted by corruption.

An investigation into the usage of COVID relief funds in Mozambique on 23 June indicated that a large portion of this funding was likely diverted to the military effort in Cabo Delgado; the report indicated as much as $84 million may have been "reallocated" to the military from these COVID funds.

The European Union on 30 June began a humanitarian airlift from Italy to Mozambique of 15 tons of humanitarian assistance. Two more flights in the coming days are expected to bring more aid to Mozambique from the EU.

Authorities stated that hundreds of new IDPs arrived from Palma to Nangade for the past two days, 27 to 28 June after new clashes were reported in Palma. The IDPs were being housed in a warehouse in the area, and a lack of humanitarian aid was reported.

Health Minister Tiago says that Mozambique will receive 1.5 million additional COVID vaccine doses in “the coming weeks”. These vaccines were expected to immunize around 720,000 individuals.  This was announced as Mozambique through private funding received 500,000 doses to into Maputo on Wednesday.

Sources stated that police reportedly attacked four journalists while following up on a story regarding the illegal detention of 3 local youths in Nampula at around 14:00 on 29 June. The reporters were identified as Leonardo Gimo from TV Sucesso, Faizal Abudo from TV Muniga, Simão Mugas from TV Muniga and Emerson Joaquim from Afro TV. The police reportedly seized their equipment during the assault and claimed that the journalists intended on defaming the police.

The Medical Assistance National Director Luísa Panguene announced on 30 June that the Polana Caniço General Hospital in Maputo city, used for COVID isolation cases is reaching near full capacity. This comes amid an ongoing spike in COVID cases in the country; 120 of the country's 176 COVID hospitalizations are in Maputo.

The Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued a level 4 travel health warning advising US citizens not to Mozambique on 28 June. This comes as Mozambique has seen a sudden increase in COVID infection rates during the past weeks.

The Ministry of Health announced the opening of another isolation center for COVID patients in Hospital Geral De Mavalane, central Maputo, on 30 June. The new center will accommodate 170 COVID patients. This comes amid a significant spike in COVID cases across Mozambique in recent days.

The Mozambican government has approved the usage of US$ 115 million funds received from the Association for International Development (IDA) to purchase additional COVID vaccine doses.  The country this week received another 500,000 doses and expects in July to receive an additional 1.5 million COVID vaccine doses.

The Bank of Mozambique announced that all activities related to foreign currency conversion by Standard Bank Mozambique are suspended until further notice. Sources had previously reported a temporary suspension of these services, while the BoM is pursuing charges against the bank and two of its employees.  One source indicated this suspension is likely linked accusations by the BoM that Standard Bank used foreign bank accounts to shield some of its currency holdings during recent fluctuations of the metical, though this is unconfirmed.

The Labour Consultative Commission (CCT) held a meeting regarding the possible increase of minimum wage in Mozambique. The meeting was attended by government officials, trade unions, and employer’s association. The meeting comes as no wage increase has been made since April 2019. The continued suspension in increasing wages was rationalized by employers claiming that the recovery efforts and survival of the companies may be interrupted by the wage increase during the pandemic.  The unions have put pressure however on the government and employers for a minimum wage increase in recent months.

Mozambicans are reported to be losing confidence in Mozambique Airlines (LAM) after several recent safety incidents. Locals say that the airline's safety incidents are due to the airline not complying with all the required procedures. The airline’s financial issues are also speculated to be affecting the quality of their services.

A Senior EU diplomat stated that France, Italy, and Spain all are “expected” to provide personnel for an EU training mission to Mozambique.  Portugal, who is already conducting military training in Moz, will also contribute to this mission.  The mission is expected to officially be green lit on 12 July at a meeting of EU Foreign Ministers.

Transit drivers stated on 30 June that there has been a drastic decrease in demand for transport between Maputo and South Africa as COVID spikes in the country. Drivers stated that during the past few days almost no trips were reported between the capital and the border. Drivers blame anti- COVID restrictions in both countries for impacting their business.

The National Institute of Social Action announced that the recent subsidy payments for Cyclone Idai Victims in four districts concluded on 29 June with no issues.  Payments of these subsidies in the past had led to some civil unrest. The districts were Buzi, Gorongosa, Muanza, and Nhamatanda. The following payments would be conducted in Beira starting 1 July.

Payments of these subsidies in the past had led to some civil unrest. The districts were Buzi, Gorongosa, Muanza, and Nhamatanda. The following payments would be conducted in Beira starting 1 July.

A bus caught fire after an engine trouble on the Macia-Bilened road in Bilene district, west of Xai-Xai on 29 June. No casualties were reported. Locals assisted in dousing the flames.

Sources indicated the number of displaced persons in Cabo Delgado could be inflated by more than 200,000, partially due to IDPs registering at more than one location in different areas to receive more food.  These inflated figures could also be part of corruption schemes.  The population of districts impacted by the ongoing insurgents in Cabo Delgado was listed as 624,000 in 2020; there are currently over 730,000 IDPs registered in Cabo Delgado, with around 100,000 people at least estimated to still be living in these districts.
Sources on 28 June claimed that there are a "few special force" officers from Zimbabwe currently present in Cabo Delgado.  This report is currently unconfirmed.

Insurgents reportedly raided and burned residences in the village of Maganja, east of Quintunda Resettlement Village, on 24 June. Displaced individuals who fled Quintunda in attempts to flee from the district were forced back to the resettlement village.

Insurgents exchanged gunfire with security forces in Nhica de Rovuma village, west of Palma, on the 22 June. Casualties were not reported. People in the area fled west towards Nangade after the incident.

Sources stated on 30 June that security forces are conducting operations around Pangane area. Locals stated that security forces have urged the locals not to speak about these ongoing operations in the area. The security officials claimed that the area is safe for locals to return.

Sources stated that inflation has been reported in Mueda driven by IDPs entering the area and after banks in the town closed down over the past month.  Sources mentioned that a kilogram of fish is around 4.74 USD while poultry is at 11.85 USD double in other areas of Cabo Delgado.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs Macamo Dlhovo and Japanese Ambassador to Mozambique signed an agreement on 30 June. The agreement was of Exchange of Notes between the Mozambique and Japanese governments, the donation of 3,891,000 USD, and supply of cold chain vehicles and equipment for the Ministry of Health.

801 new COVID cases and 6 new deaths were reported in Mozambique on Thursday.  This included 371 new cases in Maputo City and 192 cases in Tete.  A 34.5% positivity rate of COVID tests was recorded in the capital and a 40.8% positivity rate was recorded in Tete.  37 new hospitalizations were reported, and there are now 199 total hospitalizations countrywide.  4,826 active cases have now been reported across the country.

The company Portos e Caminhos de Ferro de Mozambique (CFM) intends to invest 18 billion meticais for the rail-port infrastructures in the country. 11 billion meticais will to be used for the acquisition of stock to  compete with other businesses for the rail-port infrastructures in Maputo. 3.3 billion will be used to restore the operational capacity in the areas of central Mozambique which were affected by Cyclone Idai. while 498.8 million will be used to expand Pemba port.
Security forces arrested a suspect for impersonating an INAE agent in Moatize of Tete province on 2 July. The suspect was Helder Joaquim Manuel, a MDM member.

the National Migration Service (SENAMI) announced that 93 illegal immigrants were repatriated to their home countries between the 19 and 25 June. 15 other illegal immigrants were still detained but will be repatriated while 114 were still being questioned.

The Millennium BIM Bank suspended its Western Union International transfer services on 2 July in Cabo Delgado. The suspension was due to the claims that the transfer service was being used by illegal miners and mineral dealers to receive funding.
UNICEF delivered neonatal medical equipment to the Maputo Central Hospital as part of the 200,000 USD investment to rehabilitate the infrastructure.
The Municipality of the Matola filed criminal charges against 17 suspects for illegal occupation and sale of municipal land reserves. Three technical employees were among the suspects charged.

Locals recovered a dead body found in Nanga, north of Macomia on or before 29 June.  The cause of death in this incident was not immediately clear, though locals feared insurgents may have murdered the person.

Sources stated that water restrictions would be put in place in Nampula on 1 July. The water restrictions were due to the low dam water levels. This comes as officials have previously announced that water discharge would be suspended from 29-30 June.

An outbreak of COVID cases in Mahalamba Elementary School forced the school to close on 23 June. 17 cases were reported from the school. 9 were students, 7 were teachers, and an administrator were infected. Healthcare workers have begun contact tracing in response to the infections. This may also indicate a higher number of COVID infections in Inhambane.
Road and maintenance teams have restricted vehicle traffic along EN6 road between the Pungoe river and Nhamatanda on 30 June. The construction was to last for 2 months.

Mozambican General Crisovao Chume on 01 July said insurgents in Cabo Delgado have recently used women and children as human shields, also indicating that in recent days, security forces had rescued more than 100 people from the insurgents, presumably in clashes in Palma District.  Fighting in and around Palma and the Afungi Peninsula was reported between 21-26 June.

Local media on 01 July reported that Standard Bank's CEO and head of corporate operations had been suspended by the Bank of Mozambique.  Sources earlier this week had reported the BoM had brought charges against two Standard Bank officials; this comes after the BoM suspended Standard from foreign currency exchange business in late June.
Police arrested a driver of an unlicensed bus transporting IDPs between Ancuabe and Pemba in Sunate on 30 June.

Mozambican General Crisovao Chume on 01 July that in recent days, security forces had rescued more than 100 people from the insurgents, presumably in clashes in Palma District.  Fighting in and around Palma and the Afungi Peninsula was reported between 21-26 June.  Most of those arrested were reportedly women and children. This report is currently unconfirmed.

Sources stated that the Famine Early Warning System Network in its latest report indicated that Cabo Delgado will remain in food "crisis" throughout the rest of the year until at least January 2022.  This is due to the increasing number of IDPs in the province and insecurity, and due to a lack of agricultural production in the province due to the disruption of farming due to the insurgency.

Security forces commander Francisco Assane in Afungi stated that insurgents are using women to covertly transport weapons.  This came after security forces were reported to have arrested a woman transporting weapons and spying for the insurgency in the area in late June.  The woman had reportedly gathered information from soldiers at checkpoints in Palma and Afungi that she passed to the insurgents.
Security forces arrested a woman working for the insurgents in Palma on 23 June. The detainee stated that she was forced to work with the insurgents.

5 insurgents were arrested in Monjane on Sunday, 27 June, after security forces received a tip off from woman who was assisting insurgents.  One of the insurgents was reportedly the brother of the woman.

The ICRC announced that it would increase operations in Cabo Delgado on 30 June. This will include improving access to healthcare and water by constructing/rehabilitating health centres, water distribution systems, and new water pumps.  This will include operations in Pemba, Montepuez and on the islands of Ibo, Quirambo and Matemo Islands.

Security forces exchanged gunfire with insurgents in Maganja village on 24 June. This comes as Insurgents raided and burned residences in the village; insurgents were driven back from the area in these clashes.

Officials stated that 20 million euros was required to rehabilitate the sewage network in Beira on 1 July. The sewage network repair being discussed under the sanitation master plan, which would allow 187km of sewage to be fully operational. Currently only 86km of sewage pipes were functional.

869 New COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on Friday, with 2 new deaths also reported.  New cases included 285 new cases in Tete, and 212 in Maputo City.  34 new hospitalizations were reported, increasing the total number of hospitalizations in the country to 199.  There are now 5,573 active cases in the country.

A group of 10 insurgents dressed in military uniforms on 02 July were reported to have entered and attacked the village of Namande, southwest of the Muidumbe District capital of Namacande. Local militiamen responded and engaged insurgents in a gun battle in an attempt to thwart the attack. Insurgents beheaded at least 4 people and killed another three civilians; in clashes between pro-gov militia and insurgents, 3 pro-gov militia were killed. Several houses were set ablaze, and food items were looted while communications in the area were also reported to be down.  Other sources reported an unknown number of people were missing in the wake of this attack; it was unclear if they were abducted or fled the area.

Sources also a clash on 2 July at Diaca close to the MDP/Mueda District border; insurgents reportedly attacked the area but were repelled by security forces.  Militants attacked the area in four vehicles and in "considerable" numbers, and one rapid response unit police officer was killed in these clashes.  One source also indicated insurgents seized two armored vehicles in this attack before retreating, though this has not been confirmed.  Diaca and nearby areas in recent months have been within a disputed zone of control between security forces and the insurgents.
Military spokesman Colonel Omar Saranga called on insurgent youths to surrender in Cabo Delgado. The military leader stated that the youths would reintegrated to society "without retaliation".

Security forces were reported to be on high alert in Mueda District on 03 July after militants attacked Namande village near the Mueda border on 02 July.  There was concern insurgents would attempt to infiltrate the district, though no attack immediately materialized.

A  plane transporting humanitarian goods from the EU arrived in Pemba on 3 July, the first of a series of humanitarian flights between the EU and Pemba. The plane was transporting 15 tons of goods which were to respond to the urgent humanitarian needs.
Police arrested 3 gang members for robber charges in Matendene, north Maputo City, on 1 July.

Three armed suspects robbed a civilian after firing warning shots at Naloko market in Nampula at around 19:00 on 2 July. Police responded and managed to detain one suspect while the other two managed to escape.

Three armed suspects robbed a civilian after firing warning shots at Naloko market in Nampula at around 19:00 on 2 July. Police responded and managed to detain one suspect while the other two managed to escape.

1139 new COVID cases and 9 new COVID deaths were reported in Mozambique on 03 July.  This included 521 new cases in Maputo City, and 307 new cases in Tete.  This is the 4th highest number of COVID cases in a single day during the entire pandemic in Mozambique, and the highest number of cases recorded in a single day during the ongoing third wave.

Parliament Speaker Esperanca Bias tested positive for COVID-19 on 02 July while preparing for an international trip. Bias is under home isolation and currently asymptomatic. Health authorities advised those who were in contact with Bias in the last 72hrs to comply with the protocol. It is recalled that Bias visited the Corrane camp in Meconta district, Nampula province on 01 July. The camp currently accommodates 3,969 displaced people.

On 03 July, the Portuguese secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Francisco Andre called for further support from the European Union (EU) countries in supporting IDPs in Mozambique. Andre's statement came as he received the first of three flights by the EU humanitarian airlift at Pemba International Airport which brought donations by various NGOs in Italy and Portugal to the IDPs of Cabo Delgado.

On 03 July, the Minister of Interior Amade Miquidade speaking from Beira said that many areas of the N1 road have been secured from RENAMO dissident attacks, and said life in these areas has "returned to normality".  He also said remaining RENAMO dissident members are now "confinded" and "on the defensive", also saying many of the group's members have joined the DDR process. He also urged the militants to join the DDR process of the government to ensure peace across all Mozambicans.

Reports on 03 July indicate that Frelimo deputy Margarida Salimo and wife of Councilor Roque Goncalves organized a party in Catembe attended by over 100 guests. One of the guests was Alice Magaia de Abreu, Health Councilor for the city of Maputo. Social distance and wearing of masks were not observed at the event amid the escalation of third wave coronavirus in the country.

34 people were killed and 40 others sustained injuries in a road accident involving three vehicles along National Road 1 (EN1) in Tavira, around 2000hrs on 03 July. A speeding passenger bus, Transportadora Nhacale, attempted to overtake a lorry and eventually collided with another truck from the opposite direction. The crash also affected the lorry which later stumbled and overturned on the road. Rescue operations lasted until 0300hrs the following day.

Meida reported on 04 July indicate that a group of South African spies stranded in Maputo returned home following intervention of SA Security Minister Ayanda Dlodlo. The foreign operatives were stranded for nine days after a State Security Agency (SSA) operation targeting insurgents in Cabo Delgado. The group were reportedly operating in Mozambique without the permission of the Maputo government, were identified, and detained before being released in early April.

938 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 04 July, with seven new deaths also reported.  New cases included 540 in Maputo City and 126 in Manica.  50 new hospitalizations were reported, increasing the total number of hospitalizations in the country to 228.

Police Commander-General Bernardino Rafael said on 04 July that the Transportadora Nhancale company should be banned following fatal accidents involving its vehicles, including an accident over the weekend north of Maputo city in which over 30 people were killed.

Mozambique will receive 158,000 COVID vaccine doses in two separate ceremonies at Maputo International Airport today, 05 July. 108,000 doses were donated by the COVAX program, while 50,000 of the doses came from the Portuguese Government. Apart from the vaccines, Lisbon also donated 141,934 N95 masks for health professionals.

Mozambican Police shot dead a 34-yr-old man in Magoanine, Maputo city around 2100hrs on 19 June for allegedly for throwing a stone at a police car which caused damages. The victim's dead body was only recovered by his relatives on 29 June.

The Ministry of Health announced on 05 July that 26 people have been killed by COVID-19 this July. The country's coronavirus death toll is now at 904.  There are now over 7,600 active cases in the country, as well as 228 hospitalizations.

Unconfirmed reports have indicated that UN Special Envoy to Mozambique Mirko Mazoni recently offered $4 million to RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo to join the DDR process and dissolve his group; Nhongo reportedly refused.  Manzoni since this refusal has reportedly attempted to enlist the aid of a retired high ranking RENAMO official to engage in talks with Nhongo.

Reports on 03 July indicate that the Ministry of the Sea, Inland Waters and Fisheries, the Tete Provincial Economic Activities Services, the Maritime Administration, and the coastal and inland water guards carried out a joint operation and arrested three illegal fishermen in Cahora Bassa reservoir. Three semi-industrial fishing vessels and 216 mosquito nets were recovered.

Reports on 03 July indicate that the Ministry of the Sea, Inland Waters and Fisheries announced that they will limit the issuance of new fishing licenses in a bid to stop the destruction of the ecosystem by illegal fisherman at the Cahora Bassa reservoir.
A source on 05 July disclosed that the Mozambican Government had banned the 'Cannabis' energy drink, saying it incites people to use the illicit substance.

The National Migration Service (SENAMI) again closed the border crossing at Ponta do Ouro, south Maputo, on 03-04 July. The interruption was due to the absence of healthcare employees to validate the COVID test results on the South African side. Authorities directed travelers to use the Ressano Garcia post to cross to South Africa.  This was the second weekend in a row in which this closure occurred.

Security forces arrested six workers and traders in Maputo city on 03 July, over alleged theft of goods from the National Institute for Disaster Risk Reduction Management (INGD). The suspects reportedly moved the goods from the institution to a hideout, and then distributed the items in stores in Polana-Canivo and Maxaquene.

Gorongosa District Court on 29 June sentenced 42 illegal miners to between eight and 14 months in prison including fines. The sentence came five days after the miners were arrested for illegal extraction of mineral resources, in Nhandzeia, Gorongosa district.
Security forces arrested 42 illegal miners for illegal extraction of mineral resources, in Nhandzeia, near Gorongosa National Park on 24 June.
Security forces arrested 42 illegal miners for illegal extraction of mineral resources, in Nhandzeia, near Gorongosa National Park on 24 June.

Unconfirmed reports on 04 July indicated that clashes were ongoing in Awasse.  No further information regarding this report is available; this came after clashes were reported in neighboring Diaca on Friday. Pro-government militia and insurgents have previously been active in this area.

Sources on 05 July reported that 36 former RENAMO militia members were being officially integrated into the Defense and Security Forces.  The former guerilla fighters arrived to Maputo on 02 July, and are set to undergo training to integrate into the police "within days".  This group of 36 will be assigned to protect RENAMO's leadership and carry out other associated duties.  Other sources said a further 60 RENAMO militia members will be integrated into the wider police force.  Security force officials meanwhile said they did not have a set date for the integration of hundreds more RENAMO militia members into the security forces, calling this integration a "delicate process."

A US government report released on 02 July indicated that Mozambique does not meet minimums requirements for eliminating human trafficking. The Maputo government according to the report investigates and prosecutes few human trafficking cases and does not "proactively identify" trafficking victims.

Thousands of people fled from Palma to Nangade between 26-30 June after recent insurgent attacks in Palma district The displaced were unable to travel to Pemba due to a lack of funds and were traveling by foot.
The President of Assembly of Mozambique Esperanca Bias called on local youths in Nampula not to join insurgency.
The Ministry of Health announced 737 COVID cases and 8 deaths in Mozambique on 5 July. The total cases have increased to 80,888 and deaths to 912.
Two trucks and bus crashed with each other on the road near Tavira in Manhica, north of Maputo City, on the evening of 05 July. 30 civilians were killed and 26 were injured.
A vehicle overturned after on a road in Xinavane, north of Maputo City on 04 July. The driver died after being critically injured.

South African and US authorities have recently investigated Islamic State activities in South Africa.   One militant from South Africa, Renaldo Smith, who previously joined al-Shabaab last 2018 after escaping to Cabo Delgado.  There is no confirmed information regarding collaboration between the insurgency in Cabo Delgado and militant networks in South Africa.

Health officials announced on 5 July that there has been a significant spike in COVID cases in Sofala during the past 6 months. 31 deaths were recorded in the province so far in 2021, vs just 1 COVID death in all of 2020.  602 new COVID cases have been reported in the province since 25 June, vs very few cases in May.

Long haul truck drivers and bus drivers complained that the National Road 1 is “a danger to everyone”. The drivers claimed that the conditions of N1 Road are unmaintained and have continued to deteriorate. These complaints came after over 30 people were killed in an accident north of Maputo City over the weekend.

Bus company, Carrier Nhancale, suspended their operations after a deadly vehicle accident in the Manhica district, north of Maputo. The drivers of the company were requested to gather in their establishment Maputo just before the suspension of their operations.

Officials stated that around 175,000 cubic meters of water is lost monthly due to leaks in Maputo and Matola cities. Locals stated that the issue keeps recurring even with the repairs made by the Water Investment and Heritage Fund (FIPAG).

Local sources indicated that customers of Standard Bank can not access their bank accounts in the wake of the bank's foreign currency business being suspended. Clients with foreign converted salaries stated that their accounts were affected by the suspension of the Bank of Mozambique.

1,458 new COVID cases and 11 new deaths due to COVID were reported in Mozambique on 06 July.  53 new hospitalizations were also reported.  New cases included 502 new cases in Maputo City, 393 in Maputo, and 262 in Tete.  There are now 9,015 active cases in the country, along with 251 hospitalized cases.  This is the largest number of COVID cases reported throughout the course of the pandemic in a single day in Mozambique.
The Mozambique government has delegated the majority of the chemical treatment of cashew trees to the private sector. The delegation was to encourage the private sector into the business.

The Center for Democracy and Development (CDD) claimed on 6 July in a new report that there are corrupt security officials are involved kidnap for ransom gangs in Maputo City.  The report also said that that police in Tete were reported to be facilitating illegal border crossings for people without passports or other IDs.

The Center for Democracy and Development (CDD) claimed on 6 July in a new report that there are corrupt security officials are involved kidnap for ransom gangs in Maputo City.  The report also said that that police in Tete were reported to be facilitating illegal border crossings for people without passports or other IDs.

The Tax Authority announced that they seized 144 illegal luxury vehicles in Mozambique during an operation between the 2 to 6 July. The shipment of the vehicles violated customs laws and were valued at 53 million meticais. 97 of these  vehicles were collected in the southern region, 32 in the north and 15 in the central region with a total value of 52 million Meticais

The Portuguese armed forces donated 11.9 tons of materials to the Mozambique Red Cross on 6 July. The materials were meant to support the displaced individuals affected by the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

RENAMO Secretary General Magibire stated that RENAMO President Momade will run as the party's nominee for the presidential elections on 2024.  There has been significant dissident within the party in recent years as to whether or not Momade should continue to lead the party.
A vehicle ran over a rickshaw on a road in Morrumbala district of Zambezia province on the morning of 7 July. A civilian died and another was injured.

Local media on 06 July stated that President Nyusi received a $ 1 million "contribution" payment through a Middle Eastern scrap company as part of the "hidden debts" issue last 2014.  The payment made to the scrap company had not been previously reported.

Security forces detained 16 civil servants for selling driving licenses to individuals without finishing driving school in Maputo City on 6 July. The suspects were previously working at the now defunct INATTER, which was recently closed down after officials stated that the delegation was not performing their responsibilities to maintain roads and traffic issues in the country.

Former British Prime Minister, Tony Blair stated on 6 July, that Mozambique in recent weeks has seen the largest spike percentage wise of COVID cases in Africa after a 172% increase during June. The increase in cases is believed to be due to the Delta Variant. Blair called for the increased supply and campaigns to encourage the population to be vaccinated in the region.
The Council of Minister announced on 6 July issued a two-day national mourning starting 6 July for the 30+ civilians who died during a vehicle accident in Manhica district.

Zimbabwean media claimed that the 5th Zimbabwean Brigade was being prepared for a deployment to Mozambique. The intended deployment would be part of the SADC approved stand-by force to assist in the fight against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  Other "elite forces" would reportedly be deployed along with the Zim 5 Brigade.

South Africa repatriated 60 illegal immigrants back to Mozambique without prior notice through Ressano Garcia border crossing on 5 July. Mozambican Migration Service official Celestino Matsinhe stated that the repatriation violated the agreements between the countries. South Africa is required to notify Mozambican authorities regarding the repatriation before sending the immigrants back.

The North Regional Water Administration (ARA-Norte) stated that water restrictions will imposed by the FIPAG in Nampula province. The restriction would start from 40,000 cubic meters per day down to 25,000 cubic meters per day in the upcoming months. The water restriction was to allow proper distribution to the population amid an ongoing water shortage and to avert a water crisis.
The Mozambique government has signed an agreement with Instituto Camoes to generate employment opportunities for youths affected by the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

The Provincial Office for Combating Corruption in Sofala accused two NGO officials of embezzling funds of around 8 million meticais on 7 July. The officials had reportedly stolen about $110,000 through withdrawals from the organization's accounts which were then deposited to several different bank accounts.

Security forces were accused of torturing a civilian to death on Ibo Island after detaining him at around 18:00 on 04 July. The victim who was returning from a trip to Matemo island when he was detained near a military barracks.  He was accused of being a spy for the insurgents by the security forces; after torturing the man, he was abandoned by security forces on an area road before later dying at the hospital.

Cashew producers stated on 6 July that thieves continually stealing cashew nuts from their orchards in Namuno. The producers stated that the police cannot help the producers, and have said that stealing cashew nuts is not crime.
Police arrested a Chinese national for underage marriage in Monapo District in Nampula province on 7 July. The suspect was working for a road construction company.

The Mozambican Transport Ministry removed several officials in the wake of a deadly accident in Manhica district north of Maputo over the weekend which left over 30 people dead. The officials dismissed were the General Director of the National Road Transport Institute Ana Simoes and the National Director of Transport and Safety in the Ministry Claudio Zunguze.

The Ministry of Health announced that 1139 new COVID cases and 11 related deaths occurred in Mozambique on 7 July. Maputo City recorded 433 of the new cases, while Maputo province with 355, and Tete province with 178.

The World Food Program (WFP) warned on 5 July that without new funding the food security crisis in Cabo Delgado could escalate to a “hunger emergency” in near future.  The organization said that $121 million is needed urgently to provide support to 750,000 people by the end of the year.  WFP expects that the number of the those affected by the current food crisis will increase from 228,000 to around 363,000 by October.

Police arrested three suspects in Maputo on 07 July who were involved in a murder and robbery incident in June in Nampula.  The gang had also committed crimes in Zambezia and Maputo provinces.  The leader of the gang has not yet been captured but is being sought by police.

Officials announced the closure of the schools in Nhalivilu and Mhalamba in Inhambane province due to COVID spikes on 7 July. This comes as a total of 40 individuals tested positive for COVID in Nhalivilu and 20 in Mhalamba. The schools will remain closed for 12 days as a preventive measure.

Health Minister Tiago called on Mozambican citizens to adhere to the COVID precautions strictly and minimize leaving the house. The announcement comes after COVID cases have seen an accelerated increased in the country.
Police arrested one of two NGO workers accused of embezzling 8 million meticais in Beira City on 6 July. The other wanted suspect was still at large.
Media reporting indicated that stated that locals continue to not adhere to anti-COVID measures around Maputo city, with little to no mask wearing or social distancing observed.

Health authorities stated that the current COVID wave could peak in the upcoming two to three months amid an ongoing spike in COVID cases in the country; recent testing has shown a 13.2% positivity rate, and Mozambique in recent weeks has had the largest percentile increase of COVID cases of any country across Africa.

In recent weeks, Mozambique has seen a significant spike in covid infections in children in Mozambique. Daily infections of children have risen from an average of 20 to over 50 in the past three weeks; on 06 July, 126 new COVID cases were reported in children.

A commission of inquiry in an 07 July report indicated that some irregularities found at Ndlavela prison on 7 July, though no wider scheme to prostitute female inmates as reported on by an NGO was taking place. The commission stated that the abuse took place inside the prison. The commission also stated that several prison guards colluded with inmates and abused the women inside the Sewing section of the prison.  The inquiry however also said that guards had not charged customers for sexual favors from the inmates outside of the prison.
A truck collided with a passenger bus on the road near Mafambisse, northwest of Beira, on the afternoon of 7 July. 8 civilians were killed and 13 were injured in the accident.

Vodacom and TMCel mobile operators reached a deal in which TMCel will immediately pay 200 million meticais of its debt to Vodacom. The deal stated that TMCel was to pay 12 million meticais monthly.  TMCel within three months must also present a proposal on how it will pay its remaining debt to Vodacom.
Insurgents robbed fishermen near Ilha Quifula and Ilha Magudula, south of Pangane, on 2 July. No casualties were reported.
Insurgents robbed fishermen near Ilha Quifula and Ilha Magudula, south of Pangane, on 2 July. No casualties were reported.
Insurgent activity near Matemo Island on 02 July caused civilians to evacuate from villages and hide in bush areas. The civilians feared of possible insurgent attack in the area.

Sources stated that clusters of fires were reported near the village of Namadaia on the night of 06 July, northwest of Diaca.  This could indicate new clashes between militants and security forces, or a new insurgent attack, though this is unconfirmed.

An SADC document dated 07 July and sent to the UN indicates that the SADC Standby Force (SF) will being a "deployment" to Mozambique from 15 July, for "an initial period of 3 months, and may be extended depending on the evolution of the situation."  This likely refers to the official creation of the Standby Force, rather than the deployment of forces to the country within one week.

1,437 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 08 July, along with 5 new deaths.  This included 459 new cases in Tete, 418 in Maputo City, 260 in Maputo, 118 in Manica, 83 in Gaza, 43 in Inhambane, 34 in Sofala, 9 in Zambezia, 6 in Nampula, 4 in Niassa, and 3 in Cabo Delgado.  The country currently has 309 hospitalizations, and 11,530 active cases of COVID.  This is the second highest single day tally of COVID cases during the entire pandemic.
A transit minibus overturned on a road near Chandame village in Tsangano District on 8 July. 5 civilians were killed and 9 were injured.

Local media reported that LAM currently holds debts worth $230 million, and that the company's debts have increased substantially in recent years even as the airline has attempted to cut costs which have included salary reductions.  This report comes after LAM planes in recent months have been involved in multiple safety incidents.
An illegal gold mine collapsed on 27 June, killing 2 and injuring three in Chalaua in Moma District of Nampula.
A tourmaline mine collapsed in Nacapa village, southwest of Nampula, on 27 June. An illegal miner was killed and 2 others were missing.

A former official of the Ilha de Mozambique in Nampula has been accused of involvement in a corruption scheme. The Nampula Provincial Office stated that former official Gimba diverted 3 million meticais which was intended for a coastal erosion protection project. The project reportedly was not implemented.

The International Air Transport Association (IATA) started a safety audit of LAM for the renewal of the company's Operational Safety Certificate. The audit will inspect the company's flight operations, operational control, flight dispatch, aircraft engineering and maintenance, cabin operations, cargo operations, and safety management. This comes as LAM has had three safety incidents during the past six months.

Health Minister Armindo Tiago warned on 07 July that Mozambique could run out of oxygen supplies for COVID patients amid the ongoing COVID case spike in the country in which more COVID cases were recorded in the first six days of July than in all of June.
The Minister of Health, Armindo Tiago stated that HIV cases are decreasing in Mozambique. Tiago stated that the cases have decreased from 110,000 in 2019 to 89,000 in 2020.

Sources stated that gravediggers in Maputo are burying an average of 3-4 bodies per day in area cemeteries due to COVID-19. Other sources reported as many as 10 COVID dead burials a day, which could indicate the underreporting of COVID deaths in the capital.

The Rwandan government issued a statement on 09 July, announcing the deployment of 1,000 Rwandan security force and police officers to Cabo Delgado. The force is meant to assist Mozambican security forces by conducting joint combat and security operations against the ongoing insurgency in the province.  The statement from Rwanda also indicated that the deployment was based on the signing of "several agreements" between the two countries in 2018.  The statement also said Rwandan forces would work closely with SADC forces and Mozambican troops in these operations.

1,327 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 09 July, along with 5 new deaths.  This included 718 new cases in Maputo City and 306 in Tete.  54 new hospitalizations were reported, and there are now 330 hospitalizations in the country.  There are 12,404 active cases in the country.  The case total reported on Friday was the third highest in a single day in Mozambique.

Minister of Agriculture, Celso Correia, warned on 08 July that the government will 'repress' exporters who will attempt to defraud the country by falsifying the value of their goods on export delcarations to avoid taxes.

South Africa's international operations officer, Robert McBride, was suspended following a mishandled mission in Mozambique. South Africa’s State Security Agency (SSA) did not provide further details on the suspension. The announcement came after South African website reported that four SA spies were detained in Maputo in April.

The number of COVID-19 cases in Inhambane province continues to increase. The positivity rate in Inhambane was 7.5 percent for June and it escalated to 10.5 percent in the first week of July. Inhambane currently has 232 active cases, 14 deaths and only one hospitalized individual.

SERNIC officers arrested the suspected head of a kidnap gang in the country on 08 July. The gang members, who were detained for two weeks, were reportedly responsible for the abduction of an Indian citizen on 14 June in Maputo.

Security forces announced on 09 July the arrest of two out of five gang members who defrauded civilians using fake social media accounts. The group reportedly uses these accounts to sell cars and deceive clients.

The Mozambican Government announced on 09 July that they will establish an entity within the National Institute of Road Transport (INATRO) that will monitor and eventually prevent traffic accidents in the country.

Reports on 09 July indicate that Maputo Central Hospital is running out of space to accommodate COVID-19 patients. The 40 bed-capacity ward designated for coronavirus patients were all occupied. Other patients were transferred to the Mavalane and Polana-Canico General Hospitals.

A report released by National Statistics Institute (INE) indicate that deflation continued in Mozambique for a  third consecutive month in June. The general level of prices fell by an average of 0.52 percent in June which follows price falls of 0.31 percent in May and of 0.03 per cent in April. The date is based on the consumer price indices for the cities of Maputo, Nampula and Beira, however, the level of deflation varies for the three mentioned cities. The greatest deflation was reported in Beira, where prices fell by 0.97 percent, followed by Nampula (0.63 percent), and Maputo (0.31 percent).

More than 3,000 workers were forced into unemployment in Zambezia during first and second wave of COVID-19. Businessmen were deeply concerned that the third wave of the virus may greatly affect the employment and businesses in the country.

The third European Union Humanitarian Air Bridge flight to Mozambique arrived at Pemba Airport on 09 July. The first two EU humanitarian flights arrived on 03 and 04 July. The aid is donated by Italy and Portugal to provide support for the growing humanitarian needs of the people in Cabo Delgado.
IDPs arriving into Mueda from Palma recently indicated they had been threatened by insurgents to leave the area or be killed.

Security forces arrested several civilians in Quitunda market over alleged involvement with insurgent groups. Many of these arrestes however reprotedly are arbitrary and target civilians with no ties to the insurgency.

The National Migration Service (SENAMI) announced that the border crossing in Ponta do Ouro, south Maputo, will be closed again today, 10 July, until early hours of 11 July, due to the absence of healthcare employees to validate COVID-19 test results. Authorities advised travelers to use alternative routes.

1,327 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 09 July, along with 5 new deaths.  This included 718 new cases in Maputo City and 306 in Tete.  54 new hospitalizations were reported, and there are now 330 hospitalizations in the country.  There are 12,404 active cases in the country.  The case total reported on Friday was the third highest in a single day in Mozambique.
Rwanda announced on 09 July that the deployment a 1,000-strong force to Cabo Delgado has began. The deployments will be completed by 10 July.

The number of COVID-19 cases in Inhambane province continues to increase. The positivity rate in Inhambane was 7.5 percent in June and escalated to 10.5 percent in the first week of July. Inhambane currently has 232 active cases, 14 deaths and only one hospitalized individual.
Boat transfer fare from Pemba to Palma have increased 66.6 percent due to the high risk of insurgent attacks, sources reported. IDPs are now charged 2,500 meticais, against the 1,500 meticais in May.

More than 222 Mozambican nationals were deported from South Africa in the last two weeks due to various offenses including, illegal immigration, murder, illegal possession of firearms among others. Affected individuals were sent to the borders of Ressano Garcia and Ponta D'Ouro without prior notification to the Mozambican authorities.

Rwandan troops began deploying to Cabo Delgado on the morning of 09 July.  Closed sources reported that additional forces are expected to arrive on 15 July. This followed an announcement by the Rwandan government the day before declaring that 1,000 Rwandan security force and police officers would be deployed to Cabo Delgado.  President Nyusi officially announced on 09 July that Rwandan troops would be deployed to Cabo Delgado to assist in the fight against the insurgency.

The Ministry of Transport and Communications announced on 10 July that at least 417 people have died in road accidents in Mozambique since January 2021. This is a 6 percent increase compared to same period on 2020.

Rwanda Defence and Military Spokesperson, Col Ronald Rwivanga, stated on 10 July that the 1,000 Rwandan troops that will be deployed in Mozambique will stay in the country until the "mission is finished", and that the mission has no specific time limit.  The troops will according to Rwandan security sources carry out "combat and security operations". The troops- comprising of 700 RDF troops and 300 RNP officers will be lead by Maj Gen Innocent Kabandana.

On 11 July, Portuguese Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Francisco Andre, stated that Portuguese businessmen are still interested in investing in Cabo Delgado despite ongoing security challenges in the province which has affected economic activity.
Mozambican police on 11 July warned they would arrest individuals in Maputo City who fail to wear their masks as part of the OCVID-19 safety measures.

Reports on 11 July indicate that court judges and National Criminal Investigation Service agents receive regular death threats. The threatening messages are typically received by officials who are presiding an important or high-profile criminal case. The magistrates urged the government to provide protection and ensure that these threats will not be carried out.
Seven people were killed and 15 others were injured after a commercial vehicle collided with a truck along Beira-Nhamatanda route, in Mafambisse, Dondo, on the afternoon of 07 July.
Five people were killed and nine others were injured after a commercial vehicle called chapa overturned along Chandame-Angonia road in Tsangano district on the afternoon of 08 July.

1,686 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 10 July, along with 15 new deaths. 999 of the new cases were recorded  in Maputo City, 312 in Tete, 127 in Maputo Province, 582 in Gaza.  In the past 24 hours,  61 patients were hospitalized while 25 were discharged. A total of 351 people are admitted in covid-19 inpatient centers and other hospitals, 74.1 percent of which are located in Maputo City.

Reports on 10 July indicate that a RENAMO Guerilla base in Zobue, Tete has been closed after more than 360 fighters in the area were disarmed as part of the Demilitarization, Demobilization and Reintegration (DDR) process. The process at this base began on 30 June. Nine Renamo military bases have been dismantled since the DDR process commenced in October 2019 - five in Sofala province (Savane, Muxungue, Maringue, Inhaminga and Chemba), one in Inhambane (Mabote), and three in Manica (Barue, Tambara and Mossurize). With this latest demobilization, over half of RENAMO's total armed force has now been demobilized countrywide.

Four officers from Botswana arrived at Pemba Airport on 11 July ahead the deployment of Southern African Development Community (SADC) troops.  These officers are meant to make preparations for the arrival of a larger SADC force into the country. This information was disclosed by  National Defense Minister, Jaime Bessa Neto, during a press conference in Beira. Neto also added that the arrival of Rwandan troops was articulated within the SADC, after South Africa reportedly lamented that the said forces arrived earlier than the SADC troops.

The Ministry of Health announced that 933 new COVID cases and 20 related deaths were recorded in Mozambique  on 11 July. The breakdown of the cases are as follows: 528 in Maputo City, 57 in Maputo province, 118 in Tete, 76 in Inhambane, 74 in Gaza, 35 in Sofala, 15 in Zambezia, 14 in Niassa, 13 in Nampula, two in Manica and one in Cabo Delgado. In the last 24 hours, 74 patients were hospitalized while 42 were discharged. The 20 dead were the highest number of people to die of COVID in a single day in Mozambique.
Reports on 10 July indicate that additional humanitarian support for Cabo Delgado arrived in Nacala Port, Nampula.

Reports on 10 July said that the Caritas of Mozambique resumed services of providing food to displaced people in Montepuez district. Among the items received are oil, rice, flour, blankets, shoes, mouth and nose masks and second-hand clothes.

The European Union approved on 12 July a military training mission to Mozambique to help the government fight the rising insurgency and protect civilians in Cabo Delgado province. However, it was not yet clear which countries will provide the said troops.  The forces will be deployed to Katembe in Maputo and Chimoio in Manica. The decision was made during the EU's meeting in Brussels. The training mission will last 2 years and will help Mozambique to establish a Quick Reaction Force.  Portuguese General Nuno Lemos Pires will lead the operation on the ground, which could include between 200-300 personnel.
Cabo Delgado border guards were called on by President Nyusi on 12 July to intensify border controls with Tanzania in a bid to restrict entry and exit of suspected insurgents.

Reports on 09 July said that the Association of Combatants of the National Liberation Struggle (ACLLIN) urged Tanzania to provide assistance to individuals/families fleeing from the insurgency in Cabo Delgado province. Hundreds of people from the province have been deported from Tanzania after fleeing into the country and been sent back to areas of Cabo Delgado close to the border without humanitarian supplies.

The Ministry of Health announced 92 new COVID deaths and 10,404 new cases within one week. The Ministry of Health announced that the increase in cases and deaths is alarming. COVID cases have doubled compared to the previous week which had seen 5,010 new cases; new deaths meanwhile in recent weeks have trippled.  A majority of the deaths are in the age group of 60-85 year old.

An armed man murdered his aunt and mother during a dispute over the sale of a water container in Gotite Village, north of Inhambane, on 10 July. Police arrested the suspect in response to the incident.

The Ministry of Education and Human Development, in coordination with the Ministry of Health, released new precautions to prevent COVID at schools in Mozambique. Several schools were having difficulty in complying with the new imposed precautions due to the lack of budget to provide for additional sanitation materials.
Education officials announced that 21 new COVID cases were found from schools among students and teachers in Maputo City. This comes as 14 were previously reported during the past week.

As of 12 July, 270 COVID hospital beds were occupied in the Greater Maputo Area out of 603 beds available in the capital and neighboring areas.  Increasing rates of hospitalizations look set to strain the capital area's COVID bed capacity in the coming weeks.

The Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) stated that President Nyusi did not inform parliament regarding the entry of the Rwanda security forces in the country to fight against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado, and had only announced this deployment in a speech on Friday in Mueda.

The Bank of Mozambique on 12 July fined the South African Standard Bank of 290 million meticais (about $4.5 million) and suspended the exchange and currency conversion activities of the bank for a year. The bank was fined for "serious infringements of prudential and exchange rate nature". Authorities said the local officials of the bank fraudulent manipulated the exchange rate, installed an illegal payment system, conducted financial irregularities that were associated with the exchange rate fluctuations.

RENAMO President Momade said on 13 July that a deployment of Rwandan troops to Mozambique was illegal, and that parliament and the country at large should have been notified of this deployment before it began.  RENAMO had supported the deployment of an SADC force to the country.

The Cabo Delgado governor Valige Tauabo called for locals to remain vigilant and monitor the actions of both the Rwandan and SADC security forces deployed in the province. This comes as the Rwandan forces were deployed to the province earlier on 10 July. The SADC stand-by force were expected to arrive on 15 July.

The Maputo Governor announced the residents are urged to strictly adhere to the COVID precautions in Maputo province. This comes as COVID cases and deaths have increased significantly in Mozambique. The governor stated that the curfew remains in effect from 21:00 to 04:00.
Security forces arrested eight zone secretaries for violating COVID precautions by conducting face-to-face meetings in Nampula on 10 July.

The Southern African Development Community (SADC) announced that it will deploy its forces into Cabo Delgado once Mozambique agrees to the “final details” regarding the force and its commanders.  This signals a potential indefinite delay in the deployment of SADC forces to the country, after this deployment was meant to begin on 15 July.

ISCAP issued a statement claiming to have engaged the FADM on the Mueda – Mocimboa da Praia Road in Cabo Delgado and “repelled” a military offensive in the area..  The militants claim to have captured 2 armored vehicles and 4 rifles during the fighting. Some sources indicated this likely was a claim for an insurgent attack on security forces on Diaca on 02 July, though this is unconfirmed. This is the first claim of an action in Cabo Delgado by ISCAP since the group claimed responsibility for the assault on Palma in late March – early April.

The National Directorate of Civil Identification (DNIC) announced that there has been an increase in registering fake Identity Cards in Maputo City. The DNIC stated that police have recently detected 10 cases in which fake IDs were used, often to take out loans from banks.

The MDM condemned that the government has not informed  parliament of the arrival of Rwandan security forces in Cabo Delgado. The political party said that the parliament was only informed through media and not through formal communication. MDM officials stated that the lack of communication shows that the executive's decision was illegitimate, and opposes the deployment of Rwandan forces.

Sources stated that the families with residences near the airport in Inhamabane are willing to resettle if the government provides them with a neighborhood with access to essential services. This comes as around 900 families have residences around the airport. The residents demanded energy, water, access roads, a nearby hospital, and a school.

The Integrated Development Agency of the North (ADIN) director announced that the agency is preparing a plan to begin operations in August in Cabo Delgado. The ADIN was set up almost a year ago as the government's primary driver of development and provider of employment opportunities to youth in Northern Mozambique, but the agency has yet to start up any of these activities.

The Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP) announced on 14 July that all nationals of their members states can apply for a CPLP visa or residence permit. CPLP also stated that this also provides the "same rights, freedoms, and guarantees" to the applicant.  Mozambican nationals, as Mozambique is a member of the CPLP, are eligible to apply for these visas/residence permits.

Zimbabwe is reportedly experiencing difficulty in providing finances fund its own contingent to participate in the SADC's Stand-By forces in Cabo Delgado. The Zimbabwean Ministry of Finance stated that there is no money currently to finance the operation. ZIm army officers meanwhile have reportedly said Zimbabwe lacks the "suitable weaponry" to fight against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

The Standard Bank on announced the appointment of an acting CEO to replace the former CEO Nwokocha in Mozambique on 13 July. Nwokocha was fined for fraud charges during a on-site inspection by the Bank of Mozambique. The charges led to the suspension of the Standard Bank from conducting foreign exchange activities and the suspension of two officials.

Security forces detained an IDP suspected of being an insurgent in Alto Gingone of Pemba on 10 July. The suspect's mother-in-law stated that the detainee was involved with al-Shabaab.  The man however has not been confirmed to be a militant.

Health officials announced on 13 July that cases have been doubling in Mozambique since the early July. COVID cases have increased by 206.7% during the current week. This also includes the hospitalizations for COVID inpatients as admissions have increased countrywide from 269 to 430 over a two week period.

The Council of Ministers stated that the inquiry commission has been set up and given one month to finalize the investigations regarding the major accident in Maluana that has killed 30 civilians. The inquiry commission was made of five members: former Administrative Court Counselor Judge, Dr. Muchine, Mechanical Eng. Lo Kam Chong, Mozambican Medical Association member Dr. Jacob, Civil Engr. Guiamba, and Mozambican Association for victims of road safety (AMVIRO) Dr. Alexandre Nhampossa.

Standard Bank announced on 13 July that the bank remain operational even after the sanctions placed on the bank recently for "manipulating the foreign exchange market". The bank stated that it has a clear plan to continue business and work with the Bank of Mozambique to clarify all allegations against Standard Bank.

The Ministry of Health announced 1,331 new COVID infections and 17 new deaths in Mozambique on 13 July. The country reportedly has 16,658 active cases and 372 hospitalizations. While 331 patients have recovered.

President Filipe Nyusi announced on 12 July, that the SADC has consent regarding the deployment of the Rwandan security forces in Cabo Delgado. Nyusi stated "We are a sovereign country, SADC respects this. It has allowed that we can work in a bilateral manner. We are going to work with our bothers from Rwanda who are arriving."

The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) called on public inspectors to join efforts in maintaining and securing the application of COVID restrictions around the country. INAE stated that the joint efforts would allow the reinforcements to minimize the increasing COVID cases.

Five armed robbers shot and killed a security guard and detained another before stealing from stalls at Mercardo Maguiguane in Laulane, central Maputo City, at around 01:00 of 13 July. Locals stated that the suspects also vandalized other stalls during the incident. Vendors said that the robbers stole mobile phones, computers, and other valuables.

column4: Mozambique initially expressed a strong preference for a Zimbabwean SADC commander of the SADC Standby Force, sources indicated on 13 July.  The SADC meanwhile had intended, and likely will ultimately appoint a South African general to command the force with a Botswanan officer as second in command.

Macomia teachers on 13 July were reported to have opposed returning to their schools for fear of insurgent attacks. The teachers stated that they are exposed to be used as human shields by the insurgents if an attack occurs, and do not believe Macomia district is secure, despite government claims.
US Secretary of State Anthony Blinken spoke with the President Nyusi on the phone on 14 July regarding strengthening bilateral relations and focusing on priorities in Mozambique.
The Olympic Committee of Mozambique announced three COVID cases among their delegation on 14 July. The Olympic Committee stated that members were asymptomatic and were subjected to daily testing.

Defense Minister Neto stated on 14 July, that everything was ready for the arrival of the SADC troops. Neto also denied any delay in the deployment of SADC force.  This comes as previous reports that the Mozambique government not yet reportedly signed the “State of Forces” to allow the deployment of the SADC troops.  Neto said this document was to be signed on Wednesday sanctioning the Standby Force to deploy to Mozambique - though it was unclear if this agreement was indeed signed on 14 July.

The Ministry of Health announced 20 new COVID deaths and 1,543 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 14 July. Maputo City recorded 657 of the new cases and Maputo province with 253 cases. This brings the total to 93,429 cases and  1,033 deaths.

Police reportedly detained 50 individuals for not complying with the COVID restrictions placed around Maputo city during operations that began around 15:00 on 13 July. Many of the detained individuals were not wearing masks and were selling alcohol.

Local official stated that the increased COVID cases have led to the suspension of face-to-face classes at schools in Chimoio on 14 July at the Manica Higher Polytechnic Institute and the Higher School of Journalism.

Schools in both the public and private sector have reportedly closed due to increasing COVID cases in the greater Maputo area. . Currently five schools were closed in Maputo province and another in Maputo City. 12 school staff have been infected in Maputo province.
Health officials stated that 17 hospital staff were infected with COVID at the Central Beira Hospital as of 14 July.

Sources stated that food supplies are running out at Zimpeto market due to the recent riots in South Africa. This comes as wholesale traders are reportedly unable to travel to South Africa to collect goods.

Mozambique has been added to the COVID red list of Bahrain, preventing entry to the country without a recent PCR test within 48 hours and 14-day quarantine. This comes amid rising rates of COVID in Mozambique.

The Mozambican Federation of Road Transport Associations (Fematro) issued a warning of possible food shortages as trucks intended to transport foods supplies are stranded due to the recent violence in South Africa. This comes as some trade unions have advised against travel to South Africa under the current circumstances. Fematro officials stated that trucks were unable to travel back to Mozambique due to the usual routes are affected by the riots and looting in the country. In addition, trucks that are intending to go to South Africa are also currently unable to travel to the country due to this violence. This comes as an Association of Vendors stated that the current violence and riots in South Africa could lead to the lack of essential goods in Mozambique. The shortage in goods would also affect the prices, which are expected to increase. The association president stated that even the attempt to import goods is difficult as local traders have closed their businesses due to fear of the unrest spreading in other areas of South Africa.

Defense Minister Jaime Neto stated that the document officially authorizing SADC to intervene in Moz was to be signed and delivered on 14 July. This "Status of Forces" document as of 15 July however has not yet been confirmed to have been signed.

The Southern African Development Community (SADC) and Mozambican government reportedly have rejected the inclusion of the Malawi Defense Forces as part of the stand-by force to take part against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. No specific details have been released regarding why Malawian troops would not be included in this deployment.  The Standby Force, when it is deployed, is most likely to consist primarily of South African and Zimbabwean troops.

The Ministry of Justice announced that only women guards were to be stationed at Ndlavela female prison in Maputo on 14 July. The deployment of all female security forces was to prevent any sexual exploitation of female prisoners after a recent scandal in which prison guards allegedly prostituted inmates to clients.

President Nyusi on 12 July, called for RENAMO dissidents to join DDR process, and for dissident leader Nhongo to also join this process, saying people from "Muxungue onwards" should leave the woods, saying anyone who joins the DDR process will not be criminally charged or pursued by security forces.

The Ministry of Health announced that 1,687 new COVID cases and 14 deaths in Mozambique on 12 July. The breakdown of the cases are as follows: 1,104 in Maputo City, 136 in Maputo province, 135 in Inhambane, 127 in Gaza, 97 in Niassa, 41 in Tete, 29 in Zambezia, 13 in Nampula, 4 in Sofala, and 1 in Manica.

UN envoy to Mozambique Manzoni called for additional support from the public and other stakeholders for the DDR process and to support demobilized RENAMO fighters on 11 July. Manzoni stated that the stakeholders should ensure the long-term reintegration of the former RENAMO fighters. This comes as the DDR process has now covered 52% of the total 5,221 RENAMO fighters in the country.
Health officials stated that there is a shortage of blood supplies at central Maputo hospital. Hospital officials stated that the lack of supply was due to the absence of donors due to COVID.
Seven locals lynched a suspect for poisoning tangerine juice which killed two civilians Canda area in Zavala, Inhambane on 13 July. Police responded and arrested two of the suspects.
