ISCAP released a claim on 13 July saying militants had exchanged gunfire with a security force patrol in Muidumbe on 12 July. A soldier was killed, while 3 motorcycles, and weapons were seized in these clashes.  It was unclear if this claim refered to Namacande, the Muidumbe capital, or elsewhere in the district.
Security forces and local militia ambushed insurgents after they attacked Namande village, east of Mueda, on 2 July. 4 militants were killed.
Insurgents were reported to have looted two weapons depots in Palma after security forces reportedly fled the area during clashes in late June in the town.
Sources stated that a child has died due to the lack of humanitarian aid and supplies in Nangade on 9 July.
A vehicle ran over and killed a civilian along Avenida 24 de Julho, Maputo City, on the evening of 13 July.

On 15 July, the Islamic State's Central Africa Province (ISCAP) published its fourth claim of an attack in Cabo Delgado in the past week, saying its militants had attacked the village of "Mekombe" near Palma and killed 4 "Christians" in this attack, also saying the group's fighters clashed with a Mozambican security force patrol on the Palma-MDP road.  The group said one motorcycle was seized from the patrol while another was destroyed in this clash.  This claim is unconfirmed.

On 15 July, the Islamic State's Central Africa Province (ISCAP) published its fourth claim of an attack in Cabo Delgado in the past week, saying its militants had attacked the village of "Mekombe" near Palma and killed 4 "Christians" in this attack, also saying the group's fighters clashed with a Mozambican security force patrol on the Palma-MDP road.  The group said one motorcycle was seized from the patrol while another was destroyed in this clash.  Other sources later said that security forces had clashed with militants between Ncumbi and Monjane villages on 13 July, resulting in 4 militants killed.

1,304 new COVID cases were reported on 15 July in Mozambique, along with 24 new deaths.  This is the highest number of deaths yet reported in a single day from COVID-19 in Mozambique.  524 new cases were reported in Maputo City, along with 218 cases in Tete.  69 new hospitalizations were reported, and there are now 406 hospitalizations countrywide.  There are now 18,754 active cases of the virus in the country.

In a 15 July evening address to the nation, President Nyusi announced new measures to combat the ongoing spike of COVID cases in the country.  The new measures include: The nationwide curfew will be in effect from 2100hrs to 0400hrs daily in all cities, municipalities, and towns. All classes have been suspended in Maputo and its environs, Manhica, Xai Xai, Inhambane, Beira, Tete, Chimoio, and Dondo. All Religious Services and Private Events are suspended.Pre-School classes are suspended nationwide. All Gyms, theatres, swimming pools, and casinos are again closed down. Public institutions will now operate from 0800hrs to 1400hrs Monday – Friday. Restaurants and takeaways are open from 0600hrs to 1800hrs; supermarkets may operate from 0900hrs to 1600hrs Mon-Sat, and 0900hrs to 1300hrs on Sundays and holidays. Funerals may be attended by only up to 20 people. All new measures come into force at midnight on 17 July and will last for 30 days; these measures may be adjusted as needed after 15 days. Nyusi also announced Mozambique will between now and August obtain 11 million more COVID-19 vaccine doses.

The Mozambique government has formalized its request for assistance from SADC against the insurgency on 15 July. The government has reportedly signed the “status of forces" agreement document to allow the deployment of the SADC stand-by forces.
10 displaced women drowned while traveling to Pemba near Vamizi island on 10 July. The victims were IDPs coming from Palma who were attempting to flee towards Pemba.

SADC mission officially started on 15 July after the signing of a "Status of Forces” agreement was signed in Mozambique. The SADC intervention was to last for three months, though no reports indicated troops arrived in the country on the day.

The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) arrested a supplier on  corruption charges in Nampula on 9 July. The suspect identified as Momade Rassul Abdul Rahim issued a bad check to pay off his debts. Rahim was involved with several previous crimes including money laundering, tax fraud, smuggling, and illicit development.

The Cabo Delgado governor called on 14 July for locals of Quitunda area to collaborate with the SADC and Rwandan forces who were to fight against the insurgency in the province. The governor also said that the “local population may soon return to the HQ of the district of Palma”.
Officials announced that four policemen were being prosecuted for brutality in Niassa on 15 July. This comes as the police assaulted a civilian by detaining him and shooting him in the leg.
Police briefly arrested 8 FRELIMO members for violating COVID-19 rules on 10 July. This comes as 500 individuals were reported to have gathered during a meeting. The detainees were later released.
Sources stated on 15 July that Rwandan aircraft had been travelling between Nacala to Afungi for several days. This comes as Rwandan personnel were reportedly on the present in both locations.
Sources stated on 15 July that Rwandan aircraft had been travelling between Nacala to Afungi for several days. This comes as Rwandan personnel were reportedly on the present in both locations.
RENAMO member Lt. Gen Ngonhamo, who previously served as Chief of Military Intelligence of the Movement for the political party has passed away on 15 July.
Police arrested 18 people for not wearing masks in Maputo on 15 July. This comes as officials have implemented stricter measures for COVID due to the increasing cases.
Sources stated that an average of 50 people are detained daily in Maputo for not wearing masks or following COVID precautions.

The German government will donate 4.2 million EUR to fund projects that would “strengthen stability and security” along Mozambique and Tanzania border. The funding was to promote joint security between countries. This would also minimize the suspected insurgent routes coming from Northern Mozambique.

Sources released an ISIS publication (al-Naba) on 3 July stating that new foreign forces to be deployed to Mozambique will also fail to defeat ISCAP militants, just as the Mozambican security forces have been unable to defeat the militants.
Fires were reported in the Nkonga area, southeast of Nangade on 15 July. These fire clusters may be an indication of an insurgent attack in the area, though this is not confirmed.
Fires were reported in the near of Nkonga, southeast of Nangade on 11 July.  These fire clusters may be an indication of an insurgent attack in the area, though this is not confirmed.
Fires were reported in the east of Nkonga, southeast of Nangade on 2 July. These fire clusters may be an indication of an insurgent attack in the area, though this is not confirmed.
Sources reported that fires broke out north of Diaca on 07 July. The fires may indicate insurgent activity in the area though this is not confirmed.
Fire reportedly broke out in the south of Nkonga on 9 July.  The fires may indicate insurgent activity in the area though this is not confirmed.
Sources reported of fires near Quiwia, north of Palma, on 10 July.  The fires may indicate insurgent activity in the area though this is not confirmed.
Sources stated that the Sofala governor tested positive for COVID on 16 July.

Sources stated on 16 July that security forces stationed on the road between Quitunda and Maganja were charging individuals passing through for 500 meticais. If the traveler refused, they are accussed of being links with the insurgents.
Police disposed of 19 remnant grenades and ammunition found by construction workers under a school being renovated in Machava Socimol of Matola on 14 July.
The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) arrested three Central Hospital of Nampula staff. The suspects were accused of selling blood packs to the relatives of a patient.

The Mozambique security forces issued a warning to civilians residing around Palma town and nearby areas to leave their villages and travel to Quitunda Resettlement Village by 19 July. Locals stated that residents in villages along the coast were prevented from fishing or traveling by boat. The warning comes as reports that security forces were conducting operation on the outskirts of Palma.  The orced evacuations were reportedly meant to allow security forces clearly identify any individual in the area outside of Quitunda as an insurgent.

Sources stated that two drivers of trucks transporting smuggled wood in Tica AP, Nhamatanda District, were dismissed on 13 July after being detained by forest inspectors. The drivers were released after reportedly paying 40,000 meticais.

Sources stated that two drivers of trucks transporting smuggled wood in Tica AP, Nhamatanda District, were dismissed on 13 July after being detained by forest inspectors. The drivers were released after reportedly paying 40,000 meticais.

Sources stated that two drivers of trucks transporting smuggled wood in Tica AP, Nhamatanda District, were dismissed on 13 July after being detained by forest inspectors. The drivers were released after reportedly paying 40,000 meticais.

Sources stated that the 700 Rwandan soldiers and 300 police were to be deployed to Afungi. The security forces were to secure the perimeter around the liquified national gas project. Some sources indicated that of these troops, about 500 will remain to guard the Afungi site and potentially Palma town, while the other 500 will be "operational"; this report is currently unconfirmed.

President Nyusi called on prison guards to prepare for "integration" to fight against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. Nyusi also stated that the prison guards objectives can change depending on situation.

The Ministry of Health announced 1,394 new COVID cases and 18 deaths in Mozambique on 16 July. Maputo recorded 781 of the new cases and Tete province with 188 cases. This brings the total to 96,127 cases. Admissions were at 451 cases.

On 17 July, the Ministry of Health reported 2,025 new Covid-19 Infections in Mozambique and 24 deaths due to the disease.  This included 32 cases among foreigners and 1,993 among Mozambique citizens. Most new cases of infection were diagnosed in Maputo city with 865 cases, followed by Maputo province with 684 recorded cases. This reflects the highest number of new infection reporting in Mozambique during a single day since the start of the pandemic.

France has included Mozambique on it’s COVID-19 red list.  All trips from Mozambique to France must demonstrate “pressing grounds for travel”.  Arrivals must also undergo the following procedures-p resent a negative PCR test less than 48 hours old before departure, take a PCR test upon arrival in France, vaccinated persons must self-isolate for 7 days after arrival, unvaccinated persons must self isolate for 10 days after arrival. Those who will fail to self-isolate could result in a 2,000 euro fine.

Australian-based MRG Metal company announced on 16 July that the area of Nhacutse contains very high grade heavy mineral sands. The officials of the company said that they could be looking at a 200 million tons high grade resource, which is significantly larger very high grade resource than originally targeted. The company is currently looking for an independent company to calculate a formal Mineral Resource Estimate.

41 out of 88 individuals, including athletes, coach and masseuse, who participated the final game between Ferroviario de Maputo and Costa do Sol tested positive with COVID-19. Maputo City Basketball Association (ABCM) later announced that the competitions will resume following strict and rigorous compliance with the COVID-19 prevention measures.

On 16 July, Vice President of Brazil, Hamilton Mourao, expressed willingness to work with Mozambique if the latter requests military support to fight insurgency in Cabo Delgado Province. Brazil had participated in a peace force in Mozambique in 1990s . Both nations are members of the Community of Portuguese Language Countries, Group of 77 and the United Nations.

South African Member of Parliament with the opposition Democratic Alliance, Kobus Marais, urged Defense Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula to delay the deployment of military troops to join the Southern African Development Community (SADC) forces in Cabo Delgado Province due to the current security situation in South Africa. The SA  government recently deployed 25,000 soldiers in Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal areas to restore stability and secure infrastructure following widespread looting. Marais added that troops can be sent to the neighboring country once SA's security situation has stabilized.

Southern African Development Community (SADC) expressed concern that the recent conflict in South Africa may affect the region.  South Africa has by far the largest economy in Southern Africa.  Recent violence could threaten to reduce job opportunities, essential properties, disrupt economic activities as well as affect health due to possible exposure to COVID-19. The supporters of former President Jacob Zuma ignited the violence last week following the protest brought by Zuma's 15-month jail sentence for contempt of court.

Mozambican Police haved banned use of police uniforms during performances by singers and actors in the country. Police General Commander Bernardino Rafael said the wearing such uniforms by performers may create confusion among civilians.

Several restaurant owners in Maputo City have suspended the contracts of their workers after their operations were restricted from 0600hrs to 1800hrs as recently directed by President Nyusi. The restrictions were enforced by Nyusi due to the significant rise of new COVID-19 cases and related deaths in the capital.

On 17 July, Portuguese President Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa announced the donation of "Premio Jose Aparecido de Oliveira"  he received from the Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP) to Caritas de Mozambique to support NGOs in Cabo Delgado. Sousa was awarded around 2.2 million meticais last March, however, he did not disclose if the full amount will be donated to the IDPs in Cabo Delgado.

Several of cases of beer fell out of a truck after it overturned at the roundabout at Missao Roque, in Maputo city in the morning of 18 July. No casualties reported however, the accident damaged the vehicle and destroyed beer bottles.

The Ministry of Health reported 1,260 new COVID-19 Infections in Mozambique and 19 deaths due to the disease on 18 July. Most new cases of infection were diagnosed in Maputo city with 709 cases, followed by Maputo province with 171 recorded cases. Over the last 24 hours, 21,574 active cases were recorded in the country while 447 individuals have fully recovered.

Mozambican businessmen expressed their intent to be involved in the National Vaccination Plan, procure COVID-19 vaccines and sell them to private clinics. Talks for the private purchase of more vaccine doses are already underway. The statement came after President Nyusi imposed new anti-COVID measures last week which affected several businesses.

Two people were injured and a pedestrian bridge was destroyed in a road accident along EN6, Munhava, Beira City around 1800hrs on 17 July. A lorry reportedly hit a pedestrian bridge after it exceeded the bridge's posted clearance. The collapsed bridge hit an incoming vehicle which caused injuries among its occupants.

A two-yr-old girl was sexually abused by her grandfather in Boane, Maputo on 29 June when her mother was at work. The suspect confessed to the crime but claimed that he did not know what motivated him to do the act. It was not clear if the suspect was arrested. The victim underwent medical and psychological treatment.

Rape cases against minors increased in Maputo City during coronavirus pandemic. From January to June 2021, there were 23 cases of sexual abuse in the capital against to eight cases registered same period last year.
Rape cases against minors slightly declined in Maputo Province. From January to June 2021, there were eight cases of sexual abuse in the capital against to 10 cases registered same period last year.

The World Food Programme announced on 16 July that they will receive 6.7 million euros from European Union to provide food aid for 360,000 displaced people in Cabo Delgado. A section of the donated funds will be used to support other nutrition projects for children in the region.

A report from African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights and United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees on 15 July stated that more than 732,000 people have been displaced in Cabo Delgado due to insurgency. Challenges in the access to humanitarian aid affected the response of NGOs and the government in providing support to the IDPs. Seven ot ouf 16 district in the province are inaccessible due to security or logistical challenges.

10 young men invaded Nacololo village, south of Mueda, on the morning of Thursday, 15 July and set fire to six houses causing panic among villagers. Several commercial establishments were looted during the attack. At least one of the attackers was reported to be a local man, and sources said the attack was believed to have been part of a local dispute, rather than an insurgent raid.  Other sources however said that the attackers spoke Swahili (often used by the insurgents).  No connections to the insurgency however have been confirmed.  Reports suggest that security forces later detained 7 of the 10 suspects.

Security forces arrested seven out of 10 young men who attacked Nacololo village, south of Mueda, on the morning of Thursday, 15 July. The suspects set six houses on fire and looted commercial establishments.

Member states of the Community of Portuguese-speaking Countries (CPLP) signed a mobility agreement during a ceremony on 17 July. The agreement will allow all residents of nine member states to apply for 'CPLP residence visa' and the 'CPLP residence permit' as well as 'CPLP short-term stay', 'CPLP temporary stay.' The CPLP consists of 9 member states- Angola, Brazil, Cabo Verde, Guinea Bissau, Mozambique, Portugal, and Sao Tome, and Príncipe.

Reports on 18 July indicate that "thousands" of residents of Chipinge in Zimbabwe have relocated to Mozambique after they lost their land to Green Fuel Pvt Ltd in Chisumbanje and Chinyamukwakwa village in the town. Guards attached to company reportedly harassed villagers and set their houses and properties on fire, forcing many to flee into Mozambique.
ExxonMobil announced today, 19 July, the donation of 25 tons of food products and 100 bicycles for displaced families and the homes of host families on the outskirts of Pemba.

Several schools will shift classes to online classes as an option for students for the next month due to the suspension of face-to-face classes across the country. The suspension was due to the increasing COVID cases in schools.

South Africa as of 18 July was reported to have not yet deployed troops as part of the SADC stand-by forces in Cabo Delgado due to the ongoing unrest in South Africa. The troops had been set to be deployed to the country on 15 July.

Dozens of transit minibus drivers conducted a strike and blocked Avenida 25 De Setembro against the continued police vehicle inspections in Pemba on 19 July. The drivers stated that police were asking for 2,000 meticais as bribes during these inspections.

The Association of Rwandan Refugees called on the Mozambican government to respect the Geneva convention. The association stated that around 4,000 Rwandan refugees were residing in the country, many of whom fled persecution from the current Rwandan government of Paul Kagame.  This comes after the recent disappearance of a Rwandan journalist from Inhaca, who was reportedly detained by Mozambican security forces and handed over to Rwandan government personnel at the Rwandan embassy in Maputo.

The Bank of Mozambique appointed a resident inspector to monitor the Standard Bank on 19 July. The inspector, Zaitina Chilaule will monitor the shareholders' action plan, and analyze developments of the internal control system of the bank. This comes as the Standard Bank was recently suspended from conducting foreign exchange activities.

Police shot and injured a civilian for not wearing a mask in Majune on 12 July. The victim was with his friends, who claimed that he was shot in the leg by the police. Police arrested one of the individuals for not wearing their mask.

Police shot and injured a civilian for not wearing a mask in Majune on 12 July. The victim was with his friends, who claimed that he was shot in the leg by the police. Police arrested one of the individuals for not wearing their mask.

Officials announced the arrest of the policeman who shot and injured a civilian for not wearing a mask in Majune on 12 July. The policeman was arrested on or before 19 July.  An investigation to determine the action were being conducted.

President Nyusi announced the second phase of the national COVID vaccination campaign will be extended. The second phase was scheduled to end on 17 July but was extended due to the high number of civilians who are still eligible for the vaccine.
Police arrested 48 individuals at a gathering for violating COVID precautions in Maputo city on 17 July. During the operations, 152 drivers were also fined for violating the imposed curfew.

The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) recovered two stolen Toyota SUVs in Bairro Herois Mozambicanos in Chimoio on 17 July. The vehicles were stolen by criminals who were part of a vehicle smuggling group. The vehicles were stolen from Johannesburg on 30 June.

The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) recovered two stolen Toyota SUVs in Bairro Herois Mozambicanos in Chimoio on 17 July. The vehicles were stolen by criminals who were part of a vehicle smuggling group. The vehicles were stolen from Johannesburg on 30 June.
Sources stated on 18 July, that 23,651 individuals have yet to receive their second COVID vaccination dose.
Officials stated that around 80 teachers were removed from their positions for being illegally recruited in Mecanhelas on 14 July. The teachers claimed that their removal was unfair and sudden.

USAID announced the completion of the rehabilitation of the Agrarian Institute of Bilibiza, which has been moved to Chiure, allowing 300 students to resume classes.  The institute in Bilibiza was previously destroyed by insurgents.
The Ministry of Health announced 1,373 new COVID cases and 20 new deaths in Mozambique on 19 July. 22,804 active cases in the country and 481 were hospitalized.

The National Directorate of Public Health announced that the third wave in Mozambique is being driven by the Delta variant. The country has seen an increase of 150% compared to the second wave and hospital admissions have spiked by 170%. Bed capacity for COVID patients is at 57% or 334 occupied beds. Maputo province reportedly has 42 beds occupied, out of 40 bed available.

Public Health Deputy Director Matsinhe stated the COVID in patient bed capacity of Maputo province has been exhausted. Maputo province has a 40-bed capacity but is currently catering to 42 COVID inpatients. Matsinhe stated that other COVID patients that require hospitalization were being transferred to Maputo City. Maputo City has a bed capacity of 583, with 334 beds are currently occupied as of 20 July

The National Institute of Health announced that an expansion trials of a new COVID vaccine, Sinopharm in Beira, and Maputo. The new vaccine will conduct phase 2 and phase 3 tests in Africa. The studies were to enable the clinical trials and determine the efficacy of the vaccine against the variants.

Sources stated that the trial for the "hidden debts" case will start on 23 August. The first defendant for the cases was set to the former member of the Mozambican SISE, Cipriano Mutota. The court will hear from 2 defendants per day.  Former President Guebuza will be among those will will testify in the televised court case.

A court in Cabo Delgado sentenced nine defendants for smuggling illegally obtained logs. Six of the defendants were employees of the Tax Authority. The Tax Authority employees were found embezzling money and forgery of documents, while the other suspects were charged for smuggling and illegal logging. The timber was seized in August 2020. in Pemba.
The Japanese government announced that they would donate 2 million USD to assist IDPs, asylum seekers, and refugees in Mozambique. The donation will be channeled through the World Food Program.

The Budget Monitoring Forum warned that the public debt by Mozambique may reach an "unstable" point.  Debt securities of the Mozambican Tuna Company have increased from $500 million to $900 million from 2015-2020.

The Ministry of Health announced 20 new COVID deaths and 1,224 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 20 July. The majority of the cases were recorded in Maputo City as 573 cases and Inhambane province with 175.

Sources stated that locals were returning to Quitunda due to the improvement of security. The district administration and secretary indicating the security and peace of the area.  Some locals are also reportedly considering returns to other villages in Palma as Rwandan troops deployed to the district have also helped improve the security situation.  Security force sources say only Quitunda, Maganja, and Monjane villages in Palma are currently inhabited, and the other 60 villages and towns that make up Palma district have been deserted due to insecurity.

The National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD) announced the need for 12,000 tons of relief goods to assist the IDPs in Cabo Delgado per month at resettlement sites around the province.

A group of women found three male bodies with signs of torture near Lichinga road of Lago district in Metangula village in Niassa on the morning of 19 July. The victims were found with cloths placed over their faces. Police responded and started an investigation to determine the suspects and motive of the incident.
Police stated that a woman was abducted and sexually assaulted by unknown men in Lago District, northwest of Lichinga, on 17 July.  There is no further information regarding this incident.

Sources stated that the transportation officials have not yet implemented stricter COVID restrictions almost a week after the Mozambique president issued a statement for such measures. Public transportation terminals remain without preventive measures even as COVID-19 cases continue to spike in the country.

Sources stated that IDPs were hoarding humanitarian aid hindering the distribution by the local government in Montepuez District. Some IDPs were registering family members from different villages multiple times, allowing them to obtain additional relief kits. NGOs stated that if IDPs were found with extra kits they would take them distribute them to resettlement centers.

The Association of Combatants of the National Liberation Struggle (ACCLIN) called on war veterans to assist security forces in Cabo Delgado in a speech by the organization's secretary general Fernando Faustino in Mueda on 20 July.  Faustino said it was the "mission" of war veterans to "punt an end to the bandits that are harassing this area".  Pro-government militias are active in Mueda and neighboring Nangade and Muidumbe Districts in fighting the insurgency.

Police announced on 20 July, that 646 individuals violating COVID precautions have been detained during the past week around the country. The arrest comes as President Nyusi recently announced the imposition of stricter COVID measures as cases increased during the month of July.
Police in Pemba on 19 July on 25 de Setembro Ave broke up a demonstration of public transport drivers who were protesting against police inspections and alleged corruption in the city.

Police on 19 July said they had arrested a public transport driver for attempting to bribe a police officer with 2,000 meticais after being caught without a license; this arrest and other incidents reportedly triggered a demonstration against security forces in the city.

Rwandan troops on 20 July on patrol north of Palma reportedly engaged insurgents in the Quionga area, reporting 30 insurgents killed.  Militants then were reported to have withdrawn towards the Tanzania border.  Rwandan troops have been on the ground in the Afungi and Palma areas since earlier this month.

1,704 new COVID cases were recorded in Mozambique on 21 July, along with 32 new deaths.  This is the highest death toll in a single day during the course of the pandemic; the previous high was 24 deaths in a day.  New cases included 1,111 cases in Maputo City and 161 cases in Maputo province.  82 new hospitalizations were reported, and there are now 494 hospitalizations throughout the country, along with 22,461 active cases.

The UK courts announced on 21 July, that the "hidden debts" case that will be heard in a UK court were not expected to begin until 2023.  The case was moved forward after debates regarding how the case was to be set to be conducted.

A ship transporting 36 individuals and four tons of aid sank between Pemba and Ibo early morning of 20 July. 12 civilians were killed and 14 were rescued. 10 other civilians were still missing after the incident. The aid was intended for IDPs in the Quirimbas archipelago. Officials stated that the incident occurred due to the overloading of the vessel.

Sources stated that an SADC “advance team” and a South African commander have already arrived in Pemba as of 18 July.  Those deployed reportedly included South African special force units. The advance team was meant to prepare for the arrival of SADC forces into Mozambique. Other sources said the SADC was still determining the size of the SADC mission to Mozambique, and that no command center post had yet been agreed to in the country.  None of the advance team deployed to Cabo Delgado are expected to take part in operations in the near future in Cabo Delgado.
Rwandan security forces were reportedly patrolling around Palma on 19 July after recently being deployed to the area.
Insurgent attacked the villages of Nampanha and Mandava in Muidumbe district on 19 July. Casualties were not reported.  Another report said Mandava was attacked on 18 July.

Insurgent attacked the villages of Nampanha and Mandava in Muidumbe district on 19 July; note other reports said the attack began on 17 July.  Three people were killed in the attack on Nampanha, and insurgents carried out looting in the village while also setting homes on fire.
Mozambican military helicopters on 20 July rescued a pilot who had crash landed south of MDP the day before, and destroyed his aircraft to prevent it from falling into insurgent hands.

A light aircraft was forced to crash land on a beach south of Mocimboa da Praia on 19 July; it was unclear what caused the crash, or why the aircraft was flying in the area, though it is suspected to have been carrying out reconnaissance over insurgent held MDP.  A local company later announced that one of its planes had flown from Afungi bound for Palma, and had experienced an engine failure that led to the crash landing.

The Mozambican security forces launched offensive against insurgents in Saba Saba village of Muidumbe district early morning of 19 July. No further details regarding these clashes were immediately available.
Security forces launched operations targeting insurgents in Mitope, west of Mocimboa da Praia, early morning of 20 July. This came after insurgent activity was reported in this area on 17 July.
Rwandan security forces reported to be conducting patrols after being deployed around Nangade on 20 July.

Sources stated that the SADC commander of the Standby Force is Major General Xolani Mankayi. The Maj. Gen. was welcomed by the Minister of Defense and the Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of Mozambique. Maj. Gen. Manyakai the commander of SANDF previously deployed in an SADC peace mission to Burundi.

The Ministry of National Defense denied reports that the SADC troops have arrived in Mozambique on 21 July. The Ministry of National Defense clarified that only advance teams were present in the country.

Pro-government militiamen detained two men who escaped an insurgent camp in in Nangade on 21 July. The detainees claimed that they were tortured during their 90-day detention at the insurgent camp.  Local militia reprotedly beat both men.

Portugal Defense Minister Cravinho announced it would support a joint CPLP military mission in Mozambique. Cravinho also stated however that the CPLP currently has no capacity of military intervention as such mechanisms were not developed within the organization.

Portugal Defense Minister Cravinho stated that the government “hopes” that Palma and Mocimboa da Praia residents can return to their homes by the end of the year. This comes as foreign security forces were to provide assistance to the Mozambican security forces against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

Health officials announced 260 COVID deaths over the first 19 days in July. The number of deaths was three times the deaths seen compared to January. Deputy Director Matsinhe stated that the country registered a cumulative of 24,381 new COVID cases and 1,132 new hospitalizations during the same period. In comparison, 9,628 new positive cases and 419 hospitalizations this past January.

RENAMO has called on the president to make a declaration of war against the insurgents as the country is "in a situation of war".  This comes as RENAMO previously condemned the act of the president for not formally informing the parliament regarding the deployment of Rwandan security forces to the country.
Sources stated that IDPs continued to flee from insurgent active areas including coastal Macomia to Matemo Island. The displaced people were from Namandingo, Palma, Mocimboa and Macomia.

The Minister of Land and Environment Ivete Maibasse stated that security forces detained 334 poachers related to 118 cases of environmental crimes from September 2020 to May 2021. The protection of the natural reserves was strengthened after environmental security forces have adopted improved security measures.

Officials announced that 66 containers of wood illegally exported to China were recovered after arriving at Pemba Port on 16 July. 10 other containers were enroute to the port. The 76 containers were illegally shipped out this past December.

The Dyck Advisory Group (DAG) issued a report regarding human rights violations by its employees in Cabo Delgado. DAG stated that it conducted attacks targeting “legitimate military targets” with the approval of the police. DAG also clarified that if both targets and civilians were present in the area the approved engagement was called off. DAG also denied reports of throwing hand grenades from helicopters.
Rwanda police were reported to have been deployed to Mueda district on 9 July. The deployment was to support the Mozambican forces against the insurgency.
Insurgents attacked the village of Ncumbi, southwest of Palma, on the 12 July. Casualties were not specified.
Sources stated that a 36-vehicle convoy transporting military equipment and personnel travelled from Chiure to Mueda on the afternoon of 15 July.
Displaced people were still reportedly fleeing from Palma as of 11 July, with 1,150 IDPs arriving to Ntamba, Nangade from Palma.
Sources stated that 1,270 IDPs were forcibly deported from Tanzania in June. This brings the total of the deported Mozambican IDPs from Tanzania to 9,753.

2,153 new cases of COVID and 31 more deaths were reported in Mozambique on 22 July, the highest number of cases yet recorded in a single day during the pandemic in the country, and second highest number of deaths.  1,133 cases were reported in Maputo City, along with 362 in Maputo Province.  There are now 487 hospitalizations across the country, along with 23,868 active cases.

Total reportedly may once again consider moving its Cabo Delgado LNG operations offshore amid ongoing security concerns in Palma District, though company personnel have acknowledged that any potential move would "have its own technical political challenges".
An armed man injured his son by burning him in Nampula on 19 July. The suspect and his wife were detained by the police after the crime.
An armed man injured his son by burning him in Nampula on 19 July. The suspect and his wife were detained by the police after the crime.

Elements of the Zimbabwean army are reportedly on standby for deployment to Mozambique. The Zimbabwe National Army will join the other forces of the SADC that would be deployed in Cabo Delgado.  Zimbabwean officials earlier this week indicated that "all issues" delaying a deployment to Mozambique had been resolved and the deployment would go forward in the near future.

Unconfirmed reports stated that security forces exchanged gunfire with insurgents near Awasse, southwest of Mocimboa da Praia, on 20 July. No further details regarding this incident are currently available.
Security forces detained a suspect in for sexual assault in Namutequeliua, central Nampula, on 17 July.

The Mozambique Military Spokesman Saranga stated that SADC member states that will contribute troops to the SADC Standby Force in Mozambique are South Africa, Tanzania, Angola, and Botswana. In addition, Zimbabwe previously stated that they were waiting for deployment as part of the SADC forces.

The Mozambican Ministry of Defense confirmed the arrival of the South African advance team in Pemba with the SADC standby-force commander, though said the bulk of the SADC Standby Force had yet to arrive.

Mozambique Military Spokesman stated that Malawian security forces may deploy troops to Cabo Delgado as part of the SADC force. This announcement comes after previous reports indicated Malawian security forces would not take part in the SADC Standby Force.

Palma's local police commissioner and district administrator on 14 July were reported to have withdrawn to the Quitunda area after the Mozambican military called on all residents of the Palma area to travel to Quitunda ahead of a planned security operation in the area to clear insurgents from around the town.

Mozambique security forces reportedly executed 15 insurgents on 13 July near the Rovuma River in Palma District (though the exact location was not confirmed) after capturing a group of militants who were attempting to travel into Tanzania from Mozambique.  IDPs reportedly witnessed two insurgents being executed before fleeing, and believed the other 13 were killed as well.
Insurgents attacked the village of  V Congresso, north of Macomia, on the 15 July. Six civilians were killed during the attack.  No further details were available.

Insurgents attacked the village of Mitope, seizing and beheading a civilian.  Mozambican military helicopters responded to the attack, launching rockets against the militants; no information regarding potential insurgent casualties was available.

Insurgents attacked the village of Mitope, seizing and beheading a civilian.  Mozambican military helicopters responded to the attack, launching rockets against the militants; no information regarding potential insurgent casualties was available.
A minivan caught on fire on the road between Quelimane and Nicuadala (N10) on the afternoon of 22 July. No casualties were reported.

UNCHR stated that 335,000 children are currently homeless in Cabo Delgado, and are among the 732,000 displaced people across Cabo Delgado. UNCHR also mentioned that the children make up half of the IDPs that have fled from the insurgency.

The Zimbabwe government stated that it is “still putting together a plan and package” for intervention in Cabo Delgado. This comes after reports that Zimbabwe was preparing to deploy troops to Mozambique.

The National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD) received 1.5 tons of relief goods from the Gambian community in Mozambique. The support was to provide assistance to the IDPs in Cabo Delgado.

Local media stated that hundreds of IDPs are residing in "inhumane conditions "  on Matemo Island. Several IDPs in Pemba stated that the IDPs in Matemo were sleeping outdoors and in tents made of plants.  IDPs on the island are also reportedly receiving inadequate humanitarian support.  Many reportedly want to travel to Pemba but also fear this voyage for risks of boats sinking and due to the threat of insurgent attacks at sea.

The Mozambique government announced that it intends to purchase 11 new oxygen generating machines for COVID patients. The machines would be installed in four central hospitals around the country. This comes amid COVID spikes across the country.

A new UN report on 23 July indicated that ISCAP is recruiting  individuals by promising loans, employment, and a community. The report also indicated that ISCAP leaders were reportedly from Tanzania, Burundi, DRC, and Kenya. The group is also reportedly recruiting with "promises of loans, employment, and community".

A UN report issued on 23 July stated that ISCAP had collected between 1-2million USD, ID cards, as well as ID cards and passports through attacks on Cabo Delgado banks and through other robberies and attacks by land and sea in Cabo Delgado and waters just off of the province.

A UN report on 23 July stated ISCAP is a "major threat" due to the lack of counterterrorism operations targeting the group, also saying that it could possibly expand west into Niassa or north into Tanzania.

The Bank of Mozambique’s recent sanctions against Standard Bank in recent weeks have reportedly in some cases prevented aid from being able to reach refugees in Cabo Delgado. The suspension of the Standard Bank reportedly affected the movement of funds of importers, specifically those funding social projects for refugee communities into the country.  IDPs in Ancuabe, Metuge, Pemba, and elsewhere reportedly did not receive aid because of these sanctions.

The Bank of Mozambique on 23 July stated that Standard Bank can now resume limited foreign exchange operations starting 26 July. This would include foreign exchange deposits for customers. The Standard Bank was still suspended from conducting activities in the Interbank Foreign Exchange Market.  The BoM said Standard Bank had "fully complied" with correcting "irregularities" identified by the BoM, though no clear details were provided as to why Standard Bank had originally faced sanctions.

The Mozambican government announced that 2.5 million new COVID vaccines to arrive in Mozambique 26 July. The new vaccines were the first batch of 11 million doses that were set to inoculate 1.2 million across the country. Note other reports said that only about 300,000 doses would arrive into Moz on Monday.
Five Zimbabwean police officers were arrested close to the border with Mozambique for their involvement in smuggling activity along the border with Mozambique.

Security officials announced that 9 Mozambican officers are to be assigned as liaisons to the SADC force in Cabo Delgado. Minister of Defense Neto stated that there should be no room for error for Mozambican forces to be confused in attacking civilian population.
The Maputo Judicial Court sentenced 22 defendants involved in embezzlement scheme on 20 July. The suspects embezzled 2.5 million EUR from the Agrarian Development Fund.
1443 new COVID cases and 11 new deaths were announced by the Ministry of Health in Mozambique on 23 July. Maputo city recorded the highest cases with 586 cases and Maputo province with 291 cases.

Insurgents attacked the village of Namacule of Muidumbe District on 20 July. Civilian casualties were reported. The attack comes after the insurgents left Nampanha village and stayed in the area until 22 July.
The National Migration Service (SENAMI) stated that three employees were expelled from the service between Jan to June.  Two were expelled for falsifying receipts and one for abandoning their post.

A Court in Beira sentenced two journalists to 18 months in prison for corruption charges on 23 July. The journalists were accused of receiving a bribe to not publish work related to the violation of rules at a hotel during the state of emergency.

Sources stated that Rwanda special forces had reportedly been deployed to Nangade after threats of an “imminent attack” on the town on 23 July.  Sources within the past week had reported Rwandan troops patrolling in the Nangade town area.

At least 28 people, including several military personnel, were arrested by Mozambican police on the night of 23 July in Pemba for the violation of the  curfew.  5 firearms were seized from the offending officers, who were found consuming alcohol at establishments illegally operating after hours.

59-year-old Mauritius Ambassador to Mozambique, Jean-Pierre Jhumun, passed away on the morning of 24 July due to COVID-19. He was hospitalized last week after testing positive with the coronavirus. Mauritius Minister of Foreign Affairs, Alan Ganoo, said that the ambassador's health deteriorated as he experienced difficulty of breathing.  He resided in Maputo with his son. His remains will be repatriated as requested by his mother.

The Ministry of Health announced 1,451 new COVID-19 cases and 25 related deaths in Mozambique on 24 July. 875 of the new cases were recorded in  Maputo City, and another 214 cases in Maputo province. In the last 24 hours, 316 people have recovered while 505 were admitted to the hospital due to the virus.

Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) will deploy two personnel to Mozambique as part of the European Union-led mission to combat insurgency in Cabo Delgado. The mission will include foreign troops to train and advise Mozambican forces on the development of military command structures and mechanisms for a rapid reaction force.

A Mozambican national was arrested in Delhi Airport on 16 July over alleged attempt  to smuggle narcotics into India by swallowing 36 capsules of heroin worth Rs 2.8 crore.  The ingested heroin capsules, weighed 400 grams, were recovered from the suspect.  The man originally travelled from Johannesburg; it is unclear if he had obtained the drugs in Mozambique prior to this or in South Africa.

On 24 July, Rwanda Defense Forces confirmed encounters between insurgents and  Rwandan troops on 20 July in the Quionga area, saying Rwandan troops had patrolled the Afungi area before moving north towards Quionga, where they clashed with insurgents.  Rwandan military sources did not confirm casualties in this clash, though previous reports indicated 30 militants were killed.

National Director of Medical Care, Luisa Panguene, stated on 25 July that about 70% of COVID-19 patients currently coming to hospitals arrive in critical conditions and that the number of deaths related to the coronavirus continues to increase. The current pandemic situation deeply affected medical doctors and other front liners. Panguene advised strict compliance of sanitary protocols, and immediate treatment for COVID-19 patients with  chronic diseases.

The local government of Vilankulo has proposed a suspension of classes after the number of students and teachers infected with COVID-19 increased from 14 to 58 in one week. The proposal was sent to provincial government for further evaluation.

Two sources reported that Rwandan and Mozambican troops on 24 July had clashed with insurgents in the Awasse area. At least 4 militants were reportedly killed in these clashes, with firearms, ammunition, several mortar rounds, and grenades seized from the insurgents.  Insurgents in recent days had reportedly dispatched reinforcements to the area; unconfirmed reports had indicated that security force elements had clashed with militants in the area previously on 20 July.  Sources later indicated troops captured Awasse in these 24 July clashes.  Note that other sources reported significant but unspecified Rwandan casaulties in this fighting.

A suspected insurgent attack reported on the night of 24-25 July at Quintoazi village within Mueda District, just west of the Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) border.  No further details regarding the Quintoazi attack are currently available.

Botswana on 26 July issued a statement saying it was deploying forces on Monday to Cabo Delgado as part of the SADC Standby Force.  Sources later indicated 296 Botswanan troops would be deployed to Moz as part of this SADC force.

President Nyusi in an address to the nation on 25 July confirmed the arrival of SADC troops to the country to help fight insurgency in Cabo Delgado, and the arrival of Rwandan forces since 09 July.  In this address, he also said over 826,000 people had been displaced by terror attacks in Cabo Delgado.  He also said Rwandan and Mozambican troops were already making gains against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  Nyusi did not indicate when SADC troops would arrive in the country.

The Minister of Health, Armando Tiago said the government would install a new oxygen delivery system at the COVID-19 Treatment Center in Quelimane City, Zambezia. The 100-bed capacity facility may increase its numbers of bed in case the number of admitted COVID-19 patients increased.

Maputo City and Tete Province commenced the use of rapid COVID-19 testing for symptomatic COVID cases. The use of rapid testing will help identify positive cases and break the transmission of the virus. These tests will be carried out in the health units of districts and eventually reach communities across the country. Since the rapid test is more cost-efficient than RT-PCR test, many people can gain access to it.

Members of the Association of Combatants of the National Liberation Struggle (ACLLN) in Mueda district accused officials of Provincial Directorate of Economy and Finance of Cabo Delgado of targeting its members in a "scams", allegedly swindling members of money. The officials allegedly demanded 50% of the total pension from a member of ACLLN in exchange to speed up process of disbursing their pension. Security forces said that an investigation is underway to apprehend people connected with the accusations.

The Ministry of Health announced 1,528 new COVID-19 cases and 25 related deaths in Mozambique on 25 July. 632 of the new cases were recorded in  Maputo City, followed by the Inhambane province, with 383 cases. In the last 24 hours, 151 people have recovered while 475 were admitted to the hospital due to the virus.

A source reported that insurgents attacked Nova Familia villages in Nangade district on 21 July. Civilians reportedly fled the area ahead of this attack.  Insurgents the next day also attacked Mandimba.
A source reported that insurgents attacked Mandimba in Nangade district on 22 July. Homes were burned in this attack.

302,400 doses of the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine arrived at the Mavalane International Airport in Maputo today, 26 July. The  vaccines were donated by the United States Government under the COVAX initiative, which facilitates global access to COVID-19 vaccines.. The single dose vaccine has 86% efficacy against severe symptoms of the coronavirus and tested to be effective with the highly transmissible Delta variant of the virus. This is the third batch of the 2,064,000 vaccines from the global COVAX Initiative.

Police arrested a suspect for faking a theft of a million meticais in Maputo city on 26 July. The suspect claimed that he had assistance with two of his friends and claim that the money was stolen by two robbers.

The Center for Public Integrity (CIP) issued a report that two top FRELIMO members own multiple mines in Cabo Delgado. Both members, Raimundo Domingos Pachinuapa and Asghar Fakhraleali owned Mwiriti Mining Company. Pachinuapa owns 60 percent while Fakhraleali with 40 percent of this mine. The mining company currently controls 7% of the mines in the province. CIP stated that the mining company also has indirect shares of the Montepuez Rubi Mining.

President Nyusi says that the at least 28 companies were affected by the insurgents' attacks in the Palma area. Nyusi also said that $116 million has been lost directly to impact of insurgency, while 3,250 workers were affected by the insurgency after the contracts with the gas projects were suspended.
A soldier drowned in the Mwenezi River after getting drunk in Chimoio on 22 July. The victim was traveling to his residence when he fell into the river.

Construction employees protested outside Nampula General hospital demanding their salaries on 23 July. The employees claimed that they have not been paid for two months. Construction at this site has been shut down for at least 2 months.

Sources stated that security forces fear insurgents sleeper cells who disguise themselves as civilians in Cabo Delgado, saying militants may be attempting to infiltrate areas outside of the "war zone".

Zimbabwean industries have raised concerns regarding the insurgency in Mozambique.  There are concerns that the militants could threaten the Beira-Harare pipeline eventually if the insurgency is allowed to continue to expand.

The Ministry of Health Armindo Tiago warned that the country's COVID bed capacity may run out as COVID infection rates remain high. The minister of health has called on the public to adhere COVID precautions. The minister clarified that the bed capacity for COVID inpatients is still less than 70%, however this includes that the bed capacity in Maputo province has already exceeded 100%.
CPLP leaders expressed solidarity with the Mozambique authorities against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado at a recent summit, though did not commit to any "concrete" support.

Footage showing ISCAP fighters gathered together at an undisclosed location was released on 26 July Cabo Delgado.  The video showed that the insurgents were in possession of several heavy machine guns.  A second video also emerged, showing insurgents undergoing hand-to-hand combat training.  Sources later indicated both videos were made at "a much earlier phase" of the insurgency.

The Mozambique Ministry of Health said on 23 July that there were 511 COVID hospitalizations across the country.  A majority of the hospitalizations were in Maputo City with 356 were recorded, while there were 47 COVID patients in Matola, 38 in Sofala, 17 in Tete, 14 in Inhambane, 11 in Zambezia, 10 in Manica, eight in Gaza, seven in Niassa, and three in Nampula.

The Mozambique government announced that they intended to vaccinate 20% of the country's “eligible population” by September. This comes as the 302,400 doses were received by the Ministry of Health as part of the COVAX initiative on Monday. Currently, only 3% was vaccinated as part of the national campaign last March.

The Ministry of Health announced that individuals aged 50 and older will start to be vaccinated starting next week. The vaccination was part of the second phase of vaccinations as 240,000 individuals in the country were to be inoculated.

South African opposition party the Democratic Alliance claimed that as many as 1,495 South African soldiers were already deployed in Mozambique. This statement was later clarified, and the DA said that 1,495 troops was the upper limit of troops that would be allowed to be deployed as part of the Standby Force.

Fires were reported in the north of Mocimboa da Praia on night of 24 July in the Malinde area.  It was unclear what caused these fire clusters, though they could be due to an insurgent attack or clashes between security forces and militants.

Officials announced the recovery of three containers transporting illegally logged wood from Pemba Port. The containers were illegally shipped to China, and was part of a larger group of 76 containers illegally exported to China.

Locals attacked and killed a civilian after the man was accused of theft in Maxixe on 23 July. The victim was later found innocent. Police arrested a civilian involved with the victim’s death. Locals later conducted a search for the thieves.

Locals attacked and killed a civilian after the man was accused of theft in Maxixe on 23 July. The victim was later found innocent. Police arrested a civilian involved with the victim’s death. Locals later conducted a search for the thieves.
Robbers broke into a residence and stole a laptop, two mobile phones, and cash in Maxixe on 22 July. The suspects managed to escape.
Mozambican helicopters were reported to have provided air support to Mozambican security forces and Rwandan troops who attacked insurgent positions in Awasse on 24 July.
Security forces exchanged gunfire with insurgents in Diaca, southwest of Mocimboa da Praia, on 18 July. No further information on these clashes are currently available.

The German government donated 26 million EUR for the humanitarian response in Cabo Delgado. The donation was made through the WFP. WFP stated that the funds will allow the provision of aid for 290,000 individuals.

the Attorney General of the Republic, Beatriz Buchili stated the government has set up a new Central Organized and Transnational Crime Cabinet. The team will deal exclusively with crimes such as drug, weapons, human, and organ trafficking.

The Angolan parliament unanimously on 27 July approved deploying 20 military advisers and a IL 76 type aircraft to assist Mozambique in combating the Cabo Delgado insurgency for a three month deployment.  The troops will include 2 officers in the Regional Coordination Mechanism, eight officers for the "Force Command" and 10 personnel to operate the aircraft.  This is the first time Angola's parliament has been asked to approve a deployment, after unilateral executive deployments of troops to several other African conflicts.  This small group of troops will be part of the SADC Standby Force.  The troops will reportedly be deployed on 29 July.

Locals in Inhassoro District on 27 July blocked the N1 road with tree branches, bushes, and signs, protesting against an oil and gas company operating in the area over a lack of employment for local youths.   The protest lasted for about an hour and stopped traffic in the area.  Locals said the oil and gas company was not honoring an agreement made with local associations to employ locals.  About 200 locals are employed by the project in the area.

On 27 July, Mozambique confirmed 1,703 new COVID cases, along with 34 new COVID deaths - the most deaths from COVID reported in a single day in the country during the pandemic.  862 new cases were reported in Maputo City, with 270 reported in Maputo Province.  There are currently 473 COVID hospitalizations in the country, along with 26,003 active cases.

Sources indicated that in fighting on 23 July, Rwandan troops killed 26 insurgents and captured 2 others at Mandela village in Muidumbe District.  Rwandan soldiers reportedly surprised the militants as they were preparing a meal.  This came after insurgents attacked at least three villages south of Namacande between 17-20 July, killing at least 3 people.

Rwandan soldiers reportedly surprised the militants as they were preparing a meal.  This came after insurgents attacked at least three villages south of Namacande between 17-20 July, killing at least 3 people.

The Ministry of Health announced 1,435 new COVID cases and 25 new related deaths in Mozambique on 26 July. The cases were as follows: 622 in Maputo City, 209 in Maputo province, 187 in Niassa, 185 in Inhambane, 136 in Gaza, 49 in Sofala, 18 in Nampula, 11 in Tete, 10 from Manica, 6 in Zambezia, and 2 from Cabo Delgado.

Police assaulted two journalists working for the Catandica Community Radio in Manica on 23 July. Both journalists were covering a dispute between the sellers and municipal police regarding tax collection. This comes as repots of police were forcibly collecting new taxes from the sellers.

Manica police were reportedly forcibly collecting taxes from street vendors in Catandica on 23 July. The incident was being covered by two journalist who were assaulted by police. This comes as street vendors were asked to pay 500 meticais a month.

Former RENAMO general Herminio Morais warned that insurgents may change tactics as foreign troops arrive in Cabo Delgado. Morais said that during the Civil War, when Zimbabwean troops intervened to assist FRELIMO, RENAMO guerillas split into smaller groups and spread out across a wider geographical area, and were able to recruit more effectively.  Morais said insurgents could mimic these tactics, potentially spreading into Nampula and Niassa.

The National Migration Service announced the new Ressano Garcia operating hours from 06:00 to 21:00; previously the border crossing had closed down at 2000hrs. The new timings were to adapt to the border timings of South Africa as part of their restrictive measures.  Trucks transporting goods can continue to use the border crossing up to 2300hrs.
The Ministry of Health announced that health officials have stopped contact tracing for COVID patients as COVID-19 cases have risen significantly in across the country over the past month.

Unconfirmed reports on 27 July said that Rwandan soldiers had suffered casualties in recent days in some of the ongoing clashes in Cabo Delgado, though no specific details regarding these casualties were available. Rwandan troops in the past week have been involved in clashes in Palma, Muidumbe, and MDP Districts and have also reportedly been deployed to Macomia District as well.

The South African parliament issued a statement saying that the South African National Defense Force (SANDF) was to conduct operations in Mozambique from 15 July to 15 October. The operation was under their responsibility as a member of the SADC and was authorized under the defense act of the South African Constitution.  Up to 1,495 troops may be used for this operation.  The expected funding to be used during the operations was at  984,368,057R, or over $66 million.  South African President Ramaphosa on 28 July later confirmed that a force of up to 1,495 troops had been authorized for deployment to Mozambique.

Sources stated that 50 Rwandan soldiers had been deployed to the Chai village area on 26 July. The security deployment comes after an insurgent attack in the area. The Rwandan forces were reportedly tasked with clearing insurgents from the area and reopening the road between Chai and Awasse.
Insurgents reportedly attacked Chai Village on 25 July. Insurgents reportedly destroyed two vehicles in this raid.  Other sources reported this attack occurred on 26 July.
Insurgents on 24 July were reported to have attacked Panjele village, north of Diaca, killing an unknown number of civilians and setting homes on fire during the attack.

Security forces recaptured the villages of Diaca, Roma, and Nanili along with the Awasse crossroads after gunfire exchanges with insurgents during operations on 24 July.  Skirmishes at these three villages reportedly took place while heavier fighting was reported at Awasse.

Mozambican security forces along with Rwandan troops as reported on 25 July to be conducting patrols along the Palma-Quionga road and Palma-Pundanhar road to clear these areas of militants.

President Nyusi said in a speech on 25 July that the districts of Mocimboa da Praia, Macomia, Muidumbe, Quissanga, and Palma lacked even basic health services due to the ongoing impact of the insurgency in these districts.

ISCAP reportedly claimed to have clashed with Mozambican troops on this day at Awasse and to have killed several soldiers, though this was unverified.

1 million Sinopharm vaccines arrived in Mozambique on the night of 27 July. This was the single largest batch of vaccines received so far by Mozambique during the ongoing pandemic, and comes just after the country on Monday received over 300,000 doses of the Johnson and Johnson COVID vaccine.
President Nyusi met with DRC Minister of Regional Integration Mukangzu, discussing the DRC President's support for the Mozambique president as the candidate for the SADC Executive Secretary.

The National Health Institute Director Jani denied reports of a shortage in PCR test in the country. Jani clarified the country has 86,000 PCR tests and 904,525 rapid antigen tests.  Recent reports had indicated that large numbers of people going to hospitals across the country to take a COVID-19 test had been turned away.
The US appointed Peter Hendrick Vrooman as the new US Ambassador to Mozambique on 27 July. Vrooman was previously the US Ambassador to Rwanda.

On 28 July, Mozambique confirmed 2,437 new COVID cases, along with 26 new COVID deaths.  This new case total is the highest single day total during the pandemic in Mozambique.  This includes 916 cases in Maputo City, and 466 in Maputo Province.  There are now 484 hospitalized COVID cases, and 28,092 active cases throughout the country.

The Mozambican businessman/politician Zaid Ali passed away in Beira early morning of 28 July. Ali was a known former member of FRELIMO and the owner of the Hotel Mozamcabique in Beira.

Local officials announced the suspension of all classes in Maxixe of Inhambane for the next 12 days on 27 July. The suspension was due to the extended measures against COVID. This comes as other cities have suspended school activities due to the pandemic.
The WFP stated that 370 IDPs arrived at Matemo island on 15 July after fleeing the ongoing insurgency.

Sources stated that public transportation still lacks social distancing measures which have not yet been defined by the Ministry of Transport and Communications. This includes trains, boats, and air transportation across the country.. Sources stated that buses still remain overcrowded and long lines were still notable at terminals.

The Mozambique government dismissed the Competition Regulatory Authority Chairman Julio Joao Pio on 27 July. This was due accusations that fair market competition was not being maintained. A Chinese-owner company was reportedly driving out their competitors by selling cheap products.
The Mozambique government has reportedly received a total of 1.7 million doses of COVID vaccine doses since March.  Mozambique hopes to vaccinate 20% of its eligible population by September.

Sources stated that on 22 July that 10 schools were reopening in Meluco District of Cabo Delgado that had previously been affected by the insurgency.  No recent attacks have been reported recently in the district.
Insurgents attacked a village of Namade, south Muidumbe, on 19 July. 3 civilians were killed.
Rwandan security forces reportedly received several armored personnel carriers in Mueda for a potential assault on Mocimboa da Praia on or before 25 July.

The National Institute for Risk and Disaster Management (INGD) announced the reduction of IDPs arriving at Pemba on 28 July. INGD officials stated that the decline in displaced individuals may indicate the return of stability in parts of the province that had been affected by the insurgency.

An unknown man detained and assaulted his wife before setting her on fire in Nampula province on 26 July.  The victim was critically injured and the suspect managed to escape after the crime.  The woman later died of her injuries.

Zimbabwean Defense Minister Oppah Muchiguri Kashiri said on 29 July that Harare would deploy 304 soldiers as part of the SADC Standby Force to fight the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  It was not immediately clear when these troops would be deployed, though this could take place within the next 1 week.  The troops will reportedly be non-combat troops and will provide military training to Mozambique security forces.

RENAMO Military Junta Leader Mariano Nhongo in an interview on 29 July said that he was willing to engage in talks with the government to negotiate peace, but was unwilling to speak with RENAMO leadership or with the UN's envoy to Mozambique, Mirko Manzoni.  Nhongo also said he would reject talks with Andre Matsangaissa Jr., who previously was a member of the Military Junta before defecting, calling Matsangaissa a "traitor".  Nhongo also said he was unbothered by defections from his group, and said he had enough fighters to be able to carry out new attacks, though also said he does not want to launch new attacks.  This is Nhongo's first reported interview with a media outlet and first public statement since April.
On 24 July, Rwandan security forces ambushed insurgents on a motorcycle between Mbau and Awasse, killing 2 militants
On 28 July while Rwandan security forces repelled a militant attack on RDF positions near Awasse, resulting in one militant killed.

Insurgents ambushed of Rwandan security forces between Awasse and Mueda on 28 July; this ambush was thwarted and two insurgents were killed. Rwandan Military Spokesman Colonel Ronald Rwivanga stated that a total of 14 sub-machine guns, 5 RPGs, 2 pistols, and 1 medium machine gun were captured during the past engagements with insurgents between 24-28 July.

The Ministry of Health announced 21 new COVID deaths and 1774 new COVID infections in Mozambique on 29 July. Maputo City registered the highest number of cases with 779 and Maputo province with 336 cases. This comes as 74 of the cases were hospitalized and 36 discharged.

The Zimbabwean Presidential Spokesman Charamba stated that the public will not be informed regarding the arrival of Zimbabwe Defence Forces (ZDF) units  in Cabo Delgado. Charamba posted on social media that the ZDF will not deploy in the “full glare” of the media. This comes as reports of Zimbabwean Defense Minister Oppah Muchiguri Kashiri said on 29 July that Harare would deploy 304 soldiers as part of the SADC Standby Force.  This presumably indicates Zimbabwe will not publicly disclose the date it will deploy troops to Cabo Delgado, though this deployment is likely within the coming days.

The French government reportedly will finance the Rwandan intervention in Cabo Delgado, sources reported this week. The French government has also offered to finance the Zimbabwe deployment. The funding comes as the EU, UK, and US have renewed weapon sanctions against Zimbabwe, putting potential French funding of a Zim operation in Mozambique in doubt. This report comes after France was reported to be reluctant to deploy forces to Cabo Delgado after its recent experiences in fighting an insurgency in the Sahel.  Paris however still reportedly sought to intervene in some form in Mozambique to help protect French company Total's investment in the country.

The Mozambique government has agreed to begin a large trial of new COVID vaccines in the country. The trial will test if Sinopharm and AstraZeneca vaccines could be used alternately/effectively for the first and second doses. The trial was funded by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) to determine the mixed use of vaccines to resolve shortages of supplies of various vaccines.

Media sources on 28 July reported that the humanitarian situation on Ibo island is worsening as more IDPs arrive on the island. The island is used as an alternative resettlement area by the IDPs intending to flee the insurgency.
Insurgents attacked the villages of Mandimba near Nangade early morning of 26 July. The insurgents were abducted several civilians in the villages.
Insurgents attacked Chacamba on 27 July, killing an unknown number of civilians and setting homes on fire.
Insurgents reportedly abducted civilians from the areas of Mandimba and Chacamba near Nangade on 27 July July.

Insurgents reportedly threatened to conduct an attack targeting Nangade town on 25 July. The threat was conducted during the celebration of the 35th anniversary of the town.  Militants were driven away from the area on 26 July, though no attack on Nangade ever materialized.
Pro-government militiamen exchanged gunfire with insurgents at Chai on 25 July. Casualties were no specified. The incident was response to the attack by insurgents on the village.
Insurgents reportedly killed two people in an attack near Chai Village on 22 July.

A group of five armed robbers disguised as civilians stole cash from the BCI Central in Quelimane at around 15:00 on 29 July.  The thieves reportedly broke into the bank when it was closed, and bank employees said they "didn't hear anything at all", though other bank employees were threatened with a firearm during the robbery. The suspects managed to escape from the area after the robbery.

A court in Pemba sentenced the former Pemba Mayor, Carimo for two years for corruption charges on 30 July. Carimo's sentence however was converted into a fine and he is not expected to serve any jail time.

The African Development Bank (AFDB) announced that they would provide 44 million USD to fund two projects in Mozambique on 30 July. The projects were for climate resilience and agriculture in Inhambane and Gaza provinces.

On 30 July, Mozambique confirmed 2,290 new COVID cases, along with 19 new COVID deaths.  This is the second highest daily case total in Mozambique during the pandemic after 28 July's 2,460 cases.  737 new cases were reported in Maputo City, along with 422 new cases in Maputo.  32.4% of all COVID test results received on 30 July were positive for the virus.  58 new hospitalizations were reported, and there are now 30,458 active cases of the virus in the country.

Botswanan troops on 30 July were reported to be deploying to Cabo Delgado via road routes, driving through Central Mozambique.  Sources had previously reported Botswana's troops had already been deployed to Cabo Delgado.
Municipal police and INAE teams began removing street seller stalls along the Maquinino in Beira on the evening of 29 July.

Police deployed along the Avenida Armando Tivane of Beira on the morning of Friday, 30 July. The deployment was to prevent illegal street vendors from reoccupying spaces. This comes as security forces cleared the avenues from the vendors a day before.
SERNIC arrested and assaulted several bank employees from BCI Central in Quelimane on the night of 29 July after the bank was robbed by armed suspects earlier in the day.

Defense Minister Jaime Neto stated that insurgents are being “slaughtered” in Cabo Delgado as a result of ongoing security operations. The defense minister also said insurgent casualties were difficult to tally though there were significant insurgent losses in recent weeks.

Mozambique's Defense Minister Jaime Neto announced on 30 July that the SADC stand-by forces were expected to join operations in Cabo Delgado this coming week, early August. The minister stated that also stated that the Botswana security forces were in the process of arriving into Cabo Delgado and that the Angolan forces were partially deployed in the country

Reports on 31 July indicated that human traffickers are active in Tete, using semi-collective passenger transport drivers as well as owners of some houses, as well as enlisting "influential people" to facilitate their activities.

The Ministry of Health confirmed 2,078 new COVID cases, along with 27 new COVID deaths in Mozambique on 31 July. 681 new cases were reported in Maputo City followed by  348 new cases in Maputo province.  48.2% of all COVID test results received on 30 July were positive for the virus.  53 new hospitalizations and  15 hospital discharges were reported, while 299 patients recovered from the virus.

Some people in Maxaquene neighborhood are reported to be violating curfew in Maputo as well as in other outskirts neighborhoods of the capital. Some people are seen walking, selling in the neighborhood around 2100hrs.

Inhambane province plans to vaccinate more than 60,000 people against COVID-19 as part of the second phase of the vaccination project starting on 04 August. The immunization will target people over 50 years-old, as well as teachers and other civil workers who have not been vaccinated during the first stage.
Reports on 01 August stated that at least four people die each month in Maputo City due to hepatitis. Around 260 cases of the illness were registered at the Maputo Central Hospital per year.

An fuel spill was reported at the Pemba Bay on 31 July. A source claimed that at least 10,000L of fuel have spilled. Petromoc company denied involvement with the spill and claimed that authorities would have informed them if it was the company's fault.
Reports on 01 August indicated that a mechanized brigade of the South African National Defence Force had crossed into Mozambique via Ressano Border Post, travelling to Cabo Delgado.

The Ministry of Health confirmed 1,513 new COVID cases, along with 28 new COVID deaths in Mozambique on 01 Aug. All new cases result from local transmission, 1,504 of which are Mozambicans and nine are foreign nationals. 496 new cases were reported in Maputo City followed by  361 new cases in Maputo province. 70 new hospitalizations and  40 hospital discharges were reported, while 2,465 patients recovered from the virus.

Locals captured three suspected insurgents in Nova Zambezia, Macomia district in the afternoon of 31 July, and handed them over to the Defense and Security Forces (FDS) positioned in the district. Reports claimed that the insurgents escaped from ongoing military operations.

Locals captured two suspected insurgents in the villages of V Congresso and Chai, Macomia district on 26 July, and handed them over to the local militia. Reports indicated that the suspects were executed amid confessing  that they were victims and escaped from the insurgents' den.

Pro-government militia on or around 26 July were reported to have executed an insurgent in Chai village after local civilians captured the man in the area.  The insurgent suspect was reported to have claimed to have escaped after being held captive by the insurgents.

The two claimed to have escaped after being held captive by the insurgents. A stray bullet fired by insurgents killed a person near Namiune village, Nangade on 30 July. The incident took place while insurgents were being pursued by Rwandan and Mozambican security forces.

Insurgents reportedly intercepted a vessel carrying displaced people Muichanga Island, off the MDP coast, on 29 July.  One source reported all IDPs on board were killed, while another source reported they were abducted.

Insurgents are reportedly recruiting young people from the districts of Ngauma, Muembe and Nipepe in Niassa Province, a new Institute of Social and Economic Studies report indicated. Recruiters allegedly take advantage on the financial status of the victims' families and commit a job in Maputo City, before they are later brought into bush areas by the insurgents.
