Pro-government militia were reported on 01 August to be pursuing insurgents in the Mtipuedi area.  Insurgents retreated to this area in Southern Nangade after clashes with Rwandan and Mozambican security forces on 30 July in the Nova Familia area.

Local hunters found two beheaded bodies in a swamp near Nova Familia, Nangade on 12 June. A source claimed that the victims were insurgents killed by security forces, however, insurgents are more likely to have killed the two as they regularly behead victims.
Around 0500hrs on 31 July, suspicious individuals reportedly stole a large amount of fuel in Pemba Port. In still unclear circumstances, this stolen fuel later was spilled into the waters off Pemba.

On 31 July, President Nyusi announced that no elephants have been poached in the Niassa National Reserve or in the Gorongosa National Park, Sofala for the third consecutive year. He attributed this development to the combined efforts of security forces, forestry and wildlife rangers, and the local communities, in the fight against environmental crimes.

On 30 July, Minister of Public Works, Housing and Water Resources, Joao Machatine, announced a USD200 million investment by the Mozambican Government to improve access roads in Cabo Delgado Province.

Mozambican forces and Rwandan forces recovered three AK-47 weapons, and around two hundred rounds ammunition from a vehicle in Mueda district on 01 August.  The weapons were reportedly disassembled and concealed in a suitcase.  It was unclear if any arrests were made in connection with the incident.

Unidentified men set fire to a school and a church in the district of Cuamba on the evening of 29 July. The facilities were completely burnt down. No casualties were reported in the incident.  It is unclear if the incident was related to the ongoing insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

The SAS Makhanda of the South African National Defence Force (SANDF) arrived into Pemba Bay on 01 August. The strike craft is part of the small maritime contingent of the SADC’s intervention brigade in Mozambique to combat insurgents in Cabo Delgado. Other sources reported an Air Force Cessna Caravan light aircraft arrived to Pemba last week.  Two SA Cargo planes meanwhile in recent weeks have transported special forces units to Pemba.  Elements of the 43rd SANDF Brigade have also begun to deploy to Cabo Delgado.

On 01 August, Interior Minister Amade Miquidade criticized police forces on how they deal with the civilians. He said that the officers must not intimidate the public and should earn their trust instead.

Security officials in Manica said on 01 August that around 328 cubic meters of smuggled timber were seized from January to June 2021. The smuggled wood was seized in Machaze, Macossa, Barue, Guro, and from the Chimoio area.

Saipem CEO/GM Francesco Caio  on 02 August said that the company believed it could be possible for work on the LNG project in Cabo Delgado was expected to resume in the first half of 2022.  Work was suspended on the project in April after insurgents assaulted Palma, outside of the Afungi Peninsula.

On the morning of 02 August, SERNIC recovered  8 million Meticais in Chimoio which was part of an amount of money stolen from BCI Quelimane last week. The seizure came after security forces reportedly established checkpoints in Save area to apprehend criminals, however, no arrests were reported.

Palestine asked Mozambique on 28 July to oppose the recent decision to accept Israel as an Observer State of the African Union. Aside from Palestine, Botswana, Namibia and Algeria also opposes the decision and said that Israel can only have observer status in the AU once it no longer occupies Palestine.

Mozambique received another 500,000 doses of the Chinese-manufactured VeroCell COVID-19 vaccine today, 02 August. The vaccines are part of the 11 million doses of vaccines recently acquired by the government. These doses will be used in next phase of Mozambique's immunization campaign which will commence on 04 August.

The Ministry of Health confirmed 1,421 new COVID cases, along with 17 new COVID deaths in Mozambique on 02 Aug. 364 new cases were reported in Maputo City followed by  310 in Maputo province, 257 in Niassa, 194 in Gaza, 143 in Sofala province, 106 in Inhambane, 20 in Zambezia, 11 in Tete, 10 in Manica and six in the province of Manica. 56 new hospitalizations and  44 hospital discharges were reported.

On 30 July, President Nyusi inaugurated the Matchedje solar power station. The station has the capacity of 200 kilowatt peak which can supply power to around 400 households. This is part of the government's interventions to improve electricity access in the rural areas.

President Nyusi said on 03 August that the government would could be forced to impose more anti-COVID restrictions in a bid to curb the spread of COVID-19 in the country. He urged the public to strictly adhere with the safety protocols so that the government does not need to impose any new measures, which he said would impact the country's development.

A family accused Hospital Privado de Maputo of extortion. Reports suggest that the hospital continued to charge a patient even after the patient had died. The family of the deceased victim claimed that the hospital demanded they pay a certain amount before they can retrieve the body of the victim.
Unconfirmed reports on 31 July indicate that small groups of insurgents have recently fled into Niassa province via public transport.

On 29 July, a petition was submitted SADC truck drivers association to Zambia authorities regarding the presence of unnecessary road blocks in Mozambique, as well as DRC  and Zambia. In addition, officers manning border posts in Casacatiza, Tete and Machipanda, Manica were accused of extorting drivers before allowing them to pass through the checkpoints.

Unconfirmed reports indicated that RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo stated on 30 July said that the RENAMO Military Junta is in "positions from Rovuma to Maputo". And that his group would not allow elections in Central Mozambique in 2024 if there was no "serious dialogue".

An investigation into a fuel spill in Pemba Bay over the weekend reported on 03 August that 5,000 liters were spilled in the bay, and that 300 square meters were impacted by the spill, though the origin of the spill was still unclear.  Some sources indicated a pipeline leak was the cause of the incident, while other information indicated individuals stole the fuel and then later spilled it at sea.

Mozambican and Rwandan Forces were confirmed to have control of the Awasse area on 03 August following clashes with insurgents in the area. Government troops released a video on 03 August confirming that they are in control of the area. This development came after joint forces launched an offensive against insurgents in the village between 24-28 July.  Fighting were reported again in Awasse and areas south of the village on 02 August.

Unconfirmed reports on 03 August of Tanzanian insurgents fleeing towards Tanzania, fleeing an ongoing offensive by security forces in MDP District. Tanzanian authorities meanwhile recommenced an operation in the Kibiti area where several Tanzanian insurgents had originally come from.

The Ministry of Health announced on 02 August the beginning of pre-booking for a new phase of vaccinations in the country. Apart from the electronic registration, authorities established more than 40 pre-registration posts in Maputo City.

A recently released analysis of the current situation in Cabo Delgado predicts that the Southern African Development Community (SADC) military deployment in Cabo Delgado is likely to extend through 2022 but unlikely to defeat insurgency in the province. It was said that the insurgency status will likely to stabilize due to a predicted lack of coordination between Mozambican, Rwandan, and SADC troops.

Renamo Military Junta Leader, Mariano Nhongo, claimed on 03 August that he and his fighters were frequently targeted by "bombardment" launched by Mozambican military in Gorongosa mountains. He added that he is still waiting for talks to start with the government however, he said  that he is against the participation of RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade or former RENAMO dissident Andre Matsangaissa.

International Monetary Fund (IMF) support for Mozambique still on hold, IMF rep to Mozambique Alexis Meyer Cirkel said, as the two sides have not reached an agreement on resuming direct support. Support was previously suspended in 2016 because of the US$2.2 billion ‘hidden debts’ scandal.
Security forces arrested a suspect on or before 31 July over alleged involvement in a recent arson incident in Cuamba. A school and a church were completely consumed by fire.

Authorities announced on 02 August that the vaccinations drivers and collectors of public transport for passengers, including motorcycles and bicycles, people aged over 50, state agents and teachers who have not been immunized in previous campaigns will be held on 04 August. The target population should pre-register and proceed to vaccination sites on the scheduled dates.

Reports from Cabo Delgado indicate that a growing number of HIV/AIDs patients are not taking their antiretroviral treatments due to fears that they will be stigmatized and discriminated against the society. About 160,000 people are living with HIV in Cabo Delgado province, and 9,600 of which were recorded last year.

A national mass vaccination campaign was launched against COVID on 04 August at Josina Machel High School, in Maputo. The campaign will include vaccinations at all provincial capitals and district headquarters in the country. Target population are individuals aged over 50, employees and agents of the state, drivers and collectors of passenger transport.

Members of the Mozambican cabinet approved a Policy and Strategy for the Management of Internally Displaced Persons in Cabo Delgado on 03 August. The said policy is meant to streamline and better organize the government's response to the ongoing IDP crisis and improve the provision of aid to IDPs; to date, NGOs have been the primary providers of aid to IDPs in Cabo Delgado.

On 03 August, the Mozambican parliament approved the presence of foreign military troops in the country to support the fight against insurgents in Cabo Delgado. However, opposition parties reiterated that President Nyusi violated the Constitution by not asking for Parliament's authorization for the foreign deployment.

ISCAP claimed to have attacked Pangane village in a raid on 22 July.  The group claimed a number of a number of Christian militia members were killed in the attack and their homes set on fire. This claim remains unconfirmed.

On 03 August, security forces announced the arrest of a 53 year old Chinese citizen in Chimoio for illegal possession of a firearm. A  Brazilian Tauros pistol and three ammunition clips are recovered from his possession.

On 03 August, security forces announced the arrest of  a suspect in Vanduzi for allegedly transporting 150 kilos of semi-precious stones. The stones were later seized. An investigation into the incident has been launched.

The Ministry of Health confirmed 1,429 new COVID cases, along with 21 new COVID deaths in Mozambique on 03 Aug. 595 new cases were reported in Maputo City followed by  209 in Gaza province. Over the last 24 hours, 62 new hospitalizations and  35 hospital discharges were reported.

A Tanzanian military aircraft was seen unloading military equipment, including weapons and vehicles, at the Pemba Airport on 01 and 02 August. The aircraft was made a series of flights between Mozambique and Tanzania during the mentioned time period. Reports indicated that Tanzania is sending a team of 100 soldiers to fight insurgency in Cabo Delgado, however, this development has yet been confirmed.

Former President Joaquim Chissano expressed concerns over the quality of education plummeted in universities, which resulted to college graduates without adequate knowledge, during a conference at the Pedagogical University in Maputo.

Reports on 03 August indicate that many Mozambicans still do not know how to pre-register or even the start of the immunization campaign. Citizens lack of knowledge should be addressed as the start of massive immunization campaign against COVID-19 commences on 04 August.

The Aga Khan foundation was reported to have donated three million meticais-worth of medical-surgical and laboratory equipment to help fight COVID-19 in Cabo Delgado province on 03 August. The donation is funded by the Canadian Government. The materials donated include masks, mattresses, gloves, hygiene material and sample collection among others.

Health minister Armindo Tiago expressed concern on 03 July over the issue of African countries receiving COVID-19 vaccines shortly before their expiration date which resulted to urgently vaccinate  many people in a very limited time. He added this compromises effectiveness of the vaccination campaigns.

Only 2.4 percent of the target population or 400,000 people have taken the COVID-19 vaccine in Mozambique. President Nyusi appealed to all targeted citizens to  be present at the vaccination posts as scheduled as authorities prepares to speed up the vaccination process.

On 04 August, Interior Minister Amade Miquidade claimed that insurgents in Cabo Delgado were also involved in illegal mining activities and in different forms of trafficking in the province. He directed all police units to intensify operations against illegal immigrants and miners to prevent insurgents to expand their operations to other provinces in the country.

United Nations disclosed that Islamic State's cells often expand activities across several neighboring countries, saying this had occurred from Mozambique to Tanzania.  He did not elaborate on the insurgency spreading into Tanzania, though many of the group's members are reportedly Tanzanian, and insurgents did launch a series of attacks into Tanzania late in 2020.

Zimbabwe is prepared to work with Rwanda to exchange information on the progress in Cabo Delgado Province.  This presumably will include military intelligence gathered by their respective militaries as they operate in Cabo Delgado.

Mozambique Airlines recorded a 10 percent increase of passengers from June compared to May this year. The airlines transported 37,952 passengers in June, against the 34,582 figure for May. The five most popular routes were Maputo-Nampula, Maputo-Beira, Maputo-Tete, Maputo-Pemba, and Maputo-Quelimane.
A Botswana Defence Force member was killed in a road accident in Pemba on 03 August. An investigation into the incident has been launched.
Security forces reportedly are demand 1000 meticals for motorists travelling through Metuge, sources reported on 03 August.

Former President Joaquim Chissano on 04 August urged the Mozambican Government to consider negotiations with insurgents in Cabo Delgado. Chissano said a leader of the group could be identified and a dialogue begun that could potentially end the conflict.

President Nyusi said on the morning of 04 August that more than 54% percent of Mozambique's population or 16,000,000 will be vaccinated during the National Mass Vaccination campaign against COVID-19. The mass campaign commenced on Wednesday.

Mozambique's Parliament's Standing Commission announced on 03 August that the debate on the presence of foreign troops in Mozambique won't be held until second half of October. The debate will be part of the agenda on the next ordinary sitting. The opposition party, Renamo, accused President Nyusi of violating the Constitution by inviting and accepting foreign troops into the country without the prior approval of the Assembly.

Pictures emerged on 04 August showing arms and ammunition seized by security forces in Awasse which reportedly fell to security forces in late July. Among the recovered weaponry included AK 47 and AK 49 weapons with cartridges, and several RPGs.

Chaos reported in Maputo City during the first day of the National Mass Vaccination Campaign against COVID-19 on 04 August. Residents said there was no organization on the part of the vaccination teams and that citizens waited for more than five hours without getting any vaccinations.

Renamo, the main opposition party in the country, has called for a debate in the parliament to discuss the entry of foreign troops in the country. The party accused President Nyusi of violating the Constitution by inviting and accepting foreign troops into the country without the prior approval of the Assembly. The Parliament's Standing Commission responded that the debate on the issue won't be held until second half of October.

Mozambique Electricity (EDM) said that the electricity substation at Awasse must be completely rebuilt after insurgents destroyed the station and its equipment after controlling Awasse for almost a year.  Northern Cabo Delgado has been without electricity since August of 2020 when insurgents captured the area, forcing reliance on generators in the north.

The World Food Program warned that the ongoing food crisis situation in Cabo Delgado could worsen in the coming months due to lack of international support, also saying the WFP could be forced to suspend food aid to IDPs in Cabo Delgado without new funding support in December.  Food aid in July and August was reduced to one basic food basket per family due to a lack of funding. Reports suggest that at least USD93 million is need to provide adequate aid to more than 800,000 IDPs in the province through December of this year.

The Ministry of Health confirmed 1,034 new COVID cases, along with 26 new COVID deaths in Mozambique on 04 Aug. 302 new cases were reported in Maputo City followed by 146 in Sofala province, 132 in Maputo Province, 119 in Gaza, 140 in Zambezia, 59 in Nampula, 51 in Inhambane, 47 in Manica, 30 in Tete, five in Cabo Delgado and four in Niassa. Over the last 24 hours, 66 new hospitalizations and 62 hospital discharges were reported.

In the early hours of 03 August, Mozambican Police intercepted a vehicle and recovered 2 million Meticais in Zimpeto. The seized money, which was concealed in the lining of the vehicle, was allegedly part of an amount of money stolen from BCI Quelimane, Zambezia last week. Three individuals aboard the vehicle were also arrested.  The seizure came after security forces received credible information on the suspicious movement of the suspects attempting to leave the city.

Media sources indicated that Mozambican military commanders were "annoyed" by reports that Rwandan troops had recent killed 30 insurgents near Quitunda, saying these reports were false and only meant to "promote" the image of Rwandan forces operating in Cabo Delgado.  This may refer to reports of insurgents killed near Quionga, as several sources reported Rwandan troops killed a large number of militants near Quionga on 20 July.

Officials of the Maputo Central Hospital said that their emergency service has been under high pressure since the start of the COVID-19 third wave. The hospital received more than 500 patients a day while some staff were also infected by the coronavirus. Citizens were urged to  go to the health centers with closer proximity to their houses, in a bid to decongest the largest hospital in the country

Mozambican public expenditure increased by 12% from the first half of 2021 compared to the same period on 2020. The expenditure reached 165,852.9 million meticais from January-June 2021 against 141,873.2 million meticais from January-June 2020.
Sources on 05 August reported that the ground and air operations of the Mozambican and Rwandan forces continues as they are nearing the town of Mocimboa da Praia.

Cabo Delgado Governor Valige Tauabo plans to immunize 121,000 with the vaccines against COVID-19 during the mass vaccinations which began on 04 August. The first phase of the campaign will target people aged over 50 , teachers, drivers and ticket collectors in passenger transport vans, motorcyclists, former combatants and civil servants.

Mozambican and Rwandan Forces confirmed control of the Diaca area following fierce clashes with insurgents in the area on 02 August.  This development came after joint troops launched an offensive against insurgents in the village and nearby areas, including Awasse, between 24-28 July.  Note that previous reports indicated troops were in control of Diaca since 24 July. Another report claimed that five villages in the area during combined force operations.

More than 80% of the hidden debt assets of USD 2.2 billion, illegally contracted between 2013 and 2014, arel yet to be recovered six years after the case was opened. The Central Asset Recovery Office, only managed to recover 15.6 percent of the total amount in question.  Recovered assets include 19 seized properties, 81 vehicles, 14 motrobikes, 4 vessels, and about 615 million meticais.

The quantity  of mining concessions granted in Cabo Delgado has increased by four times amid the insurgency. 46 mining projects were granted licenses in the province from 2017-2021 compared to 67 licenses granted in the past 14 years.

Hundreds of street sellers are working in poor conditions in Maquinino and Goto markets, Beira City after street stalls were removed by authorities last week. Stalls were removed as it reportedly contributed to the spread of COVID-19. Aside from the coronavirus, overcrowded markets can also contribute in the sread of orher contagious diseases such as cholera.

Sources reported that a joint Mozambican-Rwandan forces on 04 August had began a new attack on the insurgents' "Syria 2" camp, a mobile bush camp the insurgents have long operated near the Messalo River.  The exact location of the camp currently is unclear though is believed to be located within the vicinity of Mbau and the northern banks of the Messalo River.  Unconfirmed reports previously indicated shelling had targeted this base on 02 August.
Reports on 03 August indicate that a squadron of South African Rooivalk helicopters had been deployed to Pemba.
Mozambican helicopters reportedly targeted insurgent positions in Awasse on 26 July, providing support to ground troops attacking militants in the area. No information on casualties.
Rwandan troops launched an ambush targeting a small group of insurgents in Chinda on 27 July. Two insurgents were killed.

Reports indicate that Rwandan troops suffered heavy casualties during the offensive near Awasse. Flights bound to Kigali from Afungi were reported on 25-26 July to be transporting injured Rwandan soldiers. The exact number of Rwandan casualties has yet been determined.  Rwandan meanwhile has only aknowledged one soldier injured in the Awasse clashes.
Three local militia members were reportedly killed by insurgents during an attack in Nampuida, Palma on 24 July, ISCAP claimed.
ISCAP claimed its militants attacked a Mozambican government patrol in Chai on 28 July. This claim is currently unconfirmed.

ISCAP claimed to have killed a Mozambican soldier and injured another one during clashes in Mandava on 31 July. Identification documents of a soldier was seized by the insurgents.  Other sources reported a clash in Mandava on 01 August that left several soldiers killed; this is believed to refer to the same incident.

Humanitarian conditions in Macomia town has reportedly continued to improve in recent months. Nurses are now travelling from Pemba to the town three times a week to provide medical services in the area. An ambulance was also stationed in the town to take emergency patients to Pemba.

Sweden provided an additional USD 5 million to Mozambique Electricity (EDM) on 04 August to help  increase power coverage in Vilanculos district,  Inhambane. A total of USD 44 million has been donated by the Swedish government to provide over 100,000 families access to clean and reliable energy in the district.

Joint Mozambican-Rwandan forces on 04 August reportedly clashed with insurgents at Mamu village, about 9 kms east of Awasse along the N380 road, reportedly driving insurgents out of the area; satellite imaging from 04 August showed fires just west of Mamu as well as at least one fire within the village itself.  Note two other sources reported these clashes took place on 03 August.

The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) arrested a Congolese citizen and seized 400kg of crystal meth during an operation in Fomento of Matola, west of Maputo City, on 4 August. The operation was conducted after locals contacted authorities regarding the buried narcotics in the suspect's backyard. The suspect confessed that his employer and owner of the residence was in South Africa during the time of the operation.

Sources stated that COVID infections and deaths have reached peak levels across Africa in the last week of July. This comes as cases in the region have increased by 19%. The WHO regional office for Africa stated that the third wave of COVID is still affecting several countries.  Mozambique is currently in the midst of a third wave of cases.
Sources stated that Mozambique has received 302,000 vaccines from the US as of 3 August.

Mozambican forces announced on 5 August that the joint forces between the Mozambican and Rwanda forces’ main objective is to recover Mocimboa da Praia. This comes as officials state that the joint forces seized equipment from the insurgents after clearing positions near Diaca.

Sources stated that Total is reportedly paying subcontractors on the Afungi LNG project after a months long delay following the suspension of the project due to insurgent attacks.  The payment was to prevent further issues with the subcontractors.

Security forces arrested three people in connection with fuel spill in Pemba on 5 August. The suspects were reportedly on board a small naval vessel with has spilled fuel due to fuel smuggling on 30 July.

Nampula City Council Chairman Paulo Vahanle announced an improvement plan was to be followed to allow better conditions at the FRELIMO HQ in Muhala, east Nampula, on 5 August. The area was in poor condition as the it was built during the colonial period of the country.

The Mozambican Tax Authority announced it had closed several tax offices in parts of Cabo Delgado due to the ongoing insurgent threat. Officials stated that the tax collected was beyond the target revenue in the province.

Sources stated that GALP gas company was reportedly selling underweight propane tanks in Maputo City and Matola. Government inspectors visited the National Norms and Quality Institute and stated that one of the retailers was selling tanks at 10kg content but should have been 11kg.

The Ministry of Health announced 1,611 new COVID cases and 12 deaths in Mozambique on 5 August. Maputo City registered 690 cases and Manica province with 169 cases. 58 hospitalizations were reported bringing the total hospitalizations to 485, while 46 were discharged. 421 daily recoveries were reported.

Health officials stated that 9,000 vaccinations were administered on first day of vaccination campaign in Maputo City on 4 August. The number of locals were more than the expected numbers forcing other locals to move to another health center.

Sources claimed that Rwandan troops and Mozambique security forces have killed 70 insurgents in Cabo Delgado in a series of clashes as of 4 August. Reports stated that the operations occurred around Palma and Awasse recently.  This comes as Rwandan troops started operations on 20 July.

South African Airlink Airlines announced 5 August the resumption of services between Johannesburg and Nampula starting 16 September. The airlines was previously suspended for a year since March 2020. Bookings have reopened for the route for the twice a week flights between the locations.
Security forces arrested a suspect for forced marriage of children in Sofala on 2 August.

Human Rights Watch called on the Mozambican government to lift restrictions and allow displaced people to leave the insurgency affected areas in Cabo Delgado. The HRW stated that around 80,000 IDPs were displaced from the Palma attacks during past March and that thousands of IDPs remained displaced at Quitunda and lack humanitarian aid. Security forces in recent months have been reported to be not allowing IDPs to leave the Quitunda area, and to have detained and assaulted many IDPs who did attempt to escape.
Sources reported on 06 July that 2,600 former RENAMO guerillas have to date been integrated into the DDR process, along with 62 former RENAMO dissidents also gone through the process.

The Mozambican government announced the that Herminia Nhamuze was sworn in as the new director of the Ndlavela Special Penitentiary for Women on 5 August.  This comes after the female penitentiary was previously subjected to an investigation regarding sexual exploitation of the inmates.

Private companies have reportedly vaccinated over 70,000 individuals as part of the Univax program in Mozambique. This campaign is supported by 319 companies that donated 139,590 vaccines as part of the national vaccination campaign.  Companies have imported 500,000 COVID vaccine doses in recent months in this private-public partnership.
Rwandan security forces were announced to be advancing towards Mocimboa da Praia on 6 August. Col. Ronald Rwivanga stated that Rwandan troops were progressing on two fronts towards Mocimboa da Praia.

The Ministry of Health announced 28 new COVID deaths and 1,1490 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 6 August. Maputo city was recorded with the highest number of cases with 460 cases and Inhambane with 232 cases.
The Mozambican government announced the country had received 200,000 Verocell vaccine doses donated by China on 6 August. The vaccines were to provide additional doses for the vaccination campaign.
The Health and Social Action at the Municipal Council of Maputo City stated that drivers of passenger carriers will be vaccinated in Maputo City on 6 and 7 August.

Officials announced the increased fees for services in cemeteries in Maputo City on 4 August. The services have reportedly increased from 1,500 meticais to 5,000 meticais for cremation. For burial services the prices have reportedly increased to 10,000 meticais.

Health officials announced that the Mozambique government expects the peak of the third wave of COVID cases to occur within the next three weeks. The peak is expected to occur first in Tete, where the third wave began, before moving on to the Greater Maputo Area.
Police arrested 15 Malawian for illegal immigration charges in Gorongosa of Sofala on 29 July. The detainees were spotted traveling on bus.

Security forces arrested a Congolese citizen accused of hiding drugs in the yard of a rented house in Fomento neighborhood, Matola, Maputo, on the evening of 04 August. 400 kg of methamphetamine were seized from the residence. The suspect denied to having knowledge about the drugs and accused his employer who he said was in South Africa at the time.

On 8 August, President Filipe Nyusi welcomed Botswanan counterpart, Mokgweetsi Masisi, who is Acting President of the SADC's Organ on Defense and Security, in Pemba city. The visit of the Botswanan president was part of the official launch of SADC Standby Force on 9 August. The Stand-By Force is a detachment composed of land, naval, air, intelligence, logistics, etc. forces from South Africa, Botswana, Angola, Lesotho and Tanzania that will support Mozambique in its fight against terrorism and violent extremism in the districts of Cabo Delgado province.

Rwandan troops on 07 August were reported by a Rwandan military spokesman to have clashed with insurgents at Nantelemule, northwest of Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) town in MDP district, killing four insurgents and capturing weaponry including 6 grenades, 3 machine guns, and 2 RPGs.
Rwandan troops on Saturday, 7 August, were reported to have killed 4 insurgents at clashes at Quelimane village, north of MDP town, amid an advance on MDP town.
Sources indicated that clashes between insurgents and Rwandan forces had taken place at Mangoma village, about 19kms by road west of MDP, on 07 August.
Mozambican troops were reported to be advancing along the Messalo River to cut off MDP town from the south.

The US government has designated one of the leaders of ISCAP in Mozambique, Bonomade Machude Omar, as an international terrorist on 7 August. US Secretary of State Antony Blinken announced a five-man list of the newly designated international terrorists.  Bonomade Machude Omar was described by the US as responsible for attacks in both Mozambique and Tanzania, and is believed to lead the group's "Military and External Affairs" departments, and is reportedly the group's coordiator for all attacks carried out by the group in Northern Mozambique.  Omar was believed to have been one of the leaders of the assault on MDP in August 2020, and on Palma in March of 2021. Omar orignially comes from Palma District.  Omar is also a Mozambican military veteran, and reportedly has contact with a non-Mozambican known as "Abdul" or "Emir Afande", who is connected to the insurgency and reportedly has been present for major insurgent offensives.  Further details on this individual are not currently available.  In March, the US identified Abu Yasir Hassan, a Tanzanian national, as the Cabo Delgado insurgency's top leader, though this report remains unconfirmed. Blinken also stated that the new designation prevents Omar’s from accessing his assets and/or property in the US.

Mozambique President Felipe Nyusi and Botswana President Mokgoetse Masisi officially on 09 August officially launched the SADC Mission in Mozambique (SAMIM) in Pemba. The SADC contingent is made up of  military forces from South Africa, Zimbabwe, Botswana, Angola, Lesotho, and Tanzania hat will support Mozambique to combat terrorism and violent extremism in Cabo Delgado province.  The Standby Force was officially approved by the SADC on 23 June.  The beginning of SADC operations in Cabo Delgado comes as Rwandan and Mozambican troops on 08 August recaptured MDP town from insurgents, which had been held by militants for nearly 1 year.

The Ministry of Health confirmed 1,273 new COVID cases, along with 34 new COVID deaths in Mozambique on 07 August. 483 new cases were reported in Maputo City followed by 197 in Maputo Province, 163 cases from Manica, 120 from Inhambane, 88 from Sofala, 75 from Nampula, 73 from Gaza, 44 from Zambezia, 20 from Tete, 6 from Niassa and 4 from Cabo Delgado. Over the last 24 hours, 49 new hospitalizations and 45 hospital discharges were reported.

IDPs at Quitunda were reported on 06 August to continually prevented from leaving the area, after having been displaced by the assault on Palma in late March.  Security forces imposed restrictions that prevented IDPs from leaving contested areas which placed them at risk from the ongoing offensives in the province, and humanitarian aid shortages in the area also continue to be reported.

A health professional and member of the country's scientific committee claimed that the government's lack of investment in the health care system in the country has resulted in a poor response to the third wave of COVID-19 pandemic. The budget allocated to health sector is allegedly not in proportion with the growth experienced by the country in the past years.

The Ministry of Health confirmed 653 new COVID cases, along with 13 new COVID deaths in Mozambique on 08 August. For first time since July, the country registered below 1000 daily cases. All new cases were a result from local transmission, 644 of which are Mozambicans and nine are foreign nationals. 203 new cases were reported in Maputo City followed by 114 in Inhambane Province. Over the last 24 hours, 39 new hospitalizations and 54 hospital discharges were reported. Currently, the country has 27,878 active cases.

The number of unaccompanied or separated children displaced from Cabo Delgado to resettlement centers in Montepuez increased by 40% in July. 395 children were registered at the end of June compared to 550 at the end of July. These children were separated to their parents or their parents died due to the ongoing violence in the province.

SERNIC agents have recently complained regarding the alleged "freezing" of promotions and special bonuses of 50% for agents with a completed university degree. The Director of Personnel and Training at SERNIC, Fatima Ciriaco, acknowledged the complaints and said that these measures were taken due to high costs, also saying agents who were not trained in police institutions will have to go through the adaptation course at Academy of Police Science (ACIPOL). Sources claimed that the issue will not be resolved soon due to the lack of response from  the Board of the PRM Practical School on the request to start the adaptation course.

A group of 4 unidentified armed men on the afternoon of 09 August attempted to kidnap an Indian businessman outside of Taka Taka Restaurant along Av. Olof Palma  at around 1430hrs in Maputo City.  The businessman had just exited the restaurant when a group of assailants attempted to force him into a waiting vehicle.  The man's wife called for help and clung to her husband, thwarting the attempt to abduct him.  The kidnappers then drove away from the scene; police arrived moments later.  One source reported that SERNIC agents near the scene of the attempted abduction then responded to the scene, causing the kidnappers to flee.

Over 500,000 doses of Sinopharm's Verocell COVID-19 vaccine arrived in Mozambique on 09 August. A total of 485,246 people are fully vaccinated in the country since the start of the immunization campaign.

An analyst said on 09 August that Total could restart its project at Afungi within a year, following the recent success of Mozambican and Rwandan forces in Cabo Delgado Province against the insurgency. The stability of the province will influence the possibility of the project to commence. The joint forces captured Mocimboa de Praia 8 August and military operations are ongoing to secure surrounding communities.

Reports on 09 August indicate that frequent robberies occur in Maputo City throughout the day. The public expressed concern regarding persistent robberies in the city. In Mandela Stop, robberies occur amid presence of a police officers patrolling the area.

The Ministry of Health confirmed 725 new COVID cases, along with 15 new COVID deaths in Mozambique on 09 August. 265 new cases were reported in Maputo City followed by 94 in Niassa Province. Over the last 24 hours, 28 new hospitalizations and 39 hospital discharges were reported. Currently, the country has 24,102 active cases.

The statement was made during the official  launch ceremony of the SADC standby force, and this could indicate the areas where SADC, Rwandan, and Mozambican troops will next conduct operations.

RENAMO's secretary general, Andre Magibire, urged the affected fighters to remain calm and said that the party will continue pressure the Government and the United Nations to address the issue.

Three Mozambican Police assigned to the Rapid Intervention Unit (UIR) were sentenced to 12 yrs in prison by the Judicial Court of the KaMaxaquene Municipal District on 04 August on charges of passive corruption and physical and sexual assault. The defendants were each sentenced to pay compensation of 100,000 meticais to the victim, while they were sentenced to pay a daily fine of 50 meticais for a period of one year (18,750 meticais) for the crime of passive corruption. The indictment stated that the three agents physically and sexually assaulted a 22-year-old woman after finding her without a mask in the street in Maputo City in August 2020 while they demanded a certain amount for other people who failed to wear their masks.

75 people died of COVID-19 from 06-08 August, which brought the total number of people of deaths to 1,613. This is the worst weekend for COVID deaths in Mozambique during the pandemic.
Clashes reported between Mozambican and Rwandan forces and insurgents around Panjele village on 04 August. No information was available on casualties.
Rwanda said that operations in Cabo Delgado will continue following the capture of Mocimboa da Praia on 08 August.

Rwandan military said on 09 August that insurgents from Mocimboa da Praia had fled to the Mbau forest following the offensive. Rwandan and Mozambican forces anticipate new operations in the forest area soon.

Civilians are slowly returning to Quissanga district on 06 August after being displaced due to insurgent attacks, media reports indicate. Government forces were precent in the district as IDPs return.
New troop deployments have been recently reported in Quissanga District as IDPS slowly return to the area.  Some sources later reproted these were primarily foreign troops, likely SADC forces.

Businesses, hairdressing salons and car wash facilities, opened on 08 August in Maputo City in violation of anti-COVID restrictions. Authorities allowed shopping centers to operate from 0900hrs-1600hrs Monday to Saturday, and from 0900hrs-1500hrs on Sundays and holidays. However, other commercial establishments were prohibited to operate on Sundays and holidays.
76 people were arrested by Mozambican Police in Tete city on 07 August for none compliance with anti COVID measures.

Tax Authority announced on 06 August that Cabo Delgado's fiscal revenue target for the first half of 2021 surpassed by 100 million meticais, amid ongoing conflict in the province. Revenues from January to June this year reached 2.3 billion meticais compared to its projected target of 2.2 billion meticais. Authorities stated that the extraction of rubies and other precious stones earned the largest share of revenue.

Standard Bank recently indicated that it had cut the metical price for a dollar in April (during a spike in the value of the metical), saying at the time it had a large quantity of dollars, more than it was allowed to hold after the Bank of Mozambique reportedly refused to buy dollars from Standard.  This eventually led to Bank of Mozambique sanctions against Standard.

One in every two children suffers from chronic malnutrition in Mozambique while 35 percent of children, from nine to 11 years old, have a minimum of daily meals in Mozambique. During the launch of the World Breastfeeding Week, First Lady of the Republic Isaura Nyusi said on 06 August that mothers should ensure exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months until the child is two years old. The Government extended the period of maternity leave to three months, to allow mothers to have more time to breastfeed their children.

Civilians are slowly returning to Nanili, Diaca sources indicated on 05 August after being previously displaced due to insurgent attacks. Government forces urged the people to be vigilant to prevent another terrorist attack in their area.

SERNIC agents arrested seven suspects, including two police officers on 10 August over alleged involvement in the theft of more than five million meticais from a company in Maputo Province. Two other officers involved in the robbery were still at large. Reports suggest that the suspects collaborated with five company employees to participate in the armed robbery targeting the company's vehicle while on its way to a bank.

Pro government militia detained a soldier in Mueda over the weekend; the man was reported to have been suspected by locals of being an insurgent.

A 3.0 percent growth in the Mozambican economy is forecasted in 2021, a rate of 4.0 percent in 2022 and  a rate of 4.5 percent in 2023 by a consultancy. Analysts warn risks of investments due to insecurity in Cabo Delgado province despite the presence of foreign troops in the area.

The Ministry of Health confirmed 1,166 new COVID cases, along with 13 new COVID deaths in Mozambique on 10 August. 294 new cases were reported in Manica Province followed by 262 in Maputo City, 171 in Niassa, 52 in Inhambane, 83 in Sofala, 62 in Gaza, among others. Over the last 24 hours, 41 new hospitalizations and 43 hospital discharges were reported. Currently, the country has 24,182 active cases.

A recently released report profiled several leaders of the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  One of these leaders was identified as Mustafa, a deputy of Cabo Delgado Insurgent leader Bonomador Omar.  Musfafa is reported to ascertain the professions of abducted victims who would be beneficial for the group. The Mocimboa da Praia-born militant participated in the Palma attack in March.

A recently released report profiled several leaders of the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  One of those identified in the report is Lichinga-born Maulana Ali Cassimo. Cassimo between 2014-2017 was an engineer in Mecula.  Cassimo reportedly took part in several demonstrations against security force actions against artisanal miners in the Mariri area and was reported to be angry over the government's treatment of poachers in Niassa.  The report also indicated Cassimo was known to be highly critical of security forces extorting people and policy of arresting illegal miners, saying there was no economic alternative for youths in Cabo Delgado.  From 2016, he appears to have been radicalized via his involvement in a local mosque; he later left his job in 2017 and was no longer in Mecula.  Massimo was reportedly a leader of insurgents at the battles of Mocimboa da Praia in 2020 and at Palma in 2021.

A recently released report profiled several leaders of the Cabo Delgado insurgency.  One of those identified in the report is Rosa Cassamo, a Cabo Delgado-born high-ranked member of the insurgent group, acquired local power due to her husband's influence. She was head of logistics in Ilala and Mucojo. She also played an essential role in mobilizing women  to enter the insurgent group.  Cassamo is reportedly the highest ranking woman in the group, and is also reportedly considered "the queen of black magic".  Her husband, Ibraimo Mussa, is meanwhile a former FRELIMO party member, and reportedly played a prominent role in the emergence of the insurgency in his village.

Six suspects robbed a Macomia-based businessman of 1,400,000.00 meticais in cash  in Chiure. Reports suggest that the suspects tied up guard in the area before they conducted the attack.  An investigation into the incident has been launched.

Two people were killed, and nine were injured in a road accident involving a passenger bus and a lorry in Ponte Metuchira, Gondola on 10 August. The accident was reportedly caused by speeding and dangerous maneuver on the road.
An man was heavily injured after he was hit by a vehicle along EN6 road in front of Feira Market, Gondola on 10 August.

Uganda expressed a desire to support Mozambique in the fight against terrorism during the visit of Uganda’s presidential envoy Ivan Koreta  in Pemba on 09 August.  No material support however has been offered by Uganda to Mozambique.

An unconfirmed report on 09 August indicate that a kidnapping attempt on 09 August in Maputo was perpetrated by security force members, including a police officer and at least one SERNIC agent.  There are also indications that the businessman targeted in this incident, who travelled from Quelimane on 04 August, was having his movements monitored by a criminal network.

A Mozambican national was arrested in Mumbai International Airport around 0200hrs on 08 August. The suspect swallowed around 70 capsules filled with cocaine weighing 1kg with an estimated worth of Rs 10 crore. It was not clear if the suspect began his trip in Mozambique.

Workers in Tete have accused a mining company in Tete of abandoning sick employees. Employees say that the company has "tampered" with medical certificates of employees who fell ill while working for the company in order to evade responsibility.  Many workers and former workers complain the company refused to pay expenses related to illnesses.
Mozambican Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy, Max Tonela, said on 10 August that the government expects companies to return to Cabo Delgado when security is restored in the province.

Mozambique was reported on 10 August to have received a surveillance aircraft from private company, Paramount.  The company has previously provided helicopters and armored vehicles to the Mozambican military.
On 10 August, the US embassy called for both FRELIMO and RENAMO to fulfil their commitments in achieving a timely and complete disarmament process.
The Association of Transporters in Tete warned on 10 August the non-vaccinated drivers in the province could face punishment.

More than 74 billion meticais ($1.2 billion) has been spent by the Mozambican Government for the conflict in Cabo Delgado, according to estimates from a new report by a Mozambican NGO.  Nearly $1 billion is reportedly being spent on the war per year as of 2021. The spending increased three times compared to 2015 numbers, from 21 billion meticais to 62 billion meticais per year. This reportedly does not include 10 billion meticais estimated to have been spent on private military companies involved in the war in Cabo Delgado.
A small plan landed at Mocimboa da Praia's airport for first time on 10 August in two years.  This was likely a reconnaissance plane operating in the area.

Rwandan police were reported on 10 August to be have taken part in community engagement in Palma on 10 August. The soldiers shared a meal with the locals who were on their way home in nearby neighborhoods.  A small number of Palma residents have recently returned to the area from Quitunda.
An unidentified man died under suspicious circumstance in Matola on 10 August evening. His dead body was recovered the following morning. An investigation into the incident has been launched.

Only 5 of the other 15 SADC members have so far dispatched troops to Cabo Delgado. Zimbabwe is expected to send non-combat forces though they have not arrived yet. Those who have yet to send its troops are Comoros, Democratic Republic of Congo, Swatini, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Namibia, Seychelles, and Zambia.  South Africa, Botswana, Angola, Lesotho, and Tanzania so far have deployed some forces to the country.
Cabo Delgado Secretary of State, Antonio Supeia, called for IDPs in Nquiruqele village of Namuno district to be vigilant and denounce any insurgent infiltrators among IDP populations.

A group of people staged a demonstration in Limpopo District on 06 August to protest the death of an individual allegedly bewitched by a neighbor and co-worker in South Africa. The protesters destroyed homes and vehicles near the home of the alleged witch doctor. Five suspects involved in the conflict were later arrested.

A fire incident was reported in Mocimboa da Praia on 10 August. The cause of fire has not yet been determined. MDP was captured by Joint Forces from insurgents on 08 August.  No new fighting has been reported in the town in recent days.

Mozambique’s National Health Institute (INS) said on 10 August that more restrictive measures may be needed to limit the spread of COVID-19. INS classifies the pandemic in five levels – level one being of low transmission of the virus, and level five being of very high transmission. Currently, Mozambique is at level four. Should the country reach level five, a stricter set of protocols could be imposed.

Sources suggest that the attacks were launched while the Mozambican and Rwandan forces attacked insurgent positions in MDP District.  Militants who launched these attacks reportedly moved through the area via motorbikes towards the border with Tanzania.

SERNIC operatives destroyed 86kg methamphetamine and cannabis sativa in Nampula on 09 August. The destroyed drugs were seized in previous operations in the cities of Nampula and Nacala-Porto. 10 people were arrested in connection to the seizure.

Hospital admissions for COVID-19 have recently dropped in Central Hospital in Maputo. The numbers have decreased from 140 to 76 admissions over the past two days. However, despite this development authorities still warned the public regarding the importance of following COVID-19 protocols as the daily number of new cases is still high.

Margarida Adamugy Talapa , Minister of Labour, Employment and Social Security said on 11 August that around 9,039 people were unemployed due to the insurgency in Cabo Delgado, and most of those affected were in Palma, Mocimboa da Praia, and Nangade.

The US embassy in Maputo on 11 August announced that on 09 August, the US and Mozambican governments had launched a second Joint Combined Exchange Training (JCET) in which US Special Forces were providing training for over 100 Mozambican commandos and rangers. Medical and communications equipment will also be provided to units that complete this training. The US completed an initial JCET training in May, and conducted tactical combat casualty care and combat lifesaver training courses in June. The EU meanwhile will likely launch its training mission in Mozambique before the end of September. Portuguese military trainers have been in the country for some months as well. The SADC's Standby Force officially launched its operations in Cabo Delgado on 09 August, while Rwandan troops have been engaged in combat operations against the insurgents in Cabo Delgado alongside Mozambican forces for several weeks. Unconfirmed reports have indicated the US may be providing some form of support to Rwandan troops in Mozambique, or at least tacitly supports the Rwandan force's mission. Other unconfirmed reports have indicated that the French government is financing the Rwandan intervention in Cabo Delgado.

The Aeroportos de Mocambique (ADM) said on 10 August that it still has no forecast as to when the Mocimboa da Praia airport will resume operations after the Mozambican and Rwandan forces have recovered Mocimboa de Praia from the insurgents last Sunday. Other sources later confirmed the airport had largely been destroyed, with equipment either vandalized or looted, and that the airport would need to be essentially completed refurbished in order to operate again.

The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) announced on 11 August that it dismissed 11 of its agents who were involved in crimes, such as extortion, robbery and kidnapping, from January 2021 to the present. Names of these agents were not disclosed, but it was made known that they were aged 20-40 years old, and have performed various instructional and investigative functions in the Service ranging from 1 to 15 years. 5 of them were assigned in Maputo city, 5 others in Maputo province and 1 in Tete. SERNIC said it will continue to monitor the dismissed agents to prevent them from committing more crimes. Also, some agents in Maputo province were also meted with fines after it was proven that they also participated in criminal acts.

A local source on 11 August reported that many displaced residents from MDP expressed a desire to return to their homes in MDP as soon as possible, after the government declared on 8 August the Mozambican and Rwandan forces have recovered control of the said town. There are others who still do not believe that the insurgents have been completely driven out the town though, pointing out that when they are able to return to their homes and experience their normal lives again will they believe that the town is free of terrorists.

The Ministry of Health registered 1,185 new COVID cases and 14 related deaths in Mozambique on 11 August. Maputo recorded the highest with 431 cases followed by Zambezia province with 253 cases. 5,525 recoveries were also recorded on the same day, which is the highest since the pandemic began.

FADM Commander Cristovao Chume on 11 August said that no significant confrontations took place during the retaking of Mocimboa da Praia town from the insurgents on 8 August, resulting in zero casualties on either side. The commander said that this indicates that the insurgents withdrew as joint forces approached the town. Commander Chume explained that the town was retaken in a 4 part pincer movement. The first 2 arms of the pincer were via the sea: FADM navy landed at the port, while a platoon of FADM Marines aimed to control the town by land by entering it from the south of the port. The two forces completed their mission at 0700hrs and 0900hrs. The second 2 axes were assigned to the Rwandan troops: one group entered MDP from Palma (from the north) and another group from Awasse (from the south). These teams achieved their goal of securing the airport at 1100hrs.

FADM Commander Chume in an interview on 11 August indicated that the airport terminal, the machine that ensures normal functioning of the port and other structures where public and private organizations operated had sustained significant damage in Mocimboa da Praia during the insurgent occupation, also saying that the town is basically deserted. Other news reports from the town said there is no running water or electricity in the town, and reported widespread destruction and vandalism.

FADM Commander Cristovao Chume on 11 August said that the Mozambican and Rwandan forces are executing "cleaning" of small pockets of resistance remaining in Mocimboa da Praia District to secure safe conditions for the gradual return of normalcy and the displaced residents.

A local source reported on 11 August that the Southern African Development Community (SADC) will hold its 41st Summit in Lilongwe, Malawi, on 17 to 18 August 2021 with limited participants. A meeting of Council of Ministers will take place prior the summit that will be participated in person by some delegates, and via virtual platforms by others. The summit will review and discuss the progress of the Regional Indicative Strategic Development Plan (RISDP) 2020-2030 and Vision 2050. During the summit, the President of Mallawi will take over the chairpersonship of SADC from Mozambican President Filipe Nyusi, and the Executive Secretary of SADC, Dr Stergomena Lawrence Tax, will leave her post after serving for 8 years.  The deployment of troops to Mozambique is likely to be one of the primary subjects discussed at the meeting.

A local news source reported on 11 August that President Filipe Nyusi had removed Jorge David Gune from his post as Mozambique's High Commissioner in Malawi and appointed Elias Jaime Zimba as his replacement.

Data released during the launching ceremony of the SADC mission in Pemba city on 9 August indicated that the SADC intervention force deployment so far consists of 738 soldiers and 19 experts. 277 of these soldiers are from Tanzania, 270 are from South Africa, 16 soldiers are from Angola, 108 from Botswana, and 70 from Lesotho. Out of the 19 experts, 6 are Mozambican, 3 are Tanzanian, 2 are from Angola, 2 from Botswana, 1 from Lesotho, 1 from Malawi, 2 from South Africa, 1 from Zimbabwe and the SADC Secretariat.

A local news source citing local health authorities reported on 10 August that out of the 3,600 cases of COVID-19 registered in Inhambane province in July, more than 460 of these cases were among people already fully vaccinated against the disease. These people did not develop severe symptoms that required hospital treatments and no fatalities were reported among this group.

A local news report on 11 August indicated that while many displaced people are happy with the military intervention in the Cabo Delgado, there is fear in some of the displaced population currently in Nampula that they will not be allowed to return to Mocimboa da Praia. Some of them speculate that due to economic interests of foreign entities, they will be prevented from moving back to their homes.

Major General Cristovao Chume, commander of the Mozambican army, said in an interview in Mocimboa da Praia on 10 August that the recovery of MDP was only the first stage of a larger operation and that the next operations would be to "secure the remaining pockets of the insurgents" until Cabo Delgado is fully under government's control. Commander Chume could not confirm, however, how long the next stage would take as the military still needed to acquire more intelligence. Additionally, Chume and his Rwandan counterpart and joint commander, Major General Innocent Kabandana, pointed out that while most of the terrorists are from Mozambique, a number of them, especially leaders, come from several other countries, including Tanzania, Burundi, and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Chume said that the terrorists' ultimate goal was to make Cabo Delgado the starting point for setting up an Islamic State in southern Africa.

Weaponry seized from the insurgents along the Mueda-Awasse axis by the Rwandan military was displayed in Segal, Mueda district of Cabo Delgado, on 11 August.  This weaponry was seized from militants in clashes between 24 July - 03 August, and included small arms, ammunition, and RPGs.

A Mozambican helicopter reportedly attacked a suspected insurgent patrol on the road between Mocimboa da Praia and Palma, near Quelimane village in the northern Mocimboa da Praia district on 3 August. No casualties were reported.

Sources in Nangade said that there was no SADC or Rwandan military present in Nangade as of early August, and that only pro-government militia were present in the town, even as insurgents continue to launch ambushes and other attacks in the district. On 11 August, it was reported that there was tension among the members of the Youth League, youth arm of Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM), in Beira city as supporters of Lutero Simango allegedly attacked supporters of Jose Domingos. On 07 August when current president of Beira Youth League, Albino Mussendo, announced his support for a candidate for the presidency of MDM, Lutero Simango, in the presence of Muxica dos Santos, former president of Beira Youth League, who is a supporter of another candidate, Jose Domingos. Dos Santos also claimed that he and others were assaulted by Mussendo and his followers, and a motorbike belonging to the party was forcibly taken from the former by the latter on 7 August.

The executive director of the Post-Cyclone Reconstruction Office (GREPOC), Luis Mandlate, said on 11 August that resources are needed for the reconstruction of houses for 190,000 families who were affected by cyclones Idai and Kenneth between March and April of 2019 in Central Mozambique and Cabo Delgado respectively. These families remained sheltered in tents and live in terrible conditions. Mandlate confirmed that work is underway to raise funds for those affected by the cyclones.

The association said that Mozambican traffic police between the Zimbabwean border and Beira and on the road to Tete as well regularly were harassing truck drivers and demanding bribes between 50-100 meticais.

Military and media sources have indicated joint Mozambican-Rwandan troops are preparing a new offensive on the Mbau area / Messalo River Banks in Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) District, since the re-capture of Mocimboa da Praia on 08 August. On 12 August, media sources reported more than 30 military vehicles and four helicopters had arrived in Macomia town in preparation for this assault.  South African troops from the SADC Standby Force are reportedly among the troops massing for this offensive.  A construction crew meanwhile was reported in Muidumbe to be preparing a bridge over the Messalo river to allow forces to be able to travel into the town of Miangalewa.  A Mozambican general on 10 August had indicated troops would soon move to attack the insurgent bases of Syria 1 and 2 and other insurgent positions in the Mbau Forest.  Rwandan media sources meanwhile just after the fall of MDP on 08 August indicated that insurgents had fled MDP without a fight, and were known to have fled to the Mbau area, and that an offensive to target militants in Mbau would soon be launched.

Sources on 12 August indicated a construction crew was repairing the bridge over the Messalo River near Miangalewa town in order for joint forces to launch an offensive along the Messalo River and in the Mbau area.

The National Census of Artisanal Miners was launched in Moma, Nampula on 09 August. Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy, Ernesto Max Tonelas, said that the  process aims to improve the condition of mining activities carried out in Mozambique, by providing more jobs and better family income levels.

Maputo City Police announced that the suspects who attempted abduct a man in Maputo City on 09 August managed to escape. Security forces reportedly closed all exit routes in the city but failed to capture them.

A recent investigative indicates 1,000 to 2,000 insurgents believed to be currently active in Cabo Delgado Province.  Previous reports had indicated similar numbers of insurgents active in the province.

Japanese multinational Mitsui on 11 August expressed optimism about the restart of gas project in Cabo Delgado as security being restored. The company is a strategic partner of Total company in the Area 1 liquefied natural gas exploration project in the Rovuma basin.  Some companies in recent weeks have said they expect work on the LNG project could resume sometime next year.

On 10 August, Mozambican army commander Maj-Gen Cristovao Chume said 33 dead bodies of insurgents were recovered in Mocimboa Da Praia. It is unclear if Chume is referring to 33 insurgents killed during the advance on MDP, or referring to clashes in the town. Joint forces seized control of MDP town on 08 August.  Some sources have indicated that fighting did take place in MDP town between 01-04 August.

On 10 August, Mozambican army commander Maj-Gen Cristovao Chume said that aerial and artillery bombardment is ongoing against insurgents who retreated from MDP on 08 August; this bombardment is believed to be taking place along the Messalo River.

Joint forces allegedly captured insurgent leaders connected to one of insurgency’s top commanders, Bonomade Omar, with military officials saying these militants are now providing info on the insurgency.  No specific details on those insurgents reportedly captured are currently available.
Less metical volatility was reported in July 2021 compared to the  last four months. Metical registered a monthly depreciation of 0.22 percent against the US dollar which settled at 63.63.

The Mozambican Police Association reportedly is pushing for investigation into alleged security force involvement in organized crime in the country. This development came after 11 SERNIG agents were expelled for involvement in abductions, robberies and other criminal activities, after reports of two security force members recently arrested as part of an investigation into a Maputo Province robbery, and after security agents were recently implicated in a kidnapping attempt in Maputo City.

Security forces have been deployed around exit routes to prevent any insurgents still in Mocimboa da Praia town from escaping. Insurgents who left following the offensive on 08 August reportedly left in the town a large quantity of military equipment and a number of items stolen from the population.

Hidroelectrica de Cahora Bassa (HCB) warned on 11 August that they will open one of Cahora Bassa dam's flood gates on 01 September. Potential for flooding in some areas in some area as the level of the river will increase along the lower Zambezi, affecting the districts of Tambara in Manica, Tete city, Moatize, Doa and Mutarara in Tete province, Chemba, Caia and Marromeu in Sofala; and Mopeia, Luabo, and Chinde in Zambezia.

The African Development Bank agrees to fund the first ‘Industrialize Mozambique’ program projects in Cabo Delgado and Niassa provinces. The president-initiative program will help increase production in the agro-processing industry through the use of local raw materials, stimulating commercialization and generating employment for civilians.

Mozambican police arrested 13 illegal immigrants arrested in Zimpeto, Maputo City on 12 August. Eight of the suspects do not have legal documentation while five others entered the country illegally. The arrest came after security forces intercepted a Tete-bound bus loaded with 48 individuals.

The Ministry of Health registered 1,038 new COVID cases and 16 related deaths in Mozambique on 12 August. Maputo recorded the highest with 229 cases followed by Zambezia province with 208 cases. In the last 24 hours, 41 new admissions and 32 hospital discharges were registered while 1,882 Mozambicans and eight foreigners.

Cabo Delgado Governor Valige Tauabo visited Mocimboa da Praia on 12 August, the first time since the town was seized by joint forces from insurgents. Tauabo said the Mozambican Army advised against the return of civilians as clearing operations continue.

Another passenger succumbed to his wounds on 12 August following the road accident involving a passenger bus and a lorry in Ponte Metuchira, Gondola. The accident, which happened on 10 August, was reportedly caused by speeding and dangerous maneuver on the road.

A fire broke out in Chamanculo B, Maputo City in the afternoon of 12 August. No injuries were reported, however, 48 families lost their houses during the incident. The cause of the fire is still unknown.
On 12 August, authorities directed civilians not to return to Mocimboa da Praia yet as clearing operations in the town and district continue .

On 11 August, Mozambican forces announced the seizure of weapons, other military equipment and documents from insurgents  in the town of Mocimboa da Praia. Among the documents recovered were Arabic manuals on how to use various firearms and assorted religious books, a hand-drawn map of Palma with indications of positions of Mozambican forces, and other significant facilities. Meanwhile, some Mozambican military officials said some of the weaponry seized from the insurgents had not been captured from the Mozambican security forces and the source of these weapons was unclear.

On 10 August, government forces said that a group of eight women and children allegedly 'appeared' in Mocimboa da Praia. It was believed that they were the family members of insurgents in the town.  The group is now in security force custody.
An ambulance in the district of Nacala-a-Velha has just overturned very close to the entrance of the CLN on 12 August. No information on casualties.

Mozambique expressed opposition on 12 August against decision to grant Israel observer status at the African Union. The government said that the matter demanded consultation with all the AU member states, rather than a unilateral decision by the Commission.

74 percent of Mozambican people with HIV across the country are benefiting from free anti-retroviral treatment (ARVT) while about half a million HIV-positive locals are not receiving the life-prolonging treatment.  Authorities called on heath sector stakeholders to strengthen preventive actions against HIV.

The National Institute of Meteorology (INAM) warned on 13 August of strong winds of up to 60 kilometers per hour from this afternoon in the provinces of  Inhambane, Sofala and Zambezia. In addition, light to moderate rains were forecasted in the provinces of Inhambane, Sofala, Manica and Zambezia, tonight and tomorrow, 14 August.  Authorities advised the public to take safety measures during this time.

Suspected armed robbers attempted to attack an Indian businessman in Ancuabe on 13 August. Security forces responded and engaged assailants in a gun battle, which led the latter to escape towards Montepuez. Additional security forces were deployed in the area to investigate on the incident and forestall similar attacks. This was not believed to be connected to the insurgency.

President Nyusi on 13 August announced that the government would maintain all COVID-19 restrictions for another 30 days.  The only exception to this will be the allowance of in-person school exams.  Nyusi also re-iterated the suspension of face to face classes in Vilankulo, Maxixe, and Massinga, as had already been announced by the government.

A total of 1,169,972 people have been vaccinated against COVID-19 in Mozambique since March 2021, when the vaccination program in the country began. 529,117 people of which have been completely immunized. In Maputo city a total of 209,903 vaccinated, followed by Maputo province with 183,532 vaccinated people, and Nampula with 166,982.

Reports on 12 August indicate that insurgents used houses of businessmen in Mocimboa da Praia between August 2020 - August 2021. Insurgents are also believed to have kidnapped large numbers of a local businessman’s workforce a year ago, and many are likely still held by insurgents. The businessman also claimed to have lost more than 14 million US dollars, in addition to other losses, during the invasion.

Mozambican and Rwandan troops found houses in Mocimboa da Praia with signs reading "Not be touched" in Swahili, which were believed to the choice houses of the insurgents.  Troops in the town have identified an infirmary, a prison, and accommodation also used by insurgents during their occupation of the town.
Joint forces conducted patrols off Mocimboa da Praia waters on 13 August, sources reported.   Rwandan naval vessels were reported patrolling these areas.

Poor progress in post cyclone reconstruction has been reported due to lack of coordination among authorities. 77 percent of USD 1.2 million of recovery funds are allegedly being used by the various agencies with only 23 percent of which is the under the management of the Mozambique’s Post-Cyclone Reconstruction Office (GRECOP). GRECOP executive director, Luis Mandlate, said that the reconstruction of the houses will be concluded by mid 2024 - Cyclones Idai and Kenneth impacted Mozambique in 2019.

TMCell employees were reported to have not been paid their July salaries on time. The company guaranteed to pay complete salaries of all 1,800 employees by 13 August. Reasons behind the salary delay were not disclosed, though this comes after recent reports indicating TMCell is significantly indebted to Vodafone.

On 13 August, General Cristovao Chume said that top insurgent commander, Bonomar Machude Omar, is still alive and is still in Mocimboa da Praia District, and will either be killed or captured. He added that same of Omar's close associates have been captured - which had been previously reported.  Omar has been alternatively identified as either the top leader of the insurgency, a deputy leader of the group, or one of several top leaders of the group.

The Ministry of Health registered 847 new COVID cases and 19 related deaths in Mozambique on 13 August. Maputo recorded the highest with 223 cases followed by Maputo province with 133 cases. In the last 24 hours, 33 new admissions and 25 hospital discharges were registered while 1,013 Mozambicans and one foreigner.

A coordinated ISIS anti-Rwandan online campaign was reported on telegram on 11 August in response to Rwanda's intervention in Cabo Delgado. The propaganda indicates that Rwanda is a hostile Christian country  who allegedly oppressing the Muslim population.

More COVID-19 restriction violations were reported in Maputo City on 13 August. Many public places were crowded, with sidewalk vendors are present while grocery stores are open after 1600hrs in violation of restrictions.

The Bank of Mozambique filed two additional new charges on 13 August against Standard Bank officials, Adimohanma Chukwuma Nwokocha, former Chief Executive Officer, and Claudio Eliazare Banze, Information Technologies Director at Standard Bank, following the ongoing on-site inspection. The officials was accused of alleged  implementation of an illegal payment network based outside the country.
Three Matola Municipal Council employees were arrested on 13 August for allegedly stealing a vault of money in Machava Administrative Post.
Security forces arrested two Beira Municipal Council officials  in the evening of 12 August over alleged involvement in the sale of illegally logged timber in the province.

A fire broke out in Ponta Mamoli, Matutuine around 1300hrs on 12 August. The fire was contained the following day. No casualties reported, however, three houses were burnt. The cause of the fire is still unknown, but sources  suspected that it was caused by locals who set up fires to scare away reptiles.

Locals claimed that the corruption incidents and intimidation by Mozambican forces in Quitunda has effectively ended with arrival of Rwandan forces. Locals many times previously have accused Mozambican forces for seizing their properties after being displaced from Palma due to insurgent attacks.

Authorities announced on 15 August that a total of 106,195 people have been vaccinated against COVID-19 in the last 24 hours as of 15 August. Mozambique currently has a total of 560,798 people fully vaccinated against the virus.

Cabo Delgado Governor Valige Tauabo said on 14 August that six employees of the Municipal Council of Mocimboa da Praia were killed by insurgents, presumably referring to during the course of the assault on MDP in August 2020.

The Ministry of Health registered 931 new COVID cases and 17 related deaths in Mozambique on 14 August. Maputo City recorded the highest with 319 cases followed by Maputo province with 64 cases. In the last 24 hours, 31 new admissions and 28 hospital discharges were registered.

Large fires were reported in the villages of Mbau, Mangoma, and Ntowe of Mocimboa da Praia district (MDP) on 14 August. Another suspicious fire incident was recorded in Chicuaia Velha of Nangade district over the night of 14-15 August.   These fires likely indicate clashes in MDP District, particularly at Mbau, where many insurgents are suspected to have fled in the aftermath of the recapture of MDP town on 08 August.  The fire incident in Chicuaia meanwhile more likely indicates a militant attack.  Note that other sources reported these fires were the result of airstrikes targeting the insurgents, though this is not yet confirmed.

Several sources on 15 August reported that a contingent of troops from Lesotho, part of the SADC's Standby Force, had arrived in Mozambique, transported by the Angolan Air Force.  One source indicated these troops had departed from Lesotho the day before.  The size of this latest deployment was not immediately clear, though Lesotho's contribution to the Standby Force is meant to be 117 soldiers; reports last week indicated that 70 troops from the country were already on the ground in Cabo Delgado.

Vodacom plans to re-establish communications in Mocimboa da Praia district this week, after a team visited the area to assess the extent of damage caused by the insurgents. The telecom company aims to extend this development in other affected areas in Cabo Delgado, including Afungi and Palma.

Malawi’s President Lazarus Chakwera will take over  the Southern African Development Community (SADC) chairmanship from Mozambique’s Filipe Nyusi. The new leadership will be announced during the 41st Ordinary Summit of Heads of State and Government in Malawi from 17-18 August.

Mozambican military sources on 16 August said that 95% of Quissanga district remains currently uninhabited following mass displacement brought by insurgent attacks. The said attacks destroyed much of the public and private infrastructures in the district.

On Sunday afternoon, construction teams were reported to have constructed a temporary alternative bridge over the Quinhevo River near Manhila, allowing road moves once again between Palma, through Mocimboa da Praia (MDP), and to Awasse.  Other sources indicated construction crews were also working on a bridge over the Messalo River just south of Miangalewa, though it is not yet confirmed if this bridge has been completed.
