column4: There is a general consensus as of 15 August that insurgents have good intelligence which prompted them to withdraw most of their fighters from Mocimboa da Praia before Mozambican and Rwandan troops arrived into the town on 08 August. They warned that most of the insurgents had left, divided into small groups, dispersed in the region and remain intact.  Militants still possess large numbers of vehicles and weapons, as well and hundreds of fighters.

The Ministry of Health registered 405 new COVID cases and nine related deaths in Mozambique on 15 August. Niassa recorded the highest with 127 cases followed by Maputo city with 87 cases. In the last 24 hours, 25 new admissions and 27 hospital discharges were registered, while 1,051 have fully recovered.

Vaccination cards are allegedly forged across the country, according to local sources.  Forged COVID false negative tests have been produced throughout the pandemic, particularly in Southern Mozambique.

EDM connected Panjane in Magude district and Messano in Bilene to the national grid on 13 August. This is part of the government's 'Energy for All' program which aims to bring electricity to everyone in the country by 2030.

Mozambican police arrested a Tanzanian national  three kilometers from the Ponta do Ouro crossing point on 14 August, while attempting to illegally cross the border into South Africa. A quantity of cocaine,  two mobile phones and around 600 rand were recovered from his possession.

Two municipal officials were reported to have filled a container with illegally logged wood and intended to smuggle these containers from Munhava in Sofala on 12 August. The suspects were detained by the police.

Locals are reported to be returning to Palma from Quitunda as the security situation is improving in the area after the recent arrival of Rwandan troops. Locals who returned claimed that no fighting was noted in the area in recent weeks. Locals also stated that other displaced individuals are still looking for ways to travel to Pemba due to the absence of jobs or financial means.

The Mozambican government on 14 August said that it was creating conditions to allow the return of population to areas they have been displaced from in Cabo Delgado. The government stated that essential services and assistance would be provided to the local population that have returned.

The Norway government is reported to have donated 3.4million USD through the WFP to provide assistance to livelihood and school feeding programs in Cabo Delgado. The donation was expected to provide for 13,000 children and 6,500 adults.
Sources stated that around 4,000 domestic workers have lost their jobs in Greater Maputo since the start of the COVID pandemic.

RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade announced meetings with international partners on 18 August regarding problems with the DDR process.  This includes the non-payment of salaries of the DDR members and problems regarding the integration of RENAMO members into the security forces.

Mocimboa da Praia official Assuate Falume on 16 August stated that it is too early to discuss return of population to the town after its liberation from the insurgency. Residents were advised to remain patient as operations targeting the insurgents were still ongoing.

A report to the South African parliament indicated that two armored vehicles and an attack helicopter were earlier this year received by Mozambique from a South African company earlier this year.  The report also indicated Mozambique had received 5 armored vehicles from a South African company late last year, and that the company had provided to Gazelle helicopters to the Mozambican Air Force earlier this year. The Mozambican military's receiving this equipment had been reported earlier this year.

The Northern Integrated Development Agency (ADIN) announced that a technical team will visit Palma to evaluate scope of reconstruction work in the town.  This comes as displaced have reportedly begun to return to the town.

RENAMO leader Ossufo Momade warned of possible risks of insurgents setting up new bases as the offensive in Cabo Delgado continues.  Momade said as a former guerilla, he understands that the insurgents are likely to "settle in another place".
The Mozambican Ministry of Mineral Resources and Energy announced that illegal mining causes losses of around 360 million meticais to the country per year.

Electricidade de Mozambique has raised concerns of overloading of electrical connections in Maputo. Overloading has recently been reported in Chamanculo neighborhoods. The overloading has previously caused short circuits leading to a fire at a residence.

The Ministry of Health announced that 289 COVID cases and 15 deaths in Mozambique on 16 August. 28 of the new cases were admitted for hospitalization while 34 were discharged. This brings 272 admissions for COVID patients.

A police vehicle crashed onto three parked vehicles during a vehicle chase along Avenida 25 de Setembro, in Maputo on 15 August. The policeman killed himself after the incident. The suspect during the chase managed to escape.
The National Institute of Statistics stated that the Consumer Price Index calculated an inflation in Mozambique during July of 0.24%. The prices were notable among food and non-alcoholic beverages.
The New PRM Director of the Public Order for Manica Province was critically injured during an accident on the afternoon of 16 August.
Unconfirmed reports stated that large number of women were found during an operation in Cabo Delgado on 15 August. The females were reportedly held captive by insurgents.

Suspicious fires were reported in Chitunda village in Muidumbe District on 16 August, north of Namacande. This came amid report of an ongoing military operation in the area, and fires could indicate clashes or new airstrikes.

Suspicious fires were reported south of Diaca in Cabo Delgado on 14 August.  This came amid report of an ongoing military operation in the area, and fires could indicate clashes or new airstrikes.  This could also indicate new insurgent attacks.

Suspicious fires were reported in the Natandola area (south of Chinda) areas in Cabo Delgado on 14 August.  This came amid report of an ongoing military operation in the area, and fires could indicate clashes or new airstrikes.  This could also indicate new insurgent attacks.

Rwandan security forces discovered and removed a grenade in Palma town on 15 August. It was unclear if the grenade was recently placed in the area or was a remnant left behind during clashes in Palma earlier this year.

On 16 August, unconfirmed reports indicted clashes took place at Mangoma, Ntotwe, and Nantadola in Mocimboa da Praia District; Mangoma and Ntotwe were previously secured by joint forces, while control of Nantadola was still reportedly contested.

On 16 August, unconfirmed reports indicted clashes took place at Mangoma, Ntotwe, and Nantadola in Mocimboa da Praia District; Mangoma and Ntotwe were previously secured by joint forces, while control of Nantadola was still reportedly contested.

On 16 August, unconfirmed reports indicted clashes took place at Mangoma, Ntotwe, and Nantadola in Mocimboa da Praia District; Mangoma and Ntotwe were previously secured by joint forces, while control of Nantadola was still reportedly contested.

Rwandan security forces are reported to be establishing a security cordon around Palma and Mocimboa da Praia districts that is meant to eventually allow the resumption of operations of LNG Projects in the province.

Rwandan security forces are reported to be establishing a security cordon around Palma and Mocimboa da Praia districts that is meant to eventually allow the resumption of operations of LNG Projects in the province.

Tanzanian forces have recently established checkpoints around all villages within 40km of Mtwara. The checkpoints were to check the identification of the locals and individuals within the vicinity, a notable increase of security activity along the border with Cabo Delgado.

Tanzania forces are reported to be interrogating anyone travelling across the border from Mozambique as of early August. This was to identify members of the Cabo Delgado insurgency, with some insurgents believed to be fleeing into Tanzania after recent joint Mozambican - Rwandan operations targeting insurgents in Northern Cabo Delgado.

Several sources on 17 August reported that Rwandan and Mozambican forces had launched an assault on insurgent positions in the Mbau Forest, following a bombardment, potentially involving artillery, airstrikes or a combination of the two.  Other unconfirmed reports indicated that South African aircraft had launched strikes in the area, specifically on the insurgents' mobile bush camps of "Syria 1" and "Syria 2".

Several sources on 17 August reported that Rwandan and Mozambican forces had launched an assault on insurgent positions in the Mbau Forest, following a bombardment, potentially involving artillery, airstrikes or a combination of the two.  Other unconfirmed reports indicated that South African aircraft had launched strikes in the area, specifically on the insurgents' mobile bush camps of "Syria 1" and "Syria 2".

Timoteo Maquinze, the RENAMO Military Wing's Chief of General Staff, along with 8 other top ranking RENAMO military members, joined the DDR process in Beira on the afternoon of 17 August.  RENAMO chief Ossufo Momade as well as a UN rep and other top RENAMO members attended the event.

Officials stated that displaced people are no longer fleeing from northern districts to Pemba in recent weeks since the arrival of Rwandan forces in northern Cabo Delgado.  Previously, as many as 6-7 boats filled with IDPs would arrive at Paquitequete beach in Pemba.

Mozambican General Chongo Vidgal stated on 17 August that 95% of the militants in Cabo Delgado are Mozambican. Brig Vidgal also said that the ongoing offensive in MDP district is facing “little resistance”, and that militants have likely discarded their weapons and disguised themselves as civilians.

Officials announced on 17 August that unidentified individuals reportedly vandalized a pipeline in attempt to steal fuel, causing a leak in Nacala. The pipeline was reportedly old and deactivated.  This came after an oil theft incident in July resulted in a fuel spill of about 5,000 liters in Pemba Bay.

The SADC officials on 17 August met in Malawi for a summit. The meeting was a hybrid summit as several members attended through video conferencing while other members attended in-person.  President Nyusi during the summit passed the rotating presidency to Malawian President Lazarus Chakwera.

Private transporters in a cooperative in Maputo City have accused the government authorities in Maputo of appropriating 15 buses recently, accusing private transport workers of misusing electronic ticketing systems.

The Ministry of Health announced 17 COVID deaths and 1,033 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 17 August. Maputo City remains with the highest number of cases with 211 cases. Niassa was second with 189 cases.
Maputo City reportedly has vaccinated 130,578 individuals as of 17 August. 219,233 total individuals are being targeted in the current vaccination campaign.

Officials announced that 1,185,169 have been vaccinated in Mozambique as of 17 August out of a targeted 1,481,833 across the country, or about 80% of those targeted in the campaign. Over the past 24 hours 107,082 were inoculated countrywide. The Ministry of Health stated that the current phase may reach the intended plan.

There were more COVID deaths over the first 16 days of August compared to the first 16 days of July, health officials said on 17 August, though less cases over this time.  In the first 16 days of July, there were 20,042 COVID cases, vs 17,020 cases in the first 16 days of August.  During the first 16 days of this month, there were 308 deaths vs 197 from 01-16 July.

The Mozambican government has stated that an estimated 1.8 billion USD is needed to provide clean water to the entire population of the country. The government has called on private companies to invest the water sector. This comes as the government intends to increase provision of clean water from 65% to 85% of the population.

The Mocimboa da Praia Mayor Cheia Carlos Momba said that 62,000 people have fled the district during the insurgency. Mayor Momba stated that the insurgents burned down everything in the town and all public services were mostly destroyed, making the return of IDPs to the district not possible in the near term future.

Officials announced that 111 vehicles have been seized in Beira since COVID restrictions were imposed due to various violations. The vehicles have violated COVID restrictions primarily by transporting cargo and passenger limits in the city. The National Institute of Road Transport (INATRO) stated that 3,021 vehicles were inspected during these operations.

Officials stated that the Namicopo neighborhood in Nampula experiences high rates of criminality.  Motorcycle taxi drivers are often involved in criminality.  Police say the area experiences the highest rates of criminality in the city.
A fire broke out south of Chinda southwest of Mocimboa da Praia on 15 August. This is suspected to be related either to clashes between joint forces and the insurgency, or due to airstrikes.

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) on 17 August indicated that there was an urgent need to expand humanitarian assistance in Cabo Delgado. This comes as 9,200 IDPs were traveling between 28 July to 3 August to other displacement centers in the province.  There are reported to be more than 732,000 IDPs displaced from the province since 2017.  The IOM indicates that it needs $58 million to support emergency and post crisis efforts in Mozambique, including $21.7 million to provide emergency assistance in Cabo Delgado.

Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) spokesperson Col. Ronald Rwivanga stated during an interview that Rwandan forces are sharing intelligence with the SADC. This comes as cooperated sectors of responsibility were assigned to both forces. Col. Rwivanga also indicated that SADC forces were to secure Southern areas of Cabo Delgado, including Pemba, and would deploy as far north as Mueda, while Rwandan troops would secure MDP and Palma Districts.

Mozambican security forces repelled an insurgent attack at Litingina on 16 August.  Militants had been attempting to advance north to Nangade town itself. Insurgents reportedly sustained casualties in these clashes

At least 50 residents on 16 and 17 August were reported to have demonstrated in the Chingodzi Neighborhood of Tete City, near the airport, over the allegedly fraudulent sale of plots of land.  The protesters were part of a group who had been sold land by members of the Mozambican military and had built houses on this land; these houses on Monday were reported to have been "demolished without explanation".

At least 50 residents on  17 August demonstrated in the Chingodzi Neighborhood of Tete City from 0800hrs to 1500hrs on Tuesday before military police dispersed the crowd by firing in the air. Other unconfirmed reports said police had assaulted some of the demonstrators, and had also detained some of them as well.

At least 50 residents on 17 August demonstrated again in the Chingodzi Neighborhood of Tete City from 0800hrs to 1500hrs on Tuesday before military police dispersed the crowd by firing at least 100 live bullets in the air. Other unconfirmed reports said police had assaulted some of the demonstrators, and had also detained some of them as well.

The SADC on 18 August agreed to establish a joint regional terrorism center, which will be based in Tanzania.  This comes amid the ongoing Cabo Delgado insurgency.

The Mozambique Ministry of Health announced 694 new COVID cases and 13 deaths as of 18 August. The highest cases were in Maputo City with 145 cases and Maputo province with 136 cases. Admission  were at 32 and 33 were discharged during the past 24 hours.

President Nyusi conducted speech on 17 August, saying  that military offensive against insurgents needs to be partnered with aid and social/economic development.  This speech was significant in that it could indicate a new soft power approach by the government in Cabo Delgado to counter the insurgency.

President Nyusi spoke at the SADC on 17 August calling for the regional group to increase procurement of COVID vaccines. Nyusi stated that accelerated acquiring of vaccines and expanding the vaccination campaigns should be a priority for the bloc.

The Mozambican government announced that the first half of 2021 government revenue was at 127.4 billion, or about 48% of the total annual forecast of revenue predicted by the government.  This is on track to only ultimately cover 90% of the country's 2021 budget of 165.8 billion meticais.

Mozambique and Rwanda security forces as of 17 August continued to carry out clearing operations in Mocimboa da Praia. It was unclear if these operations were taking place in MDP town itself or if this referred to the wider district.  No recent confirmed clashes have been reported in MDP town.

RENAMO leader Momade issued a statement on 17 August that RENAMO members were being persecuted in Nhamatanda and Buzi districts of Sofala. Momade said that security forces in these areas were reportedly accusing the RENAMO members of supporting RENAMO dissidents, in some cases targeting demobilized RENAMO militia members.

RENAMO leader Momade stated on 17 August that the RENAMO former guerrillas are not receiving their monthly allowance paid for by the UN through the Mozambique government. RENAMO General Secretary Majibire stated that around 1,000 of groups former guerillas have not received these stipends for six months, repeating reports that surfaced last week.

The UN General in Mozambique clarified that the international community has finished providing payments to RENAMO guerillas over a year’s time. The UN General also stated that the payments should be coming from the government using public funds, though the UN can still contribute to these payments. The UN General stated that an agreement was being conducted with the government to resolve the payment of the pensions to demobilized RENAMO militia members.

RENAMO leader Momade raised concerns on 17 August over the “silence” of RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo, saying it was unclear where the dissident leader was and not possible to know if Nhongo was "planning" something.

Security forces arrested 11 Malawian citizens at an Interprovincial Bus Terminal in Maputo City on 17 August. Bus drivers believed the foreign nationals had been planted on the buses by police in order to target the bus drivers themselves.

The Teacher Training Institute (IFP) reported a COVID outbreak as 54 students tested positive in Matola as of 14 August. The officials stated that the school will be closed for 10 days before resuming.

The Mozambican government stated that precious metals and gemstones exported from the country will be subject to the issuance of certificates of origin from 20  August. The certificate of origin was to regulate the market of gems and minerals in conformity with the international practices.

The officials in Nampula have been accused of “secrecy” in process of setting up O&G exploration in Angoche in Nampula. The process has been ongoing for the past six years which was set to start by 2022. No details have been released regarding the activities of companies conducting the extraction.

Sources stated that large crowds gathered during the last day for the vaccination campaign in Maputo City on 18 August. Locals stated that they waited long queues to get inoculated. No details were available as to whether all waiting individuals were all vaccinated.

The Cabo Delgado Governor Tauabo said on 18 August that a lack of contact and of an official leadership of the insurgents makes dialogue with the insurgency impossible. Tauabo also said the group's motivations are unclear, and often shifting.

RENAMO leader Momade said on 17 August that 12 former RENAMO guerillas have been rejected from integration into the police due to a lack of qualifications.  Momade also indicated another 12 former RENAMO guerillas would be selected to be integrated into the police.

Rwandan Defense Forces Col. Ronald Rwivanga stated that the RDF has four phases for their security operations in Cabo Delgado. The first phase was to carry out combat operations to drive insurgents away from captured locations. The second phase is to carry out security operations to ensure the consolidation of these gains. The third phase was to stabilize and enable confidence of civilians in region. The last phase was to allow reform of the security sector in the province.  Rwivanga said security force reform could begin immediately as well.

Fires were reported in Mocimboa da Praia and south of the town on 17 August. The fire south of the town may indicate possible clashes between insurgents and security forces or airstrikes, though this is not confirmed.

Defense Minister Jaime Neto stated on 17 August that SADC forces are likely to go into action against insurgents “very soon” and that the SADC forces were currently deploying to areas of Cabo Delgado. Neto also stated that Rwandans have engaged militants several times over the past month and stabilized areas by driving out the insurgents.

Defense Minister Jaime Neto indicated that the road between Mueda and Palma is  now “safe” after recent security force operations, and stated that joint forces advancing against terrorist bases of “Siri 1” and Siri 2".
Mozambican helicopters fired on and killed two civilians on a road near Mucojo on 10 August.  The civilians, who were travelling to Mucojo to fish, were mistaken for insurgents.
Security forces detained and assaulted a civilian suspected to be an insurgent in Ruiea, near Mucojo, on 10 August. The victim was traveling to the coast.

Security forces exchanged gunfire with insurgents in Chicuaia Velha in Nangade on 14 August. No information was available regarding casualties. Unconfirmed reports stated that SADC Tanzanian and Botswanan forces were involved in these clashes.

Rwandan security forces resolved a dispute between civilians and Mozambican security forces in Palma on or around 10 August. The Mozambican forces reportedly had attempted to confiscate local civilians' property.  This incident generated significant support for Rwandan forces in the area.
Palma's district administrator was reported to have recently moved back into Palma after security forces recently cleared the area.  The administrator had previously been staying in Quitunda.

The SADC's Standby Force according to recent reports is being deployed to and will operate in Macomia, Muidumbe, Mueda, Nangade, and Quissanga Districts of Cabo Delgado, while Rwandan troops will secure Palma and MDP Districts.

Several sources reported ongoing clashes on Wednesday in the Mbau Forest area.  Rwandan military officials said that 90% of this forest area had been cleared, with 10% still in the hand of the insurgents. This offensive into forest areas of Southern Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) District is reportedly being carried out by troops attacking from the north from MDP town itself and via joint forces from the west coming from Mueda.  These sources also refer to airstrikes in the area prior to the joint assault to soften insurgent positions.

Large fires were reported in Miangalewa and just north of the town on 18 August. Such fires may correspond to attacks on the insurgent bases of "Syria 1" and "Syria 2" bases by joint forces. Mozambican Def. Minister Jaime Neto also this week indicated that there was an ongoing assault on the mobile insurgent bases of "Syria 1" and "Syria 2".

Two Mozambican military helicopters were reported to have "bombed" areas close to Litingina for at least 12 hours on 18 August, after an insurgent attack on Litingina was previously repelled on 16 August.  Militants were suspected to still be lingering on the outskirts of the town.  No information regarding casualties is currently available.

Sources have indicated that Rwandan troops operating in Cabo Delgado have to date been able to deal with insurgent ambushes more effectively than the Mozambican military. The Rwandan forces when met with ambushes during the recent advance on Mocimboa da Praia responded by maintaining order and launching counterattacks against insurgents, while Mozambican military units have regularly broke and fled in the face of these attacks.

Former president and still powerful political figure Armando Guebuza is reported to be “missing” in recent months. Guebuza reportedly did not attend the FRELIMO Central Committee sessions in late May, though he did make a brief public appearance days after this high level meeting.

The Ministry of Health officials announced that the around 627,382 individuals were fully vaccinated out of a total 1,750,872 who had taken the first dose of the vaccine. Fully vaccinated individuals were reported as follows: Maputo with 132,613 individuals, Maputo province with 109,713, Cabo Delgado with 66,694, and Nampula with 60,253. This comes as 104,157 were vaccinated on 19 August.

Police arrested 8 suspects wanted for attempted robbery after a brief gun battle with the suspects in Gogoma village of Sanga district on or around 12 August. Three of the robbers were injured in the gun fight. The suspects were in possession of melee weapons, an AK-47, and 6 ammunition rounds.

In Tete, the National Directorate for Livestock Development (DNDP) imposed on 19 August a ban on the movement of cattle, goats and pigs in the districts of Doa, Moatize, Maravia, Chifunde, Macanga, Zumbo and Tete city to counter an outbreak of foot and mouth disease.  An outbreak of the disease has also been reported in Magude District of Maputo Province.

The Ministry of Health announced 618 new COVID cases and 12 related deaths during the past 24 hours in Mozambique on 19 August. the cases were notable in Nampula province as 117 cases were recorded. This was followed by Maputo City with 109 cases.

Suspicious fires were reported north of Chitunda on 18 August. This comes as fires were also reported in Mbau during the same day, and could be related to either clashes between security forces and insurgents or airstrikes targeting insurgents.
Officials announced the dismissal of two newly appointed prison directors for the Ndhlavela Women’s Penitentiary on 17 August. The dismissed officials had ongoing court cases.
The UNWFP has resumed humanitarian flights to Macomia in Cabo Delgado as of 18 August.

Sources on 19 August reported that Rwandan troops believed that insurgents were receiving information regarding joint forces movements targeting insurgent positions ahead of these operations.  Most areas captured by joint forces in MDP in recent weeks are reported to be only recently deserted, with signs that people were present a short time before the arrival of joint forces.  This is an indication of possible infiltration of the armed forces by the insurgency, or at least of insurgents receiving information from inside the Mozambican military.

Several sources reported that a group of 26 journalists were selected and invited to visit the sites of military operations in Mocimboa da Praia for 5 days. The Ministry of Defense also stated that the journalist were allowed to choose the areas to cover but must inform the ministry before arriving in the area.  However, the journalists have not yet been allowed to travel to the area and are still in Pemba.  The group were initially told they would travel by land to MDP, and then later told they would travel by air.  Journalists suspect that insecurity in the north is the likely cause of this delay.  Some of the reporters ultimately remained in Pemba until the afternoon of 21 August before returning to Maputo; none were ultimately allowed to proceed into MDP District.

SERNIC agents recently were reported to have asked for a bribe from a foreign civilian at Ressano Garcia in Maputo. The Provincial Office for Combating Corruption stated that a Tanzanian citizen was detained for 19.5kg of opium.  SERNIC agents after the individual's arrest reportedly asked for USD150,000 and four luxury vehicles as a bribe for his release.  Another source said the Tanzanian drug dealer had bribed the officers and was on the run, and that a Mozambican national had been arrested at Ressano Garcia in possession of these drugs, reportedly working for the Tanzanian.

The UN issued a report stating that Islamic State (IS)'s activities in Mozambique led to the deterioration of the security situation in Cabo Delgado early 2021. The UN noted ISCAP attacks and activity on the islands of Matemo, Vamizi and Makalowe, including kidnappings and extortion attacks.  The reports also said it was unclear exactly the nature of the relations between ISCAP in Mozambique and DRC.  The report also indicated that the attack on Palma last March and previous capture of Mocimboa da Praia could have greater implications for regional peace and security. UN stated that around 2 million USD from banks, ID cards, and documents were seized from the attacks in the province.

Sources stated that insurgents destroyed the Chai Museum in Macomia during an attack in late June.  Chai is a significant village as it is where the first shots of the Mozambican War of Independence were fired.  Militants have attacked Chai multiple times during the course of the insurgency.

Health officials announced that 87,317 individuals were vaccinated as part of the first phase of the vaccination campaign in Inhambane. The initial plan was to have 88,300 individuals be vaccinated. Health officials stated that several of those not able to be inoculated had been recently infected with COVID.

USAID officials said on 20 August that the US government is ready to help rebuild infrastructure in Cabo Delgado impacted by insurgency. This comes as the USAID provided 60,000 relief kits to families affected by the insurgency.

The Cabo Delgado governor Valige Tauabo called for people to remain vigilant, saying to be on the look out for insurgents trying to blend into the civilian population during his visit in Nairoto on 20 August. The governor stated that insurgents may attempted to disguise themselves as displaced civilians.
Police arrested three suspects, a woman and two men, for falsifying paintings similar to the artworks created by Mozambican artist Malangatana. 35 fake artworks were seized during the arrest.

The Cabo Delgado Governor Valige Tauabo on 20 August stated that the return of displaced people to areas previously occupied by insurgents will be dependent on assessments made by the government. No specific timeline was stated as to when IDPs will able to return to their areas. This comes after reports that many IDPs want to return to MDP town, which was occupied by the insurgency from August 2020 - 08 August 2021.

SERNIC detained 50 foreigners with illegal residency during an operation in Tete between the 7 to 13 August. 32 were repatriated and 18 were still being repatriated. 20 foreigners were able to legalize their residency. 14 of those detained were in possession of fake SENAMI stamps.
The Ministry of Health announced 630 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 20 August. 10 deaths were announced during the past 24 hours. While 603 recoveries were reported.

The Judicial Court in Maputo rejected a list of 35 witnesses provided by the defense lawyers for the "Hidden Debts" case. President Nyusi was among the witnesses. The Judge of the case, Efigenio Baptista, said that the document was intended to harm conditions for a fair decision regarding the case. Among the witnesses included were the Mozambican President, Filipe Nyusi, the Prime Minister, Carlos Agostinho do Rosario, the Mozambican Minister of Justice, Helena Kida, and the Minister of Agriculture, Celso Correia.

A UNICEF report stated that Mozambican children are 10th most vulnerable in the world of any nation to the impacts of climate change. Children in the country have been exposed to a lack of health, education, protection, and exposure to diseases. Mozambique is also vulnerable to coastal flooding and vector borne disease.

Several sources reported that on the morning of 20 August, between 0500hrs and 0600hrs, a vehicle carrying 4 police officers, including reportedly 3 high ranking provincial police officials, encountered a "barricade" while travelling towards Ligogo village, about kms from Mavago village.  Their vehicle was then fired upon by unseen assailants.  The driver and one of the police officials were both reported to have sustained at least 2 gunshot wounds each.  Other sources late reported the driver had succumbed to his wounds.  The two other police officials fled the seen but were later reportedly located unharmed.  Police reinforcements arrived at the seen of that attack shortly after the incident and took the two injured men to Mavago Hospital; the two were later transferred to Lichinga Hospital.  One source reported two attackers were responsible for this attack.

Journalists stated that most of the villages and infrastructure between Macomia and Awasse have been destroyed and abandoned as of 16 August. Journalists traveled through the villages for the first time in months, escorted by security forces and stated that vehicles, goods, were left along the road due to the insurgent attacks.  This zone has been one of the most impacted areas by the insurgency.

Joint forces on 20 August reportedly took control over the Mbau area after several days of operations in forests near the town that included airstrikes and skirmishes with militants up to and reportedly on 20 August.  Other reports indicated the final "occupation" of this area was completed on Saturday. One source reported 11 insurgents killed in clashes in the area; Rwandan sources said around 80-100 insurgents had resisted the joint forces advance and clashed with security forces.  Other reports indicated that there was never a significant insurgent presence in the area during the joint forces offensive, and that militants had potentially fled south into Macomia, though this is also currently unverified.  Another source reported that Rwandan troops had occupied the area after a week of fighting.

Former Mozambican finance minister Manuel Chang will be extradited from South Africa to Mozambique where he will be eventually be tried for allegedly taking bribes as part of the USD2 billion “hidden debts” scandal that took place in 2013. Reports indicate that the US government was displeased with the decision, they believed that the US would be the best place for Chang to face a proper trial as several US investors lost millions in the coup. The trial for the 2013 loan scam is set to begin on 23 August in Maputo.

The new minimum wage in Mozambique may be approved by the Council of Ministers on 24 August. An agreement on the wage proposals will be subject for debate in the council. Details behind the consensus has yet been disclosed.  A new agreement on the minimum wage would likely forestall any potential over unrest over unhappiness regarding the minimum wage.

The Ministry of Health announced 510 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 21 August. The highest number of new cases was reported in Nampula Province with 125 cases, followed by Niassa and Gaza with 93 cases each, Maputo city recorded only 40 cases. Two deaths were announced during the past 24 hours, while 1,331 recoveries were reported.
The reconstruction of the 22 burned houses in Chamanculo D, Maputo City began on 21 August. The project is expected to be completed in two weeks time.

Security forces arrested two illegal immigrants, from Malawi and Eswatini, in Maputo city on 21 August. One of the suspects had an expired passport, who arrived in the city on 20 August and bound to Gorongosa. The other suspect was caught without any legal documents.

The National Migration Service (SENAMI) deployed 18 personnel at the Junta Interprovincial Bus Terminal, Maputo city, to monitor the movement of interprovincial and cross-border buses. This development is part of the ongoing operations against illegal immigrants after the arrest of several illegal immigrants in Maputo in recent weeks.

Mangroves are under threat in Inhambane Province. Several kilometers of mangroves have been destroyed along the coastal part of the province brought by residential and business constructions as well as use of mangrove wood as a method for cooking.

On 22 August, a journalist embedded with joint forces operating in the Mbau area of Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) reported 100 people had been rescued or discovered by Mozambican and Rwandan troops.  Most of those rescued were reported to be elderly people and children - people who were less mobile.  It is unclear if those found in the area were captives, family members, or other supporters of the insurgency.  This report comes just two days after joint forces declared the Mbau Forest area clear of insurgents.

Joint forces were reported to be carrying out continued operations to target militants fleeing the Mbau area with some of the group reported to be fleeing into the Quiterajo area of Macomia.  Other sources said helicopters were dropping bombs and/or strafing insurgent positions at the group's bases of Siri 1 and Siri 2, reportedly close to the banks of the Messalo River.  Militants were reported to have placed stones and logs along paths in the area to slow the advance of the joint forces, who are reportedly attempting to surround the area.

Truck drivers on the afternoon of 22 August were reported to be on strike at the Lebombo Crossing Point, just across the border in South Africa from the Mozambican border crossing at Ressano Garcia.  Drivers were protesting "over alleged non-compliance with the queue by other truck drivers", according to a Mozambican National Migration Service spokesperson.  This led to an indefinite stoppage of traffic at Ressano Garcia, with authorities saying travelers should utilize alternative routes until the situation is resolved.

Mozambican electricity company, EDM, said on 19 August that it would restore power to all districts in Cabo Delgado within 45 days. The announcement was made after the company surveyed transmission lines that were destroyed and damaged by the insurgents in recently liberated areas.  Key transmission lines that must be repaired from Awasse to Macomia, to Mueda and to Mocimboa da Praia town.  Insurgents have destroyed an estimated 313 kms of medium and low voltage power lines in Cabo Delgado.

Authorities announced that movements across the Ressano Garcia border were reestablished in the late hours of 22 August. This came hours after truck drivers were reported to be on strike at the Lebombo Crossing Point, just across the border in South Africa from the Mozambican border crossing.  Drivers were protesting "over alleged non-compliance with the queue by other truck drivers", according to a Mozambican National Migration Service spokesperson.  This led to an indefinite stoppage of traffic at Ressano Garcia.

The Ministry of Health announced 261 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 22 August. The highest number of new cases was reported in Maputo City with 56 cases, followed by Inhambane with 52 cases and Nampula with 41 cases. 15 deaths were announced during the past 24 hours, while 1,360 recoveries were reported.

The trial of Mozambique’s biggest corruption case aka 'hidden debts' starts today, 23 August, at Machava Maximum Security Penitentiary. 19 people, including former President Guebuza's advisers, as well as former officials of the state intelligence services are among the defendants. Guebuza will not stand trial today after his name was not included in the list of deponents released by the supreme court on 21 August.

The two presidential candidates vying for the nomination of the Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM), Jose Domingo and Lutero Simango urged members of the party to remain calm and refrain from creating tension with fellow party groups during the assembly in Beira city on 20 August. The statement follows reports of alleged internal disputes between members of MDM who support the two potential candidates. MDM's congress, where the new leader will be elected, is scheduled this December.

Nampula Mayor Paulo Vahanle on 22 August for regular channeling of funds for the municipality's investment and municipal development. Vahanle said that amid recent developments the city, it still needs consistent support from the government for further progress.

Security forces recovered arms and ammunition as well a motorcycle following anti-terror operations in Nangade district on or before 23 August.  The motorcycle was reportedly utilized in attacks on Litingina, Eduardo Mondlane, and Ngangolo villages.

Consultants forecasted on 23 August that the country's economic growth could accelerate by 4.4 percent in 2022 from 2.8 percent in 2021. The said growth will be sustained by strengthening domestic demand and increased exports of natural gas. ENI’s project is on track to secure its first gas exports next year which would lead to a 27.1 percent increase in country's gas production, boosting exports and revenues.

Zimbabwe police arrested  two suspected smugglers in Gozi area, just across the Zimbabwe-Mozambique border, on 17 August for smuggling 224 bags of charcoal and bribery. Reports suggest that suspects, who were aboard a truck conveying the smuggled goods from Mozambique, offered USD 200 bribe to the police which led to the arrest.

Zimbabwe police arrested  two suspected smugglers in Gozi area, just across the Zimbabwe-Mozambique border, on 17 August for smuggling 224 bags of charcoal and bribery. Reports suggest that suspects, who were aboard a truck conveying the smuggled goods from Mozambique, offered USD 200 bribe to the police which led to the arrest.

Truck drivers renewed  demonstrations on the evening of 23 August at the Lebombo Border Crossing, just across from the Ressano Garcia Border crossing between South Africa and Mozambique.  These protests again stopped traffic from crossing between the two countries. The protesters accused immigration officials of giving out “preferred” treatment to other truck drivers, saying that they were being cleared to cross the border earlier. The drivers claimed that bribing was the cause of the delays by the customs. Protesting drivers also said that tanker trucks were always being cleared faster compared to dump trucks, which they claim spend around three days before being cleared to pass through the border.

The Public Ministry on 23 August began the trial of 19 defendants in the "Hidden Debts" case. The case of the prosecution is primarily focused on Armando Ndambi Guebuza, son of the former president, saying he received the largest share of funds diverted from loans that were obtained via guarantees from the Mozambican state.  The prosecution also said the 19 had joined a "gang" to rob the Mozambican state which ultimately left the country in a difficult economic position.  Guebuza alone is accused of having stolen 28 million euros as part of this scandal.

Officials announced the full reopening of the  Ponta d'Ouro border from 21-22 August.  The border crossing for two months had not operated full time because of a lack of health officials, but will now operate 7 days a week again. SENAMI stated that South African side of the border was still lacking a health personnel to control and validate the PCR test of individuals passing through. The port was set to operate from 08:00 to 05:00 from Monday to Sunday.

Officials stated that taxes from megaprojects in different industrial sectors of the country in 2021 had seen an increase of 57.9% compared to last year, representing 15% of all state revenue collected by the government. Oil exploration revenue was with the highest revenue with 7.4 billion meticais, while energy production projects produced a revenue of 5.7 billion meticais.

The Ministry of Health announced that COVID cases have seen an increase in northern Mozambique as 57.6% of the country's cases were in the province of Zambezia, Nampula, Niassa and Cabo Delgado. 43.4% were from the southern provinces in recent days, representing a significant drop in cases in Central and Southern Mozambique.  A total of 267 cases were reported from Maputo City, Inhambane, Maputo province, Manica, Gaza, Tete, and Sofala.

The Ministry of Health announced 343 new COVID cases and eight new deaths in Mozambique on 23 August. This brings the total cases to 143,127 and total deaths to 1,808. 15 new hospitalizations were reported, while 24 were discharged.

Around 65% of the IDP population of Quitunda village just outside of the Afungi LNG Camp as of 23 August were reported to have returned to Palma town, slowly repopulating the district capital as security conditions improve in the district in the wake of the deployment of Rwandan troops in the area.

Sources stated on 23 August that residents are gradually returning to Macomia and Quissanga districts of Cabo Delgado. Locals stated that even with the return of the population, they still fear possible insurgent attacks in the districts. Quissanga has not seen any recent militant attacks, while Macomia town itself and surrounding villages have also not seen attacks for some time, though insurgents are still present in parts of northern and eastern Macomia.

Joint forces during clashes in the Mbau area on 20 August were reported to have captured 10 insurgents.  Other previous reports also indicated 11 insurgents killed in these clashes.

UAE Ambassador to Mozambique Khalid Al Qahtani conducted a meeting with Minister of the Sea, Inland Waters, and Fisheries Augusta Maita in Maputo. The two discussed the strengthening of ties and cooperation in the maritime sector between the two countries.

The Bank of Mozambique was reported on 24 August to have dissolved an illegal credit agency in Nampula. The Vision Service, Solucoes Financeiras was illegally charging 35% interest rates to customers.

Sources stated that the Rwandan forces and Mozambican forces have not coordinated with the SADC Standby Force in Cabo Delgado against the insurgency in any significant way to date.  Rwandan and Mozambican troops continue to coordinate with one another, but have not mounted any confirmed combined operations with the SADC force.  The SADC in turn have not consulted with the African Union in regards to their mission in Mozambique.

The Marracuene District Government on 24 August carried out demolitions of several homes built of "precarious materials", reportedly built illegally, within the district in the Milhulamentine area on a plot of about 1200 hectares which a private company claims to own.  A group claiming to be the owners of the homes destroyed protested at the site on Tuesday afternoon and were reported to have clashed with private guards hired by the company and police officers supporting the guards.  11 guards were reportedly injured in these clashes.  Police and the guards reportedly opened fire on the demonstrators, also physically attacked demonstrators.

The Budget Monitoring Forum on 24 August said it would challenge the extradition of former finance minister Chang back to Mozambique. Chang was previously detained in South Africa upon the request of the US. Chang is one of the defendants involved with the Hidden Debts case. The NGO believes that Chang will not be held accountable for his involvement in the Hidden Debts case in Mozambique due to the case's links to top FRELIMO elites.
The Ministry of Health announced 528 new COVID cases and 5 new deaths in Mozambique on 24 August. This brings the total deaths to 1,813 and 127,852 total cases.

The US government criticized South Africa’s decision to extradite Manuel Chang to Mozambique during ongoing Hidden Debts trial. Chang was detained in South Africa under the arrest warrant from the US. US officials stated that "justice would be better served" if he was extradited to the US.

One of 19 defendants of the Hidden Debts trial, a former government official stated that former President Guebuza and Current President Nyusi were aware of corruption scheme. State Security and Investigation Service (SISE), Cipriano Mutota stated that the two meetings concerning the scheme were conducted at the presidential palace, with then President Guebuza in attendance at these meetings.

The first defendant to testify at the Hidden Debts case, former State Information and Security Services Director Mutota, stated that President Nyusi was a key organizers of the corruption scheme during the Hidden Debts trial.

Sources reported on 25 August that Mozambican security forces detained 8 insurgents during an operation between Ingoane and Pequeue of Macomia district on 18 August along the Mpwizizi River. The insurgents were suspected to have fled the joint forces who had attacked the Mbau area. This comes as two other suspected individuals linked with insurgents were also detained on Matemo Island during the operations.
Security forces on 17 August were reported to have arrested two suspected insurgents after locals identified the two and reported their whereabouts on Matemo island.

Rwandan security forces destroyed an insurgent base in Ubaua area of Quissanga District during the ongoing insurgent clearing operations. This base was likely located in northern Quissanga District, where insurgents have maintained bases in the past.

The Central Assistance Brigade of FRELIMO Manuel Tome called for vigilance among the Sofala populace against terrorist groups. Tome stated that insurgents may withdraw from Cabo Delgado and take refuge in Sofala province.
Police detained a suspect for threatening people with a toy gun on a highway in Nampula on the afternoon of 22 August.

Security forces detained two guards for rape charges in Infantario Provincial De Manica in Chimoio on 24 August. The suspects lured three girls with valuables and sexually abused them since this past April.
The Mozambique prosecution on Monday 23 August stated that all 19 defendants in the Hidden Debts case should pay compensation to the state of $2.9 billion, not including interest.

Minister of Health Deputy Director Benigna Matsinhe stated that the vaccination campaign is taking place countrywide, and that as of 25 August, individuals with the first Sinovac inoculation would be given their second dose.
Unconfirmed reports indicated insurgents launched an attack on Litingina and Nkonga villages in Nangade on or before 22 August. A total of five civilians deaths were reported during the attacks.

Sources stated on 22 August that much of the population of the village of Litingina in Nangade had fled to Mbuide after recent insurgent attacks. This comes as insurgents reportedly attacked Litingina and Nkonga in recent days.

Security forces were to remove the placed barriers by insurgents around the “siri 2” / Syria 2 base during operations near Messalo River on 24 August. The barricade placed was to prevent the advancement of the security forces.  Joint Forces are reported to be in the process of encircling insurgents in this area after recently capturing the Mbau area from militants.
Sources stated that the Goba border post remains closed in Maputo. This is the only border post that has remained closed out of the four border crossings in the province.

A report issued on 24 August indicated that a large number of factory workers have been illegal detained and were forced to work inside the Dugongo Cimentos factory since the beginning of the COVID pandemic in Mtutuine. 300 factory workers have been "virtually held captive" since the beginning of the pandemic at the factory. The factory also placed the workers into an unofficial lockdown prevent employees from leaving starting March 2020.

Reports stated that the Dugongo Cimentos plant managers previously beat employees who stop working. A former employee claimed that plant workers were forced to take 12-hour evening shifts, were given pay cuts if they were ill, and were not allowed to obtain medical assistance.

The EU announced that it will donated 32.8 million EUR for the mapping out of risk zones along the Buzi River in central Mozambique. The project was to determine which areas are at risk for natural disasters in the Buzi District. The mapping project would show the possible effects of cyclones and floods.

The Johannesburg High Court on 25 August ordered that South Africa's Justice Minister delay the extradition of former Mozambican Finance Minister Manuel Chang to Maputo until the court has ruled on his case.  Chang now cannot be sent to Mozambique pending a further hearing on his case on the 27th of August.  Lawyers had suspected Chang would be sent back to Mozambique at any time before the Mozambican anti-corruption watchdog body the Budget Monitoring Forum launched an urgent appeal to the court to stall the extradition.  If the Budget Monitoring Forum's lawyers win the case, Chang will remain in South Africa until a further hearing is held, likely in September, over whether or not he should be extradited. Chang could be sent back to Mozambique at any time if the appeal is rejected.  Chang has been detained in South Africa since December 2018 on corruption charges, and is a key suspect in the Hidden Debts Scandal.  The trial for the Hidden Debts Case began in Mozambique on 23 August and is ongoing.

The Institute for Multiparty Democracy calls for greater transparency in DDR process.  This call for greater transparency was triggered by complaints from RENAMO that demobilized guerilla fighters are not receiving their pension benefits; the DDR process meanwhile has been delayed due to funding shortages.
The South African Airways announced it would resume operations on 23 September after a period of suspension of all flights.  The new flights will include service to and from Maputo.

The  majority of Mozambican journalists from Cabo Delgado are not being allowed to cover the ongoing insurgency, and have not recently been given any access to the northern areas of the province where the conflict is ongoing, saying security forces prevent journalists from travelling to these areas.
The Ministry of Health announced 377 new COVID cases and 9 new COVID deaths in Mozambique on 25 August. Maputo City recorded 101 of the new cases, and Nampula province with 70 cases.
Joint forces have reportedly ”surrounded” insurgent bases Syria 1 and Syria 2 in Cabo Delgado as of 24 August. The advance was reported four days after security forces seized Mbau.
Local media reproted that the municipal government  official in Chiure were “selling” land to IDPs that had been set aside to be given to the IDPs.

A group of 10 suspects was reported to have broken into the residence belonging to Director of the Tax Authority's Collections Post in Chiure on 22 August. The robbers stole 600,000 meticais after incapacitating a guard. The gang were suspected to have come from Nampula, rather than to have come from Chiure.
Locals attacked and lynched a robber who was found attempting to steal valuables from a residence in Mueda early morning of 25 August.
Locals attacked and lynched a robber who was found attempting to steal valuables from a residence in Mueda early morning of 25 August.

Energey Minister Max Tonela on 24 August stated that the Mozambican Government and Total are expected to discuss the restart of the the company's gas project in Cabo Delgado in September.  There is some speculation that the LNG project could restart in the first half of 2022.  These discussions have been made possible by the entry of Rwandan and SADC forces into Cabo Delgado and the improvement of the security situation in the province, particularly in Palma District where the country's LNG project at Afungi is located.

Sources stated that police detained two individuals and destroyed nine illegally built houses in the Milhulamentine area of Marracuene district on the morning of 24 August. Six civilians were injured during the incident.

Dozens of public transport drivers conducted a strike as a protest at Mangueiras stop near Lhanguene cemetery, south Maputo City on the morning of 25 August. This comes as the drivers condemned the unjust actions of police against them. Locals claimed that the drivers forced their passengers and later gathered at the Mangueiras stop before the protest. The protesters claimed that the police were setting up road blocks and were waiting for the semi-collective passenger drivers to fill their vehicles with passengers before detaining them and brining them to the police station to pay 6,000 to 10,000 meticais for overloading seating limits.

Unconfirmed reports indicated that a group of men were detained after being spotted by locals in Chiure and sent back to Nampula. This comes as local officials have called on locals to remain vigilant to possible insurgent movements and unconfirmed reports of insurgent recruits.
Zambian and Mozambique officials intend to have a series of meetings to discuss bilateral cooperation. The meeting would focus on the agricultural and energy sectors of both countries.

Health Authorities stated that actions were set to improve the healthcare system on 25 August. The Minister of Health, Armindo Tiago stated that the health response to the pandemic has been satisfactory and that the maintenance of PPE distribution, and provision of additional COVID bed capacity.

False reports on 25 August circulated that RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo had been captured in Manica.  President Nyusi in a speech later in the day said that a "fake Mariano Nhongo" had been arrested, with sources later saying the arrest took place in Gorongosa. The individual in question, identified as a "young man" had reached out to authorities claiming to be Nhongo, reportedly speaking to security and political leadership in Tete, Maputo, and Inhambane.  President Nyusi called on authorities to remain vigilant for such type of individuals and that the detainee would be presented to the public.

Police arrested a driver for smuggling at the Lebombo border post just across the Ressano Garcia on 24 August. The man was stopped by a K9 unit leading to his arrest. Police seized 48 packs of crystal meth during the arrest.

The Forum of Mozambican Associations of Persons with Disabilities (FAMOD) stated that they were excluded from the vaccination campaign conducted countrywide. FAMOD claimed that individuals with disabilities were were not included. FAMOD stated that they have contacted the Ministry of Health regarding the issue.
The Finnish government stated that Finnish soldiers were set to participate in EU training mission in Mozambique on 26 August. The Finnish soldiers were also to be deployed in Mali.

The Tanzania police chief said that a recent attack in Dar es Salaam could be related to the Tanzanian security forces involvement in Cabo Delgado. The police chief stated that the attack in Tanzania was a reflection of Tanzania's supporting Mozambican forces.

The Mozambican police stated that they do not have information on the location of RENAMO Junta Leader Nhongo. The police also stated that they would not reveal the locations of RENAMO dissidents for “security reasons”. This comes as police said that they are currently working to locate Nhongo.

Officials announced that drivers will now be required to fill out “travel bulletins” at police checkpoints in Nampula to reduce accidents. The bulletins were to log the travel of the drivers in the province.

A senior Mozambican intelligence officer claimed that millions of USD were used as a bribe to negotiate with Lebanese businessman Jean Boustani for the Privinest group. The official was a witness during the Hidden Debts trial. The loans of 2.2 billion USD from Credit Suisse and VTB of Russia were issued by the former government administration and were provided to the security linked companies. Privinvest was the only company that became the contractor for three security linked companies

Sources stated that the defendant Teofilo Nhangumele stated during the Hidden Debt trial that President Nyusi encouraged the maritime protection project for the economic zone. Nhangumele also stated that former President Guebuza also proposed an improved version of the project to Nyusi and other ministers during a meeting.

Sources stated that elephant and buffalo were tramping and invading agricultural areas in Mecula, Niassa on 26 August. Locals stated that the presence of the animals were sometimes stopped transportation in the area.

The Ministry of Health announced that COVID positivity rate has dropped to 10.6 percent as of 25 August. The authorities stated that 3,570 COVID tests were conducted and only 377 positive cases were reported. The 10.6% was the lowest rate since 17 June with 9.9 percent positivity rate.

The Ministry of Health announced 436 new COVId cases and 3 COVID deaths in Mozambique on 26 August.  A majority of the cases were recorded in Zambezia province with 95 cases and Inhambane province with 89 cases. While 2,046 daily recoveries were recorded.

The Judge for the Embraer case has postponed the announcement of the sentencing for the defendant on 13 September. This comes as the defendats of the case were former minister of transport and communications Paulo Zucula, former chairman of Mozambican Airlines Jose Viegas, and former SASOL country manager Mateus Zimba.

The Mozambican government announced that it would introduce cargo drones to deliver humanitarian assistance to individuals affected by natural disaster. The drone project was in partnership with the WFP and EU.

Joint forces of Mozambican military and pro-government militiamen exchanged gunfire with insurgents at Samora Machel village on 20 August. This comes as insurgents conducted an attack in the area and beheaded a civilian.
Insurgents on 20 August beheaded a civilian in Samora Machel village in Nangade.  Militants later clashed with troops in the area.
Insurgents raided Lijungo, Nangade after fleeing from the security advance in Samora Machel on 20 August. 2 civilians were injured during the raid.

The African Development Bank president Akinwumi Adesina on 27 August stated that Total may works on its LNG project in Mozambique within the next 18 months after the deployment of Rwandan and SADC forces into the country that have significantly improved the security situation since mid-July.  The bank also regards Total's LNG project in Cabo Delgado as viable in the long term.

President Filipe Nyusi announced on 27 August the resumption of in-person classes in all institutions and educational levels countrywide. The president warned that if COVID precautions were not followed that the  in-person classes may be suspended again.  Gym may also resume operations, while other COVID restrictions have been kept in place for another 30 days, beginning on 27 August.  The curfew will be relaxed slightly, and will now be in place from 2200 to 0400hrs, adjusted from 2100hrs to 0400hrs.

On 27 August, joint Mozambican-Rwandan forces attacked insurgent positions at Ntchinga in Muidumbe District, capturing the area.  While Ntchinga has been used as an insurgent base in the past, it was unclear if clashes took place in the area or if troops had occupied an abandoned insurgent base.

The National Conventional Arms Control Committee stated that there was no violation with the laws and regulations regarding the provision of arms by South Africa to the security forces in Cabo Delgado.  Specifically, two helicopters provided to the Mozambican government from a South African private company were authorized by the South Africa government.  The NCACC also said there was no proof either of claims that a South African based company, DAG, had carried out indiscriminate shootings in Cabo Delgado.

The Ministry of Health announced that 731 new COVID cases and 9 deaths were reported in Mozambique on 27 August. Niassa province recorded the highest number of infections with 269 cases and Nampula with 156 cases. Among the new cases 16 were hospitalized while 10 were discharged. The total hospitalization were at 147.

The National Institute of Health intends to conduct a study determining the effectiveness of vaccines in Mozambique. The study was to determine the effectivity in immunizing civilians as the most used vaccine in the country was the Sinopharm vaccine. Officials stated that the vaccine has seen 90 percent effectivity in preventing severe illnesses and death from COVID.

Media reporting indicated that joint forces assisted 684 displaced people to return back to Palma on 28 August. The first batch were from Quintunda village which housed around 10,000 people. Note that previous reports had indicated some IDPs had already returned to Palma town.

The Ministry of Health announced 139 new COVID cases and 9 related deaths in Mozambique on 29 August. Six of the new cases were admitted while 11 were discharged; there are currently 12,475 active cases in the country.

The Supreme Court announced the suspension of the Hidden Debts trial for a day after two tents used to conduct the trials was destroyed by strong winds in Maputo City on 28 August. The court session was to resume on 29 August.

Reports on 30 August indicated that 6 possible financiers of the Cabo Delgado insurgency had been identified, and that three of these financiers were in Tanzania while the other three were in Mozambique. Two of the financiers were reportedly in Maputo and another one in Pemba.  No specific details regarding the identities of these individuals is currently available.

The Japan Embassy in Mozambique announced a donation of EUR 1.5 million through the WFP on 30 August. The donation was to allow the provision of canned fish for a year's supply for 25,000 displaced individuals.

The Officials resumed the Hidden Debt trial on 29 August in Maputo, with Ndambi Guebuza, the son of the former President Guebuza, called to testify. Ndambi denied the testimonies of other defendants and claimed that he never received money from Privinvest, saying he was not involved in the corruption scheme.

Insurgents on 24 August beheaded several fishermen near Mucojo, and injured three other fishermen who were able to escape from the attack.  These militants were believed to have fled Southern MDP from the ongoing joint forces offensive.  Civilians in the area said militants were believed to be active in the Nagulue/Simbolongo area, north of Mucojo.

Insurgents on 24 August beheaded several fishermen near Mucojo, and injured three other fishermen who were able to escape from the attack.  Some sources reported as many as 10 fishermen killed in this attack; other sources said the fishermen were killed in a series of attacks, with beheadings also in the villages of Simbolongo, Nambija, and Nacutuco.  Note one source reported this incident as having occured on 26 August. These militants were believed to have fled Southern MDP from the ongoing joint forces offensive.  Civilians in the area said militants were believed to be active in the Nagulue/Simbolongo area, north of Mucojo.

Both Kenya and Tanzania's intelligence agencies are reported to be on high alert with Cabo Delgado insurgents reportedly on the run after Mozambican and Rwandan troops ousted the insurgents from Mocimboa da Praia in early August.  There is a concern in both countries that militants could flee north into both countries.  Recently, Kenyan security forces arrested two suspected militants, including one Tanzanian national, who were suspected of plotting a terror attack in Mombasa on the anniversary of the death of Sheikh Aboud Rogo, a Kenyan cleric killed in Mombasa in 2012.  Many of Rogo's followers fled into Tanzania, and ultimately into Mozambique, where some of them are suspected of being linked to the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

A Chinese national was killed during the course of a robbery in Beira during the week of 22-28 August.  After this incident, the Chinese embassy in Maputo put pressure on the Mozambican government to provide greater protection for its nationals living, working, and visiting Mozambique.  No further details on the incident were immediately available, though the Chinese national appeared to have been targeted specifically in the incident.
Authorities in Tete are investigating the existence of a mass grave dated back to the country's War of Independence.  The grave's location has been reported by civilians in Changara District.

Kenyan security forces have indicated that "accomplices" of two terror suspects recently arrested in the port city of Mombasa who were not yet in police custody had recently been to "Mozambique and the DRC".  One of the wanted suspects, Salim Rashid Mohammad, reportedly evaded a police dragnet and was thought to have fled back into Tanzania.  In March, Kenya reported two men wanted on terrorism charges were believed to have fled the Kenyan coast to travel to Cabo Delgado.

A South African court on 28 August ruled that former Mozambican Finance Minister Manuel Chang would remain in prison in South Africa until at least 17 September, when an appeal to stop his extradition to Mozambique will be heard.  Chang's extradition previously had been delayed until at least 27 August.

A suspicious vessel was seized last week by Mozambican military units off the Mocimboa da Praia coast.  The vessel was carrying 7.5 tones of products, destined for Maganja village in Palma District.  Maritime travel for civilian vessels is currently restricted due to security reasons between Ibo and Palma.  The vessel had false documents saying it was bound for Matemo island, but later admitted it was sailing to Maganja.   One crew member said the vessel had knowingly violated the sailing restriction in order to assist the population of Maganja.  Authorities suspect the vessel may have been transporting supplies to the insurgency.

Joint forces during the week of 22-28 August occupied the village of Naquitengue, north of Mbau, during clearing operations in Southern Mocimboa da Praia district.  It was unclear if any clashes took place at this location.

The US Government launched the Improved Family Planning Initiative (USAID IFPI) project worth USD40.5 million to increase the quality of and access to reproductive health care in Nampula, Sofala, and Zambezia provinces. The five-year project will be implemented by local and international organizations led by Pathfinder International. This development was brought by the high maternal mortality rate and other health issues of both mothers and their children in the country

A parliamentary deputy for the Mozambique Democratic Movement (MDM), Silverio Ronguane, submitted papers works as MDM's presidential candidate on 29 August. The party's new leader will be elected this December during its congress.

From January to June 2021, about 6,800 people stopped donating blood in the country due to COVID-19 pandemic. 63,308 blood donors were recorded same period last year versus 56,434 this year. Authorities urged the public to continue donating and prevent any blood shortages.

The French government announced on 30 August plans to donate 10 million vaccines to the countries of the African Union (AU) over the next three months. AstraZeneca and Pfizer vaccines will be allocated and distributed through the African Union's Vaccine Acquisition Trust (AVAT) and COVID-19 Vaccines Global Access (COVAX).  The donation is part of France's commitment to share at least 60 million vaccines by the end of the year.

South African  scientists are monitoring a new COVID-19 variant detected in the country. The new variant, C.1.2, has been detected in all provinces in South Africa a  low rate. It was first detected in May and believed to have spread to seven other countries. C.1.2 contains many mutations associated in other variants with increased transmissibility and reduced sensitivity to neutralizing antibodies, however, scientists have yet been ascertain how the antibodies affect the virus' behavior.  There is a significant threat this new variant could spread in the near future into Mozambique.

On 28 August, the Confederation of Mozambican Business Associations (CTA) asks the Mozambican Government to revoke new regulations on the imposition of fiscal stamps on alcoholic drinks and tobacco products. The group claimed that the new regulation will burden the businesses, especially now during  the pandemic.

The Ministry of Health announced 190 new COVID cases and two related deaths in Mozambique on 30 August. Niassa recorded the highest new COVID-19 infections with 63 cases, followed by Maputo City with 36. Over the last 24 hours, 11 more cases were admitted, 14 were discharged and 864 have recovered.
Revenues of the tourism sector in Mozambique have collapsed by 95% since the COVID-19 outbreak in 2020. Affected areas includes hotel and lodging, restaurants, among other investments.

Former President Armando Guebuza attended the Hidden Debts trial on 30 August  to witness the testimony of his son, Armando Ndambi Guebuza. His son was accused of association to delinquency, breach of trust, forgery of documents and passive corruption in the case. The trial started one hour late due to undisclosed reasons.

An increase of road traffic accidents has recorded in Maputo province during the curfew period. In August, 15 deaths were reported in 11 road accidents in the province. One of the causes of the said accidents is driving under the influence of alcohol. Maputo's ring road, EN1, EN2 and EN4 registered the most accidents.

Mozambican Police arrested four Mozambican soldiers in late August for allegedly assaulting people and invaded houses in Sussundenga district, Manica. The suspects reportedly stole 70,000 Meticais inside a house. Police officers recovered two Ak-47 rifles and ammunition from the suspects.  The gang of four had reportedly deserted the Mozambican army in Cabo Delgado before coming to Sussundenga.  The group were arrested during a home invasion incident.

More than 200 Mozambican doctors under the Order of Doctors of Mozambique (OrMM) remain unemployed amid shortage of health professionals as a result of Covid-19 pandemic.

Sources had originally reported this as an attack only on the Mucojo area.  Militants beheaded as many as 10 fishermen in these attacks, and were believed to be fleeing the ongoing joint forces offensive in MDP District.  One source reported these incidents as having occurred on 26 August.

Unconfirmed reports indicated that on 30 August, SADC troops in Cabo Delgado began preparing for integration into combat operations in Cabo Delgado.  This operational move reportedly came after a meeting of Mozambican, Rwandan, and SADC military personnel.

A suspicious fire incident was reported on 25 August in an area north of Palma along road to Quionga.  This incident could indicate either clashes between security forces and insurgents, and insurgent attack, or airstrikes in this area.

A suspicious fire incident was reported on 25 August in Malamba village.  No other details on this incident are currently available. This incident could indicate either clashes between security forces and insurgents, and insurgent attack, or airstrikes in this area.
