Increasing rates of malaria and diarrhea have been reported in the Maputo City outskirts, including districts of Ka Lhamanculo and KaMavota, from January to June 2021. Authorities said that poor hygiene measures as well as dirty stagnant water and garbage have caused the resurgence of water born diseases in the area.

On 25 August, President Nyusi urged senior managers of the government not participate in any type of corruption and to closely monitor their subordinates.  He admits corruption in Mozambique is still prevalent with Nampula City and Province as the most corrupt area of the country. Corruption cases leading to disciplinary action notably increased last year with 1,290 cases recorded in 2020 versus 911 in 2019.

Renamo President, Ossufo Momade, said on 26 August that payments of pensions to the demobilized 1,000 ex-Renamo guerrillas will restart soon. The said payments were suspended six months ago due to lack of funds.  The World Bank and other organizations are reportedly working together in order to restart these payments.

Residents of communities near coal mining zones in Tete have recently complained of several health issues caused by mining projects in the area. Houses have collapsed due to detonation while release of coal dust threatened the public health. Locals also complain of the non-compliance with the resettlement package by the three companies. More than 1,700 families have been resettled due to the extractive industry, with around 1,200 families still waiting to be resettled.

LAM Mozambique Airlines is reportedly selling Pemba-Nairobi flight tickets under LAM/Precision Air one way for around 43,000 Mozambican meticais. The routing is Pemba to Zanzibar to Nairobi with an ETD of 1130hrs. and ETA 1830hrs.

RENAMO President Ossufo Momade said that a recent election of the President of Marromeu city council was rigged by FRELIMO. RENAMO filed an appeal to the Ministry of State Administration, however, no response has been received to date.

The Mozambican Government approved on 26 August the new national minimum wages by sector of activity in both the civil service and in the private sector instead of national minimum wage.  This changes will take effect retroactively from 01 August. There will be a 5% increase in civil service wages to 4,691 meticais against the 4,468 meticais since 2019. Meanwhile, in other sectors, the minimum wage increase varies from 1.5% to 8.7% increase depending on its bracket. Details are as follows: Agriculture, hunting and forestry – 6.9 percent; Industrial and semi-industrial fishing – 3.7 percent; The Kapenta (Lake Tanganyika sardine) fishery on the Cahora Bassa reservoir in Tete province – 3.2 percent; Mining – 6.4 percent; Quarries and sandpits – 3.2 per cent; Salt pans – 5.1 percent; Manufacturing industry – 6.4 percent; Bakeries – 7 percent; Cashew industry – 8.7 percent; Electricity, gas and water, large companies – 7.2 percent; Small companies – 7.2 percent; Building industry – 3.2 percent; Non-financial services – 6.6 percent; Hotel industry – 1.5 percent; Banking, insurance and other financial services – 7.25 percent; Micro-finance – 5.1 percent. For the private sector, the government only sets the minimum wage. All wages above the minimum are negotiated between the employers and the unions. Union groups hoped for a higher increase, however, it's not possible as of the moment due to the negative impact of the pandemic.
Repair works on 27KM- road between 19 de Outubro and Quissanga commenced on 29 August. The project was sponsored by Northern Integrated Development Agency  (ADIN) and initiated by the government.

On 31 August, Cabo Delgado Governor Valige Tauabo urged the return of civilians to Quissanga and called on civilians to participate in the reconstruction of destroyed infrastructure. He also advises the returnees to improve their security situation and to watch out for insurgent infiltration.
Two fishermen died after their boat sank in Island of Mozambique waters on 24 August due to bad weather. Operations are ongoing to retrieve dead bodies of the victims.

Reports on 31 August indicate that 270 individuals were detained by the police last week in Nampula Province for various crimes including illegal possession of a firearm and theft. 75% reduction in the crime rate has been observed compared to the same period in 2020.
RENAMO Leader Momade warned that RENAMO is committed to peace but not afraid of any war. He reiterated that the party's goal is still the same- to free all Mozambicans from the FRELIMO government.

Combination treatments of a new malaria vaccine and anti-malarial drugs has been found to effectively reduce malaria illness and death by seventy percent compared with using either treatment alone. The success of the three-year-trial can protect millions of people in the region.

Security forces arrested eight justice officials of Jangamo, Panda, Homoine, Funhalouro, Vilankulo, Govuro, Morrumbene and Inhassoro districts in Inhambane on or before 31 August for embezzling about 31 million meticais in a scheme between 2015 - 2020. The money used to pay elected district judges, ended up in the possessions of the accused.  At least 10 people were ultimately involved in the scheme.

National Administration for Conservation Areas (ANAC) troops recovered a tractor used in illegal logging activity in Zinave National Park after pursuing an illegal logger. The driver managed to escape.

National Administration for Conservation Areas (ANAC) officers arrested an illegal logger in Zinave National Park in late August, also seizing a tractor and other equipment used in illegal logging activities.
A suspicious fire was reported in Mocimboa da Praia on 30 August. This incident could indicate either clashes between security forces and insurgents, and insurgent attack, or airstrikes in this area.

A suspicious fire was reported in the area of Litingina, Nangade district on 29 August. This incident could indicate either clashes between security forces and insurgents, and insurgent attack, or airstrikes in this area.

A suspicious fire was reported within Chai, Macomia on 30 August.  This incident could indicate either clashes between security forces and insurgents, and insurgent attack, or airstrikes in this area.

The Ministry of Health announced 263 new COVID cases and 11 related deaths in Mozambique on 31 August. Nampula recorded the highest new COVID-19 infections with 88 cases, followed by Maputo City with 35 cases. Over the last 24 hours, 28 more cases were admitted, 14 were discharged and 1,177 have recovered.

Tensions remain high between civilians and military police in Tete as of 31 August over a land dispute in the Chingodzi neighborhood, following protests and clashes between the two sides last week. During the last mediation meeting, on 26 August, the community resisted after the council directed the civilians to abandon the lands. Residents claimed that the military have threatened to kill anyone who insisted on occupying the land. Meanwhile, journalists were also prohibited by the military of taking pictures in the area.

Rwanda military personnel reported on 31 August that 1,300 people so far have been repatriated from Quitunda to Palma.  As part of their ongoing military operations, Rwandan forces will repatriate people from Kihuwa camp in the near future to their home area.

On 01 September, President Nyusi reappointed Rogerio Zandamela as governor of the country’s Central Bank until 2026. This is Zandamela's second term after he was first appointed to the post in August, 2016.

On Tuesday, the bodies of three people reportedly killed in Nivico, along the Quissanga / Ancuabe Border were discovered by local villagers.  Unconfirmed reports indicated the three victims were disremembered.  Locals feared that insurgents were responsible for this attack, though this is not yet been verified.

The Maputo City Judicial Court announced on 31 August the extension of hidden debts trial until November instead of October, due to its complexity. Judge Efigenio Baptista agreed to call Jean Boustani, a senior executive of the Abu Dhabi based group Privinvest, to give testimony in the trial. Meanwhile, Ndambi Guebuza, the oldest son of former Mozambican President Armando Guebuza, may face tax evasion charges after he refused to answer questions about his financial affairs during the trial.  Guebuza in recent testimony accused President Nyusi of being involved in the Hidden Debts scheme, and said the President shuld be called to testify.
Vodacom on 01 September announced the reestablishment of its service in Palma town, Afungi, Quionga, and Quitopo in Palma District and in Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) town and Awasse in MDP District.
Vodacom on 01 September announced the reestablishment of its service in Palma town, Afungi, Quionga, and Quitopo in Palma District and in Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) town and Awasse in MDP District.

The Ministry of Health announced 438 new COVID cases and 2 related deaths in Mozambique on 1 September. The highest cases were recorded in Nampula with 162 cases and Cabo Delgado with 99 cases. While 7 of the new cases were hospitalized and 15 COVID in patients were discharged.

The Electricity de Mozambique announced on 01 September that the company was mobilizing resources to repair the damaged electrical systems in several districts of Cabo Delgado, including the repairing of two kms of high voltage lines across the Messalo River, the rebuilding of the Awasse substation, and repairs between Awasse and Mueda, Awasse and MDP town, between MDP and Palma, the Palma-Muidumbe connections, and the restoration of grids in other villages where insurgents destroyed or vandalized the electricity network.
President Nyusi announced that the vaccination campaign would now be extended for a new phase which will cover individuals over 40 living in rural areas.

The Mozambique GDP saw an increase by 1.97% in the second quarter of 2021. The increase was compared to the same quarter of the previous year. The slight increase in GDP indicates a fragile recovery from the pandemic.
Mozambique has vaccinated 1,076,968 corresponding to 6.3% of the total population over 15 of the country as of 1 September.

Austria announced that it had donated 4.7 million USD to the victims affected by the conflict in Sofala province. The donation was to allow the investment in improving livelihoods in rural communities in Machanga, Chibabava, Gorongosa, Maringue, Chemba and Cheringoma districts.

The Maputo City Court continued the Hidden Debts Trial with defendant Bruno Langa testifying on 2 September. Langa stated that he will not disclose the what he did with the 8.5 million USD he received which he received for as "real estate and hotel consulting." Langa also stated had had met with Jean Boustani of Privinvest on a trip paid for by SISE. Sources stated that Langa used the money to purchase luxury residences, vehicles, a farm, and donated the money to his family members.

The SADC on 02 September released a statement saying that the SADC mission in Mozambique (SAMIM) is now fully operational in the province, and that the mission could be extended past its original 30 day mandate.  The SADC also confirmed an operation launched by its forces south of Mbau on 28 August, indicating SAMIM became operational in late August.

SAMIM troops had conducted an operation on 28 August in the Muera area, south of Mbau, capturing an insurgent and seizing vehicles, weapons, and documents.  The insurgent was handed over to the Mozambican military.

SAMIM troops had conducted an operation on 28 August in the Muera area, south of Mbau, capturing an insurgent and seizing vehicles, weapons, and documents.  The insurgent was handed over to the Mozambican military.

The SADC on 02 September released a statement acknowledging the death of two SAMIM members in two separate accidents; this included a Tanzanian soldier killed in an "incident involving an aircraft" on 28 August.  It was not immediately clear where this accident took place.

Military forces killed several insurgents in a gun battle at an unspecified location in Cabo Delgado province. Several insurgent hideouts were also destroyed during the operation on or before 01 September.

Military forces killed several insurgents in a gun battle at an unspecified location in Cabo Delgado province. Several insurgent hideouts were also destroyed during the operation on or before 01 September.
Mozambican Commander of the Army, Cristovao Chume, speaking from Mbau on 01 September, says insurgents in recent kidnapping cases have demanded ransoms as high as 1 million meticais.

COVID-19 cases in the country improved in August, with an almost  50 percent decline in the number of new cases vs. July. July saw 45,624 new cases of the disease while in August the number of new cases fell to 24,025.  Hospital admissions fell from 1,953 in July to 974 in August, a fall of 50.1 percent. Meanwhile, COVID-19 related deaths declined by 26.4 per cent, from 556 deaths in July to 409 in August. Deputy National Director of Public Health, Benigna Matsinhe,  warned that though this data reflects a clear downwards trend, people should still make way to receive the COVID-19 doses and continuously adhere to the safety protocols.

Farmers demonstrated in Romao area of Maputo City on 01 September over alleged illegal sale of farmlands. The group claimed that the affected lands are supposed to be dedicated for agricultural use.  The protesting group demanded to have the Direito do Uso e Aproveitamento da Terra (DUAT) of the land to be provided by the Maputo Municipality.

Total appointed Maxime Rabilloud as the new country manager for the gas project in the country on 01 September. He replaced Ronan Bescond who was assigned to join the Australian arm of the company. Rabilloud have a extensive experience in Lusophone countries, starting in Angola as general counsel and then managed the company's business in Brazil at various levels of responsibility.  This comes amid recent reports that Total could look to restart its LNG project in Cabo Delgado sometime in 2022.

The Famine Early Warning System Network in a report issued on 01 September indicated that most of Cabo Delgado will remain in a state of food "crisis" between October and January due to the ongoing conflict in which hundreds of thousands of people have been displaced in the province and harvests have been disrupted.

A Mozambican soldier accidently fired his weapon, hitting and killing a female civilian in Nangade on 23 August. No arrest has been made so far in this incident, which prompted locals to complain regarding impunity enjoyed by the soldiers.

Unconfirmed reports on 26 August indicated that new Rwandan troops allegedly entered Cabo Delgado. Details behind this development remain unclear.  This is believed to be a deployment to relieve some of Rwanda's frontline troops, rather than a deployment of additional Rwandan forces.  The Rwandan intervention force in Cabo Delgado was allegedly reported to be 1,000 soldiers and police officers strong.

Reports on 26 August indicated that Tanzanian troops were seen in Mtama, Lindi with operational vehicles including armored personnel carriers. The troops were mobilizing close to the border, likely targeting insurgents fleeing from Mozambique.

As of 27 August, food supplies remain low in Nangade town. Over 200 IDPs are reportedly present in and around Nangade. Efforts are ongoing to extend available supplies and register IDPs to access public services.

An agreement was reportedly recently made between Rwanda and Mozambique that Mozambique military will be first to break news of developments in Cabo Delgado conflict. This development came after members of Mozambican civil society accused Rwandan media in making it seem like only Rwandan troops are fighting in Cabo Delgado.  Initial press reports from Rwandan sources in Cabo Delgado included extensive detail not typically provided by the Mozambican military; as of mid-August however, these detailed reports from the Rwandan media had stopped.

Mozambican media sources reported that Interpol reportedly has an arrest warrant for Jean Boustani, one of the key Hidden Debts suspects. Other sources later confirmed this report.  Boustani, a Lebanese citizen, was acquitted of charges in 2019 by the US in connection with the case.

At least 60 artisanal mining sites in Sofala have been identified and mapped with the intention of a campaign to crack down on illegal mining in future. These sites are located in seven districts across the province - Beira, Buzi, Caia, Gorongosa Maringue, Marromeu, and Nhamatanda.
The KaNhlamanculo Court Sentenced on 26 August 10 defendants to jail terms who had been involved  in a corruption scheme in which they stole 22 million meticais.

A Financial Stability Report recently published by the Bank of Mozambique stated that the country's public debt reached 948.7 billion Meticais in 2020. The debt rose by 26 percent against 754 billion Meticais of debt in December 2019. This increase resulted from public sector spending, with a view to containing the Covid-19 pandemic and the weather effects, as well as from military spending.
Inflated food prices have been reported in Palma by families who have recently returned to their homes. Traders allegedly sold rice for 150 Meticais per kilo, while sugar is sold at 200 Meticais.

The Sofala Government will provide a monthly subsidy of 1500 meticais for a period of six months to 149,000 vulnerable families who live in Beira city and another 36,000 in Dondo district. Registration to receive the said subsidy started on 02 September.

The Sofala Government will provide a monthly subsidy of 1500 meticais for a period of six months to 149,000 vulnerable families who live in Beira city and another 36,000 in Dondo district. Registration to receive the said subsidy started on 02 September.

On 01 September, Mozambican Workers Organization (OTM) raises concern about the situation at a sugar factory in Buzi. The factory was allegedly not complying with the clauses for payment of indemnities and wages in arrears to 256 workers. OTM claimed that an agreement was signed this year and provided for compensation in three tranches – in April, July and December, but only the first tranche was paid in full.

Cashew smugglers have caused shortage of cashew nuts and forced seven cashew nut processing factories in Nampula to shut down. Currently only nine out of 16 existing factories are working, local media reported.

Mozambican police were reported to have captured a suspected insurgent in Gingone, Pemba city on 03 September.  IDPs reportedly identified the man to police on Thursday, who arrested him on Friday. The suspect was allegedly involved in the seizure of vessels and abduction of passengers off Pangane in Macomia.

On 02 September, Portugal’s Minister of Defense, Joao Gomes Cravinho, stated that the creation of EU training mission to Mozambique is 'progressing well.' However, there is no clear start date for the said training mission, which was approved in 12 July. The mission aims to restore peace and order in the province of Cabo Delgado.

On 01 September, Maputo municipality said it has a limited budget to carry out needed repairs on damaged roads in the capital. Earlier reports stated that the municipality is only filling the holes of affected roads instead of rehabilitating them as it had initially committed to do.
Two suspected criminals were arrested in Maua, Niassa around 2300hrs on 31 August. The reason behind their arrest was not disclosed.

As of 30 August, no market has set up for fish and chicken sellers in Maputo city. This is the fifth deadline authorities have missed a deadline to deliver this market as promised in the capital, which has caused conflict among sellers. Authorities attribute this to the slow work of the contractor due to lack of manpower.

The Ministry of Health announced 312 new COVID cases and five related deaths in Mozambique on 02 September. The highest cases were recorded in Nampula with 74 cases and Cabo Delgado 73 cases. In the past 24 hours,  15 of the new cases were hospitalized and 13 COVID in patients were discharged.

According to The Voice news, members of the Botswana Defense Force (BDF) deployed in Mozambique are allegedly 'vacationing' and enjoying their stay in the country. The publication said that BDF has not yet received combat orders a month after they were deployed. Note that conflicting reports in August had indicated Botswanan and Tanzanian troops had clashed with insurgents in Nangade district.

Norway donated  217.6 million Meticais to the World Food Program (WFP) in Mozambique to support livelihoods and provide school food for IDPs and host communities affected by the Cabo Delgado conflict. The two-year project will tap more than 13,000 children with school meals and another 6,500 people through the provision of opportunities and livelihoods in the province.

Mozambican Police seized a large amount of stolen electrical equipment inside HENG YE factory in Digodiwa, Nicoadala district. Five people, including three Chinese nationals were subsequently arrested over alleged involvement in this crime. The recovered items were used as raw material in the construction of porches, stairs, among others by the said company. Reports suggest that recently ten towers that transport high voltage energy were vandalized in the district, where more than 100 angles were stolen, generating a loss of approximately 700,000 meticais.

Reports on 03 September suggest that recently ten towers that transport high voltage energy were vandalized in Nicoadala district, where more than 100 angles were stolen, generating a loss of approximately 700,000 meticais.

Reports on 03 September suggest that recently ten towers that transport high voltage energy were vandalized in Nicoadala district, where more than 100 angles were stolen, generating a loss of approximately 700,000 meticais.

Electricidade de Mozambique (EDM) announced the restoration of electricity in Mueda district on 3 September. Electrical teams managed to repaired the Awasse Power Station ( or may have put a temporary solution in place as the substation is repaired) which have been damaged by insurgent attacks and out of service since August 2020.

A civil society organization, the Institute for Multiparty Democracy claimed that they were being discredited after reports of the organization being linked to President Nyusi and FRELIMO. The organization stated it is independent and seeks to strengthen multi party democracy in Mozambique.

The Ministry of Health announced 365 new COVID cases and a single new COVID death in Mozambique on 3 September. 14 new hospital admissions were reported while 9 were discharged, which 122 COVID inpatients.
A minivan collided with another vehicle on Avenida de Mozambique, between 25 de Junho and Bagamoyo, at around 05:00 3 September. 7 civilians were injured.
Defendant Bruno Langa was reportedly refusing to answer the questions asked lawyers at the Hidden Debts trial. Langa gave this answer for 26 questions.

Reports on 06 September indicated that three Rwandan soldiers have died due to undisclosed reasons. Their bodies were kept in a morgue of a hospital in Pemba.  No autopsy was allegedly carried out. Sources claimed that the soldiers died of poisoning after consuming a home-made beverage, this detail has yet been confirmed.

The Ministry of Health announced 138 new COVID cases and a single new COVID death in Mozambique on 05 September. Nampula has the highest number of cases recorded with 54 cases, followed by Maputo City with 27 cases. 11 new hospital admissions were reported and eight were discharged, while 705 have recovered from the virus.
The leader of the Islamic Council of Mozambique, Sheik Cassimo David, passed away at the Central Hospital in Maputo city on 04 September. He died due to an undisclosed illness.

The Hidden Debts trial in Maputo resumed on 06 September. Businessman Sergio Namburete and former Secretary of the former President Armando Guebuza, Maria Ines Moiane Dove, will be questioned. Namburete reportedly owned SEN-Consultoria e Investimentos, one of the companies created to facilitate the distribution of hidden debt money. Meanwhile, Dove coordinated least six meetings between the former President Guebuza and senior members of Previnvest and maintained contacts with Jean Boustani.

Data released by the National Institute of Statistics showed that the country has recovered from a 1.3 percent drop in GDP in 2020 and is expected to grow by 2.8 percent this year, provided that no restrictions similar to Q2 will be imposed in the rest of the year. Economic activity will be further encouraged following major security improvements in Cabo Delgado and growing vaccination rates against COVID.

EU Ambassador to Mozambique, António Sánchez-Benedito Gaspar, stated on 3 September that the DDR process is going "very well" and that those demobilized have been receiving their subsidies in most cases. However, RENAMO Secretary-General Andre Magibire recently denied these claims, saying that there are more than 1000 fighters under the DDR who have not received their subsidies.
Mozambique recorded 354 Covid-19 cases, 5 deaths, and 991 recoveries on 4 September.  This included 109 cases in Nampula, and 49 in Zambezia.
A child died due to drowning while playing in a well in Nudnha 2, Beira, on 3 September. This brings the total  of deaths caused by drowning in Beira to 6 during 2021.

A group of 600 police officers graduated from a police training school in Nhamatanda District in Sofala on 03 September.  Platoon commanders among this group received training from the Zimbabwean police.

Local officials in Manica stated on 2 September that 12 people have been killed and 30 others were wounded due to the human-wildlife conflict in parts of Manica province. These deaths were mostly due to crocodile, elephant, buffalo, and lion attacks from January - June 2021. Additionally, the local officials stated that wildlife has devastated 144 hectares of crops in Manica. Due to the conflict and to calm down locals, around 5 conflicted elephants were killed in 2 areas of Manica.

On 31 August, South African authorities deported 246 Mozambicans. 223 of them were deported due to immigration issues, 18 for robbery, 2 for poaching, 1 for rape, 1 for murder, and 1 for physical assault. This brings the total Mozambican deportees from South Africa to 2,479 during August 2021. A majority of charges against those deported back to Mozambique were linked to immigration offenses.

SADC forces conducted operations in Muera, south of Mbau, 26-28 August. They captured a buffer zone, intercepted a car, and arrested its Tanzanian-born driver during these operations. SADC troops also seized electrical generators, satellite dishes, drones, and binoculars, among other items.

UNICEF Representative Lucio Melandri announced on 2 September that with the improving security amid military interventions, the organization is planning new interventions in Palma and Mocimboa da Praia. This aims to ensure that all necessary services for the family and children are provided. The services will include food, shelter, health guarantees, as well as the registration of minors.

Reliable sources indicated that hundreds of tunnels were found at the "Siri 1" insurgent base near Messalo River during security force operations in the area in late August. Each of the tunnel can accommodate around 10 people.

Former Mozambican President Armando Guebuza will reportedly testify at the Hidden Debts case in  December 2021. Guebuza has been linked to the hidden debt scandal, and his son is one of the 19 defendants in the case.

The World Health Organization warned on 3 September that around 42 of the 54 African countries, including Mozambique may be at risk of not being able to vaccinate 10% of its most vulnerable population against Covid-19. This is reportedly due to richer countries "hoarding" vaccines, resulting in delays in vaccines arriving in Africa.

The Hospital Geral Polana Caniço in Maputo City noted a decreasing rate of Covid-19 cases, reported on 03 September.  Just 4 patients at the facility are currently in critical condition. A hospital official noted that they have recorded a reduction in Covid-19 hospitalization for 2 weeks, noting that the fatality rate and other factors have contributed to this, including the vaccination rate.

António Macanige, member of the Municipal Assembly of Pemba for bench of the Democratic Movement of Mozambique, warned that the official residence of the President of the Municipal Council of Pemba may be being used to embezzle money. Macanige stated that succeeding mayors have been trying to rehabilitate the house since 2,000, without reflecting significant changes and with it being uninhabited for more than 20 years. Former Mayor Sadique Yacub stated before that he was going to China to buy rehabilitation materials; however, no rehabilitation ever took place. At present, mayor Tagir Carimo also asked for cash to rehabilitate the building. Municipal Assembly opposition officials demanded the Municipal Council to present a proof of payment to show that the works have been carried out. They also called for a criminal investigation.

Rwandan Defense Force sources claimed the Rwandan stated is financing its military intervention in Mozambique, reports on 31 August indicate. Some critics however doubt these claims as Rwanda is one of the poorest nations in the world.   Other reports previously indicated France was providing financing for the intervention, though this report is unconfirmed.

In a recent statement to the press, Total noted that "it is not providing any support to foreign forces present in Mozambique". However, it stated that It does provides logistical support to the Mozambican government forces assigned to protect the activity in its LNG project. The company stressed that there are no ongoing discussions to extend this current agreement to any foreign forces operating in the province.

The Foreign Ministry of France did not confirm nor deny that it is financing the deployment of Rwandan troops into Mozambique after being recently questioned regarding its involvement in Cabo Delgado.  France did state that France is following the situation in Cabo Delgado with great concern, stressing that it supports Mozambique in its fight against terrorism. Additionally, France has called on and encouraged countries in the region and Mozambican partners to express their support to Mozambique. It also praised the initiatives by the SADC and Rwanda, in coordination with the Mozambican government, to combat the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

Reports on 4 September indicated that the Rwandan Armed Forces in Mozambique has been carrying out food deliveries for displaced individuals from the Quitunda camp and other areas of Palma district in Cabo Delgado in recent days.
A traffic accident on the road linking Nampula to Namapa in the Teterene area killed 4 people and critically wounded 6 others on 4 September.

The Ministry of Economy and Finance stated that the exchange rate in Mozambique will likely worsen next year.  The ministry stated that the impact of the pandemic has depreciated the value of meticais to 66.6 meticais per USD.
Matola municipality on 06 September was reported to have suspended the activities of 30 shipyards on area roadsides, giving shipyards 7 days to remove material and equipment from these areas.

Rwandan President Kagame stated during an interview that Rwanda security forces were not backed by funding by France or Total in their Cabo Delgado operations. President Kagame stated Rwanda itself was funding its intervention in Cabo Delgado.
Police arrested three suspects for kidnapping and murdering a woman in Tete province on 6 September. The suspects committed the crime this past 27 August.

Three armed individuals abducted and murdered a civilian in Tete province on 27 August. The suspects reportedly sexually assaulted the victim and reported to have harvested the organs of their victim.

Three armed individuals abducted and murdered a civilian in Tete province on 27 August. The suspects reportedly sexually assaulted the victim and reported to have harvested the organs of their victim.

The Mozambican government stated that county is unlikely to achieve the country's vaccination goal of 17 million people this year.  Currently around 1.2 million Mozambicans have received their vaccinations.
The Police Commander Bernardino Rafael in a speech indicated that complaints of corruption among traffic police were reported on the highway between Beira and Manica town along National Road 6.

Standard Bank of Mozambique issued restrictions are reported to be negatively affecting business conditions in the country. The Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) survey showed that economic conditions have deteriorated since August.
Four trucks collided with each other due to an accident near the Ressano Garcia Border on the night of 5 September. A driver was killed and three were injured after a fire broke out during the crash.

The Mueda Mayor Pitalavalave calls on local residents who have been displaced to return back to the district on 3 September. This comes after electrical supply to Mueda district was recently restored.
The Cabo Delgado governor Valige Tauabo stated that he does not advise return of IDPs until a “definitive restoration of security”  has been achieved across areas insurgents were active.

Fires were reported near Ntchinga village, north of Muidumbe on 27 August. This coincided with a joint forces operation to seize this village, which was previously used as an insurgent base. It was unclear if the fires were caused by clashes in the area, airstrikes, or a different cause.
A police officer shot and injured a motorcycle taxi driver at the market of Chingdozi, north Tete, on 3 September.

South African Airlines released their schedule for flights to Maputo as the airline restarts operations on 23 September. Flight SA142 would travel from Johannesburg to Maputo from 10:00 to 11:00, while SA143 departs from Maputo to Johannesburg from 11:45 to 12:50.

Sources stated on 3 September that Zimbabwe forces intends to deploy a non-combat force of 304 soldiers to Cabo Delgado in near future. This force will participate in training Mozambican military units.

The EU is reported to be financing a new project to rehabilitate roads between Nampula and Zambezia provinces. The project was to be funded with EUR124 million which would reportedly cover 2,240km of road between the provinces. The project would also provide jobs to the locals in the districts of the provinces.

Questionable reports indicated that RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo issued a statement saying his group intends to resist security forces being deployed in Manica, Sofala, Tete, Inhambane, and other areas of the country.  The statement also said that the dissident group would accept new recruits into its ranks.

Unconfirmed reports stated that the National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) suspended several officials in Maputo province. The officials reportedly included the Chief of Instruction, Macanhangane, Chief of Operational Intelligence Directorate Majavane, and Public Relations Director Panguane. The officials were reportedly involved with the abduction of a family member of a businessman.
Many IDPs are reportedly lacking food aid at a refugee center even with the relief donations in Muaja. The aid reportedly does not arrive in the community due to the large number of IDPs.

Sources stated that many IDPs have been forced to exchange sexual favors for relief food from local NGO workers in Ancuabe and Pemba, among other locations in Cabo Delgado. Other IDPs were also exchanging money for relief food.  Some relief goods were being sold 1,500 meticais which was reportedly equivalent to a 25kg bag of rice, 25kg flour, and 5l of cooking oil.

Sources stated that some NGOs employees were selling relief goods outside refugee centers and other villages in Cabo Delgado. An NGO stated that investigations were ongoing regarding the corrupt employees.

A typically reliable source reported insurgents attacked joint forces positions between 05-06 September in the "Siri 2" area, near the Messalo River Banks, but were repelled.  No further information on these clashes are currently available.

The Ministry of Health announced four new COVID deaths and 390 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 7 September. This comes as daily recoveries were at 804. Niassa province recorded the highest daily cases with 191 and Nampula province with 52 cases.

President Nyusi stated that the COVID pandemic has worsened in Northern Mozambique during a speech in Nampula on 7 September. The president stated that infections were continuing to increase in Nampula and neighboring provinces. Nyusi also stated that local awareness and education should be implemented.

The Ministry of Health announced that there are 2 days left in the ongoing vaccination campaign in Mozambique. The ministry called on the locals who have not yet been vaccinated to take the first vaccine dosage. The campaign has reportedly vaccinated 1,124,706 with the first dose while 762,370 were inoculated with the second dose.

Unconfirmed reports indicated that a suspicious group on 29 July travelling into forest areas near Majune in Niassa.  The group travelled from the Marrupa area with tickets to Lichinga.  The group in bush areas outside of Majune asked to be let off briefly and then reportedly fled into the woods.   The driver of the bus reported the incident to authorities; there is some suspicion the group may have been insurgents fleeing from Cabo Delgado, though this has not been confirmed.

Sources stated on 07 September that reports indicated that the UN offered 4 million USD to RENAMO Junta Nhongo to disband the RENAMO Junta earlier this year, and that Nhongo had refused this offer, saying the group was not motivated by money.  Similar reports first surfaced in early July, but remain unconfirmed.
A fire broke was reported on 05 September in the vicinity of Chai in Northern Macomia, possibly related to ongoing clashes or an insurgent attack.

Rwandan President Kagame in an 05 September interview stated that insurgents had planned a move into Niassa province, according to documents captured and communications intercepted from the insurgents recently.
President Nyusi in an 07 Sep speech stated that the leaders of insurgents were from several different countries. The countries included DRC, Somalia, Rwanda, Kenya, and Tanzania.

In an 07 September speech, President Nyusi indicated that security forces had recaptured "almost all" territory previously held by insurgents in Cabo Delgado in ongoing operations, and that the government was currently focused on restoring services in areas previously held by insurgents.
Sources on 08 September indicated joint forces are utilizing drones to monitor insurgent activity in the Pundanhar area.

Joint forces operations reportedly are ongoing to clear the "Siri 1" base along the Messalo River in Southern MDP, sources indicated on 08 September.  Mozambican, Rwandan, and SADC troops are reportedly still operating in this area, and using drones in this area as well as in the Pundanhar area.
Security forces rescued 19 individuals from Nanjaba village near Macomia after the group recently fled the Mbau area.  The group had reportedly been held by insurgents in the area.
Banking operations reportedly have resumed in Mueda, according to sources on 8 September.
Sources in Southern MDP reported airstrikes in recent days have targeted insurgents in the area, likely along the Messalo River.

In an audio recording released on 08 September, RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo said that he wished to organize new talks with the government, saying that his group would "never disappear".  Nhongo is also reported to have recently also reiterated recent unconfirmed reports that he received an offer of $4 million from the UN to disband his group and join the DDR process, but that he had refused to do so as his group was not seeking money.  Nhongo said if he had sought money, he could have easily attacked mines and local commercial centers to obtain cash.  Nhongo also strongly criticized the DDR process, saying RENAMO militia members had been deceived as they were not receiving their pensions.

Sources stated that around 1000 DDR former RENAMO guerillas have yet to be paid promised subsidies for the last six months.  RENAMO leader Momade stated that the UN was still organizing the funds for the salaries, but said there was "still no guarantee", and called the situation "worrying".

President Nyusi conducted a speech on 7 September indicating that talks with insurgents had been ruled out. The president said that the insurgents have made no demands and their leaders have not presented themselves. This comes after former President Chissano recently suggested the opening of talks with the insurgents.

Sources stated that Privinvest official, Jean Boustani announced that he was ready to testify in the Hidden Debts Trial through video conference. Boustani is seen as a key participant in the Hidden Debts case, and he was acquitted in a trial in the US regarding his role in the scandal, though the Mozambique Attorney General's Office has issued repeated summons for Boustani in relation to the case.

The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) detained two suspects in possession of 16,000 USD in Maputo on 8 September. The suspects were both Angolan citizens and were part of an international gang.

Police also detained three suspects who attempted to extort a driver of a fuel tanker fuel tanker in Jardim, west Maputo City, early morning on 5 September. One of the detainees was a police officer who attempted to extort 50,000 meticais for the victim's release.

Sources stated that officials in Maputo stated that the Rwandan forces were in fact being funded by France in Cabo Delgado. This comes as Rwandan President Kagame previously stated that the Rwandan forces were not being support by either France or Total and that the country's intervention in Cabo Delgado was exclusively funded by Kigali.

A video circulated widely on social networks in Mozambique depicting security force members being attacked by civilians in different incidents across the country, demonstrating general bad feeling and mistrust many civilians feel towards officers of the state.
A fire spread and killed 5 civilians who were clearing the bushes at a forest near Calvate village in Mocuba district on 7 September. A residence was burned down due to the incident.
Sources stated that illegal miners and companies were polluting the rivers with mercury in Manica. The farmers stated that their plants were affected by the polluted water.
The Mozambican government issued a three-month fishing ban in Inhambane starting 15 September. The fishing ban was to prevent the extinction of the marine species and improve the income.

The African Union (AU) donated 100,000 USD to the displaced individuals affected by the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. The AU also has promised to provide training to the security forces; this comes amid an AU mission visit to Mozambique.

Sources stated that around 380 teachers have not yet received their subsidies for the past eight months in Manica. The teachers stated that they were entitled to 650 meticais as allowance per month but not have received this stipend since 8 February.

Vendors stated that municipal officers have reportedly recently extorted informal sellers at Zimpeto Market in Maputo City. The officers were reportedly charging 150 meticais daily to the street vendors.
The Rwandan National Police conducted a meeting with the Tanzanian Police Force in Kigali to discuss the two countries' operations in Cabo Delgado.
The Ministry of Health announced 108 new COVID cases and 3 new deaths in Mozambique on 8 September. The total cases increased to 148,552 cases and 7,340 remain active cases.

Sources stated that an audio recording leadked of former Labor Minister Helena Taipo stated that President Nyusi should be defendant on the Hidden Debts case, saying that Nyusi not being held accountable for his role in the case was "letting the crocodile grow".

Air France announced that they intended to start a flight route from Paris to Maputo starting 02 December. Flight bookings were already open to Maputo International Airport. The flights will reportedly have a stopover at Johannesburg’s Tambo International Airport. Four flights per week were scheduled to travel between the countries. One of the scheduled flights was scheduled on Sunday and Thursday which would depart from Paris at 23:35 and arrive at 14:20 in Maputo. Another flight was scheduled on Monday and Friday which would depart from Maputo at 16:30 and arrive at 05:45 in Paris.

Joint security forces are reportedly to have recently warned locals to stay away from Miteda AP in Cabo Delgado due to the ongoing clearing operations targeting insurgents. Militants are believed to still be present in this area.

Joint security forces are reportedly to have recently warned locals to stay away from Miteda AP in Cabo Delgado due to the ongoing clearing operations targeting insurgents. Militants are believed to still be present in this area.

Foreign Minister Macamo stated that the military cooperation between foreign security forces and Mozambican security forces against insurgency has been effective to date. Macamo stated that the advancement of the joint forces have led to a decrease on insurgent attacks in the province, and recently has allowed IDPs to return to their homes.

Unconfirmed reports that joint forces exchanged gunfire with insurgents along the Messalo river on 3 September. No specific casualties were mentioned. Mozambican helicopters meanwhile on the same day conducted strafing attacks targeting insurgents in the south of Mbau.

Unconfirmed reports that joint forces exchanged gunfire with insurgents along the Messalo river on 3 September. No specific casualties were mentioned. Mozambican helicopters meanwhile on the same day conducted strafing attacks targeting insurgents in the south of Mbau.

Sources stated that insurgents exchanged gunfire with joint security forces at security positions near Mocimboa da Praia town on 3 September, reportedly approaching the town from the west and north.   No further details on this incident are currently available.
SADC forces deployed from Lesotho to Nangade on 28 August. The Tanzanian security forces also deployed troops to the area on 1 September.
SADC forces deployed from Lesotho to Nangade on 28 August. The Tanzanian security forces also deployed troops to the area on 1 September.
The Ministry of Health announced the deadline to receive the 2nd dose of the COVID-19 vaccine during the current vaccination phase was 11 September.

The National Migration Service (SENAMI) announced on 9 September that 75 illegal immigrants were deported in the past 7 days during a weekly operation in Mozambique. 33 of the illegal immigrants were using forged names and 24 were lacking details regarding their stay.

The Ministry of Health announced the arrival of 100,800 doses of Johnson and Johnson COVID 19 vaccines in Mozambique on 10 September. The vacines were provided through the assistance of the African Union and World Bank.

Border security forces detained two suspects for illegal possession of a weapon in Ressano Garcia on 5 September. The suspects were in possession a 9mm pistol, 1,600 meticais, and 15,000 South African Rand.

11 armed men with machetes and guns attacked a shop and stole food items and goods at Chenapamimba in Muanza District, north of Beira at around 18:00 on 9 September. A civilian was killed and two others were injured.  One of the injured persons died shortly after the attack. A local police commander said was carried out by RENAMO dissidents. No group claimed responsibility for the attack.

No group claimed responsibility for the attack.

The Ministry of Health announced 175 new COVID cases and 3 deaths in Mozambique on 9 September. The two highest cases were recorded in Nampula with 45 cases and Cabo Delgado with 41 cases. Daily recoveries were at 1,321. While five COVID cases were admitted to hospitals and 13 were discharged, leaving 86 inpatients.

On the morning of 09 September, hundreds demonstrated in Nampula after reports that they would be excluded from receiving subsidies meant to alleviate economic hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic.  Protesters marched to the premises of the National Institute of Social Action in the city before police intervened, firing shots in the air to disperse the protesters.  Multiple people, including seven journalists, were arrested by police.  Reporters covering the demo said they had equipment confiscated during the incident.

The Millennium Bim Bank announced that the bank will resume banking services in Palma when security and normalcy was reinstated in the town. Bank officials stated that their banking services could be restored around a month and a half.

RENAMO leader Momade called for those responsible for Hidden Debts cases to be held accountable. Momade stated that the suspects, if found guilty should be placed in jail and that the stolen money should be returned by the suspects to the public.

A recently released study indicated that the IMF promoted unfounded potential growth opportunities in Mozambique leading to the expansion of the country’s coal mining. The coal mining industry in Mozambique previously stated that back in 2013 that the country could become one of the world’s largest coal exporters with an estimation of 20% GDP. However, the government revenues from the industry have only ever accounted for 1.6% GDP.

The Police General Rafael stated that the police district command post would be restructured in Nampula in the near future, saying some officers in the province are corrupt while a number of commanders are incompetent.
Sources stated that local youths or unemployed individuals were being extorted to be given jobs in Inhambane. The unemployed were reportedly paying around 100 to 500 EUR to obtain a job contract.

Displaced people who have returned to Palma are reportedly experiencing food shortages. Several individuals reportedly are gathering food from fields which have been cleared from the insurgents, with security forces providing no supplies to Palma residents, while aid agencies are not operating currently in the area. Locals stated that the area was secured, and only small traders were present in the area.

Sources reported a shortage of medical supplies across Palma district, with only a single health center at Quitunda still open to civilians.  Even this location reportedly experiences regular shortages.

Father Latifo Fonseca said that Palma lacks essential services though the locals can now return to the town, saying it has been secured by Mozambican and Rwandan troops on 8 September. Fonseca warned that IDPs traveling from Quitunda of possible malaria and diarrheal diseases due to the lack of services in the town.

Joint operations between the SADC Standby Force, Rwandan troops, and Mozambican forces are reported to be ongoing in some districts of Niassa province, according to sources on 11 September. The operation targeted suspected insurgent positions and hideouts.  No specific information is currently available regarding these operations.

On 10 September, the Northern Integrated Development Agency announced that it had built around 800 houses for displaced people in a village in Ancuabe. Additionally, it has also opened access roads that were blocked by insurgents and rebuilt infrastructure in Macomia. The agency noted that it is working with the UNDP which has pledged to replace the bridge over Montepuez River.  It is also expected that the agency will sign a partnership with the World Bank in the coming days to reconstruct some schools and classrooms and open access roads, as well as to recover identification and other personal documents.  In 2022, the agency expect to spend 3.7 billion meticais on its activities, 88% of which will be donor funded.

The ICRC distributed essential household items to around 681 displaced families in Mueda, Cabo Delgado, as reported on 11 September.

The Mozambican government is planning to acquire 9.3 million doses of Johnson and Johnson Covid-19 vaccines. As of 10 September, 100,800 of these doses have arrived in the country as part of the African Vaccine Acquisition Trust (AVAT) initiative. The government aims to accelerate the implementation of the National Immunization Plan and ensure the vaccination of the majority of the population in a short period with the procurement of 9.3 million doses of vaccine. As of 10 September, around 1.6 million people in Mozambique have been fully vaccinated.

A suspicious fire was reported in parts of Bilibiza, Quissanga, NW of Pemba, late in the evening of 10 September to early morning of 11 September. No casualties were reported. Initial sources reported this incident as a fire; these types of incidents sometimes indicate a clash between security forces and insurgents, or an insurgent attack, though no such incident has been confirmed.  Other sources did report an ongoing SADC Standby Force operations between Bilibiza and Mahate. Note that Bilibiza is outside of an area where there have been any recent attacks; however, there was an attack on 31 August in Nivico, west of Bilibiza.

Mozambican Naval Forces reportedly detained 20 suspected insurgents traveling on two naval vessels in the coast between Mocimboa da Praia and Palma during regular patrols. The suspected insurgents claimed that they were unaware of the travel ban by naval vessels between Palma and Ibo Island.  Further investigations into the incident are ongoing.

The Ministry of Health announced 119 new COVID cases and no new deaths in Mozambique on Sunday, 12 September. This comes as  Inhambane and Maputo City registered the highest cases with 26 new COVID cases.

South African Justice Minister Lamola is reported to have initially endorsed a late July memorandum drafted by South Africa's Justice Department that recommended against the extradition of former Mozambican Finance Minister Manuel Chang back to Mozambique.  Lamola subsequently ordered Chang's extradition; is  unclear why Lamola had this change of heart, but this revelation could impact a hearing later this week that will decide whether or not Chang can be extradited to Mozambique.  Chang is considered a key suspect and participant in the ongoing "trial of the century" in Mozambique over the "Hidden Debts" scandal.

The Northern Integrated Development Agency (ADIN) announced that the agency intends to hire a company to manage the funds for the emergency rehabilitation of infrastructures in Cabo Delgado.1 ADIN Chairman Ngunga stated that this was to enable ADIN to direct and identify projects and potential investors to various sectors in the province.

Police in Tsangano in Tete were reported on 08 September to have detained a group of 14 civilians gathered in bush areas of the District .   The group was reportedly possessed "enough knives" for all of its members, and the group according to local media espoused a Catholic fundamentalist ideology.  No further information on these arrests are currently available.

At approximately 4pm on 13 September, Revocant Karemangingo, VP of the Association of Rwandan Refugees in Mozambique, was shot dead in Matola.  Karemangingo was reportedly approached by a group of unidentified men who addressed him in the Liberdade area of Matola, who then shot him dead at close range; he was hit by nine bullets.  Karemangingo previously was a lieutenant in the Rwandan military, and was previously targeted in 2016.  Sources indicate he was recently warned by police of a plot to kill him.  Karemangingo on several occasions had called for an investigation into the disappearance of Rwandan journalist Cassien Ntamuhanga, who was abducted on 23 May from Inhaca Island.

Sources on 10-11 September reported that SADC Standby Forces were conducting ongoing clearing operations between Bilibiza and Mahate.  Local sources could not confirm whether or not insurgents were present in the area though one source said a militant presence was "likely".  This report came after reports of fires in Bilibiza town over the night of 10-11 September.

On 10 September, an interview with RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo was aired on Radio Mozambique.  The dissident leader claimed his group was well equipped, the group's morale was high, and that he had many fighters.  Nhongo also indicated he was not interested in money but in equality and "real democracy", also criticizing the government for not paying demobilized RENAMO militia members their stipends as stipulated in the DDR process.

The leader of the exiled Rwandans in Mozambique Cleophas Habiyareme said that Rwanda President Kagame was responsible for the murder of the group's deputy leader, Revocant Karemangingo in Matola on 13 September. Habiyareme stated that the situation of Rwandan refugees in Mozambique has worsened after the new “political alliance” between Mozambique and Rwanda.

Security officials announced that joint security forces were still conducting clearing operations in house-to-house searches in Mocimboa da Praia town on 13 September, clearing between 50-60 homes per day. Two weapons and ammunition were recently seized.
The Maputo Court sentenced former Transport Minister Paolo Zucula, former SASOL Manager Zimba, and former LAM CEO Viegas to 10 years in prison for bribery charges.

A report on 11 September indicated that the Mozambican military's leadership has established a good working relationship with top Rwandan officers part of the Rwandan intervention in Cabo Delgado.  SADC leadership however reportedly has been unable to establish this same close relationship, and is reportedly "struggling to establish contact" with the Mozambican military command structure.

The Judge for the Hidden Debts cases stated that the trial will remain public on 9 September. The announcement was in response to the calls of several lawyers serving the defendants who petitioned the court to limit the public broadcasting of the trial to the public. The lawyers stated that the public broadcasting would damage the right and good name of the defendants.

The Mozambique Minister of Energy Max Tonela stated that increased security in Cabo Delgado will allow Oil and Gas projects to resume their contracts and schedules. Tonela said new schedules for O&G projects in Cabo Delgado will be drawn up "in due time".

The Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy Max Tonela stated that maintenance teams were working to restore electricity in Palma, Mocimboa da Praia, and Nangade. The minister of energy stated that electrical power in these districts will be restored by the end of month.

Sources stated that a leaked recording from the former President Guebuza stated he says does not know Theophilo Nhangumele, a defendant of the Hidden Debt Case. Guebuza stated that on the recording that Nhangumele deceived the other defendants. Nhangumele was a businessman who acted as a middleman between the Mozambican officials and Boustani, and who has implicated Guebuza, who remains one of the most powerful figures in Mozambique, as a participant in the Hidden Debts Scheme.

Sources stated on 10 September that Mocimboa da Praia was largely destroyed during the insurgent occupation of the town.  There are currently no civilians in the town, with only military in the area.  Militants destroyed the airport, looted and destroyed shops, set vehicles on fire, destroyed public buildings, and vandalized other locations during the course of their occupation.

The Bank of Mozambique monetary policy reduced the deposit ratio in Mozambican banks from 34.5% percent to 11.5% of holding foreign-denominated deposits. The local currency deposit ratio was decreased from 11.5% to 10.5%. The decrease was to allow more liquidity available in the economy.

The US and Mozambique government concluded a second Joint Combined Exchange Training on 10 September. The 6-week training involved the training of 100 Mozambican Commandos.  In July and August, more than 60 soldiers participated in Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC) and Combat Lifesaver (CLS) courses to improve the survival rate of Mozambican troops in combat.

Firefighters doused a fire that broke out inside the sugar factory in Marromeu of Sofala province on 9 September. No casualties were reported after the fire was controlled within 30 minutes after the firefighters responded.

Thousands of locals demonstrated outside the district government building in Dondo on 11 September over non-distribution of subsidies. The protesters stated that the officials of the neighborhoods were choosing who should and who should not receive subsidies arbitrarily.
Over 200 contracting companies in Mozambique have been forced to close due to the ongoing pandemic. The pandemic has also reportedly left 5000 individuals without work.

The Ministry of Health announced 52 new COVID cases and 2 related deaths in Mozambique on 13 September. Nampula recorded 21 of the new cases and Maputo City with 12 cases. Recoveries were at 778, while 10 COVID cases were admitted leaving 63 COVID inpatients.

The Minister of Interior Miquidade said on 13 September that the insurgent threat affects the whole country. Miquidade stated that the security forces must still remains vigilant regarding potential threats. The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) stated that forces have been deployed to maintain security and minimize the possible spread of the insurgency.

RENAMO leader Momade accused the government of “persecution and torture” of RENAMO members in Inhambane on 10 September. Momade stated that the members persecuted were mostly teachers who were dismissed from their work for being opposition members.

Government officials suspended the allotting of market place stands at Xipamanine area of Maputo due to the tension of stall owners during the allocation. This comes as 930 vending stalls were available and the market vendors only wanted the stalls which were advantageous for their sales.

A civilian was killed after her home was destroyed due to a herd of wild elephants who escaped Gorongosa National Park at Metuchira village on Nhamtanda district on 7 September. Two other civilians managed to escape.

Portuguese general Nuno Lemos Pires indicated on 14 September that the EU Training Mission (EUTM) in Mozambique would likely be "fully operational" in the country by the end of the year.  Pires and other EU officials are part of an "advance planning force" travelling to Maputo ahead of this mission.  Between 10-12 EU member states as well as "2 or 3" countries from outside of the EU will contribute to the mission.  Portugal will likely contribute around 60 soldiers to the mission, while the other members will likely contribute another 60.  A further 50 "on call" officers will deploy as part of the mission for short periods.  The mission will likely officially be launched in October, though not fully operational until "November or December".  The EUTM will provide training for a Mozambican rapid reaction force, and will provide training to commando and rifle units in addition to providing non-lethal equipment.
The Portuguese Minister of Environment announced that the country will invest around 2 million EUR to projects related to development.

On 12 September, reliable sources citing a Rwandan military spokesman said that a landmine detonated, targeting a Rwandan military convoy near Mbau in Mocimboa da Praia District.  One Rwandan Ratel infantry fighting vehicle's tires were damaged in the attack, though no casualties were reported. Other unconfirmed reports indicated that a Rwandan military convoy had been targeted in a complex attack in the area.

Unconfirmed reports stated that a Casper mine resistant ambush protected vehicle was targeted in the Diaca area by a landmine, also on 12 September.  No further details on this incident are currently available.
EDM announced that electrical services have been restored in Nangade on 11 September. This comes as electricity was also restored in Mueda district.

The National Institute of Social Action (INAS) stated that a large numbers individuals were registering for the COVID-19 subsidy who are not eligible in Beira and Dondo in Sofala province. INAS stated that the individuals were taking advantage of the pandemic subsidy. INAS clarified that they would start conducting background checks to qualify individuals for the subsidy.

The National Health institute (INS) announced the end of third wave of COVID in Mozambique on 14 September. INS stated that an average of 1,500 cases were reported and more than 30 deaths during the height of the third wave. The third wave reportedly started in June 2021. This comes as the first two weeks of September saw 2,943 new cases and 107 COVID inpatients were reported compared to 15,385 COVID cases and 649 in the same period of August.
Sources stated that armed men in a vehicle attempted to abducted a Rwandan civilian in Maputo in late August.  No further information regarding this incident was immediately available.
The Ministry of Health announced 221 new COVID cases and a single related death in Mozambique on 14 September. This brings the total to 149,480 COVID cases and 5,200 active cases.

The Ministry of Health stated that at least 12,750 individuals have not taken their second COVID vaccination dosage as of 14 September. This was announced as the extend vaccination campaign ended on 11 September. Officials stated that the 9% can still receive their second vaccination by going to reference health units.

Sources stated that liquor stores were still operating after curfew hours mostly in Nampula and Maputo City. The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) stated that around 51 establishments were reportedly violating the curfew hours. INAE stated that 11 restaurants, 12 bars, 68 grocery stores, and three bakeries were found operation during curfew hours and recently closed down across the country.

The Ministry of Health announced an improvement in COVID numbers in September as cases have seen a decline by 15,385 new cases and 542 admissions in August. This comes as 2,943 new COVID cases of Covid-19 and 107 admissions were reported in the first 13 days of September.

Joint security forces of Mozambican, Rwandan and SADC forces were conducting clearing operation to prevent the movement of insurgents into Niassa province from Cabo Delgado on 14 September. This comes as suspected insurgents recently have allegedly attempted to enter the province. The clearing operations were to determine the locations, hideouts, and positions of the insurgents in Cabo Delgado.

Authorities warned that floods may occur affecting the country during the coming rainy season.  Up to 1 million people across the country may be impacted during this time by the rainy season.  Cabo Delgado and Niassa will experience below normal rainfall, though there is a risk of flooding particularly in Maputo, Umbluzi, Incomati, Limpopo, and in Central Mozambique in the Buzi and Zambeze basins.

Sources on 15 September indicated that thousands of IDPs had been returned to Palma from Quitunda, escorted by Rwandan and Mozambican security forces.  Potentially as many as 20,000 IDPs, the entire IDP population of Quitunda, have been moved back to Palma.  Video posted online of this operation showed dozens of vehicles lined up were intending to traveling into the town. In addition, hundreds of locals were seen gathered on the roads of town.  There is still no regular food or water supply to Palma, and no electricity in the town.

Police on 12 September were reported to have detained a group of 44 individuals in a forest area between Tsangano and Angonia.  Police were reportedly suspicious of the group's gathering in bush areas.  The group were reported to be members of a fundamentalist Catholic group, though this is unconfirmed.  Some sources reported the group were armed with edged weapons.  Other sources said authorities were concerned the group were linked to the insurgency in Cabo Delgado, though these links are speculative.

The SADC's Mission in Mozambique (SAMIM) released a statement on 15 September saying its troops in conjunction with Mozambican security forces had "opened the roads" from Pemba to Macomia, Awasse, Mueda, and Nangade, saying these patrols had significantly reduced the risk of insurgent attacks in and between these areas, and that "calm and stability" was restored in these areas.  SAMIM also said this had allowed the return of civilians to their homes from which they had been displaced.

Police arrested two individuals suspected to be members of a religious sect in Tete on 16 September. This comes 14 other individuals were detained after being intercepted on a vehicle while traveling to Tsangano area.
Mozambique Electric stated on 14 September that they have loss amounting to 10 million meticais due to theft and vandalism of electrical transmission equipment in the country.

The Attorney General’s Office said on 15 September that they intend to appeal against the ruling that acquitted the former Mozambique Airline CEO Viegas from a bribery case. This comes as Viegas was acquitted due to the lack of evidence and expiry of statute of limitations regarding the bribery case that involved the purchase of two aircrafts.

Dozens of teenagers and women recently released by insurgents arrived in Macomia and Muidumbe districts of Cabo Delgado on 13 September. The released individuals claimed that they were abducted on 7 April from Chitunda and were transported to an insurgent base south of Mocimboa da Praia.

A second batch of teenagers and women were reportedly released by insurgents arrived in Macomia on 15 September. This comes as an earlier batch of civilians were released by insurgents arrived Macomia and Muidumbe on 13 September.

The Ministry of Education announced that they required 1.5 billion meticais to rebuild schools and recover from the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. 328 primary schools and 8 secondary schools have been destroyed in insurgent attacks.  The ministry stated that the mostly affected districts were Mocimboa da Praia, Palma, Quissanga, and Macomia.

The Mozambique Tax Authority stated that 85% of their revenues were from domestic tax collection. The Tax Authority stated that the natural gas operations were to cover the 15-20% of the remaining revenues.

The Korean International Cooperation Agency announced that they donated 5.7 million USD to farmers in Sofala province on 14 September. The donation was to enable farmers in the province to recover from the natural disasters and effects of the pandemic.
Police arrested four suspects for drug dealing in Coop, east Maputo, on 16 September. The suspects were in possession of 119 packs of heroin, a pack of cannabis, and 500g of cocaine.
Customs seized five luxury vehicles for being smuggled to the country in Maputo on 15 September. The vehicles were valued at around a total of 11.5 million meticais.

A fire broke out at Maputo Special Reserve in Matutuine on 15 September.  500 hectares were burned in the fire. Firefighters and reserve officials stated that the fire was under control after their response. The reserve officials suspected that the fire was started by a cigarette which managed to spread through a part of the Maputo Special Reserve.

The Ministry of Health announced 133 new COVID cases and four new deaths in Mozambique on 16 September. This comes as 2,106 daily recoveries were reported. While active cases were at 3,023, 45 of which are currently hospitalized.
The Mozambique Navy seized 15 naval vessels and their crew suspected to be supplying the insurgents in Cabo Delgado.   No further detail on this seizure and these arrests are currently available.

On the night of 15 September, a typically reliable source reported a renewed joint forces assault on the insurgent base of "Siri 1" / "Syria 1" south of Mbau, with several militants reportedly killed, and others reportedly captured.

column4: The Ministry of Health announced 191 new COVID cases and three related deaths in Mozambique on 15 September. The majority of the cases were recorded with Niassa and Nampula provinces with 42 cases each.
A suspicious fire incident in Palma was reported on 14 September.  These incidents are often linked to insurgent attacks or clashes.
Police rescued an abducted baby and arrested a kidnapper in Beira on 7th September. The arrest was conducted after the parents filed a complaint. The suspect was found running with the victim.

Sources stated that possible 400 residents would be possibly evicted from the housing complex of Vila Olimpica do Zimpeto in Maputo on 15 September. The housing project reportedly houses 3,000 civilians. The eviction was due to the conflcit between the Fund for Housing Development and the minister of Public Works.
column15: Vila Olimpica do Zimpeto in Maputo

column4: A Chinese company was accused of engaging in illegal logging in Sofala on 15 September. The company reportedly bought large amounts of illegally logged wood and exported them to China.
Frelimo officials called on locals to remain vigilant against insurgent attempting to potentially infiltrate Maputo area.

Unconfirmed reports stated that a document was circulating stating that the government intended to double or increase by 95% the salary for the president. The document also stated that they intend to increase around 75% of the salaries of the state leaders. This brings the head of state from 205,653 meticais to 400,000 meticais. Government officials later denied that any salary increase was being considered.
A fire burned down a restaurant in Nicuadala of Zambezia on the afternoon of 15 September. The fire was suspected to have started from another and managed to spread to the restaurant.

The joint security forces are conducting operations targeting insurgents and patrolling off Mucojo coast on 15 September. The operations were to prevent insurgents from using maritime routes to escape from the province.  Other sources reported helicopters flying over the area searching for insurgents.
Joint security forces deployed to Mucojo on 8 September to target insurgent reportedly in the area.
Joint security forces between Rwandan security forces and SADC forces deployed to Lichinga on 11 September. The joint forces were to pursue insurgent who have withdrawn from Cabo Delgado.

Insurgents fired an RPG and small arms fire targeting a Rwadan armored vehicle on the road between Mbau and Indegue on 12 September.  Insurgents in this same attack targeted one Rwandan vehicle with a landmine.  No casaulties were reported in this attack.

Insurgents fired an RPG and small arms fire targeting a Rwadan armored vehicle on the road between Mbau and Indegue on 12 September.  Insurgents in this same attack targeted one Rwandan vehicle with a landmine.  No casaulties were reported in this attack.
Sources stated that no relief food has been reportedly delivered to Nachitenje area as of 9 September.  This comes as a resupply of relief goods were expected to arrive in the area.
Locals stated that no resupply of relief goods had been provided in Katapua, Chiure on 9 September. 300 individuals were to reportedly receive aid in the area.
IDPs claimed that they have stopped receiving relief aid vouchers in Pemba on 9 September. The aid disbursement team stated that they should prepare to return to their communities.

Security forces rescued 21  individuals from the Mbau area southwest of Mocimboa da Praia. The group were believed to have been held as captives by the insurgents. Two children and several elderly were all transported to Pemba. The IDPs were experiencing health problems due to a lack of supplies in the Mbau area.  2 of the group were reported to have passed away while being transferred to Pemba.

A unit of Zimbabwean military instructors will reportedly soon be deployed to Mozambique, though this deployment has reportedly been delayed due to disagreements over the final Status of Force Agreement for this force. The 304 instructors were on standby in Nyanga area of Zimbabwe.
Sources stated that IDPs still lack the resources and aid to build or purchase residences in Northern Mozambique, and that many are forced to sell food aid in order to raise funds.

Sources stated that fake COVID vaccinations cards are circulating in Maxixe in Inhambane as of 17 September. A civil servant stated that the vaccination cards were available from individuals who have been vaccinated.

The Bishop of Pemba Dom Antonio Juliasse stated that the "conditions" for priests and nuns to resume their missions in insurgent impacted areas of Cabo Delgado have not yet been met. Juliasse stated that once IDPs can return safely to their towns and villages, the priests and nuns could consider the resumption of their missionaries.

The Mozambique National Telecommunications Institute (INCM) announced that they would start switching off analogue television signals by Monday, 20 September. The removal of analogue broadcasting transmitters were to switch television networks to digital signals.

A South African court has not issued a decision regarding the extradition of Manuel Chang to Mozambique as had been scheduled for 17 September. Instead, South African Judge Margarete Victor issued an order to delay the extradition of Chang to Mozambique until a ruling on the case at a yet to be determined time.
Local stated that roads in Machaze district required repairs and that money from the timber licensing should be used to conduct the maintenance.

The Ministry of Health announced 102 new COVID cases and a single death in Mozambique on 17 September. The majority of the cases were noted in Nampula with 22 cases and Niassa with 21 cases. While active cases were currently at 2,986 cases.

On 14 September, SAMIM  troops captured a training base used by insurgents south of the Messalo River in Cabo Delgado.  The camp was known as Sheik Ibrahim Base.  During the operation SAMIM forces seized light and medium weapons, training manuals, and other equipment.  3 elderly women who were held captive by the insurgents were also rescued.
column15: Sheikh Ibrahim Base, South of Messalo River

column4: The bodies of 5 decapitated adults were discovered in the Namaluco area of Quissanga, approx. 23 Km SE of Macomia, at dawn on Saturday, 18 September. One source indicated the five were killed on 17 September.  Sources say the victims may have been attacked by insurgents who were escaping from the Macomia forest amid heavy clashes against joint armed forces there.
