column4: Mozambique recorded 75 new Covid-19 cases, no death, and 369 recoveries on 18 September. This brings the total cases to 149,981, while deaths remain at 1,903, with a total of 145,382 recoveries. The 18 September tally of new cases include 21 in Maputo City and 11 in Cabo Delgado, which both recorded the top 2 highest number of daily cases that day.

Mozambican Police General Commander, Bernardino Rafael, called on the residents of Quissanga in Cabo Delgado to return to their homes amid gains by defense and security forces against militants operating in the district. Rafael also pledged that police will intensify its presence in Quissanga in order to allow people to live their normal lives as farmers or fishermen. Reports by local media outlets indicated that residents have started to return to the villages of Nivico, 19th October, and Tandanhangue in Quissanga. This came a day before reports of 5 people killed in the Namaluco area of Quissanga.

The Ministry of Health announced 37 new COVID cases and no new COVID death recorded in Mozambique on 19 September. Maputo City has the highest number of cases recorded with 11 cases, followed by Cabo Delgado and Nampula with eight cases each. In the past 24 hours, four new hospital admissions were reported and eight were discharged, while 224 have recovered from the virus.

Reports indicated that a Mozambican Police shot dead an 18-yr-old individual in Moamba village on or around 12 September. The officer allegedly attempted to intervene a fight between two groups where the victim was involved. The officer was later arrested and charged accordingly.

A Mozambican Police was arrested and charged on or around September for killing an 18-yr-old civilian in Momaba village a week before. The officer allegedly attempted to intervene a fight between two groups where the victim was involved.

Rwanda Defense Force Army Chief of Staff (ACOS), Lt Gen Mubarakh Muganga, arrived in Mocimboa da Praia on 18 September as part of a four-day visit to Rwandan Forces deployed in Cabo Delgado Province. He commended the troops for the success of the joint operations.

The Association of Alcoholic Beverage Producers and Importers (APIBA) warned that the requirement of sealing of locally-produced beers will bring an additional cost of five million dollars to producers which will result in price increases in the market. This new regulation was imposed on local beer manufacturers due to smuggling of beverages to avoid taxes.
A vehicle of Mozambican police was involved in a crash in Impire village on the afternoon of 18 September.  No information on casualties was available.

Reports on 20 September indicate that 15 insurgents based in Quiterajo, Macomia surrendered to security forces. The insurgents claimed that several members of their group deserted their posts in the area.

A total of 188,160 doses of AstraZeneca vaccine donated by the United Kingdom through COVAX facility arrived in Mozambique on 17 September. This is part of the ongoing UK's support to the country in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. So far, Mozambique has received 1,032,160 doses through the initiative, which is about half of the country's allocation.

A court in Montepuez sentenced a 28-year-old Tanzanian national to one year in prison and a daily fine of 150 Meticais for one year over illegal exploration and exploitation of mineral resources. He will be deported to his country after he served his sentence.

Security forces arrested a Brazilian national in possession of 4.2kg of cocaine-type of drugs at Maputo International Airport on 20 September. The illicit drugs were concealed in small candy packages inside his suitcase. He claimed that the suitcase was given by his friend to be delivered to his friend's mother.

The National Agency for Environmental Quality Control (AQUA) and the National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) dismantled an illegal timber yard, owned by a Chinese company called Cam International, over illegal exploitation of wood in Muxungue, Sofala province. Reports suggest that the company has been purchasing and trading forestry products without any license since 2013. The company also possessed a total of 6,163 cubic meters of timber logged in Machaze district of Manica province.

The second phase of water supply restrictions in Nampula province commenced on 20 September. The restrictions aim to rationalize the remaining amount of water available in the reservoir of the Monapo dam and prevent water shortage during the dry season.

On 20 September, Mozambican Police announced that former Renamo guerrilla dissidents were behind the 9 September robbery attack in Muanza district in which 10 armed men with machetes and guns attacked a shop and stole food items and goods at Chenapamima. One person was killed in the attack, while a second person who had been shot died shortly after the attack.

Three bodies of decapitated adults were discovered in the Namaluco area of Quissanga district, on 20 September. 5 bodies had previously been reported in the area; those killed in the attack may have been killed in a previous insurgent raid on 17/18 September.

column4: Local sources reported that 10 fishermen were abducted by suspected insurgents near a small lake in Quissanga District on or before 19 September.  One fisherman who escaped this attack reported the incident to a local military contingent.  A separate local source reported two decapitated bodies discovered in the area between 19-20 September.

Local sources reported that 10 fishermen were abducted by suspected insurgents near a small lake in Quissanga District on or before 19 September.  One fisherman who escaped this attack reported the incident to a local military contingent.  A separate local source reported two decapitated bodies discovered in the area between 19-20 September.

Humanitarian aid arrived in Palma on 20 September for the first time since the town was attacked by insurgents in March. United Nation's World Food Program in the country stated that at total of 2,150 families had received emergency food, hygiene and shelter kits.
On 20 September, the National Institute of Meteorology (INAM) warned of strong winds of up to 30 knots (60 km/h) 50 miles off the Mozambican coast. INAM also forecasts waves reaching 2.5 meters.

The Ministry of Health announced 49 new COVID cases and no new COVID death recorded in Mozambique on 20 September. Niassa Province has the highest number of cases recorded with 21 cases, followed by Nampula with 15 cases each. In the past 24 hours, four new hospital admissions were reported and three were discharged, while 53 have recovered from the virus.

A fire broke out in Maputo Central Hospital around 16:00 on 20 September. The fire affected the Central Operating Room and Clinic IV of the facility. Rescue teams arrived at the scene to contain the fire. The exact cause of the fire is still unknown.
President Nyusi announced that he intends to launch a campaign for Mozambique's candidature for a non-permanent position on UN Security Council.

On the night of 20-21 September, a group of 15 Cabo Delgado insurgents were reported to have crossed the Rovuma River and attacked Kagera village in Tanzania's Mtwara District 8 kms east of Mahurunga. Insurgents killed 4 people in the attack.  Between 18-33 civilians were also abducted in the incident; women abducted were reportedly sexually assaulted and then released, though a number of children abducted in the attack were not released.  Other reports had initially indicated a second attack by insurgents on the next day, though later reporting indicated a single large scale attack on the night of 20-21 September.

They also carried out looting, and killed a shop keeper.  Insurgents later beheaded at least 3 other people in the village; note one report indicated six people beheaded. Police Chief Rafael stated that “religious sects” were appearing all around Mozambique and were reportedly conducting activities that could lead to ongoing insurgency. This comes after as a religious group was detained in Tete recently.  Rafael also said there were possible connections between the group in Tete and insurgents in Cabo Delgado.

Energy Minister Max Tonela on 20 Sep stated that the Coral South Project was on schedule to begin in 2022. The project was expected to produce a 3.4 million meticais revenue annually. The project was initially begun in 2016 but was delayed during the 2017 due to the ongoing  insurgency.

The Ministry of Health announced 134 new COVID infections and no COVID deaths in Mozambique on 21 September. The majority of the cases were recorded in Niassa with 68 cases and Cabo Delgado with 10 cases.

The Southern Regional Water Administration (ARA-SUL) issued a warning regarding the possible flooding in the Incomati and Umbeluzi basins on 21 September. ARA-SUL stated that the rivers were at a high-medium risk due to the current storage of water on the rivers.

The Southern Regional Water Administration (ARA-SUL) issued a warning regarding the possible flooding in the Incomati and Umbeluzi basins on 21 September. ARA-SUL stated that the rivers were at a high-medium risk due to the current storage of water on the rivers.

Defense Minister Jamie Neto announced that he was unaware of any instances in which insurgents have used landmines in Cabo Delgado on 20 September. Neto also said if militants are using landmines, that the supply of explosives to the insurgents needed to be determined.  This follows reports recently that a Rwandan vehicle was targeted by a mine near Mbau in Cabo Delgado.
Locals raised concerns regarding the increasing pollution in Zimpeto neighborhood of Maputo city due to foreign factory running in the area. The company was reportedly recycling plastic bags.
Luxembourg officials announced on 20 September that they would provide a small team of security forces as part of the EU training mission to be deployed in Mozambique.

The National Roads Administration (ANE) stated that they were constructing four bridges across the Messalo and Montepuez Rivers in Cabo Delgado. The metal bridges were to be built along National Road 380 and along the 698 and 762 Roads in the province. The bridges are expected to be in place by the end of the year.

The Minister of Health Tiago announced that the government requires around 2 million USD of funds needed to rebuild the health center in Palma. Tiago stated health center would be equipped with the state-of-the-art equipment. The funding will also be used to restore the other health units in Macomia and Mocimboa da Praia districts.

The Malawian President Chakwera announced that Malawi was in the process of were resolving the border disputes with Mozambique in the Makanjira area. Chakwera stated that crime was prevalent along the border area near Lichinga with Malawi.

Health authorities announced that the COVID positivity rate has continued to decline in Mozambique in recent weeks. The COVID positivity rate has declined to 4.9 percent as of 17 September. This follows after on 16 September the rate was reported to be 6.5% and 7.8% on Wednesday, 15 September. These are the lowest COVID rates seen in the country since June. There continue to be higher rates of COVID currently in Northern Mozambique vs. lower rates in Southern Mozambique.

Sources stated that Cabo Delgado police received 11 new vehicles on 17 September. The new vehicles were to provide the police additional equipment to protect civilians in the province. The vehicles were intended to be used for patrols along the National Road 380 in the province.

Local officials in Pemba stated that there is a cement shortage in Pemba on 19 September. Officials stated that prices have increased by 50% due to the sudden shortage. The prices of cement were initially around 450 meticais but have increased to around 700 meticais due to the shortage.

Several locals who were victims of a landslide conducted a demonstration against the non-payment of subsidies provided by the government for their rent outside a municipal building in Maputo on 16 September. Police deployed and dispersed the protesters in response to the demonstration. Five representatives of the protesters reportedly met with the Maputo mayor.

Several locals who were victims of a landslide conducted a demonstration against the non-payment of subsidies provided by the government for their rent outside a municipal building in Maputo on 16 September. Police deployed and dispersed the protesters in response to the demonstration. Five representatives of the protesters reportedly met with the Maputo mayor.

The Ministry of Health officials announced that leprosy cases in Mozambique have seen an increase recently. The ministry stated that there are typical around 2,200 leprosy cases, primarily in Nampula.
The Mozambican government announced that reconstruction plans for Cabo Delgado were approved on 21 September. The plan included the reconstruction of the electrical grid and roads in the province.

A new report stated that crimes related to illegal firearms have seen an increase in Mozambique. The report indicated that throughout Mozambique, South Africa, and Zimbabwe, there are currently 3.8 unregistered illegal firearms circulating.   A majority of the illegal weapons were due to lost or stolen weapon; some of the stolen weapons were from policemen.
Malawian Police arrested two Mozambican nationals for human trafficking charges and detained six individuals in the south of Matamanda on border with Malawi on 14 September.
Police Commander Rafael on 19 September warned of against scams that target new police recruits in Pemba on 19 September.
Gemfields between 01 January - 30 June is expected to report a net profit of $23.8 million, partially generated by its Montepuez ruby mine.  The company over the same period in 2020.
Around 7,200 are now unemployed due to the recent closure of six cashew nut processing factories in Nampula. The closure of the factories have were due to the illegal exports of cashew nuts.

The UNHCR has called for an investigation regarding the murder a Rwandan refugee in Maputo on 20 September. The investigation comes as Rwandan refugees in Mozambique has expressed their concerns of being possibly targeted in the country since the incident.
A court sentenced a Chinese national for trafficking seahorses to 14 years in prison in Inhambane on 20 September. The detainee was also fined for 15,700 EURs during his sentence.

The Defense Minister Jaime Neto stated on 20 September that joint forces have continued to make progress in recovering areas from insurgents in Cabo Delgado. Neto said that joint forces continue to pursue terrorists, and that conditions are being created for the safe return of the population to insurgent impacted areas.

The Ministry of Health announced 79 new COVID infections and 3 related deaths in Mozambique on 22 September. The majority of the cases were recorded in Cabo Delgado with 26 cases and Maputo City with 18 cases.
Around 220 families residing near along powerlines in Inhambane, Gaza and Maputo provinces will be resettled due to the construction of the power plants in each province.

Security forces re reportedly having difficulty discerning between insurgents and civilians in Cabo Delgado, sources indicated on 19 September. Locals stated that several civilians were accused of being insurgents and were reportedly detained recently.
A civilian was killed after an artisanal mine collapsed in Moatize on 20 September. The victim was reportedly sitting on the bottom of an illegal mining area during the incident.

Sources stated that malaria cases have increased significant and were reported to be around 518,000 between January and July in Cabo Delgado. During the same period in 2020, cases were around 287,600.

Security forces continued operations targeting the insurgent base "Siri" along the Messalo River, south of Mbau, on 17 September.  One source reported clashes in the area, saying a militant logistics base had been destroyed.
Security forces arrested an insurgent leader during operations near the Siri insurgent camp along Messalo River on 17 September.  The arrested leader was reportedly a head of logistics for the group.
SADC security forces reportedly clashed with insurgents near Quiterajo, Macomia District on 15 September. Specific casualties were not reported.

SADC security forces were reported to be present in Nangade but not conducting operations to patrol the bush areas around Nangade as of 15 September. The security forces were also reported not to be engaging with insurgents in the district.

Reliable media sources reported that on 19 September, insurgents in a series of three attacks killed 17 more people in the villages of Bilibiza, Nakuta, and Tapara in Quissanga District.  This comes after other attacks in the district since 17 September in which at least 10 other people were killed.

Reliable media sources reported that on 19 September, insurgents in a series of three attacks killed 17 more people in the villages of Bilibiza, Nakuta, and Tapara in Quissanga District.  This comes after other attacks in the district since 17 September in which at least 10 other people were killed.

Reliable media sources reported that on 19 September, insurgents in a series of three attacks killed 17 more people in the villages of Bilibiza, Nakuta, and Tapara in Quissanga District.  Sources later indicated at least 7 of those killed were shot dead in Tapara.This comes after other attacks in the district since 17 September in which at least 10 other people were killed.

A new reported indicated that as of July, there were around 91,000 in the Mueda district in Cabo Delgado. A significant number of these IDPs deported from Tanzania after having fled across the Palma border.

Sources stated in a report that around 66,910 IDPs were president in Nampula province that had come Cabo Delgado province as of July. The IDPs were reportedly having issues in enrolling their children in schools due to the background. The displaced people were also residing in crowded residences in the province.

A UNCHR report stated that around 121,000 IDPs were located in Chiure and Ancuabe districts of Cabo Delgado as of July, exceeding the capacity of resources in those districts to care for that number of displaced persons.

Around 150,000 IDPs were reportedly present in Pemba as of late July. The majority of the IDPs were reportedly living in the host community to relieve the overburdening of the social services in the city.

Sources stated that IDPs in Montepuez were around 46,000 as of late July. The current number of IDPs in the district has affected the local government’s ability to integrate the IDPs into the society.

Sources stated that around 3,068 IDPs were in Quitunda and 2,000 in Maganja of Palma District in Cabo Delgado as of late July according to a UNHCR report.  Note this is a significantly smaller number of IDPs reported in the area than by other sources.
A humanitarian report stated that there were around 32,000 IDPs in Ibo District of Cabo Delgado as of late July.
According to a new report, as of July, there were 66,910 IDPs in Niassa province, displaced from Cabo Delgado.  Many of these people were living in private homes as opposed to IDP camps.
Around 125,000 IDPs were reported in Metuge district of Cabo Delgado as of late July. The district hosts some of the largest IDP camps in Cabo Delgado.

South African Truck companies stated they could lose around R10 million daily due to delays at the Lebombo Border post across from Ressano Garcia Post. The shipping delays were due to truck owners not providing money to drivers to pay for temporary import permits; other sources said Mozambique's manual  system to process truck clearances were causing delays at the border.

The National Institute of Social Action stated that 580 families excluded from COVID subsidies would be supported with subsidies. The support was in response to the reports that locals were no receiving assistance from the government despite being in need.

The Nationals Statistics Institute stated that trade for goods declined in 2020 by 16.8%. the decline was compared to the year 2019 in which 12.09 billion USD of revenues in trade were recorded. 10.05 billion USD were recorded for the revenue of trade in goods for 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

The UN called for caution regarding the sudden decline in activity of insurgents due to the improving security in Cabo Delgado. The UN stated that IPDs returning to their home areas could potentially be targeted by insurgents who are still present in many areas of Cabo Delgado.

A group of 15 insurgents who recently deserted the group in the Quiterajo area of Macomia told authorities that the group's "main base" was in the Quiterajo area, also saying many insurgents were deserting the group and that the situation within the group was "chaotic" due to ongoing joint forces offensives targeting the militants.

Sources stated that displaced people resettlement centers around Cabo Delgado were reportedly not receiving enough relief goods, foods, and aid. Areas where IDPs reported not receiving adequate relief aid included Chiure, Mapupulo, Mucojo, Quiterajo, Quissanga, Muedumbe, and Marocane.

A new report indicated that pro-government militiamen in many cases have targeted and even killed civilians in Cabo Delgado suspected of being insurgents. In one incident, pro-government militia in late July (on or around 26 July) were reported to have executed two civilians in V Congresso village in Chai AP they suspected of being insurgents; the two were later identified as civilians that had been held as hostages for four months by the insurgents.

Health authorities announced that COVID morality has decreased during the recent days as of 22 September. Just 39 COVID deaths have been reported in September, in comparison to August which saw 351 deaths from the virus.

Sources stated that several Mozambican journalists were allowed to travel to Afungi and also visit the Northern Operational Theatre in Cabo Delgado on 22 September.  The area has largely been closed off to all but a handful of Mozambican journalists for months.

The UNCHR stated that the organization's budget falls short by $8.7 million in providing assistance to the IDPs in Cabo Delgado. The funding need was estimated to be 25.7 million USD.  The UNHCR is one of many organizations attempting to provide support to over 732,000 IDPs displaced by the conflict in Cabo Delgado.
The Mozambique Tax Authority stated that a driver was arrested after being found smuggling 550 cases of wine and other products from South Africa to Mozambique inside an ore transport truck.
The Mozambique Tax Authority stated that a driver was arrested after being found smuggling 550 cases of wine and other products from South Africa to Mozambique inside an ore transport truck.

Security officials announced on 17 September that 338 smuggling cases were intercepted in Mozambique since the beginning of the year. In many of these cases, ore transport trucks are being utilized, particularly in smuggling coming from South Africa into Mozambique.

Government officials in Pemba recently indicated to IDPs they intend to allow some IDPs to return back into Mocimboa da Praia district in the near future. IDPs will reportedly be allowed to return first to Mangoma village, outside of MDP, before later being allowed to return into the town itself after it has been fully cleared by security forces.  No IDPs have yet been returned to this area however.

Unconfirmed reports from a single source stated on 20 September an accidental explosion reportedly killed 30 insurgents in Nangade District. The exact location in Nangade was not specified, though insurgents have long been active in the Nkonga area of the district. This report comes as sources have recently indicated insurgents had planted IEDs in parts of Southern MDP, and had targeted a Rwandan vehicle in one recent incident.

Sources stated that around 57 insurgents fled towards the south from Mucojo on or around 15 September. At least 30 insurgents entered Quissanga district, and are believed to be the group who carried out recent killings in Namaluco.

The joint security forces conducted demining operations in the south of Mocimboa da Praia in early September. Insurgents reportedly in a number of areas planted crude IEDs, including one specific instance in which a mortar shell connected to a package of suspected ammonium nitrate was planted - this device was connected to a remote detonator set to detonate when it received a radio signal.  Joint forces reportedly successfully identified and disarmed all discovered IEDs, with no detonations reported; EOD trained Rwandan troops were reported to have led in these demining operations.

Displaced civilians conducted a demonstration against irregularities in food distribution in Nacaca resettlement center in Ancuabe District on 15 September. The protesters claimed several IDPs were being excluded from being given relief goods. The protesters also stated that several locals were receiving the food vouchers intended for the IDPs.

In July, security forces reportedly detained a group of IDPs from the Monjane area of Palma district, accusing the group of being insurgents.  The group were later identified as non-combatant locals, but some of the group as of September 2021 were reported to remain in police custody.

On 20 September, 5 suspected insurgents were arrested by the Mozambican security forces near the administrative post in Bilibiza. The detains claimed that they intended to fish in the area at a local lake but could not provide any evidence regarding these statements. Security forces requested the nearby village elders identify the detainees.

Joint Forces comprised of Rwandan and Mozambican troops on 21 September launched a new operation targeting insurgents at a militant base in the Quiterajo area identified as "Siri 3". In clashes on the afternoon of 22 September, 5 insurgents were killed and 87 civilians (60 women and 27 children) were rescued by joint forces.  The operation was reportedly facilitated by information received from a group of 15 insurgents who surrendered to security forces in the Quiterajo area last week.

President Nyusi addressed the country during a speech on 23 September, saying the government would slightly relax COVID restrictions as other safety measures needed would be to maintained for the economy to gradually recover. The relaxed restrictions include: The curfew would be imposed between 23:00 to 04:00 for Maputo City and 24:00 to 04:00 for provincial capitals. The re-opening and 30% operating capacity of places of worship, theatres, cinemas, entertainment centers, cultural centers, and auditoriums. Allowing private social events with a maximum of 30 individuals for indoor gatherings and 50 individuals for open areas. For official meetings, a max limit of 100 individuals would be allowed. Authorization would be required from the government if the gathering is for more than 100 individuals
The Ministry of Health announced on 23 September 90 new COVID cases and a single related death in the country. This brings the total cases to 146,155 and total deaths to 1,907.

A group of at least 22 insurgents on the afternoon of 23 September was reported to have attacked Lindi village, south of Nivico and the ADDP crossroads.  Militants set fire to houses in the attack and opened fire on a bus in the village.  Four civilians were killed and two soldiers were injured during this attack and raids on other nearby raids.  3 of the four people killed were reportedly beheaded, while one person was shot dead.
South African Airlines resumed flights on 23 September after grounding all operations 16 months ago.  New flights between South Africa and Maputo are set to begin within days.
Health authorities stated that new cases of chickenpox were recorded in Pemba on 23 September. The disease was reportedly spreading in the city among children.

Security forces detained two National Migration Service (SENAMI) employees for forgery charges in Nampula on 21 September. The suspects were attempting to regularize the residency of illegal immigrants.

The Swedish government intends to conduct a training as a form of support for the DDR participants in Mozambique on 23 September. The support would also include technical monitoring and gender sensitive strategies aimed at DDR participants.
The Association of Rwandan Refugees in Mozambique President has called for an independent commission to investigate into killing of Rwandan refugee vice president Revocat Karemangingo.

The Centre for Public Integrity (CIP) stated that the COVID relief money donated to Mozambique has been used as “slush fund” by officials. CIP stated that officials transferred around 5.3 million USD to several public companies without transparency.

Rwandan troops displayed captured weaponry and a detained insurgent captured during clashes in Mocimboa da Praia district on 22 September. No specific details were stated as to where or when the insurgent was detained.
Officials in Cabo Delgado indicated that around 67 million USD of infrastructure were destroyed in Cabo Delgado province. Around 44 tourist establishments were destroyed by the insurgency.

The UN Office on Drugs and Crime on 23 September indicated that drug trafficking could increase around Cabo Delgado due to the ongoing insurgency. Traffickers could take advantage of the ongoing situation in the province to increase smuggling through the area.
As of 24 September, 1.7 million civilians or 10 percent of the total eligible population of Mozambique has received at least one COVID vaccine shot.

Tmcel, Vodacom, and Movitel on 23 September announced that they intend to fully restore their services in Mocimboa da Praia and Muidumbe districts within a matter of days.  The restoration of security in these areas has allowed for the repair of critical infrastructure.
A civilian suspected to be intoxicated fell off a building in Maputo City on 23 September. The victim was suspected to have committed suicide.

A group of illegal miners reportedly conducted illicit mining activity in Sierra Vumba of Manica province. Police have conducted an operation to stop the illegal mining and to arrest the artisanal miners.

A group of illegal miners reportedly conducted illicit mining activity in Sierra Vumba of Manica province. Police have conducted an operation to stop the illegal mining and to arrest the artisanal miners.
Sources on 23 September reported insurgents attacked the villages of Nivico and Moja near Lindi.  Insurgents reportedly set multiple homes on fire in these attacks.
Sources on 23 September reported insurgents at Namoja ambushed two buses carrying Mozambican soldiers, killing 1 person and injuring two others.

Rwandan President Paul Kagame arrived in Pemba on 24 September as part of a two-day visit to Rwandan troops currently operating in Cabo Delgado province. This comes just after Lt General Mubarakh Muganga, Rwanda's Army Chief of Staff, just concluded a visit to the province.

Officials announced that electrical services were partially restored in Mocimboa da Praia at around 18:30 on 23 September. The repair was conducted at Awasse substation, which was damaged in 2020 by insurgents during clashes with the Mozambican security forces.  45kms of power line between Awasse and MDP have been rebuilt, though further repairs are needed at the Awasse sub-station to fully restore power to the district and beyond.
A group of militants on the night of 23-24 September attacked the village of V Congresso in Nangade District.  No further details, including on casualties, were immediately available.

A local source reported that hundreds more joint forces troops were deployed to Quissanga District on 24 September after multiple insurgent attacks in the district and along its borders this week left at least 32 dead.  Sources also reported traffic along the N380 road from Sunate to Macomia had been halted after several insurgent attacks along this route on 23 September, including attacks in the Lindi area that left at least 4 people dead.  Another report indicated traffic was being stopped and searched by security forces before being allowed to travel on.

The Mozambican Hydrocarbon Company (ENH) is prepping oil prospecting activities in Mazenga area, Inhambane, local media reported on 24 September. MozGas UK Holds 80% of the shares in this block, while ENH holds the other 20%.
Joint forces vehicles on or before 24 September were reported to have become stuck along poor roads in the Mbau area, where poor roads have slowed military operations.

The UN donated an electrical generator for the Macomia District hospital on 23 September. The generator was to allow all medical services to remain operational in the town. This comes as the district hospital was being rehabilitated.
Additional security forces were deployed in Pemba on 24 September during the visit of Rwandan President Kagame.

RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo stated on 24 September that the dissident group remains active. Nhongo also claims that the previous attack last 9 September in Muanza that left a civilian killed and 2 injured was conducted by supporters of the group but not actual members of the RENAMO Military Junta. Nhongo also clarified that the attackers were not members of RENAMO Military Junta, but "may be people who want to help".

The Mozambique Electricity Company stated that electrical services will be restored in Palma by the weekend.  This announcement comes after Mocimboa da Praia announced that electrical services were restored on 23 September.
Sources stated that as of 22 September, 25,000 people have returned to Palma district since the security situation improved. Trading activities were also returning to normal in parts of the district.

The Brazil government on 23 September announced that they are “ready to cooperate” with Mozambique in the fight against insurgents.  Brazil has previously expressed similar sentiments though there is no clear indication of direct support being offered by Brazil to Mozambique.
The Norwegian government intends to phase out it's Oil for Development program in Mozambique by 2024. Norwegian officials said the country intends to prioritize funding of greener projects.

The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) announced that a Chinese owned recycling company was shut down in Maputo on 24 September. The closure was due to the waste products of the company affecting the environment of Zimpeto neighborhood in Maputo.

The Ministry of Health announced 69 new COVID cases and a single death in Mozambique on 24 September. 216 COVID patients have recovered. The majority of the cases were located in Cabo Delgado with 21 cases and Maputo city with 11 cases.

336,000 doses of Johnson & Johnson vaccine donated by the US government arrived at Maputo International Airport on 24 September. This comes as the US government previously donated 302,400 doses of COVID vaccines last July.

Sources stated that significant numbers of civilians are arriving in Mueda and are preparing to return to their towns and villages in the northern parts of Cabo Delgado where they were displaced from by the ongoing insurgency.

Sources stated that the security forces in Pemba have prepared military transport to assist civilians in traveling back into Palma, Mocimboa da Praia, and other areas cleared by the joint security forces.

Sources stated that civilians have recently begun to return to the Palma District villages of Maganja, Modjane, Senga, Ncumbi, and Quitunda. This comes as security was reported to be stable in the areas following the deployment of Rwandan and Mozambican troops across the district in July.
Insurgents were reported to have ambushed an  open box vehicle at Iba area of Meluco District at around 17:00 on 23 September. Two civilians were injured.

Security forces announced the ending of the clearing operation in Mbau area on 28 August. The operation was started on 20 August.  Insurgents were reported to have put up especially fierce resistance in the Nakitengue area, just north of Mbau

The Joint security forces conducted an operation reportedly completing the capture and destruction of the Siri 1 and Siri 2 bases along the Messalo River on 23 September. Several insurgents were detained and other were killed over the course of this multi-day operation . Other insurgents reportedly fled towards the southern areas of the Messalo River.

On 25 September, Rwandan President Paul Kagame stated that Rwandan troops cannot stay infinitely in Cabo Delgado province to fight insurgents. However, he reiterated that amid the recent success by Joint forces in the provinces, the operations is still far from over and Rwandan troops would remain in the country to defeat the militants.

The Ministry of Health announced 55 new COVID cases and one new COVID death recorded in Mozambique on 25 September. Nampula Province has the highest number of cases recorded with 13 cases, followed by Cabo Delgado with 12 cases each. In the past 24 hours, three new hospital admissions were reported and no one was discharged, while 120 have recovered from the virus.

Reports on 23 September indicated that the UK Government is cutting in half its aid budget to Mozambique, from £51 mn in 2020-21 to just £28 mn in 2021-22, due to financial impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Apart from Mozambique, Ethiopia, Kenya, South Sudan, and Somalia were also affected by the UK's aid cuts.

IDPs from Nacaca resettlement center in Ancuabe staged a protest on 15 September against the irregular distribution of food aid. The group claimed that some displaced families are excluded from the distribution list while locals are allegedly receiving food aid vouchers that were meant for the IDPs. Protesters attempted to attack aid distributors, however, security forces intervened and prevented the assault.

Notably, the data does not include Palma, Mocimboa da Praia and Muidumbe, because it is not yet possible gain access in these areas to tally IDP numbers, though many of the displaced are from these areas.

The SADC Mission in Mozambique (SAMIM) in a 26 September press release said its forces alongside Mozambican troops in an operation on 25 September had targeted an insurgent base in the Chitama area of Nangade, saying 17 militants were killed in this operation and the militant base destroyed.  SAMIM said an insurgent leader names Sheikh Dr Nijle North had been the commander of the base.  1 SAMIM Tanzanian soldier was killed in the operation, and three others injured.

In clashes on 26 September on the Southern bank of the Messalo River, SADC Mission in Mozambique (SAMIM) troops along with Mozambican forces indicated they had killed one insurgent and seized three militant firearms.  One insurgent, suspected to be a teacher, was captured in this operation.

In clashes on 26 September on the Southern bank of the Messalo River, SADC Mission in Mozambique (SAMIM) troops along with Mozambican forces indicated they had killed one insurgent and seized three militant firearms.  One insurgent, suspected to be a teacher, was captured in this operation.

On 26 September, Rwandan Media said that 4 Rwandan soldiers had been killed in clashes in Cabo Delgado over the past two months, and that 14 other Rwandan soldiers had been "seriously wounded" over this period. This is the first time Rwanda acknowledge battlefield deaths in Mozambique since the troops’ deployment in July, however, the exact location/s where the soldiers were killed were not disclosed.

On 24 September, President Nyusi, and his Rwandan counterpart, President Kagame, signed a memorandum of understanding in Mecufi on cooperation in the areas of trade and investment, emphasizing mineral resources and energy. The agreement was conducted during the official visit of President Kagame in the country.

The Mozambican government stated on 27 September that it would require $300 million for reconstruction in Cabo Delgado. $200 million is earmarked for short-term projects.

A water pipeline ruptured destroying a house in the process in Matola, west of Maputo City, on the afternoon of 26 September. The pipeline reportedly has not been replaced for 60 years.. The pipeline burst has caused a lack of water services in the municipality.

Local health officials confirmed a chickenpox outbreak in Pemba on 27 September. At least 6 cases have been reported in children in the city, after reports indicated a week before that there had been outbreaks of the disease in the city.

The Rwandan refugees residing Mozambique started that Kigali has a list of 20 Rwandan exiles on a hit list, including some Rwandan refugees in Mozambique.  The Rwandan community in the country has called for an African Union investigation into Rwandan security force killings in Mozambique.
The Ministry of Health announced 10 new COVID infections and a single related death in Mozambique on 27 September. This comes as 44 daily recoveries were reported.

The National Migration Service (SENAMI) announced that 135 illegal immigrants were repatriated and 56 allowed to legalize their residency on 27 September. This comes as SENAMI inspected 1,480 individuals for illegal immigration issues.

Mozambique health officials announced that the positivity rate of COVID testing has continued to decline to 3.5% as of 27 September. This comes as the lowest previous positivity rate was recorded on 08 June with 2.5%

A new analysis by the Open Oil that estimates of Mozambique's future LNG earnings have likely been significantly overestimated.  The country by some projections stood to make $55 billion from LNG by 2048, however, the organization's estimates say LNG will likely only generate $18 billion, also saying these earnings will not allow the national oil company, ENH, to turn a profit.  The report indicated that if oil prices remain higher, the project could earn up to $28 billion, only half of previous estimates.  Much of this new projection is due to the fact that ENH is paying higher interest rates to O&G companies operating in Mozambique than initial projections assumed would be paid. The worldwide impact of a shift away from fossil fuels to combat climate change is also expected to eat into these profits in 2040, the year when the LNG projects had been projected to begin making their most significant profits.

A document released by TotalEnergies on 28 September indicated that the company was now projecting LNG production in Mozambique in 2026 at the earliest.  The 2026 target would also only be possible if the company is able to restart work in Cabo Delgado in early 2022.  Company CEO Patrick Pouyanne said that there were "some positive evolutions on the ground but they have to be consolidated".  TotalEnergies before the suspension of its LNG project earlier this year due to the March 2021 insurgent attack on Palma had expected LNG production in the country to begin in 2024.

The Ministry of Health announced 2 COVID deaths and 32 COVID cases in Mozambique on 28 September. This comes as 255 daily recoveries were announced. Nampula recorded the highest number of daily cases with 8, followed by Inhambane and Maputo City with 6 cases each.

A Mozambican official indicated that there was no extradition agreement with Rwanda on 28 September. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation (MINEC) has stated that the MOUs recently signed by Presidents Nyusi and Kagame only were related to  agriculture, defense, and security, and related to for commercial and investment opportunities.  It has been widely speculated since May that Maputo secretly agreed with Kigali to allow the Rwandan government to target Rwandan citizens living in Mozambique.

The Mozambican military showcased  newly obtained military hardware in Pemba on 25 September. A new Mi-8/17 transport helicopter, a Gazelle light helicopter, and four Marauder Armored Personnel Carrier (APC) took part in a military parade and military displays during a joint visit by President Nyusi and President Kagame of Rwanda to the Cabo Delgado capital.

The China DH Mining Company announced that they intend to restart graphite mining in Nipepe District by 2022. The mining company was set to explore a reserve expected to contain up to 5 million tons of graphite.

The National Institute of Statistics (INE) announced that the unemployment rate in Mozambique is estimated to be at 17.5% in 2019-2020. Unemployment rates were highest in Maputo Province with a 31.6% unemployment rate and Maputo City with a rate of 37.1%. Zambezia province had the lowest countrywide unemployment rate at 10.7%.  The study noted that due to many peoples' informal jobs the actual unemployment rate was difficult to measure.
An Somali national assaulted a civilian after refusing sexual favors in Muthita area of Nampula City on 28 September.

The National Institute of Statistics (INE) stated that the richest 10% of Mozambicans account for 43% of the spending expenditure in Mozambique. The Household Budget Survey indicated that average monthly expenses in Maputo province and Maputo City were twice the national average. Each Household is expected to spend 8,108 meticais per month.

The former Secret Service Director Gregorio Leao testified implicating President Nyusi in Hidden Debts on 28 September. Leao stated that Nyusi coordinated the meetings regarding the Exclusive Economic Zone, a group which has been implicated in the Hidden Debts Scandal.

President Nyusi stated in a 25 September speech in Pemba that the insurgent attacks are not due to social inequalities in Cabo Delgado. The president stated that the province was not the poorest and that the country has not neglected the province.  Nyusi also said that terrorism in Cabo Delgado had a "global" connection.

Government sources indicated that as of 10 August, there were 34,484 IDP families in Metuge, 15,1556 IDP families in Ancuabe, 11,091 in Montepuez, 11,522 in Chiure, 6,463 in Ibo, 3,506 in Balama, 3,133 in Macomia, 2,349 in Meluco, and 928 in Namuno.  These IDP numbers did not include IDPs in Pemba, Mueda, Nangade, or several insurgent impacted districts including Palma.

Insurgents in an attack on Litingina on 24 September were reported to have set several houses on fire.  Unconfirmed sources reported insurgents also beheaded people in the area, and clashed with security forces, but these reports remain unverified.
Sources stated that insurgents were spotted crossing the Namua-Nangade road on 25 September. This comes a day after the insurgents attacked Litingina village.

Joint forces aircraft reportedly conducted at least one airstrike targeting insurgents near Chitama area on 25 September. This came as SAMIM forces reported killing 17 militants in the area during these clashes.

Insurgents attacked the village of Janguane, southwest of Nangade on 26 September. Locals stated the roads near the village were empty as civilians avoided travel.  No information regarding casualties was available.

SADC troops reportedly detained two women and physically assaulted them near Litingina village on 22 September. The women were found with two weapons and were suspected to be insurgents during the time of the arrest.
