Around 9 insurgents assaulted three women in Nazimodja village of Nangade District on 25 September.

The Mozambican government has requested UN member states support the candidacy of Mozambique for a non-permanent seat at the UN Security Council for 2023 to 2024.  Mozambique previously said it had received support from the SADC, the AU, Portugal, and other Lusophone countries.

The Ministry of Industry and Trade announced that terrorism has caused losses of 42 billion meticais in Cabo Delgado to businesses in the province. The Minister Carlos Mesquita stated that 4,965 micro, small and medium-sized companies have been "destroyed" by the insurgency.

A Human Rights Watch Report released on 29 September indicated that insurgents in Cabo Delgado are kidnapping young boys in the province and training them to fight for the group.  Militants have abducted hundreds of boys over the years, including large numbers in Palma in the March-April 2021 attack.  The report said insurgents force kidnapped boys to receive "Islamic classes and instructions for attacking villages".

TotalEnergies donated two mobile clinics for the local health services in Cabo Delgado province on 29 September. The clinics were to allow primary health care and teachings to be conducted for remote areas.
Suspected RENAMO dissidents robbed a local market in Nhamassindzira village before the Muanza attack on 09 September.
Police withdrew from the Chinapamimba area as of 29 September. This comes as police responded to the attack on a commercial establishment in the area.

A group of suspected RENAMO dissidents abducted 7 people during the attack in Chinapamimba on 9 September, sources later reported.  Note other reports questioned the links between the dissidents and this group.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) rejected the request of Mozambique that its debt contracted under issuance of bonds for countries with military conflict does not count. The IMF clarified that conflict debt still counts towards debt ratios.
Sources stated that the Mozambican parliament's next session was scheduled to begin on 20 October. The meeting was to discuss 42 issues and the annual briefing coming from the head of state.

Police stated that nine civilians died and nine were injured during the recent road traffic accidents in Inhambane on 29 September. Police stated that the accidents are usually caused by over speeding and drunk driving.
A vehicle accident occurred in Vilankulos area on 26 September. Four Malawi civilians were killed.
A vehicle was submerged after being caught in the high tide at Gadzene beach in Marracuene district on 26 September.

The Portuguese Consulate in Maputo has increased security measures as of 27 September. The consulate stated that a metal detector was installed and mobile phones were required to be left at the entrance of the consulate.  The security measures were added after a Portuguese national was kidnapped outside of the consulate in April.

United Airlines announced that the airline had partnered with local carrier Airlink to add flights to more than 40 African locations, including to Mozambique.  Some of these flights will commence before the end of 2021.

The Ministry of Finance stated there has been a yearly average recession of 3.4% in Cabo Delgado since 2017 due to insurgent attacks. The province saw a 6% growth rate from 2011 until the insurgent attacks began in 2017.

Minister of Culture and Tourism Materula stated that tourism has declined by 51.5% during 2021 compared to the same period in 2020. Materula said that the decline was brought about by the pandemic. 31% or 6,708 tourism establishments have closed down in the country, leaving 69,178 workers in the sector unemployed.
Security forces continued clearing operations in Mocimboa da Praia town as of 29 September.

A group of 73 people were rescued by security forces from the bush areas of Mocimboa da Praia on or before 27 September.  This group had reportedly lived in the bush for many months during the insurgent occupation of the area.

Security forces in MDP town have reportedly detained 28 local youths suspected to be involved with the insurgents.  It was unclear exactly when these arrests took place though local media reported this on 29 September.  It was also unclear if these individuals were arrested in MDP itself, though they were reportedly being held in MDP.

UNICEF stated that they required over $70 million to provide aid to children and caregivers in Mozambique on 27 September. UNICEF announced that they have received 25 million USD donations to provide aid and relief, though this is a significant shortfall in what the organization is appealing for.

Officials stated that around 20,000 national ID cards would be issued for displaced people in Cabo Delgado by end of year. The initiative was conducted by the  Catholic University of Mozambique and the UNHCR.

The Mozambican government announced on 28 September that they have considered closing beaches again after reopening them only four days before. The beaches included with Wimbe in Pemba, Tofo in Inhambane, Zalala beach in Quelimane, and Bilene in Gaza. This comes as locals gathered in large numbers on recently reopened beaches over the weekend, raising the risk of the spread of COVID.

Large fires were reported just south of Kitaya in Cabo Delgado on 28 September near Nhica do Rovuma.  This fire was suspicious and could indicate a clash between security forces and insurgents or an insurgent attack.
column15: South of Kitaya, Nhica do Rovuma area

column4: The brother of former MDM leader, Lutero Simango, announced that he would be running for presidency of the MDM party. Simango stated that election for the MDM leaders would take place on December.

The Minister of Finance stated on 28 September that the government hopes TotalEnergies can restart works in Cabo Delgado before a one year prediction for the restart of operations made by the company after April 2021 declaration of force majeure on the project. The restoration of security in the Palma area has led to speculation that TotalEnergies could restart the project sometime in early 2022.
The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) announced that 65 commercial establishments were closed down for violating COVID precautions between 13-27 September countywide.
The Police received 15 new vehicles in Tete province on 27 September. The vehicles were to increase patrolling capabilities of the province.
The Ministry of Health announced 2 COVID deaths and 90 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 29 September. The daily recoveries were at 123, while 1,777 COVID cases were still active.
Sources stated that Rwandan security forces reportedly "prefer" working with pro-government militiamen and were reportedly providing them with supplies.

Rwandan President Kagame in his 25 September Pemba speech stated that the Rwandan security forces were not deployed to only secure LNG projects in Cabo Delgado. Note that previous reports had indicated that Rwandan troops would secure Palma and MDP to allow the LNG project to restart.
Sources have reported that Mozambican and Rwandan troops have been garrisoned in various Palma district towns, but that these troops are not necessarily patrolling roads or bush areas.

Sources stated that locals living near the Tanzanian-Mozambique border have better food access compared to other areas of the district. The limited food access in other areas were suspected to be due to the limited security; meanwhile there appears to be some cross-border trade between Tanzania and Mozambican communities in Palma near the border.

An official stated on 30 September that around 9,000 former Mozambican liberation fighters have been living without government pensions for the past two years in insurgent affected areas of Cabo Delgado. The former liberation fighters were from Palma, Nangade, Muidumbe, Mocimboa da Praia and Macomia. Officials added that these former fighters have lost their identification, bank, and other documents due to the ongoing insurgency which has restricted them from accessing bank branches to obtain their pension.  In response, the government has announced that it is attempting to resolve the issue so that the former liberation fighters could access and obtain their pensions where they are currently residing or in a nearby area.

the National Institute of Statistics published a report stating that domestic violence against children has declined from 2018 to 2020 by 30.4%.  Nampula and Maputo province saw the highest reported cases of violence against children during this time, with 1038 and 865 cases reported respectively.
Insurgent abducted several children during an attack in Olumbi village of Palma District on or around 20 June.
Police arrested an IDP on fraud charges after the man sold vouchers for 100 meticais to other IDPs, saying the vouchers could be redeemed for food in Namutequeliua, Nampula, on 28 September .
Police arrested a school guard for sexual assault in Barragem of Nampula city on 28 September assault incident. The suspect reportedly raped a 16-year old student.
Police arrested a school guard for sexual assault in Barragem of Nampula city on 28 September assault incident. The suspect reportedly raped a 16-year old student.

Security forces announced on 30 September that they seized 1.3 tons of cannabis in two bags during the end of a weeklong operation in Mozambique. This comes as 60g of heroin and 42g of cocaine were seized across the country in different operations.

Security forces announced on 30 September that they seized 1.3 tons of cannabis in two bags during the end of a weeklong operation in Mozambique. This comes as 60g of heroin and 42g of cocaine were seized across the country in different operations.

Portugal announced that it had donated 1.217 million vaccine doses to Mozambique and Angola.   Mozambique's share of these doses reportedly arrived in the country on 28 September; sources later indicated this was a batch of 110,000 doses.

Mozambique according to the WHO is one of 40 African countries who missed a goal of having 10% of its population vaccinated against COVID-19 by the end of September.  Only 14 African countries achieved this goal; collectively, only 4% of Africa's population is vaccinated against COVID-19.  In Mozambique, about 5.6% of the population has so far been vaccinated against the virus.
The US government dedicated its new US Embassy in Maputo on 30 September. The new embassy is a 10 acre facility located along Maputo's Indian Ocean coast.

The Ministry of Health announced 2 new COVID deaths and 61 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 30 September. This comes as the 25 COVID inpatients were recorded. While Cabo Delgado noted the highest number of daily cases with 13 cases, Inhambane with 11 cases, and Maputo city also with 11 cases.

Mozambique's 2019-2020 Family Expenditure survey released recently showed that household spending and inequality has increased between 2015 and 2020 in the country. Over this five year period, median spending fell by 17%, meaning most people are poorer than they were 10 years ago.  Urban spending fell 24%, while rural spending fell 13%.  Spending was down the most in Gaza (42%), Maputo City, (38%), and Cabo Delgado (38%).  More than 90% of the country's population lives under World Bank's poverty line of $1.90.

Sources stated that Mozambican security forces assaulted a civilian in Pemba traveling on a motorcycle after the man was accused of damaging a military vehicle.  The Rwandan security forces resolved the issue stating that the incident was related to the Rwandan security forces and that the assault was unnecessary.

Sources stated that Mozambican security forces assaulted a civilian in Pemba traveling on a motorcycle after the man was accused of damaging a military vehicle.  The Rwandan security forces resolved the issue stating that the incident was related to the Rwandan security forces and that the assault was unnecessary.

Hidden Debts Judge Efigenio Baptista on 30 September said that there is "no evidence" that President Nyusi or former President Guebuza were linked to the Hidden Debts Scandal, saying that anyone with such evidence should come forward.  Baptista made this statement after several defendants over the course of the Hidden Debts case have implicated Guebuza and Nyusi of being connected to the scheme.
The Ministry of Health announced that it intends to immunize 7 million individuals by December 2021. The ministry stated that this was to prevent a possible fourth COVID wave in the country.

The Ministry of Health announced 36 COVID cases and a single death in Mozambique on 1 October. This comes as 312 daily recoveries were recorded. Cabo Delgado recorded 19 cases, being the highest for the day. Inhambane and Maputo City with 6 cases each.

Sources stated that the local airport in Chongoene will soon begin operations. The 74 million USD airport was financed by China. The airport reportedly has the capacity to accommodate 200,000 passengers annually.
IDPs from MDP in Mueda on or around 24 September were robbed of food aid by local residents who said they also should be receiving food assistance and that they too were starving.

Locals brawled with each other during a dispute over the distribution of relief goods in Maputo Village in Mueda district on 28 September. Two children were killed after suffocating during a riot over food distribution.

The Ministry of Health announced that 72,277 individuals who have received a first dose of the AstraZeneca vaccine should take the second dose on 05 October in Nampula, Tete, Manica, Gaza, Maputo, and Maputo City.
A suspicious fire was reported north of MDP town on 29 September near Malindi village.  This may indicate an insurgent attack or a clash between security forces and insurgents.
A suspicious fire was reported on 29 September in the Olumbe area.  This may indicate an insurgent attack or a clash between security forces and insurgents.

DP World announced on 1 October that the terminal and port in Maputo which the company manages is able to handle around 20,000 Twenty Foot Equivalent Units (TEUs) this past September. The port previously managed around 18,000 TEUs last September 2019.

On 29 September, pro-government militia in Muatide captured two suspected insurgents at around 1500hrs.  The two insurgents were reportedly natives of the village who were identified by the militia.  The two were taken to Mueda for interrogation.

Sources stated that Mozambican security forces assaulted and injured two civilians who were traveling to Chibau from Litingina village on the evening of 27 September. The two were fleeing from insurgents who had recently been in the area when they were assaulted.
Nelson Rego was sworn in as the new director of the National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) on 01 October.

Military helicopters patrolled over the Namatil area on 02 October after insurgents entered the village.  Militants retreated ahead of the helicopter's approach, and no airstrikes or strafing was reported in the area.

A group of at least 20 insurgents in the early afternoon of 02 October entered Namatili/Namatil in Mueda District on motorbikes and carried out looting.  Militants reportedly told locals they did not come to "mistreat" people but were searching for food. At least 100 civilians in the area fled into nearby bush areas.  Insurgents fled the village after Mozambican military helicopters approached the area. No casualties resulted from this attack.

Two sources reported multiple gunshots in Nangororo in Meluco District along the N380 road beginning in the late morning of 02 October.  One report indicated 12 or more militants had attacked the village; no further details on this incident are currently available.  Other sources later said militants also carried out looting in the village, and kidnapped at least 4 people.

SAMIM officials on 02 October confirmed the death of an insurgent leader, Sheikh Dr Njile North, also known as Rajab Awadhi Ndanjili, in an airstrike south of Chitama area between 24-27 September.  SAMIM previously identified him as the leader of an insurgent group in the Chitama area, also saying SAMIM forces with Mozambican troops had killed 17 insurgents in the area in fighting on 25 September.  Other sources later also reported at least one airstrike in the area on 25 September.   SAMIM identified Sheikh Njile North as a Mozambican national from Litingina who was the "head" of the group's Chitama base and reportedly supervised recruitment and indoctrination for the group.  Other sources indicated he is not one of the group's top leaders.

The Ministry of Health announced 31 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 2 October. This comes as 116 daily recoveries were recorded. Cabo Delgado province has the highest number of cases recorded with 11 cases, followed by Inhambane and Maputo city with 9 cases each. No related death reported in the past 24 hours, while four new hospital admissions and one was discharged.

On 04 October, the UN's Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General for Mozambique, Mirko Manzoni, commended efforts by the Mozambican Government and RENAMO party to maintain peace in the country, also calling on both sides to continue supporting the DDR process.

The Ministry of Health announced 14 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 3 October. This comes as 116 daily recoveries were recorded. Maputo City has the highest number of cases recorded with 5 cases, followed by Niassa and Nampula with 3 cases each. For the second consecutive day, no death reported in the country. Meanwhile, two new hospital admissions and three were discharged in the past 24 hours.

Mozambican Government on 03 October indicated that its priority in Cabo Delgado is the rehabilitation of access roads that were affected by insurgent attacks.  Authorities say their priority is the rehabilitation of the N380 road, the only paved road between Palma and Pemba.  Repair works are needed on a bridge along the N380 over the Messalo River, in addition to other repairs.  Works are also being carried out along the R762 road through Quissanga, where about 15kms of road have already been repaired.  Government authorities also said the water supply system of MDP was slightly damaged in the insurgent occupation, and is being repaired.

Mozambican Government is still  preparing its contingency plan two weeks before the official start of the 2021/2022 rainy season in the country. Heavy floods are expected during the aforementioned season especially in the central and southern areas of the country.  More than 1 million people are expected to be impacted during the rainy season.
Violations of safety measures of COVID-19 in Chimoio, Manica continue, with many establishments operating beyond the allowed operational hours imposed by the government.

On 4 October, in a speech commemorating the country's peace agreement to end the Civil War, President Nyusi said that Joint Forces in Cabo Delgado have made significant recent advances against the insurgency, and called on insurgents to surrender to security forces.  He also said that "attacks continue" and that recent offensives had forced insurgents out of their bases into new areas, saying militants were not "in the places they were hiding".  Nyusi also called for the surrender of RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo, calling on him to join the DDR process.  Nyusi also said more details of the SAMIM force in Cabo Delgado would be released at an upcoming Troika meeting in Pretoria on 05 October.

Authorities have prohibited vehicles on the streets of East Timor and Bagamoyo, Avenida Dez de Novembro and the central lanes of Avenida Samora Machel in Maputo City. These routes will be exclusively used by pedestrians moving forward.
The Mozambican government announced that it expected to have national ports to handle double their current handled cargo, with an increase of 41 million to 81 million tons over the next four years.

IDPs settling in Nangade were reportedly experiencing poor living conditions as of 1 October.  IDPs indicated they were not receiving relief goods and food aid.  IDPs are housed in a former cashew nut warehouse, and are not currently receiving regular food aid.

The Rwandan police announced they had arrested 13 individuals on terrorism charges in Kigali on 1 October. The suspects were suspected to be linked to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a group linked to the Islamic State in the DRC.  This group along with the insurgents in Mozambique are often linked to the Islamic State's Central Africa Province (ISCAP) franchise, though the extent of the ties between the Cabo Delgado insurgents and the ADF are not clear. The insurgents intend to conduct attacks in Rwanda allegedly in retaliation for Rwanda’s involvement in Mozambique.
Footage depicting child soldiers used by insurgents in bush areas of Macomia surfaced on 02 October.  Children as young as 5 are seen in this video handling weapons and being indoctrinated to fight.

The Ministry of Health announced that the third phase of vaccinations would begin on 20 October. The third phase was to allow the inoculation of the local population to reach 7 million in the country.

President Nyusi called for the border police to be rejuvenated to battle insurgency in a speech on Friday.  Nyusi said that security measures along the country's borders needed to be increased to deny entry to potential terrorists and other criminals.

The Mozambican government announced three days of national morning for the national cardinal Dom Alexandre dos Santos who recently passed away, beginning on 05 October.  Dos Santos was the first Mozambican national to become a cardinal in the Catholic church.

The WFP through October due to limited resources will continue to provide half monthly rations or the equivalent of about 39% of daily needed calories to hundreds of thousands of IDPs in Cabo Delgado.  The WFP during the month plans to carry out a vulnerability based targeting exercise to better target food assistance beneficiaries most in need.

Several local arts and crafts vendors in Maputo City's FEIMA park have indicated that the lack of tourism caused by the pandemic is leading to minimal revenue. Local artists stated that the art market demand has significantly declined, with some vendors saying they have seen revenues decline 75% or more.

The Islamic State's Nabaa magazine published information on 30 September, claiming two attacks in Nangade targeting "houses of Christians" in Nangade ono 24 September.  This may refer to attacks in the V Congresso area which occurred on that day.

The SADC Troika Summit met on 05 October in South Africa. The summit discussed the progress of SAMIM in Mozambique. The summit was chaired by South Africa and SADC president Cyril Ramaphosa and attended also by the Presidents of Botswana, Namibia, and President Nyusi.

Energy Minister Max Tonela on 30 September indicated that the government would meet with Total to discuss “conditions required” by the company for its return to Cabo Delgado in the near future. It was not immediately clear when these talks would take place.

The Ministry of Health announced 3 new COVID cases and a single COVID death in Mozambique on 4 October. This comes as 186 daily recoveries were reported. This is the lowest total number of cases reported in a single day this year.

The former Mozambican Prime Minister and current member of parliament Aires Ali on 03 October was implicated in Pandora Papers, which stated he had hidden offshore wealth/possessions in Seychelles. The Pandora papers stated that the former politician created a shell company to transfer his wealth to this company.  Ali also was reported to have obscured his connections to this firm.

The RENAMO leader Momade criticized FRELIMO in an 04 October speech saying the ruling party has operated in “bad faith” and the political party has lacked the ability to resolve issues in the country. Momade claims that FRELIMO owns the country and regularly commits electoral fraud.

SAMIM General Brigadier Dumisani Nzinge stated on 3 October that documents and electronic devices from insurgents indicate that most militants are native Mozambicans, though there are also a significant number of Tanzanian nationals among the group.

SAMIM Brig. General Nzinge on 03 October stated that SAMIM coordinates its operations with Rwanda through Mozambican forces which are embedded with both foreign forces. The general also described this as not ideal, and hoped that in the future the three forces would be able to directly coordinate with one another.
SAMIM General Brigadier Dumisani Nzinge called for SADC members who have not contributed forces yet to assist and support the Mozambican mission with whatever contribution they are able to provide.
A troop of 90 Mozambican navy personnel were deployed on 30 September to Ibo Island.
Sources stated that a group of 90 Mozambican Naval personnel recently deployed to Ibo have not been paid for some time, and are reportedly involved in a "money swindling scheme".

A police spokesman said on 06 October that on 28 September, police in the Zove area of Inhaminga District in Sofala had raided a base utilized by RENAMO dissidents.  Police said that RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo had been among a group of militants at the base, but that this group had fled just ahead of the police operation.  Officers recovered personal items belonging to Nhongo, as well as cooking supplies and foodstuffs.  Police also said items stolen in a raid by suspected dissidents in early September on Chinapamimba in Muanza District had been recovered.  President Nyusi earlier in the wake made a passing reference to this operation in a speech, one of the few recent times new operations targeting RENAMO dissidents in Central Mozambique has been reported.

The Ministry of Public Works stated there is currently no water supply in Mocimboa da Praia, Nangade, and Muidumbe as of 3 October due to damage inflicted on water systems in these districts by insurgents.  Repair works to restore water supplies in these districts are ongoing.

The Ministry of Public Works stated there is currently no water supply in Mocimboa da Praia, Nangade, and Muidumbe as of 3 October due to damage inflicted on water systems in these districts by insurgents.  Repair works to restore water supplies in these districts are ongoing.

The Ministry of Public Works stated there is currently no water supply in Mocimboa da Praia, Nangade, and Muidumbe as of 3 October due to damage inflicted on water systems in these districts by insurgents.  Repair works to restore water supplies in these districts are ongoing.

Sources stated that insurgents left behind a threatening note in Namatil in Swahili and Arabic demanding local authorities to return weapons captured from the group.  The note said a village in Mueda would be "turned into an inferno" if weapons were not returned.

7 women were kidnapped outside of Nacate village south of Macomia on 02 October by a group of insurgents.  SAMIM troops on 03 October deployed to the area to rescue the abducted women but were unable to locate them.  Insurgents earlier in the day had attacked Nangororo village, just over 10 airline kms south of Nacate.

On 05 October, the SADC released a statement announcing the extension of the SADC Mission in Mozambique (SAMIM) for another three months into January 2022. The statement indicated that at a meeting in Pretoria, the SADC had approved the continuation of "offensive operations against terrorists and violent extremists to consolidate stability of security".  The mission had been officially sanctioned previously for three months from 15 July, with its mandate previously officially set to expire later this month.

Unconfirmed reports stated that Mozambican troops reportedly ambushed insurgents near Litingina village on 3 October, leaving 2 militants dead.  This group of insurgents had previously raided Namatil.  At least 5 militants escaped from this clash.

Sources indicate that at least 113 Islamic teachers and imams have been killed during the Cabo Delgado insurgency as of 3 October, according to Muslim clerics and organizations in Cabo Delgado. Killings occurred in  Macomia, Quissanga, Muidumbe, Mocimboa da Praia, Palma, Nangade, and Mueda districts.
SAMIM troops shot dead 4 insurgents during an operation at Xibolongo beach near Mucojo on or around 30 September.
SAMIM forces detained 3 suspected insurgents in Montepuez District on 1 October.  No further information on these arrests are currently available.
SAMIM security forces detained 7 suspected insurgents in Montepuez district on 2 October. No further information on these arrests are currently available.

Average to above average rainfall is expected between October and March of 2022.  There is a moderate to high risk of flooding in the Maputo, Umbeluzi, Incomati, Limpopo, Buzi, Pungue, Savane, and Licungo basins.

UNICEF On 05 October indicated that there are increasing indications that militants are using child soldiers in Cabo Delgado.  The organization referred to a recent video reportedly taken in a bush area of Macomia depicting child soldiers as young as 5 years old wielding weapons and being indoctrinated to fight for the insurgency.  UNICEF also said that children forced to be child soldiers for the group are not being released by the insurgency, but are being rescued by government forces.

RENAMO leader Momade announced on 4 October that the political opposition parties, including RENAMO, are regularly prevented from carrying out normal political activities.  Momade said this includes being prevented from raising political flags at over party HQ.  Momade also said community leaders are used as a "weapon" by FRELIMO in order to harass and limit the rights of political parties and their supporters.
Local officials announced that a road paving project was ongoing in Cuamba city on 5 October. This will be the first time in its history that Cuamba will have had paved roads.
SAMIM troops launched operation on 3 October to locate seven abducted women near Nacate. The operation was not successful.
The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) arrested five individuals for attempting to smuggling pangolins in Nacala Porto on or around 29 September.
The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) arrested five individuals for attempting to smuggling pangolins in Nacala Porto on or around 29 September.

O&G Major ExxonMobil Senior VP Neal Chapman indicated this week that the company still views the Rovuma LNG project as a "very large, very competitive resource" but that current insecurity in Cabo Delgado meant operations would continue to be suspended for the immediate future, and that the company was still working with the government towards eventually starting operations in the province once security is restored.

The US Famine Warning System in a recent report said that the eastern half of Cabo Delgado will continue to experience a food crisis for at least the next 9 months due to the ongoing insurgency and the accompanying disruption of agricultural activities in insurgent impacted areas.  Over 866,000 people in Northern Mozambique are expected to require food aid for the foreseeable future.

The West International Holding (WIH) Chinese company announced that they would spend $800 million in a financial package to improve industrial development in Mozambique.  The company is a major shareholder of a cement factory in Dugongo in Maputo, where it was previously accused of the  illegal detention of local employees since the beginning of the pandemic. Other accusations also stated that supervisors were beating their employees if they refuse 12-hour shifts and do not provide medical attention to their employees.

Hidden Debts Judge Efigenio Baptista on  05 October called on Lebanese businessman Jean Bousanti to appear in person to testify at the Hidden Debts case, following a statement from Boustani's legal team that he is available to testify via teleconference at the trial.  Boustani is considered a key witness and to have played a key role in the Hidden Debts Scandal.

The Ministry of Health announced 19 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 5 October. This comes as Zambezia recorded 12 of the new cases. Active cases were at 1,298 and 21 were still admitted at health units.

On 06 October, Mozambique's Council of Ministers announced the closure of the Costa do Sol and Catembe beaches in Maputo City, Ponta d'Ouro and Macaneta in Maputo province, Bilene and Xai-xai in Gaza province, Barra, Tofo and Guinjata in Inhambane province, Estoril Macuti and Ponta Gêa in Beira City, Zalala in Quelimane city, Fernão Veloso in Nacala city; and Wimbe, Marrenganhe, and Sagal in Cabo Delgado province.  These beaches will be closed for 15 days as part of COVID prevent measures. The government said it had made this decision after Mozambicans gathered at beaches countrywide over the weekend in large numbers, ignoring anti-COVID-19 safety measures including ignoring social distancing.

Sources stated that the SAMIM currently has around 1,000 troops currently deployed in Cabo Delgado. The SADC had authorized the deployment of up to 2,916 soldiers as part of the SAMIM force.

Sources stated that the South African National Defense Forces has a battalion reserve in South Africa for possible deployment to Cabo Delgado. The SANDF also has not yet deployed any regular infantry or artillery, or frigates or a submarine as was part of the original SAMIM deployment plan.

The World Health Organization announced that a malaria vaccine is now ready to be given to children in Sub-Saharan Africa.  This vaccine will potentially save tens of thousands of lives across Africa every year, including in Mozambique, which has high rates of malaria.
The Ministry of Health announced 48 new COVID in Mozambique on 6 October. Daily recoveries were recorded at 36. The current active COVID cases were at 1,304.

In a 22 September report, the IOM said that there had been 730 newly arrived IDPs arriving in Nangade, 944 IDPs returning to Ancuabe or leaving Ancuabe for their home districts, and 393 IDPs returning to Mueda or leaving Mueda for their homes districts between the 15-21 September period.

The Mozambican Bar Association suspended a lawyer, Elisio de Sousa, for 3 months due to criminal conduct during the Hidden Debt trial.  Sousa was suspended for comments criticizing the trial process.

TotalEnergies CEO Patrick Pouyanne on 28 September said that the company does not want to make an impulsive decisions in restarting their gas exploration operations in Mozambique. The oil and gas company does not want to have to pull out their personnel from the area again if the come under new threat, saying the company will wait for security gains in Cabo Delgado to be "consolidated" before going back into Cabo Delgado.  Pouyanne had previously said that LNG production in Mozambique could begin in 2026 if the company restarted works at the Afungi LNG Camp in early 2022.
Media sources indicated that Yara fertilizer company was closing their Beira plant and were moving operations to Durban.

The National Statistical Authority indicate that 73 percent of the roads around Mozambique remain unpaved. Roads in many areas, including the N1 road, are in a poor condition, with many roads also lacking road signs.

The Mozambique Civil Aviation lost 78 million USD due to the COVID pandemic during 2020. The loss was due to the government’s focus on the health sector to improve the outcome of the pandemic in the country.
Insurgents reportedly abducted four women from Nangololo/Nangororo village in Meluco district on 2 October. Several civilians were assaulted by the insurgents during the attack.
Pro-government militiamen detained a militant in Namacande on 29 September. The militant was later shot dead by the militia.

A local media report stated on 6 October that Mozambican forces often target the local population and IDPs from Mocimboa da Praia as suspected insurgents, regularly harassing, detaining, and even sometimes killing civilians from MDP District based solely on the fact that they are from the district.

Security forces arrested a man suspected to be an insurgent in Nangade on 24 August. The detainee was reportedly a local from Mocimboa da Praia. The detainees was reportedly assaulted by the security forces during the his detention.

Tanzanian security forces recently have been reported to be “beating” individuals who attempt to cross back the Rovuma River between both Tanzania and Mozambique, suspecting these civilians are insurgents.
Sources stated on 6 October that a local from Mocimboa da Praia was reported to be missing in Nangade. The individual was last seen being questioned by security forces.
Pro-government militiamen detained and assaulted a Tanzanian civilian in Nangade on 30 September. The militiamen mistook the victim for an insurgency.

Two armed kidnappers abducted a Mozambican national, later described as police as "linked to commercial activity" near Eduardo Mondlane University campus in Maputo City on the morning of 07 October at around 0700hrs. The armed men fired warning shots before approaching the parked vehicle of the victim. The victim was reportedly dropping of his daughter to the university and was about to leave when the incident occurred.  The assailants forced the man into a waiting car and left the scene.

A doctor, Basit Gani on 07 October, Thursday morning at around 0800hrs was reportedly abducted from his home in Maputo on Friedrich Engles Avenue.  Police later confirmed this incident, saying criminals used firearms during this incident.

Brazilian security forces on 05 October seized 4.3 tons of cocaine intended to be smuggled from Rio de Janeiro to Mozambique on the morning of 5 October. Another containers filled with 700kg of cocaine was also seized. The drugs were hidden into soap boxes inside the containers aboard a ship.  This is the largest ever cocaine seizure in Rio.  Two people were also arrested in connection to the incident.
Unconfirmed reports indicated that kidnappers abducted a civilian working for Frozy in Machava, west of Maputo City, on 3 September.
Sources stated that Rwandan forces are seeking to obtain Turkish drones for the deployment in Cabo Delgado against the insurgency.

The Rwandan and Mozambique governments announced on 6 October that they have signed a trade deal to boost trade and investment. The trade agreement was conducted by the Rwanda Development Board (RBD) and APIEX of Mozambique. The two countries have also discussed direct flights between Kigali and Maputo.

The Mozambican Prime Minister do Rosario participated on 07 October in the opening ceremony for reconstruction works in Cabo Delgado. However, sources stated that the government still lack funds for the reconstruction plan for the province.
Security forces reported the seizure of 1 ton of cannabis and 5,281 kg of narcotics in Mozambique on 25 September in a series of operations.

Security forces also seized six livestock, eight computers, six televisions, 31 mobile phones, 34 motorbikes, and 17 vehicles in Maputo, Manica, and Cabo Delgado on 1 October. Security forces also seized four firearms, two of which were AK-47 and two pistols and 118 ammunition.

Other reports from villagers near Litingina on 28 September reported gunfire in the area and said they had fled into the bush.

Security forces arrested a woman and two other suspects in a murder for hire plot in Muhalaze, north of Matola, on 7 October.

Private water providers have threatened to suspend the water supply to 3 million customers in several areas of Maputo from 06 November. These suppliers currently provide water to areas of the city where the government is unable to provide services. The suppliers threatened to suspend this supply due to disagreements with the government.

Insurgent attacked Quitico village near Olumbe on 1 October. Three civilians were killed. The insurgents reportedly abducted a civilian during this raid. Security forces responded and managed to surround a group of seven insurgents who were killed is a clash after the raid.

Insurgents on or around 28 September entered Nachitenje village in Mueda district and told them to spread the word in the area that an insurgent attack in the area was imminent.

ISIS militants claimed they had conducted an attack targeting "Lukuanba", likely referring to Lucuamba village near Litingina on 24 September. The militants claimed that they beheaded two civilians and destroyed a motorcycle and a residence.

ISIS militants claimed attacking the village of Manazi Muga in Nangade District on 24 September.  The exact location of this village was not immediately clear within Nangade District.
On 20 August, insurgents attacked advancing Rwandan troops in the Naquitengue area, north of Mbau.  12 insurgents were reportedly killed in this clash as Rwandan troops repelled this attack.

In clashes on 01 September, Rwandan troops clashed with large numbers of insurgents along the north bank of the Messalo River, killing "many" militants according to the Rwandan military, though no specific number of casualties was reported.  Significant numbers of insurgents fled south of the Messalo River after this clash.

Rwandan security forces on 01 October paraded a group of 13 suspected members of the ADF/ISCAP in Kigali who had reportedly planned to carry out attacks in the Rwandan capital in retaliation for Rwanda's intervention in Rwanda.  One of the suspects said that he had been arrested on 31 August, and that a week before he had been "connected" to a Kenyan national who "was coming from Mozambique".  This individual, he said, trained the suspects on "how to use explosives to target specific buildings in revenge for Rwanda's intervention in Cabo Delgado".  This is the first report appearing to show a direct link between this group in Kigali and the Cabo Delgado insurgency.
The Tax Authority announced that airport security seized 247 buttons containing quantities of heroin at Maputo International Airport on 6 October. The drugs were reportedly being smuggled to Canada.

Mozambican and Rwandan troops on 06 October were reported to have carried out an ambush targeting insurgents in the Limala area in Southern Mocimboa da Praia District, killing an insurgent leader identified as "Muhamudu". At least 1 other insurgent was killed in this incident; some insurgents also escaped the ambush.  President Nyusi and Police Commander Bernardino Rafael both referred to this incident in speeches on 07 October, saying Muhamudu had commanded insurgents who had committed the 2019 Xitaxi massacre in which at least 52 people were killed in a Muidumbe village.

The Ministry of Health announced 25 new COVID cases and no new COVID deaths in Mozambique on 7 October. This sets the country with no fatalities for a third consecutive day. Two of the new cases were hospitalized while 2 others were discharged. This comes as Cabo Delgado and Niassa recorded 6 COVID cases each, while Nampula and Maputo City recorded 3 cases each.
Suspicious fires were reported on 07 October in the Guludo area near Mucojo in Macomia.  This incident could be related to insurgent activity or clashes between security forces and insurgents.
A vehicle collided with a minibus in Murrupula of Zambezia region on 8 October, 3 civilians were killed and several others were injured.

The Association of Doctors of Mozambique demanded a security force intervention to end the kidnappings on 7 October. The union made this appeal after the kidnapping of Dr. Basit Gani earlier in the day in Maputo City, saying the threat of more of these kinds of incidents was most significant in the capital.
Vale coal company expects that a buyer will purchase its Moatize operations by the end of the year. This comes as Vale intends to wrap up its operations in Mozambique by the end of the year.
A minibus collided with a vehicle along the road in Matama of Manhica district, Maputo Province, on 07 October.  5 people were killed and 15 others injured in this RTA.

The UK government announced the removed Mozambique from its "Red List" as of 11 October. This would allow travelers from Mozambique to enter the UK without being quarantined.   Passengers travelling to the UK must also present a negative COVID test upon arrival; new UK rules stipulate this can include a lower cost lateral flow COVID test.

RENAMO leader Momade criticized Frelimo after vandalization of a monument honoring former RENAMO leader Afonso Dlakama in Zimpinga, Manica.  Momade held FRELIMO responsible for the vandalization of the monument, saying "FRELIMO once again showed that it doesn't want peace and never wanted it".

Suspected FRELIMO supporters destroyed a memorial monument to former RENAMO leader Afonso Dhlakama in the Amatongas area of Manica on or around 04 October.  The monument was dedicated on 04 October, but destroyed within 24 hours of being erected.
The Ministry of Health announced 36 new COVID cases and 2 related deaths in Mozambique on 8 October. This comes as Cabo Delgado recorded 14 of the new COVID cases.

The Association of Rwandan refugees condemned in Maputo the intimidation of one of their members on 03 October in Nampula. In this incident, two unidentified men attempted to forcefully enter the home of Innocent Abubakar.  The two left the home but later promised they would come back.  This incident follows the 13 September slaying of Revocat Karemangingo, a Rwandan exile and member of the association in Matola.

RENAMO on 08 October accused security forces and SERNIC of being involved in multiple kidnappings in the country.  RENAMO made this accusation after the kidnapping earlier in the day of two people in the capital.  RENAMO also said that police in the capital spent more time harassing informal vendors than pursuing serious crimes.

Hidden Debt Defendant and former Economic Intelligence Service, Information and State Security (SISE) director Antonio Carlos do Rosario stated that a letter exists that proves then Defense Minister Nyusi had connected Credit Suisse to Finance Minister Manuel Chang, proving Nyusi's connection to the scandal.

The Ministry of Health announced 28 new COVID cases and one related death in Mozambique on 9 October. This comes as three daily recoveries were recorded. Meanwhile, five new hospital admissions and no were discharges were reported in the past 24 hours.

Reports on 9 October indicate that Rwanda will purchase at least 12 Turkish-made Bayraktar TB2 attack drones, likely to be used to fight the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  Previous reports had indicated Rwanda was interested in acquiring Turkish drones for this purpose.

A fire broke out in a supermarket in Maputo city in the late hours of  9 October, destroying goods stored inside the property. Rescue teams arrived at the scene to contain the fire. The exact cause of fire was not disclosed.

Security forces arrested a 24-yr-old man in Maputo City on 11 October, over alleged killing of his wife. The suspect reportedly hit and killed the victim. He later brought the dead body in a health center and claimed that his wife was hit by their neighbor's roof.

Reports on 11 October indicate that a 24-yr-old suspect allegedly hit and killed his wife in Maputo City. He later brought the dead body of the victims in a health center and claimed that his wife was hit by their neighbor's roof. Security forces later arrested the suspect.

On 8 October, the Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA) expressed concern in the alarming level of kidnap incidents in the country's major cities, including Maputo City. The group called on the Mozambican government to intervene and end the kidnappings.

The Ministry of Health announced 22 new COVID cases and zero related deaths in Mozambique on 10 October. The highest number of new cases was recorded in Zambezia Province with 11 cases, followed by  Niassa Province with five cases. Cabo Delgado reported three new case, Inhambane-two, and Gaza-one . Meanwhile, 26 recoveries and four hospital discharges were reported in the past 24 hours. Notably, no hospital admissions were recorded in the country .

The Red Cross warned on Monday of a surge of cholera, diarrhea and other water-borne diseases transmitted by contaminated water in Cabo Delgado.  The number of cholera cases in the province was 3,400 in August, compared to 2,200 cases in August 2020.  There were 28,602 diarrhea cases reported in the country so far in 2021

On 11 October, several sources reported that Mozambican forces killed RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo in an “ambush” in mountainous areas close to Gorongosa National Park in the Ndjovo forest near Mazamba in Cheringoma District of Sofala Province.  Police Commander General Bernardno Rafael in a press conference said that Nhongo and a number of RENAMO dissident militants had been shot dead in an exchange of gunfire with Mozambican police at approximately 0730hrs Monday morning.  One other militant was killed in the clash.  Three assault rifles and a pistol were also recovered in after the gunfire exchange.

The Electricity de Mozambique (EDM) announced the restoration of power to the town of Palma on 8 October. This comes as EDM continued repairs on the Awasse sub-station and replacing the cables of the 10MVA transformer. EDM also said that the a short-term repair was made to replace the damaged electrical towers at Macomia Substation and emergency generators were being installed to support the repair.

ISCAP on 08 October claimed credit for an IED attack in Kampala, Uganda, claiming the bomb had targeted a police vehicle.  This report is not confirmed.  This claim is significant as this is the first time ISCAP has claimed an attack in Uganda, and the first time the group has claimed an attack outside of the normal areas of operations of its DRC and Mozambique franchises.

On 8 October, UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres stated that it is vital to create a strong  African military force to support Mozambican Armed Forces in the fight against insurgency. He added that he will raise this issue with the United Nations Security Council.

Large crowds were present in Palma on 9 October  to hear a speech from the Prime Minister, Carlos Agostinho do Rosario. Thousands of people recently returned to Palma following the restoration of security in the area.

The Ministry of Health announced six new COVID cases and two related deaths in Mozambique on 11 October. The highest number of new cases was recorded in Maputo City with three cases, followed by  Nampula Province with two cases and Gaza-one. Meanwhile, 79 recoveries and three hospital discharges were reported in the past 24 hours. There are currently 1,108 active COVID cases in Mozambique.

On 11 October, Motorists lamented the poor condition of N7 especially in the section between Cruzamento de Tete and Pungue Sul in Manica as well as the 50 to thousand meticais toll payment required at checkpoints along this road. Another concern was the alleged establishment of another toll in the area to be launched in December. Locals have urged the government to repair and restore the affected roads as soon as possible. In response, the deputy minister of Public Works and Housing stated that the rehabilitation will commence soon and that the toll charges will aid in the cost of maintenance work.

The Minister of Labor and Social Security, Margarida Talapa, announced on 11 October that more than 97% of the companies that had been closed down due to the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 have already reopened. This development comes as some restrictions were recently lifted following the continuous decline of COVID-19 new cases and deaths in the country.
Security forces arrested a motorcycle thief in the middle of a road in Nampula last week. A suspected stolen motorcycle and mobile phone were recovered from his possession.

On 6 October, Prime Minister Carlos Agostinho do Rosario reiterated that the Reconstruction Plan for Cabo Delgado Province recently announced by the government will not replace efforts underway under the annual Social and Economic Plan (PES) and by the Development Agency for the North (ADIN). The reconstruction plan reportedly complements all the other initiatives and focuses on the districts which have been directly affected by insurgency.

Mozambican Health Minister Armindo Tiago, speaking in Maputo on 11 October, stated that it will take some time for the country to receive the new WHO approved malaria vaccine due to the steps and procedures in procuring it. Countries affected by malaria must include a vaccine against malaria in their vaccination plan, which will be sent to the Global Alliance for Vaccines (GAVI), who will allocate the said vaccines. The entire process could take up to 12 months before the vaccine will be available.

Reports on 11 October indicate that Defense and Security Forces (FDS) officers have been assaulting IDPs in the villages in Nangade over alleged suspicions that these IDPs are collaborating with insurgents in the area.

Military troops allegedly beat a civilian in Nangade district on 30 September after the latter refused to offer home-made alcoholic beverages to the soldiers. The victim was later taken to the hospital to treat his injuries.

A police officer, Gracio Matsai, was shot dead in Intaka area of Maputo City on 10 October. Matsai was attacked and killed ahead of a reported SERNIC operation to arrest him, as he was suspected of involvement in the abduction of two people in Maputo City on 07 October.

On 10 October, three additional dead bodies have been recovered after a naval vessel sank near the coast of Memba in Nampula region on the afternoon of 7 October. The death toll related to the accident has increased to 23.  Some sources indicated as many as 60 people were missing after the accident.

On 7 October, the UK Government announced that Mozambique will be removed from the red list effective 11 October. Mozambican travelers must show proof that they are fully inoculated by UK's approved vaccines and an RT-PCR test is required 48 hours after arrival. Mozambican nationals may experience difficulty in travelling to the UK as only one of the two Vaccines used by the country is vaccines approved by the UK, in addition UK is not accepting Portuguese language vaccination documentation to enter the country.

On 11 October, the National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) said that civilians across the country continue to violate anti-COVID measures, saying it will increase inspections and operations to shut down illegal gatherings, prohibited activities, and other violations of these measures in the near future.  It also warned that not adhering to these measures could have consequences for Christmas and New Years activities in the country.

Electricidade de Mocambique (EDM) stated on 10 October that electrical services resumed in Quitunda as well as in Palma town. EDM also indicated that electricity will also be restored in Muidumbe in the next three weeks.

Rwandan President Kagame, announced during a security briefing in Qatar on 12 October, that they have deployed nearly 2,000 military troops and police officers in Cabo Delgado. He added that they have initially sent 1,000 troops in July 2021 before the counter-terror operations embarked in the province, and eventually added more security operatives. He reiterated that the deployment and operation have been done swiftly and that they have yet to receive any foreign financial support.

Based on the 12 October report by the National Institute of Statistics, Mozambican transport lost 20.7percent of passenger traffic and 18.1 percent circulation of goods in 2020 during the pandemic. The railway sector saw the highest number of passenger reduction with 75.6 percent, followed by air transport, which lost 40.6 percent of passengers, and maritime transport with 25.1% less compared to 2019.

The Ministry of Health announced 27 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 12 October. The highest number of new cases was recorded in Cabo Delgado with eight cases, followed by  Nampula Province and Maputo City with four cases each, Niassa- 3, Manica -3 and Gaza-one. Meanwhile, 83 recoveries and no COVID-related deaths were reported in the past 24 hours.

The National Organization of Teachers (ONP) stated on 12 October that more than 1,600 teachers are displaced in the districts of Metuge, Montepuez, Ancuabe, Chiure, and Pemba from districts impacted by the insurgency.

On 11 October, Mirko Manzoni, Personal Envoy of the UN Secretary-General for Mozambique, stated talks with the late dissident leader, Mariano Nhongo, in recent months were unsuccessful. He added that he hopes peace and stability will now return to Central Mozambique.

Clashes were reported in Pundanhar on or before 05 October between different insurgent groups following an argument over which group would control the Pundanhar base.  One group was reportedly led by "Nuro", possibly referring to high ranking insurgent commander Bonomade Ibn Omar, while another group was led by Muhamudu Saha. No information was available regarding casualties. The exchange of gunfire drew the attention of the joint forces, who pursued one insurgent group to Lamala village, where Muhamudu and one other insurgent were killed in a joint force ambush.

A woman murdered her two children using a rake in Mieze, Metuge District on 10 October. Reports suggest that the suspect earlier planned to sacrifice a family member in exchange for her and her husband's success. Security forces later arrested the suspect.

Security forces arrested a woman who allegedly murdered her two children using a rake in Mieze, Metuge District on 10 October. Reports suggest that the suspect earlier planned to sacrifice a family member in exchange for her and her husband's success.

On 12 October, Lutero Simango , leader of the Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM) parliamentary bench warned that violence may not be over in central Mozambique after the death of dissident leader, Nhongo, over the weekend.

Ministry of Public Works, Housing and Water Resources, announced on 9 October that the restoration of the road on sections between the crossing of N7 and N6 to the Pungue river is scheduled for November. The cost of the restoration is estimated at around 95 million meticais.

Security forces seized over 2,000 cubic meters of wood that was being illegally exported via the port of Beira on or before 13 October. Two companies who owned the said wood reportedly falsified its documents.  Fines of over €27,144 have been imposed on the companies exporting this wood.

Security forces seized over 2,000 cubic meters of wood that was being illegally exported via the port of Beira on or before 13 October. Two companies who owned the said wood reportedly falsified its documents.  Fines of over €27,144 have been imposed on the companies exporting this wood.

Authorities said on 13 October that more than 14,000 state employees were released in the first half of this year after they were found to have been illegally hired.  Minister of State Administration and Public Service Ana Comoana stated that this development saved the government more than 13 million meticais, which was supposed to be allotted to the salaries of the affected workers. Disciplinary actions were underway against some state officials and agents involved in the said irregularities.

Mozambique, along with 4 other African countries, plans to build power plants fueled by coal, according to the report "No New Coal Handbook" released by think-tanks on Wednesday, 13 October. This comes despite the global fight aiming to end the establishment of more coal-fired electricity infrastructure. The report added that along Botswana, Malawi, South Africa and Zimbabwe, Mozambique has sought financing for the project from China. China, however, has recently announced it would end support for such projects in other countries, following Japan and South Korea's pledge to do the same. With this, the report has forecasted the cancellation of these plans. In addition to this, the report cited that the International Energy Agency has stated that no new coal-fired power plants should be approved past 2021 in the bid the control global warming.

On Wednesday, 13 October, the International Monetary Fund reported that the Mozambican public debt will rise to 133.6%, above the GDP, in 2021 from 2020's 128.5% and will fall to 127.6% in 2022. The reason behind this have not been specified but should be addressed in the coming week when the Fund releases the economic outlook for sub-Saharan Africa.

The Ministry of Health recorded 25 new COVID-19 cases in the country on 13 October. Out of the 25 cases, 2 are foreign nationals and 23 are Mozambicans. This is the second consecutive day the ministry has not recorded any Covid-related deaths.

A report on Wednesday, 13 October, indicated that the police still have no leads on the murder of a police officer on Sunday evening, 10 October, but investigations are ongoing to reveal the motive and the perpetrators of the murder. Gracio Matsai, a police assigned to the National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC), was shot dead in Intaka area of Maputo City. Matsai was attacked and killed ahead of a reported SERNIC operation to arrest him, as he was suspected of involvement in the abduction of two people in Maputo City on 07 October.  There is suspicion that some security force elements may have been involved in his death.

Antonio Carlos do Rosario, former director of Economic Intelligence of the Mozambican secret service, revealed in court on Tuesday, 12 October, that then defense minister and current President Filipe Nyusi, recommended the establishment of the Tuna Fishing Company (Ematum), which was used in a corruption scheme linked to the hidden debt money. Rosario said the President Nyusi agreed to the creation of Ematum, and 2 other companies, to serve as a covert operation in collecting information about the criminal activities in Mozambican waters, based on the advise of the technical team that enforce the Integrated Monitoring and Protection System (SIMP) of the Exclusive Economic Zone. Rosario added that part of the US$850 million debt of Ematum was used to obtain defense equipment but the amount was not specified. Despite Rosario's and other defendants' statements, Judge Efigenio Baptista said that they have found no evidence against President Nyusi related to the trial.

Rwandan forces on 12 October said that over 20 civilians escaped from insurgents recently and are now in military custody.  This incident was believed to have occurred in Southern MDP District amid ongoing Joint forces operations in the area.

National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) authorities on 13 October closed a commercial establishment in the Slaughterhouse market area in Nampula city for charging unusually higher than the standard prices for cement.
Joaquim Chissano, former president of Mozambique, called for peace in the country following the death of the RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo, according to a report on 13 October.

Mozambique and Zimbabwe held the 12th session of the Mozambique-Zimbabwe Joint Permanent Commission on Defense and Security in Maputo city starting 13 October. The meeting, co-chaired by Jaime Neto, Minister of National Defense, and Owen Ncube, Zimbabwe's Minister of State for National Security, aimed to evaluate the progress of the agreements reached in the fields of defense and public and state security during the 11th session, and explore new approaches to fighting terrorism. Prior to the meeting, a discussion was held between experts in the defense and security field from both countries.
An intoxicated vigilante working for a private security company was arrested for shooting and wounding an elderly person in KaMaxakeni district of Maputo city, on 13 October.
An intoxicated vigilante working for a private security company was arrested for shooting and wounding an elderly person in KaMaxakeni district of Maputo city, on 13 October.

On 12 October, former RENAMO dissident, Andre Matsangaissa Junior, said with the death of former self-proclaimed RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo, attacks by the RENAMO Military Junta in Central Mozambique will likely stop. Matsangaissa said there is no other leader in the group to organize and lead attacks.

A report on 13 October indicated that businesses are gradually opening in Macomia town, which had been captured and held by militants briefly in May 2020. This came as roads linking the town to Mocimboa da Praia to the north and Pemba the south have been reopened, and some of the displaced residents have been returning to the town and coastal areas. However, returning IDPs complain of the lack of support from the government and limited access to basic services as many buildings, including homes, and infrastructure have been destroyed by the insurgent attacks.

Some returning residents of Macomia have returned to fishing as source of livelihood and sustenance, travelling to the Macomia coast to fish off the islands of Makalowe, Magundula, and Quifula despite navy patrols warning them not to return to the area because militants remain present in the area, a report on 13 October stated.

On Tuesday, 12 October, the Mozambican National Resistance (RENAMO) secretary-general, Andre Magibire, announced in Beira city RENAMO's readiness to accept dissidents who left in the past to create their own movement, assuring them they will not be subjected to mistreatment. Magibire added that the dissidents will receive the same benefits as others. These remarks came days following the death of RENAMO dissident leader Mariano Nhongo in an “ambush” in mountainous areas close to Gorongosa National Park in Muanza District of Sofala Province.

A report on 12 October indicated that 40 Mozambican women's groups denounced alleged cases of mistreatment of pregnant women and suspected trafficking of newborn babies in the hospitals of the county. The same groups claimed that in Maputo alone, 15 cases of ill-treatment and abuse on pregnant women by health professionals were reported to them in the last quarter. They called for investigation and prosecution of the accountable health professionals involved in the said irregularities, and the provision of assistance and compensation for the victims.

On Tuesday, 12 October, Mozambican Association of Bakers/Amopao and the Mozambican government inked a memorandum of agreement that would prevent a price increase of bread through the sustained provision of firewood to bakeries. The agreement stipulates that firewood cutting permits for bread production would be issued annually and that the Ministry of Land and Environment will sell fast-growing seedlings as part of reforestation efforts.

Mozambican security units intercepted and seized 7 boats loaded with food and other supplies near Ilha Mecungo, off the coast of Mocimboa da Praia district on or around 07 October. An unspecified number of crew members and passengers were also arrested and were still detained as of 11 October. The boats were said to have come from Pemba and headed to Palma. A source indicated that the security units demanded payment in exchange for their release.

Displaced individuals have expressed anger over the lack of aid at a relocation site in Nangua, Metuge district, on or around 7 October. Some of them have complained of not receiving food for 3 months. When new IDPs arrived at the site following the recent attack on Lindi, Quissanga, the existing IDPs' anger escalated as the former were provided with food aid and housing while none were given to them.

A group of farmers from Macomia on 03 October reported seeing a group of suspicious individuals believed to be insurgents, and fled the area.  Insurgents in the past have used the Cagembe area as a base in Northern Quissanga.
Workers carrying out repair works on the bridge over Messalo River near Miangalewa are being regularly escorted by military patrols in travelling to and from Macomia and the site.

Mozambican forces and insurgents engaged in armed clash near Miangalewa, Muidumbe district of Cabo Delgado, on 1 October. Reports of casualties or material damages were unavailable; however the clash disrupted repair works being done on the bridge over the Messalo river.
The repair works on the bridge over the Messalo River were disrupted by the armed clash between the Mozambican forces and insurgents near Miangalewa, Muidumbe district of Cabo Delgado, on 1 October.

12 insurgents invaded, looted food supplies and killed a female villager at the village of Kiwengulo in Tanzania, across the Rovuma River in west Palma district on 1 October. The villager was killed as she recognized 1 of the insurgents to be from the village. Tanzanian security forces responded but were unable to apprehend the insurgents.

Tanzanian security forces responded to a village raid carried out by 12 insurgents in Kiwengulo in Tanzania, across the Rovuma River in west Palma district on 1 October. However, Tanzanian troops were unable to apprehend the insurgents who managed to carry out looting and to kill 1 of the villagers.

On 14 October, Mozambican Army Chief Cristovao Chume said that joint forces operations in Palma and Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) Districts had destroyed "approximately 100 percent" of known insurgent bases, saying that there were no "known" insurgent bases or areas directly under insurgent control left in these districts.  In Macomia, Muidumbe, and Nangade, he said there will also "no formally known bases" of the insurgency, though he also said the fight against the militants was not over.  Chume went on to say that small groups of insurgents were continuing raids on villages, primarily targeting civilians, but said that the situation had improved significantly in the province since the end of June.  The commander said that military operations now are focused on cutting all insurgent "lines of communication" between their remaining hideouts and places where insurgents obtain food.  Chume also acknowledged that the fight against the insurgency could continue for "a year, two years, three years".

On 14 October, Mozambican Army Chief Cristovao Chume said that in a meeting this week between Mozambican, Rwandan, and SAMIM generals, the three militaries had decided to establish a new joint operations command in Maputo. Previously, Mozambique had coordinated operations with SAMIM and Rwandan forces, though there was reportedly no direct communication between the Rwandan and SAMIM commands.

The Southern African Development Community's (SADC) spokesman Mpho Molomo said on 14 October that a total of 20 insurgents and three SAMIM troops have been killed since the operations commenced in Cabo Delgado on 9 August.  This includes at least 18 militants killed in clashes in Nangade District in late September.

The Southern African Development Community's (SADC) special rep for the chair of the group's organ on politics, defense, and security cooperation Mpho Molomo said on 14 October that the SADC plans to keep its force in Cabo Delgado (SAMIM) in the province until the situation on the ground is "under control".  Molomo also said that SAMIM plans to deploy more troops as well to consolidate gains against the insurgents.  Molomo also indicated that insurgents were fleeing from their original zone of operation into Niassa, Nampula, islands in the Quirimbas Archipelago, and into Tanzania.

On 13 October, Rwandan refugees expressed concerns over “death squads from Kigali” targeting them in Mozambique following the recent killing of a Rwandan exile in Maputo. Five Rwandan refugees have been killed in the last five years in Mozambique; the Rwandan state is suspected in all of these incidents.

9 of 48 defendants were arrested on the evening of 13 October in connection with a corruption case at the Mozambican Consulate in Nelspruit. The defendants were indicted for allegedly committing crimes of embezzlement, corruption, abuse of office or function, forgery of documents, aided illegal immigration and association to delinquency.

The defendants were indicted for allegedly committing crimes of embezzlement, corruption, abuse of office or function, forgery of documents, aided illegal immigration and association to delinquency.

The Ministry of Health announced 17 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 14 October.  The highest number of new cases was recorded in Maputo City with seven cases, followed by  Nampula-three, Cabo Delgado- two, Manica-two and Inhambane with one case. For the third consecutive day, no COVID-related deaths were reported.

A short circuit incident was reported in Beira on 14 October affecting several residents and destroying their property. Several affected residents staged a demonstration to protest against the incident.
A group of residents in Beira staged a protest on 14 October over an alleged short circuit incident in the area. The cause of the short circuit was not disclosed.

On 14 October, the World Health Organization (WHO)  said that 6 out of 7 COVID-19 cases are not being detected in Africa. Eight million Covid cases have been recorded so far but the WHO now estimates that 59 million have been infected. It was reported that those with symptoms and with travel intentions were tested, while those asymptomatic individuals are not being detected resulting in more transmission. To address the concern, WHO is increasing community screening in eight countries aiming to reach seven million people with rapid testing in the next year. Involved countries are Burundi, Ivory Coast, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Guinea Bissau, Mozambique, Congo-Brazzaville, Senegal and Zambia. WHO added that there is a drop in recorded new cases recently, however,  there is concern that with low COVID-19 vaccination rates which remains a threat for many.

Mozambican Police exchanged gunfire with five suspected thieves during a chase in Chimoio in the late hours of 13 October. Two of the suspects were killed while the other three managed to escape. Two firearms were recovered from the suspects. Details preceding the shootout is not available at this time.

Former British Prime Minister Tony Blair warns on 14 October that Mozambique could be “condemned to poverty” if it cuts funding to gas projects due to environmental concerns. He added that if high-income countries try to limit development opportunities, African countries may opt to seek funding from other finance partners, who may neglect the impact of environmental damages.

On 14 October, key suspect and hidden debt defendant, Antonio Carlos do Rosario called for President Nyusi to be called to testify in the hidden debt case. He claimed that  it was Nyusi who suggested issuing an $850 million guarantee in favor of one of the companies in the project, Ematum. In addition, he said that Nyusi created the shareholder structure of Ematum in his presence and that of his co-defendant Gregorio Leao.

Customs officials intercepted and arrested a Johannesburg-bound man for illegal possession of abalone at the Lebombo port on 13 October. 21 boxes of concealed dry abalone valued at over R1 million were recovered from his vehicle.

Joint force patrols were reported in the Quionga area on 14 October.

SAMIM forces rescued 47 abducted individuals in the villages of Bilibiza and Namaluco, Quissanga district on 13 October. The victims, including children and the elderly had previously been abducted in the districts of Macomia and Mocimboa da Praia. No clashes occurred during the rescue as five insurgents who were tasked to guard the victims immediately fled upon sighting the security operatives.
