Security forces arrested a Guinean national in Nampula on 12 October in possession of a fake ID card.

Security forces arrested an individual in Maputo at about 12:00 on 14 October over alleged falsification of documents. He was captured while attempting to carry out a financial transaction using a false identity card at a commercial bank.

The secretary-general of RENAMO, Andre Magibire, while speaking in Gondola on 14 October, expressed concerns about the continued delay in payment of benefits to demobilized RENAMO militia members. These complaints have been recurring for several months. The Mozambican Government acknowledges the complaints while the European Union (EU), one of the funders, guarantees that new  support for those who have went through the DDR process is being prepared. Most former militia members who went through the DDR process received an initial subsidy to support them for a few months, but since then have not received any more of the stipend guaranteed in the DDR process.

On 14 October, the European Union (EU) and the Mozambican Government launched a 26 million-Euro project, Local Development for the Consolidation of Peace (Delpaz). The project aims to financing income-generating activities to improve the socio-economic opportunities in communities affected by conflict in Central Mozambique. Delpaz is financed by EU and supported by he United Nations Fund for Capital Development (UNCDF), the Austrian Development Agency and the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation.

On 14 October, the WHO released the Global Tuberculosis Report 2021.  The report indicated that Mozambique has seen a declining number of deaths from tuberculosis.  12,400 people died from TB in Moz in 2020; this is compared to TB deaths five years earlier which saw an average of 55,000 fatalities.
On 12 October, Superior Court of Appeal of Maputo annulled the verdict against former SERNIC official who was accused of embezzling more than 250 vehicles recovered by SERNIC from criminals.

SAMIM official Molumo stated on 14 October that insurgents have spread out south of Messalo River after recent joint operations. He also said that insurgents travelling into other areas of the province was what had triggered the extension of the SAMIM mission in Cabo Delgado.  He also said the SADC was appealing to support from the International Community to continue the SAMIM mission, calling for support "in every way possible" in order to defeat the insurgency in Northern Mozambique.

The Mozambican Government on 14 October announced the prohibition of fishing for shrimp and crab effective on 1 November until 31 March 2022. The prohibition of shrimp fishing covers the Sofala coast,  Maputo Bay and Limpopo Rive. Meanwhile, crab fishing is prohibited along the entire Mozambican coast from 01 November to 31 December.

52 companies in Tete province have resumed their activities following the relaxation of some Covid-19 prevention measures, as of 14 October. These companies had suspended their activities due to the negative impact of the pandemic. Meanwhile, 42 companies have shut down in the province, terminated contracts with workers and other companies due to the coronavirus.

On 15 October the EU training mission in Mozambique (EUTM Mozambique) was launched officially.  The EU said the mission is designed to provide military training to Mozambican security forces "to restore safety and security" in the country (specifically in Cabo Delgado) and to provide better protection to civilians.  Brig. Gen. Lemos Pires will command the mission, which is expected to reach "full operational capacity" by mid-December of this year.  140 soldiers from 27 different nations will participate in the mission; about half of these soldiers will be provided by Portugal, which already has troops in country providing training to Mozambican forces.  The EUTM troops will be divided between two training centers, one to provide training to marines, and one for commando training.  The mission is expected to last for two years.  Part of the training will include the formation of a roughly 2,000 troop Quick Reaction Force split into 11 companies.  The EUTM troops will not participate in combat missions.
Reports on 15 October indicate that the National Institute of Road Transport (INATRO) computer system is malfunctioning, resulting in thousands of people unable to get drivers' licenses.

The Ministry of Health announced 19 new COVID cases and one related death in Mozambique on 15 October.  The highest number of new cases was recorded in Cabo Delgado with six cases, followed by  Nampula-two cases. In the past 24 hours, 33 people have recovered while eight are hospitalized.

The funeral of former dissident leader, Mariano Nhongo, was held in Chirassicua, of Nhamatanda District Sofala province on 15 October. Nhongo's family was afraid to attend over being arrested or killed by security forces.

The USS Hershel “Woody” Williams floating naval base arrived off of Maputo coast on 15 October. US personnel will liaise with Mozambican military and government leaders, including a ship tour and capabilities demonstrations. This is the first port visit by a US. ship in nearly a decade which reflects the strong security cooperation relationship between the US and Mozambique.

A boat carrying four people sank in Zambezi River in the early hours of 11 October. Three of the passengers were safely rescued however, the other one is still missing and believed to have drowned. Efforts are ongoing to retrieve her body.

Unidentified gunmen abducted Jair Abdula, the son of a Mozambican businessman and one of the richest men in Mozambique Salimo Abdula on night of 14 October in South Africa along with 4 of his friends.  The kidnapping took place in Benoni, South Africa. As of 18 October, his four friends have been released though Abdula remains in custody.

Lutero Simango, the brother of former MDM leader is moving towards assuming the presidency of the party. This comes as Applications Commissions approved Simango's application to compete for the party's presidency. Notably, the application of Jose Domingo, another aspiring MDM leader, was put on hold after sending incomplete requirements to the commission.

On 15 October, the Defense and Security Forces (FDS) troops were accused of looting oranges and tangerines in the districts of Mocimboa da Praia, Muidumbe, and Macomia. The looted goods were allegedly later resold in Montepuez and Pemba.

On 13 October, SAMIM, Rwandan and Mozambican commanders met in Mocimboa da Praia town  and agreed to improve intelligence sharing  and coordinate operations against insurgents. Furthermore, they agreed to work together in helping displaced families to return to their homes and resettle. Rwandan and Mozambican troops are primarily operating in Mocimboa da Praia and the neighboring district of Palma while SAMIM troops with Mozambican forces are operating  in Macomia, Nangade, Muidumbe and Quissanga districts just across Messalo river.

A minibus was ambushed in Maumbica, Sanga district in Niassa on 7 October by unknown assailants.  It is unclear if local criminals or insurgents from Cabo Delgado carried out this attack; this incident is somewhat similar to other attacks that have taken place in Niassa intermittently this year, including a 20 August ambush of a vehicle between Luatize and Ligogo.

A Mozambican doctor's union had intended to carry out a demonstration on 16 October in Maputo calling for the release of a recently abducted doctor.  Mozambican police prevented this demonstration moments before it could begin.

Mozambican Police stopped a demonstration by the Association of Doctors and the Order of Doctors of Mozambique in Maputo City on 16 October. It was reported that officers banned the gathering five minutes before it was scheduled to commence. The protesting group earlier planned a peaceful demonstration in the city to demand the release of their abducted member, Dr. Basit Gani, who was abducted on 7 October. The group reportedly sent a letter to the Municipal Council of Maputo on 11 October, requesting authorization for a peaceful demonstration however, they received the response five minutes before the protest. Authorities state that the request for the peaceful demonstration was rejected as it allegedly poses a great risk in the spread of the COVID-19 virus.

A coordinator of World Wildlife Fund (WWF) Lara Muevas, was raped and murdered in her house in Dona Alice, Costa Do Sol, Maputo City on the night of 14 October. Her body was reportedly dumped into a drainage ditch. Three suspects were arrested over alleged connection to the crime.  Her boyfriend was later believed to have perpetrated the crime.

Security forces arrested three suspects on 17 October over alleged involvement in the murder of Lara Muevas, a coordinator of World Wildlife Fund (WWF) in her house in Dona Alice, Costa Do Sol, Maputo City. Reports indicate that the victim was raped and killed on 14 October before the suspects dumped her body into a drainage ditch. Investigation into the incident is still ongoing.

On 15 October, Zimbabwe and Mozambique agreed to improve security cooperation on issues including transnational border crimes, human trafficking and smuggling. Both countries agreed to enhance collaboration in intelligence sharing, training, patrol, and other bilateral activities. This follows the recently-concluded three-day Joint Permanent Commission on Defense and Security in Maputo.

The Ministry of Health announced 17 new COVID cases and no related death in Mozambique on 16 October.  The highest number of new cases was recorded in Maputo City with six cases, followed by  Cabo Delgado-three cases, Niassa-2, Inhambane-2, Gaza-2, Maputo Province-1, and Tete-1. In the past 24 hours,  two were hospitalized while three were discharged.

On 16 October, the Defense Attaché at the US Embassy in Maputo, Fergal O'Reilly, indicated that US is focusing on military training in order to support Mozambican forces fighting armed groups in Cabo Delgado. O'Reilly added that training programs will continue next year after the Special Operations Forces of the US have completed the second joint military training against the terrorist threat in Cabo Delgado in September.

SADC Joint forces raided several houses in coastal Macomia on 15 October.  It was not immediately clear where this raid took place. 15 AK-type weapons were recovered during the operations. Residents were interrogated over alleged connection to the seized weapons.

The Ministry of Health announced five new COVID cases and one related death in Mozambique on 17 October.  Maputo City and Nampula recorded two new cases each, followed by Gaza with one case. In the past 24 hours,  88 individuals fully recovered from the virus while two were hospitalized.

Mozambican Navy troops seized three vessels sailing in prohibited areas sailing between Mocimboa da Praia and Palma districts on 17 October. 150 suspects aboard the vessels were arrested during the operation.  The suspects were accused of providing supplies to insurgents in the province.

Bulk shipment of copper exported from Southern Africa resumed in Beira Port on 18 October after being constrained by the impact of Covid-19 on logistics networks in 2020.  The port of Beira is one of the primary export points for copper produced in inland countries in Southern Africa.

On 15 October, the Forest Carbon Partnership Facility, paid Mozambique USD 6.4 million for reducing carbon emissions by 1.28 million tons since 2019. The payment is the first of four under the country's Emission Reductions Payment Agreement (ERPA) with FCPF. The agreement incudes the pursuit of the Zambezia Integrated Landscape Management Programme (ZILMP) in strategizing deforestation reduction and forest degradation while implementing other measures.

Servers of Mozambique Airlines (LAM) suffered a ransomware attack on 14 October. The state-owned company’s servers, including e-mail and some customer services, were affected in the attack. IT staff of LAM reportedly were able to successfully thwart the attack. Currently, the company's platform is gradually replaced in a bid to ensure effective and safe resumption of activities.

Reports on 18 October indicate that Total Energies provided 16 pre-fab buildings to temporarily house nurses, teachers, police, and other government officials returning to the districts of Macomia and Quissanga.

Security forces arrested a 25-yr-old man in Maputo city on 18 October for allegedly stabbing his 44-yr-old girlfriend to death. Reports indicate that the attack happened on 15 October and the suspect hid the victim's body in a drainage ditch. The suspect denied involvement to the crime and claimed that the victim hit her head on the nightstand and died.

The suspect, who was arrested on 18 October, denied involvement to the crime and claimed that the victim hit her head on the nightstand and died.

Southern African Development Community's (SADC) force troops arrested five insurgents during operations in Cagembe/Panguia area along the Macomia/Quissanga border on 15 October. 12 firearms, 10 ammunition, 16 motorbikes and four briefcases were recovered during the operations.  SAMIM forces launched an operation in parts of coastal Macomia on 12 October.

Tanzanian and Lesotho troops of SAMIM on 09 October disarmed a 60mm mortar in Samora Machel village in Nangade during patrols in the area.  It was unclear when the mortar had been fired, though the mortar was discovered next to a house as residents returned to the area.  Clashes last occurred at Samora Machel, east of Litingina, in late August following a militant raid in the area.
Suspicious fires were reported on 18 October north of MDP town in the vicinity of Malinde town.  This could indicate clashes between security forces and insurgents or a new attack by insurgents.

Sources stated on 18 October that transportation between Mocimboa da Praia and Palma is possible as this 78km stretch of  road has been cleared of insurgents. Military units are currently able to move along roads between these two towns.

One source said Massianphumbi and the RMJ had vowed to "fight on" despite the death of Nhongo.  Massiaphumbi is most likely based in forest areas near Gorongosa in Sofala.

Officials announced that security forces seized at least 179kg of ephedrine in Cariaco area of Pemba, on or before Saturday, 16 October.  These drugs were incinerated later on 16 October.  22kg of cannabis were also seized in the area.

SADC forces have recently called on displaced and hiding locals to return to their villages in Nangade district. This comes after SAMIM troops recently killed a top insurgent leader in the district.
The third phase of the new vaccination campaign in Mozambique is set to start on 20 October. The third phase stated that they would continue to target individuals 30 years of age and older.

Around 20 Rapid Police Units reportedly assaulted several civilians and injured prosecutor Flavio Chongola in Chamanculo area, west Maputo City, at around 21:00 on 17 October. The victim claimed that the police conducted the assault on the civilians after claiming that the victim violated COVID precautions. Chongola responded to the assault leading to him being assaulted as well.

The US Naval Captain Chad Graham of the HSS Hershel "Woody" William stated that Mozambique and US could conduct a joint naval operation in the future on 15 October. This comes as a US navy vessel docked at Maputo.

Sources reported that the local population were suffering from hunger and malaria issues in Namoto and Rovuma areas of Palma district on 18 October.  Civilians have only recently began returning to these areas after having been displaced by insurgent attacks.

The Public Prosecutor’s Office announced that 34 pages of the indictment in the Hidden Debts Case relating to former Economic Intelligence of the State Information and Security Service director Antonio Carlos do Rosario were missing. The prosecution stated that the cases has around 20,000 pages.  Copies of the missing pages are being sought.
The Ministry of Health announced that 10 new COVID cases and a single related death were recorded in Mozambique on 18 October. This brings the total cases to 151,112.

Sources stated that around 2000 former RENAMO guerillas in Central Mozambique who finished the DDR process have still not been provided their subsidies as of 17 October. RENAMO secretary Andre Magibire stated that the individuals who finished the DDR process hope this issue will be resolved in the near future.  The former guerillas were also lacking food supplies due to the subsidies.
The local community in Capanga area of Tete province refused to resettle to the new camps. The local community was intended to be moved as part of Benga Coal Mine operations.
Three fugitives sentenced for narcotic charges broke out jail in Quelimane at around 15:00 on 17 October.  The three as of 18 October were reported to be still at large.

The Ministry of Economy and Finance forecasted growth by 2022 in Mozambique. The areas where growth was expected were agriculture, fishing, energy, and the mining industry. The projected GDP growth for next year is predicted to be 2.9 percent. This comes as the economy was recovering from the pandemic with -1.3% percent growth in 2020 and 1.5 % in 2021.

Sources stated that no new COVID admissions were recorded in the past two weeks at Polana Canico hospital in Maputo as of 16 October. Hospital employees have recently been allowed not to wear personal protective equipment due to absence of admissions.
Several fires broke out in Mbau on the evening of 9 October. This could indicate clashes between security forces and insurgents or a new attack by insurgents.
A suspicious fire was reported within Namedi village, north of MDP on 16 October.  This could indicate clashes between security forces and insurgents or a new attack by insurgents.
A suspicious fire was reported near Nsangue village, north of MDP on 16 October.  This could indicate clashes between security forces and insurgents or a new attack by insurgents.

The Spanish government announced that they would provide 47 million EUR to Mozambique for development projects on 19 October. The 15 million EUR will be for Cabo Delgado and another 11 million EUR for the ongoing projects in the provinces.

Credit Suisse Group AG on the evening of 19 October was announced to have agreed to plead guilty to one count of criminal conspiracy to commit wire fraud and agreed to pay $547 million to UK and US authorities in a coordinate resolution over the company's role in Mozambique's Hidden Debts (HD) Scandal.   The firm admitted to having defrauded investors in the financing of a $850 million loan as part of the HD case.  Several ex-Credit Suisse Bankers also received up to $50 million in kickbacks for their role in providing these loans, out of $200 million in kickbacks received by all those who participated in the scandal.

Media reports indicate that Quelimane Hospital is in poor condition and lacks medical equipment and healthcare professionals. Locals stated that they only would admit themselves to the hospital if the were in critical condition. The hospital has denied these reports, saying misinformation is being spread about the facility.
The Ministry of Health announced 24 new COVID cases and no new COVID deaths in Mozambique on 19 October. This comes as 109 new recoveries were reported.

The Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MTC) stated that they have created a team to minimize the traffic congestion at Ressano Garcia.  Long traffic jams at this border post are common, and have occurred as well in recent days.

The National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD) announced that they created a contingency plan with a budget of 10.6 billion meticais for the rainy season. The government however only has 3.3 billion meticais for this plan, and the government is seeking international funding to support the rest of this plan.  The contingency plan would support 1.5 million people during the coming rainy season.

The South African President Ramaphosa on 19 October said that Southern African nationals would "come after" the insurgency in Cabo Delgado, and would "make sure that Mozambique becomes a country where you will not spread violence".  Ramaphosa was speaking at a memorial event for former Mozambican President Samora Machel.

Health authorities announced that individuals over 30, pregnant, and lactating mothers would be covered by current vaccination campaign in Mozambique on 20 October. The World Health Organization stated that both pregnant and lactating women would be added to the vaccination groups due to the new research.

The Ministry of Health announced that the third COVID vaccination phase intended to reach a 7 million vaccinated individuals in Mozambique by March 2022. The third phase was to include civilians from 30-49 in urban areas. The ministry of stated that they would use available J&J vaccines for this vaccination wave.

The Ministry of Health announced that they intend to vaccinate around 200,724 individuals during the third vaccination phase in Maputo City. The vaccination phase in the city was expected to finish by 3 November.

The Business Community of Portuguese Speaking Countries demanded Mozambican government increase security measures to stop the recent kidnappings in a 19 October  The organization has called security authorities to resolve kidnapping cases, saying security was an "absolutely fundamental asset of any nation".

Defendant lawyer Alexandre Chivale was on 19 October dismissed from the Hidden Debts Case over his work for the State Information and Security Service, which constitutes a conflict of interest. The Public Ministry magistrate also stated that Chivale was a shareholder of the real estate company linked with Privinvest payments, which were suspected to be used for money laundering.

A construction team uncovered a remnant explosive during excavating a private property in George Dimitrovi/Benfica in Maputo City on 19 October. Police responded to the area after being notified of the remnant explosive and stated that EOD units would remove the explosive - though the explosive was not ultimately cleared until 25 October.

Two sources stated on 20 October that a naval vessel transporting 30 IDPs from Matemo Island bound for Palma has been missing since 27 September.  The vessel was reported not to have notified security forces of their departure as they were traveling through a prohibited zone. It is not clear if this vessel sank, was intercepted by security forces, or potentially attacked by insurgents.
SAMIM forces arrested at least 40 individuals on 15 October in the Mucojo area suspected to be linked to the insurgency.  15 firearms were also seized in this operation.
On 16 October, locals stated that suspicious armed individuals were seen in Nteleonde in Montepuez District.  Locals feared these individuals were insurgents, though this was not confirmed.

Around 30,000 IDPs have reportedly to their residences throughout Palma District as of 19 October.  Many of those returnees are from Quitunda, though some returnees have come from as far away as Pemba amid the ongoing improvement of security in the district.

The Mozambican military has indicated that it had 10,000 troops in Cabo Delgado, though more accurate estimates indicate there are probably about 4,000 Mozambican troops in the province, along with about 2,000 Rwandan soldiers, and just under 1,000 SAMIM troops.

Media reports late on 20 October reported that Exxon Mobil's board was considering whether or not to continue the Rovuma LNG Project in Mozambique, among other prospective company projects in different areas of the world.  Board members were reported to have "expressed concern" regarding the company's paused Rovuma LNG Project in Cabo Delgado.  No final investment decision (FDI) has been made on this project, and this FID has been delayed several times.  Prospective carbon emissions of this project and other projects are being analyzed as Exxon attempts to lower its own carbon footprint over the coming years.

Quelimane doctors stated that IDP camps for IDPs displaced by Cyclone Idai are high-risk areas for possible respiratory disease in Namitangurine, Dhugudiua, and Furquilha. Disease, including malaria, is common in these camps.

Quelimane doctors stated that IDP camps for IDPs displaced by Cyclone Idai are high-risk areas for possible respiratory disease in Namitangurine, Dhugudiua, and Furquilha. Disease, including malaria, is common in these camps.

Quelimane doctors stated that IDP camps for IDPs displaced by Cyclone Idai are high-risk areas for possible respiratory disease in Namitangurine, Dhugudiua, and Furquilha. Disease, including malaria, is common in these camps.

The Mozambique government has included pregnant and lactating women for vaccinations as part of the third vaccination phase in the country on 18 October. The current vaccination campaign also includes individuals above 30 years old. The inclusion of pregnant and lactating women came after the WHO announced that research was conducted that allows them to take the vaccine.
Credit Suisse announced that they would forgive a $200 million debt by the Mozambique government as part of settlement with US and UK on 19 October.
On 19 October, The Russian bank VTB agreed to pay $6 million to US Security and Exchange Commission for its involvement in the Hidden Debts case.
Police arrested a murder suspect after killing his wife in Dondo in the afternoon of 20 October. The suspect conducted the murder after an argument with his wife.
Police arrested a murder suspect after killing his wife in Dondo in the afternoon of 20 October. The suspect conducted the murder after an argument with his wife.

The Swedish Regulator Finma has restricted Credit Suisse's ability to create new loans to countries with a high-risk of corruption and that are financially weak as part of a recent settlement with Mozambique. Finma will be independently reviewing Credit Suisse's bank transactions as well.

Sources stated that the first day of the third phase of vaccinations have seen a low turnout in Maputo City on 20 October. This comes as 200,700 vaccinations were expected to be conducted in the city. The vaccination also reportedly started an hour late as the schedule was set to start at 08:00.

The Ministry of Health announced that 21 new COVID cases were recorded in Mozambique on 20 October. This comes as no COVID deaths were noted for within the 48 hours. Maputo city recorded 10 of the new cases.
RENAMO MPs in parliament on 20 October called for talks with Cabo Delgado insurgents, saying that as a matter of urgency, the government should attempt to open talks with the militants.

Sources stated that around 17,000 cancer deaths were confirmed in Mozambique during 2020.  Breast and Cervical cancer were the most common forms of the disease in the country.  During the year, about 25,000 people in Mozambique were diagnosed with cancer.

The MDM party called for President Nyusi to explain his involvement with the Hidden Debts case. MDM stated that the president should clarify his links to the scandal as several defendants have alleged Nyusi and former President Guebuza were aware of and participated in the scheme.

Security forces arrested 60 individuals who were traveling near the coast of Matemo Island on 10 October. The individuals were traveling from Matemo to Palma. The detainees were later moved and held in Ibo.  These individuals were reportedly arrested for not seeking security force permission to sail in this restricted area.
Police arrested a local village chief in Matemo for allowing individuals to travel between Palma and Matemo Island on 10 October.

Mozambican military officers speaking to IDPs in Quitunda in a 16 October meeting called on locals to join the security forces, saying that the main reason for poor relations between the security forces and the local population was that the military was primarily commanded by Southern Mozambican officers, many of whom do not even speak the same languages as local Cabo Delgado residents.
The Mozambican police have reportedly has recruited as many as around 5,000 people recently into the police force.  A majority of the recruited youths, over 70%, were mostly IDPs.

On 16 October, the Mozambican and Rwandan forces conducted a meeting with the local community in Quitunda. The meeting called for the cooperation of the locals with security forces in order to identify insurgents in Palma District and beyond.

The Mozambican security forces attempted to conduct a meeting with the local villagers in Nguida of Macomia district on 13 October.  Local residents reportedly fled from security forces, fearing they would be targeted by them.  Many locals in this area prefer working with pro-government militias rather than the military.

Locals have recently reported that insurgents based along the Messalo River are struggling to feed themselves, and that militants food supplies have been disrupted as they have been driven away from farmland by recent joint forces operations.  This has forced insurgents to move around more frequently, searching for food supplies.

Groups of insurgents along the Messalo River are reported to be keeping hostages in order to use them as human shields as militants are forced to move into new areas, having been driven out of their previous territory by joint forces offensives.
The Mozambican government received a batch 149,760 doses of COVID vaccines from Belgium on 20 October as part of the COVAX initiative.
The Norwegian government has donated 179,800 doses of COVID vaccines to Mozambique on 20 October as part of the COVAX initiative.

USAID announced that they launched three programs in Cabo Delgado to support and support development of local youth on 20 October. Two projects will create training and work opportunities in order to develop skills needed for entrepreneurship and employment.  The third project will help develop leadership and vocational skills for youths between 15-29 in Cabo Delgado.

The National Agency for the Control of Environmental Quality has fined 160 forestry companies in Sofala for “various irregularities” so far this year.  The most common irregularities found by the agency was the illegal logging. The fines for the companies reached around 13 million meticais.

A union of university lecturers raised concerns over low salaries in Mozambique on 20 October. The university professors stated that their salaries were low in comparison with public educators, doctors, and magistrates.  These lecturers on 18 October submitted a complaint to the government appealing for a higher salary.

Sources stated that the government has not yet announced further details regarding the closure of 18 beaches in Mozambique which was ordered on 06 October in order to curb the spread of COVID. The ban is set to expire on by 22 October. The beaches covered by the closure are as follows: Katembe and Costa do Sol of Maputo City; Ponta D'Ouro and Macaneta of Maputo province; Bilene and Xai-Xai of Gaza; Barra, Tofo and Guinjata of Inhambane; Estoril, Ponta Gêa and Macuti of Sofala; Zalala of Zambezia; Fernão Veloso of Nampula; and Wimbe, Marringanhe, Sagal and Inos of Cabo Delgado.

On 21 October, fuel prices rose across Mozambique after an adjustment made by the Energy Regulatory Authority due to the rise in the price of a barrel of crude oil.  Cooking gas rose by 22% from 58.18 meticais to 71.02 meticais per kg.  Petrol prices rose by 10%, from 62.5 meticais to 69.04 meticais; diesel prices rose from 57.45 mets to 61.71 mets. Vehicle natural gas rose 9% from 30 mets to 32.69 mets.  The last price adjustment made by the regulatory authority took place in November 2020.  Since 21 October 2020, the price of a barrel of Brent Crude has risen 102%.
Police arrested three for the murder of an albino child in Mecuburi, northwest of Nampula, on 18 October. The suspects intended to sell the victims body parts for 8 million meticais.
Three armed men abducted and murdered an albino child in Mecuburi on 7 October. The suspects intended to sell the body parts of the victim.
Police announced that an albino Mozambican national was murdered in Monapo on 7 October.  No further details regarding this case are currently available.

The Russian bank VTB indicated on 21 October that it is still seeking a settlement of Mozambique's $817 million debt to the bank. The Russian bank previously agreed to pay $6 million to the US Securities Commission  for its role in the Hidden Debts case.

The Mozambican regulatory authority warned on 20 October that due to increasing crude oil prices, the country could see another increase in oil based product prices again in the near future.  The country from 20 October had fuel for the next 22 days; prices will be reevaluated when the next import shipments arrive.

A new employment program was launched by the government on 21 October.  President Nyusi says he wants to see the unemployment rate lowered nationally to 11% by 2035 from the 17% rate seen in 2020.  He also said the initiative is investing $27.5 million, and aims to create 50,000 jobs in 5 years.  The new program will provide training and guidance to the unemployed, specifically targeting youths.

Sources stated police were harassing locals who even are near beach in Mozambique on 21 October. A pregnant women reported that she and her and her husband while sitting in their car outside a Maputo beach were approached by police were the guns drawn and told that they were violating a government decree closing beaches to attempt to thwart the spread of COVID.

The Ministry of Health announced 17 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 21 October.  This comes as now new COVID fatalities were reported for the past 72 hours. The total COVID cases were at 151,174, with total recoveries at 148,611.

A Mozambican NGO , the Budget Monitoring Forum, called on 21 October for Credit Suisse to cancel all the debt linked with the Hidden Debts trial, amounting to $2 billion. This came after Credit Suisse in a deal with US and UK authorities agreed to cancel $200  million of this debt.  Mozambique's top court previously declared the totality of this debt "null and void", and the Mozambican government has not given any indication that it intends to pay this debt.

The Hidden Debt judge has issued a 1 week suspension of the trial which is set to resume by 28 October. The suspension was designed to allow Lawyer Isalcio Mahanjane to catch up and familiarize himself with the ongoing trial.

Reports on 19 October indicated Pemba is unable to accommodate all the IDPs who in the past 3 years have been forced to flee to the city by the ongoing insurgency.  The city's population during that time has doubled from 200,000 to 400,000.  IDPs in the city report not getting enough food aid.

Exxon in a statement on 21 Oct clarified that reports that it was considering scrapping its Mozambican operations were "wrong" but did not provide any further clarification.  Exxon's $30 billion Rovuma LNG Project has not yet seen a final investment decision which has been postponed by the company several times over security issues in Cabo Delgado.

Security forces detained two traders suspected to be working for insurgents were detained while traveling on a boat from Pemba to Palma on 14 October. The suspects, who were from Mueda, were found transporting goods worth around 400,000 meticais. The traders claimed that they were intending to sell the goods at the market in Palma.  Authorities however believe the two were taking goods to insurgents in Palma.
Locals as of 21 October in the Eduardo Mondlane village area of Mueda town say they believe insurgents are living among IDPs in the area having recently infiltrated into the district.

column4: Electricidade Mozambique dismantled a group illegally stealing electricity in Matola, west of Maputo City, on 21 October.

Locals in Maputo and Matola areas stated that the increase in fuel prices on 21 October were “unbearable”. The locals stated that with the price increase also affected gas cylinders and the new prices were not previously announced.

The Chinese government announced on 21 October a donation of food to displaced individuals and locals affected by the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. The donation was of 200 tons of rice, 300 tons of corn flour, and 24,000 liters of cooking oil.
IDPs called for land plots to be able to farm in Nangua, Metuge on 21 October. The IDPs stated that conditions in IDP camps are poor and not enough food aid is provided in these camps.

The relatives of former President Samora Machel called for a new investigation regarding the plane crash that killed the former president and 34 other people, saying the cause of the accident was still "unknown".  Machel's plan crashed in October of 1986 along the South African/Mozambican border; many have alleged the crash was not an accident.
The National Migration Service (Senami) arrested 53 illegal immigrants in Tete on 18 October. The illegal immigrants were 50 Malawian nationals and 3 Ethiopian nationals.

Locals stated on 20 October that the remnant explosive found in George Dimitorv/Beneifica has not been cleared by security forces yet. The explosive was previously found during an excavation on a private land and security forces responded to the area.

The UNHCR stated that $114 million is required in order for the aid agency to continue activities in assisting IDPs in Cabo Delgado. This comes as the organization managed to obtain only 55% of the required 254 million USD to assist the IDPs.

In a 20 October speech, FRELIMO MP Sergio Pantie said that insurgents in Cabo Delgado are “being put out of combat” as the security situation is improving.  FRELIMO also congratulated the security forces in the continued efforts in restoring security in the province.

The Government expects around $34.52 million of revenue from the production and export of LNG in 2022 from Area 4 of the Rovuma Basin, a project operated by ENI and partners.  This would be the first LNG revenue produced in Cabo Delgado.

The "Max Love" case has begun 8 years after a policeman shot dead a civilian in Quelimane in front of the governor's palace during a celebration of the victory of an MDM candidate in the race for the presidency of the Municipal Council of Quelimane.  The policeman is being tried in absentia

Two sources indicated that a group of insurgents had launched a raid in Namacande, the Muidumbe District capital, within the last 48 hours.  One source said the attack took place on 20 October, while the second source said the attack had occurred on Thursday, 21 October.  Militants entered the town and vandalized an local government administrative building.  Militants then fled the village.  No casualties were reported in this attack.    Other sources later reported that it was unclear if this attack had occurred, and this incident is currently regarded as unconfirmed.

A fire broke out and  burned down a residence in Mocone, Nacala on the night of 22 October. 13 residents managed to escape. No casualties were reported. The fire was suspected to have started due to an electrical short circuit.

RENAMO spokesman Jose Manteigas on 22 October strongly criticized rise in fuel prices announced during the week by the Energy Regulatory Authority. RENAMO’s spokesman Manteigas also said the fuel increase comes just after the national minimum wage was increased by 5%, effectively wiping out any wage gains made by regular Mozambicans.  He also said the government should shoulder the increase in fuel prices with national financial reserves.

A freight train derailed in the Murissa area of Cuamba district in Niassa on the afternoon of Friday, 22 October.  At least two children were killed during the incident and 7 others injured. The train reportedly belonged to Nacala logistics which was a with the Vale mining company in the area.
The Ministry of Health announced 21 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 22 October. The daily recoveries were recorded at 32. This brings the total recoveries at 148,643.

President Nyusi on 22 October said his government was dedicated to "dismantling" kidnap gangs operating in the country, calling for security force agencies to work together to identify and dismantle kidnap gangs.  This comes after two high profile kidnappings in early October in Maputo City, and after the recent abduction in South Africa of the son of one of Mozmabique's richest men.
Tanzanian security forces on 21 October reportedly rescued multiple hostages taken by insurgents in the Kilimahewa area, just across the Rovuma River from Cabo Delgado.  No clashes were reported.
Insurgents Over the night of 20-21 October kidnapped several people from the village of Kilimahewa in Tanzania, just across the Rovuma River from Mozambique

Over the night of 20-21 October, a group of insurgents attacked the village of Kilimahewa in Tanzania, just north of the Rovuma River, between Michenjele and Mihambwe villages.  Insurgents set fire to a cashew nut warehouse, and abducted several civilians, reportedly remaining in the area for some hours after the initial attack.  Tanzanian security forces based nearby launched an operation and were able to free all hostages taken later on 21 October; militants were presumed to have fled at the approach of the security forces.  No casualties have so far been reported.  It is assumed, though not confirmed, that the militants had been based just across the river in either Palma or Nangade District, and were not based in Tanzania.
The Police conducted an ordinance clearing operation, removing a grenade from a playground in Magige area Gurue district on 16 October. The grenade was found by the children.

Security forces arrested a SERNIC officer for soliciting bribes in Nampula at around 14:00 on 14 October. The suspect was found receiving 22,500 meticais from a civilian as a bribe to meet with detainees at a police station.

Security forces arrested a SERNIC officer for soliciting bribes in Nampula at around 14:00 on 14 October. The suspect was found receiving 22,500 meticais from a civilian as a bribe to meet with detainees at a police station.

The Ministry of Health announced 25 new COVID cases and one related death in Mozambique on 23 October.  Maputo City recorded highest with 13 new cases each, followed by Gaza with four cases. In the past 24 hours,  Two individuals fully recovered from the virus while three were hospitalized.

President Nyusi on Sunday evening, 24 October, announced that some COVID restrictions would be eased as COVID infections rates have dropped to some of their lowest levels of the pandemic.  Other measures will remain in place for the time being.  This decree will remain in place until 20 December, the longest any such update on COVID restrictions will have remained in place.  Some of these measures include: nationwide curfew in Mozambique's main cities has been adjusted to 0000 - 0400hrs; this curfew had previously started every night from 2300hrs; All beaches that were again closed in early October will remain closed; .  Other directives had been effective for 30-40 days; Bars are allowed to operate from 0900hrs to 2100hrs, not exceeding 20% capacity; Social events held indoors may include up to 50 people, up from 30; Places of worship can allow 100 people per service, up from 50; Funerals may have up to 50 people in attendance, up from 20; Shopping centers can operate from 0900hrs to 2000hrs Monday to Saturday, and 0900hrs to 1800hrs on Sundays and holidays
President Nyusi,  on Sunday evening, 24 October, warned of the threat of a fourth wave in the country, saying civilians should participate in the ongoing COVID vaccination campaign.

1 person was killed and 3 injured in a bomb attack at a popular bar in Kampala, the capital of Uganda, on the late hours of 23 October. Reports indicate that the bombers, who disguised as customers, planted the explosives under a table. Ugandan police cordoned off the area following the explosion. ISCAP later claimed responsibility of the attack and said that they targeted a gathering of “members and spies of the Crusader Ugandan government”. This is the second ISCAP bombing claimed in Kampala this month after the group claimed an attack on 08 October on a Kampala police station; this is also the second ever ISCAP claimed attack in Uganda.  ISCAP claims franchises in the DRC and Mozambique, and the expansion of attacks into Uganda also indicates a growing threat of new linkages between the DRC and Mozambique franchises of ISCAP.

On 24 October, the National Institute of Meteorology said that Central Mozambique will experience more intense rains during the rainy season than the rest of the country. This comes after the cyclones/tropical storms of Chalane, Eloise, and Guambe impacted the country last year.  Cyclones Idai and Kenneth in 2019 killed 714 people in the country, the country's deadliest ever cyclone season; this included hundreds of deaths in Central Mozambique.

On 24 October, the Committee of the Buzi and Pungue River Basins warned  eight districts in Sofala and Manica Provinces are at high risk of flooding in the comings months. Flooding could affect 1,240,000 people in the districts of Buzi, Beira, Dondo, Nhamatanda, Chibabava, Gorongosa, in Sofala, and Mossurize and Sussundega, in Manica province. Authorities stated that efforts are ongoing to reduce the impact of the heavy rains.

Flooding could affect 1,240,000 people in the districts of Buzi, Beira, Dondo, Nhamatanda, Chibabava, Gorongosa, in Sofala, and Mossurize and Sussundega, in Manica province. Authorities stated that efforts are ongoing to reduce the impact of the heavy rains.

Insurgents beheaded two people on 22 October in Lumuamua village, just south of Mucojo, while fetching water from Matemo Islands. Insurgents were reportedly dressed in military uniforms.  Three peoople escaped this attack.
Insurgents beheaded two people on 22 October in Pankoma, Mucojo, while fetching water from Matemo Islands.

Authorities held a meeting with religious leaders representing Islamic, Hindu, Bahai and Christian communities in Maputo city on 24 October to urge the mobilization of people to join the massive vaccination campaign against COVID-19 in Maputo City. The campaign is scheduled to run from 30 October to  3 November. The Health Directorate of the city decided to involve religious leaders to use their influence in urging the public to adhere to the inoculation of the COVID-19 vaccine.

Reports on 25 October indicate that the profits of Mozambican Hydrocarbon Company (CMH) sharply declined by 54% in 2021. The company had a net income of USD11.4 million in the fiscal year that ended in June 2021, compared to 2020 fiscal year results, which were USD24.7 million. Aside form the effects of COVID-19 pandemic, the decline in revenue resulted from the production and sale of 179.35 million gigajoules of natural and condensed gas against the 176.19 million gigajoules sold in the year prior.

The Electricity de Mozambique (EDM) announced the connection of Mazucane, in Chongoene district, to the national grid on 21 October. Mazucane is the 37th out of 45 administrative posts to be connected by the end of 2024. This is part of the 'Energy for All' program of the government which aims to provide electricity in all regions of the country, especially in rural areas.

UNHCR on 22 October indicated that there has been a "slight increase" recently of people fleeing their homes due to the insurgency in Cabo Delgado, with about 13,000 people displaced in recent months.  There are now estimated to be 745,000 IDPs in Cabo Delgado, vs 732,000 IDPs as of APril 2021.  The UNHCR also indicated that security conditions have been improved recently in Palma District, and that teams were able to conduct humanitarian activity in Afungi, Quitunda, and Quionga without military escorts.  UNHCR also said IDPs should only return to their homes when "all security conditions are met".  Finally, the organization said that it has only received 65% of the funds needed to operate throughout this year, forcing cutbacks in aid provided.

Security forces cleared a left over explosive device in the area of George Dmitrov/Benfica, Maputo City on 25 October. It took EOD units six days before the explosive was removed. The incident came barely a week after construction team uncovered a remnant explosive during excavating a private property in the area on 19 October.

The Ministry of Health announced five new COVID cases in Mozambique on 24 October.  All new cases were recorded in Zambezia province- three in Quelimane, one in Ile and one in Gurue. In the past 24 hours, no related deaths were recorded while three were hospitalized.
Security forces arrested two employees of the Municipal Council of Ilha de Mozambique on 18 October for allegedly diverting 3,461,023 meticais government funds to their own account.

Kenyan President Uhuru Kenyatta met with his Malawian counterpart, Lazarus Chakwera in Kenya on 23 October to discuss bilateral affairs and security situation in Cabo Delgado, Mozambique. Kenya commended and supports SADC in fighting the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

The President of the Association of Rwandan Refugees in Mozambique Cleophas Habiyareme said on 25 October that the Rwandan Embassy in Maputo City served as a "kind of operational center" directing operations to target Rwandan exiles in Mozambique.

Insurgents beheaded three people, including a child  in Nagulue, Mucojo in an attack that occurred between 21-23 October.  2 other attacks were carried out in nearby villages during this time which left at least 4 others dead.  Other sources later reported that the three people killed were discovered in advanced stages of decomposition, and had been killed some time ago.

On 25 October, World Bank’s country director, Idah Pswarayi-Riddihough, announced plans to disburse $100 million for the Cabo Delgado Reconstruction Plan (PRCD). The fund will likely to be disbursed by January 2022. The PRCD includes activities such as humanitarian assistance, restoration of destroyed infrastructures and resumption of financial and economic actions.

The water supply in Muidumbe is set to be restored on Wednesday, 27 October, after almost a year of hiatus. Parts of the Muidumbe distribution system in Ntchinga, were previously damaged during insurgent attacks.

On 25 October, an administrative Court annulled the appointment of the chief of the cabinet of the Governor of Sofala Province, Inacio Chissumba, the Director of Education, Tomas Viagueiro, Director of the Environment, Territorial Development, Helder Guandiane. The decision was made after the court determined the appointed officials did not have the proper qualifications to fill these positions.
On 25 October, the Mozambican Government forecasted that the country's economy will grow 2.9percent in 2022.

Insurgents launched an attack in Sengele village, Mtwara province, Tanzania, in northern Mozambique on 18 October. Property damage reported, however, casualty figures are still unknown. This report is currently unconfirmed.  On 20-21 October, militants attacked Kilimahewa village, kidnapping several people.

A group of at least 10 insurgents launched an attack in the community of Chitama, Nangade on 24 October. Three people, including a community leader and two local force officers, were killed in the attack.  Women were also abducted in the attack; some of those abducted were later released.  Another source later reported 4 people killed.

Due to an insurgent attack in the Chitama area, traffic was disrupted between Nangade and Mueda on Monday as people feared new militant attacks in the area.  By midday on 25 October, traffic had resumed.

Another source later reported 4 people killed.

The Ministry of Health announced one new COVID case in Mozambique on 25 October.  The new case was recorded in Nampula province. In the past 24 hours, no related deaths and no new hospital admission were recorded while six people have recovered from the virus.

Mozambican police detained and assaulted Armando Nenane, a reporter with the privately owned Imprensa Paralegal news agency, in Maputo City around 10:30 on 2 October. After he was released form detention at Ninth Police Station, he went ahead to cover the accident, however, police officers detained him again. On 19 October, Maputo police commandant Fabiao Nhancololo said that he was not aware of the incident and investigation into the incident is underway.

On 25 October, the Mozambican government said that US oil company, Exxon, will remain active in the country and engaged in its Rovuma LNG Project. The statement came after recent reports that suggested that the company might scrap the natural gas projects in northern part of the country. Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy, Max Tonela added that Exxon representatives are scheduled to visit Maputo in early November to assess the situation in relation to projects in the country.  No FID has been made by Exxon on this project.

On the evening of 25 October, a suicide bomber detonated an explosive vest inside a bus near Kampala, Uganda.  The explosion killed the bomber and injured several passengers. Police authorities claimed that the bomber was part of the wanted list members of ADF. ISCAP later claimed responsibility for this attack.  This is the third bombing claimed by ISCAP this month in Kampala, the Ugandan capital, and demonstrates an expansion of activity by ISCAP's DRC franchise, and could indicate a greater possibility of new opportunities for linkages between ISCAP in Cabo Delgado and ISCAP in the DRC and Uganda.

On the afternoon of 26 October, a minor collision was reported on a runway between an LAM plane and a military aircraft (unconfirmed reports said this was a Botswanan military plane) at the Pemba Airport, with both aircraft sustaining minor damage.  No injuries were reported as part of this accident.

Clashes between SAMIM and Mozambican troops on one side and insurgents on the other were reported on the morning of 26 October along the South Bank of the Messalo River, close to the mouth of the river, north of Quiterajo.  At least 10 insurgents were captured, all reportedly from Macomia.  A local media outlet said that among those captured was a man, Adinane Fahamo, identified as one of the group's best known recruiters in Macomia District.  Fahamo is reportedly one of several well-known militants from Ilala village, north of Mucojo.  Some of those captured were regularly active in the Pangane area.

At least 10 insurgents were captured, all reportedly from Macomia.  Another source later reported 7 insurgents captured in this operation.  A local media outlet said that among those captured was a man, Adinane Fahamo, identified as one of the group's best known recruiters in Macomia District. On 25 October, sources stated that suspected insurgent movements were seen by civilians in the V Congresso village area in Nangade District.
The Ministry of Health announced 17 new COVID cases and 1 related death occurred in Mozambique on 26 October. This comes as 313 new daily recoveries were recorded.

The Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy, Max Tonela announced on 25 October that the increase in fuel prices were a government response to prevent the collapse of oil supply. Tonela added that the importers and distributors were experiencing continued losses in the sector. The price increase also considered the change in exchange rates and the international price of fuel.  This statement was made in response to growing complaints regarding the price of fuel.

The Attorney General has launched an investigation for criminal activities conducted by lawyer Alexandre Chivale on 26 October. Chivale was recently dismissed from the defense of the Hidden Debts case for his connections to companies that reportedly received money as part of the Hidden Debts scandal.  He is being investigated on suspicious of money laundering.

Officials announced that seven individuals have died in crocodile attacks along the Zambezi river in Mutarara district since the start of 2021. The attacks took place as locals went to the river to collect water.

Road and Project Official Andre Vilanculos stated that the Buzi bridge construction is almost complete and is expected to finish by December 2021. This comes as the last 23 pillars were placed and only four were remaining. The Buzi bridge was to run for 134km and has been under construction since 2018.  Cyclones affecting Central Mozambique have slowed this project in recent years.

Union transportation employees have called for an increase in transport fares as of 26 October. This comes as the Mozambican Federation of Road Transport Associations (FEMATRO) has not revised the prices of the transportation for the past six years, and comes after a recent increase in fuel costs announced by a national regulatory board.
Transport unions in Nampula on 26 October were reported to have threatened to increase prices in response to the recent nationwide fuel price increase.
The Beluluane Gas Company LNG import terminal project has been completed in Matola and is expected to fully deliver LNG by 2024.

The Mozambican government approved the contingency plan for 2021-2022 rainy season during the 37th session of the Council of Minister in Maputo on 26 October. The plan has budgeted 10 billion meticais to assist individuals affected the expected rainy season during the last quarter of 2021 and early 2022. The government still requires 7 billion meticas to fully implement the plan.
Security forces arrested two murder suspects in Chimoio on 25 October. The suspects were involved with a robbery in which a soldier was murdered in the city on 23 October.
Two armed men stabbed a soldier to death during a robbery at a residence in Chimoio on 23 October.

Attorney General Adamo conducted a meeting with civil society organizations guaranteeing an investigation regarding the abuses of security forces in Cabo Delgado on 25 October. The civil society organizations stated that corruption, diversion of humanitarian aid, and mishandling of identification for IDPs are their main concerns.

The National Institute of Statistics (INE) stated that 38% of children below five years old were experiencing chronic malnutrition in Mozambique. 16.5% were experiencing severe malnutrition. The World Health Organization stated that the malnutrition levels in the countries are still “very high” even with the reduce in overall cases.  The malnutrition in rural areas remain very high, while urban malnutrition is rated as moderate.  The Central and Northern Provinces of the Country see the highest rates of malnutrition.

The World Food Program is reported to be preparing a “mega operation” to assist IDPs including those displaced in the islands and inland areas of Cabo Delgado province. The organization is gathering aid and food to supply the IDPs via boats and trucks. The UN program also intends to use planes and helicopters to reach the islands. WFP stated that they intended to assist around 300,000 IDPs in October.  The organization needs about $4.7 million per month to feed the most vulnerable IDPs in Cabo Delgado.  200,000 people were given food aid last month by the WFP.

The National Institute of Meteorology announced that around rainfall has flooded several neighborhoods in Maputo city on 26 October. Some of the areas affected were Costa do Sol neighborhood, Magoanine district,  Albasine district, and Rua da Beira.

The World Food Program on 25 October indicated that it was currently only able to provide half rations to 925,000 individuals in Mozambique due to a lack of resources. WFP stated that they are now implementing a vulnerability exercise for IDPs to determine allocation of food supplies.
A eight vehicles collided with each other on Namaacha Avenida in Matola at around 08:00 in the morning of 27 October. 18 civilians were injured during the incident.
Sources stated that the food aid is being diverted by local officials in Nakaka village in Montepuez district on 26 October. Several of the IDPs were relying on biscuits due to the lack of food aid.

President Nyusi was reportedly notified of the case filed against him by Privinvest in UK case on Hidden Debts. The lawsuit by Privinvest filed against the president alleged that they had made payments on his behalf, which included to his election campaign last 2014.

Prime Minister Carlos do Rosario stated on 27 October that the security situation in Cabo Delgado has been stabilized. Do Rosario also said joint security forces between the SADC and Rwandan security forces continue to dismantle insurgent bases and pursue militants.
Locals recovered the body of a drunk fishermen who drowned at a fishing port in Maputo city on 25 October.
The Montepuez Ruby Mining company aided IDPs in Montepuez district on 27 October with donations that included 1000 sheets of zinc, 2,000 blankets, and 5,000 mosquito nets.

The Ministry of Health announced 10 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 27 October. This comes as five of the new cases were recorded in Maputo City, followed by Nampula with 2 cases and Niassa with 2 cases.

The North Regional Water Administration (ARA-Norte) warned that a part of the Namutimba River may be polluted due to a recently derailed coal train near Cuamba last week that crashed into the river. ARA-NORTE stated that the water in the area was being tested for pollutants while ongoing clearing operations were being conducted to remove the derailed train. Around 120 open coal wagons fell off the bridge after the train derailed last week.

The World Bank Donated 150 million USD to Mozambique to assist the country in the Governance and Digital Economy Project that seeks to improve access to civil identification, digital public services, and business opportunities.

The USAID signed a deal with Absa Bank to increase financing of small and medium sized agribusinesses on 27 October. The deal was to promote loans for the businesses who have difficulty in accessing loans or financial support.
ExxonMobil donated food and relief goods to the IDPs in Cabo Delgado on 27 October. The donation was to cover 1200 IDPs in the province.
Rwandan security forces opened medical facilities manned by Rwandan doctors treating around 184 locals in Quiwiya, Quilinde, and Quionga areas on 22 October.

Security forces arrested three suspects smuggling three boxes filled with 28kg of drugs in Maputo on 25 October. The suspects were bound for Zavala and claimed that they were only picking up the packages.

Security forces arrested three suspects smuggling three boxes filled with 28kg of drugs in Maputo on 25 October. The suspects were bound for Zavala and claimed that they were only picking up the packages.

Former guerillas and pro-gov militia figthers from Muidumbe stated that they have to take long "alternative routes" to obtain their pensions in Pemba. The pensioners stated that they could not obtain their pensions in Muidumbe due to the lack of infrastructure after insurgents destroyed the area.

The Nacala Logisitics announced that the clearing of the derailed train transporting coal near Cuamba has been completed on 27 October. The company also stated that repairs of the railroad were also completed.

Zimtrade officials announced that Zimtrade strengthend trade relationship with Mozambique on 28 October. 80 companies from Zimbabwe attended the conference focusing on consumer goods, agriculture inputs, agriculture implements, construction, and engineering.

The Minister of Economy and Finance of Mozambique Maleiane stated on 28 October that the price increase for oil products may increase up to 75 meticais per liter. This comes as previous adjustments led to the price increase of 69 meticais per liter for oil products. Maleiane stated that the prices were only increased as necessary. The price increased included the calculation of the price per barrel of crude oil and the inclusion of the exchange of the Mozambican metical.

Tanzanian security forces were reported on 27 October to have denied reports of new insurgent attacks in October on Tanzanian villages by Cabo Delgado insurgents. The announcement comes as unconfirmed reports stated that the insurgents conduted at least two attacks along the border targeting displaced individuals.  Other sources reiterated that there have been at least two recent attacks on villages on the Tanzanian side of the Rovuma River.

Several vehicles collide with each other in Matola, west of Maputo, on the morning of 28 October. 8 civilians were killed and 35 were injured. The collision involved a transit but, water tranker truck, an SUV, a minibus, and a sedan.

Portucel Mozambique announced the export of two ships transporting eucalyptus tree logs from Beira on 28 October. The company stated that the ship exported 32,000 cubic meters of log. Three other ships are expected to export by 2022. This comes as Portucel Mozambique reportedly invested USD 130 million to plant 12 million trees on 13,500 hectares of land.
A group of 15 insurgents on 25 October reportedly surrendered to SAMIM forces in Nabala village in Mucojo AP.  This report is unconfirmed.
The Ministry of Health announced 7 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 28 October. This comes as no new deaths were recorded for the past 48 hours. Daily recoveries were also noted at 188.

South African President Ramaphosa issued a letter dated on 15 October that the deployment of the SADC forces will be extended for another three months until 15 January 2022 in Mozambique. The letter was addressed to the South African National Assembly Speaker Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula. Ramaphosa stated that the estimated cost of the extension would be around R984,368,057. Ramaphosa also said “1,495 SANDF personnel for service in fulfilment of an international obligation towards SADC, to support Mozambique and to combat the acts of terrorism and violent extremists in Cabo Delgado province”.  The SADC earlier in October had indicated that the SADC mission in Mozambique would be extended for another 3 months.

The Ministry of Health announced that 2,046,781 were fully vaccinated in Mozambique as of 27 October. 183,338 were vaccinated during the past 24 hours with Nampula recording 41,582 vaccinations and Maputo city with 5,259 vaccinations. The ministry clarified that 2,734,512 have already received at least a single dose.

The Bank of Mozambique announced several companies were not able to pay their dividends to the Mozambican government for the fiscal year of 2020. The Bank of Mozambique stated that TEMA and  EMODRAGA were not able to pay their dividends due to their losses as of 2019.

The Ministry of Mineral Resources and Energy inspector general announced that the Mozambican government lost around 3.3 billion meticais due to the smuggling of stones and minerals in 2020. The ministry also added that around a ton of gemstones were seized from smugglers worth 67 million meticais in 2020. Smugglers were most active in Nampula, Zambezia, Tete, and Manica. In 2021, 800kgs of gold has been recovered from smugglers.
Police seized two ivory spikes found along the river banks of Lissiane River in Mecula of Niassa province on 27 October. Police stated that the ivory was dropped by poachers.

The RENAMO political party called on President Nyusi to fully disclose all the details of his deal with Rwandan President Kagame regarding the deployment of forces to Cabo Delgado. This comes RENAMO asked as to why foreign forces were brought in if FRELIMO stated that the ongoing conflict in Cabo Delgado was only a disorder by locals and not armed conflict.
An Italian oil and gas company indicated on 28 October that it expects LNG projects in Mozambique to resume in mid-2022 with the gradual return of security to Cabo Delgado.

Citizen’s Observatory for Health has called for the National Health System to conduct an investigation regarding the management of resources at healthcare facilities on 28 October. This comes as patients have claimed at different hospitals that they have been asked to reuse medical supplies, and reported other medical supply shortages.

The National Petroleum Institute reportedly plans to launch the sixth bidding round for concession oil and gas areas before the end of the year. The areas will include five blocs in the Rovuma Basin, seven in Angoche, two in Zambezi Delta, and two in Save.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that the 200,000 COVID vaccine doses were donated by Portugal were set to arrive in Maputo on 30 October. The AstraZeneca vaccines would be delivered by the Portuguese Embassy to the government officials.

Brazilian security forces on 28 October detained a Mozambican national attempting to smuggle out five kg of cocaine at Rio de Janeiro Airport bound for Maputo International Airport. The smuggled narcotics were hidden in several candles as part of the suspect’s luggage.

Brazilian security forces on 28 October detained a Mozambican national attempting to smuggle out five kg of cocaine at Rio de Janeiro Airport bound for Maputo International Airport. The smuggled narcotics were hidden in several candles as part of the suspect’s luggage.

The SADC Executive Secretary Elias Mpedi Magosi conducted a visit Mozambique to review SAMIM's progress on 28 October. Magosi stated that he was to determine any needed adjustments for SAMIM in order for them to meet the objectives in the country. Magosi added that he will maintain contact with Mozambican officials to continue monitoring SAMIM and to assess their impression in order to fulfill their objectives.
The Ministry of Health announced 10 new COVID cases were recorded in Mozambique on 29 October. No new deaths were also noted. This comes as 27 daily recoveries were recorded.

Minister of Defense Jaime Neto announced that the security has been reestablished in central parts of Mozambique. Neto stated that security forces will still be on high alert in the area due to the possibility of RENAMO dissidents conducting attacks. This announcement comes after former RENAMO dissident leader Nhongo was killed by security forces on 11 October.

Police stated that sexual assault cases have seen a decline since the beginning of the year in Maputo province. Police said that the cases have dropped from 158 cases in 2020 to 49 cases this 2021. Police stated that majority of the victims were still children.

Sources stated on 30 October that drinking water infrastructure has been restored in Palma and Mocimboa da Praia, after the recent restoration of electricity and communications in these districts. Restoration works on roads in these districts are also ongoing.

Sources stated on 30 October that drinking water infrastructure has been restored in Palma and Mocimboa da Praia, after the recent restoration of electricity and communications in these districts. Restoration works on roads in these districts are also ongoing.

The editor of Ikweli Newspaper was verbally attacked by FRELIMO's head at the Nampula Municipal Assembly in a speech on 31 October. The official stated that the editor is a "mentally unbalanced journalist." Ikweli is a major publication covering developments in north Mozambique, including Nampula. This speech was largely seen as a threat from the ruling party targeting Ikweli.

On 30 October, Mozambique recorded 18 new Covid-19 cases, 1 related death, and zero recoveries. This brings the total cases to 151,288 (145 of which are active), with 1,930 deaths, and 149,209 total recoveries.

Unconfirmed reports indicated between 27-31 October, Joint Forces of Rwandan troops and Mozambican forces attacked an insurgent base in the Muela/Muera area, reportedly killing 20 insurgents and capturing a top insurgent leader.

In operations between 27-31 October, Rwandan and Mozambican forces were reported to have located and destroyed insurgent bases at Naguitengue, in the Mbau area, in the Muela/Muera area, and along the North Bank of the Messalo River in Mocimboa da Praia (MDP) District. Photos posted online showed 10 laptops, 8 phones, 2 submachine guns, and motorbikes seized in these operations, though no photographs emerged of dead or captured insurgents, or of any weapons seized.  Reports state that 12 women and children were also liberated. One unconfirmed report indicated that 20 insurgents were killed in a three day battle in the Muera/Muela area, saying an insurgent vehicle had been destroyed, also saying that a "top leader" of the insurgency had been captured.
