The Ministry of the Sea, Inland Waters and Fisheries (MIMAIP) announced that the capture of surface shrimp and mangrove crab will be prohibited starting from 1 November 2021 to 31 March 2022 as a move for the revitalization of sea life. The ban does not include the provinces of Manica, Tete, and Niassa. However, for mangrove crabs, the ban will cover the entire Mozambican coast, while for the surface shrimp this will cover the Sofala Bank, Maputo Bay, and the mouth of the Limpopo River.

About 1,000 IDP families currently live at Marokani Resettlement Center, with more than half of accommodation in the area "uncovered".  Families in the area reportedly have received little aid from the Mozambican government.

Mozambican security forces on 26 October opened fire on a group of 20 fishermen on Makalowe Island, killing 15 of them.  The security forces had reportedly mistaken the group for insurgents as the fishermen were operating in a prohibited area where vessels are banned from sailing due to insecurity.  ANother source reported 12 fishermen killed out of a group of 13.

A local media report on 1 November stated that fishermen continue to fish north of the Matemo Island in Cabo Delgado despite a ban in fishing imposed by the  Defense and Security Forces (FDS) for more than 4 months due to the insurgency there. As a result, these fishermen sometimes become victims of targeted military operations against the insurgents. This includes a recent incident in which soldiers shot dead several fishermen at Makalowe island, mistaking them for insurgents.

Mozambican Police arrested 4 people in Maputo City for drug trafficking charges on 29 October. This included a teacher, 2 students, and an official from the Municipal Council of Naamacha. They were in possession of drugs which were intended to be sold.

Mozambican Police arrested 4 people in Maputo City for drug trafficking charges on 29 October. This included a teacher, 2 students, and an official from the Municipal Council of Naamacha. They were in possession of drugs which were intended to be sold.
A child was ran over and killed in Maputo city on the morning of 1 November.
Unconfirmed reports stated that 5 insurgent were killed during operations by SAMIM/SADC forces on the south bank of the Messalo between 29-31 October.
SAMIM forces reportedly conducted an operation targeting insurgent base in Quissanga on 29 October, reportedly killing 5 insurgents planning an attack into the Quirimbas Islands Archipelago.

The Mozambican and Zimbabwean governments signed a new agreement regarding the management of water and associated ecosystem usage of the Buzi, Pungoe and Save rivers on 27 October. The agreement includes a budget of six million USD to create a project which would allow the mitigation of floods and droughts. The project was also to tackle the issue of gold mining in the areas.
Local sources stated that heavy rain fall had caused flooding in Liberdade neighborhood in Matola on 01 November.

The Ministry of Health announced that 2,254,676 individuals have been vaccinated as of 01 November. 88,864 individuals were vaccinated with their first dose within the past 24 hours as part of the ongoing nationwide vaccination campaign.

Prices of cement have increased in Maputo City and Matola as of 01 November, this includes a rise of 14% of some kinds of cement in the country. The prices of the cement previously had seen a decrease after the inauguration off the Dugongo Mozambique Cement factory this past May.

Mozambique's 2022 proposed budget which will likely be approved by parliament stands at 450.5 billion meticais, 82 billion meticais greater than the 2021 budget.  This is a substantially larger budget than last year, despite no comparable rise in revenue.  There is expected to be about a 150 billion meticais deficit between the budget and revenue in 2022.

Locals have submitted a petition calling to the government's Covid Technical and Scientific Committee for Combat and Prevention to reopen beaches in the country.  The petition says that there is no clear correlation between open beaches and COVID cases.
567 RENAMO members could reportedly join DDR process in November at Namaita in Nampula. The DDR process has been paused for some months due to a shortage of funds.

Police Commander Rafael announced on 01 November that traffic police in Manica were being "recycled", with many being dispatched for retraining.  Corruption is reportedly rife among traffic police in the province.

Police Commander Rafael announced that Manica traffic policemen were being retrained for 45 days in Nahmatanda on 01 November. The training was meant to eliminate corruption that is common among Manica traffic policemen.

The Transport and Communications Minister Rebelo announced that the country's coastal shipping system is facing significant financial difficulties due to the national maritime navigation law, which requires ships to use tugboats in every port to dock.  The use of these tugboats is expensive, and has caused a stoppage of much of the country's cabotage traffic.

The Mozambique Defense Minister Jaime Neto stated that Mozambican security forces continued operations to search for remaining RENAMO dissidents and were on high alert in Central Mozambique. The security forces were also attempting to determine if dissidents were regrouping in Sofala and Manica.

Former Prime Minister Luis Diogo stated on 29 October that the government is still not able to be able to subsidize fuel prices in Mozambique. Diogo stated that the country is still pressured by the state budget and that the country is still dependent on oil market import.  Economy and Finance Minister Adriano Maleiane on 28 October that the previous government attempted to subsidize fuel in 2015 and ended up with a debt of 10 billion meticais, saying there would be no return to generalized subsidies for fuel in the country. The government will continue targeted subsidies for public transport operators to keep bus fares low.

Minister of Economy and Finance Maleiane announced that the government has been making payments on the country's “hidden debts”. In the 2021 budget, $45 million in interest were paid on the $850 million debt to Ematum.

Mozambique's Integrated Development Agency of the North (ADIN) announced that it will intend to present a strategic plan for its reconstruction efforts in Cabo Delgado to the government by 15 November.

Private water suppliers announced that they will not cut water supplies as they had threatened to do on 06 November after resolving their dispute with the government on 30 October.  This averts a potential disruption in the supply of water to over 3 million people. The previous dispute was due to the government attempting to expand their public water supply network in areas where private water suppliers were operating. Mozambican Water Suppliers Association (AFORAMO) previous complained that the Fund for Heritage and Water Supply (FIPAG) was vandalizing their water distribution network.

Exxon CEO Darren Woods at a conference on 29 October reiterated that Exxon remains committed to operations in Mozambique, despite the delaying the company's FID in the country.  He also said that there was no final date for the FID for the company's Rovuma LNG Project in Mozambique.  This statement comes after recent reports that Exxon's board were considering scrapping the Rovuma LNG project as the company carried out across the board belt tightening exercises.

The environmental organization Friends of Earth (FOE) will sue the UK government in December in order to attempt to block UK funding of LNG projects in Mozambique. FOE has said that the UK must make the transition to renewable energies.  The UK last year said it would provide 1.15 billion pounds in funding to LNG projects in Mozambique.

The Minister of State Administration and Public Service Ana Comoana stated that around 5,000 civil servants have been affected by the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. Half of the affected civil servants were teachers. Civil servants are being ask to present themselves to authorities and be reintegrated into school districts after the disruptions caused by insurgent attacks.
Unknown men sexually assaulted and murdered a civilian in Barrio Siduava of Matola on 01 November.

The Minister of Mineral Resources Max Tonela visited the Rovuma offshore drilling site for Area 4 and stated that the drilling at the project is in its final phase. The project was to drill six wells in the Area 4 of the basin.

The Integrated Development Agency of the North (ADIN) announced that  950 agricultural kits would be given to IDPs in Marrocane, Ancuabe district. ADIN stated that this comes as they would provide agricultural kits for around 350,000 civilians affected by the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

The EU Military Training Mission in Mozambique's opening ceremony will take place in Katembee Independent Fuzileiros Company in the Dongo Military Field in Chimoio on 3 November. The training mission was set to train the FADM to create a future rapid response force.  The mission will last for two years.
The Ministry of Health announced 7 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 1 November. This comes as Maputo city recorded three cases. No new recoveries were recorded .

The Electricity Supply Corporation of Malawi (ESCOM) now expects that a project to construct a 218km interconnector line between Mozambique and Malawi will be completed by October 2023. The project was to The project was delayed as the initial deadline was set for December 2022.
Health officials raised concerns as poisoning by traditional medicines have increased in the Chifunde area of Tete as of 2 November. Several of the victims were reportedly hospitalized.
The Swiss government has donated 700 million meticais to support the health sector in Cabo Delgado. The donations will support projects in Namuno, Metuge, Mecufi, and Balama.
Sources stated on 29 October that 13 locals have died due to hippo and crocodile attacks along the Zambezi River in Tete this year. Seven of the deaths were registered in the district of Mutarara.

The Media Institute of Southern Africa (MISA) called the Mozambican authorities to account for the whereabout of missing journalist Ibraimo Mbaruco. Mbaruco has been missing since April of 2020, when he was reportedly surrounded by a group of soldiers in Palma town and taken into custody.

Police arrested a Ministry of Land and Environment employee for fraud charges in Maputo on 2 November. The suspect was charged for abuse of office, embezzlement, forging documents, defrauding, and money laundering. The suspect is believed to have embezzled as much as 320,000 Meticais.

Exxon's head of drilling and extraction Liam Mallon will conduct a two-day meeting with the Ministry of Mineral Resources and Energy officials in Maputo on 04-05 November. The meeting will also be attended by President Nyusi.  Mallon's visit to Mozambique comes shortly after Exxon reaffirmed it would continue operations in Mozambique after reports the company was considering scrapping its Rovuma LNG project.

The Mozambican Federation of Road Transport Associations (FEMATRO) president stated that a price increase for public transportation fares is inevitable. The price increase will be driven by recent increases in fuel prices, though no fare increase has yet been decided upon.  Public transportation fares have remained static for the past 5 years.

Hidden Debt Trial defendant Antonio Carlos do Rosario stated that former President Guebuza was not aware of the Hidden Debts scheme, and only became aware of it after loans had been taken out. Do Rosario said that the former president was only notified of the formation of EMATUM, Mozambique Tuna Company, after it had been formed.

The National Petroleum Institute (INP) announced on 29 October that the LNG floating platform that will operate in Area 4 of Rovuma Basin was set to depart South Korea to Mozambique within a few days. INP stated that the floating platform was being accompanied by a team for the final commissioning.

The National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction stated that 21,000 individuals may be affected by the floods in Maputo City during the rainy season between 2021-2022. Minor flooding has already taken place in the city.
Robbers stole 75,000 meticais, clothing, after breaking into a commercial establishment and the setting the shop on fire in Central C, Maputo City on the morning of 2 November.

The Ministry of Health announced 14 new COVID cases and 1 related death in Mozambique on 2 November. Daily recoveries were recorded at 37.

President Nyusi in a speech on 28 October said that the government will accept any offers to counter insurgency in Cabo Delgado. The president also called on the families and relatives of the kidnapping victims to provide assistance to authorities as a way to combat the recent waves of kidnapping.

The Prime Minister do Rosario stated that the government does not expect any tax revenue from TotalEnergies for the next 3 years after the suspension of the company's Cabo Delgado operations earlier this year due to the assault on Palma.

The Ministry of Health announced 222,821 more people have been vaccinated with their first COVID vaccine dose in Mozambique on 2 November. The vaccinations were part of the ongoing third National Mass Vaccination Campaign.

The Mozambique government is conducting talks with the World Bank to obtain a financial package of $600 million for the rehabilitation of National Road 1 (EN1). The Minister of Public Works and Housing also added that the Self-Sustained Road Maintenance Program (PROASME), would allow the maintenance of 1,500km of road in the country.

Two sources reported that an IED exploded, targeting a Mozambican armored personnel carrier at 1st de Maio village, north of Miangalewa on 29 October.  No casualties were reported in relation to this attack.  A second source had reported that this attack had occurred in the Xitaxi area on the 1 November.

The European Union Military Training Mission (EUTM) officially launched in Companhia de Fuzileiros Independente da Katembe of Maputo City and Campo Militar do Dondo of Chimoio, Manica on the morning of Wednesday, 3 November.  140 soldiers are part of this two year mission, which will provide training to Mozambican military units at training centers in Manica and Maputo.  Training will include the formation of a quick reaction force to be deployed to Cabo Delgado.

30 Mozambican soldiers are currently held in Mieze for their links to the robbery of several commercial banks in Palma. The soldiers robbed several banks in the town in the aftermath of the assault on Palma after the town had largely been deserted.  The soldiers were arrested after cash was found in their possession.  The exact date of their arrest was not immediately clear, though they may be part of a group of soldiers arrested in late May in the Palma area who were detained for bank robberies in the town.

Three pro-government militia members were reported to have carried out looting from residences in Namacande on or before 28 October, stealing solar panels, batteries, and televisions.  The three were later arrested in Miteda.

Sources stated on 28 October that three pro-government militiamen were detained for stealing valuables in Miteda village. The militiamen reportedly stole solar panels, batteries, and televisions from the residences in Namacande.

Sources stated that two Netherlands Ministries reportedly ignored the warnings from the Dutch embassy is Mozambique regarding the gas projects in Cabo Delgado prior to the assault on Palma. The ministries of Finance and Foreign Affairs in July of 2020 insured the operations of a Dutch dredging company for almost 1 billion euros, despite a warning from the Dutch embassy in Maputo that the security situation in Cabo Delgado was "deteriorating by the day".  The embassy also expressed doubt that the Mozambican military could contain violence in Cabo Delgado.

The Ministry of Health announced that 4.1 million individuals have been vaccinated during the third phase of the National Mass Vaccination Campaign in Mozambique. This comes as 247,037 individuals were vaccinated on 3 November.

The National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD) stated that around 300,000 people are at risk in Inhambane from natural disasters this rainy season.   INGD also stated that 445 classrooms and 9,000 hectares of agricultural land could be destroyed during this time.

The Nampula Municipal Assembly approved the pay rise for police in the province on 3 November. RENAMO and MDM delegates voted together to pass this pay raise, while FRELIMO delegates abstained from the vote.

The Ministry of Health announced 9 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 3 November. This comes as five daily recoveries were also recorded within the past 24 hours. Maputo City recorded 5 of the new cases.
Portugal delivered 187,200 COVID vaccine doses to Mozambique on 04 November. The vaccines were the fourth batch donated by the Portuguese government to the country.

The ACP-EU delegation visited the Metuge Resettlement Center as part of a visit to Cabo Delgado. The delegation said there was a need to units Mozambican and international forces in order to provide more humanitarian support to IDPs in the province.

Sources stated that two traffic police officers died during retraining in Metuchira area of Sofala on 3 November. No specific details were released on the how the police died. An investigation is underway to determine the deaths of the police officers.

The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) said on 03 November that it had recently suspended 10 businesses and issued warning to 35 others in Mozambique over various health and safety violations.

Minister of Health Tiago on 03 November warned of a possible 4th COVID wave in Mozambique, saying most of the circumstances that led to the previous three waves of COVID in the country are still in place.. Tiago stated that the improvement in the COVID situation should not be regarded as the end in the pandemic.

Police arrested a medical technician and a health intern for selling fake vaccination cards with complete vaccination details in Bagamoyo, west Maputo city, on 3 November. The suspect was selling the cards for 1,500 meticais.

Police arrested a medical technician and a health intern for selling fake vaccination cards with complete vaccination details in Bagamoyo, west Maputo city, on 3 November. The suspect was selling the cards for 1,500 meticais.

Police attempted to prevent a bicycle tour led by Municipal Mayor Manuel de Araujo around Quelimane on 3 November. 10 diplomats from Canada, Sweden, and Finland were participating in the tour. Araujo contacted the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and PRM Commander Rafael, who ordered the officers to stand down.
The Ministry of Health announced on 3 November that the third phase of the National Mass Vaccination Campaign has been extended until 16 November.
The Bank of Mozambique announced that the annual inflation in the country is up to 6% from January to September. The bank also stated that Metical appreciated by 15% against the US dollar.
The Portuguese Minister of Defense Cravinho told Mozambican officials that Lisbon will continue to provide military aid to Mozambique, despite the ongoing political crisis in Portugal.
Sources stated that vaccination rates have been low in Maputo City as only 66,300 individuals were vaccinated of a goal of 210,489 vaccinations for the third phase of vaccinations.

Sources stated that fire broke out underground due to the coal deposits in Moatize on 30 October, destroying at least two houses.  These coal deposits could potentially cause more fires in the town in the near to medium term future.

The Mozambique Prime Minister do Rosario announced that the country is aiming for 62% renewable energy in the country by 2030. The prime minister stated that the energy transition program should be inline with Mozambique’s investment in hydroelectric, solar and wind power energies.

The UNODC and US embassies of Tanzania and Mozambique announced the conclusion of the training for the Mozambican Navy, SERNIC, DCEA, and Marine Police in Pemba.  Some Tanzanian naval personnel and South African police also participated in these trainings. The month-long training was regarding mission planning and advanced boarding operations training.

The World Food Program (WFP) stated on 2 November that more than 930,000 IDPs and host families will require food aid in Cabo Delgado, Nampula, and Niassa from now until at least May 2022. WFP stated that the lack of funding was forcing the organization to cut supplies to IDPs.

The World Food Program (WFP) stated on 2 November that more than 930,000 IDPs and host families will require food aid in Cabo Delgado, Nampula, and Niassa from now until at least May 2022. WFP stated that the lack of funding was forcing the organization to cut supplies to IDPs.

A fire broke out and burned down a residence in Pebane Village of Zambezia on 3 November. Two civilians were killed and three others were injured.

Sources stated that food shortages are still ongoing in Palma as of 3 November. The maritime embargo from other islands has interrupted food transportation to Palma. Prices increased in the area as rice reportedly 1kg cost 270 meticais from 250, while 25kg of rice is between 2800 to 4000 meticais.

Security forces escorted convoy 14 trucks transporting essential supplies into Palma on 29 October. This convoy travelled via Mueda and MDP to reach Palma, the first such convoy to use this route since insurgents captured MDP in August of 2020.

The Mozambique government on 03 November announced that they will halt and reverse forest loss and land degradation by 2030 during COP26. This comes as the officials signed a landmark agreement to protect and restore the forests globally.

The Tax Authority announced that there were inconsistencies with the 2020 General State Account (GCE). The issue was that the State General Account collected 7,960 million Meticais in the gas sector. However, the Tax Authority of Mozambique declared that it collected 8,784 million Meticais.

Police announced the arrest of 10 suspected fishermen from Cabo Delgado after the group were intercepted in Mapanzene village, near Maimelane on the afternoon of 2 November. Sources stated that group of 15 were camped in two tents in the area. No details were mentioned if the arrest was related to illegal fishing or if the group has suspected ties with insurgency.  8 of the 10 arrested are reportedly from Palma.

The Association of Mozambican Water Suppliers (AFORAMO) announced the extension of the deadline for suspending the water supply in Greater Maputo to 13 December. The extension for the suspension was granted due to ongoing talks with the government to resolve a dispute between the private water suppliers and the government.  The dispute is related to the government's expansion of services into areas where private water suppliers operate.  If the private suppliers do suspend water supplies, this would cut off around 3 million people from access to water.

The Ministry of Health announced 14 new COVID cases in Mozambique 4 November.  This included 7 new cases in Cabo Delgado. Daily recoveries were tallied at 17.  This comes as no new COVID deaths were noted for the past 48 hours.

RENAMO officials on 04 November stated that their members were being harassed and intimidated regularly by government supporters. RENAMO added that this other opposition party members were also in fear of being persecuted and kidnapped.  RENAMO says threats against its membership occur most commonly in Central Mozambique.

Police officials denied accusations of that they had attempted to prevent tour conducted by Quelimane Mayor for European diplomats around the city on 03 November.  Police officials stated that the event was allowed and that police were simply monitoring the group.

Electricity de Mozambique (EDM) announced that they prevented electrical theft at a station in Beira on 4 November. EDM removed illegally placed cables which were used to steal electricity from the station.

Electricity de Mozambique (EDM) announced that they prevented electrical theft at a station in Beira on 4 November. EDM removed illegally placed cables which were used to steal electricity from the station.
The UAE government intends to donate 20 containers of food and medical aid for IDPs in Cabo Delgado, media reported on 04 November.
The Ministry of Health announced that 4.4 million individuals have been vaccinated in Mozambique as of 4 November. This includes 244,061 people who received a first shot on 04 November.

Exxon officials conducted a meeting with President Nyusi reinforcing their commitment to the Rovuma LNG project on 4 November. The company indicated it will go forward with the LNG project and will do so while cutting emissions by using carbon capture and storage. The company will also seek to cut other costs of the project partially through more collaboration and synergy with TotalEnergies.  Exxon executive Liam Mallon also said the company has observed "progress" regarding the security situation in Cabo Delgado though said there was still " a lot to be done" on this front.  Exxon has not made a Final Investment Decision on its Rovuma LNG Project.

Sources stated that security forces were reportedly tortured and killed a civilian in Likobe village near Chai on 30 October. The victim was reportedly at his agricultural field which was declared a restricted area by the security forces.

Sources stated that security forces were threatened civilians to avoid going into restricted areas near Chai on 30 October due to the insurgent threat in the area.  Soldiers in the area on the same day were reported to have killed a civilian found in a restricted area.

Displaced people conducted a protest march over the food aid distribution on 26 October in Nakaka in Montepuez district. The protesters stated that some of the individuals in the food distribution list were not IDPs from the area and that officials distribute food to other locals via corruption schemes.

Civil Society Organizations along with international aid organizations conducted a meeting with the Mozambique Deputy Attorney Gloria da Conceicao Adamo in Pemab on 25 October.  At this meeting, organizations told Adamo that the food voucher system put in place by the government is creating significant inefficiencies and leading to corruption, and leaving many without aid.  The organizations also said Mozambican security forces continue to target IDPs with violence and otherwise harass IDPs.

Electricity de Mozambique (EDM) announced the restoration of electrical services after three days of power outage to 30,000 customers in parts of Tete and Moatize as well as in Chiuta and Doa Districts.

Police on 26 October arrested several illegal miners in the Malema area, reportedly beating several of those arrested.  Some of those detained were later released on a 50,000 meticais bond.  Days later in the same area, 3 miners were killed when police moved to shut down an illegal mine.
Police on 03 November attempted to shut down an illegal mine in the Malema area of Pebane District; this led to a gun battle with illegal miners which left 3 miners dead.

Armed illegal miners exchanged gunfire with UIR police at the Cococo Mine near Malema village, northeast of Pebane, on the afternoon of Wednesday, 3 November. 1 miner was killed in the exchange, while two others later died of their injuries. The police stated that the illegal miners attempted to enter the mines leading to the clashes when they were stopped.

National Criminal Investigation Service officers (SERNIC) destroyed 410kg of seized amphetamine in Moamba district, northwest of Matola, on 3 November. The drugs were previously seized this past August from a residence in Matola.

Pro-government militiamen shot dead two suspected insurgents in Nagulue on Wednesday, 3 November. The suspected insurgents were in possession of two axes and machetes that were bloodstained. The suspects insurgents were both reportedly from Macomia town, and believed to have joined the insurgency when the town was captured by militants in May of 2020, and suspected of being involved with the recent attacks targeting civilians in southern Cabo Delgado.

Two vehicles crashed on the morning of 05 November on Av. Joaquim Chissano in Maputo City during the course of a car chase.  One person was killed in the accident.  A civilian in his vehicle was reportedly confronted by two men in a government vehicle who threatened him with a firearm; he fled from the two in his vehicle who then pursued him.  The two men in the government vehicle, one of whom was a soldier, had reportedly previously carried out robberies in the vehicle.

The migration services announced the reopening of the border crossing in Goba Border to Eswatini on 4 November.  This crossing had been closed for 18 months due to the COVID pandemic.

The Mozambican government signed an agreement with GL Energy to finalize a concession agreement for a 250 megawatt $400 million gas fired power plant in Nacala coast on 4 November. The first phase of the agreement was for GL to provide 50megawatts followed by the 200megawatts during the second and third phases of the project.
Officials announced that road accidents along National Road 1 (EN 1) in Inhambane have killed 71 people between January and September of 2021.

The Ministry of Health announced that 150,363 individuals were vaccinated for the COVID vaccine in Mozambique on 5 November. This brings the total vaccinated individuals in the country who have received at least one shot reached 4.5 million.
The Ministry of Health announced 13 new COVID cases and a single related death in Mozambique on 5 November. There were 117 active cases as of 05 November along with 6 hospitalizations.
Sources stated that Mozambique is on a list of 28 countries with highest rates of wildlife trafficking in the world.

The National Institute of Statistics (INE) stated that 70% of people in Zambezia live under the poverty line.  Many areas of the province lacked access to drinking water, education, housing and basic sanitation.

Officials announced the deaths of 73 individuals by wildlife in Tete province in first half of 2021. This was a significant increase compared to 2020, in which only 24 deaths were reported over the same period. Wildlife in the province has also destroyed 677 hectares of crops, mostly in Magoe and Zumbo districts.
Police officials announced that there have been 45 suicide cases in Gaza province in 2021. Police stated that the cases were mostly teenagers and other young people.

Sources stated that there are no senior officers detained in Mieze among the group of soldiers held at the prison for their involvement in a series of bank robberies in Palma between April - May.  Local media said that a number of senior officers had been "the biggest beneficiaries" of these thefts and were not under arrest.

South African kidnappers still hold the son of Mozambican businessman Salimo Abdula as of 5 November. Police stated that the investigation into the kidnapping of Jair Abdula is still ongoing.  Last week, one suspect in the case who had been arrested was released.

An earthquake with a magnitude of 4.6 on the Richter Scale occurred in Manica province at around 23:45 on 5 November. The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) stated that the epicenter of the earthquake was  near Sussundenga, 66km south of Chimoio. The earthquake was reportedly felt in the districts of Chimoio, Vanduziu, Macate, Nhamatanda, Buzi, Machaze, and Mossurize. No casualties or material damages were reported. The USGS stated that the earthquake lasted for around 30 to 40 seconds. In response to the earthquake, officials conducted a damage survey around Chimoio after the incident. Residents were advised in these areas to be vigilant in anticipation of aftershocks which may damage weakened or older buildings.
A truck and two other vehicles collided with each other on the road in Nacarroa area on the night of 5 November. Two civilians were killed.

17 people, including 4 children, were killed and 5 other people injured when a semi-collective public transport vehicle collided with a private vehicle on the afternoon of 06 November in Manhica. As of 8 November, five of the deceased have been identified. The driver of the semi-collective public transport vehicle claimed the accident was caused by over speeding of the other vehicle. The Manhica area in July of this year was the site of an accident in which at least 30 people were killed.  The N1 road in some areas of Maputo Province is in a poor condition, leading to a significant number of deadly RTAs.

The Ministry of Health announced 15 new COVID case and one related death in Mozambique on 6 November.  The highest number of new cases was recorded in Cabo Delgado with six cases, followed by Maputo City and Gaza province with three cases each, Manica, Tete and Nampula recorded one case each. In the past 24 hours, six new hospital admission were recorded while no one was discharged from the hospital.

Reports on 6 November indicate that at least 30 houses along Avenida Julius Nyerere, in the Polana Canico A and B districts, in Maputo, are at risk of collapsing due to the continuous degradation of the slope that protects the road, caused by the rainy season.

column4: Mozambican Government announced on 6 November that ENI will begin pumping LNG off the coast of Cabo Delgado province in the first half of 2022. The announcement was made following a meeting between company executives and President Nyusi. It is expected that the country will start to produce and export LNG by the end of June 2022. This development comes as authorities stated that the offshore drilling at the Coral South project was completed last week.  This will be the first LNG produced in from the country's Rovuma reserves, some of the largest LNG rserves in the world.

The Ministry of Health (MISAU) announced one new COVID case in Mozambique on 7 November.  The new case was recorded in Nampula province. In the past 24 hours, MISAU registered one hospital discharge and two new hospital admissions.

Mozambican authorities have detained 11 Pakistani nationals,  illegal immigrants, who were travelling in a car with a police officer at a checkpoint in Moatize district, in Tete, on Monday night, 1 November. Eight of the Pakistanis had passports but no visas, and the remaining three had no documents. The police officer traveling with the illegal immigrants reportedly escaped while the authorities were carrying out an inspection of the vehicle.

The Minister of Industry and Trade, Carlos Mesquita, announced on 5 November in Beira, that Mozambique and Rwanda plan to sign an agreement to waive entry visas between the two countries to facilitate business between the two. This development will mark the beginning of a new stage in commercial transactions between the two countries.

Police in Inhassoro on 04 November released 15 fishermen, most of whom were from Cabo Delgado, who had been arrested two days previously.  The group had been arrested over potential links to the Cabo Delgado insurgency as fishermen from Cabo Delgado had not previously travelled to Inhambane to work.

On 08 November, Maputo province governor Julio Parruque announced that the government will launch a series of measures in a bid to reduce road accidents in the province. These measures include increasing the awareness of motorists, heightening the security presence on the roads and a proposal to reevaluate speed limits.  Motorists may also have their blood alcohol levels tested. The announcement was made following the accident in Manhica which claimed 17 lives.

Mozambican Police shot four thieves in Tchumene, the municipality of Matola, on Monday morning, 8 November. Two thieves died on the scene, while the other two sustained injuries and are currently hospitalized. The suspects reportedly stole 1,352,220 meticais from a company in the area. Reports indicate that the suspects opened fire after they saw police officers approaching; officers then returned fire.

Two thieves died on the scene, while the other two sustained injuries and are currently hospitalized. The suspects reportedly stole 1,352,220 meticais from a company in the area. Reports indicate that the suspects opened fire after they saw police officers approaching; officers then returned fire.

On the morning of 07 November,  a locomotive owned by Nacala Logistics pulling passenger cars caught fire on the Cuamba-Nampula Railway in Malema District.  No casualties were immediately reported.  A number of passengers travelling to Nampula were stranded in the area.  This is the second significant railway accident in Northern Mozambique involving a Nacala Logistics train in just over two weeks.  On 22 October, a freight train derailed in Cuamba District in Niassa, killing 2 children and injuring 7 others.

On 07 November, 3 insurgents surrendered to Mozambican military troops in Ntchinga village of Muidumbe.  The small group of militants reportedly surrender because they were starving.  Troops seized their weapons, beat the militants, and then transported them to Mueda.

On 06 November, two insurgents surrendered south of Chai village in V Congresso. Note a second source reported this surrender took place on 02 November. The two were armed with small arms and machetes surrendered to pro-government militia who detained them and transported them to Macomia.  These two also reportedly surrendered due to a lack of food.

Rwandan ambassador to Mozambique, Claude Nikobizanzwe, announced on 8 November during a seminar in South Africa that more than 100 insurgents have been killed and at least 350 civilians have been rescued by Rwandan military forces in Cabo Delgado province since the beginning of the Rwandan intervention in July. Insurgents were pushed from Mocimboa da Praia, Palma, and Mueda districts in the region following joint operations carried out by Rwandan and Mozambican troops. In addition, Rwandan troops recovered several military weapons, vehicles, computers, mobile phones, and documents during ongoing operations.

Unidentified men vandalized an EDM's electric transformer in Ndlavela neighborhood, Matola in the early hours of 7 November. The copper cable were reportedly removed from the post. The attack caused a blackout affecting over 100 families in the neighborhood.

Unidentified men vandalized an EDM's electric transformer in Ndlavela  neighborhood, Matola in the early hours of 7 November. The copper cable were reportedly removed from the post. The attack caused a blackout affecting over 100 families in the neighborhood.

On 8 November, the Mozambican Federation of Road Transport Associations (FEMATRO) called for “severe punishment” for drivers violating traffic laws to stop deadly accidents. This follows a road accident that led to the death of 17 people in Manhica district on 6 November. The group criticized the authorities, who only take measures after more deaths happened. On 7 November, the Maputo provincial government met in an extraordinary meeting with several leaders and announced a reinforcement of security force measures along the national road 1 (EN1) in the said district.

Additional police officers will be deployed in Manhica district along N1 road to conduct 24-hour surveillance along the route, Maputo Province Governor Julio Parruque said on 7 November during an extraordinary meeting with various authorities. Other measures including, revision of signs, speed limits, works in some places and awareness campaigns for safe driving were also announced. This development came a day after 17 people died in a road accident in the district.

On 8 November, authorities announced that in the last 24 hours, 32,634 people had been vaccinated with the first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine, under the third stage of the National Mass Vaccination Campaign. This increased the number of vaccinated individuals to 4,858,830, while a total of 2,600,608 people have been fully inoculated in the country since the beginning of the vaccination program on 8 March.

On 5 November, the Constitutional Council (CC) announced numbers 1 and 2 of article 184, of Law nº 23/2007 of Labour Law, is unconstitutional for violating articles 70 and 134 of the republic. Article 70 states that “citizens have the right to appeal to the courts against acts that violate their rights and interests recognized by the Constitution and by the law”. This came after CC intervened in a dispute between a worker and the Mozambican representation of Coca-Cola after the latter argued that the case filed by the worker should first have been submitted to mediation, under an article of the Labour Law. However, details of the dispute was not disclosed.

35% of the cashew nuts produced in Mozambique are diverted to the black market, as indicated by a report issued by the bank of Mozambique on 06 November. In addition, out of 17 processing factories in the country, only nine are currently operating. Closed factories are not expected to open soon due to a lack of raw materials.

A 32-yr-old man, along with his 27-year-old accomplice, decapitated his daughter's head in Intxotxa, Gile district on 06 November in a bid to sell it for 1million meticais. Mozambican police officers later arrested the two suspects.

Security forces arrested 32-yr-old man, along with his 27-year-old accomplice, who allegedly decapitated his daughter's head  in Intxotxa, Gile district on 06 November. The suspects reportedly carried out the attack  in a bid to sell it for 1million meticais.

The Ministry of Health announced three new COVID cases and zero death in Mozambique on 8 November. Two new infections were recorded in Maputo city, while Gaza province recorded one case. In the past 24 hours, a total of 22 individuals recovered from the virus, while a new hospital admission was recorded.
On 8 November, Head of SADC Mission in Mozambique, Prof Mpho Molomo, stated that foreign intervention is playing a significant role in stabilizing the situation in Cabo Delgado Province.

Mozambican Police officers arrested a 42-yr-old suspected drug trafficker dual Mozambican/Tanzanian national in Chimoio city on or around 07 November. A quantity of cocaine and cannabis sativa were recovered from his possession. Authorities believed that the drugs originated overseas.

Mozambican Police officers arrested a 42-yr-old suspected drug trafficker dual Mozambican/Tanzanian national in Chimoio city on or around 07 November. A quantity of cocaine and cannabis sativa were recovered from his possession. Authorities believed that the drugs originated overseas.

On 8 November, Mozambique’s finance minister, Adriano Maleiane, announced the there are no reasons to anticipate a possible renegotiation of the bonds of the Empresa Mocambicana de Atum (EMATUM), which were first converted into public debt securities, due to delays in natural gas exploration in Cabo Delgado province. The public debt has risen from 5% to 9% in March 2024, which was restructured based on Total Energies’ original gas production schedule. The gas company's operations was scheduled to start in 2024 but was postponed to at least 2026 due to the insecurity in the province.

The Minister of Interior, Amade Miquidade reiterates on 8 November the need for heightened police attention in IDP camps and other resettlement areas in Cabo Delgado province due to possible terrorist attacks. Increased security presence in these areas will forestall insurgent attacks and abort any attempt to reactivate insurgency movements.

On 8 November, the Head of SADC Mission in Mozambique, Prof Mpho Molomo, stated that the Cabo Delgado insurgency could potentially spread throughout the south of the continent if it is not urgently dealt with. Molomo added that a comprehensive approach beyond military intervention is needed as the insurgency's root causes have not been resolved. He also said there was an "external element" and that some insurgents were coming from outside of Mozambique.

On the evening of 09 November, President Nyusi removed Interior Minister Amade MIquidade from his position.  Adelaide Amurane, Minister of the President's Office, was also removed from her position.  No reason was given for Miquidade's removal.

Mozambique and Zimbabwe government reps on Wednesday, 10 November, met in their first Joint Permanent Commission on Cooperation (JPCC) meeting in eight years. This came five months after the country leaders of both countries agreed to reconvene this bilateral platform.

On 9 November, authorities announced that in the last 24 hours, 94,414 people had been vaccinated with the first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine, under the third stage of the National Mass Vaccination Campaign. This increased the number of vaccinated individuals to 4,954,765, while a total of 2,609,473 people have been fully inoculated in the country since the beginning of the vaccination program on 8 March.

TotalEnergies Senior VP of Africa, Henri-Max Ndong Nzue, stated on 9 November that the security situation in Cabo Delgado is improving. However, he added that security needs to be maintained “in a sustained manner”  before the LNG project could restart. Total announced force majeure in April on the Mozambique LNG project and removed all of its staff from the site following insurgent attacks in Palma, located near the said project.

On 9 November, Zambezia Judicial Court sentenced to 20 years in prison a police officer, identified as Manuel Joao, for murder of a civilian, Max Love, in 2013 . The officer was sentenced in absentia. Reports indicate that Joao was part of the security team attached to Zambezia Governor Joaquim Verissimo.

On 10 November, South Africa's Gauteng High Court in Johannesburg ruled that former Mozambican Finance Minister Manuel Chang will be extradited to the United States, and not to Mozambique.  Another South African court in August had ruled that Chang would be extradited to Maputo.  Chang has been jailed in South Africa since 2018 in relation to Mozambique's Hidden Debts Case.
Reports on 9 November indicate that a child was abducted in Matola. The suspects allegedly blackmail the family into freeing the victim. Details behind the incident are still unclear at this time.
PRM announced on 9 November that a 50-yr-old female civilian died in Mogovolas district, Nampula last week due to famine. Further information on the incident was not disclosed.

The Ministry of Health announced 11 new COVID cases and zero death in Mozambique on 8 November. Cabo Delgado province recorded the highest number of new cases with six new cases, followed by Maputo city with two cases, Nampula- 1, Gaza-1 and Zambezia-1 . In the past 24 hours, a total of 28 individuals recovered from the virus, while no hospital admission or discharge was recorded.

The oil price hike in Mozambique has negatively impacted motorcycles taxis in Nampula City, a local media reported on 9 November. Several taxi operators called on the government to review and revise present oil prices.

Reports on 9 November indicate that insurgent movements were seen in Nangade District. Small cells of militants were reported to be moving in parts of the district though no other information was immediately available.

Prices increased by 4.14% in Mozambique between January and October 2021, according to a data released on 9 November by the National Institute of Statistics (INE). Food and non-alcoholic beverages have the highest increase with  around 1.97 percentage points (pp) and 0 .59 pp positive, respectively. Notably, in October, INE reported that all cities registered a price increase, with the city of Nampula recorded the highest with approximately of 1.20%, followed by Maputo City, with 0.87% and, finally, the city of Beira with approximately 0.47%.

An unidentified man, armed with a weapon, invaded a Command of the Police of the Republic of Mozambique (PRM) in Gurue, Zambezia, on 10 November and attacked police officers. Two officers were injured in the attack. Responding officers opened fire on the suspect; however, reports claimed that the bullet did not hit the suspect but did injure a civilian.   It was unclear if the suspect escaped or was taken into custody after this attack.

Two officers were injured in the attack. Responding officers opened fire on the suspect; however, reports claimed that the bullet did not hit the suspect but did injure a civilian.   It was unclear if the suspect escaped or was taken into custody after this attack.

Mozambican police officers seized a large amount of illicit drugs reportedly sold in a house on Rua Filipe Samuel Magaia in Nampula city on 9 November, following a series of investigations. Two people connected to the crime were also arrested. Recovered Illicit drugs include cannabis sativa (suruma), methamphetamine, “touro”, and drug-infused cookies. The exact quantity of the drugs has yet been determined; however, authorities claimed it is the most significant amount of narcotics seized in the history of Nampula police operations.  One of the suspects questioned indicated that the drugs had come from Maputo.

A group of pro-government militia looted solar panels in Ntchinga and Namacande on or before 02 November.  5 of these militia members were later arrested.
A group of pro-government militia looted solar panels in Ntchinga and Namacande on or before 02 November.  5 of these militia members were later arrested.

Mozambican police arrested at least five local militia members in Muidumbe on 2 November over the alleged theft of seven solar panels and batteries at health centers in Ntchinga and Namacande. The suspects confessed to their crimes and said they have other members, also involved in the robbery operations, still at large.  Arrests for similar looting took place in late October of 2 militia members.

On 10 November, insurgents were reported to have entered V Congresso village, north of Macomia, setting several homes on fire in the early morning hours.  Militants also reportedly beheaded two people in the village, and also carried out looting in the village, taking away food and other supplies.  Other sources later reported only one man was killed in the attack, shot dead by insurgents.  Militants reportedly were moving in the vicinity of the village on the night of 09 November.

On 09 November, a group of militants in the afternoon entered Lijungo/Liyungu village in Nangade.  Other sources later reported militants had attacked the village.  Residents due to insurgent activity in the area were reported to be fleeing Litingina town.

On 09 November, a group of militants in the afternoon entered Lijungo/Liyungu village in Nangade.  Other sources later reported militants had attacked the village.  Residents due to insurgent activity in the area were reported to be fleeing Litingina town.

Rwandan and Mozambican forces on the afternoon of 10 November clashed with insurgents at Mualela, near the Mueda-Nangade road.  Insurgents reportedly attacked security forces from different directions in the area.  Insurgents were reported to be present further north near N'gangolo.  Militants the previous day were reported to have moved through Lijungo village, north-east of Mualela.
Insurgents were reported to be present on 10 November in the Ngangolo area; clashes between security forces and insurgents took place on the same day further south at Mualela.

On the afternoon of 10 November, President Nyusi removed Defense Minister Jaime Neto from his position in a statement issued by the government.  No reason for Neto's removal was provided.  Neto was appointed to the position in January 2020.  This comes a day after Interior Minister Amade Miquidade was removed from his position. President Nyusi during the closing ceremony of a military training he was attending on Wednesday said that a "restructuring" of the Defense and Security Forces was ongoing in order to "strengthen the nucleus" of gains recently made in Cabo Delgado in the fight against the insurgency.  Nyusi did not directly refer to Neto or Miquidade in this speech.  Miquidade's Interior Ministry and then Neto's Defense Ministry had respectively taken charge of the government's fight against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado; both saw dramatic reversals at the hands of the insurgents between January 2020 and July 2021 when the Rwandan intervention in Cabo Delgado began.  These defeats may have potentially contributed to the ongoing tumult in Mozambique's cabinet.

Pro-government militia on the evening of 10 November were reported to have ambushed an insurgent force near Chai, killing 6 militants. This group of insurgents earlier in the day had raided V Congresso Village further south along the N380 road, killing two people. Militants were believed to be returning to bush camp areas along the Messalo River. Security forces recovered goods insurgents had looted in the attack earlier in the day. It was unclear if any insurgents escaped this ambush.  One source later reported 1 soldier killed and three injured in this fighting.

IS media claimed a clash between IS militants (ISCAP) and a Mozambican army patrol took place in Ngongo village, Nangade region, on 10 November. This clash reportedly left a member of the army dead. Ngongo may refer to Ngongo village east of Nangade town, or to Ngangolo just south of Litingina.  This report is unconfirmed.  Note that another source reported this attack as having occurred at "Ligogo", which could refer to Lijungo/Liyungo village near Nkonga in Nangade.

On 10 November, IS media reported that a clash between IS militants (ISCAP) and a Mozambican army patrol occurred in the village of Moihi, possibly referring to the village of Muadi in the Nangade region, which led to the soldiers fleeing.  This report is currently unconfirmed.

IS media (ISCAP) claimed to have killed a spy for the Mozambican army in the village of Kent in the Macomia region on 10 November.  This claim likely referred to a militant attack on V Congresso / Quinto Congresso on Wednesday morning.

15 insurgents carrying AK-47 and machetes attacked Mahipa village in south Cabo Delgado in the early hours of 2 November. They managed to take 300,000 metical and unspecified amount of US dollars. This attack had not been previously reported, and this attack is significantly outside the area of where insurgent attacks have occurred in the past in Cabo Delgado, casting doubt over this incident.
The Ministry of Health announced 8 new COVID cases and no deaths in Mozambique on 10 November. The ministry added that no patient was discharged from the hospital.

President Filipe Nyusi announced on 10 November that the defense and security forces are undergoing a restructuring process, aiming to ensure the enduring defeat of the insurgents in Cabo Delgado. This announcement was made just before the government announced the removal of Def Min Neto from his position later that day.

On 10 November, FRELIMO Party Secretary-General Roque Silva revealed at a national meeting to assess performance of FRELIMO municipalities in Chimoio, Manica, the major problems the municipalities under the party's management are facing. Silva said these problems include unemployment, housing, land use planning and environmental sanitation, in addition to the impact of extreme weather phenomena, the COVID-19 pandemic, terrorist attacks in the north and RENAMO dissident attacks in the central region. Silva added that addressing these problems is the only way to ensure the party win the next municipal elections, noting that voters vote for a party because of their trust the party or candidate could provide solutions to their concerns and challenges.
A report on 10 November indicated that several robbery incidents have been recently reported in Alto-Mae area of Maputo.
A report on 10 November indicated that criminal activity has significantly increased in Polana Canico neighborhood of Maputo recently.

On 9 November, a woman was detained in Gile, Zambezia, for burning down a school in Mocopo, Nahihela, where her husband works as a director. The incident took place following an argument between the couple.
On 9 November, a woman set fire to a school in Mocopo, Nahihela, where her husband works as a director. The incident took place following an argument between the couple. The woman was later arrested.

A report on 10 November indicated that SERNIC units are pursuing a fifth member of a gang responsible for a theft incident at a company in Tchumene, Matola, and a shooting incident with Mozambican Police in the same area on the morning of 8 November.

A Mozambican media source reported on 10 November that 102,893 individuals have received the first dose of Covid-19 vaccines in the country during the last 24 hours through the National Mass Vaccination Campaign. 5,072,810 people have received at least one dose of the vaccine. This brings the total of vaccinated individuals in the country to 2,626,676 since the campaign started in 8 March.

A report on 10 November indicated that in October 2021, a directive was enforced prohibiting health professionals from depriving people access to health services due to their appearance. This came a year after the Ministry of Health issued a circular discouraging health professionals from doing so. These measures followed a research from Citizen's Observatory for Health (OCS) which argued that depriving people access to health centers due to their clothing is a blatant violation to human rights, the Constitution of the Republic of Mozambique, and international treaties protecting human rights.

A truck overturned on the National Road Number 4 in Maputo city on 10 November. The accident resulted in damages to the truck, but did not result in any casualties. The cause of the accident was not specified.
A Bengali man who attempted to apply for a Mozambican Identity Card with a fake birth certificate was arrested in Nampula city on 10 November.

The Ministry of Health announced 11 new COVID cases and no deaths in Mozambique on 9 November. Out of the 11 cases, 6 were recorded in Cabo Delgado, 2 in  Maputo city, and 1 cases each in Nampula, Zambezia and Gaza. The ministry added that 28 people have fully recovered from the infection: 14 in Niassa, 11 in Maputo city, and 3 in Inhambane.

On the afternoon of 11 November, President Nyusi released a statement indicating the appointment of Arsénia Felicidade Félix Massingue as the new Minister of Interior, Cristóvão Artur Chume as the new Minister of Defense, and Constantino Alberto Bacela as the new President for Civil Affairs. This comes a day after the President Nyusi removed Defense Minister Jaime Neto and 2 days after Interior Minister Amade Miquidade was removed from his position as well. General Chume in March of this year was appointed to lead the Mozambican Army, and has emerged this year as the government's leading military figure in the fight against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. His appointment to the Defense Ministry is likely an indication that the military will continue to lead the fight against the insurgency, with the Interior Ministry playing a supporting role. Massingue will be the first Mozambican woman to occupy the Interior Minister position, and was previously National Director of Migration.

On 11 November, UN Special Envoy to Mozambique Mirko Manzoni said that within the next week, the DDR process would resume in Nampula, with around 560 RENAMO militia members in Murrupula to be demobilized.  This includes a group of 26 RENAMO Military Junta dissidents who have agreed to lay down their arms.  When these fighters are demobilized, this will raise the number of RENAMO militia members participating in the process to 3270, or 63% of RENAMO's fighting force.  RENAMO's Murrupula base will also be closed down as part of this phase of the process.  The DDR Process had been paused for almost four months due to a lack of funds.

The SADC Mission in Mozambique (SAMIM) on 11 November released a brief saying on 24 October its troops had launched an operation that had destroyed three insurgent bases north of Lake Nguri and near the River Muera.  8 women and 5 children were also rescued in this operation.  SAMIM troops seized a large weapons cache which included RPG 7 launchers, 60 mm mortars, PKM Machine Guns, AK-47 rifles, and other weaponry.
