PM Carlos Agostinho do Rosario said on 11 November that the Mozambican government would implement  “realistic measures” to protect the population from the impact of oil price hike.  do Rosario added that the government aims to safeguard essential activities to the public, including transport, agricultural, and fishing sectors. He also said that fuel prices are determined by the fluctuating cost of crude oil and its derivatives on the international market.  No specific measures to be enacted however were announced.
A road accident involving two vehicles was recorded in Maxixe on 11 November. The accident caused casualties; however, the exact number is still unknown.
Criminal gangs were reported to have demanded a tax from locals in Chamanculo, attacking some locals who have not paid this tax, sources said on 11 November.

On 11 November, authorities announced that in the last 24 hours, 132,024 people had been vaccinated with the first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine, under the third stage of the National Mass Vaccination Campaign. This increased the number of vaccinated individuals to 5,210,671, while a total of 2,645,158 people have been fully inoculated in the country since the beginning of the vaccination program on 8 March.

Mozambique's attorney-general announced on 11 November that the government would file an appeal to a South African court which recently ruled that former Finance Minister Manuel Chang would be extradited to the United States. This came a day after the SA court changed its initial decision to send Chang back to Mozambique and ruled that he should be sent to the US instead. Both US and Mozambique previously requested Chang's extradition over his alleged role in a $2 billion debt scandal. Notably, Chang has denied any allegations against him.
A man died after his wife doused him with hot water in Tsalala on 11 November. The reason behind the attack was not disclosed.

Traffic Police in Nampula disclosed that 52 people died in 36 road accidents recorded in Nampula province from January to September 2021. The province has seen a decline in year-on-year data; 74 people died in 56 road accidents in the same period in 2020. These accidents usually happen along National Road Number One (EN1) in the Nacaroa area, Netia (Monapo), Santa Filomena (Meconta), Cazuzo (district de Murrupula), Carrapira, on the Rapale/Ribaue section, among others.

A report from 9 November indicated that the rehabilitation of Save bridge stopped has been suspended due to lack of funds and impact of COVID-19 pandemic. The Save River Bridge is part of the N1 road, and the primary road crossing point between Inhambane and Sofala Provinces.  The repair of the bridge, budgeted at 5.9billion meticais ( USD 92 million), is expected to last three years. Authorities announced that the repair will resume as soon as funds are available.
A Mozambican Military officer severely beat a civilian in Nangade town on Monday afternoon, 8 November for allegedly denying him cigarette.

On 11 November, Mozambique and Zimbabwe were reported to have discussed the establishment of a pair of one-stop border posts at Forbes-Machipanda and Nyamapanda-Cuchamano and the construction of a second pipeline from Beira to Mutare and Harare. This development was discussed  during the 12th session of the Joint Permanent Commission on cooperation between Zimbabwe and Mozambique, hosted by the former. Notably, Zimbabwe has proposed to build a second pipeline from Beira to Mutare and on to Harare.  No final agreement is yet in place though a deal on the matter now appears likely.

On 9 November, authorities announced that in the last 24 hours, 94,414 people had been vaccinated with the first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine, under the third stage of the National Mass Vaccination Campaign. This increased the number of vaccinated individuals to 4,954,765, while a total of 2,609,473 people have been fully inoculated in the country since the beginning of the vaccination program on 8 March.

The Ministry of Health announced 20 new COVID cases and zero death in Mozambique on 11 November. Maputo city recorded highest with seven new cases, followed by Gaza and Niassa with four cases each, Sofala-3, and  Inhambane-2 . In the past 24 hours, one person is hospitalized while one was  discharged.

The new president of the Beira Commercial Association (ACB), Felix Machado disclosed on 11 November that the Beira business community is seeking an "urgent review of fees and taxes" saying taxes in Mozambique are too high to allow businesses to develop.

A report on 11 November revealed that only one in 10 displaced families in Cabo Delgado receives adequate food . The reports suggest that 60% of polled families in Cabo Delgado have "poor" food security situation and 27% "on edge", with only 14% of households having an "acceptable" food security status.
Mozambican Government announced on 11 November that it has met international requirements to export diamonds. The country reportedly has diamonds in the provinces of Gaza, Manica, Tete, and Niassa.

Police authorities announced the beginning of the training of a special mixed force of soldiers and police to respond to kidnappings and terrorism in Mozambique at Matalana on 11 November.    The force is being trained by Rwandan military personnel over a six month period.  The force will also be used to combat the drug trade and human trafficking in Mozambique.

14  of the 36 cold storage chambers in Xai Xai Provincial Hospital in Gaza have malfunctioned. The cause of the malfunction is still unknown. Xai-Xai Mayor Emidio Xavier confirmed that a company was contacted and will arrive on Monday to fix the issue.

On 10 November, an Australian company, Battery minerals, was granted by  a mining license to company for work in Balama, Cabo Delgado. This is part of the company’s Balama Central graphite project. Once operational, the company is expected to produce 50,000 tons of graphite concentrate per annum.

Minister of Mineral Resources, Max Tonela, met with a Russian multinational company, Zarubezhneft as the latter expressed intent to explore gas in the country. Other companies, Rozhneft and Gasprom, were also invited to join investment opportunities. Notably, Angoche, in Nampula, could be the new large hydrocarbon exploration zone in Mozambique.

Mozambican Airlines (LAM) announced on 11 November that direct flights between Maputo and Harare will resume on  19 December every Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays.  Passengers are currently allowed to connect from cities such as Beira, Nampula, Tete and Johannesburg .This development will contribute to improving exchanges between Mozambique and Zimbabwe. LAM had previously suspended flights on this route in March 2018.

Three sources on the evening of 12 November reported a group of at least 14 insurgents had attacked the village of Naida village, west of Namatil, in the north of Mueda District near the Rovuma River.  At least one person, a motorbike taxi driver, was reportedly killed in this attack.  The attack reportedly began at about 1800hrs.  Militants reported set fire to homes in the village; no further details regarding this incident are currently available.  This is the furthest west along the Rovuma River that any recent attack has occurred.

On 08 November, Mozambican authorities arrested three officers who were suspected to have directed and/or benefited from bank robberies in Palma in the aftermath of the battle for the town, when soldiers robbed several abandoned banks.  This came after recent reports that 30 soldiers who had participated in the robberies were in prison in Mieze, but no senior officers who had benefited from the robberies had been jailed.  A lieutenant colonel and two majors have been taken into custody, reportedly in Pemba.

Insurgents in an attack on 07 November raided the village of Ntuleni near Olumbe in Palma District, carrying out looting, setting huts on fire, and killing one person.  A joint force of Rwandan and Mozambican troops later arrived at the scene, clashing with the insurgents and killing 9 of them.

Rwandan and Mozambican forces on 07 November attacked a group of insurgents who had raided Ntuleni village near Olumbe, killing 9 of the militants in a gun battle.  It was unclear if any insurgents were able to escape this attack.

On 10 November, insurgents kidnapped a group of women during a raid on V Congresso Village, north of Macomia.  These women later regained their freedom, presumably after the insurgents were attacked near Chai village by security forces.

A group of 13 civilians, including 6 new born babies, escaped from an insurgent base in the Mamadolo area of Macomia and were taken into government custody on 07 November near Chai.  6 of the women are reported to be currently detained in Macomia town, likely on suspicion of supporting the insurgency.

On 10 November, SAMIM and Mozambican troops deployed to V Congresso village after insurgents attacked the area; a helicopter was also deployed to the area.  Conflicting reports later indicated SAMIM forces killed 6 insurgents near Chai, north of V Congresso.  Sources later indicated pro-government militia attacked and killed 6 insurgents in the area.

Insurgents on 10 November reportedly attacked the village of Mueia/Muhia, northwest of Nangade Town, according to a single typically reliable source.  No further detail regarding this attack is currently available.

On 09 November, a motorcycle taxi driver was murdered in the early morning hours by suspects who also stole the victim's motorcycle in Chimoio city.  A spokesman for a motorbike association in Manica said this was the sixth murder of one of the group's members in 2021 in similar robbery incidents.

Medical charity MSF is reported to have recently restarted mobile clinics in Palma town and nearby villages.  MSF is one of the first NGOs to return to Palma district despite the ongoing insurgent threat in the area.

Medical charity MSF was reported on 07 November to have distributed food in Nangade to displaced families; MSF is one of the first NGOs to return to Nangade despite ongoing insurgent attacks in the area.

Four people were killed after a trailer track lost its brake and crashed into the side of the road in Nacala Porto on 12 November. A fire gutted the truck following the accident but was later contained by the rescue teams.

Some state employees, including teachers and nurses, were reported to have returned to Mocimboa da Praia town by 10 November. They traveled to the town by land through Mueda from Pemba.  These are some of the first civilians reportedly allowed to return to the town after it was retaken from insurgents in August.

The Monitoring Forum of the Universal Periodic Review Mechanism of Human Rights in Mozambique (FMMRPU) urged the Mozambican Government on 12 November to create a special court to try human rights violations both by insurgents and security forces in Cabo Delgado province. FMMRPU criticized actions of Mozambican forces who allegedly looted banks during the conflict.

40,000 tons of food products were distributed to various regions in Cabo Delgado on 12 November that were affected by insurgency. This development was reportedly initiated by both the government and private sector ahead of the festive season.

There are currently zero hospitalizations at Polana Canico Hospital in Maputo on 12 November as COVID-19 cases in the country declines. This hospital has been the primary facility in the capital receiving COVID cases.

United Nations Special Envoy to Mozambique, Mirko Manzoni, indicated on 11 November that efforts are underway to process the pension payments of DDR participants. Those who have yet to receive their subsidy from June 2021 until the present will receive their share soon, Manzoni said. He clarified that the pension payment would only last for a year. Beyond this period, the demobilized fighters will no longer receive any pension.
Former President Joaquim Chissano petitioned for road safety in Maputo on 12 November following two major accidents in the last five months which left 50 people killed in Maputo province.
Security forces arrested  suspects on 12 November over alleged involvement in a robbery at Nacala airport.
Security forces arrested three individuals in Chimoio on 12 November over their connections to a murder of a motorcycle driver in the city.

On 12 November, authorities announced that in the last 24 hours, 131,185 people had been vaccinated with the first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine, under the third stage of the National Mass Vaccination Campaign. This increased the number of vaccinated individuals to 5,334,015, while a total of 2,662,225 people have been fully inoculated in the country since the beginning of the vaccination program on 8 March.

During a plenary session in Russia on 12 November, Mozambique was admitted to the Kimberley Process. Kimberly Process is a worldwide mechanism governing the legal sale of diamonds. This came a day after Mozambican Government announced on 11 November that it has met international requirements to export diamonds. The country reportedly has diamonds in the provinces of Gaza, Manica, Tete, and Niassa.

The Ministry of Health announced four new COVID cases and zero death in Mozambique on 12 November. This is the 6th consecutive day the country did not record any COVID-related deaths. Maputo city, Nampula, Tete, and Gaza recorded one new case each . In the past 24 hours, two people were hospitalized while one was  discharged.

Reports on 12 November indicate that President Nyusi never responded to a London court notification regarding his involvement in the case of the hidden debts. Privinvest group lawyer said at a preliminary hearing in London that the deadline for the response was on 11 November. Notably, Privinvest claims that Nyusi allegedly benefited from payments used to fund his election campaign to the 2014 presidential election and played a key role in creating and "subsequent sabotage" of the company's projects in Mozambique. Credit Suisse then asked for access to Nyusi's documents, including bank statements, letters, notes, memos. However, the representative of the Attorney General's Office of the Republic of Mozambique, Joe Smouha, claimed that the documents are subject to "criminal confidentiality."

Authorities announced on 12 November the arrest of two officials and a Mozambican seller at Lebombo port, South Africa/Mozambique border for corruption allegations following long investigation . The officials were reportedly processing passports of people in absences in a bid to prolong their stay in the country.

A group of around 30 insurgents launched an attack in Nanjaba village of Mucojo Administrative Post at around 2100hrs on the night of 12 November . At least seven houses were razed while several food items were stolen. Information on casualties is not available at this time. One source later reported 7 people killed in this attack; one person was shot dead while two others died when their homes were set on fire.  4 other bodies were later discovered in the village as well.  ISCAP later claimed an attack on 12 November on "Nambini", likely referring to this attack, saying its fighters killed 2 civilians who had spied for the Mozambican military.

More than 60 trucks loaded with wood, coming from Tambara, were seen traveling along N6 in the district of Vanduzi, Manica, bound to Beira Port between 5 and 8 November. Reports suggest that Tambara has become the epicenter of uncontrolled logging in Manica province.

A group of insurgents, including several child soldiers, attacked Mocimboa da Rovuma village near Naida village on Friday evening, 12 November. Several houses were looted and set on fire during the attack. Reports indicate that older insurgents were guiding the young militants in attacking villagers.

Zimbabwe and Mozambique have signed two memoranda of understanding to consolidate relations in the labor market and information after the 12th Session of the Joint Permanent Commission on Cooperation on 12 November.

The Islamic State militants resumed reporting its attacks in Cabo Delgado on 12 November following a three-month hiatus. This comes as 16 attacks were reported in the last three days, including several attacks reported in the group's al Naba magazine.  ISCAP also said its silence was attributed to 'technical/technological and operational circumstances.' The group did not elaborate further on the said circumstances.

Militants over the night of 12-13 November attacked Naida, Nambungali, Chitope, and Mocimboa do Rovuma Villages in Northern Mueda, close to the Rovuma River, setting fire to homes, and carrying out looting.  Sources reported at least one civilian killed in Naida; other sources indicated that more people may have been killed in these attacks.

Militants over the night of 12-13 November attacked Naida, Nambungali, Chitope, and Mocimboa do Rovuma Villages in Northern Mueda, close to the Rovuma River, setting fire to homes, and carrying out looting.  Sources reported at least one civilian killed in Naida; other sources indicated that more people may have been killed in these attacks.

Reports on 13 November indicate that Mozambican troops from Mueda town were deployed into villages in the Ngapa area amid several insurgent attacks in the area; at least one helicopter was also deployed in the area.

In Mocimboa do Rovuma, pro-government militia and according to some sources, Mozambican troops responded to a militant attack in the area and clashed with insurgents, killing at least 3 of the militants in fighting on 13 November.  ISCAP claimed to have killed 7 Mozambican soldiers during the encounter.

On 12 November, President Nyusi asked new Defense Minister Cristovao Chume, to lead the fight against insurgency in Cabo Delgado. Meanwhile, newly-appointed Interior Minister Arsenia Massingue was asked to crackdown on corruption and organized crime.

Mozambique received 506,600 doses of vaccines against COVID-19 from France under the COVAX mechanism on 12 November. This comes as  the German government donated 924,000 surgical masks to Mozambican health workers.
On 12 November, Argentina announced its readiness to donate to 450,000 of AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine to Mozambique. This comes as Argentina is also preparing to donate vaccines in Angola.
ISCAP claimed to have killed 7 Mozambican soldiers during a clash around  Mueda on 13 November, likely referring to clashes near N'gapa in Northern Mueda District on Saturday.

The Ministry of Health announced eight new COVID cases and zero death in Mozambique on 13 November. This is the 7th consecutive day the country did not record any COVID-related deaths. Nampula and Zambezia provinces recorded two cases each. In the past 24 hours, five individuals have fully recovered from the virus.

The Minister of State for Mineral Resources and Energy of Qatar, Ahmad Al Sayeg, disclosed on 13 November that Qatar wants to cooperate with Mozambique on working in the hydrocarbon sector. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the plenary meeting of the Kimberley Process in Russia. Minister Al Sayeg  is going to visit Mozambique in 2022 in a bid to fulfill plans for bilateral cooperation.

Mozambique is one of the 34 African countries included on the World Bank and IMF's heavily indebted countries' list, reports disclosed on 13 November. Other heavily indebted countries include: Ghana, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros Islands, Democratic Republic of Congo and Republic of Congo. Others include: Ivory Coast, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Rwanda, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Somalia, Sudan, Tanzania, Togo, Uganda and Zambia. The aim of the initiative is to ensure that no poor country in the world ever faces a debt burden it cannot manage.

The National Authority for Economic Inspection and Food Safety announced on Thursday, 11 November, that  apple-flavored Ceres brand juices in Mozambique were allegedly contaminated by a fungus called Patulin. The selling and consuming of the said product has been banned by the government.  Only 622 out of 2,462 boxes of 200 ml Ceres juice have been removed so far. Patulin is a mycotoxin often found in rotting apples and apple products. It can also occur in various moldy fruits, grains and other foods. The acute symptoms in humans include nausea, gastrointestinal disturbances and vomiting.

A fire gutted at least 37 stalls in the central market of Milange town, Zambezia in the early hours of Saturday, 13 November. No information on casualties. Reports indicate that the fire may have been caused by a short circuit.

President Moon Jae-in and President Nyusi attended a christening ceremony for a floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) facility in South Korea on 15 November, a Coral-Sul floating facility, set to head to Mozambique. The floating facility can process 3.4 million cubic meters of gas per year. The South Korean president said that the platform would expand energy cooperation between the two nations. The ceremony came four years after the Korean shipyard, Samsung Heavy Industries Co., won a USD2.5 billion deal to build the offshore facility.

Zesa Holdings, Zimbabwe’s state power utility will import up to 400 megawatts from Mozambique and Zambia as part of measures to end a debilitating power crisis. This development comes as Zimbabwe is spending up to USD20 million of scarce forex on power imports every month. Zesa executive chairman Sydney Gata accused the Zimbabwe treasury in the delays to sign an independent power producer (IPP) implementation agreement.

Security forces recovered more than 18,000 liters of counterfeit hydraulic oil in Chimoio city on 14 November. Authorities stated that the Pakistan-imported product does not have product information on the manufacturer, origin, among other relevant elements.

The Ministry of Health announced five new COVID cases in Mozambique on 14 November. Two COVID-related deaths were reported after seven days of zero fatalities. Maputo City recorded four new cases and Nampula recorded one. In the past 24 hours, two hospital discharges and one admission were recorded.

The Mozambican government guaranteed at least 50 percent of the necessary funding for the second phase of the presidential initiative known as “Water for Life” (PRAVIDA-II), according to Mozambican Minister of Public Works, Joao Machatine, on Friday 12 November. The project, budgeted at USD 50 million, is scheduled to begin in 2022. This development is part of  the government's initiative to ensure access to clean drinking water by 80 percent of the population  in the urban areas and 73 per cent in the rural areas by 2024.

Authorities are on maximum alert against the possible 4th wave of COVID-19 vaccine, Health Minister Armindo Tiago said on 12 November. The minister reiterated the need to adhere on the protocols, amid the continues decline of COVID-19 cases and related deaths in the country.
Sources stated IDPs fled to Nachitenje village after four villages were attacked by insurgents in Northern Mueda on the afternoon of 13 November.

Insurgent entered the village of Nachitenje on 12 November at around 0900hrs, looting food from the area.  Civilians fled from the town due to this attack.  Sources later reported 3 people were killed in the attack on Nachitenje.  Militants also abducted several people from the village.

A group of 20 insurgents entered the village of Nachitenje on 12 November at around 0900hrs, looting food from the area.  Civilians fled from the town due to this attack.  Sources later reported 3 people were killed in the attack on Nachitenje.

Officials from the National Public Safety Services announced that six individuals were killed due to fires in Zambezia province in the month of October. The fires destroyed four residences, forest, and agricultural areas. The fires have reportedly worsened due to the increase heat periods in the province.

President Nyusi announced during a speech that the government is assessing the “right time” to resume work on LNG projects in Cabo Delgado. Nyusi stated that the government was in contact with the companies discussing the adequate timing for the operations to resume.  Nyusi also said TotalEnergies will certainly return to its project in Cabo Delgado.
Local civil servants conducted a cleanup drive in Mocimboa da Praia on 13 November. The cleanup drive focused on the access roads, public and private infrastructure damaged in insurgent attacks.

Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu announced that the recent operation carried out by Tanzanian military along the border with Mozambique to “restore peace” had been successful, and that insurgents in the area had been "neutralized".  This is the first time the Tanzanian President has spoken publicly on insurgents operating in the area. Suluhu said insurgents had previously been attempting to carry out attacks in Mtwara District.

Residents refused to occupy new homes in Capanga of Moatize district after being evicted from their original homes for coal mining. The evicted locals were given residences at the resettlement area of Mboza and 30,000 meticais as compensation after 10 years.  Residents say homes they have been given are not suitable to live in.

The Ministry of Health announced that 5.6 million individuals have been vaccinated after 34,862 individuals were given their first vaccine dose in the past 24 hours as of 15 November. 2.8 million individuals have been fully vaccinated in the country.

The Mozambican Environmental Quality Control Agency (AQUA) announced that they recovered 7 containers smuggling wood on 15 November.  The containers recovered were part of a consignment of illegally exported wood shipped out of Pemba in December 2020.

Sources stated that as many as 2,000 IDPs were fleeing towards Mueda from northern villages north of Mueda district on the early evening of 13 November. This comes as several villages were attacked by the insurgents. The drivers of the several vehicles were charging around 1000 meticais to the IDPs to obtain a ride away from the areas.  Sources later confirmed that about 2,366 IDPs arrived into the area from Ngapa, Namatil, Naschitenje, Naida, Mocimboa de Rovuma, and Nahamba between 13-15 November.  48% of those who fled the area were children.
A vehicle overturned and collided on the railway bridge along National Road 1 in Vila de Manhica, north of Maputo City, on 13 November. A civilian was killed, and another was injured.
Sources stated that significant numbers of displaced civilians are returning to Muambula AP of Muidumbe district as of 14 November.

The Ministry of Health announced 5 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 15 November. This comes as no new deaths were reported. The cases were recorded as follows; 2 in Nampula, 1 each for Zambezia, Inhambane, and Maputo City.

Armed locals attacked a mobile clinic conducting circumcision services in Moneia in Zambezia province on 11 November.  It was not immediately clear why the attack occurred. The locals were armed with sticks and machetes and destroyed the mobile clinic and medical supplies. Surgical materials and medicine were also stolen from the vehicle.

Strong winds and heavy rainfall during a storm caused power outages in Milange, Mocuba, and Gurue districts of Zambezia on 13 November. Mozambique Electricity announced that a maintenance team was deployed to repair the electrical services.

Heavy rainfall and strong winds during a storm destroyed several public and private infrastructure in Mocuba, Gurue, and Milange districts of Zambezia province on 13 November. The weather has caused power outages in the mentioned districts.  Two children were killed amid this bad weather.
A vehicle collided with a motorcycle, causing a fire in Pemba on the night of 14 November.

ISCAP released several photos showing executed individuals in Mueda district on 14 November in the N'gapa area, claiming to have executed two civilians for spying in the area. This is the first release of photos by group since it released pictures of fighters preparing in Palma this past March. ISCAP also previously claimed a gunfire exchange with the Mozambican military in Mueda the day before on 14 November.
Three vehicles collided with each other along the road in Inharrime district at Chongola village on 15 November. 6 civilians were killed and 28 were injured.

ISCAP claimed responsibility for detaining and executing three suspected to be spies for the Mozambican army in Miangalewa in Muidumbe region on 11 November.  No further details on this unconfirmed incident are currently available.
The National Institute of Statistics (INE) announced that food prices have increased by 12.43% along with the cost of living of 6.42% during the course of the year as of October 2021.
A Cabo Delgado Court sentenced poachers to 20 years in prison for killing a lion at the Niassa Special Reserve on 15 November.  The poachers previously denied the charges against them.
Insurgents reportedly abducted several locals during an attack on Nanjaba village on the evening of 12 November.

Government officials announced on 15 November that smugglers have trafficked around 14 tons of gold and minerals out of Mozambique this 2021. The smuggled minerals and gold were often extracted by small time illegal miners who do not have access to formal markets.

Locals raised concerns over a lack of electricity in Ngolhoza area of Matola which has led to increase criminal activity, reports said on 15 November. Robbery and sexual assault incidents were reportedly increasing in frequency in the neighborhood.

Sources stated that SADC soldiers and Mozambican troops had clashed with insurgents during the attack on villages in Northern Mueda district on 13 November.  Troops attacked insurgents after militants attacked villages in the area. A local association stated that around 25 insurgents were killed in this fighting.  Previously clashes were reported in Mocimboa do Rovuma, though fighting reportedly occurred in other areas of the N'gapa area.

Insurgents in attacks on 12-13 November were reported to have kidnapped several people in Northern Mueda during a series of attacks.  Local sources indicated as many as 40 people were missing from villages around N'gapa.

The Municipality of Pemba issued a statement indicating that all grave burials in Muxara are only to be held from 07:00 to 15:00 except Saturdays for a period of one month. Burials on Saturdays are from 07:00 to 12:00. Any burial beyond the scheduled time would require authorization from the Municipal president and would be charged with a fee. The statement also indicated that visitations would be allowed from 13:30 to 15:00 from Monday to Saturday.

ISCAP issued a statement on 14 November claiming to exchange gunfire with security forces in Mueda district on 12 and 13 November. The militant group claimed that they killed 17 soldiers. The militants claimed that several villages were burned, and ammunition were seized during the clashes. This likely referred to fighting that took place in Mocimboa do Rovuma and other nearby areas over on Saturday.

Vodacom and UNICEF announced that launch of the Internet of Good Things online platform on 16 November. The platform was to enable and improve the lives of the locals in the country. The platform would enable access to health materials free of charge.
An illegal miner was killed after a mine collapsed in Montepuez Ruby Mining area early morning of 11 November in Namanhumbir. Two other miners were injured.

Mozambique Airlines (LAM) announced that they would be resuming flights to Harare, Zimbabwe starting 19 December. The flights would run on Wednesdays, Fridays, and Sundays at around 12:30. While returning flights from Harare to Maputo would be from 14:40.

Officials announced that an American tourist was found dead in a forested area of Panda district west of Inhambane city on 15 November. The victim was identified as 80-year old Clara Ruth Coleman, who was reported lost after she went missing after leaving a group of four other tourists during a wildlife photography trip in the area. The other tourists filed a report with the police leading to the search. Police clarified that the victim had no signs of violence or any animal attack upon recovery of the body. The police also added that an investigation to determine the cause of death had commenced, and called for tourists to be accompanied by guides during tours in unfamiliar areas.  The woman was later reported to have died of natural cases.

A group insurgents on 16 November were reported to have attacked the village of Micomela, northwest of Mueda.  An undetermined number of civilians were killed in the attack.  This report is currently unconfirmed.

The Islamic State's Central Africa Province (ISCAP) claimed responsibility for three suicide bombings conducted in Kampala on 16 November. The bombings were conducted near the Parliament of Uganda and central police station which killed three people.  Since October, at least 3 other bombings have been carried out in Uganda.  These attacks are linked to ISCAP, which also claims attacks in Cabo Delgado.

Unconfirmed reports stated that security forces and pro-government militiamen exchanged gunfire with insurgents in Nova Zambezia and Nova Vida of Macomia district on 10 November.  Troops attacked insurgents in the area after a militant raid on V Congresso village, north of Macomia.

The Ministry of Health announced that 5.7 million individuals were vaccinated in the country as of 17 November. This comes as 132,913 individuals were vaccinated within the past 24 hours.
The governments of Zimbabwe and Rwanda conducted a meeting discussing increasing security in Africa. The two also discussed exchanging information on Cabo Delgado
The Ministry of Health announced 25 new cases and no new related deaths in Mozambique on 16 November. The cases were noted in Nampula with 13 cases and Cabo Delgado with 9 cases.

The Russian government's Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Mikhail Bogdanov on 16 November expressed Russia's willingness to support Mozambique in their fight against terrorism. This could include training for the Mozambican military, and intelligence sharing.  The Russian government also stated that they intend to resolve the issues with VTB in relation with the Hidden Debts case.

Security forces have begun increased security measures against theft, forgery, illegal sales of COVID vaccination cards in Maputo city, a report indicated on 16 November. This comes after a recent case in which a health worker and an intern were arrested for being involved in the illegal sale of ID cards.

SERNIC agents on Monday night in Nampula's Muahivire-Expansao neighborhood intercepted a passenger bus and seized 80 kgs of crystal methamphetamine. Two suspects were also detained in this operation.  The bus was reportedly bound for Maputo.

The African Development Bank approved the grant of 1.5 million USD for the support of women-owned small and medium businesses in Mozambique. The grant will provide assistance to businesses owned by youths projects.

Officials announced that National ID cards were still being sold on the black market to foreigners intending to acquire Mozambican Nationality. This comes as police detained a Bengali citizen attempting to obtain a National ID card in Nampula recently.

The Islamic State's Central Africa Province (ISCAP) released a claim saying on 16 November that its fighters had captured and killed 4 pro-government militia in the Nambuenga/Nambuengli area of Mueda District, about 7 kms south-east of Mueda town.  This report is currently unconfirmed.
Several aid organizations stopped traveling via road to Quissanga from due to the insurgent attacks recently in Macomia district as of 15 November.
Unconfirmed reports stated that insurgents attacked Namatil on 16 November. Casualties and damages were not stated.
Sources stated that the recent insurgent attacks have closed off road access towards northern Mueda to IDP populations based along provincial Cabo Delgado border in Mueda district on 16 November.

The Ministry of Defense and UNICEF announced the launch of a program to prevent recruiting children as soldiers in Manica on 15 November. 100 Mozambican officers are being trained to be able to deal with child soldiers in Cabo Delgado as part of this initiative.

President Nyusi appointed the former Interior Minister Amade Miquidade as the ambassador to Rwanda on 17 November. Miquidade was previously removed from his positions as the Interior Minister the week before.
The Ministry of Health announced 9 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 17 November.  This comes as 7 daily recoveries were recorded. The positive rate has reportedly declined to 5.19%.

Sources stated that the DDR process was set to resume in Namaita area of Nampula on 19 November. The process was expected to have 560 fighters demobilized. The process in the Namaita is expected to last for three weeks and bring the total demobilized fighters up to 3,270.
The Ministry of Health announced that 5.9 million people have been vaccinated against COVID in Mozambique as of 17 November. 141,418 individuals were vaccinated within the past 24 hours.

The World Health Organization (WHO) announced that Mozambique is in the top 10 of countries with the highest premature birth rate in the world. WHO stated that 16.4 out of 100 were premature births. The premature births is the leading cause of death in infants below five years of age.

The National Institute of Statistics (INE) announced that the GDP of Mozambique has grown by 3.36% during the third quarter of 2021. The GDP was noted in the mining industry, agriculture, livestock, hunting, and forestry industries.
The Maputo Municipality has said that public transport tariffs will likely increase by 2-3 meticais.  This price increase has not yet been finalized.

The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) announced that they stopped 13 wedding parties during operations in the cities of Beira, Maputo, Matola, and Nampula.  Parties shut down were not observing anti-COVID measures.
The Nampula RENAMO Chief Magibire stated on 15 November that the DDR subsidies were set to resume “soon”.  Some DDR participants have said they have not received subsidies for months.
Locals doused a vehicle that caught on fire along Avenida 25 de Setembro in Maputo City on 16 November. No casualties were reported.
To date there have been 77 claims of attacks by ISCAP in Mozambique.  This is compared to 213 claims in DRC, 3 claimed attacks in Uganda, and 2 claimed attacks in Tanzania.

Sources stated that joint forces exchanged gunfire with insurgents at Samora Machel village of Nangade district on 10 November after militants had attacked Lijungo village. Three insurgents were killed.
Joint units of SAMIM and Mozambican military ambushed and exchanged gunfire with insurgents in Mandimba Village, northeast of Nangade District, on 9 November. Four insurgents were killed.

Pro-government militiamen killed four suspected individuals linked with insurgents in V Congresso village, north of Macomia, on 12 November. No further details are currently available regarding this report.

ISCAP claimed that on 24 July its fighters had clashed with troops at Awasse of the “African Crusader Coalition”. ISCAP stated that the clashes were in defense of Awasse and that they inflicted significant casualties on security forces.  This likely refers to reported clashes between 22-26 July in Awasse as troops advanced towards MDP town.

ISCAP on 29 July claimed its fighters exchanged gunfire with Joint forces of the Mozambican military and Rwandan forces in Namalala, north of Mocimboa da Praia, on 29 July. Casualties were reported, but specific numbers were not mentioned.

ISCAP claimed that on 04 August, insurgents ambushed joint forces in clashes in Unidade Village, north of Mocimboa da Praia. Joint forces casualties were reported along with the destroyed an armored vehicle. No specific details were mentioned regarding the numbers of the casualties.

ISCAP on 20 August claimed its fighters attacked SAMIM forces in Naquitengue, near Mbau, on 20 August. The group said several SAMIM troops were killed and other wounded, and that SAMIM vehicles destroyed.  Note this may refer to a previously reported battle in the area between Rwandan troops and insurgents in which 13 insurgents were reportedly killed.

ISCAP claimed that on 21 August, the group had detonated an IED targeting security forces along a road near Ichitonda, likely Chitunda on 21 August. The blast destroyed two armored vehicles and killed several soldiers.  This report is unconfirmed.
ISCAP claimed its fighters had ambushed government forces along a road in the south of Mocimboa da Praia on 1 September, killing several soldiers.  This report is unconfirmed.

ISCAP claimed its fighters detonated an IED targeting government security forces and later ambushing them with gunfire on road near Mbau on 5 September.  This may refer to a 12 September incident in which Rwandan forces were targeted by an IED in the Mbau area, though this is not confirmed.

ISCAP claimed its fighters had ambushed security forces on a road in Southern Mocimboa da Praia on 7 September. The group said many soldiers were killed in this attack.

ISCAP claimed that the group's fighters had targeted a military barracks on the outskirts of Mocimboa da Praia on 20 September in an assault. Several soldiers were killed and their weapons were seized.  This report is unconfirmed.
ISCAP claimed its fighters had killed a civilian in Quiterajo AP on 28 September.

ISCAP on 02 October claimed that government troops had attempted to ambush insurgents in Southern MDP District, but that insurgents had inflicted casualties on security forces.  This may refer to a Mozambican police ambush of militants in Southern MDP on 06 October, though this is not confirmed.

ISCAP on claimed that on 13 October, insurgents clashed with security forces near Namande of Muidumbe District on 13 October. The clashes extended into the following day, with several security forces reportedly killed.

ISCAP claimed on 11 November that militants had clashed with Mozambican military units in Chai, killing 1 soldier.  This likely referred to confirmed clashes in the area in which pro-government militia were reported to have killed at least 6 militants on 10 November.

Officials announced 5 deaths related to intense rainfall and strong winds in Zambezia province on 12 to 15 November. This included 2 deaths in Molumbo District, two in Mocuba District, and 1 in Maganja da Costa District. The rainfall in the province also reportedly caused damages in the area.

Officials announced that there are 925 illegal mining sites in Mozambique that are used by locals and foreign nationals in a 18 November report. The Ministry of Mineral Resources and Energy official Fernando Maguene stated that the government is losing money due to the illegal mining in the country. Maguene also added that solutions are being developed to fight illegal mining in the country.

The Zambezia Government stated that Chinde village is being threatened with erosion due to the location of the village being near the sea. The local government is determining procedures on how to intervene and prevent further erosion in the area.

Two vehicles collided with each other along Avenida Chissano in Maputo City on the afternoon of 17 November at around 1700hrs. One of the vehicle was from the National Penitentiary Service (SERNAP). Three prisoners being transported were injured during the incident.

Officials announced that operations have cleared around 3,000 snares set by poachers inside and outside of the Maputo Special Reserve over the past four years.  The operation also included increased security patrols to prevent any threats from wildlife towards nearby civilian villages and to prevent any possible poaching.

South African troops part of the SAMIM force in Cabo Delgado recently complained that they had been served "rotten food" over a several day period recently with no fresh food delivered due to a logistics issue.  Several soldiers developed diarrhea due to eating spoiled meat and vegetables.  Soldiers have complained to their officers over this situation.  SAMIM troops in Macomia have also called for a psychologist to be sent to the town to treat troops, and to "see the living conditions of the Special Forces"

President Nyusi gave a speech on 18 November saying that criminal activity including piracy and trafficking was a significant threat to Mozambique's blue economy, speaking at the 2nd International Conference of Crescendo Azul in Inhambane.
AFRICOM US Commander Townsend visited Maputo from 16-18 November, saying he was discussing Mozambique and the US's shared security challenges with the government's security leaders.

The National Roads Administration announced the prohibition of transporting logs along National Roads from 18:00 to 05:00 starting 18 November. This directive is meant to crack down on ongoing illegal logging and the trafficking of illegally logged lumber.
Police announced that an illegal miner was killed after an illegal mine collapsed in Memba district, on Nampula on 18 November.
Police arrested a man for illegally accessing the basic police training in Maputo City on 18 November. The suspect was disguised as a police officer.
The Ministry of Health announced six new COVID cases in Mozambique on 18 November. The cases were recorded as follows: Two in Zambezia, two in Gaza, and two in Maputo City.

The Ministry of Health announced that 5,998,068 people had received one shot of the vaccine, and that 3,095,180 people have been fully vaccinated in Mozambique as of 18 November.  67,052 more people had been vaccinated by the end of 18 November.

The Ministry of Health announced that the Mass Vaccination Campaign against COVID-19 will be extended until 20 December. The ministry said they will prioritize providing second shots to individuals who have already received their first shot.

Insurgents attacked the village of 5 Congresso/ V Congresso village, north of Macomia, on the morning of Friday, 19 November. Sources later said at least 4 people were killed, with at least 2 people beheaded in the attack.  Most of the village was also set on fire in the raid.  Unconfirmed reports indicated that pro-government militia were clashing with insurgents in the area in response to the attack. Locals from Nova Zambezia reportedly heard the gunshots and fled into the bush.
Pro-government militia reportedly clashed with insurgents at V Congresso on 19 November after a new militant attack on the village.  No further details are currently available.
Civilians in Nova Zambezia on 19 November heard gunshots coming from the V Congresso area, and fled into the bush fearing a new insurgent attack.

On 19 November, clashes were reported in the Ninga area in North-West Mueda between insurgents on one side and Mozambican soldiers and Tanzanian SAMIM forces on the other.  Sources reported that at least 12 insurgents were killed in these clashes.

Police arrested 3 murder suspects arrested in Dondo, northwest of Beira on 18 November. The suspects previously were involved with the death of a motorbike taxi driver. Police were conducting a search for a fourth suspect.
Four armed men murdered a motorcycle taxi driver in Dondo, northwest of Beira on or before 18 November. Police responded and detained 3 of the suspects.
A car collided with a minibus along N1 Road in Pateque area in Manhica on 19 November. A civilian was killed, and 13 others were injured.  A second person later died of their injuries.
The Ministry of Health announced 5 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 19 November. This comes as there were no related deaths for the past 4 days.

Security forces exchanged gunfire with insurgents in Nangade district on 19 November, Def Min Cristovao Chume announced. The security officials stated that 2 insurgents were killed and 10 others injured. It was unclear where these clashes took place.
The Minister of Defense Cristovao Chume acknowledged the continuation of small-scale insurgent attacks by insurgents in different areas of Cabo Delgado despite ongoing joint force operations.

The Ministry of Health announced that 59,558 individuals were vaccinated as of 19 November. This comes as 3.2 million individuals have completed their vaccinations in the country, with 6,057,629 people having received at least 1 shot.

The Minister of Defense Chume stated that an investigation is ongoing regarding the soldiers who robbed the banks in Palma. Neto clarified that 20 of the soldiers were still in prison for these robberies.

A double cab pickup truck collided with a police vehicle along the bridge of Maputo-Katembe Bridge, south of Maputo City, on the afternoon of 19 November. Three were injured, including the police officer who was driving the vehicle.

The Kenyan President Kenyatta signed an MOU with President Nyusi  on General Cooperation at a conference held in Vilankulos of Inhambane on 18 November. Further details regarding the MOU were not immediately available.

Pro-government militiamen detained 3 suspects arrested in Litingina village of Nangade District on or around 12 November. The three people arrested were suspected to have provided information to insurgents about the movements of militia and SAMIM troops in the area.
An armed woman slashed the hand of a woman who was having an affair with her husband due to a crime of passion in Rotanda, southwest of Chimoio, on 19 November.
Police announced that increase in security to along Eduardo Mondlane Avenida of Maputo City to minimize theft incidents.
Sources stated that civilians were reported to be fleeing the Negomano area due to reports of insurgents approaching the area on 19 November.
Sources on 18 November reported insurgents were present in the Quelimane, Matiu, and Micomela areas of Mueda District.

Sources stated that private security company employees in Mozambique are paid poor wages and more than 80% of these companies in the country do not contribute to the Social Security System. A Private Security Companies Union official, Sibinde, stated that 240 national private security companies regularly violate employment and tax laws.

The South African National Defense forces issued a statement acknowledging the logistical challenges in providing rations for deployed troops in Cabo Delgado. The SADC stated that rations provided between 20 and 24 October were spoilt after their mobile pantry broke down. The SADC bought two freezers and replaced the spoilt rations.

Local fishermen stated that fish are increasingly scarce along the coast of Inhambane province. Fishermen stated that locals have contributed to this scarcity as they have begun fishing due to the lack of tourism in the area due to COVID.

RENAMO Secretary General Madjibire said on 19 November that RENAMO former militia members were being intimidated by FRELIMO members and police in Buzi and Chibabava. The former RENAMO guerrillas are reportedly living in fear of being targeted by security forces and government security forces.

RENAMO Secretary General Madjibire condemned that the RENAMO former militia were being intimidated by FRELIMO members and police in Buzi and Chibabava. The former RENAMO guerrillas were reportedly living in fear and were experiencing social exclusion.
South African Airways announced the cancellation of daily flights to Maputo from South Africa starting in December. The removal of the flights was due to the lack of demand for this route.
A 50-yr-old Mozambican Police District Commandant was shot dead by another officer in his house in Mopeia, Zambezia, around 21:00 on 20 November. The reason behind the murder is currently unknown.

28 illegal immigrants were arrested and denied visas after arriving at the Chingodzi Airport in Tete City on 19 November. The group included 20 US citizens, 6 Ukrainians, and 2 Russians, including 4 minors. The immigrants are awaiting a return trip to their places of origin, which is expected on Monday, 22 November.  The group allegedly "carried out religious activities" previously in the Cateme area.

Mozambique is set to receive on 22 November over 840,000 doses of COVID-19 vaccines, under the COVAX initiative, made available by the US, according to a report on Sunday, 21 November. The vaccines, which are single-dose immunizations, add to a total of 5 million vaccines received through the support of various partners in Mozambique.

11 new COVID cases were reported by the Ministry of Health on 20 November, bringing the total number of infections to 151,488. Cabo Delgado province and Maputo City recorded the highest number of infections, with three cases each. In the last 24 hours, there were also 4 discharged and 3 newly admitted patients, increasing the total hospitalized patients to 7,043, of which 6 are still hospitalized. Meanwhile, no new recoveries and deaths were recorded. Thus, the cumulative number of recoveries remains at 149,419; and deaths at 1,936. In all, there are 129 active cases in the country.

317 Mozambicans were deported from South Africa between 6 and 12 November, of which 296 deportations were due to illegal immigration, 17 for theft, 2 for physical assault, and 2 for drug trafficking. This was announced by the National Migration Service in a report on 20 November. This is a persistent issue due to the high levels of poverty in Mozambique.

Maputo City will host the International Conference on Extractive Industry on 22 and 23 November, aiming to reflect on the gains arising from exploited extractive resources, revenue management challenges, and the role of actors and gender issues. The conference, announced in a report on 20 November, will be attended by Mozambican parliamentarians, Southern African Development Community (SADC) politicians, and other experts.

A car fell into a hole on Avenida Vladimir Lenine, Maputo City, during the early hours of Sunday, 21 November. The hole was not visible due to flooding in the area. It is unclear whether there were casualties.

Mozambique Transport and Communications Deputy Minister Manuela Joaquim announced that roadside alcohol tests, which were suspended due to Covid-19, will resume in the country per a report on 21 November. She noted that the test is the only way to reduce accidents caused by alcohol-induced drivers.

The Islamic State's Central Africa Province (ISCAP) on 19 November claimed an attack at Chacamba 2/ Migracao, saying the group's fighters had set 8 houses on fire in the area, and clashed with Mozambican army units, forcing security forces to retreat from the town.  One other source also reproted this attack, saying insurgents had set fire to homes in the village.  Sources later said 6 homes were set on fire during the attack.

No new COVID infections were reported in the last 24 hours, maintaining the total number of infections to 151,488 as of 21 November. However, 2 deaths were reported the day prior, bringing the total COVID deaths to 1,938. The total cumulative number of inpatients is still 7,043 as no new patients were recorded, 6 of which are still in hospital units. 50% of said patients are in Maputo Province. Also in the said period, there were 18 recoveries, thus the new total recoveries is 149,437 (98.1%). In all, there are 109 active cases in the country.

A water distribution pipeline exploded on Sunday morning, 21 November, at the intersection between Vladimir Lenine and Mao Tse-Tung avenues in Maputo City, which opened a huge crater where a vehicle accidentally fell in that same morning. The company Águas da Região de Maputo arrived after the vehicle had been removed, and they immediately stopped the water supply to investigate and resolve the issue. Amid the disruption, they said that water supply is expected to return on the same day.

column4: Association of Victims of Road Accidents (AMVIRO) president, Alexandre Nhampossa, announced the association's support for the implementation of a national road accident fund which, he said, will contribute to the compensation of road accident victims, as well as preventive actions against accidents. This announcement came on 21 November, which is the World Day in Remembrance of Victims of Road Accidents.  More than 50% of road accidents that occurred in Maputo City in 2021 were pedestrians being run over, per AMVIRO data estimate.

Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM) head of parliamentary bench, Lutero Simango, said that MDM is dying, and that he is the only one capable to lead it through the political crisis, per a report on Sunday, 21 November. This comes as MDM delegates vote on their next leader at the party's third congress in December. Previously on 29 September, Lutero announced he was running for leadership to succeed his late brother Daviz Simango, who died of COVID-19 in February. Lutero is running against José Domingos, current secretary general of the party, and Silvério Ronguane, deputy of the third political force with a parliamentary seat in Mozambique.

Insurgents in the early morning hours of 21 November attacked Chacamba 1 village, about 14 airline kms from Nangade town.  Militants set fire to several huts, in the town and carried out looting.  Unconfirmed reports indicated militants briefly abducted children in the area and forced them to point out homes that had food or valuables.  Residents fled from the area, but returned to the village by Monday after security forces deployed to the area.  No clashes were reported at the village.

Security forces deployed to the Chacamba area by 21 November after a militant attack in the area before, allowing the return of civilians to the area.  No clashes were reported, with insurgents presuming to have withdrawn from the area.

Mozambique President Filipe Nyusi visited Malawi at the invitation of Malawi President Lazarus Chakwera on Monday, 22 November. The meeting will assess the current stage of cooperation between the two nations in the political, economic, social, and cultural areas.

Civil servants continue to return to Mocimboa da Praia, Cabo Delgado, per a report on 22 November. There is still no economic activity and no government sources in the town, however, electricity, water, and security have all been restored.

Police in Niassa shot and arrested a Malawian in possession of two rhinoceros horns in Congerenge, Mandimba district, Niassa, according to a report on 22 November. The accused claimed that he was persuaded by his brother to broker the sale of rhino horns. Police are still working on pursuing 5 other members of the gang who were with the accused at the time of the shooting.

On Thursday, 18 November, UNICEF warned that it needs 55.7M US dollars to continue providing aid to children and their caregivers in Mozambique. In a revision made in June, they appealed for 96.5M due to the escalating needs, particularly in Cabo Delgado where Islamist terrorists have chased people from their homes, farms, and workplaces. However, only 27.5M in donations was received by end of October which, together with a 13.3M carry-forward, leaves a 58% funding gap.

In a report on 20 November, the National Commission for Human Rights (CNDH) expressed its concern for new HIV/AIDS infections in prisoners in Tete province, likely transmitted through unprotected sex and via shared instruments used by those drug-dependent. CDNH president added that 30% of new infections come from this group.

At least 2 died and 39 injured in a car accident in Milange district, Zambezia, on Saturday, 20 November, when a truck carrying Seventh Day Church-goers slipped and overturned in an aqueduct. The truck was reportedly making way for another car that was coming in front of it and the road was narrow with a slight elevation, which factored in on the accident.

Strong winds destroyed 56 homes in the districts of Guijá, Chigubo, and Chicualacuala, as well as a maternity hospital and an educational establishment, in Gaza province on Thursday, 18 November. Surveys are still being carried out to determine the true level of damage.

On Monday, 22 November, the Ministry of Health announced 4 people tested positive for Covid-19, all in Maputo city, and 23 people recovered in the last 2 days. The record of recoveries is 98.1% of the total cases since the beginning of the pandemic in the country. No death and no new admissions or discharges were reported; 4 remain in isolation centers. The updated cumulative total cases as of 22 November are: 151,492 positive; 149,460 recoveries; 1,938 deaths; 7,043 admissions; and 90 active cases. In the same 2-day period, 16,459 people were vaccinated, raising the total cumulative vaccinations to 6,190,927, of which, 3,372,361 have been fully vaccinated.

Zimbabwean businesswoman and her sister who went missing nearly 8 months ago in Palma, Cabo Delgado, during the insurgent attack on the town on 27 March, are believed to still be held by said insurgents. Their family continues to plead with the Mozambique and Zimbabwe governments to facilitate the two's safe release.

A soldier of the Defense and Security Forces (FDS) shot and injured local pro-gov't militia member in the village of Ndenganamade in Nangade, Cabo Delgado, on 15 November, after a dispute between the two. The victim had reportedly crossed paths with a group of 3 soldiers when he was shot by 1 of them.

Pro-gov militia repelled an alleged attack by insurgents against a camp owned by the company that is building the Mueda-Negomano road, in Cabo Delgado, on Saturday morning, 21 November. It was not immediately clear where this clash occurred.

An individual was arrested after being spotted with an AK-47 containing 57 ammunition at the Ressano Garcia-South Africa Border, Moamba, Maputo province on 20 November. No further details regarding this incident are currently available.

A fire broke out at the Petroda fuel tanks in the Beira port precinct, Sofala province, around 1430hrs on Sunday, 21 November. The fire was quickly contained by firefighters, although the cause was not disclosed. Petroda owners said a statement will be released on Monday, 22 November.

3,511 people in the tourism sector lost their jobs due to border closures from containing the spread of Covid-19, per a report on 22 November. Ministry of Culture & Tourism data indicate that of the 6,784 tourism establishments in the country, which includes hotels (2,462), restaurants & bars (3,986), and travel agencies (336), 696 were closed due to the pandemic. In Maputo city and Inhambane province alone, 155 hotels, 484 food & beverage companies, 12 travel agencies, and 45 dance halls were closed.

On 23 November, the SADC's Mozambique Mission (SAMIM) issued a statement saying its forces alongside Mozambican troops had killed 9 insurgent fighters in clashes in "the general area" of Macomia district on 18 November.  Another source reported these clashes took place in the Bolela area, along the Mucojo-Macomia road.  In these clashes, an insurgent leader identified as Abu Quitail was reportedly killed.  SAMIM also said  no security force casualties were reported.

In a second clash on 18 November in the Ninga area of Nangade (likely referring to Nenge, west of Litingina, or Nhanga, south-west of Litigina) two insurgents were killed.  An insurgent base near Ninga was also captured and destroyed.  No security force casualties were reported.  RPG 7 launchers, PKM machine guns, and AK47s, grenades, and electronic devices were also seized in these operations.

Mozambique's GDP has increased by 1.78% so far in 2021 according to the National Statistics Institute (INE) on 17 November. INE stated that the increase was noted after the third quarter GDP was recorded at 3.36%.

Officials announced the start of the DDR process in Cazuzu in Murrupula on the morning of 23 November. The DDR process in the area was expected to demobilize 587 former RENAMO guerillas The start of the process was attended by high ranking RENAMO officials including RENAMO representative on the Military Affairs Committee Andre Magibire, Secretary of State in Nampula province, and the Government Representative on the Military Affairs Committee.

A Tripartite Interim Agreement  between Mozambique, South African, and Kingdom of Swaziland was signed regarding the sharing of the watercourses on 18 November. The countries will ensure protection and utilization of the water resources between the three countries.

Officials announced on 22 November that the government is considering reopening beaches during the holiday season. The proposal was to be handed over to the Council of Ministers. The reopening will be based on the behavior of the beach goers; COVID rates across the country remain low though beaches were previously closed due to large crowds at beaches not observing social distancing.

The Ministers of the Mozambican and Portuguese Foreign Affairs and Cooperation signed an agreement regarding the Strategic Program for Cooperation Mozambique on 22 November. The agreement includes the donation of 80 million EUR within the next five years to Mozambique from 2022-2026.

The EU Council announced that they will provide 40 million EUR as support to Mozambican Military as part of the training program and mission by EU. The financial assistance was to provide cash to purchase equipment required by the Mozambican military.

The Ministry of Health announced that 6.19 million individuals have received at least one shot of the COVID vaccine in Mozambique as of 22 November. This comes as 16,459 individuals were vaccinated within the past 24 hours.  3.3 million have been fully vaccinated.

The Ministry of Health recorded three new COVID cases and a single related death in Mozambique on 23 November. This comes as the new cases were recorded in Sofala, Nampula and Maputo City with one case each.

The Human Rights Defenders Network stated that police arrested four rights activists in Moatize of Tete province on the afternoon of 20 November. The activists were identified as Joao Samuel Sipriqui, Tomo Joao Tomo, Maxwell Abreu, and Lucidio Torres Cassicassica. The arrest was conducted during a neighborhood meeting in the area to discuss ways to put pressure on mining company Vale to implement environmental pollution reduction measures in the area.  The group on 23 November were reportedly released.

Officials announced on 23 November that enrollment rates have seen a decline by more than 50% for 1st grade students in the country. 493,113 children out of the expected 1,300,000 have been registered for first grade classes.

The Ministry of Health announced 6.25 million individuals have received at least one COVID shot in Mozambique as of 23 November. This comes as 62,469 individuals were vaccinated within the past 24 hours.  3.44 million people have been fully vaccinated in the country.

A Zambezia anti-corruption office opened in Quelimane on 23 November. The anti-corruption was set to tackle corruption cases that had previously been forwarded to Nampula province. Over 140 corruption cases have been reported in the province this year.

The Kenyan High Commission announced the opening of their office in Maputo on 20 November. This comes as the Kenyan government recently signed an agreement with the Mozambican government to strengthen bilateral relations.
An armed man murdered a civilian in Mutanhana of Marracuene District on 22 November; further information on this incident is not currently available.
Zimbabwe Foreign Affairs and Trade Minister Ambassador Frederick Shava stated that the trade between Zimbabwe and Mozambique has increased during the 2020 to approximately 534million USD.
Police officials announced that a group of 1,500 new police will be deployed to Nampula to areas where insurgent recruiters are currently active.

Mozambique officials announced that 23 illegal immigrants were detained in Moatize of Tete province on the night of 21 November. Among those arrested were 18 Pakistani nationals and 5 Bangladeshis.

President Nyusi and Malawian President Chakwera on 23 November met to launch the Mozambique-Malawi interconnection project. The project is expected supply 50megawatts to Malawi would include the construction 400kv Matambo substation in Tete.

As of 24 November, money transfer company, Western Union has suspended its services in Cabo Delgado province.  It is unclear exactly when this suspension was instituted, though the company has confirmed a halt in its services in the province.  The company said it makes these kinds of decisions "based on a risk assessment of our products and services, our consumers and our agents, and where we do business", also indicating it would resume operations in the province when it is able to do so responsibly.  This suspension is presumed to be as part of efforts to cut off a potential financial stream to the insurgency.

State power company EDM in a 24 November press release said that on 22 November, it had successfully restored power in Muidumbe District, the last district that had still been without power due to insurgent attacks.  Muidumbe, along with MDP, Nangade, Mueda, and Palma Districts had all lost power in August of 2020 after insurgents destroyed the Awasse power sub-station.  Power was restored in Mueda on 03 September, in MDP on 11 September, in Nangade on 27 September, and in Palma on 08 October.

Security officials announced that security measures will be increased at Ressano Garcia during the holiday season. The security officials stated that the movement of people is expected to increase coming from South Africa during the holiday season. The migration booths are to be increased from 18 to 229 for the season.
The Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) announced that the mega projects from various sectors of the economy have increased by 48.1% or 21.8 billion meticais for 2021 in comparison to 2020.

Sources issued a report stating that drug smuggling groups working in the Nacala area are using Fernao Veloso beach to import and export narcotics, typically operating after midnight to avoid security. Energy Company Galp stated the company continuing to invest in Mozambique is contingent on "last peace and well being" in the country, saying if these conditions are met, the company will "continue to invest a lot of money" in the country to create jobs.

The UK government announced that it has begun accepting Mozambican vaccination cards as proof of COVID vaccinations to travel to UK. The UK previously mark Mozambique as a red list, indicating that the country has a high number of COVID cases and prevented travel without a COVID PCR Test and quarantine.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) conducted talks with the Mozambican government regarding a long-term financial program on 24 November. The program was to assist the country with the effects of COVID.  The IMF suspended regular support to the country in 2016 due to the Hideen Debts Case, though lent the country over 100 million euros in 2019 after Cyclones Idai and Kenneth impacted the country.  The IMF has also provided over 560 million Euros to Mozambique to combat the impacts of COVID.

A consultant company stated that Mozambique is expected to reach 2% GDP growth by the end of 2021. This comes as the economy of the country has seen an increase this past 2nd quarter as 3.3% GDP was reported.

The Director of Corporate Affairs at Mozal, an aluminum company on 24 October assured the local community that the dust emitted by a company factory in Boane is not poisonous. This comes as locals complained that white powder coming from the factory was blowing into their communities.
Security forces detained two suspects involved in stealing computers from the Massangena District Secretary in Gaza on 24 November.
An armed man set residence on fire with his wife inside in Marracuene District on 24 November.

Police arrested the mastermind of a child murder in Gile District on 24 November. The suspect previously arranged the beheading of a child for a ritual.  Two other people were previously arrested for this incident.

Malawi and Mozambique governments signed an agreement regarding cooperation between the two on 23 November. The agreements will create cooperation on trade and mineral resources, while the two will also set up a one-stop border crossing between the two countries.

Galp officials have raised concerns that China may replace western companies and governments in financing oil and gas projects in Mozambique and other countries. Galp officials stated that China is in the midst of replacing coal with gas, and may be interested in new investments in LNG>
President Nyusi ordered resumption of ferry services to Malawi across Niassa Lake on 24 November.  The ferry has not operated for two years due to COVID-19 restrictions.

The Ministry of Health announced eight new COVID cases and a single related death in Mozambique on 24 November. The cases were recorded as follows: Maputo City with seven of the new cases and one in Niassa province.
Police arrested a group of suspects for vehicle theft in Maputo City on 24 November. The suspects were targeting vehicle accessories in their thefts.

The Ministry of Health announced that the National Mass Vaccination has vaccinated 113,394 individuals on 24 November. This brings the fully vaccinated to 3.5 million individuals. 6.2 million people have received at least one shot.

Security forces fired warning shots and reportedly assaulted IDPs during a food aid handover in Chiure on 16 November. Security forces detained one of the IDPs, later saying IDPs were stealing food during the distribution.

ISCAP claimed on 16 November that its militants had clashed with the Mozambican military at "Nyida" village, likely referring to Nido village, along the Mueda/MDP border, west of Diaca. The insurgents stated that 7 soldiers were killed during the clash.  This report is unconfirmed.

Around 10 insurgents conducted an attack targeting Maparawe village in Mtwara region of Tanzania on 12 November. The insurgents reportedly carried out looting in the village.  An unknown number of civilians were reportedly killed.

Insurgents raided and attacked the villages of Sindano and Michawe in Mtwara region of Tanzania on 13 November, carrying out looting and killing at least 3 civilians in these raids. This comes as the insurgents previously attacked Maparawe village in the same region.

Islamic State - Central Africa Province (ISCAP) claimed responsibility for 17 attacks between 11-17 November across DRC, Uganda, and Mozambique.  ISCAP claimed more attacks than any other IS franchise during this time.

In the joint operation, park rangers and police burned charcoal kilns and arrested more than 20 people from the villages of Hochane and Madliwa in the Gerez community area. The villagers blocked the road just outside the park with a large log. Eight interviewees said that the said villagers were unarmed. When the rangers and police stopped their vehicles, four of the villagers walked toward them with their empty hands held high. However, the joint forces suddenly opened fire on the villagers, hitting and killing 6 of them.

This comes following leads from an operation conducted in June of the same year, where 36 kg of drugs were seized in Matibane, Nacala district, with one person arrested at the time.
