This comes following leads from an operation conducted in June of the same year, where 36 kg of drugs were seized in Matibane, Nacala district.
On Monday morning, 22 November, 2 militants and 1 militia died in clashes between insurgent militants and pro-gov militia at Litandacua, Macomia district.

Some local health clinics in Palma District have reportedly refused to provide services to pregnant women fleeing the ongoing conflict in the province.  This is due to ongoing tensions between IDPs and host communities.
The Ministry of Health announced 9 new COVID cases and no new deaths in Mozambique on 25 November. This comes as the cases were noted in mostly in Maputo city with 4 of the new cases.

UK imposed a travel ban on South Africa and five other African countries as part of precautions against the new COVID variant on 25 November. The National Institute for Communicable Diseases stated that 22 new cases of the new variant have been detected in South Africa. The increase in cases in South Africa puts a high risk of the new variant spreading to Mozambique, which may later be included among the placed travel ban in the African countries.

The Minister of Gender, Children and Social Action Mangrasse stated on 25 November that 15,800 individuals were victims of violence. Among the victims, 8,900 women and children were victims of sexual assault. The minister called for sensitizing the general population to increase prevention and reporting of such cases.

The Mozambican Parliament approved a draft law regarding the mandatory notification and creation of an inspection and consultation teams for public healthcare facilities in the country.  The law also allows authorities to sentence those who violate anti-COVID measures to 2 years in prison.

The Ministry of Mineral Resources and Energy of Mozambique announced that the oil and gas companies operation in Rovuma were negotiating new partnerships with the government. The negotiations were to minimize the cost of operations by the oil and gas companies.

The Sustainable Development Fund announced to create a financing window to support local business and communities involved with the logging in Zambezia. The project is meant to minimize the illegal logging and deforestation in the province.

France announced that flights from Mozambique and other African countries have been banned to stop the spread of a new COVID variant found in South Africa.  France also halted flights from South Africa, Lesotho, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Namibia, and Eswatini.

The Italian government has issued a the travel ban on individuals who have traveled in the last two weeks to the 7 African countries including Mozambique on 26 November. This comes as a new COVID variant was identified in South Africa. Italy also stopped flights from South Africa, Lesotho, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Namibia, and Eswatini.
The government of Singapore has issued a ban on seven African countries in response to the new COVID strain on 26 November, including Mozambique.

The Israeli government issued a travel ban on seven African countries after the new COVID variant found in South Africa on 26 November. The countries included were Mozambique, South Africa, Lesotho, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Namibia, and Eswatini.

SENAMI rejected 16 foreigners from entering the country due to the lack of visa and reason for stay during a week-long operation from the 13 to 19 November. This comes as 75 illegal immigrants were repatriated during the operation.

On the evening of 26 November, the US government announced new travel restrictions for Southern African countries, including Mozambique, amid the spread of a new variant of COVID-19, Omicron, in South Africa.  The US has halted travel from Mozambique, South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Lesotho, Eswatini, and Namibia; US citizens and permanent residents are exempted from the ban, but must still test negative for COVID before travelling to the US.  The emergence of this new contagious variant led to the largest fall in the US stock market in 2021 in a single day, underlining apprehension regarding the emergence of the new variant.  The new variant has not yet been confirmed to be present in Mozambique, though multiple cases have been detected in South Africa's Guateng Province, bordering Mozambique.

Germany on 26 November was reported to have banned travelers from Mozambique, as well as from several other Southern African countries, over concerns over the spread of the new omicron variant of COVID.
The Czech Republic on 26 November halted travel from Mozambique and other South African countries over concerns regarding the spread of the new omicron variant of COVID.

The Austrian government has also imposed a travel ban on Mozambique and other Southern African countries over concerns regarding the COVID Omicron variant on 26 November.

Grupo Desportivo Maputo members conducted a protest demanding the removal of a football club president and the board in Maputo on 24 November. The protesters called for a new election of board members. This comes as the club members were not being paid their salaries since this past April.

The exact location of the clashes and the number of casualties is not available at this time, though fighting likely took place in the vicinity of Naulala and Gomba villages, where insurgents were active on 25-26 November.

Qatar Airways will no longer accept passengers from 5 southern African countries, including Mozambique and South Africa; however, it will continue to accept passengers to said countries, per a report on Saturday, 27 November.

Mozambique President Filipe Jacinto Nyusi inaugurated the Chongoene Airport in Gaza province on Monday, 29 November. The airport was reportedly financed by the Chinese government costing USD 60M and has the capacity to receive around 220 thousand passengers yearly.

The Ministry of Health ensures that measures to contain the pandemic will be intensified, including mandatory testing at the borders and reinforcement of vaccination.

The National Institute of Health confirmed there are no confirmed Omicron cases in Mozambique as of Monday, 29 November, after testing all 232 positive Covid-19 cases for the month of November identified so far for the new variant. This is in line with efforts to determine whether the variant had been circulating in the country before its discovery in South Africa.  The Gov't will soon discuss new measures to delay the peak of the variant, which is expected in the months of December 2021 and January 2022.  The report also noted that only mild symptoms and asymptomatic cases have been recorded of the new variant so far, mostly identified from travelers and via contact tracing.

The Ministry of Health announced that as of Monday, 29 November, 422 were tested in the last 24 hours and 4 were positive for Covid-19; 3 in Maputo City and 1 in Maputo Province. 1 death was also recorded the day prior in Maputo Province, while 7 people had recovered. In the same period, there were no hospital discharges, while 2 were hospitalized due to complications. There are currently 3 people in treatment units.  The updated cumulative total cases as of 29 November are: 151,528 positive (of which 151,159 were local transmissions and 369 were imported); 149,492 recoveries; 1,941 deaths; 7,047 admissions; and 91 active cases.

In Italy, a patient coming from Maputo, Mozambique tested positive for the new Omicron variant, per a report on 28 November, making this the first case in Italy.  The man had initially arrived in Italy on 12 November. He had reportedly tested negative in his PCR test before boarding his flight in Maputo.  This comes amid confirmed reports that there are zero cases of the new variant in Mozambique, though this likely indicates the variant was likely present in Mozambique in early November.

Mozambican scientists say that it is unlikely that Italy's first recorded case of the Omicron variant contracted the disease in Maputo, Mozambique. They added that Italian health authorities should be investigating the patient's flight, which arrived in Rome on 12 November.

Portugal guaranteed it would provide repatriation flights for people who want to return to their country from Mozambique and vice versa, beginning Tuesday, 29 November. Per a report on 30 November, Spain will require a 10-day quarantine period for travelers arriving from Mozambique and 6 other countries, over Omicron variant concerns.

A 53-year old man, who had traveled to Mozambique after making a stop-over in South Africa, has tested positive of the Omicron variant in La Reunion, per a report from France on Tuesday, 30 November.  This comes amid confirmed reports the day prior that there are zero cases of the new variant in Mozambique.

The Mozambique Confederation of Economic Associations expressed serious concerns over the shut down of international flights to the country. Per a report on 29 November, the Association said that the country's economy had just started to recover and that this ban due to the recent discovery of the Omicron variant will negatively impact business, entrepreneurs, jobs, and families, alike.
On 29 November, a dead woman wrapped in a plastic bag was found abandoned on the former EN6 in Beira city, Sofala. No details were yet released on the incident.

SAMIM troops were active in the Mandimba area, Niassa province, per a report on 29 November, carrying out humanitarian assistance activities to the local community. Reports on 28 November indicate that former RENAMO militia will begin to receive their life long pensions from January 2022. This comes after a thousand of former Renamo guerrillas earlier this year said they had not received their subsidies for over six months.

Mozambique Navy attempted to seize an industrial fishing boat on 29 November, which was operating illegally in Area 4 of the Rovuma Sedimentary Basin. The Taiwanese flagged vessel was able to escape ultimately.

The Zimbabwe Government announced on 26 November that three of their citizens are still missing in Cabo Delgado following the insurgent attack in Palma last March. The three are believed to have been abducted by insurgents during the attack.
A suspicious fire was reported in an area east of Pundanhar on 28 November.  This could indicate clashes between security forces and insurgents or a new insurgent attack.

On Sunday, 28 November, China and Mozambique pledged to strengthen bilateral cooperation during a meeting held ahead of the Eighth Ministerial Conference of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC). Chinese State Councilor and Foreign Minister Wang Yi commended the joint efforts of both countries on the growth of its economic and trade cooperation despite the COIVD0-19 impact. Mozambican Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation Veronica Macamo said that the Mozambican government is ready to maintain solidarity and coordination on international affairs with China.
Residents in the Zona Verde neighborhood have reported 3 deaths in a week, as well as dozens of physical assaults and robberies, per a report on 29 November.
Defence and Security Forces were deployed in northeast Niassa on 25 November, following insurgent attacks in Gomba village the day prior.

This came amid fears of the spread of the new COVID variant Omicron, which appears to have originated in South Africa.

The claim also said militants had destroyed a military barracks.  This claim corresponds with a recently confirmed attack at Naulala where at least one policeman was killed in an attack on a police station and some locals kidnapped.

Increased fares for public transport in the cities of Maputo and Matola have been postponed until 02 January, after having been initially scheduled to take effect from 01 December. However, operators claim it is still not enough of an increase as it will not offset the increased fuel prices, as well as car repairs for breakdowns often caused by damaged roads in the city.

178,136 people out of a goal of 210,489 have been vaccinated in Maputo City as of 30 November, that is 85% of the targeted number of vaccinations for the 3rd phase, which has been extended until 20 December. Vaccination numbers in recent weeks have dropped with decreasing numbers of unvaccinated people showing up for jabs, and the goal of 210,000 vaccinated in Maputo during the third phase appears unlikely to be met.
On Friday, 26 November, Mozambique received 756,000 doses of Janssen vaccines from the Mastercard Foundation and the African Centre for Disease Control (CDC).

On 30 November, Mozambique announced 85,772 people were vaccinated with the first dose of the COVID vaccine in the last 24 hours. Since the start of the 3rd phase on March 8, Mozambique has given one shot to a total of 6,572,756 people, of which 3,931,200 were fully vaccinated.
Zimbabwe imposed a 14-day mandatory quarantine for all travelers, including returning residents, in a bid to prevent the spread of the Omicron variant in the country, per a report on 30 November.

Argentina imposed a mandatory 14-day quarantine and antigen test upon landing for all passengers who have been anywhere on the African continent within the last 14 days, in a bid to prevent the spread of the Omicron variant in the country. Per a report on 30 November, proof of full vaccination and a negative PCR test done within 72 hours before departure will also be required. Non-citizens and non-residents will also be required to present proof of health insurance covering Covid-19.

Fiji tightened its border restrictions to travelers, banning travel from southern African countries including Mozambique in a bid to prevent the spread of the omicron variant.  Only Fijian citizens are excepted from this rule, and can enter the country from these countries. Upon arrival, citizens will be required to complete a 14-day quarantine, with PCR tests on days 5 and 12, per a report on 30 November.

Beginning 01 December, India will require all travelers, including those from Mozambique, to declare on India's online government portal their 14-day travel history and present a negative PCR test taken within 72 hours prior to their departure. This is in a bid to prevent the spread of the omicron variant, per a report on 30 November.

Japan closed its borders to all non-citizens, which also affects travelers from Mozambique, including international students, short-term residents (except those already in the country), and those visiting family, as of 30 November, in a bid to prevent the spread of the omicron variant.

Long haul passenger trains will resume service beginning 10 December, according to Portos e Caminhos de Ferro de Moçambique (CFM) in a report on 30 November. The resumption will come in phases, starting with the south and center of the country, which is as follows: the Ressano Garcia Line (from Maputo to Moamba), Goba Line (from Maputo to Goba, Limpopo Line (from Maputo to Manhica), and, in the center region, the Sena Line (from Beira to Inhaminga). Resumption for the remaining destinations will depend on the Covid-19 situation in the country.

The Bank of Mozambique has fined 7 credit institutions for failing to comply with requirements to prevent money laundering and terrorism financing, per a report on 30 November.  This was for activities between February 2020 and June 2021. Among the 7 are Banco Commercial e de Investimentos (BCI) and African Banking Corporation (BancABC), with 53M and 64.4M meticais in fines, respectively.

The 1st Squadron of the Mozambique Police detained an individual in Maputo city for pretending to be a customs dispatcher. The individual named Raimundo Antonio Chauque was wearing aTax Authority uniform during his arrest, per a report on 30 November.

Foreigners arriving in Maputo Province must show proof of a full Covid-19 vaccination, while returning citizens must undergo rapid or PCR testing, according to province medical chief Celestina de Canceicao on Saturday, 27 November. In addition, the province has the capacity to follow up on those who test positive and carry out their own tests when needed.

Authorities hope to vaccinate 50% of the population in Mozambique beyond of 2021, according to Health Minister Armindo Tiago in a report on 30 November. He added that the target figure was 17M and to date; about 7M people have at least been partially vaccinated to date.

International Flight update in Mozambique as of 30 November: Ethiopian, Airlink, and LAM airlines from Mozambique continued to operate. Meanwhile, TAP and Qatar airlines have suspended flights from Maputo. In South Africa, KLM and Lufthansa airlines are still flying from O. R. Tambo International Airport. British Airways and Virgin Airlines are currently working to resume direct flights to the UK.

ISCAP claimed to have killed an undisclosed number of Mozambican troops in Chai, Macomia, on 29 November. ISCAP claimed that their fighters managed to return safely to their positions after this unconfirmed attack.
The International Organization for Migration donated six vehicles to the Mozambican police in Cabo Delgado on 27 November.
A fire broke out in an apartment in the Vila Olimpica neighborhood of Zimpeto, Maputo, on Monday morning, 29 November. Residents managed to contain the fire. The cause of the fire is still unknown.

An individual was killed, and three others were injured in a road accident involving two minibuses in the T-3 neighborhood in Matola on Monday morning, 29 November. The accident was reportedly caused by driving under alcohol influence by one of the bus drivers, which resulted in reckless driving.

Mozambique, along with Angola and Zambia, has the highest number of fire outbreaks reported in southern Africa, reports indicated on 27 November. Data shows that 70% of the annual burned area of ​​the entire planet took place in Africa and around 60% of the greenhouse gas emissions resulting from the burning of vegetation.

Residents along the Mozambique - South Africa border near Manguzi have expressed concern on the growing threat of cross-border car theft syndicates along the Mozambique-South Africa border, reports stated on 29 November. They claimed that authorities have failed to provide adequate security in the area to combat these criminal groups. Incidents of car theft and hijackings in Manguzi and surrounding areas are ongoing.

2 South African Infantry Battalion has recently completed training and  is preparing to deploy to Cabo Delgado as part of South African Military Involvement in Mozambique (SAMIM). 2 SAI has recently completed jungle warfare training, as well as counter IED training.

The Ministry of Health announced 20 new COVID cases and zero death in Mozambique on 30 November. Maputo city recorded highest with eight new cases, followed by Maputo Province with seven cases, Gaza with four cases, and Zambezia reported one case. In the past 24 hours, 22 individuals recovered from the virus.

Victims of the Hulene garbage heat collapse staged a protest on 30 November in Maputo city to demand a 6-month rent payment. The group called on the government to adhere to its commitment to provide monthly housing stipends until the houses being built in the Possulane area of Marracuene district are completed. Maputo City Council responded and assured protesters that rent payments would be provided once these funds are released by the government.
Reports on 30 November indicate that unidentified men assaulted students at the Paulo Samuel Kankhomba Secondary School in Chimoio. An investigation is underway to apprehend the suspects.

column4: TAAG Angola Airlines carried out repatriation flights from South Africa, Mozambique and Namibia on Tuesday, 30 November. This development came after Angola announced border closure with seven African countries – South Africa, Botswana, Eswatini, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia and Zimbabwe effective 1 December, in a bid to curb spread of Omicron COVID-19 variant. Reports indicate that TAAG will run a Luanda-Maputo-Luanda link departing at 23:59 and arriving in the Mozambican capital, Maputo City, at 05:00 local time to return passengers.
Security forces five suspected members of a criminal gang, including a security officer, were arrested in Maputo city on 30 November over alleged involvement in various assault and robbery cases.

Reports on 30 November indicate that the Water Supply Investment and Heritage Fund (FIPAG) cut off supply to Central, Mafurreira, Gilo, Lega-Lega and Sikutituno areas in Inhambane for the past three months to force the local government to settle its 2 million meticais debt.  The local government has yet to comment on the matter.

On 01 December, President Nyusi extended Police Commander General Bernardino Rafael's term in office.  Rafael has coordinated the police response to the insurgency in Cabo Delgado.  Rafael has held the position since 2017.

Former President of Mozambique Armando Guebuza was removed from the list of deponents and will no longer testify in the Hidden Debts case, as per a report on 1 December.  Maputo court judge reportedly said there was no evidence Guebuza had received money from Privinvest.  Guebuza's hearing was most anticipated as it would supposedly bring more light to the case, given that the case happened during his regime.  Another source reported Guebuza will still testify, but will be the last witness called in the trial.

Beginning 19 December, Mozambique Airlines will launch three weekly flights between Maputo in Mozambique and Harare in Zimbabwe, which is expected to reduce costs of doing business between said countries, per a report on 1 December.

On Wednesday, 1 December, France announced that only French and EU residents, along with diplomats and flight crews from Mozambique and 9 other southern African countries will be allowed entry to France on flights from Mozambique. However, these travelers must provide a Covid test result that is less than 48 hours old upon arrival, with negative results requiring a 7-day quarantine and positive results requiring a 10-day quarantine.

Portugal announced on Wednesday, 1 December, that flights to and from Mozambique will remain suspended until 9 January and passengers from the said country will be required to produce a negative Covid-19 test and undergo 14 days of quarantine upon arrival.

The Portugal Embassy in Maputo announced on 1 December that two repatriation flights will be carried out from Portugal to Mozambique, scheduled on Friday and Sunday, 3 and 5 December, arriving in Maputo from Lisbon on Saturday and Monday, 4 and 6 December.  The flights serve to support the return of travelers in both directions.

Switzerland will increase financial support for Mozambique, over the next four years, to 1.9B meticais (297M USD at the current exchange rate), for the country's economic development, service delivery, and decentralization. This was announced in Maputo on Wednesday, 1 December, by Swiss Ambassador to Mozambique, Olivier Burki.

Per a report on 1 December, the World Food Program (WFP) said a lack of monetary support continues to limit humanitarian food aid to the 935,000 displaced people and host families in Cabo Delgado, Niassa, and Nampula, who are in need of said aid until at least March 2022.  Currently the WFP is only able to provide about 39% of people's daily needs in food aid.

3 of a group of 5 suspected of fraud were captured in Maputo City by the National Criminal Investigation Service, per a report on 1 December. The gang of 5 is suspected of pocketing millions of meticais from people wanting to buy vehicles.

Fishermen in Angoche area, south of Nampula province, are reportedly smuggling drugs, transporting them with their boats from the sea to the mainland for drug trafficking networks. Per the report on 1 December, this scheme can only be possible with the support of corrupt officials of the local police.  Angoche district remains one of the main entry points for drugs in the country.

Angoche district remains one of the main entry points for drugs in the country.

Around a hundred people, mostly children, were kidnapped in the Naulala area, Niassa province, on 26 November, according to unconfirmed reports.  Two children reportedly escaped.  The alleged terrorists have reportedly moved towards the Lugenda River, along the Cabo Delgado border the following day, 27 November, after exchanging fire with the police in Naulala.

Alleged terrorists have reportedly moved towards the Lugenda River, along the Cabo Delgado border, on 27 November, after exchanging fire with Mozambican Police in the Naulala area, Niassa province.  The terrorists had also kidnapped hundreds of people, mostly children, in Naulala the day prior, per an unconfirmed report.

column4: On 01 December, UN rep to Mozambique Mirko Manzoni said that the last remaining 24 members of the RENAMO Military Junta had been demobilized in the ongoing DDR process in Murrupula District.  Previous reports said the demobilization process was taking place in the Cazuzu area, south-west of Nampula city.  Manzoni said a total of 85 dissident fighters have joined the DDR process to date.  DDR will continue in Murrupula into mid-December; by the end of the year 63% of all of RENAMO's armed forces will have been disarmed and demobilized.
7 insurgents attacked Namunda in northeastern Nangade district, Cabo Delgado, on 26 November, killing one civilian. No further details were provided.
In Niassa province, hundreds of civilians fled to Mecula, after insurgents attacked their village in Naulala on 26 November. The IDPs are reportedly being housed at a local school by officials.

Rwandan troops were reportedly deployed to V Congresso village, north of Macomia in Cabo Delgado on or around 24 November, to defend against insurgent attacks.  This came after recent insurgent attacks in the area.  The area is supposedly within the SAMIM's area of responsibility, making this a notable development.

A group of 6 insurgents disguised as local civilians fired at fishermen on the coast of Macomia district, near Messano, east of Mucojo, in an attempt to steal fish and fishing equipment on 19 November.  One fisherman was injured from the attack, but all of the fishermen were able to escape.

Insurgents fired into the air to scare off 12 fishermen in Goludo, Macomia district, on 19 November, to steal fish the group had caught.  The fishermen were reportedly from Nampula and were operating in Goludo, without the consent of the local population.

The locals in Nangade district have recently expressed their distrust over the SAMIM Tanzanian forces operating in the district after Tanzanian troops failed to respond swiftly to an 19 November attack on Chacamba, just 13 km from their military base. Locals reportedly have more faith is Basotho soldiers operating in the area as part of SAMIM.

Insurgents in recent attacks in Northern Mueda reportedly used recruits from nearby Niassa to lead these raids, including a 16 November attack on Nambungali.  Recruits from Niassa are believed to have also led attacks between 24-26 November in areas of Mecula District of Niassa.

Recently returned IDPs in Macomia district, Cabo Delgado have reported that there is more violence in the area than is being reported by the gov't, per a report on 30 November.  Some have reportedly sent family members back to overcrowded IDP camps due to their lack of faith in the security of the area. ID's who have recently returned to the area do not believe the situation will be resolved in the near to medium term future.

Recently returned IDPs in Muidumbe district, Cabo Delgado, are optimistic about the security in the area.  Muidumbe has seen relatively little violence in recent months in comparison to Nangade and Macomia districts.

Sources reported that militants on Tuesday, 30 November, ambushed a Mozambican military vehicle near Macananje/Macalange, about 20kms northwest of Mecula town.  One soldier was reportedly injured and sustained two gunshot wounds, and troops fled from the scene.  Suspected insurgents then set the vehicle on fire.  Other sources reported this attack had caused panic in Mecula town, leading to many local residents to flee into bush areas nearby.  An unknown number of troops by 30 November had reportedly been deployed to Mecula town to prevent an insurgent attack in the area, and helicopter patrols over Mecula district were reported on 01 December.

An unknown number of troops on or around 30 November reportedly deployed to Mecula town to prevent an insurgent attack in the area, and helicopter patrols over Mecula district were reported on 01 December.

On 02 December, 58 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique, including 35 cases in Maputo City and 16 cases in Maputo Province.  2 more people were hospitalized with the virus, increasing the total number of hospitalized cases to 9 in the country.  This is the highest number of cases reported in a single day since late September.

On 02 December, youths protested in Inhassoro District, calling for an oil and gas company to provide employment opportunities for local youths.  Local police arrived in the area and fired several gunshots to disperse the group.  7 of those protesting were ultimately arrested for "contempt of authorities".

On 1 December, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said that the travel restrictions imposed on southern African nations that first detected the new COVID-19 variant, Omicron are unacceptable. He appealed to 50 nations who imposed such restrictions, advised them to use 'common sense', and apply safe travel protocols instead. His statement came a day after WHO said that blanket travel bans will not prevent the international spread of the variant but will only affect the global response to the pandemic because it will discourage countries from reporting new variants.

South Africa announced that new cases of COVID-19 nearly doubled in a day, reflecting a remarkable escalation of cases a week after scientists detected the Omicron variant. 8,561 cases were reported on 1 December compared to 4,373 on 30 November.  It is currently not clear if cases are being driven by the new variant, but in any case this spike in cases could mean a new wave of cases in the near future in Mozambique as well.
Singapore on Thursday, 2 December, detected two more Omicron variant of COVID-19 cases in people who had recently travelled to Mozambique, though they had also transited through South Africa.

Health Minister Armindo Tiago said on 1 December that 53% of the vaccinated individuals with COVID-19 vaccines reside in rural areas, while 47% live in urban areas. He reiterated the government's goal to immunize 17 million people by the end of 2022. So far, more than 3.9 million people are fully vaccinated against COVID-19, while more than 6.5 million have had at least one shot.

Mozambique's Prime Minister, Carlos Agostinho do Rosario,  said on 1 December that Rwandan military presence in the country is "priceless" in the fight against insurgency in Cabo Delgado. He said that achieving peace and security in the regions is the most significant benefit Mozambican can attain from Rwanda's support.
On 30 November, many civilians fled from Mecula town and slept in the forest over the threat of insurgent attacks after militants raided a town about 20kms from Mecula.

Mozambican troops were deployed in Mecula on 30 November over fears of possible insurgent attacks. This comes as a message circulated at Mecula District headquarters alleging that armed men were roaming around the Macananje area, 20km from Mecula town.

Additional Mozambican troops were deployed in Marrupa area on 30 November over fears of possible insurgent attacks. This comes as a message circulated at Mecula District headquarters alleging that armed men were present in the Macananje area, 20km from Mecula town.

Spain carried out a repatriation flight from Maputo to Madrid with 150 passengers of 15 nationalities on 2 December. The passengers were stranded in Mozambique due to border closures. Many countries have closed borders early this week to foreigners or suspended and restricted international travel, particularly countries in southern Africa, including Mozambique.
Reports on 2 December indicate that a 73-yr-old man was set on fire by four suspects in Gune village, Zavala. The victim was accused of witchcraft. Two of the four victims were already arrested.

On 2 December, authorities announced that in the last 24 hours, 75,530 people had been vaccinated with the first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine, under the third stage of the National Mass Vaccination Campaign. This increased the number of individuals with one shot to 6,645,389, while a total of 4,053,689 people have been fully inoculated in the country since the beginning of the vaccination program on 8 March.

Hidden Debts case Judge Efigenio Baptista announced on 2 December that Jean Boustani, a senior official with the Abu Dhabi-based Privinvest group, will not testify at the current trial. Boustani has been summoned several times to appear in Mozambique; however, he ignored all summons sent by the country's attorney general. Boustani had been meant to testify remotely, and is accused of being one of the primary figures in the Hidden Debts Scandal.  Baptista said Boustani would no longer testify as he had been charged in relation to the Hidden Debts Scandal, and could not appear as a witness in the case while he is wanted by the Mozambican state.

On 2 December, the South African Association of Freight Forwarders (SAAFF) and the Minerals Council SA (MCSA) called for immediate action on the dreaded situation at the Lebombo Border Post on Maputo Corridor. SAAFF claimed that cost trucking companies R1.3bn in lost revenue so far this year, attributed to the long delays in border-crossing times. These delays can last more than three days to weeks. In addition, the border does not have 24-hour operations, which makes crossing time from an average of one to 20 hours. Recently, COVID-19 restrictions have worsened the situation.

Annual HIV/AIDS deaths in Mozambique declined by 41.5% between 2010 and 2020, Mozambique’s First Lady, Isaura Nyusi, disclosed on 1 December. 65,000 have died from the said disease in 2010 compared to 38,000 in 2020. The  number of new infections during the same period also decreased by 34.6 percent, from 150,000 to 98,000.

Security forces arrested a jail manager and jail guard in Guro, Manica on 2 December for allowing escape of prisoners. The manager was sentenced to 16 months in prison while the guard was sentenced to 14 months of prison.

On 01 December, 46 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique. 30 of the new cases were recorded in Maputo City four cases from Gaza, three each from Cabo Delgado, Nampula, and Tete, two from Maputo province, and one from Zambezia.  No deaths from Covid-19 were reported in the previous 24 hours; the country's death toll from Covid-19  remains at 1,941. Three more people were hospitalized with the virus, increasing the total number of hospitalized cases to seven in the country.  This is the highest number of cases since late September.

National Institute of Health (INS) warned on 2 December that new restrictions could be put in place in the coming days if COVID-19 new cases continue to increase. In preparation for the 'fourth wave,' the government has been intensifying its efforts to accelerate the mass vaccination of target groups and heighten surveillance of prevention measures.

Civil Aviation Authority of Vietnam approved on Wednesday, 1 December, the suspension of flights to and from Mozambique and six other African countries over concerns about the spread of the Omicron COVID-19 variant. South Africa, Botswana, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Eswatini, and Lesotho are the other affected countries. Vietnam has not detected any cases of Omicron so far but is seeing a steady increase in daily infections.
A 19-yr old boy was stabbed to death in Chipangara, Beira, on 2 December. Further details on the attack are not available at this time.
Security forces detained a military member in Maputo on 1 December over an alleged attempt to sell an AK-47 rifle.

Insurgents reportedly kidnapped at least 10 individuals from the Negomano area on or around 25 November. The total number of abducted civilians has yet been determined. One of the female victims was released to recount the incident, however, her husband is still held captive and believed to have been taken into Niassa with the insurgents.

United Nations Office for Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) plans to provide 343 million Euros support for over 1.3 million people in Mozambique in 2022, according to a UN report on 2 December. The fund will be used for the Mozambique Humanitarian Response Plan next year. Notably, in 2021, OCHA's aid reached 1.2 million people in the country.

On 2  December, the US Government launched a USD400,000 project with the Civil Society Support Mechanism (MASC) Foundation. This two-year project will help increase Mozambican institutions' capacity to adjudicate electoral disputes impartially. District judges and prosecutors will be trained in partnership with the Association for Mozambican Jurists and the Legal and Judicial Training Centre. In addition, a judicial mentoring service will be established for judges and prosecutors handling electoral disputes.

On 03 December, Mozambique recorded another 111 COVID cases, and no new deaths.  Cases were reported in Maputo City, Maputo, Cabo Delgado, Zambezia, Inhambane, Gaza, Manica, Niassa, and Nampula.  2 more hospitalizations were reported, and there are now 243 active cases in the country.  This is the highest number of cases reported since late September, and represents a 91% increase compared to the 58 cases reported the day before.  As recently as 29 November, just 4 new cases were reported countrywide.
One person was reportedly beheaded during an insurgent attack on Nova Zambezia in the early morning hours of 03 December.

Insurgents launched an attack in Nova Zambezia, approx. 20km north of Macomia Town on in the late night hours of 02 December / early morning hours of 03 December. Gunfire was reported overnight in the village, with unconfirmed reports that a number of people were abducted.  Troops deployed at V Congresso village moved towards Nova Zambezia in coordination with local militia on the afternoon of 03 December; no clashes have yet been reported and it is presumed militants withdrew from the village before the arrival of security forces.  ISCAP later claimed responsibility for this attack, saying its fighters killed a soldier and destroyed houses in the raid.

Joint forces deployed to Nova Zambezia village, between Macomia and V Congresso on 03 December after reports of an insurgent attack in the area; no clashes were reported as insurgents left the area before the arrival of the troops.

Insurgents launched an attack in Nova Zambezia, approx. 20km north of Macomia Town on in the late night hours of 02 December / early morning hours of 03 December. Gunfire was reported overnight in the village, with unconfirmed reports that a number of people were abducted.  Insurgents burned down at least 15 houses in the attack, and residents fled the area. Insurgents reportedly came from the direction of V Congresso.  Troops deployed at V Congresso village moved towards Nova Zambezia in coordination with local militia on the afternoon of 03 December; no clashes have yet been reported and it is presumed militants withdrew from the village before the arrival of security forces.  ISCAP later claimed responsibility for this attack, saying its fighters killed a soldier and destroyed houses in the raid.
A Pakistani national, identified as Raza Hassan Anwar, said to have orchestrated kidnappings in South Africa and Mozambique, was shot dead around 12:00 on 03 December in  Johannesburg.  Anwar also

The Northern Development Agency (ADIN) supplies 600 agricultural production kits to IDPs in Mueda, Cabo Delgado, on 2 December. This is part of the 39,211 kits allocated to the displaced families in this district. The kit consists of seeds, fertilizers, and hoes. The kit consisted of 12.5 kg of maize seeds, 15 beans, 2 of sesame, 150 of fertilizers, and one hoe for each family.

On 3 December, authorities announced that in the last 24 hours, 68,660 people had been vaccinated with the first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine, under the third stage of the National Mass Vaccination Campaign. This increased the number of individuals who have received at least one shot to 6,685,501, while a total of 4,114,267 people have been fully inoculated in the country since the beginning of the vaccination program on 8 March.

The third congress of the Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM) commenced on 3 December in Beira. The congress will conclude who will be the next leader of the party and discuss the internal and external affairs of the party. The election, scheduled for 4 December, will decide who will replace Daviz Simango, who died last February due to an illness.

UNICEF, partnered with Dallaire Institute for Children, Peace & Security, begins  on 3 December the training of troops in Manica on dealing with child soldiers and preventing recruitment/use of child soldiers .

Nepal banned arrivals from Mozambique and eight other countries from 3 December in a bid to curb the spread of the new Omicron COVID-19 variant. Other affected countries include South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Lesotho, Eswatini, Malawi, and Hong Kong. Travelers who have been to the aforementioned countries in the past three weeks will also not be allowed to enter Nepal, and all other international visitors already in transit must spend seven days at their own cost in hotel quarantine. Meanwhile, Nepali nationals are advised against non-essential foreign travel.
Reports on 3 December indicate that beginning January 2022, more than one million people will be vaccinated against cholera in Nampula.

The International Monetary Fund warned on 2 December of the possibility of  “economic collapse” in some low-income countries, including in Mozambique due to high debt levels.  Data shows that about 60% of the world’s poorest countries are at high risk or are already in debt distress. Mozambique is one of several countries with a significant debt burden in Africa.

The United Nations’ World Meteorological Organization (WMO) announced on 2 December that La Niña weather phenomenon is taking place for the second consecutive year. This is significant and means there is an "increased likelihood of an above-average number of cyclones strikes in Mozambique.
ISCAP claimed its fighters launched an attack targeting a Mozambican army patrol in Chai village on 2 December. No information on casualties.

The Confederation of Business Associations of Mozambique (CTA) met with National Migration Services (SENAMI) two weeks ago over visa concerns. The delay in visa issuance resulted to several inconveniences especially for those who needed business/work visa.

The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)  announced on 4 December that US Government will donate 2,016,000 single doses of Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine to Mozambique through the COVAX initiative. The vaccine shipment did subsequently arrive in Maputo City on Monday, 6 December. This was the largest single shipment of vaccine to Mozambique during the pandemic.These single-dose vaccines are part of 7,105,420 doses received by the Government under the COVAX initiative, which expedites global access to COVID-19 vaccines.

On 4 December, the Ministry of Health announced that 105 people, including nationals and foreigners, tested positive for the new Covid-19 virus in the last 24 hours, raising the total cumulative number of cases in the country to 151,868. The 3 provinces with the highest number of cases were Maputo City with 45, Maputo Province with 28, and Inhambane Province with 15. Data also showed that the ages of those infected were between 2 and 72 years. In the same period, there were no new recoveries and deaths, hence the total recoveries and deaths remain at 149,575 and 1,941, respectively. However, there were 2 discharged and 2 admissions, bringing the total hospitalizations to 7,068; of which 11 remain in treatment units. Active cases of said period are 318.

ISCAP claimed responsibility for the 3 December attack carried out on a village at Nova Zambezia, 20km north of Macomia, referring to the incident where 1 soldier was killed and several houses destroyed.

South Africa's Health Minister announced on Friday, 3 December, that the country is in its 4th wave of the Covid pandemic, stating that new cases have increased by over 300% in the past 7 days with a positivity rate of 22%. They also cited their record of 11,535 cases from just 2,465 the day prior, that is an increase of 9,070 new cases in just 1 day.  South African executive still does not want to tighten the restrictive measures, especially as Christmas approaches.  In this context, Mozambique, especially Maputo City and Maputo province, will likely see an increase of daily Covid cases and is also at risk of a 4th wave of Covid.

Lutero Simango was elected as the new president of the Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM) party during its congress in Beira on Sunday, 5 December. Simango received 452 votes, against 51 for Silverio Ronguane (MDM parliamentary deputy). Meanwhile, another candidate, Jose Domingos (MDM General Secretary), withdrew from the race.

Canada announced on 5 December that it would not accept results of molecular COVID tests done in 10 African countries, including Mozambique. Other affected countries are Botswana, Egypt, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Nigeria, Namibia, South Africa, and Zimbabwe. Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and individuals with status under the Indian Act, who have been in these countries in the last 14 days before returning to Canada, would be required to obtain proof of a valid negative COVID-19 molecular test in a third country within 72 hours prior departure to Canada, regardless of their vaccination status. This is required in addition to PCR tests on Day 1 and 8 after arrival and quarantine for 14 days.

On 5 December, 56 people tested positive for Covid-19 in the last 24 hours, of which 3 were foreigners. The new cases were detected in Maputo City, Maputo, and Inhambane, with ages ranging between 12 and 80. Altogether, the cumulative number of Covid-19 positive is 151,924, of which 151,555 are of local transmission and 369 are imported. In the same period, 3 patients were discharged, all in Maputo City, where 6 were hospitalized. 14 remain in treatment units. The cumulative number of recoveries and deaths remain at 149,575 and 1,941, respectively, with none added. The total active cases have increased to 404.

Friends of Earth members and supporters in the UK plan to deliver a letter to Workington MP Mark Jenkinson’s office on 7 December detailing the reasons why they are taking the Government to court over their support for the future fossil-fuel project in Cabo Delgado, Mozambique, urging the MP to withdraw the $1.15 billion pledge for the said project.  In a report on 4 December, a UK FoE member stressed that the fossil fuel project will only exacerbate the consequences of climate change that Mozambique is already experiencing.

President Filipe Nyusi directed the inauguration ceremony of the Canicado–Combomune–Mapai–Chicualacuala road, in Mabalane district, Gaza province, on Friday, 3 December. The 300km-road provides alternative routes to the National Road Number One (EN1) and is expected to increase agricultural, wildlife, forestry, and tourist activities in the nearby districts.

State Deputy Minister Inocencio Impissa announced that from the 784 disciplinary proceedings held in the first half of 2021, nearly 200 public servants across the country were expelled from the State Apparatus. The announcement came on Thursday, 2 December, during the Anti-Corruption Week ceremony. Impissa also said that in the same period, a further 97 public servants were demoted, 88 were fined, 132 received public reprimands, 109 were warned, and 63 were acquitted. In a review of the past year, Impissa also declared that there was a 40.5% increase in the number of disciplinary proceedings from 911 in 2019 to 1,280 in 2020.

The Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP), with which Mozambique is a member, and the G7+, a group of fragile states, said they will strengthen public health cooperation to accelerate Covid-19 vaccination in their member states, per their statement on Friday, 3 December.

The Mozambican and South African authorities suspended joint operations to stop vehicle smuggling along their mutual borders.  The two had been cooperating in these operations for the past 3 months. The two are reportedly in talks to restart these operations.  Cooperation was reportedly suspended after different security force elements have accused one another of being complicit in smuggling along the border.

Residents of Condominio Intaka Village, known as “5,000 Houses”, in the district of Intaka, in Matola municipality, Maputo province, complained about the abuses they have experienced from the condominium managers. According to residents of the condo since 2010, one example is that, lately, there have been constructions of buildings that obstruct the ventilation system of some residents, where initially, the housing design had only indicated a horizontal growth. Other complaints also include noise pollution, streets destroyed,  reduced width of streets due to redesigning of fences, and lack of security. The Condominium Administration's manager, known as Dionisio, said everything will be resolved unanimously, and that there is no need for the residents to contact the press, per a report on 6 December.

On Thursday, 2 December, the National Migration Service (SENAMI) spokesperson, Celestino Matsinhe, announced that the service would boost inspection capacity at border crossings around Mozambique, noting the expected increase in movement in the coming festive season. Already in the week prior, borders have already seen increased traffic with around 40,000 travelers in transit, against 37,000 in the week before that, said Matsinhe who also called on foreign citizens to observe the rules for entering and staying in the country.
On 1 December, Exxon Mobil Corporation announced a forecasted sales of about 26M tons per year of liquefied natural gas, partially driven by the potential start of operations in Mozambique in 2022.

The Mozambique Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) continued to signal a strong uplift in demand across the private sector in November, noting that the growth rate of new businesses had picked up the fastest in June. However, employment only ticked up a fraction as the rate of job creation softened to a seven-month low, per the report on 6 December.  Companies saw a rise in orders due to an increase in client numbers, as economic conditions stabilized following Covid-19 restrictions, while two-thirds of firms say they are optimistic for future activity.

Two sources reported that significant deployments of Mozambican military units as well as intelligence agents have been present in Pebane district, Zambezia province for more than a week.  Troops were deployed to the area after reports of that a number of insurgents from Cabo Delgado had infiltrated the Mulela area of the district.  Unconfirmed reports say a number of insurgents in recent months have travelled to this area; some of the militants may be from Pebane or from neighboring Moma District in Nampula.

Two sources reported that significant deployments of Mozambican military units as well as intelligence agents have been present in Pebane district, Zambezia province for more than a week.  Troops were deployed to the area after reports of that a number of insurgents from Cabo Delgado had infiltrated the Mulela area of the district.  Unconfirmed reports say a number of insurgents in recent months have travelled to this area; some of the militants may be from Pebane or from neighboring Moma District in Nampula.

Pro-government militia in clashes on the morning of 06 December killed 4 suspected insurgents in Nkoe village, west of the N380 road in Macomia District.  Nkoe lies north-west of Macomia town, and south-west of Nova Zambezia village, where insurgents launched an attack on 03 December.  4 AK-47s were also seized in this operation.

The Chiure Municipality announced on 5 December that the 50 water holes for water supply were running dry. The municipality stated that 6 of the wells have become obsolete. This comes as the water holes were reportedly used as backup if the FIPAG water supply fails to provide water services.
SAMIM in an announcement on 04 December said its forces continue operations against insurgents in Cabo Delgado province, though no new operations were detailed.

The Mozambican government stated that based on their data, around 2 million people are experiencing acute food insecurity in the country. The government stated that Cabo Delgado recorded the highest number with 932,136 people, while Maputo City has the lowest number of those experiencing this degree of food insecurity with 58,242 people. About 71% of this 2 million, or about 1.32 million, are in Cabo Delgado, Niassa, Nampula, and Zambezia.
The Ministry of Health announced 76 new COVID cases and no related deaths in Mozambique on 7 December. 56 of the new COVID cases were recorded in Maputo City and 18 in Maputo province.

Sources stated that IDPs in Palma District continue to experience significant food insecurity. IDPs were reportedly resorting to eating grass, wild fruits, and plants. The situation of the IDPs were worsened as the IDPs were also discriminated against the host communities.

ADIN donated and delivered 5 new vehicles to the Cabo Delgado Secretary of State to be used in districts affected by the insurgency on 5 December. The new vehicles were to strengthen the support of the government to the locals.

The Portuguese government arranged a flight from Lisbon and Maputo to repatriate individuals trapped by the decision of the EU to suspend entry and flights coming from Mozambique on 8 December. Two flights from Maputo to Lisbon were arranged on 9 and 11 December. The Portuguese government previously conducted a flight from Lisbon and Maputo on 6 December.
Sources stated on 06 December that informal sellers have reoccupied sidewalks in downtown Maputo. The informal vendors were previously removed from these areas by police in the past.

SAMIM officials announced the death of a Lesotho soldier due to illness in Cabo Delgado recently. SAMIM clarified that the soldier died due to non-combat related causes. The soldier was identified as Private Moalosi Jacob Khoaele.

Sources stated on 6 December that ongoing operations by security forces in Mecula district, with joint Rwandan-Mozambican forces reportedly surrounding the district in order to trap and destroy insurgent cells in the area.
ISCAP released an info graphic of its activity across 8 countries on 29 November claiming to have killed 18 soldiers in Mozambique during the months between August to November.

The crew of a recently seized Seychelles-flagged naval vessel stated that they had a license to fish in Mozambican waters near Area 4 of Rovuma Basin on 4 December. The Mozambican Navy stated that the naval vessel was spotted in a “conflict area” and that the crew had committed "several offenses" for which the vessel was seized and the crew arrested.

Two police officers arrested a kidnapper and rescued an abducted civilian after stopping the suspect’s vehicle at the Junction of Av. Joaquim Chissano and Acordos de Lusaka of Maputo City at around 18:40 12 November.  The male kidnapper was reportedly the boyfriend of the female victim.

Cambodia on 05 December removed travel ban on Mozambique after suspending travel from the country for one week. The ban was in response to the Omicron variant’s spread. The Cambodian government said travelers from Mozambique will now undergo a rapid PCR-test upon arrival in Cambodia and a 1-week quarantine. This comes as the Cambodian government also banned 10 other African countries besides from Mozambique.

The Provincial Assembly of Niassa president issued a warning saying that insurgents may travel to Niassa province and seek refuge due to the security operations and offensive against them in Cabo Delgado. The provincial assembly president also called for the locals to be vigilant against the insurgents.  Militants have recently launched several attacks in Niassa.

Mozambican truckers are reportedly hesitant driving through Southern Africa due to the Omicron COVID variant. Truck drivers say that panic is setting among the drivers due to possible reinfection of those who had the virus earlier. Immunized drivers have also raised concerns regarding the variant due to becoming possible carriers back to Mozambique.

The US government is  reviewing travel bans placed on Mozambique, Southern Africa, and other African countries, the US government's top infectious diseases expert, Dr. Anthony Fauci, said on 05 December. Fauci said that he hoped the ban could be lifted "in a reasonable period of time" as more information is gathered regarding the omicron variant.  He also said the Biden administration is reviewing the travel ban "literally on a daily basis".
Rwandan Security Forces units reportedly received their booster COVID vaccinations in Cabo Delgado on 6 December.
A minivan overturned after crashing along the National Road 1 near Macia District in Gaza province around 04:30 on 4 December. Five civilians were killed and seven were injured.

Police detained 17 demonstrators during a march by the Women's Observatory group near the Palacio de Justica in Maputo City on the afternoon of 7 December. Reports later said 19 women were arrested in this incident. The protesters were participating in the "16 days of Activism" campaign, which condemns abuse on women around the world.

Unknown men assaulted and killed a civilian due to a dispute in Tchumene on 4 December. The victim was reportedly punched in the chest twice leading to his death.
Police arrested three people for counterfeiting charges after attempting to bribe police in Marracuene on 4 December. The suspects previously were stopped for unruly driving.
Police exchanged gunfire with a robber after attempting to steal from an establishment in Gaza on December 4.

Joint Rwandan/Mozambican security force operations were reported to have taken place on 06-07 December in Nova Zambezia village, following an insurgent attack on the area on 03 December.  One source reported an unknown number of militants shot dead in the village who had been hiding in some of the houses destroyed in the earlier militant attack.

Joint Rwandan/Mozambican security force operations were reported to have taken place on 06-07 December in Nova Zambezia village, following an insurgent attack on the area on 03 December.  One source reported an unknown number of militants shot dead in the village who had been hiding in some of the houses destroyed in the earlier militant attack.

Sources indicated that a number of Mozambican soldiers have recently been deployed to Memba in Nampula to counter any potential insurgent activity in the area.  Insurgent recruiters have previously been active in this area, and a number of militants have also joined the insurgency from this area.

A group of Mozambican soldiers on 05 December reportedly raped two women in Memba in Nampula, sources reported.  The women had asked the soldiers for a ride in an FADM vehicle just before the assault occurred.

Sources stated that a water crisis has been ongoing for three weeks in Gurue on 7 December, affecting 200,000 people. The local population is resorting to alternative sources for water supply. The water supply in the area was reportedly old and has continuously deteriorated.
A vehicle crashed after speeding along Regional Road 703 in Velha district of Nacala on the afternoon of 6 December. Five civilians were killed and seven were injured.

The Ministry of Health announced 120 new COVID cases in Mozambique on 7 December. This comes as 74 of the new case were recorded in Maputo City and Matola area with 33 of the new COVID cases. The increase in cases has also brought up the positivity rate to 6.49%. Currently, there are 10 hospitalizations as 600 active cases were recorded.

Sources stated that security forces recently arrested an alleged insurgent religious leader identified as Austazi Muhammad in Pemba on or around 30 November. Muhammad was reportedly kept detained in Mieze of Metuge district.  Muhammed is a native of MDP District, and he was reportedly in possession of various materials in relation to the insurgency.

Mozambican police recently arrested three supposed insurgent religious leaders in Pemba identified as Muhamade Abdulai, Mwalimo Farijala, and Mwalimo Issufo.  Farijala and Issufo have reportedly been released due to a lack of evidence.

Human Rights Watch (HRW) stated that 600 women and children have been abducted by insurgents in Cabo Delgado since 2018. Some of these women and girls have since been rescued or escaped from the insurgents, though at least 200 remain unaccounted for.  Insurgents have used female abductees as sexual slaves and forced them to "marry" insurgent fighters; some of those abducted have been sold to foreign militants for between $600 - $1800.

A lawsuit filed by an environmental organization against the UK government to attempt to block the UK government's $1.15 billion in funding of LNG projects in Mozambique began on 07 December. The lawsuit was filed by an environmental organization who says the UK government has not considered how the projects would impact the environment.

Private security guards shot dead a teenage thief who found attempting to steal valuables from a parked vehicle at the Junction of Av. Albert Lithuli and Av. Ahmed Sekou Toure in Maputo City on the morning of 8 December.

Security forces reportedly deployed additional troops to guarantee security in Mecula town on 04 December. This came after insurgent attacks north-east of the town in early December.
Mozambican police Rapid Intervention Units reportedly exchanged gunfire with insurgents in Macalange on 4 December, about 20kms north-east of Mecula town. Casualties were not specified.

Food aid is reported to have been diverted from IDPs and sold at markets in the Maratane area of Nampula recently.  It was not immediately clear along the supply chain of the aid where it was being diverted.
A study by the Joaquim Chissano University in partnership with UN stated that sexual violence against women in Metuge were underreported.

Police arrested a suspect, identified as a local "prophet" of the Jehovah's Witness Church, for sexually assault charges on a 12-year-old girl in Quelimane on 5 December. The suspect claimed that he intended to marry the victim.
