The suspect claimed that he intended to marry the victim.  The Jehova's Witness Church later said the man arrested was not affiliated with their church.

Former President Armando Guebuza will still testify in Hidden Debts case according to an 07 December report, but not until next year. This comes as the Ministry called on the testimonies to be suspended due to the upcoming holidays.

The Ministry of Economy and Finance announced that the cost of Mozambique’s external debt is estimated to reach 12.9 billion USD on 6 December. The Minister of Economy and Finance stated that an average growth of 300 million per year is currently being seen in the country.

Locals reportedly attacked and detained suspected robbers after the thieves attempted to steal from residents in Maputo city on the night of 06 December. The suspects were undressed and assaulted. One of the suspects was injured.

A fire broke out in a suspected arson incident inside the office of the provincial migration director in Nampula around 23:00 on 5 December. The incident comes as the employees of the provincial migration were under investigation.

Sources stated that Yata island off the Angoche coast is used regularly for drug smuggling. The smugglers were reportedly using boats to smuggle narcotics in and around the island “every night”. Locals also claimed that the island is maintained and well controlled by drug smuggling networks.  Foreign drug smugglers are also reportedly active in the area.

Police detained a community police officer and 3 others for involvement in drug trafficking in Angoche on 4 December. The police stated that another suspect was on the run and a search operation was started to detain the suspect.
Sources stated that at least 520 IDPs fled from the villages of Matage, Laulala and Gomba after recent insurgent attacks in these areas of Niassa.

The World Food Program expects to provide aid tor 930,000 IDPs through May 2022 in Cabo Delgado, Niassa, and Nampula, but will  only be able to provide 39% of needed daily calories in aid until January 2022.  Full distribution is expected to resume after ongoing vulnerability-based targeting exercises for aid provision, primarily in Cabo Delgado, are completed.

206 COVID cases were reported on 08 December in Mozambique.  There are now 798 active cases in the country, along with 8 hospitalizations. This is the highest number of cases reported in the country in nearly 3 months since over 200 cases was last reported in a single day in mid-September in the country. No COVID deaths were reported in this latest update.

Mecula District Administrator Antonio Paulo attempted to stop local officials from leaving the district after an insurgent attack on a village on 25 November, saying security forces guaranteed the security in Mecula and nearby villages, also saying anyone leaving the village was doing so at his own risk.

A recent NGO report indicated that there is a high to moderate risk of flooding in the Maputo, Umbeluzi, Incomati, Limpop, Buzi, Pungue, Savane, and Licungo River Basins during the current rainy season.

Sources stated that three of the repatriated passengers that arrived in Lisbon coming from Maputo tested positive for the COVID Omicron variant on 4 December.  The passengers were subjected to a 14-day quarantine.

Public Works, Water Resources, and House Minister Machatine stated that there are not enough funds to improve and maintain the national roads in the country being generated by toll revenues. Taxes collected per year only allows 2 billion meticais to be obtained and the funding needed is around 14.7 billion.  This likely means more future tolls along Mozambican roads.

Insurgents launched a new raid and stole food and medicine from the village of Naulala in Mecula district on 29 November. Locals claimed that the insurgents were carrying weapons and machetes during the attack, and that the insurgents included women and men. Militants fired in the air during the attack, and civilians fled the area. Another source said this attack took place on 28 November.

ISCAP claimed its fighters had conducted an attack on Naulala village on Mecula district that occurred on 29 November, saying its fighters had burned down a Mozambican military barracks and civilians homes. This comes as insurgents did launch a raid in the area and stole food and medication from the village.
Sources claimed that insurgents attacked the village of Micomela, northwest of Mueda, on 13 November. The locals fled the village across to the border of Tanzania.

Insurgents raided Nangomwa village in Tanzania near the Rovuma River on the evening of 12 November. The insurgents abducted civilians and forced them to transport the stolen goods. This comes as the insurgent also raided Sindano and Michawe district of Mtwara region nearby on 12-13 November.
Insurgents abducted an unknown number of civilians in the Nagomwa village area of Tanzania on the night of 12-13 November.
Insurgents abducted several civilians during a raid in Sindano village of Mtwara in Tanzania on the night of 12 November.

Security forces arrested a suspected insurgent people smuggler coming from Sindano, Tanzania, along the border with Mozambique on 22 November. The man had reportedly smuggled two "bearded men" across the Mozambican border prior to the arrest.  Tanzanian police also seized guns from the man.
Sources stated that civilians were returning to Nanjaba village in early December. The locals previously fled the village last 13 November due to an insurgent attack.

A report on 8 December indicated that the Mozambican naval forces are currently conducting patrols covering 381 nautical miles off the coast of Cabo Delgado. The patrols stretched from the mouth of Rio Ligonha between Nampula and Zambezia to the mouth of Rio Rovuma in north of Cabo Delgado.

A report on 8 December indicated that the Mozambican naval forces are currently conducting patrols covering 381 nautical miles off the coast of Cabo Delgado. The patrols stretched from the mouth of Rio Ligonha between Nampula and Zambezia to the mouth of Rio Rovuma in north of Cabo Delgado.
A report on 8 December indicated that 6 individuals were detained in Inhambane due to academic fraud.

Mozambican Health Minister, Armindo Tiago, announced at the bi-annual meeting of the health sector with partners in Maputo on 8 December that the ministry has prepared a plan to respond with and reduce the impact of the potential fourth wave of the Coronavirus pandemic expected to hit the country in late December or January of 2022. Tiago explained that the plan includes accelerating the national vaccination drive, distribution of vaccine supplies throughout the country, reinforcing epidemiological surveillance, screening all travelers at all entry points of Mozambique, and awareness and information campaign on adhering to preventive measures. The partners, for their part, pledged to continue supporting the government in health emergencies.

A report on 8 December stated that mayors are complaining about delays in disbursement of funding to the municipalities of the country during the opening of the National Council of Local Authorities in Maputo City on Tuesday, 7 December. These delays affect the infrastructure improvement efforts of the municipalities, which forces them to resort to using the revenues they have collected. This, however, still causes concerns as it may soon not be capable of supporting such efforts. The President of the National Association of the Municipalities of Mozambique, Calisto Cossa, said the municipalities will have to capitalize on their collections through broadening the tax base without adding financial burden to the residents.

The National Inspectorate of Economic Activities (INAE) Spokesperson, Tomas Timba, said at a conference on Tuesday, 7 December, that the prices of commodities has begun to increase across the country, particularly the prices of vegetables. Timba added that this may be attributed to the rain experienced in the recent weeks.

A statement from the National Institute of Support to Refugees (INAR) indicated that 23 Burundian refugees were taken back to Burundi via the Maputo International Airport on the afternoon of 8 December. The Wednesday repatriation is the third batch of refugees repatriated by the Mozambican Interior Ministry, the UN High Commission for Refugees, and the Government of Burundi to help refugees who voluntarily wished to return to their countries of origin. The first 2 batches of repatriation took place in September and October.

A report on 8 December stated that public transportation fares have significantly shot up as residents flee Mecula district in Niassa province. Fares from the main village of the district to Lichinga city has risen from 300 to 500 meticais. This follows several insurgent attacks in the district.

A report on 8 December indicated that a private bank in Mecula in Niassa province had closed and that it had withdrawn an ATM from the town as a preemptive measure to prevent incidents of robbery. This came following recent insurgent attacks near Mecula and threat of such an attack in Mecula town.

A report on 8 December indicated the illegal logging incidents are becoming prevalent in the southern part of Zambezia province, specifically in Umbila specialty wood. Two trucks loaded with logs were reportedly found recently in Derre district. One of the trucks was fined by the National Environmental Quality Control Agency (AQUA) for cutting and transporting the logs to Nicoadala district even when it was not licensed to do so. The driver of truck, however, explained that the logs were cut in Morrumbala but as he was transiting in the district during the night the truck broke down and was intercepted by AQUA personnel.

A representative of Mozambican activists said 20 activists will file criminal complaints against police officers who detained them on Tuesday, 7 December. The activists were protesting in front of the Palace of Justice in Maputo when police forces stopped and detained them. Some of them were reportedly assaulted, resulting in various injuries, and their posters and materials were destroyed. The group reportedly presented documents to prove the legality of the protest but the police contested it lacked the authorization of the mayor.

4 board members of a school in Mutarara, Tete province, have been detained since 2 December over an alleged leakage of a 10th-grade exam. Photos and videos of them opening the envelopes being circulated on social media sites led to the discovery of the incident and their detention.

On 8 December, Mozambican President Filipe Nyusi called on Mozambican citizens in Tanzania to stay alert as terrorist groups continue to operate in Cabo Delgado. This took place during his speech at the 60th-anniversary commemoration of Tanzania's independence in Dar-es-Salaam. Nyusi added that the government will assess and work on a way to address the Mozambican refugees' request to establish a facility to issue civil documents in Tanzania.

Suspected insurgents on 08 December were reported to have attacked the village of Lichengwe/ Lichengue, about 10kms south of Mecula town, setting fire to homes in the town.  Aerial footage of the village showed it had largely been abandoned and destroyed.  Sources later reported 2 people decapitated in this atack; a second source said one person was shot and killed while another man was shot and then decapitated. A large number of civilians fled north to the Mbatamila area, west of Mecula town.  Sources later reported about 1,000 people displaced by this attack.
Security forces from Mecula town reportedly deployed towards Linchengwe, engaging insurgents in the area on 08 December.  No further details on these clashes is currently available.
Unconfirmed reports indicated insurgents had conducted two armed robberies of two open box vehicles transporting money and food between Linchengwe and Mecula town on 08 December.
Unconfirmed reports indicated insurgents abducted an unknown number of teachers from the Linchengwe area on 9 December.

260 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 09 December, with 172 new cases in Maputo City and 58 cases in Maputo.  No new deaths were reported.  There are now 1,019 active cases in the country.  This is the highest number of COVID cases in a single day since 07 September, when 390 new cases were reported.

Volunteers continued their ongoing cleaning/clearing works in Mocimboa da Praia town on 08 December. Despite these efforts, large amounts of clearing work remains to be done in the town, and few IDPs have returned to the area.

The Ministry of Health announced that 72,000 individuals were vaccinated within the past 24 hours in Mozambique on 9 December. This brings the individuals with completed vaccinations up to 4.4 million, while 6.9 million have received at least one dose of the vaccine.
IDPs from Lichengwe and other nearby villages fled on 08-09 December towards Mbatamila after insurgents attacked villages south of Mecula

The Portuguese government announced that they have rescheduled the delivery of the vaccinates to be donated to Mozambique. The vaccines were previously scheduled for 10 December, but the delivery of new vaccines has been put on hold as Mozambique focuses on administering the doses of the vaccine already in its possession.

Security forces arrested 21 illegal immigrants and three Mozambican nationals during an operation in Gorongosa on 9 December.  The three Mozambican nationals attempted unsuccessfully to bribe officers who spotted the group.

Security officials announced on 9 December that around 250,000 people are expected to cross borders between Maputo and South Africa during holidays. In order to accommodate demand, the Goba border in Namaacha will also be used for crossings.
A health worker tested positive for COVID Omicron Variant who traveled to Cuba from Mozambique on 27 November.

South Africa's High Court in Guateng on 08 December confirmed the extradition of former Mozambique Finance Minister Chang to the US on charges related to the Hidden Debts case.  Mozambique had unsuccessfully attempted to extradite Chang back to the country.

The Public Integrity Center (CIP) condemned the sale of fake negative tests coming from Jose Macamo Hospital in Maputo City. CIP stated that the certificates were being sold from the facility at 1,500 meticais each. The sellers of the counterfeit negative test results are reportedly communicating through an application which tells the buyer the process on how to obtain the fake test results.

National Institute for Disaster Management (INGD) officials have appealed to IDPs to focus of agricultural production instead of relying on food relief and donations. INGD stated that the IDPs come from agricultural production zones and that each house has room for gardens.  This appeal comes amid shortages in aid due to funding shortfall among aid agencies operating in Cabo Delgado.

UNICEF announced that they need $100 million for operations to support children and caregivers in Mozambique. This is meant to allow the organization to provide support for 1.2 million people in Mozambique. This is part of a $9.4 billion appeal across the world for the organization to reach more than 327 million people.

A policeman stole goods and ran away from a trader who was stopped from pursuing the officer by other police in Maputo on the afternoon of 09 December. Sources stated that the police were taking goods from other traders as well.

Unknown men fired on a public transportation vehicle along the National Road 1 near the entrance to Gorongosa village of Sofala province around 20:00 on Wednesday, 8 December. Only material damages were reported during the attack. The attack bore many similar characteristics to past RENAMO dissident attacks.

Sources stated that injured soldiers were transported from the Mecula district to Cuamba for air evacuation on 26 November, after some troops were injured in previous days in clashes with insurgents north-east of Mecula.

Portugal's Foreign Minister Augusto Santos Silva said on 10 December that Portugal would restart flights from Mozambique "within days" but only for essential travel, with passengers required to present a negative COVID test before boarding.  No specific date for the resumption of flights was provided.  Travellers would also be required to be tested on arrival to Portugal and to undergo a quarantine period on arrival in the country.  Essential travel will include "purposes of work, study, family reunification, return of residents from Portugal or residents in Portugal to Portugal".  Travel for tourism would not be allowed at this time.

Suspected insurgents on the morning of 09 December were active near Chiconono village in Muembe District in Niassa, just under airline 20kms from Muembe town itself, and just over 60 airline kms from Lichinga, Niassa's provincial capital.   Militants reportedly ambushed two vehicles in separate incidents on Thursday morning, injuring two people, and robbing vehicle occupants of cash, mobile phones, and other items.

379 new COVID cases were reported in Mozambique on 10 December, up from 260 cases the day before.  This is the highest number of COVID cases in the current 4th wave, and the first day with more than 300 case since early September.  This included 299 new cases in Maputo City, 11 in Cabo Delgado, 10 in Maputo Province, and 1 in Zambezia.  There are now 1,076 active COVID cases in the country. One new death was also reported due to COVID, the first COVID death in the country since 29 November. 321 recoveries were also reported in the past 24 hours while 13 remain in isolation units. In summary, the updated cumulative total cases as of 10 December are: 152,965 positive; 149,943 recoveries; 1,942 deaths; 7,080 admissions; and 1,076 active cases.

The letter threatened attacks in Mecula, Mavago, Muembe, Sanga, and Lago Districts. An unconfirmed armed attack reportedly took place between the Inchope-Gorongosa section, likely sometime in November, after the death of RENAMO leader Mariano Nhongo on 11 October. No further details were reported though the attack bore many similar characteristics to past RENAMO dissident attacks. No further details on this attack are available.  This was reported by a reliable media source.

Illegal mining in Mozambique has resulted in at least 35 deaths in 2021, according to a report on 10 December.  Most of these accidents took place while miners mined for gold and rubies in the provinces of Manica and Cabo Delgado. This is a significant reduction from the 73 deaths recorded in 2020, which is a result of intensified inspections and dismantling of illegal mines, as well as the organization of cooperative societies, where miners are required to meet adequate industrial safety measures.

On 10 December, 71,608 people were vaccinated with the first Covid-19 vaccine dose in the last 24 hours. Since the start of the 3rd phase on March 8, Mozambique has vaccinated a total of 7,003,190 people with one shot, while 4,508,809 were fully vaccinated.
Japan confirmed on Friday, 10 December, that one of the eight new cases of Omicron in their country had arrived from Mozambique earlier in the same week, though no specific date was mentioned.

Beginning 1 January 2022, the Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP) will allow visa-free travel between its Portuguese-speaking member states, including Mozambique, according to an announcement by Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Costa in a report on 10 December. This movement also makes room for all the member states' citizens to apply for a residence visa.

The defense and security budget will be increased by nearly 20% in 2022 compared to 2021, with an allocation of 37.9B Meticais (526M Euros), per a report on 10 December. The increase is said to be in view of the current challenges in security and the need for continuous professionalization and equipment.

A woman was arrested by Brazilian authorities at Sao Paulo International Airport, Brazil, on Monday night, 6 December, after trying to smuggle 12kg of cocaine to Maputo, Mozambique, via entry to Ethiopia. The Brazilian woman had reportedly hidden the cocaine in 81 packs of juice powder.

One of the lawyers of the 19 co-defendants in the Hidden Debts case was confirmed positive of Covid-19, resulting in the suspension of the session held on 9 December. Immediate disinfection of the court hearing site was ordered, and Covid-19 tests were recommended for all other lawyers and parties present. This may lead to a longer suspension of the trial, depending on the results.

Large numbers of returning workers over the holidays, especially those coming from South Africa where the 4th wave of Covid-19 is currently ongoing, threatens to accelerate the spread of omicron to Mozambique and other neighboring countries. Per a report on 10 December, Mozambique and Zimbabwe saw a similar surge, weeks following the December 2020 holidays. By mid-January of 2021, Mozambique private hospitals had no available beds left. Low vaccination rates may add to the spread, as only less than 15% of Mozambique's population has been fully vaccinated so far. Concerns for community transmission were also raised as citizens move between cities and rural areas during the holidays. Mozambique has enforced mandatory testing for all arrivals at its borders, which will also add to delays and crowding.

Female IDPs in Cabo Delgado are more exposed to Gender-Based Violence (GBV) by armed groups, and are often afraid to report such incidents due to threats to themselves and their families, according to a study presented by the UN Agency for Refugees (UNHCR) on 8 December.

Mozambique's ranking fell from “obstructed” to “repressed”, according to the People Power Under Attack 2021 report, an assessment on fundamental freedoms in 196 countries conducted by a global research collaboration known as CIVICUS Monitor. The downgrade in Mozambique's ranking was due to increasing physical attacks, intimidation, and harassment of journalists and activists in the country, per the report on 10 December.
Beginning Monday, 13 December, Qatar Airways announced it will resume flights between Maputo City in Mozambique and Doha, Qatar, according to a report on 10 December.

Between 13 December to 10 January, due to large movements of people over the holiday season, operating hours will be extended for two border posts in Maputo Province: Ressano Garcia will be open 24 hours a day, while Ponta D' Ouro will operate from 8:00 to 18:00, per the announcement on 10 December.

A pregnant woman was stabbed to death allegedly by a 42-year-old man, after finding out that she was pregnant by another lover. Mozambican police in Maputo City arrested the suspect, per a report on 10 December.
On 10 December, Mozambican police (PRM) in Maputo City arrested a 42-year-old man for allegedly stabbing his wife to death, after finding out that she was pregnant by another lover.

Talks between the Gov't and Private Water Providers are still underway but are nearing an understanding, according to a report on Friday, 10 December. Private water suppliers previously threatened to cut off water to potentially millions in Mozambique if the government did not negotiate with them.

On 10 December, locals in Mecula town, Niassa, raised concerns that there has been little to no efforts in the area towards strengthening security against insurgents. Locals complained that despite having many men, the Rapid Intervention Unit (UIR) was not doing its job in pursuing insurgents in areas near Mecula town. They also added that there were no military aerial patrols, except for a single recent patrol carried out by the Niassa Special Reserve's helicopter.
SAMIM troops reportedly killed at least 12 insurgents in the Mucojo area in clashes on 06 December.  Local residents discovered the bodies of the insurgents in the area later in the week.

Sources reported SAMIM forces captured 5 insurgents at "Litingima" village, Macomia, on Thursday afternoon, 9 December. Reports said that a number of insurgents had also managed to escape. This likely refers to Litingina village in Nangade.

Insurgents attacked the villages of Chinene and Nampequesso, in Niassa province on 8 December. No details of casualties were reported.  The exact location of these villages was unclear, though they are reportedly located near Lichengwe and Ntimbo, south of Mecula.  This report is currently unconfirmed.

Two residences were set on fire in the Meluluca area, Lago district, in the province of Niassa, on 10 December, causing panic in the area. The houses belonged to fishermen who said the incident had happened in the middle of the night. Nearby houses were also robbed of large sums of money. It is unclear whether this was an insurgent-related attack.

The group during this 48-hour time period also reportedly forced the judge to withdraw money from an ATM.  Police seized at least one firearm from the group.  At least 3 people participated in the attack on the judge;The group reportedly watched the judge for several days before invading her home.

On 11 December, Mozambican health officials reported 443 new COVID cases in the country in the past 24 hours, with 214 new cases in Maputo City and 150 new cases in Maputo.  In the same 24-hour period, no new deaths were reported while there were 12 recoveries.  There are now 17 hospitalizations, with 4 new admissions and no discharges reported, and 1,507 active Covid-19 cases in the country.  In summary, the updated cumulative total cases as of 11 December are: 153,408 positive; 149,955 recoveries; 1,942 deaths; 7,084 admissions; and 1,507 active cases.

Suspected insurgents on the night of 10 December reportedly attacked Kiwengulo village in Tanzania, just across the Rovuma River from Cabo Delgado and about 15 airline kms north of Pundanhar in Palma District.  One source reported 4 killed in this attack, and several houses set on fire; another source said that insurgents decapitated 4 people in the raid.  MIlitants reportedly demanded villagers take them to the homes of local officials, but Tanzanian troops arrived at the village, engaged the insurgents, and drove them out of the area.

The National Institute of Health (NIH) in Mozambique denied any connection with an alleged scheme of selling negative Covid-19 test results, reportedly discovered by the Public Integrity Center. In their statement on 11 December, the NIH said the fake negative test results were not issued by the institution and were issued through a fraudulent criminal scheme.

Russia banned the entry of travelers from Mozambique, Hong Kong, and 8 other African countries, according to an announcement on Saturday, 11 December, due to omicron concerns.  The new decree which changed the status of the countries from "restricted" to complete non-entry was signed by the Russian Prime Minister on said date.

The Mozambique Armed Defense Forces (FADM) reportedly confirmed on 11 December that insurgents had recently launched several attacks in Niassa and is inhabiting Macalange and part of Naulala, per a report on 11 December. A cell of at least 13-20 insurgents are believed to be behind these recent attacks. The report also said a Naulala native is acting as a guide for the insurgents in Niassa.

A Zimbabwean truck driver attempted to smuggle a shipment of counterfeit sneakers from Mozambique worth R3.8M (around 230,000 USD) on Thursday, 9 December, but was arrested by South African security at the Lebombo border crossing.

A Zimbabwean truck driver was arrested by South African security at the Lebombo border crossing on Thursday, 9 December, after attempting to smuggle a shipment of counterfeit sneakers from Mozambique worth R3.8M (around 230,000 USD).

As of Saturday, 11 December, 69,400 people were vaccinated with the first dose in the last 24 hours. Since the start of the 3rd phase on March 8, Mozambique has vaccinated a total of 7,063,360 people with one shot, while 4,577,292 were fully vaccinated.

On Sunday, 12 December, Mozambican health officials reported 266 new Covid-19 cases in the country in the past 24 hours, coming from Maputo city, Maputo, Gaza, and Inhambane.  In the same 24-hour period, 2 deaths were reported, while 3 recovered from the infection.  Meanwhile, total hospitalizations increased to 26, with 13 new admissions and 2 discharges reported in Maputo city.  In summary, the updated cumulative total cases as of 12 December are: 153,674 positive; 149,958 recoveries; 1,944 deaths; 7,097 admissions; and 1,768 active cases.

PRM Cmdr. Gen. Bernardino Rafael said that one of the terrorist leaders in Niassa, named Cassimo, was recently shot dead. The Commander General recounted that the first signs of insurgency occurred earlier this year in Mavago district before spreading to Mecula.  There the Defense and Security Forces (FDS) had entered an ambush where Cassimo was killed.  After his death, they concluded that these were the terrorists who had crossed from Cabo Delgado to Mecula.  This announcement came during his talk in Ressano Garcia at the launch of operations for the festive season on Sunday, 12 December.

36 former RENAMO militiamen were integrated into the country's defense and security forces as part of the Demobilization, Disarming, and Reintegration (DDR) program for the RENAMO opposition.  The 36, along with 573 other young Mozambicans, concluded their basic police training at the Oswaldo Tazama Police Sergeants' School in Nhamatanda district, Sofala province, on Friday, 10 December.

UN Sec.-Gen. Envoy, Mirko Manzoni announced on Saturday, 11 December, that the Demobilization, Disarming, and Reintegration (DDR) program has, for the first time, successfully closed a RENAMO military base in the northern region. 560 former RENAMO militiamen were demobilized in Murrupula district, Nampula province, and have moved to the reintegration phase, per the report.  The DDR process had been ongoing at this base and is now completed.  The UN hopes to complete the DDR process in Mozambique in 2022.

Nazir Takdi, was released on Friday, 10 December, after being kidnapped by 4 armed men from his car at the Eduardo Mondlane University (EMU) Campus in October 2021.  No arrest was made and, according to the National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC), his family did not cooperate in the investigations.  Takdir's release was reportedly due to the efforts of the Security and Intelligence Service (SISE).  However, it is unclear whether he was rescued or if a ransom was paid.  Bashit Gani, another man abducted in Maputo on the same day as Takdir, is still reportedly held by his kidnappers.

Police Commander General Bernardino Rafael said on 12 December that Mozambican troops had recently clashed with a group of insurgents in Mecula district, ambushing a group of militants, and reportedly killing Cassimo, a top insurgent leader from Niassa.  The exact date and location of this clash is unclear, though it likely took place in early December, either north-east or south of Mecula town, where insurgents in November and December have been active.
A 12-year-old minor was raped and impregnated, allegedly, by a 30-year-old man.  The suspect was arrested, though no location was detailed in the report on 11 December.
A 30-year-old man was arrested on Saturday, 11 December, for allegedly raping and impregnating a 12-year-old minor.  No location was detailed in the report.

PRM Filipe Nyusi inaugurated the new Montepuez-Ruaça road in Balama district, Cabo Delgado, on Monday, 13 December.  The road is approximately 135km of the N14 route, which starts at the Bridge over Ruaca river at the Niassa Border, and passes through the districts of Kwekwe and Balama, then ends at the SW side of Montepuez.

Beginning 13 December, Maputo City said it will host a vaccination caravan, which aims to fast-track vaccinations for people aged 18 and above in the capital.  The caravan will be in a pilot phase for 8 days and will be positioned in crowded points, such as markets and public transport terminals.  The initiative intends to combat the rise in Covid cases in the city, where 52% of the active cases and 87% of the inpatient cases in the country have been recorded.

A new Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), which aims to combat money laundering and terrorist financing, was signed by the Bank of Mozambique and the General Gaming Inspectorate on Friday, 10 December, in Maputo city.  The two will increase information sharing and consultations in order to fight terror and criminal financing in Mozambique.

The Hidden Debts trial has been postponed, due to lawmakers and other participants testing positive for Covid-19, and will resume on 6 January 2022, per a report on 13 December.  The first Covid case detected was on Thursday, 9 December, resulting in the cancellation of the HD trial hearing on the said date, and so far, 3 others have also tested positive for the virus. Participants were required to comply with a mandatory 14-day quarantine.

The US has suspended its support for new carbon-intensive projects abroad, as part of efforts to combat climate change and accelerate renewable energy worldwide. This move, announced on 13 December, will potentially impact the Mozambique Rovuma Venture, a $25B-project led by a US-based gas company, which aims to explore Area 4 of the Rovuma Basin in Cabo Delgado.

Speaking at a National Assembly on Friday, 10 December, South African Deputy President, David Mabuza, said that the ongoing insurgency in Mozambique could possibly spill over into neighboring states. As a SADC member, South Africa continues to provide capacity for military training, as well as provide reconnaissance and equipment support, to assist in combatting terrorism in Mozambique.

As of 13 December, 113 new Covid cases were reported in the country over the past 24 hours, with 63 cases from Maputo city and 34 from Maputo province.  1 death and 6 recoveries were reported in the same period. Meanwhile, 12 were discharged from hospitals, and 14 people were admitted. 27 people are now still under medical care.  In summary, the updated cumulative total cases as of 13 December are: 153,787 positive; 149,964 recoveries; 1,945 deaths; 7,111 admissions; and 1,874 active cases.

Total Energies reopened its information office in Pemba, Cabo Delgado, on Saturday, 11 December, 9 months after suspending its activities in Cabo Delgado due to the attack on Palma. The company's reopening aims to improve communications between interested parties in the Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) exploration project in Area 4 of the Rovuma Basin.  This is the latest sign of companies slowly looking towards an eventual restart of operations in the Palma area.

On 13 December, Mozambican police arrested a man in possession of 10 blank Covid-19 vaccine cards.  It is unclear whether the man arrested is part of a bigger network, selling the said cards.  This comes as the Public Integrity Center raised concerns two days prior about an alleged scheme of selling negative Covid-19 test results.

The Ministry of Health confirmed on Tuesday, 14 December, that 17 cases of the Covid-19 Omicron variant have been detected in Mozambique.  The location for the confirmed cases was not specified in the report.  However, two of the confirmed cases were the two suspected Omicron cases announced in November by Health Minister Armindo Tiago, where one had mild symptoms and the other had no symptoms.

MDM members were reportedly arrested in the district of Inhassoro, Inhambane province, after being accused of participating in a demonstration while the two were travelling to a party congress, per a report on 13 December.  This arrest reportedly took place on 02 Dec.  An MDM delegate said one of the members was sentenced to 2 months and 15 days in jail plus payment of around 20,000 Meticais (265 Euros).  MDM is subsequently said these arrests were politically motivated.
MDM members said that their members in Panda district  have endured harassment and intimidation from pro-FRELIMO community leaders since the end of November, per a report on 13 December.

Reports from Zimbabwe on 13 December said that the country is currently experiencing fuel shortages due to maintenance work in Beria, Sofala.  These shortages were expected to ease before the end of the week.

Mozambique recorded an increase in hospitalizations due to Covid-19, admitting 13 more people within a 24-hour period, all in Maputo city as of 12 December.   Per the report on 12 December, a total of 26 people are currently in hospitals due to Covid-19 complications.

Mozambique inflation in November was 0.99%, based on data drawn from Maputo, Nampula, and Beira, according to the National Statistics Institute (INE). The inflation was largely due to a 6.5% increase in petrol and a 4.6% increase in diesel. Per the report on 12 December, the annual inflation was 6.77%, based on data between 1 December 2020 to 30 November 2021.

In the last 3 months, 12 motorcycle drivers have died in accidents around the central province of Manica. In Chimoio, it is common to find 3 or more riders on 1 motorbike, without helmets, and driving against the flow of traffic.  Transit Police have launched a campaign to arrest drivers in the province without protective helmets, and those driving in "dangerous maneuvers", per a report on 12 December.

ISCAP claimed responsibility for an attack on 8 December, at Lichengwe, Mecula district, south of Mecula town, where the villages of Chinene and Nampequesso had also been targeted.  ISCAP said they targeted "dozens of houses belonging to Christians", per the report on 14 December.

The US Gov't launched a higher education career development program in the provinces of Maputo and Manica, through the UN States Agency for International Dev't (USAID), on 13 December.  The program aims to provide career guidance, skills development, and work readiness, by partnering with 3 Mozambican higher education institutions.

On Wednesday, 8 December, insurgents invaded the village of Temene, where they killed and kidnapped several people, and burned houses, reportedly moving from Lichengwe, south of Mecula town, where they had also carried out an attack earlier on the same day.  A source later reported a young man was killed in this attack, and that his body was mutilated and left at the scene of the attack.

Local drivers along the Mecula-Marrupa route raised concerns about the terror threats in the area, saying there is currently little movement between Mecula and Marrupa, as most of the people from these areas have fled to Lichinga and Cuamba, per a report on 12 December after recent insurgent attacks in the area.

On 13 December, the Mozambican Gov't approved the creation of a Central Office for Combating Organized and Transnational Crime, budgeted at over 69M Meticais (around 1.1M USD), and which will focus on terrorism, kidnappings, and other crimes.

A truck travelling from Mozambique, with R14M worth of illegal skin lightening products, was intercepted by South African border police in Komatipoort, along the N4 road close to the border on or around 08 December.

Local conservation groups in Niassa's Games Reserves have reportedly evacuated international and national staff from some areas per reports on 12 December, due to the expansion of insurgent attacks into Mecula and other nearby districts.
An alleged recruiter for ISCAP, the terrorist group operating in Cabo Delgado, was captured and imprisoned in Mavago, Niassa on 12 December, along with his 3 wives who also supported the recruitment.
Three men were caught in possession of rhinoceros horns in Matola, and were arrested by authorities. The horns were said to have come from Moamba district, Maputo, per a  report on 14 December.

A woman was shot dead, reportedly out of jealousy, by her boyfriend, who was an agent of the Mozambican Police (PRM) in Maputo province, on Saturday, 11 December.  The accused was also arrested on the same day.

An agent of the Mozambican Police (PRM) in Maputo province, was arrested after he shot and killed his girlfriend, reportedly out of jealousy.  The incident and arrest both occurred on Saturday, 11 December.
A police officer was held in the Cahora Bassa district, Tete Province, for his alleged involvement in a recent armed robbery, sources reported on 14 December.
A former member of the Mozambican Police (PRM), along with 4 other men, were sentenced to 28 years in prison for participating in the assault and rape of a minor, per a report on 14 December.

The body of a minor, under the age of 9, was found in a tutor's house on Saturday, 11 December, in Mulotane, Boane district.  The child had been kidnapped in early November, and no arrest was detailed in the report.

As of Tuesday, 14 December, the Ministry of Health reported 733 new Covid cases in the country in the past 24 hours, of which, 365 were from Maputo city and 238 from Maputo province.  This is the highest reported number of daily cases since 28 July, where 2,460 cases were reported in 1 day.  In the same 24-hour period, no deaths and 25 recoveries were reported. Five were discharged and 7 were newly admitted.  The country has a total of 29 currently admitted patients due to Covid, 24 of which are in Maputo city (82.75%).  In summary, the updated cumulative total cases as of 14 December are: 154,520 positive; 149,989 recoveries; 1,945 deaths; and 2,582 active cases.

On Tuesday, 14 December, PRM Filipe Nyusi warned the country of possible tightening of restrictions by the government, due to the progressive increase in Covid-19 cases in recent days.  Nyusi appealed to the unvaccinated people to get themselves inoculated, especially as many people are still seen clustered together in public places.
The US Senate blocked the appointment of US ambassadors to Mozambique and Angola, due to Republican opposition.

China donated 1 Million doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to Mozambique on Monday, 13 December.  Health Minister Armindo Tiago said the donation comes at a most opportune time, as Covid cases continue to increase in the country.

The UK has taken off Mozambique and 10 other countries from its "red list" beginning 04:00 on Wednesday, 15 December, due to diminishing concerns over the Omicron variant.  The variant has already taken hold in the UK, making up a third of the new infections recorded in their country, per the report.  Mandatory hotel quarantine will no longer be required for travelers from Mozambique.  All travelers, if fully vaccinated and with a negative PCR test taken within two days from arrival, may be released.  Otherwise, travelers must isolate at home for 10 days and take a PCR test on day 1 and day 8, or later, during the isolation period.

Australia lifted the travel ban on arrivals from Mozambique and 7 other African countries, beginning Wednesday, 15 December. The variant is now acknowledged to be present throughout the world, and the travel ban is no longer judged to be an effective way of preventing its spread.

On the evening of 14 December, a local businesswoman was kidnapped in Gondola, Manica Province just after she had arrived home and was walking from her car to her house.  Her kidnappers arrived outside of her home in a Toyota vehicle, and forced the woman into the vehicle at gun point.  The vehicle was last reported to be travelling towards Chimoio, and police set up road blocks along the N6 and N7 roads to attempt to intercept the gang; searches for the gang in Chimoio are also ongoing.
Police searches for a kidnap gang who abducted a woman in Gondola were ongoing in Chimoio on 15 December.

Authorities seized six tons of dried fish and shrimp which were illegal fished in Praia-Nova on 15 December.  Authorities stated that trawl nets were used to catch the fisheries during the closed season.
Police arrested a suspect for stealing and slaughtering two livestock in Dondo on 15 December. The suspected intended to use the meat for his wedding.

Police arrested a suspect for counterfeiting in Moatize on 15 December. The suspect was in possession of 67,000 meticais worth of counterfeit bills.
The Mozambican Defense Minister Artur Chume visited Rwandan troops in Cabo Delgado on 14 December. Minister Chume was briefed regarding the current operations of the foreign forces in the province.

President Nyusi on 15 December said that the Mozambican state could potentially impose restrictions on unvaccinated people calling for them to take the vaccine. The announcement comes as Mozambique recorded 17 new COVID Omicron cases.
Two police officers were arrested for assaulting a civilian in Chimoio on 15 December. The policemen reportedly started the assault after stopping the victim for not wearing a mask.

The Spanish government extended the travel ban on Mozambique to from 2 December to 29 December. The Spanish government stated that only Spanish nationals or residents can return to Spain or Andorra or take transit flights from the respective countries. The Spanish government also previously issued a travel ban on South Africa, Botswana, Essuatini, Lesotho, Mozambique, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Malawi and Zambia along with Mozambique.

A new report indicated on 15 December that there is an elevated risk of Mozambique being impacted by cyclones by March 2022.  8 to 12 cyclone events in the Indian Ocean are expected in the coming months.
Police arrested a suspect involved with a child murderer in Boane District on 15 December. The suspect previously abducted the child before conducting the murder.
Public transport drivers coming from Ressano Garcia in Maputo province stopped services due to poor condition of border terminal at Ressano Garcia on the morning of 14 December.

The European Union imposed travel and financial sanctions on Russian mercenary group Wagner due to reported incidents of torture and extrajudicial executions in Mozambique and several other countries.  Russian mercenaries were active in Mozambique in 2019 , fighting against the insurgents in Cabo Delgado before pulling out of the country.

Sources stated that around 20,000 HIV/AIDs patients stopped taking their anti-viral treatments in Cabo Delgado after being displaced by the insurgency. The Community Support Association was assisting in identifying the patients at resettlement centers to direct them to healthcare services.

Mocimboa da Praia District government stated that functions of the district secretariat resumed in the town on 15 December. This comes to symbolize the resumption of the other functioning services in preparation for the restoration of basic conditions in order to allow MDP's population to return to the town and district.

Angola lifted the travel ban previously imposed on Mozambique and 6 other countries, per their statement on Tuesday, 14 December.  This came after the UK and other countries lifted travel restrictions related to omicron.

Three people were killed and 12 were injured in a road accident involving two vehicles along the National Highway Number One (EN1) on Tuesday evening, 14 December. Reports indicate that two vehicles from opposite direction collided along the highway.

Mozambican Government asked the South African Constitutional Court for leave to appeal against extradition of former minister Manuel Chang to the US. Chang is currently under trial over involvement to the USD2-billion corruption scandal.

Reports indicate on 16 December that FNB Mozambique has increased the security of online transactions with its credit and debit cards. The company used the 3D Secure feature to provide an authentication method designed so that FNB customers can confirm payments relating to their purchases made online by entering a one-time password (OTP) sent by SMS to the contact associated with their card. This feature has been automatically activated on all FNB cards and does not entail additional customers.

Reports indicate on 16 December that military authorities are monitoring calls and other electronic devices of investigative journalists, political opponents, social activists, academics, among other personalities who opposed the current administration.  The government is reportedly building profiles of individuals it considers critical of the government.  Military personnel recently reportedly trained to use a new security system to track such. Sources added that aside from the administration's critics, the system will also allow tracking of criminal activities. The new security system differs from the Pegasus, made by an Israeli company, which was blacklisted in the US

Another source said the insurgent message was "while you (security forces) are walking on tarred roads, real men (the militants) are in the woods".  Other sources reported two people beheaded in this attack.

Mozambique reported 1,234 new COVID cases in the country on 16 December, including 472 new cases in Maputo City, 369 in Maputo, 198 in Gaza, 92 in Inhambane, 59 in Manica, 21 in Sofala, 11 in Tete, 9 in Cabo Delgado, 1 in Zambezia, 1 in Nampula, and 1 in Niassa.  2 new COVID deaths were reported as well.  There are now 4,571 active COVID cases in the country, as well as 37 hospitalizations, including 29 in Maputo City.  This is the highest number of cases in the country in over 4 months in a single day as the 4th wave of cases continues to escalate.
Flooding was reported in parts of Maputo on 16 December following a heavy downpour in the city.

On 16 December, Chief of the General Staff of the FADM, Joaquim Mangrasse, confirmed the infiltration of insurgents in Niassa province, especially in Mecula District.  Military sources had reported this development earlier on 11 December as well.
On 16 December, President Nyusi said that the country is expecting to receive more than 32 million vaccines against covid-19 in 2022.

President Nyusi, speaking at the Assembly of Republic on 16 December, called on the public to remain calm amid the outbreak of armed attacks in Cabo Delgado. He said that insurgents currently have no headquarters while the military troops have deactivated most of the bases. He added that insurgents are always under constant pressure from Mozambican, SAMIM , and Rwandan troops in the northern region. The joint offensive has killed 200 insurgents, including third-ranked insurgent Rajab Fakir, and 9 other militant leaders and captured 245 other insurgents. He also highlighted that insurgent attacks had been reduced by three times compared to data from last year. 160 attacks were recorded in 2020, compared to just 52 attacks recorded in 2021, thanks to Military Operations in Cabo Delgado.  Nyusi also aknowledged that insurgent troops have spread into Niassa.

Mozambican police arrested a 32-year-old woman on 16 December for allegedly attempting to  tear her husband's testicles using her teeth following an argument. The attack happened around 22:00 on 12 December. The victim  was taken to the Provincial Hospital of Xai-Xai.

A 32-year-old woman attempted to  tear her husband's testicles using her teeth following an argument in Xai-Xai around 22:00 on 12 December. The victim  was taken to the Provincial Hospital of Xai-Xai. Reports on 16 December indicate that the suspect was arrested.

Two police officers assaulted a woman and her child as they attempted to arrest her in Mocuba, Zambezia, on 16 December. The officers reportedly handcuffed the victim by her ankle. The reason for the arrest was not disclosed. Local authorities later arrested the officers involved in the incident.

COVID-19 outbreak was reported at Maputo’s Maximum Security Penitentiary Establishment (EPMS) on 16 December after 40 out of 50 inmates tested positive with the virus. However, none of the affected inmates were hospitalized nor isolated inside the facility. A prison guard claimed that The National Penitentiary Service (SERNAP) stopped the COVID-19 testing for inmates to avoid creating panic inside the facility.

Sources said on 16 December that Doctor Basit Gani, who was abducted in Maputo, was released after nearly two months in captivity. Reports suggest that he was released last week; however, further details were not disclosed.  Gani was abducted on the morning of 7 October near Eduardo Mondlane University. Notably, businessman Nazir Takdir, who was abducted less than an hour after Gani, was also released last week.

National Institute for Communicable Diseases announced that South Africa recorded 26,976 daily COVID-19 cases on 15 December. The Omicron variant of the virus influences the surge of cases. Hospitalized individuals reached 7 339, with just 6.8% in intensive care units. This recent development threatens iMozambique, which has also witnessed an escalation of its coronavirus cases in recent weeks.

Malaria cases in Nampula witnessed an 11%.9 increase of cases during the first ten months of the year compared to last year. 2,309,942 people were diagnosed with the disease in 2021, against 2,065,021 in the same period in 2020. 47.5% of the affected population were children under 5.

Reports on 16 December stated that fewer Mozambican travelers are going to South Africa ahead of the Christmas season. This was primarily caused by the fees charged for Covid-19 testing at the borders, which many cannot afford. South African authorities do not recognize negative test certificates issued in Mozambique, thus charging R300 for COVID-19 tests carried out on the driver and passengers.

The Mozambican parliament passed the final reading of the government’s budget and plan for 2022 on Wednesday, 15 December. 143 deputies of the Frelimo Party voted in favor of the plan, while the 48 deputies from Renamo and the Mozambique Democratic Movement (MDM) voted against it. The said plan foresees 2.9% growth in 2022. Notably, The budget predicts a 19.7% increase in defense and security expenses, mainly primarily caused by the counter-terrorism operations in Cabo Delgado. Total defense and security expenditure in 2022 is budgeted at 37.9 billion meticais.

Studies stated that COVID cases in Africa are likely to be around 20 times to 100 times more than the officially announced statistics, according to a report at a recent African Public Health Conference.  This could mean Mozambique has seen at least 3 million COVID cases over the course of the pandemic.
Security forces arrested two suspects for drug trafficking and counterfeiting in Mafalala, Maputo City on 16 December. The amount of drugs seized during the arrest were not disclosed.

Reports in December indicated that SAMIM forces in Cabo Delgado currently are maintaining stability/protecting civilians, while Rwandans are seen as “tip of the spear” to attack insurgents. RDF was said to be the one conducting an offensive in the areas that witnessed recent insurgent attacks, while SAMIM operations in Cabo Delgado are increasingly non-combat focused.  Rwandan troops also now regularly operate outside of Mocimboa da Praia and Palma, which had been their designated zones of operation.
Reports on 16 December stated that residents in the Macomia district are frustrated that violence continues despite significant SAMIM deployments in the district.

Reports on 16 December stated that residents of the Mecula district in Niassa prefer Rwandan intervention in the area to a SAMIM deployment. They view the deployment of Rwandan forces as their only hope to tackle insecurity in their district.
Rwandan Defense Forces were reportedly deployed to the Ngapa area on or around 25 November following insurgent attacks in that area. Further details about the deployment were not disclosed.

Reports have indicated that Rwandan Defense Forces were deployed to the Mecula area following insurgent attacks in that area; this deployment likely occurred on or before 10 December. Further details about the deployment were not disclosed.

Mozambique reported 975 new COVID cases in the country on 15 December, including 392 new cases in Maputo City, 331 in Maputo, 113 in Gaza, 81 in Inhambane, 41 in Manica, 7 in Sofala, 3 in Cabo Delgado, 3 in Zambezia, 2 in Tete, 2 in Nampula, and 0 in Niassa.  One new COVID deaths was reported as well.  There are now 3,530 active COVID cases in the country.

Tanzanian troops engaged insurgents who attacked Kiwengulo village in Tanzania, just across the Rovuma River from Cabo Delgado and about 15 airline km north of Pundanhar in Palma District in the late hours of 10 December. Five insurgents were killed, and a Tanzanian army vehicle was destroyed during the encounter. Insurgents killed at least 4 people in the attack before the arrival of Tanzanian forces, and had intended to attack the homes of local officials before Tanzanian troops arrived at the scene.
Reports on 15 December indicate that insurgent leader, identified as Bonomade Machude Omar, allegedly hid in Paquitequete neighborhood in Pemba in 2020.

According to an early December report, security forces arrested a Tanzanian national, identified as Amisse Macuthaya, who was suspected to be linked with insurgents in Cabo Delgado. He was believed to be delivering weapons to insurgents and frequently traveled to and from Tanzania. He was released from custody after paying a bribe. The date of this arrest was unclear.

Displaced people from the Quissanga district have begun to return to their homes. 150 men from Bilibiza returned on 3 December to clean the town, while another convoy of civilians arrived on 9 December.

Displaced people from the Quissanga district have begun to return to their homes. 150 men from Bilibiza returned on 3 December to clean the town, while another convoy of civilians arrived on 9 December.

The US Government issued travel restrictions to Mecula and Marrupa districts of Niassa Province on 16 December due to the threat of insurgent attacks in these areas after recent militant attacks. The US prohibited its government personnel from traveling in the aforementioned districts until further notice. They also advised to take extra caution in the vicinity of large gatherings or protests, review security plans, monitor local media for updates, and enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to receive security updates.

On 16 December, Russia announced the approval of USD 2 million support in humanitarian aid to the victims of insurgent attacks in Mozambique. The donation will be channeled through the World Food Programme (WFP) to contribute to the WFP projects in Mozambique.

Mozambique recorded 1,382 new COVID cases on 17 December, the highest number of daily new cases in the past four months.  Maputo City recorded the highest number of new cases with 564 cases, followed by 466 in Maputo province, 198 in Gaza, 139 in Inhambane, 122 in Gaza, 57 in Manica, 19 in Sofala, 8 in Cabo Delgado, 4 in Nampula, and 3 in Tete.  There are now 5,920 active COVID cases in the country and 42 hospitalizations, including 34 in Maputo City.  In the last 24 hours, no COVID-19 related deaths were recorded, while 33 infected have recovered from the virus,  25 of which are reported in Gaza province and 8 in Manica.

On 17 December, Canadian Health Minister, Jean-Yves Duclos, announced the lifting of the ban on travelers from Mozambique and nine other African countries. This will take effect from 23:59 on 18 December. Other African countries affected by this development are South Africa, Nigeria, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Lesotho, Eswatini, Namibia, Malawi, and Egypt. Duclos added that pre-arrival negative PCR tests for all travelers would also be reinstated as of 21 December.

French Navy ship Champlain docked in Pemba on 12 December. The ship was loaded with military equipment for the protection of Afungi and the LNG project. This development was preceded by an increase in inspection and patrolling operations in the Mozambique Channel, covering the territorial waters of Cabo Delgado and Zambezia. Maritime surveillance is expected to increase as the floating platform (FLNG), produced in South Korea is scheduled to enter the Mozambican waters in mid-January 2022.

Reports indicated on 18 December that SANDF troops on patrol recovered smuggled six top-of-the-line vehicles on the Mozambican border near Mpumalanga on or around 11 December. Occupants of the vehicles immediately fled upon sighting the security forces. The vehicles were handed over to the authorities for further investigation.

Two suspected drug traffickers were arrested on a beach near the town of Angoche, Nampula on 17 December.  Two kg of heroin and three motorcycles were seized from their possession.

Six people were killed and 12 were injured in a  road accident on National Road Number 1 (EN1) in Maimelane, Inhassoro district, Inhambane province on Thursday evening, 16 December. Reports suggest that the passenger transport vehicle overturned due to excessive speed.

Director-General of Mozambique’s investment and export promotion agency, Agencia Para a Promocao de Investimento e Exportacoes (APIEX), Gil Bares, said that Rwandans are welcome to invest in Mozambique. Bares, along with a 15-man delegation, is in Rwanda and attended the ongoing International Trade Fair (Expo 2021) as well as exploring investment opportunities in Rwanda.
The former minister and governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Sergio Vieira, died in South Africa on 16 December. He was in South Africa, where he was receiving treatment for an undisclosed illness.
Large numbers of IDPs were reported on 18 December to be moving through Mueda en route to Palma. Returning IDPs said they want to reclaim their land to cultivate ahead of the rainy season.

On 18 November, several sources reported gunshots in the Namina area, with some sources allegeing an insurgent attack in the area.  This report was not confirmed, and other sources later said an individual in a military uniform had been found in the area, been mistaken for an insurgent, and this had caused panic over an attack in the area.

Mozambique reported 1,252 new COVID cases in the country on 18 December, including 545 new cases in Maputo City, and 401 cases in Maputo Province.  Two new COVID deaths were reported as well.  There are now 6,978 active COVID cases in the country, as well as 48 hospitalizations. In the past 24 hours, 192 patients have recovered from the virus, 179 of them in Maputo City and 13 in Inhambane province.

130 houses were submerged in floods following heavy rains in Maputo city on 16 December. Affected neighborhoods include Albazine, Costa do Sol, Laulane, FPLM and Mavalane B. Flooded roads also resulted in heavy traffic around the area.

A terrorism report by the US Department of State on 16 December indicates that Mozambique has become a "safe haven for terrorists", saying more than 1,500 people have been killed in insurgent attacks since the beginning of 2020, with over 500,000 people displaced by insurgent attacks.  The report also said the Mozambican government and regional partners have struggled to respond effectively to terror attacks in Cabo Delgado, also saying that border security remains a significant challenge for the Mozambican government to confront.

On 17 December, the Mozambican Government declared 21 December as a day of mourning for the death of Sergio Vieira, former minister and governor of the Bank of Mozambique. Vieira died a day prior in South Africa after from an undisclosed illness.

On 17 December, the Municipal Assembly approved the new transport price list in Maputo city. Effective 1 January 2022, transport fare will increase between 2 and 3 meticais. Notably, only the ruling FRELIMO assembly members voted in favor of the fare increase,  while RENAMO and MDM voted against it, as it will incur additional expenses to the general public. This development came after transport operators have been demanding a fare rise, complaining the increasing price of oil, vehicle parts and maintenance service.

On 17 December, Maputo City Health Service announced that they will start testing for COVID-19 in communities and bus terminals in response to the fourth wave of the virus. This comes as  the country recorded 1,382 new COVID cases on the same day. 564 of which was recorded in Maputo city, which represents 40.81% of the total cases.

On 19 December, a notable increase in traffic volume was reported at the Lebombo border was reported as many travelled into Mozambique ahead of Christmas and New Years. Since the holiday season started, long queues of vehicles have been seen in the Komatipoort area. According to Lebombo Port Manager Obed Maditsi, they were anticipating a higher influx of travelers just as Christmas day nears, and another surge is expected in January as travelers made their way back from their vacation.

On 18 December, authorities announced that in the last 24 hours, 220,066 people had been vaccinated with the first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine, under the third stage of the National Mass Vaccination Campaign. This increased the number of individuals who have received one shot to 7,602,216, while a total of 5,176,054 people have been fully inoculated in the country since the beginning of the vaccination program on 8 March.

Mozambique reported 541 new COVID cases in the country on 19 December, including 288 new cases in Maputo City, and 158 cases in Maputo Province.  Two new COVID deaths were reported as well.  There are now 7,513 active COVID cases in the country, as well as 13 hospitalizations. In the past 24 hours, four patients have recovered from the virus,  three are from Niassa and one from Zambezia.

On 18 December, Turkish President Erdogan pledged to donate  15 million vaccines against COVID-19. This is part of Turkey's effort to curb the spread of diseases in the continent, where several people are still unvaccinated. Erdogan said that the Turkish-developed vaccine, Turkovac, will be shared with Africa after its emergency approval is received.

Southern African Development Community (SADC) Mission in Mozambique (SAMIM) counterterror operations has extended past its January expiration date, Naledi Pandor, the South African government’s senior international relations and cooperation representative, said on 18 December. Pandor did not provide further details on the said extension.

On 17 December, Portugal announced the resumption of to and from Mozambique. Effective from Saturday, apart from Mozambique, Portugal allows essential travel to and from South Africa, Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, and Zimbabwe. However, authorities require travelers to provide a record of departure from the said countries and undergo a period of prophylactic isolation of 14 days, at home or in a place indicated by the health authorities upon arriving in Portugal. Notably, the isolation may be cut short for travelers who obtain a negative result in a nucleic acid amplification test ( NAAT,) or rapid antigen test ( RAT) performed on the third day after arrival.

Four people were killed after their canoe sank in Pebane area, Zambezia on 15 December. The canoe was reportedly transporting people and goods between Mulai and Djogoro in Pebane district. The cause of the accident is still unknown.

Authorities of Mecuburi, Nampula disclosed on 20 December that there were no insurgent attacks in Namina over the weekend. Some sources did report a criminal incident in the area over the weekend, while others reported a man dressed in a military uniform had been mistaken for an insurgent, causing panic in the area.

Reports on 20 December indicate that the UN Migration Agency in Mozambique, the Central and Provincial Community Policing Department, and the Provincial Police Command of the Police of the Republic of Mozambique (PRM) and in coordination with IOM, conducted a capacity building activity to 26 police officers of Cabo Delgado Province, from the 14 to 16 of December, in a bid to strengthen the relationship with communities and efficiently address security concerns. The implementation districts of the activity are Pemba, Metuge, Mecufi, Ancuabe, Chiure, Balama, and Namuno. The training is part of two projects funded by the European Union (EU) with 4 million EUR and the German Federal Foreign Office (GFFO) with 4.2 million EUR.

9 of the 17 districts in Cabo Delgado have at least some non-functional schools due to insurgent attacks. According to the Adventist Development and Relief Agency (ADRA), 96,942 students were affected by the terrorist attacks, and 50,922 of which are female. Schools are not currently operating in parts or all of Palma, Mocimboa da Praia, Nangade, Muidumbe, Macomia, Ibo, Meluco, Quissanga, and Mueda

Reports on 20 December indicate that the pro-government militia in Mueda district are requesting additional military equipment support to combat insurgents in Nangade, MDP, and along the border with Tanzania.

President Nyusi announced on 13:00, 20 December, that COVID restrictions declared in October will be kept in place for at least 30 days until 21 January as the number of COVID-19 infections in the country have surged in the last couple of days. Notably, curfews will be lifted from midnight on 24 and 25 of December and 31 December to 1 January 2022.  Beaches across the country will remain closed during this period, while the curfew from 0000 - 0400 hrs also remains in place.  Nyusi also said that in the future, vaccinated persons would recieve "preferential treatment", encouraging Mozambicans to get vaccinated against COVID 19.  Other changes include the halting of prison visits for the next month.  Patients in hospitals may now only be visited by one person rather than 2 a day. Other preventative measures remain in place.  Nyusi also indicated police and the INAE will increase inspection measures, and said if a "red line" was crossed, most "drastic" measures would be announced.

On the morning of 19 December, FADM and SADC forces attacked an insurgent camp east of Chai village, north of Mocimboa.  10 militants were reported killed during an exchange of gunfire and 14 civilian hostages were rescued. An unconfirmed source reported several SAMIM troops killed during these clashes.  Some of the recued female victims allegedly worked for an insurgent leader identified as Ibn Omar. Operations continued in the area during 20 December.  This resulted in an exchange of gunfire at approximately 06:00 in the morning.  Mozambican officials later said an insurgent base had been destroyed in the area, and that militant leader Bonomade Omar had been hiding in the area, though the whereabouts of the insurgent leader are still not known.

Some of the recued female victims allegedly worked for an insurgent leader identified as Ibn Omar. Operations continued in the area during 20 December.  This resulted in an exchange of gunfire at approximately 06:00 in the morning.

Mozambique recorded 553 new COVID cases on 20 December.  Maputo City recorded the highest number of new cases with 361 cases, followed by 157 in Maputo province, 16 in Inhambane, 10 in Gaza, 3 in Nampula, 3 in Tete, 2 in Cabo Delgado, and 1 in Manica.  There are now 5,920 active COVID cases in the country and 42 hospitalizations, including 34 in Maputo City.  In the last 24 hours, no COVID-19 related deaths were recorded, while 49 infected have recovered from the virus,  and 64 were hospitalized.

International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on 21 December that Mozambique's economy is forecast to grow by 4% in 2022 but will remain vulnerable to the effect of terrorism in the northern region as well as the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. The aforementioned forecast was based on the recovery of the non-LNG economy in the country.

On 21 December, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) announced that they will start to discuss an extended credit facility with Mozambique in January 2022. The discussion is IMF's first potential programme with the country since suspending support in 2016, following the USD2 billion Hidden Debts scandal. This development will help ease financial pressure to the country as it recovers from pandemic, famine and insurgency.

RENAMO vows to settle pension delays to 2,000 former militiamen by 2022, Renamo leader Ossufo Momade said during a meeting in Soalpo, Manica on 20 December. No specific date disclosed on when the payments will be settled.  Momade called on other former guerillas to join the government's DDR process.

On Friday evening, 17 December, security forces trailed a group of suspects who kidnapped a businesswoman in Gondola, Manica.  The woman was kidnapped on Tuesday from her home. A police chase ensued in Chimoio, forcing the suspects to abandon the victim. Despite the roadblocks established by the police, the suspects managed to escape. Efforts are underway to arrest the suspects.

Insurgents ambushed SAMIM troops east of Chai on Monday twice, killing a South African soldier, the South African military reported on 21 December. Other sources reported that soldier killed was a member of South Africa's special forces.  One source said the killing may have occurred on Sunday night. SAMIM forces ultimately defeated an initial ambush, before being attacked again a short time later by insurgents while awaiting for a helicopter.  Other sources reported several Mozambican soldiers killed in this clash.  Mozambican and South African troops were previously reported to have engaged insurgents in the area on Sunday and Monday, killing at least 10 militants.
Insurgents on 21 December ambushed SAMIM troops east of Chai; SAMIM forces successfully repelled this ambush.  Insurgents would later launch a second attack, killing one South African soldier.

Mozambique reported 2,068 new COVID cases on 21 December, with 860 new cases in Maputo City, 521 in Maputo, 238 in Inhambane, 229 in Gaza, 143 in Manica, 35 in Sofala, 17 in Cabo Delgado, 8 in Tete, 9 in Zambezia, 7 in Nampula, and 1 in Niassa.  There are now more than 10,000 active cases in the country, along with 77 hospitalizations, including 62 in Maputo City. This is the highest number of COVID cases recorded in a single day since late July.

Rwandan troops closed the Afungi-Mocimboa da Praia road links on 11 December to unauthorized civilian vehicles as a measure to restore security in Palma and Mocimboa da Praia Districts.  It is not clear if a specific incident triggered these closures.

Security operations are ongoing in the area of Macomia near the south bank of Messalo River, east of Chai, on 21 December. Reports indicate that around 300-400 insurgents were positioned in the mountain areas.

On 18 December, LAM launched its first commercial flight into the Filipe Jacinto Nyusi Airport, in Chongoene, Gaza province. The said flight aims to attract travelers who want to cut travel time to Gaza province from Johannesburg or Maputo.

Reports on 20 December indicate that Total is reportedly considering several possible ways to resume work in Cabo Delgado by 2022.  This could include the use of offshore platforms and vessels to reduce operations on land, or to potentially move LNG trains further south outside areas impacted by the insurgency.  Ultimately the company does still reportedly intend to return to Afungi, though the fluid security situation could force the company to shift strategies again.

President Nyusi in a speech over the weekend indicated that Mozambique would likely to restrict some public services for individuals who have not received Covid-19 immunizations, encouraging people to get vaccinated.  This comes amid the ongoing fourth wave of COVID in the country.

On 18 December, Niassa's Mecula District local government threatened to carry out disciplinary actions against officials and other civil servants who fled the district recent due to insurgent attacks.  This is likely intended to stop others from fleeing the area and for those who fled to return to the district.
Sources on 18 December reported that security forces were providing escorts to IDPs travelling from Mueda to Palma.

Humanitarian access constraints remain high in Cabo Delgado, an NGO reported, with aid agencies operating in Cabo Delgado forced to go through a complex approval process before delivering aid.  Security forces continue to enforce travel restrictions to much of the insurgent impacted zone, with harsh penalties enforced against those who do not obey restrictions.  The situation has improved slowly since July, when Rwandan troops launched their intervention in the province, allowing greater access for aid delivery in Palma and elsewhere.
On 16 December, Mozambican police warned citizens of the fake firefighters operating in Angoche district of Nampula. These suspects allegedly intend to rob several institutions in the area.

The Confederation of Mozambican Business Associations (CTA) will begin monitoring local content of large companies operating in Mozambique starting from 2022, CTA's executive director, Eduardo Sengo, said on 15 December.  The index aims to create an indicator to evaluate the stage of local content in the country, monitor the evolution of local content in large projects, reactivate the debate on local content and contribute to the participation of SMEs in large projects.

About 575,000 people were affected by natural disasters in Mozambique in 2021, President Nyusi said on 20 December.  These disasters caused severe damages to around 59,503 houses, of which 22,544 were completely destroyed in incidents across the country.

Reports on 17 December indicate that elective surgeries at Maputo Central Hospital (HCM) have been suspended to save existing blood stocks for the festive season. During this time, the demand for blood increases. The current blood supply at HCM is 300 units of blood, which is less than the stock in 2020, which was 500 units.

ISCAP claimed to have killed two soldiers and injured several others during an ambush on SAMIM forces in an area east of Chai on 20 December.  This is believed to refer to confirmed clashes in which insurgents engaged SAMIM troops over the weekend.

Mozambican police arrested four civil servants in Inhambane province on 22 December for allegedly receiving bribes and misuse of state funds. They were dismissed from their position while awaiting trial.

Security forces arrested two suspects for drug traffickers, one Nigerian and one Mozambican nationals, in Maputo City on 20 December. Unspecified amount of cocaine were recovered from their possession.
