National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) operatives arrested three employees of the National Migration Service (SENAMI) in Nampula on 21 December over alleged involvement in a fire incident in their director's office.  One other suspect is at large. The fire incident took place in the early hours of 5 December. The suspects were also connected in illegally facilitating the entry and exit of foreign nationals.

Mozambique received 720,000 of Covishield vaccine against COVID-19 as part of the COVAX initiative on 21 December. These doses are part of 17.8 million doses expected to be received by the country under the said initiative. This development came 19 days after the Indian Government announced that they would donate 720,000 to the country. Furthermore, Eletricidade de Mozambique (EDM) donated 14,245 N95 masks and 11,400 gloves, while Good Neighbors, a South Korean NGO, donated 20,000 reusable masks.

The European Union approved on 21 December the Multiannual Indicative Program for Mozambique from 2021 to 2027. The country will receive funding of 428 million euros devoted to the developmental aspect of the program. The partnership between the European Union and Mozambique will be based on a multidimensional approach and priority areas: Green Growth, Youth Growth and Governance, Peace and Just Society.

LAM flights resumed regular weekly flights between Maputo and Harare, Zimbabwe, on 19 December. Flights between the two destinations will take off three times a week, on Wednesdays, Fridays, and Sundays. LAM also has regional flights to Johannesburg in South Africa, and Dar-es-Salam, in Tanzania.
Insurgents reportedly ambushed SAMIM forces in an area east of Chai, Macomia on 18 December. This resulted reportedly in at least one SAMIM soldier injured.
Joint forces on 17 December were reported to have fought insurgents east of Chai amid ongoing military offensives in this area.  No further details on these clashes are currently available.
Locals witnessed the movement of a large number of soldiers and military vehicles moving between Chai and Miangalewa on the morning of 19 December.
Military helicopters launched airstrikes on insurgents' bases in east of Chai, Macomia on 19 December in the early morning hours.
Unconfirmed reports indicated between 17-19 December that security forces had targeted insurgent positions in areas near Namaluco in Quissanga District.

President Nyusi in a late December speech said that security forces had "neutralized" two suspected insurgents attempting to move from Cabo Delgado into Niassa on 07 December.  The exact location of this incident was unclear, and it was not known if the two individuals were killed or captured.

Bonomade Omar, a man identified as a top insurgent leader, was reported by some people who had surrendered to security forces on 21 December to have been present in northern Macomia, but to be intending to flee either into Tanzania or into Niassa amid ongoing operations to attempt to capture or kill him. The SADC Military Mission in Mozambique (SAMIM) announced that it had killed 14 more militants and occupied militant bases in the areas east of Chai, Macomia district, during their security operations on 19-20 December.  10 militants had previously been killed in these clashes.  1 SAMIM soldier was killed while two others were injured.  2 Mozambican soldiers were killed in these clashes, along with 4 others injured.

Mozambican Police (PRM) arrested a group of suspects and seized a cache of weapons, which the group attempted to board in a transport vehicle bound for Cabo Delgado.  The arrest was made at the Anchilo Control Post in Nampula, on Monday, 20 December.  The weapons were reportedly hidden in bags and were suspected to arm and strengthen terrorist groups active in Cabo Delgado.

Mozambique on 22 December reported 2,337 new COVID cases and 3 new deaths.  836 new cases were reported in Maputo City, 595 in Maputo, 264 in Inhambane, 242 in Gaza, and 231 in Manica.  There are now 98 people hospitalized throughout the country, and 11,675 active cases.
The Mocimboa da Praia municipal officials were present on 17 December in the town, preparing for an influx of government employees back to Mocimboa da Praia on 17 December.

MMC Resources announced that they will open a new mine in Tete province in Cassolssole, Macanga District. The gold exploration company was set to conduct small-scale open pit mining. The new mine is expected to produce 300kg of gold ore per year.

A Mozambican government report released on 16 December indicated that there are still five RENAMO bases to be closed and that almost 2,000 RENAMO who have yet to be included in the Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration (DDR) process.

The Mozambican Tax Authority announced on 20 December that it will begin to collect revenue from digital transactions in the country. The taxing of digital transactions was to protect the economy and obtain sustainable revenue collection.
Officials announced the resumption the Nampula-Cuamba railway traffic on 18 December. The railway was previously stopped due to a fire in one of the passing trains which was transporting coal.

The National Health Institute (INS) announced that research for the efficacy of mixing vaccines is being conducted in Mozambique. INS stated that the phase 2 trial was being conducted to determine the two-dose regimen of the Sinopharm vaccine with a Johnson and Johnson vaccine with 28 days apart. The vaccination schedules where the second dose is not necessarily the same as the first allowing for more flexible immunization programsas a result of vaccination shortages and possible better immune response to COVID.

Mining company Vale will sell its coal mine, logistic corridor, port, and railway project in Moatize of Tete Province. The business was to be sold to Vulcan Minerals for 270 million USD. The deal was set with an initial 80 million USD and a 10-year royalty contract. This comes as Vale announced that they shifted out of the carbon fossil fuel to become carbon neutral by 2050.

Mozambique STT signed an agreement with PowerChina Hubei Engineering to construct a deep water port in Chonguene on 21 December. The port was priced at 700 million USD. The first phase of the port was contracted at 324 million USD and approved by the Ministry of Transportation. The port was set to handle 150 million tons of cargo annually.

Health authorities announced that the positivity rate was almost at 40% for COVID testing in Mozambique as of 21 December. The positivity rate was exactly at 38.24%. Most of the new cases were from the southern provinces. The worst hit areas had the higher positive rate, 50.63% in Maputo city, and 45.77% in Maputo province.

Health authorities announced that 129,403 civilians were given their first COVID vaccine in Mozambique on 21 December.  5.6 million have completed their COVID vaccinations, while just over 8 million have received at least one shot.

Public transportation drivers state that demand for transportation between South African and Mozambique has declined significantly. Terminal operations state that the decline was due to the requirement COVID vaccination records. Drivers state that they are no waiting for several days to just have passengers request for transportation.

Health authorities announced that 120,328 civilians were given their first COVID vaccine in Mozambique on 22 December. 5.7 million have completed their COVID vaccinations.  8.2 million people have received at least one shot.

Security forces were accused of closing the road between Mueda and Palma for about a month. This comes as several vehicles transporting goods were forced to wait in line to travel along this road. Other vehicles were reportedly paying bribes to the soldiers for about 5,000 – 20,000 meticais for an escort on this route.

AU issue a report stating that Mozambique requires “urgent action to avoid catastrophe” on 22 December. The report stated that Mozambique needs to address the socio-economic challenges in communities of Cabo Delgado holistically. The AU also raised concerns that the insurgency in Cabo Delgado linking with Tanzania could create a larger insurgent zone.

The Danish Government announced the lifting of travel restrictions to Mozambique on 23 December. The lifting of the travel ban included the other southern African countries. the State Serum Institute (SSI) mentioned that the travel ban is unjustified as the Omicron variant is not widespread.
Large numbers of soldier and officers took part in the holiday celebrations in Mocimboa da Praia on 22 December, demonstrating the number of troops currently in the town.

Policemen exchange gunfire with a criminal gang in Lichinga's Ceramica neighborhood on or around 18 December, after the group attempted to break into the home of a police officer. Some of the criminals were later detained. Casualties were not mentioned.

On 22 December, militants attacked the town of Naulala 2 in Niassa province.  A Niassa Special Reserve Inspector was killed and several civilians were reported kidnapped.   Several homes were also set on fire during the attack.  Other sources later reported 5 total people killed in the attack, and one person badly wounded.

Mozambique, on Thursday, 23 December, reported 2,445 new COVID cases and 1 new death in the last 24 hours.  The new cases were reported as follows: 782 in Maputo Province, 727 in Maputo City, 238 in Inhambane, 209 in Gaza, 168 in Sofala, and 119 in Manica.  There are still 98 people in hospital units across the country, with no new admissions and discharges. Meanwhile, 66 recoveries were reported also in the same period and the total active cases were at 14,101.

As of Thursday, 23 December, 108,730 people were vaccinated with the first dose in the last 24 hours. Since the start of the 3rd phase on March 8, Mozambique has vaccinated a total of 8,405,304 people with at least one shot, of which 5,866,832 were fully vaccinated.
Mozambique has joined a digital platform that allows the tracking and verification of the authenticity of COVID-19 tests. The digital platform "Trusted Travel" was launched on Thursday, 23 December.

The Mozambican government guaranteed that it would work in coordination with the private sector to expand the water supply in the country.  The agreement was signed on Thursday, 23 December.  This agreement presumably will end private water supplier threats to cut off water to certain areas over government encroachement on their businesses.

A Mozambican citizen of Indian origin was kidnapped by 3 armed men around 07:30 on Wednesday, 22 December, in Maputo city. The victim was reportedly taken after visiting his construction work in Avenida 24 de Julho.  One source reported the man kidnapped was named Ibrahim Versailles, and is a local businessman.

Prices of goods and services in the villages of Naulala and Mecula have increased by up to five times, since the beginning of insurgent attacks in the areas.  Passenger transport have also stopped circulating due to people fleeing the areas, per the report on 23 December.

Gaza Province has received an investment of USD 7 Billion for the planned infrastructure in Chongoene district, which will allow the transport of heavy sands via a high-density multi-purpose freight rail line from Chongoene to Donga, per the report on 23 December.  Part of the amount will be allocated to the construction of a multipurpose deepwater seaport, with a reported capacity of 150M tons of cargo per year.  The infrastructure is expected to boost the economies in the SADC countries.

Two pregnant women and three other individuals who were victims of insurgency in Cabo Delgado, escaped on Wednesday, 22 December, from one of the insurgents' bases on the banks of Messalo River, after being held captive for 2 years.  The women's husbands had reportedly been brutally murdered by the insurgents after the kidnapping, which occurred in August 2019 in Nangade district, per the report.  The group also indicated that many of those abudcted by the insurgents have subsequently been killed in clashes with security forces as insurgents often force their abducted victims to the frontlines of conflict.

The US government announced that it will lift restrictions which were placed on Mozambique and other African counties in November 2021 due to concerns about the Omicron variant of Covid-19.  The restrictions blocked foreign nationals who had been physically present in Mozamibque, South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Lesotho, Eswtini, and Malawi from entering the United States for a 14 day period after leaving these countries.  These restrictions will be removed on 00:01 EST on 31 December 2021. Travelers entering the US from the counties listed above will be subject to the same travel protocols the US has put in place for other countries.  This includes a requirement for foreign nationals to be full vaccinated and have a negative Covid-19 test no more than 1 day old at the time of departure.

Public Works Minister, Joao Machatine, inaugurated a new bridge over the Messalo River, in Nairoto, Montepuez district, Cabo Delgado, on 22 December. The new bridge was reportedly valued at MZN 210 million, and will allow the transit of people and goods on the R698 road, in the Montepuez-Mueda section.
TESLA signed a major deal to buy Mozambican graphite that it will use in manufacturing batteries for electric cars. The deal signed was also for a long-term contract, per the report on 23 December.

President Nyusi enacted the law on Mandatory Social Security System for employees and state agents, on Thursday, 23 December.  The law had been previously approved by the Assembly of the Republic and was passed to the office of the President for promulgation.

Portuguese President, Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa, plans to visit Mozambique in January 2022, during the official campaign period of Portugal's legislative elections, per the report on 23 December.  No further details for his visit were disclosed in the report.

Over 150 cars departed from the Junta's Interprovincial Bus Terminal in Maputo City, between 04:00 to 09:00 on Thursday, 23 December.  People and vehicles flooded the area, anxious to reach their destinations in time for the holidays, per the report.

RENAMO on 23 December said the country's secret services have failed to recognize in time the threat of terrorism in the country, referring to the increasing terrorist activities in Cabo Delgado, which has spilled over into Niassa.  The inaction of the intelligence services has reportedly placed the country in a more vulnerable situation. RENAMO party called on the head of state to re-assess the country's counter-terrorism strategies, per their statement on 23 December.

Mozambique, on 24 December, registered 2,770 new COVID cases in the last 24 hours. This is the new highest record registered in one day, breaking the previous highest record of 2,460 on 28 July.  The new cases were reported highest in Maputo City with 904 and in Maputo Province with 599.  In the same period, 4 deaths were also reported and 26 were hospitalized.  Meanwhile, 18 people were discharged and 49 had recovered from the infection.  There are now 102 patients currently in hospital units due to the virus.  In summary, the updated cumulative total cases as of 24 December are: 170,077 positive cases; 1,965 deaths; and 151,290 recoveries.

A 23 December report indicated that insurgents present in Northern Mozambique are often armed with Chinese-manufactured, cheap and common AK rifle variants, mostly captured from the Mozambican military, other security force elements, or obtained via black market trade.  These light arms are also the types used by local army units and police forces in Mozambique and Tanzania, according to the report on 23 December.
ISCAP claimed responsibility for the 10 December attack at Kiwengulo in Tanzania.

ISCAP claimed its fighters had attacked a Mozambican Army position near Mbunda Nyali village (Pundanhar area) in the district of Palma on 3 December. Several soldiers were killed and injured. No specific details regarding the casualty numbers were mentioned. The militants claimed that they burned several camps and the soldiers fled from the area.

ISCAP claimed its fighters clashed with the Mozambican army east of Chai, Macomia district, on 20 December, and reportedly seized airdropped items from the army.  This likely refers to confirmed clashes east of Chai between 17-22 December.
Over 600 people were arrested on Thursday, 23 December, near the Lebombo Border Post, in the Nkomazi area, for trying to illegally cross the border to Mozambique.

Two of the 7 suspects, who raided the home of a retired Homicide detective in Chadcombe, Zimbabwe, are believed to have fled to Mozambique. The two most wanted suspects are Washington Hamandishe and Tatenda Mumbire, per the report on 25 December.

Reports on 25 December indicate that there was an over 40km of traffic jam along the N1 road between the Administrative Post 3 in Manhica, down to the border between the provinces of Maputo and Gaza due to the breakdown of two trucks.

Around 5,000 people were tested for COVID in past 3 days at the Ressano Garcia border, Maputo Province, of which, 122 tested positive. According to a report on 25 December, the border has been packed with people from and to South Africa, where the omicron variant outbreak was first recorded.  Per the report, over 50% of the 122 positive cases were diagnosed in miners who have traveled in different parts of the country.

898 New COVID cases and 2 new deaths in Mozambique were reported by the Ministry of Health on 25 December. The new cases were reported highest in Maputo City and Sofala with 491 and 82 cases, respectively.  In the same period, 23 people were hospitalized due to COVID, while 22 patients were discharged, which brings the total current inpatients to 101.  In summary, the updated cumulative total cases as of 25 December are: 170,975 positive; 1,967 deaths; and 151,290 recoveries.

Insurgents released a photo of the seized airdropped materials, which they claimed to have captured from SAMIM, following their clashes in east of Chai, Macomia district, on 20 December.  Seized equipment included mortars, grenades, and significant quantities of ammunition.

Ressano Garcia Border recorded a drop in the movement of migrants in 2021 compared to 2020. Between 13-23 December of both years, 64,490 travelers were recorded in 2021, while 67,577 were recorded the year prior.  Some Mozambicans had been among the 200 people apprehended by South African authorities, on Friday, 24 December, who were reportedly trying to enter the country illegally, per the report on 26 December.

The Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM) president, Lutero Simango, said the Mozambican gov't should restore economic stability and credibility in the judgment of the Hidden Debts case, per his speech on 24 December.  Simango also commented on the crimes in the country and pointed out that the authorities have done little to clarify many cases, and called for transparency.

Mozambique's Ministry of Science, Technology, and Higher Education hopes to have an additional 100 doctors trained in Cuba by 2024.  A recent cooperation agreement was formalized on Wednesday prior between the two countries, per the report on Sunday, 26 December.

Nine people were killed and 12 others injured in a road accident, Saturday night, 25 December, in Siluvo, Nhamatanda, Sofala province.  The interprovincial bus, bound for Beira, was reportedly speeding when it crashed violently into a loaded truck of wood logs.  The bus driver was taken into a police unit, per the report.

Portugal extended the deadline for Mozambique's debt payment to 31 December 2021, per a report on 23 December.  On 29 September the year prior, Mozambique requested for the postponement of payment obligations with bilateral creditors, joining over 30 countries, of which 21 were in Africa, to ease public accounts amid the COVID pandemic.

Indian Naval Ship (INS) Kesari reached the port of Maputo, on Saturday 25 December, carrying 500 tons of food aid for Mozambique, as part of the Security And Growth for All in the Region (SAGAR) mission.  This is the eighth deployment of SAGAR and is being conducted in coordination with the Ministry of External Affairs, and other agencies in India.

On 26 December, Iran announced a travel ban on Mozambique and 7 other African countries, as well as 4 European countries, until 6 January 2022, due to the spike in COVID omicron variant cases, per the report.

A woman was murdered in Mavalane neighborhood, Maputo City, on Friday night, 24 December. She was reportedly with her cousins in a tent, when a young man appeared and forced her to drink an alcoholic beverage, also threatening to stab the others. The motive of the murder is unclear. Police said the suspect has been detained.

Police detained the suspect for the murder of a woman in Mavalane neighborhood, Maputo City, on Friday night, 24 December. She was reportedly with her cousins in a tent, when a young man appeared and forced her to drink an alcoholic beverage, also threatening to stab the others. The motive of the murder is unclear.

A case of homicide was reported, which likely occurred between 24-25 December, in the Lhamanculo neighborhood of Maputo City. No further details were released on the case. However, Police said the suspect has been detained.
Police detained the suspect for a homicide case, which likely occurred between 24-25 December, in the Lhamanculo neighborhood of Maputo City. No further details were released on the case.
A dead body was found on the beach in Costa do Sol, Maputo City, between 24-25 December. The circumstances of the person's death is yet unknown as of this report.
A dead body was found at the Albasine Public Transport Terminal, Maputo City, between 24-25 December. The circumstances of the person's death is yet unknown as of this report.

Oman cancelled a previous decision to ban entry for travelers from Mozambique and 6 other countries on Sunday, 26 December.  Instead, Omani authorities will now require foreign travelers, aged 18 or older, to at least have two COVID vaccine doses to enter the country.

The Maputo Central Hospital (HCM) expressed concern over the spread of COVID, as it has infected 151 of their employees, of which, 30 are doctors and 16 of the doctors were hospitalized, per the report on 26 December.  The hospital also said that between 25-26 December, 187 people (outside of HCM's staff) were tested at HCM, of which 99 were positive of COVID.  The hospital suspects that the spread of the virus is due to the omicron variant.  Adding to their COVID concern is the lack of blood in stock at the HCM.  The hospital said it needs 2,000 units of blood to function, but only has 700.  And, between 25-26 December, the HCM admitted 281 people, of which, 61 were trauma victims from car accidents and physical aggression.

527 new COVID cases and 1 new death in Mozambique were reported by the Ministry of Health on Sunday, 26 December.  The new cases were reported highest in Maputo City with 310, meanwhile the one death recorded occurred on Thursday prior.  In the same period, 11 people were hospitalized due to COVID, while 11 patients were also discharged and another 15 people recovered from the virus.  There are 79 people currently in hospital units.  In summary, the updated cumulative total cases as of 26 December are: 171,502 positive; 1,968 deaths; 151,305 recoveries, and 18,225 active cases.
One person was killed in an accident involving a light vehicle and a motorbike, along the EN6 in the district of Dondo, Sofala province, at dawn on 25 December.

Pro-gov militia forces captured 2 suspected insurgents in the villages of Litingina and Ntamba, in Nangade district, Cabo Delgado, on Saturday, 25 December.  The two men had reportedly fled from the recent fight in Macomia district and were attempting to reach Namatil to cross into Tanzania.  One of the men was Tanznaian, and other Mozambican; the two later said they were carrying out recon work for the insurgency in Ntamba and Litingina.

Close to 1.9 million people could be acutely food insecure across Mozambique by March 2022, according to the Technical Secretariat for Food and Nutrition Security (SETSAN) in a report on 27 December.  The number could drop to 1.4 million by September 2022, with the exception of Cabo Delgado, where over 800,000 have been displaced due to insurgent attacks. SETSAN added that around 39,000 people are in a food emergency situation, per the report.

"Marching Guides" have been re-implemented by the govenrment in the district of Nangade, Cabo Delgado, to control the movement of people and goods in the area, especially that of terrorists.  Per the report on 27 December, the document will be required at all checkpoints, even in movements between villages. It also costs 100 Meticais, valid only for one trip, and will be issued by district secretaries.  This 100 meticais cost is beyond the ability to pay of many locals.  These documents were previously used during the Civil War to attempt to restrict the movement of RENAMO militants.

Eni's floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) facility for its Coral Sul project in Rovuma basin was reported to be passing Mauritius on Friday, 24 December. The facility is expected to arrive to its destination off the coast of Mozambique on 5 January in 2022 after it left South Korea on 16 November. After arrival, the installation process will commence. This facility is expected to receive fuel from the Coral gas field in the Area 4 of the Rovuma basin.

On 27 December, the National Criminal Investigation Service (Sernic) announced that 2 suspects were arrested in Beira city in connection to the kidnapping of a businesswoman in Gondola, Manica province, on 14 December. A vehicle believed to have been used by the suspects in carrying out crimes was also seized during the operation. The suspects were identified to be members of a gang of 9 planning to carry out another crime in Beira.

On 27 December, the National Institute of Health (Instituto Nacional de Saúde) launched the research to assess the combination of 2 different Coronavirus vaccines - Vero Cell and Johnsons & Johnsons - safety and capacity to trigger immune response. The launching took place in Marracuene district of Maputo Province. According to the institute's director, Ilesh Jani, the vaccines were administered with an interval of 28 days. If the combination proves effective, this will help address the challenge of vaccine availability in the country.

column4: A report on 28 December indicated that the wife of Mariano Nhongo, the RENAMO dissident guerilla leader killed in October, demanded her children's release. Amelia Marcelino, alleged that her children were kidnapped by members of the Defense and Security Forces (FDS) a year ago to compel Nhongo to surrender. The police, however, denied such kidnapping took place. She also called on the government to give her information if they have already killed her children.

The Secretary of State of Niassa province, Dinis Vilankulo, confirmed, on 28 December, at a meeting with Niassa's security authorities that almost 3,000 individuals were displaced in Mecula district, northeastern Niassa, following attacks of the insurgents in the villages of Naulala 2, Chitande, Mecula, Muchenga, and Macalangelate November and early December. Vilankulo said that there is a need to raise the surveillance efforts and  coordination between the residents and the Mozambican police forces to prevent similar attacks from happening in the future.

On Monday, 26 December, the Mozambican government received food and supplies for protection against the Coronavirus given by the Indian government through its Ambassador to Mozambique. The aid, which were received by the Minister of National Defense, Cristovao Chume, were intended for the Mozambican Armed Forces and terrorism victims in Cabo Delgado.

Mozambican Armed Defense Forces and SAMIM troops recovered various weapons and munitions east of Chai, Macomia district, in recent operations targeting insurgent bases in the area.  These operations were likely carried out between 17-22 December.  Troops seized several RPG 7 launchers, PKM Machine Guns, AK-47 assault rifles and several grenades.

Local security units announced on Monday, 27 December that they had ambushed and killed 5 insurgents and captured 1 other militant in the village of Chitoio, Macomia district in Cabo Delgado. A group of 19 Insurgents had reportedly attempted to attack the village. No casualties were reported on the security forces’ side.

Mozambique on 28 December reported 3,473 new COVID cases, the highest ever number of cases in a single day and the first ever 3000+ case day during the pandemic.  3 new deaths were also reported.  47% of tests administered during this period were positive.  There are now 128 hospitalizations in the country, along with 20,642 active COVID cases.  The current spike likely has weeks before it will reach its peak and new cases begin to decline.  The country's rolling seven day average number of deaths has increased slightly to just over 2 COVID deaths per day, but this increase in mortalities has not kept pace with the exponential rise in cases seen in recent weeks.

Two suspected insurgents from Nampula, aged 12 and 18, were captured by the Mozambican troops, likely between Chai and Macomia, in Macomia district, per a report on 28 December. The insurgents claimed they were kidnapped by al-Shabaab in Palma district, and had reportedly left their bases in Macomia district, Cabo Delgado.

Flooding was reported on Monday night, 27 December, in residences and access routes in Magoanine, Mapulene, and the Av. Marcos Sebastiao Mabote road in Maputo City, as well as in Marracuene and Matola, Maputo Province, which limited transportation in the said areas.

The Indian Government was reported to have provided two interceptor vessels, as well as undisclosed types of defense equipment, to the Mozambican Military, during their visit in Maputo City on 27 December.  The donation was in support of the country's fight against insurgency in Cabo Delgado.
479 people arrived at the Mecula district HQ, Niassa, on 24 December, fleeing the threat of insurgency in Naulala and other neighboring towns. More IDPs are reportedly expected in the coming days.

Seven people of the same family were murdered by poisoning, on the morning of 25 December, in Zambezia; it was not immediately clear where in the province this incident occurred.  The suspect, who is the family's son-in-law, reportedly put rat poison in a water container used for drinking, at his mother-in-law's house.  The mother-in-law and 4 children under the age of 10 were found dead in the residence, while 2 others died in the hospital.  Mozambican police immediately arrested the suspect.

Intelligence provided by defecting insurgents, reportedly led to the successful assault operations, carried out by joint forces against insurgents near Chai, Macomia district, between 17-22 December.
Quelimane Mayor, Manuel de Araujo was notified on 29 December to appear at the Provincial Office for Combating Corruption in Zambezia.  The mayor has been accused of misuse of public funds.

A 5-year agreement was signed by the Japanese Agribusiness Agency, on 29 December, in partnership with the Integrated Development Agency from the North.  The partnership is focused on providing support in recovering small and medium agricultural businesses, in the various districts of Cabo Delgado, who have been affected by terrorism.  Communities in Niassa and Nampula will also benefit from the program.

Negotiations between the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the Mozambican Gov't, on an Expanded Financing Program, are set to begin at the end of January 2022, per their announcement on 28 December.  The implementation of a new IMF program in Mozambique would be the first such program since news of the Hidden Debts Scandal broke in 2014.
The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) arrested 104 suspected drug traffickers in the province of Sofala, per a report on28 December between April and November.

The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) in Sofala, destroyed over 20 kilos of various drugs seized, including heroine and marijuana on 28 December.  These narcotics were seized between April and November of this year.

A group of at least 20 insurgents on the morning of 27 December attacked Alassima village, around 7kms from Mecula town, setting several homes on fire, and shooting dead at least 5 people.  Insurgents also abducted a group of 11.  The militants subsequently released 4 women, but kept 7 men.  The women later arrived in Mecula town, passing a message from the insurgents that they intended to attack Mecula town in the near future.

The largest health unit in the country, Maputo Central Hospital (HCM), expressed their concern over the spread of COVID, as it has infected 151 of their employees, of which, 29 were hospitalized, including 16 doctors, while another 10 doctors are in home isolation, per the report on Sunday, 26 December.  The hospital suspects that the spread of the virus is due to the omicron variant.  This is reportedly the first time that the HCM has experienced a surge, which has affected so many of their staff.

Some of his criminal associates reportedly reported his movements to police, leading to his arrest while trying to carry out the kidnapping. However, no other source confirms this report.

Two were injured in an accident at the Nacala Port, on 26 December, after a pulley cord was detached from a ship's crane, consequently falling with heavy impact.  The specifics of how the two were injured was not detailed in the report, though one of them received serious injuries, per the report.

Ongoing clearing and cleaning operations were reported, after insurgent occupations, in areas around Palma and Mocimboa de Praia, in Cabo Delgado, on 28 December, involving soldiers, public officials, and volunteers.

18 foreign citizens and 1 Mozambican were arrested in Quelimane, Zambezia, over illegal immigration charges, on 28 December.  Among those arrested were 10 Malawians, 3 Guineans, and 2 Bengalis, while 2 others were not specified in the report.  The Mozambican who was arrested, was reportedly the driver of the car carrying the 10 Malawians, on their way to Malawi.

The South African Forces (SANDF) on 23 December, denied reports from the Democratic Alliance (DA), where they stated that the South African soldiers deployed in Mozambique do not have sufficient aerial cover, which they also said had resulted in the recent death of a soldier.  This came in context of Corporal Tebogo Radebe's death during recent clashes with insurgents in Mozambique, which the DA claims, could have been avoided.

A gang of 9 reportedly attempted to kidnap a civilian in Sofala, which was thwarted by police, per the report on 27 December.  Two of the nine suspects were detained.  The same group is believed to have perpetrated a kidnapping incident on 14 December in Gondola, Manica province.

At least 38 companies subcontracted by TotlEngergies on the LNG projects in Cabo Deglado have payments pending since the suspension of operations on 24 March, the day after insurgents attacked the city, according to the Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA) on 29 December.  CTA said the main obstacle in the payment process by Total is linked to difficulties in recognizing the contractual nature between them and the Mozambican companies in question.  CTA urged Total to speed up the process of payment, as many Mozambican companies are in dire financial situations, due to the pandemic.

A 34-year-old man attempted to smuggle 1 kg of cocaine through the Maputo International Airport, in Mavalane, Maputo City, which resulted in his immediate arrest.  The suspect, who travelled to Maputo via a flight from Brazil, had reportedly tied the drug to a strap that he had on his body, per the report on 29 December.  The man was in transit to South Africa when he was arrested.

One kg of cocaine was seized from a 34-year-old man, at the Maputo International Airport, in Mavalane, Maputo City, and the man was arrested.  The suspect, who was arrived via a flight from Brazil and was in transit to South Africa, had reportedly tied the drug to a strap that he had on his body, per the report on 29 December.

A 34-year-old man was arrested at the Maputo International Airport, in Mavalane, Maputo City, after he was found in possession of 1 kg of cocaine. The suspect, who was arrived via a flight from Brazil and was in transit to South Africa, had reportedly tied the drug to a strap that he had on his body, per the report on 29 December.

As of Wednesday, 29 December, 111,203 people were vaccinated with the first dose in the last 24 hours. Since the start of the 3rd phase on March 8, Mozambique has vaccinated over 8.7 million people against COVID-19 with one shot, of which 6,208,957 have been fully vaccinated.

Mozambique on 29 December reported 3,624 new COVID cases, which is another increase from the previous highest recorded cases the day prior.  12 deaths were also reported, which is the first sudden spike in fatalities since the outbreak of the new omicron variant.  Meanwhile, 158 people remain in isolation centers due to the virus, and 705 recoveries were also reported.  There are currently 23,549 active cases in the country.  In summary, the updated cumulative total cases as of 29 December are: 179,272 positive; 1,988 deaths; and 153,731 recoveries.

The Center for Public Integrity (CIP) found a shortage across the country from Maputo to Cabo Delgado of in chemicals needed to carry out different laboratory tests in hospitals, according to the CIP's study published on 22 December.  The said chemicals are essential for screening and monitoring diseases, such as malaria, diabetes, tuberculosis, among others.

Over 50 houses were destroyed by heavy rains and wind in Manica Province, on 26 December, resulting in 1 death, while 270 people were left homeless.  Schools and some social and economic infrastructure were also destroyed.  Per the report, food and hygiene kits have been distributed to the families.

Maputo Central Hospital (HCM), which is the largest health unit in the country, expressed their concerns over their lack of blood in stock, which is essential for responding to emergencies.  The hospital said on 27 December that it needs 2,000 units of blood to function, but only has 700, which are being used to treat children, trauma victims, as well as people with illnesses like anemia.  This came following an earlier report where the same hospital announced that 151 of their hospital staff had been infected with COVID-19, including 16 doctors.

Reports on 28 December indicated that the insurgent group in Cabo Delgado have been able to resupply their bases in Chai area, with the help of insurgent supporters in possession of ID cards, which they use to bypass military checkpoints along the roads in the region.

On 30 December, Mozambique reported 4,947 new COVID cases along with 8 deaths and 55 new hospitalizations. This set a new record in COVID cases recorded in a single day in the country. This was a 40% increase in cases compared to the day before, when a then record 3,624 cases were reported.  Maputo City saw 780 cases.  There are now 26,216 COVID cases in the country.

Around 20 to 25 insurgents attacked the village of Macalange on 03 December, opening fire on civilians and setting fire to homes in the area.  Insurgents carried out several abductions during the attack, releasing at least one woman after the raid.  Militants also carried out looting in the area.  One child was injured in the attack in a burning home.

Around 20 to 25 insurgents attacked the village of Macalange on 03 December, opening fire on civilians and setting fire to homes in the area.  Insurgents carried out several abductions during the attack, releasing at least one woman after the raid.  Militants also carried out looting in the area.  One child was injured in the attack in a burning home.

Hospital officials announced that there is a blood shortage in the Matola Provincial on 30 December. The hospital was operating with 30 units less of blood, which usually runs on 80 packs of blood during the last quarter of the year. This comes as around 500 patients were requiring blood due to diseases and accidents.
A maritime aircraft patrol airlifted an Indian Navy soldier aboard the INS Kesari in Mozambican waters off Maputo City on 30 December. The airlift was due to a medical emergency.

Mozambican President Nyusi visited Rwandan and SADC forces in Cabo Delgado on 29 December. The visit was to obtain updates regarding the security situation in the province. The president also thanked the foreign forces for their assistance with the insurgency.

The African Development Bank (ADB) announced that they will provide USD 47million for the first phase of an agricultural development project in Niassa on 30 December. The project was to strengthen the capacity of the agricultural business in the province.

The Ministry of Health announced on 30 December that 6.3 million individuals have completed their COVID vaccinations. This comes as 126,161 individuals have been vaccinated for their first dose during the past 24 hours.  8.8 million have received at least one shot.
A fire broke out inside an aluminum smelting company in Beluluane Industrial Park in Boane district around 17:53 of 27 December. The fire reportedly damaged a smoke and fumes treatment center.

Police arrested three suspects for murder and in possession of human bones and organs in Erati District of Nampula on 29 December. The three had murdered an albino person and dismembered the body, intending to sell body parts to be used in traditional medicine. The suspects intended to sell the items to healers for worth 4 million meticais.

Police arrested three suspects for murder and in possession of human bones and organs in Erati District of Nampula on 29 December. The three had murdered an albino person and dismembered the body, intending to sell body parts to be used in traditional medicine. The suspects intended to sell the items to healers for worth 4 million meticais.

Sources stated on 30 December that 22 million individuals in Mozambique have access to food compared to the previous year. This increase is compared to the previously recorded 19 million individuals who have access to food early 2021. The study also indicated that acute food and nutrition insecurity has declined from 2.7 million to 1.85 million.

The Northern Integrated Development Agency (ADIN) is partnering with the Institute for the Promotion of Small and Medium Enterprises to promote self employment among IDPs affected by violence in Cabo Delgado.
A building caught on fire in Chiure on the evening of 30 December. The fire managed to damage several electrical transmission lines while spreading.

ISCAP claimed militants exchanged gunfire with Mozambican security forces after attacking a military patrol near Kogolo in Macomia District on 20 December, saying troops were driven back in this clash.  This report is unconfirmed.

ISCAP claimed attacking Mozambican soldiers at Naulala village, north of Mecula, on 20 December. The militant group claimed that six soldiers were killed.  One other source reported this attack was verified; it was unclear if this claim referred to another attack on Naulala on 22 December in which at least one Niassa Special Reserve Officer was killed.

The Mozambican President Filipe Nyusi announced that an SADC Troika Meeting was scheduled to take place on January 2022. The meeting was to assess SAMIM's progress and consider another extension of this mission in Cabo Delgado.

Ongoing security force operations were reported on 27 December in the Chai area, sources reported, with some insurgent weapons and an Islamic State flag seized.  No insurgents were captured or killed in this operation.

The National Communications Institute (NCM) called on three mobile phone companies to improve their services due to the complaints by locals. The NCM also said subscribers often complain of not being able to use airtime and data

Since the start of the holiday season, 7,000 illegal immigrants trying to cross into South Africa from Mozambique.  Those attempting to cross were reportedly intercepted by the Border Control Management authorities at the Lebombo Border Control in Mpumalanga, per a report on 1 January.

One person, the driver, was killed in a car accident on the late night of 31 December, at the Circular Road in Maputo City, likely due to speeding. The car was headed towards Maputo City, from Marracuene in Maputo Province, when it crashed into a pole and overturned.

Two suspects were arrested for allegedly kidnapping national and foreign citizens. One arrest was made in Xinavane, Maputo and the other in Gaza, per the report on 1 January. Authorities also said that the accused had contacts in Gaza, who is also involved in the crime, though the suspects vehemently denied these.

Two suspects were arrested for allegedly kidnapping national and foreign citizens. One arrest was made in Xinavane, Maputo and the other in Gaza, per the report on 1 January. Authorities also said that the accused had contacts in Gaza, who is also involved in the crime, though the suspects vehemently denied these.

Col. Michael Khasebe, who commands 5 special force regiments of the SADC, along with members of the SANDF, expressed their grief and anger over the death of Corporal Teboho Radebe. Radebe was killed by insurgents in Mozambique during an attack near Chai village, in Cabo Delgado, in December. Col. Khasebe warned that Radebe's death would not go in vain, that the special forces were not backing down, and they will go after the insurgents in "full power", per a report on 1 January.

One insurgent was reportedly captured at Matemo Island, per a report on 28 December. No further detail were disclosed in the report.  Previous reports had indicated a group of insurgents had surrendered at Ibo Island, though other sources later indicated this was false.
Troops from the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) and the Mozambican Defence and Security Forces (FDS) continued to conduct patrols through Palma town on 02 January.

The UN's World Food Group (WFP) said it has gradually begun transitioning from life-saving food assistance to the recovery and resilience phase of activities in Northern Mozambique, per their announcement on 30 December.  WFP also said that in Mozambique, almost half of the children under 5 years old experience high malnutrition, while over 2.9M people face severe acute food insecurity.

There are over 1,700 students with special needs in Lichinga, but of the 600 schools, only one is equipped to teach the said children. Some need to be taken to other provinces, however, many do not have wheelchairs or crutches and cannot bring themselves physically to school, per the report on 2 January. There is also great difficulty in recruiting trained professionals, as most of them find it hard to overcome the difficulties of teaching people with special needs.

The Omicron COVID variant has dominated the infections in Mozambique, according to a study released by the National Institute of Health (INS) on Sunday, 2 January.  According to the study, prior to Omicron, the first variant detected was Beta, which dominated the country between January and May 2021, followed by Delta, which dominated between June and August 2021. Both previous variants were initially detected in Maputo and Tete. Meanwhile, Omicron was initially detected in Maputo in November, but also circulates Nampula, Zambezia, and Inhambane, per the report.

Judge Efigenio Baptista announced on 31 December that the Hidden Debts trial case is scheduled to resume on 17 January, as opposed to 6 January. The initial schedule of resumption was announced in December after the trial was stopped due to the record of COVID positive cases among participants.  The judge also announced that on 17 February, former Mozambican President, Armando Emílio Guebuza, will be heard. While on 8, 10, and 11 of February, the following people are scheduled for their respective hearings: former Minister of Fisheries - Victor Manuel Borges, Alberto Ricardo Mondlane - who performed the functions of Interior Minister, and current Economy and Finance Minister - Adriano Maleiane.

Mozambique on 1 January reported 2,642 new COVID cases in the country. The new cases were reported as follows: 533 in Maputo City, 390 in Sofala, 313 in Gaza, 291 in Maputo Province, and 290 in Inhambane. Despite the decrease in cases, the positivity rate rose to 43.98% from 42.66% the day prior. Six deaths were also reported in the same reporting period, due to COVID, while another six people also recovered from the infection. The number of active cases as of said date were 33,130.  Vaccination campaigns halted due to the New Year celebrations but will resume on Monday, 3 January.

Mozambique on 2 January reported 7 deaths in the country due to COVID-19, in the past 24 hours. 731 new COVID cases were also recorded out of the 1,865 people who were tested, while there were 42 new hospitalizations and 26 discharges.  In summary, the updated cumulative total cases as of 2 January are: 192,453 positive; 2,019 deaths; and 157,184 recoveries. Meanwhile, there are currently 33,246 active cases in the country.  Vaccination campaigns halted due to the New Year celebrations but will resume on Monday, 3 January.

Five people died, while 11 others were injured, in a road accident in Namacurra, Zambezia, on Saturday afternoon, 1 January, involving a passenger transport van and a freight vehicle.  The accident was reportedly caused by excessive speed, as well as fatigue and the irregular overtaking by the passenger van.  4 of the wounded are in critical condition, per the report.

A large number of nationals and foreigners, on their way back to South Africa, were reported by migration authorities at the Ressano Garcia border on Sunday afternoon, 2 January, following the end of the festive season. A line of cars could be seen around 4 km from the border. Travelers lined up at the COVID rapid test tents, most of them Mozambican miners. Mozambican authorities said that decentralization of service counters, fee payments, and escorts to cars carrying miners, were some of the measures implemented at the border to reduce congestion.

The country's currency (Metical) closed in 2021 without fluctuations against the US Dollar (USD) and other currencies of reference, per a report on 3 January.  This was reportedly unprecedented, since the Metical usually largely depreciates in the festive season, due to greater demand for the Dollar.  In 2020, 1 USD was over 75 Meticais, 1 Euro was 90, and 1 Rand between 4-5 Meticais.  However, since May 2021, the Metical has reportedly been stable.  1 USD has been around 63-64 Meticais, for over 7 months now, 1 Euro is between 71-73, while 1 Rand is around 3.9-4 Meticais.

Mozambican fleeing from terror attacks in Niassa have reportedly recently entered begun entering Malawi, in small groups, and have been spotted in Mangochi in search of a safe haven from the terrorist attacks in Cabo Delgado and in Niassa, which borders Malawi, per a report on Sunday, 2 January.

Insurgents attacked the village of Nova Zambezia, south of Chai, Macomia district, Cabo Delgado, in the early morning hours of Saturday, 1 January, which resulted in the death of three people.  Reports indicated that 1 was shot dead, while the two others were beheaded or hacked to death for trying to flee the group.  All three killed were reported to be extended family members of the district administrator of Macomia.  Insurgents also stole food, especially rice and cooking oil, from the village, following the attack.  Locals said they believed the attack was launched in retaliation for recent joint forces offensives to push insurgents out of areas near Chai.
Insurgents attacked Darumba village, located near Mucojo, Macomia district, on Friday, 31 December, where they murdered a fisherman. Other fishermen were able to escape.
Insurgents reportedly attacked Chiconono village, in Muembe district, Niassa, on 30 December. No casualties were detailed in the report.

The General Commander of Mozambique, Bernardino Rafael, is reportedly considering the possibility of prosecuting unvaccinated police agents, per a report on 3 January.  This came following his speech days prior in Maputo, where he ordered all unvaccinated officers, not to report to their units, and that they would be prosecuted should they insist on not becoming vaccinated.

ENi's floating platform for producing liquefied natural gas arrived in the Rovuma Basin, on Monday, 3 January, and is expected to be moored at the production site in the coming days.  Its arrival came earlier than expected, which was scheduled on 16 January, 60 days after its departure from South Korea on 16 November.  By June, the platform is expected to be stabilized in area 4 of the Rovuma Basin by mooring 20 main cables, deployed 2000 meters in depth. It will be anchored 50 km off the coast of Cabo Delgado, where it will produce 3.4 million tons of natural gas per year, beginning 2022. Revenue for the first year is forecasted at 34.5 million dollars and, when it reaches its peak, revenue will be at 110 million dollars annually.  The gas exploration project is also expected to provide employment to a total of 800 people, per the report.

The shipping company, CMA CGM, announced that they will offer a new shipping route to Nacala from Colombo, with the first ship to arrive on 03 February. This comes as the shipping company will continue their weekly shipments through Maputo and Beira.

The International Monetary Fund announced the provision of a debt relief to Mozambique due to the COVID pandemic on 31 December. The relief was to cover payment of 55 million USD. IMF stated that the relief was to help free up resources for the country.

On 31 December, Mozambique reported 4,861 new COVID cases and 10 new COVID deaths.  59 new hospitalizations were also reported.  There are now 30,500 active COVID cases in the country. This is the second highest daily COVID total in a single day during the pandemic, after nearly 5,000 cases were reported on 29 December.
Heavy rainfall caused flooding around Greater Maputo on the evening of 30 December. Locals stated that the flooding has been repetitive every year during the same season.

The Ministry of Health announced that 6.4 million individuals have completed their vaccination in Mozambique on 31 December. This comes as 114, 852 were vaccinated with their first those on the same day.  8.9 million people have received at least one shot against COVID.

The Ministry of Health announced that they increased their COVID testing in Mozambique. Officials stated that the current testing as of 31 December has reached 11,500 individuals, compared to the previous days which recorded 8,790 tests on 30 December and 7,294 test on Tuesday.
The Maputo City Court rejected the request for the provisional release of former official in Maputo on 28 December. The detained former official was previously charged for misusing state funds.

The Mozambican President Filipe Nyusi During a speech on 29 December said that 2022 will be a “decisive” year in the fight against insurgency in Cabo Delgado, speaking from Mueda. Nyusi called the Mozambican security forces to step up against the insurgency, saying militants had been driven out of Palma, Quissanga, Muidumbe, and Macomia but were hiding in other areas.

The Botswanan president visited the SAMIM forces in Cabo Delgado on 31 December. The Botswanan president called for SAMIM forces to continue their operations against the insurgent and clear the country from insurgency before leaving the country.
Government officials on 31 December announced that over 3,800 people have been displaced by insurgent attacks in Mecula District of Niassa.

Vaccination campaigns halted due to the New Year celebrations but will resume on Monday, 3 January. The last vaccination update released by the Ministry of Health was on 30 December, where 6.3 million individuals had completed their COVID vaccinations, while 126,161 individuals were vaccinated with the first dose during the past 24 hours.

President Nyusi and his wife Isaura on 03 January were confirmed to have tested positive for COVID-19, according to a statement from Nyusi's office.  The statement indicated that both were asymptomatic, but after testing positive for the virus with a rapid antigen test, they quarantined themselves and are awaiting results from a PCR test.  This  news comes as Mozambique finds itself in the midst of a 4th wave of COVID.  The country in recent days has seen record daily case totals, and its 7-day rolling average number of cases now stands at nearly 3,000.  COVID deaths in Mozambique remain relatively low, though daily COVID deaths have spiked to about 7 daily fatalities, up from 0 deaths per day less than a month ago.

Australian mining company, Syrah Resources, announced on 30 December that it had entered into a binding, 4-year agreement with Tesla, an electric car and battery manufacturer. Syrah will supply Tesla with "Active Anode Material" produced from graphite, which Syrah mines in Balama district, Cabo Delgado. The 106-sq. km. Balama mine is reportedly the largest graphite reserve to ever be discovered, a resource which Syrah estimates will last for over 50 years.  Syrah also exports graphite from Mozambique to China, which has an overwhelming dominance in the production of Active Anode Material, per the report.

Mozambican President Filipe Nyusi said in his New Year speech on 01 January, that 2021 was filled with enormous challenges due to the COVID-19 pandemic, paired with the impact of climate change in the country.  The imposed restrictions over the threat of COVID had delayed several developmental plans among the Portuguese-Speaking African Countries (PALOP) and Portugal but, Nyusi said, people learned to prioritize health and live more sustainably.  Further, Nyusi said that the cyclical impact of climate change made the country's challenges more complex. Several extreme weather events had hit the country, affecting almost 700,000 people and causing at least 96 deaths and 150 others injured, according to gov't data.

Doctors Without Borders (MSF) on 03 January warned that despite advances by Joint Forces, the situation remains chaotic in Cabo Delgado, which has been plagued by insurgent attacks since October 2017.  MSF noted that armed conflict in the province peaked in March 2021, after Palma district was heavily attacked, and that the conflict and humanitarian crisis persists, citing that humanitarian aid has been concentrated in the southern areas of the province where it is more stable. However, hardly any aid reaches the large northern areas of Mueda, Nangade, Muidumbe, and Mocimboa da Praia, where around 50,000 IDPs live.  Lastly, the MSF also warned of the potential outbreaks in the coming rainy season of waterborne diseases, such as cholera and malaria, noting that prevention is crucial, per a report on 03 January.
Heavy rains in the early morning of Friday, 31 December, caused flooding in Matola's Liberdade neighborhood, in Maputo.

A crocodile attack incident was reported on 31 December in the Zambezi River, Luabo district, Zambezia. A 14-year-old sustained injuries to her left hand, while two other children, aged 11 and 13, were reported missing.  PRM said the 14-year-old was washing clothes in the river, when a crocodile attacked, tearing off two of her fingers.  Meanwhile, the two other minors were reportedly last seen bathing in the river during the attack.

Over 300 households in Messano, Gaza, were connected to the national electricity grid, financed solely by EDM, per a report on Monday, 03 January.  The infrastructure, which also included 3 sub-stations and 100 lampposts for public lighting, cost 31.7M meticais and will boost other services such as water supply, health care, education, and communications.  37 administrative posts in Gaza have now been connected to the national power grid, and only 7 remain to be connected, which will be done over the short to medium term, per the report.

The increased tariff for semi-collective transport in Mozambique, known as "chapa 100", was implemented on 02 January, which instantly generated wide criticism and protests from within the civil society.  The decision has a negative impact on the most disadvantaged citizens and residents, further away from the capital, per the report. The Human Rights Network Association (ARDH) also strongly opposed the decision and said, the gov't must immediately revoke the decision. However, the ARDH also appealed to the public not to gather and resort to strikes and demonstrations, due to the threat of the COVID virus.

The Mozambican Ministry of Health on 03 January recorded 12 deaths in the country due to COVID, which were in Maputo City, Sofala, and Tete provinces.  In the same 24-hour period, there were also 903 new cases and 52 new hospitalizations due to the virus, while 31 were discharged. A total of 201 patients remain in hospital units and 1,496 others had recovered from COVID.  In summary, the updated cumulative total cases as of 3 January are: 193,371 positive; 2,031 deaths; and 158,680 recoveries. Meanwhile, the country now has 32,656 active cases, which reduced from 33,246 the day prior.

ISCAP claimed responsibility for the attack on Nova Zambezia, Macomia district, in Niassa on 02 January, saying 3 Christians were killed in the attack.  This likely corresponds to a confirmed attack that did take place on 01 January in the village in which 1 person was shot and 2 others were beheaded. Automatic weapons were reportedly used in the attack.

ISCAP claimed responsibility for an attack on "Mbaba" on 03 January, likely referring to an attack on 31 December at Darumba, near Mucojo, in Cabo Delgado, where 1 fisherman was reportedly killed. Security forces reportedly fled the area while homes were also destroyed, according to the ISCAP claim.

A stabbing incident was reported on 31 December, in the Tetereane neighborhood of Nacala, Nampula. Young men were reportedly stabbed, deeply across the face, over disputes of a girl coming out of female initiation rites. It is unclear in the report how many men were injured or who performed the crime.

A couple, aged 51 and 61, were murdered inside their home in Morrumbala, Zambezia, around 01:00 on 01 January. Three people, armed with a machete, reportedly broke down the main door of the victims' house and killed the couple using a blunt object, then fled the scene. The motive is supposedly related to family disputes, per the report.
A civilian was strangled to death allegedly by his "friend" in the district of Ile, Zambezia, on 01 January.  The suspect fled the scene before police arrived.

Mueda is reportedly experiencing water shortages, especially in the supply of drinking water, as the village welcomed more people who had been displaced by the terrorism in nearby areas, per the report on 03 January.

The General Commander of Mozambique, Bernardino Rafael, ordered all unvaccinated officers not to report to their units, in an effort to contain the spread of COVID.  Rafael also warned the officers that this was an order and, therefore, anyone who goes against it will be prosecuted, per the report on 3 January.

At least five people were killed, and 11 houses were set on fire, in a second attack carried out by insurgents in Nova Zambezia, Cabo Delgado, at around 02:17 on Monday, 03 January.  Insurgents also raided houses and took food before fleeing from the village, per the report.  Those killed reportedly resisted the raid.

Three sources on 04 January reported a suspected insurgent attack on the village of Mariria, about 1.5 kms from Muaguide town in Meluco, with several houses reportedly set on fire.  Looting was also reported in the town with large sums of money stolen and at least 4 motorcycles also stolen.  Residents reportedly fled nearby towns at the approach of "strangers" just before the attack.
Sources on 04 January reported insurgent attacks on Nova Vida and Aldeia da Paz, north of Macomia along the N380 road, though no further details on these attacks were immediately available.

Mozambican police arrested a gang of four individuals in Nampula, who were reportedly involved in counterfeiting Meticals and Dollars.  PRM said on 03 January that the gang had been under surveillance for a period prior to the arrest.  C4 Pedro de Namicopo was among the arrested for counterfeiting currency, and for theft of motorbikes.  He admitted to having been involved in past crimes, though he claims that he is now being set up by police.  He also alleged that police keep jailing him because he refused to work for them and be their "source".

The SADC announced on 04 January that it will hold a virtual Extraordinary Summit of Head of State and Gov't on 07 January, to assess the progress and mandate of the SAMIM in assisting the Mozambican Forces against the insurgency in Cabo Delgado. The said meeting is also where the formal extension of SAMIM in Cabo Delgado will likely be decided.  Prior to the Extraordinary Meeting, the Organ Troika Summit will convene on 05 January, which will focus on discussing the support for effective SAMIM operations to bring peace and stability in Cabo Delgado.

The Southern Water Regional Administration warned, on 04 January, that there is a risk of flooding in Maputo Province, calling on communities in the area to move to higher grounds.  Moderate to heavy rainfall hit South Africa and Eswatini, which forces the opening of floodgates in the small Libombo dam at 09:00. The discharge of waters from the dam will soon increase from 30 m3/s to 60 m3/s, which may cause flooding in Maputo, especially in the Mafuiane drifts in Namaacha, Mazambanine, and Boane.

The discharge of waters from the dam will soon increase from 30 m3/s to 60 m3/s, which may cause flooding in Maputo, especially in the Mafuiane drifts in Namaacha, Mazambanine, and Boane.

At least 30 people lost their lives due to car accidents, reported across Mozambique during the holiday season, per the report on 04 January.  This news comes despite current campaigns on avoiding road accidents, which are being carried out by the Ministry of Transport and Communication.

A small demonstration of 26 workers from the Maputo Shipyard was reported on Tuesday, 04 January, protesting the maritime company's failure to release their salary, including holiday allowances and 13th-month pay.  Nearly 50 workers had been without salary since June 2021, but only 26 went on strike as others could not join for reasons such as the lack of money for transport.  Workers said the issue began when new management took over the company.  When trying to claim their salary, the company would reportedly call them illiterate or "cockroach".  Despite the lack of salary, employees continued to work, until on Monday prior, they decided to plan the small demonstration.  The case has now been reported to the Ministry of Labor and Social Security.

The Mozambican Ministry of Health on 04 January recorded 11 COVID deaths and 2,975 new COVID cases in the country, with a positivity rate of 41.45%.  In the same 24-hour period, there were also 45 new hospital admissions, while 39 were discharged.  A total of 195 patients remain in hospital units and 887 others had recovered from COVID.  In summary, the updated cumulative total cases as of 04 January are: 196,346 positive; 2,042 deaths, and 159,567 recoveries. Meanwhile, the country now has 34,733 active cases of COVID-19.

The Ministry of Health announced on 04 January that a total of 9,195,386 individuals have been vaccinated with at least one dose against COVID-19.  There were 136,671 people who were vaccinated with the first dose in the last 24 hours, under the third phase of the National Mass Vaccination Campaign.  Since the start of vaccinations on 08 March, Mozambique has a total of 6,750,670 people, fully-vaccinated against COVID-19.

Between 29 December to 04 January, the weekly total of COVID deaths rose to 58, compared to only 21 total deaths in the week prior, which indicates an increase in mortality rate in the country due to COVID. Meanwhile, in the same reporting period, the number of total active cases in a week rose by 46% from 17,623 to 32,656 per the report on 04 January.

A US diplomatic security report recently published indicated that since the summer of 2021, joint operations by Mozambican, Rwandan, and SADC forces, have reportedly made substantial progress recapturing the Cabo Delgado districts that were most at risk: Mueda, Muidumbe, Nangade, Mocimboa de Praia, Meluco, Palma, Macomia, Ibo, Ancuabe, and Quissanga.  Insurgents scattered due to these intensified efforts, resulting in small-scale attacks in the nearby province of Niassa and the neighboring country of Tanzania.  The report also said that despite a lack of proof of direct command or control, the US says there are links that ISCAP is an affiliate of ISIS, per the report on 04 January.

The Ministry of Health announced that 7.1 million have been fully vaccinated in Mozambique as of 7 January. 126, 468 individuals received their first COVID vaccine in the country within the past 24 hours. The total vaccinated individuals have reached 9.4 million since the start of the vaccination campaign.

The National Migration Service (SENAMI) announced that an increase in travelers crossing Mozambique's border was noted as 230,639 travelers crossed the border between 13 December and 3 January. SENAMI stated that last year only 145,069 crossed to enter Mozambique. A majority of the travelers were passing through Ressano Garcia coming from South Africa.
The Ministry of Health announced 3,031 new COVID cases and 10 new related deaths in Mozambique on 06 January. This comes as recoveries were recorded at 4,118.

One base was reported to be in the Chai area and while another was located near Pundanhar.  It was unclear where the insurgent indicated the other 4 bases are located.  The captured insurgent also said militants currently lack ammunition, though have ample stocks of weapons. Insurgents on the afternoon of 08 January were reported to have attacked Nachipande / Alberto Chipande village north of Ngapa in Mueda District, close to the Rovuma River, clashing with pro-government militia.  Locals fled to Ngapa, Namatil, Naida, and Mocimboa do Rovuma villages nearby.  One report indicated at least one person beheaded in the attack.  It was unclear if pro-government militia were able to drive the militants away from the village.

An earthquake was felt in Niassa on 08 January, with its epicenter in Malawi. The 4.6-magnitude earthquake had hit Monkey Bay in Malawi at a depth of 10 km, on 08 January, and was specifically felt in Lichinga, Mandimba, Ngauma, and Chimbonila, in the province of Niassa. No casualties or material damages were reported.

The National Institute of Meteorology said there is a 70% probability that 4 - 6 tropical cyclones may form in the Indian Ocean in the coming months, according to a report on 08 January. However, the Institute said it is yet unclear how many cyclones will or could hit Mozambique, and how strong they might be. Regardless, they noted that the temperature of the sea waters is increasing, which is one of the warning signs in the formation of cyclones, further stressing that this is only a warning sign and that no cyclone has yet formed.

In total, the Mozambican Gov't has received over 11 million doses of COVID-19 vaccines with the support of its various partners, per the report.

Maputo City, with 579, recorded the most number of COVID cases. The National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) on Saturday, 08 January, held meetings with communities in Maputo City to strengthen collaboration with the public in combating crime. SERNIC called on the community to report any instances of misconduct, while some members of the community also called for increased protection for those who do provide reports or complaints to SERNIC.

The increase in interprovincial public transport tariffs has resulted in the reduction of the flow of passengers. Some transporters are reportedly obliged to apply the previous tariff to secure more passengers, per the report on 08 January.

An insurgent reportedly fired a machine gun on the now empty village of Nova Vida, Macomia district, on Wednesday night, 05 January. No casualties were reported. The villagers had reportedly stayed hidden in the woods despite the frequent military patrol, as they feared more attacks from insurgents.  Militants reportedly carried out looting and set fires to several homes during the course of the day.  Other sources had reported an attack in the village the day before.

More information was released on 08 January about the recently captured, 32-year-old insurgent commander, Amade Muahamed Daude, who leaked information about the 6 insurgent bases in Cabo Delgado.  He says he had lived in Macomia and later in Mocimboa de Praia (MDP), and was recruited by terrorists in 2016. He was reportedly taken to the DRC, then to Kenya and Tanzania where he was trained and taught Islamic radicalism. He returned to Mozambique in September 2017 and participated in the attack on MDP on 05 October 2017.

Mozambican President Nyusi expressed his commitment to strengthening ties of friendship and cooperation with the Russian Government, per his statement on 10 January.  Nyusi also thanked Russia's multiform support and solidarity, especially in response to COVID-19 and the fight against the impact of climate change in Mozambique.

The Association of Small and Medium Enterprises in Mozambique demanded the approval of the Local Content Law, noting that without it, only people linked to political power will reportedly benefit from oil and gas projects and not the majority of Mozambicans.  The Local Content Law ensures that at least 10% of activities in oil and gas projects are reserved for Mozambican entrepreneurs, per the report on 10 January.
Insurgents abducted dozens of youths during the attack on the village of Mariria on 4 January. This comes as the insurgents attacked and looted the village.

The SADC announced the delay of a virtual conference intended to be held on 7 January on the insurgency in Cabo Delgado and the SADC mission in the province. The SADC conference was rescheduled to occur on 12 January in Lilongwe, Malawi.

The Mozambican Government announced that it will invest $14 million for upgrading the toll booths around the country. The investment was for the maintenance of the public roads which were still requiring 58% of funding. Officials stated that they intend to install an additional 26 tolls as part of the Self-sustained Road Maintenance Program.
Police arrested three private guards suspected for stealing 29 packs of clothing in Beira on 6 January. The suspects were in charge of protecting a warehouse from which the goods were stolen.

The Ministry of Health announced that 7 million individuals have been fully vaccinated in Mozambique on 6 January. This comes as 125, 418 individuals were vaccinated with their first dose within the day.
A civilian died while attempting to mediate between two brawling individuals in Machava, Matola, on 6 January.
Robbers broke into the Patrice Lumumba Primary School and stole all the computers and peripherals in Pebane on 6 January.
Rainfall has reportedly flooded Maxaquene C neighborhood, central Maputo City, on 5 January. Locals stated that officials stated that new sewage system in the area was finished last year.
Public transportation drivers suspended operations due to worsening road conduitions around in Nkobe, Matola on 5 January.

Locals claimed that public drivers were increasing their fees when rainfall occurred in Marracuene District due to the poor road condition on 5 January. The local stated that the road conditions between Santa Isabel to Michafutene were deteriorating.

Sources stated that the water crisis in Nampula province has worsened to such a degree that locals are using any water for consumption. The Water Supply Investment and Heritage Fund (FIPAG) stated that there were no public watering holes and that each private wells were not enough to last for a year. Sources also stated that local government does not see the water supply as a priority.

The National Institute of Health (INS) stated that the Omicron COVID variant has been driving the rise in COVID cases in the country. INS stated that the Omicron became the most dominating variant on detected test samples since November 2021.
The Ministry of Health announced 3,301 new COVID infections and 15 related deaths in Mozambique as of 6 January. This comes as 74 of the new cases were hospitalized.
Local health officials announced that 23 healthcare professsionals in Gaza province have tested positive for COVID. The healthcare professsionals were asymptomatic and were recovering from the virus.

President Nyusi on 05 January was reported by the Mozambican government to have received a negative PCR test for COVID-19, though his wife Isaura received a positive PCR test.  Mrs. Nyusi remains asymptomatic, and both continue to quarantine.  President Nyusi and his wife on 03 January were reported to have both tested positive for COVID-19 via rapid tests.

On 05 January, communities in Moatize, Tete Province, who had been negatively affected by the former coal mining company, Vale Mozambique, threatened to conduct boycotts and demonstrations should the promised resettlement and compensation fail in 2022.  In the year prior, Vale has reportedly failed to deliver on its promises, detailed in a signed agreement which was arbitrated by the gov't, including financial compensation and the provision of arable land for agriculture and pasture, among others.

Mozambique’s public electricity company, EDM, reportedly dismantled over 600 clandestine electricity connections found in Beira city, Sofala, in 2021, per the report on 04 January.  EDM said it records financial losses of more than 6 million meticais every year, due to such clandestine connections, adding that they have sent over 200 complaints to court, in a bid to recover the said losses, and expects legal authorities to hold those involved criminally accountable.

The National Petroleum Institute (INP) ended its exploration in the Buzi block on 23 September and found strong signs of the existence of natural gas, per an announcement on 05 January.  The next step according to INP is to evaluate the possible discovery, which, depending on the quantities, will require gov't approval for a plan to monetize the resources.

The cost of living in parts of Niassa has exceeded the financial capacities of families, per the report on 05 January, due to the halt in the circulation of trains along the Lichinga-Cuamba and Cuamba-Mecanhelas routes.  The circulation stopped since the beginning of December 2021 due to the breakdown of locomotives and their carriage cooling system.  This has resulted in an increase in the prices of basic goods, including rice, which previously cost 1,500 meticais per 25 kg and now reportedly costs 1,800.
