Oil waste spills have reportedly polluted some areas in Matola, Maputo Province, according to a report on 05 January.  Residents accused nearby oil companies of neglect as they failed to dispose responsibly of the said waste.

One refugee reportedly said he, his wife, their 8 children, and 7 grandchildren, fled into Malawi walking barefoot from Malanga towards Lichinga in Niassa, after insurgents killed people in a neighboring village.

The African Development Bank Group (ADB) approved a $47.09 Million grant intended for the first phase of the Pemba-Lichinga Integrated Development Corridor. The project aims to improve agricultural productivity and agribusiness development in Niassa, through the advancement of capacity, skills, and entrepreneurship, according to the announcement on 05 January.

Five Mozambican soldiers reportedly abused a 32-year-old individual in Mueda, Cabo Delgado, after refusing to pay for the soldiers' alcoholic drinks on 31 December.  The soldiers reportedly threatened to jail the young man over terrorism charges, unless he paid them 300 meticais.  It is unclear whether the amount was paid by the victim, who had reportedly been displaced from Mocimboa de Praia due to insurgency.

Two individuals armed with a machete reportedly robbed people of their mobile phones along the public roads of T3, Ndlavela, and Khongolote, in Matola. The two suspects were arrested by local police, per the report on 05 January.

The Mozambican Human Rights Association (ARDH) called on the gov't to revoke the recent fare rise of between 20-25%, noting that this will have a serious negative impact on the people's standard of living including the potential dropping out of students from school.  However, transport operators say that it is impossible to run a profit without the fare rise, per the report on 05 January.

A South African national was reportedly arrested in Mozambique on 31 December in connection with the kidnapping of a young girl in Johannesburg, South Africa.  Two other suspects in South Africa were also arrested.  It was not immediately clear where this arrest took place within Mozambique.

They then burned the village and retreated to safety.  The village attack had previously been reported, though no clash had been reported before this claim.

ISCAP claimed responsibility for the attack on the Mariria village, 1.5 kms from Muaguide in Meluco, Cabo Delgado, on 04 January.  In this claim, ISCAP said local militiia had fled the area during the attack.  This claim corresponds with a confirmed attack in Mariria.

Rwanda and Mozambique signed an agreement that will expand cooperation between the two countries' security forces, and which is aimed at improving the current security operations in Cabo Delgado, per a report on 10 January. The expansion will also provide increased capacity building for the Mozambican army, as well as enhance the joint modus operandi against insurgency.  This came in conclusion to a series of discussions, which began the day prior in Kigali, between the Rwandan and Mozambican forces. Joint operations against insurgents in Cabo Delgado were reviewed, to determine how the two forces can adopt new strategies in dealing with challenges like those encountered in the past 6 months.  This likely means also at least a 6 month extension in the Rwandan deployment to Cabo Delgado.

More than 65,000 people have reportedly been isolated due to the collapse of the bridge over the Caireze river, along the Mphende-Mukumbura stretch in Magoe district, Tete Province. The bridge collapsed on Sunday, 09 January, as a result of the torrential rain in parts of the country. The river tributaries had become full, and water had overflowed, cutting the causeway connecting the bridge and resulting in the opening of a breach, per the report on 10 January.  This comes as reports from the National Institute of Meteorology (INAM) on 09 January, and on 05 January prior, had also indicated moderate to heavy (locally very strong) rains, accompanied by thunderstorms and gusty winds in the district of Magoe, as well as in Zumbu, Cahora-Bassa, Maravia, Chipunde, and Cidade de Tete, in the Tete province.

Flooding was reported in the neighborhoods of Nampula, caused by heavy rains on 10 January. Some houses had reportedly collapsed and several roads connecting to the areas outside the city were impassable.

According to the UN's report, November 2021 saw the highest number of insurgent attacks in Northern Mozambique since July 2021. Aldebaran's own incident tracking agrees with this assessment. Per the report released on 10 January, the spike in attacks in November resulted in the displacement of over 20,500 people, of whom 51% were children, 28% -women, and 4% -vulnerable people. Consolidated figures (of up to 5 weeks prior) estimate around 734,000 IDPs in northern Mozambique. 90% of IDPs cited the lack of shelter as their most urgent need, followed by food 88%, non-food items 70%, clean water and sanitation 60%, and healthcare 41%. Meanwhile, an estimate of 1.1 million people in Cabo Delgado, Nampula, and Niassa face high levels of food insecurity until the start of harvests in April.

Since October 2021, at least 20 people have died and 11 have been injured due to the effects of the rainy season in Zambezia, according to a report on 10 January. According to the National Institute for Disaster Management (INGD), over 160,000 people are at risk of flooding, of which 10,000 are already feeling its effects and, in the last 24 hours, the flow of the Licungo River has reportedly increased to 5.10 meters high, which is 90 centimeters short of reaching alert level.

The Ministry of Health announced that a total of 9,690,884 individuals have been vaccinated with at least one dose against COVID-19 as of 09 January.  There were 24,668 people who were vaccinated with the first dose in the last 24 hours, under the third phase of the National Mass Vaccination Campaign.  Since the start of vaccinations on 08 March, Mozambique has a total of 7,446,576 people, fully-vaccinated against COVID-19.

Thirty people escaped captivity from insurgents following operations by joint forces on Sunday, 09 January, in Nangade, Cabo Delgado. Most of the rescued were reportedly women and children, who said that they had escaped after insurgents abandoned their bases, following an offensive by the joint forces. The rescued talked about the mistreatment they were subjected to by the terrorists, including the lack of food and women being forced to serve as "wives". Sources also indicate that the rescued were taken to the authorities in Mueda.
Insurgents attacked Nkonga village, in Nangade, Cabo Delgado, on 07 January, where they clashed with pro-gov militia. One member of the local forces died in the clash.
Insurgents attacked Lijungo village in Nangade, Cabo Delgado, on 07 January, reportedly killing three people. Sources indicated that the bodies were also found decapitated.

Hidden Debts trial Judge Efigenio Baptista, who presides the case at the Maputo court, refused to release official documents to the parties involved in the process of the same case in the UK. Judge Baptista said it would be a violation of the Constitution to release the documents obtained for the criminal process. The decision was reported on 10 January, although, according to the lawyer in London, the request was made at the end of December, per the report.

Two judges were expelled in Mozambique over corruption allegations, per the report on 10 January. The expulsion of Judge Acacio Mitilage in Matutuine district was confirmed by the Central Office for Combating Corruption (GCCC), for the improper handling of over 50,000 euros.  Judge Rui Dauane's expulsion was confirmed by the Superior Council of Judicial Magistrates, for his lack of honesty and inability to adapt to ethical requirements.

In 2022, Mozambique will assume the rotating presidency for the Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP) union, following Cape Verde, per the report on 07 January. The CPLP aims to improve the working conditions of affiliates and workers in general, in close to nine trade union associations from the CPLP member states, per the report.

A 32-year-old insurgent commander, named Amade Muahamed Daude, was captured in Namoto near the banks of the Rovuma River, after he had reportedly fled the attacks by joint forces in Macomia on or before 08 January.

Mozambican police on Friday, 31 December, illegally prevented a press conference, which was to be held by the Association of Human Rights Networks (ARDH) in Maputo City's Xipamanine neighborhood. The press conference was supposedly aimed at talking about the increase in bus fares, which was to be implemented the following day. However, ARDH members said a heavy police contingent on board a pickup truck was parked in front of the venue, and the ARDH head was reportedly blocked from entering the building. After several more attempts to enter the building, the ARDH head was dragged into the police truck. Police said the conference was not authorized, however, ARDH said the law does not oblige organizers of press conferences to inform police or any authority beforehand.

Terrorist attacks in Cabo Delgado have affected 123,000 primary and secondary students during the 2021 school year, according to the Ministry of Education, in a report on 09 January. The attacks since October 2017 have reportedly resulted in the destruction of 43 schools, 104 classrooms, 30 administrative blocks, and 5 district education buildings, as well as the deaths of 8 teachers, per the report.

The Nampula-Niassa railway circulation was reportedly interrupted on Saturday, 08 January, due to the heavy torrential rains that fell on the headquarters in Namina, Mecuburi district, Nampula. The railway line's support soils had been eroded by about 20 meters by waters from the Namina River, leaving the railway suspended. If the same intensity of rain hits the area, part of the soil along the railway track may collapse. During this incident, 19 houses had also reportedly been destroyed by the weather event, according to the report.

On the afternoon of 11 January, an Mozambican Air Force training plane crashed into a residence in the Aeroporto Neighborhood of Maputo City, just south of Maputo Air Base.  An instructor and a trainee were killed in the crash.  The plane had reportedly collided with a power line, causing the crash.  No civilians on the ground were injured in the accident.

The National Statistics Institute (INE) recorded price inflation of general goods in the cities of Maputo, Beira, and Nampula at 6.74% for the year 2021. INE stated that the 2021 inflation had doubled compared to 2020, which was recorded at 3.52%. The increase of prices was reportedly influenced by the cost of food and beverages in restaurants, hotels, cafes, food, transportation, and other similar commercial establishments.

Islamic State released an infographic stating that its militants carried out the sixth most attacks in Mozambique of any country in 2021 that the group is operating in. The infographic also mentioned that the group has conducted 68 attacks in the country, with 217 killed and injured.
Police arrested two drug smugglers, after exchanging fire with them briefly in Zona Militar, Maputo City, on 8 January.
Police arrested two drug smugglers, after exchanging fire with them briefly in Zona Militar, Maputo City, on 8 January.

Police arrested a suspect in possession of a weapon in Polana Canico, east Maputo City, on 8 January. The suspect claimed that he picked up the weapon at Xiquelene market and was linked to an armed robbery gang.

The Tax Authority announced on 10 January, an excess in the targeted tax collected for 2021. The Tax Authority stated that they reached 105% in overall revenue, which corresponds to 278.86 billion Meticais. 16.5% of the revenue will be provided for the reimbursement of the VAT under the Budget Law. The Tax Authority also mentioned that they intend to increase the targeted revenue collection by 2022, to 293.22 billion Meticais.

The Kimberley Process Management Unit announced that Mozambique has produced 800kg of gold in the year 2021, exceeding the intended goal of only 545kg. The Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy, Max Tonela, announced that the 800kg of gold is still only a part of Mozambique’s production as data from Manica, Zambezia, and Tete were still missing.  This is the largest gold production in Mozambique in a single year.

Pro-government militiamen assaulted a local youth in the Ndenganamade neighborhood of Nangade district on 23 December. The victim was reportedly spotted violating curfew during a night patrol leading to the incident.
Pro-government militiamen assaulted a local youth in the Ntamba neighborhood of Nangade district on the evening of 30 December. The victim was reportedly violating curfew imposed in the district.
Pro-government militiamen assaulted a local youth spotted around Ntanga, Nangade town on 5 January. The victim was reportedly violating an imposed curfew.
A fire broke out at the state car park in Tete at around 07:20 of Tuesday, 11 January. Two vehicles were destroyed by the fire. No casualties were reported.

The Bank of Mozambique announced that they will audit all the microtransaction operators in Mozambique. The Bank of Mozambique stated that a list of 472 microtransaction operators to attempt to uncover "ghost institutions".

Insurgents reportedly abducted 5 people during an attack at Lijungo village on 06 January. Insurgent reportedly burned residences during the attack. Conflicting reports stated that the attack occurred the day after on 7 January.

The Provincial Directorate of Transport and Communications announced the suspension of the implementation of the new transport tariffs in Cabo Delgado. The suspension was due to the decision that the transport association in Cabo Delgado province does not have the capacity to implement the new tariff.

Around 1,500 IDPs were reported to have recently left Negomano area due to the lack of food. Many of those who have left Negomano were originally deported from Tanzania after fleeing into the country due to insurgent attacks.  Those leaving the area are reportedly travelling into Nangade, Palma, Metuge, Montepuez, and even into Nampula.
Officials said they had opened the floodgates of the Pequenos Lebombos Dam on 10 January, to release the increasing water in the reservoir caused by the rainy season.

Defense Minister Chume announced the launch of the nationwide military census for 2022, starting in Chowke of Gaza province. Chume stated that the enlistment starts from 2 January until 28 February. Those included were individuals born until 2004 and earlier, without exceeding 35 years of age.
Police arrested a suspect for counterfeiting meticais in Manicap province on 11 January.

South African President Ramaphosa stated during the SADC Summit that the SAMIM forces had achieved “significant progress” in Cabo Delgado. The South African president also said that SAMIM forces in cooperation with the Mozambican forces have created a “safe passage” for IDPs to return to their homes and resume their lives.

The Ministry of health recorded 65 COVID related deaths during the first week of January. The ministry stated that this previous week was the highest weekly death toll since the start of the fourth COVID wave in the country. While 17,620 COVID cases were noted in the past seven days, which was less compared to the previous week. Active cases were reported to be at 37,999. Hospitalizations were at 232 cases, an increase by 31 compared to the previous week.
The villages of V Congresso, Lijungo, and Litingina, have reportedly been left almost depopulated, due to people fleeing from the recent insurgent attacks in the area, per the report on 12 January.
The villages of V Congresso, Lijungo, and Litingina, have reportedly been left almost depopulated, due to people fleeing from the recent insurgent attacks in the area, per the report on 12 January.

Recent reports indicate that one person was beheaded in a wooded area along the Nangade-Mueda border between 11-12 January.  This attack came after insurgents were reported to be in the area by a local woman, and after insurgents attacked Litingina on 09 January.
Two groups of more than 10 insurgents are reportedly moving between the districts of Nangade and Mueda, according to a report on 12 January.

The Mozambican Ministry of Health on 10 January recorded 11 COVID deaths and 592 new COVID cases in the country, in the last 24 hours. The most number of COVID cases were recorded in Nampula with 152, Maputo City with 133, and Zambezia with 128.  In the same 24-hour period, 1,802 people recovered from the virus, 850 of which were from Nampula and 388 from Sofala, while a total of 232 patients remain in hospital units.  In summary, the updated cumulative total cases as of 10 January are: 210,991 positive; 2,096 deaths, and 170,892 recoveries. Meanwhile, the country's active cases of COVID-19 continued to decrease from 39,220 to 37,999.

Insurgents in an attack that began around 1400hrs on 12 January were reported to have attacked Pitolha village west of Muaguide town, setting several homes on fire.  It was unclear if there were any casualties in this attack.

On 12 January, the SADC's Troika Summit in Lilongwe, Malawi concluded and issued a statement, saying the regional bloc was extending the SADC mission in Mozambique (SAMIM) for an undetermined amount of time, also noting that it had "extended its mandate with associated budgetary implications".  The communique itself did not provide any specific time period extension, though Mozambique's state radio reported SAMIM had been extended for 3 months; other sources also later reported that the mission had been extended for another 3 months.  SAMIM was previously extended from an initial 3-month mission beginning in July 2021 into early January 2022.

A demonstration was reported at the Canongola market of Tete city, on 12 January, where traders and vendors set fire to various materials, set up barricades, and broke bottles on the road. The protest was allegedly triggered by the Municipal Police, at the behest of the mayor, attempting to impose taxes on local traders.

Insurgents reportedly attacked a village near Malanga in Niassa Province, killing people with the use of "knives", according to a report on 05 January.  The exact date of this attack is uncertain though likely occurred in late December or early January.  This report is currently unconfirmed.

Five were killed and 15 others seriously injured in Gaza, after a thunderstorm hit the province over the weekend. Some victims were reportedly hit by lightning, while heavy rains and strong winds destroyed around 5,000 houses and left 6 health centers partially submerged in flood. An estimate of over 394,000 people in Gaza could be affected by floods in the rainy and cyclone season, which runs until the end of March.
A car accident due to speeding was reported in Nhamatanda on 09 January. It was unclear whether there were casualties during the incident.

A suspected insurgent, named Mwalimo Anli Sualehe, was captured in in Macomia District on or before 11 January, during operations by joint forces.  It was unclear where exactly he was captured. The 46-year-old was reportedly responsible for indoctrinating children to support the insurgency.  He was born in Olumbe, Palma, and is known to have preached the Quran in mosques and in markets, per the report.
SAMIM forces near Litingina were reported to be on high alert and conducting operations near Litigina along the Nangade-Mueda border after insurgent activity in the area in early January.

Pro-government militia reportedly exchanged gunfire with insurgents on 11 January, near Litingina, after insurgents were seen in the area. No casualties were reported in the incident, which resulted in the retreat or insurgents per the report.

Traffic was stopped on the road between Nangade and Mueda, as well as other routes from Nangade, over the last 24 hours, according to a report on 11 January, as joint forces continued operations in pursuit of insurgents in the area.

Insurgents attacked Luneke village (also sometimes called Unidade), about 10kms south of Nangade town, at around noon on 12 January.  Insurgents reportedly beheaded two civilians during this attack. Due to this attack, traffic between Mueda and Nangade was interrupted. It was unclear whether they clashed with joint forces during this attack.

Joint SAMIM and Mozambican forces reportedly captured 7 insurgents close to Nangade town, according to a report on 13 January. The joint forces had been pursuing 2 groups of 10 insurgents in Nangade area, for several days, per a report.  It was unclear if some of those captured had participated in the Luneke attack on 12 January.
The district of Mocimboa da Praia, Cabo Delgado, announced the partial resumption of some schools in the area beginning 05 January.

The National Institute for Disaster and Risk Management (INGD) warned of flooding in the districts of Magude and Manhica, Maputo Province, due to the rise in the flow of the Incomati River, on Monday, 10 January. Extensive flooding and impassability of some localities have been recorded in the areas, per the report.

The National Institute for Disaster and Risk Management (INGD) warned of flooding in the districts of Magude and Manhica, Maputo Province, due to the rise in the flow of the Incomati River, on Monday, 10 January. Extensive flooding and impassability of some localities have been recorded in the areas, per the report.

There is a buildup of over 122 imported cars as of 06 January at Mtambaswala across the border from Negomano along the border with Tanzania, as the road between Negomano and Mueda remained impassable due to the Nahavarra village attack by insurgents on 04 January.

The Mozambican Ministry of Health on 11 January recorded 3 COVID deaths and 1,868 new COVID cases in the country, in the last 24 hours. The most number of COVID cases were recorded in Maputo City with 260, Manica with 256, and Nampula with 227.  In the same 24-hour period, 2,646 people recovered from the virus, making this the third day in a row with recoveries exceeding new COVID cases in a day.  There were also 44 people discharged from hospitals, while 33 were also admitted.  A total of 217 patients remain in hospital units.  In summary, the updated cumulative total cases as of 11 January are: 212,859 positive; 2,099 deaths, and 173,538 recoveries. Meanwhile, the country's active cases of COVID-19 continued to decrease from 37,999 to 37,218.

The Ministry of Health announced that a total of 9,792,465 individuals have been vaccinated with at least one dose against COVID-19 as of 10 January.  There were 129,866 people who were vaccinated with the first dose in the last 24 hours, under the third phase of the National Mass Vaccination Campaign.  Since the start of vaccinations on 08 March, Mozambique has a total of 7,591,682 people, fully-vaccinated against COVID-19.
Police detained 24 IDPs who had reportedly escaped from an insurgent camp, near Nkonga village, in Nangade district on 7 January.
Unconfirmed reports stated that gunfire exchanges between the insurgents and joint forces occurred at the Quirimbas National Park, south of Mucojo, on 5 January. Casualties were not reported.

Around 22,000 locals are isolated due to the submerged roads and bridges from the rising river levels in Boane district as of 12 January. The roads in the district connect to eight neighborhoods, and boats are currently being used to transport the locals to and from the district.
South African officials announced, on 11 January, that 9,171 Mozambicans were repatriated back to Mozambique due to illegal residency and criminal charges over the course of 2021.
A Mozambican soldier opened fire in the air during a dispute with his girlfriend in Ntanga neighborhood of Nangade town, on night of 10 January.

The National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD) stated that the contingency plan for the rain and cyclone season is still lacking funds for the 2021-2022 season. The INGD stated that they require around 10.6 billion meticais to aid 1.5 million Mozambicans. INGD further stated that only 7.3 billion meticais was obtained.

President Filipe Nyusi arrived in Malawi to attend the two-day SADC summit on 11 and 12 January. The summit discussed the SAMIM forces' contribution and performance against the insurgency. The summit also discussed the potential intensifying of operations against the insurgents in Cabo Delgado.

The SADC called for a comprehensive plan to rebuild Cabo Delgado province during the Troika Summit on 11 January. The SADC stated that ensuring the local population will be assisted after the clearing out of the insurgents is critical.
Security forces held a driver and seized 5 tons of smuggled fish in Tete province on 9 January. This driver paid 180,000 meticais as fine for smuggling the fish.
Security forces held a driver and seized 5 tons of smuggled fish in Tete province on 9 January. This driver paid 180,000 meticais as fine for smuggling the fish.

The National Inspectorate for Economic Activities (INAE) condemned the rise of fake inspectors who are taking money from establishments to be excluded from inspections. People pretending to be government inspectors are operating reportedly mostly in Maputo City and Matola, and are targeting establishments wanting to be exempted from inspections, according to INAE on 12 January.
Police arrested a suspect for impersonating an employee of Mozambique Electricity on 12 January.

Sources on 12 January stated that SAMIM forces were supported by just two South African Air Force Oryx utility helicopters conducting airlifts during operations in Cabo Delgado. The helicopters were transporting special forces from South Africa, Tanzania, Botswana, and Lesotho.  To date, the South African military has not deployed any attack helicopters which had been meant to be part of the SAMIM force.  Meanwhile, a South African navy vessel sent to Cabo Delgado last year has reportedly been withdrawn due to a mechanical problem and not replaced.

SAMIM forces reportedly killed 31 insurgents during operations around the districts of Cabo Delgado between October 2021 and January 2022 as part of "Operation Buffalo". During this time, SAMIM said its forces disrupted insurgent activities and positions, while also encountering resistance from the insurgents. Three SAMIM casualties, including a death, were recorded during the same time of the operations. SAMIM forces managed to seize 5 RPG-7, 5 PKM machine guns, 48 AK-47 weapons, grenades, vehicles, motorcycles, mobile phones, and other equipment during operations during this time.

The Companhia Industrial de Matola (CIM) announced on 12 January that flour prices will increase by 11%, which will also affect prices of bread in Mozambique. CIM announced that a 50kg of sack of flour costing 1800 meticais will reach 2000 meticais once the prices increase on 15 January.
Portuguese President de Sousa intended to visit Mozambique on 7 January, but the visit had been cancelled due to the current pandemic situation in the country.
Locals mobbed and injured a civilian who was accused of stealing a gas cylinder in Boane district on 07 January. The victim denied the claims and stated that he was a neighbor of the locals.
Locals mobbed and injured a civilian who was accused of stealing a gas cylinder in Boane district on 07 January. The victim denied the claims and stated that he was a neighbor of the locals.

The Community of Portuguese Speaking Countries (CPLP) announced that ease of movement agreement between countries came into force on 1 January. The agreement is initially limited for diplomatic and services passports. The agreement exempted CPLP members from being required a visa. General public passports will still require visas until each CPLP state has formalized the agreement.

IDPs were reported to be leaving Taratara IDP center in Metuge District as they returned to their homes in Quissanga on 6 January. The IDPs center was in poor condition, lacking food support and livelihood programs.

Sources stated that SAMIM forces will extend their mission again automatically in 3 months after the current extension into mid-April expires. Additional regular infantry and other support elements will be deployed for reinforcement of special forces in Cabo Delgado at this time. The infantry will assist in maintain ground against the insurgents and assist the local populace in rebuilding civil structures in the province.  There is concern however that special forces at this time could be withdrawn from Cabo Delgado at this time.
The SADC reportedly is seeking foreign funding for extended mission of SAMIM forces in Mozambique, according to a 12 January report. To date, SADC countries have funded the SAMIM operation.

An MDP official said that the return of population to Mocimboa da Praia will be allowed soon. The official stated that water, electricity, and other public services were being restored before the local population will be allowed to return.
Police arrested a suspect in possession of narcotics in Maputo on 13 January. The suspect had concealed narcotics hidden in cigarettes.

Reports on 13 January indicated that SAMIM's extension over the next three months will cost 29.5 million USD in Mozambique.  Each SADC country has so far provided funding for the mission, though the SADC will reportedly seek foreign funding for the mission going forward.

Police Gen. Commander Bernardino Rafael announced that policemen requesting payment for vehicle parking at police stations around the country should end. Locals previously complained that police were ticking drivers who did not pay police for parking at stations.

Joint forces operations between Mozambican police and Rwandan forces are ongoing in Mocimboa da Praia town, where joint forces have conducted 3,000 house-to-house searches in Mocimboa da Praia as of 13 January. A majority of these homes are abandoned, and troops have recently seized “war materials” and military uniforms believed to have been used by insurgents in attacks.  MDP was controlled for year from August of 2020 to August of 2021 by the insurgency before a joint forces offensive retook the town in early August 2021.

The  Association of Combatants of the National Liberation Struggle (ACCLIN) Sec. Gen. Fernando Faustino said on 13 January that Mozambique's combat veterans were "reinforcing surveillance" in their communities in order to prevent the spread of terrorism in Northern Mozambique.  The Association also expressed "readiness" to fight against terrorism in Cabo Delgado.

Around 3,000 individuals are reportedly at risk of losing access to a partially collapsed bridge along the Ingahome-Quelimane road, southeast of Quelimane as of 13 January. The 150m bridge was reportedly built on 2018 to replace a previously destroyed bridge last 2013. The National Roads Administration clarified that the bridge was initially built to last for 5 to 10 years, however the bridge was not built properly.

Around 70 part time and other full time professors of Universidade Lurio threatened to conduct a strike over unpaid salaries since 2021 in Nampula city on 13 January. A majority of the professors were among the Faculty of Health Sciences.  The strike would begin on 17 January.

The Chinese airline, China Southern Airlines, announced a suspension of flights to Mozambique on 11 January. The airlines also suspended flights to 37 other countries. The airline said that the suspension was temporary due to the current increasing COVID cases in these selected countries.

The National Institute of Land Transport (INATRO) announced on 13 January the suspension of producing driving licenses due to a contract termination with their supplier. INATRO clarified that the contract termination was due to the irregularities seen with the supplier. INATRO also stated that drivers will be able to use temporarily issued licenses.

Matola officials announced that they required funding of around 70 million USD to end the flooding issues around Matola on 13 January. Officials stated that the resolution for the sewage systems in Matola is part of the contingency plan for floods and soil erosion in the area.

The Ministry of Health announced that 7.9 million locals have been fully vaccinated with their second dose of COVID vaccines as of 13 January. 177, 608 individuals have been vaccinated for the first time within the past 24 hours. 9.9 million people have received at least one shot.

The Ministry of Health announced 1,724 new COVID cases and four related deaths in Mozambique on 13 January. Maputo City recorded 346 of the new cases, while Zamebzia was the second province with 221 of the new cases. 23 of the new COVID cases were hospitalized bring the total hospitalizations to 8,191. While active cases were at 204.
The Ministry of Health announced two new COVID testing sites in Maputo City on 14 January. The sites were located at the Interprovincial Bus Terminal and Mercado Central de Maputo.

A Mozambican Court in Maputo City has cleared a former Standard Bank manager, Adimohanma Chukwuma of currency market manipulation on 13 January. The former manager was previously charged with manipulating the foreign exchange and authorizing payments outside the country.  The Bank of Mozambique previously issued accusations on the former bank manager last 13 August 2021.  The court upheld a charge against Chuwuma of illegally implementing a payment network outside of Mozambique without the authorization of the Mozambican Central Bank.

The UNHCR issued a statement saying that the humanitarian situation in Cabo Delgado has been worsening due to the ongoing conflict with insurgency in the province. The UNCHR stated that displacement of the locals was the main issue during 2021. This comes as around 800,000 IDPs have been displaced in the province, including 48% were children with 84% were living in temporary shelters.

Officials announced that malaria cases have seen a decline in Mozambique by 11% in 2021 in comparison to 2020. The National Malaria Contro Program stated that 10.6 million cases were recorded on 2021, while 11 million cases were reported in 2020.

The Ministry of Health announced 1,948 new COVID cases and six related deaths on 12 January. The positivity rate reportedly increased during the past 24 hours from 30.13% to 32.12%. 312 of the new cases were in Maputo City, 215 in Maputo province, 134 in Gaza province, 363 in Inhambane, 243 in Sofala province, 231 in Zambezia province, 144 in Tete province, 126 in Nampula province, 86 in Manica province, 54 in Niassa province, and 40 in Cabo Delgado province.

The Malawi President Chakwera stated during a speech in the SADC Summit that SADC must have a plan to rebuild northern Mozambique. At the SADC's Lilongwe summit, the bloc said that their support for Mozambique was not limited to clearing out the insurgents from Northern Mozambique, but also rebuilding the local communities.

The Minister of Defense Chume in a speech on 12 January called for caution as IDPs returned to liberated areas of Cabo Delgado, also saying there were "more and more" advances against the insurgency in the province.  He also said there were positive developments in Niassaas well, and that joint forces were doing everything to eliminate terrorists from Mozambique.  He also said that there was still "work to be done" to allow the return of the population to Mocimboa da Praia.
Police arrested a suspect for sexually assaulting a minor in Mozambique on 14 January. The suspect claimed that the victim's parents accepted a bribe for the assault of the child.

Armed soldiers reportedly assaulted two individuals who were caught crossing the Mueda airstrip on 14 January.  A video of the incident showed one local being whipped by security force members for this transgression.  A military source later said the individual whipped in the video was a soldier receiving punishment.

Four armed suspected insurgents attacked fishermen at the island of Macaloe Island on the afternoon of Thursday, 13 January. A civilian was killed during the incident . The armed individuals also stole the fish from the deceased. The victims were reportedly fishermen who fled Matemo island due to the insurgency.  Initial reports had said insurgents had attacked Quilhaule Island, though other sources later reported the attack took place on Macaloe, just east of Pangane

Pro-government militiamen rescued three detained women in Luneke village on 12 January. The women were reportedly from Nampula and Niassa provinces. Insurgents had attacked the village earlier in the day; the circumstances of this rescue were not immediately clear.

ISCAP claimed an attack on Lichengue village of Mecula District, on 15 December, saying its fighters burned homes and several vehicles in the raid.  Other sources said this attack may have occurred on or around 12 December, when there was a loss of cell phone service in the area allegedly due to an insurgent sabotage incident.

ISCAP claimed its fighters had attacked Chimene village, south of Mecula, on 16 December. The insurgents claimed that a soldier was killed, and a military vehicle was burned down in the raid.  This incident is unconfirmed.

Security forces arrested two suspected insurgents during operations in Ntamba and Litingina of Nangade District during a patrol on 25 December. The detainees were reportedly transferred to Nangade town, where militia reportedly beat one of the prisoners with a stick; a video of this beating was later released online.
Joint forces in the wake of the 17-22 December Chai offensive were reported to have arrested at least 8 insurgents in the area.

Insurgents shot dead a fisherman after refusing to act as a guide for the militants near Olumbua on 31 December. The insurgents intended to travel on the main road with the fishermen to avoid suspicion.

ISCAP claimed conducting an attack targeting an armored military vehicle in Nalama of Mecula District on 03 December. The vehicle was burned down injuring several soldiers according to ISCAP.  This claim is unconfirmed.

ISCAP claimed an 06 December on Macalange, saying its fighters had burned down several homes and other buildings.  There were previously reports of insurgents attacking Macalange on 03 December, which this claim likely refers to.

Three insurgents abducted a group of fishermen after raiding Ilha Magundula, north of Matemo Island, on 12 December. Two of the fishermen were injured after escaping. The insurgents also looted food supplies from the island before returning back to the coast of Mucojo.

Security officials announced on 20 December that IDPs returning to Palma will be allowed to return after registering beforehand to prevent insurgent infiltration into the area.  Security officials stated that once economic conditions have improved significantly in the coming months, they will allow IDPs outside of Palma district to return to the area.  Authorities also reportedly suspect some IDPs from other areas are attempting to travel into Palma to take advantage of economic opportunities in the area.

Mozambican and Tanzanian security officials conducted a meeting in Cabo Delgado on 20 December. The meeting entailed strengthening their cooperation on military and policing along the Cabo Delgado-Tanzania border. Another point of the meeting was to discuss the insurgency in both countries and their scope regarding the issue.

A recently signed agreement between Mozambique and Rwanda includes an agreement to establish security cordons along Cabo Delgado borders with Niassa and Nampula to stop the spread of terrorism from Cabo Delgado into these provinces.

Police arrested a suspect for starting demonstrations in Canongola, Tete City, on 12 January. This comes as a demonstration occurred at the market of Canongola previously.

Police officials announced that 44 people were killed and 42 injured in 48 vehicular accidents that occurred last 2021 in Manica province. Police stated that the total number of accidents and casualties have seen a slight decline compared to 2020.

The Ministry of Health announced that 8.1 million locals have fully completed their COVID vaccination as of 14 January. 121,269 individuals obtained their first COVID vaccine in the past 24 hours, while 10.1 million locals have received their first COVID vaccine since the start of the National Mass Campaign.
Police arrested a murder suspect for killing a civilian after suspecting her of witchcraft in Zambezia early morning of 10 January. The suspect used a machete to conduct the crime.

The Nampula Secretary of State called for vigilance to prevent insurgency from spreading into Nampula province. The Secretary of State mentioned that insurgents intend to flee from Cabo Delgado and could attempt to entrench themselves in Nampula.

Authorities announced that trade between Mozambique and UAE has grown by 140% over the past 5 years. The volume of trade has reportedly reached 600 million USD as of 2020. The entry of Dubai Chamber of Commerce has boosted trade by 250 million USD. 400 million USD was the exports from Dubai to Mozambique.

The Ministry of Health announced 1,752 new COVID cases and four related deaths in Mozambique on 13 January. This comes as Maputo City continues to remains with the highest number of case with 346 cases, Zambezia with 221, 212 cases from Inhambane, 186 in Maputo province, 182 in Nampula, 152 in Sofala, 109 in Tete, 105 in Gaza, 88 in Niassa, 82 in Cabo Delgado, and 69 in Manica.

Sources stated on 14 January that criminal activity is currently rampant in Chiure. Some locals leave the town at night, travelling to other towns to avoid criminal attacks.  In the past 3 weeks, locals say 17 robberies have taken place in the town.
Two smugglers trafficked six Malawi men between the Malawi-Mozambique border between Mangochi and Mandimba on 14 September.  This group were later arrested by Malawian authorities.

ISCAP claimed an attack on the village of Pitolha, west of Muaguide, on 14 January, setting fire to at least 20 houses. This likely refers to a confirmed attack on this village on 12 January.  One source said the claim referenced the village of "Kitulia".
ISCAP claimed an attack on the village of Citate / Sitate, Meluco district, on 13 January, reportedly setting fire to at least 60 houses.

However, recent reports indicate a new attack was carried out by insurgents in the said village on Saturday, 15 January, where three men had been beheaded; this is likely the attack referred to in this claim.

The Mozambican Ministry of Health on Friday, 14 January, recorded 1,262 new COVID cases and 8 related deaths in the country, in the last 24 hours.  The positivity rate fell from 29.03% on Thursday to 24.15% on Friday.  In the same 24-hour period, 2,072 people recovered from the virus.

The Mozambican and SAMIM forces carried out joint operations on 16 January, seizing weapons and other materials from terrorist camps in Nangade district.  It was not immediately clear where in Nangade District this operation took place.

A freight train crashed into a truck that was traveling between the neighborhoods of Liberty and May 1st, in Moatize, Tete Province, around 12:00 on Saturday, 15 January. Only material damage was reported. Witnesses say the truck driver stopped at the railway crossing and, noting that it was safe, he went ahead. However, the train suddenly appeared, reportedly without sounding its whistle, hitting the truck.

The Hidden Debts trial will resume hearings in the giant tent installed at the Maximum Security Penitentiary in Maputo Province, on 17 January, as previously announced, after a month of interruption.  The former president of Mozambique, Armando Guebuza, will be the last deponent, scheduled to be heard on 17 February. The court expects to complete the trial within a month, though the new schedule may still change if necessary, per the announcement on 16 January.

IDPs hosted in Mecula village, Niassa are reportedly in need of more support to survive, according to Niassa Governor, Judite Massengele, in a report on 15 January. The armed attacks in Mecula district, between November and December 2021, have caused displacements to over 3,000 people, who are now sheltered in Mecula village and entirely dependent on donations. Massengele says conditions are now being created for the population to practice agriculture, so the IDPs can produce and increase their own food base, for which, the gov't, with the support of its partners, will make material and agricultural inputs available.  In addition, projects are also underway to prepare for the academic year so displaced students can take classes. Data on students and teachers are being collected, and partners have been mobilized to provide tents for use as classrooms.

A suspected insurgent named "Ali", was captured in Nangade, according to a report on 17 January; other sources later said he was captured on 29 December.  Another source identified the man captured as "Juma Said Mussa", while another report said that Mussa and Ali were different people. One source said that Ali was among a group of 7 insurgents previously captured; other sources reported he was captured in Palma district.  It was not immediately clear where the man was arrested within Nangade District. Ali was reportedly recruited forcibly from Pangane village in October 2020.  Another source described him as one of the terrorist leaders in Mucojo, Macomia district, and has reportedly spent time at the bases of Muera and Mocimboa da Praia, and had lead insurgent recruitment efforts.  He also said that he was made to command a vessel off the Mucojo coast, launching raids against civilians in this area.  He also added that the war in Cabo Delgado is being waged by the insurgents for the implantation of Islam, which, to them, must be the only religion.

In Zambezia, around 27,000 people, in the villages of Vila-Valdez and Nomiua, are exposed to danger when crossing the Licungo River to reach Maganja da Costa. The only vessel used for crossing is managed by a local committee and is in poor condition, reportedly seeping water during every voyage. The district administrator says the best solution is to build a bridge.  This comes as the Licungo river recorded fluctuations in water levels in the last week; at one point reaching 51cm short of an alert level, per the report on 16 January.

The UN Dep't for Economic and Social Affairs (UNDESA) says in the medium term, structural reforms are needed in Mozambique to accelerate the 3.8% growth forecast in its economy for 2022, due to the increased production of natural gas, exports of coal and aluminum, and infrastructure projects in mining and energy. The country's economy is reportedly growing fragile, due to the effects of the pandemic and the continued insecurity in Cabo Delgado; however, the UNDESA defends that reforms to the country's infrastructure are necessary to sustain recovery.  On the issue of public debt, the country is still feeling the effects of the 2016 debt issues, although international donors have returned to engage with the country, per the report on 16 January.

Three men were decapitated by insurgents in Nova Zambezia village, south of Chai, Cabo Delgado, on the morning of Saturday at around 0900hrs 15 January.  Locals said the victims were in the company of their wives in the fields during the incident.  The insurgents interrogated the men about the presence of the Defense and Security Forces in the area. After the interrogation, the terrorists reportedly beheaded the men and allowed the wives to go home.  A later report indicated the women were forced to carry their husbands' heads back to the village - similar to reports of another previous attack in the area.

People in Nkoe village, west of Nova Zambezia, on 16 January reported seeing insurgents within the vicinity of their village.  Nkoe is at high risk of an attack, and was also targeted by insurgents on 15 December.  Some residents fled the village due to the insurgent threat.

Joint Mozambican and SAMIM forces reportedly clashed with insurgents in the village of 3 de Fevereiro, 7km from the village of Nangade, on Saturday night, 15 January. Troops reportedly deployed to the area after reports of insurgent activity near the village. One source reported troops had previously briefly deployed to the area at the request of village elders as the village held an initiation ceremony, and that after troops left, insurgents attacked tthe village, killing 6 people.  Joint forces then swiftly returned to the village, clashing with insurgents and driving them away from the area.  No information was available regarding casaulties in this clash. This attack reportedly caused unrest in the population in nearby Nangade, as well as the IDPs sheltered in the said village.

Insurgents, in an attack at around 1700hrs on 16 January, killed 5 people in Limwalamwala, near 3rd of February village in Nangade District.  Another source reported 6 people killed, saying the attack took place on 15 January, with 4 people shot dead and two beheaded. Dozens of homes in the area were also set on fire. This came one day after reports on 15 January indicated that joint SAMIM and Mozambican forces had clashed with insurgents near 3rd of February village.  Conflicting reports said the attack occurred just after joint forces left the village after a brief deployment to the area, and that joint forces returned to the village amid the militant attack, driving insurgents out of the area.

Insurgents on 16 January raided Nkoe village in Macomia District at around 2000hrs, west of the N380 road, setting homes on fire though no casualties were reported.  Civilians from the area fled into the woods and towards Macomia town.  Prior to this raid, reports from the Nkoe had also indicated that suspected insurgents had been seen in the vicinity of the village.  The day before, on 15 January, militants beheaded three men in the Nova Zambezia area, just a few kms east of Nkoe.

One IDP said they had not received food in the last 5 months.  Others also complained of having no water and no bathroom.  IDPs are taking to the streets to ask for food in order to survive, per the report on 17 January.

Senior customs staff, customs clearance agents, and business people participated in the corruption scheme. When no buyer showed, the criminals left the severed head in the Muandiwa locality of Morrumbala, Zambezia, and fled. The crime is reportedly linked to a ritual involving the belief that a bald man's head contains gold.

The suspect was reportedly from Maputo and was only visiting when he committed the murder. Police detained the suspect early morning on 10 January.

Two schools were also destroyed, while two bridges and two health centers had also been damaged. The road connecting Memba to Nacala-Velha is also in danger of erosion from flooding, per the report.

Many children in Mogovolas district, Nampula, have abandoned school and chosen to work as illegal miners or livestock shepherds. According to the district's education service in a report on 13 January, many poor families are attracted by illegal mining, believing that it is the quick solution to their poverty.  Many students still enroll in the district though only a few remain by the end of the school year.
Residents of Inharrime, on the outskirts of Beira city, Sofala have said there has been a wave of crimes in the area is due to the lack of public lighting, per the report on 17 January.

Merchants in Maputo no longer accept 50 cent coins in payments, allegedly due to its loss of value, according to a report on 17 January. Experts say this is due to the rise in the cost of living in the province. The Bank of Mozambique has also stopped issuing 50-cent coins because the public no longer used them and the cost of production had exceeded the coin's value over time. The coins that remain in circulation are reportedly from those issued in 2006.

Around 65,000 people have had no access to the Matola Santos Health Center, which has been closed since 30 December, due to flooding in the area. Residents accused Matola's district administrator and the Mayor of being indifferent to the situation, though the local gov't says they are working to find a solution to the problem, according to the report on 17 January.

There is a lack of water in Mocimboa da Praia, which the IDPs will need upon their return, according to the district's permanent secretary in a report on 17 January.  Around 2,000 of the 171,000 inhabitants of the area have returned, and people have to travel long distances to find water despite the dangers of insurgency, on the outskirts of the region.

The Niassa governor  Judite Massengele said in a 18 January interview that there were no Rwandan troops in Mecula district, despite reports of some Rwandan troops being deployed in the area after insurgent attacks began in the district in late November. The governor also denied the accusations that security forces had kidnapped merchants and religious leaders, who allegedly collaborated with insurgents, noting that local authorities were not aware of this, according to a report on 18 January.

Around 5,000 people have been affected by the rise in the water level of the Incomati river in Manhica district, Maputo province. Both people and goods cannot cross the river due to this rise, caused by the discharges from South Africa's dams, according to the report on 18 January.

The Maputo Province Judicial Court on 14 January sentenced poaching gang leader, Admiro Chauque, to 30 years in prison and 28 years of paying fines, corresponding to 1% of the minimum wage.  Admiro was arrested for the second time, on 3 May 2021, for attempting to hunt rhinoceros along the SA/Moz border.

According to Human Rights Watch, the humanitarian crisis in Cabo Delgado worsened in 2021, due to the ongoing violence in the northern region of the province. Over 800,000 people were internally displaced due to the violence as of September. Of those displaced, 48% were children, and over 84% lived in temporary accommodation and host communities across the country. The number of IDPs increased significantly in March, when over 88,000 people fled Palma due to a major insurgent attack in the town. Many sought refuge in Quitunda, 5km from Palma, where they lacked water, food, and other basic needs. By July, UN's World Food Program (WFP) warned that the crisis risked becoming a hunger emergency. Humanitarian groups were also unable to reach communities most affected by the violence, due to security risks. Assistance reached the areas of Palma, Macomia, Mocimboa da Praia, Muidumbe, and Quissangga only beginning September, when security improved. However, during this period, allegations emerged of some aid workers demanding money or sex before distributing food parcels to women. As of October, no investigation was made by the gov't.

The Human Rights Watch reported abuses by gov't forces, during counterterrorism operations in Cabo Delgado in 2021. IDPs who had fled to Quitunda from Palma were prohibited from leaving and were physically assaulted by gov't forces when trying to flee. Distressed residents were forced to pay bribes to be guaranteed a seat on rescue flights, though no action was taken to investigate these reports. Abuse was also confirmed against imprisoned women. Prison guards took women inmates outside the prison and forced them to have sex with strangers. A reform was recommended by the Center for Public Integrity (CIP) to explicitly criminalize sexual relations between inmates and guards, and that women prisoners should be supervised only by women guards.

According to Human Rights Watch, insurgents are using hundreds of kidnapped women and girls in Cabo Delgado in child and forced marriages, and as sex slaves.  Insurgents have released others after families paid huge amounts of ransom in 2021. Meanwhile, refugees and asylum seekers who had fled the insurgency to Tanzania were forcibly returned to Mozambique. As of September, the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said over 10,300 refugees had been sent back since the start of the year.  Unresolved kidnappings continued to increase across the country in 2021, according to the National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC). At least 6 kidnapping cases remained unresolved as of October.

Northern and central Mozambique was affected by very dry seasons between October to December 2021, according to the World Food Programme (WFP). Extreme drought was reported in this period in northern Mozambique, with as little as 30% of the usual amounts of rainfall reported during this time. According to WFP's forecast, drier than average conditions will continue in northern Mozambique, extending towards the end of January 2022.

A warrant of arrest was issued against Alexandre Chivale, a lawyer for the family of former President Guebuza, for not appearing before the court during the Hidden Debts trial hearing on 18 January. The court was informed that Chivale was out of the country and on vacation. However, Judge Efigenio Baptista said Chivale's absence was a crime of disobedience as well as an act of boycott.

Traders in Manica province have accused Tax Authority agents of illegally charging them for their commercial establishments, per the report on 18 January.  Traders alleged that agents would visit their establishment and ask for all kinds of documents, including proof of start of activities, license, workers' permit, among others; and when one document is missing, agents would ask for money.  If documents are complete, the agents would allegedly look for other flaws to force the merchant to pay fines, not channeled to the state.

Vehicles and hundreds of houses were destroyed in fires, including two health centers and two classrooms, during insurgent attacks from November to December 2021 in Mecula district, Niassa, according to a report on 18 January. In all, 554 houses were destroyed by militants in different raids, including 283 in Lichengue, 122 in Macalange, 63 in Napiqueche, 28 in Naulala I, and 58 in Naulala II.
